evidence.title: Kuehne+Nagel says China's expansion and hyperscalers' data centers are keeping freight rates firm
evidence.text:
Kuehne+Nagel says China's expansion and hyperscalers' data centers are keeping freight rates firm

In a Thursday interview in London, CEO Stefan Paul pointed to two forces lifting the business: Chinese companies expanding into overseas markets and a buildout of data centers by hyperscalers. "These two blocks are driving demand," he said, adding that the mix is helping keep today's elevated cargo rates from fading in the near term.

The data center buildout and a fresh Amazon deal

Paul said demand for data center logistics is being driven largely by US tech companies and looks "secured for the next three years," with "double-digit growth" still anticipated until 2029. Kuehne +Nagel also announced a contract this week to handle data center logistics for Amazon.com Inc., a headline that helped push the stock to its highest level in two years.

According to Paul, Chinese producers - most notably carmakers - are targeting sales in regions outside the US. At the same time, he noted, "Trade lanes are growing from China into other markets like the US because this is where they find a home for their products." Net result: more China outbound flows into multiple destinations, including the US.

evidence.title: “A Shared Focus on Scale, Innovation and Customer Value”: Kuehne+Nagel CEO Stefan Paul on Long Term Amazon Partnership
evidence.text:
Kuehne+Nagel has entered into a long-term strategic collaboration with Amazon spanning logistics, cloud infrastructure and supply chain operations, as the companies look to strengthen resilience, scalability and customer service.

Kuehne+Nagel Expands Relationship with Amazon

Kuehne+Nagel has announced a long-term strategic collaboration with Amazon designed to support future business opportunities and expand services for the technology and e-commerce company and its affiliates.

The agreement builds on the companies’ existing relationship and forms part of Kuehne+Nagel’s strategic growth initiatives, with the logistics provider highlighting scale, innovation and customer value as key areas of focus.

“We are excited to enter this long-term collaboration with Amazon, with a shared focus on scale, innovation and customer value. Kuehne+Nagel’s global network, digital capabilities and supply chain expertise are well positioned to support Amazon’s evolving business needs, enabling us to accelerate future growth opportunities and create lasting value for our customers. We are setting the foundation for a new level of customer service commitment at a global scale for Amazon,” said Stefan Paul, CEO of Kuehne+Nagel International AG.

Collaboration Extends to AWS Infrastructure

The collaboration also encompasses Amazon Web Services (AWS) and the infrastructure lifecycle supporting its operations.

Kuehne+Nagel will provide services covering areas ranging from construction and equipment deployment through to ongoing maintenance, upgrades and expansion projects.

By expanding its work with Amazon and AWS, Kuehne+Nagel said the collaboration will strengthen supply chain resilience, scalability and operational efficiency as the companies support the continued growth of cloud infrastructure globally.

The agreement places Kuehne+Nagel’s logistics network and supply chain capabilities behind infrastructure throughout different stages of its lifecycle, extending the scope of the companies’ existing relationship.

The collaboration is supported by a call option on existing Kuehne+Nagel shares, which can be settled in cash or, at Amazon’s election, in shares.

Vesting will be based on commercial milestones and services delivered over a period of up to seven years.

Kuehne+Nagel has also arranged for a third-party financial institution to undertake hedging transactions in Kuehne+Nagel shares to support the arrangement.

The agreement will draw on Kuehne+Nagel’s international logistics network, which comprises approximately 88,000 employees across more than 1,300 sites in close to 100 countries.

The Switzerland-headquartered company provides Air, Sea, Road and Contract Logistics services and supports around 400,000 customers worldwide.

Through the new collaboration, Kuehne+Nagel and Amazon will build on their existing relationship as they target greater resilience and operational efficiency across Amazon’s evolving global supply chain and infrastructure requirements.

evidence.title: Les CMA CGM Startup Awards récompensent six pépites de l'IA et du maritime
evidence.text:
Les CMA CGM Startup Awards récompensent six pépites de l'IA et du maritime

Six pépites ont été primées sur quatre thèmes métiers et deux défis portés par la Fondation CMA CGM.

Les enjeux et les actualités économiques de votre région, tous les mardis.

Face aux défis de l’IA et de la décarbonation, le Groupe CMA CGM a distingué dans le cadre de l’AIM six lauréats lors de la troisième édition de ses Startup Awards, organisée avec Zebox pour tester et déployer leurs innovations sur le terrain.

Pour inventer l’avenir du transport, de la logistique et des médias, CMA CGM ( propriétaire de La Provenc e) mise sur l’hybridation avec les jeunes pousses. Lors de la troisième édition des CMA CGM Startup Awards, Rodolphe Saadé a réaffirmé, ce jeudi 24 septembre 2026, sur la scène de l’AIM installée sur la pelouse du Cepac Vélodrome, cette ambition : " Nous aimons être mis au défi chez CMA CGM ", saluant des entrepreneurs qui " pensent vite et efficacement ".

Organisé par Zebox, l’accélérateur du groupe , " ce concours international a reçu 350 candidatures, dont plus de 50% venues de l’étranger ", souligne Frédéric Guilleux, le directeur. Après les pitchs des 50 finalistes (cinq minutes de présentation, cinq de questions-réponses), six pépites ont été primées sur quatre thèmes métiers et deux défis portés par la Fondation CMA CGM : Hodor (Karim Boussetta) s’occupe de la sécurisation et la traçabilité des agents d’IA en entreprise. Crabi Robotics (Levi Gershon) a développé un robot autonome nettoyant les coques à flot pour réduire la consommation de carburant quand Meikai (Rachid Ait Addi) mesure et optimise la visibilité des marques dans l’IA générative.

Mercateam (Adrien Laurentin) mise sur la gestion dynamique des compétences et plannings sur les terminaux et Kumulus Water (Mohamed Ait Ali) produit de l’eau potable par captage de l’humidité de l’air en zone de crise. StudiAva (Wassim Benouis) fait le lien entre orientation et employabilité via l’IA FuturIA de sa plateforme. Les six lauréats rejoignent le programme Zebox, gagnent en visibilité avec CMA Médias et vont tester leurs solutions en conditions réelles au sein du Groupe et de ses partenaires.

Votre opinion compte pour nous. Rejoignez la communauté laprovence .com en réagissant sur l'article Les CMA CGM Startup Awards récompensent six pépites de l'IA et du maritime .

evidence.title: CMA CGM Start-up Awards : ces pépites qui dessinent l’avenir
evidence.text:
CMA CGM Start-up Awards : ces pépites qui dessinent l’avenir

Ce contenu est réservé aux abonnés La Tribune

La troisième édition des CMA CGM Start-up Awards a distingué six nouvelles pépites ce jeudi à Marseille, lors de l'AIM

Nouveau problème de qualité chez Airbus, sur des A321neo, mais sans impact sur la sécurité et les livraisons

Aux États-Unis, les raffineurs préviennent Trump : un embargo sur le diesel peut renchérir l’essence

Agro-alimentaire : l'Andalousie veut suspendre le régime douanier couvrant l'essentiel des achats d'huile d'olive tunisienne

Harmattan AI : à l’usine Valeo de Sainte-Florine, les salariés se bousculent pour fabriquer ses drones

Coup de tonnerre chez Eurenco : Thierry Francou démissionne

Le monde de l’innovation va toujours plus vite et l’IA en accélère encore davantage le tempo. D’où l’intérêt croisé des grands groupes et des start-up de nouer le dialogue, les premiers pour anticiper les bouleversements de leur secteur, les seconds pour trouver des issues et un marché. Lancé en 2024, le CMA CGM Start-up Awards ( le groupe CMA CGM est propriétaire de La Tribune, ndlr) a vocation à découvrir davantage d’innovation et à faire passer celle-ci au tamis du test. Depuis trois ans, le concours a étudié plus de 850 dossiers, l’édition 2026 ayant recueilli plus de 350 candidatures dont 50% en provenance de l’international. La plupart des finalistes, depuis, collaborent avec le groupe. A Marseille, ce jeudi, six nouvelles pépites ont été récompensées.

Grâce à sa plateforme attribuant une identité et des autorisations aux agents d’IA, Hodor, fondé par Karim Boussetta, sécurise et trace leurs actions dans les applications d’entreprise, ce qui lui vaut d’être lauréat de la catégorie « Smart transport and AI driven operations ». Autonome et capable de nettoyer et d’inspecter les coques sans immobiliser les navires, ce qui la consommation de carburant et les émissions qui l’accompagne, CRABI Robotics, imaginé par Levi Gershon, répond à un enjeu depuis longtemps scruté et aux attentes de la catégorie « Asset of the future ».

Remplacer les fichiers Excel dans les entrepôts et les terminaux, mais surtout permettre ainsi d’affecter les collaborateurs aux postes les plus adaptés grâce à une cartographie de leurs compétences, c’est la promesse de Mercateem, développé par Adrien Laurentin, lauréat de la catégorie « Talents augmentés ».

Plateforme offrant aux marques la capacité de mesurer, comprendre et optimiser leur visibilité dans les assistants d’IA générative, Meikei vaut à Rachid Ait Addi, son fondateur et CEO de se distinguer dans la catégorie « Next Gen Media ».

Présidentielle : l’IA, ce sujet qui divise les candidats

Réunis à Marseille lors de l’AIM, pour un premier débat autour de l’IA, les candidats à la présidentielle et leurs représentants ont exposé leur vision politique sur les enjeux qui l’entourent : régulation, souveraineté, investissement.

Google teste ses puces IA en orbite : le pari solaire des futurs data centers

Google prépare le premier test orbital de ses puces TPU avec le projet Suncatcher. Le groupe mise sur l’ensoleillement quasi continu des satellites pour alimenter de futurs calculs d’IA, mais doit encore résoudre la dissipation de chaleur, les radiations et les liaisons laser à très haut débit.

Vers la « superintelligence personnelle » : Meta dévoile ses lunettes connectées pour parler à l'IA Muse

Baptisées Ray-Ban Meta Audio, les lunettes de Meta ont été développées sans caméra. Après l'échec du métavers et des investissements colossaux, le géant californien tente de rassurer sur la protection de la vie privée. Tout en visant le marché des objets connectés dopés à l'IA.

IA et travail, la grande bascule ne fait que commencer

Après avoir automatisé certaines tâches, l’IA s’attaque désormais à l’organisation même du travail. L’essor de l’IA agentique pourrait accélérer cette transformation, en bouleversant certains métiers.

Des LLM aux world models, l’IA générative ouvre un nouveau front

L’usage des « large language model » est aujourd’hui ancré et généralisé dans la vie quotidienne et professionnelle. Mais ces modèles basés sur le langage pourraient être confrontés à des limites, laissant place aux « world models », capables de prédire et modéliser les évolutions du monde réel.

Léon XIV place l’intelligence artificielle parmi les risques pour la sécurité mondiale

Léon XIV a renouvelé jeudi au Vatican son alerte sur les risques de l’intelligence artificielle pour la paix. Vendredi, il portera à l’Unesco une doctrine déjà posée dans son encyclique Magnifica Humanitas, entre dignité humaine, désinformation et contrôle des armes.

Les salariés adoptent l’IA plus vite que leur entreprise et que leur patron

Largement familiarisés avec l’IA générative, les salariés sont aussi nombreux à s'en servir à titre personnel, tandis que les entreprises peinent encore à encadrer ces nouveaux usages.

« Les entreprises ont doublé leurs investissements IA en un an » : les leçons de l'étude du BCG

Les entreprises dépensent 3,3 % de leur chiffre d’affaires dans le déploiement de l’IA générative, soit deux fois plus que l’an passé. Elles ne mesurent encore pas bien le retour sur investissement complet, mais 50 % d’entre elles notent une réduction de 2 à 3 % de leurs coûts, rapporte la nouvelle étude du BCG. Sylvain Duranton, directeur monde de BCG X, révèle les chiffres clés en avant-première à La Tribune.

evidence.title: CMA CGM-backed wind-powered roro catches the eye in Zeebrugge
evidence.text:
One of shipping’s most distinctive new vessels has made its first Belgian call, with the wind-powered Neoliner Origin arriving at PSA Zeebrugge as part of an expanded transatlantic service.

The 136 m roro, operated by French company Neoline and backed by CMA CGM, now links Zeebrugge with Montoir-de-Bretagne, Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon, Baltimore and Halifax. The extended rotation is expected to take around five weeks in summer and six in winter, giving approximately 10 round voyages a year.

Zeebrugge has been added to give shippers in Belgium, the Netherlands, Germany and northern France direct access to the service, which CMA CGM is marketing to customers looking to reduce supply-chain emissions.

Neoliner Origin uses wind as its primary propulsion source, with two foldable SolidSail masts carrying 3,000 sq m of sail, supplemented by diesel-electric propulsion. Designed for a commercial speed of 11 knots, the vessel can carry rolling, containerised and out-of-gauge cargo. Neoline claims fuel consumption can be cut by more than 80% compared with a conventional ship operating at 15 knots.

France has emerged as arguably the most active country in developing a new generation of wind-powered cargo ships. Splash has previously covered the French-built concept Canopée, equipped with four Oceanwings to transport Ariane 6 rocket components, while French startup Vela is developing 67 m sailing trimarans for transatlantic freight. Windcoop has meanwhile ordered a 210 teu sail-powered boxship in Turkey for delivery next year and service between France and Madagascar.

evidence.title: CMA CGM adjusts BAF on France-Tunisia RoRo service
evidence.text:
CMA CGM Short Sea Lines (SSL) Intra Europe will adjust its Bunker Adjustment Factor (BAF) on the RoRo South service connecting France and Tunisia.

The revised surcharge will take effect on 1 October 2026 and will apply to both import and export cargo.

Under the new structure, the BAF for full rolling units will be €718 per unit.

Empty rolling units will face a charge of €475 per unit, while other rolling equipment will be charged €80 per linear metre.

The category includes trucks, earth-moving equipment, tracked or wheeled machinery, agricultural equipment and livestock trucks.

Passenger cars and minivans will face a BAF of €273 per unit.

For breakbulk cargo, the surcharge will be €44 per cubic metre.

CMA CGM said the adjustment follows changes in bunker prices since its previous surcharge revision.

The new BAF levels will apply to the carrier’s RoRo service connecting France with Tunisia from 1 October.

evidence.text:
CMA CGM has announced further changes to its CIMEX service portfolio connecting the Far East with the Middle East and Indian subcontinent, according to Alphaliner.

The recently shortened CIMEX1 service will remove calls at Hong Kong and Sohar.

Sohar will instead join the CIMEX3 rotation, which CMA CGM launched in July 2026. The service will also add Qingdao, Fujairah and Colombo.

As part of the CIMEX3 restructuring, CMA CGM will remove Khor Fakkan, occasional Duqm calls and the weekly westbound Singapore call.

The changes redistribute port coverage between the two services while maintaining connections between Asia, the Middle East and the Indian subcontinent.

evidence.title: CMA CGM Invokes General Average After Cargo Hold Fire
evidence.text:
CMA CGM Invokes General Average After Cargo Hold Fire

Published Sep 16, 2026 3:09 PM by The Maritime Executive

With salvage efforts underway after a cargo hold fire, CMA CGM has informed customers that it is invoking General Average for the incident involving the CMA CGM Petra . The latest fire on a containership adds further emphasis to recent reports from the World Shipping Council on the persistent danger from cargo deficiencies.

The 86,715-dwt containership registered in France is currently docked in Port Klang, Malaysia, having reached the berth on September 11. It had been holding offshore while a salvage team from SMIT was managing the situation that had begun on August 22. The LNG-fueled containership is one of the newest in the CMA CGM fleet, having only been delivered by HD Hyundai at the end of 2024, and it is employed on a route from Asia to East Africa. The ship has a rating for 8,048 TEU with 800 reefer plugs.

CMA CGM had advised customers that the crew discovered a fire in one of the holds on August 22 while the ship was in the Malacca Strait approximately 45 nautical miles northwest of Penang. The crew was able to contain the fire, with assistance from the team from SMIT and several fireboats. The ship had been sailing toward Kenya but reported it was diverting to Malaysia. There were no reports of injuries to the crew.

The ship had made its last port call in Singapore. It was operating on an adjusted schedule due to the typhoons that struck China in August. Scheduled calls at Shanghai and Ningbo had been omitted with alternate stops in Qingdao and Nansha.

The reports have not indicated the extent of the damage, but the adjusters were saying that 450 containers were due to be offloaded for inspection in Malaysia. It was also pointed out that because the fire was in one of the holds, the boxes in the area would have been exposed to the heat and smoke, as well as firefighting water or chemicals.

CMA CGM signed a Lloyd’s Standard Form of Salvage, which observers said was likely the first step toward General Average. It has also announced the use of a professional salvage team.

The fire is the latest in a series of high-profile incidents and emphasizes the continued dangers to vessels. The World Shipping Council recently issued data showing that one in ten cargo surveys show deficiencies . It is also calling for a tightening of rules pertaining to the shipment of lithium batteries, and this follows enhanced rules for the shipment of charcoal.

Get the latest maritime news delivered to your inbox daily.

Reports indicate that this was the second fire in 12 months that CMA CGM experienced in the Malacca Strait, after a cargo fire on the CMA CGM J. Madison in August 2025. Claims consultants WK Webster show that the fire on the CMA CGM Petra was followed by reports of a fire on September 4 aboard the Maersk Lanco off Brazil. The 8,700 TEU vessel made port on September 11 and was the second containership fire WK Webster lists under casualties after a four-month lull and the fourth containership fire in 2026.

The World Shipping Council pointed out that the latest statistics from insurer Allianz indicate that a containership fire occurs on average every 17 days.

evidence.title: Hapag-Lloyd revises Zim offer as Israeli approval concerns persist
evidence.text:
Hapag-Lloyd and Israeli private-equity firm FIMI submitted revised terms for their planned $4.2 billion acquisition of Zim Integrated Shipping Services, seeking to resolve Israeli government concerns over maritime security, strategic assets and the country’s access to international shipping routes.

Hapag-Lloyd Chief Executive Rolf Habben Jansen visited Israel this week ahead of the submission of a new proposal Sept. 24. The revised terms are intended to address objections raised by several government bodies reviewing the transaction, including agencies with responsibility for defense, state-owned companies, ports and shipping.

The original agreement, announced in February, calls for Hapag-Lloyd to acquire Zim (NYSE: ZIM ) for $35 per share in cash, valuing the company at approximately $4.2 billion. The price represented a 58% premium to Zim’s Feb. 13 share price, according to the carrier. Zim shareholders have approved the takeover, but the deal remains subject to Israeli governmental and regulatory clearances.

The proposed transaction separates certain Israeli strategic shipping assets from Zim’s international business. Under the structure outlined earlier this year, Hapag-Lloyd would take control of Zim’s international operations, while FIMI would establish and control a separate Israeli company, Zim Israel or New Zim, that would hold assets subject to Israel’s “golden share” protections.

Those protections are designed to preserve Israel’s ability to ensure maritime service during emergencies and maintain control over designated strategic shipping capabilities.

Hapag-Lloyd said earlier this month that it was working with Israeli ministries to revise structural aspects of the acquisition and develop a proposal that would “further strengthen Israel’s maritime security and independence.” The German carrier said the revised structure would secure Israeli access to key shipping routes, including connections from Asia.

Reported changes include tighter limits on foreign ownership of the Israeli successor company. The threshold at which a foreign investor would trigger government scrutiny or golden-share protections could be cut to 10% from 24%, according to reports. FIMI also has reportedly committed to list any shares in the Israeli company only on Israel’s domestic exchange.

The revised proposal is also expected to reinforce the operating role of the Israeli entity. Earlier reporting said the company would receive 16 vessels — more than the 11 vessels required under existing golden-share provisions — and would be debt-free. The ships would be available to the government, while the company would retain a role in maintaining Israel’s maritime links during disruptions.

For the U.S. market, the deal would primarily mean a larger, more integrated Hapag-Lloyd presence in the trans-Pacific and U.S. import supply chain, rather than an immediate change in service or pricing. Until closing, targeted for late 2026, Hapag-Lloyd and Zim must continue operating independently, and the transaction remains subject to regulatory approvals.

Zim is an important carrier in Asia–North America trades, with particular relevance to the U.S. West Coast, the U.S. East Coast and the Pacific Northwest/Canadian gateways serving the U.S. Midwest. Its own SEC filing highlights services via Vancouver and Prince Rupert that provide access to the Canadian and U.S. Midwest markets.

For Hapag-Lloyd, securing approval would add Zim’s network and commercial base to its existing global liner operations. The companies said in February that the combined organization would operate more than 400 vessels, have capacity exceeding 3 million TEUs and carry more than 18 million TEUs annually. But that wouldn’t change Hapag-Lloyd’s seventh-place ranking among global container carriers.

evidence.title: Hapag-Lloyd stock falls 1.96 percent as ZIM talks advance
evidence.text:
Hapag-Lloyd AG (ISIN DE000HLAG475) was trading at EUR 135.10 on Xetra on September 25, 2026, down 1.96 percent from the previous close. The move followed a revised ZIM framework submitted on September 24, 2026, as Maritime Executive reported.

Hapag-Lloyd and FIMI Opportunity Funds submitted a framework designed to address Israeli government concerns about the proposed ZIM takeover. The framework includes a USD 4.2 billion deal valuation, or USD 35 per ZIM share, while the parties' target for completion has shifted from the end of 2026 toward mid-2027, according to Maritime Executive .

The proposed structure would preserve an Israeli company, provide a weekly Far East route and expand Zim Israel's reefer capacity. For Hapag-Lloyd, the transaction therefore combines fleet expansion with a regulatory execution risk that remains visible in the revised timetable.

Hapag-Lloyd generated Group EBITDA of USD 829 million in Q2 2026, up from USD 820 million in Q2 2025. Liner Shipping revenue rose to USD 5.7 billion from USD 5.2 billion, while the average freight rate increased 9 percent to USD 1,475 per TEU, according to FreshPlaza .

The quarterly improvement has not erased the first-half pressure. Group EBITDA stood at USD 1.3 billion in H1 2026 versus USD 1.9 billion in H1 2025, while Group profit was a loss of USD 173 million compared with a profit of USD 775 million a year earlier. Hapag-Lloyd's 2026 outlook calls for Group EBITDA of USD 2.7 billion to USD 3.7 billion and Group EBIT of USD 0.1 billion to USD 1.1 billion, as reported by FreshPlaza .

On September 14, 2026, Barclays raised its Hapag-Lloyd price target from EUR 100 to EUR 105 but retained a Sell rating, according to MarketScreener . The revised target remains below the September 25 intraday price, placing the transaction story alongside a cautious earnings assessment.

Hapag-Lloyd stock was trading at EUR 135.10 on Xetra on September 25, 2026, at 12:32 p.m. CEST, with a daily change of minus 1.96 percent. The price stood 15.19 percent below the 52-week high of EUR 159.30 and above the 52-week low of EUR 108.70.

evidence.title: Hapag-Lloyd, Israeli investor FIMI add Far East route to $4.2bn ZIM deal
evidence.text:
ПАО "ДВМП" ИНН 2540047110 ERID: 2W5zFHrvuLC

ООО "Газпромнефть Марин Бункер" ИНН 7838392447 ERID: 2W5zFGkoFyS

Hapag-Lloyd, Israeli investor FIMI add Far East route to $4.2bn ZIM deal

Hapag-Lloyd and Israeli private equity firm FIMI Opportunity Funds have revised their $4.2bn acquisition plan for ZIM Integrated Shipping Services, adding a weekly Far East service and tighter safeguards for the Israeli operation, according to a letter sent to Israel’s Government Companies Authority on 24 September.

The acquisition price remains $35 per ZIM share. Under the revised structure, ZIM Israel would remain under Israeli ownership and management, with FIMI controlling the business and Hapag-Lloyd providing commercial support under a long-term agreement.

The weekly Far East service would be added to one Atlantic and two Mediterranean services. ZIM Israel would retain a core fleet of 16 containerships and gain access to Hapag-Lloyd’s global fleet.

Ship management and maritime expertise would remain in Israel. ZIM Israel would operate an independent IT system without third-party access, including from Hapag-Lloyd, while protections attached to the Israeli government’s Golden Share would be strengthened.

The company would also have refrigerated-container capacity twice the level currently owned by ZIM and expand its pool of Israeli seafarers. Employment provisions include a special collective agreement covering the large majority of ZIM’s workforce, a 10-year employment safety net for veteran employees and a commitment not to carry out layoffs through the end of 2027.

“We have listened carefully to the needs raised during our discussions with the Israeli government and the relevant authorities,” Hapag-Lloyd chief executive Rolf Habben Jansen said. “Together with our partners, we are now developing an improved proposal designed to further strengthen Israel’s maritime security and independence.”

The revised business plan projects about $1.7bn in additional revenue and around $200m in additional net profit over 10 years, mainly from the Far East service.

The buyers expect to submit the full package of agreements, commitments and detailed business plans within 45 days.

ZIM agreed in February to be acquired for $35 per share in cash, valuing the transaction at about $4.2bn. Shareholders approved the deal on 30 April. Completion remains subject to regulatory clearances, including approval under Israel’s Golden Share rights.

Hamburg-based Hapag-Lloyd operated 300 containerships with total capacity of about 2.5m TEU as of 30 June 2026.

ZIM was founded in Israel in 1945 and operates in more than 90 countries, serving customers through more than 300 ports. FIMI manages more than $11bn in assets.

evidence.title: Hapag-Lloyd and FIMI Submit Framework of Revised Structure for Zim Israel
evidence.text:
Hapag-Lloyd and FIMI Submit Framework of Revised Structure for Zim Israel

Published Sep 24, 2026 6:42 PM by The Maritime Executive

Israeli media is reporting that Hapag-Lloyd CEO Rolf Habben Jansen flew to Israel and that, today, September 24, with Ishay Davidi’s FIMI Opportunity Funds, they submitted what they are calling a “significantly improved framework” for their proposed takeover of container carrier Zim. The companies are saying they understood the concerns raised by factions within the Israeli government and that they have addressed the issues, creating a stronger Zim Israel as the surviving Israeli company.

The Israeli government had indicated that it would vote to reject the proposed takeover of Zim by Hapag-Lloyd and the creation of a new, smaller Zim run by FIMI. Questions were raised about the financial viability of the new, smaller shipping company that was mostly focused on the Mediterranean and as a feeder to Hapag-Lloyd. Security concerns were also raised over Israel’s control of the shipping company and ability to maintain key supply chains.

The information submitted today is said to be a framework that outlines what the companies are calling “ten material improvements” to the structure of the deal. The companies said they would submit complete documentation within 45 days.

The Israeli outlet Calcalist, which was first to break the news of the pending takeover months ago, reports it reviewed the document submitted today. It says the new proposal enhances the Israeli ownership of Zim Israel and strengthens the so-called Golden Share. It reduces the threshold to trigger a government review and ensures that Zim Israel will remain an Israeli company.

One of the key objections was the limited routes for the new Zim. The revised proposal adds a weekly route to the Far East for Zim Israel in addition to the planned service in the Mediterranean and trans-Atlantic. It also proposed to increase the size of the Zim Israel fleet, doubling its current reefer capacity to protect the Israeli food chain.

Hapag-Lloyd will enter into a long-term commercial agreement with Zim Israel, providing it guaranteed global access.

Zim Israel will maintain its vessel management and professional expertise in Israel. It will also have an independent IT system in Israel.

FIMI reports that, as part of the submission, it will present a new business plan for Zim Israel, which was reportedly validated by independent international consultants. Calcalist reports the plan projects increasing Zim Israel’s revenues over 10 years by $1.7 billion and a $200 million improvement in net operating profit.

International lawyers are also said to have reviewed Hapag-Lloyd’s corporate governance and will submit an opinion as part of the revised information packet. One of the concerns that had been raised related to the investment in Hapag by Arab sovereign wealth funds. The report says Hapag is also highlighting that it has maintained its service to Israel consistently since October 2023, despite periods of severe security disruptions.

Get the latest maritime news delivered to your inbox daily.

To address issues raised by the unions in Israel, the deal is reported to include a special collective agreement guarantee for continued employment and training of Israeli seafarers. There is also a “10-year safety net,” enhanced terms for voluntary retirement, and a commitment to avoid layoffs through the end of 2027.

The Israeli media outlet Globes, however, highlights that the valuation of the proposed deal remains the same at $4.2 billion or $35 per share of Zim. It notes that the parties had a goal of closing the deal by the end of 2026, but it is now likely to extend until mid-2027.

evidence.text:

TGI expands logistics footprint with UAC’s 43% DP World stake

UAC of Nigeria Plc is set to sell its 43 percent stake in DP World Logistics Limited, formerly known as

UAC of Nigeria Plc is set to sell its 43 percent stake in DP World Logistics Limited, formerly known as MDS Logistics Limited, to 22 Plus Invest Limited, a member of Tropical General Investments (TGI) Group, in a transaction that will transfer UAC’s interest in the logistics company to the diversified Nigerian conglomerate.

UAC disclosed the proposed transaction in a corporate announcement dated September 24, 2026, stating that completion is subject to requisite regulatory approvals.

The deal marks a significant change in UAC’s investment in the logistics business after years of working with DP World Logistics’ management to expand the company.

Fola Aiyesimoju, group managing director of UAC, said the company had worked closely with DP World’s management to support the logistics company’s growth and expansion.

He said UAC believes TGI would become a strong long-term partner for DP World Logistics following completion of the transaction, citing the group’s market knowledge and track record of building businesses in Nigeria.

“We look forward to seeing the Company continue to grow and strengthen its contribution to Nigeria’s logistics sector,” Aiyesimoju said.

The proposed acquisition will bring together TGI’s domestic market and distribution capabilities with DP World’s global logistics expertise.

Farouk Gumel, Vice Chairman of TGI Group, said the transaction reflects both companies’ ambition to reshape trade and logistics in Africa.

“By combining DP World’s global expertise with TGI Group’s deep market knowledge and extensive distribution network, we are building resilient supply chains that will unlock growth, strengthen regional connectivity and support economic prosperity for generations to come,” Gumel said.

TGI expands logistics footprint The proposed transaction allows TGI to deepen its presence in logistics and distribution, alongside its existing operations across agriculture, food processing, FMCG manufacturing, distribution, chemicals, poultry farming, real estate and financial services.

TGI has operated in Nigeria and the broader West African region for more than four decades and has expanded into markets including India and the United Arab Emirates. The group says it has more than 25,000 employees.

For UAC, the disposal comes as the group continues to operate across packaged food and beverages, paints, animal feeds and other edibles, quick-service restaurants, logistics and real estate through its subsidiaries and associates.

DP World Logistics is part of the broader global DP World network, which operates across ports and terminals, marine services, logistics and technology. DP World says it has more than 125,000 employees operating across six continents.

The value of the proposed transaction was not disclosed in UAC’s announcement.

The completion of the sale remains subject to the requisite regulatory approvals. UAC said further information could be obtained through its investor relations portal.

evidence.title: DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings confirms plan to stage Play-Offs in Middle East, despite player safety concerns
evidence.text:
DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings confirms plan to stage Play-Offs in Middle East, despite player safety concerns

In an exclusive interview with Sky Sports, DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings discussed the plans for the season-ending Play-Offs, the Strategic Alliance with the PGA Tour and the bright future the tour has within the global game

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings has confirmed that the plan is to keep the season-ending Play-Offs in the Middle East, despite ongoing conflict in the region.

The Abu Dhabi Championship is scheduled to be held at Yas Links on November 5-8, before the Race to Dubai season reaches its climax at the DP World Tour Championship the following week.

There has been speculation throughout the season over whether both events would move to a different country, with Formula 1 cancelling two events earlier in the year in the region and discussions ongoing over whether races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will go ahead.

Matt Fitzpatrick and Bob MacIntyre were among players to express concerns about travelling to the UAE, despite a relaxing of the previous "all but essential travel" guidelines from the UK's Foreign Office, with Kinnings hopeful both events can take place as planned.

"A lot of people are asking and it's an obvious question," Kinnings told Sky Sports . "The reality is we expect every intention to be playing in Abu Dhabi and Dubai.

"Work has started and we're building stuff at Yas Links and at the Jumeirah Golf Estates, so our intention is to go ahead.

"We clearly need to keep in touch with travel advisors and other people who help with us, but our plan is definitely to play the Play-Offs in the UAE."

Defending DP World Tour champion Fitzpatrick said on Wednesday that he was "not that comfortable" playing in Dubai, given its proximity to the conflict involving Iran, the United States and Israel, although McIlroy was less concerned.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"If the local governments feel like it's safe to put on these events, they are not going to put their citizens or people visiting in harm's way," McIlroy said after his opening round at the BMW PGA Championship.

"I love the Middle East. I have a lot of friends there and I'm looking forward to going back for sure."

The DP World Tour announced its 2027 schedule at the BMW PGA Championship, with the Flagship Event being held a week later next year and immediately after the centenary Ryder Cup at Adare Manor.

Introducing the 2027 DP World Tour global tournament schedule 🌍 ◾️ Three historic tournaments return ◾️ Hong Kong Open and Deutsche Bank Singapore Open co-sanctioned with Asian Tour ◾️ New dates for Amgen Irish Open, FedEx Open de France and BMW PGA Championship ◾️ 42… pic.twitter.com/mD3QTvJspe

JJ Spaun and Ryan Gerard were among the limited American players to make the trip over to England for the event, despite more spots being available to PGA Tour players, although Kinnings hopes to see more make the journey in the future.

" I think the future schedule will lend itself to that," Kinnings said. "We've got a great working relationship with the PGA Tour and we're working with them on what the future will look like.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"I think the way the schedule's set up, with golf in America stopping at the end of August, we've got the opportunity to shine from September 1 until the end of January. I think that'll mean more of the guys will come and play in great events like this and some of the other tournaments as well."

Kinnings added: "I have to say, I couldn't be more excited. I think it's a huge opportunity for international golf. We clearly have wonderful players and we have an opportunity to shine in the schedule."

The DP World Tour has yet to announce whether it will impose sanctions for its members wishing to play in the new iteration of the LIV Golf League, should LIV 2.0 go ahead as planned in 2027, with Kinnings keen to see the strongest fields possible on his circuit.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"We've been very consistent on the whole question and we're going to continue that way," Kinnings insisted. "What will happen with LIV is entirely speculation, but from our perspective we want to find a balance. As a business, we just love to have the best fields we possibly can with the best players.

"But we're also a member's organisation and our job is purely to make sure we look out for the best interests of the members. We have a wonderful tour, amazing culture and that's because of the players, so nothing's going to change on that front.

"I think we're in a stronger position as we can possibly be. We've got great partners and the future looks bright - we now just need to work out exactly what it looks like."

evidence.title: JJ Spaun’s comments on the DP World Tour gives them a massive boost amid LIV Golf’s bankruptcy
evidence.text:
JJ Spaun’s comments on the DP World Tour gives them a massive boost amid LIV Golf’s bankruptcy

JJ Spaun is a debutant at the BMW PGA Championship and appears to have fallen in love with the event.

Spaun is four shots back of the leading Ryan Gerrard after two days of play, and after his second round he sang the praises of the tournament at Wentworth and the DP World Tour generally.

The 2025 US Open champion said, “I think the new structure of the PGA TOUR and schedule moving forward, especially in 2028, this will give us more opportunity, more time, to play events abroad. This was kind of like a stepping stone, just to see how it was and if I like it.

“I definitely feel like I’m going to plan a little bit more of a global schedule or a European schedule moving forward in the fall time. So it’s been lovely so far. The community’s great. The spectators and fans are great. The boys on this tour are great. The support’s awesome. It’s been a brilliant time so far.”

These comments could not have come at a better time for the DP World Tour in what is expected to be a vitally important few months.

JJ Spaun’s comments are perfectly timed for the DP World Tour

As LIV Golf filed for bankruptcy, a mass exodus of players is expected to leave the breakaway league to play on the DP World Tour next season. Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton are among those likely to serve their PGA Tour suspensions while playing on the DP World Tour.

For many Europeans, playing on their home tour next year is a no-brainer. Players like Hatton and Rahm are already members, so they will likely relish the idea of playing around the world while they await a PGA Tour return.

However, this decision is less straightforward for the Americans. They are less familiar with the DP World Tour overall and may have reservations about playing away from home all year.

That’s why Spaun’s comments are so valuable to the DP World Tour. As an American who has not historically played much on the DP World Tour, his experiences in Europe this season have encouraged him to play abroad more often moving forward.

For any Americans listening to Spaun sing the praises of the DP World Tour and Wentworth, it could be all the encouragement they need to leave LIV Golf and join the tour for next season.

evidence.title: DP World redraws Hormuz logistics with trucking expansion
evidence.text:
DP World redraws Hormuz logistics with trucking expansion

Dubai-based firm plans to grow its truck fleet by about 40%

[Stay on top of transportation news: Get TTNews in your inbox .]

Ports giant DP World is expanding its overland logistics network in a bet that shipping through the Strait of Hormuz — vital for its flagship container and industrial hub in the United Arab Emirates — won’t return to the status quo from before the U.S.-Iran war. The Dubai-based firm plans to grow its truck fleet by about 40% and add new land routes to diversify supply chains linking Europe, the U.S. and Asia to the Persian Gulf, Chief Operating Officer for Freight Forwarding Europe Stephen Whittingham told Bloomberg in an interview. READ MORE: DP World to build 2 UAE container terminals to skirt Hormuz “I think we’ll never get back to the original normal,” Whittingham said. “There’s always going to be a level of uncertainty that exists now around this this geography, and so I think having options is really where DP World has said we’re going to be able to mitigate risk.” googletag.cmd.push(function () { googletag.defineSlot('/21737348341/ttnewscom/rectangle4', [[300, 250]], 'div-gpt-ad-22764643208').setTargeting('test', 'lazyload').setTargeting(REFRESH_KEY, REFRESH_VALUE).addService(googletag.pubads()); googletag.display('div-gpt-ad-22764643208'); }); The comments underline how the Iran war’s shock to global supply chains is likely to outlast the conflict itself, as countries and companies alike seek to reduce their dependence on the embattled waterway. The diversification drive also aligns with the UAE’s aim to cut its reliance on the strait to zero. Within days of Iran closing the strait, DP World launched a road service from western Europe to the Gulf through Turkey that currently handles as many as 50 trucks per week, Whittingham said. Most of the cargo demand is for automotive parts and everyday consumer products, he added. DP World also set up hybrid sea-and-road services for shipments from Asia and the U.S., also via Turkey. The company now wants to grow its fleet of trucks to 1,000 from 700 currently that provide a “land bridge” within the region to ports outside the Persian Gulf like Fujairah in the UAE, Salalah in Oman and Jeddah in Saudi Arabia, he said. Image DP World operates ports and terminals in 84 countries from China to South America, but had to briefly suspend operations at its Jebel Ali facility in the UAE due to debris from an intercepted Iranian attack. Before the conflict, Jebel Ali was the busiest container port outside of Asia, ranking in the top 10 globally and serving mostly as a transshipment hub integrated with one of the world’s largest industrial free zones. But Jebel Ali reportedly saw a nearly 60% drop in volumes during the first half of the year from a year earlier, according to Alphaliner data, pushing it down to 32nd biggest by volumes in the world. On new routes, the next target is to bring cargo over land from Europe to Iraq then load it onto ships to cross the Gulf to the UAE. Talks with authorities in Baghdad for a “permanent service” are ongoing, Whittingham said. Premium service All that diversification comes at a cost. Shipping goods from Europe to the Gulf via land is typically three to four times more expensive than sea, he said. But he expects some customers to continue to use the service even once Hormuz reopens. “I don’t think it’s going to go away completely,” he said, adding that even now, customers often find pure truck services more reliable than multimodal ones amid disruptions to shipping from the Black Sea to the Middle East. Arpan Podduturi of Samsara examines how AI, telematics and onboard cameras are converging to protect drivers and reduce risk. Tune in above or by going to RoadSigns.ttnews.com . “If you needed a truck tomorrow, you could get a truck tomorrow.” DP World is also investing in its ports network, most notably with plans announced in July to develop two new deepwater terminals on the UAE’s eastern coast — outside the strait. It has also committed around $800 million to terminal upgrades at Jeddah in Saudi Arabia and Tartus on Syria’s Mediterranean coast, both of which would link to the trucking networks. Funding for such projects received a boost last week when the company sold $1.6 billion in bonds. “DP World’s strong liquidity provides a substantial buffer against prolonged Middle East disruption,” Bloomberg Intelligence Credit Analyst Sharon Chen wrote in a note on Sept. 10. The bond deal “demonstrates continued funding access, albeit at a sizable spread premium.”

DP World Marks Record 8.3% Growth in Container Handling for 2024

DP World’s ports and terminals handled a record 88.3 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) in 2024, up 8.3% year-on-year, despite macroeconomic headwinds and concerns over the outlook for global trade.

The global logistics business, which now can handle over 100 million TEU across operations in 78 countries, benefitted from long-term infrastructure investment, contributing to strong growth and new services calling at its terminals.

While the Red Sea crisis posed a significant challenge to global shipping in 2024, causing delays and rerouting across major trade corridors, DP World’s record performance underscores the strength of its diversified worldwide portfolio and ability to navigate supply chain volatility, ensuring continued service for customers worldwide.

“During the last 10 years, we have invested more than $11 billion in world-class ports and logistics infrastructure to make trade flow. This record performance is further evidence that our long-term investment is providing the right services for our customers in the right places," said Ahmed bin Sulayem, Group Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of DP World.

Leading the way in terms of performance across the DP World portfolio was the Posorja terminal in Ecuador, on South America’s west coast, which posted a 87% uplift in volume to nearly 1 million TEUs driven by new services by Maersk calling at the port.

Double-digit growth was seen in San Antonio in Chile, Yarimca in Türkiye, Chennai in India, Callao in Peru, Antwerp in Belgium, and London Gateway in the UK. DP World’s flagship Jebel Ali Port also saw a 7% increase from 2023

At the same time, new ports and terminals added nearly 1 million TEUs to the total volume. This includes the new DP World- Evyap merger in Turkey, new operations at Dar Es Salaam Port in Tanzania, and the Belawan New Container Terminal in Indonesia.

DB Schenker boosts warehouse efficiency with automated components, picking systems and 100 autonomous mobile robots (AMR)

HAMBURG, Germany , Nov. 3, 2022 /PRNewswire/ -- � DB Schenker , one of the leading global logistics service providers, has partnered with Körber to implement automated warehouse operations for its new distribution center near Prague , CZ. The AMR installation, in particular, will be part of a highly automated logistics ecosystem and represents one of the largest AMR deployments of its kind in Eastern Europe .

The implementation consists of a comprehensive breadth of automation and software components. This includes a large conveyor system, value added service lines, a packaging area as well as a cross belt shipping sorter and over 100 highly integrated AMRs provided by Geek+, a trusted partner of Körber. Körber's software solution will handle the work assignment orchestration of the BoTs allowing for fast, efficient goods-to-person picking activities. Approximately 15 workstations will be equipped with advanced put-to-light and pick-by-light systems for enhanced ergonomics and performance. These systems will be working completely integrated and intertwined to enable optimized strategies for enhanced customer services. The site consists of 18,000 sqm facility, dedicated to support the needs of a leading electronics company.

"DB Schenker has experienced outstanding success since its inception as an early innovator in the Eastern European market. With COVID-19 driving more consumers online, we are well placed to increase and improve the service offering for our rapidly growing consumer base," says Ingo Brauckmann , Executive Vice President Contract Logistics / SCM Europe at Schenker.

The relationship between Körber and DB Schenker dates back to 2006, testified by many successful projects in warehouse management software, automation, voice and simulation. With implementation progress in record time and an anticipated go-live in early 2023, Körber adds to this as DB Schenker's global preferred supplier for AMR-related systems. The robots will provide Schenker the capability to scale flexibly and gradually invest while increasing operational efficiency and performance, which is forecasted to double by 2034.

"Our research has found that more than three out of four businesses make digitization and process automation a strategic priority," says Dirk Hejnal , CEO at the Körber Business Area Supply Chain. "At the same time, the issues around workplace safety and labor retention have never been greater. That's why we at Körber look forward to continuing our long-standing collaboration with Schenker."

"Körber offers the benefits from both a safety and efficiency perspective to turn today's supply chain complexities into opportunities for future-proof business operations," adds Chad Collins CEO Software, Körber Business Area Supply Chain. "With our uniquely unrivaled depth of solutions, we empower our customers stay ahead of their competition."

With around 76,100 employees at more than 1,850 locations in over 130 countries, DB Schenker is one of the world's leading logistics providers. The company operates land, air, and ocean transportation services, and it also offers comprehensive solutions for logistics and global supply chain management from a single source. In 2022, DB Schenker celebrates its 150th company anniversary. evidence.title: K+N sees growth in verticals post-DB Schenker acquisition
evidence.text:
K+N sees growth in verticals post-DB Schenker acquisition

Kuehne+Nagel (K+N) said it had continued to grow its specialist verticals business since DSV’s acquisition of DB Schenker

Kuehne+Nagel (K+N) said it had continued to grow its specialist verticals business since DSV’s acquisition of DB Schenker, partly due to efforts by shippers to diversify their business deals.

In its second quarter and first half results release, K+N said its air volumes were up and its Air Logistics business unit benefited from perishables, semiconductors, and cloud infrastructure (hyper scalers) growth.

Speaking during the company’s second quarter 2025 investor call, chief executive Stefan Paul said the forwarder had seen growth in all airfreight verticals apart from automotive.

“So we have seen now in the second quarter growth in all verticals apart from one, which is automotive.

“Where in particular, we have seen growth…is the high-tech hyperscaler market, is the perishable business, in particular fish, and is the hard cargo environment outside of automotive.”

He added the silicon, cloud (technology) and aerospace are also growth areas.

Speaking about the first half of the year overall, Paul said: “In Air Logistics, we are achieving substantial growth in the geographic breadth and frequency of services.”

In response to a question about market changes and opportunities since DSV acquired DB Schenker to establish the world’s biggest forwarder, Paul said the takeover hadn’t curbed K+N’s growth opportunities.

“I mentioned the hyperscaler, the cloud marketplace, where we have already taken advantage out of the merger, right?

“And we had a fair share of this business coming in, dominated by two players.”

Paul indicated that K+N had benefited from business diversification strategies utilised by shippers as a means to protect their shipments following the acquisition.

“And secondly, as well, not a big surprise and normally in these kind of environments that customers balance their share of wallet and they do not put all the eggs to one basket, especially where we have customers where the amount of business they have allocated to the two players together is too high from a procurement perspective, we seek good chance and we already have secured significant business in the high-tech. Same is now coming in since a couple of weeks in the healthcare sector, where we gain more and more.”

K+N is also expecting a peak season for airfreight. “The outlook for airfreight is overall robust,” said Paul. “There will be quite a peak season to be expected in airfreight.”

The company anticipates a muted peak season for seafreight on Asia-US transpacific trade, although Paul stressed Asia-Europe westbound trade still looked to be solid.

“I think the rest of the marketplace, especially Asia to Europe is very resilient. And the market will see good growth as well into the peak season.”

evidence.title: Siemens installs Desigo building automation integrated solution at DB Schenker
evidence.text:
Siemens installs Desigo building automation integrated solution at DB Schenker

International logistics giant DB Schenker has set benchmarks with its new headquarters in Essen. On 30,000 m² of floor space, the new building offers not only ideal working conditions, but it also features an impressive holistic building, safety and security technology concept from Siemens. All disciplines – room automation, access control, fire and intrusion detection, and video surveillance – are integrated in one central building management platform.

Architecturally speaking, the Ruhr region metropolis of Essen continues to reinvent itself. One recent example is the new corporate headquarters of DB Schenker, a leading international logistics provider. In the spring of 2016, the company moved into a new eight-story office building located just a few steps from the city’s main train station. It has 30,000 m2 of floor space for 900 employees. DB Schenker has dubbed the X-shaped, fully gazed structure The Grid. From here, the Deutsche Bahn AG subsidiary manages its logistics network of 700,000 customers worldwide.

With just a glance at the screen, operators can check the status of all the systems, devices and alarm management components – in each of the 431 rooms

For its new corporate headquarters, DB Schenker wanted building technology from a single source. The building owners chose the Desigo building automation system from Siemens, a seamlessly integrated solution covering the entire range of building automation – from the field level to room automation to the management level. In addition, the Desigo solution can be adapted to new requirements at any time.

The dimensions alone made the job extremely demanding. The system includes 560 Desigo room automation controllers, a DALI lighting control system, shading control for 2,000 blinds, an access control system with 40 Siport readers, a fire detection system with 1,500 detectors, an intrusion detection system with 50 elements, as well as video surveillance equipment.

Advanced visualisation of building disciplines

All the systems and devices at DB Schenker headquarters are interconnected via the Desigo CC building management platform. All disciplines can be centrally controlled, monitored and optimised from two operator screens. Support for open communication standards also allows the integration of third-party components. Even though DB Schenker uses an escape door control system from a specialised vendor, the doors can be unlocked via Desigo CC.

For maintenance, all the fire detectors in an area can be switched off from the control centre, eliminating the need to send technicians to each location

Desigo CC offers advanced visualisation of the integrated building disciplines. With just a glance at the screen, operators can check the status of all the systems, devices and alarm management components – in each of the 431 rooms.

The setpoints for valve position, room temperature or lighting can be individually adjusted for every single device and room. On-screen graphics are used to control the various disciplines; Desigo CC displays floor plans identifying all the field devices installed in any given room or floor.

This also allows central control of cross-disciplinary scenarios such as an event in a specific room or a fire in a particular area. In addition, cross-disciplinary timer groups can be defined. Alarms are displayed for all disciplines on one overview screen. Reports and trends can be displayed automatically if so desired: PDFs are created and e-mailed based on individual preferences.

For maintenance, all the fire detectors in an area can be switched off from the control centre, eliminating the need to send technicians to each location. This saves DB Schenker building services a great deal of time and personnel costs.

Adjusting temperature for energy efficiency

The individual room controllers are connected to the central control system and can hence be operated centrally as well

Every room at DB Schenker headquarters is equipped with integrated room automation controllers, allowing heating, cooling, lighting and shading to be adjusted for maximum energy efficiency. A total of 431 Desigo TRA individual room controllers were installed in offices, conference rooms and open spaces. They are equipped with sensors, but users can adjust the temperature, lighting and shading as desired using the room operator unit in each room. The panel displays a green or red leaf to indicate whether the settings are eco-friendly.

Open KNX communication standards make the room operator units freely programmable. For example, the presentation scenario can be programmed from the operator unit in a conference room to simultaneously dim the lights, close the blinds and lower the projector. The individual room controllers are connected to the central control system and can hence be operated centrally as well.

The DALI lighting controller uses the KNX standard as well, making the digital lighting systems efficient and easy to operate. Defective light fixtures are identified immediately so they can be replaced as quickly as possible to avoid repeated complaints. Optional motion sensors for autonomous DALI lighting systems were not installed at The Grid. Instead, they are replaced by occupancy buttons on the room operator units. To save even more energy, weather sensors on the roof of the building control the blinds for optimal incident light.

The measures taken to increase the energy efficiency of the building earned DB Schenker a LEED Silver certification

Heating, ventilation and air conditioning use approximately 900 data points whose signals converge in seven plant rooms. Siemens supplied and installed the field devices for heating, cooling and ventilation and set up the control cabinets.

The measures taken to increase the energy efficiency of the building earned DB Schenker a LEED Silver certification, demonstrating that the logistics provider takes its sustainability strategy seriously.

EN 54-compliant FC2080 fire control panel

The Siport system controls access to The Grid. 40 readers and 200 door locks with electric rotary knobs (offline cylinders) were installed. At DB Schenker’s request, the access system forwards timestamps to a separate system. The electric locking system secures nearly 300 doors.

The fire protection system combines an EN 54-compliant FC2080 fire control panel with 1,500 fire detectors, 900 sounders and 40 loops. This latest and most powerful Siemens fire control panel was selected because of the size of the building. DB Schenker uses multi-protocol detectors that can be tailored to individual room parameters. If the room usage changes, i.e. if the space is converted to a computer or break room, the fire detection system can be adjusted without having to replace the sensors.

Intrusion detection, video surveillance and VMS

Siemens installed a CIC 2000 intrusion detection system, a SINVR video surveillance system and SiteIQ Analytics video management system

Siemens also installed a CIC 2000 intrusion detection system according to VdS standards. 50 elements were integrated, including motion sensors and door monitors. A SINVR video surveillance system with the SiteIQ Analytics video management system rounds out the solution. 30 cameras are interconnected, 24 of them around the building as a virtual fence solution. Any violation of the defined security distance triggers automatic recording. Because the building borders on public streets, the video system uses partial pixelation.

In the past, DB Schenker had to outsource building management to specialised vendors. Now Desigo CC gives the in-house building technicians everything they need on a central screen: heating, ventilation, air conditioning, lighting, shading, fire detection and building security. The technicians work independently, although a five-year service contract ensures they can request support at any time. Siemens technicians and experts are available to assist DB Schenker technicians via remote access.

evidence.title: DB Schenker Canada Consolidated LTL Solutions for Seamless Cross-Border Shipping
evidence.text:
DB Schenker rebrands Canada Made Easy service to Canada Consolidated LTL Solutions.

MIAMI , Dec. 4, 2024 /PRNewswire/ -- DB Schenker, a global logistics leader with over 150 years of industry experience, offers its comprehensive Canada Consolidated LTL Solutions . This service provides businesses with a robust logistics infrastructure for efficient cross-border shipping and market expansion in North America .

As companies strive to expand their customer base and market share, penetrating new markets has become a key strategy. DB Schenker's innovative solution provides businesses with a robust logistics infrastructure and footprint to operate efficiently within Canada, while offering unmatched savings and reliability.

DB Schenker's Canada Consolidated LTL Solutions delivers all-encompassing logistics services. This integrated approach simplifies cargo movement to Canada by synchronizing supply chains and maintaining control of the entire shipment flow from origin to destination.

"We strategically placed origin terminals in the U.S. where, based on our customers' needs, we pick up freight from multiple companies, consolidate it, and send one consolidated line haul across the U.S.-Canadian border," said Rob Segsworth , Vice President/Head of Land, Canada at DB Schenker .

This consolidation and zone-skipping model offers businesses direct savings of 10-15% on average, compared to traditional LTL shipping. Additionally, it reduces administrative hassle by combining multiple shipments into a single customs entry.

"Instead of shipping 20 small orders to Canada, we consolidate them into one shipment and process it as a single customs entry," added Segsworth.

DB Schenker Canada also leads the industry in freight security with a claims rate of just 0.08% , compared to the industry average of 1%. By minimizing shipment touches, this solution significantly reduces damage and returns, ensuring products reach shelves faster while eliminating hidden costs tied to lost sales opportunities.

With over 70 years of experience in cross-border shipping , DB Schenker continues to set the standard for reliable, efficient, and hassle-free logistics solutions.

For more information on DB Schenker's Canada Consolidated LTL Solutions and cross-border capabilities, please visit DBSchenker.com .

About DB Schenker Americas DB Schenker is one of the largest Integrated Logistics Service Providers in the Americas with more than 10,000 employees in 123 locations providing over 27 million sq. ft. of distribution operations to its clients. DB Schenker's Americas presence includes Argentina , Brazil , Canada, Chile , Guatemala , Mexico , Panama , Peru , the United States , and Venezuela . DB Schenker offers land transport and air and ocean freight, as well as comprehensive logistics solutions and global supply chain management services from a single source. With integrated partners across the Americas, DB Schenker provides the best combination of intimate local practices, knowledge, and global capabilities.

About DB Schenker With around 76,600 employees at more than 1,850 locations in over 130 countries, DB Schenker is one of the world's leading logistics service providers. The company operates land, air, and ocean transportation services, and it also offers comprehensive logistics and global supply chain management solutions from a single source. Aiming for a sustainable future of the logistics industry, DB Schenker continuously invests in innovative transport solutions, renewable energies, and low-emission products for its customers.

evidence.title: Dachser acquires Scottish logistics partner Drummond Distribution
evidence.text:
Dachser has agreed to acquire Scottish logistics company Drummond Distribution, expanding its network with five locations between Glasgow and Edinburgh.

The companies have not disclosed the purchase price.

Drummond generated approximately £20 million in revenue in 2025 and employs around 175 people.

Dachser expands logistics network into Scotland

Drummond operates five locations across Scotland’s Central Belt.

The acquisition gives Dachser a direct presence in the region, where it currently has no locations.

As a result, Dachser said the transaction will strengthen its network coverage without creating overlapping structures.

Drummond has worked with Dachser since 2008, connecting customers in Scotland with the company’s European Logistics network.

The Scottish family-owned logistics company was established in 1927.

Deal includes warehouses and truck fleet

The acquisition includes approximately 46,500 square metres of warehouse space.

Dachser will also take over a fleet of around 100 trucks and 80 trailers.

Drummond’s existing management team, led by Damon Burns, will remain in place to ensure business continuity.

As the company’s current owners gradually leave the business, the management team will report to Mark Rollinson, Managing Director of Dachser UK & Ireland.

evidence.title: Dachser enters Scotland with acquisition of £20m haulier
evidence.text:
Dachser enters Scotland with acquisition of £20m haulier

Dachser is expanding its UK road freight network into Scotland by acquiring long-standing partner Drummond Distribution, a family-owned logistics company with around 175 employees and a fleet of approximately 100 trucks.

The purchase will give Dachser its first own locations in Scotland , adding five sites across the Central Belt between Glasgow and Edinburgh. The companies have not disclosed the purchase price.

Drummond generated approximately £20 million in revenue in 2025. The acquisition also includes around 46,500 square metres of warehousing and a fleet of roughly 100 trucks and 80 trailers.

Founded in 1927, Drummond specialises in the distribution of industrial goods and ambient food products and has worked with Dachser since 2008, connecting Scottish customers with the German logistics group’s European groupage network.

Dachser has not previously operated its own sites in Scotland. According to the company, the acquisition expands its geographical coverage without creating overlapping structures. Drummond will continue to operate under its existing management team, headed by Damon Burns, while the current owners gradually withdraw from the business.

The management team will report to Mark Rollinson, managing director of Dachser UK & Ireland.

Drummond’s main base is in Armadale, West Lothian, close to the M8 between Glasgow and Edinburgh. The company says its location puts around 60% of Scotland’s population within a one-hour drive of its depot. Its regional distribution operation covers destinations ranging from Edinburgh, Glasgow and the Borders to Aberdeen, Inverness, Fort William and Oban.

The acquisition turns a relationship stretching back almost two decades into full ownership.

“We have a long-standing and trusting partnership with Dachser,” said Damon Burns of Drummond Distribution, adding that joining another family-owned company would offer employees and customers greater stability and create further growth opportunities.

Alexander Tonn, COO Road Logistics at Dachser, said the acquisition would strengthen the company’s UK network and provide Scotland’s export-oriented industries with closer connections to European markets.

Dachser itself generated consolidated revenue of approximately €8.3 billion in 2025 and employed around 37,500 people at 427 locations worldwide.

evidence.title: Dachser enters into a strategic partnership with Synergie Canada
evidence.text:
Dachser enters into a strategic partnership with Synergie Canada

Kempten, Germany/Boisbriand, Canada (ots)

Investment in its air and sea freight forwarding business strengthens the company’s presence in North America

Global logistics provider Dachser has entered into a strategic partnership with Synergie Canada. The agreement covers the acquisition of a 10-percent-minority-share in the Canadian logistics provider.

In 2025, Synergie Canada generated revenue of approximately EUR 60 million with a workforce of about 100 employees. Founded in 2008 and based near Montreal, Quebec, the company specializes in air and sea freight services on transatlantic and transpacific routes and serves customers in the engineering, technology, fashion and aerospace industries. Synergie Canada also offers truck transport within Canada and across the border to the US. The company has been named one of Canada’s “Best Managed Companies” on multiple occasions.

“Canada is a highly attractive market for a global logistics provider like Dachser. As one of the seven leading industrialized nations, the Canadian economy is closely linked to the economies of the Americas, as well as our target markets in Europe,” explains Dr. Tobias Burger, COO Air & Sea Logistics at Dachser. “Expanding our presence in the Canadian market by acquiring a minority share of Synergie is essential for the continued growth of our business outside Europe. We’re delighted to have found the ideal partner for this expansion in Synergie Canada.”

“Synergie Canada has grown rapidly in the 15 years since it was founded, evolving from a traditional overland transport forwarder into one of Canada’s leading logistics providers for international air and sea freight,” says Marc-André Guindon, President of Synergie Canada. “Together with Dachser, we can now take the next step in our development and offer our customers even better access to international markets, particularly in Europe.”

Dachser, a family-owned company headquartered in Kempten, Germany, provides transport logistics, warehousing, and customized services in two business fields: Dachser Air & Sea Logistics and Dachser Road Logistics. The latter consists of two business lines: Dachser European Logistics and Dachser Food Logistics. Comprehensive contract logistics services and industry-specific solutions round out the company’s range. A seamless shipping network — both in Europe and overseas — and fully integrated IT systems ensure intelligent logistics solutions worldwide.

Thanks to some 37,500 employees at 427 locations all over the globe, Dachser generated consolidated net revenue of approximately EUR 8.3 billion in 2025. The same year, the logistics provider handled a total of 86.2 million shipments with a tonnage of 46.7 million metric tons. Dachser is represented by its own country organizations in 42 countries. In North America, Dachser operates 13 transportation and warehouse facilities in the US and Mexico and employs approximately 400 people.
