evidence.title: Poste Italiane stock falls as TIM stake passes 67 percent
evidence.text:
Poste Italiane stock closed at EUR 26.67 on Euronext Milan on September 21, 2026, down 0.82 percent from the previous close. The move came as the company advanced its control of Telecom Italia, with its stake reaching about 67 percent during the reopened acceptance period.

In the first day of the reopened offer window, additional Telecom Italia shares were tendered, lifting Poste Italiane's holding to about 67 percent of the capital. Ad-hoc-news reported the stake increase on September 22, 2026.

The acceptance period reopened on September 21 and is scheduled to run through September 25, 2026, according to The Globe and Mail . The transaction gives Poste Italiane indirect control of TIM Brasil through Telecom Italia, adding a large telecommunications asset to its existing postal, financial and insurance operations.

Poste Italiane reported first-half 2026 revenue of EUR 6.84 billion, up 5.9 percent from the prior-year period. EBIT increased 6.8 percent to EUR 1.77 billion from EUR 1.66 billion, while net income rose 3.5 percent to EUR 1.21 billion from EUR 1.17 billion, according to MarketScreener on September 22, 2026.

The comparison between revenue growth of 5.9 percent and net-income growth of 3.5 percent shows that earnings expanded more slowly than sales in the first half. Net financial position remained positive at EUR 4.24 billion on June 30, 2026, compared with EUR 5.64 billion at the end of 2025, a decline of EUR 1.40 billion that matters as the company integrates a larger telecom holding.

During September 22 trading, Poste Italiane was quoted at EUR 26.27, down 1.50 percent, while its market capitalization was shown at EUR 39.56 billion. The same MarketScreener snapshot listed an average analyst target of EUR 29.49 against the previous close of EUR 26.67, implying a 10.58 percent difference.

Evaluation.it assigned a fair value of EUR 26.10 and a hold recommendation in the September 22, 2026 analysis published by MarketScreener . That valuation is EUR 0.57 below the September 21 close, while the broader average target is EUR 2.82 higher, leaving the market's assessment divided around the financial and execution demands of the TIM transaction.

Poste Italiane stock closed at EUR 26.67 on Euronext Milan on September 21, 2026, after losing EUR 0.22, or 0.82 percent, against the previous close. The price and the 67 percent TIM stake now frame the next trading sessions as the reopened offer period runs through September 25, 2026.

evidence.title: Poste Italiane stock moves as Telecom Italia tender offer terms are raised
evidence.text:
Poste Italiane stock (ISIN IT0003796171) is drawing attention after the group improved the terms of its voluntary tender and exchange offer for Telecom Italia shares, raising the cash component to EUR 1.97 per share on September 7, 2026 according to Aktiencheck .

Tender offer terms and strategic rationale

According to Aktiencheck , the revised offer grants Telecom Italia minority shareholders EUR 1.97 in cash plus 0.218 newly issued Poste Italiane shares listed on Euronext Milan for each Telecom Italia share tendered.

The increase of the cash component by 18 percent compared with the initial proposal is designed to secure higher participation from Telecom Italia’s minority investors, who have until September 25, 2026 to decide whether to accept the offer, as highlighted by Aktiencheck .

Insider participation and market implications

As The Globe and Mail reports on September 19, 2026, at least one member of Telecom Italia’s corporate bodies has already accepted the offer via an off-exchange transaction, receiving the mixed consideration of cash and newly issued Poste Italiane shares for 128 Telecom Italia shares.

This insider acceptance underscores that the improved terms are considered sufficiently attractive by some key stakeholders, and it signals to the market that Poste Italiane is committed to executing the transaction on the basis of a higher cash payout than initially planned, according to The Globe and Mail .

Poste Italiane secures 66.6% of Telecom Italia at end of offer period

Published by Global Banking & Finance Review

Poste Italiane secured 66.6% of Telecom Italia’s share capital by Sept 11, 2026, after raising its offer and waiving the 66.67% acceptance threshold. The bid totals roughly €13 billion, with a reopening of the offer planned Sept 21–25.

Poste Italiane Acquires 66.6% of Telecom Italia’s Share Capital After Offer Period

Poste Italiane’s Takeover of Telecom Italia: Key Developments

MILAN, Sept 11 (Reuters) - Poste Italiane has secured a 66.6% stake in Telecom Italia's (TIM) share capital, Reuters calculations based on stock exchange data showed on Friday, at the end of the main phase of the state-backed group's takeover offer.

Poste, which had previously built a 20% stake in TIM, this week increased the cash component of its offer by 18% to €1.97 per share, while confirming an exchange ratio of 0.218 newly issued Poste shares for each TIM share tendered.

The bid was worth around €13 billion at Friday's closing prices.

Borsa Italiana, the Italian bourse, said the take-up in the buyout offer for the former Italian phone monopoly reached 58.2% of shares targeted by the bid.

This week Poste also waived the 66.67% acceptance threshold it had initially set as a condition for the bid to proceed. It said the offer period would reopen from September 21 to September 25.

evidence.text:
The past three years for International Distributions Services (LON:IDS) investors has not been profitable

Many investors define successful investing as beating the market average over the long term. But its virtually certain that sometimes you will buy stocks that fall short of the market average returns. Unfortunately, that's been the case for longer term International Distributions Services plc ( LON:IDS ) shareholders, since the share price is down 53% in the last three years, falling well short of the market return of around 15%. Shareholders have had an even rougher run lately, with the share price down 11% in the last 90 days.

Since shareholders are down over the longer term, lets look at the underlying fundamentals over the that time and see if they've been consistent with returns.

View our latest analysis for International Distributions Services

While markets are a powerful pricing mechanism, share prices reflect investor sentiment, not just underlying business performance. One flawed but reasonable way to assess how sentiment around a company has changed is to compare the earnings per share (EPS) with the share price.

International Distributions Services saw its share price decline over the three years in which its EPS also dropped, falling to a loss. Due to the loss, it's not easy to use EPS as a reliable guide to the business. However, we can say we'd expect to see a falling share price in this scenario.

What About The Total Shareholder Return (TSR)?

Investors should note that there's a difference between International Distributions Services' total shareholder return (TSR) and its share price change, which we've covered above. Arguably the TSR is a more complete return calculation because it accounts for the value of dividends (as if they were reinvested), along with the hypothetical value of any discounted capital that have been offered to shareholders. Dividends have been really beneficial for International Distributions Services shareholders, and that cash payout explains why its total shareholder loss of 46%, over the last 3 years, isn't as bad as the share price return.

We're pleased to report that International Distributions Services shareholders have received a total shareholder return of 8.3% over one year. That gain is better than the annual TSR over five years, which is 2%. Therefore it seems like sentiment around the company has been positive lately. evidence.title: Liberia: Global Logistics Services (Gls Group) Firmly Rejects Unfounded Allegations - Calls for Due Process and Protection of Rights of Legitimate Businesses Operating in Liberia
evidence.text:
Liberia: Global Logistics Services (Gls Group) Firmly Rejects Unfounded Allegations - Calls for Due Process and Protection of Rights of Legitimate Businesses Operating in Liberia

The Management of Global Logistics Services (GLS Group) issues this statement to address persistent inaccuracies in public reporting surrounding the recent cargo interception at Roberts International Airport (RIA), and to set out the company's position clearly and for the record.

For fourteen years, GLS Group has served Liberia's logistics sector with a commitment to compliance, transparency and operational excellence. Recent public commentary surrounding an ongoing investigation concerning the cargo interception has created confusion regarding the company's statutory role. This statement is intended to clarify those facts.

As a freight forwarder, GLS Group did not authorize, approve, invoice, or knowingly facilitate the shipment in question through its established corporate systems. GLS Group states the following in the strongest possible terms:

Key Facts: The Statutory Division of Responsibility at RIA Public confusion owing to misinformation about the role of Global Logistics Services' (GLS Group) has been central to the mischaracterization of this matter.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The following facts are not in dispute and are governed by Liberian law:

· GLS MENZIES is an independent and separate entity from Global Logistics Services (GLS Group); and GLS-MENZIES' role is limited to logistics, handling, and storage of cargo passing through the airport facility.

· Global Logistics Services (GLS Group) which is a freight forwarding company is engaged in customs brokerage, and project logistics, and has no operational role in cargo handling at RIA.

· The authority to screen, inspect, and clear/approve cargo for shipment from RIA rests solely and exclusively with Government agencies empowered by statute to perform those functions.

· Attributing responsibility to GLS Group misstates this statutory division of

responsibility and conflates freight forwarding with cargo handling -- two distinct functions carried out by two distinct sets of actors. For the record, GLS Group neither performs cargo handling nor cargo screening and cargo clearing/approval for shipment.

Over the past several weeks, Global Logistics Services (GLS Group) has demonstrated an unwavering commitment to transparency and the rule of law. We have cooperated fully with national security agencies and investigators:

· GLS Group management has cooperated willingly and fully with the Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency and the Joint Special Investigation Team.

· Our offices and operational facilities were made fully available to investigating authorities, who conducted on site reviews without obstruction.

· As a certified logistics provider held to strict international compliance benchmarks, our internal procedures are designed to log, handle, and escalate irregularities.

We continue to urge that the ongoing legal process run its course on verified facts, within the statutory framework described above, rather than on speculation.

GLS Group is concerned that recent public commentary has, in places, blurred the statutory distinction between terminal operations and cargo screening -- creating an impression of alleged corporate culpability that is neither supported by the facts nor by the roles assigned to each party under Liberian law.

Certain media entities and commentators have gone further, publishing defamatory commentary including but not limited to calls for the closure of freight forwarding operations and the arbitrary suspension of the concession agreement.

GLS Group would be remiss to allow its reputation to be dismantled by unverified public commentary. The presumption of innocence is not a courtesy--it is a constitutional principle that protects both individuals and legal entities until proven otherwise through due process.

GLS Group will take the necessary steps to hold to account any person or entity engaged in spreading defamatory statements in order to protect the company's longstanding integrity and reputation.

Any determination of alleged corporate culpability belongs before the courts, where it can be examined directly, transparently, and in accordance with the law. That is what due process requires. Unless and until a court determines otherwise, the constitutional principle of the presumption of innocence must be respected.

GLS Group: A Pillar of the Liberian Economy

Global Logistics Services' (GLS Group) record in Liberia speaks for itself.

· 14 Years of Commitment: Alongside credible international investors, including

Development Finance Institutions (DFIs) and other reputable global corporations, GLS Group has invested significantly in critical national logistics and aviation infrastructure.

· Taxpayer & Employer: Since inception, GLS Group has contributed significantly in taxes to the national treasury and directly created hundreds of stable jobs for Liberian citizens.

· Rigorous Standards: Our institutional and international development funding was secured only after passing intrusive and exhaustive corporate due diligence processes.

We call on all responsible institutions and members of the public to allow the legal process to run its course on verified facts, and to correctly attribute statutory responsibility for cargo screening, clearing/approval of cargo for shipment to the government agencies mandated to carry it out. GLS Group remains committed to Liberia's economy, its people, and its future. That commitment does not waiver.

evidence.title: How FedEx is Expanding SAF Procurement Across US Airports
evidence.text:
How FedEx is Expanding SAF Procurement Across US Airports

FedEx is helping to power sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) procurement with the use of new agreements projected to secure more than 20 million gallons of neat SAF across five US airports throughout the calendar year of 2027.

This agreement will work across FedEx operations at Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR), Oakland International Airport (OAK), Miami International Airport (MIA), John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) and Dallas Fort Worth International Airport (DFW).

The agreements are expected to deliver SAF at blend ratios ranging from 30% to 50%, depending on location.

FedEx is working towards its goal of sourcing 30% of jet fuel from blended alternative sources by 2030, while expanding the use of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) across its US air network.

"The latest agreements represent an expansion of SAF within the FedEx air network enabled, in part, by state and federal level incentives," says Greg Paulus, Vice President of Enterprise Sourcing.

Building on a strong year of SAF deployment

Since 2025, FedEx has secured approximately five million gallons of neat SAF through agreements that resulted in the deployment of 16.5 million gallons of blended SAF across five US airports. With this next phase of procurement, SAF blends now represent a significant share of FedEx's jet fuel use at the airports mentioned above.

"SAF is one of the most impactful decarbonisation solutions available to aviation today and an important part of our approach to reducing emissions," adds Karen Blanks Ellis, Chief Sustainability Officer and Vice President of Environmental Affairs at FedEx.

"For the market to grow, supply needs to be reliable, affordable, and sustainable. Expanding our procurement allows us to employ more SAF in our network while bolstering the demand for greater production and scale."

The new agreements are another step in putting more SAF into use across the FedEx network while demonstrating the demand that exists today. As the SAF market develops, FedEx will continue evaluating opportunities to expand its use where supply, infrastructure and economics align with the needs of its air network.

Coast-to-coast progress across five major airports

This continues the efforts of FedEx when it comes to harnessing SAF. FedEx introduced SAF at two US airports towards the end of 2025: Dallas Fort Worth International Airport (DFW) and John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK).

With these two additional deployments, FedEx began using blended SAF at a total of five major US airports in 2025. Combined, these agreements secure the equivalent of five million gallons of neat SAF.

"Expanding SAF use by FedEx to include our operations at DFW and JFK caps off a successful year of SAF deployments coast-to-coast," adds Karen.

"While we know there remains work ahead to procure more SAF and to continue to educate our stakeholders about how alternative fuels fit into our overall aviation sustainability strategy, we are proud of our steps forward in 2025."

Along with increased procurement of alternative fuels to power its global fleet of more than 700 aircraft, FedEx has long pursued other efficiency improvement projects like aircraft modernisation and fuel savings initiatives. After achieving the goal of a 30% reduction in aircraft emissions intensity from a 2005 baseline in FY24, FedEx expanded the goal to a 40% reduction by 2034.

FedEx provides customers and businesses worldwide with a broad portfolio of transportation, e-commerce and business services.

With annual revenue of US$86bn, the company offers integrated business solutions utilising its flexible, efficient and intelligent global network.

Consistently ranked among the world's most admired and trusted employers , FedEx has more than 450,000 employees focused on safety, the highest ethical and professional standards and the needs of their customers and communities.

FedEx is committed to connecting people and possibilities around the world responsibly and resourcefully, with a goal to achieve carbon-neutral operations by 2040.

FedEx joined the Hedera Governing Council, taking a seat alongside Google, IBM and Dell to help govern the enterprise blockchain network, with a focus on building trusted digital infrastructure for global supply chains.

FedEx partnered with last-mile platform OneRail to launch FedEx SameDay Local, giving retailers two-hour and end-of-day delivery options via a network of 1,000+ drivers covering nearly 99% of the US.

FedEx made a strategic investment in Nimble, an AI robotics and autonomous fulfilment company, to scale automation across its FedEx Fulfillment network of 130+ North American warehouse locations.

Six years after ending their delivery relationship, FedEx and Amazon signed a new multi-year agreement covering residential delivery of select large packages, plus an expansion of free-returns options.

FedEx has worked with Aurora Innovation on autonomous trucking, completing more than 3,200 driverless loads on Texas routes as part of its broader robotics-partnership strategy alongside Berkshire Grey, Dexterity and Nimble.

Chief Sustainability Officer & VP of Environmental Affairs

evidence.title: FedEx leads 2027 rate increases
evidence.text:
FedEx will raise US shipping rates by an average of 5.9% from 4 January 2027, while both FedEx and UPS have introduced new demand and surge fees on international shipments this autumn.

The 5.9% general rate increase (GRI), FedEx’s fourth in a row at the same average, will apply to Express, Ground and Freight services, along with minimum rates and various surcharges. Rates for Ground Economy, Ground Multiweight, International Premium and International Priority DirectDistribution will also rise, though FedEx has not disclosed specific figures for these services.

From 18 January, FedEx will introduce two further charges: a US$25 Paper Document Fee per shipment where a trade document is supplied in non-electronic format before processing, and a US$5 Paper Air Waybill Fee on US domestic and export shipments initiated with manual paper airbills.

evidence.title: FedEx Chiefs on AI: Speed isn't the problem, customs is
evidence.text:
FedEx Chiefs on AI: Speed isn't the problem, customs is

FedEx’s Raj Subramaniam and Vishal Talwar say AI must be led by the CEO, and that customs clearance, not flight speed, is logistics' real bottleneck.

Raj Subramaniam, CEO, FedEx and Vishal Talwar, EVP & CDIO of FedEx, and President of FedEx Dataworks

FedEx CEO Raj Subramaniam and Vishal Talwar, Executive Vice President, Chief Digital and Information Officer (CDIO) of FedEx, and President of FedEx Dataworks, told the WSJ Leadership Institute Technology Council that artificial intelligence at global scale cannot succeed without the CEO at the helm, and that the industry's biggest drag on efficiency is not how fast a package moves, but how long it sits still. On September 14 in New York, the two leaders sat down with Alan Murray, founding president of the WSJ Leadership Institute.

AI has to be a CEO's job, not just the CIO's Asked bluntly who runs AI at FedEx, Subramaniam did not hesitate to hand himself the responsibility. "I don't think any company today can succeed in AI without the CEO taking active leadership role in AI," he said, arguing that the line between business strategy and technology has all but disappeared. "The gap between business and technology is fast moving away. We can't have a business strategy without technology and the reverse is also the case." He called AI "the defining technology of the era" and said the strategy "has got to be top-down." Talwar, for his part, offered no resistance to the framing: "I'm 100% cool with anything Raj says here."

Two petabytes a day, and a network built to notice Subramaniam described FedEx's data as the fuel behind its AI ambitions, generated by a network that moves roughly $2 trillion of commerce a year. "The fuel for AI is data, and two petabytes of data every single day represents the movement of the world's most premium supply chain," he said. He traced the shift in how supply chains are perceived, noting that after the pandemic they became "a cool thing" and a "boardroom conversation," pushing FedEx to expand its ambitions beyond internal efficiency. Predictability for customers is one payoff he pointed to: FedEx's healthcare transportation business, he said, has grown 30% over the past couple of years as AI-driven forecasting lets healthcare customers "schedule their workflow significantly better."

Talwar broke the strategy into three layers: efficiency, customer differentiation, and, what he called the "true transformative" piece, new business models. On efficiency, he cited concrete gains: air maintenance research time cut "from 30 minutes to three minutes," a 90% improvement that gets aircraft back into service faster, and "tens of millions of dollars of annual revenue" recovered by using AI to catch mis-tracked, non-standard packages that should have carried a surcharge. On the customer side, he said certainty is what matters most: "The one thing our customers care most about is don't surprise us. They want certainty," pointing to FedEx's ability to guarantee delivery within a two-hour window on shipments moving thousands of miles from Asia to the US.

The real friction isn't speed; it's what happens when a package stops moving Pressed on whether faster delivery is even possible anymore, Subramaniam suggested FedEx is near the physical limits of aviation. "We are leaving China and delivering to every zip code in America overnight," he said. "Now we are at the speed of aviation technology and that's kind of it at this point." Asked, half-jokingly, whether teleportation was next, Talwar redirected the conversation to where he says the real opportunity lies; not in motion, but in the gaps between it. "The focus that we have is not about the speed while an object is in motion," he said. "I can put anything from China to US in 13 hours, 14-hour flight time. Then it sits in customs for clearance for another four days. The amount of time that's spent in something waiting when it's not in motion, that's where the friction in supply chain is."

Both executives were emphatic that this is not a FedEx-specific failing. "This is a problem in industry at large. It's not a problem that's just for FedEx," Talwar said, putting a number on the scale of the issue: "We are leaking about $1.9 trillion of annual value just because of these inefficiencies and friction points within supply chain. That is the problem we are out to solve." Subramaniam echoed the framing when asked how far along FedEx's AI transformation is. "I would say we are early innings," he said. "We have been building infrastructure... but there is a long way to go. The $1.9 trillion of supply chain inefficiency that's in the global system; we want to be able to have a crack at that."

Robots in the warehouse, autonomous trucks on the highway On physical AI, Subramaniam described FedEx's giant sortation hubs as "an inventory in motion system" that is almost entirely automated except at two stubborn points: loading and unloading trucks. "Packages of different sizes, shapes, weights coming through. You don't know what's coming exactly. And then it has to figure out how to actually play Tetris on the truck," he said, adding that FedEx has deployed 60 robots in one facility to test solutions ahead of peak season. He also pointed to autonomous trucking on highway middle-mile routes, developed with Aurora, connecting facilities without putting unmanned trucks on interior roads.

Talwar tied the robotics push back to data, arguing that FedEx is positioned to build something the logistics industry has never had. "A real-world model for supply chain or logistics does not exist today. And who's going to create it? It has to be one of the physical operators of that network, which is us," he said, noting that even FedEx's shipping labels remain "passive" and not yet smart devices.

Physical AI deployment at the FedEx Hagerstown hub in Maryland

Growth, not job cuts, for now Asked whether automation would eventually mean fewer employees, Subramaniam pushed back, noting FedEx added 25,000 new US employees last year. "I think you're not going to see AI delivering packages anytime soon," he said. "The last mile, the last 10 feet, those are even more complex problems to solve. And these robots are going to work hand-in-hand with our team members." He summed up the logic in three steps: "AI as a driver of growth. Growth drives packages. Packages drive people."

Geopolitics: "advanced calculus" every day Operating in 220 countries, Subramaniam said geopolitical shocks are now a daily operating reality, from rerouting around Russian and Ukrainian airspace to suspending its Dubai hub in favour of a more southern route through the Middle East. "Every twitch and turn that happens anywhere in the world has an impact on FedEx," he said. "As the world has got more complex, before basic math would have done. Now we need advanced calculus, and there are very few people who do advanced calculus, and we are one of them." Talwar said AI has not yet been applied to geopolitical risk directly, but that FedEx Dataworks is increasingly advising customer CEOs on sourcing, tariff scenario modelling and lane strategy.

On AI's risks, no daylight between the two Closing on the debate over whether AI will drive prosperity or catastrophe, Talwar said there was no disagreement between him and Subramaniam. "We both think that it's in our hands and it's up to us to apply it for good," he said. Subramaniam was equally direct: "We're on the optimistic side, let's call it that." Talwar pointed to FedEx's role in the newly formed "AI for Good" commission, which brings together public figures and industry leaders to address equitable access and responsible deployment.

evidence.title: FedEx preps 5.9% rate hike, surcharge increases for 2027
evidence.text:
FedEx preps 5.9% rate hike, surcharge increases for 2027

This story was originally published on Supply Chain Dive. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily Supply Chain Dive newsletter .

FedEx's standard shipping rates for U.S. package shipping services, including import and export volume, will increase by 5.9% on average starting Jan. 4, 2027, according to the carrier's website .

The company will increase minimum rates along with various surcharges and fees on that date as well. Rates for Ground Economy, Ground Multiweight, International Premium and International Priority DirectDistribution will climb as well, but FedEx did not mention specific increase amounts for those services.

FedEx will also introduce additional fees on Jan. 18. This includes a $25 paper document fee when any associated trade document is provided in a non-electronic format prior to processing, and a $5 fee for U.S. domestic and export shipments initiated with manual paper airbills.

Additional handling (Zone 2, weight based)

Additional handling (based on dimensions)

The standard rate increase follows a typical annual practice for FedEx, and mirrors 5.9% jumps the carrier imposed in 2024 , 2025 and 2026 . Rival UPS has done the same, although the carrier hasn't yet announced a 2027 rate hike as of Monday.

The actual rate increase amount each FedEx package will see in 2027 varies by service used, weight and shipping distance, meaning the impact will differ for each shipment.

Five of FedEx's seven major services will actually see rate increases averaging above 5.9%, including First Overnight (6.01%) and 2Day A.M. (6.65%), according to an analysis by logistics data platform Loop . Meanwhile, Standard Overnight will see a 5.16% jump, and Express Saver volume will only see a 3.09% increase on average, creating cost-savings opportunities for shipments that can handle slower transportation speeds.

"Shippers with transit-tolerant freight currently moving on 2Day should model the Express Saver alternative before their next renewal," per Loop's analysis.

Loop also noted that FedEx Ground packages between one and five pounds — a weight range common among e-commerce shipments — will see a 6.49% increase, a higher jump compared to shipments in heavier weight brackets. FedEx has reduced its emphasis on attracting general e-commerce volume in recent quarters, instead chasing more profitable shipments in customer segments such as healthcare and automotive.

- High-margin services like retail rollouts and AI-driven route optimization enhance margins, supported by circular economy initiatives like truck reconditioning.

- Fortune's 2025 "Most Innovative" recognition validates XPO's flywheel model: cost savings fund innovation, driving durable competitive advantages.

In a freight market defined by volatile demand, rising input costs, and margin compression, XPO XPO -- Logistics has emerged as a rare outlier. By combining surgical cost efficiency with bold service innovation, the company has not only weathered industry headwinds but also outperformed peers in profitability and customer retention. This dual strategy—rooted in operational rigor and forward-thinking execution—positions XPO as a compelling case study for investors seeking resilient logistics plays.

XPO’s cost discipline in 2025 has been nothing short of transformative. By aggressively shifting from third-party carriers to in-house operations, the company reduced outsourced line-haul miles to 8.8% of total miles in Q1 2025, slashing purchased transportation expenses by 53% year-over-year [1]. This shift has been amplified by AI-driven productivity tools that optimize labor scheduling, reducing hours per shipment by 1% in the same period [1]. These measures have enabled XPO to maintain a 6.9% yield growth (excluding fuel) and a 5.6% increase in revenue per shipment, even as industry-wide tonnage declined by 7.5% [1].

The implications are clear: XPO’s cost structure is now more insulated from macroeconomic swings. Unlike peers reliant on spot markets and outsourced labor, XPO’s vertically integrated model creates a buffer against rising transportation and labor costs. This is not merely a short-term tactic but a structural repositioning that enhances gross margins and free cash flow generation.

While cost efficiency provides a defensive edge, XPO’s offensive strategy lies in its ability to redefine service offerings. The company has launched high-margin solutions such as retail store rollouts and trade show transport, catering to niche but lucrative segments of the logistics market [1]. These services leverage XPO’s existing infrastructure while commanding premium pricing due to their specialized nature.

Equally impactful is XPO’s investment in AI and automation to enhance on-time performance and transit efficiency. By deploying predictive analytics for route optimization and real-time shipment tracking, the company has improved customer satisfaction and reduced delivery variability—a critical differentiator in the LTL (less-than-truckload) segment [1].

XPO’s circular economy initiative, "Regain," further underscores its innovation edge. By reconditioning trucks and trailers, the company extends asset lifecycles, reduces capital expenditures, and aligns with ESG trends [2]. This program not only lowers operational costs but also appeals to environmentally conscious clients, broadening XPO’s market reach.

XPO’s dual focus on cost efficiency and service innovation has earned it recognition as one of Fortune’s "Most Innovative Companies" in 2025 [3]. This accolade validates the company’s ability to adapt to shifting market dynamics while maintaining profitability. For investors, the key takeaway is that XPO is not just surviving in a challenging freight market—it is redefining the rules of competition.

The company’s strategic moves create a flywheel effect: cost savings fund innovation, which in turn drives higher margins and customer loyalty. This self-reinforcing cycle is rare in the logistics sector, where commoditization often erodes differentiation. XPO’s ability to balance operational discipline with creative service offerings suggests a durable competitive advantage.

In an industry where margins are razor-thin and disruptions are frequent, XPO Logistics stands out as a masterclass in operational differentiation. By marrying cost efficiency with service innovation, the company has built a moat that protects against cyclical downturns while capturing growth in premium markets. For investors, this is not just a story of survival—it’s a blueprint for outperformance in a volatile sector.

evidence.title: Expeditors International stock falls 2.32 percent
evidence.text:
Expeditors International stock fell 2.32 percent to USD 183.66 at 4:00 p.m. ET on September 24, 2026. The move leaves the logistics company 5.62 percent below its 52-week high of USD 194.59, while its second-quarter earnings remain the central fundamental reference for the shares.

Expeditors reported second-quarter 2026 revenue of USD 3.50 billion, an increase of 32.1 percent from the prior-year quarter, according to StockTitan . Operating income reached USD 350 million, up 41 percent year over year, giving the revenue gain a direct earnings effect.

The report also showed net earnings of USD 266 million and diluted EPS of USD 2.03 for Q2/2026. EPS increased 51.5 percent from USD 1.34 in the year-earlier quarter, a sharper improvement than the revenue growth.

The USD 2.03 diluted EPS exceeded the USD 1.69 consensus estimate by USD 0.34, or 20.1 percent, according to Yahoo Finance . That comparison matters because it separates the reported result from the broader earnings expansion: Expeditors did not merely grow year over year, it also surpassed the market estimate.

For investors, the numbers point to operating leverage in the current cycle. Revenue grew 32.1 percent, while operating income grew 41 percent and EPS advanced 51.5 percent in the same quarter.

At USD 183.66 on September 24, 2026, Expeditors International stock was USD 10.93 below its 52-week high of USD 194.59. The company had a market capitalization of USD 24.02 billion at the same market snapshot.

evidence.text:
Deutsche Bahn teilt mit: Rheintalbahn-Sperrung Anfang Oktober

Die Deutsche Bahn sperrt die Rheintalbahn zwischen Freiburg und Basel rund um das Wochenende Anfang Oktober wegen umfangreicher Bauarbeiten. Betroffen ist der Streckenabschnitt zwischen Freiburg (Breisgau) Hauptbahnhof und Basel Badischer Bahnhof, wie die Deutsche Bahn mitteilte. Im Rahmen des viergleisigen Ausbaus der Strecke Karlsruhe-Basel wird unter anderem am neuen elektronischen Stellwerk in Basel sowie an der Oberleitung zwischen Weil am Rhein und Basel gearbeitet. Hinzu kommen Instandhaltungsarbeiten an Oberleitung, Weichen und Gleisen in mehreren Abschnitten.

Die ICE-Linien Berlin-Schweiz sowie Hamburg-Köln-Basel beginnen und enden während der Arbeiten in Freiburg, die Linie Hamburg-Kassel-Basel endet in Karlsruhe . In Offenburg entfallen wegen weiterer Bauarbeiten sämtliche Fernverkehrshalte. Zwischen Freiburg und Basel sowie zwischen Freiburg und Basel Badischer Bahnhof sollen Busse den Ausfall auffangen, zwischen Karlsruhe und Zürich werden täglich fünf ICE-Zugpaare über Singen umgeleitet.

Im Regionalverkehr fallen die Linien RE 7 Karlsruhe-Basel, RB 26 Offenburg-Freiburg und RB 27 Freiburg/Müllheim-Basel Badischer Bahnhof/Neuenburg zwischen Freiburg und Basel Badischer Bahnhof aus. Auch zwischen Offenburg und Lahr fahren zeitweise keine Züge der Linie RB 26, dort gibt es Ersatzverbindungen über Friesenheim. Als Ersatz sind mehrere Regio-Busse mit unterschiedlichen Halten zwischen Freiburg, dem Markgräflerland und Basel im Einsatz.

Die DB rät Reisenden, sich vor Fahrtantritt über ihre Verbindung zu informieren und wegen längerer Reisezeiten im Ersatzverkehr mehr Zeit einzuplanen. Fahrräder können in den Ersatzbussen nicht mitgenommen werden, auf sehr großes oder schweres Gepäck sollte nach Möglichkeit verzichtet werden.

evidence.title: Deutsche Bahn: So soll modulares Bauen die Sanierung beschleunigen
evidence.text:
Viele Baustellen, lange Bauzeiten, unpünktliche Züge, und das noch über viele Jahre: Die malade Infrastruktur der Eisenbahn stellt die Geduld der Deutschen auf die Probe. Nur nachvollziehbar, dass sich viele Gedanken machen, wie sich dies alles beschleunigen lässt. Derzeit sieht es zwar nicht danach aus. Vielmehr wurden zuletzt die geplanten großen Gleisstreckensanierungen aus vielerlei Gründen zeitlich gestreckt. Nun aber hat die Deutsche Bahn einen neuen Trend ausgerufen: modulares Bauen.

Was ist darunter zu verstehen? Es geht darum, den Bauprozess mit industriell vorgefertigten Modulen zu beschleunigen. Die Branche versucht das heute vor allem im Wohnungsbau zu demonstrieren. Wohnungen oder einzelne Bauteile werden in einer Art Baukastensystem vorgefertigt und anschließend auf der Baustelle zu größeren Gebäuden zusammengesetzt. Die Bundesanstalt für Immobilienaufgaben schildert den Prozess so: „Durch die serielle Modulbauweise ist die Bauzeit stark verkürzt: Im Werk werden die Raummodule vorgefertigt, mit Schiff und Lkw zur Baustelle transportiert und dort mithilfe eines Krans montiert.“

F.A.Z.-Artikel häufiger in Ihren Suchergebnissen sehen

Auf der Bahntechnikmesse Innotrans hat die DB jetzt den „DB Supplier Innovation Award 2026“ verliehen. Der Sieger und die Finalisten des Innovationspreises setzen den Angaben zufolge mit neuen Methoden auf vorgefertigte Bauteile in der Sanierung und dem Bau von Bahnstrecken, Tunneln und Brücken. Gewinner ist das Unternehmen Salcef Bau mit seiner Baumethode „Fast-System“. Damit sollen schnellere Umbauarbeiten möglich sein, ohne den Bahnbetrieb komplett zu unterbrechen. Dies soll durch den Wechsel von Schotteroberflächen auf ein „Feste-Fahrbahn-System“ gelingen, unter anderem mit vorgefertigten Gleistragplatten als Basis.

Unter die Finalisten des Innovationspreises schafften es laut DB auch die Max-Bögl-Stiftung sowie die Unternehmen Ramboll Deutschland und Laing O’Rourke. Die Max-Bögl-Stiftung erhielt eine Auszeichnung für ihre Tunnel-Modul-Bauweise. Die Betoninnenschalen für Tunnel werden dabei nicht mehr vor Ort hergestellt, sondern industriell vorgefertigt.

Die Frage bleibt: Kann durch eine Änderung der Baustrategie wirklich Zeit in größerem Umfang eingespart werden? Finanzvorstand Michael Obrowski sagt: „Durch die intelligente Kombination aus vorgefertigten Komponenten, parallelisierten Abläufen und einem integrierten Bauverfahren sollen Sperrungen künftig deutlich kürzer und weniger umfangreich ausfallen.“ Das sei eine gute Nachricht für die Reisenden. Zugleich müsse sich die neue Bauweise als wirtschaftlich sinnvoll erweisen. Konkrete Zeitsparschätzungen mag Obrowski allerdings nicht abgeben.

Bentley hat sich von den Plänen einer schnellen Elektrifizierung verabschiedet. Dennoch gibt es nun ein reines Elektromodell, positioniert für jüngere Käufer. Absatzprobleme in China und am Golf belasten die Marke.

Auch in Italien, der zweitgrößten Industrienation Europas, geht es bergab. Aber es gibt einige Lichtblicke, etwa in der kaum bekannten italienischen Pharmaindustrie.

Wegen der EU-Regeln gegen Greenwashing drohen nichtkonforme Produkte auf dem Müll zu landen. Eine deutsche Sonderregel soll das verhindern. Sie reiche aber nicht, mahnen Branchenvertreter.

evidence.title: Deutsche Bahn tests insect-friendly light sources
evidence.text:
It is bright everywhere, even at night the cities are illuminated. Professional and amateur stargazers complain about this. But the flora and fauna also suffers from artificial lighting. Deutsche Bahn is therefore planning to equip train stations with different light sources. The Leibniz Institute for the Analysis of Biodiversity Change (LIB) has tested these.

The team examined light sources and demonstrated that amber LED lights with a color temperature of 1800 Kelvin (K) attract significantly fewer insects than the currently standard cool white light sources with a color temperature of 4000 K or high-pressure sodium lamps with a color temperature of 2000 K.

“We were able to show under real conditions at train stations that the choice of light source and, in particular, its spectral composition play a crucial role in attracting flying insects”, said LIB researcher Carmen Ludreschl . While there was hardly any difference in the number of attracted insects between the cool white LEDs and the high-pressure sodium lamps, there were around 40 to 50 percent fewer individuals and up to 75 percent less biomass.

The amber LEDs also performed better in terms of species: they attracted 10 to 20 percent fewer species, including endangered and protected ones. However, the best solution, the researchers emphasize, would be unlit control sites. There is no insect-friendly artificial light. “Switching off remains the best option.”

However, it’s not just insects that appreciate the warmer light of the 1800 K LEDs: in informal surveys, some train passengers also said that the warmer light was more pleasant for them.

The project was initiated by Deutsche Bahn (DB), which wants to make lighting at train stations more insect-friendly. And it has already reacted to the results that the team published in the journal Biological Conservation : at the six rural train stations in Westhavelland that were examined, as well as another one, the lighting has been permanently switched to the new 1800 K LEDs. In addition, the light source has been included in the selection list of light sources for DB’s infrastructure subsidiary DB Infra Go.

However, it is unlikely that all train stations will be illuminated with amber LEDs: EU lighting standards and safety guidelines only permit their use on uncovered platforms. Although a new paragraph in the Federal Nature Conservation Act is intended to regulate protection against light pollution, it has not yet come into force.

Light pollution throws the entire ecosystem out of balance, the LIB team emphasizes: If insects are disturbed or die as a result, the food supply for birds and bats decreases. They are also missing as pollinators for plants.

Debatte: Ist die Deutsche Bahn noch zu retten? : BILD-User sehen wenig Hoffnung für die Deutsche Bahn

Verspätungen, Ausfälle und jetzt noch langsamere Sanierungen. Wir haben die Community gefragt: Ist die Deutsche Bahn noch zu retten?

Für viele Fahrgäste funktioniert die Deutsche Bahn längst nicht mehr zuverlässig: Millionen Menschen sind täglich auf Züge angewiesen und von Ausfällen sowie Verspätungen betroffen. Nun sollen wichtige Strecken künftig auch noch langsamer saniert werden. In der aktuellen BILD-Debatte diskutieren User deshalb darüber, ob die Bahn noch zu retten ist oder ob das marode Netz, langwierige Planungen und politische Penibilität eine Wende verhindern.

Warum das Sanierungstempo sinkt, wie BILD-Leser darüber denken und wie Sie sich an der Debatte beteiligen können, erfahren Sie hier.

Bahn-Chefin Evelyn Palla (52) will künftig nur noch zwei statt bis zu vier Korridorsanierungen pro Jahr durchführen. In besonderen Fällen sollen es drei sein. Das Tempo soll an die verfügbaren Finanzmittel und die Kapazitäten im Schienennetz angepasst werden.

Weniger gleichzeitige Vollsperrungen könnten Umleitungen und zusätzliche Verspätungen zwar begrenzen, dafür dauert die Erneuerung der rund 40 ausgewählten Strecken aber länger. Ob das zuletzt genannte Zieljahr 2036 noch zu halten ist, bleibt offen.

Viele Bürger und BILD-Leser stellen sich deshalb die Frage: Ist die Deutsche Bahn noch zu retten?

Bislang liegt kein eindeutiges Abstimmungsergebnis vor. Unsere Leserschaft ist in der Frage um die Zukunft der Deutschen Bahn zwiegespalten, doch in einer Sache sind sich alle einig: Es bedarf bei der Deutschen Bahn grundlegender Reformen.

Einige halten die DB grundsätzlich für rettbar. Dafür seien jedoch umfangreiche Investitionen, modernere Technik, mehr Kapazitäten und schnellere Entscheidungen nötig. Als Vorbild werden Länder mit einem zuverlässigeren Bahnverkehr und kürzeren Abständen zwischen den Verbindungen genannt. Einige BILD-User fordern zudem weniger staatlichen Einfluss oder eine vollständige Privatisierung.

Die andere Seite zweifelt angesichts des maroden Schienennetzes, der Unzuverlässigkeit der Bahn und der langen Planungszeiten an einer Kehrtwende. Kritisiert werden auch das Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis, Probleme im Güterverkehr und die bisherigen Strukturen. Aus diesem Grund sehen einige User eine Trennung von Netz und Bahnbetrieb für unerlässlich.

Selbst diejenigen, die Hoffnung in eine bessere Zukunft der Deutschen Bahn haben, sind sich einig, dass es dazu grundlegender Reformen bedarf. evidence.title: Reports: Deutsche Bahn posts first core business profit in seven years
evidence.text:
Reports: Deutsche Bahn posts first core business profit in seven years

German national rail operator Deutsche Bahn posted a profit in its core business in the first half of 2026 for the first time in seven years, German media reported ahead of the company's earnings presentation on Thursday.

The state-owned company generated a profit in the hundreds of millions of euros in its core business between January and June, Bild newspaper and Der Spiegel magazine reported. That compares with a loss of about €760 million ($871.2 million) in the first half of 2025.

The company said in response to a query that it would not comment before the official release of the figures later on Thursday morning.

Deutsche Bahn also carried about 960 million passengers in the first six months of the year, around 17 million more than a year earlier and a record, the reports said.

According to the reports, higher fuel prices encouraged more commuters to switch from cars to trains, while rail fares remained broadly stable. Demand for long-distance services had also risen sharply since April.

New discount offers also appeared to boost demand. Around 600,000 passengers used Deutsche Bahn's last-minute ticket, while 200,000 travellers bought its family ticket, according to the reports. About 50,000 customers ordered the company's free Youth BahnCard 25 discount card.

Chief executive Evelyn Palla is due to present the company's half-year results later on Thursday.

Deutsche Bahn has struggled in recent years with poor punctuality, ageing infrastructure and weak financial performance. It reported a net loss of more than €1 billion in 2025.

Palla has launched a broad restructuring programme that includes cost-cutting measures and job reductions, while the company's long-distance business is undergoing a separate turnaround programme.

evidence.title: Deutsche Bahn has banned the consumption of alcohol at all 5,400 stations
evidence.text:
Deutsche Bahn is to ban alcohol consumption at all the stations it manages in Germany. The measure will be phased in by 15 October 2026 and is justified by the link between excessive alcohol consumption, violence and incidents involving staff and passengers.

The German rail operator Deutsche Bahn – DB has announced that it will ban the consumption of alcohol at all of the approximately 5,400 stations it manages nationwide.

The new rule will be phased in and is set to come into force across the entire network by 15 October 2026 .

“We are taking firm action: we are banning alcohol consumption at our stations. We have seen all too often that where too much alcohol is consumed, violence also increases,” said Evelyn Palla, CEO of Deutsche Bahn.

The decision follows a violent attack last Friday, which the company says has once again demonstrated the link between alcohol and assaults on railway premises.

Deutsche Bahn will introduce the measure under its right to set rules on access and behaviour in the premises it manages.

Over the coming weeks, local station regulations will be amended in collaboration with the authorities and local councils.

Around 30 stations have already been designated as alcohol-free zones, including those in Cologne, Munich and Hamburg.

From 1 September , the ban will also be introduced at the following stations:

The remaining stations will follow in stages until mid-October.

“The experience at stations where the rule already applies is clear: no alcohol means less violence and less litter,” said Evelyn Palla.

The ban applies to the consumption of alcohol in the public areas of stations, but not to the operations of restaurants, bars or other catering establishments.

Passengers will still be able to carry alcohol in their luggage or shopping, provided that the containers remain sealed .

Consequently, the measure does not prohibit the purchase or transport of alcoholic drinks, but only their consumption in areas of the station managed by Deutsche Bahn.

Anyone caught consuming alcohol will initially be asked to leave the station.

In the event of a repeat offence, Deutsche Bahn may impose a ban on entry to its premises.

The company has not announced any fines of its own, but enforcement of the measure will be the responsibility of security staff and employees responsible for ensuring compliance with station regulations.

Deutsche Bahn states that the new rule is primarily intended to protect staff and passengers, at a time when incidents of aggression on public transport have become an increasingly prominent issue in Germany.

SNCF Connect (anciennement OUI.sncf) est un service en ligne décliné en application pour smartphone et tablette permettant la réservation de billets de train, de bus et l’achat de tickets pour la RATP (Pass navigo, Ticket T+, etc.). SNCF Connect vous permet de rechercher, réserver, payer et organiser tous vos trajets en train et bus sur les lignes françaises et européennes. Vous pourrez réserver, avec ou sans compte SNCF et payer vos billets en ligne, ce qui vous évitera de vous rendre en gare pour les acheter au guichet. C’est un gain de temps et d’énergie pour les utilisateurs.

Via l’interface de l’application, entrez simplement votre gare de départ et votre gare d’arrivée, la date et l’heure souhaitée. Vous pourrez également choisir la catégorie (en fonction de votre âge), la classe et le nombre de voyageurs. Ensuite, choisissez l’horaire et le tarif qui vous conviennent. En effet, les tarifs peuvent varier en fonction des horaires (les heures d’affluence sont souvent plus chères). Procédez au paiement par carte bancaire, Visa ou Mastercard. Les paiements en ligne sont sécurisés par chiffrement, ce qui garantit la protection de vos données personnelles.

Ensuite, vous recevrez immédiatement votre billet par mail. Vous pourrez choisir de l’imprimer ou de le retirer en gare dans les machines de couleur jaune ou directement au guichet. Avec l’application, il sera directement enregistré dans l’onglet « mes voyages » et le contrôleur n’aura qu’à scanner l’écran de votre smartphone. Via l’application SNCF Connect, les informations sur votre voyage sont mises à jour instantanément. Ainsi, vous êtes informés en temps réel des retards ou des actualités sur votre ligne.

SNCF Connect pense aussi au reste de votre voyage et propose un système de navigation GPS qui vous permet de vous déplacer avec les transports en commun de la ville que vous visitez. Un système d’info trafic en temps réel vous permet de vérifier s’il y a des retards ou perturbations sur les lignes que vous devez emprunter.

Vous pouvez télécharger SNCF Connect pour votre smartphone ou tablette sous Android ou iOS.

evidence.title: SNCF: Kombo allows booking for MICE groups
evidence.text:
Kombo continues to develop its rail-related services by enabling the booking of SNCF train tickets for groups of 10 to 60 people. The booking platform for train, bus, or plane travel has set up the address kombo.co/fr/groups for this purpose, providing access to the national rail company's inventory and fares. Kombo targets associations, local authorities, sports teams, individuals for weddings or holidays, as well as companies for seminars, meetings, or incentives.

The company or business agency making the booking simply needs to log in to its Kombo account to search for routes and timetables, specifying the number of passengers for the desired journey. The system displays preferential group rates based on age groups: children (-60% for 4–11-year-olds), young people (-30% for 12–27-year-olds) and adults (from -10%). Payment can be made on the platform using the credit or debit card(s) registered to the Kombo account.

Kombo promises simple and flexible booking.

With a focus on convenience, the website also highlights the fact that users can lock in ticket prices until the group’s final confirmation, enter just one person’s name to make the booking, change or add travellers’ names at any time, as well as automatically receiving the invoice and cancelling the booking if necessary. Cancellation is therefore possible up to 46 days before the trip, with a 50% retention fee between 45 and 12 days prior to departure; tickets become non-changeable from 11 days before departure.

" Where the old method multiplied steps and intermediaries, Kombo's tool makes the organiser independent, from quote to tickets. Organising a group train journey should be as simple as booking for yourself. It was one of the last major pain points for train travel, and we wanted to fix it our way. ”, explains Matthieu Marquenet, co-founder of Kombo, in a statement.

SNCF retains control above 60 passengers

With its new group booking tool, Kombo highlights the lack of ergonomics and ease of use of the SNCF's. The rail company still has the advantage in managing large group travel, allowing for the privatisation of one or more first or second-class carriages. Or even an entire TGV if the group exceeds 250 people and depending on the client's budget. The company or agency will then have to make its booking between 3 and 8 months before the journey to allow for the train to be slotted into daily traffic.

Additionally, the SNCF enables the addition of specific services such as meal service on board (from 3 hours of TGV travel), decorating the platform with the event or company's colours, the presence of dedicated onboard staff, baggage handling, and even the provision of one or more coaches at the destination to ensure passenger transfers. In response to companies' ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) requirements, the SNCF also highlights the highly advantageous carbon footprint of undertaking MICE travel by train, particularly when compared to other modes of transport such as air travel.

evidence.title: SNCF strike on June 10, 2026: Disruptions to RER and Transilien services and train cancellations announced
evidence.text:
SNCF strike on June 10, 2026: Disruptions to RER and Transilien services and train cancellations announced

A national SNCF strike is planned for tomorrow Wednesday, June 10, 2026 . For the first time since late 2024, the four major rail unions—the CGT Cheminots , Unsa Ferroviaire , Sud Rail , and the CFDT Cheminots —have filed a joint 24-hour strike notice. In Île-de-France, passengers on the Transilien lines, the RER networks operated by SNCF, and the TGV services to and from Paris will be the most affected. For a full update on disruptions this week, read our article on transport in Paris and Île-de-France from June 8 to 14, 2026 .

Unions are blasting several files at once. At the forefront: internal reorganizations and the group’s subsidiarization, which involves creating local companies to bid on regional rail networks. A portion of the staff is transferred with a "social backpack" guaranteeing their benefits for 15 months. But for Fabien Villedieu of Sud Rail , this device is really only a "social handbag": after 15 months, the agreements lapse and conditions vary widely from one territory to another.

Unions are also pressing for fresh pay rises, arguing that the 2026 increases do not keep pace with inflation. They also flag worsening working conditions: workplace accidents rose by 20% last year, and thirteen staff suicides have been recorded so far this year, an unprecedented trend according to union representatives.

This movement marks Jean Castex's first major social test as he takes the helm at SNCF, named chief executive in November 2025. On arriving, he pledged to preside over a "unified group." The unions are holding him to his word: they demand that the railway workers in the newly formed subsidiaries enjoy the same rights as those in the public group, a claim championed notably by the CGT Cheminots and the Unsa Ferroviaire .

The management, for its part, touts a "constructive social dialogue" and notes that it has signed numerous agreements in recent months. It also points out that SNCF posted a net profit of 1.8 billion euros in 2025 and that none of its 150,000 staff earns less than the minimum wage after a 10% raise. A €1,450 bonus has also been guaranteed for all SNCF group rail workers.

The SNCF has already released its traffic forecast. On the TGV Inoui, Ouigo and TGV Lyria services, the company says that about two-thirds of trains will be in operation . It notes that any passenger whose train is canceled will be contacted again and can opt for a refund or a rebooking. For those who keep their journey, SNCF adds that “thanks to the remaining seats, all customers should be able to travel the same day.”

Intercités services will also be hit hard, with roughly one in two trains running, by day and by night. Affected travelers will enjoy the same terms: a full refund or a free exchange in case of cancellation.

Transilien SNCF Voyageurs has released its detailed outlook for tomorrow. Traffic will be severely disrupted on most RER and Transilien lines . Here’s what to expect:

Good news for Île-de-France residents seeking an alternative: the metro , the buses and the trams are not affected by this labor action. Traffic on all of these lines is expected to be normal or near-normal throughout the day. So this is the moment to prioritise these modes if your journey allows. Cycling and walking remain solid options for short trips, especially within Paris proper.

Transilien and Île-de-France Mobilités are also asking travelers who can to shift their train travel outside peak hours , or to work remotely if their job allows.

Detailed train-by-train forecasts are now available on SNCF Connect as of 5 p.m. this evening. If your train is cancelled, you have been or will be notified by email or SMS. All affected tickets, including promotional fares typically non‑refundable, can be fully refunded or exchanged for another train.

To receive this refund, you should contact 36 35 or head to the station before your originally scheduled departure. The refund is credited to the bank card linked to your account within three to five days. If you paid with Chèques-Vacances, the refund is automatically issued as a digital voucher, as noted by SNCF Voyageurs on its site .

Travelers are advised to check real-time traffic conditions directly on SNCF Connect or through the mobility app of their choice before departure, and to have alternative options ready if their trip is essential for tomorrow, Wednesday.

evidence.title: Arnaques à la carte Avantage SNCF : les autorités cyber françaises lancent l'alerte
evidence.text:
Arnaques à la carte Avantage SNCF : les autorités cyber françaises lancent l'alerte

Des escrocs usurpent en ce moment l'identité de SNCF Connect pour piéger les voyageurs. Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr alerte sur la recrudescence de ces arnaques à la carte Avantage, qui font des victimes.

2,45 euros pour une carte Avantage SNCF normalement facturée 49 euros l'année ? Sur le papier, c'est l'affaire du siècle. Ces réductions dingues, ou politiques de prix cassés comme vous voudrez, ne sont évidemment pas réelles. Il s'agit d'un piège tendu par des escrocs qui diffusent leurs fausses offres ces derniers jours par e-mail, SMS et sur les réseaux sociaux, avec pour seul objectif de mettre la main sur les données personnelles et bancaires de voyageurs séduits. Via le 17Cyber , Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr lance l'alerte.

Des escrocs copient SNCF Connect pour vendre une carte Avantage qui n'existe pas

L'arnaque à la carte Avantage SNCF est d'autant plus dangereuse qu'elle est réaliste. Les escrocs ont reproduit à l'identique les logos, les couleurs et les visuels officiels de SNCF Connect. Les faux e-mails, SMS et sites web sont à l'œil nu impossibles à distinguer des vrais. Autrement dit, même un œil exercé peut s'y laisser prendre.

Les arnaqueurs utilisent, comme toujours, ce qu'on peut appeler l'urgence artificielle. Avec des formules du type « Offre limitée », « dernières cartes disponibles », « vente flash exceptionnelle », on a le sentiment de découvrir de vraies promotions commerciales, et c'est voulu. L'idée est de faire agir vite la potentielle victime, avant que le bon sens ne reprenne le dessus.

Une fois attiré par l'offre, l'utilisateur atterrit sur un faux site et y entre ses coordonnées bancaires en croyant payer sa carte Avantage. Sauf que la carte n'arrivera jamais. Mais ses données personnelles et/ou bancaires, elles, sont déjà entre les mains des cybercriminels, leur objectif de départ.

Les bons réflexes pour ne pas tomber dans le piège

Pour ne pas se faire avoir, le réflexe de base, et peut-être le plus efficace, reste d'acheter uniquement sur des sites et applications officiels. Pour la carte Avantage SNCF, une seule adresse valide, il n'y a qu'une seule adresse valide, SNCF Connect . Si un lien vous arrive par SMS ou e-mail sans que vous l'ayez demandé, ignorez-le, même s'il a l'air parfaitement légitime. Inutile de prendre le risque.

Deux vérifications rapides peuvent aussi aider à se protéger. Il faut toujours regarder l'adresse e-mail de l'expéditeur, car les escrocs imitent les adresses officielles, mais avec de légères différences, comme une lettre en trop, un tiret déplacé, un domaine légèrement modifié. Même chose pour l'adresse du site dans le navigateur avant d'y entrer la moindre information. Quelques secondes suffisent à écarter la danger.

Et si vous êtes déjà tombé dans le piège, alors rendez-vous sur 17cyber.gouv.fr , le site officiel de l'État dédié aux victimes d'arnaques en ligne, pour signaler les faits et obtenir de l'aide. Pour les autres, le mot d'ordre de Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr est simple : « au moindre doute, abstenez-vous ».

evidence.title: SNCF and CFF renew their partnership until 2032
evidence.text:
SNCF Voyageurs has just renewed its partnership agreement with CFF, the Swiss railways, until 2032, to develop rail links between Switzerland, France and neighbouring European countries. The honeymoon between the two carriers has been going on for 45 years, notably within TGV Lyria, which is the subject of a commercial agreement until 2027, a cooperation that will be strengthened with the aim of developing traffic. " In order to meet the growing demand for international mobility, SNCF Voyageurs and CFF will study opportunities to develop European links from Switzerland. Extensions and the introduction of new direct long-distance rail services from Switzerland to France and beyond will be studied. "say the two groups in a joint press release.

This could lead to the launch of European services in the near future? " Offering new services and new destinations has always been at the heart of our partnership and the SNCF Group's strategy. "This is what Jean Castex, CEO of the SNCF group, said at the signing ceremony. It should be noted that a group of users is campaigning for the introduction of a fourth return trip per day between Paris and Lausanne via the Jura. Following an initial working meeting at the Senate on 3 February, the SNCF is due to give its opinion on the economic and operational feasibility of this additional service in April.

The renewal and deepening of this partnership is all the more important for SNCF and SBB as new rail operators are likely to launch on the major Paris-Geneva route. Trenitalia once had this project, but the French subsidiary of the Italian group FS has since refocused on launching a Paris-London link by the end of the decade.

To prepare for this future competition, TGV Lyria has undertaken to improve its service offering, which has become more personalised through its new Standard, Première and Première Signature classes. Aimed more specifically at business customers, the new classes include access to the TGV INOUI Grand Voyageur lounge at Paris-Gare de Lyon, express boarding and a meal served at the seat by the chef duo Michel Roth and Danny Khezzar.

In 2025, with 17 daily return trips, TGV Lyria carried 5.7 million passengers on its three lines: Paris-Geneva (in 3h11), Paris-Lausanne (in 3h41) and Paris-Basel-Zürich (in 4h04). However, until the end of 2026, TGVs to Lausanne via Geneva will depart from or terminate in Geneva due to work being carried out on the Swiss rail network between the two cities. The number of direct TGVs to Lausanne was reduced in February and March, also as a result of work to modernise the line around Dijon. The Lausanne-Geneva-Marseille summer service, which was discontinued in October last year, will be extended this season from 16 April to 2 November. A fourth daily France-Switzerland route will be offered from Thursday to Monday before being operated every day in July and August.

After six years as Director of TGV-Intercités, Alain Krakovitch is handing over the reins, leaving to take up the position of Director of Equipment at SNCF. He will be replaced from mid-May by Karine Dussert-Sarthe, who previously headed Orange's Ile-de-France branch. This recruitment from outside the rail company reflects the increased competitive pressure on its SNCF Passenger branch. " Karine Dussert-Sarthe will bring her fresh vision and strong expertise in marketing, customer experience and innovation, with the ambition of helping SNCF Voyageurs' high-speed services win in increasingly competitive French and European markets. "says the company on the occasion of his appointment. " I'm counting on his fresh outlook, his experience of customers and the competition, his sense of service to the French territories and his ease on the international stage. "says Christophe Fanichet, CEO of SNCF Voyageurs.

evidence.title: Air France broadens 30-year commercial relationship with SNCF French railways
evidence.text:
Air France broadens 30-year commercial relationship with SNCF French railways

In 2025, Air France and the loyalty program of French railway operator SNCF (Société Nationale des Chemins de Fer Français), known as ‘SNCF Voyageurs’ are celebrating the 30th anniversary of their commercial partnership and will broaden their activities under that agreement. The companies first joined forces in 1995 to facilitate access to airports by train and encourage the use of low-carbon transport solutions where possible to reduce carbon emissions through travel.

For the past 30 years, Air France and SNCF Voyageurs have been working together to offer ‘Train+Air’ combined travel services. This service has been considerably extended in recent years and is now available on 41 routes to and from Paris-Charles de Gaulle and Paris-Orly airports, compared with just 28 in 2022.

The result of the ‘Train+Air’ travel program means that 22 train stations throughout France are directly linked to Paris’ airports of Orly (ORY) and Charles De Gaulle (CDG), with a fully digital service that allows passengers to combine train journeys and flights in a single booking and the guarantee, in the event of irregularity, of assistance and a seat on the next flight or train at no additional cost.

Since 2019, more than 600,000 bookings have been made via the ‘Train+Air’ service by Air France customers, a fact that “underlines the growing interest of travelers in combined journeys and customers’ desire to reduce their travel footprint whenever they can,” says Air France. In 2024, the most popular routes on the Train+Air network were Lyon, Lille, and Strasbourg, with customers then connecting to flights mainly to North America and the West Indies.

Additionally, in May 2023, France became something of a trailblazer among countries trying to reduce carbon emissions across their transportation systems. The French Government formally introduced a ban on direct domestic flights that could reasonably and easily be replaced by a train journey lasting no more than 150 minutes, or 2.5 hours. However, while the ban all but ruled out air travel between Paris and several major French cities including Nantes, Lyon, and Bordeaux, connecting flights were unaffected by the new rule.

Now, following an announcement by Air France on February 10, 2025, the two companies will be strengthening their ties in this anniversary year. Effective immediately, members of Air France’s Flying Blue loyalty program will be able to convert their accrued points into electronic SNCF Voyageurs vouchers that can be redeemed for travel on SNCF’s TGV INOUI high-speed-rail network. This is done by members accessing their accounts via the Flying Blue online store.

These vouchers, for an amount of the customer’s choice (between €25 and €100, or $26 to $103), can be used across the entire TGV INOUI network for bookings made via SNCF Voyageurs-approved ticket offices that accept them and SNCF Voyageurs direct sales channels.

Flying Blue, the Air France-KLM loyalty program, allows customers to earn Miles when traveling with Air France, KLM, or Transavia, or when making purchases from affiliated partner stores. These miles can be used to purchase air tickets (award tickets), to contribute to the development of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), to make donations to charities, and now to buy SNCF Voyageurs travel vouchers.

As part of the nation’s efforts to reduce its carbon emissions through travel, Air France says it remains “fully committed to reducing its carbon footprint.” By modernizing its fleet, increasing the integration of sustainable aviation fuel, and leveraging eco-piloting practices, the airline aims to cut CO₂ emissions per passenger-kilometre by 30% by 2030, compared to 2019. As part of the emission reduction program, the carrier offers its customers more environmentally friendly travel solutions, including intermodal options in conjunction with the SNCF through the Train+Air program.

According to an Air France statement, “Air France and SNCF Voyageurs are determined to continue to improve intermodality between train and air travel and are continuing their efforts to make their offers more complementary and their customers’ journeys smoother.”

evidence.title: Alstom to overhaul 235 Panama Metro cars under a US$90m contract
evidence.text:
Railway Supply » Passenger Rail News » Alstom to overhaul 235 Panama Metro cars under a US$90m contract

Alstom to overhaul 235 Panama Metro cars under a US$90m contract

Alstom has signed a US$90 million Panama Metro maintenance contract to overhaul the 235 Metropolis cars on Lines 1 and 2, with work at intervals of up to 12 years.

The customer is the operator, Metro de Panamá S.A. (MPSA). Alstom announced the signing on 24 September 2026 and puts the value at about €80 million. It describes the scope as major maintenance and long-term overhaul of the fleet.

Work is scheduled at intervals of five, six, eight, ten and twelve years. It covers bogies, traction equipment, brakes, wheels, pneumatic systems, auxiliary equipment and other parts on which safe operation depends. Alstom says the aim is to keep the fleet reliable and available and to lengthen the working life of the trains.

The contract applies to the Metropolis fleet that Alstom built for the two lines: 47 trains, of which 26 serve Line 1 and 21 serve Line 2. Alstom’s figures put Line 1’s fleet at 26 five-car trains , which accounts for 130 of the 235 cars; the remaining 105 are on Line 2. Line 1 has carried passengers since April 2014.

Alstom has not said how long the agreement runs, when the first overhauls begin or how the work will fit around passenger service.

How it differs from the line maintenance contracts

Alstom’s other documented maintenance contracts on the network were arranged line by line and covered more than the trains. In December 2024 the company signed a four-year contract with MPSA for preventive and corrective maintenance of Line 1’s rolling stock, signalling and power supply.

For Line 2, Panama’s Cabinet approved on 31 March 2026 a six-month contract, plus two months for close-out, covering preventive, corrective, predictive and cosmetic maintenance of the Metropolis trains, the CBTC signalling and the traction and auxiliary substations. It was worth up to B/.4,329,872.89 and awarded through an exceptional procedure. The new contract deals only with the trains, but on both lines.

The September 2026 contract is the only one in this list that spans both lines, and it is limited to the trains. Dates are Alstom announcement dates, except for March 2026, which is the date of Cabinet approval. The list covers contracts documented by Alstom and Panama’s Cabinet only.

Sources: Alstom, November 2022 , Alstom, December 2024 , Gaceta Oficial No. 30504-C , Alstom, September 2026 .

Ridership and Alstom’s presence in Panama

According to Alstom, the Panama Metro carries about 400,000 passengers a day. The company has worked in Panama since 2010, built the integrated rail systems of both lines, has maintained Line 1 since 2014 and Line 2 since April 2019, and employs about 150 people in the country.

Nicolas Forissier, France’s Minister Delegate for Foreign Trade and Economic Attractiveness, attended the signing.

evidence.title: Alstom and Talgo cleared to bid in Portugal’s €504m high-speed train tender
evidence.text:
Railway Supply » UK & European Rail News » Alstom and Talgo cleared to bid in Portugal’s €504m high-speed train tender

Alstom and Talgo cleared to bid in Portugal’s €504m high-speed train tender

Alstom and Talgo, the only two applicants, have both cleared prequalification in the CP high-speed train tender for 12 trains with a €504 million base price.

Comboios de Portugal (CP) said on 22 September that its selection panel had examined both applications and admitted Alstom, which applied through ALSTOM Ferroviária Portugal, S.A. and ALSTOM Ferroviaria S.p.A., as well as Patentes Talgo, S.L. The state-owned operator will now ask the two manufacturers to submit their bids for the rolling stock.

The base price pays for 12 high-speed multiple units with their spare parts and special tools. It also covers full maintenance by the winning supplier for two years after CP receives the first train, and CP keeps an option to buy eight more units. The government’s announcement of the tender launch adds that the contract includes training for the staff who will later maintain the fleet.

The €504 million is not the whole budget. On 22 January, the Council of Ministers authorised CP to buy up to 20 units , the 12 plus the eight-unit option, within an investment of €584 million. That figure includes €45 million for workshops and equipment to keep the new trains running.

Each train must offer more than 500 seats, be adapted for passengers with reduced mobility and have room for bicycles. Wi-Fi, USB-C sockets and video surveillance are also required on board.

Deliveries planned around the Lisbon–Porto line

Bids now have to be submitted and evaluated before an award decision. Under CP’s timetable, the contract should be signed in the first quarter of 2027, with the first train handed over in the first quarter of 2031. The government has said the remaining units will then arrive at a rate of one a month, with the last delivered in the third quarter of 2032.

Infrastructure and Housing Minister Miguel Pinto Luz said Infraestruturas de Portugal would finish the Lisbon–Porto high-speed infrastructure in 2032. He added that the trains should reach Portugal by the time the line is ready, although the political crisis that forced elections in 2025 held back the purchase by a year before CP opened the tender in May . The government expects the new fleet to link the two cities in 1 hour 15 minutes, which it equates to about 300 km/h.

The fleet will run on the Iberian gauge. However, the trains must be ready for conversion to the European standard gauge, which would only require new wheelsets.

Four years separate the planned contract signature from the first delivery. The government’s schedule gives the third quarter of 2032 as the end of deliveries but does not say whether that date covers only the 12 firm units or also the eight optional ones. Sources: Government of Portugal (January) , Government of Portugal (May) , CP .

CP describes its current rolling-stock programme as the largest investment in its history. Besides the high-speed units, it has a contract with Alstom for 153 urban and regional trains, with deliveries due to begin in 2029. Meanwhile, 22 regional units ordered from Stadler have started arriving in Portugal and are going through type approval and certification.

CP chairman Pedro Moreira said the tender brings the company closer to operating high-speed services. He also linked the renewal of the fleet to a strong increase in demand for rail travel.

Renfe’s tender covers more than twice as many trains, built for a higher speed and the standard gauge, while CP asks for more seats per train. The two values cover different scopes, so they should not be divided into a price per train. Sources: CP , Government of Portugal , Spain’s Ministry of Transport and Sustainable Mobility .
