evidence.title: Alstom, Stadler provide more information on VIA equipment orders
evidence.text:
Alstom, Stadler provide more information on VIA equipment orders

BERLIN - VIA Rail Canada made news this summer with orders for 45 hybrid diesel-battery locomotives from Swiss-based Stadler, and 313 passenger cars from Alstom, to renew its long-distance, regional, and remote services. Both manufacturers discussed the orders with Trains this week at the InnoTrans trade fair.

Among key points raised in those conversations: Alstom said it will not bid on Amtrak's long-distance fleet procurement because the VIA order, along with other contracts in hand, will require its available manufacturing capacity.

Michael Keroullé, president of Alstom's Americas region, has divided his time between offices in the U.S. and Quebec since Alstom acquired Bombardier Transportation in 2021. In an interview with Trains , he confirms the 313-car VIA order will take about a decade to complete.

Detailed engineering design is underway at Alstom's St-Bruno-de-Montarville, Québec, facility. Construction of the aluminum car bodies will begin about 2029 using robotic laser welding techniques at the former Bombardier plant at La Pocatière, Quebec, a plant that Keroullé describes as "one of the most automated factories in the Alstom group." Current plans will see the pilot car ready for testing in 2029. During series production, planned for 2030-35, completed car bodies will be shipped by rail from La Pocatière to Thunder Bay, Ontario, where they will be fitted out with internal equipment and tested. Alstom says coaches, the most numerous car type in the order, are likely to be built first, as the more specialized cars, such as the panorama, sleeper, and dining cars, will be made in smaller quantities.

Asked whether construction of a 21st-century version of a dome car poses major engineering challenges, Keroullé says that the fact dome cars already exist makes building new ones easier, as approval regimes for new concepts are always more challenging. He adds that because they will be used on routes that routinely see double-stack container trains, there are no clearance issues. Alstom is confident the new dome cars will have the level of structural integrity required, but admits the number of different car types in the order brings both design and manufacturing challenges.

Alstom describes the new fleet as part of its Adessia family of trains. Like many large manufacturers, Alstom has generic names for the various types of trains it sells, although the Adessia name covers a very wide spectrum. It includes new commuter EMUs sold in Europe (a mock-up of one is featured at Alstom's display area at InnoTrans); bi-level cars for U.S. commuter railroads; and the fleet of long-distance DMUs, some of which incorporate sleeper cars, built in Mexico for Mexican operator Tren Maya. The company says the Adessia cars share a "common architecture" with modular design elements, even if they are very different car types.

Keroullé says that the tender for the new VIA Rail fleet did not specify local content requirements. Since the company was awarded preferred-bidder status in spring 2026, an ongoing "open book" dialogue with VIA has established that by making around 40% of the contract value local, with work undertaken in Canada or by Canadian companies, the order will generate an economic return worth twice its cost, in terms of jobs created and tax revenues to the Canadian government. Alstom will use factories outside Canada for some of the work - costs in its Mexican factories are a third of those in Canada. Reflecting the current uncertainty around tariffs, nothing planned for the new fleet will be imported from the U.S.

Alstom says that VIA Rail will undertake the necessary testing and integration of the new cars with its existing and new locomotive fleet.

Having won VIA's long-distance contract, Alstom might be expected to pursue a similar but even bigger contract to renew Amtrak's long-distance fleet. However, Keroullé says Alstom will not be participating in Amtrak's tender process because the company does not have the capacity to handle that fleet (projected at more than 800 cars) alongside its existing order book. New cars for commuter operators Metra, NJ Transit, and New York's Metropolitan Transportation Authority will fill its U.S. factories in the coming years.

Much of the work for Stadler's VIA locomotive order will take place at the manufacturer's factory in Valencia, Spain, and conversations with the Valencia design team at InnoTrans make the background for that 45-locomotive order clear.

Stadler's Valencia site historically worked with EMD in its previous independent life and subsequent ownership by German-based Vossloh. It was Vossloh España that undertook the design work and produced body shells and wheelsets for the EMD F125 locomotives introduced for Southern California's Metrolink beginning in 2017. Stadler bought the company in 2016, and the design work for the F125 has formed the basis for the design of the new VIA locomotives. More recent experience building diesel locomotives incorporating battery power for European operators has also contributed to the design.

VIA sought lower emissions and the ability to operate without diesel power in certain situations. Stadler will use a Caterpillar C175 engine producing around 2,700 kilowatts (3,620 hp), but in combination with the batteries, around 4 megawatts (5,365 hp) will be available as a peak output, such as when starting from a stop.

Head-end power for the passenger cars will come from either the diesel engine or the batteries; this will be determined either automatically by the locomotive software, or specified by the engineer, depending on the situation. The locomotives are designed to work in a temperature range from 45 degrees to minus-50 degrees Celsius (113 to minus-58 Fahrenheit), and will incorporate steel body shells and a 6,500-liter (1,718-gallon) fuel tank.

Final design work is underway. VIA will sign off on a final design in early 2027, locking in that design and allowing construction of the prototype. The first units will be built in Spain; localization of assembly for the remaining units is currently under discussion.

Plans call for the first locomotive to be delivered by the end of 2027 to allow three to four months of winter testing to ensure its operability in Canadian winter conditions. Production of the remaining units will then begin in 2028. Further plans call for one locomotive to be tested in a climatic testing chamber in Europe or North America, with dynamic testing of a unit at Pueblo, Colo., in 2028-29.

evidence.title: Alstom and Italo celebrate the strength of their innovative partnership at InnoTrans
evidence.text:
Alstom and Italo celebrate the strength of their innovative partnership at InnoTrans

Alstom and Italo celebrate the strength of their innovative partnership at InnoTrans

23 September 2026 – Alstom, global leader in smart and sustainable mobility, and Italo, Italy’s first private high-speed rail operator, today unveiled the next chapter of a collaboration that has been driving the evolution of Italian high-speed rail for nearly twenty years, during InnoTrans 2026.

During a talk hosted at the Alstom stand, Gianbattista La Rocca, CEO of Italo, and Michele Viale, Managing Director of Alstom Italy, spoke of the 12 new Avelia Stream high-speed trains currently under construction for Italy at Alstom’s facilities in Savigliano, Sesto San Giovanni and Bologna.

"The strength of partnership with Alstom and Italo lies in the trust we have built over time and in our ability to evolve together. It is founded on shared responsibility and a common determination to turn every new challenge into an opportunity for progress and innovation."

The collaboration between Alstom and Italo began in 2008, when Italo selected Alstom as its industrial and technology partner for the supply and maintenance of the fleet that would launch Italy’s first private high-speed rail operator. Since then, the relationship has evolved alongside Italo’s growth, becoming a long-term industrial partnership that has contributed both to the operator’s expansion and to Italy’s emergence as one of Europe’s most competitive high-speed rail markets.

Over time, the partnership has expanded well beyond the supply of rolling stock. Today, Alstom acts as the Entity in Charge of Maintenance (ECM) for Italo’s entire fleet, delivering a fully integrated, 360-degree model that encompasses maintenance, fleet management, technical support, modernization programs and digital innovation throughout the trains’ lifecycle.

Every day, more than 220 Alstom professionals work across maintenance depots to ensure fleet availability, reliability and service continuity. At the heart of this ecosystem is the Nola Digital Depot, where 24/7 operational control rooms, real-time data and digital solutions such as HealthHub, TrainScanner and TrainTracer leverage advanced algorithms and AI-powered analytics to anticipate potential issues, optimize maintenance planning and maximize fleet availability. Innovative technologies, including the 3D printing of selected components, also help improve spare parts availability and accelerate maintenance interventions.

The partnership also extends to enhancing the passenger experience through Nomad Digital, an Alstom Group company that supports Italo in the development of next-generation connectivity solutions and digital services. Among these is the pioneering deployment of a hybrid connectivity platform integrating 5G networks and Starlink satellite technology, providing passengers with a more reliable and higher-performing internet connection, even along the most challenging routes.

“The strength of partnership with Alstom and Italo lies in the trust we have built over time and in our ability to evolve together. It is founded on shared responsibility and a common determination to turn every new challenge into an opportunity for progress and innovation. Behind every milestone of this journey are our people, whose expertise, passion, and commitment help turn vision into reality and shape the future of high-speed rail.” said Michele Viale, Managing Director of Alstom Italy.

“In 2008, we chose Alstom to embark on this unique journey. Thanks to the launch of Italo, Italy became the first European country to introduce competition to the high-speed rail sector, setting an example for others to follow. With Alstom, we share a forward-looking vision of shared and sustainable mobility. Our goal is to continuously innovate to provide passengers with safety, reliability, and comfort. We started with 25 AGV trains and chose Alstom once again when we invested in 26 EVO trains. Most recently, we placed an order for 12 additional Alstom Avelia Stream trains tailored for the Italian market. These will begin service at the end of next year, bringing our total fleet to 63 trains.” said Gianbattista La Rocca, CEO of Italo.

Built in Italy and developed on the foundation of Alstom’s more than 40 years of high-speed rail expertise—supported by over 2,900 high-speed trains delivered worldwide—Avelia Stream trains reaffirm the central role of Italian railway expertise in the development of the Group’s high-speed solutions. The new train will be officially unveiled in the coming months at Alstom’s Savigliano facility, in the province of Cuneo.

ALSTOM™, Avelia Stream™, HealthHub™, TrainScanner™ and TrainTracer™ are protected trademarks of the Alstom Group.

Alstom and SAR boost existing Collaboration to strengthen Freight Rail Performance

Alstom, a global leader in smart and sustainable mobility, has signed a €22 million, five-year contract with Saudi Arabia Railways (SAR) to support the reliability and day-to-day performance of its North Freight fleet operating along the Kingdom’s North–South corridor.

Industry sources added that the North–South corridor is a key rail link for Saudi Arabia, carrying approximately 13.5 million tons of freight annually on the northern line. The corridor connects mining sites to processing facilities and export points, playing a central role in supporting the Kingdom’s industrial and logistics activities.

To help maintain reliable freight operations across the North-South corridor, Alstom will provide FlexCare Perform maintenance services to support for the critical onboard systems installed on SAR’s locomotive fleet. These systems are essential for daily operations, monitoring train performance, managing speed, and enabling communication with signalling infrastructure to ensure safe, efficient and reliable movement of freight across the network.

Alstom will also introduce a more proactive maintenance approach, combining real-time monitoring with enhanced spare parts availability to improve fleet readiness and reduce response times. The scope also includes system upgrades, maintenance documentation, digital tools, and targeted workforce training. Together, these measures will support more efficient day-to-day maintenance, strengthen operational performance and support the long-term reliability of SAR’s freight services.

“Our partnership with SAR is built on a shared ambition to strengthen rail performance and support the Kingdom’s long-term transport objectives,” said Mohamed Khalil, Managing Director Middle East. “Through this collaboration, we are enhancing reliability, supporting local talent development, and creating long-term value for Saudi Arabia’s freight sector.”

Beyond operations, the initiative will contribute to developing local capabilities. Training and knowledge transfer will support Saudi engineers, technicians, and operators, enabling the progressive localisation of technical expertise and reinforcing the Kingdom’s rail ecosystem.

By supporting a critical freight corridor and strengthening local expertise, this initiative contributes to Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 ambitions to build a more efficient, resilient, and competitive logistics sector .

Alstom is the market leader in rail services, supporting customers over the entire asset lifecycle with the broadest portfolio of services solutions. Alstom’s FlexCare Perform maintenance services are tailored to customer needs and operational requirements, from technical support with spares to fully outsourced maintenance solutions. Alstom maintains over 36,000 vehicles worldwide, including over 2,450 locomotives, and is a trusted partner for servicing both Alstom and non-Alstom rail assets.

Alstom continues to expand its local footprint in Saudi Arabia through long-term investment in people and capabilities. The company has established its Middle East regional headquarters in Riyadh, launched multiple local trainings and knowledge-transfer initiatives, and is actively supporting the development of local expertise in transport systems and mobility technologies.

Present in Saudi Arabia since 1951, Alstom remains a trusted partner in the Kingdom’s transport development journey. From the first gas turbine to today’s fully automated metro systems, the company continues to support the country’s goals for innovation, sustainability, and smart infrastructure.

ALSTOM™ and FlexCare Perform™ are protected trademarks of the Alstom Group.

evidence.title: Deutsche Bank's Retirement Cliff: Sewing Bets on AI as Bond Costs Climb
evidence.text:
Deutsche Bank is staring down a demographic shift that will reshape its German workforce within the decade. Roughly 35% of its employees in Germany will hit retirement age over the next eight to nine years — a gap CEO Christian Sewing has no intention of plugging primarily through fresh hiring. Instead, the Frankfurt lender is leaning on software and process automation, with management describing artificial intelligence as indispensable to navigating the generational handover.

That transition won't unfold gradually, according to the bank's leadership. Executives expect the rollout of modern systems across operations to move exponentially rather than step by step, with technology absorbing repetitive tasks and offsetting thinning administrative capacity.

Capital Structure Gets a Costlier Overhaul

While the bank lays long-term groundwork on efficiency, it is simultaneously reworking the regulatory capital stack — and paying up for the privilege. Newly issued securities carry a fixed coupon of 7.000% annually through April 30, 2034. Deutsche Bank says the move is designed to shore up its regulatory leverage ratio along with its Common Equity Tier 1 and total capital ratios.

The transaction swaps out two existing tranches, and the shift lays bare how much the rate environment has changed for Europe's large banks. For the same €1.25 billion in capital volume, the institution now services a markedly higher coupon. Even so, it locks in early recognition of the funds within regulatory core capital. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying Deutsche Bank?

Investment Banking Normalizes After a Strong Run

The operating backdrop is demanding discipline in other areas. In commercial real estate lending, the group has already trimmed high-risk exposures by 40% to 50% since the current cycle began.

Over in the investment banking division — a profit engine in recent quarters — a cooling-off is taking shape for the third quarter of 2026. Speaking at a Bank of America conference, CFO James von Moltke's colleague Akram indicated that segment revenues should hold steady or edge lower against a strong prior-year quarter. Trading activity ran hot in July, faded seasonally in August, and has been choppy through September. On loan loss provisions, the bank is guiding toward a figure for the current quarter that lands between the levels booked in the first and second quarters.

Crypto Custody on the Horizon, Legal Files Still Open

Operationally, Deutsche Bank is pushing ahead on digital assets. By the end of 2026, it plans to launch a custody service for digital assets in Europe, aimed at corporate and institutional clients — though the timeline remains subject to regulatory approval. Initial support is expected to cover Bitcoin and Ether, alongside stablecoins and e-money tokens including USDC, EURC and EURAU.

On the legal front, the bank is clearing old disputes even as new ones linger. About two weeks ago it reached an out-of-court settlement in a Frankfurt case involving original claims of $176 million, a step the company says will have only a minor impact on third-quarter results. In London, however, the situation remains tense: four additional former employees are still pursuing claims exceeding £600 million, according to Reuters.

Shares Drift as Investors Weigh Near-Term Drag Against Structural Bets

Market participants have turned cautious on the outlook. The stock changed hands at €31.30 in today's session, a modest daily decline of 0.8%, bringing the weekly loss to 7.9%. A separate reading put the shares at €31.59, up 0.1% — a reminder of how skittish sentiment has become around the name.

Investors are now balancing softer short-term momentum in trading against the structural efficiency potential on offer. How smoothly Deutsche Bank absorbs the retirement of more than a third of its German staff through automated processes is likely to determine the group's future operating cost base — and, by extension, how convincingly it can defend its margins in a higher-for-longer rate world.

evidence.title: Deutsche Bank Private Bank Launches Agentic AI Solution for Source of Wealth KYC Processes
evidence.text:
Deutsche Bank Private Bank Launches Agentic AI Solution for Source of Wealth KYC Processes

Deutsche Bank Private Bank today announced the rollout of an Agentic AI-enabled Source of Wealth (SoW) solution, a major step in its strategy to apply AI to complex banking processes while maintaining strong governance and controls.

The solution went live in Singapore and Hong Kong booking centres at the beginning of September, with a broader rollout across the Private Bank’s wealth management centres planned. It was also launched for the bank’s advisors in Dubai for accounts booked in Singapore.

Source of Wealth is a core element of the Know Your Customer (KYC) process and requires banks to establish and document how prospective clients accumulated their wealth. The new solution supports this process by automating research, documentation and the preparation of Source of Wealth data, drawing on information available within the client case and from approved external sources.

Yiping Li, Chief Operating Officer of Deutsche Bank Private Bank, said:

"This Agentic AI solution helps us make a complex process more efficient, consistent and scalable while maintaining robust controls and human oversight. As we continue to embed AI across our global operations, this initiative demonstrates how technology can address practical business challenges and improve client onboarding. We developed it with a clear principle in mind: while tasks can be automated, accountability remains with our people."

Integrated into the Bank’s digital KYC platform, the solution analyses information from client documentation and approved sources, helping identify gaps or inconsistencies and supporting the preparation of Source of Wealth assessments for human review. This reduces administrative effort, supports a smoother onboarding experience and allows relationship managers to spend more time advising clients.

Marco Pagliara, Head of Emerging Markets at Deutsche Bank Private Bank, said:

"This use case demonstrates how AI can support both strong controls and a better client experience. By reducing manual and repetitive tasks, we enable our relationship managers to focus more on advising clients while maintaining the high standards expected by clients and regulators. It is a practical example of how technology can improve productivity while strengthening the quality and consistency of our processes."

The solution is expected to support significantly higher client onboarding volumes while leveraging the existing operating model and control framework. Based on current forecasts, the bank’s Emerging Markets coverage region is on track to onboard approximately 30 per cent more clients in 2026 compared with 2025, and contributes towards the Singapore industry's ambition to achieve median onboarding timelines of one month or less, including more complex cases.

evidence.title: Deutsche Bank’s DWS U.S. REIT to be liquidated
evidence.text:
Deutsche Bank’s DWS U.S. REIT to be liquidated

RREEF Property Trust dealt with “heightened redemption activity”

Time is up for a real estate investment trust that dealt with heavy redemption requests and consistent outflows.

DWS, the asset manager under the Deutsche Bank umbrella, is shutting down RREEF Property Trust, Bloomberg reported . The real estate investment trust will be liquidated and have its assets sold; stockholders will receive net proceeds from those sales “when appropriate,” according to the company.

This comes on the heels of a big sell-off. In June, DWS sold a Jewel Osco-anchored shopping center in Chicago’s Wicker Park neighborhood to Houston-based Hines for $70 million. The property was originally purchased by RREEF in 2015 for $94 million as part of a larger transaction.

In July, RREEF sold the Domain WeHo apartment community in West Hollywood to CIM Group for an undisclosed price. RREEF bought the residences in 2019 for more than $103 million, The Real Deal reported at the time.

Stockholders will need to approve the winding down of the trust, which had a net asset value of $203 million as of the end of the second quarter. The trust’s investments included multifamily, retail and industrial properties.

In a statement, RREEF CEO Todd Henderson blamed the liquidation on two factors: a “period of heightened redemption activity” and difficulty landing fresh capital.

RREEF followed a similar net-asset value playbook carved by other big players, such as Blackstone and Starwood Capital Group. The trust allowed shares to be bought and redeemed based on the holdings’ value.

But fundraising for the REIT never approached the levels of its counterparts, dogged further by the interest rate hikes that began dragging commercial real estate in 2022. In the last 15 quarters, RREEF avoided net outflows in just one of them, according to Robert A. Stanger Company.

In today’s interest rate environment, other REITs have seen how redemption requests can spread and land a heavy blow.

In the spring, Starwood temporarily suspended redemptions at its $22 billion Starwood Real Estate Income Trust due to a surge in withdrawal requests, which chair Barry Sternlicht framed as a defensive move to avoid selling quality assets into a soft pricing environment.

To preserve cash, the firm cut SREIT’s annualized distribution rate for Class I shares from 6.3 percent to 4.7 percent, a liquidity squeeze that has effectively locked in most investors with more than $5,000.

evidence.title: Deutsche Bank to Launch Bitcoin and Ethereum Custody for Institutional Clients in Europe
evidence.text:
Deutsche Bank to Launch Bitcoin and Ethereum Custody for Institutional Clients in Europe

Deutsche Bank , one of Europe’s largest banks, announced plans to offer regulated digital asset custody services to institutional clients later in 2026.

JUST IN: 🇩🇪 €1.9 trillion Deutsche Bank announces it's launching Bitcoin custody services for institutional and corporate clients 💥 pic.twitter.com/zxUwPLSH17

— Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) September 16, 2026

The Frankfurt-based bank said the service will support bitcoin, ether, and select stablecoins including USDC, EURC, and EURAU. Clients will not need to build their own infrastructure. Deutsche Bank will manage wallets, private keys, and third-party transfers on their behalf.

The bank reported $2.217 trillion in assets under management as of June 30. It was founded in 1870, making it one of the oldest financial institutions to move into crypto custody.

The initial rollout will target Germany first. Clients will come from Deutsche Bank’s Corporate Bank and Investment Bank divisions, including asset managers, hedge funds, brokers, custodians, and sovereign institutions.

Gerald Podobnik, Co-Head of Corporate Bank at Deutsche Bank, said digital assets are not a replacement for the traditional financial system but a complement to it.

The custody service will use hardware-based key protection and separate warm and cold storage environments. It will also include multi-person approvals and backup and recovery controls.

External technology providers will handle some technical components. The bank has not named all of them publicly, though Taurus and Bitpanda have been previously linked to the project.

The asset list may grow over time. Any additions must pass client demand checks, product approvals, risk reviews, and regulatory requirements before being added.

Deutsche Bank’s interest in blockchain goes back to 2015. The bank joined the R3 distributed-ledger consortium in 2016 and had crypto custody on its internal agenda by late 2020.

In 2023, Deutsche Bank partnered with Swiss firm Taurus for custody infrastructure and applied for a German digital asset custody license that same year.

Its majority-owned subsidiary DWS also moved forward. Its Allunity venture secured a BaFin e-money license in July 2025 and launched EURAU, the euro-backed token now on Deutsche Bank’s custody list.

Tokenized financial instruments are also planned for a later stage, though no timeline has been given.

The service is not live yet. It still requires clearance under Europe’s Markets in Crypto-Assets framework, known as MiCA. Timing, geography, and supported assets could still change before launch.

Deutsche Bank is not the first major European bank to enter this space. Standard Chartered and BBVA already offer institutional crypto custody. Commerzbank received its BaFin crypto-custody license in 2023.

Still, Deutsche Bank’s scale puts this move in a different category. A bank with over $2 trillion in assets adding bitcoin and ether to its custody roster marks a concrete step in bringing crypto into mainstream institutional finance.

UniCredit's Takeover Efforts and Leadership Demands

FRANKFURT/MILAN, Sept 15 (Reuters) - UniCredit CEO Andrea Orcel wants Bettina Orlopp to leave her job as the CEO of Commerzbank and is opposed to the German government's demand to maintain two supervisory board seats, three people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters, as the Italian lender moves closer to taking over its German rival.

evidence.title: Germany seeks guarantees from Italy’s UniCredit over Commerzbank takeover
evidence.text:
Berlin is seeking guarantees about the future of Commerzbank as a takeover by Italy’s UniCredit looms

Frankfurt – Germany’s finance minister was due on Monday to meet the UniCredit CEO to seek guarantees over the future of Commerzbank, as the Italian lender gears up to complete a takeover of its German rival.

Lars Klingbeil would urge UniCredit boss Andrea Orcel to protect jobs in Germany and ensure Commerzbank remains a key lender to the country’s small- and medium-sized businesses, Berlin said.

Despite fierce resistance from Berlin and the German lender, UniCredit has built up a stake of nearly 50 percent in Commerzbank and is close to sealing one of Europe’s biggest banking mergers in recent years.

A German finance ministry spokesman conceded the banks had moved into a “a different phase now” and were negotiating a transaction.

But he stressed Klingbeil wanted to ensure Commerzbank’s interests and the country’s were protected during the talks in Berlin.

“Commerzbank has over 40,000 employees and we naturally want to safeguard their interests,” he told a press conference.

Commerzbank’s “core business model” in financing Germany’s small businesses, which form the backbone of Europe’s biggest economy, should be preserved too, he said.

It was also key that Commerzbank’s main operations remained in Frankfurt to ensure the city continued as “one of the most important financial centres in Europe,” the spokesman said.

Berlin still believes it has some influence over the deal through its representation on Commerzbank’s supervisory board and its roughly 12-percent stake in the bank, both legacies of a state bailout during the financial crisis.

But its leverage is now likely to be diminished given the size of UniCredit’s stake.

UniCredit started building up its holding in Commerzbank in 2024 in a bid to launch a takeover.

Commerzbank slashed thousands of jobs and hiked its financial targets in an effort to convince shareholders to back its campaign to remain independent.

But these efforts failed and, with UniCredit closing in on a controlling stake, Commerzbank’s CEO Bettina Orlopp called in late July for “constructive” talks with the Italian lender.

UniCredit wants to create a European banking behemoth better able to take on bigger US rivals and argues that a merger would strengthen the region’s fragmented banking sector.

Despite resistance in Germany, some policymakers in Brussels and at the European Central Bank have been more supportive of a possible takeover.

evidence.title: Germany seeks Commerzbank Frankfurt safeguards in UniCredit takeover push
evidence.text:
Germany seeks Commerzbank Frankfurt safeguards in UniCredit takeover push

Berlin is setting conditions for a possible UniCredit takeover of Commerzbank as the Italian bank moves closer to control of its German rival. The government wants the lender to stay headquartered and listed in Frankfurt while protecting its workforce and its role in financing Germany’s Mittelstand.

After Monday’s meeting, Klingbeil says Germany expects Commerzbank to remain a publicly listed company based in Frankfurt and to continue its strong Mittelstand business in Germany and abroad. Orcel says he is grateful for the chance to present UniCredit’s priorities and understand the minister’s position for the first time, adding that both sides should reflect on the constructive discussion to find a way forward for stakeholders and shareholders. Berlin’s stance and board influence The talks signal a softer approach from Berlin after earlier opposition to UniCredit’s pursuit of Commerzbank. Germany, which holds a near-13 per cent stake in Commerzbank, is shifting from outright resistance to setting conditions if UniCredit takes control.

Berlin still wants to avoid compulsory redundancies even if a combination of the two banks leads to some job losses, according to a person familiar with the matter. The government also intends to keep its stake for now and expects to retain two seats on Commerzbank’s supervisory board, which together with employee representatives could form a majority.

UniCredit first disclosed its stake in Commerzbank in September 2024, triggering political opposition and a prolonged stand-off with Commerzbank management. A person familiar with the government’s and Commerzbank’s thinking describes July as a turning point after more investors than expected accepted UniCredit’s offer, which had been widely seen as a low bid; Commerzbank declines to comment.

Our earlier report on the UK government’s possible acquisition of Speciality Steel UK outlined how ministers were considering deeper state intervention after the official receiver failed to secure a private buyer. We noted that the South Yorkshire plants had effectively been mothballed while the state covered wages and operating costs, intensifying scrutiny over rising public spending to sustain strategic industrial assets.

evidence.title: Italy’s Second Biggest Bank UniCredit Is Weighting up Crypto Custody: Report
evidence.text:
Italy’s Second Biggest Bank UniCredit Is Weighting up Crypto Custody: Report

UniCredit is working on crypto custody as other European banks work on digital asset services.

Italy’s second largest bank is considering expanding into digital asset offerings, including custody, according to reports.

According to a Friday Bloomberg report citing people familiar with the matter, Milan-based UniCredit is selecting a technology provider that would allow it to build the infrastructure needed to hold digital assets and facilitate their buying and selling.

Bloomberg’s reporting added that tokenized investment products and fixed-income securities, the use of stablecoins and exposure to cryptocurrencies were all on the cards.

JUST IN: 🇮🇹 Italy’s 2nd-largest bank UniCredit is considering to offer crypto asset custody — Bloomberg 👀 pic.twitter.com/NAZKJBdcES

The news comes as other banks in Europe expand crypto offerings. Spain moved first on retail, with BBVA rolling out bitcoin trading and custody to all customers via its app, using its own custody infrastructure rather than a third party; Santander’s Openbank followed with its own trading service.

Cecabank — a Spanish custodian with over €400bn under management that acts as backbone for 100+ financial institutions — went live with crypto custody in June via a partnership with Bit2Me.

And in Germany, Deutsche Bank is building custody with Bitpanda’s technology arm, while Taurus and DZ Bank got BaFin approval in January for its meinKrypto platform.

New regulation in the European Union — Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) — gives banks a legal definition, a supervisor, and a familiar set of obligations to launch crypto services.

UniCredit is one 37 lenders across 15 European countries working together to create a company called Qivalis with the aim of issuing a euro-denominated stablecoin.

Last year, the bank said it was offering professional clients a structured product tied to BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust exchange-traded fund, with full protection against losses.

evidence.title: UniCredit Takes Minority Stake in German Debt Platform VC Trade
evidence.text:
UniCredit has taken a minority holding in Frankfurt-based fintech VC Trade , deepening the Italian lender’s push into digital debt markets. Terms were not disclosed. The agreement includes a right for UniCredit to raise its ownership later and is intended both to fund VC Trade’s growth beyond Germany and to give the bank stronger tools for originating and distributing corporate debt across Europe .

VC Trade runs a digital marketplace and supporting infrastructure for private debt.

Its platform covers the full life cycle of deals such as syndicated loans and Schuldscheine—the privately placed German promissory notes that sit between a classic bond and a bilateral loan .

Issuers, arranging banks and institutional buyers use the system to standardise data, route documents and match supply with demand, cutting the paperwork that still dominates much of this market .

The firm is widely described as Germany’s Schuldschein venue by both number of deals and volume.

Some reports put more than 600 completed transactions and over €90 billion of activity on the platform since it began operating, with a network of more than 1,600 banks and investors.

The stake is not a cold start. UniCredit already arranged transactions on the platform , including a large Schuldschein for the City of Cologne earlier in 2026 with Helaba and ING Deutschland.

Buying equity turns a commercial relationship into a longer-term partnership.

Other lenders arrived first: in 2022 BayernLB, Helaba and Raiffeisen Bank International each took minority positions in a capital raise. Founders remain in control, so VC Trade keeps operational independence.

For UniCredit the deal sits inside its UniCredit Unlimited agenda, which treats fragmented European capital markets as a cost problem rather than a capital shortage.

Sam Kendall , head of advisory and financing solutions, argued that the real friction is the expense of linking money with mid-market firms and public issuers that can use it productively.

He said VC Trade’s technology attacks that friction directly by making participants easier to find and processes less manual.

CEO Stefan Fromme of VC Trade called the investment a milestone and pointed to a shared bet on end-to-end digitisation, connectivity and artificial intelligence for every party in a deal .

The move also fits a wider pattern of small, targeted technology bets. UniCredit has already taken a stake in blockchain financing specialist BlockInvest, launched DealSync, an AI matching tool for SME mergers and acquisitions, and issued Italy’s first tokenised minibond.

Germany remains a priority market for the group as it expands its corporate franchise, even as larger strategic questions—such as its interest in Commerzbank—continue in parallel.

If the partnership works as planned, borrowers should see faster placement and cleaner documentation, while UniCredit gains distribution reach without having to build a marketplace from scratch.

VC Trade, in turn, gets a pan- European balance sheet and client base to take a German product set into more countries.

Whether that combination scales will depend on adoption by other banks and on how quickly mid-market issuers accept fully digital workflows. For now, the transaction is a signal that large European banks still see infrastructure platforms—not just balance-sheet lending—as the way to modernise debt markets .

evidence.title: Fideuram (Intesa Sanpaolo), l’ex presidente Paolo Molesini vittima di una truffa hacker da 36 milioni
evidence.text:
Fideuram (Intesa Sanpaolo), l’ex presidente Paolo Molesini vittima di una truffa hacker da 36 milioni

Fideuram ha effettuato bonifici all’estero per 95 milioni su richiesta di Molesini, che si è mosso dopo aver ricevuto un messaggio WhatsApp dal finto profilo di Messina, ceo di Intesa Sanpaolo

A febbraio l’ex presidente di Fideuram, Paolo Molesini , è stato vittima di una truffa da 36 milioni di euro. Lo rivela il Corriere della Sera . Tutto parte da un messaggio WhatsApp inviato dal finto profilo di Carlo Messina, con cui il ceo di Intesa Sanpaolo chiede a Molesini di effettuare con urgenza una serie di bonifici tramite la tesoreria di Fideuram, che è la controllata del risparmio gestito di Ca’ de Sass.

La banca, scrive il finto Messina, non può procedere da sola per problemi pratici , e ha fretta di concludere l’operazione per non perdere un’ opportunità finanziaria all’estero. Subito dopo i truffatori mettono in scena un secondo raggiro. L’ex presidente riceve una telefonata in cui l’ AI replica la voce del managing partner di A&O Shearman Italia, Paolo Nastasi . I due si conoscono e il finto legale indirizza a Molesini un invito analogo a quello di Messina.

Così partono i bonifici: 95 milioni in totale soprattutto verso Cina e Hong Kong, ma subito dopo scatta l’ allarme e Fideuram aziona i sistemi di collaborazione interbancaria internazionale per recuperare buona parte del denaro. All’appello mancano però 36 milioni , spariti dopo essere stati convertiti in criptovalute . Gli inquirenti – i pm della procura di Milano Alfonso Serritiello e Barbara Benzi, con gip Sonia Mancini – stanno cercando di rintracciarli con rogatorie all’estero prima che i truffatori riescano a monetizzarli.

Le cosiddette «Ceo Fraud» sono un fenomeno in forte diffusione , che non riguarda soltanto il settore bancario. Nel caso in questione, i sistemi informatici della banca non sono stati violati e, anche alla luce delle dimensioni dell’istituto, l’impatto economico dell’episodio è risultato contenuto. La maggior parte delle somme sottratte è stata inoltre recuperata , mentre sono ancora in corso le attività per rientrare della quota residua.

Il manager coinvolto, una volta resosi conto dell’accaduto, ha deciso di rassegnare le dimissioni . Il fenomeno si inserisce però in un quadro più ampio: secondo la rilevazione dell’Association for Financial Professionals relativa al 2025, il 74% delle organizzazioni dichiara di essere stato bersaglio di tentativi o attacchi riusciti di Ceo Fraud e Business Email Compromise (Bec), contro il 63% dell’anno precedente.

I dati dell’ Fbi confermano la rilevanza economica di queste frodi: nel 2025 l’Internet Crime Complaint Center ha ricevuto 24.768 denunce per BEC, associate a perdite dichiarate per 3,05 miliardi di dollari, rispetto ai 2,77 miliardi del 2024. A rendere il fenomeno più insidioso contribuisce ora anche l’impiego dell’intelligenza artificiale: i report più recenti di Afp ed Enisa segnalano l’utilizzo di modelli linguistici per produrre comunicazioni sempre più credibili e prive dei tradizionali errori che potevano tradire i tentativi di frode, insieme alla crescente adozione di deepfake audio e video capaci di riprodurre voce e immagine di amministratori delegati e altri dirigenti durante telefonate e videoconferenze. evidence.title: Intesa Sanpaolo, dall’evento AmCham Slovenia il focus su investimenti, capitali e Intelligenza Artificiale
evidence.text:
Intesa Sanpaolo, dall’evento AmCham Slovenia il focus su investimenti, capitali e Intelligenza Artificiale

Papanicolaou (Intesa Sanpaolo): “Le banche continueranno a svolgere un ruolo essenziale nel finanziamento delle PMI, delle infrastrutture e della transizione, mentre i mercati dei capitali offriranno la scala, i capitali di rischio e i meccanismi di condivisione del rischio necessari alla crescita”

Intesa Sanpaolo, focus su risparmio, mercati dei capitali e Intelligenza Artificiale per la crescita europea

Papanicolaou è intervenuta oggi a Lubiana all’evento di AmCham Slovenia , l’American Chamber of Commerce in Slovenia, dal titolo “Who Pays for Risk? Capital, Competitiveness & Financial Markets” , dedicato al rapporto tra capitale, competitività e mercati finanziari. “ Penso che la sfida fondamentale dell’Europa sia trasformare il risparmio presente in investimenti produttivi ”, ha dichiarato Papanicolaou . “ Sebbene circa 10.000 miliardi di euro di risparmi delle famiglie europee siano detenuti in depositi bancari, il Rapporto Draghi stima un fabbisogno aggiuntivo di investimenti pari ad almeno 750-800 miliardi di euro all’anno. Colmare questo divario è essenziale per rafforzare la competitività, l’innovazione e la crescita sostenibile dell’Europa ”.

Secondo Papanicolaou , uno degli strumenti centrali per affrontare questo divario è la Savings and Investments Union , che dovrà essere accompagnata da una maggiore integrazione bancaria, da mercati dei capitali più sviluppati e da una capacità di investimento adeguata alle priorità strategiche europee. “ Non siamo di fronte a una scelta tra banche e mercati dei capitali: ritengo che il modello di finanziamento del futuro richieda entrambi ”, ha spiegato. “ Le banche continueranno a svolgere un ruolo essenziale nel finanziamento delle PMI, delle infrastrutture e della transizione, mentre i mercati dei capitali offriranno la scala, i capitali di rischio e i meccanismi di condivisione del rischio necessari alla crescita ”. In questo scenario, ha aggiunto, cambierà anche il ruolo degli istituti finanziari. “ Il nostro ruolo di banchieri non sarà soltanto quello di concedere credito, ma anche di agire come consulenti, distributori, originatori e connettori di capitale ”.

Un altro tema centrale dell’intervento è stato quello dell’ Intelligenza Artificiale , considerata un fattore sempre più rilevante per la competitività e per il miglioramento dell’efficienza operativa e dell’esperienza del cliente. Papanicolaou ha spiegato che Intesa Sanpaolo punta a un incremento della produttività superiore al 20% nelle attività di middle e back office entro la fine del Piano d’Impresa 2026-2029. “ Tuttavia, il vero valore dell’IA non risiede nella sostituzione delle competenze umane, bensì nel loro potenziamento ”, ha sottolineato, indicando come elementi fondamentali “ una governance solida, una supervisione umana efficace e investimenti continui nella formazione e nello sviluppo delle competenze ”.

L’intervento ha quindi messo al centro due direttrici considerate decisive per la crescita europea: da un lato la capacità di convogliare maggiori risorse verso investimenti produttivi, dall’altro l’utilizzo dell’innovazione tecnologica per aumentare efficienza e competitività senza rinunciare al ruolo delle competenze umane.

evidence.text:
Dopo le oltre 200 coppie del 2025, il viaggio della sesta edizione riparte dal Ponte Milvio Tennis Club di Roma: attesi, come di consueto, anche vip ed ex calciatori. Sabato mattina esibizione con Fisichella, Marcolin, Gottardi e Silenzi

Roma, Trani, Bergamo e Parma. Anche quest’anno, la Exclusive Padel Cup è pronta a iniziare il suo giro d’Italia. Sabato 26 e domenica 27 settembre scatta dalla Capitale la sesta edizione del circuito organizzato da Msp Italia, ente di promozione sportiva riconosciuto dal Coni, leader in Italia nei tornei di padel amatoriali, e firmato da Exclusive, la carta di credito premium del Gruppo Intesa Sanpaolo: una chiave di accesso a un mondo di servizi ed esperienze uniche che la Banca riserva alla sua migliore clientela, con un servizio di concierge dedicato h24 per esaudire, in ogni parte del mondo, desideri ed esigenze quotidiane dei titolari, accompagnandoli nelle loro passioni. Confermata la formula ‘itinerante’ degli ultimi tre anni: dopo la tappa di Roma al Ponte Milvio Tennis Club , la Exclusive Padel Cup si sposterà al Dorado Padel Center di Trani (24-25 ottobre), al 27 Padel Club di Bergamo (7-8 novembre) per chiudere al Pro Green Padel di Parma (28-29 novembre). Il circuito amatoriale è riservato alla categoria ‘non classificati’ o mai classificati oltre la terza, quarta e quinta fascia ed è diviso in tre categorie: maschile, femminile e misto. E per esaltare lo spirito della competizione, nel segno del fair play, le coppie si arbitreranno da sole, con la supervisione dei direttori di gara di MSP.

Nella mattinata di sabato sono in programma anche dei match di esibizione: tra i protagonisti, l’ex pilota di Formula 1 Giancarlo Fisichella , gli ex calciatori Dario Marcolin , Guerino Gottardi e Andrea Silenzi e l’ex schermidore e ora speaker radiofonico Stefano Pantano.

Quelli dell’Exclusive Padel Cup 2025 si sono confermati numeri da record, con oltre 200 coppie che sono scese in campo nelle quattro tappe disputate. Una formula, quella della Exclusive Padel Cup, che piace anche ai vip come Jimmy Ghione e agli ex calciatori e più in generale, agli ex atleti che negli anni hanno disputato il torneo: tra questi, Beppe Bergomi, Francesco Coco, Dida, Nicola Legrottaglie, Serginho, Nicola Amoruso, Dario Marcolin, German Denis, ‘Papu’ Gomez, Stefano Fiore, Nando Orsi, Cristian Brocchi. Inoltre, la leggenda del tennis Adriano Panatta, l’ex mezzofondista azzurro Gennaro Di Napoli, il pallavolista Pasquale Gravina, uno dei protagonisti della ‘Generazione di fenomeni’ di Julio Velasco, fino agli ex super cestisti Stefano Mancinelli e Gianluca Basile per finire con gli ex nazionali di rugby Paul Griffen e Alessandro Zanni. Il circuito Exclusive Padel Cup premierà i finalisti di ogni categoria a ogni tappa con premi speciali e materiale tecnico firmato Babolat. Il premio finale sarà offerto da Intesa Sanpaolo, main sponsor del torneo (per info e iscrizioni, www.exclusivepadelcup.com).

Per il sesto anno consecutivo Intesa Sanpaolo è main sponsor del circuito, una collaborazione vincente come sottolinea Tiziana Lamberti, responsabile Wealth Management & Protection Banca dei Territori Intesa Sanpaolo: "Exclusive Padel Cup è un’occasione per promuovere i valori dello sport, della condivisione e del benessere, creando momenti di incontro e relazione tra le persone. Da sempre attenta agli interessi e agli stili di vita dei propri clienti, Intesa Sanpaolo, attraverso Carta Exclusive, offre servizi ed esperienze pensati per arricchire la loro quotidianità. Come Banca dei Territori, risponde ogni giorno alle esigenze delle persone, sostenendole nelle scelte di risparmio e di finanza personale".

Claudio Briganti , responsabile nazionale padel di MSP Italia, ha aggiunto: "Siamo pronti per vivere un’altra entusiasmante edizione della Exclusive Padel Cup, convinti di poter replicare il successo delle precedenti. Siamo felici di accogliere Trani, Bergamo e Parma tra le new entry e città che ospiteranno la manifestazione, diventata ormai un appuntamento fisso e un’eccellenza nel calendario dei tornei amatoriali più apprezzati della stagione, per lo spirito competitivo ma soprattutto per quello aggregativo. Un aspetto, questo, che nella pratica del padel è assolutamente prioritario e che rende questa disciplina sempre più popolare».

Roberto Guerini , Country Manager di Babolat Italia, ha invece spiegato: "Siamo entusiasti di annunciare, per il quarto anno consecutivo, il rinnovo della nostra sponsorship tecnica per l’Exclusive Padel Cup, un torneo che si distingue per la sua qualità e professionalità. Siamo orgogliosi di contribuire a questo evento, fornendo premi significativi e rinnovando la nostra presenza attraverso la fornitura delle palle ufficiali del torneo. Siamo pronti a vivere insieme momenti emozionanti e a celebrare il gioco, i valori di sportività e la comunità che si unisce attorno a questo meraviglioso sport, tutte caratteristiche che si sposano appieno con la filosofia e la mission del marchio Babolat".

evidence.text:
Intesa Sanpaolo unit loses millions in AI impersonation scam

An AI-enabled fraud scheme has exposed new operational risks for Italy's banking sector after hitting Fideuram, the private banking arm of Intesa Sanpaolo. More than half of the stolen money is later recovered, but about 36 million euros remains missing after transfers moved through overseas accounts and into cryptocurrencies.

The fraudsters then follow up with a phone call that appears to come from a senior partner at a prominent law firm, confirming the instruction. The callers use AI technology to replicate the lawyer's voice, according to the sources. Believing the request is genuine, Molesini instructs the finance department to arrange a series of transfers to foreign accounts, mainly in China and Hong Kong.

Intesa Sanpaolo and Fideuram decline to comment. Fideuram detects irregularities in the transfers and alerts banks and authorities in several countries. Recovery efforts and wider banking risks Roughly 53 million euros is later recovered through cooperation among authorities in China, Portugal and Italy, according to the sources. The remaining funds have not been traced after passing through a network of overseas accounts and being converted into cryptocurrencies.

Neither Molesini nor any other Fideuram executives are under investigation, the sources say. However, Milan prosecutors have placed a foreign national living outside Europe under investigation on suspicion of computer fraud, one of the sources says.

Molesini resigns as chairman in March citing personal reasons, and Fideuram gives no further explanation for his departure at the time. The case adds to concerns over AI-driven impersonation fraud in Italy after criminals last year used a cloned voice resembling that of an Italian minister to persuade businessman Massimo Moratti to transfer nearly 1 million euros abroad, money that was later recovered.

evidence.title: Nebius (NBIS) Stock Surges 9% Following BNP Paribas Analyst Upgrade
evidence.text:
Nebius (NBIS) Stock Surges 9% Following BNP Paribas Analyst Upgrade

Nebius Group experienced robust momentum on Thursday. Shares of the AI infrastructure provider jumped as much as 9% during intraday trading to hit $248.90, after opening with a 6.4% advance to $241.20.

The rally stemmed from an analyst upgrade by BNP Paribas Exane. Daniel Wang, the firm’s analyst, elevated Nebius to Outperform from Neutral while simultaneously increasing the price target to $399 from the previous $260.

This revised target signals substantial potential appreciation from Thursday’s pre-market levels. The upgrade also positions BNP Paribas among the most optimistic analysts tracking the stock.

The rating enhancement comes amid several positive company developments that have bolstered the investment thesis. Earlier this month, Nebius announced price increases for its on-demand GPU cloud offerings, effective October 1.

Rates for Nvidia H100, H200, B200, and B300 instances will increase between 17% and 21%. Meanwhile, AMD EPYC Genoa CPU pricing will see approximately 25% hikes.

Market participants interpret these adjustments as evidence of constrained AI compute availability rather than operational challenges. This marks the second price increase implemented within a matter of months.

Nebius reported Q2 AI cloud revenue of $574.9 million, accompanied by an adjusted EBITDA margin approaching 50%. These metrics lend credibility to the company’s pricing strategy.

Bank of America analyst Tal Liani maintained his Buy recommendation on Nebius Thursday, with a $310 target. He highlighted the company’s balanced approach between extended hyperscaler agreements and shorter-duration, premium-priced contracts.

According to Liani, Nebius is allocating certain capacity for one- to three-year agreements priced at approximately double hyperscaler rates. He believes this strategy could drive revenue per watt significantly beyond current analyst consensus.

The company also maintains substantial contracts with Meta Platforms and Microsoft, which are scheduled to conclude in early 2026. Wang views these arrangements as indicators of additional business opportunities ahead.

“We expect incremental capacity from Q2 onwards to increasingly reflect higher priced AI cloud contracts,” Wang wrote in his note.

Thursday’s upgrade activity extended beyond Nebius. JPMorgan analyst Samik Chatterjee upgraded CoreWeave to Overweight from Neutral, raising his target from $120 to $125.

CoreWeave shares also advanced, though more modestly at 4% to reach $90.14. Nebius has delivered 193% gains year-to-date, substantially exceeding CoreWeave’s 25% appreciation over the identical period.

Chatterjee referenced the same fundamental dynamic supporting the Nebius thesis: escalating AI compute pricing. Northland Equity Capital Markets data suggests hourly compute rental costs have climbed approximately 33% since December.

Broader market conditions didn’t contribute to the advance. The Nasdaq declined 0.5%, the S&P 500 dropped 0.4%, and the Dow shed 0.4% during Thursday’s session, confirming that Nebius’s rally was purely company-specific.

Despite Thursday’s gains, Nebius trades considerably below its 52-week peak of $299.86. The company’s market capitalization stands at approximately $64.19 billion, with daily trading volume averaging around 20.4 million shares.

evidence.text:
Alphabet (GOOGL) Stock Climbs as Google Cloud Inks Major BNP Paribas Partnership

Alphabet stock (GOOGL) posted a 1% gain on Thursday following the announcement of a five-year strategic collaboration between Google Cloud and France’s BNP Paribas. Shares of BNP Paribas (BNPQY) responded positively as well, climbing 2% in response to the news.

This expanded agreement provides BNP with enhanced access to Google Cloud’s infrastructure alongside Gemini Enterprise capabilities and advanced Gemini AI models. The partnership represents a continuation and deepening of the existing collaboration between both organizations.

BNP has set an ambitious financial objective tied to this collaboration. The banking institution is targeting €750 million in AI-generated value through increased revenues and operational efficiencies by year-end 2026.

Enhanced risk management capabilities form another critical component of this strategic initiative. The bank intends to initially deploy Gemini models within its corporate and institutional banking operations.

Among the first use cases will be a proprietary generative AI assistant created specifically for that business unit. Beyond this, BNP aims to develop purpose-built AI agents optimized for distinct employee functions.

Charles Holive, who serves as BNP’s chief AI officer for corporate and institutional banking, indicated the technology has potential to accelerate how staff members create corporate credit memorandums. Research activities could also see significant speed improvements.

This partnership extends well beyond straightforward Gemini access. Google Cloud specialists will collaborate directly alongside BNP personnel to develop AI solutions customized for particular job functions.

This collaborative approach may enable BNP to transition models from pilot phases into production environments more efficiently. Sales departments are scheduled to receive comparable tools next, with trading desks and additional financial operations to follow.

BNP maintains a multi-vendor AI strategy, however. The institution renewed its independent partnership with French AI company Mistral for an additional three years earlier in 2025.

Marc Camus, BNP’s Chief Information Officer, explained that the Google and Mistral partnerships are designed to complement each other rather than overlap. Different providers will likely support distinct use cases and initiatives.

Even with this broadened Google partnership, BNP isn’t migrating all systems to cloud environments. Camus informed media that this agreement doesn’t signal an abandonment of the bank’s on-premises technology infrastructure.

Healthcare information connected to BNP’s insurance operations represents one category of data the institution maintains on private systems. Google has confirmed that BNP retains complete data ownership, and customer information won’t be utilized for training or improving Google’s AI models.

According to BNP, all AI agents developed under this partnership will undergo authentication, operate with minimal necessary permissions, and receive continuous monitoring. Lower-risk operations, including invoice automation and data organization, are considered more appropriate candidates for Google’s public cloud infrastructure.

Neither organization revealed the monetary terms of this arrangement. This expansion strengthens Google Cloud’s position among major financial services clients as European banking institutions accelerate AI investment.

Sept 24 (Reuters) - ⁠BNP Paribas will keep some sensitive customer data ⁠and critical operations off public cloud infrastructure even after ‌signing a five-year cloud and AI partnership with Google, the French bank said on Thursday.

The agreement gives BNP access to Google public-cloud infrastructure ​and Gemini models as the bank develops ⁠AI agents for internal ⁠work including corporate credit memos, sales, trading, research and structuring.

But ⁠the ‌deal does not mark a wholesale move, BNP Group Chief Information Officer Marc Camus told reporters in ⁠a call.

"The fact that we signed this ​agreement with Google ‌doesn't mean that we will get rid of our ⁠on-premise infrastructure," ​he said.

Medical information held by its insurance operations was an example of highly confidential data for which BNP avoids public-cloud solutions, ⁠he said.

BNP plans to keep using ​open-source models and to maintain its partnership with French AI company Mistral, with the providers used for different applications.

The bank said ⁠it sees scope to use Google technology for less sensitive work such as invoice processing and data management.

Google said BNP would retain ownership of its data, which would not ​be used to train, tune or ⁠refine its models. The bank said Google's AI agents would ​be authenticated, limited to the resources ‌needed for their tasks, and monitored.

BNP ​and Google declined to disclose the deal's value.

PARIS and SUNNYVALE, Calif., Sept. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- BNP Paribas and Google Cloud today announced a new five-year partnership, to expand BNP Paribas' access to Google Cloud's infrastructure and advanced AI capabilities including Gemini Enterprise and Gemini models.

Through this partnership, Google Cloud technologies will support the expansion of BNP Paribas' infrastructure and AI capabilities as the Bank moves towards broader deployment of agentic AI. It will also strengthen its existing multi-cloud and multi-model approach within its established security and data governance framework.

"Our role is to empower our businesses with the technology capabilities they need while maintaining a consistent framework for security and control. A multi-cloud and multi-model approach gives us the flexibility to select, for each case, the right model, infrastructure and level of control to meet our requirements for quality and security while delivering the best balance between cost and value. This partnership strengthens that approach and expands the options available to our businesses," said Marc Camus, Group Chief Information Officer, BNP Paribas.

"Agentic AI marks a critical shift in how global financial institutions streamline operations, assess risk, and serve their clients. Through this five-year partnership, BNP Paribas is combining its banking leadership with Google Cloud's secure infrastructure and Gemini Enterprise to deploy intelligent agents within platforms across the bank," said Thomas Kurian, CEO at Google Cloud.

From cloud and AI capabilities to business use case Through this partnership, BNP Paribas will have access to Gemini Enterprise to build, evaluate and deploy purpose-built agents tailored to specific business needs.

Starting with BNP Paribas Corporate & Institutional Banking (CIB):

The new capabilities will support the planned deployment of AI agents for targeted workflows, including the preparation of corporate credit memos to assist teams, with further applications across sales, trading, research, and structuring activities.

Gemini models will be integrated into LLM@CIB, its generative AI assistant currently available to more than 65,000 employees.

"Our approach to AI starts with the business need. We assess which technology is best suited to each use case and deploy it within the bank's security and governance framework. Agentic AI can help our teams handle more complex workflows while maintaining the appropriate level of control," said Charles Holive, Chief AI Officer, BNP Paribas CIB.

Google Cloud and Gemini technologies have already been deployed at Nickel, BNP Paribas' payment account business within the Commercial, Personal Banking & Services (CPBS) division. Gemini serves as the foundational model for Nickel Assist, helping 200 customer advisers find answers to customer requests based on Nickel's procedures and operating guidelines.

A controlled, enterprise-grade governance framework The use of Google Cloud will follow BNP Paribas' existing security and data governance requirements, which determines the type of data and workloads that can be processed in a public cloud environment. Certain categories of data will not be stored in a public cloud environment.

Security is a key pillar of BNP Paribas' agentic AI strategy, with each agent being authenticated and granted access only to the resources required to perform its assigned task. The connection of AI agents to the Group's information systems and their respective interactions will be consequently monitored and controlled.

The partnership will also contribute to BNP Paribas' existing Group-wide AI adoption program, completing ongoing initiatives with learning opportunities ranging from foundational AI literacy to specialized AI agent development.

About BNP Paribas Leader in banking and financial services in Europe, BNP Paribas operates in 64 countries and has over 180,000 employees, including more than 146,000 in Europe. The Group has key positions in its three main fields of activity: Commercial, Personal Banking & Services for the Group's commercial & personal banking and several specialised businesses including BNP Paribas Personal Finance and Arval; Investment & Protection Services for savings, investment and protection solutions; and Corporate & Institutional Banking, focused on corporate and institutional clients. Based on its strong diversified and integrated model, the Group helps all its clients (individuals, community associations, entrepreneurs, SMEs, corporates and institutional clients) to realise their projects through solutions spanning financing, investment, savings and protection insurance. The Group has a historic footprint in four eurozone markets: Belgium, France, Italy and Luxembourg. The Group is rolling out its integrated commercial & personal banking model across several Mediterranean countries, Türkiye, and Eastern Europe. As a key player in international banking, the Group has leading platforms and business lines in Europe, a strong presence in the Americas as well as a solid and fast-growing business in Asia-Pacific. BNP Paribas has implemented a Corporate Social Responsibility approach in all its activities, enabling it to contribute to the construction of a sustainable future, while ensuring the Group's performance and stability.

About Google Cloud Google Cloud offers a powerful, optimized AI stack—including AI infrastructure, leading models like Gemini, data management capabilities, multicloud security solutions, developer tools and platform, as well as agents and applications— that enables organizations to transform their business for the Agentic Era. Customers in more than 200 countries and territories turn to Google Cloud as their trusted technology partner.

evidence.title: Societe Generale bets on AI to slash costs by hundreds of millions in sweeping 2029 plan
evidence.text:
(CB-16); the desktop layout below renders the same text as a restyled . --> Societe Generale bets on AI to slash costs by hundreds of millions in sweeping 2029 plan

The French banking giant is targeting €1.9 billion in gross savings, with AI-driven IT cuts forming the centerpiece of CEO Slawomir Krupa's turnaround strategy.

Societe Generale just laid out a roadmap to cut its cost base below €16.3 billion by 2029, and artificial intelligence is doing a lot of the heavy lifting. The French bank expects AI initiatives alone to trim roughly €500 million from its IT spending, part of a broader plan targeting €1.9 billion in gross savings over the next few years.

SocGen’s strategic roadmap, unveiled on September 21, paints a picture of a bank trying to do more with less. The €16.3 billion cost base target represents roughly a 2% decrease from the bank’s estimated 2026 figures. On a net basis, after reinvestment and other adjustments, the savings come to approximately €300 million.

SocGen is aiming to push its cost-to-income ratio below 55% by 2029, down from roughly 60% today. On the revenue side, the bank is targeting a compound annual growth rate of about 3% through 2029. Return on tangible equity is pegged at 13-14% for 2029, with ambitions to push it above 15% after that.

Workforce changes are part of the equation too. SocGen plans to reduce approximately 1,800 roles in France, primarily through natural attrition rather than layoffs.

From homegrown AI to Anthropic and Microsoft

SocGen’s AI journey has already had a few plot twists. The bank initially developed its own internal AI tool called SoGPT, but earlier in 2026, the bank decommissioned SoGPT in favor of Microsoft ’s Copilot after performance gaps became apparent.

Daily. Free. Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy.

We respect your privacy. Unsubscribe anytime.

Now the bank has gone a step further by signing a strategic partnership with Anthropic , the AI company behind Claude. The agreement is designed to accelerate AI integration across SocGen’s operations, with a focus on boosting productivity and improving client services.

The projected €500 million in IT cost reductions would bring SocGen’s IT intensity ratio down to 12%.

This roadmap represents the latest chapter in CEO Slawomir Krupa’s turnaround effort, which began when he took the reins in 2023. His tenure has been defined by a focus on cost discipline, profitability improvement, and strategic simplification.

The gap between €1.9 billion in gross savings and €300 million in net reductions implies roughly €1.6 billion in reinvestment and transition costs. The Anthropic partnership will be worth monitoring closely, particularly given the European regulatory environment’s assertive stance on AI governance. For SocGen’s stock, the 2029 targets give the market a clear set of benchmarks: a cost-to-income ratio below 55% and return on tangible equity above 13%.

The workforce reduction of 1,800 roles through attrition also bears watching, as managing capability gaps while simultaneously deploying new AI tools across the organization presents significant execution challenges.
