evidence.title: CaixaBank Tech alcanzará los 2.000 empleados en 2027
evidence.text:
CaixaBank Tech alcanzará los 2.000 empleados en 2027

El proceso de expansión de CaixaBank Tech avanza al ritmo esperado, según indican desde la propia compañía del Grupo CaixaBank, el banco con mayor base de clientes digitales del sector financiero español (12 millones de usuarios).

La filial, que agrupa a los equipos especializados en tecnología y sistemas del banco, cuyos profesionales se centran en diversos proyectos centrados en tecnología para mejorar los servicios bancarios, utilizando desde blockchain a computación cuántica, pasando por inteligencia artificial, big data o cloud computing , ha cerrado 2025 con 500 personas más en su plantilla, que ya suma 1.600 profesionales y que llegará a las 2.000 en 2027.

Durante este ejercicio, según indican desde la empresa, se ha puesto especial foco en el ‘ hub tecnológico’ de la compañía en Sevilla , centrado en desarrollo de software; sólo allí se han sumado 100 personas. “El equipo en esta ciudad ha experimentado un crecimiento exponencial, pasando de 40 personas a 140 en 2025, lo que confirma el potencial de la región para atraer talento tecnológico y ofrecer oportunidades de desarrollo profesional dentro del Grupo CaixaBank”, explican desde la empresa.

Refuerzo en perfiles de ingeniería de software

Los 500 profesionales que ha contratado la filial tecnológica de Caixabank el pasado ejercicio son ingenieros de desarrollo, que no solo trabajan en el citado centro de Sevilla sino en los que también tiene la compañía en Barcelona y Madrid. Entre los profesionales más demandados, afirman desde la compañía, se encuentran expertos en IA, ingenieros de machine learning, científicos de datos, ingenieros de desarrollo de diferentes especializaciones (Backend, Python etc.), arquitectos cloud o expertos en seguridad, entre otros.

Caixabank estrena Oficina de IA y plan estratégico millonario

A finales del pasado año, el banco CaixaBank anunció la puesta en marcha de una Oficina de Inteligencia Artificial, dependiente de la Dirección de Medios y con alcance para todo el Grupo, que nace con “el objetivo de garantizar que todos los proyectos corporativos vinculados a la inteligencia artificial cumplen con la regulación, la ética y el aporte de valor real para el negocio”.

La oficina está compuesta por un equipo de nueva creación formado por profesionales con perfiles muy heterogéneos y transversales. Hasta ahora, entre los casos de uso más recientes implantados por CaixaBank se encuentra un asistente de soporte a la contratación remota, que utiliza la IA generativa para ayudar a gestores y clientes a reducir los tiempos de interacción e impulsar la contratación de productos desde los canales digitales ( app de banca móvil y web). Por otra parte, ha implementado un agente basado en IA generativa que interactúa directamente con los clientes de la app de CaixaBank para ayudarles a explorar productos. El banco también aplica la inteligencia artificial a la automatización de los procesos de negocio y operaciones, para reducir la carga administrativa en las oficinas y mejorar los procesos de decisión de los empleados del banco.

Antes del anuncio de esta nueva oficina de IA, en noviembre, el banco desveló su hoja de ruta completa en procesos y tecnología, que se integra en el Plan Estratégico 2025-2027 , que cuenta con una inversión global de 5.000 millones de euros.

La estrategia tecnológica de la entidad en los próximos años se articula en torno a cuatro objetivos: incrementar la agilidad y la capacidad comercial de sus áreas de Negocio; desarrollar nuevos servicios y simplificar procesos; potenciar la excelencia operativa mejorando la eficiencia y reforzar y evolucionar su actual plataforma tecnológica “con los mayores estándares de resiliencia y seguridad”.

evidence.title: Un tribunal de Alicante condena al Banco Sabadell a devolver 6'5 millones a la Fundación Mediterráneo por las cuotas de la CAM
evidence.text:
Un tribunal de Alicante ha condenado al Banco Sabadell a restituir a la Fundación de la Comunitat Valenciana Obra Social de Caja Mediterráneo unos 6,5 millones de euros por las cantidades que tuvo que afrontar a los afectados de las cuotas participativas de la extinta CAM.

Según la sentencia del Tribunal de Instancia de Alicante Plaza número 14, con fecha del 21 de septiembre y a la que ha tenido acceso EFE, se obliga al Sabadell a restituir las cantidades pagadas en el marco de los procedimientos sobre las cuotas participativas en la cantidad de 5.826.899,21 euros, más los intereses legales.

Estimación íntegra de la reclamación de la Fundación Mediterráneo

El fallo, contra el que cabe recurso de apelación ante la Audiencia Provincial de Alicante en 20 días hábiles, estima íntegramente la reclamación de la actual Fundación Mediterráneo y condena al banco en costas.

De esta manera, se pondrá fin a cerca de 14 años de litigios entre la Fundación y el Banco Sabadell en torno a la comercialización de las cuotas participativas (acciones sin derechos políticos) ya que la entidad presidida por Josep Oliu no tiene previsto ejercer su derecho a presentar un recurso y acatará la sentencia, según han adelantado a EFE fuentes conocedoras del proceso.

La sentencia se produce después de que Banco Sabadell se allanara a la reclamación de la Fundación pocos días antes del juicio previsto para el 24 de septiembre.

Esta resolución se suma a la dictada anteriormente a favor de la Fundación y que quedó firme el pasado 17 de junio por parte del Tribunal Supremo, un procedimiento en el que se reclamaban las cantidades abonadas por la Fundación a los cuotapartícipes hasta julio de 2018.

evidence.title: Josep Oliu, presidente de Banco Sabadell: "Después de la opa estamos en una posición sólida, y fortalecidos moral y financieramente"
evidence.text:
Josep Oliu, presidente de Banco Sabadell, durante la cita en Encuentros con Banco Sabadell. / Jose Navarro / INFORMACIÓNTV

"No estamos más tranquilos. Yo hubiese estado más tranquilo si hubiesen ganado los otros. Al revés, ahora estamos otra vez más agitados porque hay que ir decidiendo el futuro ". Con su habitual sorna, el presidente del Banco Sabadell, Josep Oliu , ha descrito de esta forma la situación en la que se encuentra la entidad, tras el fracaso de la opa que le lanzó el BBVA, hace ya casi un año. Una situación que ha descrito como "sólida", pero dejando claro que están muy lejos de relajarse y que los equipos del banco siguen con la maquinaria a pleno rendimiento.

Josep Oliu, durante su intervención en el acto. / JOSE NAVARRO

Oliu ha sido el encargado de presentar este miércoles al nuevo CEO de la entidad, Marc Armengol, en su primer acto en Alicante, un encuentro organizado por el banco, el diario Información, y Prensa Ibérica.

En su intervención, Oliu ha aprovechado para agradecer la "complicidad" de los accionistas minoritarios de la entidad en Alicante y la Comunidad Valenciana en el fracaso de la opa. Una operación que, según ha apuntado, ha dejado dos cosas. La primera, " un pequeño bache ", del que Oliu asegura que el banco ya se ha repuesto . Y la segunda, un banco mejor posicionado : "Ahora estamos en una posición sólida, fortalecidos moral y financieramente".

Sobre la situación económica, Oliu ha reconocido que estamos "en un periodo especialmente convulso en el mundo", por "la incertidumbre por los cambios tecnológicos y por la incertidumbre política, que nos lleva a no saber por dónde va a ir el precio del petróleo ni los tipos de interés".

Sin embargo, se ha mostrado optimista y ha recalcado que los cambios realizados en el sistema financiero y, en general, en la economía sitúan a España "como uno de los países mejor preparados de Europa para hacer frente a cualquier reto, uno de los países más competitivos en el contexto internacional".

Este miércoles tuvo lugar Encuentros con Banco Sabadell, la cita organizada por la entidad y el diario INFORMACIÓN. / Jose Navarro

En esta coyuntura es donde Oliu ha circunscrito el relevo en la cúpula del Sabadell, con la sustitución de César González-Bueno por Marc Armengol. "César hizo una labor fenomenal en la defensa del banco, pero tenía la familia desplazada a Portugal y decidimos que era el momento, porque había una persona disponible y capaz de tomar las riendas", ha explicado durante la introducción de su nuevo número dos.

Al respecto, ha recordado que ya ha conocido a cinco consejeros delegados en el Sabadell, y que "cada uno de ellos era el adecuado para su etapa. Creo que Marc es el que va a permitir que, en este mundo revuelto, el banco siga avanzando, sin perder lo que más le ha distinguido, nuestra forma de hacer banca y de aproximarnos a los clientes".

Oliu ha ido más allá y ha destacado que el equipo del banco "es todo joven, pero todos ellos con amplia experiencia , y eso da una visión del banco a futuro como nunca habíamos tenido".

El catalán se ha despedido reafirmando "el compromiso del Sabadell con Alicante y la Comunidad Valenciana, donde el banco tiene una parte de su corazón". Así, pese a haber trasladado la sede, la entidad ha celebrado este miércoles su consejo de administración en la ciudad y también entregará en Alicante el premio que su fundación concede a la investigación marina.

evidence.title: Banco Sabadell eleva un 12% las aportaciones de su fondo ético y solidario hasta 383.680 euros
evidence.text:
Banco Sabadell y Sabadell Asset Management–Grupo Amundi han destinado 383.680 euros a 21 proyectos sociales y de cooperación a través del fondo Sabadell Inversión Ética y Solidaria, FI.

La cantidad supone un incremento del 12% respecto a los 341.897 euros destinados en 2025 y procede de una parte de la comisión de gestión del fondo.

Las ayudas se dirigen a iniciativas desarrolladas por entidades del tercer sector españolas tanto dentro del país como en programas internacionales.

Los proyectos seleccionados abarcan ámbitos como inserción laboral y social, salud, educación, alimentación, infraestructuras y atención a colectivos vulnerables.

También se han financiado programas de cooperación en países como República Dominicana y Haití, Uganda, Tanzania, Brasil e India.

La selección de las iniciativas corresponde al Comité Ético del fondo, que analiza los proyectos presentados antes de determinar los beneficiarios.

Sabadell canaliza parte de las comisiones de gestión hacia proyectos sociales

Sabadell Inversión Ética y Solidaria combina criterios financieros con criterios éticos y medioambientales en sus decisiones de inversión.

Una de las características del producto es que una parte de las comisiones de gestión se destina directamente a proyectos solidarios.

El fondo fue creado y comercializado por Banco Sabadell y está gestionado por Sabadell Asset Management–Grupo Amundi.

Banco Sabadell comenzó a impulsar esta iniciativa ética y solidaria en 2006 y la consolidó con la creación del fondo en 2008.

Cerca de 4 millones destinados a 293 proyectos

Desde 2008, el fondo ha canalizado cerca de 4 millones de euros hacia 293 proyectos desarrollados en 35 países.

Según los datos de Banco Sabadell, estas iniciativas han contribuido a proyectos que han beneficiado a más de 234.000 personas, especialmente menores, mujeres, personas mayores, colectivos en riesgo de exclusión y personas afectadas por enfermedades o desastres naturales.

Entre las organizaciones seleccionadas en la actual edición figuran Asociación Antares, Arcores España, Manos Unidas, Cáritas Diocesana de Santiago de Compostela, Fundación Balia por la Infancia, ADACEN, ASPAYM Madrid, CESAL, Fundación Portolà, Fundación Raíces y Fundación Grandes Amigos en Acción, entre otras.

El fondo incorpora criterios financieros, éticos y ambientales

La estrategia de inversión del producto integra criterios financieros, éticos y medioambientales, al tiempo que mantiene el mecanismo de aportación de una parte de sus comisiones a iniciativas sociales.

Banco Sabadell vincula el fondo con diez Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible de Naciones Unidas, entre ellos reducción de la pobreza, educación, igualdad de género, salud, trabajo digno y reducción de desigualdades.

La entidad mantiene de esta forma una vía dentro de su negocio de gestión de activos para canalizar parte de los ingresos derivados de las comisiones hacia proyectos sociales y de cooperación.

evidence.title: Banco Sabadell inicia una recompra de acciones por hasta 331 millones de euros
evidence.text:
Banco Sabadell inicia una recompra de acciones por hasta 331 millones de euros

Sabadell pone en marcha una recompra de hasta 331 millones

Banco Sabadell inicia este lunes un nuevo programa de recompra de acciones propias por un importe máximo de 331 millones de euros . El objetivo de la entidad es mantener inicialmente los títulos adquiridos en autocartera para amortizarlos posteriormente mediante una reducción de capital.

Según la información remitida por el banco a la Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores y recogida por Europa Press, el programa permitirá adquirir hasta 467.846.248 acciones , una cifra equivalente aproximadamente al 10% del capital social de Sabadell.

La posterior amortización de los títulos reducirá el número de acciones en circulación y aumentará la participación proporcional de los actuales accionistas.

Compras a precio de mercado y con límites diarios

Las adquisiciones se realizarán a precio de mercado, aunque Sabadell no podrá comprar acciones por encima del precio más elevado entre la última operación independiente y la mejor oferta de compra independiente disponible en el centro de negociación correspondiente.

La entidad tampoco podrá adquirir en una misma sesión más del 25% del volumen medio diario negociado durante los 20 días hábiles anteriores a cada operación. Este límite pretende evitar que la actividad del programa ejerza una influencia excesiva sobre la formación del precio de la acción.

La recompra tendrá como fecha máxima de finalización el 31 de diciembre de 2026 . No obstante, el banco podrá concluirla antes si alcanza el importe máximo autorizado o adquiere la totalidad de las acciones previstas.

Una operación favorable para el beneficio por acción

Desde el punto de vista del accionista, la amortización de títulos suele tener un efecto positivo sobre métricas como el beneficio por acción, siempre que los resultados del banco permanezcan estables. Al reducirse el número de acciones entre las que se distribuye el beneficio, aumenta el resultado atribuible a cada título.

La recompra también refleja la capacidad de Sabadell para generar capital por encima de sus necesidades regulatorias y devolverlo a sus accionistas. Su impacto final dependerá del precio medio al que se ejecuten las compras: cuanto menor sea la valoración de adquisición, mayor será el efecto potencial de la amortización.

El programa refuerza la remuneración al accionista de Banco Sabadell y proporciona un elemento adicional de apoyo para la cotización durante los próximos meses, aunque su ejecución será gradual y estará condicionada por los límites diarios establecidos.

evidence.title: El nuevo Banco Sabadell: inteligencia artificial para procesos internos y pequeñas compras que mejoren la tecnología
evidence.text:
Banco Sabadell acelera su transformación tecnológica mientras trata de dejar atrás el ruido provocado por la opa de BBVA. El presidente de la entidad, Josep Oliu, y el nuevo consejero delegado, Marc Armengol, trasladaron este martes en Barcelona que el banco quiere centrarse ahora en la mejora de procesos internos mediante inteligencia artificial, reforzar la seguridad tecnológica y acometer pequeñas adquisiciones que aporten capacidades concretas al grupo, descartando grandes operaciones corporativas. La entidad catalana reivindica un modelo de « banca de relación », especialmente enfocado en empresas, en un momento en el que el 60% de las nuevas cuentas ya se abren por canales digitales. Pese a ello, tanto Oliu como Armengol insistieron en que el banco no quiere perder el componente humano en plena irrupción de la inteligencia artificial. «Van a cambiar muchas cosas estos años y hay que tratar de responder a nuestros clientes manteniendo la esencia», señaló Armengol ante periodistas.

El nuevo CEO del banco dejó claro además que, si Sabadell acomete compras en los próximos años, serán operaciones muy limitadas y vinculadas a tecnología o capacidades específicas. «No vamos a comprar nada de banca privada. Si compramos algo será algo pequeño». La referencia llega después de lo vivido con la operación de Paycomet , tras lo que el banco ha dado «un buen salto» en servicios digitales, como lo hará la tecnología de Bizum y Bizum Pro para autónomos.

La IA marcará el futuro de las plantillas

La inteligencia artificial fue uno de los grandes ejes de la conversación. Oliu reconoció abiertamente que la aplicación de esta tecnología acabará teniendo impacto sobre las plantillas del sector financiero, aunque admitió que todavía no saben en qué dimensión exacta. «La aplicación de la inteligencia artificial nos marcará la pauta de lo que va a ocurrir con la plantilla, que no sabemos todavía».

Armengol trató de complementar ese mensaje poniendo el foco en la adaptación de los trabajadores. El directivo defendió la necesidad de una «renovación de capacidades» dentro de la organización, e insistió en que la plantilla actual sigue siendo «muy valorada por los clientes». Según explicó, el banco no ha detenido en ningún momento su agenda de transformación pese a la opa de BBVA .

Precisamente sobre esa cuestión, Oliu dejó una reflexión relevante respecto al proceso de consolidación bancaria . Aunque aseguró que el consejero delegado saliente, César González-Bueno, es partidario de las fusiones, él no se considera «el gran consolidador» del sector. En su opinión, el contexto actual obliga primero a afrontar desafíos tecnológicos y de seguridad antes de pensar en grandes movimientos corporativos.

«Hay que hacer frente a retos tecnológicos y retos de seguridad. Una opa nos distrae de cuestiones que ahora mismo no convienen. Hay que ponerse al día y luego ver si tiene sentido lanzar una OPA ».

La opa de BBVA, la acción y el dividendo

Oliu también defendió la evolución bursátil del banco durante el proceso de opa. A su juicio, la operación de BBVA ha tenido «efectos evidentes» sobre la cotización, aunque considera que Banco Sabadell sigue infravalorado respecto a otros bancos comparables. «Cotizamos por debajo del PER (número de veces que la cotización está por encima del beneficio) otros bancos similares».

En paralelo, el presidente defendió la actual política de remuneración al accionista y aseguró que no habrá cambios en el dividendo . «La política de dividendo no se toca», afirmó, recordando además el programa de recompra de acciones que mantiene activa la entidad.

Sobre la resistencia accionarial frente a la opa, Oliu aseguró que el verdadero «núcleo duro» del banco han sido los pequeños accionistas. «Han sido los accionistas minoritarios, que han aguantado y rechazado la OPA de BBVA”. También destacó el respaldo de Zúrich Insurance Group gracias a la alianza aseguradora que ambas compañías mantienen.

evidence.title: ING Group Raises 2027 ROE Target Above 16% as Revenue, AI Drive Growth
evidence.text:
ING Group Raises 2027 ROE Target Above 16% as Revenue, AI Drive Growth

Interested in ING Group, N.V.? Here are five stocks we like better.

ING raised its 2027 return on tangible equity target to above 16% , up from 14%, supported by expected revenue above €26 billion and costs of approximately €13 billion.

Revenue growth is being driven by stronger lending, deposits and fee income: ING has added about €100 billion in deposits, annualized lending growth is roughly 8%, and fees are expected to exceed the previous €5 billion target.

AI and capital discipline are central to the strategy , with ING using agentic AI in mortgages and chatbots while shifting capital toward retail banking; management remains focused on organic growth and selective bolt-on acquisitions.

European Banks Are Outperforming : Can These 3 Keep It Going?

ING Group (NYSE:ING) CEO Steven van Rijswijk said the bank's improved profitability outlook is being supported by stronger revenue growth, operating scalability and capital discipline, while management remains focused on organic expansion and targeted bolt-on acquisitions.

Speaking at an investor event, van Rijswijk said ING has raised its 2027 return on tangible equity target to more than 16%, from the 14% target presented at its 2024 Capital Markets Day. The updated outlook includes revenue above €26 billion by 2027 and projected costs of about €13 billion, roughly €300 million below prior guidance.

Revenue Growth, Cost Scalability and Capital Management

→ Sandisk Joins the S&P 100—Is the Index Flow, or the AI Story, Driving the Stock?

Van Rijswijk said ING's updated targets reflect stronger-than-expected commercial activity. The bank expects an additional €1 billion of revenue compared with its earlier plan, driven by lending and deposit activity. ING has added roughly €100 billion of deposits over the past two and a half years, while year-to-date lending growth annualized at about 8%, he said.

Fee income has also developed faster than expected. ING had previously targeted approximately €5 billion of fees by 2027, but van Rijswijk said the bank has already reached that level this year. It now expects an additional €300 million to €500 million in fee growth by 2027.

→ Viking's Obesity Edge May Be Staying Power, Not Weight Loss

Despite increased customer and business activity, ING expects to keep expenses under control through shared operational hubs and technology investments. Van Rijswijk cited centralized know-your-customer processes, contact centers, operational processing and the company's cloud environment as tools that support scalability.

Capital management is the third major driver of the higher return outlook, according to the CEO. ING began using significant risk transfers last year after updating models to meet European Central Bank requirements. The bank completed about 12 basis points of risk transfers last year and expects 15 to 20 basis points this year, having completed 4 basis points year to date.

→ Chips to Bots: Qualcomm's Agentic AI Breakout

ING is also shifting its risk-weighted asset mix toward retail businesses. Van Rijswijk said retail represented 56% of the mix and wholesale banking 44%, exceeding the 55%-45% balance it had targeted for the end of 2027.

Mortgage lending has been a key contributor to retail growth. ING has about €380 billion in mortgages and is among Europe's largest mortgage lenders, van Rijswijk said. He attributed growth both to housing shortages in several European countries and to ING's digital mortgage capabilities.

In some markets, ING can process straightforward mortgage applications within 30 minutes, he said. In the Netherlands, the bank is using agentic artificial intelligence for more complex applications, reducing processing time from seven days to five days.

The bank is concentrating mortgage growth in markets where returns are attractive, including the Netherlands, Germany, Italy and Australia. In the Netherlands, ING's overall mortgage-book market share is around 14%, while its production market share has run around 18% to 19% in recent quarters, van Rijswijk said.

He said ING does not manage the business based on net interest margin alone, noting that low-risk-weighted, collateralized lending may produce lower margins but still generate attractive returns on equity. ING's lending margin moved from 126 basis points to 124 basis points, which van Rijswijk attributed more to changes in the lending-book mix than competitive pricing. He expects the margin to stabilize during the remainder of the year.

On funding, van Rijswijk said ING has more than €700 billion in deposits and maintains a loan-to-deposit ratio of about 100%, a level he described as comfortable. Approximately 95% of deposits receive the bank's core rate, he said.

ING has increasingly used targeted "micro campaigns" rather than broad deposit promotions. A German micro campaign in the second quarter brought in an additional €8 billion, van Rijswijk said. The campaigns are designed not only to bring in deposits but also to convert customers into primary banking clients, who typically conduct three times more business with ING than non-primary customers.

Van Rijswijk said ING sees substantial room to expand investment, insurance, credit-card and packaged-banking offerings. The company's assets under management have increased to €330 billion from less than €150 billion when he became CEO six years ago. ING now has 5.3 million investment customers out of 41 million total customers, he said.

The bank is consolidating nine investment platforms into one platform and selecting global asset-management partners to improve offerings across areas including private credit, private equity, exchange-traded funds and real estate.

While van Rijswijk said he believes in the universal-bank model, he acknowledged that wholesale banking's returns need improvement. Wholesale banking is currently generating a return of about 11%, and ING aims to exit 2027 at 12%. However, he said that level "is still not enough" and that the bank will continue its "capital diet" for the division until returns are closer to its desired level.

Management plans to diversify wholesale banking beyond lending, particularly through financial markets and transaction services, while continuing to shift capital toward retail operations.

ING also plans to use artificial intelligence to improve both efficiency and customer experience. Van Rijswijk said the company has 600 employees working in AI, including about 300 in a hub in Türkiye. ING uses Google as its principal AI partner and has rolled out agentic AI mortgages in the Netherlands. It also expects AI to route 75% of chatbot traffic, compared with 45% several years ago.

Van Rijswijk said organic growth remains ING's primary strategic focus, citing growth of 5% to 10% in customer-related measures, 8% in balances and more than 10% in fees this year.

The bank is open to bolt-on deals that add skills or capabilities it lacks. He cited ING's 40% stake in Spanish private bank Singular, where ING has an option to acquire the remaining shares, and an asset-management acquisition in Poland. Larger or more opportunistic transactions remain secondary to organic expansion, he said.

ING Group N.V. is a Dutch international banking and financial services company headquartered in Amsterdam. Through its banking operations, ING provides retail and commercial banking services, including checking and savings accounts, consumer and business lending, mortgages, payments, investment products and digital banking solutions.

The company serves individual customers, small and medium-sized businesses, large corporations and institutional clients. Its retail banking activities are concentrated primarily in Europe, while its wholesale banking business supports clients in numerous countries with corporate lending, trade finance, financial markets, cash management and other banking services.

ING Group: Progress on share buyback programme

ING announced today that, as part of our €1.0 billion share buyback programme announced on 30 April 2026, in total 1,350,000 shares were repurchased during the week of 14 September up to and including 18 September 2026.

The shares were repurchased at an average price of €31.92 for a total amount of €43,086,200.00. For detailed information on the daily repurchased shares, individual share purchase transactions and weekly reports, see the updates on the share buyback programme on our website.

In line with the purpose of the programme to reduce the share capital of ING, the total number of shares repurchased under this programme to date is 27,660,805 at an average price of €28.16 for a total consideration of €779,002,867.99. To date approximately 77.90% of the maximum total value of the share buyback programme has been completed.

Note for editors For further information on ING, please visit www.ing.com. Frequent news updates can be found in the Newsroom. Photos of ING operations, buildings and its executives are available for download at Flickr.

ING PROFILE ING is a global financial institution with a strong European base, offering banking services through its operating company ING bank. evidence.title: ING Group stock steadies as Jefferies reiterates Hold rating after strong Q2 figures
evidence.text:
ING Group stock (ISIN NL0011821202) is trading close to its recent highs, with the primary listing on Euronext Amsterdam around 31.74 euros as of September 18, 2026, while analysts at Jefferies have reiterated their Hold rating on the shares at this level.

Jefferies reiterates Hold rating near recent highs

According to finanzen.at on September 18, 2026, Jefferies reaffirmed its Hold recommendation on ING Group at a spot price of 31.74 euros on Euronext Amsterdam, corresponding to a daily decline of 1.21 percent from the prior close of 32.14 euros.

As The Globe and Mail reports in a TipRanks-based overview, Jefferies' stance contrasts with a broader analyst consensus that rates ING Group as a Strong Buy, with an average target price of 34.24 euros, implying upside potential of about 7.9 percent versus the 31.74-euro spot level as of September 18, 2026.

Q2 2026 results show profit and EPS ahead of consensus

As MarketBeat summarizes, ING Group reported a Q2 2026 net result of 1,947.0 million euros for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, reflecting accelerated growth in its customer base and customer balances.

According to the same overview from MarketBeat , ING Group delivered earnings per share of 0.79 dollars in Q2 2026, beating consensus expectations of 0.75 dollars by 0.04 dollars, which underlines the bank's ability to outperform analyst forecasts on profitability.

The same Q2 2026 earnings snapshot cited by MarketBeat states that ING Group generated revenue of 4.76 billion dollars in Q2 2026, highlighting a solid operating profile supported by strong margins and returns on equity.

American depositary receipts and 52-week performance

On the New York Stock Exchange, ING Group's American depositary receipts provide an additional perspective for international investors who prefer trading in dollars.

As MarketBeat reports, ING Group's ADRs most recently traded at 36.42 dollars at the regular closing session on September 18, 2026, with a day change of minus 1.34 percent compared with the previous close.

The same source from MarketBeat indicates that the ING Group ADR has a 52-week low of 23.64 dollars and a 52-week high of 37.52 dollars, positioning the latest 36.42-dollar price only around 2.9 percent below the high and more than 54.1 percent above the low.

According to the year-to-date performance data from MarketBeat , ING Group's ADR started 2026 at 27.98 dollars and has risen by 30.2 percent so far, contributing to a market capitalization of about 104.18 billion dollars as of mid-September 2026.

Risk factors and valuation considerations

For investors, the main tension now lies between ING Group's strong earnings momentum and the cautious stance of certain analysts such as Jefferies.

The Hold rating from Jefferies at a spot level of 31.74 euros suggests that, while Q2 2026 figures were robust, the bank may see limited near-term upside relative to risk, particularly given the fact that the current price is already near the average analyst target of 34.24 euros as highlighted by The Globe and Mail .

At the same time, the strong Q2 2026 net result of 1,947.0 million euros and the earnings per share of 0.79 dollars clearly above the 0.75-dollar consensus, as reported by MarketBeat , support the argument that ING Group continues to grow profitably and could justify the Strong Buy consensus.

On its primary listing at Euronext Amsterdam, ING Group stock most recently changed hands at 31.74 euros as of September 18, 2026, with daily moves of around plus or minus 1 percent according to a corporate overview published on September 20, 2026.

evidence.title: ING Group stock edges lower as Jefferies sticks to Neutral rating
evidence.text:
ING Group stock (ISIN NL0011821202) is trading close to the EUR 32 mark on Euronext Amsterdam on September 18, 2026, following a prior close of EUR 32.31 and a recent move that left the shares near their yearly range highs.

Jefferies reiterates Neutral on ING Group

Analyst attention has recently turned to ING Group, with Jefferies confirming its existing Neutral stance on the Dutch bank while the stock traded at EUR 32.31 on Euronext Amsterdam on September 17, 2026, a session in which the shares gained 1.17 percent compared with the previous close, according to MarketScreener .

The Neutral rating suggests that Jefferies sees ING Group’s current valuation broadly in line with its fundamental outlook after a run in the shares that has lifted them close to their 52-week high of EUR 32.36, versus a 52-week low around EUR 20.23 as of mid-September 2026, based on Euronext-linked data cited in recent analyst summaries such as those referenced by Ad-hoc-news .

Stock holds near recent highs on September 18, 2026

Price data for the primary Amsterdam listing show ING Group changing hands around EUR 32.26 on September 18, 2026, a modest decline of 0.17 percent versus the prior closing level of EUR 32.31, with the quote reflecting at least a 15-minute delay on Euronext Amsterdam, according to Reuters .

Additional trading data from a real-time European equity portal indicate an intraday range between roughly EUR 31.89 and EUR 32.36 for ING Group on September 18, 2026, with the last official close of EUR 32.31 sitting just below the upper end of that yearly range, underscoring how the shares have steadily advanced from their 52-week low of EUR 20.23 earlier in the period, as shown in the annual span referenced by Bolsamania .

On the New York Stock Exchange, where ING Group is also traded via its ADR in United States dollars, the shares closed at USD 36.95 on September 17, 2026, up 1.61 percent on the day, with a 52-week range between USD 23.64 and USD 37.52 and a market capitalization of about USD 105.67 billion as of that date, according to MarketBeat .

Fundamentally, ING Group’s latest quarterly figures continue to frame investor expectations for the stock. As summarized in recent coverage of the second quarter of 2026, the bank reported net profit ahead of market expectations in that period, delivering an increase versus the prior-year quarter and prompting some houses to revise their earnings and valuation models upward, according to commentary highlighted by MarketScreener .

Within those second-quarter 2026 results, ING Group’s net profit reached a level that was described as being above consensus forecasts, while revenue growth in core retail and wholesale banking segments supported a year-on-year expansion of the bank’s profitability metrics, according to the same MarketScreener summary of the quarter.

From a longer-term perspective, the market is now weighing how these stronger second-quarter 2026 earnings compare with the bank’s performance in fiscal year 2025, in which net profit and underlying income had already shown improvement versus 2024, as indicated in earlier annual reporting on the investor-relations pages of ING Group accessed via ING Group .

Beyond the Jefferies rating, broader analyst sentiment on ING Group is cautiously positive. A recent consensus snapshot for the ADR suggests that the stock is rated Moderate Buy overall, with a blended rating score of 2.75 on a scale from Strong Sell to Strong Buy and coverage from eight analysts comprising one strong buy, four buy and three hold recommendations, according to MarketBeat .

From an environmental, social and governance perspective, ING Group also enjoys a favorable assessment. As of July 2026, Sustainalytics viewed the bank’s management of ESG material risk as strong, assigning the group an ESG risk rating of 16.7, which places ING Group in the low-risk category among global banks, according to a release distributed through Via Ritzau .

Risks and what investors are watching now

For investors, one of the key questions is whether the strong earnings of the second quarter of 2026 and the supportive ESG profile can offset cyclical risks in the European banking sector. Analysts note that ING Group remains exposed to potential shifts in interest rates and credit quality across its core markets, even as its capital position and diversified franchise have helped it navigate previous downturns, as suggested by commentary on the bank’s strategic focus in European equity analysis pieces such as those covered by Bolsamania .

According to that same Bolsamania analysis, Jefferies has argued that the bank is now firmly established in its core markets, highlighting the ongoing rollout of its private banking business, which is scheduled to be finalized in the second half of 2026, and strategic advances in small and medium-sized enterprise banking that are expected to continue into early 2027.

At the time of writing, ING Group’s primary listing on Euronext Amsterdam shows the shares trading around EUR 32.26 on September 18, 2026, modestly below the previous close of EUR 32.31 and within a daily range of approximately EUR 31.89 to EUR 32.36, with the current level sitting close to the upper bound of the 52-week range that stretches from EUR 20.23 to EUR 32.36, based on combined price data from Euronext Amsterdam and European equity portals.

evidence.title: ING Group completes two risk sharing transactions
evidence.text:
ING Group completes two risk sharing transactions

ING Group completes two risk sharing transactions

ING Group today announced the successful completion of two significant risk transfer (SRT) transactions, marking the inaugural SRTs for ING Wholesale Banking. These transactions provide us with first-loss protection on diversified portfolios of corporate loans with a total notional exposure of €10.5 billion.

With these transactions, we strengthen our ability to serve corporate clients by freeing up resources to finance new growth opportunities. The transactions are expected to reduce ING's risk-weighted assets by €3.4 billion, resulting in a pro forma impact of +14 basis points on the 3Q2025 CET1 ratio.

ING aims to extend the strategic use of SRTs across Retail and additional Wholesale Banking portfolios in the coming years.

"I am very proud of the successful execution of these milestone transactions in our capital velocity strategy," said Andrew Bester, member of ING's Management Board Banking and head of Wholesale Banking. "This achievement was made possible through outstanding teamwork and the strong partnerships ING has established with leading institutional investors. These transactions demonstrate our commitment to continue supporting our clients' needs and contributing to European economic growth."

evidence.title: ING Group 2025 SREP process completed
evidence.text:
ING Group has been notified by the European Central Bank (ECB) decision on the 2025 Supervisory Review and Evaluation Process (SREP), based on which it has taken a decision on ING's prudential requirements, including capital requirements for 2026.

According to the ECB's SREP decision, the Pillar 2 additional own funds requirement (P2R) will increase by 5 bps, from 165 bps to 170 bps, and will be applicable from 1 January 2026. As a result, ING Group's fully loaded CET1 requirement increases by 3 bps. Including a recently announced increase in the countercyclical buffer requirement in Spain, ING Group's fully-loaded CET1 requirement will increase to 11.00%, while the total capital requirement will increase to 15.24%.

The ECB also notified ING Group of a 10 bps leverage ratio Pillar 2 requirement (P2R-LR). Consequently, the overall leverage ratio requirement will increase from 3.5% to 3.6% as of 1 January 2026.

As of 30 September 2025, ING Group's CET1 ratio was 13.4% and ING's Leverage Ratio was 4.4%, both well above the regulatory requirements. Further information on ING's capital requirements can be found in the ING Group Credit Update presentation on the Investor Relations section of our website, www.ing.com .

evidence.title: Labor talks between ABN Amro, unions collapse over 2 work days in office demand
evidence.text:
Labor talks between ABN Amro, unions collapse over 2 work days in office demand

Collective labor agreement talks between ABN Amro and the union were halted earlier this week as the two sides cannot agree on the request that employees have to spend 50 percent of their work time in the office, NU.nl reports. The unions do not want to continue the talks, unlike ABN Amro. The parties also disagree on the payment.

ABN Amro wants the office requirement to be a part of the collective agreement. “The ABNO Amro delegation is holding to the demand that you and your colleagues work an average of two days a week in the office, or 50 percent of working time,” FNV allegedly wrote in a letter obtained by NU.nl.

“The unions have pointed out that virtually everyone already comes regularly to the office and that many trams have made practical arrangements for that. Even so, the ABN Amro delegation would not drop the 50 percent standard,” the letter said.

Employers’ association AWVN told NU.nl that “it is quite exceptional for rules on working from home to be put in a collective agreement. That almost never happens,” a spokesperson said. “But employers are looking for a new balance, especially for office staff.”

“Every team at ABN Amro has made arrangements for working from home and coming to the office. We have received no complaints from our members about that,” FNV official Arne Gorter told the newspaper.

ABN Amro wants to resume the talks. “We will make no further comments on the demand for mandatory office attendance as long as the collective agreement negotiations are underway,” a spokesperson told NU.nl.

evidence.title: ABN AMRO earnings call signals robust profit momentum
evidence.text:
ABN AMRO earnings call signals robust profit momentum

ABN AMRO Bank NV Unsponsored ADR ( (AAVMY) ) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

ABN AMRO Bank NV struck an upbeat tone on its latest earnings call, underpinned by a near‑30% jump in net profit, higher returns on equity and upgraded income guidance. Management acknowledged headwinds, from capital dilution linked to the NIBC acquisition to margin pressure and cost uncertainty, but stressed that these risks are manageable within a robust capital position and a clear strategic plan.

Net profit climbed to EUR 781 million, almost 30% higher than a year earlier as profitability benefited from higher income and tight cost control. Return on equity improved to 12.1% for the quarter, with year‑to‑date pro forma ROE at 10.9%, putting the bank comfortably above many European peers on this key measure of value creation.

The bank raised its full‑year commercial net interest income guidance to around EUR 6.8 billion, now including the impact of the NIBC acquisition. Commercial NII was already up 5% quarter‑on‑quarter, showing that core lending and deposit spreads are still a powerful earnings driver despite a more competitive market backdrop.

Record Fees and Stronger Operating Income

Fee income reached a record level, rising 2% compared with the previous quarter as customers made more use of investment and payment services. Other income strengthened sharply to EUR 106 million, helping lift total operating income by 6% quarter‑on‑quarter and broadening the bank’s revenue mix beyond interest income.

Total client assets increased by just over EUR 25 billion in the second quarter, reflecting both market performance and new inflows. In Wealth Management, client assets grew more than 7% with EUR 2.3 billion of core net new assets, while client deposits rose over EUR 5 billion and P&BB deposits advanced more than 4.5%.

The pro forma CET1 ratio improved to 15.9%, with the reported CET1 ratio stable at a still‑solid 15.3%, underlining a sizeable capital buffer above regulatory requirements. Management has executed roughly EUR 9 billion of risk‑weighted asset optimization so far, including about EUR 2 billion this quarter, with Corporate Banking delivering around EUR 6 billion and already surpassing 60% of its RWA reduction goal.

Operating efficiency is improving, allowing ABN AMRO to cut its 2026 headline cost guidance to around EUR 5.5 billion including NIBC, but excluding restructuring and one‑off items. Headcount fell by roughly 250 FTEs in the quarter and the bank has already achieved about EUR 300 million of its EUR 900 million 2028 savings target, putting it ahead of schedule on staff reductions.

Benign Credit Costs and Solid Asset Quality

Impairments remained low at EUR 24 million, translating into a cost of risk of just 4 basis points, which is well below through‑the‑cycle expectations. The Stage 3 ratio stayed stable at 2.1%, and internal backtests indicated that coverage levels remain above historical write‑offs even as the Stage 3 coverage ratio eased to about 14%.

Strategic M&A and Technology Investments

The completed NIBC acquisition adds new capabilities and growth potential in deposits and mortgages, and the legal merger of HAL has also been finalized with IT integration set for the fourth quarter. The bank is pushing ahead on technology, with around 50 generative AI use cases already in production and a new partnership with Mistral to support tools such as voicebots and KYC/AML assistants.

Capital Dilution from NIBC Consolidation

Management flagged a near‑term capital headwind as the full consolidation of NIBC will add about EUR 6.6 billion of RWAs in the next quarter. This is expected to reduce the CET1 ratio by roughly 70 to 75 basis points, though the bank believes this dilution is manageable in light of its current capital buffer and upcoming RWA releases elsewhere.

Asset margins dipped by 2 basis points quarter‑on‑quarter, with lending margins also down about 2 basis points as growth skewed toward capital‑light, government‑backed NHG mortgages and lower loan‑to‑value exposures. Management described the Dutch mortgage market as highly competitive, suggesting further pressure on pricing even as volume demand remains healthy.

While the proportion of loans in Stage 3 stayed at 2.1%, the Stage 3 coverage ratio dropped to around 14%, partly driven by derisking and the rising share of mortgages in the book. The bank stressed that this reflects portfolio mix and prior run‑offs and write‑offs, but investors are likely to watch this metric closely as an early indicator of any turn in credit quality.

Other commercial NII had a strong quarter, helped by a robust contribution from Clearing activities, but management cautioned that this line is both elevated and volatile. Guidance now implies underlying other commercial NII of around EUR 450 million for the year, with the remainder coming from NIBC, and assumes a normalization from the current high level.

The EUR 5.5 billion cost target for 2026 includes NIBC but excludes restructuring charges and exceptional items, giving some leeway for future one‑offs. However, the outcome of collective labor agreement talks could push expenses higher, with management estimating roughly EUR 30 million in additional costs for every percentage point of inflation above its planning assumptions.

Liability margins improved by 5 basis points in the quarter, providing a useful tailwind to net interest income, but the bank warned that this may not be fully sustainable. Competition from both traditional rivals and aggressive fintechs, along with potential customer shifts between products and rate volatility, could squeeze deposit margins over time.

Capital Return Timing and RWA Volatility

Despite holding capital above its 13.75% target, ABN AMRO will wait until its fourth‑quarter capital assessment before deciding on any exceptional payout beyond the policy of up to 100% of net profit. A series of RWA moves, including NIBC consolidation, the end of the DNB mortgage floor, an EBA property loss update and the sale of Alfam, will cause near‑term volatility that management wants to assess before committing more capital.

Looking ahead, the bank guides for commercial NII of around EUR 6.8 billion in 2026, plus roughly EUR 0.6 billion in other commercial NII, and sees headline operating expenses at about EUR 5.5 billion including NIBC but excluding restructuring and incidentals. It reiterated its plan to return at least EUR 7.5 billion over time, confirmed an interim dividend of EUR 0.68 per share, maintained very low cost‑of‑risk guidance and reaffirmed both its EUR 900 million 2028 savings goal and a Wealth net‑new‑assets target of EUR 5–7 billion per year.

ABN AMRO’s earnings call painted a picture of a bank in solid shape, combining strong profit growth and capital optimization with disciplined cost management and a growing wealth and deposit franchise. While capital dilution from NIBC, tighter margins and cost and RWA uncertainties remain on the radar, the upgraded guidance and firm capital position suggest the bank is well placed to deliver attractive returns for shareholders over the coming years.

evidence.title: ABN Amro wants staffers back in office; Still plans to lay off 2,750 more people
evidence.text:
ABN Amro wants staffers back in office; Still plans to lay off 2,750 more people

ABN Amro wants to require its employees to come to the office for at least half of their workweek. The bank thinks this will increase its employees’ productivity and improve team spirit. ABN Amro cut more than 250 people from its workforce last quarter, saying it has dropped about 2,250 people since beginning a reorganization plan meant to reduce headcount by 5,000 in total.

The demand to get workers back in the office was raised during collective bargaining negotiations with the trade unions in May, Financieele Dagblad reported . “We operate on the principle that you work more than half of your workweek at the office,” the bank wrote in its latest collective bargaining proposal, according to the business newspaper.

ABN Amro’s new stance is a U-turn from the agreements in the collective agreement for banks. Since the start of the coronavirus pandemic in 2020, most of the 70,000 employees of Dutch banks have been allowed to decide for themselves where they work.

ABN Amro has been reluctant about work from home for some time. It delayed increasing a reimbursement for employees working from home, and was one of the Dutch employers who still had no a formal agreement around hybrid working in place at the start of this year. The bank also tried to call employees back to the office in 2025 .

Employees of ABN Amro told FD that this latest push to get workers back in the office stems from the new CEO Marguerite Bérard, who took office in the spring of 2025. She was reportedly surprised by the quiet office corridors of the bank’s headquarters in Amsterdam’s Zuidas district.

Some bank employees also question the productivity of remote workers, the newspaper wrote, complaining about colleagues skipping online meetings to walk their dogs or accept a package.

So ABN Amro now wants employees in-office for at least three of the five workdays in a week. The bank hopes that this will improve team spirit, according to FD. It's also hoping for a productivity boost amid its ongoing layoffs.

With its ongoing reorganization, the bank saw net profit increase to 781 million euros, 29 percent higher than the second quarter of 2025. A large part of the growth can be attributed to mortgages and loans to businesses. Earnings per share jumped by a third to 90 cents. The bank also completed its acquisition of NIBC.

The bank’s staff levels, especially external roles, fell across most departments as the bank also continues to increase its use of artificial intelligence. This despite hundreds more put to work in the Wealth Management department, where the bank saw “2.3 billion euros of core net new assets.”

Still, despite cutting the equivalent of around 2,000 jobs, the bank has only managed to marginally reduce operating expenses. The bank blamed this on inflation and salary increases secured by unions during collective bargaining negotiations. Operating expenses were down about 1 percent compared to last year, standing at 1.3 billion euros last quarter.

“We continued to integrate artificial intelligence (AI) into daily work across the bank, with almost 50 use cases in production. In the second quarter, we launched our first GenAI-powered client voice bot to answer client questions and provide guidance on selected topics,” said ABN Amro CEO Marguerite Bérard.

“We also introduced a GenAI knowledge assistant for Know Your Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) analysts, helping them access relevant policies, procedures and work instructions more easily.”

The bank also said it is not allocating a reserve of cash to potentially compensate two groups of institutional investors. They allege the bank’s failure to comply with anti-money laundering laws and regulations led to 400 million euros in losses from 2015 to 2022.

“ABN AMRO disputes these allegations and has not recognised a provision for this matter. No proceedings on the merits have been initiated yet by both groups of investors. One group of investors has filed a request for the disclosure of certain documents and preliminary witness hearings of certain former board members and employees of ABN AMRO. The district court recently denied this request in full,” the bank said.

evidence.title: Rabobank Euro To Dollar Forecast: EUR/USD To See 1.14 Before Recovery To 1.16
evidence.text:
Rabobank Euro To Dollar Forecast: EUR/USD To See 1.14 Before Recovery To 1.16

Rabobank's Euro recovery forecast depends on a retreat in Fed hike expectations, while the Iran war constrains near-term gains.

Rabobank has lowered its one-month Euro forecast from 1.16 to 1.14, while retaining a three-month recovery target of 1.16.

The Euro to US Dollar exchange rate ( EUR/USD ) stood near 1.1377 on Thursday, down 0.04% on the day after Wednesday's 0.58% decline.

The bank highlighted how far the Dollar's performance has departed from expectations:

"Clearly, the market had not expected that the USD would be entering the final quarter of the year on the front foot."

Rabobank argues that European growth has held up, but energy risks discourage investors from rebuilding Euro positions:

"That said, we retain the view that the EUR will struggle to find upside momentum during the duration of the Iran war and have revised down our 1 month forecast to 1.14 from 1.16."

That leaves even the reduced forecast slightly above spot, with June's annual low of 1.1325 just over half a cent away.

The bank estimates markets now assign roughly a 70% chance to an October Fed hike, following September’s increase.

Although the eurozone composite PMI rose to 53.1 in September, Rabobank says stronger US survey results have overshadowed Europe’s improvement.

Its recovery case rests on investors expecting more US tightening than the Fed ultimately delivers:

“Our expectation that EUR/USD will return to 1.16 on a 3 month view reflects the Rabobank house view that the market has priced in too much Fed policy tightening.”

That broadly aligns with ING’s 1.160 year-end call, discussed in our earlier comparison with Goldman Sachs .

Goldman’s three-month target is 1.14, falling to 1.12 at six and twelve months.

Rabobank’s 1.16 would require a recovery of approximately 2%, but the bank cautions:

“Next year’s French Presidential election may also limit potential for the EUR. We will be reviewing our EUR/USD forecasts in the coming weeks.”

evidence.title: Rabobank Sees Real Weakening to 5.35 as Rates Narrow
evidence.text:
Rabobank analysts Mauricio Une and Renan Alves highlight a divergence in monetary policy between the United States and Brazil. They point out that the Federal Reserve (Fed) increased its benchmark rate by 25 basis points and indicated a more restrictive policy path, while Brazil’s monetary policy committee, Copom, lowered the Selic rate to 13.75%. This combination has contributed to a softer outlook for the Brazilian Real (BRL) against the U.S. Dollar (USD).

Assessing the external environment, Une and Alves emphasize the Fed’s focus on containing inflationary pressures:

“Externally, in the United States, the Federal Reserve (Fed) raised interest rates by 25 bps and signaled a more restrictive monetary policy path to contain second-round inflationary effects. However, Rabobank believes that the stagflationary shock makes a single rate hike the more likely outcome, with any additional increase contingent on developments in the Middle East and the resilience of the U.S. economy.”

The BRL experienced a modest decline against the USD over the previous week, yet still compared favorably with many emerging peers. According to the analysts:

“The Brazilian real closed the previous week at BRL 5.1462 per USD, implying a 0.49% depreciation against the U.S. dollar over the week, ranking as the ninth-best performance among 24 emerging-market currencies.”

Rabobank’s outlook centers on shrinking rate spreads between Brazil and developed markets, combined with a potentially stronger USD and domestic fiscal challenges. The bank’s projection is summarized as follows:

“Given expectations of a narrower interest rate differential between Brazil and advanced economies throughout 2026, together with a potential global recovery of the U.S. dollar amid a fragile domestic fiscal backdrop in an election year, we expect the exchange rate to end the year at BRL 5.35 per USD.”

On this basis, Rabobank anticipates that the BRL will trade weaker against the USD into year-end, with USD/BRL moving from BRL 5.1462 per USD toward BRL 5.35 per USD.

evidence.title: Rabobank projects moderate supply, cautious demand and reshaped dairy trade through 2027
evidence.text:
Rabobank projects moderate supply, cautious demand and reshaped dairy trade through 2027

Rabobank ’s outlook for the international dairy market through the end of the current year and into 2027 describes a narrow balance between supply and consumption. Combined output from the seven largest exporting blocs is expected to expand at a restrained pace. The report also anticipates wholesale pricing shaped by cautious purchasing and financial restraint at farm level, rather than by a return to the high-surplus conditions seen in earlier periods.

Production prospects differ significantly by region. In the United States, improved returns relative to feed costs and stable feed-grain conditions have encouraged higher yields per cow. A limited supply of replacement heifers, however, restricts the pace at which the national herd can grow. The European Union faces a more constrained production setting, with environmental rules on emissions and nitrogen adding to structural pressure.

Milk deliveries in Oceania and in the southern South American countries of Uruguay and Argentina are recovering progressively. Rabobank’s assessment says those recoveries remain exposed to seasonal weather variation. The regional differences leave the major exporting blocs with uneven capacity to add supply even as the overall market expands moderately.

China is central to the report’s demand assessment. Domestic production of fresh milk has increased, while inventories of whole milk powder remain substantial. As a result, Chinese buying interest on international auction platforms has weakened. Exporting countries are therefore seeking alternative outlets in Southeast Asia, the Middle East, North Africa and Latin America. Consumption in those destinations is responsive, but buyers remain highly sensitive to the price per tonne.

Rabobank expects dairy commodities to perform differently according to their composition. Butterfat products and cheese retain a relatively firm pricing bias, supported by underlying demand from food-service businesses and the food industry in Western markets. Skimmed and whole milk powders face greater limits on price increases as large consumer-goods companies remain cautious and industrial inventories are rebuilt in key destinations.

For dairy chains and Mercosur exporters, the outlook places emphasis on financial discipline, wider destination portfolios and tight control of operating costs. The report says that international prices do not point to exponential increases and that macroeconomic volatility remains present. It identifies greater efficiency per litre, improved recovery of usable milk solids and a stronger focus on higher-value products as measures for farms and processors seeking to reduce exposure to bulk-commodity cycles.

evidence.title: Brazilian OJ Industry ‘Challenging,’ Rabobank Reports
evidence.text:
According to a September 2026 Rabobank report, the current environment for Brazilian orange juice (OJ) remains challenging for both farmers and the industry, with prices still low but starting to show some slightly positive signs. It reported that spot orange prices for the industry increased from BRL 25/box (approximately $4.30/box in U.S. dollars) in May to BRL 31/box (approximately $6.03/box in U.S. dollars) in August.

“This represents a slight price recovery, but levels remain below production costs for a significant share of growers,” Rabobank stated in its Brazil Agribusiness Quarterly report .

“FCOJ (frozen concentrated OJ) futures in New York have started to see some moderate gains to USD 1.58/lb in late-August, above the yearly low of USD 1.32/lb earlier in July,” Rabobank reported.

Regarding listed prices, FCOJ is trading near $2,800 per metric ton in Europe, while not-from-concentrate (NFC) is close to the $950 per metric ton level, according to the report.

“While the market understands that stocks are back close to normalized levels, there are concerns surrounding future production as a strong El Niño could have a significant impact on next year’s crop,” the report stated. “Additionally, demand in developed markets could start to show some traction if prices move slightly lower and some retail data is starting to show more stable volume numbers.”

Rabobank cited ample fruit availability in the current crop season as a positive factor for the OJ industry. That fruit availability will allow the industry to produce high-quality juice tailored to the specific requirements of bottlers, it stated.

“The missing piece for a recovery in demand, and eventually in prices across the value chain, remains the retail price of orange juice,” the report stated. It cited AC Nielsen data published by the Florida Department of Citrus showing that OJ retail prices in the United States are 8.5% higher than in the previous crop year, with volumes down by 6.4%. NFC prices are up by 10%, and volume is down by 3%. For reconstituted juice, prices are up by 1.9%, and volumes are down by 9.7%.

“On a positive note, prices have been flattening in recent weeks and volumes are starting to show more stability,” the Rabobank report stated. “Early signs are that demand could potentially be more stable, especially if prices remain flat or move lower.”

The report noted that signs of a strong El Niño pattern, along with extended dry spells at the end of winter and above-average temperatures for longer periods, could affect flowering for the 2027–28 crop season. “This, coupled with low grower margins and reduced investment in crop management, makes it likely that production will be lower in the next crop year,” the report stated.

For details on the current Brazilian orange crop, see the Fundecitrus forecast issued on Sept. 10.

evidence.title: Rabobank sees room for European tropical fruit production despite climate hurdles
evidence.text:
Rabobank sees room for European tropical fruit production despite climate hurdles

Europe’s tropical fruit boom may be pushing orchards beyond the Mediterranean’s traditional growing belt.

As demand for avocados, mangoes, passion fruit, and pitayas rises , Rabobank says climate pressures, water shortages, and production costs are prompting growers to explore new regions across Europe—even as those same constraints could limit the expansion.

Overall per capita consumption of fresh fruits and vegetables in the European Union has remained broadly flat at about 11.5 to 12.3 ounces per person per day over the past decade. Tropical fruit consumption, however, has continued to rise , driven mainly by avocados and mangoes , according to a September report by the bank’s RaboResearch division.

"Over the past three years, the average EU import unit value for all fresh fruits was around $0.62 per pound (€1.26/kg), compared with $1.25 per pound (€2.54/kg) for tropical fruits excluding bananas and pineapples,” the assessment notes.

Rabobank said the price difference could encourage European growers to move toward higher-value crops.

Climate pressures reshape tropical fruit supply

The continent currently relies on non-EU suppliers for about 90 percent of its tropical fruit. Rabobank said that dependence creates exposure to climate-related disruptions in key producing countries.

For example, Peru, the country bloc’s largest avocado supplier , has faced adverse weather conditions in recent years. The Andean country exported about 661,000 metric tons to the region in 2023.

"During the 2024 season, extreme temperatures contributed to average yield losses of around 40 percent across the Olmos region, one of Peru's largest avocado-producing areas," the document says.

Within Europe, commercial avocado and mango production remains concentrated in southern Spain , particularly Andalusia, Axarquía, and Granada, as well as Portugal’s Algarve region.

Land constraints and tighter water restrictions in these traditional production areas are encouraging growers to look toward areas such as Cádiz and Huelva in Spain and inland and northern parts of Portugal.

"More recently, production has started to expand beyond the Algarve into more northern and inland locations that were previously considered marginal because of low winter temperatures and frost risk," the report states.

Climate suitability alone does not guarantee that new production areas will become commercially viable, Rabobank warns.

Establishing new orchards requires substantial upfront investment , including several years before trees reach maturity, plus frost protection and automated packing infrastructure.

"The challenge is often the ability to aggregate sufficient production from numerous smallholders to justify these investments and support viable export-oriented value chains," Rabobank says.

Labor presents another challenge. Higher European wages make it difficult for local growers to compete with Latin American and African suppliers on volume and price. Instead, European production would need to bet on quality, freshness, and shorter supply chains to break into the global market.

Water availability could prove the most important constraint. Reliable irrigation infrastructure and water storage will be essential for commercial production in drought-prone Mediterranean regions, even where climate conditions become more favorable, according to Rabobank.

HELSINKI , July 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ --

Nordea Bank Abp Half year financial report 16 July 2026 at 7.30 EET

Return on equity 15.9% – earnings per share EUR 0.36. Nordea's return on equity for the quarter was 15.9%, reflecting strong performance and high profitability in a quarter where markets continued to be affected by the prolonged conflict in the Middle East. The cost-to-income ratio 2 was 44.0%, compared with 45.1% a year ago. Earnings per share were EUR 0.36, up 3% year on year.

Total iNordeancome up 4% year on year. Net interest income was down 1% year on year but up 1% quarter on quarter. Net fee and commission income was up 11% year on year, with savings income up 13% and growth across all fee categories. Net fair value result was very strong, up 11%. Costs excluding regulatory fees were flat when adjusted for foreign exchange effects, which drove a 2% increase. Operating profit was up 1% at EUR 1.6bn.

Business volume growth; AuM at record EUR 505bn. Corporate lending growth was strong, up 9%. Mortgage lending increased by 2% year on year, driven by continued growth in Sweden and Norway. Retail and corporate deposits were up 4% and 9%, respectively, and assets under management (AuM) increased by 16%, surpassing EUR 500bn.

Strong credit quality. Nordea's credit quality is very strong, with net loan losses and similar net result amounting to EUR 61m (6bp) for the quarter – well within the Group's long term expectation of 10bp.

Continued strong capital generation supporting growth. The CET1 ratio was 15.7% at the end of the quarter, 1.9 percentage points above the current regulatory requirement. Nordea's strong capital position and continued capital generation support lending growth and share buy-backs. Nordea's Board has decided to distribute a mid-year dividend for 2026 amounting to EUR 0.34 per share, which corresponds to approximately 50% of the Nordea Group's net profit 3 for the first half of 2026. The dividend record date is confirmed for 6 August 2026 and the dividend payment date will be 13 August or as soon as possible thereafter. The mid-year dividend is the first part of the total dividend distribution under Nordea's dividend policy, which stipulates a 60–70% payout ratio applicable to full-year profit.

Outlook for 2026: return on equity of greater than 15% (unchanged) and a cost-to-income ratio 2 of 44–45% (previously around 45%). Nordea has a strong and resilient business model, with a very well-diversified portfolio across the Nordic region. This enables the Group to support its customers and deliver high-quality earnings, with high profitability and low volatility, through the economic cycle. It also enables Nordea to continue to generate capital, seek opportunities to deploy it to drive growth, and distribute excess capital to shareholders in the form of share buy-backs.

(For further viewpoints, see the CEO comment. For further information on capital ratios see page 6, and for definitions see page 54, in the Q2 2026 report.)

Group quarterly results and key ratios 1

Total operating expenses excl. regulatory fees

Cost-to-income ratio with amortised regulatory fees, %

This was yet another strong quarter for Nordea. We drove good momentum across the business, continued to attract new customers and deepen existing relationships, and achieved high growth in savings and investments – all of which helped us return to year-on-year growth in total income. We are making good progress in implementing our 2030 strategy and it is starting to show through in our performance.

Of course, the world around us remains uncertain. The conflict in the Middle East has raised risks for the global economy. Even though it is too early to judge the extent of the impact, European countries in general, and the Nordics in particular, have so far weathered higher energy costs and other challenges well.

Nordic corporates continue to invest. During the quarter, we increased both corporate lending and deposits by 9% year on year, building on the strong start to the year. The higher activity reflects confidence among Nordic businesses, especially large corporates. At the same time, it shows how we are using our unique Nordic scale, strong relationships and competitive offering to capture growth opportunities.

Lending to households increased. The Nordic housing markets kept up their gradual recovery, although the pace remains slow. Mortgage volumes were up 2% year on year, led by Sweden and Norway, two strategic growth markets for Nordea. Retail deposits increased by 4%. Demand for our savings and investment products was likewise robust. During the quarter, customers continued to invest through our retail funds and pension products, and we welcomed a significant number of new private banking customers – leading to solid net flows. Assets under management (AuM) increased by 16%, to a record high of EUR 505bn, with margins stabilising.

Total income grew by 4% year on year to exceed EUR 3bn – a level of quarterly income we had previously reached only during 2024, at the peak of the higher-rate environment. This highlights not only the strength of our diversified business model but also our focused, growth-orientated 2030 strategy. Net fee and commission income increased by 11% and we had a very strong net fair value result. Net interest income development was also positive. While down 1% year on year due to lower policy rates, it was up 1% quarter on quarter: the first increase since rates started coming down two years ago.

With costs flat year on year excluding foreign exchange effects, we grew income faster than costs, which is always our aim. We continue to drive productivity gains across the business and are further expanding the use of artificial intelligence in our core business processes. At the same time, we are investing substantially in strategic initiatives focused on growth and Nordic scale. In the second quarter the cost-to-income ratio improved to 44.0% from 45.1%. Operating profit was EUR 1.6bn and return on equity was 15.9%.

Credit and asset quality remain very strong. Net loan losses and similar net result amounted to EUR 61m, or 6bp. The strength of our credit portfolio continues to result in very low loan losses, well within the Group's long term expectation of around 10bp.

In Personal Banking we drove solid lending growth and strong fee income. Total lending volumes increased by 1% in local currencies year on year and deposit volumes were up 4%. In Sweden, our fastest-growing market, we increased our mortgage market share once again. Growing numbers of customers are choosing Nordea for a broader range of their financial needs. To further attract savings flows, we launched a competitively priced Nordic index fund giving investors an easy and cost-effective way to invest in Nordic companies. Recurring savings inflows were up 8% year on year.

In Asset & Wealth Management we continued to drive solid AuM and income growth. Additional investments in our advisory capabilities, brand and digital sales supported another strong quarter in Private Banking, one of our strategic growth areas, where net flows amounted to EUR 1bn. Our Empower Europe fund, which invests in the drivers of Europe's transformation, continued to perform well. A year on from its launch, the fund has reached over EUR 860m in AuM, making it one of our most successful launches ever and demonstrating how strongly customers support the theme. Our international channels, which have generally performed well since last summer, saw some outflows as a result of the uncertainty in the Middle East and increased rates.

In Business Banking we delivered strong volume growth across all home markets, with lending and deposits up 6% and 3%, respectively. We continue to invest in our digital capabilities to make Nordea the easiest bank to deal with for small and mid-sized businesses. We are seeing good traction: customer growth accelerated this quarter. Improved onboarding and greater automation have played a part in that, making it easier for prospective customers to start banking with us. Our Nordea Business mobile app also reached an all-time-high Nordic rating, with the number of users up 10% from a year ago.

In Large Corporates & Institutions we continued to proactively support customers with their growth plans. Lending remained strong, up 14%, and deposits were up 17%. Our scale and compelling offering are driving diversified income growth. Debt Capital Markets activity remained high and we arranged more than 200 transactions during the quarter. Activity also picked up in the equity capital markets, where we facilitated several high-profile transactions, as well as in mergers and acquisitions.

Our capital position is strong, with a CET1 ratio of 15.7%, and we continue to deploy capital for profitable growth. As previously communicated, we will pay dividends twice a year going forward. Nordea's Board has decided to pay a mid-year dividend – in August – of EUR 0.34 per share, corresponding to approximately 50% of the Nordea Group's net profit for the first half of 2026.

We go into the second half of the year with confidence. The business is performing very well and our strategy execution is on course, with visible progress across all initiatives. The Nordic economies are also showing their strength. We are seeing encouraging signs of increased corporate investment and activity across the region, and Nordea is well placed to support customers as they pursue new growth opportunities.

Our strong performance and position are reflected in improved full-year 2026 guidance. We continue to expect a return on equity of greater than 15%, while we now expect a cost-to-income ratio of 44–45%.

Our ambition is to become the undisputed best-performing financial services group in the Nordics.

Frank Vang-Jensen President and Group CEO
