evidence.title: Die Moneta-Money-Bank-Aktie bleibt im Fokus tschechischer Finanzanleger
evidence.text:
Die Moneta Money Bank-Aktie (ISIN CZ0008040318) steht am 19.09.2026 bei tschechischen Finanzanlegern im Zeichen von Effizienz- und Digitalisierungsprojekten, die die Ertragsbasis des Instituts stützen sollen. Ein aktueller Bericht zu Technologieeinsätzen im Bankensektor hebt hervor, dass Moneta Money Bank mit neuen Marketing- und Entscheidungsplattformen Kampagnen bis zu viermal schneller ausrollen kann als zuvor, was die kommerzielle Schlagkraft des Retail- und SME-Geschäfts erhöht und mittelfristig die Profitabilität verbessern dürfte.

Ein Technologie-Analysebericht zum Einsatz von Customer-Intelligence-Plattformen im Bankensektor nennt Moneta Money Bank explizit als Beispiel für deutlich gesteigerte Kampagnen-Geschwindigkeit: Dort wird von einem bis zu vierfach schnelleren Deployment von Marketingkampagnen gesprochen, der Zeitbedarf sinkt von mehreren Wochen auf wenige Stunden. Diese Beschleunigung ist vor allem für das Retailgeschäft relevant, in dem Moneta Money Bank Kredite, Konten und Zahlungsdienste an Privatkunden verkauft; je schneller Angebote getestet und skaliert werden können, desto effizienter lässt sich das Produktportfolio aussteuern.

Für die operative Steuerung bedeutet eine solche Effizienzsteigerung, dass die Bank bei gleichem Kostenblock mehr zielgerichtete Kampagnen fahren kann und damit potenziell höhere Gebühren- und Zinseinnahmen generiert. Aus der Perspektive von Anlegern ist dies ein wichtiger Baustein, um die Eigenkapitalrendite zu stabilisieren oder zu steigern, insbesondere in einem Umfeld, in dem der tschechische Bankenmarkt im Wettbewerb mit internationalen Großbanken steht. Die Bewertung der Aktie hängt dabei nicht nur an klassischen Kennzahlen wie dem Ergebnis je Aktie und der Kosten-Ertrags-Quote, sondern zunehmend auch an der Frage, wie schnell Institute neue datengetriebene Geschäftsmodelle umsetzen können.

Ertrags- und Kostenkennzahlen als Bewertungsbasis

Zu den jüngsten verfügbaren Finanzkennzahlen zählen das Nettozinsergebnis und die Provisionsüberschüsse aus dem Retail- und SME-Segment, die in der jüngsten Berichtsperiode gegenüber dem Vorjahr zulegen konnten. Bei vielen mitteleuropäischen Banken sind Zinsüberschüsse im laufenden Jahr durch das weiterhin erhöhte Zinsniveau gesteigert worden, während Provisionsüberschüsse aus Zahlungsverkehr und Vermögensverwaltung durch die stärkere Nutzung digitaler Kanäle wachsen. Für Moneta Money Bank ist entscheidend, dass das Wachstum auf der Ertragsseite die Belastungen auf der Kostenseite kompensiert, etwa durch höhere IT-Investitionen und regulatorische Anforderungen.

Ein zentrales Fundamentalkriterium für die Bewertung von Bankaktien ist neben dem Ergebnis die Kapitalausstattung. Die harte Kernkapitalquote (CET1) liegt bei mitteleuropäischen Retailbanken häufig im niedrigen bis mittleren zweistelligen Prozentbereich und dient als Puffer gegen Kreditrisiken und Marktvolatilität. Für Investoren, die die Moneta Money Bank-Aktie halten oder neu einsteigen wollen, ist die Kombination aus solider Kapitalquote und gesundem Kreditportfolio ein wichtiger Faktor, der über die Dividendenfähigkeit entscheidet. Historisch orientieren sich tschechische Banken an Ausschüttungsquoten zwischen einem Drittel und der Hälfte des Jahresgewinns, wobei die konkrete Quote von regulatorischen Vorgaben und geplanten Wachstumsinvestitionen abhängt.

Dividendenprofil und Vergleich zu regionalen Peers

Die Dividende ist bei der Moneta Money Bank-Aktie ein wesentlicher Bestandteil der Gesamtrendite. In den vergangenen Geschäftsjahren haben tschechische Banken häufig Dividendenrenditen im mittleren einstelligen Prozentbereich geboten, was im Vergleich zum allgemeinen europäischen Bankenindex attraktiv wirkt. Für Anleger, die auf laufende Ausschüttungen setzen, kommt es darauf an, dass die Bank ihr Gewinnniveau hält oder ausbaut und gleichzeitig keine größeren Kapitalerhöhungen notwendig werden, die die Rendite verwässern würden.

Im Vergleich zu regionalen Peers wie großen tschechischen oder mitteleuropäischen Bankengruppen ist Moneta Money Bank stärker im Privatkundengeschäft verankert. Das bedeutet, dass Zinsmargen auf Konsumentenkredite, Hypotheken und kleine Gewerbekredite besonders wichtig sind. Steigen Refinanzierungskosten schneller als die Kreditmargen, kann dies die Profitabilität drücken; umgekehrt profitieren Institute wie Moneta Money Bank von einem Umfeld, in dem Leitzinsen stabil bleiben, während die Nachfrage nach Krediten und Zahlungsdiensten nicht einbricht. Auf dieser Basis wird die Aktie häufig im Verhältnis zum Buchwert der Bank bewertet, wobei ein Kurs-Buchwert-Verhältnis im Bereich um eins oder leicht darüber in der Region nicht unüblich ist.

Zu den zentralen Risiken für die Moneta Money Bank-Aktie zählt ein möglicher Umschwung im Zinsumfeld. Sinkende Leitzinsen können die Zinsmargen drücken, wenn Kreditzinsen schneller fallen als die Vergütung für Einlagen. Für tschechische Banken ist zudem die Entwicklung der Inflation und der Lohnkosten entscheidend, da sie die operative Kostenbasis beeinflussen. Ein weiterer Risikofaktor ergibt sich aus strengeren regulatorischen Vorgaben, etwa höheren Kapitalanforderungen oder zusätzlichen Berichtspflichten, die wiederum Investitionen in IT und Compliance erfordern.

Ein aktueller Technologiebericht weist darauf hin, dass die Einführung komplexer Daten- und Entscheidungsplattformen zwar kurzfristig hohe Projektkosten verursacht, langfristig aber Effizienzgewinne ermöglicht, die diese Kosten überkompensieren können. Für Moneta Money Bank ist diese Balance besonders wichtig: Werden die erwarteten Effizienzgewinne tatsächlich erreicht und verbessern sich Kennzahlen wie die Kosten-Ertrags-Quote um einige Prozentpunkte, kann dies den Spielraum für Dividenden und Eigenkapitalrenditen erweitern. Bleiben die Effekte dagegen hinter den Erwartungen zurück, besteht die Gefahr, dass hohe IT-Aufwendungen die kurzfristige Profitabilität belasten.

Für Anleger ist neben den Fundamentaldaten das aktuelle Kursniveau der Moneta Money Bank-Aktie entscheidend. Ein Kurs nahe dem Buchwert der Bank signalisiert, dass der Markt von einer soliden, aber nicht überdurchschnittlichen Wertschöpfung ausgeht; liegt der Kurs deutlich über dem Buchwert, wird dem Institut eine überdurchschnittliche Profitabilität und Wachstumsfähigkeit zugetraut. Liegt der Kurs dagegen klar darunter, preist der Markt höhere Risiken im Kreditportfolio oder strukturelle Ertragsschwächen ein. Die Kursentwicklung im laufenden Jahr zeigt, dass tschechische Finanzwerte im Umfeld europäischer Banken insgesamt eine moderate Performance aufweisen, wobei einzelne Institute stärker schwanken als der Gesamtmarkt.

Ein quantifizierter Blick auf die Gesamtrendite ergibt sich aus der Kombination von Kursveränderung und Dividende: Steigt der Kurs beispielsweise um 5 % im Jahr und liegt die Dividendenrendite bei 4 %, entspricht dies einer Gesamtrendite von 9 %. Bleibt der Kurs dagegen unverändert und wird eine Dividende von 5 % ausgeschüttet, erzielen Anleger dennoch eine respektable Ertragskomponente. Für Moneta Money Bank hängt diese Rechnung davon ab, wie stark Effizienzgewinne aus Digitalisierung, Kreditwachstum und stabile Kapitalausstattung zusammenwirken.

Kurzfristige und langfristige Perspektiven

Kurzfristig wird der Kurs der Moneta Money Bank-Aktie vor allem von makroökonomischen Daten, Zinsentscheidungen und branchenspezifischen Nachrichten beeinflusst. Veröffentlicht die Bank solide Quartalszahlen mit einem Gewinnanstieg im hohen einstelligen oder niedrigen zweistelligen Prozentbereich gegenüber dem Vorjahr, kann dies zu positiven Kursreaktionen führen. Fallen die Zahlen hingegen schwächer aus, etwa wenn der Gewinn um mehrere Prozent gegenüber dem Vorjahresquartal sinkt, reagieren Investoren oft mit Gewinnmitnahmen, was sich in einer geringeren Bewertung niederschlägt.

Langfristig steht für Moneta Money Bank die Frage im Mittelpunkt, ob das Institut seine digitale Transformation nutzen kann, um das Geschäftsmodell resilient zu machen. Werden Kampagnen, Kreditentscheidungen und Kundenansprache weiter automatisiert und datengetrieben ausgerichtet, kann dies die operative Effizienz nachhaltig verbessern und die Kosten-Ertrags-Quote senken. Gelingt es zudem, das Kreditrisiko stabil zu halten und Ausfälle im Rahmen zu lassen, bleibt die Eigenkapitalrendite attraktiv und stützt die Bereitschaft des Managements, eine verlässliche Dividendenpolitik zu verfolgen. Für konservative Anleger ist diese Kombination aus Ausschüttungsstabilität und moderatem Wachstum häufig entscheidender als kurzfristige Kursschwankungen.

Zum Abschluss bleibt der Blick auf die tagesaktuellen Marktdaten: Die Moneta Money Bank-Aktie wird vor allem an der Prager Börse gehandelt, ergänzt um Listings auf regionalen Handelsplätzen. Entscheidend ist, dass der jeweilige Schlusskurs im Verhältnis zum 52-Wochen-Hoch und -Tief liegt; notiert die Aktie etwa 10 % unter ihrem Jahreshoch und 20 % über ihrem Jahrestief, deutet dies auf eine Mitte des Bewertungskorridors hin. Gemeinsam mit der Marktkapitalisierung, die sich im Milliardenbereich der Landeswährung bewegt, ergibt sich für Anleger ein Bild der Größenordnung und Marktrelevanz des Instituts.

Moneta Money Bank AS ( XPRA:MONET ) reported a net profit of CZK3.3 billion for the first half of 2026, marking an 8% improvement compared to the previous year.

The bank's operating income increased to CZK7.2 billion, driven by growth in net interest income and net fee and commission income.

Moneta Money Bank AS achieved a capital adequacy ratio of 20%, an improvement of 4.5 percentage points, supported by the issuance of a EUR150 million AT1 instrument.

The bank's loan portfolio grew by more than 9%, reaching CZK310 billion, with a focus on high-margin products.

The non-performing loan (NPL) ratio dropped to 0.9%, the lowest level recorded, with a strong NPL coverage of 124.5%.

Operating expenses slightly increased by 0.2% to CZK2.9 billion, indicating challenges in cost management.

The bank's cost of risk increased to 28 basis points, driven by a commercial default and higher new lending volumes.

There was a decline in operating income from financial derivatives, partially offset by higher client FX income.

The CET1 ratio, although in excess of management targets, is under pressure due to strong loan growth and rising RWA density.

The bank's retail deposit base only slightly increased by 1.4%, reflecting a cautious approach to deposit growth amid competitive market conditions.

Q : With the excess capital and strong loan growth, is there a possibility of proposing an extra dividend in the second half of 2026? Also, can you address the rising RWA density and any potential macro model changes due to geopolitical risks? A : Tomas Spurny, CEO: We have optimized our capital structure, creating room for a potential dividend. We will review all relevant factors at the end of the third quarter to decide on an interim distribution. Regarding RWA density, it's part of our strategy due to product mix changes. We are considering securitizations to alleviate capital pressure. As for macro models, we will review input variables based on the Czech National Bank's forecast in August, but currently, no adverse changes are anticipated.

Q : Can you elaborate on the single case default provision and any other expected effects on the portfolio? A : Carl Voekt, Chief Risk Officer: The single commercial default was a one-off fraud-driven case requiring 100% coverage. There are no other similar exposures on our radar. We will review macro models in the third quarter, but current inputs do not suggest any adverse changes.

Q : What is the expected composition of loan growth, particularly for mortgages, and how do you view the loan-to-deposit ratio? A : Tomas Spurny, CEO: Mortgage growth is not our primary focus; we aim to grow it in line with the balance sheet and funding base. The loan-to-deposit ratio, currently at 68%, can increase, but we will adjust targets if necessary to maintain liquidity.

Q : How does Moneta plan to manage the increasing loan-to-deposit ratio while being cautious on deposit growth? A : Tomas Spurny, CEO: Historically, the bank operated at a 90-95% loan-to-deposit ratio. We aim to keep it below 78% and will adjust based on liquidity and market conditions.

Q : Can you provide insights into the bank's strategy for securitizations and its impact on capital management? A : Tomas Spurny, CEO: We are working on a securitization project to create space for improved bank performance. This will be pursued if there is demand for synthetic securitization, likely throughout 2027.

evidence.title: Moneta Money Bank: Faster marketing campaigns, smarter decisions
evidence.text:
Moneta Money Bank: Faster marketing campaigns, smarter decisions

Modernization journey with SAS shortens go-live time for real-time marketing campaigns: sees significant increases in digital sales and conversion rates

CARY, N.C., April 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Moneta Money Bank, one of the leading retail banks in the Czech Republic, has dramatically shortened go-live times for real-time marketing campaigns through its marketing modernization journey. Working with Trask, a global technology and consulting company, Moneta Money Bank is modernizing its marketing ecosystem with SAS Customer Intelligence 360 and SAS Intelligent Decisioning , powered by Amazon Web Services, to transform how it connects with its 1.6 million customers.

Why it matters In the highly competitive Czech banking market, where 20 retail banks serve a population of 10 million, Moneta Money Bank is redefining customer engagement. Using SAS Customer Intelligence 360 the bank is delivering personalization at scale, increasing its competitive advantage.

Key outcomes with new technical setup including SAS Customer Intelligence 360 Up to 4x faster campaign deployment – Manual processes replaced with automated (less IT dependent), real-time decisioning campaigns that once took weeks and now take hours Higher digital conversion – Real-time personalization drives a measurable boost in digital sales and conversion rates. Operational efficiency – Able to easily measure and decommission underperforming campaigns and free up times and resources to focus on experimentation.

From weeks to hours: Real-time personalization in action Moneta Money Bank is adding new capabilities such as processing millions of transactions daily, using decision rules created in SAS Intelligent Decisioning to deliver the right message at the right moment. For example, when a customer purchases an airline ticket, the bank can deliver a tailored travel insurance offer within 30 seconds via a push notification or in-app banner.

"Campaigns that once took weeks now launch in just hours with the help of SAS Customer Intelligence 360," said Jan Zdobinský, Senior Manager of Retail Development & CRM at Moneta Money Bank. "This shift has delivered way faster go-live times for real-time marketing campaigns, driving higher conversion rates across digital channels. We can now create contextual, real-time financial experiences to help us innovate faster and improve customer experience."

"Automated decisioning to fuel emerging channel personalization is certainly the future of customer engagement – and Moneta is leading the way," said Jonathan Moran, Head of MarTech Solutions Marketing at SAS. "It's great to see the strong collaboration between all parties to deliver such exceptional results relating to both customer experience improvement and marketing process automation,"

Omnichannel strategy and ROI Moneta already integrated SAS SDK directly into its mobile banking app – where ROI potential is highest – and plans to extend the capabilities to its call center and 100+ physical branches for a seamless omnichannel experience.

Agility through experimentation With SAS Customer Intelligence 360, Moneta´s aim is to run frequent A/B tests and hypothesis-driven experiments, enabling rapid optimization and innovation. This agility supports Moneta's strategy and commitment to smarter, faster customer experiences.

evidence.title: Investuje len 25 % Slovákov. Tatra banka spustila bezplatný kurz o investovaní, ktorý to môže zmeniť
evidence.text:
Tatra banka prichádza s novinkou, ktorá môže zmeniť, ako Slováci zaobchádzajú so svojimi peniazmi. Spustila vzdelávaciu platformu Invest Academy, ktorá v deviatich online lekciách vysvetľuje základy investovania. Kurz je úplne zadarmo a otvorený pre klientov aj neklientov banky. Prečo s tým banka prichádza práve teraz? Podľa tlačovej správy Tatra banky dnes na Slovensku investuje len štvrtina ľudí . Pritom by to mohli robiť takmer dve tretiny obyvateľov.

Tatra banka zistila, že Slovákov nebrzdí nezáujem, ale strach z investovania

Prečo teda väčšina stojí bokom? Prieskum, ktorý si dala Tatra banka vypracovať, priniesol prekvapivú odpoveď.

Ľudia o investovanie záujem majú. Brzdí ich hlavne nedostatok informácií , neistota, ako investičné produkty vlastne fungujú, a obavy z rizika.

Jednoducho povedané, mnohí by chceli začať, len nevedia ako.

Do ETF viete investovať od malých súm. Zdroj: shutterstock.com/TopMicrobialStock

Peniaze na účte potichu strácajú hodnotu

Čakanie však niečo stojí. Podľa Štatistického úradu SR dosiahla inflácia v auguste 2026 medziročne 3,1 % . Za prvých osem mesiacov roka boli ceny v priemere o 3,6 % vyššie ako rok predtým.

Čo to znamená v praxi? Ak máte úspory odložené na účte bez úroku, o rok si za ne kúpite menej. Práve tomu, prečo peniaze časom strácajú hodnotu, sa venuje aj jedna z lekcií nového kurzu.

Výplaty Slovákov nestíhajú za infláciou. Zdroj: shutterstock.com/fizkes

Čo vás naučí Tatra banka v Invest Academy

Platforma Invest Academy ponúka deväť lekcií, ktoré si prejdete vlastným tempom. Je určená začiatočníkom aj mierne pokročilým. Naučí vás napríklad:

Videami vás prevedie Marek Prokopec , riaditeľ spoločnosti Tatra Asset Management. S investovaním na Slovensku má skúsenosti viac ako 25 rokov a napísal aj knihu Koľko kam.

„Na úspešné investovanie dnes naozaj nepotrebujete veľa peňazí a ani doktorát z ekonómie. Stačí poznať niekoľko základných princípov, začať čím skôr a investovať pravidelne,” povedal Prokopec.

Kurz sa nevyhýba ani témam, ktoré ľudí od investovania najčastejšie odháňajú. Hovorí o mýtoch, výkyvoch na trhoch aj o strachu. Jedna z lekcií otvorene pripomína, že „najväčším nepriateľom investora je investor sám. Presnejšie jeho emócie”. Ukazuje, ako nepodľahnúť panike ani lákadlu rýchleho zisku.

Ďalšia lekcia vysvetľuje, že rozloženie peňazí medzi viac aktív je dôležitejšie ako hľadanie jedného zázračného tipu. Práve táto diverzifikácia je základom dlhodobého budovania majetku.

Peniaze a ich správne investovanie. Zdroj: shutterstock.com/marekusz

Tatra banka pridáva aj slovník do e-mailu

Kurz nie je jediná novinka. Banka spúšťa aj newsletter Live Invest Academy , ktorý bude raz mesačne prinášať prehľad diania na finančných trhoch, a jeho menšiu verziu Mini Invest Academy.

Začínajúci investori si môžu nechať poslať aj investičný slovník, v ktorom dostanú e-mailom 20 základných pojmov vysvetlených ľudskou rečou.

Investovanie nie je výsada bohatých ani ekonómov. Kto ešte nemá odložené peniaze na horšie časy, mal by začať práve tam. Ako to zvládnuť v praxi, ukazuje aj náš príbeh Prvá finančná rezerva: Ako sa mi podarilo odložiť prvých 5 000 € .

Tri štvrtiny Slovákov zatiaľ neinvestujú. Otázka znie, či patríte medzi nich aj vy. Deväť bezplatných lekcií môže byť prvým krokom k tomu, aby to tak nezostalo.

Vyštudovala som financie, bankovníctvo a investovanie a tieto témy sú pre mňa viac než len práca. Sledujem bankový trh, verejné financie aj finančné nástrahy dnešnej doby.

Na Kryptomagazine nájdete originálne spravodajstvo o kryptomenách tvorené odborníkmi, ktorí z tohto magazínu spravili najlepší zdroj informácií o digitálnych menách a decentralizovaných technológiách.

Finančné rozdielové zmluvy sú zložité nástroje a sú spojené s vysokým rizikom rýchlych finančných strát v dôsledku pákového efektu. Na 75 % účtov retailových investorov dochádza k finančným stratám pri obchodovaní s finančnými rozdielovými zmluvami u tohto poskytovateľa. Mali by ste zvážiť, či chápete, ako finančné rozdielové zmluvy fungujú, a či si môžete dovoliť podstúpiť vysoké riziko, že utrpíte finančné straty.

evidence.title: Tatra banka je slovenský klenot bankovníctva. Dosiahla rekordný zisk 265,9 milióna eur a 27 ocenení
evidence.text:
Tatra banka dosiahla v roku 2025 konsolidovaný zisk po zdanení 265,9 milióna eur, čo je o desať percent viac ako rok predtým. Konkurenčná 365.bank medzitým rozšírila portfólio o poistné produkty ČSOB Poisťovne a zaznamenala najlepší rating vo svojej histórii.

Objem úverov klientom Tatra banky stúpol medziročne o 1,7 miliardy eur. Rast o 11,4 % sprevádzal aj nárast čistých úrokových výnosov o 12,5 %. Vklady klientov sa vyšplhali na 17,2 miliardy eur, čo predstavuje takmer desaťpercentný nárast. Banka si pritom udržala rating A3 s pozitívnym výhľadom od agentúry Moody’s.

Medzi inováciami Tatra banky vyčnieva produkt nazvaný Digitálna hypotéka TB. Klient si hypotekárny úver vybaví kompletne cez mobilnú aplikáciu, vrátane nahrávania dokumentov a sledovania stavu žiadosti, bez osobnej návštevy pobočky až do podpisu zmluvy. Služba tak funguje prakticky nepretržite. Banka zároveň zjednodušila otváranie účtov pre podnikateľov a právnické osoby, ktoré taktiež preniesla do aplikácie.

Osobitný krok urobila v súvislosti so zákonom o dani z finančných transakcií. Ako jediná banka na Slovensku preplatila živnostníkom transakčnú daň a darovala im účet bez poplatkov na tri roky.

Tatra banka získala v roku 2025 celkovo 27 ocenení. Magazín The Banker jej udelil titul Banka roka 2025, Global Finance ju zaradil medzi najbezpečnejšie banky a ocenili aj jej inovácie v regióne. Ďalšie uznania sa týkali digitálnych riešení a privátneho bankovníctva.

evidence.title: Tatra banka šokovala konkurenciu. Spustila službu, ktorá nemá konkurenciu
evidence.text:
Tatra banka spravila krok, ktorý sa na prvé počutie môže javiť ako nenápadná digitalizácia zákazníckej podpory. V praxi však ide o zmenu, ktorá ovplyvňuje spôsob, akým klienti riešia svoje bankové záležitosti. Služba Podpora na diaľku, doteraz vyhradená len pre prémiových klientov, je po novom dostupná pre všetkých. Bez rozdielov ,bez podmienok, bez výnimiek.

Banka tým reaguje na realitu, ktorú dnes pozná každý klient digitálneho bankovníctva: aplikácie sú nabité funkcionalitou, no stačí jeden nejasný krok a človek sa ocitne v slepej uličke. Telefonát s operátorom často končí opisovaním obrazovky slovami, čo je často neefektívne. Presne tento problém chce Tatra banka odstrániť.

Tatra banka oficiálne potvrdila vo svojej tlačovej správe, že Podpora na diaľku je po novom dostupná pre celé portfólio klientov. Služba, ktorú si ešte donedávna mohli vyskúšať len prémioví zákazníci, je tak sprístupnená všetkým. Dôvod je jednoduchý. Rastúci dopyt po rýchlej, zrozumiteľnej a praktickej digitálnej pomoci.

Zmena má jasný cieľ, a to šetriť čas a zjednodušiť riešenie problémov. Ak banka dokáže vyriešiť záležitosť priamo počas jedného telefonátu, bez nutnosti návštevy pobočky, znamená to jednoduchší proces pre klienta aj banku. Skrátka, menej slov, viac obrazu.

Podstata služby stojí na tzv. co-browsingu. Počas hovoru s kontaktným centrom DIALOG Live môže klient zdieľať obrazovku svojej mobilnej aplikácie Tatra banky. Bankový pracovník vidí len to, čo mu klient výslovne povolí, a krok za krokom ho naviguje priamo v aplikácii.

Namiesto zdĺhavého vysvetľovania tak prichádza vizuálne riešenie. Klient presne vie, kam kliknúť, čo nastaviť a kde sa nachádza hľadaná funkcia. Všetko prebieha priamo počas hovoru.

Ako uviedla Eva Fedorová z tímu rozvoja kontaktného centra, služba má medzi prémiovými klientmi veľmi dobrý ohlas. „ Som veľmi rada, že funkcionalita, ktorá má skvelý ohlas medzi našimi prémiovými klientmi, umožní odteraz našim kolegom z kontaktného centra DIALOG Live sprevádzať aplikáciou Tatra banky všetkých našich klientov, “ povedala.

Pri zdieľaní obrazovky sa prirodzene vynára otázka bezpečnosti. Tatra banka na ňu odpovedá jednoznačne. Technológia vznikla v spolupráci so švajčiarskou spoločnosťou Unblu a funguje výhradne v šifrovanom prostredí.

Bankár nikdy nevidí PIN kódy , heslá ani čísla platobných kariet. Klient má po celý čas plnú kontrolu nad tým, čo zdieľa.

Podpora na diaľku pomáha pri kontrole kartových transakcií, realizácii prevodov, správe trvalých príkazov a inkás. Rovnako aj pri úprave limitov na kartách, nastavovaní aplikácie, push notifikácií či vyhľadávaní a podpisovaní dokumentov.

Tatra banka týmto krokom ukazuje, že digitálne bankovníctvo môže byť jednoduchšie a dostupnejšie. Pomoc prichádza priamo vtedy, keď ju klient potrebuje, po novom priamo na obrazovke jeho telefónu.

evidence.title: Tatra banka zlacňuje hypotéky: Klienti môžu využiť mimoriadnu zľavu

Tatra banka prichádza s ponukou, aká sa len tak nevidí. evidence.title: Citi CEO Expects ‘Tsunami’ of Patches Ahead of AI Guardrails
evidence.text:
Citi CEO Expects ‘Tsunami’ of Patches Ahead of AI Guardrails

Citi CEO Jane Fraser says that companies are racing to enhance their cyber defences as AI models are becoming even more powerful and are running the risk of performing fully automated attacks .

“There is a race to defend and shore up all of the firm’s perimeters and there is a tsunami of patching going on in the world at the moment,” Jane says.

Earlier this year, Anthropic released its much-anticipated Mythos model, a system that the company itself warned had the power to establish a new era of AI cybersecurity risk.

Referring to the Mythos release, Jane says: “That was not a good day.”

At that time, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and then-Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell summoned Wall Street leaders to a meeting about the model, urging them to bolster their digital systems as more powerful AI models are developed.

Since then, several AI models from firms like Google and Anthropic have independently carried out automated attacks on other companies.

Executives like Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei have since highlighted the need to slow AI development and claim the firm will implement new safety steps such as third-party technical evaluators.

There is a race to defend and shore up all of the firm’s perimeters and there is a tsunami of patching going on in the world at the moment.”

Earlier this month, former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon raised concerns about the risks of AI, warning that without proper guardrails, the technology could prove disruptive and, at worst, fatal to the global population by the end of the decade.

In response, NVIDIA’s CEO, Jensen Huang , says the technology doesn’t pose a threat to humanity.

He adds: “2030 is not going to be the end of the world. There is 0% chance that's going to be the end of the world. Scaring people is unnecessary. It is irresponsible.”

Jensen has also rejected calls to slow down AI development, claiming that companies who want an AI slowdown could be seeking liability protections for harms their products may cause.

However, mirroring Jane’s concerns, David Solomon, CEO of Goldman Sachs, says he believes a slowdown is necessary, but disagrees with industry figures like Jacob regarding the claim that the technology could prove fatal for humanity.

He adds he is “highly confident humanity will be here and that we’ll all be participating actively”.

In terms of the technology, the issue of logistics has moved from the chips to the energy required to power AI.

“The bottleneck has moved from chips into energy,” Jane adds. “We’re seeing enormous demand for energy around the world.”

Despite NVIDIA’s rejection of an AI slowdown, several major tech companies like OpenAI, Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon are also calling for an industry-wide defensive framework to combat potentially dangerous AI attacks in the future.

In a joint letter, the companies – along with more than 100 others – say there is a limited amount of time to “make our world much more secure” in the face of more powerful AI models .

“In the coming months, AI-enabled cyberattacks will become far more widespread as models around the world become increasingly capable,” the letter says.

It also calls on world leaders to expedite trusted access programmes, which give certain enterprises access to more powerful AI models ahead of use by the general public, and for all other businesses and governments to “make cyber defence an immediate leadership priority”.

evidence.title: Citigroup Inc. stock edges lower as CEO warns of AI-driven cyber risks
evidence.text:
Citigroup Inc. stock (ISIN US1729674242) has slipped back from its recent attempt to clear the USD 140 mark on the New York Stock Exchange in mid-September 2026, leaving the large US bank trading below a potential breakout level as of September 21, 2026. According to an analysis on September 21, 2026, the shares failed to sustain a move above a prior peak near USD 140.44 and retreated toward a key technical support zone around USD 131.38 on the NYSE, raising the risk of a deeper correction if that level gives way.

CEO flags AI-driven cyber risk as new theme

The latest fundamental talking point for Citigroup Inc. stock comes from comments by Chief Executive Officer Jane Fraser, who on September 20, 2026 warned that increasingly powerful artificial-intelligence models are intensifying cyber risks for global companies. As Bloomberg reported on September 20, 2026, Fraser told the Qatar Economic Forum held in New York that there is a race to defend and shore up firms' perimeters and that a 'tsunami of patching' is underway as companies rush to update systems against AI-enabled cyber attacks.

According to Telangana Today on September 21, 2026, Fraser emphasized that AI models are becoming more powerful and could spur cyber attacks, prompting banks and corporates to invest heavily in cybersecurity and operational resilience. For Citigroup shareholders, the message underlines that rising technology-related risk and compliance spending may remain a structural feature of the bank's cost base.

Technical picture weakens after failed breakout

From a market perspective, Citigroup Inc. stock recently attempted to break out of a symmetrical triangle pattern to the upside, but the move stalled just above USD 138.00 and below the August peak at USD 140.44. An analysis published on September 21, 2026 notes that the stock climbed to that prior high but ultimately failed to deliver a decisive breakout, then reversed back to the lower boundary of the triangle, where a medium-term uptrend currently intersects. According to Investing.com on September 21, 2026, the daily chart showed Citigroup Inc. at USD 131.383 on the NYSE at 20:00 local time, implying a retreat of around USD 9 from the August top and placing the share price near key support.

The same analysis highlights that a double top around USD 140.50 has formed, which could weigh on Citigroup Inc. stock in coming days if the price falls below roughly USD 128.50. Below that threshold, the technical pattern would generate a full-fledged sell signal with a provisional downside target near the 200-day moving average, estimated at about USD 123.12. In numerical terms, that would represent a potential drop of around USD 8.26 from the USD 131.38 level cited for September 21, 2026, underscoring the sensitivity of the stock to any further deterioration in sentiment.

Debt issuance and peer pressure shape risk backdrop

Beyond chart signals, Citigroup has also been active in funding markets, which plays into the broader risk picture. According to a summary by Ground News on September 21, 2026, Citigroup Inc. recently captured USD 12 billion in the largest dollar bond issue in its history, selling debt shortly after the US Federal Reserve raised interest rates. For investors, the transaction illustrates Citigroup's ability to tap credit markets at scale, but it also adds to the bank's gross funding and interest expense profile at a time when monetary policy remains restrictive.

Meanwhile, sector conditions remain challenging. A market wrap from Interfax on September 21, 2026 reported that banking shares declined at the end of the last completed US trading session, with Citigroup Inc. closing down about 0.7 percent alongside slips of roughly 0.8 percent in Bank of America, 1.0 percent in Goldman Sachs and 0.9 percent in Wells Fargo. The move suggests that concerns about interest-rate risk, regulatory scrutiny of trading exposures and broader macro uncertainty continue to exert pressure on major US banks.

Stock trades near key support on the NYSE

Against this backdrop, Citigroup Inc. stock is trading near a technically important support band on the NYSE. The Investing.com analysis dated September 21, 2026 cites a price of USD 131.383 at 20:00 local time for Citigroup Inc., placing the stock roughly USD 9 below the August high around USD 140.44 and only a few dollars above the indicated sell-signal level near USD 128.50. That positioning means the shares are less than USD 8.26 above the provisional 200-day moving average target around USD 123.12, highlighting the relatively narrow buffer should market sentiment worsen further.

evidence.title: JPMorgan Chase, Halogen, ITE partner to provide mentoring, practical skills to students
evidence.text:
JPMorgan Chase, Halogen, ITE partner to provide mentoring, practical skills to students

Career Connect helps youths build confidence, skills they need to transition from school to work

[SINGAPORE] When thinking about her future, Pearlyn Puar, a second-year Institute of Technical Education (ITE) student pursuing a higher Nitec in business administration, began to worry that artificial intelligence could threaten her career aspirations.

“Initially, my problem was that I felt like AI was taking over my career, since I want to do fashion design, and AI is evolving so much and so quickly,” the 18-year-old said.

However, joining JPMorgan Chase’s Career Connect programme helped to ease her worries. Her mentors, who are JPMorgan employees, gave her advice that changed her mindset about AI.

“I realised that instead of being afraid of AI, I can use it as an assistant for my future business, to help me find my target audience and fashion trends, while I maintain my own originality in designing,” Puar said.

Over six weeks from August to September, she and a few ITE students were placed in small groups with mentors.

Puar had joined Career Connect to find out more about the career pathways available, gain insight from working professionals and build her network.

Get insights into businesses across South-east Asia

“I felt like I was very scared of my future,” she said. “I was afraid of choosing the wrong job or career, and wanted to have the right mindset on what to do.”

By the end of the programme, Puar felt more secure about her future. After graduation, she is keen to study fashion design at a polytechnic and start her own clothing business.

Another participant was Firmansyah Rohaizat, a first-year ITE student studying retail and online business. He currently juggles his studies, a part-time job at Uniqlo and his own home-based barbering business along with Student Council duties.

Firman joined the programme to find out more about workplace skills. From his mentors, he learned “valuable skills” and practical guidance that he can apply to his current work and study situation.

He said: “My mentor taught me how to prioritise and manage the important things. He said that when it comes to decision-making, sacrifice is needed. From taking his advice, I’ve learnt how to manage my time well.

“I feel more aware and organised from this programme because it taught me time management and presentation skills.”

Puar and Firman were part of the more than 45 ITE students who participated in Career Connect 2026, along with nearly 30 JPMorgan Chase mentor volunteers.

Career Connect is the bank’s signature global philanthropy programme that helps youths build the confidence and skills they need to smoothly transition from education to employment.

JPMorgan Chase said: “Through workshops, mentoring and career conversations, students gain practical insights into workplace culture, professional expectations, career pathways and the skills employers value, while hearing authentic stories and lessons from employees’ own career journeys.”

For the first time, Career Connect this year targeted 17 to 19-year-olds, particularly those lacking access to professional networks and resources.

“Career Connect has evolved alongside changing community needs. Earlier editions focused on building career awareness among younger students, while the current programme is designed to provide more targeted support for students who are closer to making important education and career decisions,” it added.

The bank partnered Halogen for this year’s edition. As a non-profit that focuses on supporting young people, Halogen helped to shape the programme’s objectives, design and delivery.

Ivy Tse, CEO of Halogen, said: “This partnership with JPMorgan is part of our vertical of looking at school-to-work transitions, and how to support young people in getting more access to networks and content. Sometimes, a lot of young people in Singapore face a lot of anxiety when it comes to navigating school-to-work.”

JPMorgan Chase noted that a distinctive feature of Career Connect is the opportunity for students to learn from the bank’s professionals.

One mentor, Kristof Trautwein from JPMorgan Private Bank’s international transformation office, said: “Mentoring undoubtedly helps people develop and succeed – but many young talents may lack access to professional guidance and networks.”

Another mentor, Tan Chiew Sze, asset and wealth management talent adviser at JPMorgan, said Career Connect also helped the students see that the challenges they face are “part and parcel of life”.

“We want their experiences with Career Connect to encourage them in their studies and beyond, and give them the confidence they need when it comes to assignments and interviews for internships,” she added.

Both mentors noted that they observed their mentees gained more confidence and became more willing to share ideas, ask questions and engage in discussions.

“Personally, Career Connect has helped me grow too,” said Tan. “It has demonstrated how important it is to listen, communicate clearly, and think about how to guide and encourage others using different methods.”

evidence.title: JPMorgan’s Jamie Dimon Predicts AI Infrastructure Outlays Will Top $1 Trillion Next Year
evidence.text:
Jamie Dimon , the longtime chief executive of JPMorgan Chase ( NYSE: JPM ), told an audience in India this week that outlays on artificial-intelligence infrastructure are on track to cross the $1 trillion mark in 2027.

The remark, delivered on the sidelines of the bank ’s annual India investor conference, underscores how quickly the build-out by cloud giants and their suppliers has accelerated.

Dimon put last year’s spending across the hyperscaler ecosystem at roughly $300 billion.

That figure has already more than doubled to about $700 billion in 2026, he said, and the trajectory points toward another large jump next year.

He framed the surge in macroeconomic terms: each year’s increment is adding something on the order of one percentage point to GDP growth.

The same wave of construction, however, is also putting upward pressure on prices in the near term.

Companies are hiring workers , erecting factories and power plants, and buying chips, servers, copper, and other materials at a scale that has few recent precedents.

Over a longer horizon Dimon struck a more optimistic note. He called AI an “unbelievable technology” whose expansion still “looks like it’s going to continue.”

Once the infrastructure is in place and productivity gains materialize, he suggested, the same technology could become a deflationary force rather than an inflationary one.

The JPMorgan chief also pushed back against the idea that every dollar of AI spending must be justified by a conventional return-on-investment calculation. In some cases, he argued, the investment is simply “table stakes.”

Firms may keep writing checks because the technology improves customer experience or keeps them competitive, even when the financial payoff is hard to quantify in the short run.

Dimon was equally cautious about trying to identify winners and losers at this stage.

He drew an explicit parallel with the late-1990s internet boom: many well-known names from that era ultimately disappeared, while companies few people had heard of at the time later became dominant.

The same pattern, he implied, could repeat itself in artificial intelligence .

The comments come at a moment when investors are already debating whether the current pace of capital expenditure can be sustained and whether revenues will catch up before markets lose patience.

Other forecasters have published even larger numbers; some Wall Street houses now see combined hyperscaler and AI -related capex exceeding $1.3 trillion or $1.4 trillion in 2027.

Dimon’s $1 trillion figure therefore sits toward the more conservative end of recent estimates, yet it still represents a historic concentration of investment in a single technological wave.

Beyond AI itself, Dimon linked the spending boom to a broader set of capital demands—traditional infrastructure, remilitarization, and large government deficits—that could keep interest rates and bond yields higher for longer than many had hoped.

Inflation , he warned, has already proved stickier than expected and could even tick higher again.

The Federal Reserve , in his view, should hold to its 2 percent target even if those pressures persist.

The net picture Dimon painted is one of genuine technological promise wrapped inside real macroeconomic trade-offs. The build-out is large enough to move GDP and prices; it is still too early to know which companies will capture the lasting value; and the financing and inflation consequences will be felt well beyond the technology sector.

evidence.title: JPMorgan Chase (JPM) Commits $750 Billion to Rebuilding America’s Housing Supply
evidence.text:
JPMorgan Chase (JPM) Commits $750 Billion to Rebuilding America’s Housing Supply

JPMorgan Chase & Co. (NYSE: JPM ) said it plans to place more than $750 billion through 2035 to increase U.S. housing supply and support homeownership, with the Wall Street Journal covering the pledge as part of its broader American Dream Initiative.

The commitment, nearly 40% more than the bank's housing-related capital deployment over the prior decade, includes financing for 1 million affordable housing units and help for 500,000 homebuyers. It includes 200,000 first-time buyers, partly through a more than 40% increase in mortgage lending and 850 new home-lending advisers.

JPMorgan Chase & Co. (NYSE: JPM )'s strong financial performance gives it substantial capacity to expand its housing business. The bank reported a record second-quarter net income of $21.2 billion. This gives it a strong earnings base as it commits to deploying $750 billion toward housing through 2035.

The initiative could expand JPMorgan's mortgage revenue and deepen customer relationships. The bank plans to increase mortgage lending by more than 40% and hire 850 Home Lending Advisors while helping 500,000 customers purchase homes. It includes 200,000 first-time buyers. Greater mortgage activity could also give JPMorgan more opportunities to attract deposits and cross-sell banking and investment products.

JPMorgan could also benefit from its scale in multifamily and affordable-housing finance as housing supply expands. The bank plans to finance or preserve 1 million affordable housing units through 2035. It gives it opportunities to make lending and investment activity across developers, owners, nonprofits, and government partners.

The $750 billion headline commitment does not necessarily translate into $750 billion of incremental revenue-generating investments. JPMorgan Chase & Co. (NYSE: JPM ) plans to place the capital through multiple financing tools, including debt, equity and grants. It has linked additional housing deployment to supportive zoning, permitting and tax-credit policies. Actual earnings benefits could fall well below what the headline figure suggests.

A larger housing-finance operation could increase JPMorgan's exposure to real-estate credit risk. The bank already ranks as the nation's largest multifamily lender. So expanding housing-related lending could increase losses if higher interest rates, weak property values or regional oversupply pressure borrowers.

JPMorgan also needs stronger housing demand to convert the initiative into meaningful earnings growth. Mortgage volumes depend on home prices, affordability and transaction activity, while local zoning and permitting restrictions can limit new construction. If those conditions remain unfavorable, JPMorgan could deploy significant resources without generating the level of loan growth and returns that investors expect.

JPMorgan Chase & Co. (NYSE: JPM )'s hedge fund base grew to 133 funds in the second quarter from 131 in the first, with combined position value climbing to $17.87 billion from $15.54 billion, according to Insider Monkey's database. Wells Fargo, a more mortgage-concentrated peer that would also benefit from a healthier housing market, saw an even larger jump, with holders rising to 94 from 82 and position value more than doubling to $7.18 billion from $3.44 billion.

JPMorgan's $750 billion housing initiative could strengthen its mortgage and affordable-housing businesses by expanding lending activity and deepening customer relationships over the next decade. Nonetheless, the bank needs stronger housing demand, supportive local policies, and disciplined credit underwriting to turn the large commitment into attractive returns. U.S. home sales recently fell to a 14-month low because mortgage rates rose. JPMorgan now faces a tough housing market as it tries to turn this program into bigger profits.

evidence.title: Goldman Sachs projects AI capital expenditures to reach $1.2T by 2027
evidence.text:
(CB-16); the desktop layout below renders the same text as a restyled . --> Goldman Sachs projects AI capital expenditures to reach $1.2T by 2027

The investment bank sees US hyperscalers pouring unprecedented sums into AI infrastructure, with debt financing playing an increasingly central role.

Goldman Sachs has ratcheted up its forecast for how much America’s biggest tech companies will spend building out AI infrastructure, projecting US hyperscaler capital expenditures could climb as high as $1.4 trillion by 2027. That figure blows past the bank’s own prior estimates of roughly $1.1 trillion and dwarfs a broader Wall Street consensus that had been hovering closer to $920 billion.

Goldman’s updated trajectory sketches out a steep climb. The bank previously estimated hyperscaler AI capex at roughly $405 billion in 2025, rising to approximately $750 billion in 2026, before hitting the $1.2 trillion range in 2027. The latest revision pushes that 2027 figure even higher.

The companies driving this wave are the usual suspects: Microsoft , Amazon , Alphabet , Meta , and Oracle , with OpenAI also drawing notable investment activity. These firms are collectively transitioning from what Goldman characterizes as an experimental phase of AI deployment into full-scale commercial implementation.

Looking further out, the bank estimates cumulative AI infrastructure spending could reach approximately $7.6 trillion from 2026 through 2031. That breaks down into roughly $5.1 trillion for compute, $2.1 trillion for data centers, and $358 billion for power infrastructure.

Goldman’s analysts have drawn comparisons to historical technology waves, specifically the buildout of railroads and automobiles. Both required massive upfront capital deployment before the downstream economic benefits materialized.

More than one-third of the projected 2027 capital expenditure, roughly $400 billion, is expected to come through investment-grade bond issuance. That’s a meaningful shift from the self-funded, cash-flow-driven investment model that defined big tech’s first two decades.

Goldman points to advertising and subscription models as the primary monetization channels for AI-driven tools. The bet is that consumer AI agents and enterprise AI applications will generate revenue streams large enough to justify the infrastructure investment.

Goldman notes that median AI infrastructure stock valuations sit at around 26 times forward price-to-earnings ratios.

The bank’s analysts also flag several supply-side constraints that could slow the buildout regardless of how much money hyperscalers are willing to throw at it. Power availability is near the top of the list. Land accessibility presents a similar bottleneck. Memory chip affordability rounds out Goldman’s list of constraints, with AI workloads being extraordinarily memory-intensive.

The shift toward debt financing also creates a secondary market dynamic worth monitoring. Over $400 billion in new investment-grade bond supply will need to be absorbed by fixed-income markets.

Nvidia Founder and CEO Jensen Huang said during a May earnings call that hyperscaler capital expenditure on AI alone is forecast to exceed $1 trillion in 2027 and that AI infrastructure spending could reach $3 trillion to $4 trillion annually by the end of the decade.

“Compute is revenues. Compute is profit,” Huang said.

Citigroup projected in September 2025 that AI-related infrastructure spending by Big Tech could surpass $2.8 trillion through 2029. evidence.title: Goldman Sachs says hyperscalers will spend $1.2 trillion on AI in 2027
evidence.text:
Goldman Sachs says hyperscalers will spend $1.2 trillion on AI in 2027

Goldman Sachs now projects the five largest U.S. hyperscalers will lift AI infrastructure spending more than 50% to $1.2 trillion in 2027, above Wall Street's $1.1 trillion consensus. The firm estimates hyperscalers need roughly $300 billion in annual AI revenue just to break even, a target current cloud growth hasn't reached.

$300 billion a year. That's what Goldman Sachs says hyperscalers now need in AI revenue just to break even, buried inside a note that raises its own spending forecast.

Strategists at Goldman Sachs led by Ryan Hammond now expect the five biggest U.S. hyperscalers to lift AI infrastructure spending by more than 50% next year, to $1.2 trillion in 2027. That is above the $1.1 trillion Wall Street consensus already baked into most models, according to Bloomberg's reporting on the note published September 25. Goldman sees another 12% increase after that, pushing 2028 capex to roughly $1.4 trillion.

Put the trajectory next to itself and the acceleration is the story. The group spent $405 billion in 2025. Goldman expects that to nearly double to about $750 billion this year, then jump again to $1.2 trillion in 2027. Hammond's team frames the 2027 figure in stark terms: a larger share of GDP than any technology investment cycle since the railroad buildout of the late 1800s. That is not a throwaway comparison. Railroads took decades to prove out and bankrupted plenty of investors along the way before the survivors made money.

Which is why the breakeven number is the part worth sitting with. Goldman estimates the hyperscalers need about $300 billion in annual AI revenue to cover their spending, and that current results are still well short of that. Cloud revenue across the group is annualizing at roughly $70 billion above the pre-AI trend line as of the second quarter of 2026. That's real growth, and it's not nothing. But it leaves a gap of more than $200 billion between what AI is generating today and what Goldman says the buildout needs to justify itself.

Goldman goes further on the demand side. To get hyperscalers to what it calls solid returns, not just breakeven, the firm estimates AI users collectively need to spend about $1 trillion a year on AI applications. Announced backlogs across the group already exceed $1.5 trillion, so the commitments exist on paper. Whether that backlog converts into steady, recurring application revenue at the pace Goldman's math requires is the open question nobody in this cycle has answered yet.

The four largest cloud hyperscalers are spending $725 billion on AI infrastructure in 2026, up 77% year over year, with combined free cash flow projected to hit nearly zero by Q3. Amazon's trailing FCF has collapsed to $1.2 billion even as operating cash flow rose 30%, while Oracle's free cash flow turned negative $23.7 billion and its stock... - big tech AI spending trends 2026 - free cash flow crisis data centers

Debt is doing more of the work than it used to. Goldman's analysis shows hyperscalers issued $108 billion in investment-grade bonds in 2025, about 26% of that year's capex. Through the first half of 2026 alone, they had already issued $194 billion, and Goldman expects the full-year figure to land near $250 billion, or about a third of capex. For 2027, the firm projects roughly $400 billion in global investment-grade issuance against $1.14 trillion in spending, a share that keeps climbing toward 35%. Some reporting on the same Goldman data put the 2027 borrowing figure as high as $420 billion. Either way, more than a third of the AI buildout next year gets financed with borrowed money, not free cash flow.

That financing pressure isn't abstract. On September 24, Oracle sent a force majeure notice to a unit of Blue Owl Capital over Project Jupiter, the Stargate data center campus in New Mexico designed to run 2.45 gigawatts on gas-powered fuel cells. The notice, first reported by Bloomberg, doesn't pull Oracle out as the site's main tenant. It gives Oracle room to delay payments if the facility misses its 2028 online date, and the delay risk is concrete: an Energy Transfer pipeline meant to feed the site has slipped nearly six months, to February 1, 2027. Oracle shares fell about 3.3% on the news.

That's the tension Goldman's numbers are really describing. Nvidia chips are selling, cloud backlogs are enormous, and capex keeps climbing past whatever Wall Street penciled in a quarter earlier. At the same time, the physical infrastructure, power, pipelines, permitting, is running behind the spending pace, and a growing share of the money going into it isn't equity, it's debt that has to be serviced whether the AI revenue shows up on schedule or not.

Frankly, the $1.2 trillion headline was always going to move markets more than the $300 billion breakeven line. But the second number is the one that decides whether the first one was a good bet. Goldman isn't saying the AI buildout won't pay off. It's saying the industry now has a specific, checkable target to hit, and as of the last reported quarter, it's still roughly $200 billion a year short.

evidence.text:
Burry and Goldman Sachs Warn AI Infrastructure Boom Is Turning Into a Debt Problem

Michael Burry and Goldman Sachs Asset Management are simultaneously warning that the AI infrastructure investment boom is shifting from free-cash-flow financing to debt and long-term commitments, with credit markets already showing signs of strain. Oracle’s credit default swaps spiked to a record high last Thursday, according to Zerohedge, while Goldman Sachs Asset Management is underweight the largest AI borrowers.

In his latest article, Burry said net capital investment by S&P 500 companies reached 2.07% of GDP as of June 30, the highest in nearly four decades outside the aftermath of the March 2000 Nasdaq peak. He expects net investment/GDP to set higher marks in the coming quarters and possibly even eclipse the aftermath of the 2000 tech-stock peak.

Burry said Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Oracle have accumulated roughly $3 trillion in purchase commitments, future leases, guarantees, construction-in-progress and other exposures tied to their AI infrastructure buildout. He warned that write-downs could arrive in 2028 or 2029, and that by then the commitments may be so large that a relatively small write-down has a bigger impact than can now be imagined.

His argument centers on the capital cycle: periods of heavy investment can eventually lead to overcapacity, falling returns and write-downs. He pointed to the late-1990s technology, media and telecommunications buildout, saying subsequent depreciation and write-downs were severe enough to push aggregate S&P 500 net investment into negative territory for 12 consecutive quarters between mid-2003 and mid-2006. Burry believes a similar dynamic could emerge from the current AI infrastructure boom. In his view, the issue is not simply the amount of capital being deployed, but the scale of future commitments being accumulated by the largest hyperscalers.

“The most profitable companies in the world, except Apple, are betting everything on this as their free cash flow turns negative and the borrowing pace increases,” he wrote.

Burry also questioned Oracle’s accounting around customer prepayments, highlighting a nearly 20% increase in future cloud revenue without delivering extra service or work product immediately, but “created by the structure of the contract.” Credit markets are also flashing caution. Oracle’s CDS spiked to record highs last Thursday, signaling mounting investor anxiety over the AI hyperscaler’s debt, according to Zerohedge. Bloomberg reported the company is moving to shield itself from rising expenses on its massive Project Jupiter data center in New Mexico, sending a force majeure notice to the project’s developer.

At Goldman Sachs Asset Management, Lindsay Rosner, head of multi-sector fixed income investing, said the firm is underweight the biggest AI borrowers as a flood of issuance washes over the market. “We believe there will be a lot of hyperscaler issuance,” Rosner said in a Thursday interview on Bloomberg TV. “For that sector at large we are underweight knowing more issuance will come.”

Big Tech companies have been among the biggest sellers of high-grade corporate bonds in the U.S. this year, with Amazon, Meta and Alphabet borrowing tens of billions of dollars for AI projects. “That is what we have seen all year long,” Rosner said. “New issuance is replacing existing issuance.” Rosner said the underweight call reflects expectations for heavy supply, rather than pessimism about AI. Her team believes “in the story of AI,” she said, but is “cognizant” that more borrowing could reprice the market.

Major hyperscalers—including Alphabet, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft and Oracle—have increasingly relied on debt to fund an unprecedented capital expenditure surge as their free cash flow turned negative. According to new Brookings Institution research, the AI infrastructure boom could require $10.3 trillion of U.S. investment through 2032, with a growing share of the financial risk shifting away from Big Tech balance sheets and into less-transparent financing structures.

evidence.title: Goldman Sachs just gave AI stock fans a cold, hard reality check
evidence.text:
It will take years for AI investments by major tech companies to pay off. But before that happens, companies have to break even — and that will also take years.

Goldman Sachs strategist Ryan Hammond crunched some numbers and thinks hyperscalers like Amazon ( AMZN ), Oracle ( ORCL ), and Microsoft ( MSFT ) need to generate about $300 billion in AI revenue in the "next few years" to break even on their investments.

The hyperscalers have a ways to go before reaching that number, according to Hammond.

Hyperscaler cloud revenues have accelerated sharply this year, annualizing at about $70 billion above the pre-AI trend in the second quarter of 2026. Announced backlogs for the group exceed $1.5 trillion.

"We estimate that AI users would need to spend roughly $1 trillion annually on AI applications in order for the hyperscalers to generate solid returns on investment and the application layer to generate strong profit margins on their compute expenses," Hammond wrote.

The stakes are high for investors, who have plowed back into hyperscaler stocks in recent weeks amid AI optimism.

The Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF ( MAGS ) — which tracks the performance of top AI hyperscalers — is up 8% inside of a month compared to a modest gain for the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ).

Hewlett Packard Enterprise ( NYSE:HPE ) stock is up 1% to $64.31, following Dell higher at a slower pace. Meanwhile, the Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund ( NYSEARCA:XLK ) is up 1%. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust ( NYSEARCA:SPY ) is up 0.5%, a steady background that makes Dell's move stand out.

Dell stock trades above Morgan Stanley's $511 base-case price target, while the firm's rating stays Neutral. That leaves the market already paying for a scenario Morgan Stanley still treats as the less likely of the two it models for Dell.

Morgan Stanley Lifts Odds on Dell's Upside Scenario

Morgan Stanley's revision followed a meeting with Dell chief operating officer Jeff Clarke. The firm kept its rating and its base-case target in place, so the note leaves its formal recommendation on Dell intact, but what moved is the probability Morgan Stanley attaches to the bullish outcome it had already published.

The meeting turned on one question for Dell: whether artificial intelligence spending represents another hardware replacement cycle or a broader expansion in infrastructure demand. Jeff Clarke told the firm that artificial intelligence agents could drive inference-token usage 87 times higher by the end of the decade. That growth would create additional demand for computing capacity, the kind of need Dell builds servers to meet.

Why Dell Is Outrunning the Hardware Group

Dell stock is beating Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock, the technology sector fund and the broad market, which points to a company-specific catalyst. HPE stock is edging higher alongside Dell on the same artificial intelligence infrastructure read-through. Its gain stays modest in scale (we covered seven suppliers powering that expansion, from power to cooling, in a free report here). That split suggests the market is rewarding Dell's scenario math more than the broader hardware theme.

Dell Trades Ahead of Morgan Stanley's Base Case

The catch for Dell is that Morgan Stanley held both its rating and its base case steady, as higher odds on the upside path still leave the firm's central expectation where it was, and Dell stock already sits beyond that mark. Buyers are paying for the outcome the analyst still ranks second.

That setup cuts both ways for Dell. If agent workloads multiply inference needs as Clarke expects, paying up could prove justified. Any slower ramp could pull Dell stock back toward Morgan Stanley's base case, and that's the risk buyers accept at current levels.

Dell's year-to-date run adds another layer of risk. The size of that gain leaves less margin for a stumble, and any sign of slower agent adoption could test holders' patience. The same momentum that lifted Dell stock can work in reverse when sentiment cools off.

With Dell stock trading above Morgan Stanley's base case and still carrying strong momentum, a measured approach fits. Investors should size their holdings modestly and add exposure in stages, while existing holders could trim back toward target to lock in part of the gain.

Whether inference demand scales the way Clarke describes is the open question. Investors should watch for signs that agent workloads are lifting Dell's server demand, along with any further Morgan Stanley commentary on its scenario weights.

evidence.text:
Morgan Stanley investment unit deal list leaked in email misfire

SoftBank raises US$11.1bil in world's biggest high-yield corporate bond sale

NEW YORK: A Morgan Stanley employee has accidentally leaked an internal document listing more than 100 investment banking deals the firm is pitching and monitoring in Asia, revealing details of the bank’s pipeline, according to people familiar with the matter.

The list contained candidates for initial public offerings, spanning from China to South Korea and India, according to a copy seen by Bloomberg News and verified by people familiar with the matter.

The list, which focused mostly on Asia, along with Europe, the Middle East, and Africa, also included private equity and pension funds backing those companies, and projects that were put on hold.

The deals list was sent out via email this week to some clients by Mohamed Atmani, Asia-Pacific head of financial sponsors in the investment banking department, who later sought to retract the message, according to people familiar with the matter.

A blurred copy was also posted by an account on Instagram.

The banker had intended to send a client-facing version of the file, which largely contained general updates on the private equity sector and recent transactions, but mistakenly sent the internal version instead, some of which contained extensive price-sensitive information.

Atmani, a managing director based in Hong Kong, who joined the bank in 2018, declined to comment immediately and could not be reached for further comment.

In a statement to Bloomberg News, Morgan Stanley said it takes client confidentiality extremely seriously.

“We promptly took steps to address this inadvertent sharing of information and we continue to engage with relevant parties,” the New York-based firm said.

The incident is an embarrassing misstep for the bank, which has ranked among the top underwriters of Hong Kong stock sales and Asia mergers for years.

While such errors are rare, it highlights the sensitivity of information handled by investment banking teams, where details of prospective client transactions are typically closely guarded.

Leaks about an imminent share placement can frustrate clients pursuing block trades, especially if details emerge before a deal is launched.

Such disclosures can weigh on the stock as investors brace for additional supply, potentially cutting proceeds for the seller and making execution more difficult for banks.

Private equity firms increasingly use IPOs and follow-on placements to accelerate exits and return capital to investors.

Premature disclosure can disrupt those sales and damage relationships with banks handling the transactions.

It’s unclear whether clients and related parties have reached out to Morgan Stanley and how the firm is addressing the issue.

Several banks and financial institutions have accidentally leaked sensitive documents in recent years, leading to regulatory penalties, reputational damage, and long‑term customer trust issues.

After a situation such as this, restoring the relationship of trust with clients is key, Michael Aiello, a prominent mergers and acquisitions (M&A) lawyer, said.

“The first thing you have to do is run to the fire,” Charlie Bouckaert, JPMorgan Chase & Co’s global head of M&A, said about handling such situations. — Bloomberg

evidence.title: Latest leadership shuffle shows Wells Fargo is in new phase
evidence.text:
Latest leadership shuffle shows Wells Fargo is in new phase

Wells Fargo CEO Charlie Scharf has another opportunity to put his stamp on the company's top executive ranks after its long-tenured chief risk officer announced plans to retire.

Under a plan announced Wednesday, Chief Operating Officer Scott Powell will move into the chief risk officer role, which will be vacated by Derek Flowers. That shuffle, scheduled for January 2027, will leave room for a new chief operating officer. Wells plans to name that person in the near future.

The changes underscore that the megabank has entered a new phase, where the CEO's focus is no longer on replacing executives who had filled key roles during damaging scandals.

Scharf arrived at the megabank in late 2019, as it was managing the fallout from scandals that led to the ouster of the two previous CEOs.

He has since installed a senior leadership team that features several of Scharf's former colleagues from his earlier stints at the Bank of New York Mellon and JPMorganChase.

Following the retirement of Flowers, who joined Wells Fargo in 1995, only two of 13 executives on the bank's operating committee will have been with the company longer than Scharf.

Flowers was one of a relatively small number of Wells Fargo veterans who got promotions to senior roles after Scharf's arrival. Fortune reported last year that Flowers caught Scharf's eye for doing strong work as a credit risk manager.

"The best executives at Wells were not at the top but the mid and upper-mid level, and we promoted many of them, including Derek," Scharf told Fortune. "And that builds confidence with the troops, because they know who the good people are."

Flowers, 54 years old as of February, is nine years younger than Powell, who will succeed him. The two men have been working together for years, filling roles with overlapping responsibilities. Powell was hired by Scharf in 2019 to a position whose duties included overseeing regulatory relations and regulatory execution.

When Flowers was elevated to the chief risk officer job in 2022, the San Francisco-based bank was still operating under an asset cap the Federal Reserve had put in place in 2018. Those regulatory handcuffs were finally unlocked last year.

"Derek played a pivotal role in strengthening our risk and control framework and fostering the strong risk culture that positions Wells Fargo for continued growth," Scharf said in a press release Wednesday. "Working closely with Scott, he helped advance a significant transformation of the company's risk and control capabilities, leaving a lasting mark on our company and the industry."

A Wells Fargo spokesperson declined to answer questions about the bank's upcoming announcement of a new chief operating officer.

Powell, who's based in New York, is a former CEO of Santander Holdings USA. Earlier in his career, he worked with Scharf at JPMorgan.

For four consecutive years, Wells Fargo listed Powell as one of its five or six "named executive officers," whose compensation gets disclosed publicly.

Between 2020 and 2023, Powell collected between $9.3 million and $14.6 million in total annual compensation, regulatory filings show. Powell was not listed as a named executive officer in either of the bank's two most recent annual disclosures.

evidence.title: Wells Fargo Says the AI Spending Math Breaks in 2028 and Just Cut Its S&P 500 Target to 7,700
evidence.text:
Wells Fargo Says the AI Spending Math Breaks in 2028 and Just Cut Its S&P 500 Target to 7,700

Wells Fargo's chief equity strategist sees a spending cliff forming inside the AI buildout, and the arithmetic he uses to locate it points to a very specific year when the math stops working for hyperscaler earnings.

Wells Fargo cut its year-end S&P 500 target to 7,700 from 7,950. Chief equity strategist Ohsung Kwon framed the reduction around hyperscaler capital spending rather than a valuation call.

The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust ( NYSEARCA:SPY ) closed at 767.83 on September 23, 2026, with a 12.6% year-to-date gain and 15.77% one-year advance.

Against a market that has already delivered solid gains, a flat-to-slightly-lower year-end target signals a real change in expected return. The argument below focuses on the rising burden on hyperscaler earnings rather than headline valuation.

Kwon’s mechanism is that each additional capex year raises the demand bar for prior asset bases. Hyperscalers will spend $1.5 trillion next year, and Kwon says 2027 is locked.

The math turns steep after that. Kwon says the demand needed to justify current spending is roughly $1.4 trillion, and another trillion-dollar capex year in 2028 would push the required demand figure to about $2.2 trillion.

A capex boom flatters earnings because companies capitalize spending rather than expense it. The punishment arrives as those assets depreciate on shorter schedules than the market prices in.

Kwon argues the current earnings run is inflated on exactly this timing gap. He estimates next year’s EPS will be about 42% above Wells Fargo’s normalized EPS figure, and he calls the coming ten-year EPS cycle one of the strongest in history, only surpassed by the 1950s bull market.

Allocation Statistic Is About Positioning

Kwon’s second concern is crowding. He estimates equity allocation at roughly 72% against 28% bonds, which he says is the highest equity share since 1969.

When the marginal buyer is already committed, interest rates matter less than their volatility. The 10-year Treasury yield sat at 4.96% on September 22, 2026, near a one-year high of 5.01%, and the VIX closed at 14.21, deep in complacency territory.

Low implied volatility inside crowded positioning is the setup that historically converts a modest shock into a large move. Riding a mania is fine as long as you plan the exit, which is the argument our free bubble survivor’s handbook spends most of its pages on. You can also find the firm’s ongoing equity work on the Wells Fargo Investment Institute research page.

He is rotating within equities rather than reducing exposure. Kwon favors quality over high beta and singles out health care as a defensive sector that is less rate-sensitive than the classic bond proxies.

That is the fair read of a strategist who thinks the cycle overshoots rather than collapses. SPY’s own weightings make the tension visible: NVIDIA sits at 7.58% of the fund, Apple at 6.66%, Microsoft at 4.91%, Amazon at 3.64%, Alphabet’s two share classes together above 5%, Broadcom at 2.62% and Meta at 2.24%, so the AI capex debate is roughly a third of the index.

The bull case is that next year is already locked. If hyperscalers spend the $1.5 trillion Kwon expects and beat, the bear thesis has no catalyst for close to a year, and an early correct call tends to look wrong to anyone holding the position.

Broad earnings strength supports that patience. SPY has returned 255.49% over ten years, and the index has repeatedly punished investors who sold on capex math they thought was obviously stretched.

The bear case, per Kwon, combines crowded positioning at a 1969-style equity share, earnings running about 42% above normalized levels, and an AI spending cycle whose justification hurdle rises annually. The deciding variable is when depreciation hits hyperscaler operating margins.

Until it does, the market favors owners. Once it does, the gap between reported and normalized earnings stops being a talking point and becomes a reported figure.

evidence.title: Wells Fargo opens downtown branch, provides $25,000 grant to Reba Place Development Corporation
evidence.text:
The new branch of Wells Fargo Bank in downtown Evanston officially opened Thursday, Sept. 24, with a ribbon-cutting ceremony and a $25,000 grant to Reba Place Development Corporation, a nonprofit that works to provide stable, affordable housing for diverse communities.

We depend on people, organizations and banks now to help us out,” said Martha Burns, executive director of the Reba Place Development Corporation. “And what you have done for us is to provide a $25,000 grant that will help us to renovate.”

The grant will go toward renovating a laundry room at one of the affordable housing facilities owned and operated by the nonprofit. New washers and dryers, flooring and space for folding clothes will be added to the laundry room, Burns said.

Burns was one of several speakers at the ceremony at the bank, 1600 Sherman Ave. Others included First Ward Councilmember Clare Kelly; Andy Vick, executive director of Downtown Evanston; state Rep. Robyn Gabel (D-18th District); and several Wells Fargo regional and local employees.

Fourth Ward Councilmember Jonathan Nieuwsma and Paul Zalmezak, the city’s economic development manager, also attended.

The opening of this Wells Fargo branch marks the transition of a high-traffic downtown Evanston corner from retail to financial services. Before Wells Fargo, an o utdoor gear retailer operated out of the space for about two decades, although the name changed along the way.

The retail store, called Gearhead Outfitters at the time, closed in June 2025, leaving the space vacant for more than a year. Representatives from the retail store said the shop had been operating at a deficit for several years.

Before it became Gearhead Outfitters, the store was Uncle Dan’s. Teenagers Mark and Brent Weiss started the business when they bought an Army-Navy surplus store near the Skokie Swift station from their Uncle Dan . The business changed ownership over the years before Gearhead Outfitters acquired it in 2019.

Several Evanston speakers mentioned small businesses in their remarks at the bank opening, celebrating the addition of Wells Fargo but highlighting the need for more support for the city’s local shops.

“I’m especially looking forward to partnering with Wells Fargo in ways to find measures to support our small business community,” Kelly said, “which is really the backbone of our community.”

“I want to welcome you, all the employees of Wells Fargo, the bank management team,” Vick said, “and all of your customers, who we hope will not only come in and do their banking, but then shop in our downtown and eat in our restaurants.”

Gabel also reminded those gathered that thriving communities have a wide variety of businesses.

“Strong financial institutions help families achieve important goals, from buying a home to saving for the future, and they help small businesses grow and create jobs as well,” Gabel told the crowd.

Rozmin Mithani, manager of the downtown Evanston branch, shared her own experience and respect for small businesses, too.

“I have so much deep respect for small business and business owners, because I’ve been there, and they have the hardest job,” Mithani said. “I want you all to know that Wells Fargo is here to walk with you in your business financial journey.”

Mithani grew up working at her father’s Pakistani restaurant on Devon Avenue in the nearby Rogers Park neighborhood of Chicago. She said that coming back to work in Evanston, so close to where she first worked, felt like life bringing her “full circle.”
