Ageas Re partners with Slovenian insurer Triglav Group in connection with the Motor insurance business distributed by Italian Insurtech Prima

Ageas Re partners with Slovenian insurer Triglav Group in connection with the Motor insurance business distributed by Italian Insurtech Prima

Today, Ageas Re, the reinsurance arm of Ageas Group, concluded a reinsurance agreement with Slovenian insurer Triglav Group in connection with the partnership entered into by Triglav Group with leading Italian direct Motor insurance distributor, Prima Assicurazioni S.p.A. (Prima), with the objective to expand its business portfolio and to contribute to the Ageas's Elevate27 profitable growth ambitions.

Under to the agreement, Ageas Re takes an 80% Quota Share on the Prima business underwritten by Triglav Group in 2025, commencing in the coming weeks.

Prima is a rapidly growing, profitable insurance distributor that began distributing personal lines policies, mainly Motor, in 2015. Since then, it has become the number 1 in the Italian Direct Motor business. In 2024, the company generated EUR 1.3 billion gross written premiums, servicing over 4 million customers, and EUR 104 million Group EBITDA.

This agreement is in perfect alignment with Ageas's Elevate27 strategy to achieve profitable growth in an attractive European Non-Life market. The Italian Motor insurance market generates premiums in excess of EUR 15 billion, with consistent profitability. Through this partnership, Ageas Re teams up with a tech-driven, local champion, with proven track record, providing immediate market entry with considerable scale.

Ageas Re anticipates inflows from this transaction in excess of EUR 500 million in 2025 and a Net Operating Result of around EUR 15 million, spread over 2025 and 2026. The impact on Group Solvency is estimated to be no more than -4 points in 2025.

Hans De Cuyper, CEO of Ageas stated : The agreement with Triglav Group aligns well with many aspects of our newly launched strategy, Elevate27. This collaboration enables us to enter a promising European growth market in Non-Life insurance and achieve profitable growth through a partner with a strong market position."

Joachim Racz, CEO of Ageas Re continued : "I am pleased to announce this partnership. Along with the entire Ageas Re team, I look forward to establishing a successful collaboration, offering high-quality insurance products to the Italian customer distributed by Prima. We would also like to thank Howden Re for the excellent management of the process and transaction."

George Ottathycal, CEO of Prima said : "Prima Assicurazioni has experienced remarkable growth in the Italian motor insurance market, surpassing 4 million active customers in just ten years. This success is the result of our sophisticated and rigorous pricing and underwriting, outstanding user experience, and, most importantly, our carefully selected strategic partners who fully align with our cutting-edge, technology- and data-driven business model. Not only will the solidity and trust of the new partners Triglav Group and Ageas Re further expand our growth, but will also deliver significant value to our entire network of agents and brokers—and, above all, to our customers."

Andrej Slapar, President of the Management Board of Zavarovalnica Triglav, commented : "Our strategic ambition is to grow beyond existing markets and enhance Triglav Group's international recognition. The Italian motor insurance market presents a strong opportunity to support this goal, and we are pleased to be working with well-established partners Prima and Ageas Re. The Triglav Group will continue to explore opportunities for further growth and for delivering on the other objectives set out in our strategy."

Ageas is a Belgian rooted listed international insurance Group with a heritage spanning of 200 years. It offers Retail and Business customers Life and Non-Life insurance products designed to suit their specific needs, today and tomorrow, and is also engaged in reinsurance activities. As one of Europe's larger insurance companies, Ageas concentrates its activities in Europe and Asia, which together make up the major part of the global insurance market. It operates successful insurance businesses in Belgium, the UK, Portugal, Türkiye, China, Malaysia, India, Thailand, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Singapore, and the Philippines through a combination of wholly owned subsidiaries and long-term partnerships with strong financial institutions and key distributors. Ageas ranks among the market leaders in the countries in which it operates. It represents a staff force of about 50,000 people and reported annual inflows of EUR 18.5 billion in 2024.

Prima Assicurazioni is an insurtech company operating as a specialized insurance agency in the automotive, home, and family sectors, serving over 4 million clients. It has revolutionized the Italian insurance market through innovation, technology, and a data-driven strategy. Thanks to unprecedented growth over its 10-year history, Prima's evolving business model has enhanced the user experience, offering competitive pricing and fostering greater market competition. A leader in Italy's online motor insurance sector, Prima also operates a nationwide network of agents. Since 2022, the company has expanded into the United Kingdom and Spain.

For 125 years, the Triglav Group has earned the trust of clients and other stakeholders through its expertise, experience, and financial strength. It is the largest insurance-financial group in the Adria region and one of the leading groups in Southeast Europe. The Group operates in six countries, with broader international presence through insurance and reinsurance activities. Insurance and asset management are the two main pillars of its operations. The Group employs more than 5,000 people. Its mission is to create a safer future. The core values of the Group are responsiveness, simplicity, and reliability. Its vision is focused on strengthening its identity and recognition as an international insurance-financial group. Through sustainable operations, it provides a development-oriented environment for employees, maintains strong partnerships, and represents a stable, secure, and profitable investment for shareholders. The parent company of the Triglav Group is Zavarovalnica Triglav, a Prime Market issuer on the Ljubljana Stock Exchange.

evidence.title: Guy Goldstein joins Munich Re’s primary subsidiary, ERGO as Chief AI Officer
evidence.text:
Guy Goldstein joins Munich Re’s primary subsidiary, ERGO as Chief AI Officer

25th September 2026 - Author: Saumya Jain -

Ergo Group AG, the primary insurance subsidiary of Munich Re, has appointed Guy Goldstein to a newly created role of Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer (CAIO) on its Management Board, effective 1 October 2026.

In his new role, Goldstein will be responsible for the systematic implementation of artificial intelligence across the entire ERGO Group. He steps into this expanded role in addition to his position as CEO of ERGO NEXT in the United States.

In 2016, he founded the US property and casualty insurer in Palo Alto in 2016, focusing on the specific needs of small business owners, built based on its proprietary technology stack.

ERGO NEXT has been fully integrated into ERGO since last year, following a partnership with ERGO and Munich Re that started in 2017.

Markus Rieß, Chief Executive Officer, ERGO Group AG, commented, “With the creation of the Chief AI Officer role, we are underscoring our strategic ambition to implement artificial intelligence systematically along our entire value chain and in all our markets.

“By appointing Guy Goldstein, we are entrusting this responsibility not only to a recognised AI visionary, but also to someone who has already successfully established one of the most innovative AI-driven insurance ventures in the market with ERGO NEXT. We now systematically integrate this innovative strength and outstanding experience into our Group Board, making it available across ERGO as a whole.”

Simultaneously, Mark Klein, currently Chief Digital Officer of ERGO Group AG, a role he has held since 2016, will leave the company at the end of the year at his own request.

In his most recent role, he was responsible not only for all strategic digitalisation initiatives, but also for Group Marketing and global partnerships. He was initially at ERGO Digital Ventures AG and, since 2024, as a member of the Management Board of ERGO Group AG.

Rieß added, “As ERGO is evolving into the leading technology‑ and AI‑driven primary insurer, Mark Klein has laid the digital foundations for this transformation. He and his teams have done outstanding pioneering work for ERGO, rapidly building up the Group’s digital capabilities. In doing so, Mark Klein has made an exceptionally important contribution to the future-readiness of our company.

“He has also played a key role in harmonising, modernising and significantly extending the reach of our brand in recent years. For all of this, he deserves my very special thanks. I wish him all the very best for the future, both professionally and personally.”

SIGNAL IDUNA to boost efficiency and optimise job functions with Gemini Enterprise

10th October 2025 - Author: Kassandra Jimenez-Sanchez -

SIGNAL IDUNA, parent company to reinsurer SI Re, has launched Gemini Enterprise from Google Cloud for its over 10,000 employees and sales partners, aiming to boost efficiency and optimise specific job functions through decentralised artificial intelligence agents.

With the introduction of Gemini Enterprise, SIGNAL IDUNA moves beyond the capabilities of standard virtual AI assistants.

The platform can be integrated with internal systems like CRM, HR, or marketing tools, giving employees access to the data they need to build tailored AI solutions for their daily challenges.

After a successful review, these individual solutions can then be scaled up for the entire company, improving digital skills and fostering innovation from within the organisation.

Johannes Rath, Member of the Board at SIGNAL IDUNA for Customer, Service, and Transformation, commented: “We are in the midst of a major corporate transformation. In the coming decade, around 30% of our employees will be leaving the company, predominantly due to retirement.

“Simultaneously, we are on a steady trajectory that will naturally increase our workload. We have been tackling this trend for a while with a comprehensive digitalization strategy centered on artificial intelligence. The pilot phase has already shown that, by launching Gemini Enterprise, we will markedly increase our operational efficiency.”

“Since 2023, SIGNAL IDUNA has been using artificial intelligence as a key technology for its large-scale agile transformation,” said Chris Lindsay, Vice President, Customer Engineering EMEA, Google Cloud. “We have already seen the significant impact delivered through the introduction of Co SI Health Assistant, that enables customer service agents, especially those with less experience, to access the right information at the right time, leading to shorter wait times, fewer call transfers, and, ultimately, more satisfied customers.”

He added: “The results speak for themselves: information searches are now 30% faster, and inquiries that previously required escalation dropped from 27% to just 3%. Now, the roll-out of Gemini Enterprise elevates our strategic partnership to the next level. As Google Cloud, we are proud to support SIGNAL IDUNA’s innovative initiatives in responding to market trends and evolving customer needs with speed and flexibility.”

evidence.title: Groupama 2025: government bond share falls to 23% over a decade, with no rotation into alternatives
evidence.text:
Home » SFCR Analysis » Groupama 2025: government bond share falls to 23% over a decade, with no rotation into alternatives

Groupama’s government bond share fell in every year of the past decade, from 39% of total assets in 2016 to 23% in 2025.

Almost none of the released capacity went into private markets, but rather into corporate credit and unit-linked contracts, according to figures published in the French group’s Solvency II filings.

Government bonds fell from EUR 38.0bn in 2016 to EUR 23.6bn in 2025, a reduction of EUR 14.4bn, while corporate bonds rose from EUR 14.4bn to EUR 18.4bn.

The bond book as a whole shrank by EUR 10.3bn, so this was not a one for one swap, but the mix inside it changed. Government paper accounted for 71% of Groupama’s bonds in 2016 and 55% by 2025, while the share of corporate bonds rose from 27% to 43%.

Most of that shift happened in two separate years, and for what look like different reasons. In 2022 government bonds fell 22% while total assets fell 12%, as rates rose and valuations dropped across the portfolio. The balance sheet alone cannot say how much of that was revaluation and how much was selling. 2024 is harder to explain that way: total assets fell 1%, but government bonds fell 15% and corporate bonds rose 13%.

That shift carries a capital cost. Corporate bonds attract a spread risk charge under the standard formula, while EEA government bonds do not. The Groupama 2025 SFCR (page 52) shows where the risk now sits: market risk accounts for around 44% of the basic capital requirement before diversification, and the largest single contributor within it is credit risk on bonds issued by private companies, ahead of property, equity, interest rate and currency risk.

Index-linked and unit-linked assets more than doubled, from EUR 8.1bn in 2016 to EUR 16.9bn in 2025 (up by 109%). The path was not smooth, with falls in 2018 and again in 2022. By 2025 the unit-linked book is the fourth largest block Groupama reports, behind government bonds, collective investment undertakings and corporate bonds.

Assets held against unit-linked contracts are matched by liabilities that move with them, so the market risk on that book sits with policyholders rather than with the group.

A rotation to alternative assets that did not happen

On the broad measure used across this series, which counts property, unlisted equities, other loans and mortgages, structured notes, collateralised securities and collective investment undertakings, investments in alternatives did not grow over the same period.

Their proportion of total assets fluctuated between 23% and 27% across the decade. The narrower direct measure of property, unlisted equities and other loans came to 4% or 5% in every year.

This is in contrast to peers such as Allianz whose reported collective investment undertakings ballooned to 32% in 2025 from only 2% of assets in 2016. Note that most of the Allianz shift was due to reclassification under Article 1(40) of the Solvency II Delegated Regulation rather than a portfolio move, as its own reports set out. Groupama’s line barely moved.

Nor is the collective investment line a private markets proxy here. Groupama’s 2025 investment income disclosure (2025 SFCR page 24) splits it into bond funds, equity funds and two lines of cash funds.

The valuation section of the SFCR sets out how each balance sheet line is measured, but does not explain why the portfolio changed, so the quantitative disclosure is the only evidence available. What it shows is a group that took the weight of its sovereign holdings from 39% of assets to 23%, put more of the balance sheet into corporate credit, and moved a growing share of market risk onto policyholders, while leaving its exposure to private and alternative assets where it stood in 2016.

The Tour de France and the Tour de France Femmes avec Zwift have announced a three-year partnership agreement with Groupama, running until 2028. This agreement is in line with Groupama's commitment to professional cycling, which began with the creation of the Groupama-FDJ team in 2018 and continues through its subsidiary Gan, which sponsors the FDJ-SUEZ women's team.

This partnership also reflects the shared ambitions between the Grande Boucle and Groupama to invest in amateur and everyday cyclists through initiatives to support clubs and promote safety awareness. It is also based on a convergence in the promotion of cycling with a desire to be close to the French people: bringing the greatest champions of the Tour de France and the Tour de France Femmes avec Zwift to the public's doorstep, as well as establishing a presence throughout the country for Groupama with its regional offices and staff, both employees and volunteers, present all over France.

Sylvain Burel, Groupama Group Communications Director: « By becoming an official partner of the Tour de France and the Tour de France Femmes avec Zwift, we are strengthening our presence in a sport we already support at the highest level. This partnership with A.S.O. marks a new step in our ambition to pursue a coherent and ambitious sponsorship strategy. Groupama is now a key player in the cycling world. »

Yann Le Moenner, CEO of A.S.O.: « We are delighted to welcome Groupama as one of our official partners. This partnership reflects the values we share around cycling. It is another step forward in their commitment to the sport, whether for professionals, amateurs or everyday cyclists. »

evidence.title: À La Défense, Groupama Immobilier va ouvrir un lieu éphémère consacré à l’intelligence artificielle
evidence.text:
À La Défense, Groupama Immobilier va ouvrir un lieu éphémère consacré à l’intelligence artificielle

Un campus éphémère voué à l’intelligence artificielle. Quatre ans après l’ouverture du Campus Cyber , Groupama Immobilier veut faire du plus grand quartier d’affaires européen une terre où l’intelligence artificielle (IA) a toute sa place. La filiale de l’assureur français a annoncé ce mardi, en marge du Mipim, l’ouverture prochaine de la « Maison de l’IA de La Défense ».

Ce lieu s’installera dans l’immeuble de bureaux Le Diamant, en bordure du boulevard Patrick Devedjian, à Puteaux, non loin du Campus Cyber. Actuellement occupé par Groupama, le bâtiment de 14 000 mètres carrés, achevé en 1992, sera vidé en juillet prochain par ses équipes qui s’installeront, avec le reste des troupes, à Nanterre. Avant de mener un vaste projet de reconversion de son bâtiment en logements, dont des études sont actuellement en cours, Groupama Immobilier souhaite faire vivre ce site plutôt que de le laisser sans vie.

L’objectif est d’y rassembler pour quelques années des startups, des fonds d’investissement, des centres d’IA d’entreprises, des organismes de formation et des acteurs publics, avec des loyers annoncés « très inférieurs au marché ». Avec ce campus, Groupama n’ambitionne pas de faire venir des géants du secteur comme OpenAI, xAI ou Google, mais plutôt des startups. « Il ne s’agira pas d’une IA de recherche ou académique. Ça, on le laisse au Plateau de Saclay. On parle plutôt d’une IA opérationnelle », confie Roland Cubin, directeur général délégué de Groupama Immobilier, qui regrette qu’à La Défense aucun projet d’envergure n’ait été lancé jusque-là, contrairement à d’autres villes françaises.

Une bonne partie des équipements de l’immeuble de neuf étages, dont le mobilier, sera conservée. Les plateaux d’environ 1 500 mètres carrés par étage pourraient être divisés par thématiques, par exemple la mobilité ou la santé. Les cinq étages de travail, ouverts ou cloisonnés, seront complétés par des espaces communs avec une « Pitch Room » au sommet et un Genius Bar au niveau inférieur. Des salles de formation sont également envisagées. Enfin, dans le socle du bâtiment, une cafétéria et des services seront proposés aux utilisateurs.

Tout devrait aller très vite. Groupama Immobilier indique lancer deux appels à manifestation d’intérêt (les candidatures sont à envoyer à maisonia@groupama-immobilier.fr ). Le premier, disponible jusqu’au 10 mai, permettra de trouver l’opérateur du lieu. Le second, les occupants. « Les candidatures vont être ouvertes jusqu’au 10 juin », précise Roland Cubin. Un jury composé de spécialistes de l’IA, d’investisseurs et de personnalités qualifiées se réunira en juillet pour désigner les futurs occupants. Les premiers aménagements devraient alors débuter en septembre, pour une ouverture envisagée en octobre de cette année.

Prévu dans un premier temps pour fonctionner trois ans, le lieu pourrait être prolongé en cas de succès. « Si ça prend vraiment, c’est possible. On ne s’interdit rien », confie Roland Cubin. Même si, à terme, l’immeuble sera transformé, Groupama pourrait pérenniser sur un autre site son campus dédié à l’IA. « Tout est envisageable. Si ça fonctionne, on pourrait même construire un immeuble neuf », assure Roland Cubin.

Bienvenue sur le site d’actualité et d’informations dédié à La Défense, le premier quartier d’affaire en Europe, situé sur les communes de Puteaux, Courbevoie et Nanterre.

Retrouvez dès la page d’accueil toutes les informations immobilières, économiques, sociales, commerciales et culturelles qui font l’actualité du territoire, et accédez gratuitement à l’ensemble de nos articles, dossiers et galeries photos publiés depuis 2003.

The Board of Directors of Groupama Assurances Mutuelles met on 3 April 2025, under the chairmanship of Laurent Poupart, and approved the Group's combined financial statements for fiscal year 2024.

Activity (insurance premiums and other income)

At 31 December 2024, Groupama's combined premium income stood at €18.5 billion, +8.9% increase from 31 December 2023. The increase stemmed from the development of property and casualty insurance (+5.2%), sustained growth in health & protection insurance (+15.2%) and the return to growth in the savings & pensions business (+8.1%).

Insurance premium income in France at 31 December 2024 amounted to €15.2 billion, up +8.9% compared with 31 December 2023.

In property and casualty insurance, premium income amounted to €7.0 billion at 31 December 2024, up +4.3%, driven by strong growth in business and local authority insurance (+8.1%), home insurance (+5.1%) and, to a lesser extent, by the increase in motor insurance (+2.8%) and agricultural insurance (+2.9%).

The health & protection business saw strong growth (+14.8%) to €5.5 billion as at 31 December 2024, underpinned by increases in both group health (+23.5%) and individual health (+7.2%).

In savings & pensions, premium income rebounded with a growth of 9.7%, reaching €2.7 billion as of December 31, 2024. This growth was driven by an increase in individual savings & pensions (+12.6%), particularly in unit-linked savings & pensions (+22.5%), which benefited from the success of Telluma.

At the end of 2024, business reached €3.1 billion, up +8.3% at constant scope and exchange rates compared with 31 December 2023, benefiting from strong business growth in Hungary (+19.1%) and sustained growth in Romania (+7.4%) and Italy (+5.9%).

Property and casualty insurance premium income totalled €2.3 billion as at 31 December 2024, up +8.2% from the previous period. This growth was driven by property and casualty insurance for businesses and local authorities (+15.6%), mainly in Romania, by motor insurance (+6.7%), which grew significantly in Hungary, Bulgaria and Italy, as well as by strong performances in home insurance (+11.7%), particularly in Greece and Bulgaria.

Premium income in savings & pensions was virtually stable (-0.6%) at €0.5 billion, with growth in individual savings & pensions in unit-linked products (+25.5%) being offset by the decline in the group savings& pensions business (-41.8%).

In health and protection, business grew significantly (+21.8%) to €0.4 billion, benefiting from growth in group insurance (+40.0%), mainly in Romania and Bulgaria, and from the increase in individual protection (+14.1%).

The Group's premium income was €246 million, including €238 million from Groupama Asset Management and €8 million from Groupama Epargne Salariale.

Economic operating income increased to €954 million at 31 December 2024, up 52% compared with 31 December 2023.

It came from property and casualty insurance for €429 million (€316 million as at 31 December 2023) and health and protection insurance for €299 million (€233 million as at 31 December 2023). The Group's non-life combined ratio was 95.1% at 31 December 2024, an improvement of -1.7 points compared with 31 December 2023. This change is linked to the decrease in claims related to natural disasters, for which the cost net of reinsurance amounted to €637 million in 2024 compared with €968 million in 2023, as well as the improvement in the attritional loss experience and the increase in prior year reserve bonuses. Conversely, the discount effect is less than in 2023. The operating costs ratio was virtually stable at 28.1% as at 31 December 2024.

Economic operating income from savings & pensions was €327 million at 31 December 2024 (€156 million at 31 December 2023). It benefited in particular from the result of the switch of the share reinsured by Groupama Gan Vie to CNP Retraite in the PREFON Retraite reinsurance treaty, effective 1 January 2024.

Economic operating income from financial activities amounted to +€44 million and that of the Group's holding company activity was -€146 million at 31 December 2024.

The transition from economic operating income to net income includes non-recurring items, in particular the realisation of capital gains or losses, the change in the fair value of financial assets, and financing expenses. The Group's overall net income totalled €961 million at 31 December 2024, compared with €510 million at 31 December 2023.

Group's IFRS equity totalled €10.5 billion at 31 December 2024 compared with €9.9 billion as at 31 December 2023. This change is mainly due to the positive contribution of income for the financial year and the perpetual subordinated debt issue in early July 2024 for €600 million, mitigated by the redemption in May 2024 of the perpetual subordinated notes issued in 2014 for €871 million.

The Group's contractual service margin, which represents the deferred future profits of outstanding contracts in savings and pensions and long-term protection, amounted to €3.8 billion at 31 December 2024, up +€162 million compared with 31 December 2023.

Insurance investments totalled €67.2 billion, down -€3.2 billion, mainly due to the disposal of assets from the Prefon portfolio and changes in the financial markets (rise in government bond yields).

At 31 December 2024, the Solvency 2 ratio, without transitional measure on underwriting reserves, was 185%. The 12-point decrease in the rate compared with end-2023 was mainly due to unfavourable market effects reflecting the widening of government bond spreads as well as the redemption in May 2024 of perpetual subordinated bonds issued in 2014 for €871 million, partially offset by the net income for the fiscal year and by the issue of perpetual subordinated debt in July 2024 for €600 million. The ratio with transitional measure on underwriting reserves, authorised by the ACPR, was 241%.

The Group's financial strength was highlighted by Fitch Ratings, which affirmed Groupama's rating at 'A+' with a 'Stable' outlook on 9 December 2024.

A CNP Assurances está a estudar a aquisição da Coface, seguradora francesa especializada em seguro de crédito comercial, numa operação que representaria uma diversificação significativa do negócio do grupo controlado pela La Banque Postale. A informação foi avançada pela News Assurances Pro , com base numa notícia da Bloomberg , e posteriormente corroborada pela Reuters . As conversações estarão ainda numa fase preliminar e a CNP poderá acabar por não apresentar uma proposta. Também poderão surgir outros potenciais interessados na Coface.

Escolha o ECO como fonte preferida no Google

A eventual operação teria como principal obstáculo acionista a Arch Capital Group, que detém cerca de 29,9% da Coface e é o maior acionista da seguradora. Segundo a informação divulgada pela Bloomberg, uma eventual transação teria de contar com a posição deste acionista. A Coface está cotada na Bolsa de Paris desde 2014 e, após a divulgação da notícia, as suas ações chegaram a subir 8,9%, colocando a capitalização bolsista em cerca de 2,6 mil milhões de euros.

Para além da Arch, são também acionistas de referência, com cerca de 5% cada um, a Silchester Investors, a Allianz Global Investors e o empresário Olivier Goudet. Para analistas, é considerado 65% do capital em free-float.

A Coface tem um perfil bastante diferente do negócio tradicional da CNP. Especializada na proteção das empresas contra o risco de incumprimento dos seus clientes, a seguradora disponibiliza seguro de crédito comercial, informação empresarial, cobrança de dívidas, seguro single-risk , caução e factoring. A aquisição permitiria assim à CNP ganhar uma plataforma internacional num negócio diretamente ligado à atividade das empresas, às exportações e às cadeias de fornecimento, afirma o site de notícias.

A eventual operação teria também uma dimensão portuguesa. A Coface opera diretamente em Portugal através de uma sucursal, com instalações em Lisboa, disponibilizando soluções de seguro de crédito, informação comercial, cobrança, single risk e outros serviços associados à gestão do risco de crédito e disponibiliza em Portugal plataformas digitais para clientes e mediadores.

Do lado da potencial compradora, a ligação a Portugal também existe. A CNP Assurances está presente no mercado português através da CNP Partners, plataforma do grupo para Itália, Espanha e Portugal, com atividade centrada sobretudo em poupança patrimonial e proteção e previdência . A própria CNP identifica Portugal entre os 17 países onde o grupo desenvolve atividade internacional.

A presença ibérica da CNP tem mais de duas décadas. A CNP Iberia refere uma atividade em Portugal e Espanha assente em seguros de vida, acidentes e proteção de pagamentos, tanto em seguro direto como em resseguro.

Existe ainda uma segunda ligação relevante: a CNP Santander Insurance, joint venture entre a CNP Assurances e o Banco Santander, desenvolve produtos de proteção para clientes do Santander Consumer Finance em 12 países europeus, incluindo Portugal. A atividade inclui, entre outros, seguros de proteção ao crédito.

A dimensão financeira da CNP é outro elemento relevante para avaliar a possibilidade de uma eventual aquisição. Em 2025, o grupo registou 39,1 mil milhões de euros de volume de prémios, mais 8,6% em termos comparáveis, e um resultado líquido atribuível de 1,492 mil milhões de euros. O rácio de cobertura do SCR situou-se em 256%, enquanto os capitais próprios atingiram 22,7 mil milhões de euros.

A CNP é integralmente controlada pela La Banque Postale, depois de o banco francês ter concluído a integração da seguradora no seu grupo. A operação insere-se num modelo de bancassurance que combina a distribuição através dos canais bancários com uma estratégia multiparceiros em França e nos mercados internacionais. O grupo conta com mais de 8.700 trabalhadores e cerca de 10 milhões de segurados em poupança e reforma e 33 milhões de clientes em proteção de bens e pessoas.

Os números da Coface dão dimensão ao ativo que estaria em causa. Em 2025, a companhia registou cerca de 1,85 mil milhões de euros de volume de negócios e 222 milhões de euros de resultado líquido , enquanto o rácio de solvência se situou em cerca de 197%. A empresa tem ainda uma componente de serviços não seguradores, nomeadamente informação empresarial, cobrança e factoring .

No momento em que a informação é mais importante do que nunca, apoie o jornalismo independente e rigoroso.

Esta assinatura é uma forma de apoiar o ECO e os seus jornalistas. A nossa contrapartida é o jornalismo independente, rigoroso e credível.

evidence.title: CNP Assurances et Coface : le projet de rachat surprise qui bouscule le marché de l'assurance
evidence.text:
CNP Assurances et Coface : le projet de rachat surprise qui bouscule le marché de l'assurance

Le 18 septembre 2026, Bloomberg a révélé que CNP Assurances étudiait une prise de contrôle de Coface, spécialiste des factures impayées. L'opération ferait entrer le n° 2 français de l'assurance de prêt immobilier dans un métier neuf, tourné vers les entreprises. L'action Coface a aussitôt bondi de 8,9 % à la Bourse de Paris. Les discussions restent préliminaires, aucune offre n'est déposée, et rien n'annonce de changement pour les assurés de CNP.

Un scoop de Bloomberg que ni CNP ni Coface n'ont démenti

Bloomberg s'appuie sur des personnes proches du dossier, pas sur un communiqué officiel. Reuters a repris l'information le soir même, dans une dépêche diffusée à 19 h 57 . Selon ces sources, CNP prépare une offre, mais les discussions en sont à un stade précoce . CNP pourrait renoncer, et d'autres candidats pourraient se manifester.

CNP Assurances, Coface et le premier actionnaire de Coface, l'assureur Arch Capital, ont tous refusé de commenter . La Bourse a aussitôt réagi : après cette hausse de 8,9 % , la société valait 2,6 milliards d'euros en Bourse, selon Bloomberg.

Le groupe CNP Assurances a réalisé 39,1 milliards d'euros de chiffre d'affaires en 2025, pour 1,5 milliard d'euros de résultat net. Assureur de biens et de personnes, il vit surtout de l'épargne, de la retraite, de la prévoyance et de l'assurance de prêt. Il appartient à La Banque Postale , elle-même filiale de La Poste, contrôlée par la Caisse des dépôts.

Comparer mon assurance de prêt immobilier

Un conseiller Selectra compare gratuitement les offres d'assurance emprunteur pour vous aider à payer moins cher.

Coface, l'assureur qui paie quand le client d'une entreprise fait défaut

Coface vend de l' assurance-crédit , c'est-à-dire une protection des entreprises contre les factures impayées. Une PME livre sa marchandise et laisse 60 jours à son client pour payer. Si ce client fait faillite, l'assureur rembourse une grande partie de la perte. Avant de couvrir, il évalue chaque client et fixe le montant qu'il accepte de garantir.

Sans cette protection, beaucoup de fournisseurs exigeraient d'être payés comptant. Le Code des assurances la range dans une famille à part, la branche 14 « Crédit » . Elle couvre notamment l'insolvabilité des clients, c'est-à-dire leur incapacité à payer.

Coface revendique 100 000 clients sur quelque 200 marchés et plus de 80 ans d'existence. En 2025, elle a réalisé 1,847 milliard d'euros de chiffre d'affaires et 222 millions d'euros de bénéfice net. Les garanties publiques à l'export relèvent d'un autre acteur : depuis le 1er janvier 2017, Bpifrance les accorde au nom de l'État.

Assurance-crédit et assurance emprunteur : deux métiers distincts

Les deux expressions se ressemblent, mais elles ne protègent pas les mêmes personnes. L'assurance-crédit, le métier de Coface, protège une entreprise quand l'un de ses clients ne règle pas sa facture, par exemple après une faillite. L'assurance emprunteur, dont CNP est n° 2 en France, protège un particulier et sa banque en remboursant le prêt en cas de décès ou d'invalidité. Un rachat de Coface ne transformerait pas votre assurance de prêt.

L'écart de taille est net : le chiffre d'affaires de Coface pèse environ 21 fois moins que celui de CNP. L'enjeu tiendrait donc au métier. Un grand assureur de particuliers, contrôlé par un groupe public, s'ouvrirait à la clientèle d'entreprises de Coface. Le rapprochement réunirait CNP, n° 2 français de l'assurance-vie et de l'assurance de prêt immobilier, et Coface, qui se présente comme un acteur mondial de premier plan de l'assurance-crédit.

Arch Capital, l'actionnaire que CNP devrait d'abord convaincre

Pour réussir, CNP devrait convaincre Arch Capital , écrit Bloomberg. Cet assureur coté au Nasdaq détient 29,86 % de Coface, selon la société. Les salariés en possèdent 1,32 %, le reste s'échange en Bourse.

Arch a racheté 29,5 % du capital à Natixis au prix de 9,95 € par action, dividende attaché. L'opération a été finalisée le 10 février 2021 , après le feu vert des autorités de concurrence. Sur la base de la valorisation citée par Bloomberg, l'action valait un peu plus de 17 € après l'annonce.

L'AMF, le gendarme de la Bourse, a publié en juin 2026 que CNP détenait 4,62 % du capital et des droits de vote de Coface. Ces actions ont presque toutes été reçues en garantie, et non achetées. Avec une autre filiale de la Caisse des dépôts, le groupe public a dépassé 5 % le 11 juin 2026 et atteint 6 % . Cet avis ne relie pas ces titres au projet révélé par Bloomberg.

La loi fixe le chemin d'une prise de contrôle. Quiconque dépasse 30 % du capital ou des droits de vote d'une société cotée doit proposer de racheter les titres des autres actionnaires. Le Code monétaire et financier appelle cela une offre publique (article L433-3). Le bloc d'Arch ajouté aux 4,62 % de CNP ferait environ 34,5 %, donc au-delà du seuil.

Une prise de contrôle passerait ainsi par une offre encadrée par l'AMF. Les autorités de concurrence et celles qui surveillent les assureurs devraient aussi donner leur accord.

Trouver une assurance de prêt moins chère

Un conseiller Selectra compare gratuitement les offres d'assurance emprunteur pour vous aider à payer moins cher.

Emprunteur ou épargnant chez CNP : rien n'annonce de changement pour vos contrats

Rien, dans les informations publiées, n'indique un changement pour les assurés de CNP. Aucune offre n'est déposée, et Coface assure des entreprises, pas des particuliers. Votre assurance de prêt, votre assurance-vie ou votre prévoyance ne relèvent pas de ce métier.

CNP pèse lourd sur ce marché : elle se dit n° 2 de l'assurance emprunteur immobilier en France. Son activité d' assurance emprunteur a généré 3,435 milliards d'euros de chiffre d'affaires en 2025, contre 3,702 milliards d'euros en 2024. Cela fait 7,2 % de moins , un recul que le groupe explique par un « marché du crédit encore tendu ».

Si vous remboursez un prêt assuré par CNP via La Banque Postale, vous gardez un levier pour agir sur son coût. L'article L113-12-2 du Code des assurances vous permet de changer d'assurance de prêt à tout moment après la signature de l'offre. Selon le Code de la consommation, la banque ne peut refuser un contrat aux garanties équivalentes , couvrant les mêmes risques. Si elle refuse malgré tout, votre ancien contrat continue.

Nathalie, 41 ans, infirmière à Limoges, rembourse depuis 5 ans un prêt immobilier de La Banque Postale, assuré par le contrat collectif de CNP. Elle se demande si sa cotisation va changer, alors que rien ne l'annonce. À titre d'exemple, sans reprendre de tarif CNP, elle paie 30 € par mois pendant encore 15 ans, soit 5 400 € . Une délégation d'assurance emprunteur aux garanties équivalentes, choisie hors de la banque, à 18 € par mois coûterait 3 240 €, soit 2 160 € d'économie .

Le projet concerne d'abord les actionnaires de Coface et ses entreprises clientes. Pour vous, la décision utile porte sur le coût de votre assurance de prêt, rachat ou non.

Ce soir, relevez sur votre offre de prêt le nom de l'assureur et le coût total de l'assurance, puis comparez-le à une offre équivalente.

evidence.title: CNP Assurances considers Coface takeover as France insurance consolidation interest emerges
evidence.text:
CNP Assurances considers Coface takeover as France insurance consolidation interest emerges

Early-stage deal deliberations are drawing attention to potential consolidation in France's insurance sector. CNP Assurances is considering a possible takeover of trade credit insurer Coface, although the group could still decide not to move forward.

The report also says other bidders could emerge for Coface. CNP and Coface decline to comment on the matter. Potential sector impact in France CNP, or Caisse Nationale de Prevoyance, is a major personal insurer in France, with operations across Europe and Brazil. A move for Coface would extend its reach into trade credit insurance and related corporate risk services.

Coface provides protection against customer non-payment for companies and also offers business information services, debt collection, single-risk insurance, surety bonds and factoring. Any transaction would therefore connect a large personal insurer with a specialist in commercial credit risk and business services.

Our earlier article covered Orion180 Insurance’s Nasdaq debut, which priced below its marketed range and opened lower, highlighting cautious investor demand for insurance stocks in a tougher IPO market. We noted the listing as an early gauge for upcoming insurance-sector flotations, with rising climate-related claims and higher premiums shaping sentiment around insurers’ valuations and growth prospects.

France's CNP Assurances considers takeover of Coface, Bloomberg News reports

Published by Global Banking & Finance Review

CNP Assurances, the French insurer wholly owned by La Banque Postale, is exploring a takeover bid for Coface, a trade credit insurer, though deliberations are preliminary and other bidders may surface.

CNP Assurances Weighs Potential Takeover of Coface, Says Bloomberg

Potential Acquisition Discussions Between CNP Assurances and Coface

Sept 18 (Reuters) - French insurance group CNP Assurances is considering a potential takeover of Coface, Bloomberg News reported on Friday, citing people with knowledge of the matter.

CNP is working on an offer for the credit insurer, the report added.

Deliberations are at an early stage, and CNP could decide against proceeding with an offer, the report said, adding that other bidders could emerge.

CNP and Coface declined to comment on the report.

CNP, or Caisse Nationale de Prevoyance, is a leading personal insurer in France, with operations across Europe and Brazil, according to its website.

Coface provides trade credit insurance that protects companies against the risk of customer non-payment. It also offers business information services, debt collection, single-risk insurance, surety bonds and factoring.

(Reporting by Sumedha Mukherjee in Bengaluru; Editing by Maju Samuel)

evidence.title: CNP Assurances ocupa 1º lugar entre seguradoras no ranking ESG da Sustainalytics
evidence.text:
Crédito: Divulgação Reconhecimento internacional reforça estratégia de sustentabilidade do Grupo, que completa 25 anos de atuação no Brasil em 2026

A CNP Assurances tornou-se a seguradora número 1 do mundo no ranking ESG da Morningstar Sustainalytics, alcançando a melhor avaliação atribuída pela agência nessa categoria. Em 18 meses, a CNP Assurances avançou seis posições entre as seguradoras avaliadas. Em fevereiro de 2025, havia alcançado a liderança entre as seguradoras francesas e agora chega ao primeiro lugar mundial.

A Morningstar Sustainalytics é uma das principais referências globais em pesquisa, dados e ratings ESG. Com mais de 30 anos de atuação, seu ESG Risk Ratings avalia mais de 16 mil empresas em todo o mundo, considerando a exposição a riscos ambientais, sociais e de governança e a capacidade das empresas de gerenciá-los.

O reconhecimento está alinhado à estratégia global “Lead for Impact” da CNP Assurances, que busca reforçar sua atuação como seguradora responsável e acelerar o seu papel como investidor responsável, ao mesmo tempo em que intensifica o seu impulso comercial e acelera a transformação operacional e tecnológica do Grupo.

No Brasil, onde a CNP Assurances completa 25 anos de atuação em 2026, a sustentabilidade também está integrada à estratégia e se materializa em diferentes frentes. A atuação inclui iniciativas voltadas à preservação ambiental e ao desenvolvimento da bioeconomia na Amazônia, projetos de inclusão e apoio à juventude, além de investimentos e fundos direcionados à transição para uma economia mais sustentável.

“Esse reconhecimento reforça uma convicção que orienta nossa atuação também no Brasil: sustentabilidade é parte da nossa estratégia de longo prazo. Ao longo desses 25 anos, buscamos transformar esse compromisso em ações concretas, seja por meio de nossos negócios e investimentos, seja em projetos ambientais e sociais”, afirma Maximiliano Villanueva, CEO da CNP Assurances para a América Latina.

A CNP Assurances é um grupo segurador com mais de 8.700 colaboradores e presença em 17 países. Em 2025, registrou resultado líquido de € 1,492 bilhão. A CNP Assurances administra € 422 bilhões em investimentos globalmente e atua para promover uma sociedade mais inclusiva e sustentável.

No Brasil, onde está presente desde 2001, é o terceiro maior grupo segurador do país e completa 25 anos de atuação em 2026. O Brasil é o principal mercado da CNP Assurances fora da Europa, onde a empresa atua nos segmentos de seguros, previdência e consórcios, por meio de diferentes empresas e parcerias.

evidence.title: Covéa deploys Shift platform to modernise fraud and risk controls
evidence.text:
UK insurer Covéa is overhauling how it manages fraud and risk across the insurance lifecycle, selecting Shift Technology as a long-term strategic partner to support a new end-to-end approach spanning underwriting, claims and mid-term policy adjustments.

The move reflects Covéa’s shift away from fragmented fraud detection tools towards a unified platform that enables a consistent view of risk from policy inception through to claims settlement.

Shift’s AI-driven solutions will support multiple areas of the insurer’s operations, including underwriting risk analysis, claims fraud detection, compliance risk scoring and case management. The technology is designed to help Covéa protect its portfolio, strengthen decision-making and improve operational efficiency.

According to Covéa, the underwriting component of the deployment delivered a return on investment within three months of going live, driven by earlier risk identification and reduced leakage.

At the centre of the system is Shift’s role as a data analysis engine, integrating information from multiple third-party sources including CUE Data and Companies House. The platform aggregates and analyses this information to generate explainable risk signals that help teams assess exposure across motor, home, commercial and high-net-worth insurance lines.

These insights allow underwriters and claims teams to prioritise cases more effectively and intervene earlier in the policy lifecycle.

George Robbins, Head of UK Markets at Shift Technology, said, “Covéa’s approach illustrates a broader shift in the market, where insurers are no longer looking at fraud detection in isolation but as part of an end-to-end transformation agenda. By combining predictive models to surface risk, generative AI to synthesise and explain cases, and agentic capabilities to orchestrate actions, always with human oversight, insurers can take earlier, more consistent actions and generate measurable value at scale.”

The partnership is expected to expand further as Covéa explores additional automation opportunities and new risk-management use cases as part of its evolving operating model.

Stephen Long, Claims, IT & Operations Director at Covéa, said, “Shift represents a transformative step in how we manage financial crime risk across our organisation and marks an important milestone in our broader AI journey. With significant investment behind it, the platform strengthens our ability to protect our business while driving smarter, more efficient ways of working.

“It’s a major step in our financial crime strategy and a strong example of how adopting advanced AI and modernising key platforms can unlock real value. This partnership enables us to strengthen risk detection today while laying the foundations for a more resilient, automated and consistent AI-led approach for the future.”

evidence.title: Watch Axa and Covea discuss the shift from generative to agentic AI
evidence.text:
As insurers become more comfortable with generative artificial intelligence, attention is shifting to the next evolution: agentic AI systems that can reason, plan, and take autonomous action

Unlike generative tools that simply respond to prompts, agentic AI has the potential to manage workflows, make decisions and initiate follow-up actions across underwriting, claims and fraud operations.

With this in mind Insurance Post, in association with Hyland, would like to invite you to watch a webinar on the 30 September at 3pm, where an expert panel will explore how insurers can prepare for this shift, what use cases are emerging, and how organisations must rethink oversight as AI begins to act independently.

Alongside the operational opportunity, experts including Paul Hollands, chief data and AI officer at Axa UK , and Tom Clay, chief data scientist at Covea Insurance, will address the ethical, regulatory, and safety concerns of giving this technology greater autonomy.

evidence.title: Insurtech Akur8 Selected By France’s Insurance Provider Covéa Group to Streamline Pricing Processes
evidence.text:
Akur8 , the artificial intelligence (AI)-based pricing solution dedicated to insurers, announces today that the Covéa Group , an insurance provider in France, has chosen its platform to optimize its pricing processes.

This collaboration will enable Covéa to accelerate its pricing cycles, enhance the “accuracy of its risk models, and standardize its practices across its various brands, including MMA, MAAF, and GMF.”

By adopting Akur8, Covéa strengthens its ability to “respond to rapid market changes while maintaining a high level of performance and competitiveness.”

Akur8’s solution, which is said to be recognized for its “transparency and ease of use,” reportedly provides Covéa’s actuarial teams with “a more agile and collaborative approach, while meeting regulatory requirements.”

Samuel Falmagne , CEO of Akur8, remarked:

“We are delighted to collaborate with Covéa, a major player in the insurance sector in France. This adoption highlights the value that Akur8 brings to insurers seeking to combine innovation, precision, and efficiency in their pricing processes.”

“The integration of Akur8 into our operations allows us to gain agility and consistency in developing our pricing, while providing our teams with a powerful tool to analyze risks with greater accuracy.”

With this partnership, Akur8 says that it now reinforces its position as a key partner for insurers in Europe and worldwide, “supporting industry leaders in their digital transformation.”

As covered, Akur8 is transforming insurance pricing with “a transparent AI solution that automates risk modeling while ensuring full control for actuaries.”

Available globally, Akur8 explains that it focuses on helping insurers “make better decisions, faster.”

As noted in the update, Covéa is a mutual insurance group in France, encompassing “the brands MAAF, MMA, and GMF.”

With more than 11 million policyholders and clients, Covéa reportedly protects one in three people in France in the “areas of auto, home, and health insurance.”

evidence.title: Sampo stock slips 0.7 percent ahead of the open
evidence.text:
Sampo stock closed 0.7 percent lower in Helsinki on September 24, 2026. The move followed news that Solidium had sold about EUR 630 million of Sampo shares on September 23, 2026, according to STT Info .

Sampo Oyj (ISIN FI0009003305, Nasdaq Helsinki: SAMPO) ended the September 24 session at the Helsinki close after losing 0.7 percent. The same-day market report also placed Sampo among the most actively traded Helsinki shares, while the reference market moved lower.

Solidium said on September 24, 2026, that it would transfer about EUR 400 million of Sampo A shares to the Finnish state by year-end as part of an investment-program financing arrangement, STT Info reported.

The Solidium transaction remains the company-specific market item for September 25, 2026. The announcement said Solidium would hold about 2 percent of Sampo A shares after the September 23 sale and the planned transfer, according to STT Info .

Broader market context includes the September 24 US close, when the S&P 500 ended at 7,704.13, down less than 0.1 percent. That comparison provides a dated reference for the global market backdrop before the Helsinki session.

evidence.title: Sampo completes its share buyback programme
evidence.text:
Sampo plc, stock exchange release, 25 September 2026 at 8:40 am EEST

Sampo completes its share buyback programme

Sampo plc has completed its EUR 350 million share buyback programme, launched on 6 May 2026. The repurchases of shares began on 7 May 2026 and ended on 24 September 2026. During that period, Sampo repurchased 37,827,020 of its own A shares at an average price of EUR 9.24 per share. This corresponds to 1.42 per cent of all Sampo plc’s shares based on the share count prior to the start of this programme. The repurchase of own shares has reduced the company's unrestricted equity by approximately EUR 350 million.

The purpose of the buyback programme was to return excess capital to shareholders by reducing Sampo plc’s capital, as the repurchased shares will be cancelled. Following the cancellation, the total number of Sampo shares will be 2,617,847,806 shares, of which 2,616,847,806 will be A shares and 1,000,000 B shares.

Further information on share buybacks is available at www.sampo.com/sharebuyback .

evidence.title: Sampo Completes €350 Million Share Buyback Programme and Plans Cancellation of 37.8 Million Repurchased Shares
evidence.text:
Sampo Completes €350 Million Share Buyback Programme and Plans Cancellation of 37.8 Million Repurchased Shares

Sampo Completes €350 Million Share Buyback Programme and Plans Cancellation of 37.8 Million Repurchased Shares

(IN BRIEF) Sampo plc has completed its €350 million share buyback programme after repurchasing 37,827,020 A shares between 7 May and 24 September 2026. The shares were acquired at an average price of €9.24 each and represent approximately 1.42% of Sampo’s total share count before the programme began. The repurchases reduced the company’s unrestricted equity by around €350 million. Sampo launched the programme on 6 May 2026 with the objective of returning excess capital to shareholders through a reduction in share capital. All shares purchased under the programme are scheduled to be cancelled. Once that cancellation has been completed, Sampo will have 2,617,847,806 shares outstanding, comprising 2,616,847,806 A shares and 1,000,000 B shares.

(PRESS RELEASE) HELSINKI, 25-Sep-2026 — / EuropaWire / — Sampo plc has completed its €350 million share buyback programme , which was launched on 6 May 2026 as part of the company’s capital management strategy.

Repurchases commenced on 7 May 2026 and concluded on 24 September 2026.

Over the course of the programme, Sampo repurchased a total of 37,827,020 of its own A shares at an average purchase price of €9.24 per share.

The shares acquired under the programme represent approximately 1.42% of all Sampo plc shares, based on the company’s total share count before the buyback began.

As a result of the repurchases, Sampo’s unrestricted equity has been reduced by approximately €350 million.

The programme was undertaken to return excess capital to shareholders through a reduction in the company’s capital.

Sampo intends to cancel all shares purchased under the programme.

Following cancellation of the 37,827,020 A shares, Sampo’s total number of outstanding shares will amount to 2,617,847,806.

Of this total, 2,616,847,806 will be A shares, while 1,000,000 will be B shares.

The completion of the programme concludes the share repurchase initiative announced in May and reduces Sampo’s share count in line with the capital-return objective established when the programme was launched. Further information on share buybacks is available at www.sampo.com/sharebuyback .

evidence.title: Sampo to Record €118 Million Impairment Loss on Denmark IT Assets as Topdanmark Integration Advances
evidence.text:
Sampo to Record €118 Million Impairment Loss on Denmark IT Assets as Topdanmark Integration Advances

Sampo to Record €118 Million Impairment Loss on Denmark IT Assets as Topdanmark Integration Advances

(IN BRIEF) Sampo will recognise an approximately €118 million pre-tax impairment loss, including related VAT charges, in the third quarter of 2026 following an impairment review of intangible IT assets in Denmark. The assessment was carried out as the integration of Topdanmark into If Group moved into a phase focused on completing the harmonisation of core IT systems. The charge is non-cash and will be recorded in other expenses. Sampo said the impairment will be excluded from operating EPS and is expected to have only a minor effect on the group’s solvency position. The adjustment reflects the accounting impact of consolidating and aligning IT infrastructure as part of the wider Topdanmark integration.

(PRESS RELEASE) HELSINKI, 25-Sep-2026 — / EuropaWire / — Sampo will recognise an impairment loss and related VAT charges totalling approximately €118 million before tax in the third quarter of 2026 following a review of intangible assets connected with its IT systems in Denmark.

The impairment follows progress in the integration of Topdanmark into If Group, which has now reached a stage focused on finalising the harmonisation of core IT systems in the Danish operations.

As part of this integration process, Sampo conducted an impairment test covering intangible assets associated with the relevant IT systems.

Based on the outcome of the assessment, the company will record the approximately €118 million impairment loss, including related VAT charges, in its third-quarter 2026 financial results.

The impairment is non-cash and will be recognised under other expenses.

Sampo said the charge will be excluded from its operating earnings per share, meaning it will not affect the operating EPS measure used by the group to assess underlying performance.

The company also expects the impact of the impairment on its solvency position to be minor.

The accounting adjustment reflects the ongoing consolidation and harmonisation of technology infrastructure as Topdanmark’s operations are integrated into If Group.

evidence.text:
Sampo books an impairment loss on intangible assets related to its IT systems in Denmark

Sampo plc, press release, 25 September 2026 at 10:00 am EEST

Sampo books an impairment loss on intangible assets related to its IT systems in Denmark

Sampo's Topdanmark integration has progressed to a phase where the focus has been on finalizing the core IT system harmonization in Denmark. Hence, Sampo has conducted an impairment test on its intangible assets related to IT systems in connection with the integration of Topdanmark operations into If Group.

As a result of the test, Sampo will recognise an impairment loss with related VAT charges, totaling to approximately EUR 118 million before tax for the third quarter of 2026. The non-cash loss will be recognised in other expenses, and it will be excluded from the operating EPS. The effect on solvency is expected to be minor.

evidence.title: Sampo stock tracks Solidium's 70 million share sale
evidence.text:
Sampo stock (ISIN FI4000552500) was trading at EUR 8.74 on Nasdaq Helsinki on September 24, 2026, down 0.79 percent from the previous close. The immediate market story is an ownership shift: Solidium sold 70 million Sampo A shares for EUR 630 million on September 23, 2026.

According to Solidium on September 24, 2026, the sale represented 2.6 percent of Sampo's shares and was priced at EUR 9.00 per share. Solidium also plans to transfer Sampo shares worth EUR 400 million to the Finnish State by the end of 2026.

The sale price stood EUR 0.26 above Sampo's intraday quote of EUR 8.74 on September 24, 2026. That gap gives the ownership event a clear reference point, while the stock remained 15.9 percent below its 52-week high of EUR 10.39.

Sampo's investor page identifies January to June 2026 as its latest half-year reporting period. In that period, insurance revenue including brokerage was EUR 2,437 million, the underwriting result was EUR 418 million, and the combined ratio was 82.9 percent, according to Sampo .

The combination of a sub-100 percent combined ratio and positive underwriting result keeps operating performance measurable while the shareholder structure changes. Sampo's operating earnings per share for the reported period were EUR 0.17 and EUR 0.14 across the two disclosed comparison columns, as shown on the same investor page.

Sampo's A share is listed on Nasdaq Helsinki under ticker SAMPO, according to Sampo . Its market capitalization was EUR 23,196,506,460 on September 24, 2026, while the 52-week range extended from EUR 8.64 to EUR 10.39.

For investors, the key comparison is between the EUR 9.00 placement price and the EUR 8.74 Nasdaq Helsinki quote. The ownership transfer is scheduled for year end, while the operating figures come from the January to June 2026 report.

evidence.title: Tryg stock trades 15.86 percent below its yearly high
evidence.text:
Tryg stock stood at DKK 141.60 on Nasdaq OMX Copenhagen on September 25, 2026, at 10:08 a.m. CEST, placing it 15.86 percent below its 52-week high of DKK 168.30. The insurer's latest quarterly figures show higher revenue but lower net income than in the first quarter.

Tryg generated DKK 11.248 billion in revenue in Q2 2026, compared with DKK 10.522 billion in Q1. The quarter-to-quarter increase was 6.90 percent, giving the company a larger top-line base heading into the second half of 2026.

Operating income reached DKK 1.076 billion in Q2 2026, down from DKK 1.277 billion in Q1. That 15.74 percent decline means the revenue increase did not translate into higher operating profit during the period.

On September 24, 2026, MarketScreener reported that Danske Bank lowered its recommendation on Tryg to Hold from Buy and assigned a DKK 160 price target. The target stands 12.99 percent above the DKK 141.60 market price.

The recommendation change gives investors a concrete reference point between the current quote and the DKK 168.30 yearly high. It also places the DKK 160 target 4.93 percent below that high, leaving the analyst view below the recent peak.

Tryg reported DKK 874 million in net income for Q2 2026, compared with DKK 958 million in Q1. The 8.77 percent decline makes profitability the key counterweight to the 6.90 percent revenue increase.

At DKK 141.60, Tryg had a market capitalization of DKK 84,379,139,055 on September 25, 2026. The price was DKK 0.30 above the previous close of DKK 141.30, a daily increase of 0.21 percent.

Tryg's Q2 revenue growth and the DKK 160 analyst target provide two different reference points for the stock. Revenue expanded from Q1, while net income and operating income moved lower, creating a mixed quarterly earnings profile.

evidence.title: Tryg posts 88% combined ratio as Danish court ruling clouds Q2
evidence.text:
A Danish Supreme Court ruling on workers' compensation has forced several Nordic insurers to book one-off provisions in Q2 2026. Tryg A/S, which reports in Danish kroner, took the largest single charge at DKK1.2 billion pre-tax. On an adjusted basis, its Q2 insurance service result was DKK2,390 million, up approximately 4% year on year.

The ruling, handed down on April 28, 2026, lowered the compensation threshold from a loss of earning capacity of 15% to 5%. Tryg said the decision overturns more than four decades of established administrative practice in Denmark. Tryg and the Danish Insurance Association have jointly called on the Danish State to indemnify the industry for the resulting costs.

The one-off charge reduced Tryg's reported Q2 insurance service result to DKK1,190 million from DKK2,307 million a year earlier. On a reported basis, the combined ratio stood at 88.8% against 77.2% in Q2 2025. Adjusted for the provision, the ratio was 77.4%.

Tryg is Scandinavia's largest listed P&C insurer by premium volume . Gjensidige, another Nordic insurer affected by the ruling, recorded a DKK290 million net impact. Alm. Brand booked a DKK0.7 billion charge and issued a profit warning for 2026.

Tryg's adjusted combined ratio of 77.4% for Q2 compares with a Lloyd's market combined ratio of 87.6% for full-year 2025. The underlying claims ratio improved by 50 basis points in Q2 2026, up from 40 basis points in Q1 2026. Norway was among the markets delivering above-average claims performance in the period.

Insurance revenue grew 3.3% in local currencies against 4.0% a year earlier, and the expense ratio fell to 13.3% from 13.5%. The Q2 investment result was DKK262 million, up from DKK110 million in Q2 2025. Profit after tax was DKK874 million on a reported basis, or DKK1,762 million adjusted.

The solvency ratio at the end of Q2 stood at 196%, up from 192% at Q1 2026. Tryg declared an ordinary Q2 dividend of DKK2.15 per share, against DKK2.05 a year earlier, an increase of approximately 5%. The company said the solvency level supports continued shareholder remuneration.

Over the first half of 2026, the insurance service result was DKK2,845 million (DKK3,846 million), or DKK4,045 million adjusted. Revenue grew 3.4% in local currencies against 3.9% a year earlier, with an H1 combined ratio of 86.4% (80.7%), or 80.7% adjusted. The H1 expense ratio was 13.3% against 13.4%.

The H1 investment result was DKK264 million against DKK430 million in H1 2025. Pre-tax profit for H1 was DKK2,353 million (DKK3,526 million), or DKK3,553 million adjusted. The H1 ordinary dividend was DKK4.30 per share, up from DKK4.10 in H1 2025.

Tryg's group chief executive, Johan Kirstein Brammer, said the insurer handled close to one million claims across Scandinavia in H1 2026. Approximately 5,000 of those claims related to Storm Dave. Brammer said sales and retention improved across all of the group's operating markets.

Customer satisfaction reached 83 in Q2 2026 against a 2024 baseline of 81, the third consecutive quarterly increase. Tryg added partnerships with SAS EuroBonus, Lederne, and Eksjöhus during the period as part of its 2027 strategy. The company confirmed its financial targets for 2027 remain unchanged.

Any State indemnification of the industry could partially offset Tryg's DKK1.2 billion charge in future periods. No such arrangement is currently confirmed.

evidence.title: Sampo to Record €118 Million Impairment Loss on Denmark IT Assets as Topdanmark Integration Advances
evidence.text:
Sampo to Record €118 Million Impairment Loss on Denmark IT Assets as Topdanmark Integration Advances

Sampo to Record €118 Million Impairment Loss on Denmark IT Assets as Topdanmark Integration Advances

(IN BRIEF) Sampo will recognise an approximately €118 million pre-tax impairment loss, including related VAT charges, in the third quarter of 2026 following an impairment review of intangible IT assets in Denmark. The assessment was carried out as the integration of Topdanmark into If Group moved into a phase focused on completing the harmonisation of core IT systems. The charge is non-cash and will be recorded in other expenses. Sampo said the impairment will be excluded from operating EPS and is expected to have only a minor effect on the group’s solvency position. The adjustment reflects the accounting impact of consolidating and aligning IT infrastructure as part of the wider Topdanmark integration.

(PRESS RELEASE) HELSINKI, 25-Sep-2026 — / EuropaWire / — Sampo will recognise an impairment loss and related VAT charges totalling approximately €118 million before tax in the third quarter of 2026 following a review of intangible assets connected with its IT systems in Denmark.

The impairment follows progress in the integration of Topdanmark into If Group, which has now reached a stage focused on finalising the harmonisation of core IT systems in the Danish operations.

As part of this integration process, Sampo conducted an impairment test covering intangible assets associated with the relevant IT systems.

Based on the outcome of the assessment, the company will record the approximately €118 million impairment loss, including related VAT charges, in its third-quarter 2026 financial results.

The impairment is non-cash and will be recognised under other expenses.

Sampo said the charge will be excluded from its operating earnings per share, meaning it will not affect the operating EPS measure used by the group to assess underlying performance.

The company also expects the impact of the impairment on its solvency position to be minor.

The accounting adjustment reflects the ongoing consolidation and harmonisation of technology infrastructure as Topdanmark’s operations are integrated into If Group.

evidence.title: Topdanmark stock joins If after the 2025 merger
evidence.text:
Topdanmark stock has joined If's Nordic insurance structure after the July 1, 2025 integration, with the combined organization employing 10,000 people and serving more than 4.5 million customers. The company still operates as a recognizable insurance brand in Denmark, while ownership and operating scale now define the investment story.

According to Topdanmark , the group now offers insurance under both the Topdanmark and If brands in Denmark. The integration combines local insurance expertise with a Nordic platform serving private and commercial customers.

The scale is visible in the customer base. The combined organization insures one in five homes and personal cars across the Nordic region, while its agricultural business covers every second farm in Denmark, according to Sampo on September 2, 2026.

Topdanmark's agricultural insurance roots date back to 1908, and that history gives the brand a specialized position inside If's broader commercial insurance operation. The comparison between one in two Danish farms and one in five Nordic homes and cars shows how concentrated the company's strongest market position is.

For investors, the strategic change is more important than a standalone quarterly price move. Topdanmark contributes data, customer relationships and sector expertise, while If contributes a wider Nordic distribution and service platform, according to Sampo on September 2, 2026.

The company register updated September 23, 2026, lists If P&C Insurance Holding Ltd. with 90 percent ownership and 90 percent voting rights in Topdanmark. That structure places the former listed insurer within a controlled group rather than a stand-alone Danish equity story, according to Datapublica .
