evidence.title: Telenet Becomes First Belgian Telecom to Offer YouTube Premium Integration
evidence.text:
Telenet Becomes First Belgian Telecom to Offer YouTube Premium Integration

Telenet, part of the Telenet Group, is expanding its entertainment offering with the addition of YouTube Premium.

Starting today, customers can easily activate and manage their subscription via their personal MyTelenet web environment and the MyTelenet app, with payment processed directly through their Telenet bill. Telenet is the first telecom provider in Belgium to offer its customers YouTube Premium in such an integrated way.

Starting today, Telenet customers can add YouTube Premium to their subscription for €13.99 per month (YouTube Premium Individual, one user). The subscription offers customers an ad-free viewing experience on YouTube, the ability to watch or listen to videos and playlists offline, and the ability to play content in the background while using other apps. YouTube Music is also included, providing access to an extensive, ad-free music catalog.

YouTube Premium is used through the existing YouTube app and doesn't require a separate application. Customers can activate, adjust, or cancel their subscription at any time via their personal MyTelenet web environment or the MyTelenet app. Thanks to its integration with the Telenet platform, customers can easily access the YouTube app through their familiar Telenet TV box. This provides a central overview of their entertainment services and payments, providing added convenience and clarity.

By integrating popular services into one central environment, Telenet wants to give its customers more overview and control over their entertainment, with a single point of contact and a single trusted payment method.

Case study: Telenet adopts network digital twins to break automation glass ceiling

Case study: Telenet adopts network digital twins to break automation glass ceiling

During FutureNet World , Stijn Eeckhaut, Product Owner for Network Automation at Telenet, acknowledged that operators have been facing a challenge in taking network automation to anticipated heights, but also asserted that his business is seeing success for efforts to “ break the glass ceiling of network automation ”, two years into its ongoing transformation programme.

Eeckhaut used a case study presentation with a network digital twin at its core to demonstrate how a carefully staged incremental approach to implementing autonomous networks can enable the necessary shift in mindset and technology adoption.

The overarching ambitions of the project are considerable. As described by Carla Penedo , Executive Director of Cognitive Automation at Telenet’s system integrator Celfocus, the partners are working to build “ a future‑proof network platform ” that is “ intelligent, scalable, adaptable, powered by an‑AI ready infrastructure and… can continuously evolve with cutting edge AI and automation capabilities ”.

When the Belgian operator set out on its latest strategy for introducing greater autonomy, it looked to the TM Forum framework as a guide. While no official target for the desired level of autonomy was set, the goals of the project — entailing cross-domain real time decision making capability — aligned with Level 4 automation.

According to the Network and Penedo, getting to Level 4 depends on three things:

For the Telenet to achieve the benefits of autonomous network transformation, it quickly became clear that “ we needed to get better with data in a network operations context ”, according to Eeckhaut.

Carla Penedo (Executive Director of Cognitive Automation at Celfocus) and Stijn Eeckhaut (Product Owner for Network Automation at Telenet) on stage at FutureNet World 2025, London.

The critical role to be played by AI was evident, but also still evolving, meaning that the crucial first step was “ making our network data landscape AI‑ready ”. This entailed building ‘democratised’ data foundations to enable cross‑domain use cases, and in the process open silos and change the focus from how data is produced towards how data is consumed.

This also demanded commitment to data quality, and embrace of data productisation to support its use — and re‑use — in applications that can deliver value.

With these data foundations in place, Telenet and Celfocus set about creating a cognitive network operations layer enabling delivery of real‑time decision‑making capability, drawing on the cross‑domain data available. Here they collaborated with Telenet parent company Liberty Global on a new network AI product focused on a series of value‑driven use cases.

The first use case developed to leverage the potential of the new foundations and capabilities centred on service impact assessment, using a network digital twin as specific topology data was reviewed.

Collectively, the Telenet and Celfocus teams created a vision for this use case that could address planned changes in the transport network, including assessing potential effect on customers and services.

A visual approach to understanding automation impact

According to Celfocus’s Penedo, it can be essential to fully understand the existing process to be transformed at the outset of developing an automation use case.

To achieve this, customer‑facing and technical teams were gathered together (including network architects, data engineers and data scientists), to get to grips with the existing approach to impact assessment before determining the new end goal.

Through meetings and workshops and the use of a facilitation maps framework, the teams created a clear, “ visual ” and “ intuitive ” map to be used as they implemented the change in processes from an intensive manual approach to a more automated process. This was intended to minimise impact on customers and operations caused by interventions on the transmission network.

Penedo also flagged the value of mapping the transmission network topology as a series of graphs, which she said “ align naturally ” with existing network representations and capture the complexity of cross‑domain relationships to provide “ a holistic perspective ” of the infrastructure. These graphs reportedly make it easier to identify root causes of malfunctions. They also foster the use of AI algorithms to detect, predict and address faults that can impact customer service, and handle queries efficiently.

Telenet’s Eeckhaut described this approach as creating “ a very, very powerful way of asking all kinds of topology-related questions to the system ”. The operator has been able to scale this capability to cover more than 600,000 nodes, and 1.4 million edge locations between those nodes, to generate automated insight on transport network performance, encompassing around 90% of impact assessment use cases.

This automation is said to slash the time needed to generate answers to queries by up to 95%, from up‑to‑two hours, to around six minutes.

The standardised data analysis process is also said to be helping drive improvement in data quality, with network teams responsible for ensuring standards creating what Eeckhaut described as a “ reinforcing circle ” of reliable data gathering.

The change to the Telenet teams themselves is also apparently considerable.

Instilling trust, and new skills, in key teams

Getting network teams on board with the automation programme was deemed critical for its success, and it was noted that Telenet’s alignment with this outlook went as far as including a success metric that measures engineers’ adoption of the new systems.

Celfocus’s Penedo, who comes from an engineering background herself, joked about the typical engineer’s love for turning to diagrams when looking for solutions to problems, and enthusiasm for the latest trendy technologies.

She also emphasised that the real engineering achievement is in creating solutions that people can actually use and benefit from — “ Technology, even at its most innovative, is not enough ”.

“True innovation only happens when people embrace these advancements. That’s why we are not only focused on building the capabilities, but also in providing the means to foster adoption.”

For Telenet’s Eeckhaut, the shift towards autonomous networks is helping the operator build teams focused on working to “ supervise and enhance the process, rather than executing it ”. Penedo described the engineers embracing the new approach as “ hybrid experts ”, blending network expertise with new data skills that will help leverage the potential of automation in the future.

The impact and benefits have been clear, indicated Eeckhaut, pointing out that he had recently talked to the teams involved and found that trust has already built to enable them to rely on the system for multiple standard assessments, as they continue to validate system proposals for more complex cases.

According to Telenet’s Eeckhaut, adoption of the network digital twin for service impact assessment within Telenet has validated the concept of leveraging a cloud‑based graph database to link information sources together, advancing cross‑domain decision‑making capabilities.

Next steps are expected to see the operator incrementally extend the network digital twin, adding additional layers on top of the transport network and moving into domains beyond transport, such as the core and RAN, enabling more sophisticated impact assessments.

Introducing AI agents into the mix is also on the horizon, leveraging the capabilities of the cognitive network operations platform. “ We can close the loop ”, said Eeckhaut, “ and that will help us in our journey towards autonomous networks ”.

Another step on the journey will see a digital twin applied to intent validation, simulating and testing steps taken to deliver on new business objectives.

The journey to autonomous networks is obviously not complete, but Telenet appears confident it is on a trajectory that can break through existing limitations. Meanwhile, Celefocus’s Penedo summarised the achievements of the use case as meaning much more than an update to a series of onerous networking tasks.

“We are not just building technology, we are shaping the future. We are reimagining the way we can operate our networks, because we are also focussed on empowering people, streamlining operations and fostering an environment where we can really effectively use innovation.”

Telenet and Celfocus also joined Liberty Global with technology partner and host AWS on video at MWC, to share the challenge, vision, technologies, and co-creation for the cognitive automation engagement — and the hope to extend success to other LG OpCos .

AWS Studio video from MWC 2025 showcasing how AI and graph technologies are transforming telecom infrastructure at Telenet. Speakers included AWS' Praveen Sinha (Senior Solutions Architect) and Imen Grida Ben Yahia, Ph.D. (Principal AI/ML Solution Architect), Celfocus's Bruno Santos (Executive Director), Telenet's Koert Vlaeminck (Director of Network Service Operations) and Liberty Global's Alex Reichl (VP Mobile & Network API).

Featured submission from Luis Salvado Executive Chairman Celfocus

Bango announces that it is providing the technology behind Telenet’s next-generation entertainment marketplace. evidence.title: Netcracker Technology: Netcracker and Swisscom Receive 2026 FutureNet Award for Scaling Autonomous Network Operations

Netcracker Technology: Netcracker and Swisscom Receive 2026 FutureNet Award for Scaling Autonomous Network Operations

Award Highlights Successful Joint Blueprint to Scale Autonomous Operations Companywide for Leading Swiss Operator

Netcracker Technology announced today that it has received the prestigious 2026 FutureNet Award in the category of Autonomous Network Operations with its customer Swisscom for a groundbreaking operations transformation to deliver new services faster, scale innovation and improve service quality while reducing operational costs. The award was presented during the recent FutureNet World event in London.

Through a longstanding and close partnership, Netcracker and Swisscom embarked on a strategic initiative to accelerate operations autonomy across multiple self-sufficient network domains. Building on the success of Netcracker's Domain Automation Solution in the IP Transport domain, incorporating intent-based orchestration, unified inventory, closed loop assurance and AI, the collaboration focused on scaling these capabilities across the broader network landscape.

By jointly creating a replicable domain automation blueprint, Netcracker and Swisscom enabled domain teams to leverage standardized systems, tools, assets and best practices, establishing a consistent foundation for high levels of autonomy and scaling agentic AI. Delivered through a pioneering IT-as-a-Service model, the SaaS platform has accelerated adoption across domains including B2B, Fiber Access, LAN and cross-domain environments, reducing deployment times by over 60% and development costs by 40%. This SaaS-based approach has delivered strong business outcomes for Swisscom, including faster service deployment and change cycles, significantly fewer failures and substantial cost savings.

"By adopting an IT-as-a-Service model with Netcracker, we have been able to rapidly scale domain automation, reduce costs and accelerate time-to-market while laying the foundation for AI-driven autonomy at scale," said Rudolf Strijkers, Lead Architect Network Infrastructure IT at Swisscom. "By modernizing and automating new domains, and scaling them across our business, we are in an excellent position to adopt and leverage new technologies and bring additional benefits to our organization."

"The judges were very impressed by Netcracker's real-world transformation with its customer Swisscom that resulted in a clear pathway for company-wide autonomous networking," said Giles Cummings, Founder and CEO at FutureNet World. "We congratulate both companies for a truly compelling operations transformation that has led to tangible business benefits."

"Working with Swisscom for many years has put us into a position of trust and partnership that started with joint strategy sessions and led to accelerated rollout of autonomous operations across the business," said Ari Banerjee, Chief Strategy Office at Netcracker. "We are extremely proud to be recognized for this innovative and bold transformation approach, which has set a new benchmark for autonomous operational excellence in telecom."

evidence.title: Ericsson, Swisscom Unveil AI-Driven Energy & Enclosure Platform for Smarter RAN Infrastructure
evidence.text:
Ericsson, Swisscom Unveil AI-Driven Energy & Enclosure Platform for Smarter RAN Infrastructure

Ericsson and its longstanding partner Swisscom have introduced the next-generation Energy & Enclosure platform – part of the Ericsson Radio System portfolio – in Swisscom’s network.

This marks a major step forward in intelligent, automated, and energy-efficient radio access network (RAN) infrastructure. The milestone is the result of a close two-year collaboration, with Swisscom contributing operational expertise, strict performance requirements, and extensive field validation.

The successful development builds on nearly a decade of partnership focused on innovation and operational excellence. It reflects a shared ambition to unlock smarter, more sustainable network capabilities in Switzerland while setting new global benchmarks for telecom site operations. The platform is a key enabler for Swisscom as it evolves its network towards new operational models, supporting dynamic adoption of new technologies and proactive risk mitigation.

The new, future-proof Energy & Enclosure platform is a fully integrated site-energy solution that combines high-efficiency power systems, intelligent energy storage, advanced enclosures, and the Controller 6610 to deliver more resilient, secure, and sustainable networks. It gives communications service providers like Swisscom granular, software-driven control of site energy through features such as load management, load shifting, peak shaving, and hybrid solar operation—cutting energy and operational costs, while reducing carbon emissions.

A key AI feature is intelligent battery management during grid outages. The system assesses battery status, predicts consumption, and optimizes power use to prioritize critical network functions—safeguarding service continuity until power is restored. Through actionable insights, smart energy management, and predictive analytics, the platform helps operators boost energy efficiency and achieve significant cost savings. These capabilities also enable predictive maintenance and remote energy management, reducing the need for manual intervention and enhancing network resilience.

The platform offers new Ericsson products for both indoor and outdoor site types, focusing on performance, scalability, security, and energy efficiency.

Our long-standing collaboration with Ericsson is grounded in a shared focus on innovation, sustainability, and operational excellence. Through close cooperation over the past two years, we have jointly developed an intelligent energy and enclosure platform that supports Swisscom’s ambition to operate highly efficient, resilient, and environmentally responsible mobile networks. This solution enables us to further reduce energy consumption and carbon footprint while ensuring reliable connectivity for our customers.

Mårten Lerner, Head of Networks Strategy and Product Management at Ericsson

By combining Ericsson’s technology leadership with Swisscom’s operational experience, we have developed our new Energy & Enclosure Platform, including a fully digital power system designed for smart energy management. The platform provides security paired with RAN and site data collection in real time for efficient remote operation and control. With load steering and lithium energy storage, we prolong uptime during power outage. This close collaboration has resulted in a solution that enables more efficient and resilient telecom sites, empowering customers with smarter, greener, and more robust networks in Switzerland and beyond.

evidence.title: GRITEC AG und Swisscom stärken gemeinsam die OT‑Cybersecurity im Industriesektor
evidence.text:
GRITEC AG und Swisscom stärken gemeinsam die OT‑Cybersecurity im Industriesektor

Grüsch, 30. März 2026 – Swisscom und die GRITEC AG bündeln ihre Stärken, um die Cyberresilienz von Produktions‑ und Industrieunternehmen in der Schweiz weiter zu erhöhen. Die Kooperation reagiert auf die zunehmende Regulierung und die wachsenden Cyberbedrohungen, denen Schweizer Industriebetriebe heute ausgesetzt sind.

Im Mittelpunkt steht ein durchgängiger Ansatz: Von der Analyse über die technische Umsetzung bis zum Betrieb erhalten Unternehmen eine integrierte Lösung, die die mehrjährige OT‑Security‑Erfahrung der GRITEC mit den Security Services und SOC‑Kompetenzen von Swisscom verbindet. Das gemeinsame Angebot deckt den gesamten Lebenszyklus industrieller Sicherheitsanforderungen ab und unterstützt Firmen bei der effizienten Umsetzung moderner Standards wie IEC 62443, Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) oder NIS-2, inklusive nahtloser Integration in bestehende IT‑Infrastrukturen.

GRITEC steuert tiefes Know‑how in OT‑Security, industriellen Prozessen und Automation bei. Swisscom ergänzt dies durch umfassende Managed‑Security‑Erfahrung, eine hochverfügbare SOC‑Infrastruktur in der Schweiz sowie professionelle Incident‑Response‑Unterstützung.

Für Schweizer Industrieunternehmen entsteht daraus ein entscheidender Vorteil: Sie erhalten eine vollständig integrierte OT‑Security‑Lösung aus einer Hand – von der Absicherung ihrer Anlagen bis zum professionellen 24/7‑SOC‑Betrieb.

Matthias Schwaninger, Head of System Solution der GRITEC AG, betont die Bedeutung der Zusammenarbeit: «Mit Swisscom haben wir eine starke Partnerin, die unser bestehendes OT‑Security‑Angebot optimal ergänzt und es uns ermöglicht, unseren Kunden eine ganzheitliche Lösung anzubieten.»

«Die Zusammenarbeit mit GRITEC sichert unseren Kunden Stabilität in der Produktion, Risikotransparenz über die gesamte Wertschöpfungskette und eine IT-/OT-Integration mit Fokus auf Sicherheit» , sagt Philipp Schmid, Sales Director & Head Manufacturing Industries bei Swisscom.

Auch Ernst Schranz, CEO der GRITEC AG, unterstreicht die Relevanz für die Schweizer Industrie: «OT‑Security ist ein zentraler Bestandteil für die langfristige Betriebsfähigkeit industrieller Produktionen in der Schweiz. Mit zunehmender Konnektivität setzen wir gemeinsam mit Swisscom gezielte OT‑Sicherheitsmassnahmen um, um einen stabilen und wettbewerbsfähigen Industriebetrieb zu ermöglichen.»

evidence.title: Swisscom integriert Cyberschutz direkt im Router
evidence.text:
Swisscom integriert Cyberschutz direkt im Router

Swisscom erweitert sein Security-Angebot für Privatkunden. "My Security" agiert direkt im Router und soll das gesamte Heimnetz vor Malware, Hackerangriffen und gefährlichen Websites schützen. Ausserdem will der Telko seine Kunden zum Thema Cybersicherheit sensibilisieren.

Das erweiterte Sicherheitsportfolio von Swisscom namens "My Security" blockiert Malware und Cyberangriffe automatisch und bevor ein Schaden entsteht. Der Schutz wirkt direkt vom Router aus und überprüft alle Verbindungen in Echtzeit, wie der Telko mitteilt. Dafür würde es auch keine Installation eines Virenschutzprogramms brauchen. Ausserdem sollen Geräte wie Babyphones oder Überwachungskameras, die kein eigenes Abwehrsystem haben, durch den Schutzschild abgesichert sein.

Mit "My Security" erweitert der Telko sein Security-Angebot für Privatkunden, bestehend aus dem kostenlosen Identity Monitor, dem Callfilter und dem Internet Guard, wie es in der Mitteilung weiter heisst. Swisscom biete das Portfolio in vier Stufen mit verschiedenen Funktionsumfängen an: von XS bis L. Bei der XS-Stufe wird der Heimnetz-Schutz laut dem Unternehmen direkt und ohne Zusatzkosten inkludiert. Diejenigen Kunden, die mehr Unterstützung und Schutz wünschen, würden mit den anderen Abos von Premium-Services wie Expertensupport oder einer Cyberversicherung profitieren.

Zusätzlich sollen laut Mitteilung dank der "My Security App" auch mobile Geräte durch sichere Verbindungen, Passwort-Tools, Kinderschutzfunktionen und Hinweise auf Betrugsversuche geschützt sein.

Dirk Wierzbitzki, Leiter Privatkunden und Mitglied des Executive Committee Swisscom Schweiz. (Source: zVg)

"Mit dem neuen Heimnetz-Schutz machen wir digitale Sicherheit so einfach wie möglich. Damit schützen wir das ganze Zuhause automatisch, ohne Aufwand und für alle verbundenen Geräte", sagt Dirk Wierzbitzki, Leiter Privatkunden und Mitglied des Executive Committee Swisscom Schweiz. "Gerade in einer Zeit, in der immer mehr Geräte online sind, brauchen Kundinnen und Kunden eine Lösung, die ihnen den Alltag spürbar erleichtert."

Des Weiteren wolle Swisscom seine Kunden für Cybergefahren sensibilisieren. Dazu lanciert der Telko eine Awareness-Kampagne zum Thema Cybersicherheit. Die Kampagne wird laut Mitteilung in den kommenden Wochen über verschiedene Kanäle ausgespielt. Ausserdem sollen in mehr als 120 Swisscom-Shops Beratungswochen zu diesem Thema stattfinden.

Das könnte Sie auch interessieren: Swisscom und der Stadtwerke-Verbund Swisspower haben im Januar 2026 ihre Kräfte gebündelt, um die Cyberresilienz des Schweizer Energiesektors zu stärken. Lesen Sie hier mehr dazu.

Wenn Sie mehr zu Cybercrime und Cybersecurity lesen möchten, melden Sie sich hier für den Newsletter von Swisscybersecurity.net an. Auf dem Portal gibt es täglich News über aktuelle Bedrohungen und neue Abwehrstrategien.

evidence.title: Lidl’s £18.99 sunrise alarm clock could make dark autumn mornings easier
evidence.text:
Lidl’s £18.99 sunrise alarm clock could make dark autumn mornings easier

This article contains affiliate links, which means we may earn a small amount of money if a reader clicks through and makes a purchase.

It's safe to say autumn has arrived. The days are colder, the nights are drawing in and we're starting to seriously think about hibernating until spring.

We're finding it more and more difficult to get out of bed in the morning – and that's only going to get harder as winter approaches. So this handy gadget couldn't have come at a better time.

Livarno Sunrise Alarm Clock, £18.99 at Lidl

For those of us who hate the dark mornings, crave sunlight and prefer to wake to the sounds of nature, then this is a no-brainer.

Rather than the jarring sound of the phone alarm (or the children) jolting us awake at silly o' clock, this clock gently brings us back to life by simulating natural daylight. It kicks in slowly, starting 30 minutes before the alarm time set, so the whole process of leaving sleep is not such a shock. And we get to choose our preferred alarm sound, from a menu including rain, ocean waves and birdsong.

One of the joys of this past summer has been waking to the song of a particularly tuneful blackbird every day, so we know which option we'll be choosing.

It also comes with a three-year warranty and there's a back-up battery in case of power cuts. That's a lot of features for under £20.

What's more, in creating the feel of a natural sunrise, the clock helps regulate our body's natural rhythms. This suppresses some hormones while boosting others, so we feel more alert and less groggy first thing. It could even help promote a regular sleep wake cycle.

evidence.title: Sunrise on the Reaping Rating Is Different From All Hunger Games Movies, Despite Being the Same
evidence.text:
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping carries the same PG-13 rating as every film before it, yet the reasoning behind that rating sets it apart. A combination of factors points to a darker, more graphic experience when the film releases in theaters on November 20, 2026.

New Hunger Games prequel rating is like past franchise films, but it's much darker

FilmRatings.com confirmed the PG-13 classification. The Motion Picture Association flagged the upcoming prequel for "bloody images," "strong violence," "disturbing material" and "some smoking and teen drinking."

These are warnings no other installment in the franchise has ever received. On paper, the rating matches its predecessors . The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes got its PG-13 in 2023 for strong violent content and disturbing material.

Mockingjay – Part 2 received one in 2015. Mockingjay – Part 1 followed in 2014, and Catching Fire in 2013. The original Hunger Games secured its PG-13 rating in 2012 for intense violent thematic material and disturbing images, all involving teens. The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping breaks new ground, as no prior franchise movie drew a caution for bloody images and none mentioned teen drinking. This prequel does both.

The Gamemakers promise the most violent Hunger Games in history, and the source material backs that claim. Suzanne Collins set her 2025 novel during the Second Quarter Quell, which doubled the number of tributes. Sixteen-year-old Haymitch Abernathy , played by Joseph Zada, fights to survive one of the deadliest arenas ever built.

Readers have debated since publication whether the adaptation would pursue an R-rating to honor the book's brutality. The novel includes a scene where a tribute holds the head of a child: a moment nearly impossible to film within PG-13 boundaries.

The teen drinking caution connects to Haymitch's well-documented alcoholism in the original Hunger Games movies. Sunrise on the Reaping shows audiences the events that created his dependency. The smoking warning fits the same tragic arc.

Billy Ray and Michael Lesslie wrote the screenplay with Francis Lawrence at the helm. The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping serves as both a sequel to The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes and a prequel to the original 2012 film, making it the sixth one in the series.

evidence.title: Sunrise Business Launches Swiss AI Assistant for Businesses with PHOENIQS
evidence.text:
Sunrise Business Launches Swiss AI Assistant for Businesses with PHOENIQS

Sunrise Business and PHOENIQS present Sunrise Business AI Assistant: a powerful Swiss enterprise AI designed to increase brainpower productivity, leverage corporate knowledge, and automate processes.

The solution integrates with existing business applications and combines AI-powered chat, document analytics, and intelligent agents into a single platform. All essential AI components are provided and operated in Switzerland. Data is not transferred abroad.

With KMU Secure Connect, Sunrise Business also combines Internet, cloud telephony, and integrated cybersecurity in a new Plug & Work solution, ideal as the basis for the Sunrise Business AI Assistant.

With these two innovations, Sunrise is giving new impetus to its B2B strategy and consolidating its evolution from a telecom operator to a leading ICT and AI partner for Swiss companies.

Various market analyses confirm this: up to three-quarters of SMEs already use AI. Yet, data protection concerns, compliance requirements, and the definition of concrete use cases continue to represent the main obstacles to the broader deployment and systematic integration of AI into business processes.

Swiss AI for productivity, efficiency, security, and data sovereignty

The Sunrise Business AI Assistant can be rapidly implemented into core business processes. It provides controlled access to corporate expertise and provides data and document analysis, intelligent search and support functions, task automation, and workflows. The multi-model architecture allows for the use of different models and reduces dependence on a single global provider.

Companies thus gain rapid and secure access to the productive use of artificial intelligence through an end-to-end Swiss AI solution. All core components, from infrastructure to development and data processing, to operation and hosting—the so-called "full stack"—are provided in Switzerland. Customer data, uploaded documents, and workspace content are not used to train AI models. Since all components are subject to Swiss law, the solution is particularly suitable for companies with high requirements for data protection, compliance, and data sovereignty.

Upon request, an AI Success Manager can assist companies in identifying use cases, introducing the solution, and consolidating it into their daily work. Sunrise Business AI Assistant is available now as a standalone offering or as an add-on option for the KMU Secure Connect solution.

Connectivity and cybersecurity integrated into a new solution

With KMU Secure Connect , Sunrise Business expands its SME portfolio with an integrated connectivity and security solution. The new offering combines high-performance internet connections, modern cloud telephony, and integrated cybersecurity. Protection includes DNS protection, Firewall-as-a-Service, and web filtering as standard, helping to mitigate the growing cyber risks in day-to-day business operations. This provides businesses with a secure and scalable foundation for their digital infrastructure, without having to independently coordinate multiple vendors and individual solutions. By bundling these services in a Plug & Work offering, Sunrise Business significantly reduces complexity and administrative burden for SMEs.

Technological and commercial partnerships for the benefit of companies

Over the past two years, Sunrise Business has specifically expanded its offerings beyond traditional connectivity, introducing numerous ICT solutions and offerings dedicated to SMEs . To this end, collaborations with technology and solution partners such as Accenture, Anapaya, AWS, Cisco, Google, and Microsoft, as well as sales and integration partners such as swisspro AG and Gesamtwerk AG, have been expanded or recently initiated. In the past twelve months alone, Sunrise has integrated over 100 new partners into its B2B ecosystem.

SMBs particularly benefit from these partnerships. Many of them lack dedicated IT departments or security or AI specialists. At the same time, the demands for data security, cyber resilience, and digital productivity are constantly growing. Telecom and ICT solutions that reduce complexity for SMBs while providing cutting-edge technologies represent—along with the expanded partner ecosystem—a key driver for Sunrise Business's success as a growth engine.

Overall, more than 140,000 companies rely on Sunrise Business's high-performance telecom and ICT solutions.

Together with our partner PHOENIQS, ​​we offer AI as powerful as that of global providers, but entirely under Swiss control. No data is transferred abroad. Sunrise Business AI Assistant is therefore suitable for any company, including those subject to the highest requirements for data security, data protection, and regulatory compliance. This marks a decisive step in our evolution from a telecom operator to a preferred ICT and AI partner for businesses.

Thomas Taroni, Co-Founder and Executive Chairman of PHOENIQS

Fully autonomous AI is essential, but it's only part of the answer. Equally crucial is that it's intelligently designed to generate maximum value in terms of productivity, efficiency, and automation. With Sunrise Business AI Assistant, we've focused precisely on this goal. Thanks to preconfigured agents, integration with business applications, workflow automation, and intelligent support functions, this AI addresses both the simplest and most complex business needs.

evidence.title: D-Robotics Raises $400 Million Series C As Sunrise Chip Shipments Top 8 Million
evidence.text:
D-Robotics has raised $400 million in Series C funding to expand its hardware and software infrastructure for artificial intelligence-powered robots. The round included strategic investment from an unnamed global internet company, other investment institutions, and follow-on capital from existing shareholders.

D-Robotics plans to use the capital to broaden its Sunrise chip portfolio across multiple computing performance levels while developing software that spans more of the robot development lifecycle.

The company’s goal is to provide an integrated hardware and software stack capable of supporting applications ranging from established commercial robots to general-purpose humanoids.

The financing comes as D-Robotics reports rapid commercial growth.

Revenue increased several times year over year during the first half of 2026, while cumulative shipments of its Sunrise chips surpassed 8 million units. The company also said its embodied AI business has entered mass production and that its integrated AI infrastructure has completed large-scale validation.

The Sunrise S600, an embodied AI computing chip introduced in November 2025, was adopted by more than 20 major embodied AI customers within its first six months.

Customers include TARS, Spirit AI, X Square Robot, UBTECH, PaXini Tech, Astribot, FOURIER and Booster Robotics. Their applications span humanoids, wheeled industrial robots, consumer-electronics manufacturing, embodied foundation models and multimodal perception.

D-Robotics is also expanding its Gravity Program, which supports robotics companies across product development, supply-chain selection, go-to-market planning and fundraising.

The program has backed more than 500 robotics developers across 10 emerging product categories, including open-source humanoid robots, AI sports coaching, embodied AI models, AI imaging and home companion robots.

More broadly, D-Robotics said more than 500 universities and over 100,000 developers across more than 20 countries have built hundreds of types of intelligent robots using its technology.

Its platform spans high-performance computing, operating systems, Sunrise chips and RDK robotics development kits supporting humanoids, quadrupeds, home-service robots, companion devices and logistics autonomous mobile robots.

evidence.title: [Kato Mechatro #214] The Spread of AI-Powered Cobot Cells—Sunrise Robotics Accelerates Automation with GoFa
evidence.text:
[Kato Mechatro #214] The Spread of AI-Powered Cobot Cells—Sunrise Robotics Accelerates Automation with GoFa

Dust on the factory floor blocks the light. Before the morning shift begins, silence reigns. On the Sunrise Robotics production line, a GoFa™ waits quietly. Its appearance is different from conventional industrial robots. It is not large. Yet, there is something like a clear will residing within it. An AI-powered cobot cell. This is the protagonist of this story. Through the deployment of these AI-leveraged cells, the company is accelerating the automation of production processes. It is not merely a replacement of machinery. It is an intrusion into the human workspace.

The atmosphere on the floor remains unchanged. However, the focus of attention has shifted. Where humans once moved their hands, the arm of the GoFa™ now reaches out. This is not an encroachment. It is the beginning of coexistence. The AI judges, and the machine executes. This dichotomy is shaking the common sense of traditional FA (Factory Automation). Sunrise Robotics calls this change "acceleration." The words are gentle. However, the technical intent behind them is cold and calculated. Automation of the production process. A step toward this goal has appeared in the concrete form of the GoFa™.

Imagine the internal structure of the GoFa™. The actuators are designed with a focus on quietness. This is different from the rigidity of industrial robots. As a cobot (collaborative robot), safety is the top priority. However, it does not end with the mere addition of safety devices. AI intervenes. A group of sensors monitors the surroundings. Human movements, product positions, and environmental changes. These are processed in real-time.

In traditional FA, machines move according to programmed trajectories. Exception handling is limited. However, with AI-powered cells, prediction and adaptation become possible. The GoFa™ moves within a fixed cell. It is not an isolated space surrounded by walls. Even if a human stands next to it, it does not collide. How? It is the fusion of force sensors and visual recognition. It senses contact and immediately stops or corrects its trajectory. This reaction speed enables the acceleration of automation.

The Sunrise Robotics technology stack refers to the tight integration of hardware and software. The GoFa™ unit itself is composed of lightweight aluminum alloy and composite materials. The torque density of the joints is high. However, the control algorithm is the essence. The AI learns "what to do next." The AI compensates for variables in the production process, such as minor shape differences in products or changes in human movement speed. As a result, downtime is reduced. Operating rates increase. This is the substance of "acceleration." It is not magic. It is a series of probabilistic optimizations.

The industrial robot market was once dominated by industrial robots with huge arms. FANUC, ABB, KUKA, and Yaskawa. The so-called Big 4. Armed with high rigidity, high precision, and high speed, they have solidified their positions in mass production lines for automobiles and electronic components. However, recent trends are shifting toward high-mix, low-volume production and shorter delivery times. The era of mass production is passing.

Amidst this, the category of collaborative robots (cobots) has emerged. The UR series from Universal Robots led the way. Low cost, simple programming, and human collaboration. These three pillars have encouraged adoption among small and medium-sized manufacturers and research institutions. Sunrise Robotics is riding this wave. However, there is one point of differentiation. AI integration.

Conventional cobots are easy to program but not intelligent. Humans teach the steps, and the machine repeats them. However, with AI-powered cells, there is a possibility that the machine can optimize itself. This is a domain that neither the Big 4 industrial robots nor existing cobot vendors possess. Sunrise Robotics is striking this gap. It is cheaper than high-end industrial robots but smarter than existing cobots. It is a strategy to occupy this middle ground.

The market landscape is still fluid. The Big 4 are moving to defend their territory by adding AI functions to their own industrial robots. Existing cobot vendors continue to compete on price. How will the Sunrise Robotics GoFa™ survive this pincer attack? The quality of the AI and the ease of implementation are the deciding factors. The industry's attention is not on a single product, but on the ecosystem. Who provides the AI model, and who handles the integration? The reorganization of the industry landscape has just begun.

For workers on the factory floor, is the arrival of the GoFa™ a source of fear, or liberation? The answer is complex. Simple repetitive tasks are taken over by machines. This is an unavoidable reality. However, at the same time, it allows humans to focus on tasks that only humans can perform.

In traditional FA, humans were "assistants" to robots. Setup, deburring, and anomaly response. These tasks were designed to ensure the robots did not stop running. However, in AI-powered cells, the boundary between human and machine becomes blurred. The machine judges, and the human approves. Or, the machine proposes, and the human corrects. This interaction increases the flexibility of the production process.

The layout of the floor also changes. Isolated robot cells may no longer require safety fences. This is efficiency in floor space. Within limited factory space, production lines can be expanded. This has great significance for small and medium-sized manufacturing bases. They can enjoy the benefits of automation without large-scale investment.

However, there are challenges. The black-box nature of AI. Why did the machine move that way? Humans need to be able to understand and explain it. A black-box AI undermines trust on the floor. Ensuring transparency is the key to widespread adoption. Also, a change in skill sets is necessary. From the technology of operating machines to the technology of monitoring and adjusting AI. The role of the worker shifts from operator to supervisor. The speed of this transition will determine the level of confusion on the floor.

What Sunrise Robotics calls "acceleration" is not merely an increase in speed. It is a redefinition of the relationship between humans and machines. The atmosphere on the factory floor remains tense. Yet, the change is unstoppable. Every time a GoFa™ arm begins to move, human hands shift to another task. This dance creates a new form of production.

The moves by Sunrise Robotics signal a turning point for the industry. The spread of AI-powered cobot cells is not just another product cycle; it is a tectonic shift in industrial structure. Traditional factory automation was aimed at standardization and efficiency. However, with the introduction of AI, adaptability and linguistic capability are becoming the priorities.

Going forward, products like GoFa™ may become even more specialized. AI models tailored to specific processes—such as transport, assembly, and inspection—will be developed. From general-purpose cobots to specialized cells, this evolution is happening rapidly. The entry of the "Big 4" is also expected. They will likely integrate AI into their existing industrial robot platforms to achieve collaboration in high-load processes.

Meanwhile, emerging vendors will aim to provide low-cost solutions by partnering with cloud-based AI services. Hardware differentiation will fade, and competition in software and services will intensify. For Sunrise Robotics, what matters is hardware reliability and the continuous learning capability of their AI models. Once a cell is installed, it should become smarter the more it is used. This feedback loop creates customer loyalty.

Ultimately, factories will not transition completely from "human factories" to "unmanned factories." A hybrid environment where humans and AI coexist will become the norm. Sunrise Robotics' GoFa™ is a symbol of this transitional period. The acceleration of automation through AI—behind these words lies the redefinition of human work.

Technology is not cold-hearted, but it is not neutral either. It forces choices. At this very moment, factory layouts are changing. The position of the GoFa™ determines the position of the human. This geometric relationship defines the productivity of the future. Sunrise Robotics is designing that geometry. We can only wait for the results while exploring the next steps. The change has already begun. It cannot be stopped.

evidence.title: Sunrise Robotics Accelerates Automation with AI-powered GoFa™ cobot cells
evidence.text:
Sunrise Robotics needs its autonomous cells to perform precise manipulation for high-mix manufacturing, including pick & place, positioning, and machine-tending operations in human-centric environments.

Sunrise Robotics needs its autonomous cells to perform precise manipulation for high-mix manufacturing, including pick & place, positioning, and machine-tending operations in human-centric environments. The cells require high dexterity and sensing capabilities, remaining responsive, accurate, and reliable across simultaneous processes.

The company selected ABB Robotics’ GoFa cobot as the perfect fit for their intelligent robotic cells. GoFa’s combination of speed up to 2 m/s and high positional accuracy were the main decision drivers. As a result, Sunrise increased throughput by 20% - from 72 to 90 parts per hour - by adjusting GoFa’s motion parameters through software alone, with no changes to hardware or AI models.

Sunrise’s intelligent robotic cells combine on-board AI, built-in perception, and radar-based safety to operate in environments designed for people, not machines. ABB Robotics’ GoFa serves as the precision-driven physical layer where Sunrise’s AI intelligence is expressed: picking, placing, and manipulating components at exceptional speeds with high positional accuracy.

Sunrise Robotics is a European technology company headquartered in Ljubljana, Slovenia, delivering fully intelligent, autonomous robotic cells, making automation faster, more affordable, and accessible to small and medium-sized manufacturers. By unifying hardware and software into a single, holistic system, the company designs solutions tailored to the realities of modern manufacturing where flexibility, adaptability, and autonomy are essential.

To achieve its vision, Sunrise conducted a thorough evaluation of the collaborative robot market. The requirements were specific: a large working envelope for euro pallet operations at floor level, speed and positional accuracy for increased reliability, and a developer-friendly software architecture capable of running Sunrise’s AI models in real time. ABB Robotics’ GoFa met all three criteria, and the confidence that comes with deploying ABB Robotics’ technology gave Sunrise's customers additional assurance in the overall system.

Long-term reliability and support were decisive factors in Sunrise’s decision to collaborate with ABB Robotics. Its proven track record, rapid response times, and global spare-parts availability gave Sunrise and its customers the confidence that systems would remain fully supported and continuously operational for years to come.

“When you're deploying an intelligent, autonomous cell into a customer's production environment, every component must earn its place. ABB Robotics’ GoFa arms give us the performance we need and the brand trust that makes our customers even more confident in what we've built.” Robert Bevec, Product, Sunrise Robotics.

Within Sunrise’s architecture, GoFa cobot acts as the perfect embodiment of the company’s AI-driven software stack and real-world production. GoFa provides the precision, speed and flexibility that enable the company to turn AI-driven intelligence into reliable physical action. With RobotStudio ® supporting fast deployment and continuous optimization.

Sunrise has also realized significant value from being able to control ABB Robotics’ arms remotely allowing its engineers to restore autonomous cells from unexpected states without travelling to the customer site; a crucial advantage when customers have limited experience with industrial robotics. Thanks to RobotStudio ® , Sunrise can support deployments remotely, protecting customer trust, reducing operational costs, and keeping systems running without unnecessary downtime.

“GoFa's open control architecture gave us the foundation to connect our AI directly to the physical world. By leveraging its flexible motion control capabilities, we increased throughput from 72 to 90 parts per hour through a single parameter change, with no modifications to our software, hardware or AI stack. That kind of flexibility is exactly what you need when you’re optimizing live deployments for real customers.” Jose Manuel Bonilla Jimenez, Customer Success, Sunrise Robotics

On the software side, the combination of Robot Web Services (RWS) and Externally Guided Motion (EGM) provided Sunrise with a robust and layered control architecture. RWS manages low-frequency tasks such as program handling and variable subscriptions, while EGM supports high-frequency, real-time motion commands driven by Sunrise’s AI models. Together, they create a system capable of dynamically responding to what it senses in the environment.

At ABB Robotics, we are proud to support Sunrise Robotics with the flexibility and performance required to optimize live deployments for real production environments.

“By combining GoFa with AI in a proven collaborative robotics solution, organizations like Sunrise are enabled to innovate faster while maintaining the reliability their customers expect,” says Alessio Cocchi, Global Head of cobot sales.

By combining Sunrise Robotics’ AI-driven autonomy with ABB GoFa’s precision, speed, and open control architecture, Sunrise is building a scalable, adaptable robotic solution designed for the realities of high-mix European manufacturing. Early deployments are already delivering measurable results, and as Sunrise extends its fleet, the collaboration is establishing a clear path toward fully autonomous industrial cells that can be deployed at manufacturer's facilities in days, not months.

ABB Robotics as one of the world’s leading robotics companies, is the only company with a comprehensive and integrated AI-powered portfolio covering robots, cobots and Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs), designed and orchestrated by our value-creating software. We help companies of all sizes and sectors - from automotive to electronics and logistics – to outperform by becoming more resilient, flexible and efficient. ABB Robotics is at the forefront of developing and commercializing a new generation of Autonomous Versatile Robotics (AVR), leading a global innovation ecosystem of partners in advancing efficient hardware and intelligent software with industrial performance. The business employs approximately 7,000 people go.abb/robotics .

Sunrise Robotics is a new kind of robotics company, one that delivers fully intelligent, autonomous robotic cells that transform how manufacturers operate. Founded by a team with deep roots in industrial robotics, drone technology, consumer electronics at scale, and software platforms serving hundreds of millions of users, Sunrise brings together hardware and software into a single, holistic system designed for the realities of modern manufacturing.

At the heart of Sunrise's offering is a dual-arm robotic cell equipped with built-in perception, on-board AI, and radar-based safety; capable of operating both collaboratively and at full industrial speed depending on what the task demands. The cells are designed to work in environments built for people, not machines, making them well-suited to the high-mix, process-intensive manufacturing environments common across European industry. Deployment is measured in days and weeks rather than months and years, and the fleet model means skills can be added incrementally as customer needs grow.

Sunrise's mission is to augment human operators by taking on repetitive and physically demanding tasks, freeing people to focus on higher-value work, while giving manufacturers the flexibility and resilience to respond to labour shortages, process changes, and shifting supply chains.

evidence.title: A1 Telekom Austria grows faster in fixed network than with mobile communications
evidence.text:
The A1 Telekom Austria Group, which operates in seven European countries, was able to significantly increase the number of its mobile customers and slightly increase the number of fixed-network lines in 2024. However, the Group, which has been majority-owned by Mexico's América Móvil since 2014, generated more revenue growth in the fixed network than in the mobile segment.

This is evident from the A1 annual figures published on Tuesday. The company operates both mobile and fixed networks in Austria, Bulgaria, Croatia, North Macedonia, Slovenia, Belarus and Serbia. In the latter country, however, A1 fixed network services have only been available since the beginning of 2025. In autumn 2023, A1 spun off its radio tower business in Austria , which complicates the comparison of annual figures. Unless otherwise stated, the following figures are taken from the reporting required by financial law.

The annual revenue of the A1 Telekom Austria Group climbed by 3.1% to EUR 5.4 billion in 2024. Of this, EUR 3.2 billion (+2.3%) came from the mobile business and EUR 2.1 billion from the fixed network (+4%). EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization), a key financial indicator traditionally used in the telecommunications industry, rose by 5.1% to EUR 2 billion. The operating cash flow grew by 5.7% to 1.8 billion euros. However, the operating result fell by 5.4 percent to 861 million euros.

This divergence is due in particular to higher depreciation on usage rights, which in turn is due to the spin-off of the Austrian radio towers. With the transfer of parts of the passive infrastructure of the mobile communications stations to EuroTeleSites AG (ETS), leasing agreements were concluded between A1 and ETS, as A1 wants to continue to use the facilities for its mobile communications network. In A1's balance sheet, these leasing agreements lead to liabilities (leasing installments to be paid) on the one hand and to an asset (rights of use) on the other. These rights of use have to be depreciated over the term of the leasing contracts, so there is higher depreciation.

The bottom line is that the spin-off of the Austrian radio towers will lead to lower profits in absolute terms, but in the long term the debt burden should fall and higher profits per euro invested will flow. The shares of EuroTeleSites AG were distributed to the former A1 shareholders in the fall of 2023. The new shares plummeted immediately, but the ETS share price has now almost recovered to the issue level.

As the A1 Telekom Austria Group had to pay less tax in 2024, the net result did not fall quite as sharply as the operating result. A decline of three percent means an annual profit of EUR 627 million. Nevertheless, the management proposes to increase the dividend by one ninth to 40 cents per share. Nevertheless, A1 shares fell by more than one percent on Tuesday. Incidentally, if the radio tower effects were excluded from the A1 annual figures for 2023 , the net result for 2024 would be a plus of 12.5 percent instead of a minus of three percent.

At the end of 2024, the A1 Telekom Austria Group had 27.1 million mobile lines, an increase of 7.4%. The number of connections that are paid for in advance (prepaid) is shrinking, while most of the growth is not attributable to people but to machines (M2M): More and more machines are getting mobile connectivity.

The number of revenue generating units, untechnically referred to as fixed network connections, rose by 1.3% to 6.4 million. As already mentioned, however, fixed-line revenues increased more strongly (+4%) than mobile revenues (+2.3%).

In its home market of Austria, A1 used an inflation clause in its end customer contracts in April to raise prices for existing customers. Although this motivated some customers to switch providers, overall it supported sales. For the year as a whole, A1 Telekom Austria can report an increase in turnover of six per thousand to EUR 2.7 billion. At 49 percent, the Austrian contribution to Group sales is below half for the first time.

For accounting purposes, EUR 151 million in revenues (-3%) from the transit and interconnection business with third countries were added to the Austrian division. In total, this results in an increase in annual turnover of three per thousand to 2.8 billion euros. EBITDA fell by 2.3% to one billion euros, while the operating result even slumped by 21.5% to 387 million euros. This reflects the effects of the Funkturm spin-off discussed above.

The number of Austrian mobile lines has remained stable, climbing by one per thousand to 5.1 million. In 2023, there was still a small decline of six per thousand. Not least thanks to the price increase, mobile revenues grew by half a percent to EUR 1.3 billion in 2024.

A1 has to report accelerated customer loss for the Austrian fixed network. In 2023, a net 3.4 percent of connections went offline; in 2024, the figure was 4.2 percent. This decline is not limited to pure telephone connections, but also affects internet connections with lower bandwidths. These customers are often cheaper online with mobile routers. With higher bandwidths, A1 can conclude more fixed-line contracts, which means that the decline in fixed-line revenue has remained limited to eight per thousand (now EUR 1.4 billion). Accordingly, A1 management intends to continue investing in fiber optic connections in 2025, albeit to a lesser extent.

A1 Telekom Austria reports growth in both revenue and EBITDA in five of the other six markets. Only in Slovenia are both key figures developing negatively. There, competitors with flat-rate mobile tariffs are giving A1 a hard time.

Overall, the network operator generated revenue of EUR 2.6 billion in the six countries outside Austria, an increase of 5.6 percent. EBITDA even jumped by eleven percent to one billion euros. Of this, 513 million euros remained as operating profit, an increase of 7.3 percent.

evidence.title: Verizon Is Pulling the Plug on Old Home Phone Lines in 9 States
evidence.text:
The copper phone line has run into American homes since the 1800s, and it’s finally on its way out. Verizon wants to start cutting it off in nine states as soon as next month. The company has asked the FCC for permission to end traditional landline service in parts of Arizona, Delaware, New Jersey, New Mexico, Ohio, Rhode Island, South Carolina, Utah, and Virginia.

If you still pick up a phone that plugs into the wall, this could affect you. Verizon’s request covers about 277,000 home and business lines in those states. Unless the FCC steps in, the request gets approved automatically on Saturday, September 26. Service can then start ending on or after October 23.

Verizon says it spends billions of dollars a year keeping the old copper network running. Replacement parts are getting harder to find, and the copper itself is valuable enough that thieves steal it.

Plus, let’s face it, hardly anyone uses it anymore. Landline subscriptions across the country fell 81% between 2014 and 2024, according to The Woodbury Warbler reports from Verizon’s filing. In those nine states, fewer than 2.25% of people who could get the service still pay for it.

Verizon isn’t stopping at nine states, either. The carrier made a second filing that covers nine more states plus Washington, D.C., including New York, California, and Pennsylvania. That one affects about 750,000 more homes and businesses. Separately, AT&T expects to finish retiring its own copper network by 2029.

What your old landline does that a new one might not

That being said, while most of us rely on our smartphones and wireless devices to stay connected, there are some advantages to copper lines that our mobile phones do not have. A traditional copper line carries its own power, which is why it keeps working during a blackout. Verizon’s replacement home phone equipment runs on AA batteries rated for about 23 to 24 hours on standby.

That matters most in rural areas. The Virginia Association of Counties, which represents 94 counties, has asked the FCC to slow down . The group warns that some areas have no reliable cell or fiber service to switch to. It also points out that a wireless phone can’t call 911 once its battery dies.

Medical alert pendants and home alarm systems are another concern. Verizon’s own customer notice says its replacement supports “many” older alarm systems and medical devices, which isn’t the same as all of them.

Verizon is reassuring customers it won’t shut off your copper line unless a replacement service is available at your address. You should also get a letter with your actual cutoff date. If you rely on a medical alert device or home alarm, call the company behind it now and ask whether it works over fiber or wireless. It might be a good idea to keep spare AA batteries on hand as well.

evidence.title: Verizon’s Pixel 11 Pro Deal Drops $620 Off With No Trickery
evidence.text:
This might come as a bit of a shock, but Verizon currently has the best Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro XL deals we have seen to date. Verizon is taking hundreds of dollars off of each phone and there’s really just one requirement – you have to sign-up for their Simplicity Plan .

Verizon has the Pixel 11 Pro 256GB at $620 off , which brings its starting price down to $479.99. They are running the same $620 off discount on 512GB models too.

Verizon also has the Pixel 11 Pro XL at $580 off , so its starting price is $719.99.

These are incredible prices and the deal almost seems too good to be true. These are retail discounts, not monthly bill credit situations. Verizon is only asking that you sign-up for their Simplicity Plan to get this deal.

I’ve walked through this deal on Verizon’s site and it seems almost too straight-forward, but I can’t find any real downsides to it. Let’s try to break this down.

If you head to Verizon’s Pixel 11 Pro page ( here ), you’ll see the offer for $620 off the phone. To get the deal I described above, you would select “Phone only” and then in the “Choose how you want to pay” section, you would pick “Pay in full today.” You should see the price in that box as $479.99.

Now, you’ll walk through a couple of extra steps, including a Google AI Pro add-on (you can skip this) followed by the choice of Simplicity Plan and then a protection plan (you can skip this too if you want).

Verizon will then ask if you are bringing over your number from another carrier. If you are, they’ll give you a $15 discount that drops the Simplicity price to $30/mo. If you don’t bring over your number, you’ll pay $45/mo.

After you do that, you’ll be at the checkout page where you can see the Simplicity Plan and its $30 or $45 monthly price, assuming you sign-up for Auto Pay. And then at the very bottom you will see the “Due today” and the $479.99 price for the Pixel 11 Pro.

Again, there do not appear to be any strings here. Verizon is offering a huge discount on the Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro XL to get you to come to their network and sign-up for the Simplicity Plan. Since you are paying full retail for the device, there isn’t a month-to-month or device payment agreement and Simplicity operates on a monthly basis.

Honestly, I’m not sure there is a better Pixel 11 Pro deal anywhere to be found. I’m not even sure one will top this any time soon, assuming you are into signing up for the Simplicity Plan.

AT&T Slashes AI Costs by Adopting Model Routers and Open Source

AT&T cut the costs of coding and some other advanced artificial intelligence tasks by as much as 56% by using tools that route employees’ queries to cheaper models when appropriate, The Information reported Thursday (Aug. 20).

When doing so, the quality of the performance of the AI declined by only 2%, according to the report, which cited an interview with Mark Austin , an AT&T vice president who oversees AI used by the telecommunication company’s employees.

The tools AT&T used in this instance were LiteLLM model routers, which determine the complexity of the task and then decide if it can be sent to a cheaper AI model, the report said.

AT&T aims to keep its employees spending on models from Anthropic and OpenAI flat by making greater use of open-source or open-weight models. The company aims to increase the share of employees’ queries that are powered by open-source models from the current 40% to between 60% and 70% in the coming years, per the report.

AT&T is using open-source or open-weight models such as Nvidia ’s Nemotron, Meta ’s Llama and Google ’s Gemma. The company is not using open-source models from the Chinese firms DeepSeek and Moonshot but is evaluating the potential risks of using them, according to the report.

AT&T’s experience has been that the capabilities of open-source models have generally been six to 10 months behind those of frontier models, but the gap is narrowing and the open-source models are “just as good or better” than older models from Anthropic and OpenAI, Austin said, per the report.

It was reported in June that companies are looking to better manage their use of AI after seeing the costs of the technology rise.

The rising costs have been driven by the shift from chatbots to agents, which consume more computing power, as well as the AI labs’ move from flat subscriptions to token-based billing.

PYMNTS reported in July that new tools are being launched to address the issue of AI costs and that the era of “tokenmaxxing,” or pushing employees toward the biggest AI models and heaviest usage, is ending after two years of unchecked growth.

evidence.text:
AT&T Turns to Autonomous AI Agents to Slash Fraud

AT&T is deploying a new generation of autonomous AI agents across its consumer and enterprise operations to tackle escalating spam and fraud calls and cut service friction for customers and employees alike.

Complete the form to unlock this article and enjoy unlimited free access to all PYMNTS content — no additional logins required.

The telecom giant’s early efforts include a network-integrated “digital receptionist” that engages unknown callers in real time to identify spam and fraud, disconnect suspicious interactions or take messages. Behind the scenes, AT&T is also building out agent-driven tools with Microsoft, including “Ask AT&T” and an builder that automates back-office workflows and synchronizes data across systems to reduce wait times and manual handoffs.

Digital Receptionist: Fighting Fraud and Spam in Real Time

In mid-2025, AT&T began testing an AI-powered digital receptionist, AT&T ActiveArmor , built into its core network to help customers screen unwanted calls and cut through the noise of spam and fraud calls that have become increasingly sophisticated. Unlike traditional spam filters that merely flag calls, this agentic artificial intelligence engages directly with unknown callers using advanced voice-to-voice and natural language capabilities to determine legitimacy. If the caller meets predefined criteria, the call is connected; if not, the system can disconnect the line or take a message. During the interaction, the customer can watch a live transcript of the conversation and choose to intervene at any time.

This agentic approach builds on AT&T’s longstanding network-level efforts against robocalls and fraud. The company already blocks or labels billions of unwanted calls monthly, but elevates the capability by incorporating autonomous decision-making and conversational interaction rather than simple pattern matching.

Early trials suggest the tool can reduce the disruptive impact of unwanted calls, improve overall user experience and offer a new layer of fraud defense without requiring customers to install additional apps or hardware.

Agent-Driven Tools for Internal Efficiency

We’d love to be your preferred source for news .

Please add us to your preferred sources list so our news, data and interviews show up in your feed. Thanks!

While the digital receptionist addresses a direct customer pain point, AT&T’s agentic AI strategy also extends into internal workflows and employee tools. Working with Microsoft and leveraging Azure, the company introduced “Ask AT&T,” a generative AI platform tailored to employee use cases, from answering complex HR and policy questions to aiding in software development tasks.

In late 2025, AT&T further expanded this with Ask AT&T Workflows, a graphical drag-and-drop agent builder that lets business teams create custom autonomous agents to automate repetitive tasks that once required time-intensive manual work.

The first production agents built with this system handle customer service update requests by automatically synchronizing data across backend systems and pushing real-time updates without human handoffs.

According to a CIO report , this has already improved customer satisfaction and reduced service wait times, freeing employees to focus on higher-value activities. For network operations, agents can now assist engineers by correlating telemetry, identifying root causes for alerts, opening trouble tickets and even proposing code patches, all while a human engineer oversees and approves outcomes.

Governance, Oversight and the Path Forward

AT&T has institutionalized its agentic AI push through a Generative AI Transformation Office, which funnels potential use cases through a centralized review process that evaluates business value, customer impact and risk, per CIO. Each initiative must pass muster with the CFO and tie into formal business cases, emphasizing measurable ROI and customer benefit before deployment.

Human oversight and audit logging are baked into every stage of the agentic AI lifecycle. Actions taken by agents are logged with data isolation, retention policies and role-based access enforced to maintain security and compliance. Human checkpoints are required throughout complex workflows, ensuring that autonomous executions do not overstep oversight bounds.

evidence.title: AT&T Cybersecurity Spin-Off LevelBlue Launches New Program To Transform Partners Into MSSPs: Exclusive
evidence.text:
AT&T Cybersecurity Spin-Off LevelBlue Launches New Program To Transform Partners Into MSSPs: Exclusive

LevelBlue, one of the largest cybersecurity startups at its launch, according to the company, is introducing a new partner program to empower more solution providers to become MSSPs, the company’s president, Sundhar Annamalai, tells CRN exclusively.

Nearly a year after launching, cybersecurity spin-off LevelBlue is rolling out a new partner program for MSSPs, or those on the journey toward becoming an MSSP, the company told CRN exclusively.

AT&T Cybersecurity in May broke off LevelBlue as a standalone managed cybersecurity services business. Now, the provider is ready to launch its new portal, security services, and marketing and partner enablement materials for new and existing partners, Sundhar Annamalai, president of LevelBlue, told CRN.

LevelBlue today offers global managed security services, cybersecurity consulting, threat intelligence and security operations center (SOC) support. The company offers a suite of easy to integrate, scalable security services in a flexible consumption-based model for managed and unmanaged cybersecurity services, the company said.

The new program will arm MSPs with the resources they need to become MSSPs, said Annamalai (pictured above).

“We have a partner program where you can just take this on and you already have all of the resources on your side. MSPs are already doing IT services and managed network security, and so instead of trying to reinvent the wheel, our partner program is a way for them to accelerate their ability to deliver security for their embedded base of customers,” he said.

[Related: AT&T Cybersecurity Spin-Off: Managed Security ‘Startup’ LevelBlue Launched ]

The new LevelBlue partner program, launched on Monday, includes its full portfolio of services, including LevelBlue USM Anywhere, the company’s security monitoring offering for premises-based, cloud, or hybrid environments, LevelBlue Managed Threat Detection and Response, LevelBlue Managed Vulnerability Scanning, LevelBlue Penetration Testing Service and LevelBlue Incident Response Retainer.

“The announcement is a continuation of the separation and running a standalone cybersecurity business from AT&T [and] standing up a new partner program under the LevelBlue umbrella centered around our USM Anywhere platform,” Annamalai said.

Technology partnerships are also an important way that LevelBlue is approaching the market. As such, the company today offers email security powered by Check Point and managed endpoint security powered by SentinelOne, both of which are now available through partners.

“It’s not going to stop there,” he said. “We’re making technology investments in our underlying platforms and technology [and] we continue to expect to bring new services and capabilities into the partner program. The offerings we had were narrower before. Now, this launch [lets us] expand those offerings to MSPs as well as MSSPs … We want to offer our security tools, services, expertise to other MSSPs that are growing themselves.”

LevelBlue’s new program has three tiers, and existing partners will roll into one of the three tiers, Annamalai said. LevelBlue will also offer in-depth training and dedicated support for partners, according to the Plano, Texas-based company.

The aim of the program is to offer a simplified approach to cybersecurity with scalable services from both LevelBlue, as well as third-party security players, Annamalai said.

“There’s many existing security players in the space. Cisco is going from networking into security. They’re going to need players like us to help manage that those environments, particularly when they’re multi-vendor environments,” he said.

Being a “tech-enabled MSSP” itself, LevelBlue wants to package up its services for partners to offer their clients, Annamalai said.

“The space is so large that we can’t meet where our customers are all the time geographically, regionally, [or] vertically, and so we work with partners that use our technology and services to deliver cybersecurity … that’s the agenda,” he said.

Dallas-based AT&T in May 2024 revealed that it had entered into a joint venture with private equity firm WillJam Ventures to officially launch LevelBlue. LevelBlue at its launch was one of the largest startups in the cybersecurity industry to date with tens of thousands of customers and hundreds of partners coming over from AT&T, LevelBlue’s chairman and CEO, Bob McCullen, told CRN last year.

evidence.title: Better Artificial Intelligence Stock: AT&T vs. Verizon Communications
evidence.text:
Telecom giants AT&T ( T -0.54% ) and Verizon Communications ( VZ -0.79% ) aren't obvious leaders in the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution, yet their high-speed, low-latency connectivity services play a vital role in the data-intensive AI ecosystem.

Both companies are leveraging their 5G and fiber optic networks to meet the surging demand for edge computing that supports AI workloads. This dynamic, coupled with solid performance in their core wireless businesses, has been a boon for shareholders, with AT&T and Verizon stocks rising by 19% and 13% year to date, respectively.

Even with these large gains, both stocks continue to offer attractive high-yield dividends, making them compelling options for investors seeking income in 2025.

So, which stock is the better buy for your portfolio right now? Let's explore the key factors to consider.

AT&T has quietly emerged as one of this year's biggest stock market comeback stories, with shares up a remarkable 58% over the past year. The effort to refocus on its core telecom strengths -- by exiting its media ventures with the sale of its DirecTV subsidiary set to close this year -- appears to be paying off.

For the year ended Dec. 31, 2024, mobility segment revenue climbed 3.3%, reflecting a reacceleration in net subscriber additions. An ongoing expansion of its fiber network availability has been a growth driver, with consumer broadband revenue jumping 7.2% in 2024. The market is taking notice.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is playing a role in this success, not only as AT&T integrates automation as part of a broader cost-saving initiative, but also as a growth driver, capturing demand for what the company calls the "middle mile infrastructure" connecting the explosion of AI applications to end users. Better-than-expected earnings and free cash flow generation have helped improve its balance sheet through a decline in net debt.

For 2025, AT&T projects further growth and strengthening of financials. That's great news for investors considering the stock's 4.1% yielding dividend. While not yet confirmed, there's likely room for a dividend hike this year. Indeed, AT&T is projecting confidence in its outlook, announcing a new $10 billion share buyback program.

Investors who believe the company has turned the corner toward more sustainable profitable growth have ample reasons to buy and hold the stock.

While the recent rally in AT&T stock is impressive, Verizon shares stand out with several key advantages that could make them a better investment. Despite a similar market capitalization for both companies (currently around $195 billion), Verizon is larger by total revenue and more profitable, generating stronger free cash flow for 2024.

Ultimately, Verizon shares benefit from a longer track record of consistency, with the trend of steady growth expected to continue.

That contrast is particularly important considering Verizon shares are currently trading at a forward price-to-earnings ratio (P/E) of around 10, representing a deep discount compared to AT&T's 13. By this measure, investors may be getting better value with Verizon stock, a dynamic also reflected in its higher dividend yield of 5.8%.

There is also a case to be made that Verizon is the better AI stock with a more defined strategy. The company recently unveiled its Verizon AI Connect solution, enabling businesses to deploy and scale up AI workloads more effectively.

The company is citing partnerships with tech leaders like Alphabet , Meta Platforms , and Nvidia to address evolving AI demands. This development -- coupled with Verizon's pending acquisition of Frontier Communications, which will significantly expand its fiber footprint -- has bolstered its outlook.

There's a lot to like about both Verizon and AT&T, since they are set to capitalize on the long-term opportunities in the next generation of telecommunications.

That said, I believe that following AT&T's massive rally, its stock now looks expensive, making Verizon the better pick at this moment to outperform in 2025. For investors seeking a blend of value and high-yield income, along with exposure to AI growth themes, Verizon's stock could make an excellent addition to a diversified portfolio.
