Our customers are increasingly satisfied with us, and we are committed to continuing to meet their evolving expectations, while becoming an even simpler, faster and more efficient company.

Sweden delivered on plan, with particularly healthy momentum in the consumer business, where we grew both customer numbers and revenue across broadband, TV and mobile. The integration of Bredband2 is proceeding well and revenue synergies are already materializing. The enterprise market is competitive, but demand for Telia’s security and mission-critical services remains robust. Customer satisfaction improved further, reflecting our focus on network quality and customer experience.

In Finland , service revenue stabilized as expected, supported mainly by improvements in the enterprise segment, and we see increased momentum in business- and mission-critical services. Competitive pressures continued in the mobile consumer business, although improved consistently during the quarter. As a result of cost control and organizational changes, profitability grew despite the challenging environment. In March, we agreed to increase our ownership in Finland’s leading fiber operator Valokuitunen, in line with our strategy to offer converged services across the country.

In Norway , service revenue and profitability improved as we execute on our turnaround plan. Our fixed consumer business, with its new organization launched in June 2025, saw healthy service revenue growth and is on track to deliver the 2026 target volumes for fiber build-out. Pricing adjustments supported ARPU growth across mobile, broadband and TV. The market remains competitive, particularly in consumer, and we are working to reduce churn and improve profitability. In February, we announced a mobile RAN combination with ice that will substantially improve coverage, and we became Norway’s first operator to launch commercial 5G standalone.

Lithuania grew across all key segments, with mobile service revenue growth particularly strong. Construction started on a new data center in Vilnius, addressing strong domestic demand for resilient and sustainable infrastructure. A nationwide consumer survey recognized Telia as Lithuania’s leading telecom operator in customer service, confirming our strong customer satisfaction position.

Estonia delivered stable growth in the consumer business, with healthy uptake of our new Telia Shield security service. ICT deliveries in the enterprise and public sector business were affected by supply chain limitations, which are expected to improve in the coming quarters. We launched full 5G standalone with support for commercial handsets and Voice over New Radio (VoNR) in early April, allowing us to offer dedicated network capacity, ultra ‑ low latency and enhanced reliability to consumers and businesses.

In our Technology unit, we continue to simplify our IT landscape, invest in resilient networks and enhance our cybersecurity capabilities. We are deploying AI across customer service, networks and internal processes to drive efficiency and growth, and we are collaborating with Nokia to test AI-RAN technology and advance 5G capabilities for multiple industries, including mission-critical applications. Our IT costs declined in the quarter, after consistent increases throughout 2025.

We have updated our sustainability strategy, which includes four new focus areas and related targets: Securing people and digital environments, Enabling customers’ and our own climate transition, Digitally strengthening all generations and Empowering a winning culture. We will report on our progress in each area on a quarterly basis. Our work to reduce supply chain emissions continues, with 61% of suppliers having set science-based reduction targets. The ESG targets in Telia’s EUR 1.2 billion sustainability-linked revolving credit facility, signed in 2022 with 12 relationship banks, have been updated accordingly.

We are on track to deliver on our full-year outlook and 2025-27 ambitions, including free cash flow of at least SEK 10 billion by 2027. Although the direct impact of the major change program in 2024 is now largely behind us, the organization is committed to continued efficiency gains and delivered a 5% reduction in headcount and 2% reduction in operational expenses. Free cash flow was higher than in Q1 last year, driven by factors including higher EBITDA, lower cash CAPEX and a better-than-expected contribution from working capital. Our balance sheet remains strong despite leverage increasing slightly to 2.07x following the Bredband2 acquisition. We redeemed a EUR 500 million hybrid bond and replaced it with a SEK 2.4 billion hybrid, lowering future interest payments.

Our priorities are clear: customer satisfaction, profitable growth, and becoming even simpler, faster and more efficient. Over the past year, we have made necessary changes to take us into the future, and these will continue at pace. Our industry has never been so competitive. We are working every day to ensure we are well-positioned to execute on our plans and deliver on our targets. We have made significant progress, and we are ready to push for more.”

evidence.title: Telenor stock edges higher as buyback program update supports valuation
evidence.text:
Telenor ASA stock (ISIN NO0010063308) was quoted at around 133.30 Norwegian kroner on the Oslo Stock Exchange as of September 21, 2026, modestly higher on the day and supported by the company’s ongoing share buyback program reported through Oslo Bors NewsPoint on September 21, 2026.

According to Affarsvarlden on September 21, 2026, Oslo Bors NewsPoint published a status update on Telenor’s share buyback program, confirming that the telecom group is continuing to repurchase its own shares in the market.

The same overview shows Telenor’s latest quote at 133.30 NOK with a daily move of roughly 1.76 percent on September 21, 2026, indicating that investors are reacting positively to the capital return activity around the stock price level. Affarsvarlden

For fundamental context, Affarsvarlden’s key-figures section summarizing Telenor’s performance over the latest 12-month period reports revenue of 76,480 million Swedish kroner, compared with 80,169 million SEK in fiscal year 2025, marking a decline of about 4.6 percent over that span based on these figures. Affarsvarlden

The same data set shows operating profit of 16,851 million SEK for the latest 12 months versus 18,849 million SEK in 2025, implying that operating earnings are down by around 10.6 percent, a reminder that margin pressure has accompanied the topline softening over recent periods. Affarsvarlden

Despite the earnings headwind, the same overview lists a dividend yield of about 7.2 percent on the latest figures, with reported dividend payouts of 13,273 million SEK in fiscal year 2025 and 13,136 million SEK in 2024, underlining that Telenor remains an income-oriented telecom name for many shareholders. Affarsvarlden

Ownership structure and leverage profile

Affarsvarlden’s ownership table shows that the Government of Norway continues to hold about 54 percent of Telenor’s capital and votes, with Folketrygdfondet at around 4.6 percent and international asset managers such as BlackRock and The Vanguard Group owning roughly 2.4 percent and 2.1 percent respectively. Affarsvarlden

The same key-figures section lists net debt at 87,247 million SEK for the latest 12-month snapshot, down from 101,853 million SEK in 2025 and 104,597 million SEK in 2024, indicating that Telenor has reduced leverage by around 14.3 percent versus 2025 while still carrying a substantial debt load relative to equity of 68,085 million SEK in the most recent period. Affarsvarlden

Valuation and risk considerations for investors

Affarsvarlden calculates a price-earnings multiple of about 14.2 times based on the latest earnings per share data of 9.50 SEK for the trailing 12-month period, compared with a P/E of 29.2 times for fiscal year 2025 and 10.1 times for 2024, showing that valuation has compressed meaningfully from the prior year even as the share price continues to offer an above-market yield. Affarsvarlden

For investors, the combination of a high dividend yield, active share buybacks and declining net debt improves the capital-return profile, but the drop in revenue and operating profit over the latest periods underlines that Telenor still faces structural challenges in its core telecom markets and must balance generous payouts with ongoing investment and competition-related pressures.

Per the price overview referenced by Affarsvarlden on September 21, 2026, Telenor stock closed around 133.30 NOK on the Oslo Stock Exchange, with a daily gain of roughly 1.76 percent on that trading day, making this Oslo quote the primary reference price for the shares in Norwegian kroner.

evidence.title: Authorities raid Telenor offices
evidence.text:
Oslo-based Telenor’s former operations in Myanmar came back to haunt the large telecoms firm once again on Tuesday, when it was raided by Norwegian police and formally charged with possible crimes against humanity. What had been a promising expansion into Myanmar turned into a nightmare, after another military coup in the former Burma in 2021.

The company itself announced both the raid and the charges against it, after Norway’s domestic intelligence agency PST and state police unit Kripos turned up at company headquarters Tuesday morning. The company announced that it “was informed … that an investigation has been opened and charges brought against the company on suspicion of breaching the Sanctions Act, as well as complicty in crimes against humanity.”

Telenor executives have long argued that they had no choice but to obey orders from the military in Myanmar that ousted the government and once again arrested Nobel Peace Prize laureate Aung San Suu Kyi . She’s among those who have suffered under the new military coup leaders, after they ordered Telenor to release sensitive personal data, shut down its website and block telephones.

Telenor continues to claim that its employees in Myanmar “risked imprisonment, torture or the death penalty if the military authorities’ orders were not complied with.” Telenor spokesman David Fidjeland was once again claiming on Tuesday that Telenor landed in “a very demanding situation” after the coup, and that company officials “had no real choice” but to follow the coup leaders’ orders.

“We could not put our employees’ lives at risk,” Fidjeland said on Tuesday.

Telenor’s cooperation with coup leaders instead put Telenor customers at risk, including Aung San Suu Kyi and hundreds of others . Norwegian Broadcasting (NRK) published its own investigation into Telenor’s actions after the coup and reported in 2025 that the traffic data of 1,300 mobile phone customers was turned over to military officials and that nearly 500 customers risked arrest, including the Nobel Laureate who was later pardoned but kept under house arrest.

Now Telenor faces formal charges even though both PST and Kripos contended at an afternoon press conference that they have no doubt Telenor was caught in “an extremely demanding situation after the coup,” said Kripos attorney Espen Hjelmeland Hanken.

“At the same time the issue of necessity or justification is complex and built on various evaluations,” Hanken continued. “In such a serious case as this, the threshold for justification (of turning over customer records) is very high.”

Both PST and the company stressed that no Telenor subsidiaries or “private persons” (such as former Telenor bosses in Myanmar) have been charged in the case, at least not yet. Telenor later sold its operations in Myanmar and pulled out of the country.

Telenor itself noted that the company “has been in close dialogue with the Norwegian prosecuting authorities for a long time, and has handed over extensive documentation and information.” Those raiding the company on Tuesday said they wanted to secure documents regarding Telenor’s own investigation into the trouble in Myanmar.

Telenor’s troubles in Myanmar have long been a major political issue in Norway as well, since the former state telephone utility remains majority-owned by the state. “This is a very serious case and now we need to get all the facts about what the government and especially the trade minister has known about Telenor’s operations in Myanmar,” MP Per-Willy Amundsen of the conservative Progress Party told NRK on Tuesday. He leads the Parliament’s disciplinary committee, which so far has been denied access to many documents in the case.

“The state (which was a major supporter of Aung San Suu Kyi and tried to promote democracy in Myanmar) is a major owner in Telenor and (the government) has regular contact with the company regarding its operations,” Amundsen added. “We also want clarification about what the prime minister, trade minister and foreign minister has known about Telenor’s operations in Myanmar.”

Telenor Under Investigation for Myanmar Human Rights Violations

Norwegian police are probing telecom company Telenor for allegedly aiding crimes against humanity in Myanmar by providing historical traffic data to the military regime. Official raids were conducted at Telenor's headquarters, and the company is cooperating with authorities. Allegations include supporting oppressive practices and violating sanctions.

Norwegian authorities have launched an investigation into telecom giant Telenor amidst allegations of complicity in crimes against humanity following Myanmar's 2021 military coup. The inquiry focuses on suspicions that Telenor provided the military regime with customers' historical traffic data, amid claims of widespread human rights abuses.

On Tuesday, law enforcement officials conducted searches at Telenor's Oslo headquarters as part of the investigation, which also considers potential sanctions violations. Telenor confirmed it is working in close collaboration with investigators to clarify the case, following recent accusations it contributed to the repression of civic freedoms in Myanmar.

Despite completing its exit from Myanmar in March 2022, Telenor faces scrutiny over the sale of its local business unit, which allegedly included transferring sanctioned surveillance equipment. Activist voices and organizations are urging accountability for Telenor's alleged actions that may have endangered lives and privacy in the region.

evidence.title: Telenor partners with Verdane to build a global IoT leader
evidence.text:
(Fornebu, Norway, 26 May 2026) Telenor has entered into an agreement with Verdane to establish a joint ownership structure over Telenor Connexion. The transaction values the company at SEK 7.5 billion. The partnership is intended to realise value from Telenor Connexion’s strong market position while providing the company with access to long-term growth capital through an efficient ownership structure.

Over the past 25 years, Telenor Connexion has built a strong global position in managed IoT services and connectivity solutions for large, global customers. The market is expected to grow at double digit rates towards 2030. Today, the company is a top ten player globally outside China, with 31 million IoT SIM cards in operation and deliveries to more than 200 countries.

“We have bold ambitions in managed IoT, and with Verdane as a partner we gain additional power to realise them in a much more capital efficient manner. At the same time, this transaction clearly demonstrates Telenor’s ability to create value,” says Benedicte Schilbred Fasmer, President & CEO of Telenor.

Telenor Connexion delivers IoT solutions for everything from cars and water pumps to robotic lawn mowers. In January 2026, Telenor consolidated its Nordic IoT operations under one brand structure, with Telenor Connexion as the specialised IoT unit operating under Telenor IoT as the portfolio brand.

“With this structure in place, we are well positioned for the next phase. Telenor will remain a long‑term, strategic owner, and we will continue to put the full industrial strength of the Group behind Telenor Connexion. Together with Verdane, we will scale the business more rapidly in a diligent way,” says Fasmer.

Combining industrial edge with experienced growth capital

The global IoT market is experiencing strong growth. Through this partnership, Telenor combines its industrial platform, global reach and strong customer relationships with Verdane’s financial resources, transaction experience and active ownership model. This structure supports long-term growth ambitions and allows Telenor to grow in a disciplined manner. The ambition is to strengthen Telenor Connexion’s global offering and accelerate growth through both organic expansion and value-creating acquisitions.

Pekka Lundmark, the former President and CEO of Nokia, has agreed to join Telenor Connexion as Independent Chair following closing of the transaction. Mats Lundquist will continue as Chief Executive Officer of Telenor Connexion, ensuring continuity in leadership and execution of the company’s growth strategy.

Bjarne Kveim Lie, Founder and Managing Partner at Verdane, said: "We are grateful to have built a partnership based on mutual trust with Telenor and look forward to working closely together in the years to come. We believe Telenor Connexion is perfectly positioned in a well-established structural growth market that will benefit from the increasing adoption of AI through exposure to connected devices in data-intensive industries”.

Morten Weicher, Partner at Verdane, said: "We look forward to supporting the Telenor Connexion team in realising their ambitious strategy of becoming a global leader, drawing on Verdane’s significant experience in scaling industrial technology companies and more than 15 years of experience as an investor in the IoT space.”

Financial highlights and transaction structure

In 2025, Telenor Connexion generated revenues of approximately SEK 1.3 billion and delivered an EBITDA of around SEK 415 million on a pro-forma basis after the consolidation of Managed IoT Connectivity across Telenor Group. As consideration following the transaction, Telenor will receive approximately SEK 3.8 billion in cash, in addition to a seller credit of approximately SEK 0.8 billion, and recognise a gain of approximately SEK 7.2 billion. Each party commits to invest an additional SEK 2 billion in the company’s value accretive growth journey, which for Telenor will be approximately half of the proceeds received upfront in the transaction.

Telenor Group’s divestment values Telenor Connexion’s enterprise value at 18x EBITDA for 2025. As part of the transaction, the new structure will incur approximately SEK 2.2 billion in new bank debt, implying an expected post‑transaction equity value of approximately SEK 5.3 billion for Telenor Connexion. The agreement also includes a potential earn‑out if the company meets certain commercial targets, increasing the company’s enterprise value by SEK 0.3 billion.

Following the transaction, Telenor Connexion will be reported as an associated company of Telenor Group. The parties will establish a jointly owned company with 50/50 percent ownership. The board will be comprised of two representatives from each owner, in addition to an independent chair. The parties expect to complete the transaction during 2026, subject to the necessary regulatory approvals.

As part of the transaction, Verdane will acquire Telenor’s ownership stakes in Telenor Amp’s portfolio companies BLDNG.ai and Whereby.

For additional information, please contact:

Frank Maaø, SVP Capital Markets and Investor Relations (+47 91674045)

David Fidjeland, Director Media Relations (+47 93467224)

About Telenor Telenor Group is a leading telecommunications and technology company in the Nordics and Asia, serving over 200 million customers and generating annual revenues of around NOK 80 billion (2024). Telenor holds strong positions in its markets and is committed to responsible business conduct.

Driven by Telenor’s purpose, “With you, for a safer and smarter tomorrow”, we aim to create impact beyond connectivity by enabling societies to thrive in a digital future. Our cultural foundation is built on Trust, Curiosity, and Passion, guiding how we collaborate, innovate and deliver value for customers and communities.

Connectivity has been Telenor’s domain for more than 165 years, and today we combine that heritage with forward-looking solutions for security, sustainability and inclusion. Telenor is listed on the Oslo Stock Exchange under the ticker TEL. For more information, visit https://www.telenor.com .

About Verdane Verdane is a specialist growth buyout investment firm that partners with tech-enabled and sustainable businesses that help to digitalise and decarbonise the European economy. The flexible mandates of Verdane funds allow it to invest as a majority or minority control investor, replacement or growth capital, in single companies or in portfolios of companies

Verdane has raised EUR 10 billion in capital and its funds have made more than 200 investments in fast-growing businesses since 2003. Verdane’s team of over 180 investment professionals and operating experts is based out of Berlin, Copenhagen, London, Helsinki, Munich, Oslo and Stockholm and combines deep sector expertise with long-standing local networks and presence in core European markets.

Verdane is also a certified B Corporation, the most ambitious sustainability accreditation globally. The firm only backs businesses that pass its 2040 test, which indicates whether the company can thrive in a more sustainable future economy.

Verdane is partly owned by the Verdane Foundation, which is focused on two areas: climate change and more equitable and inclusive local communities.

evidence.title: Elisa's Microsoft Verification: A New Gold Standard for Cybersecurity Trust
evidence.text:
here — the single canonical is rendered immediately above the article body so the headline and body are adjacent, with dashboard data kept above this section) --> Elisa's Microsoft Verification: A New Gold Standard for Cybersecurity Trust

HELSINKI, FINLAND – July 01, 2026 – In a move that sends a clear signal across the enterprise security landscape, Finnish telecommunications and digital services leader Elisa announced today it has achieved Microsoft verified Managed Extended Detection and Response (MXDR) solution status. While partnerships in the tech world are common, this verification is a rare and rigorous endorsement, proving Elisa’s cybersecurity services meet a formidable standard set and validated by Microsoft’s own engineers.

For investors and C-suite executives, the announcement cuts through the noise of a crowded cybersecurity market. It signifies that Elisa's 24/7/365 Security Operation Center (SOC) and its proactive threat-hunting capabilities are not just marketing claims but have been battle-tested against one of the highest benchmarks in the industry. The verification confirms that Elisa’s services are deeply integrated with the Microsoft Security platform, including Microsoft 365 Defender and Microsoft Sentinel, creating a unified defense system that combines advanced technology with expert human oversight.

The Anatomy of Trust: Deconstructing Microsoft's MXDR Verification

To grasp the weight of this achievement, one must first understand the evolution from traditional security to the comprehensive approach of MXDR. For years, businesses have relied on a patchwork of solutions, from firewalls and antivirus software to more recent Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) tools. While effective in their silos, these systems often create blind spots that sophisticated attackers can exploit.

Managed Extended Detection and Response (MXDR) shatters these silos. It is a service-based model that unifies security telemetry from across an organization’s entire digital estate—endpoints, networks, cloud infrastructure, and identity systems. By correlating signals from these disparate sources, MXDR provides a single, coherent view of an organization's security posture, enabling the detection of complex threats that would otherwise go unnoticed.

Microsoft’s verification process elevates this concept further. It isn’t a simple partner program badge. To achieve verified status, providers like Elisa must demonstrate not only deep technical integration but also mature operational capabilities. This includes maintaining a 24/7 SOC staffed by security-cleared experts, proving proactive threat-hunting methodologies, and demonstrating a track record of successfully protecting a significant customer base using Microsoft’s security tools. This rigorous, engineer-led validation provides a level of assurance that is critical for organizations entrusting their digital survival to a third-party provider.

“With malicious attacks on the rise, we understand security is front and center for our customers,” said Rob Lefferts, CVP, Modern Protection and SOC at Microsoft. “Their solution closely integrates with Microsoft 365 Defender and Microsoft Sentinel and has been verified by Microsoft Security engineering to ensure that it provides comprehensive service coverage across the Microsoft Security portfolio.”

From Telecom Leader to Cybersecurity Powerhouse

For Elisa, this verification is the culmination of a long-term strategic focus. While known primarily as a telecommunications market leader in Finland, the company has been quietly building a formidable cybersecurity practice since 1995. As a provider of critical national infrastructure, Elisa has long understood the imperative of robust, resilient, and transparent security operations. Its Helsinki-based Cyber Security Center is staffed by Finnish experts who have undergone national security checks, a detail that resonates strongly with public and private sector clients concerned with data sovereignty and trust.

This Microsoft verification serves as global validation of that regional expertise. It’s a logical progression following Elisa's entry into the Microsoft Intelligent Security Association (MISA) last year, an ecosystem of trusted and reliable security companies.

“We are proud of achieving Microsoft Verified: Managed Extended Detection and Response solution status,” stated Sakari Pihlhjerta, Vice President of Cybersecurity Business at Elisa. “Together with Microsoft, we are securing our customers' local and global business operations against cyber threats with world-leading solutions. This achievement is a logical next step after Elisa joined the Microsoft Intelligent Security Association last year.”

This move positions Elisa not just as a Nordic champion but as a competitive player on the European stage, offering a compelling alternative to other global Managed Security Service Providers (MSSPs). Its unique value proposition combines the deep integration of a specialized Microsoft partner with the broad service portfolio of a major telecommunications firm.

The Proactive Defense Paradigm: What Verified MXDR Means for Businesses

The practical implications for Elisa’s current and prospective customers are significant. In an era where the median time to exploit a new vulnerability has shrunk from months to mere hours, reactive security is a losing strategy. The shift to a proactive MXDR model, now verified by Microsoft, offers tangible benefits.

First is the dramatic reduction in risk and response time. By leveraging AI, automation, and 24/7 human analysis, the service can detect and contain threats before they escalate into costly data breaches. This proactive stance is crucial as attackers increasingly use “malware-free” techniques like social engineering and identity-based attacks, which now constitute the majority of intrusions.

Second, it addresses the chronic shortage of cybersecurity talent and the problem of alert fatigue. Internal IT teams are often overwhelmed by a deluge of alerts from disparate tools. Elisa’s MXDR service acts as a force multiplier, filtering the noise, prioritizing genuine threats, and freeing in-house teams to focus on strategic initiatives.

“The Microsoft Intelligent Security Association is comprised of some the most reliable and trusted security companies across the globe,” said Maria Thomson, Director at the association. “We're thrilled to recognize and welcome Elisa's verified MXDR solution to the MISA portfolio.” This endorsement underscores the collaborative approach needed to combat modern cybercrime, where no single organization can stand alone.

Navigating a Future of AI-Driven Threats

Elisa’s achievement is particularly timely, as it aligns with the dominant trends shaping the future of cybersecurity. The rise of generative AI is a double-edged sword: while it helps defenders automate and scale their efforts, it also equips adversaries with tools to craft more sophisticated phishing campaigns and discover vulnerabilities at an unprecedented rate. The global cost of cybercrime is projected to exceed $23 trillion by 2027, a figure that demands a more advanced and integrated defense posture.

Furthermore, the relentless migration to the cloud has expanded the corporate attack surface exponentially. Securing these complex, multi-cloud environments requires the holistic visibility that an XDR platform provides. Elisa’s verified MXDR solution, built on Microsoft Sentinel's cloud-native capabilities, is designed precisely for this modern reality.

By securing this verification, Elisa has demonstrated it is not only keeping pace with the evolving threat landscape but is positioning itself at the forefront of the defensive line. For enterprises navigating this complex digital frontier, such verified partnerships are becoming less of a luxury and more of a fundamental requirement for survival.

evidence.title: Elisa to Deliver Global Cybersecurity Operations Center for Valmet
evidence.text:
Elisa to Deliver Global Cybersecurity Operations Center for Valmet

Valmet and Elisa have signed a multi-year agreement on the delivery of cyber security services and a global cyber security operations center.

In addition, Valmet will continue its long-standing collaboration with Elisa in mobile services as well as network management and expert services. Together, the companies are building an environment where telecommunications and cyber services work seamlessly together.

Elisa and Valmet have agreed to expand their existing collaboration agreements effective April 1, 2026. The agreements cover three areas: cyber security services, global network services, and mobile networks.

Collaboration in cyber security, networks, assembly management, and warehouse automation

Valmet has selected Elisa as its new provider of cyber security services, a global cyber security operations center (SOC), and related expert services. The aim of the collaboration is to protect Valmet from constantly evolving cyber security threats.

Elisa’s cyber security services will complement Valmet’s own information security organization by monitoring Valmet’s digital environment around the clock and responding immediately to potential threats. evidence.title: Elisa praises placing cybersecurity at heart of operations
evidence.text:
Elisa praises placing cybersecurity at heart of operations

Finnish operator Elisa combined cybersecurity and service operations monitoring to help faster detection and prevention of incidents, using automation to detect issues before they affect customers.

Cybersecurity is on the minds of many European telcos, with malicious activity worldwide showing no signs of abating. Elisa, the incumbent operator in Finland, opted for a proactive approach and created a hybrid cybersecurity and service operations center (cSOC), rather than having two separate ones. This has helped it stymie the effects of cyber incidents like politically motivated DDoS attacks.

The telco has seen "a lot of synergies" as a result of the move, Karri Jäkkö, Elisa's director of cSOC, told Light Reading during an interview. For example, if there is a large-scale incident, it may not be immediately obvious if it's the result of a misconfiguration or related to a cyberattack, he explained.

The cSOC also works differently to a traditional network operations center. "Instead of monitoring the network alarms and the alarms in the devices and that kind of stuff, we monitor the services from the customer point of view, so how the customers are using the services," Jäkkö said, adding it is also checking for any deviations in the network.

If there are any issues or deviations, the cSOC will try to rectify the problem automatically. If that's impossible, human engineers will step in. Elisa hopes the cSOC will help it reach its goal of having zero instances of customers notifying it of a problem. Instead, the system should be able to spot all issues automatically.

There has been progress. Since Elisa introduced this approach in 2011, Jäkkö said it has reduced the number of such incidents by 83%. At the same time, he admitted these incidents cannot be fully eliminated due to unforeseeable circumstances like power outages.

The approach can also be successful in tackling distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks. Since one of the things it monitors is Elisa's website and online shop, it can spot any spikes in malicious traffic toward the site, Jäkkö said. It can then make sure there are assistants on hand to handle any necessary manual mitigation, should it be required.

On one occasion, Elisa spotted that its addresses had been added to the attack list of NoName057(16) – a pro-Russian hacker group that has been linked to attacks in European and NATO countries. Spotting this early allowed the operator to prepare and minimize disruptions, Jäkkö argued. "One of the services had availability issues, so we were able to start the manual mitigation in the same minute, and the service effect kind of lasted for about one minute," he said.

Having Russia as a neighbor to the East, Finland currently finds itself in close proximity to Europe's main geopolitical threats. Elisa has seen some effects of this, with Russian involvement suspected in recent incidents that resulted in cuts to its subsea cables.

The company also saw malicious traffic driven toward its sites once it demanded compensation for one of the cable cuts. In general, Jäkko said there has been a pattern of DDoS attacks in Finland occurring around political events, like the country's entry into NATO in 2023, but he said it's hard to link them to a specific actor.

Another big trend in cybersecurity is the use of AI in attacks, including to detect and exploit vulnerabilities faster. It can also be used for hyper-personalized phishing attacks. "Instead of having these mass messages that you send to everybody, you can send personalised attacks to big masses," he said, adding he sees it as a big threat for Elisa as a company, "but even more for the customers and end users."

Fraud has been an important issue for operators in recent years and Finland is no exception. It saw an increase in the number of caller ID spoofing for fraudulent calls and messages around 2021, Jäkkö said, meaning fraudulent calls from abroad appeared to be coming from inside Finland. Concerned this would affect trust in Finnish phone numbers and have implications for its voice business, Elisa decided to try and prevent this.

Monitoring showed that almost 90% of all phone calls coming into Finland had a falsified phone number, Jäkkö noted. For these calls, Elisa stopped displaying the phone number, indicating instead they were coming from an unknown number. As a result, customers stopped answering and the call rate dropped from 90% to 10%, he claimed.

As there were no visible downsides, Elisa dropped the calls altogether after a few months. This approach was then replicated at a national level and as a result, he said the proceeds of this type of crime dropped from €7 million (US$8 million) to €2,700 ($3,097) in one year, citing data from the Finnish National Bureau of Investigation.

evidence.title: Elisa Oyj: Automatic monitoring of brand counterfeits and protection for the factory - Lumene Group upgraded its cyber solutions to a new era
evidence.text:
Elisa Oyj: Automatic monitoring of brand counterfeits and protection for the factory - Lumene Group upgraded its cyber solutions to a new era

Lumene Group has updated its cybersecurity services together with Elisa. One of the new services monitors online brand abuse and reacts to potential counterfeits. The cooperation also includes 24/7 monitoring of cyber threats and the protection of stores and production lines.

HELSINKI, Feb. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Finnish cosmetics company Lumene Group has completed the renewal of its cybersecurity services that began in 2024 in cooperation with Elisa. The goal of the cooperation has been to improve the protection of the company's increasingly digitalized production and brands sold in several countries. The all-encompassing cybersecurity project has been carried out by Elisa's Finnish experts, on schedule.

Lumene Group became a customer of the Elisa Security Operations Center (SOC), which monitors the services 24/7 and enables rapid response to potential cyber threats. In addition, Lumene Group implemented, for example, DDoS protection and firewalls to protect network connections at the production facility and stores.

Lumene Group, known especially for its LUMENE, CUTRIN, and IDA WARG Beauty brands, aims to double its turnover by the end of the decade, and modern cybersecurity services are a prerequisite for achieving this goal. In recent years, the company has improved the efficiency of the operations of its production facility in Espoo, and has invested heavily in digitalization, which has also further increased the importance of cybersecurity.

"We invested millions of euros in the production environment, and it would have been foolish to ignore cybersecurity," says Petri Pantsar, Head of IT Infrastructure and Cybersecurity at Lumene Group. "The comprehensive protection we have now built ensures that our production will not be disrupted and that we will maintain a safe, good and stable workplace for our hundreds of employees also in the future," he continues.

With the Cybersecurity Center OT service developed by Elisa, Lumene Group monitors the production facility, equipment in the environment, production lines and other Internet of Things (IoT) devices, which today are increasingly exposed to cyber threats.

Lumene Group also carried out penetration testing and physical security audits to find and fix potential vulnerabilities.

"Elisa's experts found the right solutions, and projects have been completed on schedule, which is rare for such large-scale IT projects," Pantsar says.

Threat intelligence service monitors the internet for brand counterfeits

In addition to traditional cybersecurity monitoring and response, Elisa and Lumene Group have built a new kind of threat intelligence service that allows Lumene Group to monitor the misuse of its brands online and quickly react to potential breaches.

"The service has proven its value when we have been able to take action against, for example, fake websites," Pantsar describes.

Lumene Group has not experienced any data breaches since the introduction of Elisa's services, but Pantsar emphasizes that continuous development and vigilance are essential.

"Information security is never complete, but we have taken significant steps in the right direction."

In addition, Pantsar praises Elisa's personnel.

"Elisa has succeeded in hiring high-quality workforce from the labor market. Personally, I appreciate the fact that the experts' way of working is professional yet relaxed."

Lumene Group is one of the leading Nordic beauty companies, specializing in the development and manufacturing of high-performing, sustainable skincare, makeup, and hair care products. The Group is home to our leading Nordic beauty brands, including LUMENE, CUTRIN, and IDA WARG Beauty. Our brands are available in 26 countries, with a global reach through online channels. Headquartered in Espoo, Finland, Lumene Group develops, formulates, and manufactures the majority of its products in-house, combining Nordic nature with scientific innovations. Our key markets include Finland, Scandinavia, the UK, Germany, and Poland, supported by a team of over 370 professionals worldwide. In 2024, Lumene Group's net sales totalled EUR 102 million. We are proud to be a certified B Corporation, reflecting our commitment to social and environmental responsibility. The majority owner of Lumene Group is Verdane, a European private equity company focused on sustainable growth. www.lumenegroup.com

evidence.title: Revealing the Invisible: The Transformative Role of ELISA in Modern Forensic Investigations
evidence.text:
Revealing the Invisible: The Transformative Role of ELISA in Modern Forensic Investigations

In forensic science, many critical pieces of evidence are invisible to the naked eye, including minute blood or saliva stains, trace amounts of toxins or drugs, the species origin of biological fluids, or the presence of specific antigens that can link individuals to crime scenes. The enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) has emerged as a powerful tool for revealing these hidden clues. This article surveys how ELISA is used in modern forensic investigations: its principles, types, strengths and limitations; its application in identifying body fluids, blood group antigens, drugs of abuse and toxins; and recent advances and future directions (e.g. improved antibodies, multiplex assays, field deployable formats). Through case examples and literature review, we show how ELISA has transformed forensic work by enabling more specific, sensitive, and rapid detection of biological and chemical evidence. We also discuss practical considerations (sample condition, cross‐reactivity), legal admissibility, and how ELISA complements other techniques such as DNA profiling, mass spectrometry, and spectroscopic methods.

Forensic science often hinges on the detection and analysis of very low-concentration substances, such as proteins, antigens, enzymes, small-molecule toxins, or drugs. Many traditional presumptive tests (e.g., colour reactions, catalysis, microscopy) may give an indication but lack specificity, sensitivity, or the ability to quantify. ELISA (Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay) is a robust immunochemical method that combines antigen-antibody specificity with enzymatic amplification of the signal to detect very small amounts of the analyte. Since its development in the early 1970s, ELISA has seen wide adoption in diagnostics; more recently, its role in forensic investigations has become transformative.

This article explores how ELISA reveals what is otherwise invisible — whether in body fluids, degraded stains, mixed samples, or trace toxins. We examine ELISA’s principles, variants, forensic applications, recent technological improvements, and the challenges and future potential in the forensic context.

ELISA is a solid-phase immunoassay: the antigen or antibody is immobilised on a solid support (often a microtitre plate well), and the binding of the complementary molecule (antibody or antigen) is detected via an enzyme-linked reporter, which catalyses a reaction generating a measurable signal (commonly colour). Key variants include:

In forensic settings, the the choice of variant depends on the analyte size, matrix (blood, saliva, urine, tissue), quality and age of the sample, required sensitivity, potential inhibitors, and whether quantitation is necessary.

Below are key areas where ELISA is already widely applied in forensic investigations.

A common problem in crime scene investigations is determining the type of biological fluid present in a stain. Identifying whether a stain is blood, saliva, semen, sweat, or another bodily fluid, and determining whether it is of human or animal origin, is critical.

ELISA and related immunoassay methods are frequently used as screening tools for drugs of abuse (opiates, cocaine, amphetamines, benzoylecgonine, etc.) in various matrices (blood, urine, oral fluids). Their utility lies in speed, relatively low cost, and the ability to process multiple samples. Confirmatory testing (e.g., GC-MS, LC-MS/MS) is often required following positive screening results to meet legal admissibility requirements. ( PubMed )

In cases where non-human blood or fluids are involved (e.g., presence of animal blood, contamination, or mixed stains), ELISA with monoclonal antibodies against specific immunoglobulins or antigens allows for distinguishing between human and non-human stains. This helps avoid false leads. ( PubMed )

Beyond identifying body fluid or drug use, ELISA of certain antigenic markers (blood group, secretor antigens) can offer investigative lead information. For instance, ABO type or secretor status, even from non‐blood fluid, might narrow the potential donor pool in the absence of DNA. Also,, detecting microbial antigens (e.g., for pathogen exposure) and toxins (such as botulinum) is possible. While less commonly used for some of these, the literature shows applications.

ELISA has several features that make it especially valuable in the modern forensic context:

ELISA is not without issues, and understanding these issues is essential for proper application in forensics.

To overcome limitations and expand ELISA’s scope, researchers and forensic labs are pushing forward in several directions:

Here are illustrative examples from the literature that demonstrate how ELISA has made a difference.

Looking forward, several areas promise further transformation:

ELISA has become indispensable in modern forensic investigations as a method for making visible what is otherwise invisible, including identifying minute traces of biological fluids, distinguishing between human and non-human origins, detecting drugs or toxins, typing blood group antigens, and providing investigative leads. Its strengths—sensitivity, specificity, throughput, and cost-effectiveness—make it a go-to screening or confirmatory tool. While limitations remain (cross-reactivity, degradation, and the need for confirmatory testing), ongoing innovations are pushing its capability forward. In many cases, ELISA complements, rather than replaces, other forensic methods such as DNA profiling or mass spectrometry. As the forensic field continues to evolve, ELISA will remain a core tool, increasingly refined, more multiplexed, more field‑capable, and ever more powerful in revealing the invisible.

evidence.title: Telecom Italia, le grand retour de l’Etat dans les télécoms
evidence.text:
Ce résumé peut avoir été écrit avec l'assistance d’une IA générative. En savoir plus

Abonnez-vous pour accéder au résumé en 20 secondes.

Un homme promène son chien dans un parc. Il s’adresse au spectateur, les yeux face caméra. Il invite les actionnaires de l’entreprise de télécommunications TIM à adhérer à l’OPA de Poste Italiane. Les habitants de la Péninsule n’ont pu échapper à cette vaste campagne publicitaire diffusée sur le service public, les chaînes privées et même sur les diverses plateformes de streaming. Il ne s’agit pas de vendre un compte bancaire ou une assurance, mais bien de convaincre les propriétaires d’actions de l’ancienne Telecom Italia de les faire participer à une opération financière de plusieurs milliards d’euros. Cette campagne singulière annonce le retour de l’Etat italien dans une entreprise qu’il avait privatisée il y a près de 30 ans afin de créer aujourd’hui un géant des télécommunications.

Poste Italiane «tient énormément à ce que cela se termine bien, commente Marco Liera, consultant et auteur de la newsletter «Il capitale», spécialisée en finance et investissements. Cette opération a été réalisée pour créer un géant national des télécommunications et du cloud, important pour Rome dans la gestion des informations à des fins de sécurité nationale.» Poste Italiane, contrôlée par l’Etat italien, possédait déjà 20,1% de TIM. Elle cherche désormais à acquérir les actions qu’elle ne détient pas encore. Pour chaque action apportée à l’offre, l’actionnaire reçoit 0,218 action nouvellement émise de Poste Italiane et 1,97 euro (1,85 franc suisse) en liquide. Le groupe postal avait initialement proposé 1,67 euro en espèces, mais a relevé son offre de 30 centimes début septembre, tout en renonçant à la condition qui exigeait que les actionnaires représentant au moins 66,67% des droits de vote donnent leur accord à l’opération. Elle a précisé que cette nouvelle contrepartie était définitive. Une nouvelle fenêtre, ouverte du 21 au 25 septembre, permet aux actionnaires qui n’avaient pas encore apporté leurs titres de le faire.

evidence.title: Telecom Italia Aktie: Enel startet Mobilfunk-Gegenpol
evidence.text:
Die Mehrheitsübernahme von Telecom Italia durch den italienischen Staatskonzern Poste Italiane zieht weite Kreise und löst erste Gegenbewegungen im Heimatmarkt aus. Mit einem Anteil von rund 66,6 Prozent hat sich Poste Italiane die Kontrolle über den traditionsreichen Telekommunikationskonzern mit Sitz in Rom gesichert.

Zusammen kommen die beiden Unternehmen auf einen kombinierten Jahresumsatz von schätzungsweise 27 Milliarden Euro sowie einen operativen Gewinn von 5 Milliarden Euro.

Der Zusammenschluss soll erhebliche Einsparungen heben. Geplant sind jährliche Synergien von rund 700 Millionen Euro, von denen etwa 500 Millionen Euro auf reine Kostensenkungen entfallen sollen.

Telecom Italia SPA Aktie: Kaufen oder Verkaufen? Hier weiterlesen ...

Mit mehr als 150.000 Beschäftigten entsteht ein gewichtiger Mischkonzern, der Telekommunikations-, Logistik- und Finanzdienstleistungen bündeln will. Auch die brasilianische Tochter TIM Brasil, an der Telecom Italia 68 Prozent hält, rückt damit unter die indirekte Führung von Poste Italiane.

Die Entstehung dieses neuen Schwergewichts verändert das Marktumfeld spürbar. Der italienische Energiekonzern Enel reagiert umgehend auf die Allianz und startet mit Enel Mobile ein eigenes Mobilfunkangebot.

Das Modell setzt als virtueller Netzbetreiber auf die Netzinfrastruktur von Fastweb und Vodafone auf. Mit Download-Geschwindigkeiten von bis zu 2 Gigabit pro Sekunde und kombinierten Tarifen für bestehende Strom- und Gaskunden positioniert sich Enel gezielt als direkter Herausforderer des neuen Bündnisses.

Zugleich sorgt die Neuordnung der Eigentümerstruktur für Anpassungen bei Marktbeobachtern. Die Ratingagentur Standard Ethics setzte ihr Nachhaltigkeitsrating für Telecom Italia aus. Zuvor war das Unternehmen mit der Note „E+“ bewertet worden.

Die Agentur begründete diesen Schritt mit dem laufenden Übernahmeangebot und dem angestrebten Rückzug von der Börse. Poste Italiane peilt eine Beteiligung von mindestens 90 Prozent an, um ein Delisting durchzusetzen.

Die veränderten Mehrheitsverhältnisse spiegeln sich auch im Börsenwert wider. Gestern schloss die Aktie von Telecom Italia bei 7,76 Euro. Seit Jahresanfang verzeichnet das Papier damit einen Zuwachs von 51 Prozent.

Mit einer Marktkapitalisierung von 16,52 Milliarden Euro bleibt das Unternehmen der Dreh- und Angelpunkt für die anstehende Konsolidierung des italienischen Telekommunikationssektors. Für Anleger entscheidet sich in den kommenden Schritten, ob die geplante Vollintegration wie vorgesehen gelingt.

evidence.title: Poste Italiane assume controle da Telecom Italia e da TIM Brasil
evidence.text:
Poste Italiane assume controle da Telecom Italia e da TIM Brasil

A Poste Italiane passou a controlar a Telecom Italia após alcançar 66,6% do capital social da companhia italiana em uma oferta pública voluntária de aquisição e troca de ações. Com a operação, a empresa italiana também passa a controlar indiretamente a TIM Brasil ( TIMS3 ).

O resultado da oferta foi confirmado pela Poste Italiane, e a liquidação das ações entregues no período inicial ocorreu na última sexta-feira (18). A mudança de controle ocorre na cadeia societária da TIM Brasil: a operadora brasileira é controlada pela Telecom Italia.

Assim, a Poste Italiane passa a ocupar o topo dessa estrutura de controle, embora as ações da TIM Brasil continuem negociadas na B3 e na Bolsa de Nova York.

Entretanto, como a empresa brasileira não foi comprada diretamente pela Poste Italiane, o que mudou foi apenas o controle que está acima dela na estrutura societária. A Telecom Italia continua sendo a controladora da TIM Brasil, mas agora a Poste Italiane é a acionista controladora da Telecom Italia.

A operação foi estruturada como uma oferta pública de aquisição e troca. Para cada ação da Telecom Italia entregue à oferta, a contraprestação estabelecida pela Poste inclui 1,67 euro em dinheiro e 0,22 ação ordinária de nova emissão da Poste Italiane.

Em comunicado, a Poste Italiane informou que a operação envolve um aumento de capital para emissão das novas ações utilizadas como parte do pagamento. Na prática, a operação permite à Poste aumentar sua participação na Telecom Italia sem realizar todo o pagamento em dinheiro.

Tender offer terms and strategic rationale

According to Aktiencheck , the revised offer grants Telecom Italia minority shareholders EUR 1.97 in cash plus 0.218 newly issued Poste Italiane shares listed on Euronext Milan for each Telecom Italia share tendered.

The increase of the cash component by 18 percent compared with the initial proposal is designed to secure higher participation from Telecom Italia’s minority investors, who have until September 25, 2026 to decide whether to accept the offer, as highlighted by Aktiencheck .

As The Globe and Mail reports on September 19, 2026, at least one member of Telecom Italia’s corporate bodies has already accepted the offer via an off-exchange transaction, receiving the mixed consideration of cash and newly issued Poste Italiane shares for 128 Telecom Italia shares.

This insider acceptance underscores that the improved terms are considered sufficiently attractive by some key stakeholders, and it signals to the market that Poste Italiane is committed to executing the transaction on the basis of a higher cash payout than initially planned, according to The Globe and Mail .

evidence.title: Fastweb trials Starlink: smartphones connected to satellites in rural areas
evidence.text:
Fastweb trials Starlink: smartphones connected to satellites in rural areas

First Italian trial of ‘Direct to Cell’: switching from terrestrial to satellite signal without antennas

For feedback, please contact english@ilsole24ore.com

For feedback, please contact english@ilsole24ore.com

Fastweb + Vodafone is bringing Starlink’s ‘direct-to-cell’ technology trial to Italia, paving the way for direct satellite connectivity for standard smartphones. The trial, the first of its kind in the Italia, will begin in the Apennine region of central Italia with the aim of ensuring mobile coverage even in areas where the terrestrial network does not reach, and represents something different from the satellite service that Starlink has been offering for some time now for internet access. This isn’t about connecting a home via a dedicated antenna, but about turning the satellite into a fully-fledged mobile radio station in space. The smartphone remains the one we carry in our pockets: when it loses the terrestrial signal, it automatically switches to the satellite network, without the user having to do anything.

This is what sets the Italian trial apart. The Direct to Cell technology uses standard 4G smartphones, without any hardware modifications or additional accessories. The best-optimised devices will also be able to use apps such as WhatsApp, Google Maps or AccuWeather, as well as text messages, whilst any 4G phone will still be able to access messaging at the very least.

The trial makes use of a portion of Fastweb’s radio spectrum, which is used by Starlink satellites to transmit the signal directly to mobile phones. The aim is to bridge the digital divide in areas where building new terrestrial infrastructure is difficult or economically unviable, by providing at least essential communication services.

“We are very excited about our partnership with Fastweb in developing this mobile satellite service, which will enhance the customer experience,” says Stephanie Bednarek, Vice President of Commercial Sales at SpaceX.

For Fastweb, satellite does not replace the traditional mobile network, but complements it. “Our aim is to contribute to the country’s digitalisation,” says Marco Raimondi, Head of B2C Products at Fastweb + Vodafone. “Once again, Fastweb is at the forefront of innovation in the Italia telecoms sector.”

For the time being, this is a trial restricted to industry professionals, authorised until 30 September and limited to a maximum of 3,000 participants. Only once the trial has concluded, and following approval from the relevant authorities, will Fastweb + Vodafone consider the commercial launch of the service. There are also some limitations: no traditional voice calls, operation only outdoors with a clear view of the sky, and performance that is inferior to that of the conventional mobile network. But the direction is clear: satellite technology is entering the mobile network and aiming to eliminate the last remaining connectivity dead zones in Italy.

evidence.title: AI, Fastweb oltre i chatbot: lancia l’agente Ross e uno spinoff incubatore
evidence.text:
AI, Fastweb oltre i chatbot: lancia l’agente Ross e uno spinoff incubatore

L’operatore lancia l’agente AI autonomo pensato come servizio as a service in abbonamento mensile e crea NextMindLab

Fastweb continua a espandere le proprie soluzioni di intelligenza artificiale e lancia sul mercato Ross , il suo agente AI autonomo . La soluzione è pensata come servizio «as a service» in abbonamento mensile ed è inquadrata in una società ad hoc controllata al 100% da Fastweb, NextMindLab , spinoff del gruppo dedicato ad incubare prodotti e servizi di AI.

L’agente AI Ross realizza azioni come inviare email, programmare un’agenda o creare e mettere online un sito. Telegram viene utilizzato come interfaccia (è già in roadmap l’integrazione con altre soluzioni di messaggistica) e si distingue per la capacità di collegare app e strumenti di lavoro in modo da avere accesso e poter svolgere compiti in autonomia sulla base delle indicazioni fornite, in modo fluido e trasversale.

Secondo i dati, Ross fa risparmiare in media fino a 2 ore e mezza al giorno , gestisce fino all'87% delle mail in entrata e organizza l'agenda con una velocità tre volte superiore alla media. Fastweb sottolinea che le infrastrutture e i modelli linguistici sono ospitati in Italia e conformi al Gdpr e all'AI Act europeo , con i dati delle conversazioni che non vengono usati per allenare i modelli AI.

Sul suo profilo Linkedin , il ceo del gruppo Fastweb+Vodafone, Walter Renna , spiega come rispetto alle chat AI tradizionali, un agente AI «agisce». Renna specifica che «il motore dietro Ross è una versione riscritta di OpenClaw, definito recentemente dal ceo di Nvidia, Jensen Huang, come il sistema operativo dei computer agentici» e Fastweb ha preso l’incarico di prendere «la potenza di un sistema agentico autonomo» e di averlo «trasformato in un servizio "as a service" sicuro».

Fastweb ha lanciato a fine aprile uno spinoff dedicato all’AI chiamato NextMindLab. Il presidente della società controllata al 100% dall’operatore tlc è Alessandro Magnino , chief strategy & transformation officer del gruppo, membro dell’executive committee di Fastweb+Vodafone ed ex top manager di Vodafone Italia. Il board è completato dal cfo, Peter Grueter , e da Giovanni Germani, head of artificial intelligence del gruppo.

Il nuovo veicolo, spiega l’oggetto sociale, si occuperò di «sviluppo, progettazione, realizzazione, gestione e commercializzazione, anche in modalità di erogazione di SaaS di piattaforme digitali, applicazioni e soluzioni tecnologiche , compresi assistenti virtuali e sistemi basati su tecnologie di AI». evidence.title: Orange Polska stock gains on 2026 growth and debt data
evidence.text:
Orange Polska (ISIN PLORNGE00014) delivered 5.5 percent revenue growth in the first half of 2026, according to Ideal Investisseur on September 22, 2026. The reported figures also show EBITDA of EUR 9.23 billion and net income of EUR 3.206 billion for the same period.

For the first half of 2026, revenue stood at EUR 20.948 billion, compared with the reported growth rate of 5.5 percent. EBITDA represented EUR 9.23 billion, with an EBITDA margin of 29.3 percent, while net income reached EUR 3.206 billion, according to Ideal Investisseur on September 22, 2026.

The comparison investors can quantify is the 5.5 percent revenue increase against the first-half revenue base of EUR 20.948 billion. That combination gives the operating update more weight than a purely market-driven share move, although the figures also show a balance-sheet counter-factor.

Net debt had risen to EUR 35.7 billion after the MasOrange integration, and the debt-to-EBITDAaL ratio was 2.4 times in the first half of 2026. The same report also identified a 3.1 percent decline at Orange Business and a 6.4 percent fall in its EBITDAaL, making the enterprise division a clear drag on the group figures.

The operating mix therefore matters: double-digit growth in Africa and the Middle East supported the first-half performance, while Orange Business weakened. The reported 29.3 percent EBITDA margin and 2.4 times debt-to-EBITDAaL ratio place profitability and integration-related leverage on opposite sides of the investor picture.

Orange Polska stock awaits a separate quote

Orange Polska stock is a Polish telecommunications equity, but the available market evidence in this update concerns Orange rather than a substantiated primary-exchange quotation for Orange Polska. The financial figures above are periodized to the first half of 2026 and dated to the September 22, 2026 report.

evidence.title: Orange Polska wydał pilny komunikat. Dotyczy nie tylko klientów
evidence.text:
Orange Polska wydał pilny komunikat. Dotyczy nie tylko klientów

Cyberprzestępcy nieustannie szukają nowych sposobów na przekonanie ofiar, że mają do czynienia z prawdziwym pracownikiem banku. CERT Orange Polska ostrzega przed serią SMS-ów, które mają uwiarygodnić fałszywe rozmowy telefoniczne. Tym razem przestępcy nie wysyłają żadnego linku, lecz próbują wykorzystać wiadomość o rzekomej weryfikacji konsultanta.

CERT Orange Polska wykrył wiadomości, które bezpośrednio podszywają się pod korespondencję bankową. W jednej z nich odbiorca otrzymuje informację o „weryfikacji pracownika banku”, a następnie kod oraz nazwisko osoby przedstawianej jako konsultant. SMS kończy się podpisem Alior Bank Polska.

Treść wiadomości może wyglądać wiarygodnie, ponieważ oszust wysyłający ją podczas rozmowy telefonicznej przedstawia się jako pracownik banku. W kolejnych wiadomościach zmieniane są przede wszystkim personalia rzekomego konsultanta oraz nazwa instytucji.

Cyberprzestępcy podszywając się pod pracownika banku szukają coraz to bardziej wymyślnych sposobów, by przekonać do siebie ofiarę.

W ostatnim tygodniu wykorzystano między innymi nazwy nadawców alior24, agricole24, ing24, ipko24, iko24, Monitoring., iPKO24, mBank, nbp, NBP, PEKA024 oraz pko bp24.

Wiadomości nie zawierają linków. Mechanizm działania opiera się tutaj przede wszystkim na socjotechnice. Oszust sam wysyła SMS podczas prowadzonej rozmowy, aby stworzyć wrażenie, że jego tożsamość została właśnie potwierdzona przez bank.

Sam kod oraz nazwisko konsultanta nie mają w tym scenariuszu większego znaczenia. Ich zadaniem jest uspokojenie rozmówcy i zwiększenie jego zaufania do osoby znajdującej się po drugiej stronie połączenia.

Najbezpieczniej samodzielnie sprawdzić na stronie swojego banku, w jaki sposób można potwierdzić tożsamość konsultanta. W wielu przypadkach odpowiednia funkcja jest dostępna po zalogowaniu do aplikacji mobilnej. Czasami podczas rozmowy aplikacja wysyła również komunikat push, którego zaakceptowanie pozwala potwierdzić kontakt.

Nie należy ufać „potwierdzeniom” SMS podobnym do tych wykorzystywanych w opisywanym schemacie. Jeśli rozmowa wzbudza jakiekolwiek podejrzenia, najlepiej się rozłączyć, samodzielnie znaleźć numer telefonu banku i zapytać, czy rzeczywiście ktoś próbował się skontaktować.

Oszuści mogą przy tym próbować odwieść ofiarę od zakończenia rozmowy, powołując się na rzekome poważne zagrożenie i presję czasu. Dlatego nie warto prowadzić z nimi dyskusji ani pozwalać, by to rozmówca dyktował kolejne kroki, a kolejne warianty tej metody mogą pojawiać się wraz z rozwojem podobnych schematów.

Orange Polska Reaffirms Its Trust in Viaccess-Orca with Multiyear Contract Extension

Viaccess-Orca announced that Orange Polska has renewed its contract with VO for the continued delivery and evolution of its TV services.

Orange Polska continues to Rely on Viaccess-Orca for Secure TV Services and the Next Phase of its Technology Evolution

PARIS — Sept. 9, 2026 — Viaccess-Orca (VO), a global leader in TV platforms and content security solutions, announced today that Orange Polska, one of Poland’s leading telecommunications operators, has renewed its contract with VO for the continued delivery and evolution of its TV services.

The multiyear extension builds on a customer relationship dating back to 2013 and reflects Orange Polska’s continued confidence in VO’s technology and expertise.

Under the renewed contract, VO will continue to support Orange Polska’s TV services with a broad range of technologies, including VO Secure Video Player, Multi-DRM, VO DRM, and VO’s Service Delivery Platform (SDP).

“We’ve worked with Viaccess-Orca for many years, and they have a strong understanding of both our technology environment and what we need from our TV services,” said Piotr Wit, Director of Home Network at Orange Polska. “This experience and expertise are becoming even more important as we continue to modernize our platform and evolve our services.”

As part of Orange Polska’s ongoing modernization program, VO is also supporting the transition to a revamped architecture designed to provide greater flexibility and enable the adoption of cloud and AI-driven capabilities over time.

“Supporting a tier-one operator like Orange Polska for more than a decade requires both proven technology and the ability to evolve as its needs change,” said Pascal Birot, Vice President of Sales EMEA at Viaccess-Orca. “We’re proud to continue supporting Orange Polska teams as they modernize their services and prepare for what comes next.”

evidence.title: Zmiany w ofercie telewizyjnej Orange Polska. Nowe i usunięte stacje
evidence.text:
Zmiany w ofercie telewizyjnej Orange Polska. Nowe i usunięte stacje

Orange Polska od 1 września znacząco zmienił ofertę telewizyjną. Z pakietów operatora zniknęło 10 kanałów, w tym stacje należące do Paramount Network, BBC News i 13 Ulica. Jednocześnie pakiet Extra TV został rozszerzony o 10 nowych pozycji. Wśród nich są Newsmax Polska, dwa kanały 4K oraz stacje dziecięce i edukacyjne.

Jeszcze pod koniec lipca Orange Polska informował część abonentów o planowanym wyłączeniu siedmiu kanałów. Ostatecznie lista stacji, które z końcem sierpnia przestały być dostępne, jest dłuższa.

Z oferty Orange Polska usunięto: 13 Ulica, BBC News, Comedy Central, Polsat Comedy Central Extra, Nick Jr., Nickelodeon, Nicktoons, MTV Polska, Paramount Network oraz TeenNick .

Większość wyłączonych kanałów należy do portfolio Paramount Skydance. Operator wcześniej tłumaczył klientom, że powodem wycofania stacji jest nieodnowienie na kolejny okres umowy z dostawcą dotyczącej ich udostępniania.

Jednocześnie od 1 września Orange rozszerzył pakiet Extra TV o 10 nowych stacji. Są to Newsmax Polska, MyZen TV 4K, Ultra TV 4K, Pogoda24.TV, Fix&Foxi, RiC.today, English Club TV, TinyTeen, LangLab i LingoToons.

Newsmax Polska jest całodobowym kanałem informacyjnym oferującym wiadomości, publicystykę oraz rozmowy dotyczące wydarzeń w Polsce i na świecie. Pogoda24.TV łączy prognozy pogody z programami dotyczącymi m.in. przyrody, ekologii i ekstremalnych zjawisk atmosferycznych.

DLA CIEBIE Jak retail media podbijają reklamę [wywiad]

Oferta Orange została też poszerzona o dwie stacje nadające w jakości 4K. MyZen TV 4K jest kanałem lifestylowym poświęconym m.in. zdrowiu, relaksowi, podróżom i dobremu samopoczuciu. Ultra TV 4K oferuje przede wszystkim treści muzyczne i dokumentalne.

Nowe kanały dla dzieci i do nauki angielskiego

Wśród nowości są również Fix&Foxi i RiC.today. Jak informowaliśmy w Wirtualnemedia.pl, oba kanały 1 września weszły na polski rynek, a Orange Polska został pierwszym operatorem, który wprowadził je do swojej oferty.

*Zrezygnuj w każdej chwili, nie wysyłamy spamu.

Fix&Foxi jest kierowany do dzieci w wieku od 4 do 12 lat. Polska wersja kanału jest zlokalizowana i oferuje m.in. animacje oraz programy edukacyjno-rozrywkowe. RiC.today nadaje natomiast programy edukacyjne w języku angielskim, mające pomagać dzieciom w nauce języka poprzez historie, muzykę i materiały poświęcone m.in. nauce, sztuce oraz przyrodzie.

Do oferty trafiły też kanały English Club TV, LangLab, TinyTeen i LingoToons , związane z nauką języka angielskiego i treściami edukacyjnymi dla różnych grup wiekowych.

Jak informuje satkurier.pl, nowe stacje zajęły w Orange TV następujące pozycje: Newsmax Polska – 46, MyZen TV 4K – 343, Ultra TV 4K – 364, Pogoda24.TV – 471, Fix&Foxi – 563, RiC.today – 577, English Club TV – 578, TinyTeen – 579, LangLab – 580 a LingoToons – 587.

30 lipca Wirtualnemedia.pl informowały , że Orange rozsyła abonentom wiadomości dotyczące wyłączenia siedmiu kanałów: 13 Ulica, Comedy Central, Paramount Network Polska, Nick Jr., Nickelodeon, Nicktoons i MTV Polska. Autentyczność wiadomości potwierdził wówczas Wirtualnemedia.pl Wojciech Jabczyński, rzecznik Orange Polska. Operator zapowiadał jednocześnie dodanie ośmiu nowych stacji.

Ostatecznie zakres zmian okazał się większy. Z oferty zniknęły dodatkowo BBC News, Polsat Comedy Central Extra i TeenNick, natomiast lista nowych kanałów zwiększyła się z ośmiu do dziesięciu dzięki dołączeniu TinyTeen i LingoToons.

Klienci, którzy nie akceptowali usunięcia kanałów oznaczonych w ich umowach jako gwarantowane, mogli do końca sierpnia wypowiedzieć bez dodatkowych konsekwencji umowę o świadczenie pakietu usług, którego częścią jest telewizja.

Ponad 2 miliony użytkowników miesięcznie

Ośrodek Studiów Wschodnich twierdzi, że w pracy doktorskiej Jakuba Wiecha znalazły się obszerne fragmenty analiz jego ekspertów wykorzystane bez podania źródła. Według OSW chodzi łącznie o 2,5 proc. rozprawy. Ośrodek poinformował Uniwersytet Warszawski. Wiech przyznaje, że w pracy zabrakło cytowania tych materiałów, ale zapewnia, że był to błąd, a nie celowe działanie.

evidence.title: Orange Polska zaskoczył siłą IT i smartfonów. Ważniejsze ma być coś innego
evidence.text:
Orange Polska zaskoczył siłą IT i smartfonów. Ważniejsze ma być coś innego

Aktualizacja: 25.09.2026 20:31 Publikacja: 23.10.2025 08:55

Orange Polska pokazał wyniki finansowe i operacyjne uzyskane w trzecim kwartale 2025 r. Na pozór odżyły kontrakty w segmencie informatycznym. Przychody grupy z tego tytułu skoczyły o 47 proc. Jednak zdaniem analityka to może być jednorazowy efekt. Specjaliści uważają, że większą uwagę inwestorzy powinni zwrócić na segment usług hurtowych, który zdaniem szefowej spółki ma przynosić większe zyski w kolejnych okresach.

Wyniki Orange Polska w trzecim kwartale 2025 r.: zysk netto pod presją kosztów finansowania

3,33 mld zł przychodu, o 7,2 proc. więcej niż raportowano przed rokiem, 899 mln zł zysk EBITDAal (wzrost o 3,7 proc.), 371 mln zł zysku operacyjnego (bez zmian) oraz 228 mln zł zysku netto (spadek o 10 proc., co firma tłumaczy wyższymi kosztami finansowania w związku z opłatą za rezerwacje częstotliwości). Tak wyglądają podstawowe dane finansowe Grupy Orange Polska za trzy miesiące zakończone 30 września. Od średniej prognoz analityków różnią się, ale nieznacznie oraz w obie strony: i na plus, i na minus. Największe odchylenie w dół (prawie 7 proc.) występuje w wypadku wyniku netto. Natomiast poziom przychodów specjalistów zaskoczył na plus (spodziewali się 4,9-proc. zwyżki).

Ogółem jednak biura maklerskie, a co za tym idzie inwestorzy nie powinni być bardzo zaskoczeni – wynika z porównania rezultatów i średniej prognoz zebranych przez PAP. O tym, że druga połowa br. ma być lepsza dla sektora pisaliśmy tutaj.

Większość stanowisk, które Urząd Komunikacji Elektronicznej otrzymał w odpowiedzi na propozycję zdjęcia regulacyjnych kajdan z giełdowego telekomu...

Jesteśmy bardzo zadowoleni z wyników za trzeci kwartał – skomentowała Liudmila Climoc, prezeska Orange Polska w informacji prasowej. – Światłowód i pakiety konwergentne w dobrym tempie zyskują nowych użytkowników, pomimo dużej konkurencji, a wyjątkowo udany kwartał z najwyższym od kilku lat przyrostem liczby klientów mieliśmy w usługach mobilnych. Przyczyniła się do tego także wprowadzona niedawno nowa oferta rodzinna – dodała. Wskazała także, że po raz pierwszy od kilku lat baza abonentów usług mobilnych wzrosła w skali kwartału o 100 tys.

Zdaniem szefowej Orange Polska na wyniki pozytywnie przekłada się działalność hurtowa. A w nadchodzących latach nowe projekty biznesowe w tym obszarze mają przynieść znaczące zyski. O co konkretnie chodzi – nie podano. To o tyle ciekawe, że z końcem roku telekomowi kończy się umowa z P4, na podstawie której użytkownicy Play mogą korzystać z masztów Orange Polska. Do tej pory nie zdradzono, czy współpraca będzie kontynuowana i na jakich zasadach.

Nie ma żadnych wątpliwości, że przyszłość jest cyfrowa, oparta na światłowodach i 5G – mówi Liudmila Climoc, prezeska Orange Polska.

Na nadzieje związane z hurtem zwraca uwagę w porannym komentarzu Paweł Puchalski, analityk Santander Biuro Maklerskie. – Zarząd Orange Polska rzadko przesadza. Czyżbyśmy mieli do czynienia z nowym bodźcem wzrostu przychodów i EBITDA? – pisze analityk, który co do zasady ocenia wyniki telekomu pozytywnie.

Z kolei wzrost przychodów w segmencie ICT jego zdaniem może wynikać z jednorazowego dużego kontraktu.

Climoc oceniła też, że za sprawą wyników trzech kwartałów br. zarząd ma silne przekonanie, że osiągnie cele założone na cały 2025 r. Cele te to wzrost przychodów i wyniku EBITDAal w niskim jednocyfrowym tempie.

Analityczka Erste: notowania mogą pójść w górę

Nora Varga-Nagy, analityczka Erste Securities spodziewa się pozytywnej reakcji rynku na wyniki Orange Polska na czwartkowej sesji. – Baza klientów telefonów komórkowych w ramach abonamentu odnotowała solidny przyrost netto, przekraczający 100 tys. w ciągu kwartału. Co zaskakujące, przychody ze sprzedaży sprzętu wzrosły rok do roku (o 3,6 proc. – red.), podczas gdy przewidywaliśmy spadek, a wzrost przychodów z IT był znacznie silniejszy niż oczekiwany. Pomimo dodatniego jednorazowego zdarzenia w bazie, EBITDAaL wyraźnie wzrósł rok do roku i przekroczył oczekiwania. Wzrost był dobrej jakości, ponieważ nie wystąpił jednorazowy wkład ze strony FiberCo (Światłowód Inwestycje – red.). Z drugiej strony, raport finansowy sugeruje, że rynek B2B nadal stanowił wyzwanie i spodziewamy się dowiedzieć więcej na ten temat podczas telekonferencji. Ogólnie rzecz biorąc, zakładam pozytywną reakcję rynku – skomentowała Nora Varga-Nagy.

Na koniec września Orange Polska obsługiwał 19,39 mln kart SIM. To wzrost o ponad 1 mln lub 5,6 proc. rok do roku. Tak duży przyrost świadczonych usług mobilnych notuje kolejny raz za sprawą usług M2M (machine to machine, czyli transmisja danych między urządzeniami takimi jak np. mierniki energii, rowery miejskie etc.).

Wzrosty kart SIM wykorzystywanych przez abonentów i użytkowników telefonii na kartę także mają miejsce, ale w skali roku chodzi odpowiednio o 336 tys. (do 9,46 mln) i 11 tys. (do 4,38 mln).

Z usług szerokopasmowego dostępu do internetu Orange Polska po trzech kwartałach br. korzystało 2,93 mln abonentów (wzrost o 2,5 proc. rok do roku).

Coraz większa część gospodarstw domowych ma usługę światłowodową: 1,69 mln, o 12,5 proc. więcej niż przed rokiem.

Liczba abonentów pakietów usług (konwergentnych) powiększyła się w ciągu 12 miesięcy o 85 tys. (4,8 proc.) do 1,84 mln.

W danych operatora widać też kolejny kwartał z rzędu wzrost abonentów płatnej telewizji. Trzeba jednak zauważyć, że od tego roku usługa ta jest stałym elementem pakietów.

W wynikach Orange Polska widać nadal podwyżki cen. W III kw. br. wskaźnik ARPO (średnia opłata za daną ofertę w miesiącu bez VAT) za pakiet usług wyniósł 130 zł, o 3,6 proc. więcej niż przed rokiem. Stacjonarny internet kosztował średnio 69,6 zł, więcej niż rok temu o 4,1 proc.

W tym roku kurs akcji Orange Polska wzrósł o ponad 33 proc. do 9,26 zł na środowym zamknięciu sesji.

evidence.title: O2 Czech Republic deploys Nokia 5G Standalone Core
evidence.text:
O2 Czech Republic deploys Nokia 5G Standalone Core

Czech Republic telecoms provider O2 has deployed Nokia 5G Standalone (SA) Core software to enable the country’s largest operator to offer a range of advanced 5G services, such as network slicing.

O2 is the first operator in the Czech Republic to deploy 5G SA, which the telco claims will strengthen its network with greater reliability, security, energy efficiency for better mobile battery life, and near zero-touch automation for managing workloads.

Nokia says deploying 5G Standalone Core will not only drive greater services and reliability for O2 Czech Republic subscribers, but also provide new revenue streams for the operator

“Deploying Nokia 5G SA Core closely aligns with and bolsters O2 Czech Republic’s cloud-first strategy and delivers more secure communications to our customers," said Jakub Votava, Network Director, O2 Czech Republic.

"This rollout allows us to deliver new 5G services faster, with even lower latency, and without vendor lock-in for our data and analytics, producing an optimised network with a host of operational efficiencies.”

Nokia says its cloud-native 5G Core portfolio, including its Packet Core solution, allows O2 Czech Republic to provide new network services in multi-cloud environments, while doing so quickly, securely, and at scale.

“Reflecting Nokia’s commitment to driving innovation and supporting the digital transformation of its customers and partners, this deployment enables O2 Czech Republic’s Core Network infrastructure and applications to be fully cloud-native, and provides a more advanced, secure, and reliable network experience for its subscribers," said Erez Sverdlov, Vice President, Cloud and Network Services Market Leader, Europe, Nokia.

At the end of Q1 2025, Nokia claims to have led the world in 5G SA Core deployments with 52 operators in live 5G Standalone service and the most 5G Standalone Core CSP customers, with 125 in total.
