evidence.title: Ericsson Unveils Four AI and Connectivity Scenarios for Japan in 2035 as Mobile Networks Evolve from 5G Standalone Toward 6G
evidence.text:
Ericsson Unveils Four AI and Connectivity Scenarios for Japan in 2035 as Mobile Networks Evolve from 5G Standalone Toward 6G

Ericsson Unveils Four AI and Connectivity Scenarios for Japan in 2035 as Mobile Networks Evolve from 5G Standalone Toward 6G

(IN BRIEF) Ericsson Japan has introduced four scenarios examining how AI, Physical AI and next-generation connectivity could influence Japanese society around 2035. Developed under the company’s “Enter New Horizons” initiative with participation from University of Tokyo students and experts, companies and local governments, the scenarios cover manufacturing, infrastructure and energy, mobility, and regional sustainability. Ericsson says they are intended as discussion frameworks rather than predictions. The initiative explores how mobile networks could evolve from 5G Standalone toward 6G and become an “intelligent fabric” connecting AI, cloud, computing resources, robots, autonomous vehicles, drones and industrial equipment. The work also considers Japan’s demographic and workforce challenges, including a government projection cited by Ericsson of approximately 10 million fewer employed people by 2040 than in 2022 if economic growth and labour participation fail to improve. The scenarios will be showcased at Ericsson Forum 2026 from 28–30 September and form part of Ericsson’s 150th anniversary activities and its 41st year of operations in Japan.

(PRESS RELEASE) STOCKHOLM, 25-Sep-2026 — / EuropaWire / — Ericsson Japan K.K. has unveiled four future-life scenarios exploring how artificial intelligence, Physical AI and next-generation mobile connectivity could shape Japanese society and industry around 2035 .

Developed through Ericsson’s “Enter New Horizons” initiative, the scenarios examine possible applications across manufacturing, infrastructure and energy, mobility, and regional sustainability as mobile networks evolve from 5G Standalone (5G SA) toward 6G.

The initiative was launched in Japan to mark Ericsson’s 150th anniversary and is intended to stimulate discussion about how connectivity could support society as AI increasingly moves from digital environments into physical systems.

The four scenarios are being presented at Ericsson Forum 2026, taking place from 28 to 30 September 2026, and are also being made available through Ericsson’s digital channels.

Ericsson stressed that the scenarios are not predictions. Instead, they are intended as a framework for discussion about possible futures and the role that communications infrastructure, AI and automation could play in addressing some of Japan’s long-term social and economic challenges.

The scenarios originated in a workshop involving Ericsson Japan employees and students from the University of Tokyo.

They were subsequently developed through further input from University of Tokyo experts and dialogue with companies, local governments and other stakeholders.

A central theme of the project is the expanding role of mobile networks as Japan confronts demographic changes and workforce pressures across areas including manufacturing, logistics, mobility, infrastructure maintenance and regional services.

Ericsson cited the Japanese Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare’s Analysis of the Labour Economy 2025, which projects that if economic growth and labour-force participation do not improve, the number of employed people in Japan could decline by approximately 10 million by 2040 compared with 2022.

Against this backdrop, Ericsson sees AI, Physical AI and the connectivity needed to operate increasingly autonomous systems as potentially important components of future infrastructure.

Physical AI refers to AI systems operating through physical machines such as robots, autonomous vehicles, drones and industrial equipment.

As these technologies become more widely deployed, Ericsson argues that dependable, high-performing connectivity will become increasingly important for coordinating machines safely and at scale.

The company expects the role of mobile networks to expand beyond connecting people and devices.

As networks move from 5G SA toward 6G and integrate more closely with AI, cloud and computing resources, Ericsson envisions them becoming an “intelligent fabric” underpinning digital society and supporting both AI and Physical AI applications.

The first of Ericsson’s four scenarios focuses on manufacturing.

It explores a future in which what the company describes as “ultra-rich” data — potentially including the skills and intuition of experienced Japanese craftspeople alongside real-time information about consumer demand — can move across global value chains.

The concept considers how this type of data exchange could contribute to advanced manufacturing, transfer specialist expertise and support the creation of new products and services.

The second scenario addresses infrastructure and energy.

It examines how drones and sensing technologies could help inspect and protect social infrastructure, while aerial network connectivity could contribute to maintaining essential services during natural disasters and other disruptions.

The third scenario focuses on mobility, exploring how connectivity and AI could coordinate the movement of people and goods more effectively across communities.

Ericsson said such systems could potentially improve safety and convenience while helping people access destinations, products and services despite changing workforce and demographic conditions.

The fourth scenario examines regional sustainability.

It considers how people and AI could work together to maintain quality of life and productive employment as Japan’s population structure changes, while also helping regional industries, knowledge and cultural traditions continue into future generations.

Ericsson has also produced a video series featuring discussions between company executives and employees and representatives of businesses and local governments associated with each of the four themes.

The “Enter New Horizons” initiative coincides with 150 years since Ericsson was founded in 1876.

Ericsson also marks 41 years in Japan in 2026, following the establishment of its representative office in the country in 1985.

Chafic Nassif, President of Ericsson Northeast Asia , said AI is increasingly moving beyond digital environments as robots and autonomous systems begin to enter physical operations and society.

He compared AI with the brain, robots with limbs and mobile networks with a nervous system connecting the two, arguing that communications infrastructure will be necessary for Physical AI to function safely and at scale.

Nassif said Ericsson intends to continue working with Japanese customers and partners to develop the connectivity required for the AI era and address emerging opportunities and challenges.

Japanese telecommunications companies also provided messages marking Ericsson’s anniversary and highlighting continued cooperation.

Yoshiaki Maeda, President and CEO of NTT DOCOMO, Inc. , said Ericsson’s work in high-performance and reliable connectivity aligns with DOCOMO’s objective of using communications technology to create wider societal value.

He expressed an interest in continuing cooperation and co-creation as communications technologies evolve.

Kazuyuki Yoshimura, Senior Managing Executive Officer and CTO of KDDI Corporation , highlighted the companies’ previous work on resilient communications infrastructure and said KDDI looks forward to further collaboration as communications and AI increasingly converge.

He said this combination could support infrastructure, daily life and industrial activity while contributing to sustainable development.

Junichi Miyakawa, President and CEO of SoftBank Corp. , said SoftBank is accelerating the societal deployment of AI under its “Activate AI for Society” growth strategy and expects telecommunications infrastructure and AI to play a combined role in Japan’s future development.

Ericsson Japan said the four scenarios will serve as a starting point for continued dialogue with customers, telecommunications partners, universities, companies, local governments and other organisations.

Through that engagement, Ericsson aims to explore how connectivity infrastructure can support AI-era applications while contributing to the long-term development of Japanese society and industry.

evidence.title: Ericsson CTO: collaboration is essential to meet the promise of the intelligent fabric
evidence.text:
Ericsson CTO: collaboration is essential to meet the promise of the intelligent fabric

Ericsson Chief Technology Officer, Erik Ekudden, is as excited as anyone by the potential of AI and other emerging technologies to transform home, work and social lives for the better. But he says it will not happen without connectivity.

His 2026 Technology and Telecoms Trends report, published today, addresses the path to the intelligent fabric: programmable, intelligent and autonomous mobile networks that will meet the security, performance and efficiency needs of AI at scale.

Pointing to rapid change, Ekudden’s vision of the next decade sees a fundamental shift in the role of mobile networks: from transporting data to sensing and acting at the speed of intelligence to support automation, human decision making and enterprise systems.

Ekudden says four interrelated developing trends are shaping the intelligent fabric.

Ekudden says: “The intelligent fabric is to the AI economy what best-effort mobile broadband service was to the internet economy in the past: the connective layer that makes everything else possible, and the differentiator that determines who leads and who follows.”

Ekudden says collaboration across an ecosystem of committed partners is required to turn the vision to reality.

“Ericsson will not build this alone, and we have never intended to,” he says. “The intelligent fabric will be shaped through deep collaboration across communication service providers (CSPs), enterprises, developers, governments and academia, all aligned on a common architecture and a shared direction.”

Ekudden says decisions made within the next three years will determine how the transformation will progress who will define it.

“Ericsson is committed to leading that effort,” he says. “We invite all ecosystem players to help shape it with us.”

evidence.title: Ericsson Federal Appoints Patrick Gorman as CTO
evidence.text:
Ericsson Federal has appointed Patrick Gorman , a veteran cybersecurity and intelligence executive, as chief technology officer .

What Will Gorman Do at Ericsson Federal?

In his new role, Ericsson Federal said Gorman will guide the company’s technology strategy and support the delivery of secure communications offerings to U.S. government customers. He will also direct efforts to align Ericsson Federal’s technical capabilities with commercial advancements to meet government objectives and contract requirements.

Christopher Ling , CEO of Ericsson Federal, said Gorman brings experience in intelligence, cybersecurity and national defense to the company.

“As we bring advanced commercial communications capabilities to federal agencies, his leadership and firsthand understanding of our nation’s most critical missions will be invaluable,” Ling added.

Gorman is a technology and national security executive with more than 40 years of experience in the public and private sectors. Before joining Ericsson Federal, he was an executive vice president at Booz Allen Hamilton , where he oversaw the firm’s 5G and cyber business and ran its Dark Labs cyber incubator and Bright Labs digital incubator.

His earlier private-sector positions include head of strategy and product at CyberGRX, chief security officer at Bridgewater Associates, and global chief information security officer at Bank of America/Merrill Lynch.

In government, Gorman was assistant director of national intelligence and chief information officer for the U.S. intelligence community. He also helped stand up the Transportation Security Administration after the Sept. 11 attacks and contributed to Pentagon doctrine on network-centric warfare and cyberwarfare. Gorman spent more than 10 years in the U.S. Air Force, working in electronic warfare, signals intelligence and psychological operations.

He holds degrees from the University of Maryland and George Washington University, completed an executive program at Harvard Business School, and graduated from the Defense Language Institute. Gorman also sits on the boards of several organizations focused on artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and privacy.

Established in 2024 , Ericsson Federal is a Vienna, Virginia-based company that adapts Ericsson’s commercial 5G and 6G network technologies, including AI and machine learning capabilities, for U.S. national security, homeland security and defense customers.

Since its launch, Ericsson Federal has built out its leadership team, appointing former Federal Communications Commission Commissioner Nathan Simington as director of policy and strategy and naming Melissa Milstead chief legal officer . The company has also secured a prime position on the Missile Defense Agency’s $151 billion SHIELD contract supporting the Golden Dome for America initiative, and supported Ericsson’s live demonstration of integrated sensing and communication technology in Plano, Texas.

In a recent GovCon Conversation video interview , Ericsson Federal CEO Christopher Ling said the company is working with Nokia and other partners to establish a commercial consortium that would deliver turnkey, integrated technology capabilities to government customers.

evidence.title: Ericsson and Beyon mark sustainability milestones with extended collaboration
evidence.text:
Ericsson and Beyon mark sustainability milestones with extended collaboration

Beyon and Ericsson (ERIC) extend sustainability Memorandum of Understanding to build on achievements and accelerate further environmental progress

The collaboration has delivered measurable gains in energy efficiency and circularity, including recycling 54 metric tons of e-waste through Ericsson’s E-Waste program.

Building on the progress achieved over the past two years, Ericsson (NASDAQ: ERIC) and Beyon have extended their sustainability Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), reinforcing their commitment to further advance energy efficiency, carbon emission reduction and circular economy practices.

Under the extended MoU, the companies will explore further opportunities to improve network energy efficiency and reduce carbon emissions through innovative technologies and solutions, including zero-footprint site. The collaboration will also continue Ericsson’s E-Waste Programme, expand sustainability knowledge sharing through workshops and expert-led sessions, and identify new opportunities for social impact collaboration.

Since the start of the collaboration, Beyon and Ericsson have worked together to advance more sustainable network operations through a combination of technology innovation, circularity initiatives and knowledge sharing.

Early in the collaboration, Batelco by Beyon’s network achieved measurable improvements in energy efficiency, including up to a 30 per cent reduction in energy consumption through Ericsson's 5G Radio Access Network product, Radio 6646, up to 22 per cent additional savings enabled by AI-driven software features, and a further 18 per cent reduction through the deployment of the single-antenna footprint Interleaved AIR 3218.

Building on these achievements, the collaboration has continued to focus on accelerating sustainability through the responsible recycling of 54 metric tons of end-of-life electrical and electronic equipment under Ericsson's E-Waste Program.

Alongside these environmental achievements, Beyon team members have participated in ongoing sustainability knowledge-sharing sessions led by Ericsson’s global experts, strengthening internal capabilities and awareness of international sustainability practices.

Shaikh Bader bin Rashid Al Khalifa, Beyon Chief Communications & Sustainability Officer , says: “The results achieved with Ericsson over the past two years demonstrate the tangible progress we are making in embedding sustainability across our operations. Delivering measurable energy efficiencies across our network, while responsibly recycling 54 metric tons of end-of-life electronic and electrical equipment, are important milestones that reflect our focus on turning sustainability ambitions into meaningful action. Building on this progress, we will continue to explore innovative solutions that improve energy efficiency, advance circularity and further reduce our environmental footprint. Our extended collaboration with Ericsson supports Beyon’s sustainability ambitions while contributing to Bahrain’s Economic Vision 2030 and the Kingdom’s commitment to achieving Net-Zero emissions by 2060.”

Petra Schirren, President of Ericsson Gulf , says: “The measurable achievements delivered through our collaboration with Beyon demonstrate how technology can play an important role in improving network energy performance and advancing circularity. From energy-efficient radio solutions and AI-enabled software to the responsible recycling of electronic equipment, we are proud of the progress achieved together. Extending our collaboration provides an opportunity to build on these milestones, explore further innovations and continue supporting Beyon in advancing its sustainability ambitions, while contributing to Bahrain’s Economic Vision 2030 for sustainable development.”

Ericsson has a longstanding relationship with Beyon through its telecom arm, Batelco by Beyon. The extension of the sustainability MoU builds on the measurable progress achieved to date and reflects both companies shared commitment to enhancing network efficiency, advancing circularity and improving environmental performance in Bahrain.

evidence.title: Ericsson, Vodafone demo AI-enabled instant call translation
evidence.text:
Ericsson, Vodafone demo AI-enabled instant call translation

The pair also showcased AI-based noise cancellation

Vodafone and Ericsson have partnered to carry out trials of network-native AI for voice services.

The two companies announced this week that they have combined in lab conditions to successfully demonstrate two AI-powered voice services, with these services being real-time noise cancellation and language translation.

According to the duo, the demos showcase the ability to utilize AI technologies to "transform the experience of a standard mobile phone call."

The trial aimed to showcase real-time noise cancellation for clearer audio and in-call language translation to break down communication barriers, all without requiring specialized apps or new phone hardware, stated Vodafone.

The call integrated a Vodafone-developed application server and AI engines with Ericsson’s IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS), using APIs to seamlessly bridge telecom and AI domains.

Ericsson notes that such architecture allows the network to apply AI-driven intelligence to voice calls as they are processed.

Through this, two key applications were showcased, the first being the ability to utilize AI-based noise cancellation, a service that "intelligently identifies and removes background noise in real time," for greater clarity.

The second use case focuses on language translation, which again heavily leverages AI in real time to translate a conversation between two different languages live during the call.

“AI is giving the mobile network back its voice. More than 50 years after the first mobile call, innovation is accelerating and shifting back into the network," said Marco Zangani, director of network strategy and architecture, Vodafone. "Over the past few years, we have built the infrastructure, data capabilities and safeguards needed to unlock AI for our customers to converse more clearly.”

Nadine Allen, head of UK and responsible for Vodafone Group at Ericsson, added: "This is a crucial step toward creating more intelligent, programmable networks that unlock new value for customers."

evidence.title: Vodafone, Ericsson trial AI-powered voice services
evidence.text:
Vodafone, Ericsson trial AI-powered voice services

Vodafone and Ericsson have successfully tested two AI-powered services that could improve the way businesses and consumers use mobile voice calls.

The trial, which focused on real-time noise cancellation and live language translation, is part of the telecom giants’ joint “Core Network of the Future” programme, which is exploring how AI can be built directly into telecom networks.

As a result, both services are delivered through the mobile network, meaning users do not need a separate app or new handset.

Meanwhile, the technology combines Vodafone’s application server and AI engines with Ericsson’s IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS).

One of the services tested uses AI to identify and remove background noise during calls, which could be useful for customers working or travelling in noisy environments, help improve call quality without requiring specialist hardware.

The second service provides live translation between two different languages during a phone call. For businesses, this offers support for customers, suppliers and colleagues who speak different languages.

Vodafone , Director of Network Strategy and Architecture, Marco Zangani, said: “AI is giving the mobile network back its voice. More than 50 years after the first mobile call, innovation is accelerating and shifting back into the network. Over the past few years, we have built the infrastructure, data capabilities and safeguards needed to unlock AI for our customers to converse more clearly.”

Ericsson Head of UK and responsible for Vodafone Group at Ericsson, Nadine Allen, added: “This successful trial with Vodafone is a critical demonstration of how network-native AI can redefine the mobile experience.

“By integrating Vodafone’s powerful AI capabilities with Ericsson’s core network and media processing technologies, we are proving that sophisticated services like real-time translation and noise cancellation can be delivered seamlessly. This is a crucial step toward creating more intelligent, programmable networks that unlock new value for customers.”

evidence.title: Nokia, NVIDIA Expand AI-RAN Trials with Global Operators
evidence.text:
Nokia and NVIDIA are expanding AI-RAN trials with mobile operators across North America, Europe, the Asia Pacific, and the Middle East, as service providers evaluate the use of artificial intelligence and accelerated computing in radio access networks.

The latest engagements involve A1 Group, Chunghwa Telecom, du, e&, Mobily, stc, TPG Telecom, and Zain Saudi. Nokia also said previously announced trials with NTT DOCOMO continue to progress. Nokia has previously announced AI-RAN evaluations with T-Mobile, SoftBank, and Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison, as well as collaborations with a growing number of technology and OEM partners.

Nokia is combining its AI-native anyRAN software with the NVIDIA Aerial RAN Computer as part of its AI-RAN platform. The companies are developing the technology to support RAN functions and AI workloads on accelerated computing infrastructure.

Nokia said its AI-RAN platform has delivered more than 20% improvements in spectral efficiency through AI-powered radio innovations. The company is continuing development through a software innovation roadmap extending into 2027 and 2028.

The operator said the improvements could allow operators to increase network capacity and make greater use of existing spectrum and infrastructure. The company is also positioning AI-RAN as a software-based evolution path for 5G and a foundation for future AI-native 6G networks.

According to Nokia, the growing use of AI applications is creating new traffic patterns, increased uplink requirements, and greater demand for distributed computing. The company said these developments are prompting operators to examine how AI can be incorporated into network infrastructure.

The latest engagements span several regions, with Nokia and NVIDIA working with operators to advance AI-RAN trials and develop the wider technology ecosystem.

Emma Falck, President of Mobile Infrastructure at Nokia, said:

AI is reshaping the future of telecommunications and creating a significant opportunity for operators to rethink the role of the radio network. Together with NVIDIA and our growing ecosystem of partners, we are helping operators transform their networks into intelligent, programmable platforms that can support both connectivity and AI services. The increasing engagement we are seeing from service providers around the world shows that AI-RAN is moving quickly from vision to commercial reality and becoming a foundational technology for the AI-native 6G era.

Ronnie Vasishta, Senior Vice President of Telecom at NVIDIA, said:

AI-RAN will transform the mobile network into one of the world’s largest distributed AI infrastructures. With NVIDIA Aerial RAN Computer and Nokia’s AI-RAN software, operators can build software-defined networks that continuously improve in performance and efficiency, while supporting entirely new AI services at the edge. Global operator momentum demonstrates that AI-RAN is becoming the foundation for 5G-Advanced today, and then software upgradable to AI-native 6G tomorrow.

evidence.title: Nokia Advances AI-RAN Adoption with Global Operator Trials on NVIDIA Platforms
evidence.text:
Nokia Advances AI-RAN Adoption with Global Operator Trials on NVIDIA Platforms

Nokia announced growing global momentum for AI-RAN, with operators across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East advancing AI-RAN from early evaluation to lab and live field trials, accelerating the evolution toward AI-native 6G networks.

Expanding engagement with A1 Group, Chunghwa Telecom, du, e&, Mobily, stc, TPG Telecom, and Zain Saudi demonstrates how AI-RAN is rapidly moving from industry vision to commercial reality. In addition, trials with operators previously announced, including NTT DOCOMO, INC., continue to progress steadily.

The announcement builds on Nokia’s recent AI-RAN milestones, including the launch of the industry’s first commercial AI-native RAN platform; evaluations with T-Mobile, SoftBank and Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison; a growing number of OEM partners; and expanded collaboration with NVIDIA on AI-RAN platform and software development tools. Together, these developments are transforming radio networks into programmable platforms supporting both connectivity and AI workloads; they are also accelerating the development of an open AI-RAN ecosystem and demonstrating the readiness of AI-RAN technologies for commercial deployment.

Nokia’s AI-RAN platform has already delivered more than 20% improvements in spectral efficiency through AI-powered radio innovations and is advancing toward further spectral efficiency gains through a continuous software innovation roadmap extending through 2027 and 2028. This enables operators to increase capacity, improve network economics and create new service opportunities by extracting greater value from existing spectrum and infrastructure investments, reducing reliance on traditional hardware refresh cycles.

As AI applications drive new traffic patterns, increased uplink demand and growing requirements for distributed computing, operators are seeking new ways to improve network capacity, spectral efficiency and monetization opportunities. Nokia’s AI-RAN platform combines its AI-native anyRAN software with NVIDIA Aerial RAN Computer to help operators unlock greater performance from existing spectrum assets, enabling software-defined architecture for 5G with a software upgrade path to 6G and laying the foundation for future AI-native networks.

AI is reshaping the future of telecommunications and creating a significant opportunity for operators to rethink the role of the radio network. Together with NVIDIA and our growing ecosystem of partners, we are helping operators transform their networks into intelligent, programmable platforms that can support both connectivity and AI services. The increasing engagement we are seeing from service providers around the world shows that AI-RAN is moving quickly from vision to commercial reality and becoming a foundational technology for the AI-native 6G era.

The breadth of operator engagement announced by Nokia shows that AI-RAN is evolving from a research topic into a strategic priority for a growing number of service providers. evidence.title: Nokia ramps up AI-RAN momentum
evidence.text:
As the vendor strikes further carrier partnerships

Nokia last week announced that it has worked with more mobile carriers to engage in proofs of concept and/or trials to advance its work with AI-RAN.

The vendor, which is currently banging the drum around AI-RAN (radio access networks) pretty loudly along with its investor Nvidia, confirmed that more mobile carriers are testing its AI-RAN offering.

Indeed, A1 Group, Chunghwa Telecom, du, e&, Mobily, stc, TPG Telecom, and Zain Saudi are the latest mobile carriers to pair with Nokia to test its AI-RAN.

Nokia also highlighted that existing partnerships are continuing to build, noting that trials with operators previously announced, such NTT Docomo "continue to progress steadily."

The vendor has notably previously named other carriers including the likes of BT, Elisa, and Vodafone Group, as those who has also engaged Nokia over AI-RAN technology, plus France's Orange Group .

The company said its operator engagement over AI-RAN now spans North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, and the Middle East.

Further partnerships have been developed with the likes of T-Mobile in the US, Indonesia's Indosat, and Japan's SoftBank Corp. All three of these telcos featured heavily in Nokia's MWC announcement in March, when the vendor mapped out its ambitions to work with Nvidia to develop AI-RAN ahead of the 6G era.

While Nokia's first commercial AI-RAN products aren't expected to go live until next year, the company spoke up about the importance of pairing with carriers to trial the technology.

According to Nokia, its AI-RAN platform has been able to deliver more than 20 percent improvements in spectral efficiency through AI-powered radio innovations, with further gains expected through to 2028.

This is important, notes Nokia, as it will enable telcos to "increase capacity, improve network economics and create new service opportunities by extracting greater value from existing spectrum and infrastructure investments, reducing reliance on traditional hardware refresh cycles."

"AI is reshaping the future of telecommunications and creating a significant opportunity for operators to rethink the role of the radio network. "The increasing engagement we are seeing from service providers around the world shows that AI-RAN is moving quickly from vision to commercial reality and becoming a foundational technology for the AI-native 6G era."

Nokia and GPU giant Nvidia first penned an agreement to develop AI-ready RAN solutions back in 2024 , long before Nvidia became an investor in the vendor.

"AI-RAN will transform the mobile network into one of the world’s largest distributed AI infrastructures. Global operator momentum demonstrates that AI-RAN is becoming the foundation for 5G Advanced today and then software upgradable to AI-native 6G tomorrow," added Ronnie Vasishta, senior vice president of telecom, Nvidia.

evidence.title: Nokia and Microsoft Link Data Suite to Fabric for AI-Driven Network Operations
evidence.text:
Nokia and Microsoft have expanded their partnership by integrating Nokia Data Suite with Microsoft Fabric, creating a shared data foundation intended to speed up telecom analytics and AI-led network automation. Nokia says network data that can take weeks to prepare could become usable within minutes through the combined platform.

The integration targets a central challenge for operators: network information is typically scattered across radio and core networks, IT systems, subscriber databases, cloud services and equipment from multiple vendors. Nokia Data Suite supplies telecom-ready data products, network-specific semantic models and quality controls, while Fabric contributes OneLake, analytics, governance and connections to Microsoft AI services .

Nokia says its reusable data products can reduce MLOps work by up to 70% by removing repetitive data-preparation tasks. Microsoft had previously said its Fabric integration could cut development time for telecom AI use cases by as much as 80%. Those are company-stated targets rather than independently verified deployment results.

The companies have identified early workloads where agents can work across network, service and subscriber data rather than a single operational dashboard.

Nokia also points to automated root-cause analysis and eventual closed-loop operations, in which automation can act after a fault is identified. The platform is designed for hybrid and on-premises deployments as well as cloud environments, a key consideration for operators that cannot move all network data into a public cloud.

The agreement fits Nokia's wider push into AI-RAN and 6G. The company has committed $1 billion and formed a partnership with NVIDIA around that effort, while saying operators in several regions are testing AI-RAN on NVIDIA platforms. Nokia has claimed more than 20% improvements in spectral efficiency in its testing.

Nokia shares rose 6.3% in European trading after the Microsoft announcement, reaching €9.39 during the September 17 session, according to the WSJ . The joint product is already available, and the companies say they plan to add further automation scenarios and operator deployments; the key test will be how extensively operators allow AI agents to move from analysis into day-to-day network actions.

evidence.title: Nokia and Microsoft build a data foundation for AI-run telecom networks
evidence.text:
Nokia and Microsoft build a data foundation for AI-run telecom networks

Nokia and Microsoft are extending their partnership with a data platform designed to help telecom operators automate more network work with artificial intelligence. The companies say the new foundation combines Nokia Data Suite with Microsoft Fabric so operators can use trusted data across several network domains.

The announcement, published by Nokia on September 17, describes the work as a multi-vendor and cross-domain solution. Nokia Data Suite supplies reusable telecom data products, telco-specific semantic models and data-quality controls. Microsoft Fabric provides unified storage, analytics, governance and AI tools. Together, the platforms are intended to make network data available in minutes instead of the weeks that traditional integration can require.

The first use cases are practical rather than futuristic. Nokia lists autonomous VoNR assurance, which can identify voice-service problems and help engineers investigate them, and geo-experience analysis, which links radio-access-network data with subscriber and location information. The companies also point to predictive maintenance and fault management as areas where agents can study live and historical data before a problem affects customers.

That approach matters because a mobile network is rarely built from one vendor or one database. Operators often have to combine radio, core, service, subscriber and operational information before an AI system can make a useful recommendation. Nokia says its products can be combined with Microsoft Fabric data from enterprise systems and third-party sources, including in hybrid and on-premises deployments.

The partnership also leaves human oversight in the operating model. Nokia describes AI assistants that provide context, recommend actions and execute workflows within defined governance boundaries. The announcement does not claim that telecom networks will run without engineers. Instead, it presents automation as a way to reduce repetitive investigation and give network teams faster evidence when they make decisions.

Nokia says the solution is available now, with more autonomous-network use cases and customer deployments planned. The immediate news is the integration of the two platforms and the initial telecom applications. Results will depend on how operators deploy the system, the quality of their data and the controls they keep around automated changes.

evidence.title: Sinch: How Retailers Deploy Focused AI to Build Trust
evidence.text:
Sinch: How Retailers Deploy Focused AI to Build Trust

As cautious spending and paper-thin margins turn the holiday retail rush into a battle for every basket, broad promises of AI efficiency are facing a sharp reality check.

Global research from Sinch indicates that commercial success hinges on restraint, with targeted applications solving explicit tasks proving far more effective than general adoption.

Retailers will not build trust in AI by making shoppers use the technology in all possible opportunities. They will build trust by proving its value

Sinch’s survey of 2,501 consumers across eight markets reveals a cautious customer base. Only 43% of global consumers think AI will make holiday shopping easier overall, down from 48% in 2025.

Privacy remains the primary reservation for shoppers , cited by 43% of respondents. A mere 7% say they have no concerns about the technology at all.

Consumer caution vanishes when AI performs specific administrative tasks. High levels of confidence emerge when automation focuses on logistics and basic query resolution.

An overwhelming 81% of global consumers trust AI to handle order tracking and shipping updates. A further 74% are happy for AI to deal with pre-purchase questions.

Confidence drops slightly for administrative changes, with 66% trusting AI for account updates and 62% for payment or billing changes. Total resistance to the technology is negligible, as only one respondent out of 2,501 stated they would never interact with an AI chatbot under any circumstance.

Order tracking is the most popular use case for 48% of shoppers. Researching a product before buying follows at 47%, while 36% use AI for general customer service.

Robert Gerstmann , Chief Evangelist and Co-Founder at Sinch, say: “AI for AI’s sake doesn’t land with shoppers but AI attached to a job they actually want done does.

“Order tracking and pre-purchase questions are the easy wins, where confidence is already high. Payment, billing and account changes are different: shoppers still want a human close by and brands need to make that handoff easy and obvious.”

Trust splits significantly when AI delivers advice rather than transactional details. Human interaction remains the preferred option for recommendations and voice communications.

More than half of shoppers, at 53%, trust a real person’s product recommendation over AI’s, while 47% trust AI equally or more.

For voice communications, 48% trust a human phone agent over an AI voice agent, 37% trust both equally and 15% want the option to transfer to a human if needed.

Regional attitudes toward automation vary sharply across international markets. The US is the most AI-skeptical market surveyed, where 26% of shoppers think AI will make holiday shopping easier and 43% say it will not.

Brazil represents the opposite extreme of consumer sentiment. In Brazil, 78% of surveyed shoppers believe AI will make their shopping experience easier this year.

Retailers can foster greater trust by focusing AI deployment on low-risk tasks and ensuring clear human escalation. Measuring success requires evaluating customer experience rather than automation volume.

Robert says: “Retailers will not build trust in AI by making shoppers use the technology in all possible opportunities. They will build trust by proving its value.

“The key here is to start with clear, low-risk tasks like tracking orders and answering product questions, be upfront about how customer data is used and escalate issues to a human being when necessary, especially when fraud or refund issues are involved.”

Automation strategy must prioritise customer benefit and friction removal over cost savings. Evaluating metrics should reflect this focus on service quality.

He explains: “Customers need to benefit from AI use, through the removal of friction, improved problem solving and better oversight of customer orders.

“Measuring success, therefore, needs to integrate customer satisfaction data and prove customer experience quality. It should never be about the volume of interactions that have been automated and ticked off.”

Maintaining human support infrastructure ultimately enables broader automated operations. Transparency reassures consumers as retailers scale their AI capabilities.

“In widespread AI agent rollout, transparency and human back up are not barriers to automation – they are what will give retailers the customer trust to use AI more effectively,” Robert adds.

evidence.title: Sinch AB: Shoppers are cautious about AI, but confident when it has a job to do
evidence.text:
Sinch AB: Shoppers are cautious about AI, but confident when it has a job to do

STOCKHOLM, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- New research from Sinch AB (publ), shows a nuanced picture of shoppers' attitudes to AI ahead of Black Friday and the holiday season: broader concerns remain, while confidence is high when AI is used for specific, practical tasks. Among 2,501 consumers across eight markets, only 43% think AI will make their holiday shopping easier this year, down from 48% in 2025. Privacy remains shoppers' top reservation about AI for the second year running , cited by 43%, and just 7% say they have no concerns about it at all.

That caution does not carry over once the task is specific. 81% of shoppers say they are confident an AI assistant can handle order tracking and shipping updates, while 74% say the same for pre-purchase questions. Confidence is lower, but still substantial, for account changes (66%) and payment or billing changes (62%).

Shoppers are also open to interacting with AI. Of the 2,501 people surveyed, only one said they would never want to interact with an AI chatbot under any circumstance. The most popular use cases were order tracking (48%), researching a product before buying (47%), and getting customer service (36%).

"AI for AI's sake doesn't land with shoppers, but AI attached to a job they actually want done does. Order tracking and pre-purchase questions are the easy wins, where confidence is already high. Payment, billing and account changes are different: shoppers still want a human close by, and brands need to make that handoff easy and obvious," said Robert Gerstmann, Chief Evangelist and Co-Founder of Sinch.

Trust follows a similar split when AI gives advice rather than just information. 53% of shoppers trust a real person's product recommendation over AI's, while 47% trust AI just as much or more. For voice interactions, 48% trust a human phone agent over an AI voice agent, while 37% trust the AI equally or more.

Confidence in AI also varies sharply by market. The US is the most AI-skeptical market surveyed : just 26% of shoppers think AI will make their holiday shopping easier, and 43% say it won't. Brazil is at the opposite end , with 78% of the surveyed shoppers saying AI will make their shopping easier this year.

About the research The findings are based on an online survey of 2,501 consumers in the United States (698), Australia (351), Brazil (350), the United Kingdom (252), France (225), Germany (225), Mexico (200) and Spain (200), conducted by Sinch in 2026.

The 2026 study follows Sinch's previous BFCM consumer research. India and Canada were included in the 2025 sample but not in 2026. Full country-level data is available on request. Read more about the survey here.

evidence.title: Sinch expands its platform with agentic conversations for AI-powered customer engagement
evidence.text:
STOCKHOLM , Feb. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sinch (publ) today announced agentic conversations, a new set of capabilities designed to operationalize AI agents across global communication channels, enabling enterprises to deploy intelligent agents across messaging, voice, and email at scale.

As generative AI and conversational channels like voice, RCS and messaging apps become central to customer engagement, enterprises are shifting toward agent-driven models. To scale, AI agents must do more than converse. They need secure integration with enterprise systems to execute actions across channels.

With agentic conversations, Sinch simplifies this transition by providing a flexible, secure and open platform that enables businesses to operationalize AI agents at their own pace and according to their technical maturity. Customers are not locked into a single agent model, proprietary data layer, or closed ecosystem. Whether they choose to build their own solutions, use Sinch's AI capabilities, bring their own agents, or integrate through Sinch's ecosystem of partners, Sinch provides the infrastructure and orchestration required to support deployment at scale, built on Sinch's global messaging, voice, and email APIs.

"Our philosophy is simple: enterprises should be free to build with us or bring their own AI," said Daniel Morris, Chief Product Officer at Sinch. "We do not believe in locking customers into a single agent model, proprietary data layer, or closed ecosystem. Whether businesses use Sinch's AI capabilities, deploy their own agents, or work with trusted partners, we provide the communications and orchestration infrastructure that makes those agents operational across messaging, email, and voice."

Agentic conversations is a suite of capabilities, including Sinch Agent Builder, developer and agent tools such as Sinch Functions and Sinch Skills, as well as a broad set of integrations, designed to help enterprises build, deploy and manage AI agents across channels. The transition toward agent-driven engagement is expected to drive substantial growth in conversational traffic across messaging, voice and email. Managing this increase in volume, while maintaining trust, reliability and compliance, will require infrastructure purpose-built for scale.

"Unlike standalone AI agent frameworks, Sinch provides the trusted communications layer that agents depend on to operate reliably across channels and markets. Sinch has long experience in carrier-grade routing, global number provisioning, regulatory compliance, identity verification, branded calling, deliverability optimization and fraud protection. That experience ensures agent-driven communications are secure, scalable, and ready for real-world deployment," Daniel Morris said.

As AI agents take on a more active role in customer engagement, enterprises are redefining how they manage trust, relevance, and conversational scale across channels. The next phase of customer communications will be shaped not only by smarter AI, but by the infrastructure that provides agents with the context, data access and intelligence needed to operate securely, reliably, and at volume. With agentic conversations, Sinch positions itself at the center of that shift.

evidence.title: Siemens and TSMC Advance AI-Powered Semiconductor Design Automation
evidence.text:
Siemens and TSMC Advance AI-Powered Semiconductor Design Automation

PLANO, Texas, Sept. 25, 2026 — Siemens has announced continued collaboration with TSMC to drive innovation in AI-powered automation and advanced semiconductor design enablement. Building on a longstanding relationship within the TSMC Open Innovation Platform (OIP) ecosystem, the companies are expanding design enablement efforts across semiconductor design workflows to help mutual customers improve productivity, accelerate design cycles, and manage increasing design complexity.

As part of this collaboration, Siemens and TSMC have enabled an AI-powered agent for automated design rule check (DRC) fixing across digital and custom integrated circuit (IC) design flows. Powered by Calibre software and tightly integrated with Aprisa software and Solido software, the agent is designed to help engineering teams reduce manual effort, improve workflow efficiency, and accelerate time-to-tapeout.

“Our continued collaboration with TSMC exemplifies Siemens’ commitment to delivering AI-driven automation and advanced semiconductor design capabilities that help customers innovate at the industry’s most advanced process nodes,” said Ankur Gupta, executive vice president, EDA IC Software, Siemens Digital Industries Software. “By combining Siemens’ EDA portfolio with TSMC’s leading process and packaging technologies, we are helping customers achieve new levels of productivity, speed and design confidence.”

“AI presents a significant opportunity to drive productivity and efficiency across increasingly complex semiconductor design workflows,” said Aveek Sarkar, director of the ecosystem and alliance management division at TSMC. “Our collaboration with OIP partners like Siemens focuses on delivering intelligent, trusted automation that empowers engineers to navigate rising design complexity while achieving stringent performance and energy-efficiency targets. By integrating AI into critical stages of the design process, we enable mutual customers to leverage TSMC’s industry-leading processes and advanced packaging technologies to accelerate the expansion of AI innovation.”

Advancing AI-Powered Semiconductor Design

Siemens and TSMC are collaborating to advance AI-powered semiconductor design with the Fuse EDA AI System and Fuse EDA AI Agent, enabling autonomous, long-running and self-verifying EDA workflows. These agentic workflows can reason across complex, multi-step design tasks, orchestrate actions across multiple EDA tools, and continuously validate and improve engineering outcomes. Fuse EDA AI Agent is further enhanced by NVIDIA AI technologies delivering greater token efficiency while improving reasoning and execution across long-running engineering workloads.

A key innovation is an AI-powered DRC-fix workflow that combines Calibre software, Aprisa AI and Solido Fuse technologies to intelligently identify, analyze and resolve design rule violations across digital and custom IC design flows. This builds on the Calibre Check Assist capability, which provides contextual guidance and design rule information during DRC debugging, helping designers diagnose and resolve violations more efficiently. The collaboration also includes agentic custom IC design capabilities powered by Solido Fuse.

The collaboration further extends to agentic place-and-route and digital implementation workflows enabled by Aprisa software. Together, these innovations help engineering teams automate repetitive and time-intensive tasks, leverage domain-aware AI guidance, accelerate design convergence and improve productivity from design creation through tapeout.

Siemens and TSMC continue to collaborate on advanced 3D IC design enablement for TSMC 3DFabric technologies. Siemens has enabled multi-machine support with Calibre 3DStack Advanced software for inter-chiplet antenna verification, including support for TSMC-SoIC, an innovative wafer-level 3D IC chip stacking platform. Further, certification work is underway to supportchip-on-wafer-on-substrate with local silicon interconnect (CoWoS-L). These enhancements deliver necessary scalability and runtime performance for increasingly complex 3D IC designs. This work demonstrates performance improvements in Interface Check Flow for TSMC-SoW.

Siemens’ EDA portfolio, including Solido Simulation Suite software, Calibre xACT software and Calibre 3DThermal software, is supporting collaborative work with TSMC across multiple innovative 3D IC and multiphysics design initiatives, including silicon photonics applications and other advanced packaging technologies.

In addition to certification for static and transient thermal analysis of TSMC 3DFabric technologies, Calibre 3DThermal software has achieved certification for TSMC A16 static and transient thermal analysis and completed enablement for the system-on-wafer thermal reference flow. Further, work is in progress for TSMC-COUPE (Compact Universal Photonic Engine) reference flow.

The companies continue to make progress on complete 3Dblox support, including chip-package co-design workflows with major mutual customers. Siemens and TSMC are also collaborating on Aprisa software capabilities for pre-sim driven die-to-die (D2D) auto-routing, helping designers derive routing configurations intended to meet signal integrity specifications.

Siemens’ EDA technologies have also been enabled to support design, implementation, and verification of TSMC-COUPE features. Joint silicon photonics development activities include design, implementation and verification flows using Innovator3D IC Integrator, Calibre 3DStack, Solido Simulation Suite, L-Edit software, and Calibre Interactive. Solido Simulation Suite software also supports PAM4 measurements associated with TSMC-COUPE technology for optical transceiver interfaces. The joint validation efforts for Calibre 3DThermal solution for TSMC-COUPE are on-going.

Siemens and TSMC continue collaborating on advanced node technology certification and design enablement. Calibre nmDRC, Calibre nmLVS, Calibre xACT and Calibre PERC have achieved certification for the TSMC A14 process node.

The Solido Simulation Suite software is certified for SPICE accuracy in TSMC N3C, A16 and A14 process technologies, enabling reliable analog, RF, and memory verification. The collaboration also extends into TSMC’s custom design reference flow, where Siemens’ technologies support reliability-aware simulation capabilities that address IC aging, real-time self-heating, and safe operating area checks, as well as Solido Design Environment for advanced variation-aware verification and automated cell optimization.

Additionally, mPower software is certified for TSMC N2P (digital and analog) and N3C (analog) transistor-level IR/EM analysis, and Siemens continues collaborating with TSMC on N2 and N3 electromigration and IR-drop custom design reference flows. Certification activities for Aprisa software and mPower analog software on A14 technology are also underway.

Scaling Ecosystem’s Advanced Node Design Expertise

Siemens Xcelerator Academy provides user-friendly, self-paced, on-demand learning resources for Siemens’ EDA portfolio. The program is now available to TSMC Design Center Alliance partners in addition to mutual customers. Siemens recently released an end-to-end digital implementation flow lab tutorial based on TSMC 5nm process technology through the program, helping broaden access to advanced semiconductor design methodologies.

To learn more about how Siemens is helping semiconductor companies accelerate innovation through AI-powered automation, advanced verification technologies and industry-leading design enablement solutions, visit https://www.siemens.com/en-us/company/electronic-design-automation .

Siemens Digital Industries Software helps organizations of all sizes digitally transform using software, hardware and services from the Siemens Xcelerator business platform. Siemens’ software and the comprehensive digital twin enable companies to optimize their design, engineering and manufacturing processes to turn today’s ideas into the sustainable products of the future. From chips to entire systems, from product to process, across all industries. Siemens Digital Industries Software – Accelerating transformation.

evidence.title: Siemens to Acquire Precision Innovations
evidence.text:
Siemens to Acquire Precision Innovations

Siemens has entered into an agreement to acquire Precision Innovations , a privately held electronic design automation software company. The move expands Siemens’ electronic design automation (EDA) portfolio with artificial intelligence (AI)-powered chip planning capabilities that help semiconductor teams optimize power, performance and area earlier in the system-on-chip design process.

Precision Innovations develops EDA software built on the open-source OpenROAD framework to help semiconductor teams evaluate design feasibility, reduce design iterations and accelerate time to market as system-on-a-chip complexity continues to grow.

The acquisition will strengthen Siemens’ EDA portfolio with AI-driven chip planning and design exploration capabilities, complementing Siemens’ existing digital design and verification solutions by enabling faster feasibility analysis and more informed downstream decisions, according to company officials.

Precision Innovations is intended to join Siemens as a key addition to its industry-leading Digital Design Creation software, complementing existing digital design and implementation capabilities to deliver a comprehensive, end-to-end digital flow that spans architecture, implementation and the full silicon lifecycle management of SoCs.

“With Precision Innovations joining Siemens, we will expand our ability to support customers as they face rapidly increasing SoC complexity and the need to explore new architectures faster and more efficiently,” said Ankur Gupta, executive vice president, IC Portfolio, Siemens EDA, Siemens Digital Industries Software. “Integrating Precision Innovations’ AI-powered early design exploration into our EDA portfolio can significantly accelerate time to silicon and improves power, performance and area.”

Precision Innovations was founded in 2019 with the mission to democratize the hardware design landscape by addressing barriers related to cost, expertise and uncertainty that have historically limited access to advanced semiconductor technologies.

The California-based company’s solutions are used by leading semiconductor and technology companies, and will significantly enhance Siemens’ existing EDA offerings across digital design and verification workflows. By combining Precision Innovations’ technologies with Siemens’ broader EDA portfolio, Siemens will be able to help customers address growing design complexity, shorten development cycles and improve engineering productivity.

“Becoming part of Siemens allows us to scale our technology and bring AI-driven chip planning to a much broader set of semiconductor teams,” said Tom Spyrou, chief executive officer, Precision Innovations. “Together, we can help designers leverage AI to evaluate thousands of design options earlier in the process and focus innovation where it matters most.”

Closing of the transaction is expected within the third quarter of calendar year 2026. Terms of the transaction were not disclosed.

evidence.title: Siemens Mobility Unveils ÖBB Railjet M at InnoTrans 2026
evidence.text:
Siemens Mobility Unveils ÖBB Railjet M at InnoTrans 2026

Siemens Mobility has given the new ÖBB Railjet M its world premiere at InnoTrans 2026 in Berlin, showcasing the electrical unit responsible for long-distance routes in the Alpine region.

As part of a 2023 agreement, 31 EMUs will be built in the Railjet M configuration as part of 100 EMUs ordered by ÖBB. These are based on the Siemens Mireo platform.

Siemens’ new revelation comes with promises of higher capacity, improved passenger comfort, and strong availability through digital technologies.

With the ability to carry 257 passengers (27 in first class, 188 in second class, and 42 on folding seats), the Railjet M accommodates those travelling, with several amenities.

These include a vending-machine catering zone, a family area with a children’s cinema and play space, and high-performance Wi-Fi linked to ÖBB’s Railnet portal.

Boasting a top speed of 160 km/h, the ÖBB Railjet M is approximately 160 metres long and fitted with ETCS, ensuring its reliability is maximised.

The focus on long-term maintenance of the ÖBB Railjet M is clear, with continuous on-board self-diagnosis and a lightweight frame intended to cut energy consumption and reduce infrastructure wear.

The vehicles follow a single-car concept, with their weight- and space-optimised bogies developed at Siemens Mobility’s Competence Centre for Bogies and Pantographs in Graz.

This allowed for additional interior space while supporting reliability under demanding Alpine operating conditions.

Earlier this year, the Railjet M was tested in the climatic wind tunnel in Vienna, where it was exposed to temperatures down to –25°C alongside simulated snowfall and high winds.

Further tests are still underway, with progress being made at the Siemens Test Center in Wegberg-Wildenrath.

evidence.title: Climate Week NYC 2026: Siemens and Gavin Newsom on Growth
evidence.text:
Climate Week NYC 2026: Siemens and Gavin Newsom on Growth

This week, thousands of business leaders, politicians and figures across all global industries are attending Climate Week NYC to gain insight from enterprises discussing pressing areas around climate change.

The event – organised by Climate Group – has seen industry and world leaders come together to discuss all things related to climate change, energy, impact, capital and market trends around climate and the business world.

Some business leaders have voiced concerns over the impact of climate policy on existing businesses, citing the unpredictable nature of governments, and how a shift in green subsidies or tax credits could impact long-term investment strategies.

However, at Climate Week NYC, many businesses have reacted optimistically to the need for a green energy transition , but also to the broader impact of climate policy on business and sustainable growth.

Discussing the importance of market collaboration to ensure economic growth and stability at the event, Helen Clarkson, CEO of the Climate Group, says: “At a time when the impacts of climate change are being felt around the world… it has never been more important to be loud about the progress we can make together.

“There are huge opportunities in building a cleaner, more resilient economy, and I remain optimistic about what we can achieve through collaboration and determined leadership.”

At a time when the impacts of climate change are being felt around the world… it has never been more important to be loud about the progress we can make together.”

This week, the event has seen leaders from all sectors and global governments unite to stress the importance of implementing climate policy and how, ultimately, it can prove to be an economic growth driver.

Major companies like Siemens – Climate Week 2026’s official opening ceremony partner – were present at the event, and many spoke about the importance of achieving climate goals with a clear vision, and how businesses can turn net-zero commitments into measurable results.

Eva Risenhuber, Global Head of Sustainability at Siemens, says: “Climate Week NYC matters because it’s where ambition meets execution. It brings leaders from business, government, finance, and civil society into the same week – and challenges all of us to move from commitments to implementation.

“It’s a chance to convene partners and customers around the real work of building a sustainable, resilient, net-zero economy: modernising infrastructure, accelerating the energy transition, and advancing circularity at industrial scale.”

On Wednesday, Siemens and the Energy Efficiency Movement held a panel titled ‘The Twin Engines of Transition: Efficiency and Electrification’, which saw panelists discuss the present relevance of energy efficiency.

Panelists discussed how technologies and operational models are already delivering measurable results to businesses worldwide, what frameworks are working, how they're financed and what it takes to scale impact across industrial systems.

Reflecting the importance of secure energy networks and market resilience, governors and ministers, including California Governor Gavin Newsom , hosted the ‘Governors' Climate Leadership Dialogue and Reception’ panel to discuss the importance of the Under2 Coalition.

The coalition is the largest global network of states and regions committed to achieving net-zero emissions by 2050. At the event, they tackled some of the most pressing topics facing climate delivery for business, including energy security, strengthening resilience and using investment to deliver change.

Speaking at the panel, Gavin Newsom said: “Clean energy means more jobs, lower household costs, stronger energy security, and the opportunity to win the clean industries of the future.”

In addition to Siemens, other major players across global industries have also been present at this year’s event, including food and beverage leader and event partner Unilever, a company that emphasises the importance of climate adaptation.

Speaking about Unilever’s presence at the event and why climate action is integral to growth, Rianne Buter, Global Head of Sustainability at Unilever, says: “Our response to climate change isn’t separate from Unilever’s growth priorities. It’s part of how we do business.”

She adds that energy efficiency and switching to renewable forms of energy can also help reduce operational costs and strengthen a company’s position despite market volatility.

Rianne adds: “By working with partners, we’re determined to win through innovation, creating products that consumers want while ensuring our business remains competitive for the future.”

evidence.title: Climate Week NYC: Siemens and MIT on Tackling AI Energy Use
evidence.text:
Climate Week NYC: Siemens and MIT on Tackling AI Energy Use

The use of AI in solving the Earth’s toughest climate challenges comes alongside a paradoxical threat, as the very technology designed to save the planet demands unprecedented power to run.

This tension took centre stage as world leaders and commercial executives gathered in New York City, US for Climate Action Week against a backdrop of urgent environmental warnings.

These discussions follow record-breaking heatwaves and El Niño-driven wildfires in Africa that have pushed sustainability to the top of the global agenda. NASA notes that Earth is warming at an unprecedented rate, with human activity as the principal cause.

Highlighting the scale of the crisis at the opening ceremony, UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband emphasised that climate loss is an urgent national security issue requiring immediate action.

Having partnerships with industry, as we think about the whole ecosystem, from the innovators at the early stages with industry, is where I think there is a lot of optimism. But we need to work together to actually be able to drive that innovation

At the same time, many people are concerned about the growing environmental impact of new technologies like AI, with rapid build-outs of data centres and surging demand for computing power creating massive energy demands worldwide.

To address these compounding concerns, a panel featuring Dr. Eva Riesenhuber , Global Head of Sustainability at Siemens and Dr. Evelyn Wang , Vice President for Energy and Climate at MIT , met with Angela Barranco , Executive Director for North America at Climate Group .

Together, they explored whether AI can solve climate issues faster than its physical infrastructure consumes resources.

Despite worries about data centre energy footprints, machine learning delivers tangible outcomes in research. Rather than making minor adjustments to single components, AI helps redesign whole systems.

Evelyn explains how research platforms at MIT accelerate sustainable chemistry without relying on scarce critical minerals.

She says: “Within a few months you can actually look at over 900 different chemistries, run 3500 electrochemical experiments and come up with an optimal catalyst, say for fuel cells that give you the highest performance to date while not using precious critical minerals.”

Angela notes that industry optimism around AI focuses on improving whole systems rather than single devices. She then asks how realistic these expectations are in practice today.

In response, Eva points out that automation has evolved from single product tweaks to complete building automation.

She says: “Take a building. You have one product in the building but this building here has a lot of products that actually optimise its energy footprint. So that’s a net zero building and it’s connected to the system. Now it becomes even more interesting when you look at a grid.”

It’s a big challenge for grids because they were never designed to be that smart. We can make them smart with software and we can use AI to move these grids much harder on what they’re capable of doing

Legacy electrical grids were never constructed to manage dynamic two-way energy flows. Modern software and AI allow operators to run existing electrical grids harder, transforming net zero buildings into connected power nodes.

Eva explains that running infrastructure at its limits removes complexity and keeps upgrades affordable for society.

She says: “We can make them smart with software and we can use AI to move these grids much harder on what they’re capable of doing. We already see all the savings of AI on the way now when you get like 30% more load on the same grid with high powered partners. We do need AI to get complexity out and be able to manage all of these different inputs and run our infrastructure to the limit.”

Expanding digital networks requires resources like energy, water and hardware materials. Communities must evaluate these environmental costs alongside potential efficiency gains.

Evelyn notes that computational demand acts as a market driver for clean power innovations.

She says: “Instead of a trade off, let’s really think about using AI as a tool, this powerful tool, and also continue to improve the data centre system, improve it for efficiency, for delivering on clean power.”

Circular manufacturing and policy support future growth

Addressing hardware disposal remains a priority for commercial entities. Companies are actively developing solutions to process complex GPU hardware at end of life.

Eva stresses that industrial ingenuity helps solve resource challenges at high speed.

She says: “People are working on the circularity of GPUs, which are incredibly hard to take apart at the end of life. I think here the ingenuity of humanity and also what businesses can bring to solve these problems are sometimes maybe even underestimated.”

Policymakers must set expectations regarding energy, emissions and water usage for technology facilities. Removing regulatory barriers supports the rollout of clean power transmission networks.

Evelyn emphasises that collaboration across governments and enterprise partners will drive sustainable progress.

She says: “Having partnerships with industry, as we think about the whole ecosystem, from the innovators at the early stages with industry, is where I think there is a lot of optimism. But we need to work together to actually be able to drive that innovation.”
