evidence.title: Bosch sees slight profit decline in H1, but affirms full-year guidance
evidence.text:
Bosch sees slight profit decline in H1, but affirms full-year guidance

Profits at Bosch were down slightly in the first half of the year, according to figures posted by the Stuttgart-based company on Wednesday, but the German automotive supplier reaffirmed its 2026 outlook.

Revenue rose by 3.6% to €46.4 billion ($52.9 billion) in the first six months compared to the same period last year, the company said in a statement.

However, earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) from operations declined from €2.3 billion to €2.2 billion, as special effects from the mobility division weighed on results, Bosch said.

Profits after taxes stood at some €1.1 billion, with Bosch confirming its full-year guidance despite a "challenging" business environment.

"After solid sales growth in the first half of the year, we see ourselves on the home stretch for 2026, but we still need a strong finish," Bosch chief financial officer Markus Forschner was quoted as saying.

This marked the first time that Bosch, which also makes household appliances, power tools and energy and building technology, posted half-year figures, after reporting its worst results in years in 2025.

Adjusted EBIT at Bosch declined by a staggering 42% last year, as the company spent billions to cut thousands of jobs, dampening performance.

Bosch, the world's largest automotive supplier, has also been struggling with geopolitical uncertainty and rising competition for several years, but these were exacerbated in 2025 by the effect of US tariffs.

At the end of 2025, Bosch employed around 412,400 people worldwide, some 5,400 fewer than a year earlier.

evidence.title: Bosch 300 Series vs. LG FlushFit: Which Dishwasher Is Best for Your Kitchen?
evidence.text:
Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

A dishwasher is an appliance you buy and ideally live with for a decade or more, so it’s important to get the decision right. Bosch and LG both sit near the top of almost every best dishwashers list , and both will leave your dishes clean without causing too much noise. Additionally, most machines from these brands feature a third rack, a stainless tub, and an app that lets you start and monitor a cycle from your phone.

However, as a customer, you’re likely looking for the best brand that’s worthy of a significant financial investment. To keep this comparison fair, I matched two similarly sized and similarly priced models: the Bosch 300 Series SHS43CF5N and the LG LDNFC33LS . Both are 24-inch built-ins that run under 50 decibels, hold 16 place settings, and clean well enough to earn a spot in most kitchens.

You can spend less on a budget dishwasher if you’re watching costs, but these two hit the sweet spot of price and performance, delivering the features that matter without crossing too far over $1,000. Where they differ is in how they dry your dishes, their control layout, and how flexible they are for loading dishes. Here’s how the two stack up, and which one is worth investing in—depending on what matters most to you.

Bosch 300 Series 24-Inch Dishwasher SHS43CF5N

Bosch 300 Series 24-Inch Dishwasher SHS43CF5N

Both the Bosch and the LG are evenly matched in capacity and hold 16 place settings, enough for a large family’s dishes or the cleanup after a holiday party. Each also has a third rack along the top for flatware and utensils, moving them out of the lower cutlery basket and freeing up the lower rack for pots and bowls. For most kitchens, neither runs short on room.

The dishwashers both have nearly identical rack flexibility, too, allowing you to adjust the upper rack for taller items and even remove the top rack when you need extra height. The one difference is the Bosch has fold-down tines, which flatten a section of the racks to fit pots, mixing bowls, or odd-shaped cookware.

It’s a notable advantage if you regularly need to wash large dishes or bakeware. That said, I have fold-down tines in my own kitchen and use them only a few times a year, so I wouldn’t consider the feature to be a deal breaker one way or the other.

The two differ a little on cycles, though not in a way that matters much day to day. Both have five on the control panel, and you can add more cycles to each one through their respective apps. Overall, though, the differences are minor, since both cover what a typical household uses, including a standard cycle, a heavy setting for pots, an auto cycle that adjusts to the load, and a quick wash.

Dishwasher controls typically sit in one of two places: along the top edge of the door or across the front. The Bosch hides its controls on the top edge, so the front is a clean, unbroken panel. The catch is that when the door is closed, you can’t see how much time is left on the cycle unless you open the machine’s door or open Bosch’s Home Connect app.

The LG puts its controls and an LED on the outside of the door, so it’s easy to see how much time is left at a glance. Although hidden controls do look tidier, in my experience you basically stop noticing front-mounted buttons within a week of living with the machine. That said, if you want the convenience of seeing how much time is left, the LG is the better option.

Almost everything else is even. Both are standard 24-inch built-ins that sit flush with the cabinets. LG brands this as FlushFit, but Bosch is just as known for its clean, integrated fit, and neither one protrudes past the counter. Both have a fingerprint-resistant finish, and both run at the same 48 dBA, quiet enough to run during dinner or while watching a movie.

Bosch offers AquaStop, a leak protection system that features sensors that automatically cut the water supply and activate the drain pump if it detects a leak. The LG relies on a smart float sensor that detects the presence of water and will automatically shut off the dishwasher. It’s a feature you hope to never need, but the Bosch has the more thorough safeguard against potential emergencies.

Both dishwashers feature an automatic cycle that can sense how dirty each load is. Bosch uses what it calls a PrecisionWash system, a set of sensors and spray arms that scan the dishes throughout the cycle and target every item in the load. The LG uses its own soil sensor and three-arm spray system that adjusts cycle length and water use to match the load.

The LG LDNFC33LS has a SteamAssist feature that loosens baked-on food before the main wash, which helps with casserole dishes and dried-on sauces that would otherwise need a soak. The Bosch has no steam option, so for stuck-on messes you rely on its hotter wash cycles and the sanitize setting. Both get dishes clean, but note that the LG model is ENERGY STAR-certified and uses less water overall compared to the Bosch.

The Bosch 300 Series SHS43CF5N dries by condensation, which can sometimes leave plastic damp. A hot final rinse and a high-temp dry heat the dishes, and as they cool, moisture collects on the stainless tub walls and drains away. It’s a closed system with no fan, which dries glass and ceramic well because they hold heat, but plastic stays cooler and can come out damp. That means you may have to towel off storage containers before putting them away.

Alternatively, LG promises to dry plastic better with its AutoVent Dry system. At the end of a cycle, it will automatically crack the door so humid air escapes and the load air-dries. With the stainless tub in combination with the steam cycle, plastic containers come out drier than they do in a sealed condensation system. If you run a lot of plastic through the wash, the LG comes out ahead.

Like a lot of modern appliances, the Bosch and LG dishwashers connect to an app, allowing you to start or schedule a cycle from another room, get a notification the moment the load finishes, and check the time remaining. Importantly, if something with your dishwasher goes wrong, both apps can help diagnose the problem, so you can provide that information to support.

In terms of overall app functionality, you can expect a similar daily experience but a much different user interface. Bosch has an app called Home Connect, and LG’s app is called ThinQ, and both handle the same core tasks.

One important thing to note, though, is that if you already own multiple Bosch or LG appliances that tap into their respective apps, sticking with the same brand keeps everything under one login and one interface. That convenience can help sway your decision if you’re otherwise torn over which model is right for you.

In the end, the Bosch 300 Series SHS43CF5N and the LG LDNFC33LS are fairly similar overall, though a few differences make them suited to different households.

For most kitchens, if more advanced leak protection and flexible loading matter to you, go with the Bosch 300 Series. It has Bosch’s reliability reputation behind it, fold-down tines that handle larger cookware, and AquaStop leak protection. Both come with a one-year warranty, plus parts-only coverage, with each offering five years on the control board and racks. Bosch backs its tub against rust for life, while LG covers its direct-drive motor for 10 years.

If drying plastic and energy use are your priorities, the LG is the better option. Its AutoVent Dry opens the door at the end of the cycle so storage containers come out drier than they do in the Bosch’s sealed condensation system, and SteamAssist cuts down on the pre-rinsing that stuck-on food usually requires. It’s also ENERGY STAR-certified (the Bosch is not), uses less water per cycle, and keeps a visible timer on the front of the door so you can check the cycle at a glance.

Brandon Russell is a freelance writer covering gear and technology. He started his journey as a news writer at a small newspaper and later began reviewing smartphones, movies, and video games. In his free time, he enjoys the slower, more intentional experience of using a 35mm film camera and making short videos about movies he grew up watching.

evidence.title: Bosch showcases technologies for the truck of the future at Mobility Experience Days
evidence.text:
Bosch showcases technologies for the truck of the future at Mobility Experience Days

Software, sensors, AI and a multi-lane powertrain strategy point to what's next for pickups and large SUVs

Flat Rock, Mich., Sept. 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) --

Bosch foresees a multi-lane highway of full hybrids, range-extended EVs and other propulsion options.

Truck buyers expect 8,000 lbs. of towing capacity as a given, and two-thirds want vehicle-to-load power built in.

Vehicle Motion Management software provides highly personalized experiences for trucks and SUVs in use-cases like off-roading.

Sensors and AI enable the truck of the future to respond to its environment.

Bosch is highlighting the key elements of what it calls the "truck of the future," a showcase of the software, sensors and powertrain technologies the company believes will define the next generation of pickups and large SUVs, as part of Mobility Experience Days at its proving grounds in Flat Rock, Mich.

The event comes as automakers face a central question: what will truck and SUV buyers demand next? Bosch's answer is that no single powertrain will win. Instead, the company is betting on what it calls a "multi-lane highway" – Full Hybrid Electric Vehicles (FHEVs) and Range Extended Electric Vehicles (REEVs) and other configurations built to serve different customers and use cases, all without asking buyers to compromise on the capability they expect.

"The truck of the future isn't defined by what's under the hood. It's defined by what the vehicle can do for the people who depend on it, and by the software and sensors that make that possible," said Paul Thomas, president and CEO, Bosch in North America and president, Bosch Mobility, Americas.

Bosch research shows truck buyers expect a baseline of roughly 8,000 pounds of towing capacity, even when they rarely use it, and that two-thirds want vehicle-to-load power to run job-site tools or back up a home during an outage. Meeting those expectations while also improving efficiency, Bosch says, requires flexible vehicle architectures and common components that can scale across multiple platforms and powertrain types.

At its Mobility Experience Days event, the company highlighted how hybrid technology for the truck of the future does not mean sacrificing performance.

The hybrid work-truck demonstrator showcases the pathway to meet emissions targets below Tier 4 Bin 20 standards while delivering performance – including towing – of a conventional internal-combustion only truck.

For the next generation of eAxle systems from Bosch, silicon carbide MOSFETs (metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor) with advanced vertical trench technology combines with direct cooling of the motor's stator windings and rotor magnets to create higher power density and significant cost reduction. By packaging the e-motor, compact inverter, and gearbox into a single, ultra-compact design , Bosch has created the ultimate modular solution for the multi-energy platform. Supporting the next generation of eAxle secondary drive for hybrid and battery electric vehicle applications, this unit operates as a dedicated boost system to provide on-demand power and instant all-wheel-drive (AWD) capability.

Software delivers vehicle dynamics control in new use cases The truck of the future goes beyond propulsion. Software provides the opportunity for highly personalized experiences, particularly when it comes to vehicle dynamics. The baseline is Bosch Vehicle Motion Management software, which can be applied in multiple use cases.

Bosch Vehicle Motion Management software combined with FOX semi-active suspension technology coordinates chassis actuators in real time to show how software-defined mobility is going off-road. The result is a vehicle that can balance off-road capability, comfort and stability by continuously adapting suspension behavior to terrain and driver inputs.

With Vehicle Motion Management off-road propulsion and braking can be coordinated into a single pedal to help precisely modulate vehicle speed during trail driving, obstacle negotiation and rock crawling while maintaining control of vehicle dynamics.

The combination of Vehicle Motion Management software with steer-by-wire provides a coordinated vehicle dynamics ecosystem where steering, braking, propulsion and suspension work together in real time. The result new levels of driving precision, personalization and automation while laying the groundwork for the next generation of software-defined vehicles.

Sensors and AI deliver personalized experiences and awareness The truck of the future will also increasingly use sensors and AI to provide hyper-personalized experiences and situational awareness by the vehicle.

Bosch will showcase its new AI cockpit inside a vehicle for the first time, as contextual awareness and scalable automotive computing work together to enable the next generation of user-centric vehicle functions and highly personalized in-cabin experiences.

The Bosch AI extension platform allows vehicles to add AI features without changes to existing hardware or system architecture. This enables automakers to easily integrate their own AI models and agents in highly successful truck programs without major system overhauls.

The truck of the future should sense and respond to its environment. Bosch will showcase its new Wet Road Detection feature for the first time in North America, which utilizes ultrasonic generation 7 to detect wetness levels in real time to help vehicle recognize changing driving conditions and adapt accordingly.

"At Bosch, our job is to give automakers the flexible architecture and the software foundation to meet the expectations of truck drivers here in the market," Thomas said. "The result is that buyers get the capability, range and affordability they're asking for, without automakers having to reinvent the vehicle for every option."

Having established a presence in North America in 1906, today the Bosch Group employs around 38,000 associates in more than 100 locations in the North American region (as of Dec. 31, 2025). In 2025, Bosch generated consolidated sales of $18.8 billion in the U.S., Mexico and Canada in 2025. For more information visit www.bosch.us , www.bosch.mx and www.bosch.ca .

The Bosch Group is a leading global supplier of technology and services. It employs roughly 413,000 associates worldwide (as of December 31, 2025). The company generated sales of 91 billion euros in 2025. Its operations are divided into four business sectors: Mobility, Industrial Technology, Consumer Goods, and Energy and Building Technology. With its business activities, the company aims to use technology to help shape universal trends such as automation, digitalization, electrification, and artificial intelligence. In this context, Bosch's broad diversification across regions and industries strengthens its innovativeness and robustness. Bosch uses its proven expertise in hardware, software, and services to offer customers cross-domain solutions from a single source. It also applies its expertise in connectivity and artificial intelligence in order to develop and manufacture intelligent, user-friendly, and sustainable products. With technology that is "Invented for life," Bosch wants to help improve quality of life and conserve natural resources. The Bosch Group comprises Robert Bosch GmbH and its roughly 500 subsidiary and regional companies in over 60 countries. Including sales and service partners, Bosch's global manufacturing, engineering, and sales network covers nearly every country in the world. Bosch's innovative strength is key to the company's further development. Bosch employs some 82,000 associates in research and development.

The company was set up in Stuttgart in 1886 by Robert Bosch (1861-1942) as "Workshop for Precision Mechanics and Electrical Engineering." The special ownership structure of Robert Bosch GmbH guarantees the entrepreneurial freedom of the Bosch Group, making it possible for the company to plan over the long term and to undertake significant upfront investments in the safeguarding of its future. Ninety-four percent of the share capital of Robert Bosch GmbH is held by Robert Bosch Stiftung GmbH, a limited liability company with a charitable purpose. The remaining shares are held by Robert Bosch GmbH and by a company owned by the Bosch family. The majority of voting rights are held by Robert Bosch Industrietreuhand KG. It is entrusted with the task of safeguarding the company's long-term existence and in particular its financial independence – in line with the mission handed down in the will of the company's founder, Robert Bosch.

evidence.title: Bosch Turns Commercial Vehicle Challenges into Technology Opportunities
evidence.text:
Bosch Turns Commercial Vehicle Challenges into Technology Opportunities

The commercial vehicle industry is facing virtually unprecedented opportunities – but also challenges. Rising transport demands driven by the growth of global trade, stringent regulatory requirements, and a worsening driver shortage are putting pressure on the industry and driving up total cost of ownership. Bosch’s answer to this is more technology that opens up new economic prospects. “The heavy-duty commercial vehicle business is a key growth area for us. We aim to double our sales in this segment by the mid2030s,” said Dr. Markus Heyn, deputy chairman of the Bosch board of management and chairman of the Mobility business sector, at the IAA Transportation 2026 in Hannover. The robust commercial vehicle market is also bolstering Bosch’s business.

While global vehicle production is expected to show an overall downward trend in 2026, the heavy-duty commercial vehicle segment (vehicles weighing over six metric tons) is proving to be more resilient. Following a strong first half of the year, Bosch expects global truck production to grow moderately by about 1 percent to approximately 3.3 million trucks, and then to 4 million units by the mid-2030s. On the basis of this forecast and the market uptake of corresponding technologies, Bosch sees the potential to double its heavy-duty commercial vehicle technology sales from today’s more than 4 billion euros by 2035. At the same time, assuming a solid final quarter, the Bosch Mobility business sector will be able to maintain its 2026 revenue level despite the current challenges and demanding market environment.

“We’re leveraging our strength as a global systems supplier to accelerate the transition to alternative powertrains and new vehicle architectures,” Heyn said. The company’s portfolio ranges from hardware and software to artificial intelligence and cloud-based services that make operating commercial vehicles safer and more economical. Bosch is also boosting its growth by entering new business areas. The company plans to establish a new joint venture with Brakes India and Wheels India, two subsidiaries of the TSF Group, to develop smart actuators for compressed air generation, compressed air treatment, air suspension, and parking brakes.

Powertrains and technology for all markets

A key element of Bosch’s growth strategy remains its broad portfolio of alternative powertrain technologies. The company is consolidating its market position in battery-electric mobility: in 2026, one-third of all newly registered battery-electric trucks in Europe are powered by electric motors and inverters from Bosch. A major new order from long-time partner Daimler Truck for the eActros electric truck underpins this success: the agreement covers the supply of electric powertrain components manufactured in Europe.

Similar to the passenger car segment, the pace of transformation in the commercial vehicle market also varies by region: electromobility is rapidly gaining momentum and is becoming especially widespread in China. Bosch estimates that by 2030, about one in four newly registered heavy-duty trucks worldwide will be climate-friendly – powered by batteries or fuel cells – with that figure going up to about half by 2035. In the North American market, on the other hand, the traditional – and in some cases, hybridized – diesel engine continues to dominate. “Achieving the world’s climate goals in the transport sector isn’t an ‘either-or’ proposition – we have to use every technology that helps us transition away from fossil fuels,” Heyn said. “Batteries are also becoming the lead technology in commercial vehicles, but in heavy-duty long-haul transport and on global markets, they will continue to rely on hydrogen and alternative fuels to supplement them.” That’s why Bosch consistently focuses on technological diversity and, in addition to fuel-cell power modules, also supplies key components for hydrogen-powered combustion engines. At the same time, the company intends to systematically expand its leading position in diesel engines and continues to optimize conventional injection systems to help vehicle manufacturers meet new emissions standards such as Euro 7. For the global fleet, renewable synthetic fuels can also help make rapid progress toward climate goals.

Smart sensors for new safety requirements

The commercial vehicle industry is undergoing a transformation, one that’s not limited to powertrain technology: to improve safety on its roads, the EU has made an increasing number of driver-assistance features mandatory in recent years; the most recent regulations were introduced in July 2026. The emergency braking assistant must now also reliably identify pedestrians and cyclists, and the driver monitoring system is required to detect not only drowsiness but also distraction. Bosch provides the necessary sensors and functions. In 2027, the company will launch new generations of its multipurpose camera and radar sensor, both of which will enable precise detection of people and vehicles, thanks to the latest AI technologies and significantly greater computing power. A digital rearview mirror with a built-in camera that analyzes driver behavior and issues warnings when it senses driver distraction went into mass production in 2026 at two well-known European manufacturers. Even outside Europe, major markets such as India and China are tightening their safety standards. In India, for example, new regulatory requirements are pushing up demand for modern driver assistance systems, such as emergency braking assist and blind-spot detection. Bosch is already working there with leading commercial vehicle manufacturers to implement the appropriate ADAS solutions in order to support the introduction of the new safety standards.

With its comprehensive portfolio of systems and sensors, Bosch helps create a complete view of the truck’s surroundings and enhances driving safety and convenience. Thanks to intelligent software algorithms, data from the various sensors in the vehicle is combined and analyzed in real time. The cameras and radar systems are also suitable for higher levels of automation. “Level 4 automated driving is the goal, in part to address the driver shortage in the logistics sector,” Heyn said regarding the automation roadmap. “The software can handle increasingly complex driving tasks, thus reducing the burden on the logistics system.”

On the path to software-driven commercial vehicles

Modern commercial vehicles are collecting and processing increasing amounts of data. The ever-expanding range of powertrain, assistance, and automation functions is leading to much greater complexity in electrical and electronic systems. In addition, competitive pressure in the industry is creating a strong incentive for systems integration, as combining components into complete systems reduces complexity and, in turn, costs. For example, vehicle functions that were previously distributed throughout the truck are now consolidated on central computing platforms for domains such as the cockpit or the vehicle. Furthermore, software and hardware are being consistently decoupled. This is a prerequisite for rolling out new features across the entire vehicle portfolio and throughout the vehicle’s lifecycle by means of over-the-air updates. Bosch and its subsidiary ETAS are developing the central E/E architectures required for this, featuring high-performance, scalable vehicle computers and the associated software platforms. “The software-defined vehicle is gradually becoming a reality in the trucking industry as well,” Heyn said. As a result, customers are benefiting from the company’s systems expertise, as it is well-versed in both hardware and software. Software-defined mobility in the trucking business addresses the industry’s most critical factor: total cost of ownership. For fleet operators, the software-defined truck significantly reduces day-to-day complexity.

evidence.title: Continental To Sell mycar Tyre & Auto To Tuhu In A$403 Million Deal
evidence.text:
Continental has agreed to sell mycar Tyre & Auto, one of Australia’s largest automotive service and repair chains, to Chinese automotive services company Tuhu in a transaction based on an enterprise value of A$403 million, equivalent to approximately €250 million. The proposed transaction includes mycar’s network of approximately 280 stores and more than 1,600 employees across Australia. Completion remains subject to regulatory approvals.

The transaction forms part of Continental’s strategy to concentrate on its core business of developing and manufacturing tires.

Under Tuhu’s ownership, mycar will become part of a company focused on automotive maintenance, repair, and related services.

The acquisition also represents Tuhu’s entry into the Australian market, providing the Chinese company with an established national automotive service network.

Continental acquired mycar in 2018 as part of its efforts to expand tire distribution in Australia and strengthen its presence in the region.

Over the following eight years, mycar expanded its store network, broadened its product portfolio, and increased its market presence.

The company provides a range of automotive services, including scheduled vehicle maintenance, tire replacement, brake repairs, suspension work, battery replacement, and general mechanical repairs.

Its approximately 280 stores make it a major participant in Australia’s automotive aftermarket.

The transaction will transfer the business and its more than 1,600 employees to Tuhu, while maintaining an ongoing commercial relationship with Continental.

Following completion, mycar will continue distributing Continental tires in Australia.

Continental has developed its own local sales organization and expects to maintain its Australian market presence through that infrastructure and its continued distribution relationship with mycar.

The arrangement allows Continental to exit direct ownership of the automotive service chain while preserving an important route to market for its tire products.

For Tuhu, the acquisition provides a platform for expanding beyond China into another major automotive services market.

Tuhu operates an integrated online and offline automotive services platform, combining digital customer engagement with a large physical network of maintenance and repair facilities.

As of June 30, 2026, Tuhu’s network comprised 8,825 Tuhu Workshops.

The company also reported approximately 31 million transacting users during the preceding 12 months, demonstrating the scale of its established Chinese operations.

Tuhu’s services include tire replacement, automotive maintenance, chassis component replacement, mechanical repairs, and vehicle detailing.

The acquisition of mycar will allow Tuhu to apply its experience in automotive service operations, digital platforms, and customer engagement to an established Australian business.

Tuhu intends to work with mycar’s existing management team and employees while adapting its operating approach to Australian market conditions.

The company’s existing strategic relationship with Continental in China provides a foundation for continued cooperation following the acquisition.

For Continental, the divestiture represents a further step in its strategic realignment.

The company plans to continue serving Australian customers through its tire manufacturing and distribution operations while transferring mycar’s direct service and repair activities to Tuhu.

The transaction’s A$403 million valuation represents enterprise value, rather than the amount of cash Continental will necessarily receive after adjustments.

Closing remains contingent on obtaining the required regulatory approvals.

“mycar Tyre & Auto has developed very successfully under the Continental umbrella and is now exceptionally well positioned in the Australian market. In Tuhu, mycar Tyre & Auto is gaining an owner with many years of experience who will actively drive the company’s strategic direction and sustainable long-term development. Tuhu and Continental have a long-standing and strong strategic partnership in China. With our own sales organisation in Australia and the continued distribution of our tyres through the mycar Tyre & Auto network, we will ensure seamless continuity for our customers.”

Dalibor Kalina, Head Of Continental’s Tire Business In Asia-Pacific

“Australia is a highly attractive and promising market for automotive services, and mycar Tyre & Auto is a distinctive business with a strong position in this market. We look forward to working closely with the existing management team and employees, while continuing our long-standing partnership with Continental. As a new entrant to the Australian market from China, we are committed to adapting quickly to the local market and building on mycar’s strong foundation established under Continental’s management and its proven track record of responsible and reliable operations. By bringing Tuhu’s capabilities and experience to Australia, we look forward to continuing to deliver value, choice and convenience for Australian vehicle owners.”

evidence.title: Continental Introduces New AI-Based Driver Monitoring System for Future Vehicles
evidence.text:
Continental has revealed a new artificial intelligence-powered driver monitoring system designed to detect distraction, fatigue, and reduced driver attention with greater accuracy, marking another significant step in the evolution of advanced vehicle safety technology.

The next-generation system combines AI-driven image analysis with in-cabin sensing to help automakers meet increasingly stringent global safety regulations while supporting the growing adoption of advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS).

The announcement comes as driver monitoring technology becomes an increasingly important part of modern vehicles.

While advanced driver-assistance systems such as adaptive cruise control, lane-centering assistance, and hands-free highway driving continue to evolve, regulators and automakers alike recognize that drivers must remain alert and ready to take control whenever necessary.

As a result, intelligent driver monitoring systems are rapidly transitioning from premium options to essential safety features.

According to Continental, the new AI-based driver monitoring system uses advanced algorithms capable of analyzing facial expressions, eye movements, head position, and full driver behavior in real time.

The technology is designed to identify signs of distraction and fatigue earlier than previous systems while reducing false alerts, helping improve both vehicle safety and the full driving experience.

Also Read: 10 Most Expensive Dodges Ever Built

Artificial intelligence is playing an increasingly important role in modern automotive safety, and Continental’s latest system reflects that shift.

Traditional driver monitoring systems typically rely on relatively simple measurements, such as whether a driver’s eyes remain open or whether their hands stay on the steering wheel. While effective in many situations, these systems can sometimes struggle to accurately distinguish between momentary distractions and genuine safety risks.

According to Continental, its new AI-powered solution processes multiple visual inputs simultaneously, allowing the system to develop a more comprehensive understanding of driver behavior.

Rather than reacting to a single movement, the software evaluates combinations of eye direction, blinking frequency, head orientation, facial movements, and other behavioral indicators before determining whether intervention is necessary.

The company says this approach improves accuracy while reducing unnecessary warnings that can frustrate drivers.

Detecting Fatigue Before It Becomes Dangerous

Driver fatigue remains one of the leading contributors to serious traffic accidents worldwide. According to road safety experts, fatigue reduces reaction times, impairs decision-making, and increases the likelihood of lane departures, delayed braking, and loss of vehicle control.

Unlike obvious distractions such as mobile phone use, fatigue often develops gradually, making it more difficult for drivers to recognize when their alertness has declined.

Continental’s new monitoring system continuously evaluates behavioral patterns associated with drowsiness.

According to the company, artificial intelligence enables the system to identify subtle changes in blinking behavior, eyelid movement, gaze stability, and head posture that may indicate fatigue before a driver experiences a complete loss of concentration.

If the system determines that attention levels have fallen below safe thresholds, it can issue visual, audible, or haptic alerts encouraging the driver to refocus or take a break.

Distraction has become another major challenge for vehicle safety. Modern drivers frequently interact with navigation systems, smartphones, infotainment displays, and other in-car technologies. Even brief moments of inattention can significantly increase crash risk, particularly at highway speeds.

According to Continental, the AI-powered monitoring system is capable of recognizing when a driver is looking away from the road for extended periods or engaging in behaviors inconsistent with safe vehicle operation.

Instead of relying solely on simple eye tracking, the AI analyzes broader driver behavior to distinguish between normal driving movements and potentially hazardous distraction.

For example, briefly checking a side mirror differs significantly from repeatedly looking down at a mobile device or turning away from the road for several seconds.

By understanding context more effectively, the system aims to provide smarter and more meaningful alerts.

Supporting Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems

The importance of driver monitoring has increased dramatically as advanced driver-assistance systems become more capable.

Technologies such as adaptive cruise control, lane-centering assistance, traffic jam assist, and hands-free highway driving can reduce driver workload under certain conditions, but they still require human supervision.

According to Continental, intelligent driver monitoring serves as a critical safety layer by ensuring drivers remain prepared to resume control whenever automation reaches its operational limits.

If the system detects that the driver is no longer paying sufficient attention, it can provide escalating warnings before requesting immediate intervention.

This capability is becoming increasingly important as manufacturers introduce higher levels of driving automation while maintaining driver responsibility.

Regulatory requirements are also driving rapid adoption of driver monitoring technology. Several global markets have introduced or are preparing regulations requiring advanced distraction and fatigue detection systems in new vehicles.

According to Continental, its latest AI-based platform has been developed with future regulatory requirements in mind, enabling automakers to integrate compliant monitoring solutions across multiple vehicle segments.

Europe has already implemented General Safety Regulation (GSR) requirements that encourage broader deployment of driver monitoring systems, while similar discussions continue in other regions.

Industry analysts expect driver monitoring to become increasingly common across mainstream passenger vehicles over the next several years rather than remaining limited to luxury models.

One advantage of artificial intelligence is its ability to recognize complex behavioral patterns that traditional rule-based software may overlook.

According to Continental, machine learning allows the monitoring system to better distinguish between harmless driver behavior and situations that genuinely require intervention.

For instance, a driver may briefly glance toward a side street while checking for traffic, which should not necessarily trigger a warning. By analyzing multiple visual cues simultaneously, AI can better understand context and avoid unnecessary alerts.

The company also notes that ongoing software development can further refine detection performance as more real-world driving data becomes available.

This ability to improve over time represents one of AI’s biggest advantages in automotive safety applications.

As interior cameras become more common, privacy remains an important consideration. Continental states that its driver monitoring technology is designed with data protection in mind, processing driver information securely while supporting manufacturer-specific privacy requirements.

Many modern driver monitoring systems perform image analysis locally within the vehicle rather than transmitting video to external servers.

This approach helps reduce privacy concerns while allowing real-time analysis without relying on internet connectivity.

Automakers implementing the technology will ultimately determine how driver data is managed in accordance with regional regulations and customer privacy policies.

Continental is one of several major automotive suppliers investing heavily in intelligent interior sensing systems.

Companies including Bosch, Valeo, Forvia, Magna, Aptiv, Smart Eye, Seeing Machines, and Cipia have all introduced increasingly sophisticated driver monitoring technologies as automakers prepare for stricter safety regulations and more advanced driving assistance features.

Many manufacturers, including General Motors, Mercedes-Benz, BMW, Ford, Hyundai, Volvo, and Tesla, have also expanded their use of interior cameras to support various driver assistance functions.

Competition among suppliers has accelerated innovation in artificial intelligence, camera hardware, image processing, and software algorithms, helping improve system accuracy while reducing implementation costs.

Industry analysts expect these technologies to become standard equipment across a growing number of passenger vehicles before the end of the decade.

Continental’s latest AI-based driver monitoring system demonstrates how artificial intelligence is becoming an increasingly important part of vehicle safety.

According to the company, the technology has been developed to identify distraction and fatigue more accurately while supporting the next generation of advanced driver-assistance systems and helping automakers comply with evolving safety regulations.

As vehicles continue incorporating higher levels of automation, intelligent driver monitoring will play a crucial role in ensuring that drivers remain engaged whenever human intervention is required.

By combining AI-powered image analysis, real-time behavioral monitoring, and seamless integration with modern safety systems, Continental aims to provide automakers with a solution that enhances both safety and driver confidence.

While fully autonomous vehicles remain under development, technologies such as AI-driven driver monitoring represent an important bridge between today’s advanced driver-assistance systems and the increasingly automated vehicles of the future.

As regulators, automakers, and consumers place greater emphasis on preventing distraction-related crashes, intelligent in-cabin monitoring is expected to become one of the defining safety technologies of the next generation of automobiles.

evidence.title: Schaeffler stock falls 2.24 percent as Q2 profit weakens
evidence.text:
Schaeffler stock fell 2.24 percent to EUR 6.97 on Xetra on September 23, 2026. The decline came as the latest quarterly figures showed higher revenue but weaker earnings than in the first quarter, leaving the stock EUR 5.01 below its 52-week high of EUR 11.98.

Schaeffler generated EUR 5.903 billion in revenue in Q2 2026, compared with EUR 5.764 billion in Q1. That increase of EUR 139 million, or 2.4 percent, shows that sales held up across the group even as profitability moved in the opposite direction.

Operating profit declined from EUR 285 million in Q1 to EUR 238 million in Q2 2026. Net income dropped from EUR 60 million to EUR 34 million, while diluted earnings per share decreased from EUR 0.06 to EUR 0.04.

The sequential comparison matters more than the revenue increase for investors. A 16.5 percent decline in operating profit and a 43.3 percent decline in net income point to weaker conversion of sales into earnings during the second quarter.

Schaeffler also reported EUR 124 million in operating cash flow for Q2 2026, up from EUR 60 million in Q1. At the balance-sheet date of June 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents stood at EUR 2.517 billion, while total debt was EUR 8.545 billion.

evidence.title: CoLab Announces Multi-Year Contract Expansion With Schaeffler to Accelerate Design Collaboration and Product Development
evidence.text:
CoLab Announces Multi-Year Contract Expansion With Schaeffler to Accelerate Design Collaboration and Product Development

Multi-year expansion makes CoLab the standard design review environment for more than 1700 engineers across North America, Europe and Asia, with the platform spanning legacy and Cloud-based development ecosystems.

ST. JOHN'S, Newfoundland and Labrador, September 15, 2026 --( BUSINESS WIRE )--Today, CoLab AI Inc. announced a multi-year expansion of its enterprise collaboration with Schaeffler AG, consolidating three previously separate agreements — with Schaeffler, Vitesco Technologies and Ewellix — into a single global contract. CoLab is now the standard design review environment for more than 1700 Schaeffler engineers across North America, Europe and Asia, in a relationship that began with a single pilot team in 2022.

The expansion comes as Schaeffler works through two transformations at once. Its merger with Vitesco Technologies and acquisition of Ewellix created one of the largest engineering organizations in mobility. At the same time, Schaeffler is moving more of its engineering data and workflows to the Cloud, as part of a publicly stated cloud-first strategy. Both come down to the same question: whether engineers across a newly combined organization can make decisions together as one engineering team.

"Accelerating product development is one of our highest priorities, and collaboration is where we have the most to gain," says Rainer Eidloth, Senior Vice President, Engineering Digitalization & IT at Schaeffler AG. "Our engineers need one place to review a design together and understand the thinking behind it. CoLab provides that extra layer, and it must work across both our current and future engineering environments."

The environment Schaeffler is building gives CoLab a distinct role. The Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) system is the authoritative record of what a design is — versions, approvals, access controls. CoLab is where engineers understand why it should be that way. CoLab is extending the capabilities of its PLM integrations to operate with cloud-based PLM, as Schaeffler completes their migration.

"Like many of our customers, Schaeffler recognizes that design collaboration is critical to their goal of accelerating product development" says Adam Keating, Co-Founder and CEO of CoLab. "By giving their engineers and cross functional teams a single place to review designs, Schaeffler is not only speeding up design cycles but also capturing critical design rationale, which can serve as the foundation for AI-driven product development."

Review cycle times have fallen significantly and CoLab is becoming the standard way design reviews are run across the merged company. Engineers reach decisions faster because the information needed to justify each one sits alongside the design itself.

Schaeffler's rapid adoption of CoLab is unique in that it took place during a period of PLM consolidation and migration. In spite of this, Schaeffler kept reviews and programs running smoothly, with CoLab acting as a connective layer across multiple CAD and PLM tools:

"Bringing three engineering organizations together is a multi-year effort, and our programs could not wait for it," says Prashant Reddy, Director of Engineering Digitalization and IT, Americas, at Schaeffler. "We needed engineers from Schaeffler and former Vitesco and Ewellix reviewing designs together, regardless of which PLM or CAD environment they relied on. Starting with one team in 2022, CoLab is now how our engineers work across the globe."

CoLab builds AI-powered software for mechanical engineering and hardware development teams. Its EngineeringOS platform helps engineers make better, faster design decisions by connecting people, data, and AI in one collaborative workspace—capturing expert knowledge as a natural part of day-to-day work.

With AI agents built into the platform, CoLab enables teams to apply that knowledge automatically to improve design quality and accelerate product development. Founded in 2017, CoLab is trusted by leading global manufacturers to drive decision velocity and bring better products to market, faster.

evidence.title: ThyssenKrupp Automotive Technology sells Automation Engineering division
evidence.text:
ThyssenKrupp Automotive Technology sells Automation Engineering division

ThyssenKrupp Automotive Technology has entered into an agreement with Agile Robots SE to sell the Automation Engineering division as part of a segment restructuring. This is reported in a ThyssenKrupp press release.

The completion of the transaction is subject to regulatory approval, which is expected in the coming months. As part of the deal, Agile Robots will create a new division called Krause Automation as a system provider and integrated solutions developer.

Automation Engineering develops automation solutions for specific products. At the same time, Agile Robots is a long-term partner of the company and has the technological capabilities, financial resources and attractive industrial concept necessary for sustainable business development through the introduction of innovative products and new industrial solutions.

The deal corresponds to the strategic restructuring of the segment with the prospect of developing automation systems in the automotive sector. Both sides are joining forces to accelerate industrialization and the introduction of innovative solutions, as well as to enter new markets beyond the automotive sector, including intralogistics, electronics and medical technology.

Prior to the conclusion of the deal, Agile Robots, ThyssenKrupp and the IG Metall trade union entered into an agreement that provides a reliable framework and the involvement of employees in the integration process. The current restructuring at the Bremen and Chemnitz/Hohenstein-Ernsttal facilities is beyond the scope of the deal and will be completed as planned.

The sale of Automation Engineering is part of a reorganization of ThyssenKrupp Automotive Technology announced in July, aimed at implementing new projects for individual enterprises, including in the field of automation. A coordinated sale is a logical element of a portfolio strategy.

Agile Robots is a German technology company with headquarters in Munich (Germany). The company combines robotics and artificial intelligence to develop industrial solutions in the automation segment. Agile Robots was founded on the basis of the German Aerospace Center (DLR). The staff includes 2.5 thousand people.

Automotive Technology is a division of ThyssenKrupp AG for the production of high—tech components and systems, as well as solutions for vehicle automation (technologies for chassis, steering and shock absorption systems, axle systems and transmission components for engines, etc.). The headquarters is located in Essen (Gersmania).

ThyssenKrupp AG is a German steel company. ThyssenKrupp was formed as a result of the merger of Thyssen AG and Krupp in 1999 and has operational headquarters in Duisburg and Essen (Germany).

Thyssenkrupp Nucera cuts fiscal 2026 outlook after abandoning SOEC stack production plans

Thyssenkrupp Nucera has scrapped its plans for in‑house mass production of SOEC stacks, taking a one‑off €30 million impairment charge and trimming its fiscal 2026 EBIT loss outlook to €105 million–€75 million (previously €80 million–€30 million), lowering sales and green hydrogen segment forecasts.

Thyssenkrupp Nucera Lowers 2026 Forecast After Ending SOEC Production Plans

Thyssenkrupp Nucera Revises Financial Outlook Following SOEC Strategy Shift

Aug 11 (Reuters) - Thyssenkrupp Nucera said on Tuesday it has abandoned plans to establish its own mass-production capacity for solid oxide electrolysis cell (SOEC) stacks, taking a one-off EBIT hit of roughly €30 million in the fourth quarter.

The charge would primarily result from an impairment of its pilot plant and capitalized development costs, the German electrolysis equipment maker said. SOEC technology is used to produce green hydrogen through high-temperature water electrolysis.

Thyssenkrupp Nucera now expects an earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) loss of €105 million to €75 million ($86.52 million) in fiscal 2026, compared with its earlier guidance for an EBIT loss of €80 million to €30 million.

Group sales are now forecast at €450 million to €500 million for the fiscal, compared with €450 million to €550 million previously, while group order intake is expected at €550 million to €670 million.

The company's green hydrogen segment sales outlook was also lowered to €100 million to €130 million, from €120 million to €170 million previously. Its outlook for the Chlor-Alkali segment, however, remained unchanged.

In May, Thyssenkrupp Nucera froze hiring in high-cost countries as part of broader savings measures, after its second-quarter loss widened due to higher costs for hydrogen projects and the termination of a U.S. pilot project.

evidence.title: Thyssenkrupp Stock Rallies 27% as Cyber Breach and Auto Cuts Barely Dent Investor Confidence
evidence.text:
Thyssenkrupp’s shares have charged ahead this year, shrugging off a ransomware attack on one of its naval subsidiaries and the lingering fallout from job cuts in its automotive division. The stock closed on Friday at €11.82, up 27.45% since the start of 2026, and sits just 10.76% below its 52-week high of €13.24 set on October 9, 2025 — a gap that suggests traders are betting the conglomerate’s broader transformation story outweighs isolated operational headaches.

The cyber-incident surfaced on July 18, when a group calling itself “The Gentlemen” listed Thyssenkrupp Marine Systems on its darknet leak site, claiming to have stolen more than a terabyte of data. The company confirmed a security breach but pushed back hard on the scale, saying it hit only a North American subsidiary of Atlas Elektronik, a TKMS division that supplies the U.S. military. Thyssenkrupp stressed that the compromised IT environment was isolated from the corporate network and that no sensitive military data is believed to have been exposed.

The attackers tried to back up their boasts two weeks earlier, releasing screenshots on July 13 that appeared to show classified engineering drawings: a confidential design of a side-scan sonar system from Marine Sonic Technology, and operating manuals for the SeaFox I and SeaFox T underwater minesweeping vehicles built by Atlas Elektronik. While basic specs of those systems are public, the full manuals are tightly controlled internally. Still, no forensics team or government agency has confirmed the group’s claim of a one-terabyte haul, and the group’s past track record includes naming victims whose alleged data breaches could never be independently verified.

“The Gentlemen” itself is a relative newcomer, formed in mid-2025 as a splinter of the notorious Qilin gang. It lured affiliates with an unusually generous 90% profit share and by mid-2026 had rocketed to the top of the most-active ransomware ranking, according to ReliaQuest’s second-quarter analysis. GuidePoint Security’s own Q2 report puts Qilin first and “The Gentlemen” second, but all researchers agree the group is among the most prolific in the current threat landscape. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying Thyssenkrupp?

Thyssenkrupp shares barely flinched at the news. The stock had already gained 6.97% in the past month alone, and the cyber breach failed to knock it off its upward trajectory. That resilience partly reflects the market’s focus on the group’s portfolio overhaul, including plans to spin off or separately list various divisions — a theme that has generated steady re-rating momentum.

Meanwhile, a very different kind of pressure continues to weigh on the automotive body solutions unit. In spring 2025, Thyssenkrupp Automotive Body Solutions announced it would cut up to 230 jobs, roughly a quarter of the workforce, across four German sites: Heilbronn, Weinsberg, Leingarten and Mühlacker. Mühlacker, with about 180 employees, was the hardest hit; the plant produces parts for the Porsche Taycan, and waning demand for the electric sports car has hammered its order book. The IG Metall union slammed the company’s perceived lack of transparency at the time, and the announcement followed an earlier plant closure that displaced around 300 workers.

More than a year on, the structural problems in the auto supply unit remain unresolved. The case illustrates how Thyssenkrupp’s exposure to specific vehicle models — especially ones with concentrated production — can cause immediate pain when sales flag. No updated employment figures for the four sites have been released, and the division’s underlying challenges are seen as persistent. Thyssenkrupp at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now.

For investors, the contrast is stark. The conglomerate’s stock is riding a wave of optimism tied to its broader restructuring and the potential value unlock from its marine, materials and industrial units. But the auto business and the cybersecurity vulnerability at Atlas Elektronik both serve as reminders that operational risks can surface with little warning — even as the share price keeps climbing.

evidence.title: Thyssenkrupp’s Dual Pivot: AI Automation Ambitions and a Decisive Spin-Off Vote
evidence.text:
Thyssenkrupp shares are treading water near a critical technical level as investors weigh two very different bets on the conglomerate’s future. The stock slid to €10.18 on Friday, leaving it barely a whisker above the 200-day moving average of €10.01. The monthly loss of 13% and an elevated volatility reading of 43% underscore just how skittish the market has become. One camp dreams of an efficiency revolution powered by artificial intelligence; the other pins its hopes on a clean break via the spin-off of the materials trading arm tk accelis. Both narratives will be tested in the weeks ahead.

The AI push took shape through an alliance with GlobalLogic, the digital engineering specialist. Thyssenkrupp plans to deploy autonomous robots, drones and advanced data infrastructure across its industrial operations — inspecting dangerous production areas, reducing downtime and accelerating green energy projects. The logic is compelling: if the technology cuts stoppages and speeds up project timelines, the holding company’s operating performance could improve without resorting to yet another divestment. But so far, no hard numbers have emerged. The market is treating the initiative as an unproven bet.

Meanwhile, the restructuring blueprint is far more concrete. The supervisory board has approved the 20-for-1 ratio for the tk accelis separation: for every 20 Thyssenkrupp shares held, shareholders will receive one new tk accelis share. Around 31.1 million new shares will be issued. Under the plan, investors will hold 49% of the materials business directly, with the parent retaining 51%. Trading in Frankfurt is slated to begin after an extraordinary general meeting on 7 August gives the go-ahead. The unit itself is no lightweight — 15,500 employees, roughly 250,000 customers worldwide and €11.4 billion in revenue in fiscal 2024/25, servicing fast-growing segments such as aerospace, defence and data centres. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying Thyssenkrupp?

Analysts are split on whether the move unlocks value. Jefferies reaffirmed a buy rating with a €13 price target in mid-June, arguing the spin-off will surface hidden assets. JPMorgan is more cautious, sticking with neutral and a €11.80 target. At current levels around €10.17, the stock trades 23% below its 52-week high of €13.24, leaving plenty of room for upside if the market buys into the holding-company model. CEO Miguel López is intent on transforming Thyssenkrupp into a pure portfolio manager — after Nucera and TKMS, tk accelis is the next independent piece to fall into place.

That said, the steel division remains a millstone. The restructuring agreement with IG Metall is in place, and a direct-reduction plant in Duisburg is under construction, but the decarbonisation bill is enormous. European steel tariffs are due to tighten from 1 July — a welcome relief for the unit — yet the structural cost burden threatens to swallow any efficiency gains. Thyssenkrupp Steel, alongside ArcelorMittal and voestalpine, is lobbying Brussels to reform the emissions trading system, warning that without better economic conditions, even the best productivity improvements will be for nothing.

Technically, the share price is at a make-or-break juncture. Holding the 200-day moving average would keep the year-to-date gain of roughly 5% intact and allow the recent fall to be written off as a normal consolidation. A bounce above the 50-day line at €10.58 would brighten the chart considerably. But a decisive break below €10.01 could turn the 52-week trough of €7.10 into a real magnet rather than a distant buffer.

The next catalyst is not a fixed date for AI milestones — investors will watch for concrete deployment progress from the GlobalLogic partnership in day-to-day operations. The hard deadline is 7 August, when shareholders vote on the tk accelis spin-off. For now, Thyssenkrupp oscillates between two extremes: the operational fantasy of an AI-driven efficiency renaissance and the gritty reality of a steel transformation that has yet to prove its financial viability.

evidence.title: Thyssenkrupp Sheds Automation Unit in Strategic Portfolio Shift
evidence.text:
Thyssenkrupp Sheds Automation Unit in Strategic Portfolio Shift

Thyssenkrupp has finalized the divestment of its Automation Engineering business, a key move in the ongoing restructuring of its automotive supply division. The unit, now sold to Munich-based Agile Robots SE, involved approximately 650 specialists departing the Essen-headquartered conglomerate. This transaction, which officially closed at the beginning of the month, is a deliberate management effort to streamline portfolio complexity. Despite this strategic progress, the company’s share price remains under pressure, continuing to trade near its annual lows.

The sale process, initiated in the summer of 2025, transfers ten international locations along with the workforce to Agile Robots. The business will operate under the new name “Krause Automation.” For Thyssenkrupp, this divestment represents a focused capital allocation strategy. The company’s automotive segment will now concentrate exclusively on four core areas deemed to have stronger growth profiles and greater synergy potential with its other industrial operations: chassis technologies, components, the aftermarket business, and forged parts.

Broader Headwinds Overshadow Corporate Action

The market’s reaction to the completed sale has been muted. Shares continue to search for a solid footing, with recent trading confined to a narrow range between €7.70 and €7.85. Analysts point out that the persistent weakness is less attributable to the automotive sector and more to the challenging environment facing Thyssenkrupp’s European steel operations. Pressure on margins from low-cost Asian imports is currently overshadowing the operational advances being made through the group’s transformation.

Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying Thyssenkrupp?

Management continues to evaluate further strategic options beyond the automation unit sale. A long-term solution for the marine systems division TKMS and the structure of the stake in elevator manufacturer TK Elevator remain key focus areas. evidence.title: BASF explores Evonik takeover as Europe chemicals consolidation pressure grows
evidence.text:
BASF explores Evonik takeover as Europe chemicals consolidation pressure grows

Europe’s chemicals sector is facing renewed consolidation pressure as BASF pursues a potential takeover of German rival Evonik. A deal would strengthen BASF’s product and geographic mix while creating a larger Germany-based player better positioned against Chinese and U.S. competitors.

Any transaction would be significant in scale. Evonik has a market capitalisation of about 8.4 billion euros, while its enterprise value including net debt is about 12 billion euros, and shareholders would be expected to seek a meaningful takeover premium.

People familiar with the business say Evonik’s shareholders and executives would need to be convinced that a combination with BASF offers a strong strategic fit as well as acceptable terms. The stance of RAG-Stiftung, which holds 44 per cent of Evonik, is likely to be decisive in whether a deal can proceed.

BASF, Evonik and RAG-Stiftung declined to comment. Dealreporter also wrote this week that BASF had explored a possible merger with Evonik this year. Industry impact and strategic rationale A takeover would mark a major step by BASF chief executive Markus Kamieth to consolidate Europe’s fragmented chemicals industry, which is under pressure from weak demand, global overcapacity and higher input costs. Investors reacted quickly, with Evonik shares rising as much as 10.6 per cent on Friday, while BASF shares fell 2.7 per cent.

A combined company would create a larger German chemicals champion with broader reach across speciality and industrial products. Together, BASF and Evonik generated 74 billion euros in revenue last year, and the merger could offer room for cost reductions in overlapping markets such as Germany while supporting growth in Asia and the U.S.

Regulatory scrutiny would be likely, but the political backdrop in Brussels has become more supportive of larger European industrial champions. Evonik operates in more than 100 countries and employs about 31,000 people, producing additives for paints and mattress foam, polymers for automotive and aerospace uses, and amino acids for animal feed.

Evonik this week announced plans to cut more than 3,200 jobs, mostly in Germany. The company is led by interim chief executive Claus Rettig after Christian Kullmann stepped aside in August due to illness, and it is closing smaller plants, selling non-core businesses and trying to expand in Asia and America.

BASF has also been reshaping its portfolio. In July it raised its earnings outlook after increasing product prices, completed the 7.7 billion euro sale of a majority stake in its automotive coatings business to Carlyle, and this month hired banks for a planned mid-2027 listing of its agricultural solutions unit.

Germany’s biggest chemicals groups are raising prices this year as they contend with surging energy costs linked to conflict in the Middle East. Some producers, however, are also getting a short-term competitive benefit over Asian rivals that depend more heavily on Gulf raw materials such as naphtha and methanol.

In our earlier coverage, we looked at reports that BASF had approached Evonik and its largest shareholder, the RAG Foundation, to discuss a possible merger and had been sounding out banks about a deal. We also noted the immediate market reaction, with Evonik shares jumping on expectations of strategic value, while both companies refrained from confirming any formal approach—leaving the status of the talks uncertain.

evidence.title: Chemicals Giant BASF Moves for Rival Evonik — Update
evidence.text:
German chemicals producer BASF said it entered initial talks over a takeover of smaller peer Evonik, a tie-up that would bolster BASF's dominant position in Europe's chemicals industry.

BASF said Friday it was in exploratory takeover talks with Evonik and the latter's largest shareholder, a foundation called RAG-Stiftung. Evonik, a chemicals producer based in Essen, Germany, earlier Friday noted BASF's non-binding approach. RAG-Stiftung, which holds a stake of 43.8% in Evonik, also confirmed the interest from BASF.

None of the companies said how much money BASF was putting on the table for its bid. Evonik's market capitalization stands at 8.42 billion euros ($9.58 billion), according to LSEG data. BASF, the much larger company, has a market cap of some 46.7 billion euros.

The outcome of these talks remains uncertain at this stage, BASF said. The company said it "continuously evaluates" potential acquisitions that could strengthen its core business and fuel growth.

"In doing so, BASF takes a disciplined approach," the company said, adding that it would inform the market of any developments in line with regulatory requirements.

In European late afternoon trading, Evonik shares were up 6.9% at 19.32 euros, while BASF shares traded 4% lower at 50.19 euros.

evidence.title: BASF approaches rival Evonik with merger proposal, FT reports
evidence.text:
By Matthias Inverardi and Patricia Weiss

DUESSELDORF, Germany, Sept 25 (Reuters) - Germany's BASF, among the world's largest chemicals makers, has approached smaller peer Evonik over a possible takeover that could strengthen its portfolio as European companies face tough competition from China.

BASF said it continuously evaluated "the strategic option of acquisitions that strengthen its core businesses, deliver a strong strategic fit, drive profitable growth and create value" and was in exploratory talks.

Evonik said earlier it had "received a non-binding approach from BASF regarding a voluntary public takeover offer for all shares of the company".

RAG Foundation, which holds 43% in Evonik, also said it had been contacted by BASF regarding a takeover offer for Evonik.

BASF has a market capitalisation of €45.8 billion ($52.2 billion), while Evonik is currently valued at €9.2 billion.

""Evonik's comparatively low valuation makes it an attractive potential partner," said Linus Vogel of Deka Investment, a top-20 investor in both companies.

"For BASF, active consolidation would be a logical response to the structural weaknesses of the European market," Vogel added.

A deal is far from certain. BASF in a statement said the outcome of the exploratory talks was "open at this stage", while Evonik said no discussion was underway.

Evonik shares continued a recent rally that traders said was partly driven by takeover speculation. The stock closed 7.2% higher on Friday. BASF shares fell 3.6%.

Evonik's products include high-tech plastics, feed additives as well as ingredients for coatings and household products, while BASF makes engineering plastics, super absorbent polymers, vitamins and a wide range of chemicals for industrial uses.

Arne Rautenberg, head of equities at mutual-funds firm Union Investment, said there was a sound business case for a deal.

"By acquiring Evonik, BASF could strengthen its position in the speciality chemicals sector and increase capacity utilisation," Rautenberg said.

Geographically, however, the companies are less complementary.

Europe is the largest market for both and BASF has pledged to increase revenue contributions from Asia and other regions.

The company, along with the rest of the European chemicals sector, has been held back by rising energy costs and weak demand.

CEO Markus Kamieth said in June that the business environment was at its most difficult in at least the last 25 years, with the global balance of industrial power shifting to Asia.

BASF is at risk of losing its years-long rank as the world's largest company by chemicals revenue to China's Sinopec.

Last year, BASF's group revenue of €59.7 billion ($68.9 billion) was almost the same as that of the chemicals segment of China's Sinopec.

European chemical producers have, however, received a temporary boost because Asian rivals are hit harder by supply disruption linked to the US-Israeli war on Iran.

Kamieth has been seeking to make BASF more focused and to exit or separate businesses that are not closely integrated and physically connected within the group's chemical plants across the globe.

The Financial Times reported earlier that BASF had approached Evonik and its biggest shareholder, the RAG Foundation, about a takeover.

(Reporting by Matthias Inverardi, additional reporting by Rachel More, writing by Ludwig Burger, editing by Christoph Steitz, Louise Heavens and Barbara Lewis)

evidence.title: BASF Ultramid® B3K Enables BOOXit Reusable Transport Boxes for Automated, Digitally Connected Logistics
evidence.text:
BASF Ultramid® B3K Enables BOOXit Reusable Transport Boxes for Automated, Digitally Connected Logistics

BOOXit reusable transport boxes made with Ultramid® B3K: robust, stackable and designed for digital logistics processes. Photo: BASF

(IN BRIEF) BASF’s Ultramid® B3K BK00464 polyamide 6 is being used in BOOXit reusable transport boxes designed for demanding parcel, healthcare and industrial logistics applications. The material combines strength, durability, impact resistance and efficient injection-moulding processing, supporting a lightweight alternative to disposable cardboard packaging and heavier metal containers. BOOXit uses a modular design based on the standard 120 × 80 cm pallet footprint and can be loaded from the front or top, stacked in interlocking configurations through its CLICKit system and handled by robotic systems. The boxes also support continuous tracking, NFC identification and ERP integration, providing a foundation for digitally managed reusable logistics. According to the companies, the containers have a service life exceeding 100 transport cycles and are described as fully recyclable. POLYTEC GROUP manufactures the boxes using large-part injection moulding expertise. Future applications could include temperature-controlled medical and pharmaceutical logistics. The system will be shown publicly for the first time at Fakuma 2026 on BASF’s stand.

(PRESS RELEASE) LUDWIGSHAFEN, 24-Sep-2026 — / EuropaWire / — BASF is supporting a new generation of reusable transport packaging with Ultramid® B3K BK00464 , a high-performance polyamide 6 used in the BOOXit transport box for demanding parcel, healthcare and industrial logistics applications.

The easy-flow PA6 material combines mechanical strength, durability and efficient injection-moulding performance, allowing BOOXit to develop a lightweight reusable transport system intended to replace conventional single-use cardboard packaging and heavier metal containers in selected professional logistics applications.

The BOOXit concept combines BASF’s material technology with a modular box architecture designed for repeated handling, automated logistics processes and digital integration.

The system can be used with or without a lid and can be loaded from either the front or the top. It incorporates a patented locking mechanism and is designed around the standard 120 × 80 cm pallet footprint, enabling integration into established logistics environments.

BASF said Ultramid B3K was selected to help meet the demanding mechanical requirements associated with reusable transport boxes that may be repeatedly stacked, transported and handled by automated systems.

The material is an easy-flow, stabilised and fast-processing injection-moulding grade based on polyamide 6 (PA6). Its processing characteristics and balanced mechanical properties are intended to make it suitable for relatively large technical components.

Transport boxes used in professional industrial and military environments can face substantial mechanical loads and demanding environmental conditions. Long service life, reliable stacking performance and resistance to impact are therefore important design considerations.

BASF said Ultramid B3K provides the material properties required to support the BOOXit system under repeated operational use, including exposure to very low temperatures.

Dr. Peter Entenfellner, CEO and Co-Founder of BOOXit , said BASF’s material supports a transport-box concept combining mechanical robustness, efficient manufacturing and the ability to establish economically viable intelligent reusable logistics systems.

He said material selection becomes particularly important when boxes are repeatedly used, stacked, transported and handled within automated operations because material performance contributes directly to operational reliability.

Beyond the polymer itself, the BOOXit platform incorporates several design features intended to improve flexibility in transport and warehousing.

Its CLICKit stacking system enables boxes to be stacked in an interlocked configuration, including arrangements in which boxes are rotated by 90 degrees to improve load securing.

Different BOOXit sizes can also be stacked together, supporting more flexible use of available logistics space.

The system has been developed with automated handling in mind and can be used with robotic equipment.

BOOXit also incorporates features designed to support digitally managed reusable logistics networks, including continuous tracking, NFC-based identification and integration with enterprise resource planning systems.

Moisture protection and automation compatibility are also incorporated into the design.

According to the companies, BOOXit boxes are designed for a service life exceeding 100 transport cycles and are described as 100% recyclable.

The reusable approach is intended to reduce reliance on disposable cardboard packaging by keeping transport containers in circulation across repeated journeys.

BASF and BOOXit said this can lower the consumption of packaging materials and reduce waste generation and associated carbon emissions compared with repeated use of single-use alternatives, depending on the logistics application and return system.

Longer service life and efficient return logistics are also intended to reduce total lifecycle costs.

The companies see additional potential for reusable, digitally connected transport systems in medical and pharmaceutical logistics.

Possible future applications include transport packaging for temperature-controlled movement of sensitive medical products, diagnostic materials and pharmaceutical goods, where durable containers, traceability and controlled logistics processes can be particularly important.

Production of the BOOXit box is carried out by POLYTEC GROUP, which specialises in plastics processing and the manufacture of large injection-moulded components.

The manufacturing partnership combines BASF’s polymer technology with BOOXit’s logistics-system design and POLYTEC’s large-component injection-moulding capabilities.

The BOOXit transport system will make its trade-show debut at Fakuma 2026, where it will be presented at the BASF booth, B4-4303.

Visitors will be able to examine the reusable transport solution and discuss the properties of Ultramid B3K, potential application areas and the role of digitally connected reusable packaging in professional logistics systems.
