evidence.title: Bayer 04 mourn the loss of Peter Hermann
evidence.text:
Bayer 04 mourn the loss of Peter Hermann

“I owe everything to football.” That’s what Peter Hermann said in March 2025 at the end of the WDR 2 podcast ‘Einfach Fußball’. His voice was already somewhat affected by the neurological condition that had recently confined him to a wheelchair. Anyone listening to this wonderful conversation about the love of football – in which Hermann’s good friend Jürgen Gelsdorf also took part – couldn’t help but catch their breath at that final sentence. “I owe everything to football” – these words were moving because they clearly came from the heart. Because they were an expression of the self-image of a man who was never drawn into the limelight. And yet, of course, the reverse is also true: football owes a great deal to Peter Hermann.

He was the quintessential assistant manager in Germany. More renowned and respected in the sport than many a head coach. An undisputed football expert, Hermann never made a fuss about himself. Down-to-earth, modest, loyal. A man with a great sense of humour and without a trace of vanity. A team player, a meticulous worker and a good listener. Someone who continued to learn even in his later years, remained curious and was always up to date. He inspired players and made them better, treating young talents and established stars with the same respect. “Peter was always there for me,” recalls Bayer 04’s honorary captain Stefan Kießling. “I owe him a great deal. He was an incredibly good motivator and he had many one-to-one conversations with the players because he simply had a great deal of tact.”

Wherever the name Peter Hermann is mentioned, he is spoken of with nothing but the utmost respect. “He had an incredible wealth of expertise. As far as I’m concerned, he’s the best assistant manager there has ever been,” says Klaus Toppmöller, who was runner-up three times with Bayer 04 in the 2001/2002 season, with Hermann at his side.

"a wonderful person with a marvellous character"

Jupp Heynckes once spoke in similarly glowing terms about his colleague, who he met in Leverkusen in 2009. With the Werkself, the pair finished as runners-up in 2011; two years later, the duo won the treble with FC Bayern, securing the Bundesliga title, the DFB Pokal and the Champions League. “Peter is a brilliant person with a wonderful character. He’s very empathetic, connects with players quickly and gains their trust straight away. That’s absolutely, absolutely vital. We understood each other perfectly – he was a great support to me and played a key part in our success in Leverkusen and Munich. Over the years, he’s become a good friend to me.” In 2017, Heynckes also insisted that Hermann should return as his assistant should he take charge of Bayern again. The record champions bought the sought-after assistant manager out of his current contract with Fortuna Düsseldorf for a substantial sum at the time. This, too, was a sign of the enormous respect Hermann enjoyed in Germany. In Munich, he won the German league title again with Heynckes in 2018; a year later, he won the double with Bayern under Niko Kovac.

Peter Hermann was never tempted to take on the role of head coach anywhere. As an assistant coach, however, he was the ideal choice at many clubs for decades – and not just at Bayer 04 and Bayern Munich. Even though the club always held a special place in his heart. He has worked there in so many different roles: as a player, assistant manager, caretaker manager during particularly difficult times, coach of the reserve team and in the scouting department. For almost 30 years, he has helped shape football at the club.

After starting his football career at his local club, FV Engers 04, and a spell at TuS Neuendorf, Hermann made the leap to the Bundesliga at the age of 21, joining Hamburger SV. The attacking midfielder played alongside the likes of Rudi Kargus, Manfred Kaltz and Kaspar Memering in the Hanseatic city. However, he only made two brief appearances for HSV and moved to Alemannia Aachen after a year. Hermann made a flying start at the second-tier side, immediately becoming a first-team regular and he went on to make 71 appearances for the Black and Yellows over two years. Bayer 04, having been promoted to Bundesliga 2 in 1975, signed the then 24-year-old in the summer of 1976 – it was the start of a lifelong association. In Leverkusen, too, Hermann quickly proved himself indispensable. In his very first match under coach Willibert Kremer, the new signing scored to make it 1–1 against VfL Osnabrück. From then on, he was in the starting line-up for all 37 subsequent matches. With just two exceptions, the fit and dynamic attacking player always played the full 90 minutes. By the end of his first season at Bayer 04, he had scored nine goals.

promotion hero and saviour in times of need

During the 1978/79 season, Hermann was one of the heroes of the club’s promotion to the Bundesliga. He contributed to what was, at the time, the greatest success in the club’s history, scoring two goals and providing numerous assists in 28 matches. The team – featuring goalkeeper Fred Bockholt, Jürgen Gelsdorf, Thomas Hörster, Dieter Herzog, Norbert Ziegler, Klaus Bruckmann and Matthias Brücken – remained something of a second family to him. Whenever time allowed, Hermann would attend the regular get-togethers with his former team-mates, many of whom remained among his closest friends even decades after promotion. Jürgen Gelsdorf, for example. “We played together for Bayer 04 for eight years,” recalls the chair of the football department at TSV Bayer 04. “Back then, we still wore our socks pulled down low. As a tireless runner and technically gifted dribbler, Peter went on to become the dedicated marker of the opposition’s playmakers – Paul Breitner could tell you a thing or two about that.” In total, Hermann played 235 competitive matches for the Werkself, scoring 35 goals along the way.

In the end, it was Jürgen Gelsdorf who managed to persuade his friend to join him as assistant manager at Bayer 04 in 1989. Hermann had just brought his playing career at VfL Hamm/Sieg to a close and accepted the offer straight away. “Peter certainly wouldn’t have thought back then that he’d end up doing this job for so long and with such success,” said Gelsdorf. Hermann was indeed to enjoy an even more successful career as an assistant manager than he had as a player. Gelsdorf: “When you look at how many world-class players he’s worked with at all his clubs, how many brilliant managers he’s worked with in a spirit of mutual trust, and how they all speak of him in exclusively positive terms, it’s truly extraordinary. You can only take your hat off to that.”

Following his time with Jürgen Gelsdorf, Hermann worked in Leverkusen as an assistant to managers such as Dragoslav Stepanovic, Erich Ribbeck, Christoph Daum, Berti Vogts, Klaus Toppmöller, Klaus Augenthaler and Michael Skibbe. Whenever the club was in a tight spot, he would step in at short notice as caretaker manager. His most precarious and nerve-wracking spell came in the spring of 1996. Hermann was now solely responsible for the team following the sacking of head coach Erich Ribbeck in the final stages of the season. The mission to avoid relegation was accomplished at the very last moment thanks to a 1–1 draw in the ‘decider’ against Kaiserslautern. “Before the match, Peter gave a very emotional speech that made a deep impression on all of us,” recalls goalkeeping legend Rüdiger Vollborn. “He knew exactly what was at stake. And he made sure we understood that too. We simply couldn’t be relegated.”

Almost exactly 25 years later, Hermann didn’t hesitate for a second when Bayer 04 asked him to step in at short notice as assistant manager under Hannes Wolf. Wolf’s task was to lead the Werkself into a European competition in their final eight matches. “The fact that we did indeed reach the Europa League, as we’d hoped, was also largely down to Peter,” said Rudi Völler, who himself was able to rely on Hermann as his right-hand man in a number of matches whilst serving as Bayer 04’s interim manager. “Peter always had a special connection to Bayer 04,” said Völler.

it was most intense under the bayer cross

Quite true. Even during his subsequent spells at FC Nürnberg, Bayern Munich, Schalke 04, Hamburger SV, Fortuna Düsseldorf, Borussia Dortmund and the DFB, the centre of Hermann’s life always remained Leverkusen-Opladen. That is where he put down roots and started a family. Peter Hermann, born in Kleinmaischeid, Rhineland-Palatinate, in 1952, was a Leverkusen man through and through. But first and foremost, he was someone who loved football. Every club he worked for could be certain of his passion, professionalism and identification with the club. Hermann threw himself into new challenges with the same enthusiasm every time. That is why he was so highly regarded everywhere. And that is why the fans never held his moves to other clubs against him. Even when, in the summer of 2022, at the age of 70, he moved from the ‘Royal Blues’ at Schalke to the ‘Black and Yellows’ at BVB, it wasn’t a problem. His six months as Edin Terzic’s assistant at Borussia Dortmund proved to be his final posting. In December 2022, Hermann had to step down due to ill health. “I really enjoyed my time at all the clubs. It was a wonderful period. But it was under the Bayer Cross that it was the most intense for me,” said Hermann, looking back.

As a regular and welcome guest at the BayArena, he also experienced the historic 2023/24 double-winning season first-hand. Hermann watched all of the Werkself’s home matches alongside Jürgen Gelsdorf. “The crowning glory was, of course, winning the Bundesliga. We actually deserved that title much earlier.” “We” – Hermann always saw himself as part of the Bayer 04 family. And rightly so. Right up until the end, he also felt a close connection to Leverkusen’s youth football. Whenever he could, he went to watch the U17 and U19 matches. And, of course, he was always fully up to speed on the young talents.

Peter Hermann passed away on Saturday at the age of 74. Bayer 04 mourn the loss of a good friend and mentor. Peter will never be forgotten.

Meanwhile, RB Leipzig's lightning start to the season, which saw them plunder nine goals in two matches, looked like a distant memory after comprehensive defeats to Werder Bremen and Italian side Como in successive outings.

However, Die Roten Bullen rediscovered their rhythm when they hosted a wayward Hamburger SV outfit last time out, with Martin Demichelis' men running out 5-0 winners. evidence.title: Bayer and Neste form partnership to scale US winter canola for biofuels production
evidence.text:
Bayer and Neste form partnership to scale US winter canola for biofuels production

German chemical giant Bayer and Finnish renewable fuels producer Neste have agreed to work together to expand the production of winter canola in the USA for use in biofuels production.

The initiative would strengthen the oilseed supply potential of lower carbon-intensity feedstocks to meet growing global demand for biofuels such as renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), the companies said on 9 September.

As part of the agreement, the companies said they would jointly scale Bayer’s newgold winter canola in the US Southern Great Plains region.

High-protein meal from the winter canola grain would be sold into the feed market. offering additional feed sources for dairy and beef cattle, poultry and pig markets.

“In times of geopolitical tensions, the need for more energy security and resilience while decarbonising the transportation sector leads to growing demand for renewable fuel,” said Frank Terhorst, head of strategy and sustainability for Bayer’s Crop Science division.

“We see the Southern Great Plains as an untapped opportunity for winter canola. The launch of newgold winter canola will provide farmers with a profitable rotational crop with wheat and improve land utilisation, while offering the opportunity to participate in a growing biofuels market.”

Bayer said it also planned to launch newgold winter canola hybrids in 2027.

evidence.title: Bayer and Neste Close Commercial Agreement to Jointly Scale newgold® Winter Canola for Biofuels Production
evidence.text:
Bayer and Neste Close Commercial Agreement to Jointly Scale newgold® Winter Canola for Biofuels Production

Commitment aims to support the growth of winter canola in the Southern Great Plains of the U.S., as a feedstock for renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel

MONHEIM, Germany & ST. LOUIS, September 09, 2026 --( BUSINESS WIRE )--Bayer and Neste, the world's leading producer of renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel, have finalized a commercial agreement to jointly scale Bayer's newgold® winter canola.

The collaboration will enable Bayer to significantly expand acres of winter canola in the Southern Great Plains of the US, strengthening the oilseed supply potential of lower-carbon-intensity feedstocks to meet the growing global demand for biofuels such as renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel, which is estimated to increase almost threefold reaching approximately 40 billion gallons by 2040.1,2 The high protein meal from the winter canola grain will be sold into the feed market, offering additional feed sources for dairy and beef cattle, poultry and swine markets.

"In times of geopolitical tensions, the need for more energy security and resilience while decarbonizing the transportation sector leads to growing demand for renewable fuel. This agreement further underscores Bayer's commitment to help scale biofuels production," said Frank Terhorst, Head of Strategy and Sustainability for Bayer's Crop Science division. "We see the Southern Great Plains as an untapped opportunity for winter canola. The launch of newgold® winter canola will provide farmers with a profitable rotational crop with wheat and improve land utilization, while offering the opportunity to participate in a growing biofuels market."

Bayer and Neste are establishing a newgold® network with additional value chain partners, to support the expansion of winter canola and ensure an additional market for farmers.

"Maximizing the contribution of novel types of raw materials to support growth in renewables requires open supply chain collaboration. By building robust value chains, we can turn agricultural innovations into scalable realities for growers and energy markets. Through the Bayer newgold® winter canola collaboration, we are establishing a value chain in one of Neste's key markets and developing opportunities to increase farm yields and grower income. This renewable raw material can be scaled rapidly in the coming years, which can help meet increasing biofuels demand," says Artturi Mikkola, Senior Vice President, Renewable Products Feedstock Sourcing and Trading at Neste.

Bayer aims to launch newgold® winter canola hybrids in the fall of 2027. These hybrids offer farmers several benefits, including winter-hardiness, TruFlex®, Bayer's second-generation Roundup Ready trait technology, and pod shatter resistance technology. Together, these advancements can deliver strong potential for yield performance and higher oil content. TruFlex winter canola, sold under the newgold® seed brand, will be designed with the goal of acting as a new profit opportunity for the Southern Great Plains, giving growers the flexibility to decide how and where it fits best in their operation.

Biofuels can play a key role in helping the transportation sector in its energy transition since electrification may not be feasible in all transportation systems like aviation, rail, heavy duty equipment or marine. Biofuels can be produced from renewable organic materials like corn, soy, canola and other intermediate oilseed crops, such as winter canola. Bayer recently presented its biofuels platform at its investor day in Huxley, IA, where it highlighted its emergent, but leading portfolio of intermediate biofuel crops, including camelina, winter canola and CoverCress™.

1 U.S. Energy Information Administration and Bayer internal estimates 2 McKinsey and Bayer internal estimates.

Bayer is a global enterprise with core competencies in the life science fields of health care and nutrition. In line with its mission, "Health for all, Hunger for none," the company's products and services are designed to help people and the planet thrive by supporting efforts to master the major challenges presented by a growing and aging global population. Bayer is committed to driving sustainable development and generating a positive impact with its businesses. At the same time, the Group aims to increase its earning power and create value through innovation and growth. The Bayer brand stands for trust, reliability and quality throughout the world. In fiscal 2025, the Group employed around 88,000 people and had sales of 45.6 billion euros. R&D expenses amounted to 5.8 billion euros. For more information, go to www.bayer.com .

Neste (NESTE, Nasdaq Helsinki) is the world's leading producer of renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), with production on three continents. The company's renewables production capacity is expected to reach 6.8 million tons annually in 2027. Neste also produces high-quality oil products at its Porvoo refinery in Finland. The company has a network of nearly 1,000 fuel stations with expanding service offering, such as EV charging, in Finland and in the Baltics. Neste's strategy focuses on growth in renewable fuels, which help its customers to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions. Neste is included in many international indices for its sustainability performance. In 2025, Neste's revenue stood at EUR 19.0 billion. Read more: neste.com. evidence.title: Living Security: Human Risk Management Leaders from Reveal Risk, Bayer, and Labcorp to Speak at HRMCon 2026
evidence.text:
Living Security: Human Risk Management Leaders from Reveal Risk, Bayer, and Labcorp to Speak at HRMCon 2026

Enterprise CISOs and cybersecurity leaders will share real-world lessons for strengthening Workforce Security, advancing Security Behavior Management, and reducing risk across humans and AI agents

AUSTIN, TX / ACCESS Newswire / August 31, 2026 / Living Security, the global leader in Human Risk Management (HRM), today announced the full speaker roster for HRMCon 2026 , its annual Human Risk Management conference taking place September 10 in Austin, Texas, with a live virtual broadcast available worldwide.

The lineup brings together enterprise practitioners, analysts, cybersecurity strategists, and workforce security leaders from Forrester, Bayer, Labcorp, Reveal Risk, Cybersecurity Insights, and Living Security. Through real-world case studies and strategic discussions, speakers will examine how organizations are building, funding, and operationalizing Human Risk Management programs to reduce cyber risk across employees, privileged users, contractors, and AI agents.

"Security leaders need more than theories about Human Risk Management-they need to understand what it takes to build these programs in the real world," said Ashley Rose, CEO and Co-Founder of Living Security. "This year's speakers will share the decisions, obstacles, data challenges, and business cases behind their programs, giving attendees actionable ideas they can apply within their own organizations."

Enterprise Human Risk Management Leaders Share What Works

Jinan Budge, Vice President and Research Director at Forrester, providing an independent market outlook on Human Risk Management, changing buyer priorities, and the impact of AI-enabled attacks.

Damon DePaolo of CVS Health, sharing insights from building Human Risk Management programs, including how to align stakeholders, validate assumptions with a live-data proof of concept, and establish success criteria that earn organizational support.

Jennifer Miller of Bayer , explaining how Bayer expanded workforce risk visibility across more than half of its workforce in six months without waiting for a perfect data environment.

Ashley Atiles and Alfonso Mancuso of Labcorp , discussing how behavioral intelligence strengthened phishing-resistant multifactor authentication by revealing user friction, workarounds, resistance, and trust gaps.

Aaron Pritz and Jim Wailes of Reveal Risk , showing how security teams can reduce risk by redesigning high-risk business workflows and making secure behavior easier.

Matthew Rosenquist of Cybersecurity Insights , examining the future of autonomous prevention, adaptive controls, and human accountability as AI agents become part of the workforce.

Gary S. Chan, Security Mentalist and CISO , delivering an interactive closing keynote on the psychology of deception, influence, trust, and security decision-making.

The conference will also feature Living Security CEO Ashley Rose and Living Security leaders Kelly Harward and Mike Siegel, who will examine how Human Risk Management must evolve as workforce identities, access patterns, and attack pathways expand beyond employees and email.

Workforce Security Lessons from Complex Enterprises

Speakers will address some of the most persistent challenges facing enterprise cybersecurity and Workforce Security leaders, including:

Building an enterprise business case for Human Risk Management

Aligning security, identity, compliance, and business stakeholders

Advancing from security awareness training to Security Behavior Management

Applying behavioral intelligence to identity and access controls

Connecting workforce risk signals to real-time security actions

Launching an HRM program with a few critical data sources and expanding over time

Measuring reductions in cyber incidents rather than activities alone

Governing access and accountability across humans and AI agents

The sessions will give CISOs, security practitioners, identity leaders, GRC professionals, and Human Risk Management teams actionable guidance for implementing and scaling HRM in complex enterprise environments.

Human Risk Management for Humans and AI Agents

As AI agents and autonomous systems gain access to enterprise data, applications, and workflows, Workforce Security is expanding beyond employee behavior. Security teams must increasingly assess risk across human and non-human identities while establishing clear governance, access controls, accountability, and measurable security outcomes.

HRMCon 2026 will examine how organizations can combine behavioral, identity, and threat intelligence to identify elevated workforce risk, prioritize interventions, and strengthen security controls before incidents occur.

HRMCon 2026 will be held September 10, 2026, at The University of Texas Club in Austin, Texas, with a live virtual broadcast available to attendees worldwide.

View the full HRMCon 2026 agenda and register to attend in person or virtually at: HRMCon 2026 Human Risk Management Conference

Living Security is the global leader in Human Risk Management (HRM), helping organizations identify, measure, and reduce workforce cyber risk across humans and AI agents. Its AI-native Human Risk Management platform combines behavioral, identity, and threat intelligence to predict risk, guide response, and prevent cyber incidents before they occur. By connecting security data to measurable business outcomes, Living Security enables organizations to continuously reduce workforce risk while strengthening organizational resilience.

evidence.title: Bio-Techne Shareholders Approve Acquisition by Merck KGaA
evidence.text:
Bio-Techne Corporation (NASDAQ: TECH ) ("Bio-Techne"), a global provider of life science tools, reagents and diagnostic products, announced that Bio-Techne shareholders voted to approve and adopt the definitive agreement under which Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany proposes to acquire Bio-Techne (the "Merger Agreement") at a Special Meeting of Shareholders.

"We are grateful to our shareholders for their strong support, which marks an important milestone toward completing the transaction," said Kim Kelderman, President and Chief Executive Officer of Bio-Techne. "Joining Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany will bring together our complementary and leading life sciences organizations while delivering substantial, near-term cash value to Bio-Techne shareholders. Bio-Techne Shareholders Approve Acquisition by Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany

MINNEAPOLIS, Sept. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Bio-Techne Corporation (NASDAQ: TECH) ("Bio-Techne"), a global provider of life science tools, reagents and diagnostic products, announced that Bio-Techne shareholders voted to approve and adopt the definitive agreement under which Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany proposes to acquire Bio-Techne (the "Merger Agreement") at a Special Meeting of Shareholders held today.

"We are grateful to our shareholders for their strong support, which marks an important milestone toward completing the transaction," said Kim Kelderman, President and Chief Executive Officer of Bio-Techne. "Joining Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany will bring together our complementary and leading life sciences organizations while delivering substantial, near-term cash value to Bio-Techne shareholders. The combined company will be uniquely positioned to support customers across the full spectrum of life science workflows from discovery and translational research through development, testing and commercial manufacturing."

The final voting results, as certified by the independent inspector of elections, will be reported in a Form 8-K filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC").

In addition to shareholder approval, the waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended, in connection with the proposed transaction expired at 11:59 p.m., Eastern Time, on September 18, 2026. Bio-Techne continues to expect the transaction to close by late 2026 or early 2027, subject to satisfaction of customary closing conditions, including receipt of remaining required regulatory approvals.

About Bio-Techne Bio Techne Corporation (NASDAQ: TECH) is a global life sciences company headquartered in Minnesota, celebrating 50 years of empowering scientific and diagnostic communities to reach better answers. The company provides high quality reagents, analytical instruments, and precision diagnostics. Its portfolio is organized into three customer focused brands: R&D Systems™, Bio Techne Spatial™, and Bio Techne Diagnostics™, reflecting the scientific journey from discovery to translational research to clinical decision making. Bio Techne operates in 34 locations worldwide and employs more than 3,000 people. In fiscal year 2025, the company generated over $1.2 billion in net sales. Its more than 500,000 products are used globally by academic researchers, biopharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, and clinical diagnostic laboratories.

evidence.title: Merck KGaA expands life science manufacturing hub in Bengaluru
evidence.text:
Merck KGaA expands life science manufacturing hub in Bengaluru

The move is the latest in a growing list of investments geared at bolstering India’s global footprint.

German life science and pharmaceutical company Merck KGaA has announced an expansion of its manufacturing facility in Bengaluru, India, to strengthen its production and supply operations in the Asia-Pacific region.

Dhananjay Singh, managing director of Merck India’s Life Science business, said the company will invest €13 million (about US$15 million) in its Jigani, Bengaluru site to expand its biology and chemistry capabilities.

According to a press release, the Jigani site will manufacture biological buffers and raw materials for diagnostic applications used in DNA research, cell culture, diagnostics, and drug manufacturing.

The expansion will add about 2,900 square meters of new capabilities to Merck’s 40,460 square-meter campus. The site already has established capabilities in specialty and fine chemicals, custom synthesis, and catalog product manufacturing.

“This investment will reinforce our global supply chain and support the ‘Make in India’ initiative,” Singh said. “We appreciate the continued collaboration from DPIIT, the Heavy Water Board, the Government of Karnataka, and Invest India as Merck expands Jigani.”

Related: Altruist Biologics preps for production following EMA GMP certification

The country launched its Make in India initiative in 2014 to support its growth as a global design and manufacturing hub.

“Merck’s Bengaluru manufacturing hub shows what the India–Germany partnership can achieve when world-class German enterprise meets India's manufacturing ambition,” added Shri Amardeep Singh Bhatia, IAS, secretary to the government of India, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry. “In the year we celebrate 75 years of diplomatic relations, Merck will make advanced materials in Bengaluru for pharmaceutical research and semiconductor manufacturing, for India and for the world, in the true spirit of Make in India.”

“India is emerging as an increasingly important hub for life science innovation and manufacturing,” said Singh during his remarks about the Merck expansion.

Indeed, the South Asian country is becoming one of the most exciting global biotech hubs to follow. In addition to attracting international investment from industry giants such as Merck, India is headquarters to a growing ecosystem of homegrown companies that are making big moves. Earlier this week, contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) Shilpa Biologicals announced a biosimilar licensing agreement with Saudi Arabia-based SPIMACO Bio. And as part of an effort to accelerate peptide manufacturing, Hyderabad-based Neuland Laboratories recently announced that its first commercial peptide manufacturing module is now operational, with further expansion in its capacity underway.

Related: Shilpa Biologicals signs MENA licensing agreement for PD-1 inhibitor biosimilars with SPIMACO Bio

evidence.title: Henkel’s investment in Egypt exceeds $113.8mln over 34 years
evidence.text:
Henkel’s investment in Egypt exceeds $113.8mln over 34 years

Henkel said it continues to invest in employee development. Women account for 55.7% of Henkel Egypt’s workforce and 57.6% of its managerial positions

Arab Finance: Henkel has invested more than €100 million in Egypt over the past 34 years, the company said as its Egyptian business marked Henkel’s 150th anniversary at Cairo’s Qubba Palace, as per an emailed press release.

The celebration brought together Henkel Egypt employees and leaders with members of the company’s global and regional leadership, including Wolfgang König, Executive Vice President Consumer Brands; Ashraf ElAfifi, President of Henkel IMEA and Corporate Senior Vice President for Henkel Consumer Brands in the High Growth Region; Ahmed Nasser, Vice President of Henkel Consumer Brands for the Middle East, North Africa and Turkey and Head of Regional Sales; and Sherif Khalil, Managing Director and President of Henkel Egypt.

“Egypt is an important strategic market for Henkel. Over the past 34 years, our investments have exceeded €100 million, clearly reflecting our confidence in the potential of the Egyptian market and our long-term commitment to the country. Today, we see Egypt not only as a promising market, but also as an important hub for production, talent and services within Henkel’s global network,” Khalil said.

Henkel Egypt’s consumer brands include Pril, Persil and Palette. In 2025, it added Schwarzkopf’s Gliss hair care line and Perwoll, a laundry care brand focused on fabric care and color protection. The company said it continues to invest in innovation and production capabilities at its 6th of October City plant to respond to changing consumer needs.

Khalil also outlined the company’s ambitions for its Egyptian operations: “As we look to the next chapter, we aspire to continue growing, expand our exports and strengthen Egypt’s role as an export hub for African markets, building on its strategic location, industrial base and outstanding talent. Our 34-year journey in Egypt is a story of trust, commitment and the ability to evolve. We have continued to operate, invest and grow through different periods and numerous challenges, with our employees, partners and the trust of Egyptian consumers always at the heart of this journey. Today, as we celebrate 150 years of Henkel, we are proud of what we have built in Egypt, but even more excited about what lies ahead. Our message is clear: we are here to stay, grow, innovate and continue contributing to shaping the future of the categories in which we operate in the Egyptian market.”

Egypt’s role in Henkel’s network extends beyond manufacturing. Established in 2014 as a small regional team, its Global Business Solutions (GBS) center in Cairo now employs more than 300 people and serves more than 75 countries in eight languages. Egyptian professionals also hold roles across other markets in the company’s global network.

Henkel said it continues to invest in employee development. Women account for 55.7% of Henkel Egypt’s workforce and 57.6% of its managerial positions.

On sustainability, the company said production operations at its 6th of October City plant have been carbon-neutral since 2024, helping avoid approximately 1,900 metric tons of CO? emissions a year. Its work in Egypt also includes youth development through collaborations with universities, institutions and civil society organizations, as well as community initiatives.

Henkel has also contributed its adhesive expertise to the restoration of King Tutankhamun’s golden mask. The company chose the historic Qubba Palace for the anniversary celebration as a setting that connects its 150-year history with Egypt’s cultural heritage.

evidence.title: Henkel To Significantly Expand Its Global STEM Initiative Researchers' World
evidence.text:
Henkel To Significantly Expand Its Global STEM Initiative Researchers' World

Henkel will invest a double-digit million-euro amount by 2030 to establish five new permanent Researchers' World locations worldwide, including a new STEM center in Düsseldorf, Germany.

Researchers' World is Henkel's global education initiative that gives children hands-on access to science and STEM education

The initiative builds on 15 years of experience, activities in over 20 countries and the participation of more than 130,000 children worldwide

The expansion aims to lower barriers and strengthen equal access to STEM education for children around the world

DÜSSELDORF, DE / ACCESS Newswire / September 23, 2026 / On the occasion of its 150th anniversary, Henkel is taking its long-standing commitment to science education to the next level. By the end of 2030, the company plans to establish five new permanent learning labs as part of its "Researchers' World" initiative (in German: Forscherwelt): a new STEM center at Henkel's headquarters in Düsseldorf and four additional Researchers' World labs around the world. In addition, mobile concepts will bring hands-on science education to children in six additional countries. Henkel will invest a double-digit million-euro amount in the expansion of Researchers' World by 2030.

"Curiosity and a spirit of discovery are essential drivers of learning and innovation. Through our Researchers' World initiative, we encourage children to ask questions, explore new ideas and develop their own solutions. By expanding the initiative internationally, we want to make high-quality STEM education accessible to as many young people as possible, regardless of their socioeconomic background," says Dr. Simone Bagel-Trah, patron of Henkel's Researchers' World and Chairwoman of Henkel's Supervisory Board and Shareholders' Committee.

"As Henkel celebrates its 150th anniversary, we are expanding our Researchers' World initiative to enable even more children to experience science, technology and innovation first-hand. We also want to reach young people who have had limited access to these opportunities so far. This project reflects our long-term commitment to social responsibility as a company, both as part of our anniversary year and beyond. We believe that education is an investment in the future of society, which is why we are committed to making a lasting contribution in this area," says Carsten Knobel, CEO of Henkel.

A global platform for curiosity, skills and equal opportunity

Founded in Düsseldorf in 2011, Researchers' World has developed into a global education initiative that promotes early STEM education in more than 20 countries across Asia, Africa, the Middle East, Europe, North America and South America. Through hands-on experiments and age-appropriate learning formats, children explore scientific concepts and discover the world of science through inquiry, experimentation and problem-solving. Since its launch, more than 130,000 children worldwide have participated in the program. As part of its expansion plans, Henkel aims to extend Researchers' World to more than 30 countries by 2030.

Düsseldorf as one of the five new permanent locations

Henkel will build a new STEM center at its headquarters in Düsseldorf. It will expand the existing concept and location with extracurricular formats, a wider target group, and dedicated access for external visitors. The center is expected to accommodate more than 10,000 children and young people annually. As one of the five new permanent locations, the Düsseldorf center will form part of a wider global network.

"By expanding our global network, we aim to further reduce financial and organizational barriers to STEM education and create accessible learning opportunities for children from different socioeconomic backgrounds and educational pathways," explains Dr. Ute Krupp, who is responsible for the Researchers' World initiative at Henkel. "Our learning programs support scientific literacy, critical thinking, collaboration and creativity - skills that help young people understand and shape a changing world."

Further information and free teaching materials are available at www.henkel-researchers-world.com

About Henkel With its brands, innovations and technologies, Henkel holds leading market positions worldwide in the industrial and consumer businesses. The business unit Adhesive Technologies is the global leader in the market for adhesives, sealants and coatings. With Consumer Brands, the company holds leading positions especially in laundry & home care and hair in many markets and categories around the world. The company's three strongest brands are Loctite, Persil and Schwarzkopf. In fiscal 2025, Henkel reported sales of about 20.5 billion euros and adjusted operating profit of around 3.0 billion euros. Henkel's preferred shares are listed in the German stock index DAX. Sustainability has a long tradition at Henkel, and the company has a clear sustainability strategy with specific targets. Henkel was founded in 1876 and today employs a diverse team of about 50,000 people worldwide - united by a strong corporate culture, shared values and a common purpose: "Pioneers at heart for the good of generations." More information at www.henkel.com

evidence.title: Henkel Celebrates 150th Anniversary With Global Employee Events, Special Benefits and Expanded STEM Education Initiative
evidence.text:
Henkel Celebrates 150th Anniversary With Global Employee Events, Special Benefits and Expanded STEM Education Initiative

The anniversary celebrations brought employees together to celebrate 150 years of Henkel.

(IN BRIEF) Henkel is celebrating its 150th anniversary on 26 September 2026 with employee events worldwide, special workforce benefits and an expansion of its Researchers’ World STEM education programme. Founded by Fritz Henkel in Germany in 1876 as a small detergent business, the company now employs around 50,000 people in more than 70 countries. A major anniversary festival at Henkel’s Düsseldorf headquarters is expected to attract around 18,000 employees and family members. All employees will receive an additional day of leave during their birthday month, while participants in Henkel’s employee share programme will receive a one-time 41% anniversary bonus on their personal investment in Henkel shares. Henkel is also expanding Researchers’ World, which has already reached more than 130,000 children in over 20 countries. By the end of 2030, the company plans five new permanent learning locations, including a STEM centre in Düsseldorf, as well as mobile programmes in six additional countries. Henkel plans to invest a double-digit million-euro amount in the initiative over the coming years.

(PRESS RELEASE) DÜSSELDORF, 22-Sep-2026 — / EuropaWire / — Henkel is marking its 150th anniversary on 26 September 2026 with employee events around the world, special anniversary benefits for its workforce and an expansion of its global Researchers’ World STEM education initiative.

The company traces its origins to 26 September 1876 , when Fritz Henkel founded a small detergent factory in Germany. Today, Henkel employs around 50,000 people in more than 70 countries and operates internationally across industrial and consumer markets.

Dr. Simone Bagel-Trah, Chairwoman of Henkel’s Supervisory Board and Shareholders’ Committee , said the development from a small start-up into a global company was made possible by generations of employees who took responsibility and demonstrated a pioneering spirit.

Carsten Knobel, Chief Executive Officer of Henkel , said the company’s employees have been central to its development over the past 150 years through their ideas, expertise and commitment. He said the anniversary is therefore primarily an occasion to recognise Henkel’s teams worldwide while looking ahead to the company’s future.

Throughout the anniversary year, Henkel is organising events and activities for employees across its operations in more than 70 countries.

One of the largest celebrations will take place at the company’s headquarters in Düsseldorf, Germany, on 26 September, where approximately 18,000 employees and family members are expected to attend an anniversary festival.

The programme will give visitors opportunities to explore Henkel’s businesses, innovations and 150-year history and will include entertainment, family activities and a concert produced specifically for the anniversary.

Henkel is also providing special benefits to employees worldwide as part of the milestone.

All employees will receive one additional day of leave during their birthday month.

Employees participating in Henkel’s employee share programme will also receive a one-time anniversary bonus of 41% on their personal investment in Henkel shares, giving participating employees an enhanced opportunity to share in the company’s performance.

Henkel is using the anniversary to expand its social engagement in science, technology, engineering and mathematics education.

The company plans to further develop its Henkel Researchers’ World initiative, which has provided hands-on STEM learning opportunities for children for more than 15 years.

Researchers’ World currently operates in more than 20 countries across Asia, Africa, the Middle East, Europe, North America and South America and has reached more than 130,000 children.

By the end of 2030, Henkel plans to establish five new permanent Researchers’ World learning locations.

These will include a new STEM centre at the company’s Düsseldorf headquarters and four additional permanent locations in other countries.

Henkel will also introduce mobile concepts designed to extend hands-on science education to children in six additional countries.

The company plans to invest a double-digit million-euro amount in the expansion of Researchers’ World over the coming years.

Henkel was originally founded in Aachen, Germany, in 1876 before relocating its headquarters to Düsseldorf several years later.

evidence.title: Henkel celebrates 150 years with employees around the world
evidence.text:
Henkel celebrates 150 years with employees around the world

150 years ago, on September 26, 1876, Fritz Henkel founded a small detergent factory in Germany. Today, Henkel employs around 50,000 people in more than 70 countries. The company is celebrating this milestone anniversary with events for employees around the world. �My great-great-grandfather could hardly have imagined 150 years ago that one day 50,000 employees across the globe would celebrate this anniversary together. His small start-up has grown into a global company. This was possible because generations of people at Henkel have taken responsibility and demonstrated a pioneering spirit,� said Dr. Simone Bagel-Trah, Chairwoman of Henkel�s Supervisory Board and Shareholders� Committee. �Remaining successful over a period of 150 years cannot be taken for granted. The people at Henkel have always been and continue to be the decisive factor: employees whose ideas, expertise and dedication have continuously moved our company forward. This anniversary is therefore first and foremost their anniversary and an opportunity to thank our teams around the world. Together, we want to continue embracing change with courage and successfully shape Henkel�s future,� said Henkel CEO Carsten Knobel.

Henkel employs people in more than 70 countries. Throughout its anniversary year, the company is bringing employees together at events and activities at locations around the world. The celebrations reflect the company�s international footprint and recognize the commitment of its global teams. One of the largest anniversary events will take place at Henkel�s headquarters in D�sseldorf, Germany, on September 26. Around 18,000 employees and their family members are expected to attend the festival. Across the site, visitors will be able to explore Henkel�s businesses, innovations and 150 years of company history. The program will also feature live entertainment, activities for families and a concert exclusively produced for the anniversary celebration.

Henkel is marking the anniversary with special benefits for employees worldwide. All employees receive an additional day of leave during their birthday month. In addition, participants in Henkel�s employee share program receive a one-time anniversary bonus of 41 percent on their personal investment in Henkel shares, providing employees with an enhanced opportunity to participate in the company�s success.

As part of its 150th anniversary, Henkel is further strengthening its social commitment through STEM education. Building on more than 15 years of experience with its �Henkel Researchers� World� initiative, the company is expanding the program to provide hands-on STEM learning opportunities to even more children worldwide. The initiative is already active in more than 20 countries across Asia, Africa, the Middle East, Europe, North and South America, with more than 130,000 children having participated in its activities to date. By the end of 2030, Henkel plans to establish five new permanent Researchers� World learning locations: a new STEM center at its headquarters in D�sseldorf and four additional locations in other countries. Mobile concepts will further extend the initiative�s reach by bringing hands-on science education to children in six additional countries. Henkel will invest a double-digit million-euro amount in the expansion of Researchers� World in the coming years.

Henkel was founded in Aachen, Germany, in 1876 and relocated its headquarters to D�sseldorf a few years later. From its beginnings as a small detergent manufacturer, the company developed into an international business with leading market positions and strong brands such as Loctite, Persil and Schwarzkopf. Henkel�s history has been shaped by entrepreneurial spirit, innovation, international expansion and the ability to respond to changing social, economic and technological conditions. Today, the company holds leading positions in both its industrial and consumer businesses, with Adhesive Technologies as a global leader in adhesives, sealants and coatings, and Consumer Brands holding leading positions in many markets and categories worldwide. The independent study � Henkel: From Detergent Manufacturer to Global Player � by Professor Dr. Joachim Scholtyseck provides a comprehensive academic account of Henkel�s history. The book examines the company�s development from its foundation to the present day and was published by C.H.Beck in July 2026. Beiersdorf announces share buyback, sees 2026 margin slightly below 2025

Published by Global Banking & Finance Review

Beiersdorf launches a €750 million share buyback over two years and forecasts 2026 core EBIT margin slightly below 2025, citing cost pressures and FX headwinds, while organic sales are seen flat to slightly up.

Nivea-maker Beiersdorf's 2026 margin forecast disappoints investors

Beiersdorf's Financial Outlook and Market Reaction

March 3 (Reuters) - Shares in Beiersdorf dropped more than 12% on Tuesday after the Nivea-maker forecast a slightly lower 2026 core operating profit margin the night before, disappointing already cautious investors.

The German consumer goods group expects 2026 sales to be flat or grow slightly on an organic basis, while its operating margin, excluding special items, is expected to be slightly below last year's 14.0%. It said raw material cost increases and unfavourable foreign exchange effects would weigh on the results.

While the market had expected a cautious outlook, no growth and the potential for falling margins was a negative surprise, a local trader said. Analysts from J.P. Morgan also said the outlook was disappointing.

The group said it expected first-quarter results to come in below the full-year range, citing disruptions in the U.S. retail and China travel retail landscapes.

Competitor L'Oreal had also reported problems in Chinese travel retail for the fourth quarter of 2025, but said the country had made a return to positive luxury consumption .

As of Monday's close, Beiersdorf's shares were up more than 11% this year, outperforming the broader sector which was up around 9%. Those gains were wiped off on Tuesday.

The company said on Monday it would launch a share buyback programme of up to 750 million euros ($877 million) over the next two years.

The group's sales rose 2.5% organically to 9.9 billion euros in 2025, but sales of its flagship Nivea brand grew only 0.9%. Earnings before interest and taxes , excluding special factors, rose slightly to 1.38 billion euros.

Jefferies said in a note Nivea's weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter growth would raise concerns over what was required to improve performance at the core brand.

Beiersdorf plans to refocus Nivea on its popular face care products at a more accessible price range, as these products perform well in specific local markets, while broadening its range of deodorants and body care products, group CEO Vincent Warnery said in a call on Tuesday.

Skin in the AI game: Beiersdorf Ventures invests in AI biology platform Turbine

As a co-investor in the USD 25 million Series B round, Beiersdorf AG is signalling that artificial intelligence is becoming strategically important for skin research. The Hamburg-based group is participating through its venture unit in the AI biotech Turbine, founded in Budapest and now also headquartered in London.

With its USD 25 million investment in the Series B financing, Beiersdorf underlines once again the growing strategic relevance of AI for skin science. The round is led by Interactive Venture Partners, with further participation from Accel and MSD Global Health Innovation.

Turbine pursues a radically data-driven approach: the company virtualises biological experiments using a “Virtual Cell” model. At its core is an AI-powered platform that digitally replicates experimental assays and enables simulations at scale. Via a no-code interface (“Virtual Lab”), pharma researchers can test millions of hypotheses in silico before only selected candidates proceed to wet-lab validation. The system is based on proprietary perturbation datasets that are continuously expanded and used to fine-tune the model in a “lab-in-the-loop” approach. AI is therefore not an add-on, but the integral backbone of the technology.

For Beiersdorf, the investment fits strategically. In recent years, the group has been selectively backing deep-tech approaches in skin biology, active ingredient research and digital diagnostics. Investments have included data-driven skin analysis start-ups and biotech platforms aimed at identifying novel targets or enabling personalised skincare. With Turbine, a technology is added that could simulate how active ingredients interact with skin cells, inflammatory pathways or safety parameters – potentially accelerating and refining product development.

At the same time, Turbine is expanding its footprint in the pharmaceutical industry. According to the company, it already collaborates with major players such as Merck & Co. , AstraZeneca and Bayer AG . Virtual assays have reportedly been deployed across more than 30 discovery programmes to prioritise drug combinations and rationalise experimental design.

With the new capital, Turbine is now broadening its previously oncology-focused offering into immunology. At the same time, it has announced a partnership with an undisclosed top 10 pharmaceutical company. An early beta tester was Ono Pharmaceutical , at a time when the Hungarian-founded firm had already raised around USD 25 million in several tranches between 2022 and 2023 in its first financing round.

The platform aims to model immune cell behaviour based on proprietary datasets and to systematically identify combination therapies, an area that, due to its biological complexity, is increasingly difficult to address through experimental approaches alone.

For Beiersdorf, the investment highlights how even a traditional consumer goods company increasingly views AI-driven systems biology as a strategic tool – not only for pharma, but potentially also for the next generation of scientifically substantiated skincare products.

evidence.title: Beiersdorf’s share price plunges after Nivea-maker lowers 2025 sales forecast
evidence.text:
Beiersdorf’ s share price has plunged after lowering its sales forecast for the year due to “more difficult market challenges” in the second half.

The personal care giant’s stock tumbled by as much as 12% in early trading on the German stock exchange on Wednesday (6 August), as it warned of lower growth due to economic uncertainty, cautious consumer spending and tariff unpredictability.

Organic sales growth for the full 2025 financial year in its consumer business, which includes Nivea , Eucerin and Coppertone , is expected to be between 3% and 4% – down from the 4% to 6% previously expected.

EBIT margin is expected to increase by 20 basis points above the previous year’s levels of 13.4%, a reduction from the 50 basis points the company had previously forecast.

Overall, the business expects sales of around 3%, with forecasts for its Tesa business unchanged.

The company said in a statement that the downgrade was due to “the challenges and volatile developments in large areas of the world” which are “causing a high degree of uncertainty in the markets”.

The downgraded outlook came in Beiersdorf’s latest financial results, which showed organic sales growth for the group of 2.1% to €5.2bn in the first half of the year.

Consumer business sales hit €4.3bn, up 1.9%, driven mainly by double-digit growth in the derma segments and “breakthrough innovations” across all regions.

Mass market growth was slower than expected in the first half of the year “due to broader economic uncertainties," the company said.

Nivea showed “modest performance in slower markets and against strong prior-year comparison”, the company said.

The brand’s sales grew 1% organically and declined 1.2% nominally to €2.9m.

In luxury, La Priarie ’s sales fell 10.7% organically and 10.8% nominally in the first half to €243m.

However, the second quarter “showed encouraging dynamics” with organic sales growth down by only 1.5%, with 3% growth in China driven by its ecommerce business, which grew sales by 36%.

Chantecaille delivered “outstanding double-digit sales growth of 16.1%”.

Derma brands Eucerin and Aquaphor continued to outperform the market “in a slower-growing derma market, which underscores the strength of Beiersdorf’s innovation pipeline”.

Organic sales in the derma business grew 12.2% organically and 10.5% nominally to €790m.

Beiersdorf said that it expects its innovation pipeline to accelerate growth in the second half, however, and it will not reduce its marketing spend “to ensure continued investments in the upcoming strategic launches”.

This includes the launch of Nivea Epigenetics Serum with Epicelline, which is expected to boost sales.

“In the first half of 2025, Beiersdorf delivered a solid performance,” said Vincent Warnery, CEO of Beiersdorf.

“However, the global skin care market experienced a slower growth than expected, particularly in the second quarter and into July 2025.

“This is why we adjusted our guidance for the group and the consumer business segment for the full year of 2025.

“Nevertheless, we expect to accelerate growth in the second half driven by our strong innovation pipeline.

“Validated by the successful performance of Epicelline in our Eucerin brand, the launch of the Nivea Epigenetics Serum is expected to contribute significantly to our business in the second half of 2025 and bring Nivea back to its stronger growth path.”

Recently launched product ranges such as Nivea Luminous630 Skin Glow and Derma Control antiperspirant are also expected to boost sales in the latter half of the year.

On a call with investors, Warnery said that in addition to the mass market slowdown, former growth drivers have “slowed significantly” – particularly emerging markets and Eastern Europe – “with market value growth moving from double digit to mid-single digit, and volume growth in emerging markets declining from mid-single digit to nearly zero”.

“This was due to economic uncertainties and more cautious consumer spending,” he added.

“The unpredictable nature of US tariffs has been adding further uncertainty.”

evidence.title: Linde Has Quietly Compounded for Years. These 3 Stocks Share Its Stickiest Advantage
evidence.text:
Linde Has Quietly Compounded for Years. These 3 Stocks Share Its Stickiest Advantage

Some companies grow quietly because their customers physically cannot leave them, and four stocks have turned that structural trap into decades of compounding returns most investors overlook entirely.

Boring is a portfolio construction choice. Consider that Linde ( NASDAQ:LIN | LIN Price Prediction ) has raised its quarterly dividend every year in the recorded history from $0.825 in December 2018 to $1.60 in 2026, while quietly compounding at 61.42% over five years. The four names below share a specific structural feature: their customers are physically or contractually tethered. A gas plant sits inside a semiconductor fab’s fence line. A safety mark is molded into a product. A technician is stationed at the refinery. Leaving means re-engineering the relationship, not filing a change order.

Linde: Air Separation Units Behind the Fence Line

Linde is the world’s largest industrial gas supplier. Its on-site business builds air separation and hydrogen units on customer property under take-or-pay contracts that run for years, sometimes decades. The customer does not switch suppliers because the supplier’s plant is bolted to their site. In the second quarter, sale-of-gas backlog reached a record $8.1 billion after adding $1 billion of new electronics wins, with total project backlog of $11.00B.

Margin history is the pricing-power evidence. Q2 2026 operating margin was 29.5% with return on capital of 23.5%, and reported pricing rose 2%, broad-based across all geographies, generally tracking local inflation. On durability, the dividend has stepped up every year on record, reaching a trailing 12-month total of $6.30. Risk: the U.S. home-care business (LinkCare) is dragging margins, and management is evaluating strategic options while cost inflation continues to bite.

Air Products: Contracts Measured in Decades

Air Products ( NYSE:APD ) runs the same behind-the-fence model as Linde. It builds, owns, and operates air separation and hydrogen facilities for refineries, chemical plants, and semiconductor fabs. Recent commitments include four air separation units and underground pipeline systems for a Taiwan semiconductor customer, and a Samsung deal for multiple production facilities in South Korea. The traditional industrial gas backlog stands at approximately $3 billion, and management is targeting roughly $1.5 billion per year in project capex going forward.

On pricing, Q3 2026 adjusted operating margin was 25.6%, with 110 bps of margin expansion, and adjusted EPS was $3.47 versus $3.34 estimated. The dividend record is the clearer durability signal: quarterly payments extend from 1999 through 2026, with the per-share amount rising from $0.18 in 1999 to $1.81 in 2026 (that kind of multi-decade raise streak is exactly what we screened for in our free Dividend Kings guide ). Shares carry a beta of 0.924 for the group’s smallest name, while APD itself has returned 17.41% year to date. Risk: management just recorded a $2.9 billion pre-tax charge exiting the Louisiana Clean Energy Complex and the Casa Grande Arizona project, a real capital-allocation stumble on the clean-energy megaproject strategy.

UL Solutions: A Certification Mark That Locks In Retesting

UL Solutions ( NYSE:ULS ) is the independent safety-science firm behind the UL Mark. Once a product carries the mark, changing certifiers means retesting entire product lines, and customers are enrolled in ongoing surveillance programs that recur every quarter. Ongoing Certification Services generated $270M in Q2 26, versus $237M in Certification Testing and $248M in Non-cert Testing & Other. Retesting also travels with product change: when input costs rise, CEO Jenny Scanlon noted, customers “value engineer that product and redesign it or change your formulations,” and that “frequently leads to retesting of that product.”

Margin trend supports the pricing thesis. Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 140 bps to 26.8%, and full-year 2026 is guided to about 27.0%. Adjusted EPS was $0.59. Shares trade at a P/E of 27. On dividends, ULS is a young public company; the record shows quarterly payments rising from $0.125 in 2024 to $0.145 in 2026, an emerging pattern rather than an aristocrat pedigree. Risk: management flagged geopolitical uncertainty and China regulatory exposure, and the pending ~€575M acquisition of Eurofins’ Electrical & Electronics testing business still requires regulatory approval.

Mistras Group: Technicians Stationed at the Refinery

Mistras Group ( NYSE:MG ) is the small-cap in the roster and the most operational. It runs non-destructive testing, inspection, and monitoring programs on pipelines, refineries, aircraft components, power infrastructure, and bridges. Its Integrated Field Solutions business, essentially technicians stationed on customer sites running continuous asset-integrity programs, generated $164.2M of $193.1M in Q2 26 revenue. Management described the recurring nature of the work directly: “Our proprietary technology solutions, including the ARC crawler, monitoring technologies, and PCMS data offerings, continue to play an increasingly important role in our customer inspection programs.”

Margins are lower than the industrial-gas peers, but trend and cash conversion have both improved: Q2 26 adjusted EBITDA margin was 13.3%, up 30 bps, and operating cash flow swung to $14.91M from -$9.26M year-over-year. Bank-defined leverage was approximately 2.2 times as of June 30, 2026, the lowest since 2018. There is no dividend, so this is a stability case. Risk: heavy oil & gas customer concentration is producing inspection deferrals as elevated crude prices delay maintenance, and management said it “anticipate that a majority of the deferrals from the first half of 2026 will continue to be pushed further out.”

These businesses will not make headlines the way an AI stock does, and that is precisely their appeal. The industrial-gas duopoly earns its returns because the customer cannot swap suppliers without unbolting a plant; the certifier earns its returns because the mark is molded into the product; the inspection firm earns its returns because the technicians are already on site. Position them as ballast, size them modestly, and let the compounding do the unglamorous work.

evidence.title: Linde stock gains 1.62 percent after earnings beat estimates
evidence.text:
Linde plc (ISIN IE000S9YS4E6) closed at USD 464.91 on Nasdaq on September 22, 2026, gaining 1.62 percent from the prior close. The move followed second-quarter figures that exceeded analyst estimates, putting earnings growth and the full-year outlook at the center of the valuation debate.

According to MarketBeat on September 23, 2026, Linde reported Q2 2026 earnings per share of USD 4.50, exceeding the USD 4.49 consensus by USD 0.01. Revenue reached USD 9.29 billion versus the USD 9.02 billion estimate, while revenue increased 9.3 percent from Q2 2025.

The comparison is important because Q2 2025 EPS was USD 4.09. The latest result therefore represents a USD 0.41 increase, or 10.0 percent, over the prior-year quarter, while the revenue figure also exceeded expectations by USD 0.27 billion.

MarketBeat reported on September 23, 2026, that Linde maintained fiscal-year 2026 earnings guidance of USD 17.70 to USD 17.90 per share and issued Q3 2026 guidance of USD 4.45 to USD 4.55 per share. The current-year consensus cited in the report was USD 17.86 per share.

That range leaves the reported Q2 result only USD 0.01 above consensus, so the stronger signal is the combination of 9.3 percent year-over-year revenue growth and maintained full-year guidance. Erste Group Bank lowered its fiscal 2027 EPS estimate to USD 19.60 from USD 19.62 on September 23, 2026, while the current-year consensus remained USD 17.86.

The Nasdaq close of USD 464.91 on September 22, 2026, stood 15.2 percent below the 52-week high of USD 548.20 and above the 52-week low of USD 387.78. Market capitalization was USD 214.31 billion, and volume reached 1.93 million shares against an average of 1.87 million shares.

Analyst sentiment remains positive in the available September 2026 coverage. Marketscreener reported on September 23, 2026, that UBS maintained a Buy rating and a USD 612 price target. The target is USD 147.09 above the September 22 close, but it represents an analyst view rather than a forecast made in this article.

The next earnings date listed for Linde is October 30, 2026. Until then, the Q3 guidance range of USD 4.45 to USD 4.55 per share provides the clearest company-specific checkpoint, while the stock's position 15.2 percent below its yearly high shows that the market has not returned to that peak valuation.

evidence.title: Krones: Aktie fällt auf 52-Wochen-Tief
evidence.text:
Die Zurückhaltung von Analystenseite hat den Aktienkurs des Maschinenbauers Krones spürbar belastet. Am Dienstag nahm Bernstein Research die Erstbewertung des Titels mit der Einstufung „Market-Perform“ auf. Das Analysehaus setzte das Kursziel bei 111 Euro an. In der Begründung verwiesen die Experten auf die mittelfristigen Perspektiven: Der Ausblick für den Umsatz sowie den Auftragseingang im Jahr 2027 falle verhalten aus.

Die skeptische Einschätzung traf am Markt auf einen ohnehin sensiblen Nerv. Marktteilnehmer reagierten zurückhaltend auf die Annahme, dass das Wachstumstempo in den kommenden Jahren nachlassen könnte. Bei Industrieaktien achten Investoren derzeit besonders genau darauf, wie sich die Visibilität der Auftragsbücher über das laufende Turnusgeschäft hinaus entwickelt.

Die Kursreaktion spiegelte diese Skepsis unmittelbar wider. Am Mittwoch setzte die Aktie ihren Rückgang nach dem vorsichtigen Kommentar fort. Mit einem Abschlag von 1,8 Prozent auf 109,80 Euro gehörte das Papier zu den größten Verlierern im MDax. Am heutigen Freitag notiert das Papier bei 106,40 Euro.

Krones Aktie: Kaufen oder Verkaufen? Hier weiterlesen ...

Damit zeigt sich, wie schwer sich der Titel nach den jüngsten Abgaben tut, wieder an Boden zu gewinnen. Die verhaltene Stimmung erfasst auch das breitere Branchenumfeld, in dem sich deutsche Maschinenbauer behaupten müssen.

Zusätzliche Einordnung für die Situation von Krones als Maschinenbauer liefert der VDMA. Der Verband senkte seine Produktionsprognose für den Maschinenbau für das Jahr 2026, was die Herausforderungen für den gesamten Industriezweig unterstreicht. Allerdings zeichnet die Entwicklung kein rein negatives Bild: Für den Monat Juli meldete der Verband zugleich ein Auftragsplus, was auf punktuelle Nachfrageimpulse im Sektor hindeutet.

Neben den zyklischen Bedingungen steht die operative Aufstellung des Unternehmens im Fokus. Vor rund einem Monat erfolgte die Eröffnung einer Produktionsstätte in Indien; seither verbucht die Aktie ein Minus von 6,8 Prozent. Im gestrigen Handel markierte der Kurs bei 105,20 Euro zudem ein 52-Wochen-Tief.

Die neusten Krones-Zahlen sprechen eine klare Sprache: Dringender Handlungsbedarf für Krones-Aktionäre . Lohnt sich ein Einstieg oder sollten Sie lieber verkaufen? In der aktuellen Gratis-Analyse vom 25. September erfahren Sie was jetzt zu tun ist.

evidence.title: Bernstein Cuts Krones to Neutral, Questioning the Packaging Giant's 2028 Revenue Ambitions
evidence.text:
Krones shares came under pressure Wednesday after Bernstein Research turned cautious on the German filling and packaging equipment maker, downgrading the stock from "Outperform" to "Market-Perform" and setting a price target of EUR 111.00. The MDAX-listed stock fell 3.9% to EUR 107.80, placing it among the session's weaker performers. A second reading later in the day showed the shares down 2.1% at EUR 109.80, still hovering just below Bernstein's target.

At the heart of the downgrade is analyst Benjamin Thielmann's view that Krones' revenue and order growth outlook for 2027 looks more subdued than previously hoped — and that the company's official 2028 sales target may now be at risk.

A Capital Spending Pause Across the Beverage Chain

Thielmann's caution rests on current investment budget data from beverage producers and bottlers, who are holding back on new project approvals amid persistently elevated cost pressures. The restraint is particularly pronounced in the Asia-Pacific region, a key growth market for the Neutraubling-based group. When international beverage majors postpone or stretch out large-scale projects, the knock-on effect on equipment makers' order intake is immediate. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying Krones?

The broader industry mood reinforces that picture. A survey by trade body spiritsEUROPE found that 60% of European spirits producers rate the general business environment of the past twelve months as having worsened, while only just under a third intend to raise investments next year. Brewers face their own squeeze, with rising costs, consumer inflation and declining volumes forcing many drink makers into cost discipline. For suppliers like Krones, that translates into more deliberate decision-making on major orders and capacity expansions.

Bernstein's neutral stance cuts against a predominantly positive analyst consensus. In July and August, houses including Jefferies, Berenberg, Deutsche Bank and DZ Bank had all recommended the stock as a buy. The more cautious call lands on a share price that has already been struggling: Krones is down 20% since the start of the year, with the second reading putting the year-to-date decline at 19%. After years in which the sector benefited from catch-up effects and the shift toward sustainable packaging formats, customer spending discipline has moved back to the center of investors' attention.

The downbeat medium-term view contrasts with a fundamentally stable operating picture. In the second quarter of 2026, Krones generated revenue of EUR 1.34 billion, up from EUR 1.32 billion a year earlier, while earnings per share edged up to EUR 2.23 from EUR 2.21. For the full year 2026, market experts on average expect earnings per share of EUR 10.18 and a dividend increase to EUR 3.11, after EUR 2.80 per share was paid out for 2025. Internally, the company is pushing ahead with its own initiatives, pooling group-wide resources for digitalization and automation within the Krones.digital unit.

Whether Krones can defend its 2028 timetable will likely hinge on how order intake in Asia develops over the coming quarters — and on whether the beverage industry's investment pause proves temporary or becomes entrenched.
