evidence.title: Krones Bets on High-Speed Filling Tech While the Market Stays Skeptical
evidence.text:
Krones Bets on High-Speed Filling Tech While the Market Stays Skeptical

Krones is gearing up for a pair of international trade fairs that will put its engineering ambitions on full display, even as its stock continues to lag. The Bavarian packaging and bottling specialist plans to unveil a slate of high-throughput, resource-saving systems in Dubai and Nuremberg, targeting beverage producers that need to do more with less.

At the Gulfood Manufacturing show in Dubai this November, the company will roll out technology it says sets new benchmarks for processing speed. The ErgoBloc L for PET applications is designed to handle up to 104,000 bottles per hour, a figure made possible by two modular filling and capping units working in tandem. For can filling, Krones will present the Modulfill Bloc FS-C, capable of managing up to 135,000 units per hour.

Speed is only part of the pitch. Under the banner “Year of Water,” Krones is putting sustainability front and center, showcasing water treatment solutions alongside HST high-pressure homogenizers used in dairy, pharmaceuticals and biotechnology. The company, which posted revenue of EUR 5.66 billion in fiscal 2025, is clearly angling to position itself as a partner for complex production processes that also demand resource efficiency.

Steinecker’s Dynamic Fermentation Takes the Stage in Nuremberg

For the BrauBeviale in Nuremberg, Krones has announced additions to its portfolio for alcohol-free beer production and container cleaning. A technical highlight comes from subsidiary Steinecker: a dynamic fermentation process that, combined with specialty yeasts from Novonesis, is already in use with customers worldwide.

Another piece of the forward-looking roadmap is the Modulfill HES filler, built to process as many as 78,000 glass bottles per hour. Series production of that unit is scheduled to begin at the end of 2026. Krones is also betting on Lavasonic HI ultrasonic cleaning technology to cut energy and water consumption during pallet cleaning. For packaging and palletizing, the company will show the Smartpac NXT system for glass and PET along with a newly developed Layer Pusher. Both are aimed at extending the shelf life of end products by reducing oxygen pickup during filling.

A Dividend Leader With a Bruised Share Price

All of this product momentum stands in sharp contrast to how the equity has performed. Krones closed yesterday at EUR 112.00, down 17% since the start of the year and roughly 22% below its 52-week high of EUR 144.20, set in February. The weak run has nonetheless pushed the stock to the top of the MDAX dividend yield table at 2.5%, backed by a payout of EUR 2.80 per share.

That combination — the highest yield in the index and one of its weakest price performances — is a classic setup that can cut both ways. Long-term service contracts with beverage and food groups keep the company’s cash flows predictable, and Krones has so far largely offset rising material costs through price adjustments. Those factors help explain why the distribution has held steady through a difficult market year. The biggest risk to the share price remains restrained capital spending by large beverage manufacturers.

Second-quarter 2026 figures offer partial support for the bull case: earnings per share edged up to EUR 2.23 from EUR 2.21 a year earlier.

How Krones Stacks Up Against the Rest of the MDAX Dividend Field

GEA sits second with a 2.0% yield on a dividend of EUR 1.30, its shares trading at EUR 64.85 and up about 13% year-to-date — a stark contrast to Krones. Efficiency programs have bolstered the food-and-process-industry equipment maker’s profitability, and its focus on resource efficiency should keep demand steady even as environmental rules tighten. The cyclical nature of machinery manufacturing remains a risk, though the stock’s position above its 200-day moving average suggests the market is currently optimistic.

Hochtief ranks third at 1.7%, paying EUR 6.60 per share against a stock price of EUR 396.20. The construction group has climbed 69% over twelve months, even as it has lost some ground recently. Its global footprint through subsidiaries Turner and CIMIC in North America and Australia drives earnings power, and a focus on infrastructure and energy-transition projects makes the business less vulnerable to traditional building-cycle swings. At a price near EUR 400, even small moves shift the percentage yield noticeably.

Airbus shares fourth place with a 1.6% yield on a EUR 3.20 payout, its stock at EUR 196.40 and nearly flat year-to-date — a sign the market treats the dividend as a side note. Normalizing global travel and a hefty order backlog underpin the aerospace group’s finances, while its duopoly position in commercial aircraft gives it considerable pricing power. Supply-chain issues remain the chief risk to production ramp-ups and, indirectly, to future payouts.

Südzucker rounds out the list with a 1.6% yield on a payout of just EUR 0.20 per share. Its low price of EUR 12.32 stands out against the rest of the ranking, yet the stock has gained 35% since the start of the year. The cautious dividend policy reflects volatile earnings in the sugar business, which is heavily exposed to world market prices and agricultural policy decisions. The CropEnergies division ties the group even more closely to energy markets, adding further swings.

A high dividend yield doesn’t automatically signal generosity. When a share price falls sharply on operational trouble, the calculated yield jumps — the effect market participants call a dividend trap. At Krones and GEA, the operating numbers so far argue against that scenario, even though Krones has posted the steepest decline in the group.

Payout ratios matter just as much. Companies that distribute nearly all their profit lose room to invest in research and development. Airbus demonstrates that a moderate dividend and heavy future spending need not be mutually exclusive. The interest-rate environment also plays a role: when fixed-income securities offer similar yields at lower risk, dividend stocks face stiffer competition. For Airbus, dollar exchange-rate exposure adds another variable; for Südzucker, EU agricultural rules set the framework for future distributions.

Five very different stories emerge from the ranking. Krones and GEA deliver the highest yields from stable niche markets, Hochtief is catching its breath after a spectacular rally, Airbus prioritizes growth over payout size, and Südzucker remains the wildcard with strong price momentum and a small dividend. For anyone investing, the more useful question isn’t the headline percentage — it’s whether the operating base behind each distribution can carry it.

evidence.title: TRUMPF introduces compact robotic laser welding cell
evidence.text:
The TruLaser Weld 3000 supports CAD-based programming, AI-assisted path correction and welding of steel and aluminum components.

At EuroBLECH 2026 , TRUMPF is introducing the TruLaser Weld 3000, a robotic laser welding cell with AI-assisted programming and a compact enclosure.

The TruLaser Weld 3000 can be programmed at the machine or offline using TruTops Weld software. Offline programming allows operators to create programs for new components while the machine remains in production. Programs generated from CAD data can be adjusted with the TeachLine Touch function, which allows operators to reposition weld points through the machine’s touchscreen.

The TeachLine AI function uses an AI-based process to detect deviations in weld points and adjust the robot path based on the actual component configuration. According to TRUMPF, the functions can reduce programming and setup time by up to 50 percent. The system is also designed for operation by employees with different levels of programming experience.

The TruLaser Weld 3000 uses welding optics that are approximately 40 percent smaller than previous versions. The smaller optics allow the robot to access areas such as the interiors of deep housings, crates and boxes.

The system includes BrightLine Scan, which combines a high-frequency scanner with motorized focus adjustment. The function supports gap bridging of up to 0.4 mm and wider welds for compensating for component tolerances. BrightLine Weld distributes laser power between inner and outer cores in the laser light cable to reduce spatter during welding, including deep-welding applications.

For gaps of up to approximately 1.5 mm or materials requiring filler metal, FusionLine combines laser welding with filler wire to deposit additional material.

The TruLaser Weld 3000 has a protective enclosure measuring 3.65 × 3.65 m. This is approximately 24 percent smaller than the smallest version of the TruLaser Weld 5000. The cell can process pallet-sized components using a KUKA Iontec robot with a reach of 2,100 mm.

Component positioning options include a conventional welding table, a tilt-rotate positioner and a rotary changer. The rotary changer allows components to be loaded and unloaded while welding continues in the other work area. With 3 kW or 4 kW of laser power, the TruLaser Weld 3000 can weld stainless steel and structural steel up to 8 mm thick. It can also weld aluminum up to 6 mm thick. Applications include equipment and plant engineering, sheet metal components for data centers, medical technology and kitchen and food-processing equipment.

For more information, visit trumpf.com .

Puja Mitra has an MBA in Marketing and HR as well as an MA in Economics. As a Managing Editor, she has experience managing CAD, CAM, and CAE directories. She also handles design, BIM, manufacturing, digital transformation, and computing news. With over 14 years of editing experience, she has a particular interest in content and technical writing.

evidence.title: TRUMPF Unveils Next-Generation TruBend 3000 Series at Blechexpo 2025
evidence.text:
TRUMPF Unveils Next-Generation TruBend 3000 Series at Blechexpo 2025

At Blechexpo 2025, TRUMPF introduced the completely redesigned TruBend 3000 series — a new generation of bending machines built for speed, precision, and efficiency. This latest model features advanced technologies originally developed for the high-end TruBend 5000 series, enabling up to 40% faster throughput than its predecessor.

“The new TruBend 3000 offers users a highly capable, technology-driven solution that can handle around 85% of all sheet metal bending tasks,” said Wolfgang Weingartsberger, Product Manager at TRUMPF. “It delivers outstanding accuracy and productivity in its class.” Depending on configuration, the machine provides a press force ranging from 85 to 230 tonnes and supports bending lengths between two and four meters.

TRUMPF designed the new TruBend 3000 to meet the growing demands of small and medium-sized manufacturers facing rising costs, tighter deadlines, and quality challenges. To guarantee consistent results, the system integrates TRUMPF’s ACB Laser automatic angle measurement technology. Using a combination of laser sensors and cameras, it checks the bending angle before each operation and automatically adjusts the press beam for precision. This ensures uniform quality across all parts, minimizes waste, and helps reduce production costs.

The machine is compatible with TRUMPF’s “TecZone Bend” programming software, which allows users to create programs while the machine is running, maximizing uptime. Operators can simply upload a 2D or 3D model, and within seconds, the software generates the correct bending sequence, tool selection, and collision checks. Even users with limited programming experience can quickly prepare the next job directly on the machine’s touch display.

Energy efficiency is another highlight of the new model. Its “On-Demand Servo Drive” activates the motor only during the bending process, cutting energy use by about 30% compared to traditional hydraulic drives — supporting both cost savings and sustainable manufacturing.

Safety remains a top priority in the new design. The built-in “Bend Guard” protection system uses cameras and matrix sensors to continuously monitor the work area. If it detects any obstruction, such as the operator’s hands, the machine immediately stops. Work can resume quickly using a foot pedal reset, ensuring both protection and productivity.

Ideal for small and mid-sized fabricators, the TruBend 3000 is optimized for both one-off and series production. Its digital interfaces allow seamless integration with other TRUMPF automation and storage systems, making it a strong fit for smart factory environments.

Customers also benefit from TRUMPF’s global service network and digital support tools, including condition monitoring, remote assistance, and the TRUMPF Service App. “Up to 80% of issues can be resolved remotely without waiting for an on-site technician,” noted Mr Weingartsberger. With the new TruBend 3000, TRUMPF continues to combine innovation, safety, and sustainability — setting a new standard in sheet metal bending technology.

evidence.title: German machine tool manufacturer Trumpf announces €23m loss
evidence.text:
German machine tool manufacturer Trumpf announces €23m loss

The German mechanical engineering company Trumpf on Wednesday posted a loss due to the difficult global economic situation and costs associated with job cuts.

Earnings after taxes for the 2024/25 financial year were minus €23.4 million ($27.2 million), the company announced on Wednesday. In the previous year company made a profit of €392.8 million.

The medium-sized company manufactures machine tools and also specializes in lasers. It supplies the latter mainly to industrial companies in the semiconductor industry.

Recently, the company has also been providing technologies for the defence industry. Trumpf's financial year runs from July to the end of June of the following year.

Earnings from ordinary activities – i.e. before interest and taxes (EBIT) – fell to €59 million, down €442 million or 88.2% on the previous year's result. Adjusted for the structural measures taken, EBIT was €230 million.

Trumpf boss Nicola Leibinger-Kammüller said she "cannot be satisfied with such a result." Nevertheless, she said, the company had achieved a "tremendous feat." Trumpf saved €350 million by cutting back on investments in new construction projects, among other things, and also reduced working hours and thus salaries.

Leibinger-Kammüller blamed "the slowing global economy and geopolitical uncertainties" for the downturn, but expressed confidence that the worst is now over, pointing to "cautious signs of improvement."

In spring, Trumpf announced a reduction of 1,000 jobs worldwide.

evidence.title: Siemens and TRUMPF Accelerate Digital Manufacturing and AI Readiness
evidence.text:
Siemens and TRUMPF Accelerate Digital Manufacturing and AI Readiness

Sept. 15, 2025 – Technology company Siemens and leading machine tools and laser manufacturer TRUMPF today announced a partnership that promises to elevate industrial production by harnessing advanced digital manufacturing solutions. The collaboration joins Siemens' Xcelerator portfolio with TRUMPF's renowned machine-building and software expertise. The partnership addresses a critical challenge in modern manufacturing: the disconnect between information technology (IT) and operational technology (OT) systems that has historically hindered production efficiency and innovation. By leveraging Siemens' Xcelerator portfolio and TRUMPF's manufacturing excellence, the collaboration aims to deliver comprehensive solutions that bridge this gap.

Both companies are working on open and interoperable IT interfaces that will help to advance artificial intelligence (AI) readiness for motion control applications. The following people appear in the photo above, from left to right: Tom Schneider (TRUMPF), Stefanie Frank (Siemens AG), Cedrik Neike (Siemens AG). Stephan Mayer (TRUMPF), Yürki Voss (Siemens AG) and Till Küppers (TRUMPF). “Real transformation in a factory begins when machines on the shop floor are connected through a shared digital backbone–so that data flows seamlessly, decisions happen faster, and production responds to changing conditions,” said Cedrik Neike, member of the Managing Board at Siemens AG and CEO of Siemens Digital Industries. “By working with TRUMPF, we’re making that connection effortless.

We’re bridging the gap between IT and OT so that manufacturers can move faster, adapt in real time and prepare for the AI era. I’m proud to see two European champions leading the way.”

In today’s rapidly evolving industrial landscape, software is no longer just an add-on to hardware, it’s becoming the key differentiator in manufacturing. From intelligent control systems to data-driven optimization, a seamless integration of hardware and software enables entirely new levels of flexibility, efficiency and value creation. For Siemens and TRUMPF, this shift has created significant opportunities, but also new complexities. Therefore, collaboration is essential and will enable faster innovation cycles, better integration of hardware and software and a more scalable approach to delivering solutions and value through standardized interfaces. The collaboration will also deliver tangible customer benefits through modular system architecture and unified system solutions.

Standardized interfaces will allow for seamless connectivity between shop floor equipment and enterprise-level systems. Customers will benefit from increased operational efficiency, reduced engineering costs and future-proof scalability by using open, modular automation solutions. These are critical to ensure future-proof AI readiness, that will permit customers to achieve faster time-to-market, improved production flexibility and competitive manufacturing operations. “TRUMPF is a leading company for smart factory solutions in the sheet metal industry. The cooperation with Siemens underpins our position as a solution provider.

Thanks to the open standards, our customers will benefit even more from the digital networking of the production–from our machines to robots, grippers and part recognition with the help of AI. We’re taking industrial manufacturing to a whole new level with Siemens", said Stephan Mayer, CEO of Machine Tools at TRUMPF. The partnership builds on regular exchanges among development teams at Siemens and TRUMPF, which underscores the importance of vibrant ecosystems for solving industry’s most pressing challenges.

Siemens AG (Berlin and Munich) is a leading technology company focused on industry, infrastructure, mobility and healthcare. The company’s purpose is to create technology to transform the everyday, for everyone. By combining the real and the digital worlds, Siemens empowers customers to accelerate their digital and sustainability transformations, making factories more efficient, cities more livable and transportation more sustainable. A leader in industrial AI, Siemens leverages its deep domain know-how to apply AI–including generative AI – to real-world applications, making AI accessible and impactful for customers across diverse industries.

Siemens also owns a majority stake in the publicly listed company Siemens Healthineers, a leading global medical technology provider pioneering breakthroughs in healthcare. For everyone. Everywhere. Sustainably.

TRUMPF is a high-tech company offering manufacturing solutions in the fields of machine tools and laser technology. It drives digital connectivity in manufacturing through consulting, platform products and software. TRUMPF is one of the technology and market leaders in highly versatile machine tools for sheet metal processing and in the field of industrial lasers. In 2024/25, TRUMPF employed 17,750 people and generated sales of 4.3 billion euros (preliminary figures).

With about 90 companies, the TRUMPF Group is represented in nearly every European country as well as in North America, South America and Asia. The company has production facilities in Germany, France, the United Kingdom, Italy, Austria, Switzerland, Poland, the Czech Republic, the United States, Mexico and China.

evidence.title: TRUMPF Inaugurates First Manufacturing Facility Embracing ‘Make in India’ Vision
evidence.text:
TRUMPF Inaugurates First Manufacturing Facility Embracing ‘Make in India’ Vision

In a landmark move that aligns with India’s national manufacturing mission, TRUMPF , the global leader in industrial machine tools and laser technology, inaugurated its first manufacturing facility in India today at Nighoje, Pune. The new facility marks a significant milestone in TRUMPF’s strategic expansion and is set to play a key role in accelerating smart manufacturing adoption across the Indian subcontinent.

The grand inauguration ceremony was graced by senior leadership from both TRUMPF Germany and India, including Stephan Mayer, CEO Machine Tools and Member of the Management Board, TRUMPF Germany; Till Kueppers, COO Machine Tools, TRUMPF Germany; Pradeep Patil, Managing Director of TRUMPF India; and Mohammed Hidayath, Director – Sales, TRUMPF India. Speaking at the event, Mr Mayer emphasised TRUMPF’s long-term commitment to the Indian market, noting, “This new manufacturing unit in Pune is an investment in India’s future as a global manufacturing hub.”

The Pune facility will initially produce the TruBend 1000 series bending machines, designed to deliver performance and efficiency at a competitive price point. By 2025, TRUMPF also plans to localise production of the TruLaser 1000 series, which combines German precision with affordability, making it ideal for India’s fast-evolving manufacturing sector. With this strategic localisation, TRUMPF aims to enhance supply chain responsiveness, reduce lead times, and offer advanced sheet metal processing solutions tailored to Indian industry needs.

TRUMPF’s leadership believes this manufacturing move is pivotal in supporting the Indian government’s ‘Make in India’ initiative, a national program that encourages global companies to manufacture locally and contribute to India’s economic self-reliance.

Reflecting on TRUMPF India’s journey, Pradeep Patil, Managing Director of TRUMPF India, expressed deep gratitude toward customers and partners who made the company’s manufacturing milestone possible. “This milestone would not have been possible without the complete faith and trust our customers have placed in TRUMPF. Your encouragement and support have been the true catalyst behind this achievement,” he stated during the inauguration ceremony.

Mr Patil highlighted that since TRUMPF began operations in India in 2006, the company has steadily expanded its local presence, now boasting two fully functional Experience Centres in Pune and Bengaluru, a dedicated Laser Application Lab, and four warehouses supporting nationwide delivery. Backed by a 23-member strong support team, TRUMPF India currently handles over 15,000 shipments annually, serving more than 700 customers across the country.

He added that with the new manufacturing facility now operational, TRUMPF is not only scaling its production but also strengthening its ecosystem. “By 2025, all operations at the new plant—including assembly, testing, quality assurance, and logistics- will be fully functional. This is a proud moment for our entire India team as we take the next step in becoming a true local manufacturing partner to Indian industry,” Mr Patil concluded.

The inauguration event witnessed the presence of over a dozen distinguished industry leaders and dignitaries. Among them were Mohini Kelkar, Vice President of IMTMA; Rajesh Nath, Managing Director of VDMA India; Kalpesh Saraf, Regional Director of IGCC, Swamy Magod, Managing Director of Magod Group of Companies, Atin Agarwal, Chairman and Managing Director Auto Mech (India) Pvt. Ltd., Bharat B Gupta, President of JBM Group, Sudhir Mande, Managing Director, M M Industrial Controls Pvt Ltd, K Chandrasekhar, Managing Director, Unique Punch Systems Private Limited, Vaishnav Jayachandran, CEO of Kentex Engineering Works, Vijay Suttatti, Managing Director of Suttatti Enterprises Ltd, and several others from leading Indian manufacturing companies. The guests were treated to a traditional ‘Pagdi’ ceremony and lighting of the ceremonial lamp, followed by a guided tour of the state-of-the-art TRUMPF facility and a networking session.

TRUMPF India’s Nighoje site also houses its head office and showroom, and the new manufacturing line further elevates this location as a comprehensive hub for sales, application engineering, service, and now, production. This expansion is complemented by TRUMPF’s growing presence in other Indian cities, including a new showroom planned in Bengaluru and a software R&D centre in Chennai.

Globally, TRUMPF was founded in 1923 in Germany and today operates as a technology powerhouse with a portfolio spanning machine tools for flexible sheet metal processing, laser systems for cutting, welding, and additive manufacturing, and Industry 4.0-ready software solutions. The company is renowned for delivering cutting-edge automation, precision engineering, and digital manufacturing technologies that are shaping the future of industry worldwide. With this new facility, TRUMPF reinforces its message of “local presence with global standards,” enabling Indian manufacturers, MSMEs, and large enterprises to access world-class production technologies without compromise. The company’s decision to invest over €5 million in India underlines its confidence in the market and its commitment to empowering India’s industrial transformation journey.

evidence.title: TRUMPF expands its U.S. manufacturing footprint
evidence.text:
The latest expansion of TRUMPF’s manufacturing facilities in Farmington, Conn., is a 55,800-sq.-ft. addition that houses the company’s newest Smart Factory, what company leaders call its automated fabricating systems that are tied to an automated storage and retrieval system.

In the midst of increased tariffs and bold political talk about rebuilding U.S. manufacturing might, TRUMPF formally commemorated the opening of the seventh expansion of its manufacturing operations in Farmington, Conn.—its 55,800-sq-ft. Smart Factory.

“This building is not just a manufacturing facility. It’s the next step in American manufacturing,” said Lutz Labisch, president/CEO, TRUMPF Inc.

This $40 million investment in this digitally connected fabricating system is part of the company’s “local for local” strategy, according to Labisch. TRUMPF wants to manufacture machine tools in the geographic locations where it sells the tools, whether the U.S., Europe, or Asia, he said. TRUMPF has been manufacturing in Connecticut since 1974.

“The Farmington Smart Factory provides a blueprint that enables manufacturers to reshore production and remain cost-competitive while adapting to changing needs, overcoming skilled labor shortages, and meeting strict safety standards,” said Burke Doar, TRUMPF’s executive vice president.

During the formal grand opening on May 20, attendees got to see the Smart Factory in action. A 700-slot Stopa material handing and storage system acts as the spine to the automated system. It not only feeds the different fabricating processes attached to it, but also provides temporary storage of work-in-process that might be moving from blanking to forming.

The Farmington Smart Factory, like the other 300 similar setups in North America, incorporates various blanking and forming machine tools. As it is currently set up, one side has an TruBend 5230 automated press brake with the company’s ToolMaster automated tooling changer; a TruMatic 5000 with automated parts sorting; and a TruLaser Center 7030 laser cutting machine, also with parts sorting capabilities. On the other side of the automated material handling and storage system is a TruLaser 5030 with a PartsMaster, which can feed a laser-cut skeleton directly to an operator for ergonomic breakout if the parts aren’t being fed back into the Stopa system; a TruBend Center panel bender; and a station with two TruBend press brakes for manual forming are located.

What is noteworthy about this Smart Factory concept, according to TRUMPF officials, is that it is also connected to a nearby powder coating line. Lidar is used to measure incoming parts to be powder coated, and the automated spray guns can adjust to accommodate spray patterns when those parts arrive.

The system has a five-stage pretreatment system and two powder coating lines, one that always sprays white and the other that accommodates multiple colors. It typically takes about 20 minutes to conduct a changeover to another color.

Doar said the Smart Factory concept is less about the size of the actual systems and more about the powerful impact of digital connectivity on production activity, providing metal fabricators with real-time updates of what’s happening on the shop floor and the ability to make changes to production flow easily with the help of manufacturing executive software. He added that metal fabricators in the U.S. see the Smart Factory as a competitive advantage, and that’s why this country is home to more than half of TRUMPF’s Smart Factory installations in the world.

This commitment to supporting its manufacturing efforts in the U.S. comes on the heels of TRUMPF moving production of its largest laser tube cutting machine, the TruLaser Tube 7000, to Connecticut late last year. It is produced alongside laser cutting machines and material automation used in operation with that equipment.

Flanked by company officials and local dignitaries, Dr. Nicola Leibinger-Kammüller, TRUMPF’s CEO, cuts the ceremonial ribbon to formally open the company’s newest manufacturing addition to its campus.

In 2026, the company also plans to start manufacturing TruBend 3000 press brakes in the same facility.

In addition to welcoming customers and partners to see the new expansion, TRUMPF shared several announcements with guests during the event:

Festo’s CPX-AP-I-16DIO M12 configurable digital I/O module simplifies decentralised I/O design

Festo has addressed this challenge with a new configurable digital I/O module for the CPX-AP-I decentralised I/O platform. Designated CPX-AP-I-16DIO M12 (or M12 for short), the new module enables more efficient use of decentralised I/O across a machine.

The new M12 configurable digital I/O module provides 16 channels that can each be configured as a digital input or digital output to match application requirements. Users can configure the module channel by channel, divide it into eight inputs and eight outputs, or configure all 16 channels as outputs. Selected output channels provide up to 500mA for high-current devices.

The module comes with a default 16-input configuration for immediate installation and commissioning, while output functions are enabled through software parameterisation. Individual LED indicators on each channel simplify commissioning and troubleshooting by providing clear operating and diagnostic status.

Available now, the M12 module gives machine builders greater freedom to design around the needs of the application instead of the limitations of fixed I/O modules. A single M12 module can support a wider range of machine configurations, reducing the number of module variants that must be specified, stocked, and maintained over the life of a machine.

The new module is part of Festo’s CPX-AP-I decentralised I/O platform, a high-performance system that distributes I/O, valve terminals, and IO-Link devices throughout a machine. Supporting up to 80 modules over distances of up to 50m between modules, the platform reduces wiring, simplifies modular machine architectures, and allows machine builders to expand or reconfigure systems without redesigning the entire control architecture.

Expanding connectivity with CC-Link IE Field Basic

Festo has also introduced a new CPX-AP-I bus node supporting CC-Link IE Field Basic, expanding the platform’s connectivity for Mitsubishi Electric Automation environments. Widely used throughout Asia, the industrial Ethernet protocol enables machine builders to integrate CPX-AP-I decentralised I/O into Mitsubishi PLC architectures without additional gateways or custom engineering.

The new bus node allows machine builders to retain the same CPX-AP-I decentralised I/O architecture while changing only the network interface for Mitsubishi Electric systems. The result is less engineering effort, faster machine adaptation for regional markets, and a common automation platform that supports multiple industrial Ethernet protocols, including EtherNet/IP, PROFINET, EtherCAT, Modbus TCP, and now CC-Link IE Field Basic.

evidence.title: Festo India to showcase precision wafer handling at SEMICON India 2026
evidence.text:
Festo India to showcase precision wafer handling at SEMICON India 2026

Festo India will participate in SEMICON India 2026, taking place September 17–19 at Yashobhoomi, Delhi, where it will present its Seamless Automation approach for semiconductor and electronics manufacturing.

The company’s booth, located at Hall 1, Booth 1256, will bring together electric and pneumatic automation, motion control, precision handling, sensing, process control and digitalisation under a single technology portfolio aimed at semiconductor fabs, equipment OEMs and electronics manufacturers.

The semiconductor-relevant offering, by Festo, spans electric automation for repeatable positioning, pneumatic and proportional pressure control for controlled force and motion profiles, and precision wafer handling designed to move substrates with minimal vibration. The lineup also includes wafer alignment and transfer solutions for EFEM and equipment applications, piezo-based technologies for pressure and flow control, and valve solutions for vacuum, gas and fluid handling. Cleanroom-compatible components and condition-monitoring tools round out a portfolio addressing wafer fabrication equipment, sub-fab systems, gas supply, cooling circuits and vacuum technology.

Rather than centring its participation on a single product launch, Festo said its focus at the show is on demonstrating how pneumatic, electric, piezo and digital technologies work together in application-specific solutions. Recent developments in this space include high-precision piezo-based pressure control, micro-positioning with force detection, and pin-lift technology that positions wafers to micrometre-level accuracy. One example the company points to is its wafer warpage solution, which uses multi-channel pressure control and closed-loop force feedback to handle warped wafers and substrates.

Festo said its semiconductor technologies target a specific set of manufacturing challenges: wafer damage during handling, vibration during motion, particle contamination in cleanroom environments, and stability during vacuum and process-gas operations. Its cleanroom-compatible products, along with semiconductor-specific seals, greases and double-packaging options, are built for contamination-sensitive settings, while proportional valves and mass-flow control aim to keep process conditions consistent across repeated cycles. On the digital side, the company’s condition-monitoring and predictive-maintenance tools are meant to give machine builders visibility into equipment health rather than just control over individual actuators or valves, an approach that extends to remote I/O, simulation, virtual commissioning and data-driven process optimisation.

Festo said the semiconductor sector was among its fastest-growing industrial segments globally in 2025, with India its strongest-growing market. The company operates a Global Production Centre and R&D facility in Krishnagiri, Tamil Nadu, and invested more than 8 percent of its turnover in R&D last year.

“SEMICON India 2026 comes at an important moment for India’s semiconductor journey, as the country moves from building capabilities to creating a more integrated and globally competitive semiconductor ecosystem,” said Ravi Sastry, Managing Director, Festo India. “At Festo, we see automation as a critical enabler of this transformation. India’s semiconductor opportunity is not limited to chip fabrication. It encompasses the entire ecosystem, from wafer processing and equipment manufacturing to advanced packaging, testing, electronics manufacturing and the supporting infrastructure required to build a resilient value chain. We look forward to building long-term partnerships and contributing our automation expertise to India’s journey from Silicon to Systems.”

Festo said it expects the exhibition to generate new customer enquiries, engagement with equipment OEMs, and technology collaborations across front-end, back-end and advanced packaging applications as India’s semiconductor manufacturing base expands. Visitors to Booth 1256 can expect application-oriented demonstrations covering precision motion, wafer and substrate handling, controlled gripping, micro-positioning and digital monitoring.

evidence.title: Festo introduces AI-based predictive maintenance platform to improve automation uptime
evidence.text:
The AX Motion Insights platform integrates AI with maintenance workflows, enabling distribution and fulfillment operations to predict points of failure, plan interventions, and reduce unplanned downtime. | Source: Festo

While automation promises a future where robots can do work around the clock, seven days a week, without tiring, downtime caused by unexpected issues still holds us back from that future. Festo this week introduced its new Festo AX Motion Insights platform, which it said can reduce unplanned downtime in robotics.

The platform combines AI -based predictive analytics with maintenance workflows, which Festo said can reduce unplanned downtime across conveyors, sortation systems, palletizers, gantries, and material-handling equipment.

This latest platform works with Festo’s existing software lineup. Festo AX Motion Insights Electric software monitors servo drives and electric axes. AX Motion Insights Pneumatic software provides condition monitoring for pneumatic cylinders.

AX Data Access serves as the data layer that makes operational technology (OT) data available for information technology (IT) analysis and integration. Together, Festo said the platforms enable fulfillment centers to scale predictive maintenance capabilities as needs develop rather than committing to a single, monolithic software rollout.

Festo said the platform provides flexible deployment options that support on-premises and cloud-based environments. This allows fulfillment and distribution centers to align predictive maintenance with existing IT and operational requirements while maintaining control over how and where data is collected and used.

Festo is a global manufacturer of pneumatic and electromechanical systems, components, and controls for process and industrial automation. The company has subsidiaries in more than 60 countries, and a wide-ranging 36,000-product catalog.

Motion Insights looks for problems, then takes action to prevent them

Motion Insights identifies where problems are likely to occur. Smartenance AX, Festo’s maintenance management software, is the link to action. Smartenance AX turns predictive insight into planned maintenance by directing crews to the most likely point of failure instead of reacting after a machine stops.

It combines asset tracking, maintenance planning, and a digital machine logbook, allowing condition data from Motion Insights to trigger targeted maintenance tasks. In addition to Smartenance AX, Motion Insights can also be integrated with other maintenance management systems, allowing condition data to inform existing workflows where customers prefer to keep their current platforms.

AX Motion Insights Pneumatic provides universal condition monitoring for pneumatic cylinders from all manufacturers without requiring additional sensors, hardware changes, or mechanical modifications. The software detects anomalies and performance drift in pneumatic motion , identifying not only impending failures, but also underperformance that can lead to inconsistent handling, increased air consumption, and throughput loss.

AX Data Access connects automation systems to enterprise IT environments by making operational data available for analysis beyond the control layer. By bridging OT and IT, AX Data enables fulfillment centers to correlate motion performance, maintenance activity, and energy use with broader operational metrics.

Festo plans for scale and easy deployment

AX Motion Insights software is scalable by design. Machine builders and system integrators purchase licenses only for the functions and assets they need, with the ability to expand coverage over time as automation requirements evolve.

Machine builders and system integrators can incorporate AX motion insights software into their after-sales support contracts as a value-added service for their customers.

AX Motion Insights Electric integrates directly with Festo CMMT multiprotocol servo drives and electric axes used throughout fulfillment center automation systems. Festo multiprotocol servo drives are compatible with the leading industrial communication protocols, allowing a single drive platform to operate across mixed PLC and network environments.

This simplifies standardization, reduces hardware variation in inventory, and helps system integrators commission and support automation systems more efficiently, Festo claimed. The company plans to include support for additional brands of servo drives and axes.

SEW-EURODRIVE will showcase its comprehensive MOVI-C® modular automation portfolio at Propak Cape, highlighting how integrated drive and automation technologies can help processing and packaging companies reduce energy consumption, improve efficiency and achieve more consistent production performance.

The exhibit will include the full MOVI-C® range together with a robotic arm, illustrating the depth of automation technology available to machine builders, OEMs and end users seeking increasingly intelligent and energy-efficient production solutions.

According to Jonathan McKey, National Sales and Marketing Manager at SEW-EURODRIVE South Africa, achieving meaningful energy savings requires more than simply selecting an energy-efficient motor or drive.

“Energy efficiency needs to be considered across the complete machine or production line,” McKey says. “Our approach is to work closely with customers to understand the application, the operating cycle and where energy is being consumed. From there, we can engineer an integrated drive and automation solution that supports both optimum performance and reduced energy usage.”

MOVI-C® provides a single modular automation platform incorporating drive technology, motion control, control technology, software and communication capabilities. This allows individual machine functions to be coordinated within an integrated architecture, supporting precise control of motors and movement throughout processing and packaging applications.

For packaging operations in particular, accurate speed, positioning and synchronisation are fundamental to achieving high throughput while avoiding unnecessary mechanical and energy losses. Intelligent drive control allows equipment to operate according to actual process demand rather than continuously running at maximum output.

The ability to coordinate multiple axes is equally important in applications such as conveying, handling, positioning, sorting, palletising and robotic systems, where accurate movement and repeatability can directly influence productivity and product quality.

McKey emphasises that SEW-EURODRIVE’s role extends beyond supplying individual components.

“We partner with customers from the engineering and specification stage through to commissioning and lifecycle support,” he says. “This allows us to look at the complete application and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, simplify automation and optimise the performance of the installed equipment.”

The company’s presence at Propak Cape will reinforce this system-based approach, demonstrating how motors, gear units, frequency inverters, decentralised drive technology, controllers and software can function as an integrated automation ecosystem.

For processing and packaging companies facing increasing pressure to improve productivity while managing electricity costs, McKey says automation and energy efficiency must increasingly be considered together.

“The objective is ultimately to help customers produce more efficiently, with better control of their processes and a lower overall energy requirement,” he concludes.

evidence.title: SEW-EURODRIVE Expands Integrated Automation Solutions: From Industrial Robots to AMRs and AGVs
evidence.text:
SEW-EURODRIVE Expands Integrated Automation Solutions: From Industrial Robots to AMRs and AGVs As high-mix, low-volume production and frequent process changes become major challenges in manufacturing, the approach to robot automation is evolving. Beyond the speed and precision of individual robots, the importance of an integrated automation environment—taking into account connectivity with peripheral equipment like conveyors, engineering and commissioning times, and future system expansion and maintenance—is rapidly growing.In response to these shifts in manufacturing environments, SEW-EURODRIVE announced that it is offering robot solutions that connect industrial robots, mobile robots, and peripheral transport systems into a single automation architecture.The core strategy is to combine the company's established drive technologies, such as gear units, servomotors, and inverters, with controllers and software to unify not only individual robot axis controls but also the motion of the entire production line.Support for Industrial Robot Kinematics Including Delta and Articulated ArmsSEW-EURODRIVE’s industrial robot solutions are configured to apply to various kinematic structures, including Delta Robots, Articulated Arms, SCARAs, and Gantries.Targeted at a wide range of manufacturing tasks—such as Pick & Place, palletizing, packaging, sorting, assembly, and inter-process material transfer—the solution adopts a modular approach that allows drive and control components to be combined according to the robot structure and operational requirements.For Delta Robot solutions, the offering is broadly divided into three packages: - Controller Package: Powered by the MOVI-C® CONTROLLER and MOVIKIT® Robotics, managing robot motion and trajectory paths. - Robot Axis Package: Composed of MOVIDRIVE® modular units and servomotors. - Mechanical Package: Utilizing PxG® precision planetary gear units.Each package can be implemented individually or combined depending on project needs, offering flexibility whether retrofitting existing equipment or building new automation systems from scratch.Streamlined Robot Engineering via MOVIKIT® RoboticsOn the software side, MOVIKIT® Robotics handles essential robot control functions. It enables parameter-based configuration for path control, coordinate transformation, jog operation, and homing routines. By reducing the need for users to program individual functions from scratch, the software focuses on minimizing complexity during system setup and commissioning.Through the MOVISUITE® RobotMonitor, users can preview kinematic structures and movement paths in a 3D interface. This allows operators to verify movements, set up paths, and prepare for commissioning prior to running physical equipment.With this software-driven engineering environment, SEW-EURODRIVE minimizes interfaces between robot controls and drive systems, while providing long-term agility for post-deployment modifications and maintenance.Expanding Automation Scope to AMR and AGV Internal LogisticsSEW-EURODRIVE’s automation domain extends beyond stationary industrial robots to mobile robots traversing production and logistics floors.Utilizing Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) and Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs), the systems transport parts, pallets, and heavy loads between production processes, leveraging bidirectional and omnidirectional drive technologies to adapt to diverse factory layouts.Crucially, support for standardized VDA 5050 interfaces and customized communication solutions enables seamless integration with existing fleet management systems or third-party mobile robots. This allows manufacturers to build an integrated operating environment without being locked into a single vendor for their entire logistics infrastructure.Mobile Robot Platform 1600 Handling Up to 1.6 TonsAmong its mobile robot lineup, the Mobile Robot Platform 1600 offers a modular platform capable of attaching top load-handling devices based on the target payload and production setting.Based on SEW-EURODRIVE's official German specifications, the Interface variant handles payloads up to 1,600 kg, while the Lift and Conveyor series support up to 1,250 kg.For charging, the system can incorporate MOVITRANS®, SEW-EURODRIVE’s contactless energy transfer technology. Unlike cable-plug charging, vehicles receive power wirelessly at designated locations, significantly reducing mobile robot downtime.(Note: The local supply scope and timeline for the Mobile Robot Platform 1600 may vary by project, requiring specific verification of local certifications, fleet management interfaces, and load-handling attachments prior to implementation.)Robots, Conveyors, and Transfer Axes under One Control EnvironmentOn actual production lines, robots rarely operate in isolation; they move in sync with conveyors, rotary tables, lifts, and transfer axes. When individual equipment relies on separate control environments, building interfaces, troubleshooting failures, and adapting to future reconfigurations become highly complex.SEW-EURODRIVE proposes configuring both robot axes and surrounding transfer axes within the same engineering environment built around the MOVI-C® automation platform. By linking mechanical drive components, motion control, and software, the company aims to simplify interfaces and maintain a consistent control architecture during line modifications or expansions.In industries such as automotive, secondary batteries, food & beverage, packaging, and logistics—where robots operate alongside numerous transfer systems—overall line connectivity drives productivity and operational efficiency just as much as individual robot performance.Accordingly, SEW-EURODRIVE plans to expand its automation portfolio by pairing its foundational gearmotors and inverters with precision gear units, servo systems, motion control, software, industrial robots, and mobile units.In robot automation, how effectively you connect surrounding transport equipment and how quickly you can build and commission the entire system matter just as much as individual robot specs, said Jae-han Jeong, Team Leader of Technical Application Support at SEW-EURODRIVE Korea. We plan to continuously propose solutions that encompass our customers' entire production process by unifying mechanical, drive, control, and software elements into a single automation environment.

evidence.title: How SEW-EURODRIVE built a document automation engine to unlock millions in savings
evidence.text:
The use of ECM (Enterprise Content Management) has enabled German industrial giant SEW-EURODRIVE to embrace back-office process automation, AI-enabled information access and improved operational efficiency at enterprise scale.

That reflects a very large ECM engagement - more than 22 TB of managed content and at least 313 million documents now held in its chosen partner's repository, with the capacity to absorb annual growth of a further 30-35 million documents generated by its complex, document-based workflows.

The company - whose systems power everything from airport baggage handling and conveyor belts to bottling plants and autonomous logistics vehicles, and whose customers include Coca-Cola, Carlsberg and Gatwick Airport - says that in one area alone, its sales process, a 2023 analysis found more than €17 million in time-saving benefits over the previous three years.

That includes AI-enabled document and process automation that lets sales specialists automatically extract key details from incoming orders and enquiries - a capability the company estimates saved at least €1 million on its own between 2020 and 2023.

Other benefits of committing to its supplier's 'Intelligent Content Automation' technology include 90 per cent time savings in some document-centric processes, full payback within six months, and an overall 336 per cent ROI across the 2020-2023 period.

SEW-EURODRIVE's Group Manager for Enterprise Content Management, Benjamin Schaller, says the payoff is not only faster operations and less paperwork but a better 'corporate memory bank':

Yes, we're getting better time savings and quicker retrieval speed, but we have customers with a very long history with us and who really appreciate the fact that we can literally offer them documents from contracts they took out in the 1950s with us if they want to - literally in a millisecond.

Of course, you don't need to go back 70 years in most cases, but it's still great for our customer relationships that they can call up and say, 'Hey, we ordered something five years ago, but we don't have any documentation about this anymore; can you tell me what we ordered?' and our salespeople can always say, 'Yes we can - and very easily.'

With roots stretching back to 1931, Schaller works for a 23,000-strong, privately held global leader in drive and automation technology. In total, the company operates 18 production plants and 92 assembly plants across 57 countries.

From its headquarters in Bruchsal, near Karlsruhe in the Baden-Württemberg region of Germany, the company runs an extensive sales and service network that provides advice, spare parts and repairs to customers anywhere in the world.

Its products range from highly customisable, modular gearing systems to electric motors, electronics for regulating speed and automating drive systems, and automated guided vehicles - or, as Schaller jokes:

You may not interact directly with our products - but you've likely been moved by them at least one time in your life, I can guarantee you!

That combination of product range and extensive customization is key to why ECM - or, as Schaller's vendor partner now prefers to style it, 'Document Intelligence' - matters so much at a company like his.

Due to the extensive product configuration we want to offer and all the related customer interaction that necessitates, we handle a lot of incoming sales documentation.

We encourage use of our sales portal of course, but there is still a lot of document-based communication needed between sales and buyers. I think what we do here is just much more complex than more standardized e-commerce.

He also sees ECM as critical to freeing up his salespeople's time:

With all that in quotation and order entry and back and forth, you're talking a lot of repetitive processing; there's really not a lot of value creation going on there.

So, instead of them being overloaded with bureaucracy, we wanted the guys to be able to focus on customers and chasing leads instead.

Schaller describes his role at SEW-EURODRIVE as 100%e about reducing manual processing so colleagues can focus on higher-value work.

In practical terms, that means leading an internal team of 10 ECM specialists responsible for every application tied to ECM processes - in effect, everywhere in the business that documents are involved.

He says his sales colleagues were initially sceptical about AI being introduced into their process, but were soon won over by the time savings it delivered.

Other challenges, he says, centered on rolling out the system in a way that balanced global standardization with local requirements - such as aligning with the German implementation of the EU's GDPR, known locally as the Datenschutz-Grundverordnung, or DS-GVO.

The decision to bring in this specific vendor predates his tenure, he notes, but managing the many Doxis applications and automation use cases now built on the platform falls to him and his team:

We handle around 150,000 documents per day globally - but even now, many processes are still manual, so we never really stop pushing for automating document-heavy workflows.

Schaller notes that his organization uses a number of content and collaboration technologies, and constantly checks Doxis's capabilities and suitability for projects against other market options such as Microsoft SharePoint.

In 2023, SEW-EURODRIVE's main ECM partner, Doxis - then still known as SER Group - commissioned a Total Economic Impact (TEI) study from Forrester Consulting to quantify the business impact of the Doxis Intelligent Content Automation platform.

The platform, Forrester believes, streamlined document management and collaboration, and delivered significant productivity gains through process automation and the use of AI to speed up document search and retrieval. It also avoided costs by reducing reliance on legacy systems and removing the need for additional headcount.

For example, SEW-EURODRIVE was able to shut down legacy ECM systems as part of the migration to Doxis and avoid hiring additional staff - which alone resulted in estimated savings of €640,000 over the period studied.

Automating routine content-centric workflows delivered time savings of up to 90% - equivalent, according to the study, to at least €6.1 million recovered in end-user productivity. Holding all documents in one central place opened up a further €9.6 million in end-user productivity gains over the period analysed.

For Schaller, that translates into benefit that is both large-scale and long-term:

Document Intelligence means we can see the quote, we can see the order, the delivery note, the quality documents from production, how the steel was checked when we bought it, the assembly report, the delivery notes - the whole business process from the beginning to end.

If we had multiple solutions doing this, then it would be much harder to get this overview. You would need so many more interfaces, in fact, that I don't think it would even be possible.

Schaller notes that not all user documents go into his ECM, and that there are clear policies about what to use when.

Nonetheless, he is keen to continue the work to automate even more:

Not everything goes into Doxis - if it's collaboration stuff, we advise people to use other platforms - but ECM definitely plays a big role in our whole digital transformation.

After all, there's other use cases in Procurement and Finance where people are doing manual work which we want to get rid of and keep on automating out all the repetitive things they're doing as much as possible.

evidence.title: SEW-EURODRIVE Expands PxG Servo Portfolio with New Economy Series
evidence.text:
SEW-EURODRIVE Expands PxG Servo Portfolio with New Economy Series

Aug. 11, 2026 — SEW-EURODRIVE has expanded its PxG planetary servo gear unit portfolio with the introduction of the PxG economy series, adding three performance classes for machine builders and OEMs seeking cost-effective servo performance for standard industrial automation applications.

The new P1.G, P2.G and P3.G gear units extend the existing PxG family below the P5.G, P6.G and P7.G precision range. The expanded portfolio allows customers to match gear unit performance more closely to application requirements rather than specifying higher levels of precision, torque capacity or load capability than the machine requires.

Right-sized performance for standard automation

The PxG economy series is designed for applications with low to medium technical requirements. Typical uses include packaging equipment, assembly machinery, material handling systems, carton erectors, gantry robots and machine tool portals.

Each performance class addresses a different level of mechanical demand. P1.G is intended for standard applications with relatively low overhung loads. P2.G provides additional load capacity for applications with increased radial forces. P3.G combines cost-optimized straight gearing with higher-capacity bearings for applications requiring greater mechanical strength while remaining within project budget constraints.

The PxG economy series is available in five sizes with peak torque ratings from 11 to 500 Nm. The gear units are offered in one- and two-stage configurations, provide rotational clearance from 6 to 12 arcminutes and have a rated service life of more than 20,000 hours.

The modular system includes solid-shaft designs with smooth, keyed or splined output options, depending on the performance class. Food-grade lubrication options and multiple mounting interfaces support use across a range of machine designs. The series is also integrated into SEW-EURODRIVE engineering tools, including SEW-Workbench, DriveCAD and DriveConfigurator, to support selection and system design.

The PxG economy series expands customer choice across the servo portfolio by providing:

The new economy range complements the existing PxG precision portfolio with a lower-cost option. Together, the economy and precision series give customers a broader range of planetary servo gear units within one modular platform.

“Every automation application has different performance requirements,” said Anecia Hoffield, servo product manager, at SEW-EURODRIVE. “The PxG economy series gives machine builders more flexibility to select the performance their machines actually need while maintaining the quality, engineering support and long-term reliability they expect from SEW-EURODRIVE.”

The introduction of the PxG economy series continues SEW-EURODRIVE’s expansion of modular motion solutions designed to help OEMs balance machine performance, system cost and long-term operating value.

Founded in 1931 in Bruchsal, Germany, SEW-EURODRIVE is a global leader in Industrial Automation, with operations in more than 50 countries, 17 manufacturing plants, 92 assembly facilities and more than 21,000 employees. The company holds more than 1,000 patents, continuously driving technological advancements in gearmotors, frequency inverters, servo drives and Industry 4.0 solutions.

SEW-EURODRIVE provides engineered solutions in countless industries, including automotive, food & beverage, pharmaceuticals, mining, steel, logistics, energy and more, providing customized automation solutions that enhance efficiency, productivity and sustainability. Despite its global reach, SEW-EURODRIVE remains family-owned, ensuring long-term vision, strong values and a commitment to excellence.

At Electra Mining Africa this year, SEW-EURODRIVE will dedicate one of its two exhibition stands to showcase an exciting range of electronics and mechatronics solutions to help mines improve reliability and reduce operating costs.

This will include an immersive look into the future of intelligent plant operation as the company focuses on predictive maintenance, digital monitoring and real-time energy optimisation, according to Willem Strydom, Business Development Electronics Manager at SEW-EURODRIVE South Africa.

“A key attraction will be demonstrating how we conduct plant energy surveys using specialised measurement equipment deployed by our field service teams,” he says. “These surveys provide practical insights into reducing energy usage, carbon emissions and operating costs.”

Strydom points out that many customers initially believed that simply installing higher efficiency motors would solve their energy challenges. However, the company’s experience shows that much larger savings often lie elsewhere in the system.

“We look at the whole system, not just the motors, and analyse operating loads, automation logic, gearbox efficiency and maintenance practices,” he explains.

This process identifies where energy is being lost unnecessarily with applications such as pumps, conveyors and lifting systems often among the most promising opportunities for optimisation. Visitors to Electra Mining Africa will also be able to see how SEW-EURODRIVE’s DriveRadar® Internet of Things (IoT) platform continuously monitors equipment condition and performance.

“This enables mines to shift away from time-based maintenance schedules toward condition-based interventions,” Strydom says.

The predictive maintenance system also enables operations to compare equipment performance before and after maintenance work, providing measurable feedback on whether interventions are actually improving plant efficiency.

Werner Engelbrecht, Works Manager for Electronics and Mechatronics at SEW-EURODRIVE South Africa, says one of the company’s biggest findings during site assessments is the extent to which many industrial applications remain over-engineered.

“We can also demonstrate how intelligent automation can eliminate hidden energy waste,” Engelbrecht says. “In some conveyor applications, for example, systems continue running unnecessarily because they lack basic control intelligence.”

SEW-EURODRIVE’s stand will also feature one of the largest motors ever displayed by the company locally - an 11 tonne medium voltage motor rated at 1850 kW and 6,6 kV - which highlights its expanding presence in heavy-duty mining and industrial applications.

Strydom says the company expects strong interest from mining operations across southern and central Africa, where energy supply constraints are increasingly shaping operational strategies.

“With mines expanding into areas where infrastructure cannot always keep up, companies are being forced to become more efficient in everything they do,” he concludes.

evidence.title: Voith and Sun Paper set new benchmark for multi-fourdrinier packaging paper machines
evidence.text:
Voith and Sun Paper set new benchmark for multi-fourdrinier packaging paper machines

Voith has successfully started up PM 47, a new packaging paper machine supplied to Sun Paper at its Yanzhou production site in Shandong Province, China. With a wire width of 8.66 meters and an annual design capacity of 700,000 tons, PM 47 achieved its maximum operating speed of 1,400 m/min only 10 days after start-up, making it among the fastest-running multi-fourdrinier packaging paper machines worldwide.

The project progressed from civil construction to first reel in just 11 months and 8 days, while ramping up to its maximum operating speed only 10 days after start-up. These achievements reflect the combination of Voith’s full-line technology and the close collaboration between the project teams of Voith and Sun Paper.

The startup of PM 47 further strengthens the more than 20-year partnership between Voith and Sun Paper, a collaboration that has delivered numerous successful paper production projects and industry benchmarks.

"The PM 47 project has set a new record for wide, high-speed packaging paper machines of this type. This success was driven by the strong collaboration between both teams, who worked in parallel shifts throughout installation and commissioning with around-the-clock responsiveness. It is a perfect combination of Sun Paper's execution speed and Voith's technology and expertise," says Ying Guangdong, Deputy General Manager and Chief Engineer, Sun Paper Co., Ltd.

1,400 m/min: Full-Line Technology Supports Record Performance

Voith delivered PM 47 as a full-line supplier. The scope of delivery included the OCC stock preparation system, the UKP virgin fiber system, wet-end process systems, the paper machine from headbox to reel, as well as automation and digitalization technologies.

A key component of the project is the OCC line, designed for a capacity of 2,200 tons per day, making it among the highest-capacity OCC lines in Asia. The system also features Voith’s IntensaPulper, among the world’s highest-capacity low-consistency pulpers, enabling reliable and efficient raw material processing under large-scale production conditions.

The production line is equipped with Voith’s advanced automation and digital solutions, including MCS, QCS, OnCare.CM and MillOne, covering process control, quality management, condition monitoring and production data management. The MillOne platform provides a centralized environment for production data visualization and analysis.

In addition, permanent magnet motor technology has been extensively applied throughout the stock preparation process, helping reduce energy consumption and further improve operational efficiency.

Record-Fast Start-up and Ramp-up Performance

Following installation of the final equipment, the machine successfully produced paper only four days later, demonstrating the effectiveness of the commissioning process and the close collaboration between both teams.

After start-up, PM 47 reached an operating speed of 1,300 m/min within the first week and increased to 1,400 m/min after only 10 days. The rapid ramp-up highlights both the machine’s excellent operating performance and the expertise of the joint project team throughout installation, commissioning and start-up.

“PM 47 is another important milestone in the long-standing partnership between Voith and Sun Paper. The project combined advanced technology, strong execution and outstanding teamwork. Together, we achieved an exceptionally fast start-up and ramp-up, setting a new benchmark for the industry,” says Carlos Lin, SVP Order Execution & Operations, Voith Paper Asia. “Voith looks forward to continuing to support Sun Paper’s sustainable growth with innovative technologies, integrated solutions and long-term partnerships.”

The Voith Group is a global technology company. With its broad portfolio of systems, products, services and digital applications, Voith sets standards in the markets of energy, paper, raw materials and transport. Founded in 1867, Voith today has around 21,000 employees, sales of $5.4 billion and locations in over 60 countries worldwide and thus is one of the larger family-owned companies in Europe.

evidence.title: Voith Launches PowerDrive Mining at Electra Mining Africa 2026, Combining Electric Conveyor Drives, BeltControl Automation and Integrated Safety Systems
evidence.text:
Voith Launches PowerDrive Mining at Electra Mining Africa 2026, Combining Electric Conveyor Drives, BeltControl Automation and Integrated Safety Systems

PowerDrive Mining: Voith’s first electric drive system for belt conveyors.

(IN BRIEF) Voith has launched PowerDrive Mining, its new fully coordinated electric drive system for belt conveyors, at Electra Mining Africa 2026 in Johannesburg, positioning the technology as a cost-efficient and lower-risk alternative for new conveyor installations, retrofits and replacements. The system integrates major drivetrain components, braking, backstop functionality and Voith’s new BeltControl controller, which is specifically designed for belt conveyor applications and supports smooth starting, controlled acceleration and braking, synchronized multi-drive operation and harmonized ramp profiles to reduce stress on belts and steel structures. PowerDrive Mining is supplied preassembled, factory-tested and with a pre-parameterized control concept, reducing project-specific programming and helping shorten engineering, installation and commissioning times. Voith says its integrated scope and material-optimised design can achieve purchase-price levels of around 30% below the market benchmark, while remote diagnostics, clear fault messaging, enclosed rotating components and a standardized operating concept are intended to improve safety, serviceability and uptime. The system is being showcased from 7 to 11 September 2026 at the Johannesburg Expo Centre, Nasrec, Hall 5, Booth E10.

(PRESS RELEASE) HEIDENHEIM, 7-Sep-2026 — / EuropaWire / — Voith has launched PowerDrive Mining , a new fully coordinated electric drive system for belt conveyors, at Electra Mining Africa 2026 in Johannesburg.

The system combines key drivetrain components, braking, backstop functionality and dedicated conveyor control within an integrated package designed to simplify mining conveyor projects, reduce interface risks and shorten installation and commissioning times.

PowerDrive Mining is being presented from 7 to 11 September 2026 at the Johannesburg Expo Centre, Nasrec , where mining companies and original equipment manufacturers can see the technology at Voith’s Hall 5, Booth E10 and discuss specific application requirements with company specialists.

Voith said the system is intended to provide mining operators with a cost-competitive, preassembled and factory-tested conveyor drive solution that combines compact high-power hardware with coordinated multi-drive control, supporting smoother start-up, lower mechanical stress and more reliable day-to-day operation.

PowerDrive Mining integrates drivetrain, braking and control

PowerDrive Mining has been developed specifically for belt conveyor applications and brings together essential drivetrain and safety-related components in a single coordinated system.

Voith said this integrated approach can reduce the engineering and coordination burden associated with conveyor installations involving multiple suppliers, components and technical interfaces.

The company also provides associated engineering and service support from a single source, giving customers clearer system responsibility throughout the project lifecycle.

By integrating the mechanical drive package, braking, backstop and control functions, Voith aims to lower technical integration risks while simplifying project planning and system implementation.

BeltControl designed specifically for conveyor applications

A central element of PowerDrive Mining is BeltControl, a controller developed specifically around the operational requirements of belt conveyor systems.

Its integrated control logic supports smooth start-ups, precise acceleration and braking, synchronized operation of multiple drives and coordinated ramp profiles.

These functions are intended to reduce mechanical stresses on conveyor belts and supporting steel structures, helping limit wear while maintaining stable operation in demanding mining environments.

Coordinated multi-drive control is particularly important on large or heavily loaded conveyor installations where several drive units must operate together without generating excessive belt tension or structural loads.

Preassembled system reduces on-site engineering and commissioning

Voith designed PowerDrive Mining to address the tight construction schedules and limited shutdown windows often associated with mining conveyor projects.

The system is delivered preassembled and factory-tested, while the controller is supplied with a pre-parameterized concept.

Instead of requiring extensive project-specific programming on site, commissioning teams can configure the system primarily through parameterization.

Voith said this approach reduces engineering requirements, lowers the potential for implementation errors and shortens the time needed for quotation, design, installation and commissioning.

Its compact configuration can also provide advantages during retrofits and equipment replacement projects, particularly in conveyor galleries and other locations where installation space is restricted.

Voith targets investment cost around 30% below market benchmark

PowerDrive Mining has also been developed with cost efficiency in mind.

According to Voith, the combination of an integrated scope of supply, material-optimised design and reduced coordination requirements enables the system to target purchase-price levels approximately 30% below the market benchmark.

The company positions the solution as a way for mining operators to combine competitive capital expenditure with simplified engineering, rapid installation and long-term operational reliability.

By reducing the number of individual interfaces and suppliers involved, Voith also aims to lower indirect project costs associated with coordination, troubleshooting and commissioning.

Integrated safety features support reliable conveyor operation

PowerDrive Mining incorporates several safety and durability features intended for harsh mining environments.

The system includes an integrated brake and backstop, enclosed rotating components and a robust housing design.

Voith said the coordinated system architecture is engineered for durability and long service life while helping operators maintain high conveyor availability.

The integrated control environment also supports remote diagnostics, clearly structured error messages and a globally standardised operating concept.

These capabilities are intended to help maintenance teams identify faults more quickly, reduce troubleshooting time and potentially lower service costs.

Remote diagnostics and standardized operation support lifecycle performance

Beyond installation and commissioning, Voith has designed PowerDrive Mining around long-term serviceability.

Remote diagnostic capabilities can help technical teams assess operating conditions and faults without immediately requiring extensive on-site intervention.

A standardized control and operating concept is also intended to make the system easier to deploy and maintain across mining operations with multiple conveyor installations or geographically dispersed sites.

Voith said the combination of integrated hardware, coordinated control and lifecycle support provides mining customers with clearer system ownership and reduced operational complexity throughout the equipment’s service life.

Electra Mining Africa 2026 provides launch platform

Voith is using Electra Mining Africa 2026 as the international launch platform for PowerDrive Mining.

The Johannesburg exhibition brings together companies from across mining, engineering, energy and industrial technology, providing Voith with an opportunity to demonstrate the new system directly to mining operators, equipment manufacturers and engineering partners.

PowerDrive Mining represents Voith’s first electric drive system developed specifically as an integrated solution for belt conveyor applications, combining drivetrain technology, BeltControl automation, safety functions and service capabilities within one coordinated package.

The Voith Group is a global technology company. With its broad portfolio of systems, products, services and digital applications, Voith sets standards in the markets of energy, paper, raw materials and transport. Founded in 1867, Voith today has around 21,000 employees, sales of € 4.8 billion and locations in over 60 countries worldwide and thus is one of the larger family-owned companies in Europe.

The Group Division Voith Turbo is part of the Voith Group and a specialist for intelligent drive technology, systems as well as tailor-made services. With its innovative and smart products, Voith offers highest efficiency and reliability. Customers from highly diverse industries such as oil and gas, energy, mining and mechanical engineering, ship technology, rail and commercial vehicles rely on the advanced technologies and digital applications of Voith.
