evidence.title: Dassault Systèmes stock down 25% over one year and testing its support at €20.17
evidence.text:
BNP Paribas Exane downgrades Dassault Systèmes to underperform with a €17 target

On Thursday, September 17, BNP Paribas Exane downgraded its opinion on Dassault Systèmes from "market perform" to "underperform", setting a price target of €17. This level represents a downside potential of approximately 17% compared to the current price of €20.53, which explains the pressure on the stock in the morning session. This revision comes in a tense macroeconomic context: the US Federal Reserve has just raised its benchmark interest rates by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00%, the first hike since 2023, while signaling that inflation remained "too high". This monetary tightening weighs on the valuations of technology and software stocks, of which Dassault Systèmes is part. For reference, when publishing H1 2026 results on July 23, the group had confirmed its annual guidance with a revenue target of €6,356 million, in a tone deemed confident by management.

The stock briefly tests its support at €20.17 before rebounding slightly above

In trading this morning, the Dassault Systèmes price briefly broke through its support at €20.17, touching a low of €20.16, before recovering to around €20.53. This test of the threshold illustrates the fragility of the current technical configuration: the stock is trading below its 20-day moving average at €21.71 (gap of -5.44%) and below its 50-day moving average at €20.68, two moving averages that constitute a ceiling. Only the 200-day moving average at €20.20 remains slightly below the current price, offering minimal support. The resistance at €23.09 appears distant in this context, especially since the MACD shows a negative histogram of -0.13, confirming a short-term downward trend. Over the week, the stock is up 1.79%, but it has declined 5.3% over one month and 25.05% over one year, illustrating the depth of the erosion from its peaks. The next reference level to watch remains the support at €20.17, which has just been tested.

In Germany, the introduction of tachographs for commercial vehicles weighing between 2.5 and 3.5 tonnes and used for international transport is driving costs up by as much as 80%. Operators are adopting a range of strategies in response.

Flexibility and automation at Michelin’s Alessandria plant

The rubber-tyred metro systems of Paris, Tokyo and Mexico City have one thing in common: they run on tyres made in Piedmont. Michelin’s Alessandria plant is the only site in the Group that manufactures them, although its main activity is truck tyres . The Piedmont site celebrated 55 years in operation on 16 September 2026 with a ceremony opened by Agostino Mazzocchi, president and chief executive of Michelin Italiana, before handing over to the plant director, Francesco Pepe. The anniversary is part of initiatives marking Michelin’s 120 years in Italy, where the Group has invested more than €430 million over the past five years.

The Alessandria plant employs 950 people across a site covering around 470,000 square metres and has production capacity of 1.2 million tyres a year. Alongside its truck tyre range and tyres for metro systems, the production lines also manufacture large tyres for earthmoving, civil engineering and agricultural machinery. Some 60% of production stays in Italy and Europe, while the remaining 40% goes to markets worldwide. “This is a very significant figure in a context where companies are relocating production abroad,” Pepe stressed. The plant serves both the replacement market and original equipment manufacturers, including makers of trucks, semi-trailers, cranes, quarry vehicles and special-purpose vehicles. For road haulage companies, the reference product is the Multilife model, which Mazzocchi described as the heart of Alessandria’s operations: tyres designed to be regrooved and retreaded, extending their useful life. “It is an approach that helps reduce the total cost of ownership for transport companies and, at the same time, limit resource consumption and CO2 emissions,” explained the president of Michelin Italiana.

Alongside its production lines, the plant has a research centre that works in coordination with the Group’s centre, based at its Clermont-Ferrand headquarters, to validate new materials and new tyres before industrialisation. One of the results is Infinicoil technology, which was developed in Alessandria and is now produced at the site. Pepe says it “makes it possible to reduce consumption during use and tyre wear”. The second example cited by the plant director among products developed in Piedmont is a specific size of the Michelin X-Crane 2 tyre, designed for self-propelled mobile cranes. He explained that the market needed a tyre capable of supporting heavy loads in an application where a truck tyre was no longer sufficient and no existing size met that requirement. When the Group decided to enter the segment, it entrusted Alessandria with development, industrialisation and production.

Innovation also extends to processes, including intralogistics. Of all the Group’s sites, Alessandria was chosen as the pilot plant for the introduction of autonomous guided vehicles in an industrial department. Having successfully completed the trial phase, the technology now operates in the preparation department and is ready to be rolled out to other Michelin plants. Pepe emphasised the organisational impact of the innovation: “When we talk about automation, digitalisation and technology, we are not talking about replacing people, but about supporting them and working alongside them”. Operators who previously drove forklift trucks now focus on improving flows, maintaining automated systems and monitoring them through digital applications.

This reskilling is matched by an intensive training programme, with more than 70,000 hours delivered in 2025. The site was also the pilot, among the Group’s 80 industrial plants, for the Employee Experience project. The initiative entrusts mixed working groups drawn from different departments, functions and levels of responsibility with designing solutions to problems reported by employees themselves. Facilities have also been refurbished, with new changing rooms, break areas, amenities, offices and meeting rooms, while a new security gatehouse opened in May.

The third pillar identified by Pepe is flexibility , an area in which the Group regards the site as its global benchmark. The plant director described a market that moves through different phases and can generate sudden demand for particular production volumes or mixes: “In some cases, we are asked to put sizes back into production that we have not made for months, perhaps even for a few years”, he said. The response is based on a very broad portfolio of ranges and sizes, the technical expertise needed to manage it and a series of alternative organisational arrangements. These allow the plant to adapt rapidly to fluctuations in demand.

Alessandria is also making progress on environmental performance. By 31 December 2025, water consumption had been cut by 64% compared with 2019, against an overall Group target of 50% by 2030. “Our area is rich in water, but we do not know whether that will still be the case in the years ahead”, Pepe commented. For energy and CO2, where the 2030 targets use 2010 as the baseline, the decisive step came in July 2026, when the plant shut down the gas turbine at its thermal power station and replaced it with electric heat pumps powered by electricity certified as coming from renewable sources. As a result of this measure, from 1 January 2027 Alessandria will also meet its 2030 target for energy efficiency and emissions, three years ahead of schedule. The installation of photovoltaic systems and the sourcing of biomethane are now under consideration.

evidence.title: Niagara’s food scene makes Michelin list again. Here are the six restaurants earning culinary recognition
evidence.text:
Revé restaurant in Niagara-on-the-Lake is a new addition to Michelin Recommended.

Pearl Morissette remains Niagara's only two-star restaurant among the six recognized establishments.

Revé restaurant in Niagara-on-the-Lake is a new addition to Michelin Recommended.

Six Niagara restaurants were recognized in the fifth annual Michelin Guide Toronto and Region — two are newly added and one retains its two Michelin Stars.

Released Tuesday, the Michelin Recommended list features both old entries and new additions. Of the 11 restaurants added to this year’s guide, two are located in the Niagara Region: oddBird in St. Catharines and Revé in Niagara-on-the-Lake.

Located near the Meridian Centre in downtown St. Catharines, oddBird at 52 St. Paul St. combines elevated dining and comfort food. It offers a raw oyster bar and Russian-style caviar service, alongside burgers and fried chicken.

A post shared by oddBird. (@oddbird.niagara)

Revé, located at 242 Mary St., offers a four-course and 10-course service, with the option to reserve a premium experience at the chef’s counter. The restaurant’s menu changes with the seasons, and often features seafood, beef and pasta.

A post shared by REVÉ • NIAGARA-ON-THE-LAKE (@experiencereve)

The returning favourites holding their Michelin status

Fat Rabbit in St. Catharines held its place on Michelin’s Recommended list. The restaurant at 34 Geneva St. is known for its butcher services and small shareable plates. Fat Rabbit also has a rotating menu to “showcase some of the lesser-known cuts of meat.”

A post shared by Fat Rabbit (@fatrabbit)

Also holding its place on Michelin’s Recommended list is Trius Winery and Restaurant . Executive chef Frank Dodd works with local farmers, growers and producers to create a menu that reflects wine country cuisine. Located at 1249 Niagara Stone Rd., the Niagara-on-the-Lake eatery offers lunch, dinner and tasting menus as well as a “dinner and a movie” option.

A post shared by Trius Winery & Restaurant | MICHELIN Recommended (@triuswines)

Bib Gourmand of The Michelin Guide , which highlights restaurants that serve high-quality food at a reasonable price, featured Les Incompetents in St. Catharines on the list.

A post shared by Les Incompetents (@barlesincompetents)

Sitting at 386 St. Paul St. , Les Incompetents considers itself a “French(ish)” bar, looking to invoke “play and whimsy” with its food. The restaurant’s entree menu offers baked oysters, cordon bleu chicken sliders and other plates with a French twist.

Niagara’s only two-star Michelin restaurant

Pearl Morissette in Jordan Station holds two Michelin Stars, remaining the only establishment in Niagara with any star rating.

A post shared by Mystic Halifax (@mystichalifax)

Located at 3953 Jordan Rd., the restaurant serves an ever-changing fixed-price menu inspired by seasonal French cooking.

evidence.title: Are Michelin Defender LTX M/S2 Tires Any Good? Here's What Drivers Say
evidence.text:
Are Michelin Defender LTX M/S2 Tires Any Good? Here's What Drivers Say

Michelin makes all sorts of tires, including truck tires like the Defender LTX M/S2. But are they any good? In general, user opinions suggest they are indeed high quality, delivering long tread life, a comfortable ride, and great traction in a variety of conditions. You can buy these high-quality Michelin tires at Costco , as well as a number of other tire dealers.

Tire Rack has recorded a large amount of user feedback on these tires, with customers returning 970 survey ratings and reporting a combined 26 million miles on LTX M/S2 tires. According to Tire Rack drivers, the LTX M/S2 has excellent wet- and dry-weather performance, and also excels when it comes to comfort and treadwear. On the other hand, it wasn't quite as satisfactory for off-roading or driving in winter weather.

On Michelin's website, the LTX M/S2 has a rating of 4.7 stars from more than 2,300 reviews, with 84% of drivers awarding it 5-star ratings and 95% recommending the tire to others. That said, not everyone was happy with their choice: just over 160 reviews on the Michelin product page as of April 2026 give the LTX M/S2 tires average or lower scores for their design, safety, and performance.

The most common problems reported by drivers revolve around higher-than-expected road noise from the premium tires and tread life that doesn't live up to Michelin's 50,000- or 70,000-mile treadwear warranty. In fact, many drivers report significant tire wear, to the point of requiring replacement, at around 30,000 miles.

What's special about Michelin's LTX line of tires?

Michelin is a premium tire brand that demands a high price compared to many other major tire brands . Discount Tire, for example, lists the Michelin Defender LTX M/S2 at $245 per tire, climbing to over $603 depending on the size. The substantial investment might be worth it, as the LTX M/S2 tires have some of the best treadwear ratings among Michelin tires . At launch, Michelin touted that its improved LTX M/S2 tire outlasted three of its leading competitors by 25,000 miles, thanks to an updated compound that Michelin calls "Evertread 2.0."

Michelin Defender LTX tires come in three varieties: LTX Trail, LTX A/T2, and the LTX M/S2. The LTX A/T2 boasts, as the name suggests, all-terrain capabilities, while Michelin markets the LTX Trail for "on and off-road safety made to last." Each has tread patterns that appear well-suited for gravel forest road travel or the occasional foray off-road. Michelin suggests that the M/S2 is a solid all-season tire capable of handling mud and snow, although the feedback we discussed earlier indicates that it's better on asphalt than anything else.

To determine if Michelin Defender LTX M/S2 tires are any good, we turned to the drivers who use them on their vehicles. We sorted through reviews and ratings shared on TireRack.com, a popular online tire retailer, as well as an r/tires subreddit thread dedicated to the Michelin Defender LTX tire family.

We also turned to the large number of reviews posted on Michelin's LTX M/S2 product page, although some of the older entries predate the release of the improved M/S2. While drivers' opinions of the M/S2 are largely favorable across all platforms, not everyone felt the premium tires lived up to their expectations — as you'd expect with such a popular brand. Thus, we made sure to include an overview of common complaints as well.

evidence.title: Michelin Launches Tire With Artificial Intelligence That Reads Wear in Real Time and Promises to Reduce Operating Costs
evidence.text:
Michelin Launches Tire With Artificial Intelligence That Reads Wear in Real Time and Promises to Reduce Operating Costs

New Michelin System Uses Vehicle Data and Artificial Intelligence to Monitor Load and Tire Wear in Real Time with Accurate Predictions Focused on Fleets, Safety and Efficiency

Michelin announced that it will present, next month, at the Consumer Electronics Show 2026 in the United States, a tire system with artificial intelligence capable of monitoring wear in real time, promising to reduce costs and anticipate operational failures.

Michelin’s proposal is to surpass traditional monitoring, focused only on pressure, by using dynamic vehicle data for continuous and predictive analysis.

Developed in partnership with technology company Sonatus, the solution combines two tools called SmartLoad and SmartWear, integrated into a single digital ecosystem.

Data centers could nearly double their electricity use by 2030, testing local power grids

Stephen Hawking’s Final Warning to Humanity is Becoming Reality

Taiwan Prepares Additional $20 Billion in Business Investments in the U.S. Amid AI-Powered Global Chip Race

GlobalFoundries Develops Test Chip with New Memory: 40% Smaller and Up to 60% More Energy Efficient, Targets AI, Cars, and IoT for 2027

According to Michelin, the set can replace the current tire pressure monitoring system, known as TPMS, with relevant operational gains for drivers and fleets.

The company estimates that the global adoption of the technology could generate savings of US$ 1.68 billion, equivalent to R$ 9.5 billion at current exchange rates, by 2030.

Information about the financial impact and functioning of the system was released by the website Carscoops , mentioned by Michelin in the official announcement of the news.

Unlike conventional sensors, the system does not rely solely on internal tire data, broadening the scope of operational analysis.

The artificial intelligence crosses information from the vehicle, including braking intensity, load carried, lateral forces in turns, and usage patterns over time.

With this set of signals, the software calculates the wear and actual load supported by each tire, providing a more accurate reading of remaining useful life.

The goal is to replace generic alerts with specific predictions, tailored to driving style and the real operating conditions of each vehicle.

According to Ali Rezgui, Vice President of the Digital Twin area at Michelin, the system transforms complex data into practical and actionable predictions.

He stated that the technology can extend the life of tires, reduce operational costs, and increase safety, as well as support sustainable mobility strategies.

A sensitive point in connected vehicles is the destination of information collected during daily use in different operational conditions.

In the case of Michelin’s solution, the company states that all data remains stored in the vehicle itself, with no sending to external servers.

The integration occurs through the Sonatus Collector, a platform that allows configuration of the system in different models with low technical adaptation effort.

This decision aims to meet automakers and consumers concerned with privacy and digital security, keeping control of the information within the vehicle.

This positioning differentiates Michelin in a scenario with increased scrutiny over data-based automotive systems, especially in the United States.

To demonstrate the technology, Michelin and Sonatus will take a 1970 Ford Bronco equipped with the smart tire system to CES.

The contrast between a classic utility vehicle and sensors based on artificial intelligence is part of the strategy to present it to the event audience.

During the fair, visitors will be able to monitor real-time data about tire health through the MyTires app, developed by Michelin.

The proposal is to show that the technology does not depend on exclusive platforms for electric vehicles or latest-generation models.

According to the website Carscoops, the demonstration reinforces the system’s flexibility across different automotive architectures.

Michelin is not alone in the race for smart tires, with competitors investing in solutions based on advanced data.

Pirelli launched, in 2021, the Cyber Tire platform, capable of collecting driving data and identifying road surface conditions.

In the United States, however, Pirelli’s technology has come under scrutiny related to national security and data control.

The Chinese company Sinochem holds about 37% of the Italian manufacturer, which has increased oversight from American authorities.

New federal rules are expected to prohibit certain software in connected vehicles starting with the 2027 model year, with hardware restrictions planned for 2030.

If there are no exemptions, cars equipped with Cyber Tire technology may face limitations in the local market, according to the current regulatory landscape.

evidence.title: Renault Revives Gordini as a 270 HP Electric Coupe Concept
evidence.text:
Renault Revives Gordini as a 270 HP Electric Coupe Concept

Renault has reinterpreted the cult 8 Gordini as a two-seat electric coupe.

The car celebrates Gordini, the performance operation that scored racing and rallying success with tuned Renaults before being folded into Renault Sport. The original 8 arrived in 1962 as a four-seat sedan with a rear-mounted engine.

The new concept reworks that formula into a two-seat coupe measuring 4120mm long, slightly more than a Clio. It runs 19-inch wheels up front and 20s at the back. A 270 horsepower electric motor supplies the power.

Renault insists the concept is a one-off. It will eventually go on display at Renault's new Flins museum, the site where the 8 was originally built. The car carries hints of design features and technology that could reach future production models, but Renault is not positioning it as a preview of a specific model.

Renault 8 Gordini Concept: All The Details

Concept car chief Roman Gauvin framed the project around the original's modest character. "The original 8 was a very humble car, a sort of working-class hero," he said. "We wanted to keep that honesty for this concept. It's not a two-metre-wide, 1000bhp machine: it's still approachable and makes you smile."

Gauvin also addressed how Renault sees itself against dedicated sports car makers. "It's about how we position ourselves against sports car brands: for us, it's the fun factor. We're not here to design a car that's going to shave half a second off a lap time at the Nürburgring; it's fun, small, agile and nimble."

The styling keeps the original's round headlights. Renault has also fitted lower spotlights that reference the Gordini version's rallying heritage. The concept wears Gordini's historic blue and white finish, right down to the racing stripes.

evidence.title: New Renault Megane E-Tech arrives with 307 miles of range and 24-minute charging
evidence.text:
The new model-year Renault Megane E-Tech Electric has arrived. Buyers get a new 67 kWh LFP battery that gives the 215 hp compact car up to 307 miles of range. When the battery runs low, it can charge from 15 to 80 percent in about 24 minutes. The EV originally debuted in 2022. Renault has now cut back the previous range of configurations to a much simpler lineup as it faces growing competition in the EV market.

The new LFP (lithium iron phosphate) battery powers a 160 kW motor at the front axle, which produces 221 lb-ft of torque. Renault quotes a maximum WLTP range of exactly 307 miles. According to the company, DC fast charging from 15 to 80% SoC takes around 24 minutes, a 25 percent improvement over the previous model. Every Megane E-Tech comes standard with a heat pump, battery preconditioning to improve charging performance and a bidirectional 11 kW AC onboard charger. A more powerful 22 kW onboard charger is available at extra cost. Regenerative braking with steering wheel paddles and one-pedal drive are also standard.

The updated Megane E-Tech starts at about €34,990 for the Techno trim, while the Esprit Alpine costs €37,990; both include 19% VAT. Renault has also streamlined the lineup: only the battery and powertrain combination described above and these two trims will be available. The Techno includes leatherette dashboard accents, a heated steering wheel, an EV route planner, a digital rearview camera and new 19-inch alloy wheels. Power-adjustable seats and a driver assistance package with augmented vision features are optional. Renault continues to list cargo capacity at 15.5 cubic feet.

The higher-end Esprit Alpine has distinctive 20-inch alloy wheels and Alpine design details. Inside, it adds power-adjustable massaging seats, a Harman Kardon premium audio system and additional driver assistance features, including Active Driver Assist, a 360-degree camera and Easy Park Assist. Renault has expanded the exterior color range to seven choices, including the new Satin Slate Blue. Both trims feature the OpenR link infotainment system with a 12-inch screen and built-in Google services. A future update is expected to add the Gemini AI assistant alongside Google Maps and the Play Store. A new ventilated Qi2 wireless charging pad for smartphones completes the technology updates.

evidence.title: Renault 8 Gordini Concept revives 1960s icon as electric coupé
evidence.text:
Renault 8 Gordini Concept revives 1960s icon as electric coupé

Chic concept combines retro-inspired styling with a 201kW rear-mounted electric motor

Renault has revealed its new Renault 8 Gordini Concept, a two-seat electric coupé inspired by the original Renault 8 Gordini launched in 1964.

Measuring 4,120mm long, 1,880mm wide and 1,270mm tall, the concept reinterprets the historic model with a low, wide stance, squared-off wheel arches and a six-headlight layout. It also features the trademark Gordini double white stripe running down the driver’s side of the bodywork.

The concept rides on 19-inch alloy wheels at the front and 20-inch wheels at the rear, while power comes from a 201kW electric motor mounted on the rear axle.

Inside, the minimalist cabin combines elements inspired by the original car with a more contemporary design twist. The dashboard visor spans the width of the cabin, while a horizontal brushed-aluminium strip houses the round digital instruments. Their thick bezels echo the three-dimensional design of the headlights.

Brushed aluminium is also used for the controls and larger sections of the cabin, replacing plastic surfaces and contrasting with Alcantara upholstery. The cabin is completed by supportive bucket seats upholstered in blue corduroy.

Despite its production-ready appearance, Renault has no plans to manufacture the 8 Gordini Concept as a series model. The company describes it as “an exploratory concept and an exercise in style” created to reinterpret Gordini heritage for the modern era and add to its heritage collection.

The Renault 8 Gordini Concept will be displayed on Renault’s stand at the Paris Motor Show from October 12 to 18.

evidence.title: The only thing wrong with the new Renault 8 Gordini is the fact you can't buy one
evidence.text:
As thrillingly impressive as it is, Renault appears to have missed the mark with the riveting new 8 Gordini – not due to the fact it’s all-electric, but because there appear to be two chances of it ever rolling off the production line: Buckley’s and none.

The two-door EV is a modern interpretation of the Renault 8 Gordini launched in 1964, which became a French performance icon and rallying hero long before Renaultsport and Alpine became synonymous with the company’s hottest machinery.

The Gordini story began with racing driver and engineer Amédée Gordini, nicknamed “The Wizard” for his ability to extract serious performance from small engines. His ties to Renault began in the late 1950s and eventually spawned a series of road and competition cars.

Renault considered around 300 design proposals for this modern interpretation before settling on the finished concept, which reportedly took just two months to develop.

There’s no mistaking the inspiration. The original’s V-shaped nose, four-headlight layout, boxy proportions and distinctive twin white stripes over brilliant blue paint have all been updated without being diluted.

But Renault didn’t simply modernise an old design. The four-door body of the 1960s car has been replaced by a more dramatic two-door sedan silhouette, complemented by heavily flared wheelarches, 19-inch front and 20-inch rear wheels and a diffuser that screams aggression.

Extra driving lights reference the R8 Gordini’s off-road triumphs, while an F1-style rain light is among several nods to Gordini’s motorsport history. At 4.12 metres long, she’s compact like a true rally car, although it is substantially wider and lower than its ancestor.

The minimalist interior is just as striking as the outside. Renault has resisted the temptation to fill the dashboard with giant screens, instead fitting simple circular instruments to a brushed-aluminium fascia.

Blue corduroy features across the lower dashboard and bucket seats, with Alcantara and leather used elsewhere. The centre-console switchgear is brushed aluminium, and the uncluttered look should be forwarded to some modern designers to serve as inspiration.

Technical details are scarce, although Renault has confirmed the 8 Gordini is electric, rear-wheel drive and produces 198kW. That represents an enormous jump over the original, which was also rear-wheel drive but mounted its 1.1-litre, four-cylinder, 71kW mill behind the cabin.

Renault hasn’t disclosed the battery capacity, performance figures or driving range. It also hasn’t confirmed whether the car shares its aluminium underpinnings with the wild Renault 5 Turbo 3E, which produces around 397kW.

There are no plans to put the new 8 Gordini into production. For now, it remains a one-off design exercise that will be displayed at the Paris Motor Show.

Turning it into reality would almost certainly make it an expensive proposition. The Renault 5 Turbo 3E costs roughly $270,000 before Australian taxes and charges, so fans would need exotic money if it ever does start rolling into showrooms.

Renault advanced design boss Romain Gauvin says concepts such as the Gordini allow the company to experiment while changing perceptions of what the French brand can be.Given the finished product, Renault might find plenty of people willing to encourage it to go one step further and actually build the thing.

You can almost hear the sound of Japanese aftermarket tuning fans petitioning Nissan to make this one a reality.

evidence.title: Renault Duster hybrid launch on October 17
evidence.text:
Renault Duster hybrid launch on October 17

Renault is finally gearing up launch the Duster hybrid in India on October 17. This will be the third powertrain option on the Duster, adding to the existing 1.0-litre and 1.3-litre turbo-petrol engines. Called the E Tech system, Renault says it draws from its experience and expertise in Formula 1.

The strong-hybrid Duster combines a naturally aspirated 1,789cc four-cylinder petrol engine with two electric motors, a 20hp unit acting as a generator and a 49hp motor powering the wheels. Combined, the system produces 160hp and 172Nm, and it is supported by a 1.4kWh battery pack.

Unlike the Toyota hybrid system seen on the Hyryder, Grand Vitara and Victoris, Renault’s E Tech setup works differently. The Duster’s hybrid combines a petrol engine with electric drive and a battery, and it sends power to the wheels through a multi-mode automatic gearbox. While Toyota’s full hybrid uses an e-CVT and a power split device for a largely step-free driving feel, Renault’s hybrid transmission uses fixed gear ratios and can shift between them. This means engine rpm is expected to rise and fall more like a conventional automatic, and you may notice gear engagements as it switches between electric drive, engine drive, and a combination of both. It also uses a larger 1.4kWh battery pack compared to Toyota’s 0.60kWh unit.

As with any full hybrid, the efficiency gains come from low-speed electric running, regenerative braking and the ability to keep the petrol engine off when it is not needed. However, real-world fuel economy will still depend on traffic conditions, speed, ambient temperature and driving style. That said, Renault claims the engine will enable 80 percent of city drives to be done in EV mode.

The strong hybrid is expected to help make up for the absence of a diesel engine option on the new Duster. This will also directly compete with the likes of the Maruti Grand Vitara, Victoris and Toyota Hyryder strong-hybrids in the midsize SUV segment.

evidence.title: Renault 8 Gordini celebrates electric comeback – but only as a one-off
evidence.text:
Renault 8 Gordini celebrates electric comeback – but only as a one-off

Renault has recently revived some of its most legendary models as one-off pieces. Now, the Renault 8 Gordini, introduced in 1964, is getting the same treatment: the classic sedan is being reimagined as a two-seater electric coupe with a design inspired by motorsport.

Renault is not only riding the nostalgia wave with its production models like the Renault 5 E-Tech Electric and Twingo E-Tech Electric but is also reviving some of its most iconic models from its 125-year history as one-off creations. Following on from the Showcar R17 Electric Restomod and the Renault 5 Diamant , Renault has now reintroduced the Renault 8 Gordini. First launched in 1964, it’s been reimagined as an all-electric version that pays clear homage to motorsport. With its flat and wide body and a 200-kW electric powertrain, it almost looks like a caricature of a modern rally car.

The concept car was unveiled today at Renault Carwalk – the brand’s showroom on the Champs-Élysées in Paris. The one-off will also be on display at the Renault stand during the Paris Motor Show (12 to 18 October 2026). “With Renault 8 Gordini Concept, we wanted to spark emotion by drawing on both our heritage and modern times, bringing together the icons of yesterday and the future,” explained Alexandre Malval, Vice President of Design at Renault. “This exercise in style sets out to reinvent Renault 8 Gordini for the modern day. The aim of this coupé is to inspire emotion and capture the imagination of all car enthusiasts. And when I talk about emotion, I’m not talking about nostalgia, but real passion for cars.”

The original Renault 8 Gordini was first introduced with a 95 hp rear-mounted engine. According to Renault HQ, it delivered genuine motorsport performance but also demanded advanced driving skills – “an efficient but demanding drive… [it] was a superb “training car” for a generation of drivers, including Jean Ragnotti”. With the Gordini, Renault made advanced performance accessible a decade before the GTI phenomenon. The characteristic double white stripes became its trademark.

Renault naturally retains these stripes in the electric revival. The concept car measures 4.12 metres in length, 1.88 metres in width, and 1.27 metres in height, and is equipped with 19-inch wheels at the front and 20-inch wheels at the rear. With its 200-kW motor, the two-door coupé is far more dynamic than the original four-door model. Visually, the aggressive front end of the concept is emphasised by the V-shaped design and six headlights. Renault has not disclosed further technical specifications – likely because the extreme design is intended to capture all the attention.

“We updated the distinctive styling of the original Renault 8, which was virtually symmetrical from front to rear, to give it a more dynamic look,” Malval emphasises. “With the flowing cabin lines, wide track, prominent wings and wheels of 19 inches at the front and 20 inches at the rear, it appears to hug the road. The decision to make the rear wheels larger creates a visual sense of momentum: a nod to the rear layout that was the hallmark of the hugely enjoyable ride delivered by the original.”

Incidentally, unlike the R17 show car, which resulted from a collaboration between renowned designer Ora Ito and Renault’s design teams, the Renault 8 Gordini Concept’s design is 100 per cent an in-house Renault development. The project began with an internal competition at Renault Design, which sparked a wave of enthusiasm. Outlining the development process, the company explained:”Over 300 sketches were spontaneously submitted by brand designers. Every avenue was explored: from classic retro to futuristic styling, concepts fusing heritage with modern edge, or GT-inspired looks. From these 300 or so proposals, two projects were selected for development as 2:5 scale mock-ups. This made it possible to compare the two and create a new blueprint, bringing together the best of each one.”

evidence.title: Stellantis Hiring Freeze Comes After Engineering Surge
evidence.text:
Stellantis has put a temporary freeze on white. collar hiring in North America, just months after the automaker made a major push to bring thousands of new engineers into the company.

According to the Detroit Free Press , Stellantis confirmed that white collar onboarding has been paused at its North American headquarters in Auburn Hills, Michigan. The Chrysler Technology Center (CTC) is home to a wide range of salaried positions, including engineering, vehicle testing, research, design, marketing, and other corporate operations.

That makes the hiring freeze a pretty dramatic shift, considering Stellantis spent the first half of 2026 bringing thousands of new engineers into the company.

The automaker brought on at least 2,000 new engineers during the spring, according to previous company announcements. Stellantis had also been steadily rebuilding its white collar workforce toward the end of 2025.

Now, the company is shifting its attention toward bringing those new employees into the organization and making better use of the workforce already in place.

Stellantis spokesperson Jodi Tinson told the Detroit Free Press that the first half of the year was “marked by unprecedented hiring to support both the Value Creation Program and the FaSTLAne 2030 strategic plan .”

Tinson said Stellantis is now “entering the next phase of our talent strategy, focused on integrating new employees, accelerating internal career opportunities and continuing to build the capabilities of our workforce.”

The hiring pause comes as Stellantis continues moving forward with its FaSTLAne 2030 turnaround strategy, which includes tighter control over spending and changes to how the automaker directs its money.

In North America, Jeep® and Ram remain major priorities as Stellantis works to strengthen its business following several difficult years for the company.

Putting new white collar hiring on hold gives Stellantis another way to control expenses without immediately reducing the workforce it just spent months building.

For employees already inside the company, Stellantis says the next phase will also put more emphasis on internal career opportunities.

For now, there is no public timeline for when Stellantis will begin white collar hiring again.

It’s a big change from just a few months ago, when Stellantis was actively hiring engineers at a rapid pace. Now that thousands of those new employees are in place, the company is shifting its focus toward getting them settled in and making the most of the workforce it already has.

evidence.title: Stellantis recalls nearly 240K Ram 1500 trucks for rearview camera problem
evidence.text:
Stellantis is voluntarily recalling more than 239,000 2025 and 2026 Ram 1500 trucks because of a software problem that could prevent the rearview camera from displaying while the truck is in reverse. (Stellantis)

Stellantis is recalling nearly a quarter-million Ram 1500 pickup trucks because of a potential problem with their rearview camera system.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration says the recall involves approximately 239,131 Ram 1500 pickup trucks from model years 2025 and 2026. The agency says the rearview camera system may not display the camera's output when the driver shifts the truck into reverse.

The NHTSA says radio software may prevent the rearview image from displaying, increasing the risk of a crash when the driver is backing up.

The issue first appeared between Oct. 6, 2023, when the first 2025 model year Ram 1500 was produced, and Feb. 23, 2026, when the final 2026 model year Ram 1500 was produced.

The agency said similar vehicles that were not included in the recall were built after that timeframe or were built with a different radio and/or camera.

Chrysler is conducting a voluntary safety recall on all affected vehicles to update the radio software. The NHTSA says the automaker will begin notifying owners of affected vehicles starting Thursday.

In the meantime, owners can visit the website and enter their vehicle identification number to see if their vehicle is included in the recall.

evidence.title: Unifor-Stellantis talks remain at an impasse
evidence.text:
Unifor-Stellantis talks remain at an impasse

Published: September 25, 2026 at 6:11a.m. EDT

Contract talks between Unifor and Stellantis remain at an impasse.

Unifor posted a video to its social media pages Thursday evening stating there are still no formal talks scheduled, although communication with the company remains open.

The biggest sticking point remains the future of Stellantis’ Brampton Assembly Plant.

Unifor says Stellantis continues to maintain its position on closing and potentially selling the plant, while the union says it wants a resolution for workers there before a new contract is reached.

Previous contract talks stalled on Sept. 11 , and the current collective agreement expired Sunday night.

Unifor National President Lana Payne says this week, she spoke with Premier Doug Ford, top officials in the Prime Minister’s office, and the Federal Industry Department.

She says the closure of the Brampton plant would have serious consequences for other plants as well.

“It would be devastating for our members, for the suppliers, for the entire auto industry. If Stellantis is allowed to break its commitment to our Brampton members and get away with it, this will become a major problem for thousands of Unifor members in other facilities like Windsor, Etobicoke, and our distribution centres in Mississauga and Red Deer.”

Payne says they will not stop fighting for all of the Stellantis plants.

“We will continue to press the company and government for an outcome that is acceptable to our members and to our union because the last thing we want, the very last thing we want, is to lose an auto plant during this trade war, reducing the number of good union auto jobs in Canada and handing a victory to Donald Trump.”

Unifor Local 444 President and Stellantis Master Bargaining Committee Chair James Stewart says workers are not currently in a legal strike position.

“Our collective agreement expired on September 20th, and as previously reported, Unifor, as of today, is not in a legal strike position. Unifor and Stellantis remain in conciliation - a process required under the Ontario Labour Relations Act - and that conciliation process must conclude before union members can legally go on strike or be locked out by the employer.”

Stewart says the union is considering its options, but there is no strike vote scheduled at this time.

“We’re assessing all of our options, including when to set a legal strike deadline if that becomes necessary. For now, the terms and conditions of our current agreement, that’s the 2023 collective agreement, remain in effect. A strike is always our last resort for our union and something we don’t take for granted. We’ll make that decision based on what’s in the best interest of our members.”

Unifor represents more than 9,000 Stellantis workers across Canada, including those at the Windsor Assembly Plant.

Unifor says the lines of communication with Stellantis remain open, but there are currently no formal talks scheduled. The union says it will provide an update when that changes.

SpaceX lift helps Peugeot Invest absorb Stellantis slump

Peugeot Invest said on Thursday that the value of its SpaceX exposure rose by €131 million in the first half, based on its results for the period. That gain came through funds run by Valor Equity Partners and acted as a counterweight to a sharp decline in Stellantis NV, which fell 47% and would have nearly flattened overall returns without the SpaceX lift .

Fulfilling his pledge to be more proactive, the company revealed this week that it is buying a minority interest in Mérieux NutriSciences for $175 million.

Minority shareholders continue to apply pressure on multiple fronts, citing the Stellantis exposure, a stubborn gap between Peugeot Invest's market price and the assessed value of its assets, and governance concerns. Douin also noted that selling the stake in Immobiliere Dassault closes the company's chapter in real estate. Asked about Stellantis, he stated that Peugeot Invest is still in step with the automaker's management and turnaround plan despite "disappointing" performance. "At this stage there is no project to do a decoupling or anything else" regarding the holding, he said, emphasizing that any such move would require careful consultations with all shareholders to assess tax and legal implications. He described the position as "not an ordinary investment, it's the historic investment and that's the way it's treated, as a legacy investment that we continue to focus on."

evidence.title: Volvo Group turns a supplier challenge into a logistics win
evidence.text:
Volvo Group turns a supplier challenge into a logistics win

Volvo Group North America’s cab plant in Kings Mountain, N.C., is a busy operation. It’s where cabs are built for Volvo’s Class 8 heavy-duty trucks, including over-the-road tractors, along with medium-duty trucks used in applications like refuse collection and other city fleets.

Those cabs and related components are then moved from Kings Mountain into Volvo Group’s production network in Virginia and Pennsylvania, where they have to arrive on time and in the right sequence to keep production on schedule. Any delay in that flow can affect build plans, customer commitments, and the broader truck market that Volvo Group serves.

Before Volvo Group acquired the Kings Mountain operation, the site was part of the company’s supplier network. Volvo initially set out to help the supplier improve the flow of materials and get cab production back on track. Starting with an assessment of the logistics operation, Volvo looked at the constraints around the site and what it would take to support better movement in and out of the facility.

“We were looking at it as a supplier issue at first,” says Dave Yancey, project manager, production logistics, at Volvo Group North America. “They were behind on our cab production, and it was affecting our markets. We sat down to assess the operation and figure out how to fix the logistics flow, including the warehouse capacity we needed to support the site.”

A familiar partner for a fast-moving problem

Volvo needed a logistics partner that could step in quickly, understand its production environment, and help stabilize the warehouse side of the operation. The company had options, but this project didn’t come with months to plan from scratch. Material was already coming in, cab production needed support, and the Kings Mountain site was still changing.

A. Duie Pyle (ADP) already had a track record with Volvo Group, having provided regional less-than-truckload (LTL) service and value-added logistics support. It also handled cab storage for Volvo Group’s Mack Trucks operation in Macungie, Pa., during an earlier production challenge.

“When I was in Macungie, we had a major success story with the ADP team,” Yancey says. “They were storing our cabs at the time and helped us through some production issues. I liked the system they used and thought this would be a perfect model.”

What started out as a supplier-support effort became part of a larger transition when Volvo Group acquired the Kings Mountain operation. ADP already had agreements in place with the supplier, so the acquisition added contract complexity at the same time the warehouse had to keep receiving, organizing and moving material.

“Once we got the agreements straightened out, it was full speed ahead,” Yancey says. “The attitude from the ADP team was: ‘Tell us what we need to do and we’ll make it happen.’”

How Do You Really Do It: Implement real-time visualization in a way that impacts results?

And with that, Volvo took over a 180,000-square-foot warehouse that still needed the basics before it could fully support the operation. Material had to be received, staged, and stored while utilities, equipment, and warehouse processes were still being put in place.

“It started as just a warehouse with no electricity,” says Yancey. “We used pallet jacks to unload inbound material, and then we started getting power, forklifts, racking, shelving, and scanning. It went from being an empty shell to a functioning warehouse.”

Working together, Volvo and ADP moved the initial material into the warehouse over roughly nine days, even as new inbound shipments continued to arrive. Once electricity, forklifts, and other equipment were in place, the operation started to function more like a true warehouse. By the following spring, ADP and Volvo were adding racking to increase storage capacity and make better use of the space.

Yancey says ADP brought in a capable team to help Volvo get through that stretch. “We have a lot of good people inside Volvo Group, but we can also be spread very thin,” Yancey says. “ADP was able to jump through hoops, make things happen and bring in the right people to get this done.”

With this project, both Volvo and ADP had to carefully assess where parts belonged inside the warehouse and how quickly those parts needed to move. The operation was organized around truck model and product line, including Class 8 highway trucks, Class 6 trucks and cab-over models.

Each had its own parts profile, and some of the existing supplier’s part numbers didn’t follow Volvo’s normal numbering conventions. “This added complexity to the setup,” says Yancey.

As production patterns became easier to see, ADP and Volvo used that information to set up more directed putaway and improve turn times. “We set the operation up by model so we could move the fast-moving parts to the front and make our turn time quicker,” Yancey says. “If something didn’t move as often, we could put it deeper in the warehouse.”

There were also repacking requirements to consider because some of the manufacturer’s parts came in on one-way pallets or in packaging that didn’t match its standards. Some pallets also arrived with multiple part numbers or incomplete identification, which made them harder to receive, store and move efficiently. ADP had to move those parts into Volvo-approved containers before they could move through the warehouse and back to the plant.

Finally, the new warehouse had to meet Volvo’s compliance requirements, including both ISO and environmental standards. That meant handling cardboard, plastic, wood pallets and other waste streams properly rather than sending everything to a landfill. It added another layer of discipline during the early months, when ADP and Volvo were still improving the physical setup, training new employees, and bringing the warehouse up to Volvo’s standards.

Going into the project, Volvo’s supplier had its own warehouse system, but ADP could generate inventory reports multiple times a day and help Volvo compare physical inventory against what the plant expected to see. That gave the teams a better handle on inventory accuracy while the operation was still settling in.

Volvo and ADP also built key performance indicators (KPIs) around the parts of the operation Yancey wanted to measure, including repacking activity, pallet handling and inbound and outbound volume. The prior day’s KPIs were available by noon the next day, followed by weekly and monthly summaries. That gave the team a way to spot bottlenecks, track warehouse performance, and make decisions as the operation matured.

With its first wave of inbound material under control, the newly-acquired operation started to find its footing. Power came online within the first few days, forklifts followed and the warehouse began taking on the pieces it needed to function properly, from racking and shelving to scanning.

By the following spring, ADP and Volvo were adding more racking to increase storage capacity and make better use of the space. “The facility went from being a shell to a functioning warehouse,” says Yancey. “The early stages of the transition were challenging, but overall it was a huge turnaround. The warehouse runs extremely well.”

For ADP, Volvo’s Kings Mountain project grew out of a relationship built on both execution and trust. Chris Incudine, VP of solutions design at ADP, works closely with Yancey and says Volvo was asking the company to step into an unusual situation: help take over a supplier’s logistics operation because the manufacturer needed help stabilizing it.

“If you take the relationship out of it, you basically have a customer asking us to go run their supplier’s operation for them because they had more trust in us than they did in the supplier,” Incudine says. “That’s a unique scenario. There has to be a level of trust there, and that trust came from the partnership we’d already built.”

ADP, which wasn’t operating in North Carolina at the time, also had to step outside its own regional network to support the project. Incudine says the strength of the Volvo relationship made the decision possible. Regional LTL carriers like ADP can be a strong fit for this kind of work because they tend to know their customers closely, understand the freight and can respond quickly when a transportation issue becomes a broader supply chain challenge.

“We wouldn’t have been in North Carolina three years ago if we hadn’t gotten an ask from such a strong partner,” Incudine says. “I think it speaks to the level of partnership and trust we’d built through execution and transparency.”

That transparency had to flow both ways, of course. He says Volvo was direct about what it needed, while ADP was equally direct about what was working, what needed attention, and where the operation needed support. That open communication helped both companies work through a project that was anything but simple. “It wasn’t all easy. There was blood and sweat—and some tears,” he says, laughing, “but we got Volvo what they needed.”

Volvo Cars sets former Porsche North America leader as global CEO

This story was originally published on WardsAuto. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily WardsAuto newsletter .

A former top executive for Porsche in North America will take the global helm at Volvo Cars next year when the current CEO retires for the second time.

Klaus Zellmer will assume the role of president and CEO at Volvo Cars by Oct. 1, 2027, Volvo Cars said in a Sept. 20 press release . He will replace Håkan Samuelsson, who — along with the rest of the board of directors — will work with Zellmer "to ensure a seamless transition."

Zellmer, who was named CEO of the Volkswagen Group subsidiary Škoda Auto in 2022 , claims more than 30 years working in the auto industry

Born in 1967, Zellmer graduated with a degree in business administration and then spent three years from 1994 working at the Institute for Automotive Economics at the Nürtingen-Geislingen University of Applied Sciences in Germany.

He spent more than 20 years working at the Porsche brand, where he held several senior leadership positions, including CEO of Porsche Deutschland and CEO of Porsche North America.

After this period he became a member of the board of management of Volkswagen Passenger Cars, where he was responsible for marketing, sales and after sales before taking the lead role at Škoda.

Zellmer has led Škoda to record sales results in 2025, followed by further growth and record deliveries of electric vehicles in the first half of 2026.

"Klaus Zellmer combines deep automotive expertise with broad international leadership experience and a strong record of guiding organizations through transformation and changing market conditions," said Eric Li, chairman of Volvo Cars in a statement. "His experience from both the high-end premium segment and high-volume brands, is an excellent fit for Volvo Cars."

The news follows Samuelsson's recent announcement of a product blitz of 13 new models, in a bid to double profit margins for the automaker.

Samuelsson has led the company over two tenures: from 2012 to 2022, and again since April 2025 , when he returned to develop the "future strategic roadmap for the company in very challenging times for the automotive industry", the company said in its statement.

evidence.title: Volvo Cars Names Klaus Zellmer As President And CEO To Lead Next Growth Chapter
evidence.text:
Volvo Cars has appointed Klaus Zellmer as President and Chief Executive Officer, selecting an automotive industry veteran with more than three decades of experience across Škoda Auto, Volkswagen and Porsche to lead the company through its next phase of development.

Zellmer will assume the position no later than October 1, 2027. Current CEO Håkan Samuelsson will work with Volvo Cars’ Board of Directors to provide a seamless leadership transition.

Zellmer currently serves as Chairman of the Board of Management and CEO of Škoda Auto, where he has overseen a period of significant growth and increasing electric vehicle sales.

Under his leadership, Škoda became one of Europe’s best-selling automotive brands and delivered record results in 2025. The company followed that performance with additional growth and record electric vehicle deliveries during the first half of 2026.

That combination of experience in both high-volume automotive markets and premium brands was a major factor in Volvo Cars’ decision to appoint Zellmer.

Before joining Škoda, Zellmer served on the Board of Management of Volkswagen Passenger Cars with responsibility for Marketing, Sales and After Sales.

He previously spent more than 20 years at Porsche, holding several senior leadership positions across the premium automaker.

His roles included CEO of Porsche Deutschland and CEO of Porsche North America, giving Zellmer extensive experience across European and U.S. automotive markets as well as premium vehicle sales and brand management.

Zellmer’s background also spans industrial operations, technology, commercial strategy and organizational transformation, capabilities that Volvo Cars sees as increasingly important as the global automotive industry continues changing.

Automakers are simultaneously navigating electrification, software-defined vehicles, changing consumer expectations, new competitors and substantial capital requirements associated with developing the next generation of vehicles.

Volvo Cars has been working through that transition while maintaining its longstanding positioning around safety, Scandinavian design and premium vehicles.

Chairman Eric Li said Zellmer’s experience leading organizations through periods of transformation and changing market conditions makes him particularly well suited to Volvo Cars.

The board expects Zellmer to build on the company’s existing foundation while strengthening Volvo Cars’ position in the global premium automotive market.

His appointment also marks the next stage of a leadership transition that began when Samuelsson returned to Volvo Cars in April 2025.

Samuelsson previously served as CEO from 2012 through 2022 before returning for a second tenure during a particularly challenging period for the global automotive industry.

Since his return, Samuelsson has worked to provide stability while helping develop Volvo Cars’ future strategic roadmap and preparing the company for a long-term successor.

His two tenures have therefore covered some of the most consequential periods in Volvo Cars’ modern history, including the company’s expansion as a global premium automaker and its more recent shift toward electrification.

Zellmer will inherit a company with an established global brand and an increasingly electrified vehicle portfolio.

Volvo Cars has expanded its lineup with a growing range of fully electric vehicles while continuing to compete across SUVs, sedans, estates and hybrid models.

The company’s challenge will be maintaining the characteristics that have historically differentiated Volvo while adapting to an industry increasingly influenced by batteries, software, artificial intelligence, connectivity and digital consumer experiences.

Zellmer’s recent experience at Škoda could provide relevant lessons.

Škoda has balanced significant sales volume with the expansion of its electric vehicle offering, while operating within the broader Volkswagen Group technology and manufacturing ecosystem.

His earlier experience at Porsche adds another dimension, particularly as Volvo seeks to reinforce its position as a premium brand rather than compete solely on vehicle volume.

Zellmer, who was born in 1967, began his automotive career after earning a degree in Business Administration.

He spent three years beginning in 1994 at the Institute for Automotive Economics at the Nürtingen-Geislingen University of Applied Sciences before beginning a career that would eventually span several of Europe’s largest automotive brands.

His appointment gives Volvo Cars a leader with experience across multiple areas of the industry, including sales, marketing, technology, premium vehicles, mass-market brands and international operations.

For Zellmer, the opportunity involves leading a company approaching its centennial while preserving a brand identity closely associated with safety and Scandinavian design.

Volvo Cars’ board sees the appointment as an opportunity to combine those established strengths with further transformation as the company competes in a rapidly evolving global automotive market.

“Klaus Zellmer combines deep automotive expertise with broad international leadership experience and a strong record of guiding organisations through transformation and changing market conditions.”

“His experience from both the high-end premium segment and high-volume brands, is an excellent fit for Volvo Cars. The Board is confident that, under Klaus Zellmer’s leadership, Volvo Cars will build on its strong foundations and enter its next chapter with a clear ambition to strengthen its position as a leading premium car company.”

“I am delighted to join Volvo Cars at such an important moment in the company’s development. Few automotive brands have built such a strong and lasting reputation for safety, consistently applying this core value across the mobility sector.”

“The company has a solid foundation and an experienced team, and I look forward to working with colleagues across Volvo Cars to build on these strengths.”

“After almost 100 years, Volvo Cars’ ability to reinvent itself time and again is both a remarkable achievement and an ongoing challenge. I look forward to contributing to the company’s continued development and to shaping its next chapter together.”

evidence.text:
Home › News › Volvo Cars picks VW margin operator to succeed Samuelsson

Volvo Cars picks VW margin operator to succeed Samuelsson

Delaying Zellmer's start until October 2027 suggests that Volvo Cars wants its 13-model plan embedded before he takes over. By Stewart Burnett

Volvo Cars has abruptly announced the appointment of Klaus Zellmer, currently Chief Executive of Škoda, as its next President and Chief Executive, with the German boss taking over the reins no later than 1 October 2027. Current Chief Executive Håkan Samuelsson, who returned to the role in 2025 to replace the ousted Jim Rowan, will remain in place until then to oversee what the company called a “seamless transition”.

Zellmer brings nearly 30 years of experience almost entirely within the Volkswagen Group, including more than two decades at Porsche where he ran both the German and North American operations, followed by a spell on Volkswagen Passenger Cars’ board overseeing marketing, sales and aftersales. He has led Škoda since 2022, delivering record results in 2025 and record electric vehicle (EV) deliveries in the first half of this year, at an operating margin of 8.3% against Volvo’s own 3.5%.

Samuelsson returned to the top job in April 2025 on a fixed mandate to stabilise Volvo Cars after predecessor Rowan, a former Dyson and BlackBerry executive with no prior automotive experience, was ousted following software delays on the EX90 and a since-abandoned pledge to sell EVs and nothing else by 2030. It has since reneged and pivoted towards hybrids due to what it characterises as demand realities in its most critical markets.

On his return to the role—he was also Rowan’s predecessor—Samuelsson launched an SEK18bn (€1.6bn) cost and cash savings programme and cut 3,000 jobs. Under his leadership, the automaker set out a 13-model electrified product offensive earlier in September targeting an operating margin above 8%, split between seven Western-market vehicles built on existing SPA2 and SPA3 platforms and six models developed specifically for China alongside majority owner Geely.

Zellmer inherits that plan directly, including a commitment to triple parts commonality with Geely to 30% from around 10% today. Chairman Eric Li said Zellmer’s “experience from both the high-end premium segment and high-volume brands is an excellent fit”. In his own statement, Zellmer acknowledged the scale of what he is taking on: “After almost 100 years, Volvo Cars’ ability to reinvent itself time and again is both a remarkable achievement and an ongoing challenge.”

The roughly 12-month gap between the announcement and Zellmer’s actual start date is unusually long for a Chief Executive transition, giving Samuelsson time to embed the new strategy operationally before handing over execution. Zellmer’s own career, built almost entirely in European and high-volume markets at Škoda and Porsche, has given him comparatively little direct exposure to the China-specific, Geely-co-developed models that now sit at the centre of Volvo’s next chapter.

Rowan, Samuelsson and Zellmer trace a complete arc in barely three years, from a software-first bet on pure electrification to an emergency caretaker to a career operations executive charged with delivering margin. The speed of that reversal says as much about how quickly the EV transition’s economics shifted underneath Volvo as it does about any single leader’s fit for the role.

evidence.title: Cyber Attack on Scania Results in Major Document Theft
evidence.text:
Cyber Attack on Scania Results in Major Document Theft

The recent cyber attack on Scania has raised significant concerns regarding data security and corporate protection measures. The hackers reportedly infiltrated the systems of the Swedish truck manufacturer, Scania, and made off with a staggering 34,000 documents—a figure that underscores the magnitude of this information breach. These documents were stolen from the company's corporate insurance division, a segment that is a part of the broader TRATON Group.

Details surrounding the infiltration suggest that the attackers utilized stolen credentials from a third-party IT vendor to gain access to Scania's systems. This method of entry is increasingly common in cyber attacks and highlights the vulnerabilities that can arise from third-party suppliers. The initial access took place on May 28, and the attackers used malware designed for stealing information to facilitate their breach.

Scania's transparency in addressing the incident stands out, with company representatives confirming the breach and detailing how it occurred. A spokesperson stated, "We can confirm that a security incident occurred in the application insurance.scania.com, which was provided by an external IT partner." This level of transparency can be commendable in terms of restoring stakeholder confidence but does raise questions about overall data security practices.

On May 30, following the breach, the attackers initiated a scheme of extortion. They dispatched emails to several Scania employees from an account on ProtonMail, threatening to publicly disclose the sensitive data unless their demands were met. The extortionists escalated their pressure tactics by also employing compromised email accounts of third parties to further manipulate the situation.

The stolen data potentially includes confidential details about Scania's insurance clients and the vehicles they operate, based on vehicle identification numbers (VINs). This information can have serious implications, not just for Scania but also for its clients who rely on the integrity of their corporate insurance services. The full extent of the ramifications is unclear, but the compromised information could lead to targeted phishing schemes or other malicious activities.

Scania is a significant player in the commercial vehicle sector, commanding nearly 19% of the European market for trucks and buses, as indicated in their latest financial report. The company has a workforce of approximately 59,000 employees worldwide and reported revenues surpassing $22 billion in 2024. Given its importance in logistics and transportation, this breach raises broader concerns within the industry about the security measures governing sensitive data.

This incident sheds light on the escalating cybersecurity threats faced by companies involved in logistics and transportation. Data breaches can disrupt supply chains, impact delivery systems, and erode customer trust. Moreover, the repercussions can extend beyond the immediate financial implications, affecting branding and long-term relationships with clients and partners.

The cyber attack on Scania underscores a growing menace in the logistics field—data security is no longer just an IT issue but a critical business concern. evidence.title: Scania Confirms Data Breach that Leaked Insurance Claim Documents
evidence.text:
Scania Confirms Data Breach that Leaked Insurance Claim Documents

Auto giant Scania has disclosed a data breach stemming from a third-party managed system in May 2025, which resulted in threat actors stealing insurance claim documents.

Sweden-based Scania is a subsidiary of Traton SE, a member of the Volkswagen Group. Specializing in heavy commercial vehicles, such as trucks and buses, it commands nearly a fifth (19%) of the European car market. It operates in ten locations worldwide, employing over 59,000 people. In 2024, the Swedish truck manufacturer reported $22 billion in annual revenue.

Scania learned of the data breach after the threat actors contacted its employees, threatening to leak the stolen documents online unless a ransom was paid.

Scania data breach leaks insurance claim documents

According to the threat actor, the data breach leaked 34,000 insurance claim documents, likely containing sensitive information.

However, details that may have been leaked are currently unclear, but they could include personal information, insurance details, and health data. Similarly, the number of victims impacted by the Scania data breach remains unknown.

According to threat intelligence platform Hackmanac , the attacker has listed the stolen insurance claim documents for exclusive sale to a single buyer, suggesting that Scania had refused to pay the ransom. Hackers usually publicize a data breach after the victim organization becomes uncooperative.

“Hi guys. We hacked new target and selling full attachment of ‘insurance.scania.com’. Full attached files is 34,000 and first time hacked + just will 1 hand sell,” the hacker posted.

The attacker claims the data breach was a first-time intrusion, suggesting that they did not have persistence. They also posted a few image samples of the stolen insurance claim documents as proof.

Meanwhile, Scania has confirmed the data breach and disclosed that it affected a third-party-managed subdomain ‘insurance[.]scania[.]com.’ Subsequently, other internal information systems and IT infrastructure were not affected during the attack and ransomware was likely not deployed.

Leaked insurance claims documents claimed to have limited risks

The automotive giant also assessed the impact of the data breach and claimed that the leaked insurance claim documents posed limited privacy risks. However, leaking insurance claim documents risks reputational damage, which could potentially undermine the company’s brand.

For now, the impacted subdomain has been taken offline to prevent further compromise. The company is also in the process of notifying the victims and regulatory authorities. Scania has also launched an investigation into the insurance data breach to determine the nature of the information stolen.

The Swedish bus and truck manufacturer also disclosed that the threat actor leveraged stolen credentials harvested using an infostealer, which extracts authentication credentials from web browsers, configuration files, and other sources.

Automakers are lucrative targets for cyber attacks due to the vast amount of personal information they collect from their customers. Additionally, their strong financial position and powerful brands make them more likely to pay the ransom.

In May 2025, the Stormous ransomware gang listed the Volkswagen Group on its data leak site, claiming it had breached the company and stolen troves of sensitive information. However, Volkswagen rubbished those claims, asserting that its investigation had uncovered no evidence of unauthorized third-party access to its systems or misuse of its company data.

Transport Solution Company Scania Confirms Cybersecurity Incident

Scania, a transport solution organization, has confirmed it faced a cybersecurity incident. The company has stated that the malicious actors leveraged compromised credentials to gain access to its Financial Services systems, allowing them to acquire insurance claim documents. The malicious actors have threatened to leak the online activity unless their demands are fulfilled.

Erich Kron, Security Awareness Advocate at KnowBe4, comments, “Stolen credentials continue to be a significant security concern and were used in this attack. This outlines the need for additional account security such as MFA to help protect accounts . While it’s not a perfect solution, MFA, especially the type that is phishing resistant, can improve account security greatly. This is important not only for internal accounts, but also for external vendors and those outside of the organization that may occasionally need access. Victims whose information was stolen should be on high alert for the potential of social engineering scams that may reference this data and use it against them.”

The organization states that breach’s impact was limited, and that privacy authorities have been notified regarding the incident.

evidence.title: Major truck manufacturer Scania confirms insurance site cyber attack
evidence.text:
Major truck manufacturer Scania confirms insurance site cyber attack

Swedish heavy vehicle manufacturer Scania has confirmed that threat actors successfully breached its insurance and financial services division.

A member of the Volkswagen Group, Scania is a major producer of large trucks, buses and heavy industrial vehicles and engines. It employs over 59,000 people worldwide, sells over 100,000 vehicles annually and has an annual revenue of US$20.5 billion.

Earlier this month, a threat actor going by “hensi” claimed a cyber attack on the company URL “insurance[.]scania[.]com”, claiming to have exfiltrated data.

“Hi guys. We hacked new target and selling full attachment [sic] of [Scania insurance],” the threat actor wrote in a post spotted by Hackmanac .

“Full attached files is 34,000 and first time hacked + just will 1 hand sell.”

At the time of writing, the website listed is down, saying it has “been temporarily taken offline” and that there is “system maintenance in progress”.

However, speaking with BleepingComputer , Scania confirmed that threat actors had breached its network and exfiltrated data.

“We can confirm there has been a security-related incident in the application ‘insurance.scania.com’, the application is provided by an external IT partner,” a Scania spokesperson told BleepingComputer .

“On the 28th and 29th of May, a perpetrator used credentials for a legitimate external user to gain access to a system used for insurance purposes; our current assumption is that the credentials used by the perpetrator were leaked by a password stealer malware.”

“Using the compromised account, documents related to insurance claims were downloaded.”

Following the breach, the threat actor used an @ proton.me email address to extort company employees directly and began publishing samples of the data.

“Early on the 30th (CEST), the attacker sent emails from proton.me to a number of Scania employees threatening to disclose the data.”

“A follow-up email with similar content came later from an unrelated [third] party whose email had been compromised. The data was later leaked by an actor named Hensi.”

While Cyber Daily has not observed the leaked data or samples, insurance documents typically contain large amounts of personal data, including names, phone numbers, email and physical addresses, and potentially even medical and financial information.

Scania has launched an investigation into the breach and has notified privacy authorities of the incident. It also added that the cyber attack’s impact was limited.

The company has since disabled the breached application.

evidence.title: Hackers claim breach of Scania’s corporate insurance arm, allegedly stealing 34,000 files
evidence.text:
Hackers claim breach of Scania’s corporate insurance arm, allegedly stealing 34,000 files

Scania, one of Europe’s leading manufacturers of commercial vehicles, has reportedly fallen victim to a cyberattack, with hackers claiming to have stolen tens of thousands of internal documents from the company’s corporate insurance division.

The alleged breach surfaced on a restricted-access hacker forum frequented by cybercriminals for trading stolen data. In a post published by the attackers, they assert that they successfully infiltrated Scania’s corporate insurance infrastructure and exfiltrated 34,000 confidential files previously unavailable to the public.

At this time, the specific contents of the stolen files remain unknown. However, given the nature of corporate insurance operations at Scania, the data may include sensitive information related to customers, including details such as vehicle identification numbers (VINs) and commercial vehicle ownership.

Scania’s official website currently displays a maintenance notice on the VabisLine system, the platform allegedly targeted in the breach. The message reads, “We are currently performing maintenance on the VabisLine system. The system has been temporarily taken offline.” It is not confirmed whether this downtime is directly connected to the reported cyber incident.

Efforts to contact Scania for comment on the incident are ongoing, and the company has yet to release an official statement addressing the allegations.

With approximately 59,000 employees worldwide and annual revenues surpassing $22 billion in 2024, Scania holds a substantial 19% share of the European commercial vehicle market, according to its first-quarter 2025 financial report. Its scale and global footprint make it a high-value target for cybercriminal groups.

The automotive sector continues to face mounting pressure from sophisticated cyber threats. Earlier this month, hackers also claimed responsibility for a breach involving the Volkswagen Group, further highlighting the persistent risk faced by multinational manufacturers holding vast amounts of sensitive customer and corporate data.
