evidence.title: Damen Shipyards and SAFEEN Group to bring the first electric tug to the Middle East
evidence.text:
Damen Shipyards and SAFEEN Group to bring the first electric tug to the Middle East

Damen Shipyards and SAFEEN Group, part of AD Ports Group, have signed an agreement for the lease and purchase of an all-electric Damen RSD-E Tug 2513. The RSD-E Tug 2513 will be the first fully electric tug to operate in the Middle East.

The powerful yet compact new tug, which is just 25 metres in length but has a bollard pull of 70 tonnes, is capable of manoeuvring even the largest vessels and can undertake two or more assignments before being recharged, which takes just two hours.

from left to right: Kommer Damen (Chairman of Damen Shipyards Group), Pascal Slingerland (Damen Shipyards Regional Sales Director, Middle East) and Capt. Adil Banihammad (CEO Marine Services & General Manager SAFEEN Marine Services)

Following the successful launch of the class in August 2022 in the Port of Auckland, New Zealand, Damen Shipyards began series production on speculation with an initial run of six vessels. The first to be completed has now departed Damen Song Cam Shipyard in Vietnam and is en-route for Khalifa Port in Abu Dhabi. There it will join the tug fleet operated by SAFEEN Group, the region’s leading maritime services provider.

Damen’s Financial Services (DFS), a subsidiary of Damen Shipyards, is providing a leasing package to support the purchase. DFS offers this service as it enables clients to finance their transition to a more sustainable future. DFS has recently acquired a second RSD-E Tug 2513 which is available on a lease- to-own basis.

The contract was signed on the second of May in Abu Dhabi by Capt. Adil Banihammad and Mr. Kommer Damen. The vessel will be unveiled to the international towage community at the 27th International Tug & Salvage Convention, Exhibition & Awards taking place from 21 to 23 May in Dubai.

Following that it will enter service in Khalifa Port handling container ships, car carriers and other traffic.

With shore-based charging facilities yet to be introduced, it will operate initially in hybrid mode with the Tier III compliant generators being used to charge the batteries.

“We are delighted to be working with SAFEEN Group as they once again lead the way in setting new standards in sustainability in the Middle Eastern maritime community,” says Pascal Slingerland, Damen Shipyards Regional Sales Director, Middle East. Source: Damen Shipyards Group

evidence.title: Damen Shipyards and BigLift to Bring 11 Tugs from East Asia to Europe
evidence.text:
Damen Shipyards and BigLift to Bring 11 Tugs from East Asia to Europe

Published May 20, 2024 2:05 PM by The Maritime Executive

Damen Shipyards and leading heavy lift specialist BigLift Shipping have completed a major logistical feat. A single vessel has transported eleven Damen tugs from the shipbuilder’s yards in Vietnam and China to Europe.

While such voyages usually require six months to plan and organise, this one had less than two months to prepare and ensure that each stage was executed on time. The ship used to transport the eleven Damen tugs was BigLift’s Happy Star, a 156-metre heavy lift vessel equipped with two heavy lift mast cranes of 1100 mt each.

The Happy Star departed Halong Bay, Vietnam, for Europe on the fourth of April and arrived 38 days later at Vigo, Spain, to unload one vessel before continuing on to Rotterdam. It will arrive there on the 19th of May to unload the remaining ten.

These mass deliveries do not take place often as it is rare that so many vessels are ready to be despatched at the same time. The last such event occurred in 2015 when Happy Star transported 22 vessels of various types on the same route. However, this brings advantages versus delivering vessels on their own hulls. These include having the vessels and their equipment arriving in pristine condition. The marine environment also benefits from having fewer emissions with just one ship, albeit a larger one, doing all the work. These outcomes align well with Damen’s commitment to sustainability andoperational excellence.

“At Damen we aim to provide our clients with a holistic service that includes not only building their boats but also delivering them to where they are needed with the entire process managed by Damen experts,” says Rimmert Berlijn, Damen Services Heavylift Coordinator. “This is all part of being a total maritime solutions provider. In addition, clients taking advantage of this service also enjoy the peace of mind that comes with knowing that that their vessels are fully covered by Damen’s warranty programme right from the start.”

Sanne Wiegerink, Commercial Manager at BigLift Shipping, describes this voyage as a shining example of Dutch excellence. “The Happy Star, one of the Netherlands’ premier heavy lift vessels, transporting tugs for a distinguished Dutch shipbuilder, ultimately serving various Dutch clients. We take immense pride in our contribution to this remarkable project.”

The products and services herein described in this press release are not endorsed by The Maritime Executive.

evidence.title: The Fraud Case That Claimed Rolls-Royce Used Scrap To Build Engines Powering The B-52, Global Hawk, & MQ-25
evidence.text:
A judge in Indianapolis opened the door for two Rolls-Royce quality control employees to bring forth fraud claims in 2012. The two whistleblowers alleged that the company delivered roughly 180 engines for military aircraft that were knowingly manufactured using scrap parts and defective materials. The lawsuit also claimed that critical safety tests were skipped, and quality control measures were bypassed to cut costs and expedite production.

These engines have been installed on a wide range of US military platforms including the Lockheed Martin P-3 Orion, C-130 Hercules, Northrop Grumman E-2 Hawkeye, and the Bell V-22 Osprey. After the judge's first ruling survived an initial motion to dismiss, the company publicly rebutted, claiming the case was entirely without merit.

The original filing came in 2008 under the lawsuit 'United States of America ex rel. Thomas McArtor v. Rolls-Royce Corporation.' The former employees also accuse the company of retaliation along with fraudulent quality assurance practices. The plaintiffs claim that RR kept a 'secret set of books' to track the engines containing defective parts, which were said to come from legacy model lines like the model 250, T56, and AE2100.

The case brought by former quality control staff appears to have been settled out of court, as there has been no activity in the US legal system since the 2012 ruling. However, just a few years later, Rolls-Royce agreed to pay over $800 million to defer prosecution in an international bribery and corruption case. Whether there was any direct connection between the two incidents has never been publicly revealed.

While speculators might suggest this could cast a shadow of doubt over the commercial engine replacement program that is upcoming for the Boeing B-52 Stratofortress bombers , there does not appear to be any direct connection. The scope of the allegations appears to be limited to only turboprop and turboshaft power plants and not the BR725 turbofan, on which the F-130 is based for the B-52J.

In February, RR was cleared to conduct a critical design review along with the USAF and Boeing to move forward with the CERP modernization program to bring the B-52 fleet up to the J standard. The first two BUFFs are expected to arrive at RR facilities later this year, with initial operating capability scheduled for 2033. Along with the new engines, the host of upgrades coming to the 76-strong Stratofortress fleet is expected to keep them in the air until the 2050s, or a century of service.

Analyzing the allegations of disgruntled employees against RR is important in understanding the context of the company's selection as the prime contractor for one of the most important modernization programs in the USAF . Not long ago, RR faced bankruptcy after a quality-control crisis following its delivery of Trent 1000 engines for the Boeing 787 Dreamliner, which suffered severe turbine blade cracking. These defective commercial turbofans cost the company over $3 billion and derailed the entire business into damage control.

Found an error? Send it info@simpleflying.com so it can be corrected.

The USAF cannot afford to have a chronic maintenance issue unfold on one of its most valuable strategic bombers. This is especially important going forward as the B-52J will be one of only two platforms in the fleet after the Northrop Grumman B-21 Raider replaces both the B-2 Spirit and the Rockwell B-1 Lancer. If the B-52 fleet goes down because of a massive quality-control issue, it would reduce the USAF's strategic-strike capability by as much as 30% under the future force structure.

So why was RR chosen, given the tumultuous years leading up to its contract award in 2021? For one, the engine the B-52J powerplants will be derived from is a tried-and-true platform used in business jets around the world. This engine will not be a cleansheet design with unproven technology like the Trent 1000 was for the Dreamliner. More importantly, since Tufan Erginbilgic took the helm of the legendary engine builder in 2023, the company has course-corrected and returned to a focus on quality first and foremost.

The next chapter in the story of the B-52 is now being written.

When Tufan Erginbilgic took over as CEO of Rolls-Royce in January 2023, he famously labeled the entire corporation a "burning platform" that required a holistic cultural and operational overhaul. Erginbilgic replaced a legacy corporate culture of comfortable consensus with one of aggressive technical challenge. Under this mandate, internal engineering teams working on the F130 were empowered to surface design constraints or component anomalies early rather than masking them to meet expectations.

For the B-52J program, his leadership shifted the company from passive contract execution to aggressive, data-driven accountability. The USAF operates under a zero-fail mandate for its heavy bomber fleet. In the eyes of a vital and stringent customer like the Department of Defense, cutting corners could have easily spelled the demise of the 121-year-old company if discovered after the fact.

The US military also evaluated Rolls-Royce's supply chain resiliency following the commercial Trent 1000 crisis. This scrutiny forced a highly collaborative design phase to ensure that F130 production lines at the expanded Indianapolis facility are well insulated from standard commercial aerospace supply bottlenecks.

Looking directly at the engine itself, its design is also lower risk from a performance and maintenance standpoint. Unlike the massive widebody turbofans of the 787, the F130 is a smaller, low-bypass engine operating under conservative limits. The core architecture has already logged millions of flight hours on corporate aircraft and the US military’s own C-37 fleet. The BUFF also possesses extreme physical redundancy thanks to its eight-engine twin-pod configuration.

The Boeing 787 comes with both GE and Rolls-Royce engine options, although GE's engines have become more popular in recent times.

The B-52J program plays a central role in rebuilding Rolls-Royce’s corporate reputation under Erginbilgic. Delivering the F130 CDR on budget and on schedule proves that the company has eliminated the manufacturing variances that triggered historical whistleblower lawsuits. Executing the B-52J modernization program serves as a calling card, proving the Indianapolis factory can deliver robust military projects.

RR has already translated that standing into a major win for the US Army's Future Long-Range Assault Aircraft program, officially designated the MV-75. Rolls-Royce is actively testing its advanced AE 1107F engines to power this next-generation tiltrotor fleet, directly replacing the aging Sikorsky UH-60 Black Hawk. The AE 1107F shares an 80% parts commonality with the rest of RR's trusted AE engine family.

This AE design continuity directly reduces supply chain risks, lowers logistical costs, and positions the company to win future drone or rotorcraft contracts. For the business as a whole, this complements the massive improvements to the Trent 1000, pioneered by improvements to the Trans 7000 on the Airbus A330neo.

With its defense and widebody departments back on track, the company is renewing efforts on next-gen power plant design like the UltraFan 30. There is even speculation of a potential reentry into the narrowbody commercial jet engine market.

A closer look at the latest updates on the Airbus's flagship jet.

Getting Back Into The Single-Aisle Business

The UltraFan 30 concept is a demonstrator aimed at re-entering the narrowbody market, currently dominated by CFM International and Pratt & Whitney. An opening exists because of chronic issues with the Pratt & Whitney geared turbofan series, which have left many Airbus A320 and A220 operators grounded for months or even years.

Airbus has had to leave virtually complete aircraft sitting in backlogs awaiting GTF engines due to the severe factory bottleneck. Airframes have been cannibalized to consolidate fleets and keep the most serviceable jets operating. Some GTF-equipped planes have even been scrapped almost immediately after delivery. This leaves the duopoly vulnerable to losing market share to a third entrant, Rolls-Royce.

Unveiled as a physical mock-up in early 2026, the UltraFan 30 is a 30,000-pound (13,608 kg) thrust-class geared turbofan. It scales down the company's massive widebody technology platform into a single-aisle footprint. The engine aims for a 20% reduction in fuel burn over current generation powerplants with native compatibility for 100% sustainable aviation fuel operations. Ground testing of a fully functional prototype engine is scheduled for 2028.

Boeing and others are taking note as Rolls-Royce works with Airbus to develop the next-generation long-range jet engine.

RR boldly claims that the UltraFan 30 will be 20% to 25% more fuel-efficient than the current CFM LEAP and P&W GT engine series. They claim the next-gen engine will achieve this generational improvement with an ultra-high bypass ratio of 15:1 running on SAF, thanks to a 90-inch (228.6 cm) carbon titanium fan, a 50-to-1 overall pressure ratio, and a 20-megawatt power gearbox.

Notably, the UltraFan 30 is not actually a cleansheet design but rather a major evolution that derives from the BR 725 and Pearl engine series, like the B-52 F130 power plants. The UltraFan 30 borrows directly from the mature, ultra-low-emission core technology proven in the Pearl 10X , according to Aerospace America.

However, the race is on to determine if RR can make a true bid for the next-gen narrowbody market as Boeing and Airbus are expected to start selecting power plants for their next single-aisle airframe by late 2028. The company secured €64 million from the EU’s Clean Aviation Joint Undertaking for its UNIFIED consortium but has not secured commitments from the United Kingdom to help back the multi-billion dollar development. This has led RR to consider shifting production to Germany or the US.

Erginbilgic emphasized at the Farnborough Airshow that "once they make an engine decision, you are either in or you are out" for the next 20 to 30 years, making the success of the UltraFan 30 the absolute linchpin of Rolls-Royce's long-term commercial growth.

evidence.title: Škoda JS to supply control rod drives for Rolls-Royce SMR's reactors
evidence.text:
Škoda JS to supply control rod drives for Rolls-Royce SMR's reactors

Škoda JS is part of the Czech majority state-owned CEZ Group, which also has a 20% stake in UK-based Rolls-Royce SMR.

Earlier this year Škoda JS and Doosan Enerbility were selected by Rolls-Royce SMR for pre-production work for key components - including the reactor pressure vessel - with work which encompasses "early supplier engagement, design finalisation and manufacturing readiness to support the delivery of first power at the earliest possible date".

The Pilsen-based firm has now added the contract for the control rod drive mechanisms, which are key bits of equipment in a nuclear reactor, ensuring the precise movement of the control rods which control the reactor’s power, ensuring its safe operation. According to CEZ "each drive is a unique electromechanical linear motor, almost eight metres long and weighing 450 kg, capable of safely controlling the nuclear reactor in all operating modes".

Czech Minister of Industry and Trade Karel Havlíček said: "Small modular reactors are a technological opportunity for our companies with global reach. The contracts that Škoda JS has already concluded with Rolls-Royce SMR are clear proof of this. Small modular reactors will not only strengthen the energy security and self-sufficiency of our country, but will also create new jobs and create opportunities for follow-up investments."

The first of Rolls-Royce SMR's 470 MWe small modular reactors is due to be built in North Wales in the UK, with the first in the Czech Republic to be built at Temelín, with an expected operational date "in the second half of the 2030s" and with five or six more units to follow across three sites.

Rolls-Royce SMR CEO Chris Cholerton said: "Škoda JS has proven that it is one of the few companies in Europe capable of providing one of the most important components of our power plant … our cooperation shows the clear benefits that this project brings to industrial companies."

Daniel Beneš, Chairman and CEO of ČEZ, said: "A global supply chain for small modular reactors is now being formed, and it is essential for our industrial companies to act quickly and now. This opportunity is unique. If they manage to get involved in this chain right from the start, they can win attractive contracts for the next decades. Škoda JS now faces the task of developing a prototype directly for small modular reactors so that it can subsequently supply them to Rolls-Royce SMR all over the world."

The Rolls-Royce SMR is a 470 MWe design based on a small pressurised water reactor. It will provide consistent baseload generation for at least 60 years. Ninety percent of the SMR - measuring about 16 metres by 4 metres - will be built in factory conditions, limiting activity on-site primarily to assembly of pre-fabricated, pre-tested, modules which significantly reduces project risk and has the potential to drastically shorten build schedules.

In October 2024, Rolls-Royce SMR was selected by ČEZ to deploy up to 3 GW of electricity in the Czech Republic, and ČEZ took a 20% stake in Rolls-Royce SMR. The plan is for the first SMR to be deployed in the area of the Temelín site (which already has two gigawatt-scale VVER-1000 units), with further projects being developed for coal-fired power plant sites, including Tušimice.

In June 2025, Rolls-Royce SMR was selected as the UK government's preferred technology for the country's first SMR project. In November, the UK government announced that Wylfa on the island of Anglesey, North Wales, would be the site to host the three Rolls-Royce SMR units. It said the site - where a Magnox plant is being decommissioned - could potentially host up to eight SMRs. A final investment decision is expected to be taken in 2029.

Škoda JS has long experience in the construction and servicing of nuclear power plants, including manufacturing 21 VVER-440 reactors and three VVER-1000 reactors, as well as supplying engineering, equipment and servicing for nuclear power plants, research reactors and spent nuclear fuel storage facilities in Central and Eastern Europe, Scandinavia, France, Germany, the USA, Austria, Finland, Belgium, the UK, China and Armenia.

evidence.title: Inside The $400 Million Test Cells Rolls-Royce Built To Keep The B-52, V-22, & C-130J Flying
evidence.text:
Rolls-Royce has been selected as the engine supplier for a range of important US military aircraft platforms. To support these programs, it has made investments in aero-engine test infrastructure, expanding its ability to perform its development work domestically. The engines Rolls-Royce is currently contracted to supply are mature engine designs or modern iterations of modern designs. The investment better positions Rolls-Royce for future high-performance engines, including where difficult problems increasingly involve thermal management and integration more than just producing shaft horsepower.

In particular, this may help lay the groundwork for Rolls-Royce to win future Increment 2 contracts for the USAF's Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) program. BAE Systems has already reportedly complained that Rolls-Royce's engine is too expensive for the British BAE Brontanax CCA , with Rolls-Royce previously saying it was targeting high-performance Increment 2 USAF CCAs. Here is what to know about the importance of its $1 billion investment in its Indiana facilities.

Rolls-Royce's Massive Indianapolis Military Engine Complex

In August 2026, Rolls-Royce announced it had completed a $1 billion decade-long project in its Indiana manufacturing, assembly, and test facilities. The effort is intended to support the US Air Force's B-52 and C-130J, the Army's MV-75, and the Navy's MQ-25 programs. Rolls-Royce stated, " The investment — the largest the company has made in the United States — modernized advanced manufacturing across the Indianapolis campus and added full engine-test capability ."

This includes new ground test facilities and an altitude test facility in West Lafayette. Even though Rolls-Royce is a British company, it notes that more Rolls-Royce defense products are built in Indianapolis than anywhere else in the world. The campus is responsible for testing and building engines for a range of defense and commercial platforms, including the future engines of the upcoming B-52J bomber and the US Army's incoming MV-75 Cheyenne II tiltrotor (which partially replaces the Black Hawk).

It is also responsible for the engines currently powering the V-22 Osprey, the MQ-25A Stingray tanker drone, and the C-130J Super Hercules. Since 2001, the campus has delivered over 14,000 engines. Rolls-Royce employs around 3,500 people in Indianapolis, which in turn helps to support a larger Indiana supply chain. This is Rolls-Royce's flagship project in the United States; it has spent more than $1.5 billion in US facilities over the last decade.

Investing In Current & Future US Engines

The $1 billion project splits into roughly $600 million in advanced manufacturing and around $400 million in new engine-testing infrastructure. The advanced manufacturing work was mostly completed in 2021. The new test cells are calibrated to support the current fleets and to provide for future upgrades.

Indiana Gov. Mike Braun said, " Rolls-Royce has called Indiana home for three decades, and this billion-dollar investment is a vote of confidence in Hoosier workers and our state. Advanced manufacturing like this is exactly what keeps Indiana’s economy strong and growing. We are proud that Indiana is home to Rolls-Royce in the U.S., and we look forward to their continued success for generations to come. "

At the heart of the facility is the Allison-derived AE family of engines powering multiple US-origin aircraft. These include the AE 2100 powering the C-130J Super Hercules, the AE 3007 powering the MQ-25 Stingray, the AE 1107 family on the current V-22 Osprey and upcoming MV-75 Cheyenne II tiltrotors, as well as RQ-4/MQ-4 drone applications and others. The B-52J's F-130 (discussed below) is a completely different lineage of engines.

The B-52 Stratofortress is powered by eight aging engines, but the US Air Force will upgrade to the F130 engines from Rolls-Royce.

The F130 Engines For B-52J Stratofortress

In September 2021, Rolls-Royce received a contract to replace the aging engines on the Air Force's fleet of B-52H Stratofortress bombers with the Rolls-Royce F-130 engine under the Commercial Engine Replacement Program (CERP). The engine is based on the Rolls-Royce BR700 family of turbofan engines that powers commercial regional and corporate jets like the Bombardier Global Express, the Boeing 717, and the Gulfstream V.

Variants of the engine are already in service with the United States Air Force, powering the C-37 VIP transport and the E-11 BACN aircraft. While the number of aircraft to be upgraded with the new engine is relatively modest (76 bombers), these bombers have eight engines each. The CERP program has demand for around 650 F-130 engines (with spares). While commercial variants of the engine are built in Germany, these military engines are built in Indiana.

The contract is valued at around $2.6 billion for 608 engines plus spare engines, associated support equipment, and commercial engineering data. The first B-52J aircraft is expected to enter service in 2033. A B-52 testbed aircraft that was part of the CERP program crashed in 2026 ; it is unclear if this will have an impact on the timeline.

Rolls-Royce will also be supplying the engines for the new MV-75 Cheyenne II fast assault tiltrotor for the United States Army. The type is currently a priority for the US Army and is under an accelerated development timetable. It is expected to enter initial service around 2030. The tiltrotor's engine, the AE 1107F, is related to the Rolls-Royce T406 engine (company designation AE 1107C-Liberty) powering the V-22 Osprey tiltrotor.

In 2025, Rolls-Royce announced it had begun AE 1107 engine testing to support prototype delivery for the MV-75 (FLRAA). Rolls-Royce says the AE engine lineage has over 90 million flight hours across 16 commercial and military platforms. These AE engines share a common core with around 80% commonality across the engine family. The Army accepted slightly less optimization than a clean-sheet design in exchange for a much lower development risk and faster production.

The V-280 Valor demonstrator was powered by the General Electric T64-GE-419 , but production aircraft will be powered by the AE 1107F. This is one of Rolls-Royce's most strategically important US military wins since its F-130 B-52J win. Rolls-Royce is to be the exclusive propulsion supplier, proving the engines and much of the integrated propulsion system for each aircraft. The company is expecting production ramp-up in 2028 with two engines per aircraft.

The next chapter in the story of the B-52 is now being written.

With well over 500 examples delivered and many more on order, the Lockheed Martin C-130J Super Hercules is the most popular tactical airlifter on the market. It is powered by four AE 2100 engines and offers a significant leap in capabilities compared with the Allison T56-A-15 turboprop engine-powered legacy C-130H. While most Super Hercules have likely already been built, it is expected to remain in production into the 2040s.

As stated, the AE 1107 family already powers the V-22 Osprey tiltrotor, mostly developed for the Marines, but also in service with the Air Force, Navy, and Japanese forces. The program is mature and is currently winding down. The Air Force received its final CV-22 in July 2025, while the Marine Corps closed out its program of record, receiving the 359th example in July 2026. 11 more Ospreys remain on order with the Navy.

The contract for MQ-25 Stingray tanker drones is important , although the number to be supplied is comparatively limited. The MQ-25 is powered by the AE 3007N, an existing common core engine adapted for autonomous carrier aviation. The US Navy currently plans to purchase 76 of the aircraft across three squadrons. These aircraft are powered by a single turbofan providing more than 10,000 lbf. This means Rolls-Royce will only provide 76 engines plus an unknown number of spares.

As stated, all of these aircraft programs leverage existing mature Rolls-Royce designs, but the investment into testing facilities in Indiana points to the company's CCA Increment 2 ambitions . Rolls-Royce says , " As the US Air Force accelerates development of Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA), propulsion is no longer a supporting function, but a strategic enabler of range, survivability, mission flexibility, and operational scale. "

While much of the conversation about CCAs is low-cost and dispensability, Rolls-Royce believes the USAF will need high-end platforms for its requirements operating across the vast and contested environments of the Indo-Pacific. Here, range, electrical power, payload, and embedded installations all matter. It says that the AE 3007 is " already doing the kinds of mission CCA will demand, " while its new clean-sheet Orpheus engine offers a " scalable engine family concept designed to enable affordable propulsion capabilities across multiple autonomous missions. "

It believes Orpheus provides flexibility to respond quickly as CCA requirements mature without restarting development cycles from scratch. With these engines, the company says a customer can have 90% of the capability " tomorrow instead of waiting seven or eight years for perfection ." It should be noted that CCAs will likely span a range of low-end and high-end systems and that requirements for those designed for the European theater will be considerably different from those intended for the Indo-Pacific.

evidence.title: Rolls-Royce is putting its bespoke, $4.7 million ‘Project Nightingale’ electric convertibles through torture, testing them from the sub-zero Arctic to the boiling Arabian ...
evidence.text:
Rolls-Royce has built plenty of cars designed to cross continents in extraordinary comfort, but Project Nightingale is about to take that idea to another level. The British marque is building just 100 examples of this fully electric, two-seat convertible, and it has now begun testing them in environments that stretch from the sub-zero conditions of the Arctic Circle to the boiling deserts of the Arabian Peninsula. At 5.76 meters, the open-top luxury EV is almost as lengthy as the Phantom, yet its enormous body accommodates only two people. Before customer deliveries begin in 2028, Rolls-Royce will subject the cars to 350 collective weeks of testing to make sure this unusually extravagant machine can deliver its promise wherever its owners choose to drive. The journey has already started in Southern Europe, although Rolls-Royce has not revealed the precise location of the prototypes. From there, the testing program will venture into dramatically different conditions, including Mediterranean corniches, Arctic environments and the Arabian Peninsula, with the cars climbing to altitudes of up to 2,750 meters. At another stage, the prototypes will be taken to a private high-speed facility and pushed to 155 mph. The choice of Southern Europe is also a nod to Rolls-Royce history, since Sir Henry Royce and his engineers once used roads around the French Riviera for demanding speed and durability testing. More than a century later, Project Nightingale is following a remarkably similar philosophy, although the machine being tested could hardly be more different.

The quietest details are getting the hardest testing

The car has already spent more than 1,430 hours undergoing aerodynamic modeling, digital simulation, and wind tunnel testing, but computer models can only go so far. Now the engineers have to find out what happens when the sleek electric convertible is actually moving through the air at speed. At up to 155 mph, they will examine its aerodynamics while working to make wind noise inside the cabin almost imperceptible. That is particularly important here because Nightingale’s electric powertrain removes much of the mechanical noise that would normally mask small sounds from airflow, seals, fabrics and moving components.

Rolls-Royce has even developed a patented fully electric wind deflector specifically for the car. Rather than simply keeping hair from being blown around, the system is designed to stop high-pressure air behind the vehicle from curling forward into the cabin, reducing turbulence around the occupants and helping retain warmth when the roof is lowered in colder weather. The roof itself is an equally elaborate piece of engineering, combining cashmere, fabric and high-performance composites for sound insulation. It will face 10 separate tests covering its fabric, mechanism and performance at temperatures reaching 80°C (76°F), with the extreme conditions intended to reflect the year-round use Rolls-Royce expects from its clients.

Then there is the Piano Boot, a feature that sounds almost theatrical because it is. Opening sideways on a cantilever, the boot has been designed to turn an everyday action into another carefully choreographed Rolls-Royce moment. Engineers will open and close it as many as 15,000 times, checking not just whether it continues to work but whether the movement remains effortless and the closing sound retains the intended character. At one cycle a day, that testing figure would represent more than four decades of use, giving some meaning to Rolls-Royce’s description of “generational effortlessness.”

A giant electric roadster with nowhere to hide

The testing becomes even more interesting when the scale and proportions of Nightingale are considered. This is effectively a Phantom-sized roadster with a monumental hood, a deeply enclosed two-seat cockpit and a long, tapering tail, yet it carries fewer occupants than many ordinary sports cars. Its design draws from late Art Deco and Streamline Moderne, with a nearly one-meter-wide grille, 24 deeply mounted grille vanes and enormous 24-inch wheels inspired by yacht propellers. The rear incorporates the Aero Afterdeck, a single-piece carbon-fiber element developed to provide high-speed stability without the visual clutter of a conventional spoiler.

It is also the first model in Rolls-Royce’s new Coachbuild Collection , placing it between the marque’s regular production cars and singular commissions such as Boat Tail and Droptail . That makes the project more complicated than simply creating an outrageous one-off because Rolls-Royce has to translate extreme coachbuilding into a collection of 100 individually commissioned cars without making them feel mass-produced. The car’s electric architecture helps shape that ambition, allowing cleaner front and rear surfaces without the packaging demands of a combustion engine and exhaust system. Rolls-Royce has not yet disclosed final figures for power, battery capacity, range, acceleration or charging performance.

Perhaps the most fascinating part of Nightingale is what happens when the roof comes down and the engine falls silent. After designers noticed birdsong with unusual clarity during an early prototype drive, Rolls-Royce studied nightingale recordings and translated their sound patterns into the Starlight Breeze interior, which features 10,500 illuminated stars in three sizes. All 100 examples have already been spoken for, and they are being engineered to travel from hot deserts to Arctic roads and high-altitude routes while retaining the marque’s signature serenity, with even the sound of the Piano Boot closing after 15,000 cycles receiving scrutiny. For Rolls-Royce, the challenge is not simply building 100 extravagant electric convertibles, but ensuring each one remains unmistakably Rolls-Royce wherever its owner takes it.

Rolls-Royce begins global testing for Project Nightingale

The scope of Project Nightingale's test programme reflects how far Rolls-Royce is extending its all-electric ambition

Rolls-Royce Motor Cars has begun physical road testing for Project Nightingale, a coachbuilt series of 100 all-electric motor cars. The programme commits 350 collective weeks of engineering, taking prototypes from Mediterranean corniches to the Arctic Circle and the Arabian Peninsula.

Aerodynamic modelling and wind tunnel work already exceeds 1,430 hours; high-speed proving to 155 mph will follow at a private test facility. The Piano Boot, a side-opening boot, faces 15,000 operating cycles; the roof undergoes 10 tests at temperatures to 80°C.

In a statement, Chris Brownridge, Chief Executive, Rolls-Royce Motor Cars, said: “Project Nightingale captures the same audacious spirit that drove Sir Henry Royce to build his experimental ‘EX’ motor cars in the 1920s: a desire to discover what Rolls-Royce is truly capable of, unconstrained by convention. Few motor cars in the marque’s history have asked so much of those who create them. That is why Project Nightingale is being tested with the same rigour with which it was imagined.

“The programme begins on the roads of Europe, where Rolls-Royce first proved itself to the world a century ago, before continuing across every climate in which our clients may choose to drive. Every detail is being refined to an extraordinary degree, down to the sound of the Piano Boot closing after 15,000 operating cycles. Nothing less would be worthy of the brand, or this truly exceptional motor car.”

evidence.title: Rolls-Royce begins global road testing of coachbuild collection 'Project Nightingale'
evidence.text:
Rolls-Royce begins global road testing of coachbuild collection 'Project Nightingale'

Limited to 100 units worldwide, the coachbuild collection will undergo 350 weeks of cumulative testing. The program begins in southern Europe, where Rolls-Royce first established its validation methods over a century ago. The piano boot will be put through up to 15,000 open-and-close cycles.

Rolls-Royce Motor Cars announced Tuesday that it has begun global road testing of the prototype for its coachbuild collection, Project Nightingale.

Unveiled in April, Project Nightingale combines the complete design freedom of coachbuilding with Rolls-Royce's uncompromising all-electric powertrain and a new open-top driving experience. Limited to 100 units worldwide, the vehicle represents the boldest expression of what Rolls-Royce can achieve today while pointing toward the brand's future.

Project Nightingale will undergo the most rigorous global testing program in the brand's history, accumulating 350 weeks of cumulative trials. Real-world road testing will span a wide range of environments — from Mediterranean coastal roads and the Arctic Circle to the deserts of the Arabian Peninsula — validating the vehicle's performance in extreme temperatures and at altitudes of up to 2,750 meters above sea level.

The testing program is set to begin in southern Europe, where Rolls-Royce first established its approach to validating early vehicle development more than a century ago.

The name Project Nightingale derives from "Le Rossignol," the French word for nightingale. Le Rossignol was also the name of the residence that Henry Royce built for his designers and engineers near his winter retreat on the French Riviera. In the early 20th century, Rolls-Royce engineers used that base and a test facility in Châteauroux to conduct speed and endurance trials on routes including the road between Monte Carlo and London.

The rigorous validation philosophy that has defined Rolls-Royce for more than a century carries through to the development of Project Nightingale. Development began roughly three years ago, and the project has now entered full-scale road testing. The prototype has already completed more than 1,430 hours of aerodynamic analysis, including advanced digital simulation and wind tunnel testing.

The aerodynamic design of Project Nightingale will be validated again at a confidential high-speed test facility, where the vehicle will reach speeds of up to 249 kilometers per hour.

Airflow inside the cabin will also receive careful attention. A fully electric wind deflector — newly developed and patented by Rolls-Royce specifically for Project Nightingale — will be tested across a range of speeds. The device prevents high-pressure air generated at the rear of the vehicle from re-entering the cabin, reducing interior turbulence while helping retain warmth inside when driving with the roof open in cold weather.

The same commitment to refinement and ride comfort extends to the roof. A proprietary sound-absorbing material combining cashmere, fabric and high-performance composite materials lines the roof's interior, which will undergo 10 separate tests covering the material itself, the opening and closing mechanism, and operational performance. Testing will include conditions at extreme temperatures of up to 80 degrees Celsius.

The engineering details unique to Project Nightingale are also subject to testing. The piano boot — a first for Rolls-Royce — is designed to open sideways via a cantilevered structure and will undergo up to 15,000 open-and-close cycles to ensure smooth operation over time.

Chris Brownlie, CEO of Rolls-Royce Motor Cars, said Project Nightingale carries forward the bold spirit that led Sir Henry Royce to build his experimental "EX" vehicles in the 1920s — a desire to explore what Rolls-Royce could truly achieve, unconstrained by convention. "The testing program begins on the European roads where Rolls-Royce proved its capabilities to the world 100 years ago, and will extend to cover every climate our customers may one day drive in," he said, adding that the team would refine every detail to the highest degree of finish befitting Rolls-Royce and Project Nightingale.

Meanwhile, Rolls-Royce recently unveiled the Phantom Hummingbird, a one-of-one bespoke model inspired by the delicate beauty of nature. The company operates its bespoke program to offer customers personalized products and experiences, creating value while giving them a meaningful opportunity to express their individuality.

evidence.title: US Army Receives Two Turreted AMPV Prototypes From BAE Systems
evidence.text:
The US Army has taken delivery of two turreted infantry fighting vehicle prototypes, known as the Armored Multi-Purpose Vehicles 30mm (AMPV 30s), from BAE Systems.

With $17 million in internal funding, the company developed the vehicles in just six months before delivering them to the army in April to support the service’s Transformation in Contact (TiC) 2.0 initiative, BAE Systems announced this month.

Following delivery, the army’s TiC unit tested the AMPV 30s through field evaluations, including live-fire testing.

“Throughout this effort, our team demonstrated how we can integrate new design solutions in a time-effective and more cost-efficient manner for the Army,” said Bill Sheehy , VP of BAE Systems’ Ground Maneuver futures.

The AMPV tracked combat platform is intended to replace the army’s Vietnam-era M113 family of vehicles in Armored Brigade Combat Teams.

Its baseline family consists of five variants: general purpose, mortar carrier, medical evacuation, medical treatment, and mission command.

BAE Systems expanded the AMPV family by experimenting with turreted configurations, including the AMPV 30s equipped with Kongsberg’s Medium Caliber Turret, a compact and lightweight remote turret system also in production for the US Marine Corps’ Amphibious Combat Vehicle .

The AMPV was designed with a modular, open architecture and a common top plate, allowing the platform to accommodate more than 30 different turret systems.

AMPV 30s are designed for enhanced survivability and connectivity, featuring counter-drone capabilities, a cross-platform target handoff system that provides connectivity between multiple vehicles for target identification and synchronization, and a 360-degree situational awareness camera system.

The delivered AMPV 30s bring the total number of turreted AMPV prototypes BAE Systems has invested in over the past two years to eight, as part of its efforts to support the army’s modernization needs.

evidence.title: Thales, BAE Systems Team Up on British Army Battlefield AI
evidence.text:
Thales and BAE Systems Digital Intelligence are teaming up to support the British Army’s next-generation battlefield intelligence system under Project ZODIAC.

Thales UK signed a memorandum of understanding with BAE Systems Digital Intelligence, Frazer-Nash Consultancy, and CACI to support ZODIAC and the future development of the Land Intelligence, Surveillance, Target Acquisition and Reconnaissance (ISTAR) capability.

ZODIAC is designed as a tactical battlefield system that will combine digitalized ISTAR with deployed data-fusion analysis and command-and-control capabilities. The aim is to help deployed forces process information and support decisions faster.

“It is an opportunity to connect sensors, data, and decision-makers into a coherent operational capability that helps commanders understand and act faster,” Thales CTO Mike Sewart said.

Thales said its work with the three companies will draw on their expertise in artificial intelligence-enabled decision-making and open system architectures.

Land ISTAR covers the systems and processes used to gather information about an operational environment, identify potential targets, and provide that information to commanders and forces.

For the British Army, the program is intended to create a network of sensors that can be centrally coordinated while remaining compatible with current and future communications and information systems.

Other army systems also contribute to the broader ISTAR network.

Watchkeeper , for example, uses radar, cameras, and other sensors to collect and distribute intelligence, while the Ajax family includes dedicated reconnaissance and command-and-control variants.

evidence.title: BAE Systems Australia, Skyryse establish partnership for autonomous rotary and fixed-wing aircraft
evidence.text:
BAE Systems Australia, Skyryse establish partnership for autonomous rotary and fixed-wing aircraft

BAE Systems Australia has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with aviation firm Skyryse, establishing a partnership to explore government and commercial opportunities for future autonomous rotary and fixed-wing aircraft.

BAE Systems Australia has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with aviation firm Skyryse, establishing a partnership to explore government and commercial opportunities for future autonomous rotary and fixed-wing aircraft.

BAE Systems Australia is at the forefront of mission autonomy development and integration through the company’s Vehicle Management System (VMS), which is part of several evolving platforms in the land and air domains.

Skyryse has emerged as a leader in aviation automation and simplified flight controls following the development of SkyOS to support piloted, optionally piloted and fully autonomous flight in helicopters and fixed wing aircraft.

Under the MoU, Skyryse’s SkyOS will become the preferred aircraft operating system and flight control logic provider to BAE Systems Australia on joint projects.

“Partnering with Skyryse will allow BAE Systems Australia to leverage more than 40 years of sovereign autonomy development with our Vehicle Management System and seek to grow our collective opportunities in the rapidly developing autonomous aircraft market,” according to Andrew Gresham, Managing Director of Defence Delivery, BAE Systems Australia.

“Together, Skyryse's software-defined SkyOS and BAE Systems Australia’s Vehicle Management System bring complementary capabilities that can help deliver the next generation of optionally piloted and autonomous aircraft for our customers in an increasingly competitive and evolving environment.”

As Skyryse’s SkyOS evolves, both companies will collaborate to strengthen the partnership’s market offerings and drive sales success.

“As government, commercial, and defence sectors look to modernise existing fleets while accelerating the adoption of autonomous capabilities, software is becoming the defining technology in aviation,” according to Mark Groden, Founder and CEO at Skyryse.

“SkyOS is uniquely positioned because it combines human-rated flight software with autonomous capabilities in a certifiable, software-defined platform. Together with BAE Systems Australia, we're exploring how that foundation can enable the next generation of optionally piloted and autonomous aircraft, including future clean-sheet designs.”

evidence.title: BAE Systems receives $16 million to qualify RH45® technology for radiation-hardened space missions
evidence.text:
Manassas, Va. — September 16, 2026 — BAE Systems has received $16 million in Defense Production Act Title III funding via the Department of War’s (DOW) Warfighting Investments, Resourcing, and Execution directorate to demonstrate and qualify its radiation-hardened 45 nanometer (nm) technology.

For more than a decade, RH45 ® technology has enabled space customers to develop their own solutions with a library of advanced capabilities and proven application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) design and manufacturing methods. With manufacturing now on GlobalFoundries’ proven 45nm silicon-on-insulator (SOI) technology through the firm’s facility in Malta, New York, this contract reestablishes the RH45 ASIC Storefront. It strengthens the domestic supply chain for state-of-the-art radiation-hardened microelectronics, enabling missions that depend on cost-effective, high-performance capabilities.

The RH45 ASIC Storefront is a high-reliability, radiation-hardened platform offering a suite of qualified building blocks compatible with industry-standard design tools that allow customers to develop their own integrated circuit designs. Based on commercial 45nm technology, these building blocks provide critical functions needed for space operations. RH45 chips can withstand the harsh space environment with better power and performance than prior generations of transistor electronics. Used in the most demanding environments, these chips enable military, civil, and commercial customers to carry out planetary exploration, communications, national security, surveillance, and weather operations. These chips also play a key role in strategic radiation-hardened missions for defense applications.

“Design flexibility is important when it comes to supporting space missions,” said Joe Dziezynski, Space Systems product line director at BAE Systems. “Our RH45 ASIC library is a unique and trusted capability that allows our customers to target specific functions while meeting radiation-hardened requirements. These integrated circuits are the heart of computers whose advanced processing powering cannot fail when carrying out critical objectives in the challenging space environment.”

“This investment builds upon our longstanding partnership with BAE Systems, a valued customer of our differentiated SOI technology,” said Ezra Hall, senior director of Aerospace and Defense Business Line at GlobalFoundries. “It reaffirms our commitment to providing continuity of supply for critical defense applications and to supporting BAE Systems with secure, U.S.-manufactured semiconductor solutions. Together, we are accelerating the development of next-generation technologies that meet the highest standards of performance, reliability, and security – including in challenging space environments for critical space missions.”

RH45 technology is being integrated into single-board computers (SBCs) that will be available to space agencies and spacecraft manufacturers, including BAE Systems’ Endura™ SBC. Endura will provide powerful processor cores, hardware accelerated input/output, and advanced security features to deliver exponential improvements in size, speed, and power efficiency. As a platform-agnostic supplier, BAE Systems develops and produces high-reliability space electronics , from standard components and SBCs to complete system payloads.

Work on the RH45 ASIC is performed by BAE Systems’ Space Systems group in Manassas, Virginia. This facility is a U.S. Department of War Category 1A Microelectronics Trusted Source, covering design, aggregation, broker, packaging and assembly, and test services.

Land Forces Australia – Perth – 6-8 October

evidence.title: BAE Systems says Golden Dome role includes $1.2 billion Epoch 2 missile-warning program, U.S. space business grows 30%
evidence.text:
BAE Systems says Golden Dome role includes $1.2 billion Epoch 2 missile-warning program, U.S. space business grows 30%

By Martin Chomsky (Defence Industry Europe)

BAE Systems expects its U.S. space business to play a significant role in the Golden Dome missile-defense architecture, including through the $1.2 billion Epoch 2 missile-warning and tracking program. Tom Arseneault, President and CEO of BAE Systems Inc., said the company supports several of the mission solutions underpinning the initiative.

Arseneault outlined the company’s position during BAE Systems’ first-half 2026 earnings call. He listed Golden Dome alongside munitions production, drones and counter-drone systems, and space-based capabilities among the U.S. administration’s defense priorities.

“Our capabilities will also play critical roles in the U.S. Golden Dome architecture, and we support a number of the key mission solutions which underpin it,” Arseneault said. He pointed to Epoch 2 as one of the programs already contributing to that effort.

BAE Systems completed a preliminary design review for the $1.2 billion Epoch 2 resilient missile warning and tracking program earlier in 2026. Arseneault said the program will provide a multi-satellite constellation and a ground command-and-control system for Golden Dome.

The work comes during a period of rapid growth for BAE Systems’ U.S. space operations. Sales in its Space & Mission Systems business rose almost 30% in the first half of 2026 from the same period a year earlier.

Arseneault said national-security and military-space capabilities remain central to the administration’s focus on homeland defense. BAE Systems is positioning its spacecraft, payload and ground-system businesses around that demand.

The company’s Elevation and Evolve spacecraft product lines were developed in response to demand for systems that can be delivered more quickly and at lower cost. They are designed for missions in low and medium Earth orbit, geostationary orbit and cislunar space.

Arseneault said BAE Systems combines those spacecraft with payloads and ground systems to offer full mission solutions. He also said customer demand for the spacecraft product lines has been strong since their introduction.

The Evolve spacecraft has also been selected by Vantor, formerly Maxar, for its next-generation high-resolution imaging satellites. Arseneault said the platform is positioned across a range of national-security and military-space missions.

The space business is becoming a larger contributor to BAE Systems’ financial performance. Chief Financial Officer Brad Greve said Space & Mission Systems generated £1.6 billion of orders in the first half, while Electronic Systems sales rose 11%, led by 29% growth in space.

Greve linked part of that expansion to acquisitions that increased BAE Systems’ exposure to U.S. space and intelligence budgets. He cited the Raytheon UTC spinoffs and Ball Aerospace among deals that added durable revenue growth and were accretive to margins.

BAE Systems is continuing to invest in technology and production capacity across the areas it sees aligned with U.S. defense priorities. For the company, Golden Dome sits within a broader push into missile defense, military space and other homeland-defense programs rather than a single standalone opportunity.

U.S. Air Force F-35A Lightning II fighters and an E-3 Sentry operated together in a binational maritime strike scenario over the Bering Sea from Sept. 18 to 22, 2026.

evidence.title: BAE Systems says expected U.S. THAAD contract for 2,800 seekers will drive fourfold production increase over seven years
evidence.text:
BAE Systems says expected U.S. THAAD contract for 2,800 seekers will drive fourfold production increase over seven years

By Lukasz Prus (Defence Industry Europe)

BAE Systems expects a U.S. contract covering procurement of 2,800 seekers for the THAAD program over seven years, part of a broader expansion in American munitions production. Tom Arseneault, President and CEO of BAE Systems Inc., said the planned award would represent a fourfold increase in production.

Arseneault outlined the expected ramp during BAE Systems’ first-half 2026 earnings call, citing sharply higher demand for missiles and interceptors. He said the company supports 10 of 12 munitions programs identified by the U.S. Department of War as critical priorities.

“There are 12 munitions that the Department of War has identified as critical, we support 10 of those 12 priority programs,” Arseneault said. BAE Systems has signed framework agreements and is moving through contracting on multi-year procurements that could double, triple or quadruple current production rates depending on the program.

THAAD is among the clearest examples of that expansion. “We soon expect to receive a contract to begin procurement for 2,800 seekers over seven years, which represents a fourfold increase,” Arseneault said.

The expected award sits within a larger U.S. munitions opportunity for BAE Systems. Arseneault said combined revenue across the priority multi-year programs represented a multi-billion-dollar opportunity.

The company is committing additional capital to support those production increases. BAE Systems recently approved another $250 million for capital projects in its Electronic Systems business tied to production ramps on THAAD, AMRAAM and Tomahawk.

That spending builds on more than $4 billion invested in BAE Systems’ U.S. workforce and facilities since 2020. Arseneault said those investments expanded capacity by 2 million square feet, advanced research and development and increased the workforce by about 14%.

BAE Systems expects capital expenditure in its U.S. business to rise 40% year over year, driven largely by the acceleration in munitions production. Arseneault said the company continued to invest in technology and production capacity to meet record demand across U.S. defense priorities.

The contracting structure is also moving toward longer-term commitments. Arseneault said BAE Systems had signed five framework agreements for munitions programs, with three more under negotiation and several multi-year contracts being negotiated under agreements already in place.

BAE Systems typically operates at the Tier 2 level in those munitions programs, meaning its backlog can build later than that of the prime contractors, Arseneault said. He added that the company expects the programs to support accretive margins over time for its Electronic Systems and Space & Mission Systems businesses.

evidence.title: Melrose Industries Aktie: Garden-Grove-Vorfall belastet Ausblick
evidence.text:
Die operative Neuausrichtung des britischen Luftfahrtzulieferers Melrose Industries zeigt im laufenden Geschäftsjahr greifbare Fortschritte. Nach der Abspaltung der Automotive-Sparte stützt sich das Unternehmen auf das Kernasset GKN Aerospace.

Vor allem die Triebwerkssparte sorgte im ersten Halbjahr 2026 für Zuwächse bei Umsatz und bereinigtem operativem Ergebnis. Dennoch steht die Aktie an den Märkten weiterhin unter Druck. Am gestrigen Donnerstag schloss das Papier bei 4,72 GBP, was einem Tagesverlust von 1,7 Prozent entspricht.

Die Halbjahresergebnisse für 2026 belegen eine fundamentale Verbesserung. Melrose konnte den Verlust je Aktie im Vorjahresvergleich verringern. Da die gewichtete Aktienanzahl unverändert blieb, resultiert diese Entwicklung aus dem operativen Geschäft. Bei konstanten Wechselkursen legte der Konzernumsatz zu, während der bereinigte operative Gewinn und die entsprechende Marge noch deutlicher anzogen.

Wesentlicher Treiber dieser Entwicklung sind die Triebwerksstrukturen sowie die Beteiligung an langfristigen Risk-and-Revenue-Sharing-Partnerschaften. Zugleich verbesserte sich der freie Cashflow spürbar, und das Management hält an seinen Zielen für Umsatz sowie Mittelzufluss im Gesamtjahr fest.

In der Strukturen-Division zeigen derweil eingeleitete Effizienzprogramme und die Neuverhandlung von Vertragspreisen Wirkung. Die Margen in diesem Segment erholen sich schrittweise, bleiben jedoch hinter dem Triebwerksbereich zurück. Zudem wies das Unternehmen zum Ende des Halbjahres keine vertraglichen Kapitalverpflichtungen aus.

Engpässe und Nachwirkungen in Garden Grove

Trotz der stabilen Nachfrage bremsen operative Hürden das Tempo. In der gesamten Luftfahrtindustrie machen Engpässe in den Lieferketten dem Konzern zu schaffen. Es fehlt an Rohmaterialien, speziellen Guss- und Schmiedeteilen sowie an qualifizierten Fachkräften. Diese Faktoren erschweren den zügigen Hochlauf neuer Flugzeugprogramme.

Zusätzliche Unsicherheit birgt der Vorfall im kalifornischen Werk Garden Grove, bei dem es zu Problemen mit einem überhitzten Chemietank kam. Dieser Zwischenfall belastet die Erwartungen an das Gesamtjahresergebnis und wirft Fragen hinsichtlich möglicher Rechtskosten auf. Damit bleibt auch der finanzielle Spielraum für künftige Ausschüttungen an die Anteilseigner vorerst mit Risiken behaftet.

Die Mischung aus operativer Erholung und externen Belastungen spiegelt sich auch im Chart wider. Mit dem gestrigen Schlusskurs notiert das Papier rund 31 Prozent unter seinem 52-Wochen-Hoch von 6,83 GBP, das im Februar markiert wurde.

Unter den Marktbeobachtern herrscht derweil geteilte Stimmung. Während BNP Paribas Exane die Einstufung für den Titel im Mai auf „Underperform“ zurücknahm, halten andere Beobachter an neutralen bis positiven Einschätzungen fest. Für die weitere Entwicklung der Aktie dürften vor allem zwei Faktoren ausschlaggebend sein: die Beständigkeit der Margen im Triebwerksgeschäft und die verlässliche Eindämmung der Folgekosten aus Übersee.

The aerospace and engineering specialist's weaker showing stood out against a market where a clear majority of constituents were advancing, prompting renewed scrutiny of the pressures currently facing UK-listed industrial businesses tied to civil aviation supply chains.

What Is Weighing On Melrose Industries Today

Melrose Industries has built its modern identity around aerospace structures and propulsion components, supplying engine parts and systems to major aircraft manufacturers. That positioning has generally been viewed favourably given the multi-year recovery in global air travel and aircraft production rates, but it also leaves the organisation exposed to the pace at which aircraft makers can ramp up deliveries. Any signs of supply chain friction, whether in raw materials, skilled labour availability or component certification timelines, tend to feed quickly into sentiment around Melrose Industries shares, and today's underperformance is being read by some market watchers as a reflection of these ongoing production-rate uncertainties.

Industrial Stocks Diverge Sharply In Today's Session

The pullback in Melrose Industries shares highlights just how differentiated the industrial stocks category has become within the wider London market. While commodity-linked names have been buoyed by the sharp squeeze in copper markets, with exchange warehouse stocks tightening and prices trading near record levels, engineering and aerospace-focused businesses like Melrose Industries have not benefited from the same tailwind. Weir Group, by contrast, sits closer to the mining equipment supply chain and stands to gain more directly from elevated metals prices and continued capital spending by mining companies on processing and extraction technology. The divergence between these two well-known industrial names illustrates how commodity cycles and aerospace production cycles can move in entirely different directions within the same broad category.

Defence Spending And Aerospace Demand In Focus

Beyond civil aviation, Melrose Industries also carries meaningful exposure to defence-related aerospace programmes, an area that has drawn growing attention amid heightened geopolitical tensions and rising defence budgets across several major economies. Investors tracking the stock are watching for updates on order intake and programme timelines within this segment, since sustained defence spending could offer a partial offset to any softness in civil aviation deliveries. The balance between these two demand drivers remains a key factor shaping how the market interprets Melrose Industries' near-term trajectory.

What UK Investors Are Watching Across Industrials

For UK-focused investors, today's session offers a useful snapshot of how the industrial stocks category is currently split between commodity beneficiaries and manufacturing-cycle-sensitive names. Melrose Industries' underperformance, alongside similar softness in names such as Informa and Sage Group, contrasts with the strength seen in mining-linked and travel-related shares elsewhere on the index. This divergence underscores the importance of understanding the specific end markets each industrial business serves, rather than treating the category as a single homogeneous group. As global supply chains continue to normalise unevenly across sectors, differentiated performance within UK industrials looks set to remain a recurring feature of daily trading sessions.

Looking ahead, Melrose Industries' next scheduled updates on aerospace production volumes and margin progression will be closely watched for signs of whether today's weakness reflects a temporary wobble or a more sustained shift in sentiment. Meanwhile, continued strength in copper and other industrial metals could keep providing support for equipment-focused peers like Weir Group, reinforcing the split between commodity-exposed and manufacturing-exposed corners of the UK industrial landscape. Investors following the sector will also be keeping an eye on broader signals from aircraft manufacturers regarding production schedules, since these have a direct bearing on how component suppliers such as Melrose Industries are positioned heading into the remainder of the year.

evidence.title: Shareholder Returns Accelerate as Melrose Industries Completes Transformation
evidence.text:
Having successfully concluded its multi-year strategic shift to become a specialized aerospace group, Melrose Industries is now channeling significantly improved profitability into substantial capital returns for its shareholders. The company's enhanced operational efficiency is funding a capital return program running into the hundreds of millions of pounds, delivered through share buybacks and an increased dividend.

The foundation for this generous capital return policy was laid by the company's 2025 full-year performance. Revenue advanced by eight percent to approximately £3.59 billion, while adjusted operating profit saw a more pronounced jump of 23 percent to £647 million. A key highlight was the expansion of the operating margin to 18 percent, a clear indicator of the transformation's success.

Market observers are also watching how the company manages the contrasting dynamics within its industry. While the defence segment benefits from robust demand, the civil aerospace sector continues to grapple with supply chain constraints. evidence.text:
Renishaw stock stood at GBp 5,565 on the London Stock Exchange on September 23, 2026, after the precision engineering group reported fiscal 2026 revenue of GBP 815.8 million, up 14 percent from GBP 713.0 million. The results put operating performance at the center of the investment case, with adjusted operating profit rising 36 percent to GBP 152.9 million.

According to the fiscal 2026 results released through TradingView on September 23, 2026, adjusted operating margin expanded from 15.7 percent in fiscal 2025 to 18.7 percent in fiscal 2026. Adjusted earnings per share increased 30 percent from 137.8 pence to 179.5 pence, while adjusted profit before tax rose 32 percent to GBP 168.0 million.

Position Measurement was the clearest growth engine. Revenue increased 26 percent to GBP 260.9 million, while adjusted operating profit rose 53 percent to GBP 71.5 million and the segment margin reached 27.4 percent.

Specialised Technologies delivered the fastest revenue growth, up 43 percent to GBP 107.5 million, and moved from an adjusted operating loss of GBP 9.9 million in fiscal 2025 to an adjusted operating profit of GBP 4.7 million in fiscal 2026. Investing.com reported that management expects fiscal 2027 capital expenditure to double as Renishaw expands encoder capacity.

Renishaw stock was priced at GBp 5,565 on September 23, 2026, against a 52-week range of GBp 3,290 to GBp 5,785. That places the share price GBp 220 below the yearly high, a 3.8 percent gap calculated from the high of GBp 5,785.
