evidence.title: Smiths Group Signals Confidence With Portfolio Overhaul
evidence.text:
Smiths Group Signals Confidence With Portfolio Overhaul

Smiths Group ( (SMGZY) ) has held its Q4 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Smiths Group’s latest earnings call struck a distinctly upbeat tone, with management stressing that a sweeping portfolio transformation has reshaped the business into a focused premium industrial engineer. Strong cash generation, robust margins and confident guidance for fiscal 2027 underpinned the optimism, even as executives acknowledged ongoing macro headwinds from the Middle East, tariffs and weak U.S. housing.

Smiths has effectively redrawn its corporate map, completing the disposals of Smiths Interconnect and Smiths Detection at what management described as very attractive valuations, crystallizing £3.3 billion of enterprise value. The reshaped group now positions itself as a streamlined industrial engineering player, concentrating capital and management attention on higher-growth, higher-margin niches.

High-Grading the Portfolio and Strategic Exits

Beyond the headline disposals, Smiths is pruning lower-growth and lower-margin activities, particularly within Flex-Tek, while adding exposure to faster-growing segments through the DRC deal. It also agreed to sell three noncore Flex-Tek industrial units for £40 million and launched a process to divest John Crane’s U.S. legacy asbestos liability, a move aimed at structurally de-risking the balance sheet.

Resilient Fiscal 2026 Financial Performance

Despite a difficult macro backdrop, Smiths delivered 1.2% organic revenue growth to £1.9 billion and 1.9% organic growth in headline operating profit to £399 million. Margins edged up 20 basis points to 20.6%, return on capital employed hit 23.5% and headline EPS rose 6% to 86.8p, while total group headline EPS climbed 12% to 135.7p.

The cash engine remained strong, with £384 million of operating cash flow and an impressive 96% cash conversion, slightly ahead of internal guidance. The board proposed a final dividend of 33.5p, taking the full-year payout to 48.5p, a 5.4% increase that signals confidence in future cash flows.

Acquisitions added 2.6% to revenue growth, reinforcing Smiths’ strategy of building into adjacent high-growth areas. The £165 million purchase of DRC stands out, giving the group a stronger foothold in data center-related demand, an area management sees as structurally supported by AI and cloud investment.

Smiths’ margin story is increasingly underpinned by cost discipline and pricing execution, notably within John Crane and Flex-Tek Aerospace. The acceleration plan drove a £5 million reduction in central costs, while Smiths Excellence savings and mix and execution benefits helped offset inflationary and tariff headwinds.

John Crane posted 2.3% revenue growth, led by strong demand for original equipment, especially dry gas seals, with growth rising to 4% when excluding the £20 million Middle East hit. Headline operating profit increased 3.5% organically to £270 million and margins expanded 30 basis points to 23.9%, underscoring the resilience of the business model.

Regional and Industrial Strength at John Crane

Geographically, John Crane delivered mid-single-digit growth in the U.S. and Latin America despite regional volatility. Industrial revenue grew 2%, powered by solid demand in mining and water, even as chemicals and parts of China remained weak, particularly where Middle East-linked projects slowed.

Flex-Tek Aerospace proved a standout, generating 10.6% revenue growth on the back of a strong order book, renewed deals with major engine makers and a mix of price and volume gains. Strategic focus areas, including India and maintenance, repair and overhaul, logged strong double-digit growth, with acquisitions adding another 6.4% to the top line.

Construction Returns to Growth Late in the Year

Construction revenue fell 3.6% for the full year, reflecting a tough U.S. residential backdrop, but momentum improved steadily and turned positive in the fourth quarter with 2.9% growth. New customer wins in flexible ducting and multifamily projects helped stabilize the segment, suggesting a potential base for recovery.

Smiths continued to fund its technology pipeline, investing £64 million in research, development and engineering, about 3.3% of revenue, alongside £39 million of capital expenditure at 2% of sales. Key projects included machining, testing, automation and capacity upgrades at John Crane, plus commercial and strategic growth initiatives across the portfolio.

Balance Sheet De-Risking and Cash Flow Upside

The company executed two major pension transactions and began a process to offload John Crane’s U.S. asbestos liability, moves expected to materially lighten future obligations. Management highlighted that asbestos-related cash outflows have averaged about £20 million annually over five years, so removing these liabilities should boost free cash flow and capital flexibility.

Capital returns are being turbocharged, with Smiths having completed a £500 million buyback and a £1 billion program linked to Smiths Interconnect. A further £1.5 billion tied to the Detection sale remains to be executed and is expected to be largely completed by the end of calendar 2027, offering ongoing support for EPS.

Management guided to around 4% organic revenue growth for fiscal 2027, a headline operating margin of about 21% and operating cash conversion in the low 90s. John Crane is expected to be second-half weighted due to continued first-half Middle East disruption, while Flex-Tek should see first-half skew from strong aerospace, an anticipated Thermal Solutions rebound and fast-growing DRC contributions.

The company voiced strong conviction in reaching its medium-term goals of 5% to 7% organic revenue growth and 21% to 23% operating margins sooner than previously expected. Structural tailwinds in global energy, expanded exposure to cooling and data center applications via DRC and the ongoing evolution of the Flex-Tek portfolio underpin this confidence.

Smiths highlighted the stickiness of its revenue streams, noting that aftermarket accounts for over 70% of John Crane’s sales and around 70% of construction revenue comes from repeat distributor relationships. In aerospace, more than 75% of revenue is tied to long-term agreements, contracted positions or repeatable programs, reinforcing visibility.

John Crane secured major new contracts across LNG and natural gas liquids, as well as global Performance Plus agreements in energy and chemicals, broadening its installed base. Construction is expanding distribution for flexible and metal ducting, Thermal Solutions is scaling customized heat and cooling systems for data centers and Aerospace is targeting greater share on key engine platforms and growth in India and MRO.

Each business now operates with a five-year innovation roadmap spanning technology, products, materials and processes, aiming to sustain differentiation. Recent launches include John Crane’s 93AX separation seal, which has seen strong customer uptake, and new dry gas seal products for larger, higher-pressure machines, with materials work supporting future hydrogen applications.

Operationally, the acceleration plan focuses on site consolidation, footprint optimization, ERP harmonization and automation to cut structural costs. Smiths has already delivered £20 million of annualized benefits and remains on track for £30 million to £35 million, providing a cushion against external shocks and funding further investment.

Over recent years, Smiths has channelled around £700 million into eight Flex-Tek acquisitions, more than doubling the division’s size and delivering double-digit revenue CAGR. Management underscored that these deals have generated returns above the cost of capital, reinforcing the group’s M&A credentials.

Within four months of ownership, DRC generated £35.5 million of revenue at a pro forma growth rate well above 20% with an attractive margin, validating the deal rationale. Management expects the data center sector to grow more than 20% annually over the next decade, driven by AI and cloud, positioning DRC as a key future growth engine.

Executives emphasized that Smiths has real pricing power, with increases executed across John Crane, Flex-Tek Aerospace, Thermal Solutions and Construction. Construction alone saw two price increases during the year, helping offset cost inflation and tariff impacts and supporting the modest margin expansion.

John Crane entered fiscal 2027 with an order book around 1x revenue, providing a solid baseline for the year. Roughly two-thirds of Aerospace revenues were already covered, and DRC built a strong order book for the current and next calendar year, enhancing confidence in the top-line outlook.

Tariffs were a drag in fiscal 2026 despite mitigation measures, but management expects them to be broadly neutral in fiscal 2027 after pricing and sourcing adjustments. This should remove one of the external headwinds that previously pressured margins and earnings.

External Challenges and Market Conditions

The company was candid about the external hits it took in fiscal 2026, including conflict-related disruption in the Middle East, a weak U.S. residential construction market, tariff costs and softer volumes. Nevertheless, management stressed that the business proved resilient, using its diversified footprint and recurring revenue base to absorb shocks.

The conflict in the Middle East cut John Crane revenue by £20 million, mainly in the second half, as maintenance programs slipped, projects shifted out and customers reined in capex and opex. Smiths assumes similar disruption in the first half of fiscal 2027, though the drag should lessen in the second half as the impact annualizes.

Weak U.S. Residential Construction and Flex-Tek Impact

Flex-Tek’s construction business faced a 3.6% revenue decline amid a soft U.S. housing market, where starts fell 0.8% and permits 2.1%. Combined with Thermal Solutions weakness, this pushed Flex-Tek’s overall revenue down 0.4% for the year despite strong aerospace performance.

Thermal Solutions and Industrial Softness

Thermal Solutions revenue dropped 6.2% as residential HeatKit destocking in the first half and the completion of an ultra-high-temperature project weighed on volumes. The Sureheat contract represented a £7 million year-on-year drag and HeatKit destocking a £13 million hit, while industrial demand in chemicals and China also softened.

Smiths carried higher inventory levels to support its order book and maintain service during geopolitical and supply chain disruptions, which, along with slower Middle East collections, lifted receivables. Tariffs remained a fiscal 2026 headwind and higher tax and finance costs, plus adverse FX and sale-related accounting, partly offset EPS gains.

Forward-Looking Guidance and Medium-Term Conviction

Looking ahead, Smiths sees fiscal 2027 as another year of steady progress, with 4% organic growth, a 21% margin and cash conversion in the low 90s framed as realistic targets. Over the medium term, management reiterated firm belief in achieving 5% to 7% organic growth and 21% to 23% margins, supported by energy, data centers, aerospace and a structurally stronger portfolio.

Smiths Group’s earnings call painted the picture of a business leaning into structural growth themes while methodically tackling legacy issues and external shocks. For investors, the combination of solid cash flow, ambitious but credible guidance and substantial ongoing buybacks suggests a company intent on translating operational progress into shareholder value, even as macro risks linger.

The group said a new share buyback program amounting to 1.5 billion pounds from the proceeds of the sale of Smiths Detection has also now commenced. evidence.title: Smiths Group jumps 6% as margin beat reinforces Stifel 'buy' case
evidence.text:
Smiths Group jumps 6% as margin beat reinforces Stifel 'buy' case

Smiths Group (LSE:SMIN) PLC shares jumped as much as 6.3% to an intraday high of 2,754p after annual margins beat expectations, and broker Stifel said the results offered reassurance that growth should improve during the current year.

Stifel retained its 'buy' recommendation and 3,000p price target, which represented 15.8% upside from Monday's closing price before Tuesday's rally.

Organic revenue grew 1.2% in the year to July 2026, matching market consensus but falling short of the company's previously reduced 2% guidance.

However, Stifel calculated that the result implied organic growth of around 3.9% during the fourth quarter, a clear sequential improvement from the flat performance recorded during the third quarter.

The operating margin increased by 20 basis points organically to 20.6%, beating the 20.2% market consensus and the company's guidance for a result slightly above 20%. Continuing earnings per share rose 6% to 86.8p.

John Crane delivered 2.3% organic growth despite an estimated £20 million impact from disruption in the Middle East. Excluding that effect, the division's growth would have been around 4%.

Flex-Tek returned to growth during the second half, advancing 0.9%. Stifel estimated that the division achieved mid-single-digit growth during the fourth quarter, including a 2.9% improvement from its construction operations.

Smiths expects organic revenue to grow by around 4% during the year to July 2027, broadly matching the 3.9% market consensus, while its operating margin is forecast to reach approximately 21%.

Growth at John Crane is expected to be weighted towards the second half as Middle East disruption continues, while Flex-Tek should benefit earlier from strength in aerospace and thermal solutions despite subdued US construction demand.

Stifel noted that Smiths shares had traded sideways in recent months because of the limited improvement in underlying organic growth. However, the broker said the stronger fourth quarter and reassuring guidance suggested the current financial year should deliver better momentum.

The broker's longer-term investment case rests on Smiths' transformation into a more focused industrial engineering group following the £3.3 billion disposal of its Interconnect and Detection businesses.

It also expects the company's substantial share-buyback programme and progress towards medium-term targets of between 5% and 7% organic growth and margins of between 21% and 23% to support earnings and shareholder returns.

Yet every pharmaceutical autoclave, food steriliser, data centre heat-pump loop, and chemical distillation column depends on one unglamorous constant: precisely controlled heat and steam.

That is the problem Spirax-Sarco Engineering plc is built to solve. The company has evolved from a classic steam-trap maker into an integrated thermal energy and fluid management platform, stitching together advanced steam systems, electric thermal solutions, and highly accurate peristaltic pumps and dosing technologies. evidence.title: Spirax-Sarco Engineering rebrands as Spirax Group
evidence.text:
Spirax-Sarco Engineering rebrands as Spirax Group

Spirax-Sarco Engineering today announces its decision to rebrand as Spirax Group. The change reflects the development of the Company over many years into a larger and stronger Group of three aligned Businesses with differentiated and complementary capabilities:

· Steam Thermal Solutions (previously Steam Specialties)

· Watson-Marlow Fluid Technology Solutions

Together as Spirax Group, these leading Businesses are united in their purpose to engineer a more efficient, safer and sustainable world. Our new name balances our history and where we have come from, with who we are today. It creates more distinction between the Group and its Spirax Sarco trading Division (part of Steam Thermal Solutions), providing improved clarity for all stakeholders.

Group Chief Executive Officer, Nimesh Patel said:

"This is a natural evolution for our Company which is home to three strong solutions-focused Businesses that improve the efficiency and safety of critical industrial processes across our customers' thermal energy and fluid technology activities. As Spirax Group we can help everyone better understand who we are and how we work together across our Businesses to help customers meet their operational, sustainability and decarbonisation goals."

Spirax Group's new website and updated brand can be viewed at www.spiraxgroup.com .

The Group is also proposing to change its legal name to Spirax Group plc. This is subject to shareholder approval through a special resolution at the Company's AGM in May 2024. Shareholders should note that their shareholdings will be unaffected by the commercial rebrand or proposed legal name change. evidence.title: Leonardo da Vinci Was Obsessed With Flight. So Why Did He Draw a Wingless Beetle Next to His Water Engineering Notes?
evidence.text:
A largely overlooked sketch in one of Leonardo da Vinci's manuscripts shows a wingless beetle known for producing a substance long used as an aphrodisiac. A new study proposes three reasons the flight-obsessed Renaissance genius might have drawn it.

Leonardo da Vinci (1452–1519) filled his notebooks with insects: dragonflies, bees, wasps, butterflies — almost all of them winged. That focus lines up with what historians already knew about him. Leonardo was fixated on the mechanics of flight , and scholars have long read his drawings of flying insects as studies feeding into his designs for flying machines.

But he didn’t limit himself to winged creatures. He also sketched a crab, worker ants, and what researchers now believe was a longhorn beetle ( Morimus asper ), a wingless species common in Tuscany.

A new paper in the journal npj Heritage Science , by entomologists Marco A. Bologna and Alberto Zilli, adds one more overlooked example to that list — and this one comes with a stranger backstory.

The drawing sits on folio 36-recto of the so-called Codex Arundel (MS 263), a bound volume of Leonardo’s notes on hydraulics, geometry, and other subjects now held at the British Library in London. It shows a beetle from the family Meloidae — the “blister beetles,” so named for the irritant compounds they secrete.

Bologna and Zilli identify it confidently as a member of the genus Meloe , commonly known as the oil beetle : a wingless insect that produces cantharidin , a compound used for millennia both as a medicine and — more famously — as an aphrodisiac.

According to Carlo Vecce, a leading expert on Leonardo’s life and work, the sketch likely dates to the artist’s second stay in Florence, around 1503–1504. What makes its placement odd is the company it keeps: the same page is otherwise filled with sketches and notes on fluvial dynamics — the behavior of rivers and flowing water. There’s no obvious reason for a beetle to be there at all.

The drawing is precise enough for the researchers to narrow it further. Both sexes of Meloe lack wings and share short wing-cases and a swollen abdomen, and the specimen’s antennae suggest it’s a female.

Two Meloe species live in the part of Tuscany where Leonardo was likely working: one restricted to the Alps and Apennines , and one — Meloe proscarabaeus — that also ranges across the lowlands near Florence. Bologna and Zilli conclude the second is the more likely match.

Leonardo’s fascination with flying animals — bats, birds, insects — is well documented and tied to his interest in the biomechanics of wing movement. So why sketch a wingless one, in the middle of notes about water? The researchers propose three possibilities, and say the first two aren’t mutually exclusive:

Cantharidin: an old and widespread reputation

That third theory is where the paper spends the most time. According to Vecce, Leonardo owned a copy of the Hortus Sanitatis — an early printed natural-history encyclopedia, published in 1491 by Jacob Meydenbach — whose section on animals describes blister beetles’ use as both irritants and aphrodisiacs.

Cantharidin itself is a toxic compound produced by two related beetle families. Civilizations across China, Peru, South Africa, and the Mediterranean independently discovered and used it for at least two thousand years — as an aphrodisiac, an anti-inflammatory, a treatment against tumors and warts, and, in higher doses, a poison.

Its use as a male aphrodisiac and vasodilator in Greek and Roman medicine is documented by Hippocrates , Aristotle, Galen , Dioscorides , and Pliny the Elder, and it stayed in use in Italian folk medicine through the Middle Ages, the Renaissance, and into the 1800s. The beetle most associated with the practice was Lytta vesicatoria — still known today by its common English name, “Spanish fly” — though Meloe species were used as well.

None of this was foreign to Leonardo’s other interests, the authors note. He wrote and drew extensively — and sometimes explicitly — about the human penis and its physiology, including observations on the role of blood flow in erections (Codex Windsor, folio 2-verso) and, elsewhere in his notes, an actual aphrodisiac recipe (Codex Atlanticus, folio 482-recto).

The researchers stop short of settling on one explanation. Picking a single theory for an isolated, out-of-context drawing, they write, would be speculative — Meloe isn’t exactly a common beetle to sketch, and nothing else on the page explains why it’s there.

What they do argue is that following the most plausible leads can point toward other overlooked corners of Leonardo’s notebooks, and toward a fuller picture of a mind that treated almost nothing as beneath its curiosity.

evidence.title: Leonardo wins EU deal for security and defence space observation
evidence.text:
You've read 1 of 3 free articles this week.

Leonardo wins EU deal for security and defence space observation

Leonardo has been awarded by the European Space Agency (ESA) a fully funded contract to define the architecture of the future EU Earth Observation Governmental Service (EOGS), a key capability designed to harness space data in support of Europe’s autonomous decision-making in the fields of security and defence. The contract is one of the two parallel architectural studies funded by the European Commission and signed with ESA under the Financial Framework Partnership Agreement (FFPA). The project will propose architectural options to support the future implementation of the EOGS. The European Resilience from Space for Earth Observation (ERS-EO) activities are parallel preparatory activities for EOGS, including the preparation of relevant capabilities and their potential federation with national and European dual-use Earth Observation assets. Led by Leonardo, the study will capitalise the competences, technologies and solutions from Telespazio, Thales Alenia Space, e-Geos and a qualified network of European partners, and will define a sovereign, resilient and federated end-to-end Earth Observation architecture, covering the entire value chain: space systems and sensors, ground infrastructure, data processing and services. Starting from the operational needs of security and defence users, the project will assess current capabilities and will perform a gap analysis. It will then evaluate different architectural solutions for performance, resilience, responsiveness and affordability, leveraging Leonardo’s, and entire Space Alliance, technological and industrial capabilities in Earth Observation, including its proprietary earth observation constellation. A central element will be the federation of existing and future European assets, enabling different national, institutional and commercial capabilities to operate as part of an integrated system. ESA’s Director of Earth Observation Programmes, Simonetta Cheli, said, “This is an important step in paving the way towards a sovereign European Earth observation capability supporting security and resilience. We are pleased that Leonardo is now poised to contribute to the blueprint to help shape Europe’s Earth observation capabilities for the next decade and beyond, bringing together national, institutional and commercial assets within a shared operational framework aimed to strengthen Europe’s resilience and strategic autonomy.” Massimo Claudio Comparini, Managing Director of Leonardo’s Space Division, said, “Europe’s strategic autonomy increasingly depends on its ability to access, understand and use critical data from space. Through the EOGS study, Leonardo will contribute its and Space Alliance technologies, infrastructures and expertise to help shape a sovereign Earth Observation capability supporting Europe’s security, resilience and technological independence.” The project brings together a broad European industrial ecosystem covering seven European countries: Italy, France, Germany, Spain, Luxembourg, Portugal and Poland. The Leonardo-led consortium includes its joint ventures Telespazio, Thales Alenia Space as well as e-GEOS and OHB, GAF, HiTec, Alioth, CEiiA, Argotec, Satlantis, KPLabs, AIKO, and SITAEL. evidence.title: HawkEye 360 and Leonardo expand European space intelligence offering with dedicated RF capacity and local data delivery
evidence.text:
HawkEye 360 and Leonardo expand European space intelligence offering with dedicated RF capacity and local data delivery

By Martin Chomsky (Defence Industry Europe)

HawkEye 360 and Leonardo have signed a memorandum of understanding to combine HawkEye 360’s space-based radio-frequency sensing with Leonardo’s space service solutions for European customers. The agreement sets out a framework for a sovereign, multi-sensor intelligence offering that integrates RF data with Leonardo’s geospatial and sensing capabilities.

Leonardo will lead overall data integration and manage institutional engagement across Europe through its geospatial solutions, while HawkEye 360 will provide dedicated RF data capacity tailored to European operational requirements. The initial phase will add a customized RF layer to Leonardo’s global intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance service offering, including exclusively reserved capacity for defined European areas of interest.

Data generated under the arrangement will be delivered through Italian ground stations and European Union-based cloud infrastructure. The companies said the approach is intended to reduce latency and strengthen European data sovereignty.

“We are aligning closely with Leonardo to contribute advanced RF sensing capabilities to Europe’s sovereign ISR frameworks,” said John Serafini, Chief Executive Officer of HawkEye 360. “Our technology is adaptable and matured through years of operational heritage, and this collaboration represents an important step in supporting European nations with reliable, integrated RF insights embedded within their own architectures.”

The memorandum also establishes a phased pathway for broader industrial cooperation over the coming years. The companies plan to explore collaboration on RF localization, electro-optical and hyperspectral payload technologies, including their evolution, manufacturing and hosting on their respective systems.

The agreement also covers plans to expand interoperability between HawkEye 360’s RF analytics and Leonardo’s sensing solutions. The companies said this work is intended to support a scalable industrial partnership around future European intelligence capabilities.

“Through this collaboration, Leonardo will integrate HawkEye 360’s specialized RF capabilities with our space services expertise to deliver a multi-sensor solution tailored to European geospatial information requirements,” said Massimo Claudio Comparini, Managing Director of Leonardo’s Space Division. “This further strengthens Leonardo’s and its affiliated role as a trusted European integrator of sovereign space-based intelligence and strategic data provider.”

HawkEye 360 uses space-based collection, proprietary signal processing and artificial intelligence-powered analytics to detect, geolocate and characterize radio-frequency emissions worldwide. The company provides RF data and analytics to defense, intelligence and national security organizations, including the U.S. government and allied partners.

evidence.title: Leonardo continues to strengthen its cybersecurity sector with the acquisition of Becrypt in the UK
evidence.text:
Leonardo continues to strengthen its cybersecurity sector with the acquisition of Becrypt in the UK - Company

Leonardo continues to strengthen its cybersecurity sector with the acquisition of Becrypt in the UK

Agreement to acquire Becrypt to enrich Leonardo’s proprietary portfolio reinforcing its position in Trusted Cybersecurity

Leonardo, through its UK wholly owned subsidiary Leonardo UK Ltd, has taken a further step to strengthen its role in the cybersecurity sector by entering into a binding agreement for the acquisition of the UK company Becrypt. The acquisition will immediately enhance Leonardo positioning in UK and Five Eyes cyber defences domain and complements the strong existing collaboration between Leonardo UK Ltd (Leonardo), the UK Government and the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), to secure the country’s most sensitive environments. The operation builds also on the company’s delivery of next-generation cyber solutions across Italy, NATO, and the wider European defence landscape.

The initiative marks the next phase of Leonardo’s continuous enhancement of its Zero Trust solutions, leveraging Becrypt’s cutting-edge capabilities in secure data transfer, endpoint security, data and cloud security. It builds on Leonardo’s recent industrial partnerships and acquisitions in cybersecurity across Europe, notably Axiomatics (Attribute-Based Access Control), SSH Communication (Privileged Access Management and Post-Quantum Encryption) and Arbit (Data Diode and Cross Domain Solutions), in line with Leonardo’s industrial strategy.

Roberto Cingolani, Chief Executive Officer and General Manager of Leonardo, stated: “This latest acquisition in the UK marks another step forward in Leonardo's strategy to build resilient and sovereign cybersecurity in Europe that overcomes current technological fragmentation. It also testifies to our long-term commitment to the UK, a core home market which plays an important role in strengthening our international footprint. Also, thanks to the capabilities acquired in Zero Trust, we are rapidly developing Leonardo's reach in the cyber domain, which is essential for protecting our nations' sensitive data and critical infrastructures which face rapidly evolving threats. This is why cybersecurity sits at the heart of Leonardo's industrial strategy, playing a key role as an enabler for the development of our multi-domain solutions.”

Bernard Parsons, Chief Executive Officer of Becrypt said: “Being part of Leonardo provides Becrypt with the global reach and scale necessary to deploy our technology across a wider field. This will accelerate the development of our secure platforms, ensuring that the critical sectors we serve have access to the most advanced tools required to maintain information superiority and digital security.”

Closing of the Becrypt acquisition is subject to regulatory approvals and expected within Q2 2026. During the process, Leonardo was supported by PwC acting as financial advisor and by GOP acting as legal advisor.

Founded in 2001 and headquartered in London, Becrypt Ltd employs around 100 people, developing technology designed to protect data up to Top Secret classification. The SME’s core offering portfolio includes secure operating systems, secure collaboration, and secure data transfer solution and mobile device management platforms, responding to the UK Ministry of Defence (MOD) needs for Multi-Domain Integration. Becrypt Ltd represents a unique strategic asset, delivering endpoint security and secure data transfer solutions to the UK MOD and wider government departments, to enhance the security in this highly sensitive and mission-critical segment.

evidence.title: Leonardo Debuts in International Operations at Defence Cyber Marvel to Enhance Cybersecurity Skills
evidence.text:
Leonardo has taken a notable step by participating in its first international operation at the Defence Cyber Marvel, a multinational exercise dedicated to digital security overseen by the UK Ministry of Defence. This initiative is designed to boost the cyber capabilities of allied forces as they confront evolving digital threats.

As part of its commitment, Leonardo deployed a team of 11 apprentices from its Cyber and Security division based in Bristol. These apprentices collaborated closely with professionals from the British Army’s Royal Signals reserve unit to address a range of challenges posed during the exercise. Their primary mission involved safeguarding a complex network comprising Windows, Linux, and operational technology systems from a series of simulated cyber attacks, all conducted in Singapore’s time zone, which hosted most of the military and industry teams participating in the event.

In preparation for this critical undertaking, Leonardo’s full-time Security Operations Centre personnel provided rigorous training to ensure that the apprentices were fully equipped for the challenges ahead. The mentorship offered by Royal Signals personnel was invaluable, guiding the apprentices throughout the exercise.

Oliver, the team lead, shared insights on the experience, highlighting the unique scheduling demands that saw the team begin their workday at 1 AM UK time. “While it was a struggle to adjust at first, the team quickly came together. The late-night sessions added to the realism and intensity of the exercise, showcasing the commitment and resilience of the apprentices,” he remarked.

During the event, Leonardo’s specialists engaged in the analysis of real-time intelligence, which played a crucial role in informing their defensive strategies. They examined indicators of compromise, fortified their systems, and isolated potential threats. Expressing pride in the experience, Oliver emphasized its significance in cultivating essential skills for effective cyber defense. “As apprentices, we’re always looking for new opportunities, and this was the perfect way for us to improve our blue team skills,” he noted.

The Defence Cyber Marvel, now in its fifth year, operates in collaboration with several notable organizations, including the British National Crime Agency, the UK Cabinet Office, the Department of Business and Trade, and the Department of Work and Pensions. This year’s competition, hosted in Singapore, attracted approximately 2,500 participants from 29 countries and featured 70 diverse organizations, all united in their commitment to enhancing digital competencies and effectively countering real-world cyber threats.

evidence.title: Indra and Leonardo join forces to boost cyber defence capabilities
evidence.text:
Indra and Leonardo join forces to boost cyber defence capabilities

By connecting operations centres and exchanging cutting-edge threat intelligence, the collaboration is expected to boost strategic autonomy and provide a stronger deterrent.

Indra Group and Leonardo have signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the aim of jointly exploring and developing business opportunities in the field of cybersecurity in Europe, NATO , and other international markets.

The signing of this agreement took place the last Thursday at Leonardo's facilities in Rome. José Vicente de los Mozos , CEO of Indra Group, and Roberto Cingolani , CEO of Leonardo, were responsible for formalizing this alliance with which both companies intend to accelerate innovation and provide specialized training in cybersecurity, as well as offer managed cyber defense services to both public and private clients.

For his part, Ángel Escribano , president of Indra, highlighted the importance of this agreement by stating that " they organize and accelerate European industrial cooperation with clear governance." Additionally, he emphasized that the agreement will enable the activation of value chains around sovereign capabilities for Europe and NATO. The collaboration translates into strategic autonomy and effective deterrence, thanks to the interconnection of operations centers and the advanced exchange of threat intelligence.

José Vicente de los Mozos pointed out that the alliance with Leonardo will bring solutions to the market that strengthen the digital resilience of systems and operations, while Roberto Cingolani stated that "European defense must innovate, anticipate, and cooperate."

Leonardo offers its own platforms designed for demanding sectors such as Defense, Space, and Strategic Organizations. The company has consolidated its 'Made in Europe' cybersecurity portfolio, based on Zero Trust principles and data-centric protection. Its Global Cybersec Center adopts a federated model to ensure the cyber mission of its clients.

On the other hand, Indra Group, through its IndraMind initiative, has 3,000 highly qualified professionals to address current challenges, such as hybrid warfare and protection and security. Indra leads European R&D programs in cyber defense, such as the ECYSAP cyberspace situational awareness platform and the EU GUARDIAN project, which seeks to create AI-based solutions.

evidence.title: Fincantieri, Leonardo Joint Venture Wins $4.2B Italian Navy DDX Destroyer Deal
evidence.text:
The Italian Navy is moving ahead with its DDX destroyer program after Orizzonte Sistemi Navali (OSN), a Fincantieri-Leonardo joint venture, secured a major contract for two vessels.

The 3.7-billion-euro ($4.2 billion) deal from OCCAR (Organisation for Joint Armament Co-operation) includes approximately 1.3 billion euros ($1.5 billion) in options and covers the ships’ development and production, along with logistical studies and initial in-service support.

Fincantieri will serve as the platform system integrator, while Leonardo will design and develop the warships’ combat system.

OSN will enter into sub-supply contracts worth around 1.8 billion euros ($2 billion) for Fincantieri and approximately 1.7 billion euros ($1.9 billion) for Leonardo in the coming weeks.

The first destroyer is expected to be delivered by 2033, followed by the second in 2035.

“With the DDX programme, Italy is making a generational leap in its maritime defence capabilities and strengthening a strategic asset that involves the entire national system,” said OSN CEO Giovanni Sorrentino .

“This programme represents much more than the construction of two new naval units: it is the result of an extraordinary synergy among Italy’s industrial excellence, the Defence sector – and in particular the Italian Navy – and the international procurement agency OCCAR, bringing together innovation, expertise and strategic vision.”

Italy’s next-generation destroyers will feature high levels of digitalization, automation, and integration among sensors, weapon systems, multi-domain command and control systems, and platform management systems.

The 180-meter-long (591-foot) DDX platform, featuring an open and scalable design, can accommodate 251 cot spaces.

With a 13,500-tonne displacement, the destroyer can sail for a range of over 4,000 nautical miles (7,408 kilometers/4,603 miles).

Innovations expected for the warship include a DC power sub-network with its associated energy storage system and a stabilization system integrated with the steering system, as well as algorithms and methodologies for calculating thermal and electrical balances.

The destroyer will feature an integrated air and missile defense capability, equipped with SADOC 5 C5I high-power, fully digital S-band active electronically scanned array radar, and MBDA’s weapon system.

An electronic warfare suite from Elt Group, along with artillery and close-in defense systems equipped with advanced smart munitions, will also complete the warship’s combat system.

evidence.title: Fincantieri Delivers 5th PPA ‘Domenico Millelire’ to Italian Navy
evidence.text:
Home » Fincantieri Delivers 5th PPA ‘Domenico Millelire’ to Italian Navy

Fincantieri Delivers 5th PPA ‘Domenico Millelire’ to Italian Navy

On September 24, 2026, the delivery of the PPA – Multipurpose Combat Ship Domenico Millelire , built by Fincantieri for the Italian Navy, took place in Muggiano (La Spezia).

The ceremony was attended by Admiral Aurelio De Carolis, Commander in Chief of the Naval Fleet, Chief Inspector Admiral Cristiano Nervi, Director of NAVARM, and Joachim Sucker, Director of the Organisation Conjointe de Coopération en matière d’Armement (OCCAR); they were welcomed by Biagio Mazzotta, Chairman of Fincantieri, Pierroberto Folgiero, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director of Fincantieri, and Eugenio Santagata, General Manager of Fincantieri’s Naval Vessels Division.

This vessel is part of the renewal plan of the operational lines of the Italian Navy vessels, approved by the Government and Parliament under the aegis of OCCAR (Organisation Conjointe de Cooperation sur l’Armement, the international organization for cooperation on arms).

The PPA is a highly flexible ship with the capacity to serve multiple functions, ranging from patrol with sea rescue capacity to Civil Protection operations and, in its most highly equipped version, first line fighting vessel. There will be indeed different configurations of combat system: starting from a “soft” version for the patrol task, integrated for self-defence ability, to a “full” one, equipped for a complete defence ability. The vessel is also capable of operating high-speed vessels such as RHIB (Rigid Hull Inflatable Boat) up to 11 meters long through lateral cranes or a hauling ramp located at the far stern.

The firm order covers development, production and initial in-service support for the first DDX, with the second vessel covered by an option.

OSN, owned 51% by Fincantieri and 49% by Leonardo, is expected to award subcontracts worth about €1.8bn ($2.05bn) to Fincantieri, including around €800m ($910m) of options, and about €1.7bn ($1.93bn) to Leonardo, including approximately €480m ($546m) of options.

Fincantieri will act as platform system integrator, while Leonardo will design and develop the combat system.

The first destroyer is scheduled for delivery in 2033, with the second due in 2035 if the option is exercised.

The 180-metre vessels will displace about 13,500 tonnes, have a range of 4,000 nautical miles and carry crews of 251. Their digital architecture is also designed to support the integrated operation of unmanned surface and underwater vehicles.

“With the DDX programme, Italy is making a generational leap in its maritime defence capabilities and strengthening a strategic asset that involves the entire national system,” OSN chief executive Giovanni Sorrentino said.

OSN acts as a whole-warship system integrator on Italian naval programmes and has worked on programmes including FREMM frigates and new-generation offshore patrol vessels.

Fincantieri is an Italian shipbuilding group whose activities span naval vessels, cruise ships, ferries, offshore and specialised vessels, marine systems and lifecycle services.

Leonardo is an Italian aerospace, defence and security group with activities including aircraft, helicopters, electronics and cyber systems.

OCCAR, which signed the DDX contract on behalf of Italy, is an international organisation that manages cooperative armament programmes.

evidence.text:
Four Seasons II’s Keel Laid at Fincantieri

Fincantieri announced that, at its Ancona shipyard, together with Marc-Henry Cruise Holdings LTD, Joint Owner and Operator of Four Seasons Yachts, the keel was laid for the Four Seasons II.

“As part of the ceremony, and in the presence of Gilberto Tobaldi, director of the Ancona shipyard, Ben Trodd, CEO of Four Seasons Yachts, and other honored attendees, a commemorative coin was welded into the yacht’s hull.

“Rooted in maritime tradition, the coin serves as a symbol of good luck and a blessing for the vessel,” the shipyard said in a post.

“With 34,000 gross tons, 207 meters in length and 79 suites, the Four Seasons II introduces residential-style suites, expansive terrace decks, and advanced environmental technologies,” Fincantieri added.

“Every aspect has been thoughtfully conceived to foster a seamless connection between guests, the sea and the destinations beyond, reflecting our enduring commitment to designing and building the ships of tomorrow.”

As previously reported, the ship will start sailing in 2028 , debuting in April in the Eastern Mediterranean following its delivery from Fincantieri.

The new ship will retain the same residential-style, “all-suite” concept that characterizes the first vessel in the class, the companies said.

evidence.title: Fincantieri-Leonardo venture signs €3.7 billion Italian Navy destroyer deal to strengthen defence against ballistic and hypersonic missiles
evidence.text:
Fincantieri-Leonardo venture signs €3.7 billion Italian Navy destroyer deal to strengthen defence against ballistic and hypersonic missiles

By Martin Chomsky (Defence Industry Europe)

A Fincantieri-Leonardo joint venture has signed a contract worth approximately €3.7 billion for two new Italian Navy destroyers, setting in motion one of Italy’s largest naval defence programmes in recent years. The agreement with European procurement agency OCCAR includes approximately €1.3 billion in options and covers development, construction, logistics studies and initial support in service.

The ships, known as DDX, are intended to replace the Italian Navy’s Horizon-class destroyers and strengthen its ability to counter air and missile threats. The programme puts Fincantieri in charge of the naval platform and Leonardo in charge of the combat system, bringing both companies into a project scheduled to deliver its first ship in 2033 and its second in 2035.

Orizzonte Sistemi Navali, the contracting joint venture, is owned 51% by Fincantieri and 49% by Leonardo. It expects to award subcontracts in the coming weeks worth approximately €1.8 billion to Fincantieri, including €800 million in options, and €1.7 billion to Leonardo, including €480 million in options.

The planned combat system combines Leonardo’s SADOC 5 C5I system, a fully digital S-band AESA radar and an MBDA weapon system. According to the companies, the ships are designed to provide integrated air and missile defence against missile, ballistic and hypersonic threats while sharing information with other forces.

At 180 metres long and 13,500 tonnes, each destroyer will carry a crew of 251 and have a stated range of 4,000 nautical miles. The design also provides for integrated control of unmanned surface and underwater vehicles, extending the ships’ role beyond air defence.

Fincantieri plans to equip the destroyers with a digital architecture that draws together information from onboard systems to support operations, maintenance and logistics. The platform will also include energy storage linked to a DC power sub-network and a stabilisation system integrated with steering.

“The DDX programme represents a strategic milestone for Fincantieri and for Italy’s national defence industry,” Fincantieri Chief Executive Pierroberto Folgiero said. He described it as “one of the most significant naval programmes launched in Italy in recent years”.

Leonardo Chief Executive Lorenzo Mariani said the programme reflected the navy’s confidence in the company’s technology and its investment in systems that connect operations across different domains. “With these two new-generation units, the Armed Force will be able to rely on naval platforms offering advanced operational performance and capable of addressing a broad spectrum of threats,” he said.

For Orizzonte Sistemi Navali Chief Executive Giovanni Sorrentino, the contract also carries industrial importance beyond the two ships. “With the DDX programme, Italy is making a generational leap in its maritime defence capabilities and strengthening a strategic asset that involves the entire national system,” he said.

General Dynamics Land Systems has secured a $49.3 million U.S. Army contract modification for 20 additional Stryker Double V-Hull A1 vehicles.

The W93 warhead and Mk7 reentry body assembly are intended for the Navy’s submarine-launched ballistic missile fleet

Canada has moved closer to acquiring six Saab GlobalEye airborne early warning and control aircraft after signing a non-binding term sheet with the Swedish defence group.

HMS Agamemnon, Britain’s sixth Astute-class nuclear-powered attack submarine, has left BAE Systems’ Barrow-in-Furness shipyard for the first time and begun sea trials.

The company said the hub is intended to shorten the path from laboratory work to defense-ready capabilities in navigation, communications, sensing and advanced computing.

Lockheed Martin said on September 22 that a twin launcher for FGM-148 Javelin anti-tank guided missiles had completed a successful demonstration on Kongsberg’s Medium Caliber Turret in Norway.

Finland and Sweden conducted their first joint operational air-identification mission on 24 September 2026, deploying F/A-18 Hornet and JAS 39 Gripen Quick Reaction Alert fighters over the Gulf of Finland.

U.S. Air Force F-35A Lightning II fighters and an E-3 Sentry operated together in a binational maritime strike scenario over the Bering Sea from Sept. 18 to 22, 2026.

The United Kingdom has taken command of NATO’s Joint Force Command Norfolk for the first time, placing a British officer at the head of the Alliance’s Atlantic-focused operational headquarters.

SYNOPTICS specializes in high-precision laser crystals and optical components used in solid-state laser systems

KNDS France has begun delivering R3-standard EBRC Jaguar armoured vehicles to the French Army, with close to 25 vehicles delivered or upgraded by 18 September 2026.

Italian shipbuilder Fincantieri delivered the PPA multipurpose combat ship Domenico Millelire to the Italian Navy on 24 September at its Muggiano yard in La Spezia.

evidence.title: Pirelli MotoGP testing should have been “mandatory for all”
evidence.text:
Enea Bastianini believes in-season Pirelli MotoGP testing should have been “mandatory for all”.

The Tech3 rider, who will join Trackhouse Aprilia next year, is among nine riders who must wait until December’s post-season Valencia test for their first laps on Pirelli MotoGP rubber.

Two of those, rookies David Alonso and Dani Holgado, at least have experience racing on the Italian tyres in Moto2.

But established MotoGP riders Pecco Bagnaia, Fabio di Giannantonio, Fabio Quartararo, Alex Marquez, Jorge Martin, Ai Ogura and Bastianini have all missed Pirelli testing due to team changes.

Not every manufacturer has imposed a blanket ban on departing riders trying an 850cc prototype. Joan Mir and Luca Marini rode Honda’s new machine at Brno in June, and Pedro Acosta appeared for KTM at both Pirelli tests.

Meanwhile, the use of adapted 1000cc bikes at the Red Bull Ring on Monday highlighted a possible compromise that could have allowed more riders to gain Pirelli experience without sampling 2027 machinery.

“Well, for me, yes. It [would be] nice to try the Pirellis here on Monday,” Bastianini said during the Red Bull Ring weekend. “I tried with KTM to [negotiate] to see if it was possible to try, but at the end they told me no.

“It’s better for everybody to try the Pirellis before arriving in Valencia. It was better to be mandatory for everybody. That has not been planned for us. And, well, I'm not alone.”

Valencia, where track time is likely to be restricted by cool conditions, will begin a reduced programme of five official winter test days.

“Just in one day [at Valencia] it will be very complicated to think about how will be the future with the Pirellis,” Bastianini said.

“I know there are some riders with an advantage, like the Moto2 riders and also Nicolo [Bulega], coming from Superbike to the MotoGP.

“I think it will not be a very big problem by the first race. But, like I said, for me it was better to have the chance to try before.

“I don't know why the organisers didn't think about the test like, ‘OK, all the riders need to test the Pirelli’. Every rider.

“I can give some comments to the factory. And, for me, I tried the tyre for the future.

“That for me is an advantage for everybody: For the factory and also for the rider.”

The 2027 rookies will receive two additional days of running at the Sepang Shakedown, further increasing the Pirelli mileage for the likes of current Ducati test rider Nicolo Bulega.

Bastianini joked that Bulega has already done enough Pirelli laps: "He can come directly for the first race!”

MotoGP has used Michelin tyres since 2016. The French brand will replace Pirelli as exclusive WorldSBK supplier from next season.

evidence.title: Pirelli Bets $1.2 Billion on Rome, Georgia, but Its Own Board Wasn't Unanimous
evidence.text:
Get the latest local stories in your inbox.

Pirelli Bets $1.2 Billion on Rome, Georgia, but Its Own Board Wasn't Unanimous

Pirelli's board of directors has signed off on a $1.2 billion expansion of the company's U.S. headquarters and manufacturing campus in Rome, Georgia, a project expected to create 1,000 new jobs and dramatically reshape the site's production capacity over the next several years. But the vote on Tuesday wasn't unanimous — three board members nominated by Chinese state-owned Sinochem voted against the plan, exposing lingering friction inside the Italian tire maker's boardroom even as local officials celebrated the news.

The board approved the investment by majority vote on Tuesday, with directors Zhang Haitao, Xi Xiaohong and Wang Kun casting dissenting votes, according to a statement carried by PR Newswire . Sinochem had been Pirelli's largest shareholder, with a roughly 34% stake, and the three dissenting directors were nominated by the Chinese firm, underscoring how geopolitics has followed the company's American growth plans into the boardroom itself. As CBS Atlanta reported, the expansion was announced alongside Georgia Gov. Brian Kemp, who said Pirelli has been a valued presence in the state for over two decades.

Pirelli's U.S. headquarters sits at 100 Pirelli Drive in Rome, Georgia, roughly 70 miles northwest of downtown Atlanta — a site the company has operated since 2002, per the same account. The plant currently produces around 400,000 passenger car tires annually, while Pirelli employs 234 Georgians in operations around the state, according to CBS Atlanta. Under the new plan, that capacity is set to climb 15-fold, to 6 million tires per year by 2033, the station notes.

The scale-up will happen in two stages starting in 2027. The first phase will lean on Pirelli's proprietary Modular Integrated Robotized System, or MIRS, with production capacity beginning to increase from 2028 and ultimately reaching 3 million tires annually during the phase, according to Investing.com . A second phase will then add a fully automated conventional manufacturing facility, layering on another 3 million tires of capacity to reach the 6 million target by 2033.

Most of the hiring tied to the expansion is expected to happen in 2029, per CBS Atlanta's reporting, with the plant projected to reach full operations in 2033. The buildout will strengthen what Pirelli describes as its local-for-local strategy, allowing the company to better serve the U.S. market from domestic soil rather than relying on imports.

Claudio Zanardo, a Pirelli executive, said the United States is one of the company's most important markets and offers significant opportunities for growth, according to CBS Atlanta's account of the announcement. That framing lines up with broader industry data: the U.S. accounts for roughly 40% of global volumes in the premium High Value tire segment, making it the largest single market in the world for that class of product in 2026, according to Modern Tire Dealer .

Part of what the expansion enables is U.S. sales of Pirelli's sensor-embedded Cyber Tyre technology, alongside advanced robotics the company plans to introduce at the Rome site. That path to market required clearing a specific regulatory hurdle: following governance changes introduced under Italy's 2026 Golden Power Decree, Pirelli secured clearance from the U.S. Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security to market the connected-tire system domestically, according to Just Auto . U.S. trade authorities have tightened rules around Chinese-linked components in connected vehicle systems, and Pirelli's ownership structure was also changing.

That change came in July, when Sinochem reduced its equity stake in Pirelli from 34.1% to 20.1%, selling a 14% share to Lumina Crown, an investment vehicle controlled by Czech businessman Michal Strnad, Just Auto reports. The reduction left Sinochem with a 20.1% stake.

The same week the board approved the U.S. investment, Pirelli also approved an organizational restructuring that immediately eliminated its Corporate General Management function, according to European Rubber Journal . That change will lead to the departure of Corporate General Manager Francesco Tanzi by the end of the year; Tanzi is expected to assist with the executive transition before moving into a consultancy role, the trade publication reports.

The 1,000 new positions planned for the Rome campus would represent roughly five times Pirelli's current regional headcount, based on CBS Atlanta's reporting of the company's existing 234-person Georgia workforce. Pirelli has said the €1 billion ($1.2 billion) investment will not affect its 2026 financial targets, maintaining a consistent capital expenditure-to-revenue ratio through the project's 2027-2033 rollout, according to PR Newswire's coverage of the board's announcement.

evidence.title: Pirelli prepares for the 2027 MotoGP season: different tyres to change the races, too
evidence.text:
Pirelli prepares for the 2027 MotoGP season: different tyres to change the races, too

Pirelli completed testing yesterday at the Red Bull Ring ( TIMES HERE ) in Austria, another key stage in the tyre development program for the 2027 MotoGP World Championship. Starting next season, the Italian company will become the sole supplier for MotoGP as well, extending the role it already plays in Moto2 and Moto3 to the premier class.

A total of 18 riders took to the track , including regular riders, test riders, and rookies. Representing Honda were Johann Zarco, Diogo Moreira, and Takaaki Nakagami; for Yamaha , Toprak Razgatlıoğlu, Jack Miller, Izan Guevara, and Augusto Fernández; and for Ducati , Marc Márquez, Franco Morbidelli, and Fermín Aldeguer.

Aprilia entrusted the work to Marco Bezzecchi, Raúl Fernández, and Lorenzo Savadori, while KTM fielded Pedro Acosta, Brad Binder, Pol Espargaró, Maverick Viñales, and Senna Agius.

This particularly large and diverse group allowed Pirelli to gather feedback from riders with varying levels of experience, riding styles, and familiarity with MotoGP.

The program involved both the 850 cc prototypes designed for the new regulations and some of the current 1000 cc MotoGP bikes, which were suitably adapted to simulate the future technical configuration. This coexistence is necessary at this stage of development, as not all manufacturers have reached the same point in the development of their 2027 bikes.

“The day at the Red Bull Ring represents another step forward in the development program for Pirelli’s lineup for the upcoming season of the FIM Grand Prix World Championship, in which we will also extend our role as sole supplier—a role we already successfully fulfill in Moto2 and Moto3—to the premier class,” commented Giorgio Barbier , Pirelli’s Moto Racing Director. “This is a comprehensive process that includes both collective tests like today’s and private development activities carried out by the manufacturers, and it will culminate in the first official 2027 tests scheduled for Valencia in early December, with the participation of all next season’s regular riders."

"We are pleased with the outcome of the test conducted in Austria: the riders—including several rookies who were of great help by bringing different riding styles to the table—had the opportunity to evaluate slick tyres in soft, medium, and hard compounds, both on the front and rear, using in some cases prototypes of the future 850 cc bikes and in others the current bikes, which were suitably adapted. The feedback gathered—which is positive overall and confirms the high performance level of the tested solutions, particularly in terms of grip and stability—provides us with valuable insights to continue development and define with ever-greater precision the characteristics of the product line we will make available for the upcoming season. As always, I thank the manufacturers, teams, and riders for their active collaboration.”

The test took place under stable weather conditions with sunny skies. Track temperatures ranged from 19 to 38 degrees, allowing for work across a fairly wide range.

Pirelli brought slick tyres in soft, medium, and hard compounds, available for both the front and rear. The teams were able to set their own schedules, following the Italian manufacturer’s recommendation to start with the softer compounds and then gradually move on to the others.

But Pirelli’s arrival could change more than just the name on the sidewall of the tyres. While greater customization of Pirelli’s presence is expected —with sidewalls coloured according to the compound, as is already the case in F1 —the Italian company will likely approach MotoGP with a different philosophy than the one Michelin has followed so far.

Pirelli has informed us that the rule regarding minimum pressure will be maintained, with corresponding penalties for failure to comply with the established values. This decision is primarily driven by safety concerns and is therefore intended to remain in place despite the change in supplier.

What could change more noticeably, however, is the behaviour of the tyre during the race . One of the characteristics of Michelin tyres—with a few exceptions, such as what happened in Austria—is that they guarantee relatively consistent performance over the race distance.

In the World Superbike Championship, where Pirelli has been the sole supplier for over twenty years, a drop in performance over the course of the race is, in contrast, a common occurrence. Tyre deg thus becomes a factor to be interpreted and managed, one that highlights the rider’s skill, the bike’s setup, and the team’s strategy.

It is not yet possible to know whether this philosophy will be fully transferred to MotoGP, because the power outputs, aerodynamic loads, and characteristics of the future 850 cc prototypes will require specific solutions. However, the experience Pirelli has gained in production-based racing suggests the possibility of races in which tyre management will once again play a more significant role.

Throughout the day, Pirelli engineers worked closely with manufacturers, teams, and riders to collect data and technical feedback. The information gathered will be used to continue development and define the tyre range to be used in the 2027 MotoGP World Championship.

The next decisive step will be the first official tests of the 2027 season, scheduled for Valencia in early December, when the new tyres can be tested by all the regular riders on the future MotoGP grid. It will then be possible to begin to understand not only how fast they will be, but also how they will change the structure and management of the races.

evidence.title: 2026 Pirelli Scorpion Range Review | Three new tread patterns from the Italian rubber specialists
evidence.text:
Italian tyre manufacturer Pirelli has given its Scorpion MTB tyre range an overhaul for 2026, with three new tread patterns and simplified nomenclature to make choosing the right tyre easy.

Pirelli has revamped its much-loved Scorpion gravity tyres with a fresh take on compounds, carcasses and tread patterns, making it easier for riders to choose the right option.

Three new tread patterns have been introduced to the Scorpion lineup, and the older, slightly confusing ‘M’ series nomenclature is no more.

Which is right for you and why? Let’s dive into the new offerings from one of the world’s biggest names in tyre manufacturing.

Fresh Sting | Pirelli’s revamped Scorpion lineup

Pirelli has built this new range of Scorpion gravity tyres around a three-step selection process, aiming to remove some of the guesswork and help you choose the right tyres.

Step 1 is picking the tread pattern based on your riding style and terrain.

Step 2 is choosing your casing based on the level of support and protection you want.

Step 3 is compound selection: grip vs. rolling speed vs. durability. What matters to you more?

Of course, this isn’t much different from how you would select tyres from any other brand. However, the updated tread patterns, compounds and casings are a bit easier to understand as you stare up at the tyre wall in your local bike shop.

Three new tread patterns | Emperor, Black Sting & Red Claw

The Emperor is an all-rounder for mixed and variable terrain, aiming to deliver a predictable feel, and it essentially replaces the M series tyres in the previous lineup.

The centre strip sees two chunky knobs that alternate in their spacing. The blocks that sit close together form something of a paddle and see one horizontal slit to bolster climbing and braking traction, flanked by two smaller transition knobs. The wider treads drift out into the transition zone and see a vertical cut on the leading edge, helping them bend and claw into the ground as the tyre is leant over. The shoulder treads are well supported and feature a cutout parallel to the rolling direction, again for cornering grip.

Optimised for 2.4in to 2.6in sizes, the Emperor is available in all three compounds and all three casing options.

According to Pirelli, the Black Sting slots in as the tyre optimised for hard-packed trails and fast rolling speeds. While the layout is reminiscent of the Emperor, the centre strip is more tightly packed, with the blocks arranged in a 2-3-2 pattern. The siping follows a similar formula as well: the closely spaced blocks have a horizontal cut in the tread, the wider blocks a vertical cut, and the shoulder tread the same cutout.

It’s well suited as a front or rear on a lightweight trail setup or as a rear tyre on a bigger downhill or enduro bike, paired with the Emperor up front.

The Black Sting is available in 2.4in and 2.6in sizes across all casings and compounds.

Last but not least is the Red Claw, which is designed for loose, dusty, off-camber conditions. It features sharp braking ramps and wider spacing for more damping and support when things get steep and rowdy.

The Red Claw should be equally at home in intermediate wet conditions, with wide, self-clearing knobs to shed any mud or debris. It can be run as a pair in shifting conditions or as a front tyre paired with an Emperor on the rear for a well-balanced setup.

The Red Claw is available only in the Soft and Super Soft compounds and in DualWall and DH+Wall casings.

Pirelli has split the compounds into three distinct options and ditched the jargon-laden naming convention in the old range. If you’re an F1 fan, you will instantly recognise the colours, as they lean into their racing pedigree.

Super Soft is designed for maximum grip and shock absorption. This is your high-performance, race-day compound, offering maximum chemical grip at the expense of wear life and durability.

Soft is the solid all-rounder: longer life, good grip, and confidence-inspiring, predictable handling.

Medium is a high-mileage compound prioritising fast rolling speed and high durability.

Four casing options with varying levels of protection

While Pirelli has streamlined its compounds, but with four casing options, the selection can get a bit blurred.

Simply put, if you want a hard-hitting DH casing with the most protection in the range, the DH+Wall is your ideal choice.

The DualWall is intended for long-travel enduro/e-MTB riding, including days in the bike park and enduro racing. It is said to have slightly better rolling characteristics than the DH+Wall, with less sidewall protection.

HardWall is for aggressive trail riding and enduro, for longer days on big, pedal-focused bikes. Pirelli claims it rolls quicker than the heavier casings, with less damping and protection.

ProWall is intended for lightweight trail riding and downcountry, efficient on climbs and flat trails, yet with enough support and protection to be composed on descents.

Pirelli’s Australian distributor, FE Sports, fired out two pairs of tyres before the official launch so we could clock up some trail time.

We received one set for our trusty Rocky Mountain Element downcountry bike and another for a hard-hitting enduro setup on a Focus Sam² e-bike.

Pirelli Emperor & Black Sting | Focus Sam²

Initially, the tread pattern on the Emperor looks great over the handlebars, very much like a do-it-all front tyre similar to a Maxxis Minion DHRII.

The rubber is soft, with good rebound on trail. There’s plenty of front-end grip that builds confidence on all types of terrain, and I never felt the tyre got overwhelmed or lacked in grip. It transitions well between the centre and corner knobs, with plenty of lean angle.

The Black Sting out back was equally as impressive. It has great rolling attributes and a smooth transition phase between centre and side knobs.

With the tyre side-loaded, the purchase is impressive, and the carcass roll offered plenty of compliance without feeling washy. The soft compound does occasionally feel a bit wallowy on flatter, more hard-packed surfaces, and it was a sensation that took a little bit of getting used to.

We’d be curious to try the Medium compound on both of these tyres to see if that reduces this feeling and what sacrifice it makes in terms of traction. Even still, this combo pairs a grippy, predictable tyre up front with a faster-rolling offering in the rear, making for a well-balanced setup for the summer months.

Pirelli Emperor | Rocky Mountain Element

The tyres on our Rocky Mountain Element downcountry bike use the same Emperor tread pattern we ran up front on the Focus Sam², but in the lighter ProWall casing. Rolling out of the carpark, it was immediately noticeable how much quicker they felt than the Schwalbe Nobby Nic Super Trail they replaced.

The shorter-travel bike is much less forgiving to set up than a longer-travel machine, so the added damping of the soft compound, slightly taller knob height and refined casing were a blessing. The bike tracked well, cornered on a dime and was all-around confidence-inspiring. However, I wonder whether the harder Medium compound would suit a short trail ripper better for longer days in the saddle, both for the rolling speed and durability.

As a front tyre, the Emperor has plenty of positive grip with the tyre in edge. As a rear tyre, it performs well under braking, and sees a predictable transition phase when leaning into corners and on off-camber singletrack.

In this spec, they offer a confident ride and plenty of compliance. After sending them through some fairly spicy terrain, where I would usually be concerned about pinch flats or damaging rims with a lighter-weight tyre, I was suitably impressed to come out the other side with both tyres and rims intact.

It’s still early days, but all in all we are rather impressed with what Pirelli has baked up.

Pirelli has done a fantastic job simplifying and extending the Scorpion range of tyres. The naming of the tread patterns, casings and compounds is now much easier for the end consumer to understand and choose the right option. And while we haven’t had any trail time aboard the Red Claw, it’s fairly clear where that sits within the lineup, with the open tread pattern design better suited to loose, dusty trails.

The compound choice on these tyres is great; plenty of thought has gone into the range, with the right compounds and sizes available on the tread patterns you would expect.

While the four options for casing may feel a little overwhelming at first, we’ve boiled it down to the following use cases:

All in all, the updated Pirelli lineup is impressive and happily goes head-to-head against industry giants such as Maxxis , Schwalbe or Continental . The Pirelli rubber will be staying on for longer-term testing to see how it performs over the dry and dusty summer months.
