evidence.title: PIRELLI: BOARD OF DIRECTORS MAJORITY APPROVES US MULTI-YEAR INVESTMENT PLAN OF APPROXIMATELY €1 BILLION
evidence.text:
THE INVESTMENT WILL INCREASE PRODUCTION CAPACITY AT THE ROME, GEORGIA PLA NT TO 6 MILLION CAR TYRES BY 2033, INCLUDING CYBER TYRE TECHNOLOGY, WITH AROUND 1,000 NEW JOBS EXPECTED

NO IMPACT ON 2026 TARGETS. CAPEX-TO-REVENUE RATIO FOR 2027-2033 IN CONTINUITY WITH PREVIOUS PERIODS

THE PROJECT IS AIMED AT SUPPORTING GROWTH IN WORLD'S LARGEST HIGH VALUE MARKET AND STRENGTHENING LOCAL-FOR-LOCAL STRATEGY

BOARD APPROVES NEW ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE

MILAN , Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Board of Directors of Pirelli & C. S.p.A. met today and majority approved - with the contrary vote of board members Zhang Haitao, Xi Xiaohong and Wang Kun - an investment plan for the United States worth approximately €1 billion (around $1.2 billion), aimed at expanding the Rome, Georgia plant, which already produces the most technologically advanced solutions for the U.S. market.

The investment plan will support Pirelli's growth in the High Value segment in the United States, the world's largest market for this segment, accounting for approximately 40% of global volumes. The project will strengthen the company's local-for-local strategy, enhance supply chain resilience, and meet the growing demand for technologically advanced "Made in USA" products. Furthermore, the investment reinforces Pirelli's long-term commitment to the country, where the company has operated in the State of Georgia since 2002 and established strong relationships with government institutions, local authorities, and universities.

The expansion plan will be implemented over several years starting in 2027 and increase annual production capacity at the Rome plant, including Cyber™ Tyre technology, to approximately 6 million car tyres upon completion in 2033 and is expected to create around 1,000 new jobs.

The expansion of the Rome plant, which will become a state-of-the-art industrial hub, will take place in two phases. The first phase will involve a gradual increase in robotized production based on the latest evolution of MIRS (Modular Integrated Robotized System), a proprietary Pirelli technology, with production capacity progressively increasing from 2028 and ultimately reaching 3 million tyres per year. This will be achieved through autonomous modular robotic systems capable of manufacturing technologically advanced High Value tyres. In addition, a fully automated conventional production facility will be built using the most advanced manufacturing processes and dedicated to premium products, with an additional production capacity at completion of 3 million tyres per year at full operation.

The plant will be able to produce the most advanced technology products, including Cyber™ Tyre. Following the governance changes introduced under Italy's 2026 Golden Power Decree, Pirelli obtained authorization from the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) to market the Cyber™ Tyre system in the U.S. market, a country increasingly adopting connected and autonomous vehicles.

This expansion plan will permit Pirelli to implement the growth of production capacity in a gradual manner and in line with the evolution of demand, maintaining very high efficiency standards and optimizing the costs of raw material transformation and investment. The project timeline is consistent with the industrial requirements of the High Value segment, which require highly specialized manufacturing processes, small-batch management of a broad product mix, and integration of Pirelli's proprietary technologies.

The project will not have an impact on the company's 2026 targets, with the capex-to-revenue ratio for 2027-2033 seen remaining substantially in continuity with previous periods, while preserving the Group's cash generation.

Pirelli also announces that today the Board of Directors approved a new organizational structure which foresees the elimination of Corporate General Management function with immediate effect. The Board therefore approved the terms and conditions relative to the resolution of the employment relationship of the Corporate General Manager Francesco Tanzi. To ensure a smooth transition, Mr. Tanzi will maintain his executive employment relationship with the Company until December 31, 2026.

In accordance with the current Pirelli Group Remuneration Policy, Mr. Tanzi will be entitled, in addition to the amounts accrued up to the date of termination of his executive employment relationship, to a severance indemnity equal to 13 months' remuneration, to be paid by February 2027.

Also pursuant to the Pirelli Remuneration Policy, Mr. Tanzi will retain the rights accrued up to the date of termination of his employment in connection with participation in the following incentive plans: (i) the 2023 Annual STI Plan, with regard to the deferred portion and related company matching component; (ii) the 2024 and 2025 Annual STI Plans, with regard to the deferred portion; and (iii) the 2026 Annual STI Plan and the 2024-2026 Long-Term Incentive Plan. These incentive plans remain subject to the customary claw back mechanisms set out in the Remuneration Policy.

To protect the Group's strategic and operational know-how, Mr. Tanzi will remain bound, for the two years following termination, by a non-compete covenant covering the principal countries in which Pirelli operates, in consideration of a payment equal to 130% of his gross annual salary. The amount due will be paid by the Company to Mr. Tanzi in eight quarterly installments in arrears over the two-year non-compete period.

Following the termination of his employment, given his expertise and knowledge of the Group acquired over the years, Mr. Tanzi will remain engaged by the Company under a two-year consultancy agreement with annual compensation of 350,000 euro, gross of applicable withholding taxes. As well as non-monetary benefits valued at 45,000 euro, gross.

The terms and conditions of the termination of Mr. Tanzi's employment and the subsequent consultancy agreement were approved today by the Board of Directors following the favorable opinion of the Remuneration Committee, acting also in its capacity as the Related Parties Committee for remuneration matters, based on its assessment of compliance with the criteria set out in the Remuneration Policy approved by the Shareholders' Meeting.

Mr. Tanzi does not hold any Pirelli shares.

The Board of Directors of Pirelli, met today, following the declaration by Marco Tronchetti Provera & C. S.p.A. ("MTP & C. SpA") concerning the existence of MTP & C. SpA's control over Pirelli, has instructed the Audit, Risk and Corporate Governance Committee to initiate discussions with the controlling shareholder, also with the support of external experts, in order to define the framework governing the relationships arising from the control situation. This includes analyzing the conditions for the possible adoption of a group governance regulation, taking into account governance best practices followed by listed companies and adhering to principles of transparency, efficiency and market protection, while preserving Pirelli's legal and managerial autonomy.

evidence.title: Pirelli's latest Scorpion tyres feature F1-style compounds and treads designed with Fabien Barel
evidence.text:
Pirelli's latest Scorpion tyres feature F1-style compounds and treads designed with Fabien Barel

New Pirelli Scorpion Gravity range blends F1 and MotoGP tech with a tread pattern designed by one of the most successful downhill racers ever

Pirelli’s new Scorpion Gravity range includes new treads, casings and compounds. The three new tread patterns are called Black Sting, Emperor and Red Claw.

There are four casings, which Pirelli says are all eMTB-compatible, and three compounds colour-coded and named after those used by Pirelli in its Formula 1 tyres.

Three-time downhill world champion Fabien Barel has had “direct input” into the development of the new range and says the Scorpion Gravity tyres offer "the kind of confidence you notice within the first few turns".

The three tread patterns are named after species of scorpion and designed to work best in the terrain native to each animal. The Black Sting is designed for dry hardpack, the Emperor is an all-rounder and the Red Claw works best in loose or muddy conditions, according to Pirelli.

The Emperor pattern is designed to replace Pirelli’s less creatively named RACE M tread pattern and the Red Claw replaces the RACE T.

With four casings on offer, there is plenty of choice, balancing weight and toughness. The casings are designed to work across every type of riding, from trail to downhill, along with enduro and even freeride.

The lightest ProWALL casing features sidewall protection and Pirelli claims a weight of 700-900g. It’s designed for climbing efficiency without compromising reliability and descending performance.

The HardWALL casing has additional reinforcement and Pirelli claims it weighs 900-1,100g. It looks to be aimed at more aggressive trail riders seeking additional reinforcement to protect against pinch-flats.

DualWALL is designed for enduro , bike parks and freeriding. It’s dual-ply and weighs 1,100-1,300g.

The DH+ is a full downhill racing -oriented casing, featuring a tougher dual-ply carcass with additional sidewall and bead reinforcement. Pirelli claims tyres with the DH+ casing weigh from 1,300g to over 1,500g.

Pirelli is the sole tyre provider for F1 and will be for MotoGP too, from 2027. The compound names and colours for the Scorpion MTB range match the F1 compound names and colour-coded sidewall graphics.

The hardest compound is the yellow-lettered 'Medium' compound, which is said to balance grip and durability. The intermediate compound is called 'Soft' and comes with red writing on the sidewall. The purple SuperSoft compound is the softest and Pirelli says it offers maximum grip and damping.

Pirelli recommends the SuperSoft for the front, but says it can also be used on the rear for racing.

The new Pirelli Scorpion Black Sting, Emperor and Red Claw are available now online and through selected bike shops.

Prices range from £54.99 to £79.99, depending on spec.

evidence.text:
Here’s how Prysmian’s latest deal with AWS emphasizes sustainability

Posted by Brad Randall | Sep 22, 2026 | COMPANY NEWS , Data Centers , ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT , Innovation , Investment , Partnerships , Sustainability , TECHNOLOGY

The project reportedly marks the first known installation of inert-anode-smelted, low-carbon aluminum in a data center facility.

Edited by Brad Randall, Broadband Communities

Cable manufacturer Prysmian has landed a deal to supply power cables made with zero-direct-emission aluminum to an Amazon Web Services data center near Columbus, Ohio.

In a joint venture with mining giant Rio Tinto and distributor Wesco, Prysmian will supply building wire produced with ELYSIS technology, an aluminum smelting process that emits pure oxygen instead of greenhouse gases, according to Prysmian . The project marks the first known installation of inert-anode-smelted, low-carbon aluminum in a data center facility, Prysmian said last week.

The announcement highlights growing demand from hypescalers and digital infrastructure providers for green supply chain solutions to power data center expansion. The contract comes on the heels of Prysmian and Rio Tinto’s initial March 2026 launch of the low-carbon aluminum building wire.

The cables are manufactured at Prysmian’s Sedalia, Missouri, plant using aluminum produced with hydropower in Quebec, Canada, Prysmian said.

For Prysmian, the deployment also aligns with its broader target to draw 55% of its revenues from sustainability-linked solutions by 2028 and reach net-zero emissions by 2035. AWS aims to hit net-zero operations by 2040.

evidence.title: Prysmian Chooses Aluminum Cable for Amazon Data Center
evidence.text:
MILAN, Italy — As investment in AI, cloud computing and data centers accelerates, so does the need for electrical infrastructure to power them. Prysmian and Rio Tinto , in collaboration with Amazon, have taken a significant stride toward reducing the carbon footprint of that infrastructure, with electrical cables made using ELYSIS® aluminum that have been contracted for installation in an Amazon data center in Ohio, USA.

ELYSIS® technology produces aluminum with no direct greenhouse gas emissions from the smelting process by replacing traditional carbon anodes with proprietary materials that release pure oxygen instead of greenhouse gases.

The project marks the first known use of inert-anode-smelted aluminum in a data center, demonstrating how innovation in one of the most fundamental materials used in electrical infrastructure can support the rapid expansion of digital infrastructure while reducing its embedded carbon footprint.

Prysmian is using the aluminum to manufacture the electrical cables at its Sedalia, Missouri, facility for deployment in Amazon’s data center infrastructure.

The project builds on the collaboration announced by Prysmian and Rio Tinto in March 2026 to introduce aluminum building wire produced using the ELYSIS® technology. Prysmian’s partner, Wesco, is supporting the distribution and delivery to the project site.

Prysmian has targeted net zero Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions by 2035, and over 55% of its revenues to be sustainability-linked by 2028.

“We aim to reach net-zero emissions across our operations by 2040 through decarbonizing our operations and supply chain, down to the raw materials. Traditionally, making aluminum is carbon-intensive, but this wire was made with technology that emits oxygen instead of carbon dioxide and perfluorocarbons,” said Joern Tinnemeyer, VP of Data Center Engineering at Amazon Web Services (AWS) . “Prysmian, Rio Tinto, and Wesco are showing that lower-carbon materials aren’t a future concept – they’re here and going into Amazon data centers today.”

“The data center industry needs advanced technologies like this: cables that can effectively carry power, meet high-quality standards, and make a positive impact on the sustainability of the entire value chain,” said Srinivas Siripurapu, Chief Sustainability, R&D, and Innovation Officer for Prysmian . “We have partnered with organizations that share our mission for sustainability-driven innovation, from Rio Tinto’s supply of low-carbon aluminum to the delivery of product through our partnership with Wesco, and ultimately Amazon’s final product.”

“Data center customers are increasingly looking for solutions that help them meet aggressive growth targets while advancing their sustainability objectives,” said David Speidelsbach, Vice President, Sales and Strategic Initiatives at Wesco . “This project demonstrates what is possible when manufacturers, distributors and end users work together to accelerate innovation. Through sustainable supply chain solutions that help reduce material waste and support circularity, we’re proud to collaborate with Prysmian and Amazon to help bring more sustainable infrastructure solutions to one of the world’s fastest-growing industries.”

“This collaboration with Prysmian and Amazon demonstrates how innovation across the value chain can help deliver practical, lower-carbon solutions for customers. All of the aluminum supplied by Rio Tinto for these cables was produced in Quebec, Canada, using hydropower, including the aluminum made with ELYSIS® inert anode technology. By combining renewable power with a breakthrough smelting process that eliminates direct greenhouse gas emissions and produces oxygen as a by-product, we are helping create a new pathway to support the decarbonization of critical data center infrastructure,” said Matt Schicke, Rio Tinto Aluminum Vice President, Sales and Marketing .

evidence.text:
Tech buying on the stock market, with a focus on Nvidia. ST and Prysmian rise

Former Pirelli Cavi, promoted by Intermonte, focuses on the acquisition of Atkore

For feedback, please contact english@ilsole24ore.com

For feedback, please contact english@ilsole24ore.com

(Il Sole 24 Ore Radiocor) - The reassuring outlook provided by Nvidia – which, according to CEO Jensen Huang, will sell twice as many chips next year thanks to developments in artificial intelligence – is bolstering the technology sector, which, following gains on Wall Street and in Asia, is also gaining ground in Europe. On the Milan Stock Exchange, buying interest is thus favouring Stmicroelectronics and Prysmian , the latter increasingly linked to the sector due to the need for infrastructure electrification.

The former Pirelli Cavi is also benefiting from the assessment by Intermonte analysts, who have decided raise the target price to 154 euros (from the previous 130 euros), 26 per cent above the current price, and to upgrade the stock’s rating from ‘neutral’ to ‘outperform’. The experts are focusing on the acquisition of Atkore, which ‘adds 12 per cent to the estimated EBITDA for 2028. We are also slightly increasing the standalone estimates for the Transmission and Digital Solutions divisions, bringing the estimated EPS for 2027/2028 to €6.18/€7.79, representing increases of +4% and +12% respectively”.

The upgrade reflects “greater visibility on estimates — thanks to the structural growth of energy networks, electrification and data centres — and the fact that Prysmian’s business has historically managed to hold up well when the macroeconomic environment deteriorates”. Experts point out that the share price “has fallen by 17 per cent over the last three months, compared with a 9 per cent decline in our weighted panel of comparable companies. In our view, this relatively sharper fall has made the risk/reward ratio attractive at current prices”.

Looking in more detail at the Aktore transaction, the impact on EPS is estimated at ‘-3.8 per cent in 2026 – a negative effect due to the issue of new shares – +4.1 per cent in 2027’, which would be the first year of Atkore’s consolidation, and ‘+11.6 per cent in 2028’.

Another area of focus is data centres. According to Intermonte, “revenues from data centres in the Energy divisions are around three times higher than those of the Digital Solutions division. The I&C (Industrial & Commercial) division grew organically by 13.4 per cent in North America in the second quarter of 2026, driven mainly by demand from data centres. The Transmission division has an order book of €17 billion, with a margin of 21.2 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, compared with the 18–20 per cent target indicated during the Capital Markets Day. The profitability of Digital Solutions rose from 16.8 per cent to 23.8 per cent, thanks to a shift in volumes from telecommunications towards major US cloud and data centre operators (hyperscalers).’

evidence.title: Brembo Just Launched Its Most Powerful Brakes Ever on a Chevrolet
evidence.text:
Brembo braking power and panache are not just for performance cars anymore, big heavy performance trucks and SUVs are now getting their own special Brembo treatment in the form of this innovative new six-piston caliper, the Brembo Boldika. The Italian brand claims this is its most powerful caliper to date, capable of generating 8,500 Nm of stopping force per corner. That's 6,269 lb-ft in freedom units and it's what you need to rein in a 4-ton truck hauling a 7-ton trailer. Its first application was the Chevrolet Silverado EV RST Stars and Steel Edition that just went on sale, and more fitments are coming.

Generating this much stopping force can induce excessive flex in traditional sliding caliper designs, which the driver perceives as less-confident pedal feel. So Brembo houses three pistons in each of two aluminum caliper halves that are bolted to a cast iron bridge that also serves as the chassis mount (via four bolts, double the traditional amount).

Iron bridge showing four mounting holes.Brembo

What about galvanic corrosion, you fret? Program manager Ben Pohl notes, "They have to meet 10- or 15-year corrosion durability. The bracket itself is zinc/nickel coated, which is a very robust coating, so both of them have an additional layer of corrosion protection before they ever go together. And then of course we paint it, which gives another layer of protection." On the Silverado EV, they're painted Torch Red and wear both Chevy and Brembo badging.

The Boldika design incorporates "Brembo Enesys zero-drag" technology, a pair of springs that help the pads return to their resting position after braking to reduce residual brake torque, increasing range and maximize pad life.

Enesys springs removed, note partial retaining pins.Brembo

Swapping pads should be a breeze as well—just remove the caliper-mounting bolts, slide the caliper off, pop out the Enesys springs, and the pads are free to fall out the middle, as the retaining pins don't span across both halves.

These first Boldika calipers are designed to fit a 15.7-inch rotor inside a 20-inch wheel, but the design is easily scalable, and other heavy trucks and SUVs with differing needs are likely to adopt the design in the near future. Note that for now they're envisioned as front brakes only, as axle-shaft endplay on the live axles on most HD pickups is better handled by sliding calipers than fixed designs like this, where pad movement can result in a mushy pedal feel. At about 31 pounds each, these calipers aren't light, but then, they've got a big, worst-case-scenario job to do if your 14,000-pound trailer loses its brakes.

Relative to other high-capacity calipers, these don't require dramatically greater hydraulic pressure or fluid displacement during normal operation, but their impressive rigidity is said to impart a very confident brake pedal feel on a loaded rig. And by pushing these extra large (20-square-inch) pads away from the rotors when they're not in use, they're expected to last a lot longer as well.

It's unclear whether workaday trucks will adopt the Boldika. Matching the Boldika's stiffness and pedal feel with a conventional sliding caliper at these loads would likely impose significant mass and packaging penalties, but their two-piston designs are way cheaper to manufacture, rebuild, and replace, and packaging all of the caliper pistons inboard requires less clearance between the caliper and the wheel spokes. Plus, business owners and employee drivers are less likely to prioritize superior pedal feel and shiny painted design. Note that the design is also future-proofed, as it is capable of operating with Brembo's by-wire Sensify system that uses electrohydraulic actuators at the corners. Stay tuned for our upcoming instrumented testing of a Silverado EV Stars and Steel edition.

evidence.title: Brembo Brake Caliper for MotoGP 2027: Lighter and Already in Testing
evidence.text:
Brembo Brake Caliper for MotoGP 2027: Lighter and Already in Testing

MotoGP faces a profound technical shake-up in 2027. With the switch to 850cc displacement, reduced aerodynamics, the removal of ride-height devices, and the tyre change from Michelin to Pirelli, the demands on almost every part of the prototypes are changing. The braking system is no exception. Brembo reacted early and has unveiled a completely reworked brake caliper designed specifically for the new generation of 850cc machines.

What is new about the Brembo brake caliper for 2027?

The new Brembo brake caliper for 2027 is about 80 grams (roughly 0.18 lbs) lighter than the current part and does away with the distinctive cooling fins. In their place is a much simpler, more technical-looking shape that results from what is known as topological optimization. Starting from the component’s 3D model, material is removed exactly where no high forces act, and kept only where it is actually needed. For the teams, the switch remains straightforward, since the caliper uses the same brake pad as the current version and is largely designed as a plug-and-play solution. This means the new part can be compared directly with the previous design without having to replace the entire package.

The caliper is getting lighter because braking loads with the 850cc machines are expected to be somewhat lower than with today’s bikes. The reasons are the smaller displacement, reduced front-end aerodynamics, the removal of downforce systems, and a changed overall weight. Brembo therefore redesigned the caliper from scratch. Per component, the saving amounts to about 80 grams; across both front calipers combined, that adds up to around 160 grams (about 0.35 lbs). Andrea Pellegrini, who is responsible for motorcycle racing at Brembo, puts the benefit of this saving into context: “Dynamically, the rider doesn’t really feel the difference directly, but for engineers, having lighter solutions is always important, because it then allows us to position weight where it’s needed on the bike.” This weight shift can matter especially at the front wheel, where mass strongly influences handling.

Does the braking feel stay the same for riders?

Yes, the braking feel is expected to remain largely unchanged, because Brembo keeps the same hydraulic ratio and the same pistons as on the previous caliper. With this, the manufacturer wants to avoid altering the feedback at the lever that has been fine-tuned over years. Externally the part looks new, but functionally it should feel familiar to the rider. The anti-drag system is also retained, preventing the pads from touching the disc as soon as the rider releases pressure on the lever. The caliper also keeps the quick-release fittings, which are useful when the caliper needs to be removed for a wheel change or disc work, without having to bleed the system every time. One change concerns the anti-shaking valve, which is no longer housed in the brake caliper but has been relocated to the master cylinder.

How did the current finned caliper come about?

The current caliper, fitted to the 1000cc machines, was introduced in 2020 to cope with significantly increased power, temperatures, and loads. Part of this load resulted from growing aerodynamics and downforce. At the time, Brembo increased the surface area in contact with the air to dissipate more heat. The cooling fins used for this became a defining feature and were later also adopted for the calipers in Moto2 and Moto3. Many of these approaches originate from Formula 1, from which Brembo has transferred, among other things, finned brake calipers and supercooling pistons into motorcycle racing. With the switch to the 850cc bikes, this development is now partly reversing, because the thermal demands are different.

When will the new brake caliper be used?

The new brake caliper could already be used towards the end of the current season and is likely to be one of the central technical innovations of the 2027 season. Brembo has delivered one set to every manufacturer and team, so that everyone has the same opportunity to test at the same time. Some teams have already tried the part during testing in Misano, with more expected to follow in Brno. The final decision then lies with the teams. The fact that Brembo is equipping every motorcycle at all is not a regulatory requirement, but the result of a choice made by all the teams.

For the brake discs, it looks like the large 355-millimeter discs, also known in the paddock as “pans” because of their shape, could be used less often in the first year of the new era. The most commonly used solution is expected to be the 340-millimeter discs, available in a standard and a ventilated version. Brembo is nevertheless keeping all variants in its range, since the choice depends on the tracks and the teams’ requirements. For 2028, Pellegrini considers the 355mm discs useful on particularly brake-intensive circuits such as Austria and Motegi. The large disc was originally introduced to reduce the risk, on such tracks, of having to interrupt a race for a disc change. If performance were to drop significantly with the new machines, Pellegrini says a return to the 320-millimeter discs, which have not been used for around three years, would also be conceivable.

How does this new development fit into MotoGP 2027?

The brake caliper is just one piece of a comprehensive overhaul that the entire grid is preparing for. As early as spring 2026, Ducati ran a first 850cc prototype with test rider Michele Pirro during a private shakedown in Misano, fitted with simplified aerodynamics, no ride-height adjustment, and early versions of the Pirelli tyres. From Brembo’s point of view, these tyres are seen as the biggest unknown, since no one can yet reliably predict how the performance level will develop. This matters for the brakes, because longer braking phases heat up the system more, while shorter, harder braking tends to produce pressure spikes instead. Regarding the weight of the new machines, there has so far been talk of roughly eight to twelve kilograms (about 18 to 26 lbs) less, though precise figures are still pending. A first joint test with Pirelli is planned for the period after the Misano Grand Prix, initially using adapted current machines.

➜ This article is part of our comprehensive overview: 2026 MotoGP Season: The Complete Overview – Teams, Riders, Calendar & Championship Standings . Find all key information on this topic in one place.

The new Brembo brake caliper for 2027 is about 80 grams (roughly 0.18 lbs) lighter than the current part. Across both front calipers, that adds up to a saving of around 160 grams. This is achieved through topological optimization, where material is kept only where it is actually needed.

No, the braking feel is expected to stay largely the same. Brembo keeps the same hydraulic ratio and the same pistons as the current caliper, so the feedback at the lever remains familiar. The anti-drag system and the quick-release fittings are also retained.

The new caliper could be used as early as the end of the current season and is expected to be one of the key technical innovations for the 2027 season. Brembo has already supplied the part to all teams; initial testing took place in Misano, with further running planned in Brno.

From 2027, MotoGP switches to 850cc displacement, reduces aerodynamics, removes ride-height devices, and changes tyre supplier from Michelin to Pirelli. The changes are intended to make racing safer and to limit costs and effort, while also altering the demands placed on the braking system.

The 340-millimeter discs, available in standard and ventilated versions, are expected to be the most commonly used option at first. The larger 355-millimeter discs may be used less often in the first year but will remain part of the range. For particularly brake-intensive tracks, they are expected to be an option again from 2028.

evidence.title: What Is Brembo Sensify and Why It Could Reinvent Braking
evidence.text:
What Is Brembo Sensify and Why It Could Reinvent Braking

The solution is called Sensify, and it was first announced back in 2021. Initially scheduled to enter the market two years ago, in 2024, it has finally been adopted by an unnamed “leading global manufacturer” and should roll down the roads shortly.

Knowing that, we here at autoevolution thought it would be best to have a look at a piece of technology that may significantly change braking for the first time in, well, forever, if you really think about it.

First, what is Sensify ? Almost all of today’s braking systems are hydraulic in nature. When the driver presses a pedal inside the cabin’s footwell, the mechanical force is transformed into pressure within the brake fluid lines by means of a master cylinder.

The brake fluid then transfers the pressure from the master cylinder to the wheels by using a piston that clamps pads onto a rotating metal disc, generating friction to slow down the car. In all of this, naturally, the brake fluid plays a crucial role. Sensify does not use any, nor does it need hydraulic circuits and centralized actuation.

The system still relies on a pedal in the cabin, only this time we’re dealing with a simulator of sorts, not an actual mechanical pedal that performs an action when pressed. Instead, when that happens, a signal is sent to an electronic control unit.

Photo: Brembo This unit then translates the input into commands for the actuators to push the brake’s pistons and apply brake pressure. All four wheels on the car have them, and they can brake with different forces to suit the driving and stopping needs.

For the record, the physical setup of the system comprises the existing collection of Brembo calipers, discs, and friction materials, but they now work under the coordination of an artificial intelligence of an undisclosed nature.

According to the Italian supplier, the Sensify idea comes with several important advantages over traditional systems. The first is, naturally, the absence of braking fluids, which leads to lower maintenance costs.

Then, the way the system works continues to provide the driver with the pedal feel they’re used to, thanks to the feedback the pedal offers, while at the same time delivering a safer and more precise braking action, even in complex and highly variable driving conditions.

Because there’s a lot of software involved in the Sensify, updates can be made to it as the need arises. Unlike other electromechanical braking technologies currently being researched, the Sensify comes with adaptable hardware and software, and that means it can be used on pretty much all vehicle types imaginable, from cars to vans and from internal combustion rides to electric ones.

Photo: Brembo Because the thing is plug-and-play in nature, it can be made part of more advanced solutions, including autonomous systems and other advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS). It allows for independent control over each wheel, and it delivers shorter locking times, lower drag torque, and lower disc consumption. Where such a thing is available, the Sensify can also help with regenerative braking.

Because it comes with fewer components than a traditional solution, Brembo’s idea could translate into more space in the passenger compartment. The pedal tech is adaptable, and it can be installed either on the right side or the left side of the vehicle, and, finally, the level of pedal response can be customized to suit the needs and requirements of different drivers.

As said, Brembo said at the beginning of May that large-scale series production for the Sensify has begun on behalf of a leading global manufacturer, but does not name it. On top of that, we’re told that new contracts have already been signed, and that could lead to hundreds of thousands of units being produced each year from now on.

According to Daniele Schillaci, CEO of Brembo, the technology has been designed to orchestrate the entire corner ecosystem, at the same time supporting “safer mobility, while paving the way for the next generation of software-defined vehicles, reflecting our long-term purpose of shaping a zero accident future.”

While the merits of the new braking technology are beyond questioning, the part with the zero-accident future is a bit hard to swallow, just as in the case with GM , which reminded us about its push to get there earlier this month as well.

To me, no matter how advanced the technology, a world with zero crashes is something that will probably never be fully realized, for the simple reason that driving is subject to too many variables, many of them well beyond our control.

If you are watching Brembo (BIT:BRE) this week, you are not alone. The Italian automotive parts maker has seen some attention from investors after its shares delivered a modest gain over the past week. There hasn't been a single headline-grabbing event; however, it is exactly these quieter moments that often raise important questions for anyone trying to assess the company's true value.

Brembo's stock story has been anything but dull when you look at the bigger picture. Despite a dip over the last month, shares are actually up around 20% over the past three months, with annual gains just above breakeven. Over the longer term, the stock has outperformed many of its peers, though this year's returns have been mixed. Strong recent growth in net income has outpaced revenue growth for the last year, which hints at improving operating margins within a challenging sector.

After this bout of short-term momentum and a mixed annual return, the question for investors is whether Brembo is offering a real buying window now or if the market is already factoring in all the company's future growth.

Price-to-Earnings of 14.5x: Is it justified?

Brembo currently trades at a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 14.5x, which is higher than the European Auto Components industry average of 13.1x but below the broader Italian market average of 17.6x. This indicates the market is placing a premium on Brembo shares relative to direct sector peers, while still valuing them less highly than the country's overall equities landscape.

The P/E ratio is a widely used metric in assessing whether a stock's current price reflects its earnings power. It allows investors to compare the valuation of different companies within the same industry and evaluate whether a stock appears attractive based on its profit generation potential. In cyclical, margin-sensitive sectors such as auto components, P/E multiples can reflect market confidence in future earnings and operational resilience.

For Brembo, the higher multiple compared to its industry suggests investors might be anticipating solid future growth or margin improvements. evidence.title: Brembo RCS Corsa Corta RR Master Cylinder Kit First Look
evidence.text:
Brembo is marking its 50th anniversary in racing with a master cylinder kit that will appeal to collectors and serious riders—the RCS Corsa Corta RR kit. Tailored for high-performance motorcycle riders who demand precision and exclusivity, this limited-edition race-replica kit, capped at just 500 numbered units, blends MotoGP-derived technology with striking gold-accented aesthetics.

The RCS Corsa Corta RR evolves from Brembo’s renowned RCS Corsa Corta brake lever and master cylinder. Machined from aerospace-grade aluminum alloy with a hard-anodized finish, it mirrors the brake master cylinders used in MotoGP and WorldSBK. A titanium lever pin, straight from MotoGP spec, ensures lightweight durability, while the pump body sports a laser-etched serial production number (001/500 and up) and a gold pad-printed Brembo logo for a premium touch.

The kit includes a brake fluid reservoir with a billet aluminum cap featuring a gold Brembo symbol, paired with a black wristband sporting a gold 50th-anniversary logo. These elements highlight the kit’s limited production, complementing its technical focus.

The Brembo RCS Corsa Corta RR offers adjustable features for precise braking control. Its lever allows fine-tuning of the bite point via a top-mounted selector, providing three settings—Race, Sport, and Normal—to suit varying riding styles or track conditions. The Ratio Click System (RCS) enables precise braking force distribution without compromising system performance, offering real-time feedback to optimize setups for wet roads, tight corners, or high-speed sprints.

This master cylinder isn’t just about function—it also earned Brembo a Red Dot Award in 2023, following the original RCS Corsa Corta’s win in 2019 . For demanding riders, this kit offers a rare chance to own a piece of Brembo’s racing legacy, blending cutting-edge tech with collector-worthy industrial art. With only 500 units produced, this kit offers elite riders a rare chance to own MotoGP-inspired technology that doubles as industrial art. Availability begins this month; check with your dealer for pricing.

evidence.title: Specialized and Brembo seal a revolutionary alliance for MTB
evidence.text:
From Formula 1 and Moto GP to MTB, this is how Brembo brakes are being used by Specialized in competition

For weeks, all rumors pointed to Brembo as the manufacturer behind the brakes being tested by the Specialized Gravity team. Something that has just been confirmed by this legendary Italian brand that has been dedicated to braking the fastest motorcycles and cars on the planet for years.

Specialized and Brembo seal a revolutionary alliance for MTB

Brembo and Specialized, one of the most influential brands in the cycling industry, have announced a strategic collaboration aimed at enhancing brake performance in the world of downhill Mountain Biking. The alliance, focused on the Specialized Gravity team, marks a decisive step for Brembo's entry into top-level mountain biking.

The collaboration will result in the joint development of a specific braking system for downhill MTB, which is already being tested by the team riders during the 2025 DH World Cup. With this agreement, both brands aim to maximize their experience in innovation, design, and competition.

Brembo, known for its successes in disciplines such as Formula 1, MotoGP, or the World Superbike Championship, is now applying that same philosophy of precision and extreme performance to cycling. For Specialized, this collaboration reinforces its commitment to innovation and its dedication to providing its athletes with the best tools to compete at the highest level.

“This partnership represents a significant milestone for Brembo, as we are bringing our braking expertise to the pinnacle of competitive mountain biking for the first time. Specialized shares our vision for performance, innovation, and design, and we couldn't ask for a better partner for this journey”, stated Andrea Poggi, Chief Marketing Officer of Brembo.

Armin Landgraf, CEO of Specialized, noted: “We firmly believe that competition is the best testing ground for innovation. This collaboration with Brembo will allow us to develop cutting-edge technology that will benefit not only our riders but also the entire cycling community in the long term”.

The collaboration will include intensive R&D work to create a completely new braking system that meets the extreme demands of professional downhill riding. It is expected that this technology will evolve over time and that some of that development will reach consumer products. For now, the focus is on giving the Specialized Gravity riders a real competitive advantage on every descent.

With this alliance, Brembo also celebrates its 50 years of participation in motor competitions, making the leap to a discipline to which it already dedicated a project in 2008 with specific models for DH, but it did not continue.

It is worth remembering that earlier this year Brembo acquired the suspension brand Ohlins, so it would not be surprising to see more official Ohlins teams using Brembo brakes in the future.

evidence.title: Christian Horner could now change Ferrari’s plan to ‘honourably’ sack Fred Vasseur
evidence.text:
Christian Horner could now change Ferrari’s plan to ‘honourably’ sack Fred Vasseur

Whispers are growing in the Formula 1 paddock that Ferrari had already started to put a plan in place to sack Fred Vasseur before Christian Horner began flirting with the job.

Vasseur has stood at the Ferrari helm since December 2022 after he replaced Mattia Binotto as the team principal in Maranello. Yet the Scuderia’s dream of fighting Mercedes to win the 2026 drivers’ title becoming ever smaller is beginning to put Vasseur’s tenure at serious risk.

Ferrari always faced an uphill struggle to finally deliver their first drivers’ title since 2007 this year. But wins for Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc in Barcelona and Silverstone started to build belief that a title bid may be possible, only to then see Andrea Kimi Antonelli run away.

Ferrari already planned to sack Fred Vasseur at the end of 2026 before Christian Horner’s flirtation

Hamilton and Leclerc still believe in Vasseur , it is reported, but Ferrari’s struggles are starting to make the 58-year-old’s seat on their pit wall very hot. It is also said that Ferrari’s hierarchy is not happy with Vasseur’s team management after seeing Hamilton and Leclerc’s clashes.

READ MORE: Who is Christian Horner? Everything to know from Red Bull past to net worth

Vasseur does not want to “waste energy” discussing his future , but the rumours concerning his position could now start to grow after former Red Bull team principal Horner revealed he would forgo shares to join Ferrari , as joining the pride of Italy would be the Briton’s “dream”.

Horner has been hellbent on becoming a stakeholder in whichever team he joins next, but is willing to forget that dream if Ferrari ever call. And PlanetF1 reports that Horner’s revelation has come amid growing ‘whispers’ that Ferrari were already starting to plan to drop Vasseur.

The ‘turbulent period’ that Ferrari are currently enduring is said to have already seen Ferrari put a plan in place to replace Vasseur in an ‘honourable discharge’. The move would free the Frenchman to take up a ‘lower-profile’ position, but Horner could now change Ferrari’s plan.

READ MORE: Who is Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur? Everything you need to know

Ferrari have long viewed their WEC team boss Antonello Coletta as a potential successor for Vasseur, with deputy F1 team principal Jerome d’Ambrosio another candidate. But Horner’s public come-and-get-me plea may now convince Ferrari chairman John Elkann to reconsider who should replace Vasseur at the end of the 2026 season and lead the Scuderia into 2027.

Elkann has long dreamed of appointing Horner , but has always failed to convince the Briton to move to Ferrari to date. The Scuderia chief previously tried to hire the long-time Red Bull boss back in 2022. Reports have continually linked Horner with Ferrari since he left Red Bull in July 2025, as well, but his wish to become a stakeholder in an F1 team had been an issue.

Now, Horner revealing that Ferrari are the “only” F1 team for whom he would give up on his wish to become a stakeholder could put Vasseur in even murkier waters. So, it remains to be seen whether Vasseur can lead a revival and save himself, or whether the damage is done.

evidence.title: Vasseur says Ferrari rumours are putting team “in a corner”
evidence.text:
Frédéric Vasseur has criticised the stream of rumours surrounding Ferrari, arguing that repeated reports of internal tension are putting the Formula 1 team “in a corner.”

The Ferrari team principal addressed the subject amid renewed scrutiny over the management structure at Maranello and the relationship between Lewis Hamilton and senior personnel.

Vasseur believes certain stories force Ferrari into an uncomfortable position: answering every claim risks giving it greater credibility, while remaining silent can be interpreted as confirmation.

“Certain rumours put the team in a corner,” Vasseur said.

The latest controversy followed reports in the Italian media suggesting Hamilton had asked Ferrari to replace members of its technical and operational staff. The seven-time world champion publicly rejected those claims, insisting he had never demanded anyone’s dismissal.

Hamilton explained that his recommendations were intended to improve Ferrari’s working methods rather than determine who should remain employed. He also defended the people working at Maranello and stressed that organisational decisions belong to the team.

The driver had already denied asking Ferrari to replace staff before the Azerbaijan GP weekend.

For Vasseur, the wider problem is that speculation can rapidly become accepted as fact around Ferrari. The Italian team attracts greater domestic and international attention than most of its rivals, making every difficult result, radio message or internal adjustment a potential source of crisis stories.

That attention also creates a difficult balance. Ferrari must be capable of questioning its own performance without allowing legitimate internal debate to be presented as evidence of instability.

The team has made changes during Hamilton’s time at Maranello, but restructuring is not unusual during the development of a new technical programme. Ferrari’s chassis department is led by Loïc Serra, while Enrico Gualtieri remains responsible for the power-unit operation.

Vasseur’s response does not mean Ferrari is satisfied with every aspect of its performance. Instead, his argument is that improvement requires clear internal analysis—not decisions driven by outside pressure.

On track, Charles Leclerc qualified second for the Azerbaijan GP, although George Russell’s pole lap was 0.837s faster . Hamilton ended the session sixth, 1.332s away from the Mercedes driver.

The result gave Ferrari a valuable front-row starting position but also underlined the performance gap it must address. Separating that technical reality from the constant noise surrounding the team is precisely the challenge Vasseur wants Ferrari to manage better.

The race starts on Saturday, September 26, at 12:00 UK time . It begins at 07:00 ET and 04:00 PT in the US, 16:30 in India and 21:00 AEST in eastern Australia.

George Russell starts from pole for Mercedes, ahead of Charles Leclerc and Oscar Piastri. Isack Hadjar qualified fourth, followed by Lando Norris and Lewis Hamilton.

The race was moved to Saturday because Sunday, September 27, is Azerbaijan’s Remembrance Day, a national day of mourning. The entire F1 weekend was brought forward by one day.

Vasseur said certain reports were putting Ferrari “in a corner”, because responding can amplify speculation while silence may be treated as confirmation.

evidence.title: Horner calls Ferrari “dream job” and says he would drop equity demand
evidence.text:
Christian Horner has made his clearest declaration of interest in Ferrari, saying he would abandon his demand for an ownership stake to work for the Italian team.

The former Red Bull team principal has repeatedly insisted that any Formula 1 comeback must provide sufficient authority and a meaningful stake in the project. However, Horner told The Times that Ferrari represented the sole exception.

“I’ve always just been an employee. I spent 21 years sitting on the pit wall and I don’t need to go back and do that,” Horner said.

“At this stage of my life, there is only one team for which I would accept not having equity. Ferrari is the most important brand in Formula 1. It is a dream. And you could say it is F1’s sleeping giant.”

Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera interpreted the remarks as an open message to Ferrari’s senior management, although there is currently no evidence of negotiations between the parties.

Horner has been linked with several Formula 1 projects since leaving Red Bull in July 2025 after 20 years in charge.

His previous position was that he would only return if given the power to transform a team and compete for championships. Horner was also associated with a consortium interested in purchasing Otro Capital’s 24% stake in Alpine.

Aston Martin and potential future Formula 1 projects have also appeared in speculation surrounding the British executive. Ferrari, however, would apparently persuade him to accept a conventional senior management position without ownership.

During Horner’s tenure, Red Bull won eight drivers’ championships and six constructors’ titles , establishing the Briton as one of the most successful team principals in Formula 1 history.

He also revived his long-running rivalry with Mercedes boss Toto Wolff.

“I feel like I’ve got one more dance in me,” Horner said. “And Toto needs somebody to ruffle his fucking hair.”

Ferrari has given no indication that Horner is being considered as an immediate replacement for Frédéric Vasseur.

The Frenchman signed a new multi-year contract in July 2025 and continues to oversee Ferrari’s technical restructuring. The team has recently reorganised its power-unit department and is recruiting additional engineers for the engine, chassis and aerodynamic groups.

Vasseur nevertheless remains under pressure because Ferrari has failed to mount a sustained championship challenge under the 2026 regulations. Both Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc have also publicly discussed the team’s inconsistent performances.

Hamilton has strongly supported Vasseur and recently denied reports that he had asked Ferrari to replace members of its staff .

Horner’s declaration therefore creates an obvious alternative should Ferrari eventually reconsider its leadership, but it does not confirm an approach, negotiation or vacancy at Maranello .

GRANDE PRÊMIO follows every session of the Azerbaijan GP LIVE and in REAL TIME .

The race starts on Saturday, September 26, at 12:00 UK time . It begins at 07:00 ET and 04:00 PT in the US, 16:30 in India and 21:00 AEST in eastern Australia.

George Russell starts from pole for Mercedes, ahead of Charles Leclerc and Oscar Piastri. Isack Hadjar qualified fourth, followed by Lando Norris and Lewis Hamilton.

The race was moved to Saturday because Sunday, September 27, is Azerbaijan’s Remembrance Day, a national day of mourning. The entire F1 weekend was brought forward by one day.

Horner described Ferrari as his “dream job” and the only team he would join without demanding an ownership stake.

evidence.title: Christian Horner reveals Ferrari is the ‘one team’ he would make an exception for
evidence.text:
Christian Horner has revealed Ferrari is the “one team” he would make a career exception for, coinciding with whispers of a potential leadership change at the Scuderia gathering steam in the paddock.

Horner was let go from Red Bull last year after a highly successful 20-year career, following a turbulent period of internal power struggles within the squad and a desire from the parent company to take over marketing control.

Christian Horner opens door to Ferrari role amid Fred Vasseur speculation

Since leaving the paddock, Horner has been linked with numerous teams in relation to a quick return.

This included speculation that the 52-year-old could join either Alpine or Aston Martin – the latter seeing him partner with Adrian Newey once more.

In the case of Alpine, Horner is part of a consortium looking to purchase Otro Capital’s 24 per cent stake in the team.

There have also been discussions surrounding a potential 12 th team on the F1 grid, with Chinese electric car manufacturer BYD.

Speaking to The Times , Horner re-iterated his position that any return to the paddock will come with a key criterion: some form of stake in the game by way of a shareholding or ownership position, rather than being a employee in the way he was at Red Bull.

“I’ve been a hired hand. I did 21 years sitting on the pit wall. I don’t need to go back to that,” he said.

However, providing an immediate caveat to this, he added that there is just one squad on the grid for whom he would reconsider his stance of needing to have an ownership position: “At this stage in my life, there’s only one team for which I would accept non-participation in ownership.

“Would I consider Ferrari? I mean, Ferrari is the biggest brand in Formula 1. It’s the dream. And arguably, it’s the sleeping giant of Formula 1.”

Horner’s opening the door to a Ferrari conversation comes at a time when speculation about Fred Vasseur’s future with the team has bubbled up in the F1 paddock, whispers that refuse to fade away in the wake of a turbulent period for the squad.

Multiple sources have indicated to PlanetF1.com that the stage is set for a succession plan to be enacted at Ferrari after this season, in a move that will allow the 58-year-old to return to a lower-profile life and focus on personal priorities.

The suggestion is that of an ‘honourable discharge’ type-scenario being tabled for Vasseur to accept, with the team’s performance and dynamic said to only be a factor in the thinking behind the idea.

If this scenario does come to pass, the succession plan is not yet clear: speculation continues to link Antonello Coletta from Ferrari’s WEC programme, while there is also the potential for deputy team principal Jerome d’Ambrosio to step up into the role.

However, Horner’s indication of interest could yet prove to be highly tempting for Ferrari chairman John Elkann should the decision be taken to part ways with Vasseur, given the British executive’s exceptional track record of success and ability to handle politically charged environs.

Lewis Hamilton blames F1 power unit rules after Liam Lawson near-miss

FIA confirms Lewis Hamilton punishment after ‘dangerous’ Liam Lawson incident

Toto Wolff ‘needs his hair f***ing ruffled up’

While links drawn between Horner and Ferrari are likely to catch the eye, the Red Bull boss of 20 years cooled anticipation of an imminent return, even if the continued noise around him suggests, “Perhaps I wasn’t that unpopular.

“There comes a point in time where a team’s competitiveness outweighs other egotistical stuff,” he said.

“I’m in a very fortunate position that I can afford to be picky. If I don’t do anything, I can live here for whatever time I’ve got left on the planet, and just worry about whether it’s going to rain and make the grass green or not.

“But is that going to fulfil me? No. I still feel that there’s another dance. And Toto needs to have his hair f***ing ruffled up.”

evidence.title: ‘Alarm bells’ ring at Ferrari after hearing what Oliver Bearman said about Baku engine failure
evidence.text:
‘Alarm bells’ ring at Ferrari after hearing what Oliver Bearman said about Baku engine failure

Ferrari are concerned for Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc after hearing what Haas’ Oliver Bearman said about his engine failure during FP2 at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

The second practice session in Baku on Thursday offered a sombre outlook for Ferrari, after Leclerc and Hamilton lapped far from the pace that Mercedes star George Russell set on the streets. And seeing Haas ace Bearman park his VF-26 due to a Ferrari PU failure drew alarm.

Leclerc marginally edged Hamilton to be the quickest Ferrari driver as Russell set the pace in FP2 in Baku . Russell set the benchmark with a 1:43.347 after relishing a slipstream down the main straight, which helped him to pip Leclerc in P4 by 1.126s and Hamilton in P5 by 1.318s.

Ferrari are ‘concerned’ after Oliver Bearman’s sudden engine failure during FP2 in Baku

Bearman would only rank P20 in the FP2 timesheets at the Azerbaijan GP , having missed out on the qualifying simulations after his session came to an abrupt end. The Briton suffered an immediate failure with his Ferrari engine straight after he returned to the track following a red flag stoppage for the marshals to recover Arvid Lindblad’s crashed Racing Bulls at Turn 8.

READ MORE: How to watch the 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix and why the race is on Saturday

Haas star Bearman immediately radioed his team to note that “my engine just switched off” after parking up early in FP2. And his comments are reported to have set off ‘alarm bells’ at Ferrari , as they fear not only for Bearman but for Hamilton and Leclerc at the Azerbaijan GP.

That is according to Formula1.it, which reports that Ferrari suspect a ‘serious’ issue brought Bearman’s FP2 at the Azerbaijan GP to an end after only half an hour. There is now ‘concern’ in Maranello that the issue could recur in Baku, and potentially even at the upcoming races.

Ferrari and Haas do not yet know whether Bearman will need to take a grid penalty in Baku for a new engine. But Ferrari are investigating the issue with a degree of concern for Leclerc and Hamilton, as Bearman’s PU failure may suggest Baku’s very long straights have revealed a reliability concern with the upgraded engine that the Maranello natives recently debuted.

Bearman received Ferrari’s ADUO2 engine upgrade from its debut at the Italian Grand Prix, whereas Haas teammate Esteban Ocon has continued to use the Scuderia’s previous power unit. Ferrari had only offered Haas one of their ADUO2 power units for its debut at Monza.

The ADUO2 power unit did not meet expectations, however, as Ferrari only gained 5hp with their engine upgrade at Monza , rather than 15hp that were initially predicted. Their limited gains further meant Hamilton suggested that he lost 0.6s on Monza’s straights to Mercedes .

Practice in Baku initially suggested that Ferrari could build some optimism for their engine’s progress, though. Jolyon Palmer was encouraged by Ferrari’s straight-line speed during FP1 in Baku on Thursday, but any optimism was soon destroyed by Bearman’s reliability failure.

CNH Industrial Thailand and Farm Chokchai Unveil Field-To-Feed Precision Farming Showcase for Thailand's Corn and Livestock Sectors at New Holland Day 2026

NORTHAMPTON, MA / ACCESS Newswire / September 24, 2026 / CNH Thailand and Farm Chokchai, hosted New Holland Day 2026, with live field demonstrations for some of the most advanced field-to-feed precision farming products in the market.

New Holland Day brought together farmers, agricultural entrepreneurs, and industry experts from across Northeast Thailand to showcase a connected, full-cycle farming system that included soil preparation, planting, harvesting, to stubble management and livestock feed production.

Tailored to the region's corn and livestock sectors, the event underscored how precision technology and mechanization can improve productivity, forage production, farm profitability, and prioritise sustainability.

"Thai farmers need solutions that are reliable in the field and can create value across the entire production cycle," said Mark Brinn, Managing Director - Southeast Asia and Japan at CNH. "New Holland combines dependable machinery and practical precision technology. evidence.title: CNH Industrial stock holds near analyst value after debt pricing
evidence.text:
CNH Industrial N.V. (NL0010545661) stock was covered at a USD 9.00 price target on September 22, 2026, when Bernstein maintained its Hold rating. The published consensus target was USD 13.44, creating a USD 4.44 gap between the named target and the broader average.

According to The Globe and Mail on September 22, 2026, Chad Dillard of Bernstein reaffirmed a Hold rating and a USD 9.00 price target for CNH Industrial. The same report placed the average analyst target at USD 13.44 and described the consensus view as Moderate Buy, a difference of USD 4.44 from Bernstein's target.

The spread matters because it separates a conservative published target from the wider consensus rather than presenting one uniform market view. For investors, the central issue is therefore the distance between the USD 9.00 downside reference and the USD 13.44 average target.

CNH Industrial Capital Canada priced a two-part private debt offering totaling C$550 million on September 22, 2026, according to Seeking Alpha . The transaction gives the financing arm a specific C$550 million capital-market reference, while also placing funding conditions alongside the equity valuation discussion.

The debt transaction and the analyst split describe two different parts of the company: financing capacity on one side and expectations for the industrial equipment business on the other. The available figures point to a market debate centered on valuation and funding rather than a single operating metric.

CNH Industrial stock keeps the gap visible

CNH Industrial stock therefore enters September 23, 2026, with three clear reference points: Bernstein's USD 9.00 target, the USD 13.44 consensus target, and the C$550 million debt offering. The USD 4.44 target gap is the most concrete measure of disagreement in the current coverage.

The share price remains tied to the issuer's primary US listing, while the analyst figures use USD and the financing announcement uses Canadian dollars. These currencies are not interchangeable, so the targets and debt amount should be read as separate dated reference values.

Pricing of CNH Industrial Capital Canada Ltd. Cdn$200 million notes due 2028 and Cdn$350 million notes due 2030

Basildon, UK — 21 September 2026 — CNH Industrial N.V. (NYSE: CNH) today announced that its indirect wholly owned subsidiary, CNH Industrial Capital Canada Ltd., has priced (i) Cdn$200 million in aggregate principal amount of 4.00% notes due September 25, 2028, with an issue price of 99.935% (the "2028 Notes") and (ii) Cdn$350 million in aggregate principal amount of 4.40% notes due September 25, 2030, with an issue price of 99.989% (the "2030 Notes", and together with the 2028 Notes, the "Notes"). The Notes are being offered on a private placement basis to certain accredited investors in each of the provinces of Canada, which offering is expected to close on September 25, 2026, subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions.

CNH Industrial Capital Canada Ltd. intends to add the net proceeds from the offering to its general funds and use them for working capital and other general corporate purposes, including, among other things, the purchase of receivables or other assets in the ordinary course of business, as well as the repayment of indebtedness as it becomes due.

The Notes, which are senior unsecured obligations of CNH Industrial Capital Canada Ltd., will in each case pay interest semi-annually on March 25 and September 25 of each year, beginning on March 25, 2027, and will in each case be guaranteed by CNH Industrial Capital LLC, CNH Industrial Capital America LLC and New Holland Credit Company, LLC, each an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of CNH Industrial N.V.

The securities offered in the private placement have not been and will not be qualified for sale to the public under applicable securities laws in Canada and, accordingly, any offer and sale of the securities in Canada will be made on a basis which is exempt from the prospectus requirements of such securities laws.

CNH Industrial Capital LLC is an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of CNH Industrial N.V. and is headquartered in Waterford, Wisconsin. Emissions software update shapes the latest story

The current discussion around CNH Industrial centers on an emissions-related software update program that the group plans to roll out from the fourth quarter of 2026, giving equipment owners more control over the timing of critical engine repairs, according to Simply Wall St on September 20, 2026.

For investors, the emissions software update is not only a technical change but also a potential cost and uptime factor for CNH Industrial's customer base, which could influence future service revenue and margins as the program is implemented from the fourth quarter of 2026 onward, as highlighted by Simply Wall St .

At the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange on September 20, 2026, CNH Industrial stock stood at USD 13.45, with the NYSE listing serving as the primary reference for the shares; this closing level, combined with the recent double-digit percentage gains over the last 30 and 90 days, frames the stock as having already priced in a substantial portion of the emissions software update narrative while still trading a few percent below the USD 13.82 valuation anchor mentioned in recent coverage.

evidence.title: Iveco Group Reorganizes Leadership as Chief Sustainability Officer Departs
evidence.text:
Iveco Group Reorganizes Leadership as Chief Sustainability Officer Departs

The announcement marks a significant shift in the commercial vehicle manufacturer’s leadership structure during a period of major industry transformation.

Ziosi has held a central role in advancing the Turin-based company’s institutional relations and sustainability agenda. His departure triggers an internal reorganization of Global Affairs and Sustainability activities designed to maintain continuity while strengthening alignment with business priorities during Iveco Group ‘s transformational phase.

Olof Persson, Iveco Group’s CEO, acknowledged Ziosi’s contributions in a statement. “He has consistently advanced the interests and positions of our Group in a complex and ever-evolving environment, always guided by a broader vision focused on creating value for our society as a whole, supporting causes that matter to our communities and promoting sustainability and responsible business practices,” Persson said.

Ziosi will remain in his current position until his departure date to ensure a smooth handoff of responsibilities. This approach allows ongoing initiatives to maintain momentum while the company designs new reporting structures for sustainability and external affairs.

Iveco Group employs 33,000 people across 16 industrial sites and 22 research and development centers globally. The company operates five primary brands: IVECO commercial vehicles, FPT powertrain technologies, IVECO BUS and HEULIEZ mass transit solutions, and IVECO CAPITAL financing services.

Organizational Restructuring and Strategic Priorities

The reorganization following Ziosi’s exit reflects broader priorities within Iveco Group as the transportation industry undergoes significant change. Rather than appointing a single successor to the Chief Global Affairs and Sustainability Officer role, the company is distributing responsibilities internally to better align with immediate business needs.

This structural adjustment signals that sustainability and institutional relations will be integrated more directly into business unit operations rather than managed as a separate executive function. The move suggests that Iveco Group views these capabilities as essential to competitive positioning during the industry’s shift toward electrification and environmental compliance.

Ziosi’s departure comes as automotive manufacturers face intensifying pressure to demonstrate measurable progress on emissions reduction and supply chain sustainability. His tenure coincided with a period when climate strategy has become inseparable from business survival in industrial sectors.

The commercial vehicle sector is navigating accelerate d regulatory timelines, decarbonization mandates, and stakeholder demands for transparent sustainability reporting. Leadership changes at major OEMs often precede or accompany strategic shifts in how companies approach these challenges.

Iveco Group has not disclosed specific succession details or interim arrangements beyond stating that Global Affairs and Sustainability activities will be reorganized internally. The company indicated that further announcements regarding structural changes may follow, though no timeline was specified.

Ziosi’s move to pursue a new professional opportunity outside Iveco Group opens questions about where his expertise in institutional relations and sustainability will be applied next. Executives with deep experience in automotive industry navigation and climate strategy remain in demand across the sector and in related industries.

The reorganization will be complete by Ziosi’s departure date, allowing Iveco Group to enter the final quarter of 2026 with its Global Affairs and Sustainability functions fully integrated into business operations. The company’s ability to execute this transition while maintaining stakeholder engagement and regulatory compliance will test whether distributing these responsibilities enhances or complicates strategic execution.

Iveco Group’s approach, embedding sustainability and institutional relations throughout the organization rather than concentrating them in a single officer role, reflects a broader shift in how mature industrial companies are structuring climate and stakeholder engagement functions. Whether this model strengthens or weakens the company’s competitive position will depend on execution during a period when regulatory, market, and investor scrutiny of automotive industry sustainability commitments continues to intensify.

Ziosi is departing on September 30, 2026, to pursue a new professional opportunity outside the company.

Iveco Group will reorganize Global Affairs and Sustainability activities internally, distributing responsibilities to strengthen alignment with business priorities.

Iveco Group has not announced a specific successor; responsibilities will be reorganized internally across the organization.

Iveco Group employs 33,000 people across 16 industrial sites and 22 research and development centers globally.

evidence.title: Iveco Group announces Senior Leadership Team changes
evidence.text:
Iveco Group announces Senior Leadership Team changes

Iveco Group announces Senior Leadership Team changes

Turin, 10 th September 2026 . Iveco Group N.V. (EXM: IVG) announces that Michele Ziosi, Chief Global Affairs & Sustainability Officer and member of the Senior Leadership Team, will leave the Company on 30th September to pursue a new professional opportunity.

Mr Ziosi has played a key role in strengthening the Group's institutional relations and sustainability agenda during a period of profound transformation for both the Company and the broader transport industry. He will remain in his current role until his departure date, ensuring continuity and a smooth transition of responsibilities.

Following his departure, the Global Affairs and Sustainability activities will be reorganised internally to ensure full continuity of ongoing initiatives, while further strengthening alignment with business priorities and the specific needs of the Group during this transformational phase.

Olof Persson, CEO, Iveco Group, commented: "I would like to thank Michele for his commitment, professionalism and valuable contribution to Iveco Group over the years. He has consistently advanced the interests and positions of our Group in a complex and ever-evolving environment, always guided by a broader vision focused on creating value for our society as a whole, supporting causes that matter to our communities and promoting sustainability and responsible business practices. On behalf of the Senior Leadership Team, I wish him every success in his future endeavours."

Iveco Group N.V. (EXM: IVG) is a global player in the automotive industry, built on a strong Italian heritage and with a consolidated international reach. The Group channels decades of engineering excellence and innovation into sustainable mobility and customer driven technologies. Its five brands play a leading role in their respective domains: IVECO, a pioneering commercial vehicles brand offering heavy, medium and light duty trucks; FPT, a global leader in advanced powertrain technologies in the agriculture, construction, marine, power generation and commercial vehicles sectors; IVECO BUS and HEULIEZ, renowned for their mass transit, premium bus and coach solutions; and IVECO CAPITAL, the Group's financing arm supporting them all. Iveco Group employs 33,000 people and operates 16 industrial sites and 22 R&D centres. Further information is available at www.ivecogroup.com

Iveco Group wraps up another year of social responsibility engagement

Turin, 22 December 2025 . From Italy to Brazil, Iveco Group concludes another year of social impact initiatives around the world: in Italy, Fondazione Telethon – whose research on ultrarare genetic diseases Iveco Group has been supporting for many years – is hosting a charity marathon on the national TV networks from 14 th to 21 st December; in Brazil, the 2025 edition of the Solidarity Cargo project just took place, providing care and essential services to communities in need for the 10 th consecutive year.

Throughout 2025, Iveco Group worked closely with these and other local non-governmental organisations in countries where it operates to deliver tangible, measurable and lasting impact. The Group’s social responsibility efforts focus mainly on three areas: fostering health and wellbeing; reducing inequality and protecting diversity and vulnerable groups; and preserving biodiversity.

Fondazione Telethon NOF1 Project, global Ultrarare genetic diseases pose a significant challenge for diagnosis and treatment and recent advances in genomic analysis have opened new pathways to diagnose many of these disorders. Iveco Group supported the Fondazione Telethon NOF1 Project which leverages these advances by identifying treatable mutations in patients with ultrarare genetic diseases.

Gambella Town Primary Hospital in partnership with Medici con l’Africa Cuamm, Ethiopia Iveco Group supported the purchase of supplies to the Gambella Town Primary Hospital in Ethiopia to ensure the continued operation of the hospital’s paediatric ward and services for hospitalised women and children, particularly those suffering from severe malnutrition.

Reducing inequality and protecting diversity and vulnerable groups

Carga Solidaria, Brazil The 2025 edition of the IVECO Solidarity Cargo took place in Tabuleiro do Norte to improve healthcare access and help prevent road accidents. IVECO set up an ophthalmology clinic, offering the local community free screenings, consultations and diagnostic exams.

PizzAutobus, Italy Iveco Group donated to PizzAut an IVECO Daily food truck for the PizzAutobus project, the first step toward creating a fleet of over 100 food trucks that will help to generate approximately 500 permanent jobs for autistic people.

PRO-Jeunes in partnership with Eni and IRC, Ivory Coast In collaboration with energy company Eni and the International Rescue Committee, Iveco Group expanded economic opportunities for young people in the Ivory Coast through the PRO-Jeunes project. The project helps participants transition into full and productive employment by providing training in automotive mechanics, domestic electricity and solar energy.

Fishing for Litter campaign in partnership with Ogyre, global Fishing for Litter offers economic support to local fishers to recover waste found in the sea. The initiative combats overfishing and habitat degradation while creating new opportunities for local fishing communities by enhancing their entrepreneurial skills.
