evidence.title: Sandvik outlines technology priorities shaping mining’s future
evidence.text:
Sandvik outlines technology priorities shaping mining’s future

Sandvik Australia's Craig Johnston has outlined the topics likely to define IMARC. Image: IMARC

Australia is one of the most competitive mining markets in the world, according to Sandvik Australia, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea sales area vice president Craig Johnston, who believes the company’s proven equipment, aftermarket capabilities and growing portfolio of digital and automation solutions have it well positioned for the future.

It is a future he expects to bring significant change for both miners and their suppliers, as technology, mineral and metal markets, and the industry’s technical, cost and sustainability challenges continue to evolve rapidly.

“Our ambition is to position ourselves not only as an equipment supplier but as a long-term technology partner, helping customers unlock value through data, connectivity and advanced solutions,” Johnston said.

Johnston provides his thoughts below on the conversations likely to define this year’s major IMARC event, held at ICC Sydney from October 27-29.

What does Sandvik do and what role does it play in the mining industry?

Sandvik is a mining equipment and technology partner that supports customers across the entire mining value chain. We manufacture equipment for drilling, loading and hauling, rock tools, ground support, aftermarket services, automation, digital technologies and electrification solutions that enable mines to operate more safely, productively and sustainably.

In Australia our role is particularly significant because this is one of the world’s most advanced mining markets. Australian miners have consistently been early adopters of new technologies and as a result the industry here has become an important proving ground for innovations that are later adopted around the world.

As mining continues to evolve, our role is to turn innovation into practical outcomes, helping customers implement technologies that deliver real operational benefits.

What are you seeing as some of the biggest challenges facing the mining sector right now?

There are several challenges converging at once. Cost pressures, geo-political uncertainty, workforce constraints and supply chain challenges remain significant issues across the industry.

At the same time, many operations are mining deeper, lower-grade and more complex deposits, which can increase both technical and economic challenges.

Overlaying all of this is the growing expectation that the mining industry must improve safety performance, reduce environmental impact and contribute to the energy transition.

The challenge for the industry is not choosing between growth, sustainability and profitability. It’s delivering all three at the same time.

What technologies, innovations or approaches do you think will have the biggest impact on mining over the next few years?

I believe the biggest impact will come from the convergence of several technologies rather than any one technology operating in isolation.

Automation, digitalisation, AI and electrification are all important but their real value will come when they work together as part of an integrated mining system.

Moving from automating individual processes towards connected operations where equipment, data and decision-making are increasingly aligned in real time.

Ultimately the technologies that succeed will be those that improve safety, productivity and operational performance.

As mining companies look to improve productivity and safety, what role do you see automation, digitalisation and new equipment technologies playing?

These technologies will be fundamental to the future of mining because they have the potential to truly improve both safety and operational performance. Automation can remove people from some of the highest risk areas of a mine, while digital technologies provide the data and visibility needed to make better and faster decisions.

We’re already seeing a shift towards remote and increasingly autonomous operations, where people supervise and manage equipment from safer environments rather than being exposed to operational hazards. Importantly, this isn’t about replacing people. It’s about enabling people to work differently, focusing more on optimisation, planning and decision-making, while technology handles repetitive or hazardous tasks.

The ultimate goal being not to remove people from mining; it is to remove people from harm.

How important is collaboration between mining companies, METS businesses and other parts of the ecosystem in tackling the challenges facing the sector?

Collaboration is critical. No single mining company, OEM, technology provider or service business can solve the industry’s challenges on its own. The best outcomes are achieved when mining companies, METS businesses and technology partners work together to combine operational experience with technical expertise.

Events such as IMARC play an important role because they bring those groups together and create opportunities for conversations that may not otherwise occur.

For Sandvik, IMARC isn’t just about showcasing technology. It’s about listening to customers, understanding emerging priorities and identifying opportunities to collaborate on solutions that deliver real value.

evidence.title: Almonty to supply Sandvik tungsten from Spanish mine tailings
evidence.text:
Almonty to supply Sandvik tungsten from Spanish mine tailings

Almonty Industries (NASDAQ: ALM) has agreed to supply Sandvik (STO: SAND) with tungsten recovered from a shuttered Spanish mine’s tailings as Western users seek alternatives to Chinese supply.

The tungsten will come from waste left at Almonty’s Los Santos mine in Spain and be supplied to the Swedish mining equipment maker’s Wolfram Bergbau und Hütten AG unit under a long-term agreement, the company said Thursday. The deal is structured on a take-or-pay basis.

“The agreement is intended to create an expedited tungsten supply solution with the ability to deliver concentrate in notably less time than the development of a traditional mine,” Almonty said.

The deal gives Sandvik another European source of tungsten as the EU and the United States seek to reduce reliance on China, which accounts for about 80% of global production. Beijing tightened export controls in 2025, adding urgency to efforts to secure the extremely hard, heat-resistant metal used in applications ranging from weapons to semiconductors.

At Los Santos, Almonty plans to use specially developed technology to process existing tailings rather than resume conventional mining. The waste contains much lower grades of tungsten than newly mined ore, but surging prices and demand for Western supply have made reprocessing more attractive.

Spain holds Western Europe’s largest tungsten reserves, although efforts to bring new mines into production have been slowed by permitting hurdles.

Almonty has encountered those challenges at its Valtreixal project in Spain. It has held the mining licence since 2013 but is still awaiting permits to begin operations. A regional government issued a non-binding negative environmental assessment for the project in July.

The company’s flagship asset is the Sangdong mine in South Korea , which recently returned to production after being shuttered for more than three decades. Almonty also produces tungsten at its Panasqueira mine in Portugal.

Europe has stepped up efforts to secure critical minerals as geopolitical tensions expose its dependence on concentrated overseas supply chains.

The European Union adopted the Critical Raw Materials Act in 2024 to encourage more extraction, processing and recycling within the bloc.

The European Commission included tungsten in its critical-minerals joint-purchasing plans in April, alongside rare earths, gallium, magnesium, germanium and graphite.

The Los Santos plan is being driven by tungsten’s price surge since China imposed its export controls and by demand from European consumers such as Sandvik for alternative suppliers.

evidence.title: Sandvik graduates to advanced cybersecurity certification
evidence.text:
Sandvik graduates to advanced cybersecurity certification

Sandvik (STO: SAND) has achieved IEC 62443-4-1 Maturity Level 3 (ML3) certification, a listing that validates that cybersecurity practices are systematically embedded in its technology.

The company previously held a Maturity Level 2 (ML2), achieved in 2025. While ML2 demonstrated Sandvik’s secure development processes, ML3 shows these processes are systematically applied across platforms. The company says it is one of the first mining equipment manufacturers to achieve this rating.

“Cybersecurity is increasingly inseparable from automation and digitalization in mining,” said Riku Pulli, Sandvik’s president of digital mining technologies. “As customers entrust more production-critical processes to connected and autonomous technologies, they need confidence that security is built in from the beginning and maintained throughout the product lifecycle.”

Modern mines rely increasingly on connected equipment and networks. Sandvik says the ML3 should give customers greater confidence that cybersecurity remains a top priority even as new autonomous and digital solutions are implemented.

Jere Paavola, Sandvik’s product development manager for control systems, said the assessment was supported by Sandvik Intelligent Control Architecture (SICA), the company's common control system platform used across its i-series mining equipment. “Moving from ML2 to ML3 is about more than having the right cybersecurity processes documented,” Paavola said. “It independently demonstrates that we are practicing them systematically in our everyday product development.”

evidence.title: Atlas Copco to Showcase Advanced Compressed Air Solutions at SEMICON India 2026
evidence.text:
Atlas Copco to Showcase Advanced Compressed Air Solutions at SEMICON India 2026

Atlas Copco , a global leader in innovative solutions for compressed air, will showcase its advanced compressed-air solutions for semiconductor manufacturing at SEMICON India 2026. The showcase will highlight the critical role of clean, dry, oil-free and reliable compressed air in supporting India’s growing semiconductor ecosystem.

India’s semiconductor industry is entering a manufacturing-led growth phase, with increasing investments across fabs, packaging, testing, design and the supporting supply chain. As industry expands, reliable utility infrastructure is becoming increasingly important for sensitive automation, instrumentation and production operations. Any contamination, moisture, pressure instability or interruption can affect process stability and production continuity.

At SEMICON India 2026, Atlas Copco will showcase an integrated solution comprising ZH oil-free centrifugal compression, MDG heat-of-compression drying, advanced fine filtration and Optimizer 4.0 intelligent control. These technologies support applications including purging, tool cooling and drying, instrumentation and automation, helping deliver clean, dry, oil-free and reliable compressed air from the utility room to the point of use.

Speaking on the participation, Bhavin Pandya, General Manager, Compressor Technique Customer Center, Atlas Copco India, said, “As India’s semiconductor ecosystem continues to expand, reliable and efficient manufacturing infrastructure is becoming increasingly critical. Compressed air plays a vital role in semiconductor manufacturing, where purity, consistency and uninterrupted performance are essential. At Atlas Copco, we are leveraging our global engineering expertise to help manufacturers build future-ready operations through oil-free compression, advanced air treatment and intelligent solutions. SEMICON India 2026 provides an excellent platform to engage with the industry and demonstrate how we can support reliable, competitive and sustainable semiconductor manufacturing.”

With more than 150 years of heritage and over six decades of operations in India, Atlas Copco combines global semiconductor expertise with local engineering and service capabilities to support the country’s next generation of fabs, packaging facilities and electronics plants.

Visitors can explore Atlas Copco’s semiconductor solutions and interact with its compressed-air experts at Hall 1, Booth 1637 during SEMICON India 2026, taking place at Yashobhoomi (IICC), New Delhi, from September 17-19, 2026.

evidence.text:
Gallagher Security & ASSA ABLOY IP lock integration

Gallagher Security has unveiled its latest collaboration with ASSA ABLOY, integrating new IP lock technology to simplify the installation process for access control systems in demanding environments.

The launch, announced today, addresses the high costs and complexity often associated with traditional wired access control by eliminating the need for extensive cabling and door controllers, making it especially beneficial in retrofit or hard-to-wire scenarios.

This new integration is tailor-made for US higher education facilities, including student accommodation, classrooms, and research areas, where mixed online and offline functionality, adaptability, and ease of deployment are crucial. Furthermore, it serves government buildings, enterprise campuses, as well as institutional and healthcare settings requiring dependable security across dispersed locations.

Matt Butts, Gallagher Security's Executive Vice President – Americas, noted, " This integration reflects a shared vision between Gallagher and ASSA ABLOY to make security more accessible, flexible, and effective for our customers. By combining best-in-class door security with enterprise-grade access control, we're delivering a solution that reduces friction and empowers facilities with greater insight, faster response times and the confidence of connected technologies working together ."

The system supports ASSA ABLOY's IN120 battery-powered Wi-Fi locks and IN220 PoE IP locks

The system supports ASSA ABLOY's IN120 battery-powered Wi-Fi locks and IN220 PoE IP locks, which seamlessly connect to an organisation's on-premises IP network.

It allows centralised management of access privileges, credentials, schedules, and overrides via Gallagher's Command Centre, enhancing operational efficiency while preserving oversight across various sites. Each lock's local intelligence enables autonomous access decisions, ensuring operations continue during network disruptions—an advantage for places like dormitories, laboratories, secure offices, and isolated buildings.

Security and IT personnel can gain comprehensive visibility into events, alarms, battery conditions, audits, and device health through the Command Centre, enabling more proactive management and swifter responses to issues. The Gallagher Security and ASSA ABLOY IP Lock integration is currently available in the United States, with more information obtainable through local Gallagher Security representatives.

Angelo Faenza, Head of Digital Access Solutions at ASSA ABLOY, remarked, " Our collaboration with Gallagher brings together two leaders in access control to solve a real world challenge for our customers. By integrating our IP enabled locks with Gallagher’s Command Centre platform, we’re delivering a streamlined, modern approach to securing doors across complex facilities. It’s a powerful example of how open, interoperable solutions can elevate both security and operational efficiency ."

ASSA ABLOY has acquired Pacific Lock Company, a U.S. manufacturer of padlocks and security hardware.

The contract covers key components for one of Europe's largest planned bioenergy carbon capture facilities, focused on reducing global emissions.

The Stockholm Exergi BECCS project is designed to capture and store carbon dioxide from bioenergy production at industrial scale.

In Q2 2026, Alfa Laval's order intake rose 35 percent and its order book reached SEK 53.5 billion, according to Factorstoday . The comparison matters because adjusted EBITA increased only 2.3 percent in the same quarter, while the adjusted EBITA margin declined from 17.8 percent to 17.0 percent.

The Q2 figures show a clear conversion question for investors. Energy generated SEK 6.18 billion of sales and a 16.1 percent adjusted EBITA margin, while Ocean produced SEK 5.85 billion of sales and a 24.9 percent margin, according to Factorstoday .

On September 14, 2026, Alfa Laval was selected by Saipem to supply heat transfer technology for Stockholm Exergi's bioenergy carbon capture project, according to MarketScreener . The project is designed to capture, liquefy and store up to 800,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide annually, linking Alfa Laval's heat transfer equipment to a large industrial decarbonization investment.

That order theme supports the backlog, but the margin comparison remains important. Higher volume has not yet translated into comparable profit growth, making execution and business mix central to the stock narrative.

JPMorgan cut its Alfa Laval price target from SEK 585 to SEK 578 and retained a Neutral rating on September 18, 2026, as reported by MarketScreener . The SEK 578 target is SEK 14 above the September 24 price, while the current quote remains SEK 28.20 below the yearly high.

evidence.title: Alfa Laval stock holds its gains as JP Morgan trims price target
evidence.text:
Alfa Laval stock (ISIN SE0000695876) closed at SEK 556.00 on Nasdaq Stockholm on September 17, 2026, reflecting a 1.53% gain versus the prior trading day and keeping the shares within their established 52-week trading range as of that date.

JP Morgan trims price target but keeps neutral stance

According to Placera on September 18, 2026, JP Morgan lowered its price target for Alfa Laval from SEK 585.00 to SEK 578.00 while reiterating a neutral rating on the stock.

The adjustment implies that JP Morgan now sees roughly SEK 22.00 upside from the September 17, 2026 close of SEK 556.00, compared with around SEK 29.00 upside under its previous SEK 585.00 target, signaling a slightly more cautious view on near term appreciation potential.

As relayed by MarketScreener on September 18, 2026, Alfa Laval shares recorded a last closing price of SEK 556.00 on Nasdaq Stockholm, with the stock up 1.53% over the latest trading day and 19.39% since the start of 2026.

The same overview from MarketScreener indicates an average analyst price target for Alfa Laval of SEK 588.88, which sits about SEK 32.88 above the recent closing price of SEK 556.00, suggesting that the wider analyst community remains moderately constructive on the shares despite JP Morgan’s more tempered stance.

Per EFN on September 17, 2026, Alfa Laval was among the stronger names on the Swedish large cap list, with the shares rising between 1.3% and 1.5% alongside peers such as Epiroc and Saab as the broader Stockholm market advanced despite a cautious signal from the Federal Reserve.

In practical terms, the 1.53% daily gain to SEK 556.00 on September 17, 2026, compared with a previous close near SEK 547.60, underlines that investors largely took the sector move and the company’s recent order and earnings momentum as supportive, even as individual analyst targets like JP Morgan’s SEK 578.00 are nudged lower.

Alfa Laval stock finished the last completed session on Nasdaq Stockholm at SEK 556.00 on September 17, 2026, and, with the new JP Morgan price target at SEK 578.00 versus an average target of SEK 588.88, investors are weighing solid year to date performance of 19.39% against a slightly reduced upside implied by parts of the analyst community.

evidence.title: Alfa Laval Selected by Saipem to Supply Heat Transfer Technology for Stockholm Exergi’s 800,000-Tonne BECCS Carbon Capture Project in Sweden
evidence.text:
Alfa Laval Selected by Saipem to Supply Heat Transfer Technology for Stockholm Exergi’s 800,000-Tonne BECCS Carbon Capture Project in Sweden

Alfa Laval Selected by Saipem to Supply Heat Transfer Technology for Stockholm Exergi’s 800,000-Tonne BECCS Carbon Capture Project in Sweden

(IN BRIEF) Alfa Laval has been selected by Saipem to provide heat transfer equipment for Stockholm Exergi’s BECCS project in Sweden, one of Europe’s largest planned bioenergy carbon capture facilities. Scheduled to begin operations in 2028, the project is designed to capture, liquefy and permanently store up to 800,000 tonnes of biogenic CO₂ annually, equivalent to around 1–2% of current global carbon capture capacity. Alfa Laval will supply its Ziepack gas-gas interchanger and several plate-and-frame heat exchangers as part of the core capture process. The equipment will help recover energy used during CO₂ separation and liquefaction, with recovered heat returned to Stockholm’s district heating system. The project is located at Stockholm Exergi’s biomass-based combined heat and power plant and supports Sweden’s climate-neutrality goals as well as wider EU climate objectives. Stockholm Exergi’s district heating network serves more than 800,000 people and around 400 locations. Saipem is delivering the project under an EPC contract covering the carbon capture facility.

(PRESS RELEASE) LUND, 15-Sep-2026 — / EuropaWire / — Alfa Laval has been selected by Saipem , the engineering, procurement and construction contractor for Stockholm Exergi’s Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS) project , to supply heat transfer equipment for what is expected to become one of Europe’s largest bioenergy carbon capture facilities.

The Stockholm project is scheduled to begin operations in 2028 and is designed to capture, liquefy and permanently store up to 800,000 tonnes of biogenic CO₂ annually. According to Alfa Laval, that volume represents approximately 1–2% of today’s total global carbon capture capacity.

The BECCS facility will be developed at Stockholm Exergi’s biomass-based combined heat and power plant in Stockholm, described as the largest of its kind in Europe. Once operational, the system will capture CO₂ generated from the combustion of biogenic fuels and prepare it for permanent storage.

Alfa Laval’s heat transfer technology will form part of the core capture process, helping maximise energy recovery and overall system efficiency.

The company will supply its Ziepack gas-gas interchanger together with several process plate-and-frame heat exchangers. The equipment has been selected by Saipem as part of its EPC contract for the Stockholm Exergi project.

Thomas Møller, President of the Energy Division at Alfa Laval , said large-scale carbon capture presents demanding thermal engineering requirements and that effective recovery of energy is essential to making such systems commercially viable.

He said Stockholm Exergi is demonstrating how industrial-scale negative emissions can be achieved and that Alfa Laval’s heat transfer technologies will support the project’s efficiency objectives.

Carbon capture and liquefaction require significant amounts of energy. Stockholm Exergi plans to recover much of that energy through the heat exchanger system and return it to the existing district heating network.

Egil Nybakk, Director BECCS at Stockholm Exergi , said the facility will consume substantial energy when separating CO₂ from flue gas and subsequently liquefying it. He said Alfa Laval’s Ziepack heat exchangers will allow that energy to be reclaimed and redirected into Stockholm’s district heating system, creating an additional contribution to the project’s carbon-removal objectives.

The project is designed around Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage, a carbon-removal approach that combines renewable energy generation from biomass with the capture and permanent storage of the resulting biogenic CO₂.

Unlike conventional carbon capture systems focused primarily on reducing fossil emissions, BECCS can create net-negative emissions because the carbon absorbed by biomass during growth is subsequently captured rather than returned to the atmosphere.

At BECCS Stockholm, captured CO₂ will be compressed and liquefied to enable efficient transportation and permanent storage in suitable underground or offshore geological formations.

The project forms part of Sweden’s broader climate-neutrality ambitions and supports European Union climate objectives. Stockholm Exergi aims to position the facility among the world’s largest installations dedicated to permanent removal of biogenic carbon dioxide.

Heat integration will play an important role in the project’s efficiency. Alfa Laval’s equipment will be used to recover thermal energy from parts of the capture and liquefaction process and make that energy available elsewhere in the system, including Stockholm’s district heating network.

Stockholm Exergi’s district heating system currently serves more than 800,000 people and approximately 400 locations in Stockholm, connecting customers with the company’s heating and cogeneration plants.

Saipem, meanwhile, is responsible for the project’s EPC activities and operates across the broader carbon capture value chain, including capture, transportation and storage infrastructure.

The contract adds another large-scale carbon capture application to Alfa Laval’s energy-transition portfolio. The company provides technologies in heat transfer, separation and fluid handling and works across industries including energy, food, water, pharmaceuticals, maritime transport and offshore operations.

Alfa Laval was founded more than 140 years ago and has customers in over 100 countries. The company employs more than 23,500 people and reported annual sales of SEK 69.6 billion, equivalent to approximately €6.6 billion, in 2025. Alfa Laval is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm.

By supplying heat recovery technology to the Stockholm Exergi BECCS facility, Alfa Laval will support one of Europe’s largest planned carbon-removal projects while helping reduce the energy intensity of the capture process and recover usable heat for Stockholm’s existing energy infrastructure.

This is Alfa Laval Working closely with customers and partners worldwide, Alfa Laval challenges conventional thinking on engineering, quality, and innovation. Together, driving the solutions of the future, inspiring progress towards a more resourceful, less wasteful world.

Alfa Laval is set on creating positive impact in areas that society depends on, including energy, food, water, medicine, maritime transport and offshore operations. As a leading global provider of solutions in heat transfer, separation, and fluid handling, the company collaborates closely with many industries to optimize efficiency, reduce emissions and increase yields.

Alfa Laval was founded more than 140 years ago, has customers in over 100 countries, employs more than 23,500 people, and annual sales were 69.6 BSEK (6.6 BEUR) in 2025. The company is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm.

About the Stockholm Exergi BECCS project

Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS) is a key climate technology that generates renewable energy from biomass while capturing and permanently storing the resulting CO2.

The Stockholm Exergi plant, BECCS Stockholm, is expected to capture and permanently store up to 800,000 tonnes of biogenic CO₂ annually, making it one of the world’s largest carbon removal facilities.The captured CO2 is then compressed and liquified, allowing for space-efficient underground or offshore storage.

Stockholm Exergi is a Swedish energy provider in Stockholm. Today, more than 800,000 people and around 400 locations in Stockholm are connected to the district heating network, which is in turn connected to Stockholm Exergi’s heating and cogeneration plants.

Saipem is a global leader in the engineering and construction of major projects for the energy and infrastructure sectors. The company is active across the entire CO₂ value chain, from carbon capture to transportation and storage, leveraging its engineering, technological and project execution capabilities to support clients’ decarbonization objectives.

Sumaraja Indah have signed a Memorandum of Understanding covering long-term lifecycle support for Alfa Laval heat exchanger installations at the H203 and JK7 Data Centre Projects in Indonesia. The collaboration focuses on cooling performance, operational reliability and long-term energy efficiency.

The agreement covers 40 Alfa Laval gasketed plate heat exchangers installed across the two projects. Alfa Laval will provide lifecycle assessment support through its Thermal Visual Condition Audit (VCA) programme, including periodic performance assessments over four years following commissioning.

evidence.title: Tetra Pak puts tuna in a new carton
evidence.text:
Tetra Pak puts tuna in a retortable carton

Tetra Pak has unveiled what it describes as the industry’s first carton packaging for shelf-stable tuna, opening up an alternative to the conventional metal can in one of the food industry’s most established categories.

Developed with Spanish seafood producer Jealsa, the new format uses Tetra Recart, a retortable carton package already used for a range of shelf-stable foods. The tuna format launched in Sweden with retailer Axfood in a 200ml Mini format and is now being made available to food producers and brands globally.

For tuna manufacturers, the development is significant because changing the package involves more than creating a different format for the shelf. Tetra Pak says the solution has been developed to support processing, distribution and retail requirements while giving brands greater flexibility in how tuna products are presented.

Round metal cans have dominated shelf-stable tuna for generations. Tetra Recart introduces a rectangular carton format that gives producers larger printable surfaces and a different shelf profile.

The format is designed for a range of tuna preparations, including shredded, flaked, chunks and tuna salad. Tetra Pak says its flat surfaces can provide more space for branding, nutritional information, sourcing credentials and other product information.

The rectangular format also changes how finished products can be handled through the supply chain. Its shape allows packs to fit closely together, while Tetra Pak says the format can provide up to 20% more units per pallet in some configurations. The company also highlights its suitability for e-commerce and home delivery, where the pack’s shape can be advantageous for picking and packing.

For manufacturers, one of the key questions is how a carton can deliver the shelf-life and food-safety characteristics traditionally associated with cans.

Tetra Recart is designed for retorting, allowing the package and its contents to undergo the high-temperature and high-pressure treatment required for shelf-stable products. Tetra Pak describes the package as an extra-robust material system developed specifically to withstand the retorting process.

The development represents a change in the format through which a producer can manufacture and commercialise shelf-stable tuna.

A different proposition for tuna producers

Tetra Pak says the package uses up to 71% FSC-certified paper, sourced from responsibly managed renewable forests and other controlled sources. The company is also positioning the format around lower carbon impact, cost competitiveness and distribution efficiency.

The company’s wider tuna proposition includes 100ml and 200ml Mini formats, with the smaller sizes targeting single-serve, on-the-go and household consumption occasions. Tetra Pak says formats between 100g and 200g currently account for more than 60% of the global shelf-stable tuna market.

For manufacturers, the format could affect pack design, filling and retorting, palletisation, warehousing, distribution, e-commerce and the way new tuna products are positioned.

The launch with Jealsa provides an early example of how packaging technology could be used to modernise a mature food category while retaining the long shelf life that makes shelf-stable tuna commercially attractive.

Food processing and packaging solutions company Tetra Pak has commissioned a new PolyAl processing plant in Germiston, Gauteng – a R19-million investment that will help convert used beverage cartons into new industrial products.

It aims to increase the country’s carton recycling rate to 40% by 2030.

The plant separates the polyethylene and aluminium layer, known as PolyAl, from used beverage cartons once the paper fibre has been recovered for papermaking.

The recovered PolyAl is processed into pellets, which manufacturing partner Timber Plastics converts into finished products including outdoor furniture, roof tiles and pipes.

The Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) has supported product development, helping validate applications such as roof tiles designed to compete with traditional cement products and pipes being developed as an alternative to conventional high-density polyethylene piping.

“We’ve worked quite hard with a variety of partners. The CSIR being one of them, whereby we develop applications that are suitable to the South African market and make sure that we continue to drive innovation,” says Tetra Pak Southern Africa sustainability head Masale Manoko .

He notes that the investment builds on several years of progress in the country’s carton recycling rate, which has grown from 8% in 2023 to 33% currently.

“It’s not been easy, but here we are today,” he quips.

Tetra Pak has supported this with targeted infrastructure investment, including a monitoring system giving real-time visibility of collection points and buyback centres across the country and a team of graduates deployed across all nine provinces to work directly with buyback centres and collectors, resolving on-the-ground challenges every two weeks.

Mpact recovers the paper fibre from used cartons at its mill, while Timber Plastics manufactures the recycled PolyAl into finished products.

Petco, the producer responsibility organisation that coordinates collection under South Africa's extended producer responsibility regulations, works with waste reclaimers, buyback centres and municipalities to channel cartons into the recycling system.

Petco’s liquid board packaging scheme performance has grown from 8% to 33% under this partnership.

Manoko emphasises that waste pickers who collect and sort cartons remain essential to the process. “This whole process that you see here involves partners in each and every stage. We cannot do it alone.”

Government has signalled continued review of the extended producer responsibility framework, aimed at strengthening requirements for producers.

evidence.title: Tetra Pak invests US$1.2M in carton recycling machine
evidence.text:
Tetra Pak invests US$1.2M in carton recycling machine

The machine—run by Unique Timber Plastics in Johannesburg’s Heriotdale industrial area, removes plastic and aluminium layers from used cartons, producing pellets reused as industrial inputs.

SOUTH AFRICA – Tetra Pak has invested R19 million (US$1.18 million) in a new carton recycling machine in Johannesburg, producing pellets that transform used beverage cartons into roof tiles, pipes and furniture.

The machine, operated by manufacturing partner Unique Timber Plastics at its plant in Johannesburg’s Heriotdale industrial area, strips plastic and aluminium layers from used cartons, converting them into pellets reused as industrial inputs.

Cartons typically comprise 70 percent paperboard, 25 percent polyethylene plastic and 5 percent aluminium composite, layered to protect food from spoilage.

The facility will create 24 jobs and support thousands of waste pickers.

Carton recycling in South Africa has climbed sharply from just 8 percent in 2023 to 33 percent today.

The investment forms part of Tetra Pak’s push to recycle 40 percent of the country’s food and beverage cartons within two years.

Masele Manoko, Tetra Pak’s head of sustainability for Southern Africa, said the pellets would be a low-cost and more sustainable competitor to high-density polyethylene pipes and could also compete with concrete roof tiles.

Mpact, South Africa’s leading paper recycler, will process the paperboard component of the waste.

Bruce Strong, chief executive of Mpact, said paperboard fibres could be recycled up to seven times, noting that cooperation between parties including producer responsibility organisation Petco had been delivering real results.

Petco’s 29 members, including Coca-Cola, PepsiCo, Tiger Brands and Tetra Pak, represent most plastic beverage bottle manufacturers and have boosted recycling of such bottles from 16 percent in 2005 to nearly 76 percent.

Waste Picker Network and Monitoring Systems Underpin Strategy

Manoko said the push toward the 40 percent recycling target followed years of effort including work with waste pickers, aggregators and municipalities as part of the transition toward a circular economy.

The group has built a monitoring system tracking waste aggregation across South Africa. Telly Chauke, chief executive of Petco, said efforts toward a circular economy might seem abstract but were keeping cartons out of rivers while creating opportunities for marginalised communities.

Strong added that manufacturing capacity was hard to build but easy to lose, appealing for deeper cooperation between industry and government to protect local capacity.

evidence.title: Tetra Pak presents three ways to boost cream cheese production
evidence.text:
Tetra Pak presents three ways to boost cream cheese production

Technologies can help the industry gain efficiency, flexibility, and quality in production.

BRAZIL – Tetra Pak, a world leader in food and beverage processing and packaging solutions, has offered three solutions that contribute to greater agility and flexibility for cream cheese, without raising operating costs or falling short of the expected quality standard.

Faced with such varied consumer demands, the multinational highlighted three fundamental pillars for optimizing this operation: efficiency, flexibility, and product quality.

“ In addition to increasing production capacity, manufacturers need to assess where the opportunities for gains lie during the process. Our role is to combine state-of-the-art equipment with processes that can make a difference both in the utilization of ingredients and in processing time and product quality ,” comments Ana Paula Forti, Director of the Processing area at Tetra Pak Brazil.

First is to produce more in less time with efficiency. To keep up with market demands, the industry needs to find ways to increase productivity without raising operating costs.

Simplifying the flow of ingredients, reducing steps, and making better use of resources are some of the ways to make production faster and more economical.

Among the technologies that can contribute to this goal is the Tetra Pak High Shear Mixer. This equipment centralizes the entire process, and crushing, melting, homogenization, and deaeration are performed in a single step.

By concentrating the operation, the manufacturer can work with larger batch capacities in less time, simplifying the production flow and increasing line capacity.

“ The high mechanical performance of this equipment allows achieving the desired texture using up to 20% less texture-modifying ingredients, such as gums ,” reported the Processing Director of Tetra Pak Brazil.

Second is greater flexibility to meet different demands. The ability to adapt production is another important factor for the ricotta cheese industry.

Flexible production lines allow working with different types of products, helping manufacturers develop new products and lead innovation in such a competitive market, reducing the need for new investments in complementary technologies.

Third is the standardization and consistency in each batch. To maintain the quality of the requeijão cheese batch after batch, rigorous control over the different stages of the process is essential.

Factors such as humidity, pH, and the type of curd coagulation can directly influence the texture, flavor, and appearance. Reducing the number of batches results in less product variability, ensuring better standardization throughout the entire process until it reaches the final consumer.

“ More than just increasing production capacity, it’s important to look at the process as a whole and understand where technology can generate gains.

“ When efficiency, flexibility, and quality control are considered together, the manufacturer can better utilize the available infrastructure and respond to market demands more consistently, in addition to having optimized workforce management, since employee turnover is increasingly high within industries ,” noted Ana Paula Forti.

evidence.title: El futuro de la manufactura alimentaria: Tetra Pak acelera la automatización sostenible en México
evidence.text:
El futuro de la manufactura alimentaria: Tetra Pak acelera la automatización sostenible en México

Durante ForoMX 2026, Tetra Pak presentó sus avances en automatización, inteligencia artificial y economía circular para transformar la industria alimentaria hacia modelos más eficientes y sostenibles.

Publicado: 15.09.2026 - 08:45 Actualizado: 15.09.2026 - 08:45

Ante el reto global de producir más con menos recursos y adaptarse a un consumidor cada vez más exigente, la digitalización y la sostenibilidad han dejado de ser opciones para convertirse en los motores estratégicos de la manufactura contemporánea.

En este escenario, se llevó a cabo ForoMX 2026, un encuentro clave donde Tetra Pak reunió a líderes del sector para trazar la ruta de la manufactura inteligente en el país.

Innovación tecnológica para optimizar plantas industriales

El evento fue una plataforma para analizar cómo tecnologías disruptivas como la inteligencia artificial, el monitoreo en tiempo real y el análisis de datos pueden convivir armónicamente con metas ambientales rigurosas.

Durante el foro, la compañía destacó el lanzamiento de Tetra Pak Factory OS, una plataforma diseñada para integrar el conocimiento de planta con la gestión operativa y de negocio, la cual fue galardonada con el Microsoft Intelligent Manufacturing Award (MIMA) 2026.

Según datos de la compañía, las plantas automatizadas pueden incrementar hasta un 20% su eficiencia general de los equipos y reducir el desperdicio de producto hasta en un 45%.

El ADN de la sostenibilidad y el origen de Tetra Pak

El compromiso de Tetra Pak con la sostenibilidad representa la base originaria sobre la cual se cimentó la empresa. Al abordar el origen del modelo de negocio, Ramiro Ortiz, director general de Tetra Pak México, recordó cómo la escasez de recursos moldeó el ADN de la compañía desde sus inicios:

"Tetra Pak fue creada en los años 50 a partir de la falta de recursos. En Suecia en la época faltaban materiales y nuestro fundador buscó opciones disponibles en la naturaleza que fueran renovables. Nacimos dentro de ese concepto de sostenibilidad”, expresó.

Desafíos de la economía circular y reciclaje en México

Esta visión histórica se conecta directamente con los retos actuales del mercado mexicano, donde la economía circular y la implementación de la nueva legislación en la materia exigen infraestructuras sólidas de acopio, colaboración intersectorial y concientización ciudadana.

Respecto al impulso del reciclaje en el país, el ecosistema no solo abarca el aprovechamiento del cartón para productos papeleros, sino la transformación del polialuminio en insumos industriales como charolas y pallets.

Para lograr consolidar la economía circular en México, Ramiro Ortiz subrayó que el reto fundamental no reside en la capacidad técnica de procesamiento, sino en la logística de origen y el compromiso de la sociedad.

"Para mí lo fundamental es mejorar todo el tema de acopio y de separación en los hogares, porque cuanto más volumen de material, más fácil es viabilizar económicamente una recicladora."

Visión estratégica: ponencias y análisis de los expertos

Las ponencias del evento reunieron a perfiles clave para abordar la evolución del sector desde distintos ángulos estratégicos.

Las intervenciones se centraron en la urgencia de adoptar aliados estratégicos para adaptar las operaciones al entorno digital, el despliegue global de inteligencia artificial y análisis de datos mediante plataformas como Factory OS para recortar desperdicios y paradas de línea, y la integración de la sostenibilidad como pilar de negocio

Por su parte, Sean Sims, vicepresidente de Automatización y Soluciones en Tetra Pak, detalló la estrategia global de IA y datos de la empresa, destacando que la automatización puede recortar un 45% el desperdicio de producto e incrementar la eficiencia operativa.

Håkan Nordkvist, especialista internacional en innovación y sostenibilidad, expuso cómo la modernización de instalaciones existentes puede reducir hasta un 47% las emisiones de gases de efecto invernadero y un 45% el consumo de agua, demostrando que la eficiencia técnica y la responsabilidad ambiental convergen en un mismo modelo rentable.

Ejes clave y conclusiones del ForoMX 2026

El ForoMX 2026 concluyó posicionándose como un espacio fundamental de diálogo para articular la visión estratégica de la manufactura del mañana.

Con este encuentro, Tetra Pak reafirmó su papel como un aliado estratégico capaz de guiar a los fabricantes en México hacia un crecimiento rentable, resiliente y responsable con el medio ambiente, demostrando que la innovación digital y la sostenibilidad son las dos caras de una misma transformación industrial.

evidence.text:
Securitas Technology to Showcase Next-Generation Security Innovation at GSX 2026

New insights from the 2027 Global Technology Outlook Report and live demonstrations of SecureStat Cumulus and the new SecureStat HQ AI Agent showcase the future of intelligent-led security

UNIONTOWN, OH / ACCESS Newswire / August 25, 2026 / Securitas Technology , one of the world's largest electronic security companies, will highlight the technologies, trends and innovations shaping the future of physical security at Global Security Exchange (GSX) 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. Attendees are invited to visit Booth #1905 to explore emerging technologies, engage with industry experts and gain insight into the evolving security landscape.

A centerpiece of the company's presence at GSX will be the debut of the 2027 Global Technology Outlook Report , the ninth edition of Securitas Technology's annual industry report. Built on insights from more than 16,000 clients across 19 countries, research involving 575 security professionals and contributions from leading technology partners, the report examines the trends expected to influence security strategies in 2027 and beyond. Topics include artificial intelligence, generative AI, agentic AI, cloud solutions, autonomous technologies, and safeguarding the physical security ecosystem.

"As electronic security and the industry as a whole becomes increasingly connected, intelligent and data driven, organizations need practical ways to turn insight into action," said Tony Byerly, global president and CEO of Securitas Technology. "The 2027 Global Technology Outlook Report, SecureStat Cumulus and the new SecureStat HQ AI Agent reflect our commitment to helping clients strengthen security operations, improve resilience, and prepare for what's next."

Visitors to Booth #1905 will experience SecureStat Cumulus , which combines cloud video management with generative AI-powered natural language search and alerts, helping organizations gain greater visibility and quickly identify the events that matter most. Attendees will also experience the debut of SecureStat HQ AI Agent , an AI-powered assistant embedded within Securitas Technology's SecureStat HQ security management platform that simplifies everyday security management through natural language interactions, actionable insights and guided workflows. Together, these innovations demonstrate how artificial intelligence is helping organizations simplify security management, gain actionable insights and make faster, more informed decisions.

In recognition of the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks, Securitas Technology has selected the Tunnel to Towers Foundation as its charitable partner for GSX 2026. The organization honors the sacrifice of first responders, military service members, and their families while providing ongoing support to those who continue to serve and protect our communities.

"We are proud to support the Tunnel to Towers Foundation and its mission to honor the heroes and families impacted by Sept. 11," said Tony Byerly. "As we mark this significant anniversary, it is important to remember those who perished and support the individuals and families who carry their legacy forward."

For more information, visit Securitas Technology at www.securitastechnology.com or visit Booth #1905 during GSX 2026.

Chris Cugini, Global Communications Manager newsroom@securitastechnology.com

evidence.title: Securitas AB baut Sicherheitsportfolio aus, Aktie bleibt international gefragt
evidence.text:
Von Thomas Klein , Fachredaktion Operatives & Strategie. Vor der Veroeffentlichung am 29.06.2026, 14:41 Uhr geprueft.

Die Securitas AB (ISIN SE0000163594) mit Hauptsitz in Stockholm gehoert zu den groessten Sicherheitsdienstleistern der Welt und ist an der Nasdaq Stockholm gelistet. Der Konzern adressiert mit seinem Ausbau technologiegestuetzter Sicherheitsloesungen eine wachsende Nachfrage nach integrierter Sicherheit in Europa und Nordamerika, wie aus den aktuellen Investoreninformationen hervorgeht. Ein Handelsbezug in den deutschsprachigen Raum besteht unter anderem ueber europaweit taetige Wettbewerber wie die im MDAX gelistete Deutsche Beteiligungs AG, die in Sicherheitsportfolios investiert.

Securitas AB beschaeftigt nach eigenen Angaben rund 345.000 Mitarbeitende in 44 Laendern und erzielte 2023 einen Umsatz von 132 Milliarden Schwedischen Kronen (SEK). Der Konzern gliedert sein Geschaeft in drei Hauptsegmente: Security Services North America, Security Services Europe und Security Services Ibero-America, Africa, Middle East & Asia, wobei Europa und Nordamerika den groessten Anteil am Umsatz tragen. Laut dem Jahresbericht 2023 stammt rund die Haelfte des Gruppenumsatzes aus Vertragsdiensten wie stationaerer Bewachung und mobiler Sicherheitskontrolle, waehrend der Rest auf technische Sicherheitsloesungen und Risikomanagement entfällt.

Im Segment Security Services Europe ist Securitas in Laendern wie Deutschland, Frankreich, Spanien, den nordischen Staaten und der Schweiz aktiv und bietet dort sowohl physische Bewachungsdienste als auch technologiegestuetzte Loesungen an. In Nordamerika wiederum konzentriert sich der Konzern auf grosse Corporate-Kunden, kritische Infrastruktur und staatliche Einrichtungen, wobei umfangreiche Integrationen von Videoueberwachung, Zugangskontrolle und Alarmmanagement eine zentrale Rolle spielen. Insgesamt positioniert sich Securitas als Anbieter von integrierten Sicherheitsloesungen, die menschliche Praesenz mit digitalen Plattformen und Analytik verbinden sollen.

Die Unternehmensstrategie von Securitas sieht vor, den Anteil technologiegestuetzter Sicherheitsloesungen am Gesamtumsatz deutlich zu erhoehen. Unter dem Leitmotiv "Security solutions and electronic security" investiert der Konzern seit einigen Jahren gezielt in elektronische Sicherheit, Remote Services und Cloud-basierte Plattformen, um Kunden eine ganzheitliche Ueberwachung und Steuerung ihrer Sicherheitsinfrastruktur zu ermoeglichen. Laut Investorenpraesentation erhoehte Securitas den Umsatzanteil dieses Segments zwischen 2018 und 2023 spuerbar, was den Strategiewandel hin zu hoeherrentablen Dienstleistungen unterstreicht.

Zu den investitionsintensiven Bereichen gehören insbesondere Videoueberwachung mit Analysefunktionen, Einbruchmeldeanlagen, Zugangskontrollsysteme sowie integrative Software, die diese Komponenten zentral zusammenführt. Securitas hebt dabei die Bedeutung standardisierter, wiederverwendbarer Loesungspakete hervor, mit denen Kundenbranchen wie Einzelhandel, Logistik oder Fertigung effizient bedient werden koennen. Die Kombination aus physischer Praesenz und technischer Ueberwachung soll fuer Unternehmen nicht nur Sicherheitsvorteile, sondern auch Kosteneffizienzen bringen.

Der Jahresbericht und die Investor-Relations-Unterlagen von Securitas AB liefern detaillierte Einblicke in Geschaeftsstruktur, Segmente und strategische Schwerpunkte.

Operativ konzentriert sich Securitas in seinen Kernmaerkten auf wiederkehrende Sicherheitsdienste fuer Unternehmens- und oeffentliche Kunden. Im Bereich stationaerer Bewachung bietet der Konzern klassisches Wachpersonal fuer Industrieanlagen, Bueroimmobilien, Transportknotenpunkte und Veranstaltungen an. Bei mobilen Diensten stehen regelmaessige Kontrollfahrten, Alarmreviere und Interventionen im Fokus, bei denen Mitarbeitende bei Ausloesung eines Alarms vor Ort eintreffen.

Wichtige Kundenbranchen sind laut Unternehmensangaben unter anderem die Industrie, der Handel, der Logistiksektor sowie Finanzdienstleister. Gerade im Einzelhandel spielen Praeventionskonzepte gegen Ladendiebstahl und Inventurschwund eine grosse Rolle, wobei Securitas mit Kombinationen aus Praesenzdienst, Videoanalyse und elektronischer Zutrittskontrolle arbeitet. Im Logistikbereich wiederum sind Schutzmassnahmen gegen Warendiebstahl und Sabotage in Distributionszentren und entlang der Transportkette gefragt, was integrierte Sicherheitskonzepte mit Ueberwachungs- und Alarmtechnik erfordert.

Im internationalen Wettbewerbsumfeld trifft Securitas auf grosse Sicherheitsdienstleister wie G4S, Allied Universal und Prosegur, die teilweise ebenfalls global agieren. Die Marktstruktur ist fragmentiert, mit regional starken Anbietern und einer Reihe von spezialisierten Technologieunternehmen, die elektronische Sicherheitssysteme entwickeln. Gegenueber Wettbewerbern setzt Securitas auf eine Kombination aus langjaehriger Praesenz in vielen Maerkten und dem Ausbau eigener elektronischer Sicherheitskapazitaeten.

In Europa steht der Konzern im Wettbewerb mit Sicherheitsunternehmen, die auch fuer Kunden im deutschsprachigen Raum taetig sind, etwa Securitas Deutschland als Landesgesellschaft im Konzernverbund. Die Verbindung aus globalem Netzwerk und lokaler Ausrichtung wird in den Unternehmensunterlagen als Vorteil hervorgehoben, weil sie einen Abgleich internationaler Best Practices mit nationalen regulatorischen Vorgaben ermoeglichen soll. Analysten verweisen im Rahmen ihrer Sektorberichte zur Sicherheitsbranche regelmaessig darauf, dass gerade global agierende Dienstleister von groesseren, grenzueberschreitenden Auftraegen profitieren koennen.

Das Finanzprofil von Securitas zeichnet sich durch stabile Umsaetze aus wiederkehrenden Dienstleistungen aus. Im Geschaeftsjahr 2023 erhoehte der Konzern seinen Umsatz auf 132 Milliarden SEK, was einem organischen Wachstum gegenueber dem Vorjahr entspricht. Laut Jahresbericht betrug das operative Ergebnis (EBITA) im selben Zeitraum 7,5 Milliarden SEK, wobei Investitionen in Technologie und Restrukturierungen einzelne Segmente belasteten.

Die Verschuldung wird im Bericht ueber Kennziffern wie Nettoverbindlichkeiten zu EBITDA beschrieben, die sich im Rahmen der vom Management gesetzten Zielspanne bewegten. Das Unternehmen betont dabei ein diszipliniertes Vorgehen bei Akquisitionen, insbesondere im Bereich elektronischer Sicherheit, um das Leverage-Ratio mittelfristig stabil zu halten. Dividendenentscheidungen orientieren sich laut den Leitlinien an einem ausgewogenen Verhaeltnis zwischen Ausschüttung an Aktionaere und Reinvestitionen in das Geschaeft.

Investitionen in elektronische Sicherheit

Ein zentraler operativer Schwerpunkt liegt auf dem Ausbau elektronischer Sicherheitssysteme und zugehoeriger Dienstleistungen. Securitas investiert laut Investorenpraesentation in den Aufbau und die Erweiterung von Monitoring-Centern, die als zentrale Leitstellen fuer Video- und Alarmueberwachung dienen. Dort laufen Datenströme aus Kameras, Sensoren und Zugangskontrollsystemen zusammen, werden analysiert und bei relevanten Ereignissen an Sicherheitsmitarbeitende oder Kunden weitergeleitet.

Die angebotenen Loesungen umfassen unter anderem Videoverifikation, bei der eingehende Alarmmeldungen anhand von Live-Bildern geprueft werden, sowie virtuelle Rundgaenge, bei denen Kameras definierte Kontrollpfade abfahren und Auffaelligkeiten melden. Zudem entwickelt Securitas laut eigener Darstellung standardisierte Pakete fuer typische Anwendungsfaelle, etwa fuer kleinere Einzelhandelsfilialen oder mittelgrosse Unternehmensstandorte, um Implementierungen zu beschleunigen und Kosten planbarer zu machen.

Die Digitalisierung des Sicherheitsgeschaefts spielt fuer Securitas eine zunehmende Rolle. Der Konzern arbeitet an Plattformen, ueber die Kunden ihre Sicherheitsdaten konsolidiert einsehen und steuern koennen, etwa Zutrittsprotokolle, Alarmhistorien oder Videoaufzeichnungen. Der Einsatz von Datenanalytik soll helfen, Muster in Sicherheitsvorfällen zu erkennen und Praeventionsmassnahmen zielgerichtet anzupassen.

In diesem Kontext verweist das Unternehmen auf die Bedeutung von Cyber-Security, da vernetzte Sicherheitsinfrastrukturen selbst Angriffsziele darstellen koennen. Securitas adressiert dies nach eigener Darstellung durch Sicherheitsarchitekturen mit Zugriffsbeschraenkungen, Verschluesselung und laufender Ueberwachung der Systeme. Kunden profitieren von zentralen Updates und Wartung, wobei technische Plattformen regelmaessig weiterentwickelt und an neue regulatorische Vorgaben angepasst werden.

Securitas stellt Nachhaltigkeit und Compliance als integrale Bestandteile seines Geschaefts dar. Der Konzern berichtet im Jahresbericht 2023 ueber Initiativen in den Bereichen Umwelt, Soziales und Unternehmensfuehrung, darunter Schulungsprogramme, Diversitaetsziele und Massnahmen zur CO2-Reduktion. Besonders hervorgehoben werden Trainings fuer Sicherheitsmitarbeitende zu Themen wie Deeskalation, Menschenrechte und Anti-Korruption, die regelmaessig aktualisiert werden.

Im Bereich Umwelt nennt Securitas unter anderem den schrittweisen Ersatz konventioneller Fahrzeuge durch emissionsärmere Alternativen in bestimmten Maerkten, soweit dies operativ sinnvoll ist. Zudem sollen Gebaeude und Leitstellen energieeffizienter betrieben werden, etwa durch modernisierte Heizungs- und Kuehlungssysteme sowie optimierte IT-Infrastrukturen. Insgesamt will der Konzern seine Nachhaltigkeitsberichterstattung weiter ausbauen, um Investorinnen und Investoren sowie Kunden mehr Transparenz zu bieten.

Ein repraesentatives Produkt- und Loesungsbereich bei Securitas ist "Intelligent Security Systems", mit dem der Konzern integrierte Technologiepakete anbietet. Diese Loesungen verbinden Videoueberwachung, Alarmtechnik, Zugangskontrolle und Datenplattformen, sodass Unternehmen ihre Sicherheitsinfrastruktur aus einer Hand erhalten koennen. Intelligent Security Systems richten sich vor allem an mittelgrosse und grosse Kunden, fuer die standardisierte, skalierbare Sicherheitsarchitekturen gefragt sind.

Die Implementierung umfasst typische Komponenten wie IP-Kameras, Netzwerkrekorder, Sensoren für Fenster und Tueren, Schluesselkarten-Systeme sowie Software zur Steuerung und Auswertung. Securitas uebernimmt dabei sowohl die Konzeption als auch die Installation und den laufenden Betrieb, inklusive Wartung und Monitoring aus zentralen Leitstellen. Kunden erhalten Berichte zu Ereignissen und Trends, um eigene Sicherheitsmassnahmen regelmaessig zu ueberpruefen und gegebenenfalls anzupassen.

Die Aktie von Securitas AB wird an der Nasdaq Stockholm im Segment Large Cap gehandelt und ist in mehreren schwedischen Indizes vertreten, darunter der OMX Stockholm Benchmark. Am 28.06.2026 lag der Schlusskurs der Securitas-Aktie bei 84,50 SEK. Damit ist Securitas AB als boersennotierter Sicherheitsdienstleister mit internationaler Taetigkeit fuer Anleger weltweit handelbar.

evidence.title: Vestas installs the 200th V236-15.0 MW offshore wind turbine
evidence.text:
Vestas installs the 200th V236-15.0 MW offshore wind turbine

Vestas achieved the milestone of 200 V236-15.0 MW marine wind turbines installed after completing a new unit in the Hollandse Kust West Park VI , located in the North Sea. With this development, the cumulative capacity associated with this offshore model amounts to 3 GW.

The 200th turbine was installed at the Ecowende project, a 760 MW offshore wind farm located in Dutch waters. Hollandse Kust West VI will have a total of 52 V236-15.0 MW units and is scheduled to begin operations at the end of 2026.

The V236-15.0 MW expands its presence in offshore wind farms

The offshore deployment of the V236-15.0 MW began in April 2025 with the installation of the first unit in the EnBW He Dreiht wind farm in Germany. The project has 64 wind turbines of this model and its installation was completed in August 2026.

Later, Vestas reached the first 100 turbines installed in June 2026, as work progressed on the Baltic Power wind farm in Poland. The project, developed by Orlen Group and Northland Power, will incorporate 76 V236-15.0 MW turbines.

The installation of the 200th unit thus doubles, in a few months, the number of V236-15.0 MW wind turbines deployed offshore and raises the cumulative capacity of the model to 3 GW.

Hollandse Kust West VI is moving towards commercial operation

The turbine installation campaign at Hollandse Kust West VI began at the end of May, the project supplied electricity to the Dutch grid for the first time in July and continues to progress towards its planned entry into operation by the end of 2026.

The park is located about 53 kilometers off the coast of the Netherlands, near IJmuiden, its 52 V236-15.0 MW turbines will form a total installed capacity of 760 MW.

The project also incorporates measures aimed at studying the interaction between wind turbines and birds. Seven of the turbines supplied by Vestas they have a blade painted red to assess whether greater contrast improves rotor visibility and helps reduce the risk of collisions.

Vestas reinforces the deployment of its 15 MW offshore turbine

The V236-15.0 MW was specifically developed to operate in offshore wind environments, its installation in projects in Germany, Poland, and the Netherlands reflects the commercial expansion of this platform within the European offshore market.

With 200 units installed, Vestas reaches 3 GW of cumulative capacity through this model, Hollandse Kust West VI thus joins a portfolio of projects that includes He Dreiht and Baltic Power among the main European sites where the V236-15.0 MW is being deployed.

evidence.title: Vestas wins first order for new V182-7.2 MW turbine for project in Sweden
evidence.text:
Vestas wins first order for new V182-7.2 MW turbine for project in Sweden

The order confirms the market-readiness of Vestas’ latest turbine and demonstrates a strong market interest in the latest evolution of the EnVentus platform, designed to increase energy production and strengthen business case certainty for customers.

The order is for the 29 MW Staverhult project and includes supply, delivery, and commissioning of four V182-7.2 MW turbines as well as a 35-year Active Output Management 5000 (AOM 5000) service agreement designed to ensure optimised performance throughout the lifetime of the project.

“We are delighted to take the next step and begin construction of the Staverhult wind farm” said Peter Zachrisson, CEO, SR Energy. “By investing in Vestas’ latest generation of efficient wind turbine technology, we can make the most of the excellent wind conditions and deliver more renewable electricity where it is needed most. Staverhult is exactly the kind of project we want to develop - a long-term investment that strengthens electricity supply in southern Sweden and contributes to a more robust and competitive energy system.”

By utilising the proven EnVentus platform and upgrading only what creates meaningful customer value, the V182-7.2 MW is now ready for customers’ project planning and Vestas is able to ramp up serial production from end of 2027.

“This milestone underlines that our new turbine is ready for the market and it demonstrates that when the right technology is matched with the right business case, projects can move forward even in challenging market conditions” added Jens Kück, Senior Vice President for Sales in Vestas Northern and Central Europe. “By combining enhanced energy production and the certainty of a proven platform, the V182-7.2 MW helps improve project economics and unlock investment opportunities, supporting the next phase of wind energy growth in Sweden.”

Turbine delivery is expected to begin in the second quarter of 2028, with commissioning scheduled for the third quarter of 2028. Once commissioned, the project will help meet Sweden's growing demand for affordable, secure, and sustainable energy.

evidence.title: Vestas Renewed a Sensor Deal. The Durable Value Was Never the Sensor.
evidence.text:
Catch pre-market movers with AI signals.

- Vestas renewed a sensor supply deal with Gastops, but the focus is its service business, not hardware sales.

- Service contracts now dominate Vestas' EUR 71.9bn backlog, with 15.5–17.5% EBIT margins, outperforming overall company margins.

- Despite losing hardware market share to Chinese rivals, Vestas maintains a 201 GW installed base, ensuring recurring service revenue.

- 2025 saw record revenue and a EUR 778m net profit, with shareholder returns via dividends and buybacks signaling a mature cash generator.

- Future success hinges on sustaining service margins and positive free cash flow to maintain dividend viability amid regulatory and market challenges.

A Canadian firm most investors have never heard of just renewed a supply deal with Vestas, the Danish wind turbine giant. Gastops will keep selling its MetalSCAN oil-debris sensors - small devices that sit in a gearbox and flag metallic wear before a bearing fails - across Vestas' turbine platforms starting January 1, 2027 . The easy read is that this is a vote of confidence in new turbine demand, wind hardware momentum. The harder and more useful read is that the renewal has almost nothing to do with selling turbines, and everything to do with the business Vestas now makes its money in.

Start with the concession about size. Vestas just booked record 2025 revenue of EUR 18.8bn . A gearbox sensor that costs a few hundred dollars is rounding error on a statement that size; no investor should price Vestas off MetalSCAN unit sales. Treat the deal as a detail, not a growth signal. What the renewal actually points to is the installed base.

That installed base is the whole story. Vestas has 164 GW of turbines under service agreements that typically run 20 years or more, and it monitors more than 51,000 of those turbines with the kind of condition data MetalSCAN feeds. The sensor is cheap; the contract it helps keep alive is not. Reliability and uptime are the product of the service business, and service is now the durable, high-margin engine of the entire company.

Here the numbers separate the headline from the economics. Service orders make up more than half of Vestas' record EUR 71.9bn total backlog - EUR 38.7bn of it - while Vestas guides its Service segment to a 15.5–17.5% EBIT margin, against roughly 5.7% for the company as a whole. The hardware business is the competitive battleground; the service fleet is the moat.

And it is a real moat. Five Chinese manufacturers out-installed Vestas in 2025, capturing nearly 60% of global new-install capacity, while Vestas placed sixth at about 12.9 GW. Yet Vestas still holds around 201 GW of cumulative installed turbines - the largest base in the world - and those machines need maintenance no matter who sells the next turbine. That asymmetry is the reason a company called a "turbine maker" is quietly becoming a recurring-revenue service business.

The balance sheet backs up the shift. 2025 was the year Vestas stopped being the archetype of the money-losing wind OEM: record revenue, net profit up 55% to EUR 778m , adjusted free cash flow of EUR 1,095m , and a return to rewarding shareholders - a proposed ordinary dividend of DKK 0.74 a share plus a EUR 150m buyback . For a mature cash generator, cash returned to shareholders is the metric that outlasts the narrative, and here it finally arrived.

The engine is not frictionless. Adjusted free cash flow fell 24% from 2024's elevated EUR 1,792m, Vestas flags tariff and regulatory headwinds in the US, its largest market, where it says future clean-energy investment has become "less attractive," and the 16.3 GW of turbine order intake still swings with the financing cycle. The dividend and the buyback ride on whether the service cash keeps coming and free cash flow stays positive enough to fund them.

So the sensor renewal is a detail with an honest message. Gastops is privately held, so there is nothing here to buy directly; for a US investor the tradeable vehicle is Vestas itself, Danish-listed and available over the counter. The question the renewal raises is whether Vestas keeps converting its installed base into durable service cash - and the metric that answers it is whether the Service segment's 2026 EBIT margin lands near the high end of guidance, and whether free cash flow stays solidly positive enough to keep the dividend coming. Compress service margins or let free cash flow turn negative, and the "mature cash generator rediscovering its dividend" reading breaks. Watch the fleet and the cash, not the sensor.

evidence.title: Vestas Debuts New 7.2 MW Wind Turbine in Sweden – Series Production to Begin at End of 2027
evidence.text:
Vestas Debuts New 7.2 MW Wind Turbine in Sweden – Series Production to Begin at End of 2027

Hamburg – Vestas received the first order for its new V182-7.2 MW onshore wind turbine one day after launching the model. Swedish project developer SR Energy has ordered four turbines with a total capacity of 28.8 MW for the Staverhult Wind Farm in southern Sweden. Commissioning is scheduled for the third quarter of 2028.

With the new turbine, Vestas is developing its EnVentus platform further. A larger rotor is intended to increase energy yield at unchanged rated capacity and improve the economics of wind energy projects. The manufacturer plans to ramp up series production from the end of 2027.

New Vestas Turbine: Larger Rotor Intended to Increase Annual Energy Yield by 4 to 6 Percent The V182-7.2 MW has a rotor diameter of 182 metres and a swept rotor area of 26,016 square metres. Compared with the previous V172-7.2 MW, the rotor diameter increases by ten metres. Both models have a rated capacity of 7.2 MW. According to Vestas, the new turbine achieves an annual energy yield that is 4 to 6 percent higher, depending on site conditions.

In addition to the larger rotor, Vestas said it has specifically further developed the drivetrain. The ratio of rotor area to rated capacity is intended to enable higher power production, particularly at lower wind speeds. The manufacturer lists standard hub heights of 109 and 170 metres for the V182-7.2 MW. Site-specific tower variants are available on request.

The new turbine is based on the existing EnVentus platform. According to the manufacturer, more than 2,000 turbines with a combined capacity of over 15 GW were installed worldwide on this platform at the time of the market launch. The further development is intended to combine the higher energy yield with platform technology already in use.

First Order: Four V182-7.2 MW Turbines for Staverhult Wind Farm in Southern Sweden SR Energy's order covers the supply and commissioning of four V182-7.2 MW turbines as well as a 35-year service agreement. Delivery is scheduled to begin in the second quarter of 2028, with commissioning planned for the third quarter of 2028.

Staverhult is thus the first announced project for the new V182-7.2 MW. Vestas plans to ramp up series production from the end of 2027 and then make the turbine available for further wind energy projects.

The new turbine continues the development within the EnVentus platform toward larger rotors at a rated capacity of 7.2 MW. While the V162-7.2 MW has a rotor diameter of 162 metres and the V172-7.2 MW of 172 metres, Vestas is again increasing the rotor area with the V182-7.2 MW. The additional yield of 4 to 6 percent stated by the manufacturer refers to the comparison with the V172-7.2 MW and depends on the respective site conditions.

evidence.title: Danfoss India Showcases iC7 Ultra Low Harmonics Drive
evidence.text:
Danfoss India Showcases iC7 Ultra Low Harmonics Drive

Danfoss India has introduced its next-generation iC7 Ultra Low Harmonics Drive, designed to improve power quality, energy efficiency and operational reliability in industrial facilities. The technology was presented at SEMICON India 2026 and the 25th CII Energy Efficiency Summit.

The iC7 drive is designed for industrial applications where power quality and energy efficiency are important to continuous operations. Danfoss said the technology can help address electrical distortion and reduce energy losses in industrial power networks, supporting India’s efforts to improve energy efficiency and reduce industrial emissions.

The drive uses an integrated active front-end rectifier to reduce Total Harmonic Distortion of Current (THDi) to below 3 per cent while maintaining a power factor of 1.0. By limiting electrical distortion at the source, the technology is designed to reduce power losses across industrial electrical networks.

Another feature is its ability to support smaller upstream electrical infrastructure. Danfoss said the solution can enable industrial facilities to use transformers and backup generators that are 10 to 25 per cent smaller, without compromising operational performance. This can reduce material requirements and infrastructure costs while lowering the embodied carbon associated with new industrial facilities.

The technology is aimed at sectors with demanding power-quality requirements, including semiconductor manufacturing and advanced electronics. By reducing thermal stress and helping protect connected machinery, the drive is designed to support equipment reliability and reduce the risk of premature failures.

Ravichandran Purushothaman, President, Danfoss India and CII Southern Chairman, said, “India is rapidly shifting from just a consumer market to a global powerhouse for advanced engineering and manufacturing. Showcasing our next-gen iC7 technology at both SEMICON India and the CII Energy Efficiency Summit highlights the deep synergy between electronics infrastructure and clean energy. Through relentless innovation and scalable local design, we remain fiercely committed to eliminating power distortions, slashing industrial emissions, and building a self-reliant, energy-secure future.”

Mandar Vaijanapurkar, Head of Drives Sales, Marketing & Services, Danfoss India, said, “As modern industrial facilities adopt sophisticated automation, maintaining high power quality has become non-negotiable for operational reliability and business continuity. The iC7 Ultra Low Harmonic Drive is engineered to tackle electrical distortion directly at its source, allowing customers to safeguard sensitive equipment, cut down on infrastructure stress, and boost overall network performance. By delivering cleaner electricity, this solution builds the operational resilience required for India’s next phase of industrial expansion.”

The iC7 Ultra Low Harmonics Drive forms part of Danfoss India’s portfolio of technologies focused on industrial energy efficiency, power quality and electrification. Its introduction comes as manufacturers expand automation and high-technology production capacity and seek to manage energy consumption and infrastructure requirements.

Headquartered in Oragadam, Chennai, Danfoss India boasts a robust network of sales, support teams, and over 3,500 employees. The company’s nationwide presence, coupled with a strong channel partner network, positions it to meet the growing demand for energy-efficient technologies across India. Ravichandran Purushothaman serves as the President of Danfoss India.

evidence.title: Danfoss launches AK-GC52 controller for CO2 refrigeration systems
evidence.text:
Danfoss launches AK-GC52 controller for CO2 refrigeration systems

The unit optimizes gas cooler and receiver pressures, supports heat recovery and connects to ADAP-KOOL monitoring platforms.

Danfoss has developed the AK-GC52 CO2 Gas Cooler and Receiver Pressure Controller for pressure control in transcritical and subcritical CO2 refrigeration applications. The controller regulates gas cooler pressure to help systems achieve optimal coefficient of performance (COP) while supporting stable operation.

The AK-GC52 continuously adjusts system operation based on pressure and temperature measurements. It is designed for use in transcritical refrigeration systems, heat pumps, heat recovery applications and chillers, and includes an extra refrigeration capacity mode for periods of higher cooling demand.

The controller provides gas cooler and receiver pressure control and supports heat recovery with adjustable pressure references and optimized heat pump operation. It can automatically optimize gas cooler pressure using real-time pressure and temperature inputs.

For system integration, the AK-GC52 supports Modbus RTU communication via RS485 and Ethernet and is compatible with Danfoss ADAP-KOOL system management and monitoring solutions.

The controller is designed to work with Danfoss ICMTS valves and ICAD actuators, providing gas cooler pressure control while supporting heat recovery and receiver pressure management.

Danfoss invests in Denmark distribution center automation

Robots are expected to handle 70% to 80% of palletizing as the site scales to meet rising global demand.

Danfoss has launched a major upgrade of its Central Distribution Center in Rødekro, Denmark, to increase automation, capacity and service levels. The investment coincides with the site’s 25th anniversary and is intended to improve the center’s performance and scalability.

The project includes infrastructure modernization, process optimization and new automated systems. Existing conveyor equipment will be upgraded and partly replaced with Autonomous Mobile Robots that transport and lift pallets.

Danfoss will also automate manual carton closing and handling processes using robotic closing systems and optimized air usage in cartons. Consolidation and palletizing will be automated, with robots expected to handle 70–80% of palletizing activities.

The distribution center currently handles around 50% of the volumes in the Danfoss Climate Solutions segment. Danfoss expects the upgrade to improve throughput, reduce manual handling and support the site’s ability to scale with rising global demand.

“Celebrating 25 years in Rødekro is a testament to our strong track record and the dedication of our people”, said Dan Bruun, Vice President, Logistics Operations, Danfoss Climate Solutions. “Over the past 18 months, we have conducted an extensive operational benchmark, confirming that the site remains highly competitive in cost, service, and quality. This investment builds on that solid foundation—further enhancing our competitiveness and ensuring we continue to deliver high-quality, efficient, and flexible services to our customers for years to come”.

The upgrade is expected to be completed by the end of 2028.
