evidence.title: CEZ, a.s. - The General Meeting of CEZ, to be convened for 1 June 2026, will decide on the Optimization of the Ownership Structure and Governance of CEZ Group
evidence.text:
CEZ, a.s. - The General Meeting of CEZ, to be convened for 1 June 2026, will decide on the Optimization of the Ownership Structure and Governance of CEZ Group

Aktualizacja: 23.04.2026 15:20 Publikacja: 23.04.2026 15:20

The General Meeting of CEZ, to be convened for 1 June 2026, will decide on the Optimization of the Ownership Structure and Governance of CEZ Group proposed by the Board of Directors to implement the current Business Policy

At its meeting held today, the Board of Directors of CEZ, a. s., approved a proposal for the Optimization of the Ownership Structure and Governance of CEZ Group and resolved to submit it for approval to the General Meeting to be convened for 1 June 2026.

The proposed Optimization of the Ownership Structure and Governance of CEZ Group comprises:

A. a transfer of the customer segment of CEZ Group to a company controlled by CEZ, a. s. the Customer Segment Subsidiary Company or CSSC , and

B. a potential sale of a minority stake in CSSC and of stakes in other companies within the customer segment of CEZ Group.

The customer segment of CEZ Group primarily includes:

The Board of Directors proposal is the outcome of the strategic direction approved by shareholders at the General Meeting on 28 June 2022 as part of the Business Policy of CEZ Group. This Business Policy anticipates a differentiated focus on the generation and customer segments together with a corresponding realignment and optimization of the ownership structure and governance of CEZ Group’s assets.

If the proposed Optimization of the Ownership Structure and Governance of CEZ Group is approved by the General Meeting, the Board of Directors will decide whether the customer segment will be transferred to CSSC in one or more transactions and will determine the form, scope, and timing of such transfer. The Board of Directors will also decide whether, and to what extent, a portion of the financial debt of CEZ, a. s., will be transferred to CSSC provided that the relevant conditions are met (including, for instance, the obtaining of the required creditor consents). Currently, the transfer of the customer segment to CSSC is expected to be implemented by the end of the first quarter of 2027.

The transfer of the customer segment to CSSC may contribute to an increase in the value of the customer segment and CEZ Group as a whole. The separation of stable, regulated, and customer-centric activities from generation activities exposed to a higher market volatility and different investment risks may enable CSSC to attract a broader range of financing banks and investors. This, in turn, may facilitate a more efficient capital allocation and more favourable financing terms.

The transfer will lead to a more targeted management of the generation and customer segments, as well as to more precise key performance indicators KPIs, which may enable a more effective delivery of such KPIs and enhanced transparency. A clearer segmentation of CEZ Group’s assets may thus contribute to a more accurate reflection of the value of the individual segments in the market valuation.

At the same time, the transfer of the customer segment to CSSC will create a scope for potential future monetization, strategic partnerships, and the sale of a minority stake in the CSSC group.

If the proposed Optimization of the Ownership Structure and Governance of CEZ Group is approved by the General Meeting, the Board of Directors will be authorised to decide whether any potential sale of a minority stake in CSSC and of stakes in other customer segment companies will be carried out or not. In its decision-making, the Board of Directors will take into account market conditions, investment opportunities, and other relevant circumstances.

In the event of any such sale, the Board of Directors will also decide on its form (such as a public offering of shares with a potential admission to trading on a stock exchange, a direct sale, a combination of such forms, or another structure) and will determine which stakes will be sold, in what size, and when. The proposal is structured such that CEZ Group retains at least a 51% stake in CSSC and also in each tier of the ownership chain leading to strategic companies involved in the distribution, sale, and trading of electricity and gas, as well smart energy services i.e. CEZ Distribuce, a. s., GasNet Group, CEZ Prodej, a.s., CEZ Group’s trading arm, and CEZ ESCO, a.s..

If approved by the General Meeting, the Optimization of the Ownership Structure and Governance of CEZ Group will ensure readiness and flexibility to respond to new opportunities and risks, including in light of uncertainty regarding future global developments in energy markets and beyond.

Any sale of a portion of the structurally separated customer segment may contribute to the realisation of its added value potential and support returns for shareholders of CEZ, a. s. CSSC may constitute an attractive asset for investors focused on regulated, lower-risk assets who currently do not invest in CEZ, a. s., in particular due to its ownership of nuclear or coal assets, such as infrastructure or pension funds.

In the coming years, CEZ Group also plans to undertake a capital-intensive investment programme encompassing, for instance, construction of gas-fired generation units and investments in its existing portfolio of generation assets.

In addition, it is not possible to look away from the intention of the Czech Republic, as a 69.8% shareholder, to carry out a buyout of shares held by minority shareholders of CEZ, a. s., while utilising CEZ Group’s financial means, which has been enshrined in the Policy Statement of the Government of the Czech Republic dated 5 January 2026 and has been repeatedly publicly proclaimed by members of the Government.

For these purposes, approval of the Optimization of the Ownership Structure and Governance of CEZ Group by the General Meeting will create a scope for optimization CEZ Group’s financial position.

CEZ Group in Romania becomes the EVRYO Group

The CEZ Group in Romania has announced a rebranding process through which it will become the EVRYO Group. The new identity “highlights the Group’s commitment for a green future and puts the benefit of people, communities and the entire planet at the center of all actions.”

“We are proud to be part of such an active industry and to contribute to its accelerated evolution towards a green future for the benefit of all people. We have both clear sustainability objectives and a target of zero emissions for the year 2040, as well as concrete plans through which they will become reality. We stand by the people, each of them, and continue all our projects,” said Angelica Barbu, Chief People and Brand Officer EVRYO.

Bringing together the companies Distributie Energie Oltenia, Ovidiu Development, Tomis Team, MW Team Invest, TMK Hydroenergy Power and EVRYO Power, the EVRYO Group manages and operates the largest operational onshore wind farm in Romania, produces green energy through the hydropower system near Reșita and operates the first floating photovoltaic solar energy system in Romania.

Skoda Auto India plans 10 product introductions in 2026

Strong sales growth in 2025, expansion in market reach and upgrades to key models underpin the company’s roadmap

Updated - January 20, 2026 05:31 pm IST - MUMBAI

“We have changed how we operate and how the brand is perceived,” Ashish Gupta, brand director, Skoda Auto India, says. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

Having grown 107% by selling 72,665 units in 2025, Skoda Auto India is planning to sustain the momentum through the introduction of 10 products, largely upgrades, in 2026.

“If I were to sum up 2025 in one word, it would be transformative. It marked 25 years of Skoda in India and also turned out to be our strongest year so far. We grew volumes significantly year-on-year and expanded our footprint to 183 cities with more than 325 customer touchpoints. More importantly, we have changed how we operate and how the brand is perceived,” Ashish Gupta, Brand Director, Skoda Auto India, said in an interview.

“We moved from being seen largely as a niche, urban brand to becoming far more accessible and relevant across markets. Our market ranking improved meaningfully from 11 to 7, and we entered several new territories. These achievements give us a strong foundation going into 2026,” he said.

Mr. Gupta said the focus would be on deepening reach, strengthening service coverage and continuing to build trust.

“We are working towards expanding our market coverage closer to 90%, supported by a strong product plan and structural improvements that allow us to deliver better value to customers,” he said.

On the product line-up, Mr. Gupta said, “We will be expanding the Kylaq range with new variants such as Classic Plus and Prestige Plus, while the Kylaq Sportline will follow later in the year.”

“We will now also be introducing a significant upgrade to the Kushaq, along with a similar update for the Slavia later in the year. In addition, some globally iconic products will make a return, including another batch of the Octavia RS and the introduction of the Kodiaq RS. There will also be feature enhancements across the portfolio, and one more global product introduction planned later this year,” he said.

While the company plans to introduce electric vehicles, the timing has not yet been decided.

“The question for us is not so much about timing, but about which electric vehicle makes sense for India. For EVs to be successful here, they need to be positioned at the heart of the market in terms of pricing, and that requires a high level of localisation. That is what we are working towards,” Mr. Gupta said.

“Globally, Skoda has a proven electric portfolio, including products like the Enyaq and the Elroq, which are among the best-selling EVs in Europe. However, given the current taxation structure and uncertainty around free trade agreements, introducing fully built units in India does not make strategic sense at this stage,” he said.

Skoda Auto India on Tuesday introduced the new Kushaq, for which pre-bookings have opened, with deliveries scheduled for late March 2026. The Kushaq has driven the company’s growth surge in India.

Klaus Zellmer, CEO of Skoda Auto, said, “The updated Kushaq reinforces the importance of India as the springboard for Skoda Auto’s strategy to grow our international markets. The Kushaq has rapidly established itself with customers in India and as an export to ASEAN and the Middle East.”

“Now we are setting the next benchmark for the model’s overall value proposition. This update incorporates Modern Solid design elements as well as a broad range of advances from the infotainment and driver assistance features, offering even greater comfort and safety,” he said.

“Together with the Kodiaq and the Kylaq, Skoda Auto offers an SUV fleet on the Indian market that caters to significant segments and price points. Taking the Kushaq to the next level creates the opportunity for additional demand and further growth in our most important market outside Europe,” he added.

Mr. Gupta said, “At Skoda, our mission is to democratise European technology and make it more accessible to customers across India. Today, boundary lines between cities and regions are blurring, and aspirations are merging. We are meeting these aspirations by launching products that cater to these evolving customer preferences.”

“With the premiere of the new Kushaq today, we further build our legacy of having a class-leading range of ‘real automatics’ across our portfolio, offering an SUV that comes with the most important safety, comfort, design and convenience features as standard, led by our proven European engineering,” he added.

Once fully completed, H2Offices will offer approximately 67,000 square meters of modern office space in total. The development is surrounded by a landscaped environment at one of Budapest's busiest business locations.

The completed façade follows the architectural design of the wider H₂Offices complex while incorporating measures intended to improve energy efficiency and long-term performance.

Skanska describes Phase 2 as a planned Zero Emission Building project. Its energy strategy combines efficient building systems, heat pumps for year-round use, rooftop photovoltaic panels and low primary energy demand.

During operation, the building’s energy needs are intended to be met entirely through on-site renewable generation and certified renewable electricity backed by Guarantees of Origin. Skanska says this approach is intended to deliver zero market-based Scope 2 emissions associated with purchased energy.

The development is targeting LEED Platinum, WELL Platinum and Access4You Gold certifications, covering environmental performance, occupant well-being and accessibility.

evidence.title: Skanska invests EUR 66M in sustainable Nowy Format office project in Kraków
evidence.text:
Skanska invests EUR 66M in sustainable Nowy Format office project in Kraków

An announcement from Skanska AB ( ($SE:SKA.B) ) is now available.

Skanska is expanding its sustainable office portfolio in Central Europe with a major new project in Kraków, Poland, reinforcing its role as a leading global construction and project development group. The company continues to focus on environmentally certified, tenant-friendly office buildings that align with EU Taxonomy criteria and broader decarbonization goals.

Skanska will invest about EUR 66 million, roughly SEK 720 million, in the first phase of the Nowy Format office complex, booking a PLN 140 million construction contract in Europe in the third quarter of 2026. The initial nine-storey building, Nowy Format A1, will provide 21,400 square meters of leasable space, extensive gardens and terraces, and operate without connection to the city heating network, relying on heat pumps and 100 percent renewable electricity.

The development is designed to secure LEED and WELL Core & Shell certifications, as well as a Building without Barriers designation, underscoring Skanska’s focus on sustainability and accessibility. Located on a former printing plant site in central Kraków, with strong tram links and airport access, the three-building complex will ultimately offer around 48,000 square meters of office space, with construction of the first building starting in late 2026 and completion slated for the third quarter of 2028.

This investment strengthens Skanska’s presence in Poland’s office market and supports its strategy of delivering energy-efficient, high-quality workplaces in prime urban locations. The combination of green amenities, renewable energy use and compliance with EU Taxonomy criteria is likely to appeal to corporate tenants seeking sustainable offices, enhancing Skanska’s competitive position in European commercial real estate.

The most recent analyst rating on ($SE:SKA.B) stock is a Hold with a SEK270.00 price target. To see the full list of analyst forecasts on Skanska AB stock, see the SE:SKA.B Stock Forecast page .

Skanska AB is one of the world’s largest construction and project development companies, operating across selected markets in the Nordics, Europe and the U.S. With 2025 revenue of SEK 179 billion and a workforce of about 25,900 employees, the group focuses on creating innovative, sustainable real estate and infrastructure solutions. Its commercial development arm in Europe prioritizes environmentally certified office projects that support healthy living and modern workplace needs.

The company leverages its scale and expertise to deliver large, complex projects with a strong emphasis on green building standards and long-term urban development. By integrating renewable energy, advanced certifications and accessibility features, Skanska positions itself as a leader in sustainable construction and office development, aiming to shape how people live, work and connect in major metropolitan areas.

evidence.title: Vinci Energies acquires Bühler Group’s UK automation business
evidence.text:
Vinci Energies acquires Bühler Group’s UK automation business

Vinci Energies in the UK and RoI has acquired Bühler Group’s CDD Automation Solutions – a UK-based systems integrator for the food and feed industry.

Vinci Energies is a global business unit of the Vinci Group, delivering specialised energy, industrial and digital infrastructure services.

It also regularly operates alongside group divisions such as Vinci Construction on major civil infrastructure works.

CDD Automation Solutions was established in 1981 and has been part of the Bühler Group since 1991.

The systems integrator provides “bespoke control systems across major industrial platforms including Rockwell Automation, Siemens, and Aveva”, delivering “project execution, services, upgrades, local automation solutions and 24/7 support for the food industry,” Vinci Energies said.

CDD Automation Solutions, which employs 32 people, will become part of Vinci Energies’ brand called Actemium.

Vinci Energies in the UK & ROI managing director Scott Van Der Vord said: “The acquisition of CDD Automation Solutions underlines our commitment to continue to invest in and build out our automation and control expertise across the United Kingdom and Ireland.

“Ensuring we are well positioned to deliver advanced process optimisation, energy efficiency and manufacturing resilience across multiple sectors.”

He added: “We are pleased to welcome our 32 new colleagues from CDD Automation Solutions into our ecosystem, where they join an established community of more than 230 control systems specialists in the UK.

“A community that continues to thrive on shared learning and expertise, enabling our clients to benefit from a best-of-both-worlds approach – local familiarity with global innovation and support.”

Bühler Group head of region Europe Flavio Diaz said: “Following a strategic decision to focus on Bühler’s core offering, we were pleased to identify Vinci Energies as a suitable home for CDD Automation Solutions given the similarities in business model and values, making this acquisition a great fit for both parties.

“We believe this will give CDD Automation Solutions a strong environment to continue building on its expertise and serving customers under the ownership of Vinci Energies.

“Bühler UK looks forward to continuing working closely with CDD Automation Solutions to service our clients requesting non-standard solutions.”

Image (l-r): Scott Van Der Vord, managing director for Vinci Energies UK & RoI, and Scott Vallette, managing director of CDD Automation Solutions).

evidence.title: VINCI - First Half 2025 Financial Results
evidence.text:
Pierre Anjolras, VINCI’s Chief Executive Officer, made the following comments:

The economic performance of VINCI’s businesses in the first half of 2025 mirrored that of previous years. Despite the turbulent macroeconomic and geopolitical environment, the Group posted a revenue growth, driven by Concessions and Energy Solutions (particularly abroad) as well as an increase in operating earnings across all businesses, in terms of both value and margin. Net income was close to that seen in the first half of 2024, despite the significant increase in the French corporate income tax in 2025. The Board of Directors has decided to keep the interim dividend unchanged with respect to the current financial year.

The infrastructure concessions managed by VINCI recorded solid growth, with passenger numbers increasing at airports and traffic levels rising on motorways, both in France and abroad. The integration of recent acquisitions by VINCI Airports (Edinburgh and Budapest airports) and VINCI Highways (Northwest Parkway of the Denver ring road in the US and Via Cristais in Brazil) took place efficiently. VINCI Autoroutes reached an agreement with the grantor (the French state) regarding investments relating to the good condition of the Escota network at the end of the concession contract in February 2032. Lastly, the Group took part in the consultation led by the French Ministry of Transports as part of the Ambition France Transports summit, relating to the funding of mobility infrastructure in particular after existing motorway concessions contracts expire.

Energy Solutions continued to benefit from highly favourable market trends in electricity generation and transmission infrastructure, data centres, digitalisation of industrial processes and building solutions, but also in business areas related to defence and sovereignty. As a result, business levels were well oriented at VINCI Energies and Cobra IS, particularly in Europe, where the Group strengthened its presence again with further acquisitions of companies with strong local footprints. This healthy growth was accompanied by a further increase in operating margins.

In Construction, where market conditions varied depending on the country and business sector, the focus was maintained on the selective approach to accepting new business and operational excellence at worksites. Combined with acquisitions focused on the most promising areas of expertise and geographical regions, this strategy led to an improvement in VINCI Construction’s operating margin, although its revenue fell slightly. In property development, while demand continued to fall in both the residential and non-residential segments in France, VINCI Immobilier returned to profit.

The Group’s order book, which was already very strong, increased further as the level of order intake exceeded that of revenue. Order intake in flow business, which accounts for the vast majority of the Group’s revenue in Energy Solutions and Construction, is still well oriented. Thus, VINCI can look to the future with serenity, while remaining selective and continuing to prioritise margins over volumes.

Regarding external growth, the main transactions completed or announced since the start of the year concerned VINCI Energies, particularly in Germany, and VINCI Construction in the United Kingdom. Among other highlights, it is worth mentioning the financial closing by Cobra IS of the first public-private partnership (PPP) in electricity transmission in Australia and the new photovoltaic facilities entering into service in Brazil, taking total renewable energy production capacity to 1.2 GW.

The excellent overall performance of VINCI’s businesses in the first half of 2025 once again demonstrates the strength of the Group’s “multi-local” model and its highly decentralised organisation, its ability to adjust quickly to market developments, and its resilience. Driven by a long-term vision, VINCI is well prepared to deal with unforeseen events and to continue delivering all-round performance encompassing success in both financial and non-financial terms.

VINCI’s Board of Directors, chaired by Xavier Huillard, met on 30 July 2025 to approve the consolidated financial statements for the six months ended 30 June 2025. 6

The Board approved a 2025 interim dividend of €1.05 per share – unchanged compared with last year – to be paid on 16 October 2025.

The changes set out below are relative to the first half of 2024 unless otherwise stated.

VINCI’s financial statements for the first half of 2025 show an increase both in revenue and operating earnings. Net income attributable to owners of the parent saw only a limited decline in the face of the increase in the French corporate income tax for 2025. Free cash flow was slightly positive despite the normal seasonal decline in the operational cash position in the first part of the year.

Consolidated revenue rose by 3.2% to €34.9 billion (organic growth of 1.2%, a 2.5% positive impact from changes in the consolidation scope and a 0.5% negative impact from exchange rate movements).

Concessions revenue totalled €5.7 billion, up 7.7% on an actual basis and 5.7% on a like-for-like basis, and broke down as follows:

ENERGY SOLUTIONS: €13.7 billion (up 6.2%)

Energy Solutions revenue totalled €13.7 billion, up 6.2% on an actual basis and up 4.2% on a like-for-like basis, with faster growth in the second quarter (up 6.5% actual and up 5.1% like-for-like). That revenue was driven by business outside France, which accounted for 69% of total Energy Solutions revenue and grew by 7.9% on an actual basis and 5.2% on a like-for-like basis these first six months. This semester confirmed the strong position of VINCI Energies and Cobra IS in markets that are being driven in particular by the energy transition, digital transformation and the focus on defence and sovereignty. In addition to those trends, there is the positive effect of the bolt-on acquisitions that VINCI Energies is continuing to make in order to improve its geographical coverage and bolster its expertise.

All four of VINCI Energies’ business lines (Infrastructure, Industry, Building Solutions and ICT 12 ) achieved revenue growth.

Outside France (58% of the total), revenue came to €5.9 billion, up 7.5% on an actual basis and up 2.7% on a like-for-like basis (including a 3.9% like-for-like increase in the second quarter). Revenue growth was particularly strong in Germany – VINCI Energies’ largest market outside of France (€1.6 billion) – as well as in the Netherlands (€0.7 billion), Switzerland, Morocco and the United States.

In France (42% of the total), revenue was €4.2 billion, up 2.2% on an actual basis and 1.8% on a like-for-like basis.

Revenue from flow business (59% of the total) rose by 3%. Trends are well oriented in Europe – particularly in Spain and Portugal – and in Brazil.

In EPC 13 projects (41% of the total), the strong 18% increase in business levels was due to the ramp-up of turnkey projects to build HVDC 1 3 converter platforms and the first regasification terminal in Germany, where business levels have doubled. In addition, there were the revenue contributions of projects to install high-voltage power transmission lines in Brazil, and the start of a large-scale power transmission contract in Australia as part of a PPP.

This change reflects varying market conditions depending on the country and business sector:

Ebitda amounted to €6.1 billion, equal to 17.6% of revenue, as opposed to €5.7 billion and 16.8% in the first half of 2024. The Concessions business generated Ebitda of €3.9 billion, accounting for 63% of the Group total, including:

The Energy Solutions business generated Ebitda of €1.3 billion, accounting for 21% of the Group total, including:

Finally, Ebitda in the Construction business totalled €0.8 billion, 16 up €0.1 billion year on year.

Operating income from ordinary activities (Ebit) rose to €4.1 billion from €3.9 billion in the first half of 2024, and broke down as follows:

Consolidated net income attributable to owners of the parent was €1.9 billion (€2.0 billion in the first half of 2024). The decrease was limited despite the higher corporate income tax in France, which had a negative impact of €297 million in the first half of 2025. 17 The decline in earnings per share 18 was smaller (down 3.5% from €3.46 in the first half of 2024 to €3.34 in the first half of 2025), because of VINCI’s share buy-back policy.

On a constant taxation basis – i.e. excluding the impact of the higher corporate income tax in France 17 – net income attributable to owners of the parent would have risen by almost 10% to €2.2 billion (€3.86 18 per share).

Free cash flow was slightly positive at €46 million (€361 million in the first half of 2024), although it should be noted that most of the Group’s free cash flow is generated in the second half of the year. 19

Consolidated net financial debt totalled €23.3 billion at 30 June 2025, up €2.9 billion relative to 31 December 2024 and almost unchanged over 12 months (€23.4 billion at 30 June 2024).

VINCI Autoroutes’ traffic levels rose by 2.3% in the second quarter of 2025, including a 2.7% increase for light vehicles and a 0.4% decrease for heavy vehicles. Traffic levels were particularly strong in the month of June. 20

In the first half of 2025 as a whole, traffic levels were up 2.2% (light vehicles up 2.5% and heavy vehicles up 0.6%).

Passenger numbers at VINCI Airports continued to grow in almost all of the network’s 14 countries, and growth accelerated overall in the second quarter. This positive momentum is due in particular to low-cost airlines increasing their capacity, along with strong customer demand, resulting in high load factors. Overall, the 72 airports in the VINCI Airports network welcomed more than 159 million passengers 21 during the period, an increase of 6.4% compared to the first half of 2024 (6.0% in the first quarter and 6.7% in the second).

There were remarkable increases in passenger numbers in Japan, Mexico and at Budapest airport, and numbers also rose in Portugal and at Edinburgh airport, driven in particular by the development of long-haul routes. On the downside, uncertainty in the United States affected passenger numbers at airports in the Dominican Republic and Costa Rica.

Order intake at VINCI Energies, Cobra IS and VINCI Construction totalled €31.9 billion, down €2 billion compared with the first half of 2024. As mentioned in previous publications, this decrease was due to a high base for comparison. Apart from two orders totalling €2.5 billion recorded by Cobra IS in early 2024 – for offshore windfarm energy converter platforms in Germany – the Group had won a number of large contracts in the first half of 2024. 22 However, order intake in flow business – which accounts for the vast majority of revenue for VINCI’s Construction and Energy Solutions businesses – rose by 2%.

Nevertheless, it is important to note that order intake in the first half of 2025 remained higher than revenue for the same period for Energy Solutions (€15.6 billion vs €13.7 billion) and for VINCI Construction (€16.3 billion vs €15.2 billion).

Accordingly, the Group’s order book grew again, rising to €71.3 billion at 30 June 2025, a 6% increase year on year (up 9% outside France and down 1% in France), representing more than 14 months of average business activity. France accounts for 29% of the order book, Germany 19% and the rest of the world 52%.

In the French property development sector, VINCI Immobilier saw the number of housing unit reserved fall by 14% to 2,081 units in the first semester. Bulk sales to social and institutional investors rose, while individual sales fell due in particular to the end of the Pinel tax incentive plan in 2024.

Vinci's Strategic Expansion in Australia: A Gateway to Long-Term Infrastructure Growth

- VINCI secures €431M in Australian infrastructure projects, aligning with government ESG goals and addressing urban mobility challenges.

- Projects include low-carbon concrete and koala conservation plans, enhancing sustainability and biodiversity while reducing emissions by 60%.

- VINCI’s ESG alignment and financial resilience attract investors, leveraging Australia’s $48B infrastructure budget for long-term growth and net-zero targets.

VINCI, a global leader in infrastructure and construction, has positioned itself as a transformative force in Australia's evolving infrastructure landscape. With a series of high-value contracts awarded in 2025, the company is not only deepening its footprint in the region but also aligning its operations with the Australian government's ambitious ESG agenda. For ESG-aligned global investors, VINCI's strategic expansion in Australia represents a compelling opportunity to capitalize on long-term infrastructure growth while supporting sustainability and social responsibility.

VINCI's recent wins in Australia—three major projects totaling €431 million (A$773 million)—underscore its commitment to addressing the country's infrastructure challenges. These projects, spanning Queensland and New South Wales, include the Coomera Connector Stage 1 South (A$410 million), the Moreton Bay Road Upgrade (A$86 million), and the M5 Motorway Westbound Upgrade (A$277 million). Collectively, they aim to alleviate traffic congestion, enhance connectivity, and support urban growth in key economic hubs like the Gold Coast and western Sydney.

The Coomera Connector, for instance, involves constructing a 4.4 km stretch with three bridges, including a 300-meter structure over the Nerang River. This project is designed to reduce reliance on the M1 Pacific Motorway, easing pressure on an aging transportation network. Similarly, the M5 Motorway Upgrade in Sydney will improve safety and accessibility for pedestrians and cyclists, aligning with global trends toward multimodal transport. These projects not only address immediate infrastructure gaps but also future-proof Australia's mobility networks against population growth and climate risks.

VINCI's Australian projects are deeply embedded in the company's global ESG strategy, which prioritizes carbon neutrality by 2050 and a 40% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2030. In Australia, where the Labor government has set a 2030 target of 82% renewable electricity and a 2050 net-zero goal, VINCI's initiatives resonate with national priorities.

VINCI's Australian operations are not just environmentally progressive but also financially robust. In 2024, the company generated €1.4 billion in revenue in Australia, with VINCI Construction contributing €1.2 billion. This strong performance is underpinned by long-term government contracts, stable cash flows, and a diversified portfolio across transport, construction, and energy.

For ESG-focused investors, VINCI's alignment with global standards—such as the Science-Based Targets initiative (SBTi) and the Paris Agreement—adds another layer of appeal. Its ESG Risk Rating (ranked 17 out of 337 in the Construction & Engineering industry) reflects its proactive approach to sustainability. Moreover, VINCI's emphasis on employee ownership and stakeholder engagement fosters accountability and long-term value creation, a critical factor for institutional investors prioritizing governance.

VINCI's expansion in Australia is a strategic bet on a market poised for sustained infrastructure demand. With the Australian government committing A$30 billion to transport projects in its 2024 budget and A$18 billion to renewable energy, VINCI is well-positioned to benefit from this pipeline. For investors, the company's ability to deliver large-scale, ESG-aligned projects while maintaining profitability offers a rare combination of growth and responsibility.

However, risks remain. Regulatory changes, supply chain disruptions, and rising material costs could impact margins. Yet, VINCI's focus on innovation—such as its Leonard platform for climate resilience and partnerships with local stakeholders—mitigates these challenges. Additionally, its alignment with Australia's Net Zero Plan and ESG reporting frameworks ensures transparency and adaptability in a rapidly evolving regulatory landscape.

VINCI's strategic expansion in Australia is more than a commercial move—it's a blueprint for sustainable infrastructure development. By leveraging cutting-edge technology, prioritizing biodiversity, and embedding ESG principles into its projects, VINCI is not only addressing Australia's infrastructure needs but also setting a benchmark for global construction firms. For investors seeking long-term, ESG-aligned opportunities, VINCI's Australian ventures represent a compelling intersection of profit, purpose, and planetary stewardship.

As the world transitions to a low-carbon economy, VINCI's ability to deliver projects that align with both economic and environmental goals will be a key driver of its—and its investors'—success in the decades ahead.

VINCI Announces Leadership Appointments for Airports and Autoroutes Sectors to Strengthen Strategic Growth

VINCI Announces Leadership Appointments for Airports and Autoroutes Sectors to Strengthen Strategic Growth

(IN BRIEF) Nicolas Notebaert, CEO of VINCI Concessions, has announced leadership changes within VINCI Airports and VINCI Autoroutes as part of a strategic restructuring. Sabine Granger has been appointed as the CEO of VINCI Autoroutes, while Rémi Maumon de Longevialle takes over as CEO of VINCI Airports. These appointments are part of VINCI’s efforts to strengthen its leadership and continue providing efficient management across its key infrastructure sectors. Both Granger and Maumon de Longevialle join VINCI Concessions’ Management Committee, further enhancing the company’s leadership team.

(PRESS RELEASE) PARIS, 14-Feb-2025 — / EuropaWire / — Nicolas Notebaert, Chief Executive Officer of VINCI Concessions , has announced a restructuring within the organization, appointing new chief executive officers for VINCI Airports and VINCI Autoroutes, two key sectors where he will continue to serve as President. These changes are part of the ongoing effort to strengthen leadership within the group.

Sabine Granger has been appointed as the new Chief Executive Officer of VINCI Autoroutes , the leading motorway concessionaire in Europe, overseeing the Group’s motorway operations in France, including ASF, Cofiroute, Escota, Arcour, and Arcos. In addition to this role, she has been named Managing Director of Autoroutes du Sud de la France (ASF), following her appointment by the ASF Board of Directors on 4 February 2025. A graduate of Skema Business School, Ms. Granger has dedicated her career to the VINCI Group, beginning in finance within the Construction and Energy divisions before transitioning to VINCI Airports in 2012. She held various operational and managerial positions, including leading Quimper Airport in 2015 and driving several airport concession tenders both in France and internationally. Most recently, she led VINCI Airports’ regional airport operations across France.

Rémi Maumon de Longevialle has been named Chief Executive Officer of VINCI Airports , which, as part of VINCI Concessions, stands as the world’s largest private airport operator, managing over 70 airports. Mr. Maumon de Longevialle brings a wealth of experience, holding engineering degrees from École Polytechnique and ENSAE Paris, as well as a master’s in public policy from Sciences-Po Paris. He began his career at PwC before joining VINCI in 2012, initially working on structured finance within VINCI Concessions. In 2014, he transitioned to VINCI Airports, where he played a key role in its development, eventually serving as Chief Financial Officer starting in 2018.

evidence.title: Bouygues stock draws higher analyst targets after Q2 gains
evidence.text:
Bouygues stock stood at EUR 43.14 on Euronext Paris on September 24, 2026, down 0.25 percent. The latest analyst revisions put the valuation debate beside a sharply improved second-quarter earnings profile.

JPMorgan raised its Bouygues price target from EUR 73 to EUR 75 on September 16, 2026, while maintaining an Overweight rating, according to Yahoo Finance . Morgan Stanley also lifted its target from EUR 53 to EUR 57 and kept an Equal Weight recommendation, according to Bourse Direct .

The two revisions point to a wide range of views rather than a single consensus signal. JPMorgan's EUR 75 target sits EUR 31.86 above the September 24 market price, while Morgan Stanley's EUR 57 target is EUR 13.86 higher.

Bouygues generated EUR 14,087,879,645 in revenue in Q2 2026, compared with EUR 12,229,258,969 in Q1 2026. That represents a sequential increase of 15.2 percent.

Net income reached EUR 381 million in Q2 2026 after a EUR 94,356,918 loss in Q1. Diluted earnings per share moved from a loss of EUR 0.24 in Q1 to EUR 0.99 in Q2, giving the earnings comparison more weight than the modest daily share-price decline.

The Q2 earnings call also highlighted EUR 715 million of operating income, versus EUR 38 million in Q1. The improvement gives the analyst target increases a concrete operating reference, although the share price remained below both revised targets on September 24.

Bouygues stock traded at EUR 43.14 on Euronext Paris on September 24, 2026, with a daily change of minus 0.25 percent. The combination of a softer session and stronger Q2 profit leaves the market price below the EUR 57 and EUR 75 targets discussed by Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan.

evidence.title: Bouygues stock reports profit growth as shares trade at EUR 43.25
evidence.text:
Bouygues (ISIN FR0000120503) reported EUR 287 million in net profit for the first half of 2026, an increase of 65.9 percent from EUR 173 million a year earlier. Shares were trading at EUR 43.25 on Euronext Paris on September 23, 2026, down 0.83 percent from the previous close of EUR 43.61.

StockSentinel reported that Bouygues generated EUR 26.292 billion in H1 2026 sales, down 2.2 percent from EUR 26.870 billion in H1 2025. The contrast between lower revenue and higher earnings points to improved profitability rather than top-line expansion.

Current operating profit from activities, or COPA, rose 4.1 percent to EUR 829 million from EUR 796 million. The group margin increased to 3.2 percent from 3.0 percent, giving the earnings improvement a measurable operating base.

Equans contributed EUR 460 million in COPA during H1 2026 and achieved a 5.2 percent operating margin. Its order book stood at EUR 27.6 billion at June 30, 2026, up 7 percent year over year, making the services division the clearest driver of Bouygues earnings quality.

MarketScreener reported that Bouygues repurchased 263,100 shares from September 7 through September 11, 2026. The transactions followed shareholder authorization granted on April 23, 2026, adding a capital-return element to the earnings picture.

At EUR 43.25 on September 23, 2026, Bouygues had a market capitalization of EUR 16.798 billion. The same session showed an intraday high of EUR 43.74, a low of EUR 43.18 and volume of 82,560 shares, placing the stock near the lower end of its daily range.

MarketScreener lists November 5, 2026, for the third-quarter results. That date gives investors the next scheduled checkpoint for testing whether the H1 margin improvement is carrying into the second half.

evidence.text:
Eiffage stock was trading at EUR 105.25 on Euronext Paris at 10:55 a.m. CET on September 24, 2026, down 0.61 percent on the session. The latest operating figures show revenue growth accompanied by a faster increase in earnings.

In the first half of 2026, Eiffage generated revenue of EUR 12.20 billion, an increase of 2.3 percent from the same period a year earlier, according to Boursorama . The company said growth in its works division supported the first-half performance.

The order book provided a second quantified signal. It reached EUR 31.5 billion at the end of the first half, up 7 percent year over year, with growth across all business lines, the same report said.

Net income attributable to the group climbed 12.1 percent year over year to EUR 342 million in the first half of 2026, according to Boursorama . Earnings therefore grew 9.8 percentage points faster than revenue, a useful distinction for investors assessing operating leverage.

Eiffage confirmed its overall 2026 outlook in the first-half update. The company's results page lists the first half 2026 results and detailed presentation under August 26, 2026, providing the reporting timetable for the figures, Eiffage reports.

The share price of EUR 105.25 on September 24, 2026, puts the daily market move alongside the operating data. The 0.61 percent decline was smaller than the 2.3 percent first-half revenue increase and the 12.1 percent net income gain, leaving earnings delivery as the clearer company-specific measure in this snapshot.

Eiffage is an industrial company active in engineering and construction, with additional operations in concessions, infrastructure and energy systems. Its five reported areas are Construction, Infrastructure, Energy Systems, Concessions and Holding.

evidence.title: Eiffage remporte un second contrat de conversion offshore de 2 GW en Allemagne
evidence.text:
Eiffage, through its Belgian subsidiary Smulders, has won a second contract awarded by 50Hertz, the operator of the transmission system in northern and eastern Germany, for the construction of an offshore conversion station. Smulders operates within the joint venture NSORe (Neptun Smulders Offshore Renewables), owned equally with Neptun Werft, part of the Meyer Werft group, dedicated to high-voltage direct current offshore substations. Several German industrial companies, such as Covestro, which now sources 100 MW of offshore wind power for its German sites , are already relying on this sector to secure their electricity supply. The new contract covers a 2-gigawatt conversion platform for the LanWin3 project in the North Sea.

In June 2026, NSORe, teamed up with Siemens Energy, had already been awarded by 50Hertz the contract to build a 2-gigawatt conversion station for the LanWin6 offshore grid connection project. The new contract follows the same pattern for LanWin3, a project also located in the North Sea. As with LanWin6, Siemens Energy will supply the high-voltage components for the installation. NSORe remains responsible for the full implementation and turnkey delivery of the project.

The contract covers the overall system design, delivery of parts, construction, onshore and offshore installation, and commissioning of the platform. This division of tasks between the two partners mirrors the organization already established for LanWin6. It illustrates the gradual structuring of the offshore substation supply chain in Northern Europe.

Manufacturing split between Germany and the Netherlands

The platform's main components, starting with the topside, which forms its main structure, will be manufactured at the NSORe factory in Rostock-Warnemünde, Germany. Smulders will handle the manufacturing of the steel structures, or jacket foundations, at its Dutch plant in Vlissingen. This geographical split draws on the existing industrial network of the two joint venture partners.

According to Eiffage, the two contracts should enable the production of significant volumes of offshore wind electricity in the North Sea for the German power grid, while strengthening NSORe's position as a partner for offshore wind projects. The French group generated revenue of 25.3 billion euros in 2025, nearly 36% of it outside France, with 87,000 employees. Its subsidiary Eiffage Métal, present at 19 production sites across Europe and active notably in offshore wind and nuclear energy, recorded revenue of 1.7 billion euros in 2025 with 3,450 employees.

evidence.text:
Eiffage stock (ISIN FR0000130452) was trading at EUR 107.68 on Euronext Paris on September 23, 2026, at 3:10 a.m. EDT. The quote showed a daily change of -0.21 percent, leaving the shares up 0.05 percent over five trading days but down 11.97 percent since the start of 2026.

Eiffage reported first-half 2026 revenue of EUR 12.20 billion, an increase of 2.3 percent from EUR 11.93 billion in the first half of 2025. The figures were published in the company results release dated August 26, 2026, carried by Finanzwire .

The increase was not uniform across the group. Eiffage's 2026 outlook calls for slightly higher revenue in contracting and continued growth in its energy systems business, while operating margins are expected to improve, according to the detailed results coverage dated August 26, 2026 from MarketScreener .

The market data put the short-term move in perspective. A 0.05 percent five-day gain contrasts with a 11.97 percent year-to-date decline, so the latest trading pattern has not erased the broader 2026 loss.

For investors, the revenue comparison matters because it pairs modest top-line growth with a more demanding share-price backdrop. The next test is whether the group's margin improvement and contracting growth can translate the confirmed outlook into stronger operating results during the second half of 2026.

Eiffage stock stood at EUR 107.68 on Euronext Paris on September 23, 2026, at 3:10 a.m. EDT. The reference quote was down 0.21 percent on the session, with the year-to-date comparison at -11.97 percent.

evidence.title: Eolien en mer : Eiffage, membre de la co-entreprise NSORe, remporte un second contrat pour une station de conversion offshore HVDC en Allemagne
evidence.text:
Eiffage, au travers de sa filiale belge Smulders, membre de la co-entrerprise NSORe (Neptun Smulders Offshore Renewables), vient de remporter un second contrat attribué par 50Hertz (opérateur du système de transmission du nord et de l’est de l’Allemagne) pour une station de conversion offshore.

NSORe est une co-entreprise détenue à parts égales entre Smulders et Neptun Werft, entité du groupe Meyer Werft, dédiée aux projets de sous-stations offshore HVDC (courant continu haute tension).

En juin 2026, NSORe, en groupement avec Siemens Energy, s’était déjà vu confier par 50Hertz le contrat de construction d’une station de conversion de 2 gigawatts pour le projet de raccordement au réseau offshore LanWin6. Le nouveau marché porte également sur la réalisation d’une plateforme de conversion de 2 gigawatts destinée au projet LanWin3 en mer du Nord.

Comme pour le projet LanWin6, Siemens Energy sera en charge de la fourniture des composants haute tension pour le projet LanWin3 récemment remporté. NSORe est responsable de la mise en œuvre complète et de la livraison clés en main des installations. Le marché comprend la conception du système dans son ensemble, la livraison des pièces, la construction, l’installation à terre et en mer, ainsi que la mise en service.

Les éléments principaux tels que le topside – structure principale de la plateforme offshore, seront fabriqués dans l’usine NSORe de Rostock-Warnemünde. Smulders assurera la fabrication des structures métalliques (fondation jacket) dans son usine de Vlissingen aux Pays-Bas.

Ces deux contrats permettront de produire d’importants volumes d’électricité éolienne offshore en mer du Nord pour le réseau électrique allemand. Ils renforcent par ailleurs le positionnement de NSORe comme partenaire clé des projets éoliens offshore.

evidence.title: Ferrovial stock draws a Hold rating after Kepler downgrade
evidence.text:
Ferrovial stock drew a Hold rating after Kepler Cheuvreux downgraded the company on September 17, 2026. The BME-listed infrastructure group closed at EUR 47.73 on September 18, up 0.19 percent on the session.

According to MarketScreener on September 17, 2026, Kepler Cheuvreux moved its view on Ferrovial to Hold and cut its price target. The report cited a last close of EUR 47.91 and an average target of EUR 61.72, a difference of 28.82 percent.

That comparison is the central market signal. The target remains materially above the cited closing level, yet the rating change puts more weight on valuation and execution than on a simple upside calculation.

Ferrovial's investor relations page identifies the company as a transport and infrastructure operator and lists fiscal year 2025 revenue of EUR 9.6 billion, capitalization of EUR 40.6 billion and total liquidity of EUR 5.1 billion. The same page also lists the September 16, 2026 release about autonomous machinery in airport construction, linking the group's operating profile to large infrastructure projects.

The fiscal year 2025 figures provide the balance sheet context for the rating debate. Revenue of EUR 9.6 billion and liquidity of EUR 5.1 billion show the scale against which the market evaluates concessions, construction activity and new project awards.

Ferrovial's reference close was EUR 47.73 on BME on September 18, 2026, with a 0.19 percent daily gain. The combination of a Hold rating, a EUR 61.72 target and fiscal year 2025 revenue of EUR 9.6 billion leaves valuation and project execution as the clearest points for market assessment.

evidence.title: Nashville’s Traffic Nightmare Is Now a $9.2B Ferrovial (FER)-Led Project
evidence.text:
Nashville’s Traffic Nightmare Is Now a $9.2B Ferrovial (FER)-Led Project

On August 19, Ferrovial (NASDAQ: FER ) announced it had been selected to deliver the I-24 Southeast Choice Lanes, a 26-mile project running between Nashville and Murfreesboro. It is the largest single capital investment in Tennessee's history and the state's first public-private partnership. The price tag is $9.2 billion, though Ferrovial isn't carrying it alone, since its DriveTN consortium also counts Transurban and Tikehau Star Infra as partners.

Choice lanes are familiar ground for Ferrovial, which has replicated the model in Washington, D.C., Charlotte and Dallas-Fort Worth. On Virginia's 66 Express corridor, similar lanes shaved up to 50% off peak-hour travel times. That is the pitch for I-24, a stretch of highway that already ranks among the region's most jammed: drivers who opt in get steadier speeds, and those in the free lanes should see less traffic too.

The business behind the bid looks healthy, too. Ferrovial's July 28 results showed adjusted EBITDA up 21.6% on a like-for-like basis to €746 million over the first six months of the year, with U.S. highways doing most of the lifting. Those roads are sending cash home as well, since Ferrovial received €357 million in dividends from North America. And the construction order book reached an all-time high of €18 billion, so plenty of work is already in hand. The pipeline keeps filling: Ferrovial bid on I-285 East in Georgia in July, and its D35 Highway bid in the Czech Republic was the most cost-effective submitted, with technical evaluation still underway.

Beyond the roads, the balance sheet looks sturdy. Ferrovial ended the first half with €1.3 billion in net cash, excluding infrastructure projects, meaning cash outweighs debt outside those projects. The airport arm is progressing too: Ferrovial has finished funding the $1.1 billion in equity it pledged for New Terminal One at JFK, and construction there is 92% complete.

Start with the line that looks worst on the page. Net profit for the first half of 2026 came in at €258 million, versus €540 million for the same period of 2025. That earlier figure included capital gains from asset rotation, which makes the comparison harsh, but the mismatch is still there: EBITDA climbed while reported profit fell.

Then there is the work itself. Construction turned 3.5% of revenue into adjusted EBIT, right on target, so there isn't much room for a costly overrun on a big job. North America also accounts for 47.9% of the order book, so plenty rides on one region. The $24.8 billion in concession value cited for the project is a figure for Tennessee, not a profit forecast for Ferrovial. And a winning bid is not a finished road: I-24 still has to be financed, built and operated, and the CEO talks in terms of decades.

Twenty-six hedge funds held Ferrovial in the latest quarter, up from 25 the quarter before. A small vote of continued interest, not a stampede. Just 0.97% of the float is sold short. That signals very little organized skepticism. But at 42.55 times forward earnings, as of September 18, the stock already assumes plenty of growth, so a stumble could hurt.

The I-24 win hands Ferrovial another big road built on a model it already knows. Bulls need Tennessee's lanes to deliver time savings like Virginia's while the US highway engine keeps humming, and bears need the profit line to keep trailing EBITDA. For you, the real question is whether a proven playbook can justify a demanding price.

evidence.title: Ferrovial, a pioneer in the use of autonomous machinery for airport construction
evidence.text:
Ferrovial, a pioneer in the use of autonomous machinery for airport construction

Ferrovial, a leading global infrastructure company, is strengthening its commitment to cutting-edge innovation by implementing technologies capable of automating critical tasks on construction sites. The company, through its Construction business unit, is using autonomous machinery and advanced control systems for the first time in the construction of the new runway at Rafael Hern�ndez International Airport in Aguadilla, Puerto Rico. The $239 million dollars project involves the construction of a new runway measuring 3,350 meters in length and 46 meters in width, without interrupting airport operations. To carry out the project, Ferrovial has deployed three compaction rollers that have been technologically adapted to operate autonomously , under the supervision of a single operator. This solution enables the rollers to perform multiple passes within a previously defined area, following planned trajectories. The automation of the machinery allows continuous and precise control of each compaction phase , while helping improve productivity by reducing downtime typically associated with manual operations. One of the key advantages offered by this technology is the ability for a single operator to supervise several machines operating simultaneously. This model facilitates more efficient management of resources on-site and paves the way for new ways of working in which coordination between people and autonomous machinery will become increasingly relevant. By incorporating AI-powered vision systems and obstacle detection technology, the company is further enhancing safety across its operations . With this technology, machinery can automatically stop when people or vehicles are detected, reducing the risk of incidents in high-activity work areas. As these technologies evolve, an increase in collaborative models among construction companies, regulatory agencies, and technology providers is expected, with the goal of creating common standards and accelerating large-scale adoption across the industry.

evidence.title: Ferrovial Uses Digital Technology and AI to Power Long-Term Infrastructure Growth
evidence.text:
Ferrovial Uses Digital Technology and AI to Power Long-Term Infrastructure Growth

Ferrovial, one of the world’s largest infrastructure companies, is transforming how major transportation projects are designed, built, and operated through digital engineering, centralized data management, and artificial intelligence.

The strategy has helped the company reduce project risks, improve efficiency, and strengthen its long-term concession business, which now accounts for the majority of its value.

The company develops, finances, constructs, and operates major assets—including toll highways and airports. Because its revenue depends heavily on infrastructure remaining operational for decades, completing projects on schedule is critical to avoiding construction delays and lost toll income.

To minimize these risks, Ferrovial has standardized digital workflows across its projects using Bentley Systems’ engineering software. Design, construction, and operational teams work from a shared digital environment, eliminating duplicate work, reducing errors, and ensuring that project information remains consistent throughout the entire asset lifecycle.

The approach also enables field teams to access 3D models, update asset information in real time, and prepare infrastructure for long-term maintenance before construction is completed.

Ferrovial also adopted technologies such as drones, LiDAR, and digital engineering platforms to improve productivity and manage large-scale projects with fewer personnel. This strategy recently contributed to winning a new USD 1.5 billion contract on Texas’ Grand Parkway toll road.

Ferrovial is now extending its digital strategy through artificial intelligence. Working closely with Bentley Systems, Ferrovial is exploring Model Context Protocol (MCP) technology, which will allow AI agents to interact directly with engineering software while keeping human experts in control.

evidence.title: ACCIONA Energía Boosts Chile’s Grid Transmission Capacity By 60% Using AI
evidence.text:
ACCIONA Energía has completed an artificial intelligence-based grid digitalization project in Chile that increases electricity transmission capacity by 60% in the southern part of the National Electric System. The project, known as the Transfer Control Automation System, is designed to improve the use of existing transmission infrastructure and support the integration of additional renewable energy.

The system enables the grid to accommodate an estimated 239 GWh of additional wind power generation annually. This amount of clean electricity is equivalent to the yearly consumption of approximately 100,000 households. By increasing the amount of renewable power that can be transmitted through existing lines, the project can reduce the need for electricity from thermal power plants and help lower greenhouse gas emissions.

The technology uses advanced digital, communications, and automation solutions to optimize high-voltage transmission corridors in Chile’s Araucanía and Biobío regions. The system specifically improves transmission capacity along the Mulchén–Santa Clara and Santa Clara–Charrúa corridors, helping address grid constraints that can limit renewable energy generation.

The project involved cooperation among several companies and institutions across Chile’s electricity sector. Grid operators Transelec, Ferrovial, SAESA, CELEO, and Transmisora Sur Andes participated in the initiative, along with renewable energy developers Enel Green Power and WPD. Before implementation, the system underwent extensive testing and validation through computer simulations conducted by the University of Santiago, Chile, in coordination with the National Electric Coordinator.

ACCIONA Energía said the project demonstrates how digital technologies and artificial intelligence can improve the efficiency and flexibility of existing power networks. Instead of relying only on new transmission construction, advanced control systems can help unlock additional capacity from infrastructure already in operation.

The project also adds to ACCIONA’s experience in electricity transmission and smart grid infrastructure. The company has more than two decades of experience designing, financing, constructing, and operating substations and transmission lines. It has delivered more than 70 power grid projects across markets including Spain, Mexico, Kenya, Peru, and Australia.

The Transfer Control Automation System highlights the growing role of digitalization in supporting renewable energy integration. By enabling more wind power to reach consumers through existing infrastructure, the project provides a scalable approach to improving grid capacity, reducing emissions, and supporting Chile’s energy transition.

evidence.title: SIKA DELIVERS 4.0% LOCAL CURRENCY REVENUE GROWTH AND UPGRADES FULL-YEAR GROWTH EXPECTATIONS
evidence.text:
Ad Hoc Announcement Pursuant to Article 53 of the SIX Exchange Regulation Listing Rules

SIKA DELIVERS 4.0% LOCAL CURRENCY REVENUE GROWTH AND UPGRADES FULL-YEAR GROWTH EXPECTATIONS

In the first half of the year, Sika delivered 4.0% revenue growth in local currencies, with organic growth of 2.9%. In the second quarter, both local currency and organic growth accelerated compared to the first quarter, reaching 6.8% and 5.7%, respectively, with each region recording stronger revenue growth.

Thomas Hasler, CEO: “In the first half of the year, Sika delivered improved momentum, with the second quarter building on our good start to the year. Our investments in industry-leading innovation, efficient global manufacturing and sourcing, and our digital transformation allowed us to continue to gain market share throughout the first half of the year. Our focus on delivering a best-in-class customer value proposition and forging strong customer partnerships meant that we outpaced the construction market. As a result of our accelerating leadership in strategically important growth segments such as infrastructure and data centers, we expect to continue outperforming the industry. More and more customers are relying on Sika for their most critical projects because of our expertise and innovative solutions. We continuously innovate to develop and offer industry-leading products, and we partner with customers to deliver the best solutions. Our customer focus allows us to protect our leading margins.”

“The Fast Forward program further strengthens our competitive position and our profitability. We will accelerate innovation, channel investments, digitalization, and strengthen our customer focus while delivering CHF 80 million in cost savings this year.”

“I am extremely proud of the outstanding results of our Global Employee Survey. The engagement score of 88 index points reflects the exceptional motivation and commitment of our employees worldwide. In the first half of the year, our teams once again contributed to our strong results through their dedication and customer focus. Their engagement is the driving force behind Sika’s success.”

“Our year started strongly against a muted market and geopolitical uncertainty. Our continued share gains across our markets enable us to raise our revenue growth guidance from 1–4% to 3–6% in local currencies. We are comfortable with current consensus CHF EBITDA expectations.”

INCREASED MATERIAL MARGIN – EBITDA MARGIN RISES TO 19.0% In the first half of 2026, Sika grew its material margin to 55.7% (2025: 55.1%). The key factors behind this increase were a sustained focus on product innovation, procurement efficiency, and pricing. Half-year EBITDA amounted to CHF 1,063.0 million (2025: CHF 1,070.4 million), representing a margin of 19.0% (2025: 18.9%).

Net profit in the reporting period amounted to CHF 552.1 million (2025: CHF 554.4 million). Operating free cash flow amounted to CHF 139.6 million (2025: CHF 181.9 million).

GAINS IN MARKET SHARE ACROSS ALL REGIONS Sika accelerated local currency growth in the EMEA region (Europe, Middle East, Africa) to 7.7% (2025: 1.9%) in the first half of the year. Eastern Europe in particular recorded strong growth. Germany showed an improved second quarter performance. After a dip in March, the Middle East showed significant momentum in the second quarter and achieved strong double-digit growth, driven by infrastructure investment projects. Across the EMEA region, Sika’s agile and resilient supply chain has proven to be a structural advantage – deepening existing customer partnerships and accelerating new wins.

Sales in local currencies in the Americas region increased by 2.9% (2025: 3.5%). After a slow start to the year, regional performance improved in the second quarter. Infrastructure investments remained at a solid level in the first half of the year. Sika delivered strong growth across new and refurbishment infrastructure projects. Sika’s growing leadership in data center projects drove another period of double-digit growth in this high-performing category. In Canada, Sika delivered strong growth through the first half of the year. Performance was mixed in Latin America, with modest growth overall.

Sales in local currencies in the Asia/Pacific region over the first half of the year decreased slightly by -2.0% (2025: -1.7%). The Chinese construction industry declined by a double-digit percentage, driven by continued weakness in residential construction. Excluding the Chinese construction business, Asia/Pacific posted good organic growth of 7.7%. Growth was strong across most of the region, with India and Southeast Asia being standouts.

IMPLEMENTATION OF FAST FORWARD ON TRACK The implementation of Fast Forward is on track. The company has made targeted structural adjustments in China and introduced efficiency-enhancing measures in other markets. With Fast Forward, Sika is accelerating digital transformation, improving customer service, strengthening its supply chains, driving operational efficiency, and delivering on its ambition to become the digital market leader in the industry. The initiatives under Fast Forward have enabled Sika to handle recent supply chain volatility and fluctuating raw material costs effectively, thereby deepening its relationships with customers.

Sika expects to save around CHF 80 million in the 2026 financial year. The total annual savings of CHF 150 to 200 million will take full effect from 2028.

ACQUISITIONS AND INVESTMENTS In the first half of the year, Sika concluded the acquisition of the leading Swedish mortar manufacturer Finja, strengthening its presence in northern Europe and expanding its cross-selling opportunities across the Nordics. Sika also announced the acquisition of Akkim in the first half of the year, a leading global manufacturer of adhesives and sealants based in Turkey with annual net sales of around CHF 220 million. The closing of the acquisition is expected in the third quarter of 2026.

In the first half of the year, Sika made targeted investments to expand production capacity in growth regions. New plants were opened in Bangladesh (concrete admixtures and mortar), Tanzania (concrete admixtures and mortars for East Africa), Belgium (new plant and technology center for concrete admixtures), Argentina (dry mortar), Colombia (mortar, tile adhesives, and coatings), and the USA, specifically in Florida (concrete admixtures) and New Jersey (mortar). The new highly efficient plant in Florida features the highest level of automation among all Sika admixture plants in the country. In New Jersey, Sika expanded its production capacity in the northeast region, enabling it to supply construction projects locally in major metropolitan areas with high-performance products. With its new plant and technology center for concrete admixtures in Ham, Belgium, Sika is expanding its production and innovation capacity in Europe. Sika also established a new national subsidiary in Kyrgyzstan during the first half of the year, reinforcing its presence in Central Asia. Sika’s global network now comprises 103 national subsidiaries.

OUTLOOK After a strong first half of the year, Sika is raising its sales growth expectations for 2026 to between 3% and 6% in local currencies. For 2026, Sika expects the global market to remain muted. For the year as a whole, Sika expects to achieve an EBITDA margin of 19.0% to 19.5%, and is comfortable with current consensus CHF EBITDA expectations.

The measures taken as part of Fast Forward to increase productivity, accelerate innovation, and digitalize the entire value chain are strengthening Sika’s leading market position and delivering measurable top- and bottom-line results. Sika is confirming its medium-term strategic targets for sustainable and profitable growth as part of Strategy 2028.

SIKA CORPORATE PROFILE Sika is a specialty chemicals company with a globally leading position in the development and production of systems and products for bonding, sealing, damping, reinforcing, and protection in the building sector and industry. Sika has subsidiaries in 103 countries around the world, produces in over 400 factories, and develops innovative technologies for customers worldwide. In doing so, it plays a crucial role in enabling the transformation of the construction and transportation industries toward greater environmental compatibility. In 2025, Sika’s 33,700 employees generated annual sales of CHF 11.20 billion.

“ This strategic decision strengthens Sika’s ability to deliver innovative and sustainable construction solutions for the demanding construction projects of our valued customers. ~ Jim Walther, President and CEO, Sika Corporation USA ”

This unique, closed-loop roof recycling program celebrated its 20 th anniversary in 2025 and has taken back millions of pounds of end-of-life Sika roofing membranes and incorporated back into new roofing products. The new plant should help this recycling program impacts exponentially in the coming years.

evidence.title: SIKA REPORTS FULL-YEAR 2025 RESULTS - EXECUTING PLAN TO ACCELERATE GROWTH
evidence.text:
SIKA REPORTS FULL-YEAR 2025 RESULTS - EXECUTING PLAN TO ACCELERATE GROWTH

Ad Hoc Announcement Pursuant to Article 53 of the SIX Exchange Regulation Listing Rules

SIKA REPORTS FULL-YEAR 2025 RESULTS - EXECUTING PLAN TO ACCELERATE GROWTH

"In 2025, we announced seven bolt-on acquisitions that will create significant value for our shareholders as we rapidly deliver on both the cost and revenue synergies targeted. We also undertook additional investments to expand manufacturing capacity adding efficient supply capabilities in faster growth regions. Through our investments, Sika has a clear roadmap to accelerate future growth, leaning further on our industry-leading product innovation to efficiently solve customer needs.”

"We expect global market conditions in the construction industry to remain muted in 2026, with a continuation of the market trends seen in 2025. While the first half will be softer for the industry, we anticipate improving momentum as the year progresses - and remain confident in Sika's ability to outperform the market by 3% to 6% in local currencies.”

"I want to express my sincere gratitude to all our employees for their exceptional commitment over the past year. Their strong engagement and unwavering support for the many initiatives we pursued made a decisive difference for Sika.”

SIKA DELIVERS SALES GROWTH IN LOCAL CURRENCIES

In 2025, Sika generated sales of CHF 11,201.3 million (2024: CHF 11,763.1 million), down -4.8% year on year. In local currencies, revenues grew 0.6% year on year. The currency effect of -5.4% was primarily attributable to the weak US dollar. The local currency performance reflects continued market share gains in all regions. Organic growth for full year 2025 was -0.4%, +1.2% excluding Chinese construction business; acquisitions contributed 1.0% to sales growth.

INCREASE IN MATERIAL MARGIN AND STRONG CASH CONVERSION

Sika improved its material margin, achieving 54.9% (2024: 54.5%) in 2025. This increase reflects the strong focus on new product innovation while also managing input cost inflation. Profitability at the EBITDA level was impacted by one-off costs related to the Fast Forward investment and efficiency program previously communicated. These costs amounted to CHF 108 million (of which CHF 86 million were recognized in EBITDA) in 2025, reducing EBITDA to CHF 2,064.7 million (2024: CHF 2,269.5 million) and resulting in an EBITDA margin of 18.4%. Adjusted for the one-off Fast Forward costs, the EBITDA margin was 19.2%, underlining the strong profitability of Sika’s core business. The Fast Forward program will deliver a payback through growth and efficiencies in less than two years.

Net profit for 2025 was CHF 1,045.3 million (2024: CHF 1,247.6 million) and operating free cash flow was CHF 1,356.1 million (2024: CHF 1,402.9 million) - which represented a year-on-year improvement in operating free cash flow conversion to 12.1% of sales (2024: 11.9%). Following the strong free cash flow performance, Sika reduced net debt in 2025, reinforcing its strong credit rating.

Sika’s largest region EMEA (Europe, Middle East, Africa) achieved sales growth of 2.2% in local currencies (2024: 7.3%). Business performance was particularly strong in the Middle East and Africa, where Sika recorded double-digit growth. Parts of southern Europe likewise posted solid growth rates. Eastern Europe delivered sequential improvement throughout 2025.

In the Americas region, sales increased by 2.2% in local currencies (2024: 11.2%). Following a strong start to the year, conditions softened in the second half. In the fourth quarter, the longest government shutdown in history had a negative impact on commercial construction activity, as reflected in the weakening of a number of construction sector indicators throughout the quarter. In the USA, data center investment remained a bright spot in 2025, and Canada and Latin America proved to be resilient.

In the Asia/Pacific region, sales declined by -5.3% in local currencies (2024: 2.4%). The results were impacted by the double-digit decline in sales in the Chinese construction business. Excluding China construction business, the region recorded positive organic growth of 2.5%. In China, Sika’s short-term focus is on driving structural adjustments and protecting margins. By contrast, the markets in India and Southeast Asia - as well as the Automotive & Industry segment - recorded dynamic growth.

Through its Fast Forward program, Sika is strengthening the organization for the future. The company is accelerating innovation and digital transformation and is building on its leading position across all markets.

As part of the Fast Forward program, Sika implemented targeted structural adjustments in China and introduced efficiency-enhancing measures in other markets. Efforts are in full swing to optimize the production network and simplify organizational structures to increase efficiency. At the same time, Sika is investing in accelerating the digital transformation of its entire value chain. The investments will run for the duration of the program through to 2028. Sika expects this to generate annual savings of between CHF 150 and 200 million, with the full impact expected in 2028. Around CHF 80 million of these savings are expected to take effect in 2026.

During the year, Sika advanced its ESG performance in line with leading global standards and company ambitions. Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions decreased by -6.1%, while water discharge and waste disposed per ton sold declined by -3.4% and -5.7%, respectively, reflecting disciplined operational execution, tighter process control, and circularity initiatives. A strong safety culture led to reduction in lost time accidents of -14.1%. With products and solutions that reduce carbon footprint and extend lifecycle of buildings, Sika continues to expand its leading role as a technology partner for sustainable construction.

2025 DIVIDEND PROPOSAL AND NEW ELECTIONS TO THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS

At the Annual General Meeting on March 24, 2026, the Board of Directors will propose an increase in the gross dividend per share to CHF 3.70 (+2.8% year on year). Half of the dividend is to be distributed from the reserves from capital contribution.

Barbara Frei and Lukas Gähwiler will be proposed for election to the Board of Directors at the Annual General Meeting on March 24, 2026. Barbara Frei is a former member of the Executive Committee of Schneider Electric. Lukas Gähwiler is Vice Chairman of the Board of Directors of UBS Group AG. Paul Schuler, who has been a member of the Sika Board of Directors since 2021, will not stand for re-election.

Sika is convinced that it can accelerate its growth strategy when the global construction environment improves through the investments made in innovation and digitalization. Sika affirms its medium-term strategic targets for sustainable, profitable growth under the Strategy 2028.

In 2026, Sika expects global market conditions to remain muted, with a low single-digit percentage decline for the year as a whole. While the first half will be softer for the industry, the company anticipates improving momentum as the year progresses.

For 2026, Sika expects sales growth of 1% to 4% in local currencies; in line with company ambition to outperform the market by 3% to 6% in local currencies including bolt-on acquisitions. Sika expects to deliver an EBITDA margin of 19.5% to 20.0% for the year.
