Nestlé considering options after Russia seizes control of subsidiaries

Swiss food giant Nestlé reacted cautiously on Friday to Russia's presidential decree placing two of its subsidiaries under external administration, describing it as a "temporary" move.

According to the decree, published on Thursday, the subsidiaries are to be managed in future by Russian firm LEV Management.

"Nestlé is committed to taking all necessary steps to protect its rights and ensure continuity of business operations in the interests of all stakeholders, particularly its employees," the company said from its headquarters in Vevey on Lake Geneva.

Nestlé produces confectionery, baby food and pet food at six sites in Russia.

Before Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, its Russian business accounted for around 2% of group revenue, which today stands at just over 89 billion francs ($108 billion).

Analysts estimated the value of the Russian business at the equivalent of up to 1.7 billion francs.

Nestlé had not wound down its business following the invasion, arguing that populations in conflict regions also need food.

Other corporations, including French food group Danone, Danish brewery Carlsberg and Dutch company Heineken, had also been placed under state administration in Russia and subsequently sold their businesses.

evidence.title: Carlsberg Britvic and Danone spearhead calls for mandatory health reporting in UK
evidence.text:
Carlsberg Britvic and Danone spearhead calls for mandatory health reporting in UK

15-Sep-2026 Last updated on 15-Sep-2026 at 18:30 GMT

Carlsberg Britvic and Danone North Europe are two of the leading food and drink manufacturers that have backed calls for mandatory health reporting.

They, along with KP Snacks, Nomad Foods and Premier Foods, have stepped up to introduce healthy food and drink sales reporting in the UK from next year.

This is ahead of the UK Government plans for a mandatory system, which would make the UK the first country in the world to introduce mandatory healthy food sales reporting across the food and beverage sector.

They have pledged to use the current Nutrient Profiling Model, which is used for existing High Fat, Sugar and Salt restrictions. The Government has consulted on updating the model and broadening the scope but using this would delay reporting, they said.

Healthier Food Targets and Reporting forms part of the UK Government’s approach to improving population health through prevention.

The soft drinks industry has already faced a clampdown by the UK Government.

The Soft Drinks Industry Levy (SDIL) was introduced in 2018 to target the amount of sugar in soft drinks though a tax system. The UK Government recently announced plans to extend this to milk based drinks and drop the reduce the levy level from 5g per 100ml to 4.5g per 100ml.

Soft drinks taxes are also used in other countries across the globe. Recently, in Germany, over 300 drinks companies , signed a letter opposing plans for a sugar tax on soft drinks.

This latest letter to the Secretary of State for Health and Social Care, the five UK food and drink businesses pledged to publish healthy food sales data and called on government to work with industry to implement a mandatory reporting system for all food and drink businesses.

The food and drink manufacturers, along with trade association The Food and Drink Federation (FDF), highlighted the positive moves already made by the industry.

The FDF said that its members’ products now contain 19% less sugar, 18% less salt and 17% fewer calories than they did five years ago.

The letter said: “We believe that the introduction of mandatory healthy food sales reporting for all large food and drink businesses is critical to support this progress. It will provide consistent data and evidence to inform future policymaking, as well as an incentive to encourage continued investment in healthier food and drink across industry.”

Richard Hall, Vice President General Secretary, Danone North Europe, said: “At Danone, we believe transparency is one of the best ways to drive progress on health and have long chosen to go beyond mandatory health and nutrition reporting requirements.

Hall added: “We welcome this group, which will play an important role in driving greater transparency and consistency in the wider food system. The more we collectively measure and share, the easier it is to see what’s working, where barriers remain and the opportunities to accelerate progress towards better health outcomes.”

Karen Betts, Chief Executive at The FDF, said that the data and transparency that reporting will bring will incentivise companies to “double down on progress” and give the government a valuable tool to measure the impact of health policies.

“In this way, this group of early-movers can test the best ways to collate and report data to support our broader sector and government in informing any future legislation,” she said.

Danone completes its acquisition of Huel, extending its portfolio in Functional Nutrition

Press release – Paris, September 4, 2026, 6:00 PM CEST

Danone completes its acquisition of Huel, extending its portfolio in Functional Nutrition

Danone announces today that it has successfully completed its acquisition of Huel, a leading player in complete, nutritionally balanced meal solutions.

By combining the direct-to-consumer and community engagement capabilities of Huel with the scale and global reach of Danone, more consumers will have access to nutritionally complete and convenient, sustainable food.

Huel will be consolidated in Danone's financial statements from September 1, 2026.

Antoine de Saint-Affrique, Danone SA Chief Executive Officer said:

"Today we are happy to officially welcome Huel to the Danone family. Together, we will unlock and fuel new opportunities for growth by extending the reach of Huel's market-leading products with our global scale and scientific credibility. The unique expertise they bring in the field of consumer and community engagement will also further strengthen our capabilities.

James McMaster, Huel's Chief Executive Officer said:

"After a decade building the Huel brand, we begin the next step in Huel's journey. With Danone, our ambition is to be even more relevant to our loyal customers and win a new following in new places around the world."

Huel is a global leader in complete, nutritionally balanced meals, offering a broad range of products including powders, ready‑to‑drink shakes, Hot & Savory meals, nutrition bars, supergreens and functional beverages. Built on a science‑driven formulation approach, all Huel products provide essential macronutrients and micronutrients in convenient, plant‑based formats. With a predominantly direct‑to‑consumer model and best‑in‑class digital capabilities, Huel has developed a highly engaged community and strong brand advocacy. Its portfolio is designed to deliver sustainable, accessible nutrition that supports modern, active lifestyles.

Danone is a leading global food and beverage company operating in three health-focused, fast-growing and on-trend Categories: Essential Dairy & Plant-Based products, Waters and Specialized Nutrition. With a long-standing mission of bringing health through food to as many people as possible, Danone aims to inspire healthier and more sustainable eating and drinking practices while committing to achieve measurable nutritional, social, societal and environmental impact. Danone has defined its Renew strategy to restore growth, competitiveness, and value creation for the long-term. With c.90,000 employees, and products sold in over 120 markets, Danone generated €27.3 billion in sales in 2025. By supporting FoodCorps and the American Heart Association, Danone is Furthering American Health and Nutrition

WHITE PLAINS, N.Y. and LOUISVILLE, Colo. , Sept. 4, 2025 /PRNewswire/ -- Danone North America today announced expanded support of nutrition and health education through national sponsorships with FoodCorps and the American Heart Association . Aligned with its mission to bring health through food to as many people as possible, Danone is sponsoring or supporting these organizations to help increase access to nourishing foods and to deliver nutrition education that empowers families across the U.S. to make healthy choices.

"As a leading food and beverage company, we know that we play a critical role in supporting the health of our communities across the US and Canada , which is why we're committed to increasing access to and education about nutrient-dense food," said Dan Magliocco , President of Danone North America. "We support mission-aligned organizations like FoodCorps and the American Heart Association because meaningful health outcomes happen when we work together to provide tools and education that empower lasting change."

Fueling Impact through Strategic Nutrition Initiatives

Danone's work with FoodCorps and the American Heart Association are part of a broader nutrition strategy rooted in its global Danone Impact Journey (DIJ) — an enterprise-wide action plan to help improve health outcomes through food access, nutrition science & research and community-rooted partnerships.

Danone North America recognizes the importance of and has long advocated for good childhood nutrition. The company is already reducing sugar in family favorites like Danimals pouches and Danonino cups. Danone North America is also advancing kids' and families' nutrition via innovations like Silk Kids Oatmilk Blend, including key nutrients for growing kids.

In addition to these new sponsorships, Danone continues to support public health through its long-standing support for the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants and Children (WIC), helping ensure families can access nutritious options like yogurt, plant-based foods and baby food.

Together, these actions underscore how Danone is supporting the health of families and communities across the country.

Building on a 2023 commercial pilot, Danone and FoodCorps have strengthened their partnership to deliver hands-on nutrition education and nourishing foods to students nationwide. In the 2023-2024 school year, Danone helped FoodCorps reach more than 500,000 students with cooking lessons, taste tests, school gardens and more.

"We're proud to partner with Danone, whose deep commitment to nutrition access and innovation mirrors our own," said Curt Ellis FoodCorps co-founder and CEO. "Our work together is about more than shifting what's on the lunch tray — it's about shifting systems and building a future where every child is nourished, supported and equipped to make informed choices about their food."

As part of their shared commitment, Danone and FoodCorps are activating programming like taste tests, garden education and community events. At a recent "Spring Festival" day in Newark, New Jersey , more than 130 students engaged in Silk Soymilk sampling, education and garden explorations.

The organizations are also partnering on an omni-channel " Return to Routine " shopper marketing activation running through September 15 . This campaign features Silk Kids Oatmilk Blend, Happy Tot products, Too Good & Co. pouches and Danimals drinks, aligning with the back-to-school season. Designed to help kids and parents eat, feel and do good with quality products, the activation will also include a $250,000 donation to FoodCorps in support of their Nourishing Futures initiative.

Scaling Impact with the American Heart Association

Danone is also a national supporter of the American Heart Association's Healthy for Good™ initiative, which delivers practical nutrition tips, heart-healthy recipes and simple food guidance to communities nationwide.

As part of this support, Danone is helping advance the initiative's efforts, educating around smart ingredient swaps to make healthy eating more delicious, doable and affordable. The program sponsorship helps create and promote engaging, accessible content that highlights simple changes families can make in their everyday meals to help reduce saturated fat and support balanced nutrition.

One example of a smart swap from the American Heart Association's Smart Swap Guide suggests using plain, fat-free Greek yogurt instead of full-fat sour cream or mayonnaise to reduce saturated fat without sacrificing flavor. These kinds of practical choices reflect the goals of Healthy for Good™, which encourages small changes that can lead to meaningful, lasting health outcomes.

"The American Heart Association is committed to longer, healthier lives for everyone, everywhere; that starts with small steps," said Dr. Eduardo Sanchez . Chief Medical Officer for Prevention for the American Heart Association. "Healthy for Good equips people with practical, science-based resources to live healthier every day. With the support of partners like Danone, we can reach more families with tools to eat smart, move more and reduce stress."

As a proud supporter of Healthy for Good™ , Danone is helping make actionable, science-backed nutrition guidance more accessible — supporting people on their journey to better health.

Danone North America is a purpose-driven company and an industry leader in the food and beverage category. As a Certified B Corporation ® , Danone North America is committed to the creation of both economic and social value, while nurturing natural ecosystems through regenerative agriculture. Our strong portfolio of brands includes: Activia ® , DanActive ® , Danimals ® , Dannon ® , evian ® , Follow Your Heart ® , Happy Family ® Organics, International Delight ® , Light + Fit ® , Oikos ® , Silk ® , So Delicious ® Dairy Free, STōK ® Cold Brew Coffee, Too Good & Co™, and YoCrunch ® . With approximately 6,000 employees and 14 production locations across the U.S. and Canada , Danone North America's mission is to bring health through food to as many people as possible. For more information on Danone North America, visit danonenorthamerica.com.

evidence.text:
Danone and Kate Farms to join forces to serve people with health needs across both medical and everyday nutrition

Press release - Paris, May 12, 2025, at 7:00 A.M. CEST

to serve people with health needs across both medical and everyday nutrition

Danone announced today that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire a majority stake in Kate Farms, a fast-growing U.S. business offering a wide array of plant-based, organic nutrition products for both medical and everyday needs. Kate Farms' highly complementary products will enhance Danone's specialized nutrition offerings.

The partnership builds on Danone and Kate Farms' shared commitment to offer nutritional solutions that positively impact people's health, and their continued efforts to support improved standards of care to better serve communities in the United States. Kate Farms' trusted nutrition products will reach more consumers and patients, bringing high-quality nutrition to more people with a wide range of health needs.

Following the closing of the transaction, Kate Farms' Chief Executive Officer, Brett Matthews, will serve as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Danone's North American Medical Nutrition business. Kate Farms' senior management will retain a minority stake in the combined business.

The transaction remains subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory approval.

Brett Matthews, Kate Farms' Chairman and Chief Executive Officer said:

"Kate Farms is focused on helping people live their best lives through quality nutrition. We are excited to be working alongside Danone, who share our mission. We are both focused on going above and beyond to help people with health needs and the medical professionals supporting those needs in the U.S. Together, we can bring our innovative scientifically developed nutritional products to more and more people. Building on Danone's expertise, we can also expand internationally. It is rare that two companies come together by virtue of the same values and a philosophy of building a growth company that helps people live their best lives, delivered by team members who show their heart and expertise every day. As a business founded on and guided by deeply held values, it was important for us to partner with an organization that is aligned with our mission in this way, and we believe Danone is the perfect fit to continue to make nutrition the foundation of health. ”

Shane Grant, Danone Group Deputy CEO, CEO Americas said:

"We are thrilled to join forces with Kate Farms and are looking forward to welcoming Brett and his team to Danone. This partnership aligns perfectly with our science-based and patient-centered approach to specialized nutrition, and it marks another important milestone in Danone's 125-year Specialized Nutrition history. Kate Farms' innovative medical nutrition products expand our offerings, enhance our ability to provide better solutions for people with wide-ranging health needs, and support healthier lives, both in the U.S. and globally.

With a deep 80-year heritage and over 5,000 team members in the U.S., Danone has built a thriving local presence across the country. This new partnership further builds on that footprint and enhances our commitment to the growth of our communities.”

With a long-standing mission of bringing health through food to as many people as possible, Danone aims to inspire healthier and more sustainable eating and drinking practices while committing to achieve measurable nutritional, social, societal and environment impact. Danone has defined its Renew strategy to restore growth, competitiveness, and value creation for the long-term. With over 90,000 employees, and products sold in over 120 markets, Danone generated €27.4 billion in sales in 2024. Danone's portfolio includes leading international brands (Actimel, Activia, Alpro, Aptamil, Danette, Danio, Danonino, evian, Nutricia, Nutrilon, Volvic, among others) as well as strong local and regional brands (including AQUA, Blédina, Bonafont, Cow & Gate, Mizone, Oikos and Silk). Listed on Euronext Paris and present on the OTCQX platform via an ADR (American Depositary Receipt) program, Danone is a component stock of leading sustainability indexes including the ones managed by Moody's and Sustainalytics, as well as MSCI ESG Indexes, FTSE4Good Index Series, Bloomberg Gender Equality Index, and Access to Nutrition Index. Danone's ambition is to be B Corp TM certified at global level in 2025.

Kate Farms was founded when a little girl named Kate was failing to thrive because she couldn't tolerate any of the available tube feeding formulas. Her determined parents, Richard and Michelle, had the transformative idea to develop a formula using high-quality, organic, and plant-based ingredients without the common allergens and ingredients often found in traditional formulas. In 2015, Brett Matthews partnered with Richard and Michelle and became Chairman and CEO to build a great team of people and bring Kate Farms into healthcare to help people with health conditions.

Kate Farms provides nutritional formulas and shakes for children and adults, intended for both oral and tube feeding, whether as sole-source or supplemental nutrition. They are available nationally and eligible for insurance coverage with Medicare, Medicaid, private insurance, and in 33+ states for WIC†. All formulas and shakes are made with organic pea protein, fiber, and phytonutrients, and without the top nine allergens, artificial sweeteners, colors, or flavors. Today, Kate Farms can be found in more than 1,400 U.S. hospitals, online at www.katefarms.com , Amazon, and in select retail stores. For more information on our full product portfolio, visit www.katefarms.com .

Minority investors in Kate Farms include Novo Holdings, Goldman Sachs, Kaiser Ventures, Main Street Advisors, Coefficient, Aliment Capital, and Ithaka.

†WIC is a registered service mark of the U.S. Department of Agriculture for USDA's Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children.

Danone: 2025 Danone Shareholders’ Meeting: approval of all resolutions

Press Release – Paris, April 24, 2025, at 5:35 PM CEST

2025 Danone Shareholders' Meeting: approval of all resolutions

Danone's Shareholders' Meeting was held today, chaired by Gilles Schnepp, Chairman of the Board of Directors. 72.66% of Danone's total outstanding share capital was present or represented in this Shareholders' Meeting.

Danone's shareholders approved all the resolutions put to the vote, including the statutory and consolidated financial statements for the 2024 fiscal year, the renewal of the existing financial authorizations, and the distribution of a dividend of €2.15 per share in cash, up +2.4% compared to last year. The ex-dividend date (or ex-date) is set on May 5, 2025, and the dividend will be payable on May 7, 2025.

In addition, the Shareholders' Meeting approved the proposed renewals of terms of office of Antoine de Saint-Affrique, Chief Executive Officer, as well as Patrice Louvet, Géraldine Picaud and Susan Roberts, independent Directors.

This Shareholders' Meeting was the opportunity to present Danone's strategy, its development perspectives and the 2024 fiscal year's highlights, including the commitments and priorities implemented as part of its sustainability journey.

The presentations made during the Shareholders' Meeting and the answers to all written questions sent by shareholders are available on Danone's corporate website ( www.danone.com ). The detailed voting results per resolution and the video webcast of the Shareholders' Meeting will be available on the website on April 25, 2025 at the latest.

Continuation of the global Employee Share Subscription Plan: in parallel with the French employee shareholding plan implemented again this year, the Board of Directors decided to continue in 2025 its capital increase program reserved to employees working for Danone foreign subsidiaries or in a situation of international mobility within the Group, launched in 2019. Under this program, eligible employees of Danone foreign entities were able to subscribe to new shares with a 30% discount of the reference price. The subscription period took place in March 2025. The capital increase reserved for international employees was opened to around 85% of Danone employees worldwide, working in 48 different countries. The new shares will be listed under the same code as the existing Danone shares (ISIN code: FR0000120644) and will be fungible with those shares from their admission to trading.

evidence.title: Unilever Embraces AI for Beauty Innovation
evidence.text:
Unilever is increasingly using artificial intelligence (AI) to transform the way it develops new beauty and personal care products. The company is using AI, automation, and machine learning to make research and product development faster, more efficient, and more competitive.

Unilever’s Beauty & Wellbeing division is one of the company’s important areas for future growth. The division includes well-known brands such as Dove, Vaseline, Dermalogica, and Nutrafol. It generated around EUR 12.8 billion in revenue by 2025, highlighting its importance to Unilever’s overall business.

The company is using AI across different stages of product development. These technologies help teams analyze information, test ideas, improve formulations, and speed up decision-making. As a result, processes that previously took several days can now be completed much faster.

One major improvement has been seen in product formulation. According to the company, formulation cycles that once took five or six days have been reduced to just one or two days. This allows researchers and product teams to test and improve products more quickly.

AI is also helping Unilever reduce the time needed to turn an initial idea into a finished product. The company has reported a 75% improvement in the time required for generating product claims. Faster processes can help Unilever respond more quickly to changing consumer preferences and new trends in the beauty market.

The use of AI could also allow employees to spend more time on creative and strategic work instead of repetitive tasks. By combining human expertise with advanced technology, Unilever aims to develop products more efficiently while maintaining quality.

As competition in the global beauty and personal care market continues to increase, technology is becoming an important tool for major companies. Unilever’s growing use of AI shows how traditional consumer goods businesses are adopting new technologies to accelerate innovation and support long-term growth.

evidence.title: Colman’s Mustard put up for sale as Unilever seeks to clear £48bn McCormick deal
evidence.text:
Colman’s Mustard put up for sale as Unilever seeks to clear £48bn McCormick deal

Colman’s Mustard, one of Britain’s best-known food brands, is being put up for sale as Unilever seeks to clear a potential regulatory obstacle to its planned £48bn combination with US spice maker McCormick.

Unilever has appointed Rothschild bankers to oversee the sale of Colman’s and its associated assets, according to people familiar with the matter. The decision reflects concerns that transferring the brand to McCormick could create competition problems because the US group already owns French’s Mustard.

The planned transaction would combine Unilever’s food business with McCormick to create a global food powerhouse, with brands including Marmite and other major Unilever food products expected to form part of the enlarged group.

Advisers to Unilever concluded that retaining Colman’s within the transaction could give competition authorities grounds to challenge the deal, given the overlap between Colman’s and French’s in the mustard market.

The UK Competition and Markets Authority and the US Federal Trade Commission are expected to scrutinise the wider transaction for potential anti-competitive effects. Divesting individual brands or business units is a common remedy when regulators identify competition concerns in large mergers.

By offering Colman’s separately, Unilever is seeking to address the issue before it threatens the broader transaction.

The sale would mark a significant change for a brand with unusually deep British roots. Colman’s traces its origins to 1814, when Jeremiah Colman, a flour miller, began grinding mustard seed at a watermill in Bawburgh, Norfolk.

A later member of the Colman family introduced the brand’s distinctive bull’s head logo, intended to convey both the mustard’s fiery strength and its association with British beef.

The company received a Royal Warrant from Queen Victoria in 1866, cementing its status as one of Britain’s best-known food manufacturers.

Colman’s remained part of Reckitt and Colman, once a major British consumer goods group, until Unilever acquired the brand in 2005.

Its identity has also become closely associated with Norwich. Colman’s signature yellow is reflected in Norwich City FC’s colours, while the company sponsored the football club’s shirts during the 1990s.

The prospect of the brand changing hands again has already prompted concern among analysts and consumer-goods observers, particularly given the possibility of another American owner.

Colman’s has never been owned outside Britain during its 212-year history, making a sale to an overseas buyer potentially significant for a brand that has become embedded in British food culture.

The planned disposal comes as Unilever seeks to separate its food operations into a larger business with McCormick, a transaction that would reshape the global packaged-foods industry.

The combined company would bring together some of the industry’s best-known brands, but the presence of two major mustard businesses under the same ownership would have presented an obvious regulatory challenge.

A Unilever spokesman confirmed the decision to sell.

“A decision has been taken to market the Colman’s brand and assets to potential buyers in order to proactively seek to address potential competition concerns from the planned combination of Unilever Foods and McCormick.”

The sale process could therefore determine the future ownership of one of Britain’s most recognisable food brands, while allowing Unilever to pursue its much larger strategic transaction with fewer regulatory complications.

The relative weakness was driven mainly by underexposure to semiconductors and technology hardware, while software, cloud services, and financial holdings also weighed on performance. The strategy benefited from holdings in areas tied to AI infrastructure, with semiconductor exposure and AI-related investments gaining from strong demand. Looking ahead, Brown Advisory sees an attractive environment for active stock-picking, with its ready-to-buy list at its highest level since the COVID-19 period and an estimated 12%-13% average five-year base-case IRR, while maintaining a focus on quality, valuation discipline, and long-term cash-flow generation. In addition, please check the Fund's top five holdings to know its best picks in 2026.

In its second-quarter 2026 investor letter, Brown Advisory Global Leaders Strategy Fund highlighted stocks like Unilever PLC (NYSE: UL ). evidence.title: ‘A marketer’s dream’: Unilever’s Ryu Yokoi on intelligence as a real driver of brand growth
evidence.text:
‘A marketer’s dream’: Unilever’s Ryu Yokoi on intelligence as a real driver of brand growth

In the latest edition of The Brand Growth Drumbeat video series, Unilever’s Ryu Yokoi and Kantar’s Jeff Greenspoon explore why growth in the AI era belongs to brands turning intelligence, consistency and cultural relevance into long-term ‘meaningful difference’.

Sponsored content is created for and in partnership with an advertiser and produced by the Drum Studios team.

$13 trillion. 12 zeros. That’s the total value of the world’s top 100 brands, according to this year’s Kantar BrandZ Global Top 100 – reaching an all-time high after growing 22% year on year.

Last year, Apple was the only Top 100 brand with a value of over $1tn. Now, there are four: with Google, Apple, Microsoft and Amazon (in that order) exceeding the mark. Nvidia, in fifth place in the ranking, comes close at nearly $815bn.

And while it’s been a strong decade overall for the Global Top 100, the results tell a story of resilience, value creation and growth. In a market dominated by economic pressure, AI-driven disruption, fragmented attention and rising expectations, the brands driving sustained growth are proving to be those who are best able to turn intelligence into action.

That theme is central to a conversation with Jeff Greenspoon, chief executive of the Americas at Kantar, and Ryu Yokoi, chief media and marketing capability officer for Unilever North America and Personal Care.

For Yokoi, AI represents both a creative and operational unlock for marketers. “AI is a marketer’s dream,” he says, pointing to its ability to dramatically accelerate everything. But both Yokoi and Greenspoon argue that speed alone isn’t enough. The brands that are pulling ahead are those using intelligence not simply to react faster, but to build stronger, more consistent and culturally resonant brands over time.

The AI era, Greenspoon says, has fundamentally changed how marketers must think about ROI: “It’s not enough to just say, ‘here’s the clicks and here’s the engagement and here’s the lift that a campaign drove’. Over time, the brand impacts of any individual interaction will compound over time.”

Kantar argues that marketers need to focus on building what it calls “Meaningful Difference” – that is, creating experiences across channels that compound into stronger consumer relationships and ultimately stronger growth. Brands that drive meaningful difference over time are twice as likely to grow than those that don’t.

That idea sits at the core of BrandZ’s long-running valuation framework, which measures how brand equity translates into financial performance. Greenspoon points to Kantar’s 21 years of tracking more than 20,000 brands globally as evidence that long-term brand investment continues to outperform.

“In the last 21 years, the brands that we track in our strong brands portfolio have grown over 500%,” he says. “We see that in times of good, they grow faster, but also in times of [difficulty]… those brands are being more resilient, they’re recovering faster, and they’re driving more growth than their peers that have not invested into brand.”

But Greenspoon also believes AI is making brand consistency even more commercially important for another reason: algorithms themselves are learning what brands stand for. “The more consistent a brand can be in how they tell their story, how they develop new products and services, and how they structure the information around their brand will also help train AI [and] the LLMs to understand their brand,” he says.

From ‘chasing moments’ to ‘building worlds’

That challenge of maintaining consistency across fragmented touchpoints is something Unilever is grappling with daily.

Yokoi describes how the company’s “social-first” pivot has dramatically increased the complexity of marketing execution. “It’s more for the brands to be thinking about,” he says. “It’s not just positioning yourself for an ad, but thinking about how you interact with creators, with people in real life when you’re activating and trying to create those moments where you cross over social first and IRL moments.”

Unilever has developed what Yokoi calls a “brandverse” approach: a deeper articulation of brand identity that goes beyond traditional positioning. “It really emphasizes not just our brand or point of difference, what we stand for, but also who we hang out with and what it is like to hang out with us,” he explains. “Having that clear has really been beneficial to us in terms of giving everybody consistency.”

For Yokoi, the key shift is moving away from reactive marketing toward building enduring ecosystems around brands. “Our mantra internally is: we want to build worlds instead of chasing moments,” he says.

That philosophy is particularly visible in Dove.

“We have built a real world around the area of self-esteem and body positivity,” Yokoi says. “That has expressed itself in many ways, whether that’s self-esteem education that the brand puts out, support of body positivity in sports… or any of the many experiments and campaigns that the brand has done over time.”

One example Yokoi highlights is Dove’s Cannes Grand Prix-winning campaign exploring how generative AI systems depict beauty. The campaign challenged major LLMs to generate representations of beauty and then compared those outputs with prompts framed through Dove’s perspective on “real beauty.”

“When we prompted the same LLMs to what beauty looked like according to Dove, the images that came back looked exactly like you would hope,” Yokoi says. And for him, the significance went beyond the campaign itself. “We had actually trained those LLMs through over 20 years of disciplined, consistent depictions of women framing real beauty over that period,” he says.

That idea that brand consistency now shapes not only human perception but machine understanding closely mirrors Kantar’s own perspective on the future of brand growth.

Both leaders stress that success in the AI era is less about accumulating endless signals and more about creating frameworks that help organizations act decisively. “Good intelligence really looks like two things,” says Greenspoon. “First and foremost, do you understand how intelligence can turn into action?”

Strong intelligence also gives brands “the ability to say no to things,” he adds, like resisting the temptation to chase every new platform, trend or channel.

At Unilever, Yokoi describes a similarly disciplined approach grounded in cross-channel measurement, attribution modelling and cultural insight: “We very much want to understand and really have a real pulse on where culture is. And then we have a huge emphasis on attribution and cross-channel measurement, understanding the productivity of every penny that we invest.”

That combination of cultural intelligence plus commercial accountability may ultimately define the next era of brand leadership. As Greenspoon puts it: “The brands that can stay consistent to their north star and innovate… are two times more likely to grow than the brands that only stay consistent.”

And in a world increasingly shaped by algorithms, the world’s most valuable brands prove that building their intelligence advantage creates the difference needed to grow.

evidence.title: Diageo India revamps McDowell’s No 1 with upgraded blend, premium positioning
evidence.text:
Diageo India revamps McDowell’s No 1 with upgraded blend, premium positioning

The transformation marks a significant repositioning of one of India’s largest whisky brands, which sells over 30 million cases annually

The revamped McDowell’s No 1 is positioned in the mass-premium segment, where Diageo sees changing consumer expectations around value | Photo Credit: TOBY MELVILLE

Diageo India has unveiled a major revamp of McDowell’s No 1, combining an upgraded whisky blend with a redesigned bottle and a more premium brand identity as it seeks to appeal to a new generation of consumers.

The transformation marks a significant repositioning of one of India’s largest whisky brands, which sells over 30 million cases annually.

The company said the move goes beyond a packaging refresh, with the new offering retaining the brand’s established Scotch cues while adding greater emphasis on quality, craftsmanship and drinking experience.

The revamped McDowell’s No 1 is positioned in the mass-premium segment, where Diageo sees changing consumer expectations around value.

According to the company, consumers are increasingly looking beyond price and seeking products that combine quality and refinement with an aspirational social image.

At the centre of the relaunch is an upgraded blend comprising select imported Scotch, Indian malts and premium grain spirits. The whisky is matured in select oak and American barrels and blended across India and Scotland, with the company claiming that the process delivers additional smoothness.

The new liquid has undergone more than 100 quality checks. Diageo describes it as having aromas of vanilla, grain sweetness and mellow malt, with notes of matured wood and sweet spice. The palate combines gentle sweetness with malty, woody and vanilla notes, followed by a clean finish with hints of vanilla cream.

Ruchira Jaitly, Chief Marketing Officer, Diageo India said consumer perceptions of value were changing, with quality, craftsmanship and experience becoming increasingly important alongside affordability.

The company said it validated its consumer insights through research involving more than 10,000 consumers across 11 markets. The findings, it said, were used to evolve McDowell’s No.1 while retaining the familiarity and trust built by the brand over decades.

Diageo said the relaunch is aimed at redefining the mass-premium whisky segment while maintaining McDowell’s No 1’s accessibility and broad consumer appeal.

evidence.text:
Diageo India Upgrades McDowell’s No. 1 To Target Premium Demand

Diageo India has revamped its flagship McDowell’s No. 1 whisky with a new recipe and packaging to appeal to consumers who prefer higher-quality drinks. The move aims to keep the brand relevant as drinking habits shift. Investors will monitor if this strategy improves profit margins without affecting the company's massive sales volume in a highly competitive and regulated market.

United Spirits, known as Diageo India, is rebranding its most popular whisky, McDowell’s No. 1. The company has updated the blend, which now includes a mix of imported Scotch, Indian malts, and premium grain spirits. It has also introduced new packaging to give the product a more modern look. This flagship brand sells over 30 million cases every year, making it a critical part of the company's sales and revenue.

The company decided to make this change after researching the preferences of 10,000 consumers across 11 markets. The goal is to move the product away from being seen as a basic, low-cost option. Instead, the company wants the brand to be viewed as a higher-quality choice. This shift aligns with a broader trend in the Indian liquor industry, where drinkers are increasingly choosing better brands rather than just looking for the lowest price.

For investors, this move is a balancing act. While upgrading the quality can attract more customers and potentially lead to better profit margins, it also comes with risks. If the price increases significantly, the company could lose its large base of cost-conscious buyers.

The Indian alcohol sector also faces specific challenges that investors should keep in mind. It is a highly regulated industry where taxes vary from state to state, which can limit the company’s ability to change prices freely. Additionally, companies in this space must manage the rising costs of raw materials, such as grains and glass packaging. These costs can put pressure on the company’s profits, so keeping expenses stable while trying to elevate the brand's image is a significant task for the management.

Moving forward, the primary challenge for the company will be maintaining its sales volume while successfully positioning the brand as a premium choice. Investors should pay attention to the company’s future quarterly reports to see if the brand’s sales volume remains steady or grows. They will also look for signs of improved profit margins and observe how well the company manages the competitive pressure and regulatory hurdles that often impact the Indian beverage market.

evidence.text:
Diageo Names Divan Raimagia Global Head Of Cyber Resilience

Diageo appoints Divan Raimagia as VP and Global Head of Cyber Resilience, bringing 18 years of experience across cybersecurity, OT, ICS and technology risk.

Diageo has appointed Divan Raimagia as Vice President, Global Head of Cyber Resilience. Raimagia announced the move in a professional update, marking a new chapter in his nearly 18-year career in cybersecurity and technology risk.

His appointment brings experience in operational technology (OT) and industrial control systems (ICS) into a global cyber resilience role covering a business with manufacturing, supply chain, technology, and corporate systems across multiple markets.

Raimagia's professional background spans cybersecurity, information security, cyber risk, security architecture, network security, OT security, and industrial control systems.

His experience has involved protecting technology environments and critical operational systems, including areas where enterprise IT and operational technology meet.

That background is relevant to the wider cyber resilience challenge facing organizations with both digital and physical operations. Cybersecurity in such environments involves not only protecting information but also considering the resilience of systems supporting day-to-day operations. At Diageo, Raimagia will take on that challenge at a global level as Vice President – Global Head of Cyber Resilience.

Bringing OT Security Experience To Diageo

Before joining Diageo, Raimagia was associated with Adani Green Energy, where his professional profile identifies him as an OT and ICS cybersecurity leader.

His work included cybersecurity requirements for environments where information technology and operational technology intersect. Earlier in his career, Raimagia worked with Wipro Technologies. His experience there and across subsequent roles covered areas including network security, data center environments, and cybersecurity architecture.

Together, these roles have given him exposure to enterprise IT as well as operational technology security, two areas that increasingly need to work together as organizations build broader resilience strategies.

Raimagia joins Diageo as the company continues to focus on cybersecurity and IT resilience within its wider risk-management framework. Diageo has identified sophisticated cyber and IT threats, including third-party risks and unauthorized access, as issues that could affect information, operational systems, and business continuity.

Its Digital and Technology organization includes a dedicated cybersecurity function, while its Information Management & Security team works on protecting the organization against evolving cyber threats while supporting business operations.

The company's approach also extends beyond preventive security controls. Diageo has been strengthening cyber incident-response processes, conducting cyber crisis exercises, and working with independent cybersecurity experts to assess and test the resilience of its systems.

It has also been progressing work related to NIS2, with a focus on governance, cyber resilience, and operational security across factories and business-critical operations.

From Cybersecurity To Business Resilience

The scope of these initiatives shows why cyber resilience roles increasingly extend beyond traditional enterprise security. For companies operating manufacturing and supply-chain environments, a cybersecurity incident can involve operational systems as well as conventional IT infrastructure. That makes the ability to prepare for, respond to, and recover from cyber incidents an important part of the broader technology risk framework.

Raimagia's experience across OT and ICS security places those operational environments within his new global mandate at Diageo. He holds an engineering degree from Rajiv Gandhi Proudyogiki Vishwavidyalaya and professional certifications, including ISO 27001 Lead Auditor and Certified Chief Information Security Officer.

evidence.title: Stella Artois to front AB InBev sponsorship deal with UEFA
evidence.text:
September 24 – AB InBev has selected Stella Artois as the beer brand that will front its UEFA club competition sponsorship from 2027/28, ending the Champions League’s three-decade association with Heineken.

The rights themselves were secured by AB InBev last year, but the brewer had not previously confirmed which of its brands would carry them.

That question was answered at the company’s Capital Markets Day in St Louis with Stella set to activate across the Champions League, Europa League and Conference League from the start of UEFA’s next commercial cycle in 2027.

The six-season agreement runs through 2032/33 and has been reported at around €200 million per year, although neither UEFA nor AB InBev has disclosed the financial terms themselves.

At that level, the package would be worth roughly €1.2 billion across its lifespan.

For comparison, Heineken’s current UEFA agreement has been reported at around €120 million annually. If those figures are broadly comparable, the new deal represents an increase of about 67% in the beer category.

The change also closes one of football sponsorship’s longest-running relationships, with Heineken group brands tied to UEFA’s leading club competition since 1994, initially through Amstel before Heineken itself took the lead role.

AB InBev had plenty of options for the replacement. Its portfolio includes Budweiser, Corona and Michelob Ultra, but Stella has been chosen as the better fit for what the company describes as the “premium expression of European football”.

AB InBev says Stella is performing strongly in Brazil and growing in Mexico, the US and Africa, but is still relatively underdeveloped across parts of Asia. The Champions League gives it a regular global platform across most of the year rather than the short burst offered by a major tournament.

David Beckham, already Stella’s global brand ambassador, was wheeled out to reveal the UEFA link to investors. The deal will begin at the same time as a wider overhaul of UEFA’s club commercial operation.

From 2027, US agency Relevent takes over from TEAM Marketing as commercial partner to UC3. TEAM’s own relationship with UEFA stretches back into the 90s, making 2027 a fairly substantial reset: new commercial agency, new beer partner and a fresh rights cycle aimed at pushing revenues higher.

evidence.title: AB InBev expands product mix to target shifting drinking habits
evidence.text:
AB InBev expands product mix to target shifting drinking habits

Anheuser-Busch InBev is adapting its drinks portfolio as consumers rethink alcohol spending and show greater interest in health and wellness. The brewer says it will use smaller pack sizes, functional beer variants and a broader push beyond beer to lift consumption and revenue growth.

The world's largest brewer by market value is aiming to increase beer consumption and raise revenue from non-beer categories such as canned cocktails and energy drinks. Executives outlined the strategy at a capital markets event, highlighting pressure from strained household budgets and changing consumer preferences.

Chief Marketing Officer Marcel Marcondes says the company sees a major opportunity among infrequent beer drinkers, especially budget-conscious consumers. He says data points to strong potential to make beer more affordable, particularly in developing markets, through both smaller packs and larger formats that offer more volume for less.

Marcondes also says non-alcoholic beer consumed with casual meals is another important opening for growth. He adds that AB InBev plans to support that segment with zero-alcohol beers in different flavours, with low calories and with added protein or electrolytes; the company has already launched a version of its Spaten beer with added protein in Brazil. U.S. demand pressures and category expansion Brewers including AB InBev have been trying to revive weak beer demand in major markets such as the U.S., where some consumers are cutting back because of pressure on their finances or shifting tastes. The company, which owns brands including Corona and Stella Artois, is responding by broadening its offer beyond traditional beer occasions.

In the U.S. in particular, AB InBev is pushing further into adjacent categories through products such as its Cutwater canned cocktails and energy drinks. Executives say energy drinks alone could add $25 billion to the company's addressable market.

Chief Executive Michel Doukeris says AB InBev remains a challenger in those segments, leaving substantial room for expansion. The strategy signals a wider effort by the brewer to capture spending across more beverage categories while defending volumes in its core beer business.

evidence.text:
Heineken stock (ISIN NL0000009165) was trading at EUR 71.24 on Euronext Amsterdam on September 25, 2026, up 0.06 percent from the prior close. The latest operating figures show earnings growth outpacing beer volumes.

In a September 23, 2026 analysis, Investing.com reported that Heineken's organic operating profit increased 6.7 percent in the first half of 2026, while consolidated volume grew 0.4 percent. Organic net revenue rose 2.7 percent during the same period, creating a quantified gap between financial growth and physical volume.

The operating margin also expanded by 55 basis points to 14.6 percent in the first half. Net revenue per hectoliter increased 2.3 percent, while premium volume grew 6 percent, pointing to pricing and mix as the main earnings lever rather than broad volume expansion.

Investing.com said Heineken maintained its 2026 guidance for organic operating profit growth of 2 percent to 6 percent. Free operating cash flow reached EUR 1.38 billion in the first half, with cash conversion at 97 percent.

The company is also targeting gross savings toward the upper end of its EUR 400 million to EUR 500 million range. The reported figures make margin delivery and cash conversion more important for the stock than volume growth alone.

evidence.title: Heineken, GoLoud and audioXi Expand Greenlight Music Platform with Branded Podcast
evidence.text:
Heineken has expanded its GREENLIGHT music platform into long-form audio through a branded podcast developed with GoLoud and audioXi, as the drinks brand looks to build deeper engagement with younger music audiences.

The Greenlight Podcast, hosted by Dara Quilty, features interviews with Irish and international artists and forms part of the wider Heineken GREENLIGHT initiative, which has staged live music performances in venues around Ireland.

The podcast has featured artists and musicians including Sprints, Gurriers, Pillow Queens, Le Boom, Theo Katzman, Cory Wong, Aimée, Mark McCabe and Niall Breslin, as well as a festival special recorded at All Together Now with Kelly-Anne Byrne.

The series, which began in May and will continue until October, has been developed as an original content property by Heineken, GoLoud, audioXi and Bauer Media Audio Ireland.

It is designed to extend the GREENLIGHT proposition beyond individual live events, giving audiences longer-form access to artists through interviews covering their careers, influences and ambitions.

A dedicated GREENLIGHT music stream has also been created, allowing listeners to hear music from featured artists and continue engaging with the platform between podcast episodes.

Heineken GREENLIGHT has so far featured more than 65 artists across 20 venues, with acts including Sprints, Basement Jaxx, Mike Skinner and TOMORA taking part.

Following activations in Dublin, Cork and at All Together Now, the platform is due to move to Galway for a bank holiday weekend takeover.

The podcast and wider audio campaign are also being used by Heineken and audioXi to test the effectiveness of branded digital audio among younger audiences.

audioXi and audio research and analytics company Veritonic commissioned a brand uplift study aimed at measuring the impact of the campaign among Gen Z consumers.

According to audioXi, the research showed a substantial increase in recommendation intent among Gen Z. The campaign incorporated immersive 3D audio, Heineken GREENLIGHT’s sonic branding and music-focused content.

According to Clara Pryor, senior account manager, audioXi, the campaign marked the first time an alcohol brand in Ireland had conducted a digital audio brand lift study and the first occasion on which audioXi had measured the effectiveness of 3D audio.

“As the first alcohol brand in Ireland to conduct a digital audio brand lift study and the first time we’ve measured the effectiveness of 3D audio, this campaign demonstrates how innovation in audio can translate into real brand impact,” she said.

“By combining immersive 3D creative, Heineken GREENLIGHT’s distinctive sonic logo and authentic music-led content, GREENLIGHT has shown the role audio can play in building meaningful connections with the next generation of consumers.”

The partnership also illustrates the increasing role being played by media owners in developing branded entertainment formats which extend beyond conventional spot advertising and sponsorship.

In this case, Bauer Media Audio Ireland and its audioXi and GoLoud businesses have been involved across concept development, artist partnerships, production, distribution and promotion.

Rachael Crawley of Heineken said the project was intended to extend the brewer’s involvement in Irish music culture.

“The collaboration with the Bauer team has been exceptional from start to finish. It reflects a shared ambition to create culturally resonant platforms that go beyond traditional brand partnerships,” she said.

“As an extension of Heineken GREENLIGHT, this podcast reinforces Heineken’s role in shaping and supporting music culture in Ireland, creating new ways for audiences to engage with the intimate moments and conversations that matter within the scene.”

evidence.title: Heineken to buy 300 pubs from U.K.'s Stonegate for €350 million
evidence.text:
Heineken to buy 300 pubs from U.K.'s Stonegate for €350 million

Heineken is on the verge of buying 300 pubs from Stonegate, Britain’s largest pub chain, The Times reported.

Stonegate has approximately 3.5 billion euros in debt and wants to sell 1,000 of its best pubs to ease the burden.

Heineken is prepared to pay 350 million euros for the 300 pubs. The brewer already runs about 2,350 pubs in the U.K. under its Star Pubs & Bars banners and brews brands including Amstel, Birra Moretti, and Cruzcampo.

Stongate operates about 4,500 pubs nationwide but is trying to sell 1,000 prime sites to raise cash. Most of the debt was incurred when the company bought rival Enterprise Inns for 3 billion punds in 2019, leaving it loaded with loans just before the pandemic forced British pubs to close for months.

Since the pandemic, the British pub sector has also been hit by soaring costs for beer, energy, and wages, and by higher employer taxes introduced by former Chancellor Rachel Reeves.

Although Heineken came close to a deal after talks this summer, people familiar with the matter reportedly caution there is no guarantee it will close. Several other suitors, including large investment firms, reportedly remain in the running, some of them potentially interested in the full 1,000-pub portfolio.

evidence.title: Britvic stock reports 9 percent volume growth in Carlsberg
evidence.text:
Britvic stock reports 9 percent soft drink volume growth in August 2026 as the brand portfolio becomes a larger part of Carlsberg's growth plan. The company was acquired by Carlsberg in January 2025, and its shares were subsequently canceled from trading, according to Zavia .

Carlsberg's August 2026 update put Britvic at the center of a faster integration. Soft drink volumes increased 9 percent, while the category reached 30 percent of Carlsberg's portfolio, according to The Investment .

The comparison with the earlier plan is material. Carlsberg now expects to capture 50 percent of the total GBP 110 million synergy pool in 2026, compared with its previous expectation of 30 percent to 40 percent, according to Echo.ie .

The faster synergy schedule also changed the earnings framework. Carlsberg narrowed its 2026 operating profit growth guidance toward the upper end of 4 percent to 6 percent, up from a previous range of 2 percent to 6 percent, with the Britvic integration helping offset weaker Chinese beer demand.

For investors, the key distinction is ownership. Britvic's operating performance still generates measurable value, but the standalone equity story ended when Carlsberg completed the acquisition on January 17, 2025. The relevant exposure now sits inside Carlsberg rather than in a separately traded Britvic share.

evidence.title: Carlsberg Malaysia’s Top Ten Charity Campaign Targets RM6.5mil Proceeds to Improve Access to Quality Education
evidence.text: Extending financial support six vernacular schools and one education foundation SHAH ALAM, 25 September 2026 – What started as a community effort to support education has grown into Malaysia’s longest-running and highest fundraising education platform – Top Ten Charity Campaign (“Top Ten”). This November, the campaign will continue to provide a fundraising platform for five vernacular schools in the Klang Valley, with a collective target of RM6.5 million for school building funds. Participating schools comprise SJKC Yak Chee, Puchong; SJKC Bukit Tangga, Rawang; SJKC Chung Hua, Klang; SJKC On Pong 2, Ampang; and SJKC Ladang Regent, Elmina. Top Ten is a flagship community engagement project funded by Carlsberg Malaysia and jointly organised by two Chinese dailies. Running since 1987, proceeds collected by the schools will be channelled towards the enhancement of teaching facilities and multipurpose halls, infrastructure upgrades, auditorium development and educational equipment. This is aligned with Carlsberg Malaysia’s pledge towards United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG 4): Quality Education by helping create better learning environments for students and educators alike. Welcome address by Stefano Clini, Managing Director of Carlsberg Malaysia Speaking at this year’s campaign press conference, Carlsberg Malaysia’s Managing Director Stefano Clini said: “What has sustained Top Ten for nearly four decades is our belief that meaningful change happens when communities come together behind a common purpose. While education needs have evolved over the years, the campaign has continued to evolve alongside them, supporting a broader range of educational needs while staying true to our purpose of Brewing For A Better Today and Tomorrow”. “We are honoured to play a part in contributing back to the local communities we serve, recognising education as one of the most important foundations for growth. Malaysia has grown from an agriculture-focused economy to an industrial and manufacturing base and is now moving towards a more services- and knowledge-driven economy. This makes education even more critical in ensuring local talents are future-ready to contribute to the country’s continued economic progress.” “More than the proceeds raised, Top Ten is about and ensuring quality education remains within reach and equipping the future workplace with the knowledge, skills and confidence to compete in the new-age economy amid AI disruption. ,” Clini noted. Since 1987, Top Ten has raised a cumulative total of RM601.8 million and benefited over 700 schools and educational institutions nationwide, helping to provide equal opportunities for quality education for generations of students. Built on the generosity of donors and supporters, the campaign continues to demonstrate the meaningful impact of collective giving, earning recognition from the Malaysia Book of Records as the longest-running and highest fundraising charity show in support of education. Keynote address by Deputy Education Minister YB Tuan Wong Kah Woh Delivering the keynote address at the launch, YB Tuan Wong Kah Woh, Deputy Minister of Education, said: “The Top Ten Charity Campaign is the longest-running fundraising platform in Malaysia for our schools, and one of the most successful. Thank you so much for being with us over the past 39 years, and for your continued support. I look forward to more collaboration in the years to come, so that we can ensure our students continue to prosper in a good learning environment.” Presentation of contributions to Dong Zong and SJKT Ladang Dovenby, Perak Beyond the five fundraising schools, this year’s campaign also extends support to broader education initiatives, with RM10,000 channelled to the Dong Zong Chinese Education Complex and Future Education Fund and RM50,000 supporting STEM education advancement for SJKT Ladang Dovenby in Sungai Siput, Perak. While remaining rooted in supporting vernacular education, Top Ten has evolved alongside the communities it serves, broadening its impact over the years to include educational institutions, tertiary education initiatives, schools in East Malaysia and, more recently, STEM-focused learning opportunities. evidence.text:
Carlsberg Malaysia makes revenue revival with Somersby, Sapporo boosts

16-Sep-2026 Last updated on 16-Sep-2026 at 02:09 GMT

Carlsberg Malaysia has made a stunning return to revenue growth by sticking with its premiumisation strategy

The firm recently announced its H1FY2026 financial results, reporting a 5.9% year-on-year growth in revenue to RM1.22bn (US$) and 3.1% year-on-year growth in net profits to Rm181.9m (US$).

More importantly, it saw growth return to all areas of its portfolio, where its mainstream sales grew 6%, premium products grew 5% and alcohol-free brews grew 45% - a stark difference to its performance in the first quarter of the year where negative sales performances were reported across the board .

Despite this, Carlsberg Malaysia managing director Stefano Clini stressed that caution is still the name of the game for the firm due to a combination of various challenging factors still looming.

“We are seeing early signs of the 10% increase in excise duty imposed [in Malaysia] last November, impacting [consumer] sentiment and discretionary spending, which remained cautious in the second quarter,” he said at a press event announcing the results.

“We also need to continue to monitor external developments closely, including potential supply chain risks arising from Middle East tensions, [and also] stay focused on disciplined value management, cost optimisation and prudent resource allocation.”

That said, Clini expressed encouragement for the firm’s first-half performance, highlighting plans to continue strategies and initiatives that have yielded positive results thus far.

“For instance, we launched Somersby Apple Light across Malaysia and Singapore in April to offer consumers a lighter, lower-calorie and lower-sugar cider option in line with the growing health and wellness trend,” he said.

“We have also seen strong double-digit growth coming from Sapporo Premium Beer, which has been supported by expansion into more outlets and strong consumer demand.”

Both Somersby and Sapporo fall under Carlsberg Malaysia’s premium portfolio, and its initiatives with both brands have been in line with the firm’s longstanding premiumisation strategy.

The firm’s chairman Tan Sri Dato’ Chor Chee Heung had recently reaffirmed Carlsberg Malaysia’s focus in this area to ensure ‘sustained return on investment’, and the recent results show that it is serving them well.

Clini also highlighted Sapporo as its best-performing premium brand, and how Carlsberg Malaysia has been directing investment into it.

“The goal has been to reinforce Sapporo’s role as a recognised Japanese lager brand associated with brewing excellence,” he said.

Sapporo recently marked 150 years as the ‘Iconic First Beer of Japan’.

“In Malaysia, consumers are increasingly drawn to premium brands that offer more than quality alone — brands with a strong identity, authentic story and experiences that feel meaningful,” Clini added.

The wider Carlsberg Group recently announced a strategic partnership with Sapporo across Asia, although this did has had no impact on Carlsberg Malaysia’s existing arrangements with the Japanese brand.

Despite its overall positive performance, the firm was pulled down by negative growth in Singapore where it saw a -4% year-on-year drop in revenue and -21.6% year-on-year decline in profits, cinching Singapore’s status as a challenging market for Carlsberg.

“Singapore reported lower revenue and profit [as any] growth in domestic sales amid weak consumer sentiment was outweighed by lower export sales and the strengthening of the Ringgit Malaysia against the Singapore Dollar,” he said.

In response to this, Carlsberg Malaysia has appointed its former marketing director Olga Pulyaeva as the new Carlsberg Singapore general manager to work specifically on this market.

evidence.title: Carlsberg upbeat on annual profit despite first half miss
evidence.text:
Danish brewer Carlsberg has today forecast full-year profit towards the upper end of its previous guidance range even as it missed half-year estimates, saying benefits from its 2025 purchase of Britvic were being delivered faster than expected.

The world's third-largest brewer behind Anheuser-Busch InBev and Heineken, which acquired Britvic as part of a pivot to soft drinks after years of weak beer sales, now expects annual organic operating profit growth of between 4% and 6%. It previously forecast between 2% and 6% growth.

The maker of Kronenbourg 1664 and Tuborg missed analyst forecasts across sales volume, revenue and profits in the first half, in part as a result of severe weather in China, its largest market, where beer demand had already been low.

Carlsberg said it would deliver approximately 50% of the total expected £110m synergies from its takeover of Britvic in 2026, compared with the previous expectation of 30% to 40%.

Partnerships with Pepsi - now Carlsberg's second-largest brand thanks to production, sales and distribution agreements - also drove growth.

"We do think that soft drinks add a stronger growth impetus than beer," CEO Jacob Aarup-Andersen told reporters on a call, adding however beer would remain a key part of Carlsberg's portfolio and that brewers were in the midst of an effort to rejuvenate the category.

Analysts said Carlsberg's performance in Asia was the main disappointment. Aarup-Andersen said severe weather, including typhoons and flooding, had affected its business in China and the impact would likely continue into the third quarter.

Overall, its half-year performance was "underwhelming", RBC Capital analyst James Edwardes Jones said.

Carlsberg and its rivals have also been hit by geopolitical upheaval including the Russian war in Ukraine, US tariffs and, most recently, the Iran war, which is putting more strain on consumer wallets.

This strain and shifts in drinking habits have prompted some consumers to cut back on alcoholic beverages, leaving brewers battling to increase lacklustre sales volumes.

Carlsberg reported first-half operating profit of 7.45 billion Danish crowns ($1.15 billion), missing analyst expectations for 7.55 billion crowns.

NBC Marks 75 Years in Nigeria, Coca-Cola HBC Reaffirms $1 Billion Investment and Pledges $1.25 Million for Young Entrepreneurs

The Nigerian Bottling Company has clocked 75 years of operations in Nigeria, with the Coca-Cola system using the milestone to reaffirm its long-term investment commitment and announce fresh support for young Nigerian entrepreneurs.

Delivering President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s remarks at the anniversary event, Senator (Dr) George Akume said: “Seventy-five years ago, Nigerian Bottling Company began a journey in Lagos. Tonight, we celebrate what that journey has produced. But more importantly, we look forward to what the next chapter can bring: more investment, stronger industries, better jobs, deeper local production and greater opportunities for Nigerians.”

He added that Nigeria welcomes companies willing to produce locally, develop Nigerian talent, strengthen supply chains and contribute to their host communities.

Since its first production run in Ebute Metta in 1951, NBC has expanded into an operation spanning eight plants, eleven depots and 52 commercial territories, supporting jobs, local supply chains, talent development and community investment across the country. Through its operations and value chain, NBC continues to contribute to economic activity in manufacturing, logistics, distribution, retail and other sectors.

Reflecting on the company’s origins, Anastassis G. David, Chairman of Coca-Cola HBC, said: “In 1951, Anastasios Leventis negotiated the rights for the whole of Nigeria. It was a big, bold decision, but it was also a statement of belief. Belief in Nigeria, as a country of exceptional importance, scale and prospect. Belief in its people, in communities across the nation. And belief in what could be achieved by investing for the long term. This belief echoes our own confidence in Nigeria’s future, which remains as strong today as it has ever been.”

Sola David-Borha, Chairperson of the Board at Nigerian Bottling Company, said the company’s endurance rested on trust — earned over time through consistency and sound governance.

A recent economic impact study by Steward Redqueen found that the Coca-Cola system contributed approximately US$1 billion in value-added economic activity across its Nigerian value chain in 2024, supporting more than 160,000 jobs. That figure includes nearly 3,000 direct roles and approximately 157,200 jobs across retail, agriculture, manufacturing, transport and services. The study also found the Coca-Cola system sourced almost US$601 million worth of goods and services from Nigerian suppliers that same year.

Goran Sladic, Managing Director of Nigerian Bottling Company, said: “Seventy-five years of Nigerian Bottling Company is 75 years of growing with Nigeria. We are proud of the role we have played in creating opportunities, developing people, supporting communities and strengthening local value chains. As we look to the future, our ambition is to build on that legacy and continue creating value for years to come.”

Zoran Bogdanovic, CEO of Coca-Cola HBC, reaffirmed the group’s commitment to Nigeria. “This is a remarkable milestone for any company. For us, it represents far more than longevity. It reflects a shared history with Nigeria, a country where Coca-Cola HBC’s story began, and a history of which we are very proud,” he said.

Bogdanovic said the Coca-Cola system is continuing to deliver on its 2024 commitment to invest up to US$1 billion in Nigeria over five years, subject to a predictable and enabling business environment. “We have already begun advancing that commitment through investments to expand manufacturing capacity at our Asejire Plant in Oyo State and our Challawa Plant in Kano State,” he said.

Those investments are expected to strengthen production capability, support Nigeria’s growing consumer market and create further opportunities across the local manufacturing and supply ecosystem.

Marking the anniversary, Bogdanovic announced a $1.25 million commitment by the Coca-Cola HBC Foundation to support young Nigerian entrepreneurs over the next three years. The funding will help them build and sustain businesses in Nigeria’s hospitality and food service sector through business grants, structured entrepreneurship training, business formalisation support and dedicated mentorship.

evidence.text:
The Coca-Cola HBC share price fizzes 4% after announcing an earnings upgrade!

After 90 minutes of trading today (5 August), the Coca-Cola HBC (LSE:CCH) share price was up more than 4%. This was down to the drinks giant just releasing its numbers for the six months ended 3 July.

Let's take a closer look and see whether the reaction of investors is justified. More importantly, is there an opportunity here?

Coca-Cola HBC has the exclusive rights to produce and sell Coca-Cola , and the group's other beverages, in 28 countries across Europe and Africa. It's doing so well that it's announced a full-year earnings upgrade. It now expects organic earnings before interest and tax to be " in the range " of 8%-10%. Previously, it was forecasting 7%-10%.

Energy drinks (it owns Monster ) are performing particularly well. During the first six months of 2026, organic volume growth was 26.1% higher than for the same period a year earlier. For all brands, the increase was 7.5%.

Impressively, despite intense competition, squeezed disposable incomes, and supply-chain inflation, the group also managed to improve its gross profit margin by 1.1 percentage points.

Overall, it was a healthy set of numbers. Therefore, I can understand why its share price performed so strongly during early trading.

But in some respects, we shouldn't be surprised that the results were good. After all, last week (28 July), The Coca-Cola Company , the US-listed business and 21% owner of Coca-Cola HBC, raised its full-year guidance after reporting a strong set of results for the three months to 3 July.

Net revenue increased by 7% compared to the same period a year earlier. More impressively, earnings per share (EPS) grew 16%. The company said the football World Cup was a contributing factor to the healthy growth. It now expects a 9%-10% rise in comparable EPS versus the 8%-9% previously forecast.

And yesterday (4 August), Coca-Cola Europacific Partners , which operates in 31 countries in Europe and Asia, reported a 5.6% increase in reported volumes and a 9.1% rise in diluted EPS, compared to the same period a year ago.

It's pretty clear that the group's performing strongly across the planet. No doubt this is helped by having the world's best-selling drink in its portfolio. Indeed, what could possibly go wrong?

In fact, a few things. Firstly, although Coca-Cola HBC distributes many sugar-free and low calorie versions of its drinks, it's still vulnerable if consumers decide to switch to healthier alternatives. And with over 40% of sales coming from the world's number-one drink, this high dependency could become a problem if tastes change.

Also, income investors are likely to prefer other higher-yielding stocks.

However, Coca-Cola CCH owns many other famous brands across a diverse number of categories, as part of its emphasis on offering a drink for every occasion at any time of the day.

Significantly, the group says it remains " on track " to acquire Coca-Cola Beverages Africa during the second half of the year. In my opinion, this could be a game-changer. The $2.6bn deal will provide access to another 14 markets, which account for around 40% of all volumes sold on the continent.

After looking at this morning's results, I haven't changed my mind. I believe Coca-Cola HBC remains a stock to consider. In fact, I have some in my own portfolio. Cheers!
