evidence.title: Coca-Cola HBC (LON:CCH) Might Have The Makings Of A Multi-Bagger
evidence.text:
Coca-Cola HBC (LON:CCH) Might Have The Makings Of A Multi-Bagger

If we want to find a stock that could multiply over the long term, what are the underlying trends we should look for? Typically, we'll want to notice a trend of growing return on capital employed (ROCE) and alongside that, an expanding base of capital employed. Ultimately, this demonstrates that it's a business that is reinvesting profits at increasing rates of return. With that in mind, we've noticed some promising trends at Coca-Cola HBC ( LON:CCH ) so let's look a bit deeper.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

What Is Return On Capital Employed (ROCE)?

If you haven't worked with ROCE before, it measures the 'return' (pre-tax profit) a company generates from capital employed in its business. The formula for this calculation on Coca-Cola HBC is:

Return on Capital Employed = Earnings Before Interest and Tax (EBIT) ÷ (Total Assets - Current Liabilities)

0.18 = €1.3b ÷ (€12b - €4.9b) (Based on the trailing twelve months to June 2025) .

So, Coca-Cola HBC has an ROCE of 18%. On its own, that's a standard return, however it's much better than the 15% generated by the Beverage industry.

View our latest analysis for Coca-Cola HBC

Above you can see how the current ROCE for Coca-Cola HBC compares to its prior returns on capital, but there's only so much you can tell from the past. If you'd like, you can check out the forecasts from the analysts covering Coca-Cola HBC for free.

Coca-Cola HBC is displaying some positive trends. Over the last five years, returns on capital employed have risen substantially to 18%. The company is effectively making more money per dollar of capital used, and it's worth noting that the amount of capital has increased too, by 31%. This can indicate that there's plenty of opportunities to invest capital internally and at ever higher rates, a combination that's common among multi-baggers.

On a separate but related note, it's important to know that Coca-Cola HBC has a current liabilities to total assets ratio of 41%, which we'd consider pretty high. This can bring about some risks because the company is basically operating with a rather large reliance on its suppliers or other sorts of short-term creditors. Ideally we'd like to see this reduce as that would mean fewer obligations bearing risks.

What We Can Learn From Coca-Cola HBC's ROCE

All in all, it's terrific to see that Coca-Cola HBC is reaping the rewards from prior investments and is growing its capital base. And investors seem to expect more of this going forward, since the stock has rewarded shareholders with a 95% return over the last five years. Therefore, we think it would be worth your time to check if these trends are going to continue.

Like most companies, Coca-Cola HBC does come with some risks, and we've found 1 warning sign that you should be aware of.

evidence.title: Mondelez International unveils RM90mil investment in Crumb Tower, deepening commitment to Malaysia
evidence.text:
Mondelez International unveils RM90mil investment in Crumb Tower, deepening commitment to Malaysia

SoftBank raises US$11.1bil in world's biggest high-yield corporate bond sale

KUALA LUMPUR: Mondelez International has launched its completed RM90 million Crumb Tower at the Cadbury Confectionery plant in Shah Alam, reinforcing its long-term confidence in Selangor and Malaysia as a strategic base for advanced chocolate manufacturing.

The tower was officially launched by Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, who recognised the investment as a reflection of the state’s continued ability to attract and retain high-value manufacturing activities.

In a joint statement today, the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) and Mondelez International said the investment builds on more than 50 years of manufacturing in Selangor, where Cadbury products have been made since 1974, and strengthens the Shah Alam plant through greater automation, advanced process technology and improved operational efficiency.

"The facility produces chocolate crumb, a key ingredient previously imported from markets including South Africa and Australia, strengthening self-sufficiency and supply-chain resilience while creating capacity to support markets beyond Southeast Asia.

"The Crumb Tower integrates three advanced systems: a fully enclosed high-capacity powder-handling system, a new-generation T-reactor, the first of its design in Malaysia, and an advanced fat-handling system built to rigorous process-safety standards, enabling a highly automated and digitally controlled process that meets international quality and food-safety standards, with halal requirements integrated throughout production,” the statement said.

MIDA chief executive officer Datuk Sikh Shamsul Ibrahim Sikh Abdul Majid said the agency is pleased to have supported the project.

"This investment reflects the company’s continued confidence in Malaysia as a strategic manufacturing base while demonstrating the value that quality investment can bring through advanced technology, local talent development, stronger domestic supply chains and future export opportunities.

"Importantly, the localisation of chocolate crumb production strengthens Malaysia’s manufacturing

capabilities and supply chain resilience,” he said.

He said food manufacturing remains one of Malaysia’s most resilient and fastest-growing sub-sectors, securing RM4.9 billion in approved investments in the first half of 2026, a 40.9 per cent increase year-on-year.

Sikh Shamsul said MIDA welcomes Mondelez’s continued commitment to Malaysia and its contribution to the country’s position as a competitive regional hub for high-value and halal food manufacturing.

Meanwhile, Mondelez International Malaysia and Singapore managing director Simon Crowther said the Crumb Tower reflects its continued commitment to investing in Malaysia and strengthening the company’s manufacturing capabilities through advanced technology and local expertise.

"By producing crumb locally, we are building greater self-sufficiency while positioning Shah Alam to play a larger role within our regional manufacturing network,” he added.

Mondelez International Southeast Asia MSC director Nitin Binnani said the project is a significant milestone for the company’s regional manufacturing and supply-chain network.

"By bringing chocolate crumb production in-house at Shah Alam, we are not only strengthening supply-chain resilience and leveraging domestic production but also building world-class technical capabilities locally.

"The advanced systems we have integrated here -- from the new-generation T-reactor to the automated powder- and fat-handling systems -- set a benchmark for operational excellence.

"This positions the Shah Alam plant as a true reference site within our global manufacturing network and underscores our confidence in Malaysian talent and expertise,” he said.

The statement said the investment also strengthens local technical capabilities by reducing manual powder and fat handling and expanding the use of process control, data analysis and specialised equipment maintenance.

It said Malaysian engineers and operators have been trained to manage the new systems, while local technology suppliers have been qualified to support other Mondelez sites globally.

The Shah Alam facility is now positioned as a reference plant for chocolate crumb operations within Mondelez’s global manufacturing network, it added. - Bernama

evidence.title: PepsiCo (PEP) Stock Dips as Company Plans to Reverse Earlier Price Cuts
evidence.text:
PepsiCo (PEP) Stock Dips as Company Plans to Reverse Earlier Price Cuts

Shares of PepsiCo experienced a decline of around 0.5% Thursday following a Bloomberg report indicating the food and beverage corporation is gearing up to implement new price increases. Trading opened at $130.18, significantly beneath the company’s 52-week peak of $171.48.

According to the report, PepsiCo intends to boost pricing on supermarket-sized chip packages, encompassing popular brands such as Doritos and Ruffles. Other offerings like SunChips are also projected to experience cost adjustments.

The ironic element? These identical products underwent price reductions earlier in the current year as part of an affordability initiative.

Unfortunately, that approach yielded disappointing results. Volume growth remained stagnant even with reduced pricing, based on information from sources familiar with the matter quoted by Bloomberg.

The company is now reversing portions of that decision. A company representative confirmed the forthcoming price adjustments will fall within the low-to-mid single digit range, approximately aligned with current inflation rates.

The company representative emphasized that revised pricing will remain lower than pre-2025 levels despite the adjustments. PepsiCo maintains its dedication to making products accessible to consumers even as select items become more expensive.

From a timeline perspective, these price modifications are projected to take effect late this year or during the first quarter of 2027. This window provides additional months for strategic planning around pricing decisions.

This policy reversal highlights the challenging position facing consumer packaged goods manufacturers currently. Companies must balance escalating production expenses against budget-conscious consumers increasingly selective about spending.

On Thursday, Citigroup decreased its PepsiCo price objective from $145 down to $142 while maintaining a neutral stance. This revised target nonetheless indicates roughly 9% upward potential from present trading levels.

Citigroup’s conservative approach mirrors broader Wall Street sentiment. The stock currently holds a consensus “Hold” designation, with seven analysts recommending Buy, twelve suggesting Hold, and one advising Sell. The mean price objective stands at $156.65.

Additional recent analyst activity includes TD Cowen and Weiss Ratings both confirming Hold recommendations within the past sixty days. Bank of America lowered its target from $173 to $164 during June.

PepsiCo’s most recent quarterly results, announced July 9, exceeded Wall Street projections. The corporation delivered $2.20 earnings per share versus the $2.19 consensus estimate, alongside revenue totaling $24.18 billion compared to anticipated $23.95 billion.

Top-line growth reached 6.4% on a year-over-year basis. Management has provided full-year EPS guidance spanning $8.55 to $8.71, with the Street modeling $8.57.

Options market activity has shown elevated interest recently. Market participants purchased 48,807 call contracts, representing approximately 62% above typical volumes, which some interpret as bullish positioning.

Regarding insider transactions, EVP David Flavell divested 2,900 shares in late July at $139.54 per share, generating proceeds exceeding $404,000. This sale reduced his position by approximately 3.7%.

Institutional shareholders maintain dominant ownership positions, controlling roughly 73% of outstanding shares. PepsiCo additionally announced this week it is affirming its investment pledges in Saudi Arabia as part of global expansion efforts.

evidence.title: PepsiCo to raise some chip prices after cutting them earlier this year
evidence.text:
Lay’s products are displayed on a shelf in a New York supermarket. Parent company Pepsico will increase prices for some chip brands, including Doritos and Ruffles. ADAM GRAY/Reuters

PepsiCo PEP-Q is set to raise prices for some chips to keep pace with inflation, a spokesperson for the company said, as the Lay’s maker works to revive sales in the United States.

PepsiCo is navigating shifting consumer preferences toward healthier snacking, weak demand from households pressured by rising fuel prices and higher commodity costs this year.

In February, PepsiCo cut prices by up to 15 per cent on products including Lay’s and Doritos after customer backlash against several rounds of previous price hikes.

The fresh round of price hikes will be implemented for some chip brands in the low- to mid-single-digit percentage range, which was in line with inflation, a spokesperson for PepsiCo told Reuters.

The new prices will be lower than they were before the price cuts earlier this year, and the company is trying to maintain lower prices where it can, the spokesperson added.

Prices are expected to go up on products including grocery-store-sized bags of chips from brands such as Doritos and Ruffles, and some sodas by the end of this year or in early 2027, according to a report by Bloomberg, which first reported the hikes, citing people familiar with the matter.

Analysis: PepsiCo under pressure to show results from turnaround drive

Activist investor Elliott Investment Management, which disclosed a roughly US$4-billion stake in PepsiCo last year, has pushed the company to reinvigorate its soda business, boost its share price and explore selling non-core food assets.

Elliott did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

PepsiCo shares, which have fallen nearly 10 per cent so far this year, dipped about 1 per cent in morning trading.

Several food and beverage companies have been contending with rising packaging and logistics costs as the Iran war keeps oil prices elevated.

In its latest earnings report, PepsiCo warned of higher commodity costs in the second half of the year and posted a 2-per-cent drop in second-quarter sales in its North American food business, although it kept its annual forecast intact.

The company also said in July that high gas prices had dented consumer demand more than it had anticipated.

Volumes in PepsiCo’s North America business have been negative through this year, despite the price cuts and CEO Ramon Laguarta’s plan to review its North America supply chain, which was announced in December.

With North America unlikely to recover this year despite PepsiCo’s efforts, “everything is likely ’in play’ for Elliott to dial up activism,” said BNP Paribas analyst Kevin Grundy in a note on Wednesday.

evidence.title: PepsiCo (PEP) Stock Price Target Cut Ahead of Possible Price Hikes
evidence.text:
PepsiCo (PEP) Stock Price Target Cut Ahead of Possible Price Hikes

PepsiCo stock slipped roughly 0.5% on Thursday after Bloomberg reported the snack and beverage giant is preparing to raise prices again. The stock opened at $130.18, well below its 52-week high of $171.48.

The report says PepsiCo plans to hike prices on grocery-store-sized bags of chips, including Doritos and Ruffles. SunChips and other brands are also expected to see increases.

Here’s the twist. These are the same products PepsiCo cut prices on earlier this year in an affordability push.

That strategy didn’t work as hoped. Sales failed to pick up despite the lower prices, according to people familiar with the plans cited by Bloomberg.

Now the company is walking some of that back. A PepsiCo spokesperson said the price increases will be in the low-to-mid single digits, roughly in line with inflation.

The spokesperson was careful to note the new prices will still sit below where they were before this year’s cuts. PepsiCo says it remains committed to its broader affordability effort even as certain items get pricier.

Timing-wise, the increases are expected to land at the end of this year or in early 2027. That gives the company a few more months to figure out its next move on pricing.

The reversal shows how tricky it is for consumer goods companies right now. They’re stuck between rising input costs and shoppers who are watching every dollar.

Citigroup trimmed its price target on PepsiCo to $142 from $145 on Thursday, while keeping a neutral rating. That target still points to about 9% upside from current levels.

Citigroup isn’t alone in playing it cautious. The stock carries a consensus “Hold” rating, with seven analysts at Buy, twelve at Hold and one at Sell. The average price target sits at $156.65.

Other recent moves include TD Cowen and Weiss Ratings both reiterating Hold ratings in the last two months. Bank of America cut its target to $164 from $173 back in June.

PepsiCo’s last earnings report, released July 9, actually beat estimates. The company posted $2.20 in EPS against a $2.19 consensus, with revenue of $24.18 billion versus $23.95 billion expected.

Revenue was up 6.4% year over year. PepsiCo has guided for full-year EPS between $8.55 and $8.71, and analysts are penciling in $8.57.

Options traders have been active too. Investors bought 48,807 call options recently, about 62% above the average volume, a signal some read as a bet on a rebound.

On the ownership side, EVP David Flavell sold 2,900 shares in late July at an average price of $139.54, a transaction worth just over $404,000. That trimmed his stake by roughly 3.7%.

Institutional investors continue to hold the bulk of the company, owning about 73% of shares outstanding. PepsiCo also confirmed this week it is reaffirming its investment commitments in Saudi Arabia as part of its international operations.

evidence.title: PepsiCo shutters 60-year-old Maryland plant, laying off 143 workers as weakening soda demand drives nationwide closures
evidence.text:
PepsiCo shutters 60-year-old Maryland plant, laying off 143 workers as weakening soda demand drives nationwide closures

More than 100 workers in Maryland have lost their jobs, as PepsiCo announced it was ending manufacturing and warehouse operations at a bottling plant that's at the heart of the community.

The Pepsi Bottling Group plant in Cheverly has been operating for more than 60 years and is considered a local landmark, according to a report from NBC4 Washington.

Dave Ramsey warns nearly 50% of Americans are making 1 big Social Security mistake. Here's what it is and 3 simple steps to fix it ASAP

The tax breaks in Trump's 'big beautiful bill' expire after 2028. Here are 4 moves to make before the window closes

It's the latest PepsiCo facility to see major layoffs, with the food and beverage giant shuttering or reducing operations at several facilities since 2024.

On Sept. 14, PepsiCo laid off 143 employees of the Cheverly plant in fleet, transport, manufacturing and warehouse operations, plus other salaried employees, the company said in a letter to the Maryland Department of Labor and the Cheverly mayor. According to the letter, 98 of those workers are represented by the Teamsters Local 639 union.

PepsiCo said that sales and delivery operations jobs would not be impacted.

Prince George's County Council Member Jolene Ivey told NBC4 that it was difficult news for the community.

"It's hard for the people who are losing their jobs, 100% that is the most important thing," she told NBC4. "And then for those of us who've just grown up with the Pepsi plant there, it just seems ... I don't know, it's just hard. You hate to think that something like that is going away. It's just been a part of our fabric."

According to a Cheverly official who NBC4 spoke to, the facility is the highest grossing revenue generator in the town and added roughly $200,000 annually.

Ivey told NBC4 that the aging factory faced power and water issues, which she said contributed to the decision.

"The building is so old," Ivey told NBC4. "The upgrades were so expensive and they were having problems with being able to keep the electricity going all the time. And the water itself cost too much for the company to upgrade to keep it going."

NBC4 reported that PepsiCo said in a statement that the decision was related to changes in consumer demand, technology and its operating network.

Since 2024, several PepsiCo facilities around the country have faced closures or major layoffs. In October 2024, PepsiCo announced the closure of four bottling plants, in Cincinnati, Chicago, Harrisburg, Penn., and Atlanta.

In July 2025, the company announced it would end manufacturing, transport and maintenance operations at its Detroit site. That announcement came just a week after the company said it was looking to move toward "integration" between PepsiCo's Frito-Lay North America and PepsiCo Beverages North America, to boost productivity.

In November 2025, PepsiCo said it would close two Florida Frito-Lay manufacturing facilities in Orlando, with 500 employees impacted.

In February 2026, PepsiCo said it would close a Frito-Lay warehouse in California, impacting nearly 250 workers. And in August 2026, PepsiCo permanently laid off more than 100 employees at its PepsiCo Beverages Sales building in Columbia, S.C., saying it was "shifting how warehouse logistics are managed" at the facility.

According to The Street, the latest round of layoffs is part of the company's efforts to improve productivity across its North American operating network.

Those changes are in response to "shifting consumer demand" and "sales declines," according to a separate report from The Street. Weakening demand has been attributed to both stubborn inflation and changing consumer tastes.

In July, speaking on an earnings call, PepsiCo CEO Ramon Laguarta said that "Results were tempered in the quarter as U.S. food and beverage category performance moderated with consumer budgets tightening due to rising inflationary pressures."

In addition to its restructuring, PepsiCo has responded to changing consumer tastes by launching healthier versions of some of its products and acquiring the prebiotic soda brand poppi.

evidence.title: RIP ProNutro: PepsiCo pulls the plug after 64 years
evidence.text:
RIP ProNutro: PepsiCo pulls the plug after 64 years

It’s gone! ProNutro, the cereal generations of South Africans breakfasted on, won’t be returning to the shelves in any form.

“After a long review process, PepsiCo has made the difficult decision to discontinue ProNutro in South Africa,” the company said in a statement on Wednesday.

That decision comes five months after PepsiCo replaced the original ProNutro with a “new generation” version made using a totally different manufacturing process.

Bokomo called it “The Original, Pushed Further”, but it pushed many of the brand’s devotees away.

The only warning consumers got was a banner at the top of the box which read: “New Generation ProNutro taste and texture”.

On social media, consumers complained about its strange taste, lumpy texture and a “chemical” smell when opening the packet. Many took issue with the new instructions to “whisk” the cereal after adding milk.

READ | Wendy Knowler | ‘It tastes weird’: New generation ProNutro is not going down well

In April, PepsiCo told News24 that “substantive national consumer testing” had been done with more than 300 consumers in Gauteng, KwaZulu-Natal and the Western Cape.

Half of them were ProNutro consumers. The other half were “non-ProNutro ready-to-eat cereal users”, included to ensure “that a new consumer base was represented”.

Amazingly, no children were among the tasters. PepsiCo said it chose not to test directly with children, relying instead on “adult proxies, caregiver insights, and rigorous internal standards”.

READ | Wendy Knowler | A ‘sorry’ after the disastrous ProNutro fail

Later that month, PepsiCo apologised to consumers on social media: “Mzansi, we’re sorry. We’ve heard you and while we can’t bring the old ProNutro back, we are finding ways to improve it.”

It said it would work on the new version’s “mixability” and keep consumers updated.

Now, five months on, the company says while mixability could be improved, “we were not able to recreate the taste and texture consumers associated with the original ProNutro using the new generation production process”.

The original product – a blend of cooked maize, soya, peanuts and skimmed milk – was roller-dried: slathered onto a scalding, spinning drum, then scraped off as a crisp, dry film.

The roller-drum process was developed in the 1960s, “at a time when water and electricity were more readily available and affordable than they are today”, PepsiCo said.

The ageing equipment was becoming increasingly difficult to maintain, and consistent quality was a growing challenge.

New, more cost-efficient processes have not been able to replicate ProNutro’s distinctive characteristics.

Also, sales of ProNutro had been declining and PepsiCo “continued to subsidise the brand for many years”, it said.

PepsiCo says the production process “could not simply be transferred to another manufacturer or reproduced elsewhere in the same way”.

There was “no clear like-for-like replacement for the original line”, it added, and any major production investment would have pushed up the price substantially.

Earlier this year, PepsiCo told News24 that replacing the old machinery would add about R25 to the price of a 500g pack, a premium it doubted its customers would be willing to pay.

Companies have been known to bring back the original versions of iconic products in the face of mass public rejection. Unilever recently brought back its original Sunlight “green bar” soap after widespread condemnation of its reformulated version.

And Coca-Cola did an about-turn within three months after its New Coke bombed with consumers.

But PepsiCo says that was not an option for ProNutro. For one, the machinery that was used to make the original product has been scrapped.

“After carefully reviewing every available option, we could not return to the original way of making ProNutro in a manner that was reliable, affordable for consumers and environmentally responsible,” the company said.

Dare consumers hope that somehow another manufacturer will come to market with a version of the old ProNutro, similar to how Peck’s Anchovette made a comeback?

PepsiCo acquired Pioneer Foods in March 2020 in one of its biggest acquisitions outside the US. In the following year, the group killed Peck’s Anchovette for similar reasons to ProNutro, prompting howls of protest from ardent fish paste fans.

In response, Cape Gulf Brands and Premier Fishing acquired Peck’s Anchovette, partnering initially with Pick n Pay as their exclusive retail launch partner, though the iconic product has since expanded to major retailers nationwide.

So could another company bring ProNutro back? There is a chance, albeit a small one.

Nestlé and Purity still use the energy-intensive roller-drum drying process for their baby cereals – Cerelac and Purity Baby Cereal – because it produces a light, non-sticky texture that babies can swallow safely.

But they can sell the baby cereals at a premium price – about double what the original ProNutro sold for until about six months ago.

ProNutro was launched commercially in 1962 by Durban company Hind Brothers & Co. The world’s first nutraceutical cereal was the result of years of research by Dr Francis Fox of the South African Institute for Medical Research, who worked with Dr Willem Odendaal, among others, on a high-protein food to combat malnutrition.

Johannesburg-based food scientist Nigel Sunley, who was involved with ProNutro from 1981 and was tasked with its research and development when he joined National Brands, calls the decision to kill ProNutro “insane”.

When National Brands sold its cereals business to Bokomo in 1997, Sunley was part of the deal, and became factory manager of the ProNutro plant in Wadeville on the East Rand.

Along the way, he earned the nickname “Mr ProNutro”.

He started his own consultancy in 2007 but was called in to consult on technical issues several times after that.

Sunley’s team experimented with making ProNutro on cooker-extruders, the technology he believes is behind the “new generation” version, in the 1980s and 1990s. He says they managed to produce a palatable product that kept its nutritional quality, but they couldn’t match the original flavour and texture.

Plenty of nutrient-dense products are made on extruders, Sunley says, but “when the benchmark is the original ProNutro, it’s quite tough”.

He believes it was commercial madness to scrap the machinery. “It seems they did not understand people’s passion for the product.”

In his view, ProNutro’s diehard devotees would have been prepared to pay a premium for the original as a niche product.

Asked whether he had anticipated that PepsiCo would kill the brand altogether, Sunley said: “I suppose it was right at the back of my mind. But I didn’t think they would be so stupid.”

If you managed to stockpile the original ProNutro when it began disappearing from shelves, be aware that the last-ever batch of the original reaches its best-before date next month.

And while many shelf-stable foods can safely be eaten for some time after that date, that doesn’t apply to ProNutro, says Sunley.

“The soya flour in the product has an unstable oil content, so it starts going rancid from the 12-month mark.”

evidence.title: ICA Gruppen Grows Market Share, Reports Lower Profit
evidence.text:
ICA Gruppen Grows Market Share, Reports Lower Profit

ICA Gruppen saw an increase in market share, but lower profits, in the first four months of 2025, primarily due to strategic price reductions in Sweden .

The sale of Rimi Baltic to Denmark’s Salling Group was finalised on 2 June, having received all the necessary regulatory approvals.

This sale, which completes the divestment of operations in the Baltic countries, will reduce ICA Gruppen’s debt, providing the company with more financial resources and flexibility to focus its investments on its Swedish business.

While ICA Sweden outpaced market growth, its operating margin for the first four months of the year dropped to 2.3%, from 3.5% in the same period last year.

The company attributed this decline to price investments and the cost of double bonus coupons offered to members of the Stammis loyalty programme .

These coupons were implemented to mitigate the impact of inflation , which was driven by factors like increased cocoa and coffee prices during the period.

Excluding non-recurring items, ICA Sweden’s operating profit amounted to SEK 859 million (€78 million) – down from SEK 1.19 billion (€108.9 million) in the comparable period.

Apotek Hjärtat expanded its bricks-and-mortar market share during the four months, but experienced weaker online sales.

Overall, Apotek Hjärtat’s total growth exceeded the market by the end of the period. ICA Bank, including ICA Insurance, saw increased profit due to business growth and lower credit losses, though insurance earnings were hampered by higher claims.

ICA Gruppen’s total net sales for the first four months rose by 5.5%, to SEK 45.2 billion (€4.1 billion).

Operating profit, excluding one-time items and the impact of lease accounting (IFRS 16), decreased to SEK 1.2 billion (€109 million), resulting in a 2.8% operating margin – down from 3.8% in the previous year.

Overall profit for the period increased by SEK 203 million (€18 million), to SEK 1.22 billion (€111 million). This increase is entirely due to a SEK 362 million (€33 million) gain from discontinued operations (Rimi Baltic), compared to a small loss in the same period last year.

ICA Gruppen’s CEO, Nina Jönsson, commented, “During the first four months, ICA Sweden gained market share, and online sales performed favourably. However, earnings were weaker than last year.”

Jönsson furthered, “It was gratifying that food prices started to fall again in April – down 0.2% from March, according to Statistics Sweden’s Consumer Price Index .”

evidence.title: Axfood AB's Dividend Analysis
evidence.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Axfood AB ( AXFOY ) Gears Up for Its Next Dividend Payment

Axfood AB ( AXFOY ) recently announced a total dividend of $0.47 per share, with the ex-dividend date set for 2026-09-18. This payment consists of $0.47 per share in cash dividends, payable on 2026-10-13. For investors, the ex-dividend date is a critical marker: shareholders must own the stock before this date to qualify for the payout, while the paydate indicates when the cash actually lands in accounts. As investors look forward to this upcoming payment, the spotlight also shines on the company's dividend history, yield, and growth rates. Using data from GuruFocus, let's look into Axfood AB's dividend performance and assess its sustainability.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 6 Warning Signs with AXFOY.

High Yield Dividend Stocks in Gurus' Portfolio

This Powerful Chart Made Peter Lynch 29% A Year For 13 Years

How to calculate the intrinsic value of a stock?

Is AXFOY fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Axfood AB operates food retail and wholesale businesses in Sweden. The company runs various food retail grocery chains, discount stores, hypermarkets, restaurants, cafes, and pharmacies through different brands. Its operating segments include Willys, Hemkop, Dagab, City Gross, and Snabbgross. A majority of revenue is generated from the Willys segment, a discount grocery chain offering various products in both group-owned stores and online. This segment also includes the partly owned cross-border grocery chain Eurocash. For value investors, this diversified footprint across discount and premium formats provides exposure to a defensive, consumer-staples business with relatively stable demand across economic cycles.

Axfood AB has maintained a consistent dividend payment record since 2009, a track record spanning more than 15 years. Dividends are currently distributed on a bi-annual basis, meaning shareholders receive two payments per year rather than a single annual distribution. This cadence can be attractive for income-focused investors who prefer more frequent cash flows. Below is a chart showing annual Dividends Per Share, which tracks historical trends and helps investors gauge how management has prioritized returning capital over time.

As of today, Axfood AB currently has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 3.73% and a 12-month forward dividend yield of 3.83%. The trailing yield reflects dividends actually paid over the past year, while the forward yield is based on expected future payments. The gap between the two suggests an expectation of increased dividend payments over the next 12 months, a modest but meaningful signal for income investors comparing Axfood AB against peers in the consumer staples space.

Over the past three years, Axfood AB's annual dividend growth rate was 4.30%. Extended to a five-year horizon, this rate decreased to 4.20% per year. Over the past decade, Axfood AB's annual dividends per share growth rate stands at 6.60%. This pattern, faster growth over ten years than over the most recent five, indicates a gradual moderation in dividend increases, a trend worth monitoring for those relying on the payout for income.

Based on Axfood AB's dividend yield and five-year growth rate, the 5-year yield on cost of Axfood AB stock as of today is approximately 4.58%. Yield on cost measures the annual dividend return relative to an investor's original purchase price, assuming reinvestment and growth, and illustrates how a steadily rising payout can compound returns for long-term holders.

To assess the sustainability of the dividend, one needs to evaluate the company's payout ratio. The dividend payout ratio provides insights into the portion of earnings the company distributes as dividends. A lower ratio suggests that the company retains a significant part of its earnings, thereby ensuring the availability of funds for future growth and unexpected downturns. As of 2026-06-30, Axfood AB's dividend payout ratio is 0.79. And this may suggest that the company's dividend may not be sustainable, since nearly four-fifths of earnings are being paid out rather than retained.

Axfood AB's profitability rank offers an understanding of the company's earnings prowess relative to its peers. GuruFocus ranks Axfood AB's profitability 9 out of 10 as of 2026-06-30, suggesting good profitability prospects. The company has reported positive net income for each year over the past decade, further solidifying its high profitability. This combination of a high payout ratio and strong profitability presents a nuanced picture: earnings cover the dividend, but the margin for error is thinner than for companies retaining more capital.

To ensure the sustainability of dividends, a company must have robust growth metrics. Axfood AB's growth rank of 9 out of 10 suggests that the company's growth trajectory is good relative to its competitors. A high growth rank implies expanding revenues and earnings, which can support future dividend increases even when the current payout ratio runs high.

Revenue is the lifeblood of any company, and Axfood AB's revenue per share, combined with the 3-year revenue growth rate, indicates a strong revenue model. Axfood AB's revenue has increased by approximately 6.20% per year on average, a rate that outperforms approximately 56.23% of global competitors. Steady top-line expansion in a defensive industry supports the case that the dividend can be maintained and potentially grown.

The company's 3-year EPS growth rate showcases its capability to grow its earnings, a critical component for sustaining dividends in the long run. During the past three years, Axfood AB's earnings increased by approximately -0.60% per year on average, a rate that outperforms approximately 33.85% of global competitors. The slight decline in earnings per share, despite revenue growth, highlights pressure on margins and explains why the payout ratio has climbed.

Lastly, the company's 5-year EBITDA growth rate of 2.50% outperforms approximately 39.27% of global competitors. EBITDA, or earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, is a rough measure of operating cash flow. Moderate growth here suggests the company generates stable cash to fund payouts, though not at a pace that would comfortably support aggressive dividend increases.

Axfood AB's upcoming $0.47 per share dividend, payable on 2026-10-13 to shareholders of record before the 2026-09-18 ex-dividend date, continues a payout record stretching back to 2009. The stock offers a trailing yield of 3.73% and a forward yield of 3.83%, with a 5-year yield on cost near 4.58%. However, a payout ratio of 0.79 and slightly negative three-year EPS growth warrant caution. Strong profitability and growth ranks of 9 out of 10, plus 6.20% annual revenue growth, provide offsetting support. Value investors should weigh this balance of reliable income against limited earnings expansion before deciding whether Axfood AB deserves a place in their income portfolio.

evidence.title: Axfood’s climate goals win Science Based Targets validation
evidence.text:
Axfood’s climate goals win Science Based Targets validation

Axfood AB ( (SE:AXFO) ) has issued an update.

Axfood has had its climate targets validated by the Science Based Targets initiative, aligning the food retailer’s decarbonisation strategy with the Paris Agreement’s 1.5°C pathway and sharpening its focus on cutting emissions across operations and its value chain. The company has already shifted all Group-owned and procured warehouse-to-store transport to renewable fuels or electricity and continues to invest in energy efficiency, lower-impact refrigerants and a more sustainable product range.

The approved targets commit Axfood to reduce absolute Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions by at least 70% by 2030 from a 2024 base year, ensure that at least 70% of its suppliers set science-based climate goals and cut land use, forestry and agriculture-related emissions by 30.3%. By joining the SBTi framework, Axfood seeks to strengthen collaboration with suppliers, meet rising stakeholder demands for transparency and comparability, and reinforce its positioning as a leader in sustainable food retail.

evidence.title: Axfood: Margin Improvement Can't Overcome Sales Deceleration - Too Early To Buy
evidence.text:
Catch pre-market movers with AI signals.

- Axfood's stock fell 21% from its 52-week high after Q2 2026 results showed 1.7% sales growth, a sharp slowdown from prior years' 5-8% growth.

- While adjusted operating margins improved to 3.8% (target: 4.5%), revenue deceleration raises concerns about sustainability of margin gains without volume growth.

- At 20x forward earnings, the stock remains expensive for a company with weak sales momentum, requiring 5%+ organic growth to justify valuation expansion.

- Analysts recommend holding until Q2 confirms stabilized sales growth or management demonstrates a credible path to 5%+ organic expansion while maintaining margin progress.

Axfood shares are about 21% below their 52-week high, sitting around SEK 266 after the company released its second-quarter 2026 interim report. The market is clearly troubled by something. The question is whether the selloff has created a buying opportunity or whether the stock's problems are only becoming visible at this point.

The answer, based on the H1 2026 results and consensus expectations, is that Axfood is not out of the woods. Profitability is improving, but revenue growth has decelerated sharply from the blistering pace investors got used to over the past two years. The stock is cheaper, but not cheap enough to ignore the revenue slowdown.

Axfood reported first-half 2026 net sales of SEK 44.8 billion, up just 1.7% from the prior-year period. That is a meaningful deceleration. For context, Axfood's fiscal 2025 retail sales grew 8.7%, and even excluding the City Gross convenience chain acquisition, organic retail growth was 5.3%. The Swedish grocery market grew 4.5% over that same period, meaning Axfood was outpacing the market by a wide margin.

Now the pace has slowed to 1.7% on a consolidated basis for the first half of 2026. Q1 alone showed net sales growth of only 2.6%, driven by higher volumes, with retail sales up 3.8% . The trajectory is clear: the high-velocity growth phase that carried Axfood's stock to SEK 339 is over.

Wall Street consensus for Q2 calls for net sales of SEK 23.5 billion and an adjusted operating margin of 4.28% . If actual Q2 results land near consensus, the improvement in the second quarter over the first would be almost entirely margin-driven, not volume-driven. That distinction matters because margin gains without sales growth are ultimately limited - you can only deflation-proof or price-optimise so far before volume suffers.

On the profitability side, the quarter delivers. Q1 adjusted operating profit rose 12.1% year-over-year to SEK 806 million, with the adjusted operating margin at 3.8%. Management's strategic target is an operating margin of at least 4.5% . Consensus for Q2 puts the adjusted margin at 4.28%, which would put the company much closer to that target.

But margin improvement in a grocery business during a period of weak sales growth tells you something about the trade-off. Either Axfood is cutting costs at a rate the market can't sustain, or it's relying on deflationary price normalization to protect margins while volume growth stalls. Neither path is indefinite.

The company's own title for the release - " strengthened presence and positive earnings development " - captures the management view. But the investor's job is to decide whether that narrative compensates for revenue deceleration at a stock trading on SEK 57 billion in market capitalisation .

At SEK 266 and a market cap of roughly SEK 57 billion, Axfood has clearly lost ground. Consensus EPS for Q2 is SEK 3.09, which implies roughly SEK 12–13 of annualised earnings if the second half continues the margin trajectory. That would put the stock at about 20 times forward earnings.

For a grocery operator growing consolidated sales at 1.7%, a 20x earnings multiple is not a discount. It is a standard multiple for a business that is executing adequately but not accelerating. The stock would need to demonstrate that the margin path toward 4.5% is durable and that sales growth can at least return to the mid-single-digit range before investors should expect multiple expansion.

The bear case is straightforward: if Swedish grocery demand softens further, or if competitors intensify price competition, Axfood's margin trajectory stalls, and the stock has no growth tailwind to fall back on. The 52-week low of SEK 252.90 is already within striking distance.

Axfood becomes a buy if one of two things happens. First, if the Q2 report - released today - shows that retail sales growth has reaccelerated, particularly on an organic basis excluding City Gross integration. Second, if management guidance signals a credible path back to 5%+ organic growth while maintaining the margin trajectory.

Neither condition is visible in the H1 numbers so far. The sales growth deceleration is the dominant feature of this quarter, and margin improvement alone does not offset it at the current multiple.

Axfood is a well-managed grocery operator with a clear margin-expansion playbook and a growing convenience-channel footprint through City Gross. But the business has entered a phase where revenue growth has meaningfully slowed, and the stock isn't cheap enough to bet on a recovery that hasn't materialised.

I'm not downgrading. The margin trajectory and market-share gains from the prior two years are real achievements. But at SEK 266, the risk/reward is tilted toward patience. Wait for Q2 to confirm that volume growth is stabilising before deploying capital here.

Axfood And WITRON Realise Full-Range Distribution Centre In Southern Sweden

In December 2025, Swedish food retailer Axfood and the WITRON Group signed an agreement to build a new full-range logistics centre in Kungsbacka, near Gothenburg in southern Sweden.

The 90,000 square metre highly automated facility will supply more than 400 stores with different dry, fresh, and frozen items.

On peak days, more than 560,000 cases will be picked in a store-friendly manner using fully and semi-automated processes.

The project further expands the strategic partnership between Axfood and WITRON, which previously collaborated on the omni-channel distribution centre in Bålsta near Stockholm.

This solution will give us a more flexible, efficient and sustainable logistics chain for product supply to our stores in the southern parts of Sweden, thereby strengthening the entire Axfood family’s competitiveness,” comments Simone Margulies, president and CEO of Axfood.

“It feels very good to have the agreement in place for this strategically important automation solution. With the experience we have built together with Witron in Bålsta, we know that this technology will give us the right conditions going forward and as a natural step, we feel confident in continuing this journey also in southern Sweden,” said Hans Bax, managing director of Dagab.

The new facility will store and pick products across three temperature zones: ambient goods (+18 °C), fresh goods (+2 °C), and frozen items (-26 °C).

As in Bålsta, the system will use several WITRON logistics modules, including Order Picking Machinery (OPM), All-in-One (AIO) and the Car Picking System (CPS), supported by a fully automated shipping buffer.

This buffer will sequence pallets by delivery route to enable efficient truck loading.

The logistic centre will include more than 500,000 storage locations for pallets, roll containers and totes supported by 111 stacker cranes and over 16 kilometres of conveyor technology.

All processes will be managed through a multifunctional warehouse management system connected to supplier, routing and sales systems, enabling end-to-end supply chain optimisation.

Since early 2025, Axfood and WITRON have already operated a highly automated omni-channel distribution centre in Bålsta, supplying stores and online customers via click + collect and home delivery.

The system handles more than 22,000 dry, fresh, and frozen products.

For more information, visit www.witron.de .

evidence.title: Axfood AB: Growth in all segments and increased market shares
evidence.text:
Axfood AB: Growth in all segments and increased market shares

Axfood summarises another strong quarter with high customer traffic, volume growth and increased market shares, as well as positive earnings trends in all operating segments. The Group continues to invest in strategically important areas in order to become even more efficient and further improve its competitiveness. In recent years, the logistics structure has been developed to enable continued profitable growth, and in the quarter plans were announced for a new, highly automated logistics centre in Kungsbacka with the aim of increasing capacity and efficiency also in southern Sweden.

President and CEO Simone Margulies comments on the interim report for the third quarter 2025: "Thanks to affordable and attractive offerings, more and more consumers are choosing to shop with us. Having maintained our momentum, we delivered a strong performance in the quarter and gained market shares. Axfood's retail sales increased approximately 19% and just over 6% excluding City Gross, while market growth amounted to slightly more than 5%. With its position as Sweden's leading discount grocery chain, Willys is continuing to develop its offering. Among other initiatives, existing stores are rapidly being upgraded to the new Willys 5.0 store concept, and the rate of new store establishments is also accelerated in the coming years, with the aim of opening at least ten new stores each year. Hemköp, which operates in the traditional grocery segment, is also modernising stores at a rapid rate in order to enhance the customer meeting. Its offering is continuously being developed, with a focus on price value, fresh products and meal solutions. Our restaurant wholesaler, Snabbgross, delivered growth of 6% in the quarter.

City Gross was acquired nearly a year ago to create new growth opportunities. The organisation is following a clear plan and has a comprehensive development agenda in order to reverse the store chain's weak development in recent years. We are seeing positive trends in like-for-like growth and cost levels as a result of our initiatives. City Gross has excellent potential as a pure-play hypermarket operator, an attractive segment that is continuing to account for a growing share of the market.

With increased loyalty and growth in the store chains, earnings improved in all operating segments. In addition to efficiency and cost focus in our base operations - with respect to both logistics and our central processes and ways of working - the operating margin for the Group as a whole increased. Dagab is continuing its efforts to optimise the flow of goods and streamline the Group's new logistics structure. The logistics centre in Bålsta, the fruit and vegetable warehouse in Landskrona and the recently expanded high-bay warehouse in Backa are all clearly contributing to the Group's capacity and efficiency. We have also initated work to establish a new highly automated logistics centre in Kungsbacka which will strengthen the Group's product supply in southern Sweden.

The Food 2030 report, Axfood's proposal for a more sustainable food strategy for Sweden, was presented during the quarter. In addition, the phase-out of fossil fuels in our own and procured transports continued to reduce our emissions during the quarter, and our new solar park in Hallstavik in the Uppland region is now fully operational. We also continued to launch innovative new products focused on improved sustainability and health.

Our performance in the third quarter demonstrates the strength of our business model, with higher growth than the market and improved earnings in all operating segments. The development shows how we with our different concepts and brands drives loyalty and growth in all segments of the market - both organically and through expansion. With our integrated value chain, we create competitive advantages and efficiency in base operations. Together with a high rate of development, a strong corporate culture, and highly engaged employees, I am convinced that we are poised to continue to challenge and strengthen our market positions also in the years ahead."

Axfood will present the interim report for the third quarter 2025 in a webcast at 9:30 a.m. (CET) today, 23 October 2025. The report will be presented by Simone Margulies, President and CEO, and Anders Lexmon, CFO. You can find a link to the webcast at axfood.com. A link to register to participate via conference call is also available at axfood.com. Upon registration, a telephone number and conference ID for the conference call will be provided.

For further information, please contact: Alexander Bergendorf, Head of Investor Relations, Axfood AB, tel +46 73 049 18 44

The information herein is such that Axfood AB (publ) is required to make public in accordance with the EU Market Abuse Regulation. The information was submitted for publication, through the agency of the contact person listed above, at 7:00 a.m. CET on 23 October 2025.

This document is an English translation of the Swedish original. In the event of any discrepancies, the Swedish version shall govern.

Axfood aspires to be the leader in affordable, good and sustainable food. Our family of companies includes the store chains Willys, Hemköp and City Gross as well as Tempo, Handlar'n and Matöppet. B2B sales are handled through Snabbgross, and our support company Dagab is responsible for the Group's product development, purchasing and logistics. The Axfood family also includes Urban Deli as well as the partly owned companies Apohem and Eurocash. Together the Group has more than 15,000 employees and sales of close to SEK 90 billion. Axfood has been listed on Nasdaq Stockholm since 1997, and the principal owner is Axel Johnson AB. Read more at www.axfood.com.

evidence.title: Axfood And WITRON Join Forces For New Automated Logistics Centre
evidence.text:
Axfood And WITRON Join Forces For New Automated Logistics Centre

Axfood has announced plans to establish a new highly automated logistics centre in southern Sweden to ensure higher capacity and efficiency for the group’s future growth.

Letters of intent have been signed with WITRON to use the company’s automation technology and with the Municipality of Kungsbacka to locate the logistics centre to Frillesås. WITRON is a market leader in dynamic warehouse and order-picking systems.

The centre is expected to be completed in 2030. The investment need for the future automation solution is estimated to amount to €260-280 million during the period 2025 to 2030.

“We are building for the future," said Simone Margulies, president and CEO of Axfood. "With the new logistics solution, we will become even more competitive and create synergies within the group."

She added, "We are investing to meet future needs for goods delivery to both the group’s own stores and our customers’ stores in a flexible and efficient way.”

The investment will be financed through a combination of operating cash ﬂow and credit facilities.

Axfood intends to enter into a long-term lease contract for the logistics property, and discussions with potential property owners are ongoing. The detailed development plan process has been initiated.

To optimise logistics operations, the logistics centre in Kungsbacka will primarily handle store volumes to food retail and will primarily replace the existing warehouse in Backa.

At the same time, the new logistics centre is built to handle volumes that currently is handled from the warehouses in Jönköping and Hässleholm. Fruit, vegetables, and flowers will continue to be handled from the warehouse in Landskrona.

Overall, Axfood’s capacity with the new logistics centre is expected to increase by at least 20% compared to the current volume in southern Sweden.

"Through the establishment in Frillesås, Kungsbacka, we will become more efficient in adapting to how the future food retail is evolving," said Hans Bax, managing director of Dagab.

"With the establishment of our logistics centre in Bålsta, we have experience from these types of facilities and feel conﬁdent in pursuing this initiative together with our automation partner WITRON.”

evidence.text:
Orkla stock closed at NOK 94.35 on the Oslo Bors on September 24, 2026, up 1.18 percent. The close was 28.1 percent below the 52-week high of NOK 131.20 and 4.8 percent above the 52-week low of NOK 90.00.

Orkla ASA (ISIN NO0003733800, Oslo Bors: ORK) traded at NOK 94.35 on September 24, 2026, according to the dated market data. The session move followed a buyback plan for up to 80 million shares and NOK 4.0 billion, as Ad-hoc-news.de reported on September 24, 2026.

The share price was NOK 4.35 above the reported 52-week low and NOK 36.85 below the reported 52-week high. The same report put Orkla market capitalization at NOK 92,247,398,645 on September 24, 2026.

The buyback authorization remains the latest company-specific market item cited for Orkla. Norway's central bank raised its policy rate to 4.50 percent on September 24, 2026, and said another increase remained possible, according to Yahoo Finance reporting on the Reuters dispatch; the decision is relevant to Norwegian equities through domestic interest-rate conditions.

evidence.title: Orkla stock falls 1.11 percent as buyback starts
evidence.text:
Orkla stock stood at NOK 93.25 on the Oslo Stock Exchange on September 23, 2026, down 1.11 percent from the prior close of NOK 94.30. The move came as the Norwegian consumer goods group began a share buyback program worth up to NOK 4 billion.

According to Inderes , the program can cover up to 80 million shares and is scheduled to run from September 22, 2026, until December 31, 2027, at the latest. The stated purpose is to reduce share capital and return excess capital to shareholders.

The scale matters against Orkla's market capitalization of NOK 91.17 billion as of September 23, 2026. The maximum buyback authorization therefore represents 4.39 percent of that equity value, although the final amount depends on actual purchases.

Orkla's latest reported interim period was Q2 2026, released on August 20, 2026, according to the company's Orkla investor page. The earnings-call transcript hosted by Yahoo Finance says underlying adjusted EBIT grew 2.5 percent, while reported revenue declined 5 percent because of currency translation effects.

That combination gives the buyback a specific operating backdrop. Earnings quality improved on an underlying basis, but the reported top line remained exposed to exchange-rate movements.

At NOK 93.25 on September 23, 2026, Orkla stock was 28.92 percent below its 52-week high of NOK 131.20 and 3.61 percent above its 52-week low of NOK 90. The market is therefore pricing the shares near the lower end of their annual range while the capital-return program enters its opening phase.

Orkla ASA (0FIN), the Oslo-based Norwegian branded consumer goods company, has revealed a share repurchase programme valued at up to NOK 4,000,000,000, set to begin on 22 September 2026. Approved by shareholders during the Annual General Meeting on 23 April 2026, this initiative aims to return surplus capital by decreasing the company’s share capital. The buyback will be independently overseen by ABG Sundal Collier and is scheduled to continue until 31 December 2027, subject to renewal conditions.

Details on Orkla’s NOK 4 Billion Buyback: Scope and Share Capital Reduction

The programme authorises Orkla to repurchase its own shares worth up to NOK 4,000,000,000, with a cap of 80,000,000 shares eligible for buyback. This maximum share count is based on a minimum share price of NOK 50 per share, as stipulated by the AGM authorisation. Orkla intends to seek shareholder approval to cancel the repurchased shares, indicating the buyback is designed to reduce total share capital rather than retain treasury shares indefinitely.

ABG Sundal Collier to Execute Buyback under EU Market Abuse Safe Harbour Regulations

ABG Sundal Collier has been appointed to independently manage the share repurchase programme, making all trading decisions without influence from Orkla. All transactions will comply with the Market Abuse Regulation (EU) No 596/2014 and Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/1052, known as the Safe Harbour Regulation. This regulatory framework ensures legal certainty for buyback activities and protects against market manipulation allegations when conditions on pricing, volume, and disclosure are met.

2026 AGM Authorisation Enables Programme; 2027 Renewal Essential for Continuation

The share buyback is authorised by Orkla’s Board following approval at the Annual General Meeting held on 23 April 2026. The company notes that continuation past the 2027 AGM depends on shareholder approval to renew the buyback authorisation. Investors will closely watch the 2027 AGM agenda, as failure to renew could halt the programme before its scheduled end in December 2027. This announcement complies with the Norwegian Securities Trading Act Section 5-12 and the Market Abuse Regulation.

Capital Return Strategy Reflects Orkla’s Strong Financial Position Ahead of 2027

Orkla’s choice to return excess capital through a structured buyback programme highlights a strategic capital allocation decision by its Board. By reducing share capital instead of pursuing acquisitions or holding cash, the company demonstrates confidence in its financial stability. Operating primarily in the Nordic and Baltic regions across branded food, confectionery, and consumer goods sectors, Orkla aims to boost shareholder returns through this initiative. Investor relations contacts include SVP Annie Bersagel and Investor Relations Manager Ole Andreas Steensland Dahl, both based in Oslo.

evidence.title: Orkla Snacks Completes Acquisition Of Vegan Confectionery Firm
evidence.text:
Orkla Snacks Completes Acquisition Of Vegan Confectionery Firm

Orkla Snacks has completed its acquisition of The European Candy Group (CCI), a major manufacturer of vegan sugar confectionery , it said in a statement.

The group announced its planned acquisition of CCI on 31 July, and the deal has now received the necessary regulatory approvals to proceed.

“CCI is a natural strategic fit for Orkla Snacks, adding production capacity to support continued BUBS growth in the Nordic markets and enable faster expansion into new European markets," commented Ingvill T. Berg, CEO of Orkla Snacks .

"We are also welcoming a strong business, highly skilled employees, valuable expertise and a broad customer network spanning several European markets."

CCI operates four factories across the Netherlands and Germany and has been producing selected products for Orkla Snacks' BUBS brand since 2025.

Orkla said that following the takeover, it will continue to operate its 'existing, profitable business', while also scaling production of BUBS.

“Becoming part of Orkla Snacks marks the beginning of an exciting new chapter for CCI," added Alfred Attema, CEO of CCI.

"Through our collaboration over the past year, we have got to know Orkla Snacks well, and we look forward to developing the business further together. This provides a solid foundation for our employees and customers."

Additional capacity is also being added at Orkla's BUBS factory in Jönköping, Sweden, to support continued growth in Europe and international markets.

BUBS has gained 'strong momentum' in the US in recent years, with the brand currently available in more than 60,000 stores, including major retailers such as Target, Walmart, Kroger and CVS.

Orkla Snacks reported annual turnover of approximately NOK 9.7 billion in 2024.

evidence.title: Orkla India chief backs FSSAI push for front-of-pack food labels
evidence.text:
Orkla India chief backs FSSAI push for front-of-pack food labels

Sanjay Sharma says packaged food industry backs FSSAI's push to empower informed consumer choices

Orkla India managing director and CEO Sanjay Sharma has backed the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India's (FSSAI) proposed front-of-pack labelling (FOPL) norms for packaged foods, saying consumers have the right to access clear nutritional information before making purchasing decisions.

Speaking to PTI, Sharma said the packaged food industry supports FSSAI's broader objective of empowering consumers as awareness about nutrition and food choices continues to grow.

“Consumers deserve greater information about the products they consume,” Sharma said, adding that the industry is aligned with the regulator's intent to help consumers make informed choices.

Sharma, who is also engaged with industry body CII on the issue, said the key debate is not over whether front-of-pack labels should be introduced, but what form the labels should take and how they should be implemented.

“The industry is (ready) for the entire thing. The question is what should be the label and how should it be done,” he said.

The comments come amid ongoing discussions over FSSAI's proposed phased implementation of FOPL on packaged food products. The proposed system seeks to provide prominent information on sugar, salt and fat, particularly to help consumers identify products containing higher levels of these nutrients.

The issue is currently before the Supreme Court. On Friday, the apex court sought further clarification from FSSAI on its proposed front-of-pack labels covering “nutrients of concern”, including fat, sugar and salt.

Sharma said the industry has already held extensive consultations with FSSAI and made several submissions regarding the proposed framework. While reiterating the industry's support for the initiative, he stressed that the format and implementation mechanism need to be carefully considered.

He also called for the regulator to follow the established process for framing such regulations, including consultations with industry stakeholders, consumer organisations and other relevant bodies.

“The standard process is to come out with a draft, do consultations with the industry, with the consumer bodies which take care of consumer interest, with all people who are concerned with regulations, with the WTO, and eventually get notified as legislation,” Sharma said.

He expressed hope that the established regulatory process would be followed, noting that draft food regulations are required to be notified to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) before final notification in accordance with India's international trade obligations.

Sharma said he would not “second guess” the Supreme Court's eventual decision, given that the matter is currently pending before the apex court and FSSAI has already submitted its recommendations.

Orkla India, part of Norwegian conglomerate Orkla ASA, has a significant presence in India's packaged food market. Its portfolio includes brands such as MTR, Eastern and Rasoi Magic, with products spanning ready-to-cook and ready-to-eat meals, vermicelli, spices and other convenience foods.

FSSAI's proposed FOPL framework is aimed at giving consumers easily accessible nutritional information on packaged foods, with the broader objective of enabling more informed choices and encouraging greater awareness of dietary intake.

On Friday, the Supreme Court asked the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, which has proposed phased implementation of front-of-package labelling (FoPL) on packaged foods, to come up with more clarifications on the planned labels of "nutrients of concern", fat, sugar and salt.

He said the point of contention was not the principle of labelling but its format and implementation, adding that the industry has made "a lot of consultations and submissions" to FSSAI on the issue.

The broader industry is supportive of the initiative, while discussions continue on the format and implementation of the proposed labels, said Sharma, who is already engaged with industry body CII on this issue.

"The industry is (ready) for the entire thing. The question is what should be the label and how should it be done," Sharma said, noting that the industry has made several submissions to the regulator on the matter.

Orkla India, part of the Norwegian conglomerate Orkla ASA, is a leading packed food company here.

It owns household brands such as MTR, Rasoi Magic and Eastern, with a play in convenience foods such as ready-to-cook (RTC), ready-to-eat (RTE) meals, vermicelli, as well as in the blended and pure spices space.

Noting that the FOPL matter is currently pending before the Supreme Court, with FSSAI having submitted its recommendations, the Orkla India chief said he did not wish to "second guess" the apex court's eventual view.

He, however, underlined that FSSAI's standard regulatory process should ideally be followed for a matter of this nature.

"The standard process is to come out with a draft, do consultations with the industry, with the consumer bodies which take care of consumer interest, with all people who are concerned with regulations, with the WTO... and eventually get notified as legislation," he said.

Draft food regulations must be notified to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) before final notification, in line with India's international trade obligations.

"I do hope that those processes will be followed," Sharma added.

FSSAI's proposed FOPL regulations seek to mandate labels on packaged food indicating levels of sugar, salt and fat, aimed at helping consumers identify products high in these components.
