evidence.title: Ikea closes 5 U.S. stores, plans to shutter another
evidence.text:
Ikea closes 5 U.S. stores, plans to shutter another

The furniture industry has suffered amidst a tumultuous housing market and tariffs .

Ikea , it seems, has not been immune to this.

TheStreet reports that the Swedish company is closing its small-format store in San Marcos, Texas — located in a key spot along I-35 — just 14 months after it opened.

“As part of our strategy to build a more affordable, accessible, and sustainable future for Ikea in the U.S., we have made the decision not to renew our lease for the San Marcos small-format store,” a company press release reads. “The store will close on Nov. 1, 2026.

“We continue to test, explore, and develop new ways for customers to meet Ikea, while investing in home delivery, pick-up services and our online experience.”

These smaller Ikeas — like the one coming to Westlake, Ohio — were touted as ways to bring “key products that [Ikea knows] the customers want” without people having to hike through a massive warehouse.

TheStreet notes that Ikea hasn’t said whether or not these stores are generally underperforming, but given that the brand has closed 13 locations this year so far — five of which are in the U.S. — speculation has arisen.

As previously stated, the furniture industry has been struggling as whole: According to FurnitureToday , manufacturers experienced flat orders at the start of year, with a seven percent year-over-year decrease in shipments.

FurnitureToday cites broader market challenges such as tariffs and oil prices as part of the issue, while TheStreet additionally points to the housing market: Weak real estate sales tend to lead to a drop in furniture purchases. Even Wayfair — which did experience growth in its second quarter — highlighted the current “depressed housing turnover” during a recent earnings call.

Interestingly, TheStreet states that value-focused chains such as Bob’s Discount Furniture have experienced growth and announced plans to expand. This is similar to the current dollar store mania , to which shoppers of all incomes are flocking as a ways to save cash.

evidence.title: Ikea Is Back With Its Own Smart Plug, the Most Affordable Model I’ve Ever Tried
evidence.text:
Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Senior Editor / Home Security and Smart Home

Senior Editor / Home Security and Smart Home

Article updated on April 30, 2026, 10:00 am EDT

After swinging for the fences with a new smart security system and the coziest smart lamp ever , Ikea is rounding off its smart home takeover in 2026 with a new smart plug . So far, everything I’ve tested from Ikea has impressed me this year, either as incredibly affordable ways to start up your smart home or particularly clever product designs.

Now the Swedish meatball and furniture company has returned with the tiny Grillplats plug , equipped to give any ordinary American outlet smart powers. It also offers full Matter compatibility, which means you can use it with your Apple Home, Google Home, SmartThings or Alexa app — with a couple caveats.

At under $8, this is the cheapest smart plug I’ve tested. It currently controls my Wi-Fi router , making it easy to reboot — a common part of smart home testing — but there’s plenty more the plug can do. Here’s what I thought of it.

What’s in the plug? Ikea sticks to the basics

I haven’t tested a smart plug that includes a physical controller before.

Today’s smart plugs are compact, inexpensive and can turn a wide variety of household appliances on or off with remote app control. Ikea’s version leans into these advantages, but also includes a small remote for on/off activation if you don’t like using apps, a handy add-on I’ve never before seen with a smart plug.

While Ikea’s model isn’t the smallest I’ve tested, it’s compact enough to fit on a standard outlet without getting in the way, which is the most important part of smart plug design.

Otherwise, the basic plug doesn’t have many bells and whistles, just a small LED indicator light and a side button to power it on or off. That’s one of the nice things about most smart plugs: There’s no learning curve, you can start using them immediately.

Ikea’s compact plug doesn’t have any extras, such as a dual socket, but that also keeps the price low.

I do like smart plugs with extra features, such as dual outlets, but those tend to cost more, and Ikea is clearly aiming at the low-cost end of the market. That’s why it’s reassuring that this plug doesn’t have any noticeable design issues or flimsiness.

I have a full guide on some of our favorite ways to use a smart plug , but your options will depend on what devices you have around your home. Lamps, heaters, fountains, fans and even coffee makers are common choices for smart upgrades.

Thanks to Matter support, Ikea’s smart plug only takes seconds to connect to an existing platform.

One of my favorite aspects about this new crop of Ikea smart devices is how easy they are to set up. All they require is a quick scan of a QR code or the input of the Matter PIN, and the smart plug connects in a few seconds to your platform of choice.

But there is one catch. You’ll need a Matter hub for this connectivity to work. Ikea offers its own Dirigera hub, but at over $100, it’s an expensive investment. This plug works far better if you already have a hub in your home, such as a HomePod, Apple TV, newer Amazon Echo device , SmartThings hub or a Nest Hub. That gives you plenty of options. If you don’t have one of these, Ikea’s plug suddenly becomes a much more expensive investment.

Ikea’s app controls are very easy to use on Apple Home.

I chose Apple Home for my testing platform, as I like its streamlined interface. Here, another advantage of the Grillplats plug surfaces: It’s easy to both set schedules and connect with other smart devices on the same platform. For example, you could connect the smart plug to a lamp, then link it to an Ikea motion sensor so the lamp automatically turns on when motion is detected in the room.

This smart plug can connect with other devices on the same platform.

Small tricks like that give you room to experiment with Ikea’s plug. However, you won’t find energy management options on this plug like you would with a model such as Emporia’s, so it’s not much use for tracking your electricity.

Final thoughts on the Ikea Grillplats smart plug

A small LED and button are the only things this smart plug needs.

Ikea delivers once again with a super-affordable smart plug that has the easiest setup process I’ve ever seen for a device like this. Of course, you’ll need a Matter hub to make everything work, so you better have a device that has hub features from Amazon, Apple, Google or Samsung — or be willing to buy Ikea's own .

This issue aside, the Ikea plug is worth considering for anyone who wants to expand their smart home. The included remote control is a unique touch for those who don’t like using app controls, and automations are worth setting up if you have extras such as motion detectors.

It would have been nice to see energy tracking options for this plug, but even without those, Ikea’s plug stands out as a well-made option available for only around $8, a price you can’t beat for a device like this.

Last year, Ikea's new CEO Juvencio Maeztu spoke to Fast Company on why the chain is committed to keeping prices low , citing inflation and high costs of living. Maeztu also credited "the need to socialize" as to why Ikea stores still draw customers while other chains are collapsing.

"People still have the need to go out," Maeztu said. "That's why it's important that we call it a meeting place—not necessarily a shopping center—and when you visit our meeting place it's a way to connect with the communities . . . to create traffic with engagement and food and events."

evidence.title: Who is Electrolux's New Procurement Chief Daniele Rossi?
evidence.text:
Who is Electrolux's New Procurement Chief Daniele Rossi?

Daniele Rossi brings more than 30 years of procurement, supply chain and leadership experience to his new role as Head of Procurement at Electrolux Group , having joined the business on 1 September 2026.

Daniele's career spans some of the biggest names in home appliances and industrial manufacturing, including Whirlpool, Indesit and Ariston Group, where he held senior roles across sourcing, supply chain, quality and product development, as well as CEO and Vice President positions in the Americas. Most recently, he served as Chief Procurement Officer at Italian steel company Acciaierie d'Italia (formerly ILVA), where he led procurement and supply chain through a period of significant financial and operational transformation.

Now based in Susegana, Italy and reporting to Chief Product Officer, Michelle Shi-Verdaasdonk – who served as Chief Procurement Officer for the company from 2024 to 2026 before her promotion to her current role – Daniele is focused on positioning procurement as a strategic driver of cost leadership and innovation at Electrolux Group, leveraging the company's global scale, embedding design-to-cost thinking earlier in the product lifecycle and deepening collaboration with suppliers to unlock sustainable, cutting-edge product development.

In an interview published on Electrolux Group's website, Daniele discussed his plans for procurement at the company.

When asked what drew him to the role, he said: "What excites me about Electrolux Group is the combination of its rich heritage, seen in its comprehensive product portfolio and global brand equity, and its forward-looking strategic transformation.

"I firmly believe that procurement is central to unlocking the value needed for this next chapter, and I want to help to lead this."

Looking at how procurement supports Electrolux Group's wider ambitions, Daniele points to structural efficiency and talent development as central priorities. "As a function, we will further leverage Electrolux Group's global scale to drive structural efficiency and cost leadership and develop the next generation of global leaders to drive success within procurement across the company," he says.

He also sees a growing role for suppliers as innovation partners, rather than simply sources of components. "We will also focus more on unlocking our suppliers' innovation potential to codevelop cutting-edge, sustainable products."

On the Group's procurement strategy specifically, Daniele highlights the function's new position within the business. "Procurement is now fully integrated into the new Product Organisation so we have a window of opportunity to drive more 'design-to-cost' initiatives in the early stage of R&D," he explains. "By aligning component standardisation and platform-sharing across global product families, we can reduce complexity and cost before a product ever hits production."

Sustainability, agility and AI reshaping procurement

Asked about the trends shaping global procurement more broadly, Daniele identifies three macro forces. "Global procurement is being reshaped by three macro trends: a continued shift toward sustainability, the critical need for more agility, and the acceleration of AI."

He unpacks each in turn: "Sustainability is fully integrated into sourcing decisions, meaning we need to evaluate suppliers based on their carbon footprint, environmental performance and respect for labour standards."

On agility, he adds: " Agility and responsiveness have become our main form of defence. In the current times of geopolitical turmoil and trade disruption, procurement must build highly adaptive, diversified supply networks that can move quickly to absorb uncertainty."

AI, Daniele says, underpins both. "AI and digital transformation are the enablers behind all of this, moving us away from manual tasks and toward predictive analytics. This means we can better anticipate market shifts and automate the tracking of indirect spend."

On balancing responsible sourcing with cost savings, he is direct: "Sustainability and responsible sourcing are no longer optional; they are interconnected strategic imperatives and a 'must-have' for modern procurement." He continues: "We must leverage our industry leadership in sustainability further to position our products and brands as market champions. By doing this, we can command a better selling price in the market."

A competitive advantage for Electrolux Group

Looking ahead, Daniele believes procurement's biggest opportunity lies in redefining its role within the business. "The biggest opportunity is to evolve from a traditional cost-control function into a strategic driver of innovation and cost leadership."

"Rather than just negotiating prices, we can engage with our direct material suppliers much earlier in the product lifecycle to codevelop sustainable solutions, improve time-to-market, and build supply resilience," he says.

"Also, by standardising and automating our global indirect spend, we can unlock efficiencies. I believe the Procurement function is a competitive advantage for Electrolux Group."

evidence.title: Leading Electrolux From 20,000ft and 10ft Underground
evidence.text:
Leading Electrolux From 20,000ft and 10ft Underground

You can read this and more in the magazine

Michelle Shi-Verdaasdonk believes leadership is about far more than setting a vision. It is about walking the path alongside your teams, navigating uncertainty with confidence and turning strategy into execution.

Following her appointment as Electrolux Group's Chief Product Officer, her remit now spans product strategy, R&D, design, electronics, connectivity and procurement, placing her at the heart of the company's innovation agenda.

Drawing on almost 25 years of experience across the entire value chain, Michelle shares the leadership lessons that have shaped her career, from leading through global disruption to empowering teams , staying curious and delivering meaningful business impact in an increasingly complex world.

Over the course of your career, you’ve held many roles – how has this strengthened your leadership skills?

Working throughout the value chain, from research, development and manufacturing to procurement, business strategy and everything in between, has helped me tremendously in navigating the whole value chain end-to-end.

Not only am I able to see the big picture, but I also have the deep knowledge to understand whether the high-level strategy can be executed or not.

I often say, we don’t live in the PowerPoint world; we live in real life where only execution counts. Without deep knowledge across the value chain, the strategy might be sound, but if it can’t be executed successfully, then the strategy is only as valuable as the piece of paper it’s written on.

Looking back at your career, what moments or influences most shaped your view of what good leadership looks like?

I have been so lucky in my career to have had so many amazing role models to look up to. I have learnt two important principles in leadership which have shaped how I lead.

Firstly, having a vision is a must in leadership; you can’t lead if you don’t know where you want to take your teams. Secondly, vision is not an ambitious neverland; a good leader needs to know how to build the path to guide the teams to achieve the vision.

Leaders who do not get close to the work risk being absent when it matters most

I am a keen hiker, so I often use hiking as an analogy for these two principles. As an impactful leader, not only do you need to point out the peak we are trying to get to, but you also need to break down the seemingly far-away – sometimes impossible – peaks into different stages and milestones for the teams to achieve.

Good leaders are also the guides on the hike. You prepare the team with the right tools and understanding of the route. You lead the way - walking every step the team walks. You motivate and encourage when the route gets difficult, and you carry the weight when a team member is struggling.

You celebrate every milestone and look back to see how far you've come. Then you repeat, until you and the team reach the peak together.

What are your top priorities to strengthen competitiveness at Electrolux?

Good products are defined by consumers; it is important to have consistency in brand positioning and product offering.

Electrolux Group has been in people’s homes for over 100 years; our products are part of their day-to-day life, and our goal is to continue to make it better. This is the promise we make to our consumers.

Chief Product Officer is an amazing role to be in as I get to listen to the pain points of consumers, discover ways to solve them with our R&D engineers and bring existing and new products to consumers’ homes.

How have your past experiences changed the way you lead innovation?

One thing I have learnt is the power of aligning product strategy closely with go-to- market and brand strategy. More is not more in product strategy; consumers tend to lean towards certain brands to solve different pain points or gain different levels of satisfaction.

It is crucial to know what product attributes we want to win in and which ones are okay to be on par with the competitors.

Simply throwing technology at consumers won't yield a competitive edge. True market leadership comes from deploying the right technology to solve specific pain points – aligning key product capabilities directly with your brand positioning.

You’ve led supply networks through significant global disruptions. What did those experiences teach you about keeping teams focused and resilient?

When I navigated through the pandemic period, the intensity during those three years taught me that global disruptions are going to be the norm. The frequency and intensity will only increase.

The most important part I have learnt is that as difficult as each disruption seems, there is always a solution. As a leader, I need to keep the teams calm, have clear communication with the stakeholders and leave no stone unturned to find short-term solutions to relieve the disruption.

The consistent and constant risk simulation is also important. We have seen a constant stream of global disruptions over the past six years.

While they take different forms – from geopolitical conflicts and waterway blockages to tariffs, export restrictions, and inflationary pressures – the underlying pattern repeats. Knowing the types of disruptions and linking them closely to risk assessment and mitigation has to be a day-to-day activity for leaders.

This way, when the next disruption hits the newspaper headlines, you can pull out the mitigation plan straight away, take a breath and work through it with the teams.

What advice would you give to leaders who want to evolve into shaping business strategy and delivering impact at a senior level?

The world is more real now than when I started my career almost 25 years ago. Disruptions are happening everywhere and every day. Leaders need to be able to adapt and be on the ground to solve issues every day.

Gone are the days of leadership that remains at a high level; in today’s environment, leaders who do not get close to the work risk being absent when it matters most.

Having a vision and empowering the teams is not enough to steer through the turbulence we all face. To stay status quo is to go backwards. Leaders who deliver impact and leave a legacy in these turbulent times are the ones who have vision and can also execute.

Having a vision is a must in leadership; you can’t lead if you don’t know where you want to take your teams

I often use the phrase “zoom in and zoom out”; the principle of leadership where you can be 20,000ft one minute and the next, be 10ft underground trying to understand how a team can solve a problem. And then, back to 20,000ft to ensure the solution would align with the strategy.

It’s not easy to be a good leader right now – the courage needed to make tough decisions, whilst staying curious to learn and absorb, is a fine balance for leaders to strike. Hence, to be a good leader is also to have the physical and mental fitness to take on the challenges with a smile every day.

Italian unions call one-day strike at Electrolux over job cut plan

Published by Global Banking & Finance Review

Italian metalworker unions (FIM, FIOM, UILM) have called a one-day nationwide strike at Electrolux’s Italian plants on September 15, after failed talks over a restructuring plan affecting up to 1,700 roles, including the closure of the Cerreto d’Esi facility.

Italian Unions Announce Strike at Electrolux to Protest Job Cuts and Plant Shutdown

Electrolux Restructuring Sparks Union Action in Italy

MILAN/STOCKHOLM, Sept 9 (Reuters) - Italian unions on Wednesday called a strike at Electrolux's facilities in the country on September 15, saying there had been no progress in talks with the appliances maker on a restructuring plan that includes job cuts and a plant closure.

• Metalworker unions FIM, FIOM and UILM said in a joint statement that Electrolux had not withdrawn its plans for layoffs in the country or a proposal to close the kitchen hood-making facility in Cerreto, central Italy.

• The strike call came after unions held two days of talks with the company at the industry ministry.

• Electrolux launched a restructuring plan in May, which could impact up to 1,700 roles. The company told Reuters at the time that it intended to close the Cerreto plant.

• The unions also announced a protest outside the Cerreto plant on the day of the strike.

• They added that further action, including strikes, could be called if the company does not withdraw its plan for job cuts and divestment in the country.

• CEO Yannick Fierling said in July that the restructuring in Italy was progressing "according to plan".

• Electrolux is trying to turn round its business and restructure its global operations in the face of weak demand and cut-price competition.

• The company did not immediately reply to a request for comment.

(Reporting by Giulio Piovaccari and Greta Rosen Fondahn. Editing by Mark Potter)

evidence.text:
STOCKHOLM , July 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ --

Highlights of the second quarter of 2026

President and CEO Yannick Fierling's comment

Underlying earnings improvement and strategic execution on track

The second quarter marked an important milestone for Electrolux Group, as we took decisive actions to accelerate our transformation and strengthen the Group's long-term competitiveness. The announced partnership with Midea Group in North America, global organizational and footprint initiatives, and the successful completion of the rights issue are important steps in executing our strategic priorities. With implementation advancing according to plan and some positive impacts from our plan to improve efficiency already coming through, our focus is now on delivering the expected benefits of these initiatives.

Solid commercial execution in regions EMEA APAC and Latin America resulted in organic sales growth above 4% for both regions in a highly competitive market environment. In Europe, the Electrolux and AEG brands continued to strengthen their market and price position, driven by core categories, such as built-in kitchen, in a continued subdued market. In Latin America, leveraging our strong market position, growth was supported by strong performance in small domestic appliances, driven by an extended product portfolio. In North America, weak market conditions continued to impact demand, with organic sales declining broadly in line with the estimated market contraction of approximately 3%. The newly extended U.S. Section 232 import tariffs valid from April 6, also applicable to Mexico, increased cost pressure across the industry, impacting earnings in the second half of the quarter. This additional cost pressure prompted widespread industry pricing actions. Electrolux Group led these increases, implementing price adjustments during the quarter between 5% and 20% depending on product category, compensating for part of the increased cost pressure from tariffs.

The earnings improvement was driven by operational improvements in EMEA APAC and Latin America. In North America, weak market conditions and tariff-related cost pressure continued to weigh on performance. The cost pressure from the extended tariffs will remain and impact earnings in the coming quarters. External factors were negative, impacted by tariff costs and the consequences of the Middle East conflict resulting in higher logistics and raw material costs. Cost-efficiency initiatives contributed SEK 1.4bn in improvements during the quarter, supported by procurement savings and the first impacts from our plan to improve efficiency across the organization over the next two years. Cash flow also improved and, together with the successful completion of the approximately SEK 9bn rights issue, strengthened our balance sheet and financial flexibility.

Market outlook unchanged and business outlook for the full-year partly revised

Looking ahead, the market environment remains characterized by geopolitical uncertainty and macroeconomic volatility, which may continue to weigh on consumer demand throughout the year. We maintain a Neutral market outlook for Europe and a Negative outlook for North America for the full year. In Brazil, our Positive full-year market outlook remains unchanged, although the cumulative effects of elevated interest rates and inflation continue to affect consumer financing and spending.

In the business outlook we have revised the capital expenditure outlook from SEK 4bn to approximately SEK 3.0-3.5bn.

Execution key focus in a challenging market

Our short-term priorities are clear: execute the transformation of North America, accelerate efficiency improvement across the organization, optimize the global manufacturing footprint and increase agility and performance focus throughout the organization.

We are reshaping Electrolux Group to become a more competitive, resilient and consumer-centric company. The actions taken during the quarter mark important progress in executing our strategic priorities. While there is more work ahead, these initiatives strengthen our foundation for sustainable value creation over time.

evidence.text:
Smartway Helps Auchan Luxembourg Save 1.2m Products from Food Waste

Published on Thursday, 24 Sep 2026 12:16 by IK France Opinion -->

On Thursday 24 September 2026, food-waste technology company Smartway reported that Auchan Luxembourg had saved more than 1.2 million food products from waste since deploying its solutions across four stores in 2023.

According to Smartway, Auchan Luxembourg is highlighting the results of the partnership as it marks its 30th anniversary. The retailer has relied on Smartway’s technology solutions to strengthen its food waste policy, helping to avoid 1,495 tonnes of CO₂ emissions and generate close to €1.83 million in savings for consumers.

Luxembourg was the third country in the Auchan Group to adopt Smartway’s solutions, after Romania and France. In 2023, the retailer introduced two modules: Smartdetection, which automatically identifies products approaching their use-by date and alerts teams in real time; and Smartdecision, which calculates the optimal discount level for each item, maximising the chances of sale while preserving margins.

Smartway reported that, three years after deployment, the food waste prevention coverage rate had risen by 38%, meaning that more at-risk products were identified and dealt with before going to waste. The sell-through rate of discounted products increased by 14%, while the value recovery rate rose by 62%.

In total, 1,245,864 products were saved from waste, representing 1,495 tonnes of avoided CO₂ emissions. Optimised markdowns also generated €1,828,874 in savings for Auchan Luxembourg customers.

According to Smartway, automating the detection of short-dated products has reduced the need for manual shelf checks while limiting the risk of oversights and improving team efficiency. Store teams now require less than forty minutes per store each day to check all shelves.

“ For 30 years, Auchan Luxembourg has taken concrete action to reduce food waste. Our partnership with Smartway fits fully within this long-term approach. Results were visible from the very first weeks of deployment and continue to be demonstrated over time, in operational, environmental and economic terms. This ability to quickly generate value while supporting our responsibility commitments is a real asset for our teams and our customers, ” said Fabrice Le Bon, Store Director at Auchan Opkorn.

Auchan Luxembourg has partnered with Stëmm vun der Strooss to redistribute unsold food since 2009, with the initiative now saving more than 125 tonnes of food per year. The retailer had also introduced donations to local organisations, promotions on short-dated products and ordering tools designed to limit waste at the source before deploying Smartway’s artificial intelligence solutions in 2023.

evidence.title: Auchan’s Russian business gets a CEO from the Kremlin two days after transfer to “temporary management”
evidence.text:
Auchan’s Russian business gets a CEO from the Kremlin two days after transfer to “temporary management”

Ilya Berdnikov, who previously worked at Russia’s Federal Agency for State Property Management (Rosimushchestvo), has become CEO of Auchan Retail Russia. Berdnikov took up the post on Sept. 19 — two days after Vladimir Putin placed the French retailer’s Russian business under the temporary care of JSC L.E.V. Management.

As The Insider previously found, a week before the decree JSC L.E.V. was headed by former Ministry of Internal Affairs general Andrei Krayushkin, while the JSC itself was still listed among the ready-made shell companies available for purchase for 450,000 rubles ($5,340) — with the option to replace the CEO and complete the deal “same-day.”

The business outlet Kommersant reported Berdnikov’s appointment, citing Auchan’s press service. The previous CEO, Asya Balabai, will remain with the company as executive director.

Berdnikov held the post of executive director at Rosimushchestvo starting from December 2024, the paper writes, citing information from his social media accounts. Previously, he worked at the X5 retail group, the Georgian winemaker Askaneli, and the Canadian construction company Bothwell Accurate Co., and also developed the startup SolidRobots in Canada.

A Kommersant source in the retail market claims that previous CEO Balabai will in fact continue to run day-to-day operations, while Berdnikov will oversee the company. L.E.V. Management head Andrei Krayushkin, meanwhile, will manage the overall process without a formal job title at Auchan.

On Sept. 17, Putin placed the Russian assets of Auchan and Nestlé (along with those of several other companies) under the temporary authority of L.E.V. Management. The Insider found that L.E.V. Management was registered only in October 2024, with charter capital of 15,000 rubles ($178). In 2025 it had no revenue, posted a net loss of 15,000 rubles ($178), and had an average headcount of one employee.

On Sept. 10, one week before Putin’s decree, Andrei Krayushkin — the former first deputy head of Russia’s Main Directorate for Migration Affairs and a police major general — became CEO of L.E.V. Management.

After the assets were transferred, L.E.V. Management said it intended to keep Auchan operating as a single retail chain and to ensure that stores continued running without interruption. No leadership changes have yet been reported at the other companies placed under L.E.V.’s management. At Lemana PRO (formerly Leroy Merlin), the temporary administrator promised to preserve the existing management system and current senior leadership. Nestlé’s Russian division also continues to operate under executive director Denis Voityuk.

The mechanism for placing foreign assets under temporary management has been in effect in Russia since April 2023. Formally, the foreign owner retains ownership rights, but the structure appointed by Russian authorities receives broad powers to manage the assets. This scheme was previously applied to the Russian businesses of Danone and Carlsberg, which subsequently lost control of their companies in Russia.

Temporary manager of French supermarket chain Auchan and former Leroy Merlin retailer Lemana PRO calls for stores and staff to be retained, promises drone protection

L.E.V. Management, the firm granted temporary control of the Russian assets of Auchan and Lemana PRO (formerly Leroy Merlin), has asked the companies’ executives to keep their store chains and staff intact.

In a letter to Auchan cited by RBC, L.E.V. Management CEO Andrei Krayushkin said that “purchasing, deliveries, store operations, and meeting obligations to customers, suppliers, and employees must continue without interruption.” “Auchan LLC’s stable operations are directly tied to food security,” the letter says.

Krayushkin also promised to “implement measures to protect Auchan’s properties from attacks,” including drone attacks. According to the letter, any staffing decisions, if they become necessary, will be “discussed in advance with the current management of Auchan LLC.”

Auchan’s Russian press office said the company was ready to maintain the necessary working relationship with the temporary manager and to “promptly discuss any issues that arise.” All of the company’s facilities are operating normally, the press office said.

On September 17, Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a law placing the Russian assets of Auchan, Nestle, Lemana PRO, and FM Logistic — a French logistics operator that worked with those companies — under the temporary control of L.E.V. Management.

Journalists found that L.E.V. Management was registered in October 2024 with registered capital of 15,000 rubles. Krayushkin, who heads the firm, is a major general in Russia’s Interior Ministry and served as first deputy head of its migration directorate from 2016 until at least 2020.

To justify the move, the Kremlin said these are companies from unfriendly countries “that are now actively involved in military operations against our country.”

evidence.title: Carrefour y Auchan lanzan un mensaje al sector: la inteligencia artificial forma parte del negocio
evidence.text:
Carrefour y Auchan lanzan un mensaje al sector: la inteligencia artificial forma parte del negocio

Ambas cadenas dejan atrás la fase experimental e integran la IA generativa en la producción de sus catálogos digitales para optimizar costes y ganar agilidad comercial.

La inteligencia artificial ha superado definitivamente la fase de experimentación en el sector de la distribución alimentaria. Lo que hace apenas un año se percibía como una tecnología de apoyo para automatizar tareas puntuales comienza a consolidarse como un elemento estructural dentro de las estrategias de negocio de los grandes retailers.

Carrefour y Auchan son un claro ejemplo de esta evolución. Tras eliminar progresivamente los folletos impresos en favor de formatos digitales, ambas compañías han dado un nuevo paso al incorporar la inteligencia artificial generativa en la producción de sus catálogos promocionales , uno de los principales activos comerciales de la distribución.

Más allá de la innovación tecnológica, este movimiento refleja un cambio de paradigma en la forma de concebir los procesos de marketing, comunicación y creación de contenidos.

Del ahorro de costes a la transformación del modelo operativo

Los primeros resultados confirman que el impacto de la IA trasciende la eficiencia operativa.

Carrefour, genera mediante inteligencia artificial el 100% de las imágenes de sus catálogos promocionales, después de que a finales de 2025 esta tecnología representara el 37% de la producción. La compañía ha conseguido reducir en un 50% los costes asociados a la creación de imágenes , al tiempo que ha acelerado significativamente los tiempos de desarrollo de las campañas.

Auchan , por su parte, también ha obtenido resultados positivos en el rendimiento comercial de estos contenidos. Según la compañía, las imágenes creadas mediante IA aumentan un 19% los clics en sus promocionales digitales.

Estos indicadores demuestran que la adopción de la inteligencia artificial no responde únicamente a una lógica de reducción de costes, sino también a la mejora de la eficacia comercial.

La creatividad no desaparece , cambia de función

Uno de los aspectos más relevantes de esta transformación es la redefinición del trabajo creativo.

En Carrefour, la intención estratégica desarrollada por Publicis continúa siendo el punto de partida de cada campaña. Sin embargo, la producción visual se apoya ahora en modelos de inteligencia artificial especializados, mientras que los equipos internos concentran sus esfuerzos en la conceptualización, la supervisión creativa y la construcción de los mensajes.

La IA asume la ejecución; las personas mantienen la estrategia, el criterio y la identidad de marca.

Este cambio anticipa una evolución que probablemente veremos extenderse a otros departamentos de las organizaciones, donde el valor diferencial estará cada vez menos en producir contenidos y cada vez más en dirigirlos .

El catálogo promocional entra en una nueva etapa

Desde hace más de cuatro décadas, el folleto promocional ha sido uno de los principales instrumentos comerciales de la gran distribución. Con la digitalización y la inteligencia artificial, este soporte evoluciona hacia un formato mucho más dinámico, flexible y adaptable.

La posibilidad de generar imágenes en cuestión de minutos permitirá responder con mayor rapidez a cambios en el surtido, campañas estacionales, disponibilidad de productos o nuevas necesidades comerciales. En el futuro, incluso será posible desarrollar catálogos altamente personalizados según segmentos de clientes o contextos específicos de compra.

La IA convierte un proceso tradicionalmente rígido en una herramienta capaz de evolucionar prácticamente en tiempo real.

Una ventaja competitiva que irá más allá del marketing

La experiencia de Carrefour y Auchan pone de manifiesto una tendencia de mayor alcance.

La inteligencia artificial no representa un proyecto aislado dentro de las áreas de innovación, sino una capacidad transversal que comienza a impactar en marketing, comunicación, operaciones, análisis de datos, atención al cliente y gestión comercial .

Para el sector de la distribución alimentaria, la cuestión no consiste en decidir si incorporar inteligencia artificial, sino en determinar la velocidad y la profundidad con la que será integrada en los procesos críticos de cada empresa.

Carrefour y Auchan no solamente están optimizando la producción de sus catálogos promocionales. Están mostrando cómo la inteligencia artificial comienza a redefinir el funcionamiento del retail desde dentro y cómo la transformación digital deja de ser un proyecto para convertirse en parte del modelo de negocio.

evidence.title: Hundreds of Thousands Affected by Auchan Data Breach
evidence.text:
French retail chain Auchan is notifying hundreds of thousands of customers that their personal information was stolen in a data breach. The incident, the company said in notifications sent last week, impacted names, addresses, email addresses, phone numbers, and loyalty card numbers. No banking information, passwords, or PINs have been compromised in the incident, the retailer said. “We are writing to inform you that Auchan has been the victim of a cyberattack. This attack resulted in unauthorized access to certain personal data associated with your loyalty account,” reads the notification, a copy of which was shared by local media . Auchan says it took the necessary steps to contain the attack and improve the security of its systems, and that it notified the French data protection watchdog CNIL of the incident. The company is advising the impacted customers to remain vigilant of phishing, scams, and other types of attacks that could be fueled by the stolen information. Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading. The retailer told French media that several hundreds of thousands of customers were affected by the incident. However, the company did not share information on how the data breach occurred, who was behind the attack, and whether it has received any extortion demands. SecurityWeek has emailed Auchan for additional information on the data breach and will update this article if the company responds. This appears to be the second data breach that Auchan has disclosed over the past year. The new notification seems to be the same notice that the company sent to its customers in November 2024. 22 September 2026 – How can we simplify and make hassle-free the journey for a passenger who cycles or rides a scooter to the station and then continues their journey by train? This is the challenge taken up by Decathlon, a global multi-specialist sports brand and designer of mobility solutions, and Alstom, a world leader in rail transport and smart mobility, who are today unveiling the results of a joint design, exploration and R&D initiative at the InnoTrans 2026 trade fair.

Stemming from a field study into the real-life challenges faced by travellers, this partnership brings together the innovative strengths of two French champions to combine rail engineering with the ergonomics of soft mobility, with the aim of creating a seamless journey that benefits both passengers and the environment.

"The role of design is to simplify people’s lives. With Decathlon, we have sought to remove the obstacles that still complicate travelling with a bike or a scooter."

This collaboration brings together two unique and highly complementary areas of expertise:

Alstom brings its global expertise in trains, rail systems and passenger flow management.

Decathlon brings its in-depth knowledge of cyclists, everyday mobility and user experience, underpinned by its expertise as a designer and manufacturer.

By combining Alstom’s rail-industry timeframe (designing interiors and rolling stock over long cycles) with Decathlon’s design agility, the teams have devised new solutions to make intermodal travel intuitive, from leaving home to reaching the final destination.

To turn this vision into reality, Alstom and Decathlon have devised a comprehensive mobility chain where each stage flows seamlessly:

A connected bike or scooter designed for use on trains: The result of extensive design research, the new generation of equipment is perfectly adapted to the constraints of train travel (enhanced ergonomics, compact design) whilst incorporating smart connectivity.

A seamless experience from the moment you enter the station: Thanks to advance booking via a mobile app, passengers are automatically guided along the platform to the identification terminal for instant registration of their soft mobility equipment.

A redesigned ‘Soft Mobility’ area on the train: On board, a dedicated, secure compartment accommodates bicycles and scooters. There’s no longer any need to keep an eye on your equipment: the layout ensures peace of mind for everyone, prevents the aisles from becoming cluttered and allows passengers to settle comfortably into their seats.

"The role of design is to simplify people’s lives. With Decathlon, we have sought to remove the obstacles that still complicate travelling with a bike or a scooter. Beyond the product itself, we share the same conviction: mobility is no longer thought of in terms of individual modes, but as a continuous experience. The aim is simple: to enable everyone to switch from one mode of transport to another as easily as possible, because the green transition will only succeed if it is also synonymous with freedom and the pleasure of getting around."

— Alexis Bonnet, Design Director at Alstom

"Within the Decathlon teams at B’twin, ‘Living by bike’ is not only our dream but also our commitment. With this in mind, we are delighted to be working with Alstom to explore how we can bring two modes of transport that complement each other naturally – cycling and rail – even closer together."

— Cédric Mollet, Head of B’twin / Decathlon

Through this initiative, Decathlon and Alstom aim to demonstrate that innovation is not just about inventing new vehicles or new infrastructure, but also about making connections between different modes of transport simpler, smoother and more accessible to everyone.

evidence.title: New Balance Sues Decathlon Over Kiprun Shoe Logo In Trademark Fight
evidence.text:
New Balance has taken one of the world’s largest sporting-goods retailers to federal court, arguing that a logo appearing on Decathlon’s Kiprun running shoes comes too close to one of the most recognizable letters in the sneaker business.

New Balance Athletics, Inc. filed its complaint against Decathlon America LLC and Decathlon USA LLC on September 15 in the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts. The case, New Balance Athletics, Inc. v. Decathlon America LLC et al., No. 1:26-cv-14235 , asserts federal trademark infringement under the Lanham Act.

At the center of the dispute is Kiprun’s angular “K” design.

According to New Balance, one orientation of the logo may resemble a stylized K. But when Decathlon mirrors the symbol on the opposite side of its running shoes, New Balance says the result is “unmistakably an N” — placing it uncomfortably close to the Boston-based company’s longstanding footwear trademark.

Decathlon, according to allegations described in the complaint, has maintained that its symbol represents a K rather than an N. New Balance says it began communicating its concerns to Decathlon in January 2026 and asked the company to change or discontinue the disputed design, but Decathlon declined.

That distinction — K or N — may make for an easy visual debate, but trademark law asks a more complicated question.

Under 15 U.S.C. § 1114 , infringement can occur when an unauthorized use of a registered mark or a sufficiently similar imitation is likely to cause confusion, mistake or deception in connection with goods or services.

Because the case was filed in Massachusetts, First Circuit precedent is particularly important. Courts in the circuit traditionally examine factors including the similarity of the marks, similarity of the products, sales and advertising channels, the classes of purchasers, evidence of actual confusion, the defendant’s intent and the strength of the plaintiff’s trademark. No single factor necessarily decides the case.

That framework helps explain why New Balance’s complaint does more than simply place the two logos side by side.

The company points to its history with the “N,” which dates to the 1976 New Balance 320 running shoe. New Balance alleges that variations of the mark have appeared on nearly all of its footwear for approximately five decades and says it has spent hundreds of millions of dollars promoting its N-based trademarks while selling hundreds of millions of pairs of shoes bearing them worldwide.

New Balance also cited social-media discussions in which consumers and running enthusiasts remarked on similarities between Kiprun footwear and New Balance shoes. Those posts may help New Balance argue that consumers are already making an association between the designs, although their ultimate evidentiary significance will be for the court to determine.

The stakes extend beyond one logo. Both companies compete in athletic footwear, including performance running shoes, making the dispute one between companies selling similar products to overlapping groups of consumers.

New Balance is seeking an injunction preventing continued use of the allegedly infringing design, destruction of products bearing the disputed mark and monetary relief to be determined through the litigation. The company has demanded a jury trial.

This is not New Balance’s first courtroom fight over its N branding. The company previously brought U.S. trademark lawsuits involving Michael Kors and Nautica that were resolved, and in 2017 obtained an approximately $1.5 million judgment in China in litigation involving its branding.

The Massachusetts docket initially assigned the matter to Magistrate Judge Jessica D. Hedges. The court’s assignment notice states that unless the parties consent to magistrate-judge jurisdiction, the assignment operates as a referral for pretrial nondispositive matters and reports and recommendations on dispositive issues until reassignment to a district judge.

Neither company had publicly provided a substantive response to the lawsuit when the dispute was first reported.

For now, New Balance has made its allegations. Decathlon will have an opportunity to answer them, and the court has not determined that trademark infringement occurred.

evidence.title: New Balance sues Decathlon over alleged copycat shoe design
evidence.text:
New Balance has filed a trademark infringement lawsuit against French sporting goods retailer Decathlon, alleging that a logo used on its Kiprun performance running shoes is confusingly similar to New Balance’s iconic “N” mark.

The lawsuit, filed Sept. 15 in the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts, alleges that Decathlon’s Kiprun logo infringes New Balance’s trademark rights. New Balance says it has used its N marks on footwear since the 1970s and argues that consumers may perceive the mirror-image version of Decathlon’s design as an N. New Balance is seeking a recall of all shoes with the design, destruction of products bearing the mark and monetary damages to be determined at trial by jury.

The dispute centres on the logo used by Kiprun, Decathlon’s running brand. According to the complaint, New Balance first contacted Decathlon about the design in January and subsequently sent additional communications asking the company to stop using what New Balance considers a trademark infringement. According to the court documents, Decathlon denied the claim, arguing that the design is clearly a “K.” New Balance says the design’s mirror image resembles its N mark and could confuse consumers.

The company points to the way the logo appears in online marketing, where it says the mark can be perceived as an N when viewed without the surrounding shoe or other branding. It has also included numerous examples of customers pointing out the similarity on social media as evidence of customer confusion.

New Balance identifies eight Kiprun shoe models in its complaint. One of them is the Kipstorm Lab, a US$350 carbon-plated racing shoe that Kiprun athlete Jimmy Gressier of France wore when he set the European 5K record of 12:57 in March 2025 (Gressier lowered that mark to 12:51 in 2026).

Decathlon has not publicly commented on the lawsuit.

This is not the first time New Balance has taken legal action over an N-shaped logo on footwear. In the complaint, the brand says the U.S. District Court has already recognized its design after its suit against USA New Bunren International in 2019, among several others.

In 2017, a Chinese court awarded New Balance US$1.5 million in damages and legal costs for three domestic shoe companies’ use of its logo. Then, in a 2019 decision, the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware found that New Bunren’s stylized N marks infringed New Balance’s trademarks. The court also found that New Bunren’s online advertising constituted use in commerce, even though the company argued it had not sold the shoes in the U.S.

In 2021, New Balance filed another trademark lawsuit in Massachusetts, this time against the Michael Kors fashion retailer. The complaint alleged that N-shaped designs on the company’s Olympia and Pippin shoes were confusingly similar to New Balance’s N marks.

The Decathlon lawsuit is the latest in New Balance’s efforts to protect the N design it says has become closely associated with its footwear.

evidence.title: Comau automates picking, handling, and palletizing for Decathlon
evidence.text:
Comau designed its MyCo family of cobots for quick installation, easy programming, and rapid redeployment. | Source: Comau

Comau SpA yesterday said it has designed and validated an order-preparation system tested in Decathlon’s e-commerce fulfillment operations. The system is part of MASTERLY, a European initiative designed to accelerate the transition from traditional mass production to highly flexible, customized manufacturing systems.

The system uses the Turin, Italy-based company ‘s MyCo collaborative robot with a ROS 2-based software architecture. It integrates an advanced modular gripper to autonomously manage picking , handling , and palletizing tasks across variable product flows.

“Comau’s role in the MASTERLY project is fully aligned with our commitment to advancing next-generation manufacturing by promoting reconfigurability, efficiency, and human-centric automation,” said Alessandro Piscioneri, the head of product and solution management of advanced automation solutions at Comau.

“The project also highlights the strategic value of combining intelligent robotics, digital technologies and systems integration to create highly flexible logistics and fulfillment operations capable of adapting to rapidly changing production and market demands while maintaining operational continuity, scalability and ease of use,” he stated. “Comau’s growing strategic focus on intralogistics includes strengthening our capabilities through acquisitions, including Automha and Invent, which enable us to deliver increasingly integrated and intelligent solutions across the entire warehouse and production value chain.”

Comau designs system for complex fulfillment

Comau said it engineered MyCo to manipulate objects varying in shape, weight, and material. In addition to MyCo, the solution also incorporates advanced sensors , vision-based object recognition, digital twin capabilities, and workflow orchestration tools.

The company said the system can manage the rigid, soft, and porous materials commonly found in e-commerce fulfillment environments. Comau also claimed that its system enables real-time optimization and smooth interaction between operators and the automated processes. This helps it ensure high flexibility while maintaining consistent throughput and operational reliability, it said.

Comau said the knowledge gained and functionalities validated during the project will contribute to the continued evolution of its MyCo platform. The company said it expects these improvements to become part of its broader portfolio of advanced intralogistics capabilities.

MASTERLY uses AI, automation for supply chain resilience

Comau noted that its role within the MASTERLY project reflects its use of advanced AI -backed automation to address evolving production challenges. This includes increasing variability, supply chain disruptions, and the need for rapid reconfiguration.

The company acknowledged that it developed the intelligent warehousing and logistics system with the project’s ecosystem of technology partners. Comau said its scalable and versatile automation is designed to improve workplace ergonomics, reduce physical strain, and enhance operational flexibility within human-centric production environments.

The project parameters were driven by Decathlon’s operational requirements within the targeted fulfillment process, which has provided the foundation for implementing and validating several advanced functionalities. Key partners included Decathlon itself and STAM, a Genoa-based systems integrator, alongside the broader MASTERLY consortium.

Decathlon has worked with other robotics companies, including Exotec , Geek+ , PAL Robotics , and Simbe Robotics .

evidence.title: Arnault family consolidates LVMH control through Dior holding overhaul
evidence.text:
Arnault family consolidates LVMH control through Dior holding overhaul

The Arnault family is restructuring its ownership chain to tighten long-term control over LVMH, the world's largest luxury group. The plan would place nearly all of the family's stake and voting power in the company under a single listed holding structure with enhanced control protections.

Once completed, the transaction would centralise 49.76% of the family's shareholding and 65.55% of its voting rights in LVMH in a single holding company. Two layers of family holdings would be merged into Christian Dior SE, which would then be renamed Agache and converted into a societe en commandite par actions, a French joint-stock structure often used by dynastic owners to preserve corporate control across generations.

An extraordinary meeting of Christian Dior SE shareholders is expected in December to approve the transaction. A tender for the 2.44% of minority shares not owned by the family is due to launch in the first quarter of 2027, subject to approval by French regulators, and the stake was worth 1.63 billion euros at Tuesday's market close; no forced sale of remaining minority shares is planned. Succession and governance implications The reorganisation marks Bernard Arnault's most significant move to strengthen his family's grip on the 194 billion euro luxury empire since 2022. The new Agache SCA structure would add further protections by making it extremely difficult for shareholders to wrest control of the company or push for a break-up.

The move follows earlier steps to reinforce the family's position, including a 2022 restructuring that gave each of Arnault's five children an equal vote and required unanimity on critical decisions involving LVMH. Another major step came in 2017, when the family streamlined several holding companies and bought out Christian Dior minority shareholders, increasing its economic stake in LVMH from 36% to almost 47%.

All five of Arnault's children already hold operational roles within the group, while succession planning is drawing increasing attention from investors. Arnault, 77, has said he has no intention of stepping aside in the foreseeable future, and some of his children also hold managerial and board roles in the family's holding companies.

The restructuring also comes after an improvement in operating momentum at LVMH. In late July, the group's core fashion and leather goods division reported sales growth for the first time in two years.

In our earlier report on the Arnault family’s plan to simplify LVMH’s ownership chain through Christian Dior, we explained how Agache would be merged with Christian Dior and the combined entity renamed Agache. The piece outlined that the December transaction is designed to preserve the family’s control by consolidating 49.76% of LVMH’s shares and 65.55% of its voting rights under a single holding company, alongside a tender offer for the remaining Christian Dior minority stake.

evidence.title: LVMH’s Arnault family takes steps to simplify corporate structures to consolidate control
evidence.text:
LVMH ’s owners, the Arnault family, are seeking to consolidate control of the shareholding structure of ‌the luxury group.

The board of directors of Christian Dior was informed of a project today (24 September), with a proposal to merge Agache, LVMH’s apex holding company, into Christian Dior while converting Christian Dior into a limited joint-stock partnership.

This conversion would then trigger the filing of a mandatory tender offer on Christian Dior shares, without implementing a squeeze-out – a legal process where a majority shareholder forces remaining minority shareholders to sell their shares for cash.

The merger would be submitted for approval to the governance bodies of the relevant companies, notably an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) of Christian Dior, which would be called upon to vote on these transactions at the end of 2026.

This is subject to obtaining waivers to mandatory tender offer situations on Christian Dior and LVMH from the French Financial Markets Authority (AMF).

For the Arnault family, the move will allow them to control within a single company.

Christian Dior said in a company statement: “The tender offer would take place in the first quarter of 2027, subject to the clearance of the AMF, and would not be followed by a squeeze-out.

“Christian Dior shareholders who would choose not to tender their shares in the tender offer would thus remain shareholders of the listed entity resulting from the merger (Agache SCA), which would bring together the controlling stake in LVMH (aggregating the stakes currently held by Agache, Financière Agache and Christian Dior) as well as the other assets received from Agache.”

Cosmetics Business has contacted LVMH for a comment.

evidence.title: LVMH falls from grace: Why the luxury giant has dropped out of Europe’s top 10
evidence.text:
LVMH falls from grace: Why the luxury giant has dropped out of Europe’s top 10

​LVMH, once Europe’s most valuable company, has now fallen out of the region’s top 10 listed firms for the first time since 2017. Its market capitalization has declined to around €201 billion as shares fell 37% this year and more than 50% from their 2023 peak. But what factors can explain this crisis, and how lasting is the shift in demand likely to be?

In mid-September 2026, LVMH shares fell about 2.5–2.6% in a single session, a rare occasion for the luxury segment. This reduced the group’s market value to approximately €201 billion ($232 billion). So its capitalization has become below that of L’Oréal, and LVMH left the list of Europe’s ten largest listed companies for the first time since 2017. At its 2023 peak, LVMH was Europe’s most valuable company, with its shares trading above €900 and a market value above $500 billion.

However, the stock has since lost around 55% from that maximum. Currently, the shares are trading at levels last seen during the pandemic. These problems also cost LVMH its status as France’s most valuable listed company. Analysts admit that the ranking can fluctuate with daily price moves, but the overall trend is clear. Vincent Juvyns, chief investment strategist at ING in Brussels, commented, “Those who claim that Europe is back are wrong, Europe is not back: what LVMH tells us is that its main growth engine, luxury, is broken.”

LVMH reported first-half 2026 revenue of €38.6 billion, and it is down 3% on a reported basis. Profit from recurring operations stood at €8.7 billion, constituting a 4% decline. At the same time, the group’s net profit remained stable at €5.7 billion. Operating margin is still satisfactory at 22.5%, and free cash flow is about €4.1 billion. Another modestly positive signal is growth accelerated in the second quarter to 3% organically (or 4% excluding the impact of Middle East conflict).

Fashion and leather goods returned to organic growth in the second quarter, and it is important considering this being the group’s major source of revenue. Currency instability and the changes in the structure of global demand largely explain the reported figures. Chairman and CEO Bernard Arnault said of the half-year results: “LVMH demonstrated its solidity and effective strategy. Our Maisons—which remained focused on ensuring the utmost quality in our products, and several of which are pursuing their creative renewal—continued to inspire dreams and enhance their desirability.” Despite many problems, Jonathan Anderson’s first designs for Christian Dior and recovering champagne and cognac sales may become the factors reversing the current negative tendency.

Weak demand in China has been a central factor of the current financial issues. The Asian market has cooled amid economic pressure and a property crisis and shifting consumer preferences towards domestic brands. Sales at major luxury labels in China recorded double-digit declines in recent months. Conflict in the Middle East has also constrained spending in key shopping destinations such as Dubai. LVMH analysts appeared to be mostly unprepared for such challenges.

These external factors resulted in successive price increases that reduced the number of aspirational middle-class buyers. Their demand for luxury goods has appeared to be more price elastic than expected before. Overall, the luxury sector’s growth estimates are currently questionable despite years of strong post-pandemic expansion.

Impact on Bernard Arnault and investor sentiment

The share-price decline has also affected Bernard Arnault’s personal fortune. According to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index, his net worth fell by about $65 billion since the start of 2026. This is the most rapid decline among all the world’s 500 richest people. He is now valued at roughly $143 billion. Capital flows show the higher interest in U.S. technology stocks at the moment, and outflows from the luxury segment remain high.

Several firms, including RBC Capital Markets and Jefferies, have lowered their ratings in recent weeks. In particular, their experts mention the low pace of recovery in the second half as additional risk factors. The stock trades near multi-year lows as short-term and speculative traders have shifted to other companies.

Despite the ranking reassessment, LVMH remains the world’s largest publicly traded luxury group by market capitalization, and it is still above Hermès and Richemont. Management has expressed confidence in the long-term desirability of its brands, appealing to product quality and new creative solutions. The group continues to prioritize operational discipline to maintain financial stability even if a crisis continues in the following months.

Whether LVMH can reclaim its status will depend on a recovery in Chinese demand, stabilization in other key markets, and the ability of Louis Vuitton and Dior to re-engage their customer base. In any case, the current low point may become a good entry point for long-term portfolio investors, as there are clear cyclical patterns observed in the luxury segment.

Sophie Maddaloni appointed General Secretary of Kering

Kering - Press release - Sophie Maddaloni appointed General Secretary - 09152026

SOPHIE MADDALONI APPOINTED GENERAL SECRETARY OF KERING

Kering announces the appointment of Sophie Maddaloni as General Secretary of the Group, effective immediately. Based in Paris, she joins the Executive Committee of Kering and reports to Jean-Marc Duplaix, in his capacity as Group Chief Operating Officer.

In her new role, Sophie Maddaloni is responsible for the Group's governance and for safeguarding its interests, as well as for upholding the highest standards of compliance. She oversees the Legal, Internal Control, Internal Audit and Security departments, working closely with Executive Management and the Board of Directors.

Drawing on solid experience gained within major international groups, Sophie Maddaloni brings recognized expertise in legal affairs, governance and organizational transformation. Her track record and in-depth knowledge of Kering will be valuable assets in supporting the implementation of the Group's strategic priorities, further strengthening its governance standards and sustaining its long-term development.

Sophie Maddaloni began her career in 1991 at Elf Aquitaine, where she spent more than ten years in a range of international tax roles, supporting the evolution of the group that is today TotalEnergies. She joined Alstom T&D in 2002 as Vice President Tax, then Technip in 2004, where she headed the Group's tax and legal entities functions.

Sophie Maddaloni joined Kering in 2017 as Group Tax Director. In this role, she led the transformation of the tax function and contributed to strengthening Kering's compliance and risk management framework.

Sophie Maddaloni holds a master's degree in business law from Université Paris II Panthéon-Assas and a postgraduate degree (DESS) in international business law and taxation from HEC Paris - Université de Sceaux.

evidence.title: Colman Domingo Says “Men Should Be Locking Arms to Make Sure Women Have What They Need” at Kering’s Caring for Women Dinner
evidence.text:
Beyond monetary donations, what’s the best way an A-list star can contribute to organizations that benefit women and children? “It’s always been important to me to stand firm with these organizations — not only in support, but with my presence,” Colman Domingo explained on the red carpet for Thursday’s Caring for Women Dinner, the annual benefit produced by the Kering Foundation at The Pool in New York City. “Anytime I’ve been in rooms like this, I’ve thought, ‘Look at all these female leaders’ — but hey, we’re the men. Men should be locking arms to make sure women have what they need in access and information and support. I was raised a feminist, and I’ll die a feminist.” Related Stories Movies Anya Taylor-Joy Kidnaps Chris Evans in Netflix's 'Sacrifice' Trailer Lifestyle Paris Hilton and Colman Domingo Join Kering Foundation's Caring for Women Gala

Domingo served as master of ceremonies at this fifth-annual fundraiser produced annually by Kering, the luxury conglomerate that owns brands that include Gucci , Brioni, Balenciaga , McQueen and others. Stars on the red carpet included both longtime supporters and first-time attendees, from co-hosts Salma Hayek Pinault and her husband, Kering chairman of the board François-Henri Pinault, as well as fellow co-hosts Simone Biles, Dakota Johnson, Pamela Anderson and Benecio Del Toro .

“My friend Salma and her husband, Mr. Pinault, I wanted to be here for them, and it’s an honor to be here,” Del Toro, attending for the first time, said. “Of course it’s important to bring attention to gender-based violence, something that comes from the heart and is just and right and urgent.”

The night raised more than $5 million to benefit four organizations, all dedicated to ending violence against women and children: Activating Change , which advocates for people with disabilities and the deaf community experiencing criminalization and incarceration; Fondo Semillas , a Mexico-based organization working to achieve justice and equality for girls, women and the trans community; JBWS , which protects and supports victims of domestic abuse; and The New York Women’s Foundation , which provides grants to social programs and other women-led organizations.

If there’s an unsurprising element about this evening, it’s the fact that guests turn up in their best black-tie looks by Kering brands. That included Biles in a draped Balenciaga gown, Moore in Bottega Veneta, Anderson in a sleek black gown by Gucci, and del Toro in a Brioni tuxedo, while Paris Hilton, on hand to DJ the night’s after-party, wore a silver stone- and sequin-embroidered Gucci gown. Even the tableware came courtesy of Kering-owned brand Ginori 1735, which provided its famed chain-themed Catene porcelain dinnerware for the night’s tables.

Domingo arrived on the red carpet in Valentino (30 percent of which is owned by Kering) with jewels by Boucheron, as the Oscar nominee was named the jeweler’s first American ambassador earlier this year. “I’m a host, so I felt the need to bring a little sparkle and some light in the room with me tonight,” Domingo explained of his jewelry and his beaded suit. “I’ve always believed in storytelling in the things I wear, while also having some fun. The world is such a hard place as it is, we need to inspire people to embrace a bit more whimsy.”

Funds were raised not only through guest tickets but also the live auction, a mix of one-of-a-kind items and experiences Balenciaga, Bottega Veneta, Gucci, Pomellato and others. But for the first time, the event will extend its fundraising via an online auction that kicks off on Sept. 14 and ranges from a vintage Boucheron brooch and a London shopping experience at McQueen to a signed leotard donated by Simone Biles, also among the night’s first-time attendees.

“Gender-based violence against women and girls is a violation of their fundamental human right to live safely,” the Olympic champion explained on the red carpet. “That’s why the advocacy work and the nonprofits are more important than ever. The work they’ve done over the past couple of years has been really inspiring to watch, so I’m just grateful to be a part of it.”

The night also took on the look of a mini-reunion by co-stars from The Shards with Homer Gere, Graham Campbell and Jordan Roth in attendance. “I’ve had the time of my life, literally every second of every day with this cast,” Roth said of working on the show. “But that’s also the genius of Ryan Murphy, who understands not only culture, but how to cast incredible people. I am the luckiest of humans.”

“This is my first one of these kinds of things,” the 26-year-old Gere, son of Richard Gere and Carey Lowell, admitted as he looked around the wood-paneled outer rooms of The Pool. “I’m not sure what to say yet, because I just got here. It’s great to see Jordan, a familiar face. But everyone’s been very nice, I know it’s going to be a lovely night.” Up next for Gere: White Lies , directed by Oliver Stone, he said. “It stars Josh Hartnett as a family man who kind of ruins his family and then tries to get it back together,” the actor explained. “That might not be a great description of it, but it’s been incredible to work with Oliver Stone and everyone involved.”

Wearing a Bottega Veneta tuxedo, Kering CEO Luca De Meo, who joined the company in September 2025, noted that Thursday night likewise was his first experience at the event. “I had always heard about it, but it’s incredible to think about the millions of people who have been helped by the money raised over the years,” he said. “In Europe it’s slightly different, a little more rare, to do something like this, but overall I find people in America, both businesses and private donations, to be incredibly generous. Though this isn’t something we do for the business, we do it for the causes.”
