Estão feitas as contas aos resultados do retalho na bolsa de Lisboa. Num momento em que está quase fechada a “earnings season” do semestre, Sonae e Jerónimo Martins mostraram ambas os números da atividade no passado dia 29 de julho. Enquanto a dona do Continente apresentou mais um conjunto de resultados robusto , a beneficiar da procura doméstica, a empresa que detém o Pingo Doce reconheceu um semestre “bastante mais exigente do que o esperado” , com a polaca Biedronka a debater-se com um ambiente de deflação no país. À imagem dos resultados, também o desempenho bolsista indica direções divergentes, com a Sonae a brilhar e a Jerónimo “sob pressão”. Mas os analistas deixam uma mensagem positiva para o futuro.

Escolha o ECO como fonte preferida no Google

Pingo Doce mais próximo do Continente. Lidl foge à Mercadona

Depois de terem escalado mais de 76% em 2025, as a ções da Sonae, que fixaram máximos históricos em julho , continuam a destacar-se com uma valorização anual próxima de 26% , suportada pela forte performance operacional da empresa da Maia. Já a Jerónimo Martins tem sentido o impacto da desaceleração na Polónia, com os investidores a castigarem a empresa, que desce quase 14% em 2026. Apesar de as ações de ambas as empresas não terem registado fortes oscilações após o reporte das contas, os resultados têm sido e deverão continuar a ser o principal motor das ações.

Para João Queiroz, head of trading do Banco Carregosa, “a Sonae beneficia atualmente de uma narrativa mais favorável aos investidores , assente na diversificação, na redução da alavancagem financeira, no crescimento dos resultados e na existência de ativos cujo valor implícito ainda não parece totalmente refletido na cotação”, ao passo que a “ Jerónimo Martins continua fortemente dependente da evolução da Biedronka, que representa a maior fatia das receitas do grupo”.

Num ambiente que continua a ser marcado por uma forte concorrência, as duas maiores empresas de distribuição nacionais conseguiram aumentar as suas vendas, suportadas pelas promoções. No caso da dona do Continente , que reforçou a liderança, as receitas superaram os 5,6 mil milhões de euros, com a CEO Cláudia Azevedo a notar “novamente excelentes resultados” do retalho alimentar, que viu o volume de negócios crescer 6,8% no primeiro semestre, para 3,5 mil milhões de euros , sustentado pelo contínuo crescimento dos volumes. No global, a MC , que junta o retalho alimentar, saúde, beleza e bem-estar, registou um volume de negócios atingiu 4,4 mil milhões de euros, o que representa aumento de 7,9% face ao período homólogo.

“Excelentes resultados” do Continente apoiam vendas da Sonae

O grupo liderado por Pedro Soares dos Santos registou uma subida de 5,1% nas vendas, para 18,2 mil milhões de euros, com as vendas do Pingo Doce a crescerem 5,3% para 2,7 mil milhões de euros, com o Like For Like (LFL) – sem efeitos de abertura/fecho de lojas – nos 3,7%. Na Polónia, a forte queda da inflação alimentar, a partir de setembro de 2025, levou a Biedronka – que é o maior negócio do grupo – a operar com uma “enorme pressão” da deflação no cabaz. Nos últimos seis meses, as vendas cresceram apenas 1,7%, para 12,6 mil milhões de euros.

Os analistas aplaudiram os resultados apresentados pela Sonae, destacando o crescimento dos vários negócios do grupo, desde o retalho, à beleza, passando pela eletrónica e pela Musti, nos cuidados animais. Já a Jerónimo Martins teve uma reação menos favorável, com a Morgan Stanley a descer a avaliação para as ações da empresa de 15,5 euros para 15,10 euros, após a divulgação das contas.

A Sonae apresentou um conjunto de números positivos, essencialmente suportados na Sonae MC, que mantém um desempenho quase sem críticas a apontar, beneficiando muito da fórmula atual de crescimento do país, mais pessoas, mais consumo. Ou seja, alavancando numa economia fortemente orientada para a procura doméstica, salários a crescerem francamente acima da inflação e população empregada a crescer num ritmo ainda elevado, acima dos 2%.

“A Sonae apresentou um conjunto de números positivos, essencialmente suportados na Sonae MC, que mantém um desempenho quase sem críticas a apontar”, reconhece António Seladas, fundador da AS Independent Research, que avalia as ações da empresa com um “target” de 1,85 euros e uma recomendação “neutral”. O especialista acrescenta que a empresa da família Azevedo tem beneficiado “muito da fórmula atual de crescimento do país, mais pessoas, mais consumo . Ou seja, alavancando numa economia fortemente orientada para a procura doméstica, salários a crescerem francamente acima da inflação e população empregada a crescer num ritmo ainda elevado, acima dos 2%”. Por outro lado, “a decisão, há uns anos, de abrir lojas no formato de maior proximidade, em zonas densamente povoadas que cresceram muito com a imigração e turismo revelou-se decisiva” .

No que diz respeito à dona do Pingo Doce, António Seladas, que manda “comprar” a empresa e avalia os títulos com um preço-alvo de 20,90 euros, diz que “a JM está sob pressão, porque o seu principal mercado, no retalho alimentar, Polónia está a sofrer com um ajustamento forte dos preços no alimentar , concretamente deflação alimentar (cabaz alimentar na Polónia com queda nos preços)”. “Ainda assim, [a empresa fechou o semestre] com um desempenho extraordinário ao nível dos volumes, mantendo ou ganhando quota de mercado num nível absolutamente elevado “, sustenta.

Jerónimo Martins lucra menos 3,3% até junho

“Em resumo, a Sonae MC foi, sem dúvida, uma das empresas portuguesas que mais beneficiou do desempenho macro dos últimos anos, concretamente mais pessoas (Imigração e Turismo), mais consumo”, afirma o analista, destacando que “aparentemente, neste momento existe algum abrandamento nesta dinâmica, a imigração dever-se-á ressentir com a postura menos favorável das autoridades e o crescimento do turismo está a abrandar” e, “se assim for, a dinâmica de vendas, que foi inesperadamente forte nos últimos anos e particularmente nos últimos 12 meses, deverá ressentir-se”.

Já a Jerónimo Martins “regista uma dinâmica, quase oposta, na Polónia, tem sofrido, este ano e 4º Trimestre de 2025, de uma forma inesperada, com a deflação no retalho alimentar, aparentemente, essencialmente, justificada, devido ao excesso de aumentos de preços no passado que agora ajustam”. “ Este fenómeno, deflação, dever-se-á manter intenso no próximo trimestre e perder intensidade no 4º trimestre de 2026 e 1º trimestre de 2027. Ou seja, um efeito base muito favorável, particularmente a partir do 2º Trimestre 2027″, antecipa.

João Queiroz, Head of Trading do Banco Carregosa, faz um “balanço global é positivo para ambas as empresas, mas por vias diferentes. A Sonae apresentou crescimento robusto nas vendas, melhoria das margens, forte aumento dos resultados líquidos e reforço da solidez financeira, beneficiando da diversificação do portefólio entre retalho alimentar, eletrónica, telecomunicações, imobiliário e cuidados para animais”. Já a Jerónimo Martins , destaca, “demonstrou elevada resiliência num contexto mais desafiante, marcado pela deflação alimentar na Polónia, principal mercado do grupo . Apesar da pressão sobre preços, conseguiu aumentar vendas, EBITDA e margem operacional, sustentada pelo crescimento de volumes, disciplina operacional e forte competitividade comercial”, explica.

A Sonae destacou-se pela aceleração do crescimento e criação de valor transversal à carteira de ativos e de insígnias, enquanto a Jerónimo Martins evidenciou capacidade de defender rentabilidade num contexto operacional consideravelmente mais exigente.

“Em síntese, a Sonae destacou-se pela aceleração do crescimento e criação de valor transversal à carteira de ativos e de insígnias, enquanto a Jerónimo Martins evidenciou capacidade de defender rentabilidade num contexto operacional consideravelmente mais exigent e”, conseguindo aumentar volumes e melhorar margens na Polónia, apesar da forte deflação alimentar na Polónia. “Este é um resultado particularmente relevante porque demonstra que o grupo conseguiu preservar a sua liderança comercial sem sacrificar de forma significativa a rentabilidade”, defende.

Escalada da Sonae deixa maior potencial na Jerónimo

Após um período de fortes ganhos, a Sonae surge com menor potencial de subida face às avaliações dos analistas, enquanto a Jerónimo Martins surge com uma margem de progressão superior a 30% face aos preços-alvo dos bancos de investimento.

Os sete analistas que acompanham a companhia liderada por Cláudia de Azevedo avaliam os títulos da empresa com um target de 2,24 euros, o que confere um potencial de subida de 10,6% face ao valor de fecho de sexta-feira. Já os 26 analistas que seguem a empresa da família Soares dos Santos têm um preço-alvo médio de 23,04 euros para a companhia, uma avaliação que confere um potencial de cerca de 32% às ações da dona do Pingo Doce.

“Em termos prospetivos, a Sonae parece reunir condições para continuar a beneficiar do crescimento dos resultados e da reavaliação dos seus ativos, enquanto a Jerónimo Martins poderá depender mais da normalização da dinâmica de preços na Polónia e da capacidade de transformar crescimento de volumes em crescimento de resultados”, antecipa João Queiroz. “ Em ambos os casos, a qualidade operacional permanece elevada, mas o mercado tende atualmente a atribuir um prémio superior à visibilidade e diversificação oferecidas pela Sonae “, conclui.

No momento em que a informação é mais importante do que nunca, apoie o jornalismo independente e rigoroso.

- The company's ESG strategy includes 100% recyclable packaging by 2025 and 45% female leadership targets, aligning with EU sustainability mandates while boosting sustainable product sales by 30% since 2019.

- Supply chain innovations like AI analytics and FISHY cybersecurity framework help mitigate trade tensions and geopolitical risks, with 65% of seafood sourced sustainably to meet ESG-conscious consumer demand.

In the first half of 2025, Sonae (SOSSF) has emerged as a standout performer in a volatile global economy, leveraging strategic resilience, ESG integration, and technological innovation to drive growth. With revenue surging 18% year-over-year to €10 billion and EBITDA exceeding €1 billion—a 4.5% increase—Sonae has demonstrated its ability to navigate macroeconomic headwinds while accelerating value creation. This article evaluates how the Portuguese conglomerate's forward-looking strategies position it as a compelling long-term investment, even amid trade tensions, supply chain disruptions, and regulatory shifts.

Sonae's H1 2025 results reflect a blend of organic growth and strategic acquisitions. The company's core segments, including food retail (MC division) and telecommunications (NOS), delivered robust performance, with NOS achieving its best operational and financial results ever. Free cash flow of €360 million in 2024 (despite a €160 million debt increase from acquisitions) underscores Sonae's liquidity strength, while a 16% leverage ratio (LTV) highlights manageable debt levels.

The proposed 5% dividend increase further signals confidence in the company's financial health. For investors, this combination of profitability, cash flow generation, and shareholder returns is a strong indicator of a well-managed business.

Sonae's ESG initiatives are not just compliance-driven but strategically embedded in its growth model. By 2025, the company aims to achieve 100% recyclable plastic packaging and 45% female leadership in senior roles by 2026. These goals align with the EU's Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) and European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS), which mandate enhanced transparency.

The company's Continente Producers Club and Traffic Light System (TLS) for sustainable seafood sourcing have already driven a 30% increase in sustainable product purchases since 2019. With 65% of its fish sold from sustainable sources, Sonae is not only mitigating environmental risks but also appealing to a growing base of ESG-conscious consumers.

Sonae's supply chain strategies in H1 2025 highlight its adaptability to macroeconomic volatility. The company has diversified suppliers and adopted digital tools like AI-driven analytics and supply chain mapping to mitigate risks from trade tensions (e.g., U.S.-China tariffs). For example, the FISHY architecture—a cybersecurity framework leveraging distributed ledger technology—ensures real-time threat detection in ICT supply chains, a critical advantage in an era of rising cyberattacks.

The WTW Global Supply Chain Risk Report 2025 notes that geopolitical risks are now the top concern for 19% of businesses. Sonae's proactive approach—relocating production to climate-resilient regions and prioritizing sustainable sourcing—positions it to outperform peers in uncertain environments.

While Sonae's debt increased by €160 million due to acquisitions, its leverage remains well within conservative limits. The company's focus on high-margin sectors like pet care and cybersecurity—both acquired during H1 2025—demonstrates disciplined capital allocation. These sectors are poised for long-term growth, with the global pet care market projected to exceed €100 billion by 2030 and cybersecurity spending expected to hit €300 billion annually.

Sonae's strategic resilience is evident in its ability to balance short-term profitability with long-term sustainability. For investors, the company's alignment with ESG trends, technological agility, and diversified revenue streams offer a compelling case for inclusion in a macro-resilient portfolio. However, caution is warranted regarding potential regulatory risks in the EU's evolving ESG landscape and the sustainability of its debt-funded growth.

Recommendation : Buy for long-term investors seeking exposure to a diversified conglomerate with strong ESG credentials and a track record of navigating macroeconomic volatility. Target price: €12.50 (based on 12x EBITDA).

In conclusion, Sonae's H1 2025 performance underscores its ability to transform challenges into opportunities. As global markets grapple with trade tensions and regulatory shifts, Sonae's strategic foresight and innovation make it a standout player in the European investment landscape.

evidence.title: Walmart Self-Checkout Case Resurfaces After Alabama Mum Won $2.1m Jury Verdict
evidence.text:
A Walmart self-checkout case involving Alabama mother Lesleigh Nurse has resurfaced online after a video revisited the $2.1 million jury verdict she won.

The dispute began at a Walmart in November 2016 after Nurse said a self-checkout scanner froze while she was paying for groceries. She was stopped before leaving the store and accused of failing to pay for about $48 worth of items.

According to her lawsuit, the accusation led to her arrest on a shoplifting charge. Her criminal case was later dismissed, but her legal dispute with Walmart continued.

The case has returned to public attention because of renewed online discussion, not a new court ruling.

Nurse's lawsuit centred on her claim that a checkout problem led to an accusation she said was incorrect, followed by an arrest and later civil proceedings against Walmart.

How the Walmart Self-Checkout Case Started With a Scanner Problem

Nurse said she was shopping with her husband and three children when the self-checkout machine malfunctioned. She said a Walmart worker came over to help resolve the issue, and she believed she had completed the transaction before leaving.

According to Nurse's lawsuit, she was stopped while trying to leave Walmart and accused of failing to pay for 11 items, including Christmas lights, bread, and Cap'n Crunch cereal. The disputed merchandise was valued at about $48.

Nurse said employees did not accept her explanation and that she was arrested on suspicion of shoplifting. Her criminal case was later dismissed after a Walmart employee and defendant in the civil case failed to respond to a subpoena and appear in court, according to her lawsuit.

#foryourpage #news #fyppppppppppppppppppppppp #breakingnews

The dismissal did not end the dispute. Nurse said she later received letters from a Florida law firm seeking a $200 settlement to avoid a possible civil claim. Her lawsuit alleged that Walmart instructed the firm to send the letters.

The amount requested was higher than the value of the groceries involved. Nurse questioned why she should pay money over an accusation she disputed.

'At first you think, well, I'll pay it and it will all go away. But then, I'm like, I didn't do anything wrong, why would I pay for something I didn't do?' Nurse told WKRG .

The Walmart Self-Checkout Case Led to a $2.1M Jury Award

Nurse filed her lawsuit in 2018 through Mobile attorney Vince Kilborn. Her complaint alleged that Walmart had a broader practice of seeking payments from Alabama customers accused of shoplifting, including people who disputed the accusations.

Walmart's lawyers argued that Alabama law permitted such payments. The company's defence position was that the practice was legal and that associates had acted appropriately.

A Mobile County jury later ruled in Nurse's favour and awarded her $2.1 million in damages. The verdict followed testimony about civil settlement demands used by Walmart and other retailers in states where such practices are allowed, according to trial reports.

The case gained renewed attention after a social-media video revisited the dispute. Some commenters criticised self-checkout systems, while others shared claims of similar experiences. One issue discussed online was whether Walmart produced footage from the self-checkout area.

Walmart Responds After the Self-Checkout Verdict

Walmart disputed the jury's decision following the verdict. A company spokesperson said Walmart believed its employees had acted appropriately and that the damages awarded were not supported by the evidence.

'We continue to believe our associates acted appropriately. We don't believe the verdict is supported by the evidence and the damages awarded exceed what is allowed by law. We will be filing post-trial motions,' the company said in a statement.

Walmart also said it planned to appeal the ruling. The outcome of any later appeal or post-trial proceedings is not included in the available reporting.

Renewed interest in Nurse's case has centred on wider questions about self-checkout disputes, store security decisions, and how retailers respond when customers challenge accusations of unpaid merchandise.

Nurse was arrested after an alleged $48 self-checkout loss; the criminal case was dismissed; she received a $200 demand; and a jury later awarded her $2.1 million in damages.

The case does not prove that self-checkout disputes routinely lead to wrongful arrests. It does show how quickly an unresolved payment problem can move beyond the checkout, into police records, civil demands and a courtroom. That is the part shoppers keep returning to, even years later.

With the current inflationary wave gripping the United States, Cramer discussed the role that the firm could play in keeping prices down and create long term value:

“That’s why I mean I still think that Walmart is trying to keep prices down. They really are. They’re trying to make it so that this is a Sam Walton moment, where you know there was one place that was good to you.”

For Walmart Inc., successfully keeping prices low to generate long term tailwinds might just be the trick for otherwise lackluster performance. In fact, even though he has been optimistic about the firm, Cramer has nevertheless also advised caution. For instance, in his August 24th appearance, the CNBC TV host remarked that “you have to let go of your Walmart unless you think you have a plan. The miss that Cramer was discussing was Walmart Inc.’s second quarter earnings, which saw the firm miss comparable sales growth estimates. While the retail giant posted 2.6% in U.S. comparable sales growth, analysts had penciled in 3.5% to 3.8%. Style is very much in ascendance at Walmart.

evidence.title: Some Target baskets can track you in-store. Here's what to know
evidence.text:
Some Target baskets can track you in-store. Here's what to know

Target has used beacon-based tracking technology in its stores since at least 2015.

Some Target baskets carry a Bluetooth Low Energy Beacon that transmits its location to "smart" lights in the store. The lights can interact with the beacons and Target's app to find a shopper's location, help them navigate around a store or send location-specific offers. Because the basket-mounted beacons transmit only locations and do not collect information about the shopper, it is technically Target's app that tracks shoppers, not the beacons.

In August and September 2026, a claim ( archived ) circulated online that the retailer Target used a Bluetooth device on its baskets that tracked shoppers in store.

The claim came from an Aug. 29 TikTok video in which a person who appeared to be a Target employee claimed the retailer fitted its baskets with trackers that followed shoppers throughout the store.

Hello, I just want to make a PSA: You are now being tracked at Target. These baskets, this thing, that's a tracker, so they're now tracking shoppers at Target, at your local Target, for, supposedly, "consumer habits."

Other users shared similar claims about Target's alleged tracking on Facebook ( archived ), Instagram ( archived ), Threads ( archived ), X ( archived ) and Reddit ( archived ). Snopes readers also contacted us about the claim.

In short, Target does track shopper locations using the basket-mounted Bluetooth beacon that the TikTok user showed in their video. The beacon transmits its location to Target's "smart" overhead LED lights , which in turn can communicate location information to its app.

Acuity Brands, which Target said supplied its LED lights, explained in a news release in 2017 that by using its lights and beacons attached to items such as shopping carts it could deliver " highly accurate, real-time positioning services for customers" through a retailer's app. Acuity Brands said Target renewed a multiyear deal for products including its indoor location services in 2020.

According to its privacy policy, Target still used LED light and Bluetooth technology to track shoppers in-store in August 2026. The policy advised that customers who did not want to share their store location data could disable location sharing on their device or in the Target app.

We contacted Target to confirm how it collected and used data about customers in store using Bluetooth beacons, as well as how customers could opt out of tracking. We await a reply to our query.

The TikTok user who shared the video about Target's basket-mounted beacons on Aug. 29 shared another video ( archived ) the day after, identifying the exact product Target used to track shoppers as a Bluetooth beacon from Acuity Brands. A Reddit user who posted ( archived ) about the device six months earlier showed a device with the same FCC ID as the one the TikTok user identified.

The Federal Communications Commission grants FCC IDs to products that meet the necessary regulatory standards for wireless communication.

The product's user manual said it is a Bluetooth Low Energy Beacon that "communicates its position to Atrius Assets," the software that Target has used since at least 2020 for indoor location services.

Bluetooth Low Energy Beacons are small devices that send out radio signals that can be picked up by nearby devices. Beacons can only transmit — not receive — data, so they generally rely on apps to interpret and use the data they are sending.

In terms of tracking, if many beacons are sending their location, a device can interpret those signals and triangulate the location of an individual beacon, or individual shopper holding a basket fitted with a beacon. Target wrote in its news release in 2019 that its lights interacted with its app to find customer locations, suggesting that the basket-mounted beacons sent their signals to the lights.

It was unclear from the available information whether Target used the data it gathered about individual shoppers' routes through their stores beyond providing location-based offers through the app or guiding customers to specific products.

Target used Bluetooth beacons since at least 2015

The technology publication TechCrunch reported that Target and other retailers have used beacon technology to track shoppers in store and send them location-based offers since at least 2015 and that the retailer added Bluetooth beacon-driven indoor mapping to its app in 2017.

Target appeared to still use this technology in 2026. Its privacy policy in August 2026 said Target might use location information shared by customers' phones to " help you find nearby Target stores; or, in-store location through the use of your phone's blue tooth signal, LED light chip technologies or other technologies will permit Target to find nearby products for you, get you real-time deals, auto-sort your shopping list and more."

Target said in its privacy policy that shoppers who wished to opt out of sharing their in-store location could prevent their devices from sharing their location with Target "by adjusting the permissions on your mobile device or within the relevant app."

It did not appear from the beacon's manual that shoppers could turn the device off themselves, meaning Target would still collect information about where the basket traveled if a shopper used it, but could not connect that data to a specific phone or customer if the device's owner turned off location sharing or did not use the Target app.

evidence.title: Target Bets Big on AI and Automation to Reverse a Five-Quarter Sales Slide
evidence.text:
Target Bets Big on AI and Automation to Reverse a Five-Quarter Sales Slide

Target (TGT) is staging an aggressive turnaround effort centered on artificial intelligence and supply chain automation, and early signs suggest the strategy is beginning to bear fruit. After four consecutive quarters of declining sales, the Minneapolis-based retail giant posted a surprise return to same-store growth in the first quarter of fiscal 2026, sending its stock sharply higher and prompting management to raise its full-year sales outlook.

Andrea Zimmerman, president of Target's India division, told a Reuters Summit in Bengaluru that the company is fundamentally rethinking how it deploys AI. A key driver of that shift is a move from subscription-based software pricing to token-based models, which is forcing Target to reassess where and how it invests in the technology. "We are eyeing more investments to convert our data into useful insight," Zimmerman said, according to Reuters. The remarks underscore a broader corporate push to modernize operations as the retailer fights to reclaim market share lost to larger rival Walmart (WMT) and a prolonged consumer pullback in discretionary spending.

The AI push extends deep into Target's supply chain. About a week before Zimmerman's comments, the company appointed industry veteran Jeff England as its new chief supply chain and logistics officer. England has made no secret of his mandate: modernize a logistics network that still relies heavily on manual and repetitive tasks. He has signaled that AI and automation tools will be central to that overhaul, a move analysts say is long overdue for a retailer of Target's scale.

Target's renewed focus on technology comes at a pivotal moment. For the fiscal quarter that ended January 31, the company had logged its fourth straight period of declining sales. CEO Michael Fiddelke, who has been steering the turnaround, has framed AI not as a novelty but as a critical lever for improving efficiency and the customer experience.

Then came the numbers that changed the narrative. For the first quarter ended May 2, Target reported net sales of $25.44 billion, a nearly 7% jump from a year earlier and comfortably above the Wall Street consensus of $24.64 billion. Earnings per share surged roughly 32% to $1.71, blowing past the $1.47 analysts had expected. The most closely watched metric — comparable-store sales — swung to a 5.6% gain, marking the first positive reading in five quarters.

Target described the sales growth as broad-based across multiple categories, a signal that consumer demand may be firming up after a long stretch of caution.

The upbeat results prompted the company to raise its full-year guidance, though management tempered the optimism with a dose of caution. Target now expects net sales growth of around 4% for the fiscal year, roughly two percentage points higher than its previous forecast. CEO Fiddelke said the company is "maintaining a cautious outlook given the work we know we have in front of us," a reference to ongoing economic uncertainty and the heavy lifting still required to modernize operations.

Investors have responded. Since the beginning of the year, Target's stock has climbed more than 28%. Yet even after that rally, the valuation remains relatively modest. Shares trade at less than 17 times trailing earnings, a steep discount to the S&P 500's average multiple of about 26. The stock also offers a dividend yield of roughly 3.6%, which income-focused investors have found attractive.

Wall Street analysts, however, are not uniformly bullish. According to data compiled by TipRanks, the consensus rating on Target is a Moderate Buy, based on 11 Buy ratings, 14 Holds, and 2 Sells over the past three months. The average 12-month price target sits at $133.04, implying only about 6% upside from current levels. The split in analyst opinion reflects a debate over whether the first-quarter recovery is sustainable or merely a temporary bounce.

Motley Fool noted that Target has struggled to win over investors in recent years, with many favoring Walmart for its grocery-heavy business that offers greater stability during discretionary spending downturns. The publication argued that the combination of strong earnings, raised guidance, and a cautious-but-constructive management tone could set the stage for further gains — especially if consumer spending continues to strengthen.

Target's AI strategy is unfolding against a backdrop of intense competition and a retail landscape being reshaped by technology. Walmart has poured billions into automation and AI-powered supply chains, while Amazon (AMZN) continues to set the pace on data-driven logistics. For Target, the bet is that smarter use of data — from inventory management to personalized marketing — can close the gap. The shift to token-based AI pricing, as highlighted by Zimmerman, suggests the company is not just spending more on technology but also becoming more disciplined about how it measures return on those investments.

Whether AI can power a durable sales turnaround remains an open question. The first-quarter numbers offer a promising start, but the retailer still faces the challenge of sustaining momentum in an economy where consumer confidence can shift quickly. For now, Target is betting that a smarter, more automated operation will give it the edge it needs to compete — and the early returns have caught the market's attention.

evidence.text:
Target to open more than 30 new stores in 2026, with the first seven opening this March

Retailer's 2,000th store to open in Fuquay-Varina, N.C., featuring Target's open-layout design that delivers an elevated guest experience

MINNEAPOLIS , March 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Target Corporation (NYSE: TGT ) today announced plans to open more than 30 new stores in 2026, including its 2,000th location in Fuquay-Varina, N.C. The openings are part of a new chapter in the company's strategy to drive long-term, sustainable growth by investing in stores. This includes plans to add more than 300 new stores by 2035, with seven locations welcoming guests this March as part of the company's continued expansion.

Target's new stores and remodels are supported by its $5 billion capital investment plan for 2026 — reflecting its commitment to deliver a more consistent, elevated shopping experience, while leveraging technology to fulfill online orders faster and easier for guests. This comes alongside an investment of hundreds of millions of dollars in additional store payroll and training to improve guest service in 2026.

These investments help Target deliver against the growth priorities laid out by CEO Michael Fiddelke that will guide the retailer's decision-making in 2026 and beyond.

"Guests tell us all the time they want a Target closer to home, and this investment helps us do exactly that," said Adrienne Costanzo , chief stores officer, Target. "That means even more neighborhoods will get the full Target experience: trend-forward style and value, technology that makes the trip effortless and awesome teams who deliver easy, inspiring and friendly moments every single day."

The 148,000-square-foot North Carolina store, located near Raleigh, represents the future of Target's elevated guest experience with its open, easily navigable layout, convenient same-day services and winning team delivering a more relaxed and enjoyable shopping visit. In fact, 92% of shoppers at Target's newest store format are highly satisfied with the overall experience, according to guest surveys.

Six other new Target stores open this March in Bakersfield and Delano, California; Springfield, Missouri; Jersey City and West Orange, New Jersey; and Dallas, Texas. They are among more than 30 new stores Target is opening this year, and more than 130 remodels. Next-day delivery will also launch in more than 20 new metro areas including Indianapolis, Memphis, Tenn., and Cincinnati, reaching 60% of the U.S. population.

Like the Fuquay-Varina store, each new location is bringing the best of Target: an easy, inspiring and friendly experience that keeps guests coming back, whether they're stopping in, picking up or shopping digitally. The retailer is also making a commitment to the neighborhoods it calls home.

"Every time we open a new Target store, we're planting roots in that community," Costanzo said. "That means in addition to delivering a better shopping experience that's faster and more reliable, we're creating growth and opportunity — through good jobs, support for local nonprofits and long-term economic investment in the neighborhoods we serve. When our teams and communities thrive, so do we."

MINNEAPOLIS , March 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- At its financial community meeting today, Target Corporation (NYSE: TGT) unveiled its multi-year strategy under Chief Executive Officer Michael Fiddelke to accelerate its return to growth. The strategy includes plans to refresh the store experience across the chain, invest in store payroll and training to elevate the guest experience and strengthen key areas of the assortment.

"This new chapter of growth at Target is defined by clear choices and rooted in a deeper understanding of our unique lane in retail, the guests we serve and the areas where we're distinctly positioned to win," said Fiddelke. "This work is underway, and by putting style, design and value at the center of every decision, we're making big changes to lead with a trend-forward assortment, elevate the guest experience, accelerate with technology and equip our teams to deliver the most delightful experience in retail, for today and over the long term."

evidence.title: Kroger seeing 'meaningful results' from AI
evidence.text:
Kroger seeing 'meaningful results' from AI

The Kroger Co. outlined its artificial intelligence strategy at GroceryShop 2026, detailing how customer insights, operational data, retail expertise and a portfolio of proprietary models are already driving meaningful results. Kroger's AI initiatives are supported by privacy, security and responsible AI governance processes designed to help ensure appropriate use of data and human oversight.

Yael Cosset, executive vice president and chief digital officer, described a strategy built on using AI to improve the customer experience, make work easier for associates and produce better business outcomes.

"This isn't new for Kroger," said Cosset. "We've long been using data science and artificial intelligence to serve our customers by precisely forecasting demand, connecting customers with the most relevant savings opportunities and helping them find and get the products they need. Our latest investments in AI allow us to connect relevant business and operational signals to make decisions and take action faster."

Kroger's AI strategy begins with a data foundation built on a longstanding loyalty program and years of customer and operational insights and data science. The company expands its broad portfolio of proprietary models spanning from demand forecasting, to operational optimization, personalization and generative AI capabilities.

Kroger's combination of proprietary and third-party frontier models with shared infrastructure, including data, services, agentic capabilities and governance guardrails, enables the company to move faster on proven capabilities, better orchestrate agents across workflows and manage performance in a more disciplined, and reliable manner.

"The goal is not autonomy everywhere," said Cosset. "The goal is using the right level of AI based on risk, repeatability and the need for human judgement. Different cases will sit at different stages, and strong governance remains at the center."

Kroger's AI Shopping Assistant is helping customers plan meals for the week, find new recipes and build a cart around budget and dietary needs as well as preferences. Conversational search helps customers plan meals, discover relevant products and find what they need more easily.

The company is also working on improving agents for frontline teams to cut through the noise of dozens of daily notifications and tasks and surface only the most important information. Additionally, Kroger is making AI literacy training and tools available to more than 400,000 associates across the enterprise.

"It's about more than simply granting access," said Cosset. "Teams need the skills and discernment to use AI responsibly, understanding where it is useful and redesign work around this new capability. At our core, the human connection to a customer or fellow associate will never be replaced by AI. Instead, AI will give our associates more time and insight to create that connection."

Cosset outlined a future in which grocery shopping becomes an outcome-based experience instead of a series of individual and functional transactions. In this model, customers may choose to share information relevant to their shopping needs and AI agents handle planning, shopping and fulfillment.

Rather than formulating a weekly shopping list, customers may choose to share their goals and preferences, allowing AI agents to assist with planning and completing their shopping.

Kroger's advantage in this future, Cosset argued, is the same as it is today: A deep knowledge of customer shopping patterns, visibility into product availability and fulfillment, making the customer experience better.

Albertsons names Meg Whitman executive chair

Albertsons Cos. Inc. announced that Meg Whitman has been appointed to the newly created role of executive chair of the company’s board of directors. With Whitman’s appointment, Kim Fennebresque has transitioned from chair to lead independent director, and the board has expanded from 10 to 11 members. Whitman will work to support Susan Morris, CEO of Albertsons Cos., and her entire senior team.

Main Street Produce, also doing business as Freshway Farms, has named Vince Ferrante CEO of the vertically integrated berry grower-shipper, effective Sept. 28. Mark Murai, CEO since 2024, will become chairman of the board. As chairman he will guide the company's strategy, growth and partnerships.

Kroger leader, food as medicine champion to retire

The Kroger Co.'s Colleen Lindholz, president of Kroger Health, will retire after more than three decades with the company.

ALDI dropping prices, offering U.S. shoppers $86M in savings

ALDI is helping shoppers stretch their grocery budgets even further this fall, delivering an estimated $86 million in savings through additional price investments on the season’s fresh favorites. With the addition of the lower prices, nearly one-third of the everyday in-store assortment at ALDI is priced lower than last year.

Simbe's autonomous retail shelf intelligence fleet surpasses 3,000 units

Simbe has surpassed 3,000 autonomous units under contract: the largest commercially committed fleet of shelf intelligence technology identified in company research. In the decade since introducing Tally, the world’s first inventory robot, Simbe is building on that sustained leadership to evolve from leading in autonomous shelf digitization to building a broader platform for the physical store.

California grapes partner with the San Francisco 49ers

The California Table Grape Commission and the San Francisco 49ers have teamed up for the 2026 football season, bringing together two iconic California brands through a new partnership designed to build excitement for California grapes among consumers in Mexico.

Costco Wholesale COST posted market-beating financials for its fourth quarter last night, which is why the retailer’s share price sits comfortably in the green at writing.

Yet, a deeper dive into COST’s balance sheet suggests it’s actually brewing something even more exciting than strong quarterly figures — at least for income-focused investors.

Versus its year-to-date high, Costco stock is currently down over 15%; but for long-term investors, that muted performance may be the very reason it’s a compelling buy after the Q4 report.

Costco stock may soon pay a special dividend

Costco received a “non-recurring” $0.15 per share boost to earnings from International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) tariff refunds in its fourth quarter.

Paired with renewal rates lingering near record highs above 90%, this demographic expansion acts as a long-term multiplier on future membership fee revenue.

How Wall Street recommends playing COST shares

With a cash-fortified balance sheet guarding the downside and a maturing customer base driving top-line lifetime value, COST stock offers an attractive entry point before the next structural leg up.

Costco Q4 2026 earnings beat expectations on tariff refund

For the 16-week period ending Aug. 30, Costco Wholesale disclosed fourth-quarter net income of $2.998 billion, or $6.75 per diluted share, compared with $2.610 billion, or $5.87 per diluted share, in the same period last year. Results topped Wall Street expectations, with analysts surveyed by Zacks Investment Research forecasting earnings of $6.48 per share, according to the Associated Press .

On the top line, quarterly revenue climbed to $95.72 billion, versus $86.16 billion in the year-ago period. Analysts surveyed by FactSet had expected $6.54 per share in earnings and $94.97 billion in revenue, according to the Wall Street Journal .

The quarter was aided by a non-recurring benefit of $0.15 per diluted share tied to refunds received under IEEPA tariff provisions, net of partial reinvestment of those refunds into lower prices for members, the company said. Chief Executive Ron Vachris said on a Thursday investor call that Costco reinvested some of the $184 million in tariff refunds into price reductions on everyday staples, produce, meat, beverages, and certain non-food items including home furnishings, according to the Wall Street Journal.

According to the Wall Street Journal, Chief Financial Officer Gary Millerchip told investors that the payments received so far amount to slightly more than one-third of what Costco anticipates collecting in the fiscal first quarter, and that the company intends to keep directing most of those funds back into lower prices.

Same-store sales for the quarter increased 9.4%, driven by a 10.7% gain in the United States, a 5% rise in Canada, and 7% growth across other international markets. Digitally enabled comparable sales climbed 19.5%. Stripping out the impact of fuel prices and currency movements, comparable sales were 6.7% higher on an adjusted basis.

Net sales grew 11.2% to $93.9 billion from $84.4 billion a year earlier. Membership fees reached $1.85 billion, up from $1.72 billion. For the full fiscal year, net income rose to $9.226 billion, or $20.76 per diluted share, from $8.099 billion, or $18.21 per diluted share, a year earlier. Full-year net sales grew 10.1% to $297.2 billion.

Costco stock ended Thursday's session down 0.9% at $896.48 and was down 0.2% in Friday premarket trading.

The company currently operates 939 warehouses globally, including 647 in the United States and Puerto Rico. It expects to open 33 warehouses in fiscal 2027, including five relocations, according to the Wall Street Journal.

evidence.text:

Walmart just reported its slowest comparable sales growth in six years.

10 stocks we like better than Costco Wholesale ›

Costco's (NASDAQ:COST) fourth-quarter earnings report after Thursday didn't do much to move the stock, as it was flat after hours. However, that may be more of a credit to the company's reliability than anything else, as Costco delivered another round of strong results, outperforming virtually every one of its retail peers.

At a time when consumers are feeling pressure from inflation and the high cost of living, Costco's comparable sales rose 6.7% adjusted for fuel prices and foreign exchange. Revenue in the quarter rose 11.1% to $95.7 billion, beating estimates at $94.89 billion.

On the bottom line, earnings per share rose 15% to $6.75, though it earned a $0.15 benefit from tariff refunds, equivalent to nearly $70 million.

If there was a weak spot in the earnings report, it was that its membership fee revenue rose just 7.3%, its third straight quarter of slowing growth in that category. However, the company is still adding members, and it's delivering all three pillars of its growth: new members, same-store sales, and new store openings.

Additionally, its e-commerce growth remained strong at 19.5%, showing its online retail platform remains popular.

As the largest warehouse club chain, Costco doesn't exactly have a direct competitor, but Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT) is its closest peer. Not only does Walmart own Sam's Club, but it also makes the majority of its revenue from groceries like Costco, and the two companies are among a small group of national, multi-category retailers, including Target and Amazon .

Walmart has done much to reinvent itself over the last decade, and it's paid off. It's become the #2 e-commerce business behind Amazon, with a network of pick-up kiosks, and it's attracted more higher-income consumers, shedding its perception of a discount retailer while maintaining its commitment to everyday low prices.

However, its upswing seems to have hit a roadblock in the second quarter, as comparable sales growth fell to its slowest pace in six years, at 2.6%. Adjusting for new federal drug-price-capping rules that weighed on pharmacy revenue, comparable sales were up 3.4%. Walmart noted that rising gas prices were squeezing household budgets, and shoppers had cut back on discretionary goods.

Still, that's only half the comparable sales growth that Costco just generated, showing its resilience in a challenging time for retailers. Costco has the advantage of catering to mostly higher-income customers who are less sensitive to inflation, especially at a time when the stock market is at an all-time high, and Costco continues to deliver value for its members.

Costco is one of the most expensive retail stocks on the market, even as it is down 5% over the last year. At a price-to-earnings ratio of 43, it's even more expensive than Amazon. By comparison, Walmart trades at a P/E of 39.

While Walmart's reinvention in recent years remains commendable, Costco is the better buy here. It has the most resilient business model in brick-and-mortar retail, and it's one of the few retailers still opening new stores. Costco doesn't even have 1,000 stores around the world, indicating it has plenty of runway, especially as it's proven to be popular in countries like Canada and China.

After growing through both the pandemic and the post-pandemic era, Costco continues to deliver strong results even as other retailers struggle with inflation.

It may take more time for Costco to grow into its valuation, but the stock continues to look like a long-term winner .

evidence.title: The Home Depot and The Home Depot Foundation Aim to Provide 15 Million Introductions to Skilled Trades Careers by 2032
evidence.text:
The Home Depot and The Home Depot Foundation Aim to Provide 15 Million Introductions to Skilled Trades Careers by 2032

Though 4.1 million skilled trades jobs are expected to open over the next decade, currently only 6% of young people express interest in pursuing these careers. To address this gap before students enter the job market, The Home Depot is expanding its workforce development strategy with the launch of Path to Pro Skills Explorers . Designed for youth ages 11 to 17, this free, hands-on and online educational curriculum introduces middle and high school students to high-demand, high-earning careers in the trades.

It’s all part of a new commitment by The Home Depot and The Home Depot Foundation to provide 15 million introductions to the skilled construction trades by 2032 and expand their support for students.

Developed in partnership with Scouting America and piloted with Boys & Girls Clubs of America, Skills Explorers provides turn-key resources that introduce youth to foundational trades skills such as woodworking, plumbing, electrical work, and construction safety through engaging, hands-on learning experiences.

Designed for flexibility, Skills Explorers can be used wherever youth learn and grow, including classrooms, after-school programs, community organizations, and at home. The program includes:

To support these efforts to introduce more youth to the trades, The Home Depot Foundation is awarding more than $13 million in grants as part of its Path to Pro initiative. This includes an incremental investment expanding work with Boys & Girls Clubs of America and a new partnership with Scouting America, enabling them to integrate construction skilled trades curricula into their programming. Education Grants will also be available for youth organizations nationwide.

Additional grants will continue support of hands-on training, certification, scholarships, and entrepreneurship programs through leading workforce and education nonprofits, including Home Builders Institute (HBI), 100 Black Men of America, Construction Ready, the Folds of Honor Foundation and Syracuse University’s D’Aniello Institute for Veterans and Military Families.

Team Depot, the company’s associate volunteer force, will also begin engaging local nonprofits across the U.S. in hands-on youth activities, creating opportunities for more than 470,000 associates to share their skills and passion for building with the next generation.

The addition of Skills Explorers marks the newest chapter in a long-standing commitment by The Home Depot and The Home Depot Foundation to solve the nation’s skilled labor gap. To date, Path to Pro has graduated more than 200,000 individuals from the Skills Program, and the Foundation has certified 70,000 and introduced over 700,000 people to trade careers.

"For nearly a decade, The Home Depot and The Home Depot Foundation have provided free training to separating military, youth, career changers and other communities interested in pursuing a career in the trades," said Michael Rowe, Executive Vice President – Pro, The Home Depot. "However, with a lack of youth interested in these careers, we’re expanding our programs to introduce more people to the trades, because closing the skilled labor gap starts long before someone applies for a job. We have to start by helping young people see what's possible."

Teachers, parents, and youth leaders can download the free Skills Explorers curriculum and explore training resources by visiting https://www.pathtopro.com/skills-explorers/ .

evidence.title: The Home Depot (HD) Posts Record Sales Growth Amid CEO Leave
evidence.text:
The Home Depot (HD) Posts Record Sales Growth Amid CEO Leave

On August 18, 2026, The Home Depot, Inc. (NYSE: HD ) reported fiscal second-quarter net sales up 5.7% to $47.86 billion. It is the best comparable sales growth since 2022, in the same earnings report where the company confirmed CEO Ted Decker is on a temporary medical leave of absence.

Home Depot's results prove the business can perform even with its top executive absent, but the housing market conditions constraining growth haven't changed. Is this sales strength durable evidence of a real turnaround or a temporary boost from smaller projects while big-ticket renovations stay frozen?

Adjusted profit of $4.92 a share beat the $4.73 analysts expected, and comparable sales rose 1.7%, beating the 0.9% guess. The Home Depot, Inc. (NYSE:HD) got $730 million back in tariff refunds this quarter, using most of it to lower the cost of goods sold. The company grew its Express Delivery service nationwide, promising delivery in three hours or less. It kept its full-year forecast of 2.5% to 4.5% sales growth despite the leadership gap, a sign leaders trust the business doesn't depend on just one person. This sales strength lands even as rival Lowe's and the broader home-improvement category continue to describe the same frozen housing backdrop, which means Home Depot's beat shows real share gains, not just an easier market.

CFO Richard McPhail admitted The Home Depot, Inc. (NYSE:HD) hasn't yet seen the mix of factors that unlocks bigger renovation projects, and how often people buy and sell homes has stayed at a multi-year low for four years straight. It means this sales gain relies on smaller projects, not the big-ticket remodels that drive real profit growth. Decker's medical leave adds real uncertainty at a $337 billion company with 470,000 workers and more than 2,300 stores. Splitting his job between two leaders instead of naming one clear stand-in leaves investors, workers, and Wall Street all guessing who's really running the company day to day. That doubt alone can hurt confidence no matter how well the business performs this particular quarter.

Home Depot's results show real resilience even without its CEO front and center, but the housing market conditions holding back bigger renovation spending remain exactly where they were before this quarter.

evidence.title: Lowe's vs. The Home Depot: Which Retail Stock Is the Better Buy in 2026?
evidence.text:
As the housing market enters a new phase in 2026, many investors are choosing between Lowe's Companies ( LOW +0.25% ) and The Home Depot ( HD +0.70% ) to capture a recovery in the home improvement space.

Both retailers dominate the home improvement market, but they cater to slightly different needs. While one leans heavily into professional contractors, the other has historically focused on do-it-yourself homeowners. Comparing these giants involves looking how they match up on scale, profitability, and valuations to see which offers a more compelling opportunity for investors.

Lowe's operates 1,748 stores across the United States. It sells maintenance, repair, and remodeling products to both do-it-yourself shoppers and professional contractors. The company has focused on improving its digital offerings and expanding its "Pro" customer base to boost sales stability.

In fiscal 2025, revenue reached $86 billion, up roughly 3% from the prior year. The company generated net income of approximately $6.7 billion during this period. Net margin, the percentage of revenue retained as profit, was roughly 7.7%.

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is 4.2, indicating that debt exceeds shareholder equity. The current ratio, which measures a company's ability to pay short-term debts with its short-term assets, is roughly 1.1. Free cash flow, or the cash left over after paying for operating costs and equipment, was nearly $7.7 billion for fiscal 2025.

The Home Depot operates a massive network of 2,359 stores across the United States, Canada, and Mexico. It serves three main groups, including do-it-yourself, do-it-for-me, and professional customers. The company focuses on large-scale logistics and e-commerce to maintain its position among home improvement retailers.

For 2025, revenue reached nearly $165 billion, showing growth of roughly 3.2%. Net income for the year was nearly $14.2 billion. Its net margin of 8.6% reflects the profit remaining after all expenses are paid.

As of its February 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 5.1. This ratio measures how much debt a company uses relative to its shareholder equity. The current ratio, which compares short-term assets to short-term debts, is approximately 1.1, while free cash flow reached nearly $12.6 billion during the fiscal year.

Lowe's faces intense competition from physical retailers like Walmart and digital giants like Amazon . Its performance relies heavily on the health of the housing market and consumer spending levels. Disruptions in the supply chain or rising labor and material costs could also impact its bottom line.

The Home Depot is also sensitive to economic shifts, particularly high interest rates, which can slow large renovation projects. The company has recently acquired businesses like SRS and GMS, which carry risks of integrating these large operations. Failure to stay ahead of competitors in price and service could result in a loss of market share.

Lowe's appears to be the more value-oriented choice based on its lower Forward P/E , which compares the stock price to future earnings estimates, and its lower P/S ratio .

Sector benchmark uses the SPDR XLY sector ETF. Valuation metrics sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

Both companies are set up to accelerate growth when the housing market recovers. There should be plenty of pent-up demand as higher interest rates have held back big purchases for the last few years.

These companies closely match in terms of financial health, capital efficiency, margins, and the strategic investments they are making to drive growth. They are both pursuing the same AI opportunities to help customers plan their projects.

Home Depot is the better dividend stock, offering a high yield of about 2.9%, compared to Lowe’s 2.2%. However, analysts expect Lowe’s to grow earnings at about 9% annually, compared with about 5% for Home Depot.

Moreover, Lowe’s forward P/E of 17 is cheaper than Home Depot’s 21 earnings multiple. Given the difference in valuation and growth expectations, Lowe’s appears to be the more attractive stock right now. I would buy Home Depot for the yield, but Lowe’s may offer more upside when demand picks up.

NIKE, Inc., NKE The sportswear company has experienced a difficult period as demand patterns continue changing across major markets. Analysts have reduced earnings expectations for the coming fiscal years. The latest outlook reflects concerns over slower sales momentum and weaker product performance.

evidence.text:
Nike (NKE) Stock Tumbles as Bank of America Slashes Rating and Price Target

Nike stock experienced a premarket decline exceeding 2% on Friday following a downgrade from Bank of America, which shifted its rating from Neutral to Underperform.

BofA analyst Lorraine Hutchinson simultaneously reduced the firm’s price objective to $30 from the previous $47 level. This revised target represents approximately 17% downside potential from the company’s most recent closing price.

The investment bank now anticipates Nike’s revenue revival will be delayed until fiscal 2028. This represents a meaningful pushback from BofA’s earlier projections of a quicker recovery trajectory.

The firm revised its earnings per share forecast for fiscal 2027 downward by 11% and its fiscal 2028 projection lower by 12%. The updated fiscal 2027 estimate now stands 14% beneath the Visible Alpha consensus expectation.

The North American wholesale channel had emerged as a relative strength for Nike , posting 14% growth during fiscal 2026 even as overall revenue remained stagnant. However, BofA believes this positive trend is nearing exhaustion.

Retail sellout velocity is currently trailing shipment rates, indicating retailers are experiencing difficulty moving inventory at the pace Nike is delivering it. Traditional franchise footwear is experiencing declining consumer interest, while certain recent product introductions have failed to generate meaningful traction.

This dynamic may prompt wholesale partners to adopt a more conservative purchasing stance. BofA projects North American wholesale revenue will turn negative beginning in the second quarter and persist through the remainder of fiscal 2027.

Revenue from Nike’s Greater China region contracted 17% during the most recent reporting period. Research from BofA’s Luxury Goods analysts, conducted through on-the-ground visits in China, revealed a nuanced situation.

Their findings pointed to subdued athletic demand and new product offerings that aren’t connecting with Chinese consumers. Performance running category momentum is slowing, while surplus inventory is accumulating amid softening consumer demand.

Additionally, Nike is strategically reducing its footprint with online marketplace partners in China. BofA anticipates this transition will generate heightened promotional activity through the second quarter before enabling Nike to establish more unified brand positioning across digital channels.

The shares have experienced significant pressure over the past year beyond today’s decline. Nike stock has dropped 44% year to date, contrasting sharply with the S&P 500’s 12% advance.

BofA noted this decline already incorporates a 40% reduction to fiscal 2027 earnings estimates during the same timeframe. The firm’s analysts believe the stock cannot sustain premium valuation multiples amid continued earnings estimate reductions.

One positive development involves tariff exposure. Current duty rates on Nike merchandise range from 10% to 12.5%, representing a decline from approximately 20% a year earlier.

BofA anticipates Nike’s recently appointed CFO will prioritize expense reduction initiatives. Operating expense optimization is viewed as a probable area of concentration.

Dividend sustainability represents an additional concern highlighted in the research note. BofA’s fiscal 2027 projections imply a payout ratio of 107%, indicating the dividend payment would surpass net income.

This factor contributed to BofA’s decision to downgrade its income rating on the shares. With revenue under pressure, the bank stated Nike’s profit trajectory will rely substantially on gross profit margin improvement and enhanced expense discipline.

Nike Pulls Back on Bank of America Downgrade and $30 Price Objective; Dick’s Ticks Up, On Holding Holds Flat

Bank of America just told investors that Nike's comeback is running a full year behind schedule, and the market is punishing the stock while its rivals barely flinch. Whether the selloff stays contained to one brand or spreads across athletic…

Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel .

Nike ( NYSE:NKE | NKE Price Prediction ) is slipping after Bank of America concluded that the sneaker giant’s turnaround will arrive a full fiscal year later than expected, and the selling looks specific to the brand. Meanwhile, Dick’s Sporting Goods ( NYSE:DKS ) stock is up 2% to $136.29, a gain for one of Nike’s key retail channels. On Holding ( NYSE:ONON ) stock is up 0.2% to $30.51, barely shifting even with its larger running rival in retreat, according to Bank of America.

Bank of America Pushes Nike’s Recovery Out a Year

Analysts led by Lorraine Hutchinson at Bank of America downgraded Nike to Underperform from Neutral and lowered their price objective to $30. Nike’s sales recovery now looks likely to arrive a fiscal year later than the stronger previously expected, with revenue forecast to decline through the year ahead. Bank of America summed up its view by stating that “risks are rising” for the turnaround.

North America wholesale is likely to slow. The recent bright spot for Nike still sees sell-through lagging sell-in, according to the stronger, and that gap could leave retailers less willing to back new product. Hutchinson’s team also pointed to weak sports demand in China , product innovation that isn’t connecting with consumers, and excess inventory built up by soft demand. With the top line under strain, the stronger stated that Nike’s earnings outlook increasingly depends on gross margin expansion and cost control, and it expects the incoming chief financial officer to focus on reducing operating overhead.

Bank of America’s call on Nike is a timing argument. The stronger still projects a turnaround coming, just a year later than it anticipated, and a recovery pushed further out is worth less in present terms, so the downgrade mainly asks the market to pay a lower multiple for a delayed payoff given how far Nike stock has already fallen this year.

Across athletic retail, the reaction looks contained to one name. Dick’s, a key channel for Nike product, is higher, and On Holding, a direct rival in premium running, is holding its ground, which marks the selloff as specific to Nike, tied to its own inventory, product, and China questions.

Nike’s own leadership highlighted the same pressure points earlier this year. Elliott Hill was chief executive at the time. On the company’s fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter earnings call on June 30, he stated, “Overall, the results aren’t there yet.” Hill added that sell-through in Nike Sportswear and Jordan Streetwear “remains challenged, impacting both current discounting and future order books,” which lines up with the wholesale worry Bank of America raised.

North America wholesale is the clearest test of Bank of America’s call on Nike, since that channel has been a recent source of strength for the brand. Investors may want to watch for signs that retailers such as Dick’s grow less willing to back new Nike product, a shift that would support the firm’s sell-through concern. Any early move by the incoming chief financial officer on overhead could also shape how quickly margins carry Nike’s earnings story.

Dick’s and On Holding also offer a gauge of whether the pressure on Nike spreads across athletic names. A slide in either stock could extend the story from one brand to the broader category, and investors holding several of these names should weigh their overall exposure to the group with that risk in mind. Until one of those names cracks, the downgrade remains a verdict on Nike’s execution.

Alibaba launches new AI chip, CEO Eddie Wu calls it ‘most powerful’ in China; expansion plans ahead

Chinese technology giant Alibaba Group on Tuesday launched a new artificial intelligence (AI) chip, which it described as “the most powerful AI chip in China,” while announcing plans to significantly expand its data centre capacity in the coming years

Hangzhou [China], : Chinese technology giant Alibaba Group on Tuesday launched a new artificial intelligence chip, which it described as “the most powerful AI chip in China,” while announcing plans to significantly expand its data centre capacity in the coming years.

The latest chip called Zhenwu V900 was unveiled by Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu at the company’s annual Apsara Conference in Hangzhou on Tuesday, as per an official release. Zhenwu V900 is capable of scaling up to 500,000 cards per cluster, the company said.

Speaking at the Apsara Conference 2026, Alibaba Group CEO Eddie Wu said machine intelligence currently represents less than 3 per cent of human capacity, leaving significant room for growth as

AI capabilities scale. To support this expansion, Alibaba is investing across three key areas: AI models, chips and cloud infrastructure.

The company is advancing Recursive Self-Improvement and plans to develop Qwen models with 5–10 trillion parameters as it works towards artificial superintelligence .

In parallel, Alibaba plans to expand its global data centre capacity to more than 20 gigawatts by 2032 to meet growing AI demand.

“Alibaba will join forces with all our partners to commit fully to AI infrastructure development, forging an AI cloud designed for the Machine Intelligence era. Our target is that by 2032, the global data center capacity operated by Alibaba Cloud will surpass 20GW, fueling the industry’s exponentially rising demand for AI,” Wu said, as per the release.

The company launched Qwen Intelligence for mobile devices. It is an end-to-end solution that enables mobile devices to reason through and execute truly complex tasks.

Wu also outlined the company’s strategic roadmap for the “Machine Intelligence” era, noting that machines are increasingly becoming a key force behind thinking.

He said machine thinking currently accounts for less than 3 per cent of overall human thinking, leaving significant room for growth as machine intelligence scales towards 1,000 times human capacity.

“In the future, the total amount of Human Thinking will continue to grow, but Machine Thinking will expand even faster, ultimately shouldering 99.9% of all Thinking,” he said.

JD.com Proposes Remedies to Address EU Probe in $2.5 Billion Ceconomy Deal

Overview of JD.com's Ceconomy Acquisition and EU Investigation

Aug 20 (Reuters) - Chinese e-commerce giant JD.com has offered remedies in the European Union's probe of its $2.5 ‌billion bid for German electronics retailer Ceconomy, according to an EU regulatory filing.

• The filing did not specify the remedies offered.

• The European ​Commission opened a full-scale investigation into the deal ​in May under the Foreign Subsidies Regulation that ⁠targets unfair foreign state aid, citing concerns that JD.com might have received ‌foreign ⁠subsidies that could distort the bloc's market.

• JD.com was hit with ​a formal notice of regulatory concerns over its bid last month.

• China said on ​Wednesday that the EU's investigation constituted "improper extraterritorial jurisdiction" and ordered entities not to implement or assist with the probe.

Approach 1: Rakuten Group Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) Analysis

The Discounted Cash Flow, or DCF, model estimates what a company might be worth by projecting its future cash flows and then discounting them back to today in ¥ terms. In this case, Simply Wall St uses a 2 Stage Free Cash Flow to Equity approach for Rakuten Group.

Rakuten Group currently reports last twelve month free cash flow of a loss of ¥23.2b. Despite that starting point, the model uses analyst inputs and extrapolated figures to project future free cash flow, including an estimate of ¥656.2b in 2029 and further projections through 2035. All of these are converted into today's value using a discount rate.

Bringing all those discounted cash flows together produces an estimated intrinsic value of ¥4,188.37 per share. Compared with the current share price, the DCF output suggests the stock is 76.1% undervalued according to this model, so the market price sits well below this cash flow based estimate.

Approach 2: Rakuten Group Price vs Sales

For companies where earnings are limited or volatile, the P/S ratio is often a useful cross check because it looks at how much you are paying for each unit of revenue rather than profit. It is particularly relevant when P/E is less meaningful or negative.

What counts as a reasonable P/S ratio usually reflects growth expectations and risk. Higher growth and lower perceived risk can support a higher multiple, while slower growth or higher risk tends to point to a lower one.

Rakuten Group currently trades on a P/S of 0.89x. This sits above the Multiline Retail industry average of 0.69x, but below the peer group average of 1.49x.
