evidence.title: Sonova sees China as key growth and innovation hub
evidence.text:
Sonova sees China as key growth and innovation hub

Sonova, the Swiss hearing care solution provider, will step up its localization efforts, expand its application of artificial intelligence, and accelerate digital innovation in China as the country plays an increasingly important role in its global growth strategy, according to its top executive.

Eric Bernard, CEO of Sonova, said China is not only one of the world’s largest hearing care markets, but also an important base for developing new products and service models that could later be introduced to other Asian markets and beyond.

“China ranks very high on my list of priorities,” Bernard said during his first visit to the country as the group’s CEO.

The speed of innovation, strong digital infrastructure, and availability of skilled talent make China an ideal market for testing new hearing care solutions, he added.

The Swiss company plans to give its China team greater autonomy, strengthen its research and development capabilities in Shanghai, and integrate artificial intelligence and digital tools into its products and services.

It will also expand remote hearing tests, online fitting support, and AI-enabled screening services to reach consumers beyond major cities where access to trained hearing care professionals remains limited.

China has about 220 million people with hearing loss, with the prevalence reaching about 45 percent among those aged 60 and above, according to information released by the National Health Commission last year.

Bernard said many people still regard hearing loss as an unavoidable part of aging rather than a health condition that can be effectively managed. Consumers often wait eight or nine years before seeking professional help.

To address these challenges, Sonova is working with governments, hospitals, universities, and local partners to raise public awareness, train hearing care professionals, and improve screening and intervention standards.

Bernard said China’s rapidly aging population, expanding middle-income group and growing focus on healthy aging will generate stronger demand for accessible hearing care.

To better capture these opportunities, Sonova will leverage the Hainan Free Trade Port to accelerate the introduction of innovative hearing care products and services to the Chinese market.

With more than 18,000 employees and operations spanning over 120 countries and regions, Sonova runs a manufacturing base in Suzhou, Jiangsu province and a research and development center in Shanghai.

evidence.title: Alcon expanding eye care biz in China
evidence.text:
Having operated in China for more than 30 years, Geneva-headquartered eye care company Alcon plans to step up investment and deepen localization, with rising demand for higher-quality eye care and rapid technological advances underpinning its confidence in the market's long-term prospects, a senior executive told China Daily.

"China is one of our most important markets in the world and is strategically important for our international business," said Rick Kozloski, president of Alcon China, in an interview earlier this month on the sidelines of the 30th Congress of the Chinese Ophthalmological Society in Tianjin.

Alcon is exploring collaboration opportunities with Chinese innovators in areas such as artificial intelligence and robotics, which could help shape the future of ophthalmology, Kozloski said.

"We're very interested in partnering with Chinese experts and innovators," he said.

The company invests nearly $990 million in research and development worldwide each year and is looking to involve Chinese specialists earlier in the product development phase to better address local client needs.

Feedback from Chinese surgeons has already helped Alcon improve Wavelight Plus since the personalized laser vision-correction technology made its global debut in China in 2023 during the China International Import Expo, he said.

Beyond post-launch feedback, Alcon is increasingly involving Chinese ophthalmologists earlier in the innovation process through advisory boards and product development discussions, helping ensure future technologies are designed around local patient needs from the outset.

China's manufacturing expertise, potential cost advantages and policies encouraging multinational companies to produce locally are also reinforcing Alcon's commitment to the country, Kozloski said, adding that Alcon is increasing investment in local manufacturing.

"Some of the most advanced technologies in the world are made here," he said.

A survey released in May by the European Union Chamber of Commerce in China found that 75 percent of respondents considered production in China more efficient than elsewhere. Some 94 percent regarded China as an important sourcing destination, citing delivery speed, cost, reliability and quality.

The company is localizing production of the "wavelight refractive excimer laser", which has entered the final stage of regulatory review. Subject to approval, the localization effort is expected to further strengthen Alcon's ability to serve the China market, Kozloski said.

The manufacturing push follows investment in the company's local supply chain. About two years ago, Alcon invested in a new distribution facility and operating model in Kunshan, Jiangsu province, to improve distribution efficiency, he added.

Kozloski said his assessment of China's long-term market potential remains unchanged, supported by its large population of people with myopia, growing demand for cataract treatment as the population ages and steady growth in demand for refractive surgery.

Patients' expectations are also rising, with greater emphasis on the quality of vision after treatment, creating sustained demand for more advanced products and services, Kozloski added.

National volume-based procurement is helping more patients gain access to advanced intraocular lenses, including extended depth-of-focus and trifocal lenses, Kozloski said.

Alcon will participate actively in the next round of procurement and continue investing in professional education programs, he said.

Alcon Launches UNITY M, a Premium Ophthalmic Microscope Delivering Precise Control

Alcon (SIX/NYSE: ALC), the global leader in eye care dedicated to helping people see brilliantly, today announced the initial commercial launch of UNITY M, an Alcon brand premium surgical microscope that delivers precise control to ophthalmic surgeons, in select markets including the U.S. and Japan followed by Europe. 1,2,4 UNITY M will be featured at the upcoming Congress of the European Society of Cataract and Refractive Surgeons (ESCRS). The microscope is the latest addition to Alcon's UNITY platform, combining advanced optics, novel illumination, improved ergonomics, and intuitive usability in a modular design that enables practice-specific customization and future scalability. 1-3,5-7,†,‡,§

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260901560640/en/

Alcon Launches UNITY M, a Premium Ophthalmic Microscope Delivering Precise Control

"The idea behind the UNITY platform is to develop clinic-based and operating room equipment solutions with a seamless user experience that improve surgical workflows," said Ian Bell, SVP and Chief Operating Officer of Alcon. "By partnering closely with Eye Care Professionals to understand their most significant unmet needs, we developed UNITY M to provide a flexible, future-ready visualization platform that gives surgeons precise control and personalization in the operating room."

UNITY M offers surgical precision through advanced visualization technologies designed to provide stable, consistent views throughout surgery. 2,† Base model includes:

"Visualization is fundamental to every procedure I perform because it directly impacts the level of control I have throughout surgery," said Dr. Eric Rosenberg, SightMD, Long Island, New York. "During critical moments of a case, having a stable view helps me operate with confidence and precision. The combination of a stable red reflex, advanced illumination and enhanced depth of field provides the visualization I need to maintain control from one stage of surgery to the next, while the platform's flexibility allows me to tailor the system to my specific preferences."

UNITY M also features a modular architecture that allows surgeons to tailor the system to their clinical needs. 3 Designed with the ophthalmic surgeon in mind, both anterior and posterior segment surgeons can configure the platform with purpose-built optimizations and adopt modular upgrades over time, creating a system that evolves alongside their practice. 2-4,11

Like other equipment within the UNITY platform, UNITY M is designed for current and future integration with Alcon's ecosystem of products, digital innovations and services. As the third addition to the UNITY platform, following UNITY VCS and UNITY CS, UNITY M reflects Alcon's continued commitment to building a connected, future-ready ecosystem, including forthcoming modular UNITY M additions to help seamlessly power practices. 3,13,14 UNITY M has received CE Mark and regulatory approvals in India, Europe, Canada, Japan and the U.S., with inventory beginning to ship in September. For more information on UNITY M, visit the Alcon booth at ESCRS [Excel London C231] and join the special Alcon symposium Unity Surgical Platform From Vision to Impact in Clinical Practice, on Sunday, September 13 at 9:30 AM or speak to your Alcon sales representative.

evidence.title: Exclusive: Broadwood says Alcon’s earnings reveal STAAR bid came from ‘weakness’
evidence.text:
Exclusive: Broadwood says Alcon’s earnings reveal STAAR bid came from ‘weakness’

Investing.com -- Alcon AG's (NYSE:ALC) latest earnings are drawing fire from new acquisition STAAR Surgical 's (NASDAQ:STAA) largest shareholder, Broadwood Partners, which said the results underscore why the Swiss eye-care company "needs STAAR far more than STAAR needs Alcon."

The remarks came after Alcon posted modest third-quarter growth and reaffirmed its full-year outlook, sending shares up 4% in Wednesday trade. But Broadwood founder Neal C. Bradsher told Investing.com that Alcon's continued weakness in its implantables division highlights the company's dependence on the proposed STAAR deal.

"Alcon's results today, including the continuing weakness of its implantables business, demonstrate why Alcon needs STAAR far more than STAAR needs Alcon, and why Alcon has been pursuing STAAR so aggressively for more than 19 months," Bradsher said to Investing.com in an emailed. "Alcon's recent public pessimism about STAAR is simply a transparent strategy to deter other bidders and enable Alcon to buy STAAR on the cheap."

Implantables net sales rose just 2% in the third quarter to $432 million, reflecting the launch of PanOptix Pro but also "continued competitive pressures," according to the company. For the first nine months of 2025, implantables revenue totaled $1.3 billion, down 1% from a year earlier, or flat on a constant-currency basis, highlighting the sluggish backdrop Bradsher cited.

Broadwood Partners, holder of over 27% of STAAR's stock, has been waging a months-long campaign against the proposed sale to Alcon, arguing the deal undervalues the company and reflects a flawed sale process.

On the company's earnings call, CEO David Endicott defended the proposed $28-per-share acquisition, saying STAAR's implantable collamer lens (ICL) technology is "complementary to our refractive laser business."

"We continue to view the transaction as attractive and believe Alcon is best suited to maximize the value of their implantable collamer lens," Endicott told analysts. "We like this deal, but it isn't essential to our long-term growth plan."

When asked about alternatives if the deal falls apart, Endicott said, "We'll figure that out when we get there. We hope this gets done, but if it doesn't, we've got a great plan."

The comments mark continued escalation in an increasingly personal set of jabs between Alcon and Broadwood. Earlier this month, the two sides traded public attacks after Alcon released an investor presentation accusing Broadwood of attempting a "silent takeover" of STAAR and warning that the activist's plan to oust three directors "risks disenfranchising the broader stockholder base."

Broadwood swiftly fired back, calling Alcon's presentation "replete with fallacious arguments and baseless claims," and argued that STAAR's board had misled shareholders about the deal's process and prospects.

Alcon's materials also took aim at Broadwood and fellow dissenter Yunqi Capital, questioning their investment track records. Bradsher countered that Alcon's criticism was "selective and misleading," quipping that if Alcon's own returns since its 2019 spinoff from Novartis matched Broadwood's, "its stock would be trading at more than $150 per share, instead of $75."

As Investing.com previously reported, roughly 72% of STAAR's outstanding shares had already voted against the merger ahead of the originally scheduled October 23 meeting, with just 18% voting in favor. STAAR later postponed the vote to December 19 to allow time for a revised "go-shop" process, though Alcon has refused to raise its offer price so far.

All three major proxy advisory firms, ISS, Glass Lewis, and Egan-Jones, have recommended that shareholders vote against the deal.

Alcon reported third-quarter net sales of $2.59 billion, up 6% from a year earlier, or 5% in constant currency, an improvement from 3% growth in the prior quarter. Core diluted EPS came in at $0.79 with a 20.2% core operating margin, slightly below last year's 20.6%. Net profit slipped to $237 million from $263 million, weighed down by higher taxes.

The company maintained its full-year guidance after two downward revisions earlier this year, offering relief to investors.

By division, Surgical net sales rose 6% to $1.4 billion, driven by implantables, consumables, and equipment, while Vision Care revenue increased 7% to $1.2 billion, supported by stronger demand for contact lenses and ocular health products. Both segments grew 5% in constant currency.

Endicott pointed to "encouraging topline growth" from new products such as the Unity VCS surgical system and PanOptix Pro lens, saying early uptake "lays the groundwork for a solid 2026."

STAAR shareholders are set to vote on the proposed Alcon merger on December 19, following a go-shop period that allows the company to solicit rival bids. While Alcon has held firm on its $28-per-share offer, Broadwood has urged the board to reject the deal outright and pursue alternatives once the vote concludes.

Exclusive: Broadwood says Alcon's earnings reveal STAAR bid came from 'weakness'

evidence.title: Fresenius discontinuing Chinese sales of 4008A hemodialysis system
evidence.text:
The company’s plans, announced today, include discontinuing local production and sales of the 4008A hemodialysis system, launched in 2019 as a cost-effective option for emerging markets. Fresenius will instead focus in China on more cutting-edge technologies for in-center dialysis and critical care, including the high-volume hemodiafiltration-enabled 5008S CAREsystem, multiFiltratePRO, and other advanced dialysis products.

Fresenius will also exit its China peritoneal dialysis (PD) business, though it will maintain existing obligations in the market. In addition, it is strengthening local leadership, including appointing market GM Rex Liu.

The goal, according to company officials, is a more localized portfolio, increased commercialization of locally relevant innovation, and a focused go-to-market approach. The moves appear to recognize how much China’s status has risen in the world since Fresenius entered the market more than two decades ago.

“China is an important market for our Care Enablement business,” said Helen Giza, Chief Executive Officer for Fresenius Medical Care. “As the market evolves, we are refining our portfolio to focus on the areas where we can create the greatest value for patients and customers.”

Fresenius expects the portfolio optimization actions in China to result in €110 million in impairment charges, scrappage and termination costs, expected to be recognized in Q3 2026, with no meaningful impact expected on the future revenue outlook for Care Enablement’s China business.

“We are confident that this is the right portfolio and strategy that will best position us to compete and grow in China,” said Joe Turk, CEO of Fresenius Medical Care’s Care Enablement operating segment. “We remain committed to the market and will continue leveraging our local manufacturing footprint and China Design Center to support profitable growth.”

evidence.title: Die Fresenius-Medical-Care-Aktie untersucht einen Cyber-Vorfall
evidence.text:
Die Fresenius-Medical-Care-Aktie notierte am 23.09.2026 um 20:00 Uhr UTC bei 22,41 USD an der NYSE und lag damit 0,40 Prozent unter dem vorherigen Wert. Am selben Datum teilte Fresenius Medical Care mit, dass das Unternehmen einen Cybersecurity-Vorfall mit unbefugtem Zugriff auf eine begrenzte Zahl interner Systeme untersucht, wie Fresenius Medical Care meldet.

Der Vorfall ergänzt die operative Entwicklung des Dialysespezialisten um ein digitales Risikothema. Die Mitteilung nennt interne Systeme als betroffenen Bereich und datiert die Untersuchung auf den 23.09.2026, ohne den Geschäftsbetrieb in der Mitteilung mit einer konkreten Kennzahl zu verknüpfen.

Für die fundamentale Einordnung bleibt das zweite Quartal 2026 entscheidend. Im Bericht vom 03.08.2026 stieg der Umsatz im Jahresvergleich um 1 Prozent auf 4,861 Mrd. EUR, während das bereinigte operative Ergebnis um 23 Prozent auf 569 Mio. EUR zulegte, wie Fresenius Medical Care berichtet.

Die Zahlen zeigen eine klare Verschiebung im zweiten Quartal: Das bereinigte operative Ergebnis wuchs um 23 Prozent, der Umsatz jedoch nur um 1 Prozent. Die bereinigte operative Marge erhöhte sich dadurch von 9,9 Prozent im zweiten Quartal 2025 auf 11,7 Prozent im zweiten Quartal 2026.

Auch das bereinigte Konzernergebnis verbesserte sich um 13 Prozent auf 303 Mio. EUR. Das unbereinigte Konzernergebnis sank dagegen um 3 Prozent auf 218 Mio. EUR, während das bereinigte Ergebnis je Aktie um 24 Prozent auf 1,13 EUR stieg.

Am 23.09.2026 lag die Aktie bei 22,41 USD und damit 0,40 Prozent unter dem vorherigen Wert. Die 52-Wochen-Spanne reicht von 20,02 USD bis 27,64 USD; die Marktkapitalisierung betrug 12.037.067.098 USD.

evidence.title: Cybervorfälle: Fresenius, Stadtwerke Landsberg …
evidence.text:
Cybervorfälle: Fresenius, Stadtwerke Landsberg …

Der Dialyse-Konzern Fresenius Medical Care ist wohl Opfer eines Cyberangriffs geworden, wie gerade bekannt wurde. Auch die Stadtwerke Landsberg sind Anfang September 2026 einem Cyberangriff zum Opfer gefallen. Hier ein Sammelbeitrag an Sicherheitsmeldungen, die mir die Tage untergekommen sind.

Im Umfeld des GUTcert-Vorfalls (siehe Hackerangriff auf die GUTcert; Kundendaten abgeflossen – ein KRITIS-Problem? ) hat mich ein Blog-Leser zum 20.9.2026 auch auf einen Cyberangriff auf die Stadtwerke Landsberg aufmerksam gemacht. Die Stadtwerke haben zum 7.9.2026 auf ihrer Webseite über den Vorfall informiert.

Die Stadtwerke Landsberg KU wurden zum 1. September 2026 Opfer eines Cyber-Angriffs, in dessen Folge zentrale IT-Systeme verschlüsselt wurden. Forensiker untersuchen den Vorfall. Der Betrieb der kritischen Infrastruktur (Stromnetz, der Wasserversorgung, Kläranlage, Fernwärme, Glasfasernetzes, Ladeinfrastruktur, Inselbads und Parkgaragen) sind von dem Angriff nicht betroffen.

Der Dialyse-Konzern Fresenius Medical Care ist Opfer eines Cyberangriffs geworden. Laut nachfolgendem Tweet hat die Gruppe ShinyHunters Fresenius Medical Care als Opfer aufgelistet.

Fresenius Medical Care ist ein Gesundheitsunternehmen mit Hauptsitz in Deutschland, das sich auf Dialyseprodukte, -dienstleistungen und -behandlungen für Menschen mit Nierenerkrankungen spezialisiert hat. Das Handelsblatt berichtet inzwischen in diesem Beitrag einige Details. Beim Cybersicherheitsvorfall, sei es zu einem unbefugten Zugriff auf eine begrenzte Anzahl interner Systeme gekommen. "Der Vorfall hatte keine Auswirkungen auf Medizinprodukte, die Patientenversorgung, die Produktion oder auf den laufenden Geschäftsbetrieb." Der Zugriff sei eingedämmt und werde derzeit von Forensikern untersucht.

Die Cineplexx Kinobetriebe Ges.m.b.H. ist der größte Kinobetreiber in Österreich und ein Tochterunternehmen der Constantin Film-Holding mit Sitz in Wien. Zum 27.8.2026 erreichte mich eine Lesermail "vor ein paar Stunden gab es von Cineplexx AT eine E-Mail 'zum Schutz deines Kundenkontos haben wir dein Passwort vorsorglich zurückgesetzt.'" der Leser hat dort gleich zwei Konten und zwei E-Mails erhalten. Auf reddit.com finden sich unter "cineplex_hacked" etliche Betroffene, die auch die Meldung erhielten, und einen Hack vermuteten. Offizielle Meldungen konnte der Leser keine finden. Da in der Mail keine Links enthalten waren, um auf PW Reset zu klicken, sondern explizit die Site aufgerufen werden muss, klang das schon nicht nach einem Hoax. Die Auflösung findet sich in diesem Beitrag vom 28.8.2026 – es war eine Vorsichtsmaßnahme.

Cyberangriff auf Dienstleister für Stromzähler

Mir liegt von einem Leser noch die Kopie eines Zeitungsausschnitts aus Stuttgart vor, nach dem das IT-System eines Dienstleisters für Stromzählermontagen in Baden-Württemberg gehackt wurde. Dabei wurden Kundendaten durch die Angreifer abgezogen. Der Fall muss sich bereits im Juli 2026 ereignet haben. Bei einer Internetsuche bin ich auf diesen Beitrag des SWR gestoßen, der noch einige Informationen enthält.

Cyberangriff auf Kreishandwerkerschaft Borken

Die Kreishandwerkerschaft Borken wurde in der Nacht zum 11. September 2026 Opfer eines Cyberangriffs. Die Attacke legte die gesamte EDV, die Server, die Telefonie und den E-Mail-Verkehr der Hauptgeschäftsstelle in Bocholt sowie der Geschäftsstelle in Ahaus lahm. Eine Quelle ist diese Webseite , betroffen vom Ausfall waren 31 Innungen mit rund 2.000 Mitgliedsunternehmen. Mitte September bekannte sich die Ransomware-Gruppe Rhysida zu dem Angriff und drohte mit der Veröffentlichung erbeuteter Daten.

Bereits im August 2026 bin ich auf den nachfolgenden Tweet gestoßen. Ein Sicherheitsforscher mit dem Alias Dirk-jan hat eine Technik vorgestellt, mit der sich Windows Hello for Business-Schlüssel aus einer kompromittierten Benutzersitzung über die (inzwischen gefixte) Schwachstelle CVE-2025-55241 missbrauchen lassen.

Es sind keine Administratorrechte, keine PIN, keine biometrischen Daten erforderlich. Der Hack ermöglicht die vollständige Persistenz in der Entra ID-Cloud über ein Implantat auf Benutzerebene. Details hat der Sicherheitsforscher in diesem Artikel dokumentiert.

Anbieter Cisco hat zum 18. September und zum heutigen 23. September 2026 Sicherheitshinweise auf kritische Schwachstellen in seinen Produkten veröffentlicht . Also drüber schauen und patchen (danke an den Leser für den Hinweis).

In der Firmware von Synology-NAS-Systemen gab es gleich mehrere Schwachstellen, über die Angreifer auf Daten hätten zugreifen können. heise hat die Details die Tage in diesem Artikel zusammen getragen.

Ende August 2026 machte die Meldung dies Runde, dass bei Anrufen im Mobilfunknetz Nutzerdaten (z.B. eindeutige Gerätekennungen (IMEI-Nummern)) an Dritte gelangen könnten. Das Thema ist u.a. in diesem Beitrag behandelt worden.

Eine neue cPanel-Sicherheitslücke (CVE-2026-87899) in CalDAV/CardDAV ermöglicht es jedem angemeldeten cPanel-Konto, Code als Root auszuführen und die vollständige Kontrolle über den Server zu erlangen. Eine zweite Sicherheitslücke (CVE-2026-87900) im WP Toolkit ermöglicht es authentifizierten Benutzern, Datenbanken anderer Konten zu ändern. The Hacker News hat das Thema in diesem Artikel aufgegriffen.

Stephan Berger schreibt in diesem Tweet , dass sie bei einem kürzlich bearbeiteten Sicherheitsvorfall auf VMkatz gestoßen seien. "VMkKatz extrahiert Windows-Geheimnisse – NTLM-Hashes, DPAPI-Hauptschlüssel, Kerberos-Tickets, zwischengespeicherte Domänenanmeldedaten, LSA-Geheimnisse, NTDS.dit, BitLocker-Schlüssel – direkt aus VM-Speichersnapshots und virtuellen Festplatten, auf dem NAS, dem Hypervisor, wo auch immer sich die VM-Dateien befinden."

Der Defender hat das Programm mit der folgenden Signatur erkannt: VirTool:Win64/Vekesz.A Die auf der GitHub-Seite verfügbare Standardversion wird ebenfalls vom Defender markiert.

Gehört wohl mitlerweile zur Tagesordnung. Es vergeht ja gefühlt kein Tag mehr, an dem nicht wenigstens eine Meldung zu einem Sicherheitsvorfall kommt. Also nichts gegen die Meldungen, das ist voll okay… Ich find es eben erschreckend, wie sich das in den letzten Jahren entwickelt hat.

Die in den Medien erscheinenden Meldungen sind nur die Spitze des Eisberges. Die meisten an die Öffentlichkeit gelangenden Sicherheitsvorfälle sind keine Meldung mehr Wert. Und dann gibt es ja noch die Vorfälle, die u.A. wg. Zahlung oder schlichter Verheimlichung oder Stumpfen Nichtbemerkens oder Geheimhaltung nie an die Öffentlickeit gelangt sind.

Was ich wirklich erschreckend finde ist der verhängte Digitalisieurngszwang bei allen möglichen problematischen Bereichen wie zB Rechnungen und Archivpflichten. Wer kein entsprechend sicheres Backup hätte würde dann zB bei einem Ransomware-Angriff damit erpresst werden, dass er keine gesetzlich zu archivierenden Daten mehr parat hat. (Gerade bei zB Mail-Archivierung können da schon in kleineren Unternehmen ob der Speicherfristen Unmengen an Daten auf jetzt sehr teurer Hardware zusammenkommen.) Da muss ich sagen: Wirtschaftlichen Erfolg gab es in Deutschland schon lange vor all diesen Auflagen; und irgendwie hat das Staatswesen auch überlebt. Cyberkriminalität wird es solange geben, wie es Datenverarbeitung gibt. Das andere Problem ist rein selbstgemacht.

Über den gleichen Hebel, z.B. Beschränkung oder Deaktivierung der digitalen Identität, die demnächst alternativlos für den Datenzugriff allerorts nötig ist, wird der Bürger dann auch vom Staat leicht beeinfluss- bzw. hart formuliert auch erpressbar, wenn er unbequeme Meinungen vertritt.

Klar, das chinesische „Vorbild" sollte schließlich auch unseren Politikern bekannt sein. – Einerseits streiten die sich herum, wie sie unser Rechtssystem wasserdicht kriegen für den Tag, an dem Extremisten an die Regierung kommen. Andererseits bauen sie eine Überwachungsmaschinerie auf, die geradezu nach Missbrauch schreit. Naive Blauäugigkeit oder gar eigene finstere Absichten? Bei manchen Nachrichten (siehe heute: Digitalisierung der Bonpflicht) weiß man wirklich nicht mehr, was man denken soll.

Und tut man in der Politik noch so, als würde man damit den Bürgern und der Wirtschaft einen Gefallen tun… Der angebliche Abbau von Bürokratie ist reine Verarsche. Auch die Umstellung auf digitale Bons erzeugt erst mal nur zusätzlichen Aufwand, gerade für kleinere Betriebe. Von der E-Rechnung wollen wir gar nicht erst anfangen…

Der Witz an den digitalen Bons ist, dass die so angepriesene Papiereinsparung einen winzigen Bruchteil von dem beträgt, was man durch eine Beendigung der Shrinkflation und sonstigen Verbrauchertäuschungen durch große Packungen an Papier und Plastik einsparen könnte. Schon an einer der riesigen Schinkenpackungen kann man durch Normalisierung der Größe mehr Material einsparen als für 20 Bons benötigt wird.

Man ermöglicht über die ausschliesslich digitalen Bons das Bürger Tracking auch für Bargeldzahlungen, solange es die noch gibt.

Die Schwachstellen bei Synology wurden schon im Juni 2026 gefixt.

evidence.title: Die Fresenius Medical Care-Aktie meldet einen Cyberangriff
evidence.text:
Die Fresenius Medical Care-Aktie (DE0005785802) notiert am 21.09.2026 zum Xetra-Schluss bei 38,53 EUR und damit 19,5 Prozent unter dem 52-Wochen-Hoch von 46,05 EUR. Der wichtigste Unternehmensanlass am 23.09.2026 ist ein Cyberangriff auf eine begrenzte Zahl interner Systeme, über den Tagesschau am 23.09.2026 berichtet.

Nach Angaben der Tagesschau verschafften sich unbefugte Personen Zugang zu mehreren internen Systemen. Medizinische Geräte, Patientenversorgung, Produktion und laufender Geschäftsbetrieb seien am 23.09.2026 nicht beeinträchtigt gewesen.

Der Vorfall ist für Anleger deshalb relevant, weil mögliche Folgekosten und Auswirkungen auf Abläufe erst mit weiteren Untersuchungen quantifiziert werden können. Die MarketScreener veröffentlichte am 23.09.2026 die Stellungnahme von Fresenius Medical Care zum Cybersicherheitsvorfall.

Operativ liefert Fresenius Medical Care zugleich ein belastbares Zahlenbild. Im ersten Halbjahr 2026 erhöhte sich der Umsatz laut Investing.com um 7,3 Prozent auf 11,8 Mrd. EUR. Das EBIT stieg im selben Halbjahr um 9,8 Prozent auf 1,34 Mrd. EUR; die EBIT-Marge lag bei 11,4 Prozent.

Der Vergleich zeigt den Schwerpunkt der Entwicklung: Das Nettoergebnis je Aktionär nahm im ersten Halbjahr 2026 um 12,8 Prozent auf 530 Mio. EUR zu. Für das zweite Quartal 2026 wird zudem ein bereinigtes operatives Ergebnis genannt, das 23 Prozent über dem Vorjahreswert lag; bereinigt um TDAPA-Effekte betrug der Anstieg 34 Prozent.

Am 21.09.2026 schloss die FMC-Aktie auf Xetra bei 38,53 EUR, nach 38,84 EUR am Vortag. Der Rückgang um 0,8 Prozent entsprach einem Minus von 0,31 EUR; der DAX gewann in derselben Sitzung 1,1 Prozent und lag bei 25.575 Punkten.

Der Abstand zum 52-Wochen-Hoch von 46,05 EUR beträgt 16,3 Prozent. Für Anleger stehen damit zwei gegensätzliche Signale nebeneinander: ein Halbjahresumsatz von 11,8 Mrd. EUR mit 7,3 Prozent Wachstum und ein Cyberrisiko, dessen finanzielle Folgen noch in den kommenden Berichtsperioden sichtbar werden können.

Die Fresenius Medical Care-Aktie schloss am 21.09.2026 auf Xetra bei 38,53 EUR und lag damit 0,8 Prozent unter dem Vortagesschluss von 38,84 EUR.

Fresenius Kabi inaugurates its new production line, a 28 million investment

The aim is to increase production capacity for plastic bottles used in infusion therapies and to ensure a steady supply

For feedback, please contact english@ilsole24ore.com

An investment of over 28 million euros, forming part of a wider three-year investment plan in Italia totalling 100 million euros, aimed at increasing production capacity for plastic bottles used in infusion therapies.

Fresenius Kabi has inaugurated a new production line at its plant in Isola della Scala, Verona – one of Europe’s leading centres for the production of infusion solutions – in the presence of Adolfo Urso, Minister for Made in Italy.

Every day, in Italian and European hospitals, millions of patients receive infusion therapy: this is used to administer life-saving medicines, provide hydration, ensure clinical nutrition or support surgical procedures and intensive care. To ensure continuity of care, it is essential to invest in the facilities where these infusion therapies are produced, so as to ensure a reliable supply even during periods of heightened international instability.

The site currently helps to meet around 40 per cent of the national hospital demand for infusion solutions, and in this respect represents a strategic piece of infrastructure for the Italian healthcare system.

There are five production plants and two R&D centres operating in Italia, reflecting the group’s strong presence in the country, with its German parent company.

The development of the Isola della Scala plant forms part of Fresenius’s ‘local for local’ strategy, which aims to manufacture medicines in the same geographical areas where they are used, thereby reducing reliance on supplies from third countries and increasing the resilience of supply chains.

The expansion of production capacity at the Veronese Scala site will be accompanied by a wider programme of technological innovation at the site, underlining the company’s commitment to industrial development, the enhancement of professional skills and the creation of jobs in the local area.

Industrial investment strengthens Italia’s and Europe’s ability to ensure the availability of critical medicines, reducing the vulnerability of supply chains and contributing to the continent’s health security.

Fresenius Kabi offers a wide range of medicines, medical technologies, nutritional solutions and active pharmaceutical ingredients, supporting healthcare professionals and patients across the country. With five manufacturing sites, a distribution centre and two research and development centres, Italia serves as a strategic hub for the company’s European operations in the Pharma, MedTech and API sectors.

Over 90 per cent of Fresenius Kabi’s products sold in Europe are manufactured on the continent. The company’s Italian sites include plants dedicated to the production of antibiotics, active pharmaceutical ingredients, infusion solutions and medical devices for blood treatment. In Italia, the workforce numbers around 1,400 employees; o over 90 per cent of Fresenius Kabi’s products sold in Europe are manufactured on the continent.

“ The project also represents a concrete sign of confidence in the Italian manufacturing sector and in the role our country can play in European pharmaceutical manufacturing,” says Marco Pianta, Country General Manager at Fresenius Kabi – “At a time when the availability of critical medicines has become a permanent fixture on the agenda of European institutions, investing in production capacity means investing in patient safety. At a time when much pharmaceutical production has gradually shifted outside Europe, we continue to invest in local manufacturing capacity, thereby strengthening Italia’s contribution to European healthcare security.”

evidence.title: Fresenius Medical Care Refines China Commercial Strategy with a Focus on Long-Term Growth and Market Leadership
evidence.text:
BAD HOMBURG, Germany , Sept. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fresenius Medical Care (FME), the world's leading provider of products and services for individuals with renal diseases, today announced refinements to its China commercial strategy to support long-term growth and strengthen its market position through a more localized portfolio, increased commercialization of locally relevant innovation and a focused go-to-market approach.

Fresenius Medical Care has operated in China for more than two decades. The market represents approximately 6-7% of the Company's Care Enablement operating segment revenues and offers long-term growth opportunities supported by rising prevalence of chronic kidney disease, continued expansion of dialysis care and increasing demand for advanced treatment technologies.

"China is an important market for our Care Enablement business," said Helen Giza, Chief Executive Officer for Fresenius Medical Care. "As the market evolves, we are refining our portfolio to focus on the areas where we can create the greatest value for patients and customers."

As part of these actions, Fresenius Medical Care strengthened local leadership, including the appointment of market General Manager Rex Liu. The Company will increasingly focus on innovative technologies for in-center dialysis and critical care, including the high-volume hemodiafiltration-enabled 5008S CAREsystem, multiFiltratePRO, and other advanced dialysis products. As part of the portfolio focus, the Company will both discontinue production and sales of the 4008A hemodialysis system locally and exit its China peritoneal dialysis (PD) business while maintaining existing obligations in the market.

"We are confident that this is the right portfolio and strategy that will best position us to compete and grow in China," said Joe Turk, Chief Executive Officer for Fresenius Medical Care's Care Enablement operating segment. "We remain committed to the market and will continue leveraging our local manufacturing footprint and China Design Center to support profitable growth."

The portfolio optimization actions related to the PD business and discontinuation of the 4008A platform are expected to result in one-time costs of approximately €110 million primarily attributable to impairment charges, scrappage and termination costs. The charge will be treated as a special item and is expected to be recognized in the third quarter of 2026. The portfolio adjustment is not expected to impact the future revenue outlook for Care Enablement's China business in a meaningful way.

Fresenius Medical Care is the world's leading provider of products and services for individuals with renal diseases of which around 4.5 million patients worldwide regularly undergo dialysis treatment. Through its network of 3,513 dialysis clinics, Fresenius Medical Care provides dialysis treatments for approx. 290,000 patients around the globe. Fresenius Medical Care is also the leading provider of dialysis products such as dialysis machines or dialyzers. Fresenius Medical Care is listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (FME) and on the New York Stock Exchange (FMS).

Fresenius Medical Care Refines China Commercial Strategy with Localized Portfolio Focus and €110 Million Q3 Special Item

(IN BRIEF) Fresenius Medical Care has refined its China commercial strategy to concentrate on locally relevant innovation, advanced in-center dialysis and critical care technologies while withdrawing from selected product areas. China represents approximately 6% to 7% of Care Enablement revenues, and the company continues to view the market as offering long-term growth potential. FME will focus more heavily on products including the 5008S CAREsystem and multiFiltratePRO, while discontinuing local production and sales of the 4008A hemodialysis system and exiting its China peritoneal dialysis business. Existing market obligations will continue to be fulfilled. The company has also strengthened local leadership, including appointing Rex Liu as Market General Manager. The portfolio changes are expected to generate approximately €110 million of one-time costs in Q3 2026, mainly from impairments, scrappage and termination expenses, which will be treated as a special item. (PRESS RELEASE) BAD HOMBURG, 25-Sep-2026 — / EuropaWire / — Fresenius Medical Care (FME) has announced changes to its commercial strategy in China aimed at supporting long-term growth, sharpening its market positioning and increasing the focus on locally relevant products and innovation.

The company said the refinements will concentrate its China activities on selected technologies for in-center dialysis and critical care while adjusting parts of its existing product portfolio and go-to-market model.

Fresenius Medical Care has operated in China for more than two decades. The market currently accounts for approximately 6% to 7% of revenues in the company’s Care Enablement operating segment.

FME said it continues to see longer-term growth potential in the country, supported by increasing prevalence of chronic kidney disease, expansion of dialysis care and growing demand for more advanced treatment technologies.

Helen Giza, Chief Executive Officer of Fresenius Medical Care , said China remains an important market for the Care Enablement business.

She said the company is refining its portfolio as market conditions evolve, concentrating resources on areas where Fresenius Medical Care believes it can generate the greatest value for patients and customers.

As part of the revised strategy, the company has strengthened its local management structure, including the appointment of Rex Liu as Market General Manager.

Fresenius Medical Care plans to increase its emphasis on advanced technologies for in-center dialysis and critical care.

Products identified as important to the strategy include the 5008S CAREsystem, which supports high-volume hemodiafiltration, and multiFiltratePRO, alongside other advanced dialysis technologies.

At the same time, the company will discontinue the local production and sale of its 4008A hemodialysis system.

Fresenius Medical Care will also exit its peritoneal dialysis business in China, while continuing to fulfil its existing obligations in the market.

The portfolio decisions form part of a broader effort to align FME’s offering more closely with market demand and locally relevant innovation while maintaining the company’s manufacturing and product-development capabilities in China.

Joe Turk, Chief Executive Officer of Fresenius Medical Care’s Care Enablement operating segment , said the revised portfolio and commercial approach are intended to strengthen the company’s ability to compete and grow in the Chinese market.

He said Fresenius Medical Care remains committed to China and will continue to use its local manufacturing footprint and China Design Center to support profitable growth.

The portfolio optimisation associated with the withdrawal from the peritoneal dialysis business and discontinuation of the 4008A platform is expected to result in approximately €110 million in one-time costs.

According to Fresenius Medical Care, these costs will primarily consist of impairment charges, scrappage and termination costs.

The company expects to recognise the charge in the third quarter of 2026 and will classify it as a special item.

Despite the portfolio changes, Fresenius Medical Care said the adjustment is not expected to have a meaningful impact on the future revenue outlook for its Care Enablement business in China.

The revised strategy therefore combines a narrower product focus with continued investment in locally relevant technology, manufacturing capabilities and commercial execution.

FME said the changes are intended to position the business for sustainable long-term development while directing resources toward product categories and technologies it considers better aligned with the evolving Chinese renal care market.

evidence.title: Fresenius Medical Care untersucht Cybervorfall: Keine Auswirkungen auf Patientenversorgung gemeldet
evidence.text:
Der Dialysekonzern meldete den Vorfall am 23. September 2026. Betroffen ist nach bisherigen Informationen eine begrenzte Zahl interner Systeme. Das Unternehmen erklärte, dass weder Medizinprodukte noch Patientenversorgung, Produktion oder der laufende Betrieb beeinträchtigt seien.

Fresenius Medical Care ergreift Gegenmaßnahmen und untersucht den Vorfall gemeinsam mit externen Cybersicherheitsexperten. Auch zuständige Behörden sind eingebunden. Wie der Zugriff gelang, welche Systeme konkret betroffen sind und ob Daten entwendet wurden, ist bislang nicht bekannt. Angaben zu möglichen Schäden machte das Unternehmen ebenfalls nicht.

Dies deutet zunächst auf einen Vorfall hin, dessen Auswirkungen auf den operativen Betrieb nach Unternehmensangaben begrenzt sind. Für Anleger bleibt die Informationslücke zu möglichen Datenabflüssen und Folgekosten jedoch ein Unsicherheitsfaktor. Entscheidend für die weitere Einschätzung sind der Umfang der betroffenen Systeme und ob sich die bisherige Einschätzung zur Patientenversorgung und zum laufenden Betrieb bestätigt.

Im Mittelpunkt stehen nun die Ergebnisse der laufenden Untersuchung und mögliche weitere Angaben zu betroffenen Systemen, Daten und finanziellen Folgen. Bis dahin lässt sich das Ausmaß des Cybervorfalls nicht abschließend beurteilen.

Diese Inhalte wurden ganz oder teilweise automatisiert unter Einsatz künstlicher Intelligenz erstellt und können Fehler, Ungenauigkeiten oder unvollständige Informationen enthalten. Trotz sorgfältiger Prüfung übernehmen wir keine Gewähr für die Richtigkeit, Vollständigkeit und Aktualität der bereitgestellten Informationen.

Die Inhalte dienen ausschließlich Informationszwecken und stellen weder eine Anlageberatung noch eine Empfehlung oder Aufforderung zum Kauf oder Verkauf von Finanzinstrumenten dar. Sie ersetzen keine individuelle, fachkundige Beratung.

Eine Haftung für Vermögensschäden oder sonstige Schäden, die aus der Nutzung der Inhalte entstehen, ist – soweit gesetzlich zulässig – ausgeschlossen.

evidence.title: Sartorius and NIBRT partner to establish world’s first continuous bioprocessing training center
evidence.text:
Please contact clientservices@accessintel.com or call 1-888-707-5814 if you are unable to login.

Sartorius and NIBRT partner to establish world’s first continuous bioprocessing training center

Sartorius AG (Göttingen, Germany) and the National Institute for Bioprocessing Research and Training (NIBRT) (Dublin, Ireland) are partnering to establish the world’s most comprehensive training center for intensified and fully continuous bioprocessing in Dublin, Ireland. Starting in the fourth quarter of 2026, the center will serve as a hub for practical training and knowledge sharing to help the biopharmaceutical industry adopt intensified, digitalized and continuous manufacturing processes.

As part of the collaboration, Sartorius will equip NIBRT with its state-of-the-art Pionic technology — an end-to-end modular cGMP platform for integrated continuous bioprocessing with advanced analytics and digital tools. Through the collaboration, the new facility is expected to provide more than 1,000 scientists, engineers and students each year with hands-on experience in intensified upstream and downstream processes designed for efficiency, flexibility and sustainability.

“As biopharma manufacturing undergoes a major shift from batch processes toward more efficient, continuous processes, Sartorius is once again at the forefront of this transformation. While technological innovation is the first step, training current and future engineers and operators is critical to making the change a reality,” said René Fáber, Head of the Bioprocess Solutions Division and Member of the Executive Board at Sartorius. “Our partnership with NIBRT underscores Sartorius’ commitment to building global capabilities and accelerating the adoption of innovative and sustainable bioprocessing technologies.”

“This collaboration marks a significant step in advancing workforce training and supporting the transition toward intensified and connected manufacturing,” said Darrin Morrissey, CEO of NIBRT. “By integrating the Pionic platform into our training facility, we will give biopharma professionals the chance to gain first-hand experience with cutting-edge technologies that drive process efficiency and performance.”

The Process Intensification Training Center will become a key element of NIBRT’s global training and education network, serving industry professionals and academic partners in Ireland, Europe and worldwide. Beyond training, the center will also enable collaborative research and pilot-scale demonstrations , strengthening the global biomanufacturing ecosystem.

evidence.title: Sartorius stedim biotech, Siemens sign pact in the area of automation
evidence.text:
The Siemens technology group and Sartorius Stedim Biotech (SSB), a leading international supplier for the biopharmaceutical industry, have agreed on long-term cooperation in the area of automation.

This agreement provides that Sartorius Stedim Biotech will preferably use Siemens automation technologies, which will include industrial PCs, the S7-1500 software controller, the TIA Portal and the SCADA system Simatic WinCC, among others.

These hardware and software components will be employed in many products and solutions that SSB offers its customers for the development and manufacture of biopharmaceuticals, such as vaccines and monoclonal antibodies.

Sartorius Stedim Biotech has already been using established Siemens automation solutions for process control in its large-scale bioreactor and filtration systems for quite some time.

To standardize its own product portfolio even further, SSB has decided to introduce a new, configurable automation system for its range of systems.

Under the agreement recently concluded, cooperation between the two companies will therefore be extended to further Sartorius Stedim Biotech products. These will be successively equipped with Siemens automated solutions in the coming months and can thus be integrated into process control systems, such as Simatic PCS 7 and Simatic Batch.

Essentially, such SSB products are single-use bioreactors of the BIOSTAT® STR series, various filtration systems and the FlexAct® system. The latter is a flexible module that is used to control many different process steps within biopharmaceutical production.

During this year’s ACHEMA trade show that will be taking place from June 11 to June 15, 2018, in Frankfurt, Germany, Siemens and Sartorius Stedim Biotech will be jointly presenting the FlexAct module, a first product based on the new automation platform.

evidence.title: B. Braun VetCare ofrece una formación gratuita sobre prevención de infecciones y manejo del catéter intravenoso
evidence.text:
B. Braun VetCare ofrece una formación gratuita sobre prevención de infecciones y manejo del catéter intravenoso

B. Braun VetCare ha organizado una nueva formación gratuita sobre prevención de infecciones y manejo del catéter intravenoso , dirigida especialmente a los profesionales que trabajan con pacientes hospitalizados.

El curso se desarrollará entre el 28 de septiembre y el 1 de octubre y estará impartido por Aina Claret , veterinaria diplomada por el Colegio Americano de Emergencias y Cuidados Críticos Veterinarios (ACVECC).

La propuesta formativa utilizará tres casos de pacientes hospitalizados para abordar de forma práctica el manejo del catéter intravenoso y finalizará con una sesión en directo.

La prevención de infecciones asociadas al catéter, en el centro de la formación

La compañía enmarca esta formación en la importancia que puede tener el manejo de los catéteres periféricos dentro de las estrategias de prevención de infecciones y uso responsable de antimicrobianos en los hospitales veterinarios.

B. Braun VetCare destaca, en este sentido, los resultados de investigaciones realizadas en perros y gatos hospitalizados. Uno de los trabajos citados por la compañía encontró que el 45 % de los aislados procedentes de catéteres periféricos que presentaron flebitis y complicaciones mecánicas eran multirresistentes , definidos como resistentes a tres o más clases de antimicrobianos.

La compañía pone el foco así en que la prevención de las infecciones asociadas al catéter no depende únicamente de cómo se responde cuando aparece una complicación, sino también de actuaciones cotidianas como la preparación de la piel, la higiene de manos y el número de manipulaciones y accesos a la línea .

Otro de los estudios destacados por B. Braun VetCare fue realizado sobre 182 perros en España. En este caso, Acinetobacter spp. fue el microorganismo aislado con mayor frecuencia, con un 21,7 % , y los autores lo señalaron como un patógeno emergente relacionado con la colonización de catéteres.

Estos resultados refuerzan, según plantea la compañía, la necesidad de contemplar el manejo del catéter dentro de las políticas de prevención de infecciones y de uso responsable de antimicrobianos en los centros veterinarios.

La formación pretende trasladar estos aspectos a la práctica clínica mediante tres casos de pacientes hospitalizados , que servirán para trabajar las diferentes cuestiones relacionadas con el manejo del catéter intravenoso.

El programa está especialmente orientado a profesionales que participan directamente en la hospitalización y el manejo diario de estos dispositivos, incluidos veterinarios con menor experiencia y auxiliares técnicos veterinarios.

La formación se desarrollará gratuitamente del 28 de septiembre al 1 de octubre y culminará con una sesión en directo impartida por Aina Claret.

B. Braun VetCare mantiene abierto el registro para los profesionales veterinarios interesados en participar en esta nueva actividad formativa.

evidence.title: Ostravské dialyzační středisko B. Braun Avitum se stěhuje do Senatoria. Nabídne více míst
evidence.text:
Ostravské dialyzační středisko B. Braun Avitum se stěhuje do Senatoria. Nabídne více míst

Dialyzační středisko B. Braun Avitum v Ostravě se po 25 letech stěhuje ze stávajícího pracoviště v areálu Nemocnice AGEL Ostrava – Vítkovice do nových prostor v kompletně zrekonstruovaném Senatoriu Ostrava. Pro pacienty to znamená více dialyzačních míst, komfortnější prostředí pro pravidelnou několikahodinovou léčbu, lepší parkování i širší nabídku ambulantní péče včetně hojení ran a stomické poradny.

Nové umístění zároveň otevírá cestu k dalšímu rozvoji domácí dialýzy v zařízeních dlouhodobé péče, která může vhodným pacientům výrazně snížit zátěž spojenou s dojížděním. Návaznost na nemocniční péči zůstane zachována díky spolupráci s Nemocnicí AGEL Ostrava – Vítkovice. Provoz na nové adrese je plánován od poloviny listopadu.

Nové pracoviště vzniklo v přízemí zrekonstruované budovy Senatoria Ostrava na Pavlovově ulici v Ostravě-Zábřehu. Umístění v areálu zařízení dlouhodobé lůžkové péče zároveň otevře možnosti pro užší spolupráci při léčbě pacientů s onemocněním ledvin, včetně širšího rozvoje domácích metod dialýzy. „Po čtvrtstoletí v areálu dnešní Nemocnice AGEL Ostrava – Vítkovice, dříve známé jako Vítkovická nemocnice, se pro naše ostravské pracoviště otevírá nová etapa. Nové středisko nabídne pacientům výrazně modernější a komfortnější prostředí, větší kapacitu a kvalitní zázemí pro dlouhodobý rozvoj dialyzační i ambulantní péče v regionu. Blízkost Senatoria nám navíc umožní dál rozvíjet péči přímo tam, kde ji pacienti potřebují,“ říká MUDr. Martin Kuncek, jednatel B. Braun Avitum.

Nové pracoviště bude také šetrnější k životnímu prostředí. Součástí jeho vybavení je systém ECOMix Revolution, který připravuje koncentráty pro dialyzační roztoky přímo na středisku. Omezuje se tak přeprava objemných tekutých koncentrátů a díky opakovaně použitelným zásobníkům snižuje množství plastového odpadu. „Modernizace dialyzačního střediska pro nás není jen otázkou nových prostor a přístrojů, ale také lepších podmínek pro zdravotnický tým. Technologie, jako je ECOMix Revolution, pomáhají zefektivnit provoz, snižují ekologickou zátěž a zároveň ulevují personálu od části fyzicky náročné manipulace s těžkými kanystry. Právě takové změny jsou důležité, pokud chceme dlouhodobě udržet kvalitní péči i dobré pracovní zázemí,“ zdůrazňuje Ing. Petr Macoun, Ph.D., jednatel B. Braun Avitum.

19 dialyzačních míst a dva izolační boxy

Kapacita dialyzačního střediska se zvýší z dosavadních 15 na 19 dialyzačních míst. Součástí nového pracoviště budou také dva samostatné izolační boxy, každý se dvěma lůžky. Větší kapacita umožní ošetřit více pacientů v jedné směně a vytvoří prostor pro další rozvoj péče. Nový dialyzační sál je navržen tak, aby personálu poskytoval lepší přehled o pacientech a umožnil efektivnější organizaci provozu. Otevřenou dispozici doplňuje pracovní zázemí pro sestry a lékaře. Středisko je kompletně vybaveno dialyzačními přístroji B. Braun nejnovější generace. „Nové dialyzační středisko v Senatoriu bude výrazně větší, vzdušnější a lépe uspořádané. Díky otevřené dispozici sálu budeme mít lepší přehled o pacientech. Dva izolační boxy nám zároveň umožní odděleně pečovat o pacienty, jejichž zdravotní stav takový režim vyžaduje,“ vysvětluje MUDr. Iveta Skácelíková, primářka Dialyzačního střediska B. Braun Avitum v Ostravě.

Více pohodlí během několikahodinové léčby

Výraznou změnu pocítí pacienti také v komfortu. Každé dialyzační místo je vybaveno vlastní televizí se sluchátky. Nové prostory nabídnou moderní klimatizaci a ventilaci, možnost regulovat intenzitu osvětlení i prostornější a modernější pacientské zázemí. „Pacienti k nám zpravidla docházejí třikrát týdně a na středisku tráví několik hodin. Záleží proto i na tom, zda je jim příjemně, mohou si odpočinout nebo sledovat vlastní televizní program, aniž by rušili ostatní. Nové vybavení a možnost upravovat osvětlení i teplotu jim pomohou čas strávený léčbou lépe zvládat,“ popisuje výhody primářka Iveta Skácelíková. Zlepší se také možnosti parkování. Pro dialyzované pacienty budou u nového pracoviště vyhrazena parkovací místa, kde budou moci parkovat zdarma.

B. Braun Announces Approval and Commercialization of First Generic Sugammadex Injection in the U.S. Market

BETHLEHEM, Pa. , July 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- B. Braun Medical Inc. (B. Braun), a recognized leader in smart infusion therapy and pharmaceutical manufacturing, announced the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval of Sugammadex Injection, 200 mg/2 mL (100 mg/mL), AP-rated generic BRIDION ®1 * (Sugammadex Injection) in the U.S. market. The product, which will be available July 28, 2026 in a single-dose vial with a 24-month shelf life, represents B. Braun's first launch of a generic pharmaceutical vial in the U.S. market.

Sugammadex is indicated for the reversal of neuromuscular blockade induced by rocuronium bromide. In clinical studies, Sugammadex Injection demonstrated faster recovery compared to neostigmine and was associated with fewer adverse events in clinical studies. 2

"With the launch of Sugammadex Injection, B. Braun is continuing to expand our portfolio of essential injectable medications used in acute care settings," said Jeremy Greene, Senior Director, Pharma Marketing. "This AP-rated generic option provides healthcare systems with an affordable solution and reliable supply of a critical anesthesia reversal agent. The addition helps us continue supporting hospitals and providers in delivering patient care."

B. Braun Medical Inc. (B. Braun) is a leader in smart infusion therapy and safe and effective pharmacy products, patient and provider safety, and sustainable health solutions. evidence.title: From science to safety, GALAPAGOS CELEBRATES THREE TSUNAMI READY DESIGNATIONS BY IOC of UNESCO
evidence.text:
From science to safety, GALAPAGOS CELEBRATES THREE TSUNAMI READY DESIGNATIONS BY IOC of UNESCO

Puerto Ayora, Galápagos, September 8, 2026. – Puerto Baquerizo Moreno, Puerto Ayora, and Puerto Villamil celebrated their “Tsunami Ready” recognition by the Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission (IOC) of UNESCO during a ceremony held in Puerto Ayora on September 8, 2026, bringing together international, national and local authorities, scientific and technical institutions, authorities of the Navy, and representatives of the archipelago’s communities.

The ceremony celebrated a process of recognition that began with San Cristóbal in 2024, when Puerto Baquerizo Moreno became the first “Tsunami Ready” community in South America, followed by Puerto Ayora and Puerto Villamil in 2025. Such recognitions highlight the commitment and progress made by communities on the islands of San Cristóbal, Santa Cruz, and Isabela in risk assessment, preparedness, and response capacity regarding tsunamis. Thus, the Galápagos improves its position as a model of cooperation among science, institutions, and communities for risk reduction and the protection of life.

IOC and the International Tsunami Information Center (ITIC), in coordination with national and local institutions, joined efforts ten years ago to achieve these recognitions. Over the years, training sessions, experiences and best practice exchanges, field exercises, and drills with communities were conducted, along with initiatives to consolidate research, observation, and information sharing. This work made it possible to articulate institutional capacities from the Governing Council of the Galápagos Special Regime, INOCAR, the National Secretariat for Risk Management, the Galápagos National Park, and the local governments of San Cristóbal, Santa Cruz, and Isabela, besides other stakeholders in the risk management system.

The ceremony was attended by the National Secretary for Risk Management, Minister Carolina Lozano; the President of the Governing Council of the Special Regime of the Province of the Galápagos, Felipe Haro Cáceres, represented by the Council’s technical secretary, Pablo Falconi; Christa von Hillebrandt-Andrade of NOAA’s International Tsunami Information Center (ITIC); Commander Juan Carlos Tapia, Executive Director of the Navy’s Oceanographic and Antarctic Institute (INOCAR); Sandro Vaca, Acting Director of the Geophysical Institute at the National Polytechnic School; Tatiana Villegas, UNESCO Country Representative, as well as representatives from the National Navy, local governments, community committees, and other institutions that are part of the National Decentralized Risk Management System.

Minister Carolina Lozano, National Secretary for Risk Management, underlined the substantive value of the Tsunami Ready Recognition Programme (TRRP): “connecting science and warning systems with the capacities of communities, and translating knowledge about the ocean into effective measures for the safety and well-being of societies. Risk assessment, community preparedness, institutional coordination, and response capacity supported the integrated perspective of this process at Puerto Baquerizo Moreno, Puerto Ayora, and Puerto Villamil.

During the ceremony, the UNESCO Director and Country Representative in Ecuador emphasized that this recognition goes beyond the certificate, above all, it is the result of a sustained process of work, coordination, and commitment for protecting people. “We need science, observation systems, timely information, and effective warning mechanisms (…) We are not able to stop a tsunami, but we can invest in science and monitoring, in institutional strengthening, and, in particular, in preparing communities to act” she said.

Christa von Hillebrandt-Andrade from NOAA’s International Tsunami Information Center, recalled that the December 26, 2004, Indian Ocean tsunami, which caused more than 227,000 fatalities across 14 countries, taught us a painful lesson: “Uncommon hazard does not eliminate the risk, and tsunamis are not aware of borders”. She observed that, from the profound grief caused by that disaster, a global mission was born: “Transforming vulnerability into preparedness, a mission facilitated today by the TRRP”.

The mayor of Santa Cruz, Ms. Fanny Uribe shared this affirmation with the audience: “Complying with international standards, having clear rules, gathering points and evacuation trails, especially in an area of high seismic, and volcanic activity are examples of human resilience.

Patricio Andrade, fifth-generation migrant and community leader, expressed great appreciation and support from the people of the islands to the TRRP for its statement endorsing well-being and safety of the population. This appreciation from the communities reinforces one of the programme’s core principles: tsunami preparedness must be a people-centered effort. In the Galápagos, protecting communities also entails protecting the infrastructure, livelihoods, and conditions that make it possible to preserve one of the planet’s most valuable ecosystems.

The plan to extend the “Tsunami Ready” to Floreana Island was also announced during the event. “We need to certify Floreana to be 100% Tsunami Ready in Galapagos” expressed Ing. Pablo Falconi, Technical Secretary of the Governing Council of the Special Regime of the Province of the Galápagos. This would make a significant milestone for the archipelago and demonstrate a comprehensive commitment to the safety and preparedness of its communities. In Ecuador, the three recognized localities are currently part of the “Tsunami Ready” communities registered under TRRP. The UNESCO-IOC Tsunami Ready Recognition Programme is an international, community-based initiative designed to strengthen resilience to tsunamis through greater risk awareness, preparedness and capacity through 12 indicators. Recognition is renewable every four years, encouraging communities to maintain these preparedness measures over time.

The “Tsunami Ready” designation also contributes to the objectives of the United Nations Decade of Ocean Science for Sustainable Development . To date, there are 124 TR recognized communities as per Tsunami Viewer .

It also promotes the Ocean Decade Tsunami Programme , as well as the United Nations initiative “ Early Warnings for All ,” aimed at ensuring that the most exposed and vulnerable people have access to effective, people-centered early warning systems.

evidence.title: Galapagos Tortoise Rings in 'Milestone' 60th Birthday With Favorite Foods
evidence.text:
Keepers at Perth Zoo celebrated one of its oldest residents' 60th birthday with a feast of his favorite foods, footage shared on September 19 shows.

Galapagos tortoise Cerro, who has lived at Perth Zoo since 2005 and "remains a firm favorite among visitors," enjoyed prickly pear, hibiscus flowers, carrots, celery, rockmelon, and lots of love from staff on his special day.

"Keeper Liam went all out […] The birthday boy wasted no time digging in!" the zoo said on X.

"Cerro's milestone is a testament to the dedication and expertise of Perth Zoo's animal care team and highlights the important role zoos play in global conservation," the zoo said in a press release. "Over his shell-tastic six decades, the gentle giant has inspired thousands of visitors as an ambassador for his wild counterparts, and Perth Zoo hopes he will continue delighting guests for many years to come."

Perth Zoo said Cerro is "still relatively young for a Galapagos tortoise," a species among the longest-living animals on Earth, with an average lifespan of more than 100 years.

Galapagos tortoises are considered endangered, with fewer than 20,000 living on the Galapagos archipelago, according to Perth Zoo. Credit: Perth Zoo via Storyful

evidence.title: These 'alien tortoises' are back on a Galapagos island where they had been extinct since the 19th century
evidence.text:
Link: https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9._g.pKhUMkRnoOZwX4iq2fhLAqba5Rz0jb3mINKRqASmxf0/world/1410258%2Fthese-alien-tortoises-are-back-on-a-galapagos-island-where-they-had-been-extinct-since-the-19th-century

These 'alien tortoises' are back on a Galapagos island where they had been extinct since the 19th century

The story of the giant tortoises of the Galapagos is a story of pirates. Starting in the 16th century, these sailors began arriving at the islands, followed later by whalers, together sealing the destiny of the hundreds of thousands of specimens that inhabited the archipelago.

The resilience of the giant tortoises, which, according to experts, arrived in the Galapagos from South America 2 to 3 million years ago, became their greatest disadvantage: since they could survive for up to a year without food or water, they were captured by sailors, knowing they would endure in the holds of their ships.

"And when these people wanted to eat, the tortoises were simply there, ready to go, and they had fresh meat," Jorge Carrión, conservation director at the Galapagos Conservancy, an organisation that has been working to preserve the archipelago since 1985, told CNN.

In just two centuries, between 100,000 and 200,000 tortoises disappeared from those almost mythical islands that Charles Darwin visited in 1835 aboard the HMS Beagle on a voyage that would become key to his theory of evolution.

The giant tortoises of the Galápagos are not a single species; each island has its own species of tortoise that, over time, adapted to its environment. Several of these became completely extinct because whalers stopping in the archipelago caught them for food and introduced other threats, such as invasive species.

The first to go extinct, around 1850, was the Floreana tortoise, named after the island where it lived.

"They were very unusual tortoises, with a really pronounced shape - what we call a 'saddle' shape - that isn't found anywhere else on the planet," said James Gibbs, vice president of Science and Conservation at the Galapagos Conservancy and a professor at the State University of New York.

Infant tortoises born at the Fausto Llerena Land Tortoise Breeding Center.

During a 2000 expedition to Wolf Volcano, the highest point in the Galápagos Islands, located on the northern tip of Isabela Island, researchers led by Gibbs found tortoises with a shell shape unusual for the area.

"There were thousands of native species there... but it quickly became clear that there were also some strange tortoises," recalled Gibbs, whose connection to the Galápagos Islands goes back decades: he arrived as a volunteer when he was just a university student, and the islands, he says, transformed him, leading him to dedicate his life to their conservation.

On subsequent expeditions, they again encountered many of these "highly sculpted, saddle-shaped" tortoises living together in narrow canyons. "We called them aliens because we didn't know what they were," he remembers. They took blood samples and sent them to geneticists at Yale University, who confirmed that there were differences compared to the known species on that island and used the same term: aliens. Four years later, further genetic studies confirmed that they were from the Floreana lineage.

But how was it possible that they had become extinct on one island and reappeared 150 years later on a volcano at the other end of the archipelago? There are two hypotheses, said Carrión. One is a natural process: when there is heavy rain, flash floods sweep away everything in their path, which could have transported the tortoises between islands. But scientists believe that humans were most likely responsible.

"Remember that pirates and whalers used to come to the Galápagos and take dozens or hundreds of tortoises on their ships. One possibility is that an accident occurred near Wolf Volcano," he explains. The other is purely logistical: Isabela Island, due to its location, was the last checkpoint for ships before they ventured into the Pacific. There, they checked the weight of the tortoises and if the ship was over its weight limit, they would discard some, which, fortunately for the future, may have ended up on an unexpected island.

A giant tortoise, a species that once numbered in their hundreds of thousands on the Galapagos Islands.

The Fausto Llerena Land Tortoise Breeding Center has been working since 1965 to protect these giant reptiles. They have already successfully bred, raised and released species from the islands of Española and Santa Fe, among others. Nineteen specimens of the Floreana lineage were transferred there after their discovery on Wolf Volcano, for care and reproduction.

Freddy Villalba, from the Galapagos National Park Directorate, has been a park ranger for 23 years and manages this breeding center.

They work with adult tortoises and eggs laid in captivity, as in the case of those from Floreana, or collected from the wild. They mark, weigh and place the eggs in incubators at different temperatures. At this stage, the turtles' sex is still undetermined: it will be determined by the temperature at which the eggs develop, said Villalba. In incubators programmed to 29.5C, female turtles will develop, and in those at 28C, it will be males.

After four months of incubation, the eggs hatch and the staff transfers the newborn turtles to dark, humidity-controlled boxes where they will remain for a month, feeding exclusively on their yolk sac, replicating the process they would undergo in the wild.

Thirty days later, they emerge into enclosures where they feed on chopped leaves called "elephant ears," their diet for the first two years. During this initial stage, they must be "very carefully protected," said Villalba, because they measure eight to nine centimetres and are easy prey for predators.

In February 2026, 158 baby tortoises were released on Floreana Island with satellite tracking devices so scientists could study how they respond to their habitat, and how the habitat responds to them. With resources from NASA, specialists identified the best areas for their release, where they could later nest.

The release of giant tortoises back to Floreana island has helped the species regain territory in what was once a much larger range.

These are descendants of the tortoises found more than 20 years ago on the volcano, which have "thrived tremendously," said Gibbs. "You never know how animals brought from the wild will adapt to captivity, but these have thrived remarkably. They are voracious eaters and highly reproductive; in a very short time, they have produced 800 baby tortoises and will continue to produce an average of 60 per year," Gibbs added.

Walter Chimborazo, a field assistant with the Galapagos Conservancy at the breeding center, witnessed the birth of the tortoises that now roam Floreana Island. "They were so small, smaller than the palm of my hand," he recalled.

Their release makes him happy, of course, but it also leaves him with the bittersweet feeling of goodbye.

"I've spent more time here at work than at home... On one hand, I'm happy, but on the other hand, I'm sad because I'm really not going to see them again."

His father worked at the same breeding center. Chimborazo knows his job is a privilege and is proud of having given his all: "I know I took care of them; I raised them. I taught them so they could survive on their island."

The recently released tortoises are hybrids, explained Cristian Sevilla, director of Ecosystems at the Galapagos National Park. Their genetic makeup is partly that of the Floreana tortoises, which went extinct in the 19th century, and partly that of native species from the Wolf Volcano area.

"We haven't yet found a pure Floreana tortoise, but we believe they exist. We found some young specimens on Wolf Volcano that are 50 percent Floreana and 50 percent a native species, which implies they necessarily had a purebred parent," Gibbs explained. "Therefore, it's likely that some are still roaming the vastness of this volcano; perhaps they are some of the original tortoises that whalers brought and left there." Floreana tortoises can live for more than 100 years in the wild.

Carrión described the giant tortoises as "ecosystem engineers" of the archipelago. "They help disperse seeds. They help build and modify the plant communities of the Galápagos ecosystems and are therefore essential not only for themselves as tortoises, but also for the ecological dynamics of the ecosystems," he explained.

The key lies in their diet: each giant tortoise eats up to 225kg of vegetation per year.

"The process of digesting a single bite of plant material takes about a month," said Gibbs, "so the remains aren't expelled until after that time." "By then, the animal has already migrated and travelled many kilometres, thus dispersing enormous quantities of seeds. And many plants, in fact, don't germinate very well unless they've passed through the digestive tract of a giant tortoise."

A worker carries a crate used to transport infant giant tortoises.

But also, weighing up to 400kg, they're like excavators, Gibbs explained: "They dig through the vegetation; they flatten it and prepare their beds for the night."

"If they disperse seeds, they're helping other species to feed on these plants. If they create spaces, these spaces are occupied by other species, such as land birds, for example," Sevilla said.

By working on the recovery of the giant tortoises, the conservationists are restoring this unique ecosystem. Conservation efforts have also eradicated some of the invasive species that arrived with humans, such as goats, pigs and donkeys, and are working to control two other major threats: rodents and cats.

The Galápagos Islands have some of the highest levels of endemism on the planet, meaning species that are found nowhere else. Around 80 percent of land birds, 97 percent of reptiles and land mammals, more than 30 percent of plants and more than 20 percent of marine species there are endemic.

One of the characteristics that has made the Galápagos Islands a key reservoir of biodiversity is their remote location - in the Pacific Ocean, nearly 1000km off the coast of Ecuador - which has allowed species to "evolve separately from the mainland," said Carrión.

That doesn't mean their lives are without challenges, he added: "Life here in the Galápagos is very beautiful, but it's also very harsh for the species; they have to survive very severe conditions" such as aridity in some areas, water stress, salinity stress and UV radiation stress.

The way Galápagos species interact with humans is also unusually friendly. "There's a rule to maintain a distance of 2 metres (6.6 feet) from the wildlife, since the animals don't perceive humans as a threat... You really manage to connect with and understand the animals," said Gibbs.

Giant tortoises are a curiosity today, only living in the wild in the Galápagos Islands or the Aldabra Atoll in the Indian Ocean. They were the first megafauna species to spread across Asia, South America and North America. Until just 10,000 years ago, they even inhabited areas as far away as Florida.

The Galápagos Islands have been the site of extraordinary conservation work, a collaborative effort between the government, civil organisations and the local population. This work has allowed more than 9000 giant tortoises to be bred in captivity and released into the wild over the past 60 years.

But full recovery takes time. The lesson of the tortoises is one of patience. "They grow slowly, yes, but they are very constant and persistent. It's like the fable of the tortoise and the hare: in the end, the tortoise wins the race," Gibbs reflected.

And at the same time, they are extraordinarily noble. As Gibbs put it, "They are such resilient, long-lived and tenacious creatures that they have, in fact, allowed us to solve some of the problems we have created."

Ngā P
