evidence.title: This sustainable Galapagos cruise showed me a side of the islands Darwin never saw
evidence.text:
Expedition yacht La Pinta brings the iconic wildlife, natural wonders and ecological warnings of the Galapagos into view.

This was not the Galapagos wildlife encounter I expected, but considering I’d already spotted five of the iconic “Big 15” animals between the airport and the seaport, run-ins with the 9,000 other species that inhabit the archipelago were as inevitable as they were unpredictable.

Nearly 200 years after Charles Darwin sailed through the Galapagos Islands on HMS Beagle, I boarded La Pinta, an expedition ship with 39 guests and 33 crew members — roughly the same soul count as Darwin’s vessel.

But our voyage wasn’t a retelling of Darwin’s diary with a luxurious slant.

Our four-night northern itinerary visited places Darwin never did or never could. From the misnomer of Darwin Bay to the lava fields that solidified after the famous naturalist’s arrival, the expedition team sought to show us the Galapagos beyond the Big 15.

With every exciting prediction of what awaited on Chinese Hat or Baltra Island came a reminder that a single camera flash, footprint, or piece of trash could immediately impact this enduring yet extremely delicate habitat.

Galapagos sustainability is achieved one step at a time

“This place is so dry that your footprint will stay there until the rains cover it…so maybe six months or even years.”

Dennis Ballesteros, our naturalist guide, gestured to the volcanic sand surrounding Bartolome Island’s wooden boardwalk. To think that a single sidestep off the designated path could disrupt the life of a lava lizard or lava cactus seems almost impossible to believe.

That is, until you realise that a series of seemingly insignificant events impacted the evolution of virtually all life throughout the archipelago. Even with strict guidelines limiting 1,840 people per day in the entire 7,800 square kilometre national park, our little group of nine could do serious damage through neglect or ignorance.

Ballesteros was born and raised in the Galapagos. He’s just as passionate about photographing his home as he is protecting it, which is why he never once danced around the consequences of our choices.

“It’s forbidden to use flash,” the wildlife photographer said. “It stresses the animals. After they stress, they will actually change their behaviour. Perhaps they won’t be there next time.”

Bartolome Island spoils shutterbugs. We posed in our panga (a type of small, open-top boat) with penguins only feet away, then swam alongside them. An astounding moment for sure, but also just a routine day in the Enchanted Isles.

Reef sharks joined our snorkel session on Tuesday; dozens of Nazca boobies waddled along with us on our Thursday hike.

When red-footed boobies nest at eye level and sea lions sunbathe at your feet, it’s easy to forget that our arguably low-impact presence can instantly wound this welcoming world. And, sadly, some damage can’t be reversed.

“When we see an animal in danger, we have to call the park rangers,” Ballesteros said. “Only a veterinarian can help the animal.”

Even with the best of intentions, a local and experienced naturalist like Ballesteros can’t intervene if a sea lion is tangled in marine debris or if a giant tortoise chomps on a piece of litter.

This ripple effect emanates from every decision, forcing Galapagos visitors to weigh the worth of the “perfect” photograph against the health and safety of everything beyond the lens .

Cruises in the Galapagos are as diverse and ever-evolving as the wildlife

Only 69 vessels authorised for touring the Galapagos have live-aboard permissions, though we rarely saw another ship on our journey from Santa Cruz to Santiago and Genovesa Islands.

La Pinta leans into lavishness with its hot tub, observation lounge, and fitness centre; amenities that Captain Robert FitzRoy and his Beagle crew could only dream of. But don’t expect the all-day buffet and casino perks of a traditional pleasure cruise.

You won’t find a TV in your seaview suite either because the Galapagos deserve your full attention, even when you shower and sit. La Pinta acknowledges its role in interacting with and impacting every element of the Galapagos.

“Everything has a different cycle,” hotel manager Gaby explained. “We want to give everything we can a new life.”

The ship’s internal system filters seawater into the water used by guests. All black and grey water produced (toilet paper is disposed of separately via bathroom trash cans) is then filtered again and released back into the sea.

To cut down on the filtration process itself, La Pinta sells reef-safe sunscreen, eco-friendly bug spray and stocks every bathroom with 100 per cent biodegradable body products recreated from a one–time extraction of Magnolia mashpi flowers.

These body lotions, shampoos, and shower gels — which are used across Metropolitan Touring’s other properties like Finch Bay Hotel on Santa Cruz Island — encourage visitors to take accountability for the way their daily decisions might harm the ecosystem of the archipelago.

Seeing the bigger picture in the Galapagos

No one dared move as the Galapagos short-eared owl waited for an unlucky storm petrel.

“Every three or four trips, we’re lucky to see one owl,” Ballesteros told us, only moments before we saw our third.

Watching this endemic species hunt is as unusual as it is to swim with dozens of hammerhead sharks — you could visit the Galapagos year after year and never encounter either animal.

Swimming with spotted eagle rays, making way for blue-footed boobies, and tiptoeing around giant tortoises is unforgettable. But when my mind wanders back to Eden Islet, Prince Philip’s Steps, or Sullivan Bay, I don’t tally up which of the Big 15 made it onto my camera roll.

Instead, I think about the dozens upon dozens of species I saw — and the dozens of opportunities I had to make a conscious effort to feel one with this natural world without wrecking it.

It’s easy to champion the Galapagos as a must-see destination; it’s even easier to lament how tourism is forever altering this beautiful place. Galapagos cruises are a prime example of adaptive radiation: like Darwin’s finches, each ship tries to diversify and specialise itself for survival.

La Pinta’s crew strives to evolve in ways that go beyond achieving a 100 per cent carbon-neutral voyage for every passenger. They promote the importance of traveller accessibility just as strongly as they strive to protect and preserve the national park.

“It was the last dream of a kid to come here before he died,” Ballesteros told us as we watched the birds of Genovesa Island care for their chicks. “He couldn’t walk, but we are not allowed to roll a wheelchair on the island.”

Ballesteros weighed a dying wish against a delicate ecosystem and made a decision.

“I picked eight crew members, we lifted the wheelchair, and we walked the whole way,” he told our teary-eyed group. “We were not impacting anything, and he had the best time of his life.”

“Our mission, from our hearts, is to make this the best experience for you all.”

I had a sense that Ballesteros wasn’t just talking to our small group; he was speaking to every form of life La Pinta had the privilege to encounter and the duty to protect.

Nick Dauk was a guest of Metropolitan Touring in April 2025.

evidence.text:
Bavarian Nordic finder sin nye topchef hos konkurrent

Tidligere på året annoncerede Bavarian Nordic, at selskabets topchef stopper. Nu er arvtageren udnævnt.

Medicinalselskabet Bavarian Nordic har udnævnt Tarja Stenvall som sin nye administrerende direktør.

Det skriver selskabet i en børsmeddelelse torsdag morgen.

Udnævnelsen kommer, efter at det tidligere på året blev annonceret, at Paul Chaplin fratræder rollen.

Tarja Stenvall kommer ifølge Bavarian Nordic med over 20 års ledelseserfaring fra medicinalselskaberne Sanofi, AstraZeneca og Pfizer.

Hun tiltræder officielt den 15. oktober.

Anne Louise Eberhard, som er formand for bestyrelsen i Bavarian Nordic, siger, at Tarja Stenvall er blevet valgt efter en grundig proces.

- Tarja Stenvall har dokumenteret erfaring med at skalere og lede en global life sciencevirksomhed og kombinerer strategisk vision med omfattende erfaring fra den globale medicinal- og vaccineindustri og passion for at forbedre og beskytte liv, siger Eberhard i meddelelsen.

Senest har Tarja Stenvall været direktør i Sanofi med ansvar for diabetes og hjerte-kar-sygdomme.

Selv kalder hun det for en "enormt spændende" mulighed, at stå i spidsen for Bavarian Nordic.

- Virksomheden har opbygget en førende position inden for vacciner og samtidig fastholdt en stærk dedikation til at forbedre og beskytte menneskers liv, hvilet gør det til en særdeles attraktiv mulighed, siger Tarja Stenvall i meddelelsen.

Bavarian Nordic sælger rejsevacciner mod blandt andet rabies, TBE og den myggebårne sygdom chikungunya.

Selskabet sælger også vacciner til landes beredskaber mod udbrud af sygdommen mpox, som tidligere var kendt under det danske navn abekopper.

Paul Chaplin har stået i spidsen for Bavarian Nordic siden 2014. Da hans afgang blev meddelt i marts, lød det, at det skete af personlige årsager.

evidence.title: How Bavarian Nordic is bringing mpox vaccine outreach to the pharmacy counter
evidence.text:
Over the course of four years, mpox has gone from dominating healthcare headlines to all but disappearing from the daily news cycle. However, that doesn’t mean that it’s not a public health concern in the U.S.

Recognizing the challenge this disease poses, Bavarian Nordic is betting the neighborhood pharmacy can keep mpox as a core part of prevention conversations, too.

The vaccine manufacturer recently launched a national pharmacy initiative designed to connect eligible adults with mpox education and vaccination through individualized outreach, conversations with pharmacists and access to immunization at pharmacy locations.

The initiative will initially operate across 14 priority U.S. markets with the potential to expand. It focuses on adults who may be at increased risk for mpox and have either not received a vaccine or have not completed the recommended two-dose series.

Rather than wait for people to seek out vaccination on their own, the initiative is intended to identify opportunities to raise the subject when eligible patients are already interacting with a pharmacy.

“That’s really only half of it,” said Peter Costa, head of medical affairs for North America at Bavarian Nordic, about making vaccines more widely available. “There continues to be this need for education.”

Pharmacists occupy an increasingly valuable position between awareness and action, Costa said. Patients may see them while picking up HIV preexposure prophylaxis , seeking other sexual health services or receiving a seasonal vaccine, creating what he described as familiar “touch points and time points” for a relevant conversation about mpox.

The strategy reflects a broader shift in how mpox vaccination is delivered. During the 2022 outbreak, Bavarian Nordic’s Jynneos vaccines were distributed from the Strategic National Stockpile, and vaccination efforts were heavily concentrated in public health clinics and temporary sites.

The company’s vaccine became commercially available in the U.S. in April 2024, allowing it to move into more conventional health care settings.

Jynneos is administered in two doses given 28 days apart. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention advises that two doses provide greater protection than one and that infections among fully vaccinated people have generally been milder than those among unvaccinated people.

Still, vaccination coverage has lagged. A CDC analysis published in 2023 estimated that 37% of people at risk had received at least one dose and 23% had received two as of January 2023. Bavarian Nordic cited the analysis in announcing its initiative, saying millions of eligible Americans remained without optimal protection.

The campaign arrives as the CDC is again emphasizing the role providers can play in identifying people who may benefit from vaccination.

In a guidance update on September 4 , the agency encouraged healthcare professionals to take comprehensive social and sexual histories as well as counsel eligible patients about vaccination. The health agency also said patients should be able to self-attest that they are eligible without specifying which risk criterion they meet.

Yet those conversations can be difficult, particularly when providers do not feel prepared to discuss sexual behavior or when patients fear being judged. To remedy this issue, Bavarian Nordic has worked with HealthHIV and the National Coalition for LGBTQ+ Health on how HCPs can incorporate mpox education into broader sexual health discussions, Costa said.

A conversation about PrEP, sexually transmitted infection testing or another routine vaccination can provide a natural opening, he added. The goal is to make mpox prevention part of an existing care pathway instead of treating it as a separate or exceptional interaction.

Scott Bertani, director of advocacy at HealthHIV and the National Coalition for LGBTQ+ Health, described pharmacies as a potential “one-stop access point.” They can combine education, insurance processing, vaccine administration and scheduling for a second dose, often without requiring a separate clinical appointment.

“Pharmacists are one of the best people to communicate with because they are the interface between a referring provider often, but they’re also the central point for individuals to access other health services for which maybe stigma or access could be a challenge,” Bertani said.

Stigma remains a particularly delicate part of mpox communication. Although anyone can contract the virus through close contact, U.S. cases have disproportionately affected gay, bisexual and other men who have sex with men, as well as some transgender and nonbinary people.

Both Costa and Bertani said they believe some of the stigma attached to mpox has eased since 2022, but the decline in attention poses its own problem.

“Lower visibility can create different problems for all of us,” Bertani said. “People may feel less singled out while also becoming less likely to recognize that mpox is something that’s still relevant to them.”

For medical marketers, the initiative illustrates a role manufacturers can play beyond supplying a vaccine , particularly during quieter periods when societal attention and public health funding may recede.

Still, that involvement requires careful boundaries. Some government agencies and nonprofit organizations restrict how they work with industry, and manufacturers have an obvious commercial interest in increasing vaccination.

Bertani said partnerships must therefore be structured credibly, incorporating community groups and providers to help shape education around what patients actually need.

The strongest initiatives also connect awareness to a place where a patient can act, he said. In this case, the pharmacy provides that endpoint.

“You can build from a coalition awareness, but you also have to have some kind of access point,” Bertani said. “It doesn’t depend on one person or one setting.”

For Bavarian Nordic, the measure of the initiative will be whether it can turn a familiar health care encounter into completed care, including bringing people back for a second dose.

“The sense of urgency has faded, but the need for prevention has not,” Brian Hujdich, executive director of the National Coalition for LGBTQ+ Health, said in the initiative’s announcement.

evidence.title: Recordati stock trades above the EUR 51.29 tender offer
evidence.text:
Recordati stock (ISIN IT0003828271) stood at EUR 52.90 on Borsa Italiana on September 23, 2026, up 0.19 percent and 3.14 percent above the EUR 51.29 tender offer. The valuation dispute intensified after Palliser Capital urged the board to seek a higher bid.

As Reuters reported on September 14, Palliser asked Recordati's board to withdraw its support for the EUR 51.29-per-share offer from CVC Capital Partners and Groupe Bruxelles Lambert. Palliser argued that the proposal undervalues the Italian pharmaceutical company.

According to Business Wire , Palliser called for consideration of at least EUR 60 per share. That figure is EUR 8.71 above the existing offer, creating a clear benchmark for the dispute.

Recordati's first-half 2026 revenue increased 6.6 percent to EUR 1.4 billion, according to the company's Q2 earnings-call transcript published by Yahoo Finance . Like-for-like growth at constant exchange rates was 9.1 percent, showing that the reported increase was not solely a currency effect.

EBITDA rose 8.8 percent to EUR 540 million, with a 38.3 percent margin. Adjusted net income increased 6.7 percent to EUR 350 million, while reported net income climbed 24.8 percent, giving the takeover debate a stronger operating backdrop.

At EUR 52.90 on September 23, 2026, Recordati stock traded EUR 1.61 above the tender price and 11.83 percent below Palliser's EUR 60 proposal. The market level therefore sits between the existing bid and the activist investor's requested consideration.

evidence.title: Recordati, al via la procedura di licenziamento collettivo a Campoverde: 55 esuberi
evidence.text:
Recordati, al via la procedura di licenziamento collettivo a Campoverde: 55 esuberi

Lo stabilimento farmaceutico di Aprilia coinvolto in un piano di riorganizzazione

È ufficialmente iniziata la procedura di licenziamento collettivo alla Recordati di Campoverde . L’azienda ha comunicato lo scorso 10 settembre l’avvio del percorso alla rappresentanza sindacale, a Unindustria e agli organismi interessati, indicando complessivamente 55 esuberi : 7 tra gli impiegati e 48 tra operai e qualifiche speciali. Si apre così una nuova fase per uno degli stabilimenti del comparto farmaceutico più rilevanti del territorio pontino.

Alla base della decisione, secondo quanto comunicato da Recordati , ci sono motivazioni di carattere industriale, organizzativo e produttivo. Lo stabilimento di Campoverde realizza principi attivi farmaceutici destinati sia alle specialità del gruppo sia al mercato esterno e conta attualmente 301 dipendenti a tempo indeterminato .

Recordati: «Riduzione dei volumi e maggiore concorrenza»

Nel documento aziendale un ruolo centrale viene attribuito all'evoluzione della domanda e ai cambiamenti che stanno interessando il mercato dei principi attivi. Per quanto riguarda il cosiddetto canale captive , cioè le produzioni destinate alle specialità farmaceutiche del gruppo, stanno assumendo maggiore peso i principi attivi ad alto valore aggiunto e quelli destinati ai farmaci per le malattie rare. Si tratta, secondo l'azienda, di produzioni caratterizzate da lotti più ridotti e da una maggiore complessità.

Sul mercato merchant , invece, Recordati evidenzia la pressione della concorrenza internazionale , con particolare riferimento ai produttori cinesi e indiani.

Nel corso del 2026 è inoltre prevista la cessazione della produzione interna dell'intermedio Valcian , insieme alla razionalizzazione del layout produttivo della Difenilidantoina e della Fenitoina Sodica .

Ma è soprattutto la contrazione dei volumi prevista per i prossimi anni a rappresentare uno degli elementi centrali del piano. Nell'ultimo triennio le produzioni di principi attivi e intermedi destinati al mercato esterno sono state pari a circa 570 tonnellate . Per il periodo 2027-2029 , il piano prevede una riduzione di circa 120 tonnellate, pari al 21% .

Meno linee produttive e chiusura del reparto 337

La riorganizzazione prospettata dall'azienda prevede una concentrazione delle attività su un numero inferiore di linee produttive, che arriverebbe a circa il 25% di quelle attualmente operative . Nel piano è prevista anche la definitiva chiusura del reparto 337 .

A questo si aggiungono la razionalizzazione dei processi produttivi e la soppressione del presidio infermieristico , con la possibilità di affidare il servizio a una società esterna.

Secondo Recordati, la riduzione delle linee e dei volumi determina la necessità di intervenire anche sull'organico. L'azienda considera l'eccedenza occupazionale di carattere strutturale e sostiene di non poter ricorrere a misure alternative in grado di evitare, totalmente o parzialmente, i licenziamenti.

Nella comunicazione vengono quindi escluse ipotesi come Cigo, Cigs, contratti di solidarietà e part time collettivo , considerate non adeguate a una situazione che l'azienda ritiene non temporanea. Recordati afferma inoltre che non risultano posizioni vacanti che possano essere utilmente ricoperte dai lavoratori individuati come eccedenti.

L'avvio della procedura apre adesso la fase del confronto sindacale . Gli incontri sono previsti nella sede di Unindustria in via Montesanto a Latina , dove dovranno essere analizzati il quadro occupazionale, i profili professionali coinvolti e le possibili soluzioni.

Il confronto dovrà quindi entrare nel merito delle motivazioni alla base del piano e delle ricadute sui 55 lavoratori indicati come eccedenti , affrontando anche le eventuali misure per attenuare l'impatto occupazionale.

Sul tavolo c'è anche un possibile intervento economico. Recordati ha infatti comunicato la disponibilità a valutare erogazioni aggiuntive rispetto a quanto previsto dalla legge o dai contratti collettivi per i lavoratori interessati.

I licenziamenti, qualora la procedura si concludesse senza soluzioni alternative, verrebbero attuati nei termini previsti dalla legge, indicati dall'azienda in 120 giorni .

Per lo stabilimento di Campoverde si apre dunque una vertenza che mette insieme due questioni strettamente legate: da una parte il piano di riorganizzazione e il futuro produttivo del sito, dall'altra la tutela dei livelli occupazionali . Il confronto tra azienda e sindacati sarà ora chiamato a verificare il quadro delineato da Recordati e a discutere le possibili conseguenze sui 55 posti di lavoro indicati nella procedura.

evidence.title: RECORDATI ANNOUNCES THE WINNER OF THE 12TH EDITION OF THE ARRIGO RECORDATI PRIZE FOR SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH
evidence.text:
RECORDATI ANNOUNCES THE WINNER OF THE 12TH EDITION OF THE ARRIGO RECORDATI PRIZE FOR SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH

RECORDATI ANNOUNCES THE WINNER OF THE 12TH EDITION OF THE ARRIGO RECORDATI PRIZE FOR SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH

The 2026 Award, open to early career investigators from around the world, was dedicated to advancing research in paediatric oncology, focused on sarcomas

Paediatric sarcomas are among the leading causes of cancer-related death in children, yet there has been little innovation in treatment progress over the past 40 years

Dr. Laura Broutier has been awarded the €250,000 research grant for her DISARMS project on fusion-negative rhabdomyosarcoma

The project aims to uncover the mechanisms that allow tumour cells to survive chemotherapy and prevent relapse and metastasis, with the ultimate goal of identifying new, low-toxicity therapeutic approaches

Milan, 17 September 2026 – Recordati S.p.A today announced Dr. Laura Broutier as the winner of the 12th edition of the International Prize for Scientific Research Arrigo Recordati , dedicated this year to advancing research in paediatric oncology, with a specific focus on sarcomas.

At the 58th Annual SIOP Congress, in Texas, Dr. Broutier was awarded the €250,000 research grant for her project, "DISARMS - Disrupting Invasion, Stemness And Resistance in RhabdoMyoSarcoma by targeting dormant persister cells."

The winning project was selected by an independent Review Committee of internationally recognised experts following the assessment of research proposals submitted by early career investigators from around the world.

Established in 2000 in memory of the Italian pharmaceutical entrepreneur Arrigo Recordati, the Prize aims to promote scientific research and inspire biomedical discoveries benefiting people worldwide. Since 2019, reflecting Recordati's commitment to rare diseases, the Prize has been dedicated to the promotion and recognition of excellence in orphan disease treatment research.

"It is a privilege to award the 12th Arrigo Recordati Prize to Dr. Laura Broutier and her team, and to support research with the potential to make a meaningful difference for children affected by these devastating diseases," said Andrea Recordati, Chairman of Recordati. "Paediatric sarcomas remain an area of significant unmet need, where progress in treatment has been limited for decades. Supporting outstanding researchers and innovative science is one way we can contribute to advancing knowledge and, ultimately, to improving outcomes for patients and their families."

Paediatric sarcomas are a diverse group of rare cancers arising in bone and soft tissues and are among the leading causes of cancer-related death in children. Despite advances in the understanding of their biology, there has been limited innovation in treatment over the past 40 years.

Advancing understanding of the pathophysiology of paediatric sarcomas is critical to developing targeted therapies that are both effective and tolerable, while limiting treatment-related toxicity. Translational research that bridges laboratory discoveries with clinical applications is therefore essential to developing new therapeutic approaches and improving outcomes for children affected by these diseases.

Fusion-negative rhabdomyosarcoma is the most common soft-tissue sarcoma of children and young adults, yet survival has not improved in four decades and treatment toxicity precludes further dose escalation. The mechanisms allowing tumour cells to survive chemotherapy and later drive relapse and metastasis remain poorly understood.

Combining patient-derived organoids, single-cell technologies, and genetic engineering, we have uncovered a dormant, drug-tolerant persister cell state whose signature predicts patient survival in independent cohorts. Building on this foundation, the DISARMS project aims to decode how this cell state couples chemoresistance to an invasive, pro-metastatic programme, and to exploit its vulnerabilities in rational, low-toxicity drug combinations to eliminate the cells conventional chemotherapy spares. As dormant persister programmes are increasingly recognised across cancer types, the framework developed here may extend beyond rhabdomyosarcoma.

Dr. Laura Broutier is an Inserm researcher and group leader at the Cancer Research Center of Lyon, in the "Childhood Cancers & Cell States" team led by Dr. Marie Castets and Prof. Jean-Yves Blay. After a PhD on cancer cell death resistance and a postdoc in Cambridge, pioneering the first liver tumour-derived organoids, she redirected this expertise toward paediatric cancers — rare diseases with almost no dedicated models. Her group now grows 3D tumoroids directly from children's biopsies, including sarcomas, developing innovative approaches to decipher and bypass the molecular and cellular processes that drive treatment resistance, relapse and dissemination.

Dr. Broutier leads the DISARMS project together with a multidisciplinary team combining expertise in patient-derived organoid modeling, single-cell multiomics, computational biology, cancer cell metabolism and translational paediatric oncology. Dr. Maëlle Broustal, a third-year PhD student in biology and bioinformatics who is directly involved in the project, received the Award on Dr. Broutier's behalf at the 2026 Award Ceremony.

"I am deeply honoured that the DISARMS project has been selected for the 2026 Arrigo Recordati Prize," said Dr. Laura Broutier. "Our research seeks to understand how a small population of tumour cells can survive chemotherapy and later drive relapse and metastasis. With the support of this Prize, we hope to identify vulnerabilities that can be translated into rational, low-toxicity therapeutic approaches, with the ultimate goal of improving outcomes for children and young adults with rhabdomyosarcoma. I am also particularly grateful for the recognition of the team behind this work."

The Award Ceremony was held in San Antonio, Texas, during the SIOP Congress.

The International Prize for Scientific Research Arrigo Recordati

The Prize is an international award that aims to promote scientific research and inspire biomedical discoveries benefiting people worldwide. It was established in 2000 in memory of Arrigo Recordati, who strongly believed in the power of scientific research to drive the growth of the pharmaceutical industry and provide products beneficial to public health and individual well-being. His legacy continues to inspire a new generation of researchers — driven by the belief that scientific discovery is the true engine of progress in healthcare.

Over the last almost 20 years, Recordati has developed, produced and marketed medicines for the treatment of rare diseases through Recordati Rare Diseases, dedicated entirely to serving patients globally living with rare conditions and focused on key treatment areas including rare metabolic diseases, endocrinology and hema-oncology. From 2019, to reflect our commitment, the Prize is dedicated to the promotion and recognition of excellence in orphan disease treatment research.

Contacts recordatiprize2026@recordati.com

Recordati is an international pharmaceutical Group listed on the Italian Stock Exchange (XMIL: REC), with roots dating back to a family-run pharmacy in Northern Italy in the 1920s. We are uniquely structured to provide treatments across specialty and primary care and rare diseases. Our fully integrated operations span clinical development, manufacturing of active ingredients and finished products, commercialization and licensing. We operate in approximately 150 countries across EMEA, the Americas and APAC, with around 4,700 employees. We believe that health is a fundamental right, not a privilege. Today, our purpose "Unlocking the full potential of life" aims to empower individuals to live life to the fullest, from common conditions to the rarest.

Recordati S.p.A (0KBS), the global pharmaceutical company listed on the Italian Stock Exchange, has awarded Dr. Laura Broutier the 12th International Prize for Scientific Research Arrigo Recordati. The €250,000 research grant was presented at the 58th Annual SIOP Congress held in San Antonio, Texas, on 17 September 2026. Dr. Broutier’s DISARMS project focuses on fusion-negative rhabdomyosarcoma—the most prevalent soft-tissue sarcoma affecting children and young adults—where survival rates have remained stagnant for 40 years.

DISARMS Project Aims to Target Drug-Resistant Persister Cells in Fusion-Negative Rhabdomyosarcoma

The DISARMS project—Disrupting Invasion, Stemness And Resistance in RhabdoMyoSarcoma—investigates why a subset of tumour cells evade chemotherapy and cause relapse and metastasis. Dr. Broutier’s team at the Cancer Research Center of Lyon employs patient-derived organoids, single-cell analysis, and genetic engineering to study dormant, drug-tolerant persister cells whose molecular signatures predict patient outcomes. The goal is to discover low-toxicity drug combinations capable of eradicating these resistant cells beyond the reach of standard chemotherapy.

Paediatric Sarcomas Present a Major Unmet Medical Need with Limited Therapeutic Advances in Four Decades

Paediatric sarcomas, cancers arising in bone and soft tissues, remain a leading cause of cancer mortality in children. Despite biological insights, treatment innovations have plateaued for approximately 40 years, with further chemotherapy dose increases limited by toxicity. Translational research connecting laboratory discoveries to clinical therapies is essential to develop effective, tolerable treatments. The recognition of dormant persister cells across various cancers suggests that findings from the DISARMS project could have broader applications beyond rhabdomyosarcoma.

Arrigo Recordati Prize Honors Excellence in Rare Disease Research Since 2019

Created in 2000 to honor pharmaceutical pioneer Arrigo Recordati, the international prize supports scientific research and biomedical innovation benefiting patients worldwide. Since 2019, the award has concentrated on orphan disease research, aligning with Recordati’s strategic focus through its Recordati Rare Diseases division, which develops, manufactures, and markets therapies for rare conditions globally in areas such as rare metabolic diseases, endocrinology, and haema-oncology. The winner was chosen by an independent committee of renowned experts evaluating submissions from early-career researchers worldwide.

Recordati’s Rare Disease Focus Strengthens Its Global Pharmaceutical Presence

Operating in roughly 150 countries across EMEA, the Americas, and APAC, Recordati maintains integrated capabilities including clinical development, active ingredient production, finished product manufacturing, and commercialization. Its Recordati Rare Diseases division represents a key pillar within its specialty and primary care framework. The DISARMS award exemplifies Recordati’s mission to unlock life’s full potential, spanning common to rare conditions. L’Opa su Recordati, iniziata il 31 agosto scorso, potrebbe avere un percorso tortuoso per il malumore di alcuni azionisti riguardo al prezzo offerto, pari a 51,29 euro per azione . Ad uscire allo scoperto contro l’operazione è stato Palliser Capital, che in una lettera rivolta al board torna sul tema della valorizzazione del titolo nell’operazione, ma anche sulle modalità. Il fondo chiede al consiglio di amministrazione di «ritirare il proprio sostegno all’offerta e di agire responsabilmente adottando tutte le misure disponibili per tutelare gli azionisti di minoranza, incluso chiedere all’offerente di riconoscere agli azionisti di Recordati un corrispettivo equo e congruo, pari ad almeno 60 euro per azione , mediante un incremento del corrispettivo dell’offerta».

Le domande sono suggerite automaticamente da 24Ore AI sulla base del contenuto visualizzato.

Il board della società italiana aveva rilasciato un parere favorevole a maggioranza (sei su dieci) il 16 luglio scorso. A votare contro i quattro amministratori indipendenti (Diva Moriani, Joanna Le Couilliard, Piergiorgio Peluso e Stephen Sands), che, a fronte della fairness opinion di Rothschild & Co Italia, avevano giudicato non adeguato il prezzo dell’offerta. In quell’occasione Respighi BidCo, il veicolo societario controllato pariteticamente da CVC Capital Partners (Fund IX) e Groupe Bruxelles Lambert (GBL) che ha lanciato l’Opa, aveva reso chiaro che termini e condizioni «rimangono immutati», chiudendo così la porta a qualunque ipotesi di rilancio. Il prezzo di 51,29 euro, per un’operazione del valore di 10,7 miliardi di euro, incorpora un premio del 12,89% rispetto al prezzo del 25 marzo 2026, pari a 46,06 euro per azione, data dell’annuncio della manifestazione di interesse non vincolante dei fondi.

Ora il fondo londinese rilancia il tema del prezzo e non solo: «L’Offerta non è altro che un’operazione profondamente iniqua e altamente irregolare, concepita per costringere gli azionisti di minoranza di Recordati a cedere le proprie azioni a un prezzo fortemente penalizzante» si legge nella nota di Palliser Capital, che prosegue: «Un’operazione strutturata attraverso l’approvazione di amministratori non indipendenti caratterizzati da profondi conflitti di interesse e interessi personali nel buon esito dell’operazione, e portata avanti nonostante l’opposizione unanime e senza riserve di tutti gli amministratori indipendenti del consiglio».

A Piazza Affari oggi il titolo viaggia a quota 52,55 euro per azione , sopra il livello dell’Opa, con un incremento a metà mattina di meno di mezzo punto percentuale.

Nell’ambito dell’offerta pubblica di acquisto (OPA) volontaria totalitaria promossa da Respighi BidCo (veicolo di CVC e GBL) sulle azioni ordinarie Recordati, risulta che oggi 14 settembre sono state presentate 3.840 richieste. Pertanto, complessivamente le richieste di adesione raggiungono quota 98.278.175, mantenendosi intorno al 49,50% sul totale degli strumenti oggetto di offerta.

Nella quota vanno calcolate la partecipazione del 46,82 detenuta da Rossini S.à r.l. ,società di investimento attraverso cui il fondo CVC Capital Partners detiene la quota di maggioranza e controlla Recordati; la partecipazione di Andrea Recordati , presidente di Recordati, che ha aderito all’Opa cedendo 200.000 azioni ordinarie per un valore complessivo di 10,26 milioni di euro; la partecipazione di Arisca S.r.l. , società strettamente collegata ad Andrea Recordati, che ha aderito cedendo 122.903 azioni ordinarie per un valore totale di 6,31 milioni di euro; la quota del ceo di Recordati Rob Koremans di 78.426 azioni per un controvalore di oltre 4 milioni di euro.

La fairness opinion di Rothschild & Co Italia

Rothschild & Co, incaricata dagli amministratori indipendenti di Recordati, ha bocciato sotto il profilo finanziario il prezzo di 51,29 euro per azione offerto da Respighi BidCo. La fairness opinion, datata 14 luglio 2026, conclude infatti che il corrispettivo è «inadeguato sotto il profilo finanziario». Il giudizio è particolarmente significativo perché non si basa su una singola metodologia, ma sul confronto di sei diversi approcci valutativi: il metodo dei flussi di cassa attualizzati (DCF), i multipli di società quotate comparabili, le transazioni comparabili, i premi storicamente riconosciuti nelle Opa italiane, l’andamento storico del titolo e il target price degli analisti. Il prezzo di 51,29 euro si colloca al di sotto dei valori ottenuti dalla maggior parte delle metodologie utilizzate da Rothschild, la cui analisi si è basata anche sul business plan 2025–2029 di Recordati e sulle informazioni ricevute dal management tra aprile e luglio 2026.

Valutazione di Rotschild & Co Italia risultante dall’applicazione di ciascuna delle metodologie usate

«Alla luce delle considerazioni sopra esposte e fatto salvo quanto ivi indicato, Rothschild & Co ritiene che, alla Data di Riferimento, il Corrispettivo non sia congruo sotto il profilo finanziario» conclude la banca d’affari.

Nel dettaglio l’analisi in base ai flussi di cassa attualizzati (DFC) ha preso in considerazione il business plan di Recordati al 2029 e ha proiettato i risultati anche oltre tale orizzonte arrivando al 2034. Rothschild ha inoltre isolato Isturisa, medicinale utilizzato nel trattamento della sindrome di Cushing, e lo ha valutato separatamente per un arco temporale che arriva al 2040 attraverso un approccio sum-of-the-parts.

Per il business Recordati al netto di Isturisa, Rothschild ha utilizzato un costo medio ponderato del capitale (WACC) compreso tra 7,8% e 8,3% e un tasso di crescita perpetua tra 1,75% e 2,25%. Dal 2030 ha inoltre normalizzato gli investimenti di mantenimento a circa 100 milioni di euro l’anno, adottando nel complesso ipotesi di crescita più prudenti rispetto allo storico e alle proiezioni del management. Rothschild, infine, ipotizza, dopo la perdita dell’esclusiva, un’erosione dei ricavi compresa tra il 65% e l’80%. Anche adottando questa ipotesi relativamente prudente, il DCF restituisce un valore compreso fra 52,01 e 61,25 euro per azione, con il limite inferiore già superiore ai 51,29 euro dell’Opa.

La fairness opinion di Lazard, incaricata dal board, porta a una conclusione opposta rispetto a quella di Rothschild: Lazard ritiene congruo, sotto il profilo finanziario, il corrispettivo di 51,29 euro per azione. La banca d’affari francese ha indicato il DCF (Discounted Cash Flow) come metodologia principale. Ha valutato i flussi di cassa unlevered e after-tax di Recordati dal 30 giugno 2026 fino al 31 dicembre 2040, utilizzando un tasso di crescita perpetua dello 0,25%-0,75% e tassi di attualizzazione/WACC del 7,70%-8,70%. Il DCF produce un valore per azione di 44,98-54,21 euro. Il prezzo dell’Opa, quindi, si trova all’interno del range, vicino alla parte alta dell’intervallo.

Lazard ha anche analizzato il comportamento del titolo. Nei 52 settimane precedenti al 9 luglio 2026, Recordati aveva oscillato tra circa 44,48 e 54,60 euro. Al 25 marzo 2026, data considerata “ undisturbed ”, il prezzo spot era 46,06 euro, mentre i prezzi medi ponderati erano 46,35 euro a un mese, 48,80 euro a sei mesi e 50,35 euro a dodici mesi.

Lazard ha, inoltre, esaminato selezionate società quotate operanti nel settore biofarmaceutico (BioMarin, Ipsen, Orion, Sobi e UCB) prendendone in esame l’ enterprise value espresso come multiplo dei ricavi e dell’Ebitda attesi di tale società comparabile, calendarizzati per ciascuno degli esercizi chiusi al 31 dicembre 2026 e al 31 dicembre 2027.

Confronto con società comparable del settore

«Sulla base di quanto precede - si legge nel documento - Lazard ha applicato multipli dell’Ebitda pari a +/- 1,0x rispetto al valore mediano del multiplo EV/ Ebitda Adjusted CY2026 dei principali comparabili (core peers), corrispondente a 12,4x-14,4x, all’Ebitda stimato della società per il CY2026, al fine di calcolare un intervallo di valore implicito per azione, in ciascun caso utilizzando l’Ebitda stimato della società tratto dalle previsioni della società. I risultati di tali analisi hanno indicato un valore implicito per Azione compreso tra euro 51,44 ed euro 61,41».

Sulla base, invece, dell’analisi delle transazioni precedenti, Lazard ha applicato «multipli dell’Ebitda pari a +/- 1,0x rispetto alla mediana del multiplo EV/Ebitda Adjusted LTM delle transazioni comparabili, pari a 12,6x (da 11,6x a 13,6x), all’Ebitda Adjusted LTM al giugno 2026 della società. I risultati delle analisi hanno indicato un valore implicito per azione compreso tra euro 46,71 ed euro 56,55».

Infine Lazard ha esaminato l’andamento storico del prezzo (e dei volumi di negoziazione) delle azioni nel periodo di 52 settimane terminato il 9 luglio 2026. In tale periodo, il prezzo di negoziazione intraday del titolo è oscillato tra circa euro 44,48 ed euro 54,60 per Azione. Sulla base di quanto analizzato nel documento, la banca d’affari ha dichiarato congruo il prezzo dell’offerta.

Amplifon in the spotlight, market on the upswing and positive sentiment towards GN Hearing

The share price is being buoyed by a mix of news, ranging from positive comments from Bofa’s 2026 Healthcare Conference to GN’s strong performance in Copenhagen, where Amplifon is set to acquire its hearing division

For feedback, please contact english@ilsole24ore.com

For feedback, please contact english@ilsole24ore.com

(Il Sole 24 Ore Radiocor) - Another strong session for Amplifon: the share is among the top performers on the FTSE MIB, up by over 1 per cent to €11.78, a far cry from the lows of around €8 reached last March. A mix of news regarding the stock is driving the price higher, starting with positive comments from Bofa’s Healthcare Conference 2026. The conference, as summarised by Bofa analysts, provided generally reassuring indications for the sector, but – they emphasise – with upside potential increasingly dependent on the specific performance of individual companies. Amplifon’s management, the analysts report, confirmed that it ‘sees a recovery in the growth of the hearing aid market to around 3 per cent, supported by stabilisation in France and improving trends in Italia and Spain’. Management confirmed that market momentum continued into the third quarter. Focus on the acquisition and integration of GN Hearing: net synergies of €60–80 million will mainly stem from increasing GN Hearing’s internal sourcing from the current 40% to 90% by 2029. Synergies from GN, Fit4Growth and operating leverage will support profitability in 2027, whilst the net debt-to-EBITDA ratio will stand at around 3.5 times at closing, with a target reduction of around 0.3 times per year.

The positive sentiment surrounding the share was also indirectly bolstered by GN’s strong performance on the Copenhagen Stock Exchange , the group from which Amplifon is set to acquire the hearing division. GN shares closed at a five-month high yesterday following a positive report from Sweden’s leading bank, SEB, which recommends buying the shares and highlights, amongst other things, the strong performance of the group’s products.

Finally, it is worth noting that EssilorLuxottica has launched the new Nuance Audio Plus in the US, an evolution of over-the-counter hearing aids for people with mild to moderate hearing loss. The target customer base, as Intermonte analysts explain, differs from that of Amplifon (which focuses on patients with more debilitating hearing loss) and therefore the overlap in the customer base is limited; however, they also state that the main impact of Nuance may be the expansion of the category, increased penetration of the hearing care market and a reduction in social stigma, rather than any real disintermediation of the traditional channel.

evidence.title: Amplifon Calls Shareholders’ Meeting to Advance GN Hearing Acquisition
evidence.text:
Amplifon Calls Shareholders’ Meeting to Advance GN Hearing Acquisition

Sep 17, 2026 | Growth Strategies , Industry News | 0 |

Amplifon’s board has moved to formalize the next phase of its planned acquisition of GN Hearing, calling a shareholders’ meeting to approve a capital increase that would give GN Store Nord a stake in the Milan-based hearing care company.

Amplifon S.p.A., the global leader in hearing care retail, announced on Sept 17 that its board of directors has resolved to convene both an Extraordinary and Ordinary Shareholders’ Meeting to approve a series of measures tied to its pending acquisition of GN Hearing — the hearing aid division of GN Store Nord A/S.

The centerpiece of the agenda is a proposed share capital increase of 56,000,000 new ordinary Amplifon shares, to be issued exclusively to GN Store Nord as part of the deal’s equity consideration. The shares are priced at €11.267 each — equal to the weighted average price of Amplifon shares over the preceding three months — giving the equity tranche a value of approximately €631 million.

The total consideration for the acquisition comprises the 56,000,000 newly issued shares plus a cash component of €1.69 billion, subject to customary financial adjustments at closing. The cash portion is being financed in part through a €1.35 billion senior loan subscribed in June, with a maximum duration of 24 months, which may subsequently be refinanced through a combination of bank and bond financing.

Closing of the acquisition is currently expected by the end of 2026, subject to the satisfaction of relevant conditions precedent.

Once the share issuance is complete, GN Store Nord will hold 17.09% of Amplifon’s share capital, representing 9.13% of voting rights, while Amplifon’s controlling shareholder, Ampliter S.r.l., will hold 32.07% of the share capital, representing 63.69% of voting rights.

The new shares subscribed by GN will be subject to lock-up arrangements, released on a staggered basis over the 15 months following closing: slightly less than one-third of the shares will be released nine months after closing, with the remaining shares released in subsequent tranches until the lock-up expires in full.

As part of the contractual arrangements governing the deal, GN Store Nord has the right to designate a representative to Amplifon’s board of directors upon closing. GN has notified Amplifon of its intention to designate Scott Davis as its representative. The board has resolved to propose that shareholders increase the number of directors from 9 to 10 and appoint Davis as a non-executive independent director, contingent on the acquisition closing.

The board will also ask shareholders to confirm the appointment of Francesca Fiore, who was co-opted as an independent non-executive director in May 2026 following the resignation of Nicola Bedin.

Corporate Structure Refinements Also on the Agenda

Alongside the acquisition-related items, the board has approved a partial demerger by way of spin-off, announced on July 30, 2026, aimed at making the group’s corporate structure more efficient. The transaction entails the transfer of shareholdings held by Amplifon in wholly-owned companies resident outside the European Union to a newly incorporated beneficiary company, Amplifon Partecipazioni I S.r.l., wholly owned by Amplifon and based in Italy. No economic or financial impacts are expected in connection with the transaction.

The shareholders’ meeting agenda also includes proposed amendments to Amplifon’s articles of association to align them with Italy’s new Capital Markets Law framework, including provisions governing how shareholders’ meetings may be conducted and updated thresholds for shareholder participation rights.

Amplifon , which operates approximately 9,700 locations across 24 countries, entered into the agreement with GN Store Nord on March 16, 2026. The acquisition of GN Hearing would represent one of the largest consolidation moves in the global hearing care industry in recent years. Additional details on the shareholders’ meeting date and supporting documentation will be made available at corporate.amplifon.com .

evidence.title: Amplifon reduces complexity and costs by optimizing data governance and increasing end-to-end data visibility
evidence.text:
Amplifon reduces complexity and costs by optimizing data governance and increasing end-to-end data visibility

From clearer data flows to more effective governance and optimized operating costs, Amplifon is making its organization more efficient and sustainable.

Building a data governance framework capable of ensuring transparency and control across the entire data platform, enabling rationalization and harmonization of KPIs on a global scale.

Amplifon , a global leader in the hearing care retail market, operates internationally with demanding business functions and rapidly evolving analytics needs. It therefore requires a data platform capable of scaling quickly without compromising reliability or efficiency. In recent years, it has transformed its data platform, moving from a legacy environment to a modern cloud-native architecture.

The transition ensured operational continuity and enabled analytics to scale rapidly across different markets. As adoption increased across countries and functions, the focus moved beyond enablement alone, to improving efficiency, managing costs sustainably, and ensuring greater consistency in how the underlying data behind reports, KPIs, and business analysis are defined and managed.

Amplifon , with the support of Target Reply , introduced a solution for Data Governance designed as a layer of visibility and governance for the entire corporate data ecosystem.

The platform ensures end-to-end observability of flows and consumption patterns, providing a clear view of how data is produced, transformed, and used. This approach allows teams to manage the architecture as a whole, moving beyond the management of individual assets or isolated reports.

Within this layer, metadata provides a reliable context for analyses supported by Artificial Intelligence. The interaction between AI and the information assets is enabled by an architecture based on MCP (Model Context Protocol) , which links metadata to AI agents in a structured, governed way.

In this model, an MCP Server exposes information in a controlled manner, while specialized agents use this context to analyze dependencies, reconstruct transformation logic, and support critical activities such as troubleshooting and impact analysis . Every operation occurs in full compliance with security and governance protocols, including SSO and RBAC controls, ensuring that AI operates exclusively within the defined permission perimeter.

From end-to-end visibility to streamlining, efficiency, and harmonization

With the support of Target Reply , Amplifon has structured its solution on three key pillars, designed to ensure continuity in governance without slowing down business operations:

End-to-End Visibility and Lineage: Through the scanning of metadata across the entire data platform, the solution makes the dependancies between tables, transformations, pipelines, and reports explicit. This transparency allows teams to anticipate how each change propagates through the system, optimizing the activities of troubleshooting , ticket management, and impact analysis during the development phases.

Guided Rationalization: By starting with this information, it has become possible to initiate a guided rationalization through a combined top-down and bottom-up reading. On the one hand, the report analysis based on usage and similarity ( usage & similarity ) allows for identifying duplications and consolidation opportunities; on the other hand, complete visibility enables mapping and decommissioning tables and pipelines no longer connected to active consumption.

Data Harmonization: Transparency into lineage and transformation logic allows for comparing KPI definitions across different countries, highlighting any discrepancies and tracing their causes. This facilitates a progressive alignment process on a selected set of indicators, where AI scales the analysis on large volumes while business and data stakeholders maintain guidance on strategic decisions.

Amplifon’s journey shows how control over the data ecosystem translates into immediate operational benefits, making governance an enabler of reliability and international scalability.

Greater understanding of data flows and more immediate reading of dependencies and uses across the entire platform

Reduction of operational effort , thanks to faster investigations and troubleshooting and more reliable impact analysis

Solid foundation for harmonizing KPIs , making differences and calculation logics visible, comparable, and traceable

Acceleration thanks to AI , which reduces the effort needed to turn insights into actions and supports large-scale analysis

Amplifon is an Italian group based in Milan, a world leader in the hearing care retail market (solutions and services for hearing). Founded in 1950, it operates through a network of 10,000 audiology centers in 25 countries and employs over 20,600 people worldwide. It is a publicly traded company on the Italian Stock Exchange and in 2024 it recorded revenues of over 2.4 billion euros, primarily offering the sale, fitting, and support of hearing solutions and related services.

Target Reply is the Reply group company spealizing in Big Data and Advanced Analytics solutions. Target Reply supports companies from needs identification through to solution design and implementation, using data integration technologies, data modeling, predictive analytics, all while using the most innovative tools in the field of Business Discovery and Big Data. Target Reply has gained significant experience with major Italian and foreign corporate groups and is capable of operating in all major markets: Telco, Finance, and Manufacturing.

evidence.title: Die DiaSorin-Aktie reagiert auf Ransomware-Angriff und bleibt nahe Jahreshoch
evidence.text:
DiaSorin S.p.A. (ISIN IT0003497168) sieht sich laut einem Cybersecurity-Bericht vom 03.09.2026 mit einem Ransomware-Angriff der Gruppe Settra konfrontiert, während die DiaSorin-Aktie per 03.09.2026 mit rund 76,08 EUR auf einem hohen Bewertungsniveau nahe ihrem jüngsten Jahreshoch notiert. Laut aktuellen Kursdaten eines europäischen Finanzportals lag der Schlusskurs am 03.09.2026 bei 76,08 EUR, was einem Plus von rund 12,63 Prozent seit Jahresbeginn entspricht und die robuste Performance der Aktie unterstreicht. Für Anleger stellt sich damit die Frage, wie stark ein solcher Sicherheitsvorfall das Vertrauen in den Diagnostikspezialisten und seine künftige Ergebnisentwicklung beeinflusst.

Nach Angaben eines auf IT-Sicherheit spezialisierten Portals meldete die Ransomware-Gruppe Settra am 03.09.2026 einen Angriff auf DiaSorin S.p.A., der sich gegen die Infrastruktur des Unternehmens richtete und sensible Systeme des Diagnostikanbieters betreffen soll. Der Bericht beschreibt DiaSorin als führendes Biotech-Unternehmen in Italien mit dem Schwerpunkt auf In-vitro-Diagnostik, dessen Internetpräsenz unter der Domain int.diasorin.com geführt wird. Ein solcher Vorfall kann operative Abläufe, Forschung und Entwicklung sowie die Kommunikation mit Laboren und Klinikpartnern beeinträchtigen und damit kurzfristig Kosten verursachen, etwa für forensische Analysen, zusätzliche Sicherheitsmaßnahmen und mögliche Systemwiederherstellungen.

Für einen Diagnostikspezialisten wie DiaSorin ist die Verfügbarkeit und Integrität von Labor- und Patienten­daten zentral, weil viele Kunden auf schnelle und zuverlässige Testergebnisse angewiesen sind. Wird die IT-Infrastruktur durch Schadsoftware eingeschränkt, kann dies temporäre Verzögerungen bei der Datenauswertung, bei der Versorgung von Laboren mit Reagenzien oder bei der Qualitätssicherung auslösen. In der Regel investieren betroffene Unternehmen nach solchen Vorfällen deutlich mehr in Cybersecurity, was sich zunächst kostensteigernd auswirkt, langfristig aber die Widerstandsfähigkeit gegenüber weiteren Angriffen erhöht. Anleger sollten daher neben klassischen Fundamentaldaten auch die Fähigkeit des Unternehmens berücksichtigen, seine digitale Sicherheit zu stärken und regulatorische Anforderungen im Gesundheitssektor zu erfüllen.

Laut einer aktuellen Kursübersicht eines internationalen Finanzportals wird DiaSorin an mehreren europäischen Handelsplätzen gehandelt, unter anderem an der Wiener Börse mit dem Ticker DIAS, wo die DiaSorin-Aktie per 03.09.2026 mit einem Schlusskurs von 76,08 EUR geführt wird. In der historischen Kursreihe zeigt sich, dass der Kurs noch am 28.08.2026 bei 73,75 EUR lag und damit innerhalb weniger Handelstage um rund 3,16 Prozent auf 76,08 EUR angestiegen ist. Diese Bewegung illustriert, dass die Aktie zuletzt tendenziell gefragt war, auch wenn der Ransomware-Bericht die Nachrichtenlage nun dominiert. Zusätzlich weist die Performance-Übersicht eine Jahres­performance von plus 12,63 Prozent aus, was darauf hindeutet, dass DiaSorin im laufenden Jahr besser abschneidet als viele defensivere Titel im europäischen Gesundheitssektor.

Ein weiteres auffälliges Detail aus der Kursübersicht ist, dass der Titel in den Tagen Ende August und Anfang September mehrfach mit identischen Schlusskursen notierte, bevor der Sprung auf das aktuelle Niveau erfolgte. Die Kursspanne der letzten Wochen bewegt sich damit in einem Bereich von rund 73,75 EUR bis 76,76 EUR, wobei der Wert 76,76 EUR als technischer Orientierungs­punkt für kurzfristig orientierte Marktteilnehmer dient. Ein italienisches Börsenportal beschreibt auf Basis dieser Spanne eine operative Handelsempfehlung, bei der ein Einstieg in die DiaSorin-Aktie um 76,76 EUR mit einem Stop-Loss bei 73,56 EUR und einem kurzfristigen Gewinnpotenzial begründet wird. Der Abstand zwischen Einstiegskurs und Stop-Loss liegt damit bei gut 4,2 Prozent, was das Risiko­profil dieser taktischen Strategie verdeutlicht.

Weitere Nachrichten, Analysen und Kennzahlen zur DiaSorin-Aktie finden sich gebündelt in der Themenübersicht von ad-hoc-news.de sowie im Investor-Relations-Bereich des Unternehmens.

DiaSorin hat sich in den vergangenen Jahren als Spezialist für In-vitro-Diagnostik etabliert und bietet eine breite Palette von Testsystemen an, die vor allem in klinischen Laboren und Krankenhäusern eingesetzt werden. Das Portfolio umfasst unter anderem immundiagnostische Tests für Infektionskrankheiten, Onkologie und Autoimmunerkrankungen sowie molekulardiagnostische Lösungen für die schnelle Identifikation von Pathogenen. Ein zentraler Baustein ist dabei die eigene Plattform für automatisierte Testdurchführung, auf der Labore eine Vielzahl von Assays in standardisierten Workflows verarbeiten können, was Effizienzgewinne und eine hohe Reproduzierbarkeit der Ergebnisse ermöglicht.

Die wirtschaftliche Bedeutung dieses Portfolios lässt sich daran ablesen, dass DiaSorin über seine Diagnostikprodukte wiederkehrende Erlöse aus dem Verkauf von Reagenzien, Verbrauchsmaterialien und Serviceleistungen generiert. Viele Kunden sind aufgrund regulierter Prozesse und validierter Testverfahren langfristig an bestimmte Plattformen gebunden, was die Visibilität der Umsätze erhöht. In jüngeren Zwischenberichten, deren vollständige Kennzahlen im Investor-Relations-Bereich abrufbar sind, hebt das Unternehmen die Bedeutung von Produktinnovationen und Erweiterungen des Testmenüs hervor, um zusätzliche Indikationen abzudecken und neue Kundengruppen zu erschließen. Für Anleger ist entscheidend, wie stark diese Produktbasis Wachstum und Margen stützt und ob Cybersecurity-Vorfälle den Ausbau der Plattformen oder die Einführung neuer Assays verzögern könnten.

Die DiaSorin-Aktie schloss laut einer aktuellen Kursübersicht eines europäischen Finanzportals am 03.09.2026 an der Wiener Börse mit 76,08 EUR, nachdem sie am 02.09.2026 noch mit einem Schlusskurs von 76,08 EUR bei einem Tagesplus von 3,16 Prozent aus dem Handel gegangen war. Damit liegt der aktuelle Kurs knapp über dem Niveau von 73,75 EUR, das Ende August mehrfach als Schlusskurs verzeichnet wurde und nun als kurzfristige Unterstützungslinie gilt. Sollte der Markt den Ransomware-Angriff als beherrschbaren Vorfall einstufen, könnte die Aktie ihre Position nahe dem Jahreshoch behaupten; bei anhaltenden Sicherheitsbedenken wären temporäre Rücksetzer in Richtung der Stop-Loss-Marke von 73,56 EUR nicht ausgeschlossen.

evidence.title: DiaSorin stock slips as ransomware claim and FTSE MIB exit weigh on sentiment
evidence.text:
DiaSorin S.p.A. stock (ISIN IT0003497168) is trading modestly lower on September 4, 2026, with the shares quoted around 75.96 EUR in Milan, down about 1.04% intraday according to market data from Teleborsa and Borsa Italiana.

Index change and cyber incident shape the mood

According to a recent corporate news overview , DiaSorin is set to be replaced in the FTSE MIB index by Technoprobe, reducing its weight in Italy's blue chip benchmark and prompting repositioning by index-focused investors. Market data compiled by Borsa Italiana for September 3, 2026, showed DiaSorin shares at a last value of 76.22 EUR with a price at 75.84 EUR earlier in the session and a daily change of about plus 0.50%, indicating a modest gain before the latest pullback.

Sentiment has also been affected by cybersecurity headlines. On September 3, 2026, ransomware group Settra claimed responsibility for an attack on DiaSorin's infrastructure, specifically referencing the int.diasorin.com domain, as reported by DeXpose cybersecurity monitors . A separate breach listing published on September 3, 2026 and reviewed on September 4, 2026 by GalaxyWarden reiterates that the int.diasorin.com host was included on Settra's list, reinforcing the perception of a targeted cyber incident.

Short-term trading signals and recent price levels

Intraday on September 4, 2026, Teleborsa data show DiaSorin changing hands at around 75.96 EUR, with the session's low and high reported near 75.70 EUR and 77.38 EUR respectively, pointing to a trading range of about 1.68 EUR on the day.

A trading commentary published by Teleborsa on September 4, 2026 highlights that DiaSorin is seen with positive expectations, describing the shares as suitable for purchase at a level of about 76.76 EUR with an indicative stop loss at 73.56 EUR. This implies a potential short-term upside of roughly 3.20 EUR from the stop level to the suggested entry point, a difference of about 4.3% based on these reference prices. For retail investors, such trading signals underline that the stock is currently being watched not only for fundamentals but also for tactical opportunities in a volatile environment.

Recent quote histories compiled by MarketScreener show a closing price of 76.08 EUR for DiaSorin on September 3, 2026 and 73.75 EUR on September 1, 2026, indicating a gain of about 2.33 EUR or approximately 3.2% over these two sessions. Over the last five trading days, MarketScreener data cite a performance of about plus 2.55% for the shares, and a gain of around 12.63% over a longer comparison window, signalling that the current intraday weakness comes after a period of appreciation.

Investors can follow detailed news, regulatory filings and additional figures for DiaSorin stock directly via the DIA SORIN themed overview and the company's Investor Relations portal.

Diagnostics portfolio supports the investment case

DiaSorin is a specialty diagnostics company focusing on immunodiagnostics and molecular diagnostics for infectious diseases, oncology and other clinical areas. Its product range includes reagents and instruments used by hospital and laboratory customers to run tests for conditions such as hepatitis, HIV and other viral and bacterial infections, helping clinicians make timely treatment decisions.

A representative product segment is its molecular diagnostics platform for respiratory pathogens, which contributes to revenue by providing test panels for viruses like influenza and other respiratory agents. Historically, DiaSorin reported that pandemic-related testing had boosted demand in earlier years; investors now pay attention to how the mix shifts towards routine testing and specialized assays as emergency volumes normalise. While up-to-date segment revenue figures for fiscal year 2025 or the latest half-year are not explicitly visible in the current day-filtered search results, the company's established presence in high-value diagnostics supports the longer-term investment narrative.

DiaSorin stock near recent highs in Milan

DiaSorin is listed on Borsa Italiana and included in Italy's FTSE MIB index until its upcoming replacement, with the shares traded in EUR under the ticker typically cited as DIA. Based on Teleborsa and MarketScreener data, the latest completed closing price stands at 76.08 EUR as of September 3, 2026 on the Milan exchange. As of intraday trading on September 4, 2026, the stock is quoted at about 75.96 EUR, placing it slightly below that most recent closing level.

(Il Sole 24 Ore Radiocor) - Il profit warning di Qiagen (in calo di oltre 6 punti a Francoforte) trascina in rosso Diasorin . Così la società di diagnostica quotata a Piazza Affari scivola di circa 3 punti in un FTSE MIB in rialzo. A pesare sulle sue performance sono, come detto, i risultati preliminari di Quiagen, attiva come Diasorin nella produzione di tecnologie per campioni e analisi per la diagnostica molecolare. La società ha chiuso infatti il primo trimestre con ricavi preliminari pari a 492 milioni di euro (+2% reported e -1% a cambi costanti), contro un'attesa di circa 500 milioni di euro, e un utile per azione a cambi costanti di 0,54 dollari, in linea con il consensus.

Ha inoltre tagliato la guidance 2026, con ricavi ora stimati a in rialzo dell'1-2% a cambi costanti (dal +5% precedente e a fronte di un consensus del 5,9%) e un utile per azione di 2,43 dollari (da oltre 2,50 e un consensus pre-warning di circa 2,51). " La debolezza riflette principalmente il crollo della domanda di test per gli esami del sangue QuantiFeron (-5% a cambi costanti), legata ai minori movimenti migratori negli Usa e al difficile contesto in Medio Oriente", spiega Intermonte. Il comparto per l'anno in corso è "atteso flat da circa 503 milioni di ricavi (dall'iniziale previsione del +9% annuo). A questo si aggiunge la "cautela persistente dei clienti Usa" che, sempre secondo la banca d'affari, ha frenato il segmento Life Sciences. Nel secondo semestre dovrebbe però arrivare "un'accelerazione" , secondo quanto ipotizza Qiagen, "grazie al lancio di nuovi prodotti e al miglioramento sequenziale di QuantiFeron".

Per quanto riguarda gli effetti su Diasorin, "il profit warning di Qiagen ha un duplice read-across negativo", spiega Intermonte. Da una parte, c'è infatti la " debolezza persistente del segmento Life Sciences Usa , che genera circa un terzo dei ricavi di Diasorin (circa 15% del fatturato totale)". Dall'altra, il "crollo della domanda sul QuantiFeron, test commercializzato in partnership con DiaSorin".

Questo segmento, secondo gli analisti, contribuisce a circa 100 milioni di ricavi annui per DiaSorin (pari a circa 8% del gruppo), con impatto diluitivo sul margine per via delle royalties pagate dall'azienda tedesca". In più, aggiungono gli esperti, "rappresenta storicamente un driver rilevante per la crescita della divisione Immunodiagnostica (65% del fatturato di gruppo)". Le prospettive rischiano poi di non migliorare per il futuro , dal momento che la debolezza del settore, potrebbe legarsi "alle politiche restrittive sull'immigrazione dell'amministrazione Trump, che potrebbero persistere per tutto il 2026".

evidence.title: NewAmsterdam, Menarini Secure EU Approval for Obicetrapib-Based Ubeslo and Evlarco
evidence.text:
NewAmsterdam Pharma Company N.V. (Nasdaq: NAMS or "NewAmsterdam" or the "Company"), a late-stage, clinical biopharmaceutical company developing oral, non-statin medicines for patients at risk of cardiovascular disease ("CVD") with elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol ("LDL-C"), for whom existing therapies are not sufficiently effective or well-tolerated, along with partner Menarini Group ("Menarini"), today announced that the European Commission (EC) has granted marketing authorization for Ubeslo® (obicetrapib 10 mg monotherapy) and Evlarco® (10 mg obicetrapib plus 10 mg ezetimibe fixed-dose combination) for patients with primary hypercholesterolaemia, both heterozygous familial ("HeFH") and non-familial or mixed dyslipidaemia, marking the first regulatory approval of obicetrapib worldwide.

"The European Commission approval of Ubeslo and Evlarco marks a major milestone for NewAmsterdam as the first regulatory approval of obicetrapib globally, a novel oral therapy, and validates years of work focused on delivering a potential new treatment option for patients who continue to struggle to achieve recommended LDL-C levels despite previously available therapies," said Michael Davidson, M.D., Chief Executive Officer of NewAmsterdam Pharma. "This first-in-class approval reflects the strength of the clinical evidence supporting obicetrapib, the dedication of our team and partners, and our commitment to addressing one of the largest unmet needs in cardiovascular medicine. Together with Menarini, we look forward to bringing Ubeslo and Evlarco to patients across Europe and building on this important milestone as we advance our vision of making obicetrapib available to patients around the world."

The European Commission approval follows the positive opinion adopted by the European Medicines Agency's Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) and is supported by data from NewAmsterdam's comprehensive clinical development program evaluating obicetrapib, including the Phase 3 BROADWAY, BROOKLYN and TANDEM trials, which demonstrated statistically significant LDL-C reductions of up to 40% with obicetrapib monotherapy versus placebo and approximately 50% with obicetrapib combined with ezetimibe versus placebo, with a tolerability profile comparable to placebo. NewAmsterdam and Menarini continue to advance the clinical development of obicetrapib through multiple ongoing Phase 3 trials, including PREVAIL, a cardiovascular outcomes trial, as well as REMBRANDT and RUBENS.

"This approval represents an important advancement for patients across Europe who require additional LDL-C lowering despite available therapies," said Elcin Barker Ergun, Chief Executive Officer of Menarini Group. "We are proud to reach this significant achievement alongside NewAmsterdam and look forward to leveraging our well-established commercial capabilities and deep cardiovascular expertise to bring Ubeslo and Evlarco to healthcare providers and eligible patients throughout Europe."

Under the parties' licensing agreement, Menarini holds exclusive commercialization rights for obicetrapib in Europe and is responsible for regulatory interactions and commercialization activities throughout the region. NewAmsterdam is entitled to tiered double-digit percentage royalties ranging from the low double-digits to mid-twenties on net sales in the Menarini Territory and up to an additional €833 million upon the achievement of various clinical, regulatory and commercial milestones.
