Amgen (AMGN) Stock Pops 4% as Sjögren’s Drug Could Be First of Its Kind

Amgen (AMGN) stock jumped roughly 4% in premarket trading Tuesday, hitting $406.02 just after the open, after the company reported positive topline results from a Phase 3 trial of its experimental Sjögren’s disease drug, dazodalibep.

The trial, called OASIZ 301, met its primary endpoint. Patients showed statistically meaningful improvement in systemic disease activity at Week 48, measured by the EULAR Sjögren’s Syndrome Disease Activity Index (ESSDAI).

The move pushed AMGN back above its 50-day moving average.

The study enrolled around 621 patients with moderate-to-severe systemic Sjögren’s disease. Results showed improvements as early as Week 4, and those gains held through the end of the 48-week period.

Sjögren’s is a systemic autoimmune disease that causes dryness, fatigue, chronic pain, and can affect major organs. There are currently no FDA-approved medicines for the condition.

That gap in the market is a key part of the story here. If dazodalibep clears regulatory review, it would be the first approved treatment for Sjögren’s.

Dazodalibep is a CD40L antagonist fusion protein. It works by disrupting the interactions between T cells, B cells, and other immune cells that drive the disease.

Jay Bradner, Amgen’s head of research and development, said the speed and durability of the results reinforced the company’s confidence in the drug and its broader Phase 3 program.

The most common side effects in the trial were nasopharyngitis, urinary tract infections, hypertension, and infusion-related reactions. Most were mild to moderate. Discontinuation rates due to side effects were low and similar across the treatment and placebo groups.

Amgen is not alone in this space. Novartis (NVS) is also developing a Sjögren’s treatment called ianalumab, which works differently by targeting the BAFF protein.

Ianalumab showed 1.3- to 1-point improvements over placebo on a 42-point symptom scale in its trial. Leerink Partners analyst David Risinger said it is likely to win approval in the coming months.

Risinger rates AMGN stock a market perform.

Amgen plans to present full data from OASIZ 301 at an upcoming medical conference. The detailed readout will give investors a clearer picture of how dazodalibep stacks up against ianalumab.

A second Phase 3 study, OASIZ 303, is looking at dazodalibep in patients with moderate-to-severe symptomatic Sjögren’s disease. That study is expected to wrap up in Q4 2026.

evidence.text:
Amgen's Experimental Drug Shows Benefit in Late-Stage Sjögren's Study

Amgen said Tuesday that its investigational therapy dazodalibep cleared the primary endpoint in a late-stage study of patients with moderate to severe Sjögren's disease. The company reported a statistically significant effect that it also described as clinically meaningful after 48 weeks of treatment, and noted that some participants began to improve within four weeks.

Common side effects reported were swelling inside the nose, urinary tract infections, increased blood pressure, and infusion-related reactions. Jay Bradner, Amgen's EVP responsible for R&D, AI, and data, said the readout "reinforces our confidence in dazodalibep," adding that it supports the broader program for people living with this autoimmune condition.

Analysts say the second pivotal study is vital to gauge the size of the effect, with completion targeted before year end. Should the program hit its goals, Citi analyst Geoff Meacham estimates the drug could ultimately bring in $1.1 billion in annual revenue.

Sjögren's is an autoimmune disorder where the body's defenses attack its own tissues, often the glands that produce tears and saliva, leading to dry eyes, dry mouth, and complications like fatigue and chronic pain. Around 4 million people in the US are affected. Care today centers on easing symptoms with treatments such as eye drops and anti inflammatory medicines because there are no FDA approved therapies for the disease.

Why Is Gilead Sciences (GILD) Widening Lenacapavir Access Across 120 Countries?

Gilead Sciences (NasdaqGS:GILD) expanded its royalty-free voluntary licensing of once-yearly lenacapavir for HIV prevention to 120 high-incidence countries.

The biopharma group signed a regional agreement with the Pan American Health Organization to widen access to twice-yearly lenacapavir across Latin America and the Caribbean.

The PAHO partnership creates a direct pathway for 14 additional countries in the region to obtain lenacapavir for HIV prevention programs.

Gilead's broader licensing of lenacapavir for HIV prevention is one piece investors may want to weigh against the rest of our view on the stock. We have also spotted 2 warning signs worth knowing about at Gilead Sciences.

For readers tracking how large drug developers link infectious disease pipelines with digital tools, it is worth comparing Gilead's latest HIV prevention move to the companies featured in 37 healthcare AI stocks .

Gilead Sciences is a US biopharmaceutical group with a focus on treatments for areas of unmet medical need, so expanding access to an HIV prevention medicine aligns closely with its core infectious disease expertise. The business operates across the US, Europe, and other international markets, which gives it a broad base for public health partnerships like these.

3 things going right for Gilead Sciences that this headline doesn't cover.

The expanded royalty free licenses and the PAHO agreement tilt Gilead Sciences further toward a volume based access model in HIV prevention, especially in low and lower middle income markets. That can support manufacturing scale and brand reach, while relying on partners like Dr. Reddy's and Hetero to handle much of the production and local distribution complexity.

This news lines up closely with the existing Narrative that highlights Yeztugo or lenacapavir access as a key catalyst, and also underlines a listed risk around execution in international PrEP markets. The move strengthens the case that Gilead is leaning into global prevention, while still leaving questions on pricing, reimbursement and long term profitability in these regions.

The clearest test over the next couple of years is whether countries move from agreements to funded rollouts, especially as Phase 3 PURPOSE 365 data matures and PAHO's revolving funds translate into concrete procurement. evidence.title: Citi downgrades Boston Scientific as cyberattack recovery compounds competitive pressure
evidence.text:
Analysts at Citigroup bowed to the uncertainty surrounding Boston Scientific’s (NYSE:BSX) immediate financial future, delivering a downgrade to its stock rating as headwinds in its cardiac business are complicated by its recovery from a major cyberattack last month.

Citi’s researchers have lowered their estimates for the company eight times so far this year, most recently on September 9, after Boston Scientific disclosed it may miss previous financial targets following August 25’s cyberattack that caused a global network outage.

That week Boston Scientific also reported that business operations were restored and it was working through its backlog of product orders, and that the incident no longer impacted the enrollment of new patients in its remote monitoring programs for cardiac device implants, including pacemakers and cardioverter-defibrillators.

However, Citi’s analysts said the company’s key growth drivers still face significant pressure during the wait for new products, such as pending physician reimbursement for its Watchman franchise and increased competition for its Farapulse pulsed field ablation systems.

“For years, BSX has been a steady beat-and-raise stock, and while we are confident that it will work through this, the time to resolution is opaque, investor patience has run thin, and we don’t have a handle on the recovery path,” Citi’s analysts wrote.

The firm moved the company’s rating from buy to neutral and lowered the target price from $57 to $50, adding “while we want to believe that this is the final revision, our level of confidence in that is low and, as we have seen, resolving cybersecurity hangover effects can be protracted.”

Citi said its models predict a 7.6% drop in Watchman sales in the second half of this year, with an 8.8% decline in 2027, and that Farapulse will face an uphill climb through early 2028 when new Farawave catheters are expected to debut.

Still, analysts described Boston Scientific’s future pipeline as robust, pointing to the continuing clinical development of its Tivus ultrasound platform in renal denervation, acquired through its $600 million acquisition of SoniVie in May 2025. They also highlighted the company’s re-entry in TAVR, with its $1.5 billion play this year for valve developer MiRus, though that may take two to three years to garner an FDA approval.

In the shorter term, Boston Scientific delivered positive results this year from a pivotal study of its Seismiq coronary intravascular lithotripsy catheter and has submitted it to the agency for review, with a commercial launch estimated for early next year.

BSX chares are down more than 13% over the past month, trading at nearly $44 apiece. The S&P 500 is down nearly 1%.

evidence.title: Boston Scientific fully restores operations after cyberattack
evidence.text:
Boston Scientific fully restores operations after cyberattack

This story was originally published on MedTech Dive. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily MedTech Dive newsletter .

Boston Scientific has restored its operations weeks after being hit by a cyberattack.

The medical device maker has fully restored manufacturing, order fulfillment and shipping operations, the company said in a Wednesday statement posted to its website. Boston Scientific said that its distribution network is working at or above normal levels as the company fills customer orders and reduces backlogs that have built up over the past few weeks.

"As order processing continues, we are working to fulfill customer orders as quickly as possible, including those pending prior to the August 25 cybersecurity incident and those received during the disruption," Boston Scientific said in the statement. "While some customers may continue to experience temporary delays, we are prioritizing manufacturing and distribution efforts to support ongoing customer demand and minimize the impact on patients and healthcare providers."

Boston Scientific, working with CrowdStrike and other third-party cybersecurity experts, has not identified evidence of ongoing threat activity or evidence of compromise to the company's systems or products since implementing containment procedures on Aug. 25.

Late last month, Boston Scientific disclosed a cyberattack that significantly disrupted its business , taking down manufacturing, order processing and shipping. The company was the latest medical device firm to be hit by a cyberattack this year.

CEO Mike Mahoney said at the Wells Fargo Healthcare Conference on Thursday that "all of our plants were shut down and distribution centers were shut down globally." The CEO added that during the shutdown some procedures were lost due to hospital supply.

"Some areas or some regions or some businesses would have adequate supply, many didn't," Mahoney said. "Hospitals were unsure — as we were at the time — how long it would be, and so some hospitals likely ordered from others during that time, which would be understandable."

Due to the disruptions to its business, the company said earlier this week that it will likely miss third-quarter and full-year sales and earnings guidance. The full impact is still unclear. Mahoney said at the Wells Fargo event that "it's hard to pinpoint that exact dollar amount at this point."

An essential part of understanding the financial impact is figuring out what the recapture rate will be for the business, Mahoney said. Boston Scientific plans to give more specific information on its next earnings call, scheduled for Oct. 28.

Even before the attack, Boston Scientific was having a challenging year. The company has slashed its guidance twice this year due to ongoing struggles for key businesses.

Stifel analysts, in a note to investors earlier this week, wrote that "we suspect that both investors and the stock 'view' 2026 as being something of a lost year for Boston Scientific."

Boston Scientific unlikely to meet guidance due to cyberattack

evidence.title: Boston Scientific continues to make progress on cyberattack recovery
evidence.text:
Boston Scientific (NYSE: BSX) announced on LinkedIn that it has now fully restored manufacturing, order fulfillment and shipping operations after a cybersecurity incident identified on Aug. 25.

In the LinkedIn post, out yesterday, the Marlborough, Massachusetts–based minimally invasive medtech company said: “As order processing continues, we are working to fulfill customer orders as quickly as possible. While some customers may continue to experience temporary delays, we are prioritizing manufacturing and distribution efforts to support ongoing customer demand and minimize the impact on patients and healthcare providers.”

In an accompanying video, CEO Mike Mahoney described the development as a significant milestone.

“Our operating capacity continues to rapidly increase, and our products are moving through our distribution network at or above normal levels,” Mahoney said. “And our teams continue to work around the clock to fulfill customer orders, reduce backlogs, and accelerate the delivery of products to customers and the patients who depend on them the most.

“I’ve talked many times about the winning spirit of Boston Scientific. It’s easy to talk about when things are going well, but moments like this show what it really means. It means staying focused when the path isn’t easy, being agile, helping one another, and doing whatever we can to deliver for patients and customers.”

Earlier this week, Boston Scientific said the cybersecurity incident will make it unlikely to meet previously set full-year guidance . It’s still uncertain when operations will be fully restored.

BSX shares are down more than 8% over the past five days, trading around $43 apiece.

The cybersecurity incident is the latest in a string of cybersecurity incidents that medical device companies have disclosed this year. Earlier this year, an Iran-backed cyberattack effectively wiped out data on Stryker’s Microsoft-based IT system, with the ortho and surgical devices company still working through some after-effects . Medtronic , Intuitive , Novocure , and iRhythm have also reported cybersecurity incidents.

evidence.title: Boston Scientific stock falls as cyberattack prompts guidance cut and BTIG lowers price target
evidence.text:
Boston Scientific stock (ISIN US10117L1017) was trading around USD 44.98 on the New York Stock Exchange as of September 8, 2026, after the company warned that a recent cyberattack will prevent it from meeting its previously issued guidance for the third quarter and full-year 2026, a setback that has drawn a swift reaction from analysts and investors.

Cyberattack forces Boston Scientific to withdraw 2026 guidance

According to Diamatix on September 9, 2026, Boston Scientific reported that a cybersecurity incident identified on August 25, 2026 disrupted key information technology systems and led to a global interruption of operations.

As Diamatix reports, the company now expects a material impact on its results for the third quarter and the full year 2026 and has said it is unlikely to meet its previously issued net sales growth and adjusted earnings per share guidance ranges for 2026.

In a market summary, WXXV News 25 noted on September 9, 2026 that Boston Scientific shares fell about 5.9 percent after the company said the network outage caused by the cybersecurity incident means it is unlikely to meet forecasts for sales and profit for the third quarter and full year 2026.

Previous 2026 guidance now withdrawn ahead of Q3 update

Before the cyberattack, Boston Scientific had provided detailed guidance for full-year 2026. As Simply Wall St summarizes, the company recently guided for full-year 2026 adjusted earnings between USD 3.28 and USD 3.32 per share, with expected sales growth of 5.5 percent to 6.5 percent.

For the third quarter of 2026 alone, Boston Scientific had projected adjusted earnings of USD 0.80 to USD 0.82 per share, according to Simply Wall St .

These guidance ranges are now off the table: Diamatix notes that Boston Scientific has stated it is unlikely to achieve its previously issued net sales growth and adjusted earnings per share guidance for the third quarter and full-year 2026 because of the disruption.

Analyst BTIG cuts price target but keeps Buy rating

The cyber incident and guidance withdrawal have already prompted a notable analyst reaction. On September 9, 2026, BTIG lowered its Boston Scientific stock price target from USD 60.00 to USD 56.00 while maintaining a Buy rating on the shares, according to MarketBeat .

As GuruFocus explains, BTIG maintained its Buy rating on Boston Scientific but reduced the price target by about 6.67 percent, from USD 60 to USD 56, reflecting a more cautious stance on near-term performance while still seeing upside.

BTIG’s new target of USD 56 implies roughly 24.4 percent potential upside from the company’s current share price level cited in the analyst report, per MarketBeat .

Consensus targets still well above current share price

Despite BTIG’s cut, the broader analyst community continues to see Boston Scientific stock as undervalued. Based on data compiled by MarketBeat , Boston Scientific has an average rating of Moderate Buy with a consensus 12-month price target of USD 71.46.

This consensus target of USD 71.46 stands significantly above the roughly USD 44.98 share price cited in recent valuation commentary, implying more than 50 percent upside if the stock were to reach the average target, according to figures highlighted by GuruFocus .

Another overview from Simply Wall St shows a current average one-year price target of about USD 76.48, with individual analyst estimates ranging from USD 55.00 on the low end to USD 106.00 on the high end.

Operational recovery and key risks after the cyber incident

While the cyber incident has clearly increased near-term earnings uncertainty, Boston Scientific is working to restore operations. As Diamatix reports, major distribution centers are now processing and shipping orders at or above normal operating levels, sterilization facilities are operational and manufacturing has resumed across most of the company’s global facilities.

The company’s update also indicated that product quality analyses had not identified impairment to device function and that a disruption affecting activations for remote monitoring of certain cardiac devices had been resolved, meaning activations can resume, according to Diamatix .

An additional clinical perspective from Omnicuris on September 9, 2026 notes that comprehensive internal product assessments confirmed no impairment to physical device integrity or software code and that rigorous quality audits verified complete product sterility, meaning healthcare providers can continue to use Boston Scientific implants and consumables without concern over manufacturing defects related to the incident.

Stock valuation and recent performance metrics

The guidance withdrawal and cyberattack have weighed on Boston Scientific stock performance. A recent performance snapshot from Simply Wall St cites a Boston Scientific share price of about USD 45.29, with analysts estimating an average one-year target of USD 76.48, suggesting the stock trades at a discount to perceived fair value.

In a separate options-focused analysis, Trefis notes on September 9, 2026 that Boston Scientific shares are trading near USD 45 and sit about 58 percent below their 52-week peak, highlighting how sharply the stock has pulled back from earlier highs.

That same analysis from Trefis illustrates the discount by pointing to an approximate USD 44.98 share price compared against a 52-week high around USD 108, underscoring the magnitude of the drawdown that long-term investors have experienced.

Next earnings update expected in late October

Investors will get more clarity on the financial impact of the cyberattack when Boston Scientific reports its third-quarter 2026 results. As summarized by Simply Wall St , the company plans to provide an updated outlook when it releases Q3 results, which market commentary currently expects around October 28, 2026.

Until that update arrives, the combination of withdrawn guidance, a significant recent share-price decline of around 58 percent relative to the 52-week high and mixed analyst reactions, including BTIG’s price-target cut, is likely to dominate the narrative for Boston Scientific stock.

Boston Scientific stock price and exchange reference

Boston Scientific stock is primarily listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker BSX. Recent market data cited in analyst and valuation overviews place the shares around USD 44.98 to USD 45.29 as of September 8, 2026, with the stock trading well below the consensus 12-month analyst price target range between USD 55 and USD 106.

New additions advance surgical planning, implant flexibility and connected care across Stryker's Foot & Ankle portfolio

PORTAGE, Mich. , Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Stryker (NYSE: SYK ), a global leader in medical technologies, announced today that it will showcase new advancements across its Foot & Ankle portfolio at the 2026 American Orthopaedic Foot & Ankle Society (AOFAS) Annual Meeting in Seattle, including the launch of Prophecy Surgical Planning for the Incompass Total Ankle System and the introduction of Hoffmann LRF smartHEX.

Prophecy has established itself as an important surgical planning tool in ankle surgery, processing more than 100,000 1 cases over the past 14 years. Now available with Incompass, Stryker's comprehensive total ankle replacement system, Prophecy enables surgeons to leverage this depth of experience through patient-specific surgical planning, enhanced 3D planning tools, and both resect-through and pin-through fixation options. The addition of Prophecy Surgical Planning further strengthens the connection between preoperative planning and implant selection, enabling surgeons to make more informed decisions.

Expanding beyond total ankle replacement, Stryker will also introduce Hoffmann LRF smartHEX, the newest advancement in its limb reconstruction portfolio. The platform combines expanded frame options, mobile guidance and updated planning software designed to support complex deformity correction. Through the mobile application, smartHEX creates a connection between patients and their surgeon-prescribed correction plan, bringing patient guidance, surgeon planning and correction capabilities together throughout treatment.

"AOFAS gives us an important opportunity to demonstrate how Stryker is building on decades of foot and ankle experience, customer insight and data," said Jacobs. "By bringing Prophecy Surgical Planning to Incompass and introducing Hoffmann LRF smartHEX, we are continuing to connect planning, implants and reconstruction technologies in ways that give surgeons more flexibility across the continuum of foot and ankle care."

evidence.title: Stryker still working through cyberattack after-effects, stock down more than 10% this week
evidence.text:
Stryker (NYSE: SYK) stock plunged this week after its CFO said the orthopedic and surgical device giant is still managing supply disruptions after an Iran-backed cyberattack earlier this year .

SYK shares are down more than 10% over the past five days, trading at around $273 apiece, though the stock was up more than 1% today.

During a Sept. 8 presentation at Wells Fargo’s 21st annual healthcare conference, held in Boston, CFO Preston Wells said Stryker’s peripheral vascular business, acquired last year through the $4.9 billion purchase of Inari Medical , hadn’t recovered as company officials expected. The business involves catheter-based mechanical thrombectomy devices.

“As we talked about at the end of last year, we obviously had some sales force execution things that we were working through as we were kind of bringing the sales force up to a Stryker standard. We got that to a point in the first quarter that we felt really good about where that was headed only to have the cyber event. … Our manufacturing was taken down for several weeks. We brought that back up. And for all of our existing businesses, it’s just a process of restarting. You restarted back on the processes that you have and … you’re off and running. On the peripheral side, … there’s a lot of process things that have to still get improved as that business is able to ramp and scale. And so as we think about integrations for us and we integrate manufacturing, you’re always going to run into some things over time.”

Stryker now expects to rectify peripheral vascular business challenges the fourth quarter of 2026, according to Wells. The company had previously said it planned to work through issues by the third quarter.

William Blair analysts led by Steven Lichtman described the peripheral vascular problems as among a number of incremental headwinds described during Stryker’s Wells Fargo presentation. “The integration of the legacy Inari manufacturing facility into Stryker’s system is taking longer than expected, with the setback of the March cyberattack having ripple effects. Management talked about a potential 70- to 80-basis-point impact to third-quarter sales (about $45 million on our estimate).”

evidence.title: Siemens Healthineers, Novo partner to expand non-invasive liver fibrosis testing in MASH
evidence.text:
Siemens Healthineers (XETRA: SHL) and Novo announced a collaboration to expand awareness and non-invasive blood-based testing for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and its progressive form, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). The partnership centers on deploying Siemens Healthineers' Enhanced Liver Fibrosis (ELF) test alongside Novo's cardiometabolic disease reach to drive earlier patient identification and reduce reliance on liver biopsy. Financial terms were not disclosed.

The ELF test is an in vitro diagnostic blood-based assay that quantifies three extracellular matrix remodeling biomarkers — hyaluronic acid, procollagen III amino terminal peptide, and tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinases 1 — to stratify risk of advanced fibrosis progression in MASH patients. Siemens Healthineers describes the ELF test as the first blood test authorized in the US to support clinician assessment of disease progression risk in patients with advanced fibrosis due to MASH. The test carries a Category 1 CPT code (81517) and is available through major national laboratory providers, with results unaffected by body composition parameters such as BMI.

Under the collaboration, both companies will conduct disease awareness activities, support earlier assessment pathways, and promote adoption of non-invasive testing (NIT) approaches across the healthcare continuum. Novo contributes its standing in cardiometabolic medicine — including its US-approved obesity drug semaglutide (Wegovy), which received approval to treat noncirrhotic MASH with moderate to advanced liver fibrosis — while Siemens Healthineers provides diagnostic infrastructure and laboratory solutions.

The deal extends a pattern of Siemens Healthineers building MASLD-focused alliances ahead of an anticipated expansion in MASH treatment uptake. Days before this announcement, Siemens Healthineers Korea signed a separate memorandum of understanding with Boehringer Ingelheim Korea on blood biomarker-based liver health screening in patients with obesity and metabolic diseases. Siemens Healthineers is also a founding member of the MASLD Diagnostic Coalition , a multistakeholder group established in February 2026 and financially supported by Novo focused on advancing non-invasive diagnostics access.

evidence.title: Siemens Healthineers and Novo Partner to Expand Blood-Based Testing for MASLD and MASH
evidence.text:
Siemens Healthineers and Novo Partner to Expand Blood-Based Testing for MASLD and MASH

Sep 21, 2026 | Company News , Diabetes & Metabolic Diseases |

The collaboration aims to broaden clinical access to non-invasive diagnostics like the ELF blood test to detect liver disease before serious complications develop.

Siemens Healthineers and Novo have announced a collaboration focused on advancing care for patients living with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and its progressive form, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) . The organizations are engaged in several initiatives to strengthen disease awareness, support earlier clinical assessment, and expand patient access to non-invasive blood testing.

According to the companies, MASLD affects millions of people worldwide, including nearly a quarter of US adults, and is closely associated with obesity, type 2 diabetes, and cardiovascular disease. Furthermore, the announcement noted that MASLD has become the leading indication for liver transplant among women, with healthcare costs associated with the condition projected to exceed $635 billion by the end of the decade. Although the condition is reversible if detected early, silent progression and low disease awareness have left many individuals undiagnosed until significant liver damage develops.

“Too often, liver health flies under the radar,” says Michele Zwickl, head of laboratory solutions for Siemens Healthineers North America, in a release. “People deserve the same level of awareness as for other major diseases, creating a better opportunity to intervene before serious complications develop.”

Expanding Access to Non-Invasive Testing

Historically, clinical assessment of liver fibrosis has relied heavily on specialized imaging equipment or invasive procedures such as liver biopsy, which are not widely accessible to patients, according to the release. While clinicians recognize that liver biopsy remains necessary for certain individuals, consensus has grown around the role non-invasive tests play in the broader management of MASLD and MASH.

The collaboration seeks to advance solutions that make disease assessment more accessible across the healthcare continuum, including increasing the adoption of non-invasive testing approaches to provide diagnostic insights while reducing reliance on invasive biopsies.

Among these diagnostic options is the Enhanced Liver Fibrosis (ELF) test from Siemens Healthineers, which is the first and only blood test authorized in the US to help clinicians assess the risk of disease progression in patients with advanced fibrosis due to MASH and guide patient management decisions, according to the companies. The test is available through major national laboratory providers and covered by Category 1 CPT code 81517. In addition to supporting high patient testing volumes, blood-based testing avoids failure rates and unreliable results associated with certain other non-invasive modalities; for example, ELF test results are not impacted by patient body composition characteristics such as BMI.

“Earlier triage is one of the most important opportunities to improve the future of MASH care,” says Michelle Long, senior international medical director for MASH at Novo, in a release. “Our collaboration recognizes that patients, clinicians, laboratories, health systems, and industry partners all have a role to play in creating a more effective pathway for liver disease assessment and management.”

evidence.title: Elekta stock holds steady as margins and turnaround plan stay in focus
evidence.text:
Elekta stock (ISIN SE0000163628) has been trading at a relatively steady level on Nasdaq Stockholm in mid September 2026, with investors focusing less on short-term price swings and more on the company’s turnaround story and efforts to improve margins and cash generation as of September 20, 2026.

Margins remain central to Elekta’s turnaround

The Stockholm-based cancer care technology group has been working for several quarters to lift profitability in its core radiation therapy equipment and software business, with recent interim figures for its latest reported quarter showing revenue growth paired with ongoing pressure on operating margins compared with the prior year period, according to data summarized on investor portals in September 2026.

In the most recent fiscal year reported within the past two years, Elekta posted higher full-year revenue than the preceding year, but the operating margin remained in the single-digit range, underlining that the company still has some way to go before reaching the double-digit margin levels targeted in its strategic plan; historical context from the prior fiscal year shows that revenue increased by a mid-single-digit percentage while the margin only improved by around one percentage point year on year.

Order intake, cash flow and competitive landscape

Alongside margins, Elekta’s turnaround has also emphasized stabilizing order intake and strengthening free cash flow, with the latest quarterly report indicating that net sales in the most recently reported quarter grew versus the same period a year earlier and that cash flow before financing improved compared with the historical performance of the company in the fiscal year two years ago.

The company operates in a concentrated global market for radiation therapy and oncology software, where large projects, public tenders and hospital investments can cause volatility from quarter to quarter; in the last reported financial year, Elekta’s order bookings increased compared with the previous year, but delays in installations and supply chain constraints had an impact on revenue recognition and profitability, which is why management’s focus has shifted strongly toward execution, efficiency and service revenue.

Analyst focus on valuation and execution risk

Recent analyst commentary compiled on financial portals in September 2026 points out that Elekta’s valuation reflects both its solid installed base and recurring service revenues and the execution risk associated with delivering on its margin and cash flow targets, with some houses emphasizing that any disappointment versus guidance on operating margin or cash conversion could weigh on Elekta stock even if revenue growth remains intact.

Conversely, the same overviews show that analysts see scope for upside if Elekta can convert its strong pipeline of orders into higher-margin revenue and sustain double-digit growth in software and service offerings, since this would support a re-rating of the shares relative to peers in the broader medical technology sector and potentially narrow the valuation gap compared with competitors that already deliver higher operating margins and more robust free cash flow.

On Nasdaq Stockholm, Elekta stock continues to trade in Swedish krona at a level that is broadly in line with its quotations earlier in September 2026, leaving the shares neither near a 52-week high nor close to a 52-week low and underscoring the market’s wait-and-see stance on the company’s ability to expand margins and strengthen cash generation as of mid September 2026.

evidence.title: Elekta AB Data Breach
evidence.text:
On August 30, 2026, the extortion group shinyhunters claimed to have targeted Elekta AB, a Swedish organization operating within the healthcare sector. The claim was accompanied by significant credential exposure, including 15 records related to employee Microsoft 365 accounts, external records, and third-party integrations such as Marketo, Concur, and Hightail. The earliest captured credentials date back to April 30, 2024, suggesting a substantial period of potential compromise before the leak-site listing. shinyhunters asserted unauthorized access to Elekta AB’s systems and data, though no independent verification of these claims has been completed as of the reporting date. Over the preceding 60 days, shinyhunters has claimed 24 victims, with a notable concentration on entities in the US and Israel, and a primary focus on the Technology and Healthcare industries. Elekta AB, as a healthcare organization based in Sweden, aligns with the group’s typical sector targeting. The group maintains a moderate operational tempo with consistent targeting logic, suggesting their activities are methodical and predictable within their chosen victimology.

SOCRadar CTI’s analysis of stealer-log data indicated a severe exposure in the sampled data for Elekta AB. The telemetry identified two employee Microsoft 365 credentials, two external records, and eleven corporate third-party credentials linked to platforms such as Marketo, Concur, and Hightail. The timestamps for these exposed credentials range from April 30, 2024, to August 25, 2026, indicating that this data has been available for over two years prior to the threat actor’s claim. The identified credential exposure, specifically concerning employee M365 accounts, external records, and third-party service credentials, presents a potential pathway for unauthorized access. While the exact intrusion method used by shinyhunters is not confirmed, such exposed credentials could facilitate initial access, lateral movement, or privilege escalation within Elekta AB’s environment. This data could be leveraged to gain access to corporate systems, potentially enabling ransomware deployment or data exfiltration. Given the detected credential exposure and the threat actor’s claim, it is recommended that Elekta AB conduct a thorough review of its security posture. This includes continued monitoring of dark web and stealer-log feeds for any further exposure, proactive credential hygiene checks, and immediate password rotation for all potentially compromised accounts. A review of multi-factor authentication (MFA) enforcement, alongside monitoring of Microsoft 365, VPN, and remote-access portal activity, is also advised to detect and mitigate any ongoing or potential future compromise attempts.

This report is intended for threat intelligence and security awareness purposes. SOCRadar does not host, redistribute or buy stolen data. evidence.title: Elekta to work with academics on AI-directed radiotherapy
evidence.text:
Elekta to work with academics on AI-directed radiotherapy

Radiotherapy specialist Elekta has joined forces with two academic groups in the Netherlands to explore the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to deliver more effective personalised therapy to patients.

The Swedish company will collaborate with scientists at the Netherlands Cancer Institute and University of Amsterdam (UvA) on a project that aims to use AI to improve the quality of imaging used to direct radiotherapy and guide the delivery of treatment.

While commercial vendors and academic institutions have created AI tools for radiation oncology, none have yet been widely adopted by clinicians in clinical practice.

The initiative – dubbed the Partnership for Online Personalized AI-driven Adaptive RT (POP-AART) – is focusing on adaptive radiotherapy, which changes to account for internal anatomical changes that occur over the weeks and months that can elapse during treatment.

This a great challenge that should be a part of every treatment session, because the patient and the tumour are continuously in motion and change shape over time, said Elekta, adding that in the past this has been impossible to achieve due to "computational and workflow complexities".

AI and machine learning promises to overcome that obstacle, according to Jan-Jakob Sonke, group leader of adaptive radiotherapy at UvA.

"Not only is it our ambition to create incredibly innovative AI algorithms – we also want to make sure that they can be applied to clinical practice so patients can receive even better treatment," he said.

That means giving patients the right dose of radiation, at the right spot, with the least damage to surrounding healthy tissue.

The POP-AART lab – led by Sonke and UvA associate professor on computer vision and deep learning Efstratios Gavves – has six PhD students working on the same number of research topics.

Two are focusing on developing models that can improve the quality of images provided by cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) and aid in their interpretation, while two more will look at using deep learning (DL) to combine different images to improve accuracy (registration) and separating healthy from tumour tissue (segmentation).

The final two projects will concentrate on AIs that can predict the best dose distribution for particular anatomies and to optimise radiation treatment plans.

The POP-AART lab has been backed by a grant from the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO).

evidence.title: Elekta Executive: AI, Adaptive Radiotherapy Could Transform Cancer Care in Africa
evidence.text:
Home » Headlines » Elekta Executive: AI, Adaptive Radiotherapy Could Transform Cancer Care in Africa

Elekta Executive: AI, Adaptive Radiotherapy Could Transform Cancer Care in Africa

After arriving in Morocco from India for her first GITEX, Swati Sharma said software is becoming essential to closing cancer care gaps across Africa.

Swati Sharma, head of software at Elekta for Turkiye, India, the Middle East, and North Africa

Casablanca — Swati Sharma, head of software at Elekta for Turkiye, India, the Middle East, and North Africa, believes that artificial intelligence and software are becoming critical tools for cancer care in regions where access to treatment remains uneven, particularly across Africa and other low and middle income countries.

Speaking during a DigiTalk podcast project by Morocco World News recorded at GITEX Future Health Africa Morocco 2026, Sharma said software can help reduce geographical barriers that often prevent patients from receiving timely care.

“It helps you break those geographical and language barriers,” she said during the interview.

Sharma, who is based in Delhi, traveled to Morocco with her team from India for what she described as her first GITEX experience. She said Morocco had surprised her during earlier visits because of the warmth of the people and the familiarity many Moroccans have with Indian culture and Bollywood films.

At the conference, Sharma delivered a keynote focused on how AI and software are transforming oncology and radiotherapy. She said the discussion drew a mixed audience of clinicians, biomedical students, startup founders, and healthcare professionals interested in health tech.

According to Sharma, many African countries are seeing cancer cases rise faster than healthcare systems can expand treatment capacity. She said software is increasingly being used to close part of that gap by connecting hospitals, specialists, and expertise across borders.

Research in the field reflects that shift. Adaptive radiotherapy, one of the technologies Sharma discussed during the interview, is being developed to adjust cancer treatment in real time according to changes in a patient’s anatomy and tumor response.

Elekta’s adaptive radiotherapy systems, including its Unity MR-Linac and Evo CT-Linac platforms, are designed to combine imaging and treatment delivery with AI-assisted workflows. The company says these systems aim to improve precision while reducing unnecessary radiation exposure to healthy tissue.

Sharma said adaptive radiotherapy is one of the technologies healthcare workers should pay close attention to because oncology is moving toward more personalized and targeted treatment.

“When you adapt your treatment protocols to your patient’s anatomy, you are in a way giving targeted treatment,” she said.

Studies published in recent years have shown growing interest in MRI-guided adaptive radiotherapy, particularly for difficult cancer cases where tumors move or change shape during treatment. Researchers say the technology may help improve treatment accuracy and reduce side effects.

Read also: Mamabox Brings AI-Powered Maternal Support at GITEX Future Health Africa 2026

During the interview, Sharma repeatedly returned to the issue of accessibility.

She recalled her early experience as a radiotherapy technologist in India, where one of the first cancer patients she treated was a 13-year-old girl from a remote Himalayan tribal area who had to travel long distances by helicopter to receive care. The patient later died after interruptions in treatment linked to complications and access difficulties.

“That is what we are trying to change,” Sharma said. “We have to be closer to the patients.”

She added that software allows expertise to move without forcing patients to travel. Hospitals and specialists in different countries can collaborate remotely, share treatment protocols, and support facilities with fewer trained professionals.

The shortage of oncology specialists remains a major issue globally. The World Health Organization has repeatedly warned about widening cancer care gaps in lower income countries, where access to radiotherapy, screening, and specialized doctors remains limited.

Sharma also pushed back against concerns that AI could replace healthcare workers. She described AI as a support tool rather than a substitute for doctors.

“It is not going to replace anyone,” she said. “It would actually take away those repetitive tasks so that you get more time with the patients.”

She said doctors in many developing healthcare systems spend large portions of their day dealing with administrative systems and computer work instead of patient interaction.

For Sharma, the broader goal remains improving patient outcomes regardless of whether the work comes from clinicians, engineers, or software teams.

“At the end of the day,” she said, “we have to have a better patient health plan.”

evidence.title: Elekta AB: Report from the Annual General Meeting 2026 of Elekta
evidence.text:
Elekta AB: Report from the Annual General Meeting 2026 of Elekta

Elekta AB (publ) has held its Annual General Meeting on September 3, 2026. The statement at the Meeting from the CEO and President will be available on Elekta's website, www.elekta.com . Documents from the Meeting with complete details concerning all resolutions are also available on the website.

A summary of the resolutions made by the Meeting follows.

Accounting documents and discharge from liability The Meeting resolved to discharge the Directors, as well as those who have held the position of CEO and President, from liability for the financial year of 2025/26, after the income statements and balance sheets for the Parent Company and the Group were adopted.

Dividend and disposition of the Company's earnings The Meeting resolved, in accordance with the Board of Directors' proposal, on a dividend corresponding to SEK 2.40 per share and that the remaining profits are carried forward. The dividend is to be divided into two payments of SEK 1.20 per payment.

The first record day is September 7, 2026. The second record day is March 5, 2027. The dividend is expected to be paid out on September 10, 2026, and on March 10, 2027, respectively.

Board of Directors The Meeting resolved, in accordance with the Nomination Committee's proposal, to reelect Laurent Leksell, Ann Costello, Jan De Witte, Tomas Eliasson, Jan Kimpen, Wolfgang Reim, Jan Secher, Volker Wetekam and Cecilia Wikström, and to elect Cecilia Felton, as Directors for the period until the end of the next Annual General Meeting. Laurent Leksell was reelected as the Chairman of the Board of Directors.

The Meeting resolved, in accordance with the Nomination Committee's proposal, that the remuneration to the Board of Directors shall be increased in relation to the previous year.

Auditor The Meeting resolved, in accordance with the Nomination Committee's proposal, to reelect Ernst & Young AB as the Company's Auditor for the period until the end of the next Annual General Meeting, with the authorized Auditor Jakob Wojcik as the Auditor in charge. Furthermore, the Meeting resolved, in accordance with the Nomination Committee's proposal, that the fee to the Auditor shall be paid according to an invoice approved by the Company.

The Board of Directors' Remuneration Report The Meeting resolved, in accordance with the Board of Directors' proposal, to approve the Board of Directors' Remuneration Report.

Acquisition and transfer of own shares The Meeting resolved, in accordance with the Board of Directors' proposal, to authorize the Board of Directors during the period until the next Annual General Meeting, on one or several occasions, to resolve on acquisition of such number of Series B shares that the Company, after the acquisition, holds no more than ten percent of the total number of shares in the Company.

Furthermore, the Meeting authorized the Board of Directors, in accordance with the Board of Directors' proposal, during the period until the next Annual General Meeting, on one or more occasions, to resolve on the transfer of own Series B shares in conjunction with the financing of any company acquisitions or other strategic investments, to cover costs related to the Company's share-related incentive programs and to adjust the company's capital structure. The amount of shares transferred may, however, not exceed the number of Series B shares held by the Company at the time of the Board of Directors' resolution on the transfer.

Long-term performance-based share program for 2026 The Meeting resolved, in accordance with the Board of Directors' proposal, on the adoption of a long-term performance-based share program for 2026 (" PSP 2026 "), and on the transfer of own shares in conjunction with PSP 2026.

The program includes the CEO and President and other members of the Executive Committee, senior executives within the Group's extended management team and additional selected key individuals, in total no more than 30 employees. The program entitles to allocation, free of charge, of Series B shares in Elekta following three years after the start of the program, provided continued employment in the Group and the fulfilment of certain performance targets. The maximum number of Series B shares that can be allotted is dependent on the degree of fulfilment of four performance targets, (i) total shareholder return (" relative TSR ") compared to the OMXSPI index, (ii) revenue growth (" Revenue growth "), (iii) operating margin (" EBIT% ") and (iv) reduction of CO2 equivalents from the operations.

For the PSP 2026, the minimum performance requirement regarding the relative TSR target is that Elekta's relative TSR outperforms the OMXSPI Index by at least +3 percent, and the maximum requirement is that Elekta's relative TSR outperforms the OMXSPI Index by at least +15 percent. The minimum requirement for the Revenue growth target is that Elekta's compounded average growth rate amounts to at least 4 percent, and the maximum requirement is that Elekta's compounded average growth rate amounts to at least 7 percent. The minimum requirement for the EBIT% target is that Elekta's operating margin, under certain assumptions, amounts to at least 14 percent in the last year of the relevant period, and the maximum requirement is that Elekta's operating margin, under the same assumptions and time period, amounts to at least 16 percent. For the target concerning reduction of CO2 equivalents, the minimum requirement is that emissions from Elekta's operations are decreased by at least 38 percent during 2026-2029, compared to the base year 2021-22, and the maximum requirement is a decrease by at least 40 percent.

Before the number of shares to be allocated is finally determined, the Board of Directors shall assess whether the allocation is reasonable in relation to the Company's financial results and position, conditions on the stock market and other relevant circumstances. The Board of Directors shall also be entitled to make other adjustments if there are significant changes in the Group or its external environment that result in the terms and conditions for allocation under PSP 2026 no longer being appropriate.

The total costs for PSP 2026, at maximum allocation of performance shares, are estimated at not more than SEK 84.8 million. The costs have been calculated as the sum of the salary costs, including social and administrative costs for the program. Administrative costs have been estimated to amount to less than SEK 1 million. If no allocation of performance shares is made, only administration costs will arise.

Furthermore, the Meeting resolved, in accordance with the Board of Directors' proposal, on the transfer of not more than 1,533,619 Series B shares, with deviation from the shareholders' preferential rights, to participants in the PSP 2026, in order to ensure the delivery of performance shares in accordance with the terms of PSP 2026.

Contribution to Elekta Foundation The Meeting resolved, in accordance with the Board of Directors' proposal, on a contribution to Elekta Foundation of up to SEK 10,000,000. Elekta Foundation was established by the Annual General Meeting's resolution on August 25, 2021, with the objective of improving access to, and quality of, cancer care with special focus on radiotherapy.

For further information, please contact: Peter Nyquist, Head of Investor Relations Tel: +46 70 575 2906, e-mail: Peter.Nyquist@elekta.com Time zone: CEST (Central European Summer Time)

About Elekta Elekta is shaping the standard of care, together with healthcare providers, by developing precision radiation medicine that brings advanced radiotherapy into routine clinical practice. Our solutions support consistent, efficient and personalized care, addressing evolving patient needs. Through adaptive radiotherapy, precision treatment delivery and integrated workflows, Elekta supports care teams across a range of clinical settings. Each year more than 2 million patients are treated using Elekta solutions across 130 countries. Elekta is headquartered in Stockholm, Sweden, with over 4,000 employees and offices in more than 40 countries. The company is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. For more information, visit elekta.com.

evidence.text:
Getinge transforms sterile reprocessing with Automatiq - a full range of logistic automation modules

Getinge is unveiling Automatiq, a new family of next generation automated solutions designed to help Central Sterile Supply Departments (CSSDs) achieve safer, more consistent and less labor-intensive sterile reprocessing. Automatiq seamlessly combines smart robotics, intelligent conveyor systems and advanced software to optimize sterile reprocessing and enhance workflow efficiency at every step.

CSSDs play a vital role in infection prevention and represent one of the most precise and physically demanding processes in the hospital. During traditional manual processes, CSSD professionals encounter ergonomic challenges and repetitive handling, which can cause delays, strain, and errors. Automatiq supports these essential functions to improve reliability, save valuable time, and empower CSSD professionals to focus on other critical priorities.

TORONTO , Nov. 25, 2025 /CNW/ - SteriPro International Inc. , Canada's leading provider of outsourced medical device reprocessing services, today announced a strategic partnership with Getinge USA Sales, LLC that aims to reinforce safer workflows and deliver a scalable model for the future of surgical services within Sterile Processing departments across North America.

The partnership brings together two complementary strengths: SteriPro's deep expertise in operating large-scale off-site reprocessing centers and Getinge's proven leadership in sterile processing equipment, automation, and digital workflow solutions. Working together, the companies will provide hospitals with a more complete, end-to-end pathway for optimizing sterile processing--from designing and operating high-performance off-site centers to integrating technology that supports full visibility, traceability, and efficiency across the instrument lifecycle.

By combining SteriPro's operational model with Getinge's technology portfolio, the collaboration is designed to help healthcare facilities raise quality, increase transparency, and achieve meaningful cost efficiencies while building a more resilient sterile processing infrastructure across North America.

"Partnering with Getinge is a catalyst for scaling SteriPro's off-site reprocessing center model through a growing network of Reprocessing Centers of Excellence," said Ajay K Jain, Managing Partner, SteriPro International Inc. evidence.title: IQVIA and Swedish Orphan Biovitrum’s PNH Study: A Potential Game-Changer for Pegcetacoplan
evidence.text:
IQVIA and Swedish Orphan Biovitrum’s PNH Study: A Potential Game-Changer for Pegcetacoplan

IQVIA Holdings ( (IQV) ), Swedish Orphan Biovitrum Ab ( (GB:0MTD) ) announced an update on their ongoing clinical study.

IQVIA Holdings and Swedish Orphan Biovitrum are collaborating on a clinical study titled ‘A Single Arm, Long-term, Multicentre Observational Study to Evaluate Effectiveness of Pegcetacoplan Under Real World Conditions in Patients With Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria (PNH).’ The study aims to assess the real-world effectiveness of pegcetacoplan, a treatment for PNH, over a period of up to 72 months. This research is significant as it seeks to provide comprehensive data on the long-term impact of pegcetacoplan in a real-world setting.

The study focuses on the drug pegcetacoplan, which is intended to treat patients with Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria (PNH). Pegcetacoplan is administered as per its label to evaluate its effectiveness and safety in real-world conditions.

This observational study follows a cohort model, collecting both retrospective and prospective data. The primary purpose is to gather information on the effectiveness and safety of pegcetacoplan, alongside patient and clinician-reported outcomes and healthcare resource usage.

The study commenced on February 20, 2023, and is currently recruiting participants. The primary completion and estimated study completion dates are not specified, but the last update was submitted on May 9, 2025. These timelines are crucial for tracking the study’s progress and ensuring timely data collection.

The update on this study may influence investor sentiment positively, as successful outcomes could enhance the market position of Swedish Orphan Biovitrum and IQVIA Holdings. The study’s results could potentially impact stock performance, especially if pegcetacoplan proves to be effective, offering a competitive edge in the PNH treatment market.

The study is ongoing, and further details are available on the ClinicalTrials portal.

evidence.title: EnBW opens flagship charging site with XCharge hardware
evidence.text:
EnBW opens flagship charging site with XCharge hardware

EnBW has opened a flagship charging site with twelve fast-charging points at its headquarters in Karlsruhe. The site uses new XCharge C7 chargers and will also serve as a testbed for charging technology, construction methods and amenities at future charging sites.

The publicly accessible charging park is located at EnBW’s headquarters at the junction of Gerwigstrasse and Ostring in Karlsruhe’s Oststadt district. The initial twelve high-powered charging points can eventually be expanded to up to 20. This means EnBW has kept to the schedule it announced when construction began in June, when commissioning was planned for autumn.

One notable feature is the charging hardware used. At the Karlsruhe site, EnBW is deploying XCharge’s new-generation C7 fast charger with up to 480 kW for the first time in regular operation.

EnBW had already announced the Karlsruhe charging park in June as its first own site with charging capacity of up to 480 kW, although it did not name the manufacturer at the time. Shortly afterwards, XCharge announced that the upgraded C7 would be used at the site. Until now, the maximum charging power of the fast chargers deployed across the EnBW network had been 400 kW.

From ten test chargers to 480-kW rollout

The installation in Karlsruhe follows a longer testing phase for XCharge technology at EnBW. In August 2025, the first C7 entered real-world operation at EnBW City in Stuttgart. In December , the field test was expanded to a total of ten XCharge fast chargers at four locations in Baden-Württemberg. At the time, these generated up to 400 kW power.

At the start of 2026, EnBW and charging infrastructure manufacturer XCharge signed a long-term framework agreement. This followed the field test, which had involved more than 20,000 charging sessions. In March, however, the focus was still said to be on fast chargers with 400 kW ‘and potentially more’. In June, XCharge finally unveiled the upgraded C7 with charging power of up to 480 kW.

“With the new C7, we have introduced a product to the European market that reliably meets the demanding technical requirements of charging network operators and their customers”, said XCharge Europe chief Albina Iljasov. “The new 480 kW charging technology will primarily be deployed at locations where customers typically spend only a short time and want to add as much driving range as possible during their stop—for example, at EnBW fast charging parks along Germany’s major highways”, adds Lars Jacobs, Chief Commercial Officer and acting technical head of EnBW’s e-mobility division.

Additionally, EnBW plans to equip a ‘double-digit’ number of fast-charging parks with the 480-kW technology by the end of 2026. However, the energy company has not yet named any specific additional locations.

A reference site for construction and operation

The new XCharge hardware is only one aspect of what is intended to make the Karlsruhe site a reference charging park. EnBW also wants to test new solutions for the construction and operation of charging parks there. Its location directly next to the company’s headquarters and its charging laboratory is useful for this purpose: new charging technology can first be tested under laboratory conditions and then operated under real-world conditions at the publicly accessible charging park.

EnBW is also taking a different approach to the site’s design. According to the company, the new canopy is largely made from sustainably certified timber. When construction began in June, EnBW announced a partial canopy with a PV capacity of 16 kWp. As the company told electrive , this has also been implemented. The glass canopy with integrated PV modules typically associated with EnBW is therefore not being used here.

The construction site itself also served as a testbed. According to EnBW, it used electric construction machinery as well as machines powered by alternative fuels. A local solar and storage system supplied parts of the construction site with electricity. According to general contractor Leonhard Weiss, this helped save up to 50 tonnes of CO2 compared with a conventionally operated construction site.

The reference concept also includes the design of the charging break. The site is accessible around the clock and features an automated toilet facility as well as vending machines for drinks, coffee and snacks. There are also seating areas. A pizza vending machine is planned to be added in future.

The site is therefore not intended solely as a testbed for new charging technology. In Karlsruhe, EnBW also wants to gain experience with the design of charging sites and additional amenities. Such facilities are not entirely new for the company, however: EnBW already operates small Rewe-to-go stores at some locations, while toilet facilities are also available at other charging parks.

According to the company, EnBW now operates more than 9,000 of its own fast-charging points in Germany. When the XCharge framework agreement was announced at the beginning of March, the figure was still more than 8,000. And the expansion will continue. EnBW says it is systematically expanding its fast-charging network in line with demand, with the aim of providing up to 20 per cent of the fast-charging points needed in Germany by 2030.

EnBW Energie Baden-Württemberg AG stock (ISIN DE0005220008) closed at EUR 25.10 on Xetra on September 18, 2026, up 0.4% versus the prior session and leaving the shares around EUR 1.40 or 5.3% below their 52-week high of EUR 26.50 as of that date. As of September 21, 2026, the company is also in the spotlight for its majority stake in the newly inaugurated He Dreiht offshore wind farm, described as Germany’s largest offshore wind project and a key asset for strengthening security of supply.

Stock trades in upper part of recent range

According to a Xetra trading overview referenced in a German market report on September 21, 2026, EnBW Energie Baden-Württemberg AG stock finished the session of September 18, 2026 at EUR 25.10, after trading between an intraday low of EUR 24.80 and an intraday high of EUR 25.30, so the closing price came close to the top of that day’s range. Ad-hoc-news notes that this close represented a daily gain of 0.4% compared with the prior day’s finish, while the broader DAX index slipped by about 0.1% on the same trading day, meaning EnBW modestly outperformed the blue-chip benchmark on that date.

The same report states that EnBW’s Xetra-listed shares remained EUR 1.40 or roughly 5.3% below their 52-week high of EUR 26.50, a level that provides a nearby reference point for investors monitoring whether the stock can retest its recent peak. Ad-hoc-news also reports that about 320,000 EnBW shares changed hands on Xetra on September 18, 2026, roughly in line with the stock’s recent average daily volume, suggesting steady trading interest rather than a sudden surge or drop in investor activity.

Offshore wind farm underscores renewables strategy

As an additional operational catalyst, EnBW has underscored its role in the newly inaugurated He Dreiht offshore wind farm, which is described as Germany’s largest offshore wind project and an important contribution to the country’s energy transition and supply security. Energy-pedia reports on September 21, 2026 that EnBW holds 50.1% of the project via a dedicated project company, while the remaining 49.9% is owned by a consortium including Allianz Global Investors on behalf of Allianz entities, AIP Management and Norges Bank Investment Management, so EnBW maintains a controlling stake in the asset.

This majority position in He Dreiht fits into EnBW’s broader strategy of expanding offshore wind and other renewable capacity, which the company and sector observers see as key to replacing conventional generation and supporting grid stability. Pravda notes that the utility ranks among Germany’s largest energy companies, operating in power and gas supply, network infrastructure and renewable projects, particularly wind and solar, and emphasizes that the completion of a record-scale wind farm strengthens both national renewable output and EnBW’s position in the offshore segment.

An overview of European utilities’ analyst coverage dated September 21, 2026 shows that, within that sample, no formal consensus rating or explicit price target range is listed for EnBW at the time of the snapshot, whereas peers such as RWE have multiple active investment bank targets in EUR terms. Finanzen.net lists several price objectives for RWE, for example EUR 68.00 from UBS and EUR 75.00 from Jefferies, but in its section for EnBW the table shows zero Buy, Hold or Sell ratings and no average target price, highlighting how coverage intensity can differ significantly even among large utilities.

For investors tracking the sector, that contrast means EnBW’s stock narrative is driven more by company-specific developments such as project milestones and financial reporting than by frequent target changes from major banks, whereas peers with dense analyst coverage may see their share prices respond more immediately to rating and target updates. Finanzen.net still includes EnBW in its utilities list, however, which underlines the company’s importance in the European power sector despite the absence of a consolidated consensus figure in that specific overview.

Ad-hoc-news In that frame, the closing price stood nearer the top than the bottom of the annual band, which can be interpreted as a sign that the market has already priced in a portion of the company’s current project pipeline and operating performance.

On the same trading day, EnBW’s performance relative to the DAX index, combined with its trading volume of about 320,000 shares, suggests that the stock is neither excessively volatile nor illiquid under normal conditions, which may be relevant for retail investors and institutional portfolios seeking exposure to German utilities with a meaningful transition agenda. evidence.title: Uniper Reserves 40,000 Tons of eSAF Annually From Danish ENDOR Project
evidence.text:
Uniper has signed a long-term purchase agreement with Arcadia eFuels covering the future production of synthetic aviation fuel (eSAF) from the ENDOR project, located in Vordingborg, Denmark. The agreement, announced jointly on September 23, 2026, and signed in Düsseldorf, covers 40,000 metric tons of eSAF per year for more than ten years, according to the companies' joint statement. Deliveries are expected to begin in the early 2030s, subject to preconditions and the plant's entry into commercial operation.

A commitment conditioned on ENDOR's start-up

The joint statement describes this purchase commitment as legally binding. However, it makes the start of deliveries contingent on preconditions agreed between the parties, meaning the signing does not constitute an actual fuel delivery. For Arcadia eFuels, the agreement provides a commercial outlet that could help finance and build the ENDOR project. For Uniper, it opens access to supply aimed at the European market, which is underpinned by regulatory obligations on sustainable fuels.

Production combining renewable electricity, hydrogen and captured CO2

According to Arcadia eFuels, eSAF production will combine renewable electricity, on-site hydrogen and captured carbon dioxide. The two companies cite a potential reduction of up to 98% in lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions compared with conventional kerosene. The statement does not, however, detail the methodology used to establish this performance for the volumes actually under contract. The volume reserved for Uniper would be equivalent, according to the companies' estimate, to the fuel needed for around 1,000 annual flights of a Boeing 787-9 between Düsseldorf and Abu Dhabi.

An evolving European regulatory framework

The European ReFuelEU Aviation regulation requires fuel suppliers to make minimum shares of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) available at covered airports across the European Union. It also sets a specific sub-target for synthetic fuels, built around an average calculated over a given period alongside annual minimums. The ENDOR project has also secured a grant agreement under the EU Innovation Fund, confirmed by the European Commission. Arcadia eFuels nonetheless states it is still working toward a final investment decision, which has not yet been taken.

Uniper, a publicly owned company, expands its synthetic fuels portfolio

Uniper remains overwhelmingly owned by the German federal state. The agreement with Arcadia eFuels thus involves a publicly owned company in building a supply of synthetic aviation fuels, whose industrial scale, actual timeline and certified fuel characteristics still need to be documented. The signing took place in Düsseldorf, in the presence of Mona Neubaur, Minister for Economic Affairs of North Rhine-Westphalia, and Anette Galskjøt, Consul General of Denmark in Hamburg. The public support obtained and the purchase contract with Uniper strengthen the commercial framework of the ENDOR project, without guaranteeing at this stage that it will be built or brought into service.

evidence.title: Uniper workers back IPO as Germany advances utility privatisation
evidence.text:
Uniper workers back IPO as Germany advances utility privatisation

As Germany steps up plans to reduce its holding in Uniper, labour representatives are pushing for an initial public offering instead of a sale to a strategic buyer. They argue that a stock market listing would better preserve the state-owned utility's structure, jobs and operating sites as the divestment process gathers pace.

Privatisation options and bidder interest

Geilhorn says worker representatives fear a buyer could split up the company, cut jobs and shut sites. He says recent roadshows indicate investor interest in Uniper shares, while two people familiar with the matter say early meetings to test appetite for an IPO have gone well.

Geilhorn adds that a sale to strategic investors such as EPH would be unacceptable. Two people familiar with the matter say EPH, owned by Czech billionaire Daniel Kretinsky, is among parties that submit indicative bids for Uniper by a September 21 deadline, while Canada's CPPIB and Brookfield also submit a joint indicative bid. CPPIB and Brookfield decline to comment. State stake and market implications Uniper remains a politically sensitive asset after receiving a 13.5 billion euro bailout during Europe's energy crisis in 2022. The company could be valued at around 10 billion euros in what may become one of Europe's biggest utility transactions this year.

Berlin owns 99.12% of Uniper and has announced plans to sell up to 74.12% of the company, while retaining a 25% plus one-share blocking stake in the systemically important utility. That structure leaves the government with continued influence even as it pursues privatisation, and keeps the outcome important for Germany's energy sector and for employment at the group.

Our earlier coverage of Europe’s power sector turning back to coal explained how surging gas prices disrupted generation economics and pushed utilities—especially in Germany—to run coal and lignite more, with limited flexibility after nuclear closures. We noted that this shift could persist beyond winter, highlighting the strategic pressure on systemically important assets as policymakers balance affordability, supply security, and the energy transition.

evidence.title: Uniper secures synthetic jet fuel supply deal with Arcadia eFuels
evidence.text:
Uniper secures synthetic jet fuel supply deal with Arcadia eFuels

As aviation faces mounting pressure to cut emissions, Uniper is expanding its position in sustainable fuels through a long-term procurement agreement for synthetic jet fuel. The deal covers 40,000 metric tons annually for more than 10 years from a Denmark-based project, with deliveries expected from the early 2030s.

Long-term supply agreement for Denmark project

The fuel is to be supplied from Arcadia eFuels' Endor project in Denmark. The agreement provides for annual volumes of 40,000 metric tons over more than a decade.

Uniper Chief Executive Michael Lewis said the main challenge is now to move sustainable aviation fuels from promising projects to industrial scale. He added that the agreement is also an important step in building a strong position in a market with significant growth potential. EU aviation fuel rules support market growth Aviation remains one of the hardest sectors to decarbonise, making lower-emission fuels one of the few available options to reduce pollution from air travel. Arcadia eFuels Chief Executive Amy Hebert said eSAF is already a practical response to the industry's need to diversify supply and that the agreement brings expanded production in the EU closer.

Supplies are expected from the early 2030s and would equal the fuel needed for about 1,000 Boeing 787-9 flights a year from Duesseldorf to Abu Dhabi, according to the companies. EU rules required 2% of fuel made available at regional airports to be sustainable aviation fuel in 2025, rising to 6% in 2030, while eSAF must make up 1.2% of the total from 2030 and 5% from 2035.

Our earlier coverage of EU carbon market (ETS) changes explained how member states are seeking to reduce energy-cost volatility by adjusting the market stability reserve for CO2 permits. The agreed approach would keep more spare allowances in the reserve and delay cancellations until 2030, with a new, higher cancellation threshold starting in 2031—measures intended to cushion sharp price swings while final negotiations with the European Parliament continue.

evidence.text:

El Rey Felipe con Ignacio Galán en la inauguración de la exposición Iberdrola

Iberdrola muestra los orígenes y el futuro de la electricidad en una exposición inmersiva en Madrid

Bajo el título Un viaje electrizante: experiencia inmersiva Iberdrola, la muestra recorre la evolución de la tecnología eléctrica

​El Rey inaugura la exposición 'Un viaje electrizante', organizada por Iberdrola en su 125 aniversario

Bajo el título Un viaje electrizante: experiencia inmersiva Iberdrola , la compañía energética ha organizado una muestra en Madrid que recorre la evolución de la tecnología eléctrica desde sus orígenes y permite adentrarse en el futuro través de una experiencia inmersiva e interactiva que combina innovación y divulgación.

La exhibición, en el Palacio de Cibeles , invita a descubrir los principales hitos que han marcado la historia de la electrificación, desde los primeros descubrimientos científicos hasta las últimas innovaciones tecnológicas, y muestra a través de contenidos virtuales cómo serán las ciudades del futuro en la «era de la electricidad».

La muestra incluye piezas originales de gran valor histórico y tecnológico, un recorrido con gafas de realidad mixta y talleres educativos para acercar la electricidad e impulsar las vocaciones científicas en las nuevas generaciones.

A través de la trayectoria de Iberdrola, la exposición permite también conocer algunos de los grandes hitos que han marcado la historia del sector eléctrico, desde las primeras centrales hasta la expansión de las energías renovables, las redes inteligentes, el almacenamiento energético y la electrificación de la demanda.

La exposición forma parte del programa « 125 años luz », con el que Iberdrola celebra durante 2026 sus 125 años de historia mediante iniciativas dirigidas a empleados, clientes, accionistas y al conjunto de la sociedad.

Las entradas, gratuitas, se pueden conseguir mediante reserva online en entradas.com y en taquilla.
