evidence.title: How ArcelorMittal Is Reinventing the Steel Sector
evidence.text:
Posts Technologies ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih Print 316 22 September 2026

How ArcelorMittal Is Reinventing the Steel Sector

Innovation at ArcelorMittal sets new benchmarks for technological sophistication across the global steel industry

ArcelorMittal is a long-standing leader and was once the world’s largest steel producer. But as excess capacity engulfed global markets, economies of scale ceased to offer meaningful benefits. The company pivoted toward efficiency, divesting a number of assets and prioritizing intensive growth over extensive expansion.

Today ArcelorMittal ranks second in global steel output, yet remains the undisputed technology leader. And in the modern industrial landscape, technological leadership carries far more weight than simply producing the next ton of steel.

ArcelorMittal’s technological edge manifests across three pillars: product innovation, green transition, and digitalization.

The company invests approximately $300 million annually in R&D, with $335 million allocated in 2025. More than 1,650 researchers work across 14 centers in 9 countries. Its patent portfolio exceeds 16,000, with 128 newly protected inventions in 2025 alone.

Roughly one-third of ArcelorMittal’s R&D budget is directed toward developing new products for the automotive industry. Of its 14 research centers, 6 are dedicated to automotive applications.

The automotive sector is driving demand for advanced steel products through tightening emissions and fuel economy regulations, rising consumer expectations for safety, and an industry-wide push for lightweighting across the entire value chain.

ArcelorMittal commands a leading share of the automotive market (approximately 16% globally) and ranks as a top player in the fast-growing advanced high-strength steel (AHSS) segment.

Today the company produces steels with strengths up to 2,000 MPa – a stark contrast to the 340 MPa maximum available just 20 to 25 years ago.

The flagship automotive portfolio centers on three core pillars: ultra-high-strength steels for body structures, innovative solutions for electric vehicles, and sustainable production methods.

Usibor® and Ductibor® are designed for hot stamping. Usibor® enables component weight reduction of 40–50% while delivering strengths of 1,500-2,000 MPa. These grades are used in structural elements for body strengthening and passenger safety.

Fortiform® is a family of third-generation advanced high-strength steels (3rd Gen AHSS) for cold stamping, with tensile strengths of 980, 1,050, and 1,180 MPa, reducing component weight by 10-20%.

The iCARe® electrical steel range is engineered to enhance electric motor efficiency.

In response to growing demand for sustainable solutions, ArcelorMittal launched the XCarb® recycled and renewably produced line. These are the same flagship grades (notably Usibor® 1500), but manufactured using 75% scrap and 100% renewable electricity, cutting the carbon footprint by nearly 70%.

S-in motion® offers a comprehensive suite of engineering solutions and technology platforms for automakers. In effect, customers receive pre-validated calculations, 3D configuration models, and crash-test results, enabling rapid integration of new steel grades into future vehicle architectures. S-in motion® solutions can reduce body-in-white weight by 20-26%.

ArcelorMittal is the first steel company in the world to embed its own engineers within an automotive customer’s organization to provide direct engineering support.

ArcelorMittal also supplies advanced steel solutions for the construction industry. In 2025, the company introduced 22 new products to support sustainable building and energy infrastructure.

Magnelis® is an innovative metallic coating with a distinctive self-healing property. When the steel is cut or scratched, the protective layer effectively “heals” the exposed edges, halting corrosion entirely. The coating consists of a zinc-aluminum-magnesium alloy containing 3% magnesium and offers a warranty of up to 25 years.

For wall sandwich panels, the iQ+ System® product family delivers 15% higher thermal resistance at the same panel thickness compared to standard solutions.

Amstrong® Ultra – ArcelorMittal’s range of ultra-high-strength steels (UHSS), combines excellent formability with low-temperature toughness and fatigue resistance. As a superior alternative to conventional structural steels in the 460 MPa yield strength range, these grades enable manufacturers to reduce steel thickness and weight, generating material cost savings.

HISTAR is a high-strength, low-alloy structural steel produced using ArcelorMittal’s patented QST (Quenching and Self-Tempering) thermal treatment technology. Unlike conventional steels, where yield strength decreases with increasing thickness, HISTAR profiles maintain consistent high performance – even at element thicknesses up to 125 mm. Replacing standard S355 steel with HISTAR 460 can reduce the total weight of columns and heavy trusses by roughly 24-50%, depending on load conditions, significantly alleviating foundation loads.

ArcelorMittal is fully engaged in developing solutions for the green energy transition, offering more than just steel.

Helioroof® – the company’s flagship product launched in October 2025, is a fully integrated insulated steel roof with embedded solar elements. A dedicated production line was built at the Contrisson plant in France, featuring state-of-the-art automation and quality control. The product represents five years of development and stands as a powerful example of the shift from materials supplier to integrated engineering provider: steel plus energy.

In the renewable energy space, Magnelis® long-lasting coating combined with Hyper® high-strength steels has become the material of choice for lightweight solar mounting systems. Heavy coating weights of up to 800 g/m² and Hyper® grades with yield strengths up to 700 MPa were introduced to the market for customer testing in 2025.

The company is also working on solutions for the hydrogen economy, electricity grids, carbon capture, storage and utilization, and bioenergy.

ArcelorMittal Europe was the first in the EU to announce its carbon neutrality target in 2050, setting a benchmark for the global steel industry.

In June 2020, the company detailed its climate goals in its inaugural Climate Action Report, outlining two pathways: Smart Carbon solutions (CCS/CCU) and DRI-based production. A portfolio of R&D initiatives was launched, covering all promising technologies, including steel electrolysis. Projects such as Steelanol, Carbon2Value, Everest, Initiate, H2 Hamburg, and Siderwin helped refine iron- and steelmaking processes.

The most significant progress came from the Steelanol project, focused on CCU application in Ghent, Belgium. Commissioned in 2022, the plant became the first in Europe to produce ethanol from CO₂ and CO captured from blast furnace gases. LanzaTech’s technology converts carbon in gases into valuable feedstock for the chemical industry or fuel. The facility has a nameplate capacity of 80 million liters of ethanol per year. Despite its technical success, the project’s economic viability remains uncertain due to European regulatory ambiguity: the ethanol produced is not classified as «advanced biofuel,» preventing emissions reductions from being credited. Favorable regulatory changes could unlock the project’s full potential.

Current plans target a 10% reduction in carbon intensity (Scope 1+2) across the ArcelorMittal group by 2030, from a 2018 baseline. The company is already on track, having reduced carbon intensity by 4.1% in 2025 relative to 2018.

Up to 2030, primary progress will be driven by constructing electric arc furnaces in Gijón (1.1 Mt) and Dunkirk (2.0 Mt), as well as capacity expansion in Sestao, while DRI-based production will only become economically viable later. The carbon intensity of EAF-produced steel in Dunkirk after project completion will be 0.6 t CO₂ per tonne (Scope 1+2).

A new global trend set by ArcelorMittal is steelmakers’ investment in renewable generation. The company operates 1.9 GW of generating capacity in India, Brazil, and Argentina, primarily developed with partners. Another 1.4 GW of renewable projects are in the pipeline.

ArcelorMittal also contributes to standardizing low-carbon products to level the playing field. Through its XCarb® umbrella brand, the company offers two product types:

ArcelorMittal’s technology transformation strategy extends beyond internal R&D centers to deep integration with the global startup ecosystem. The key vehicle is the XCarb® Innovation Fund, launched in 2021. With an investment portfolio exceeding $280 million, the fund strategically finances breakthrough technologies at the intersection of industrial decarbonization, alternative energy, capable of accelerating not only ArcelorMittal’s own climate commitments but also the decarbonization of the broader global steel industry.

Beyond direct investments, the fund launched the XCarb® Accelerator Programme to source and support early-stage startups worldwide.

The company continues R&D in ironmaking processes. The Volteron™ iron electrolysis project successfully operated a 1:1 vertical cell pilot. Engineering for a full-scale industrial plant has been completed, demonstrating the technology’s techno-economic feasibility.

In 2025, the R&D team validated the techno-economic feasibility of green blast furnace top gas recycling using oxygen on a pilot blast furnace in Germany – one of the initiatives for decarbonizing the blast furnace route.

In 2025, ArcelorMittal continued deploying advanced models to improve the energy efficiency of reheating furnaces. These solutions have been industrialized across 23 furnaces at 19 plants, delivering significant reductions in energy consumption.

ArcelorMittal’s product leadership is no accidental – it is the outcome of digital innovation. AI Augmented Product Development (AAPD) has accelerated the development of selected automotive and industrial steel grades, cutting design time by up to five times, speeding time-to-market, and accelerating patent analysis.

In 2025, ArcelorMittal spearheaded a strategic initiative called Accelerate Digital Innovation (ADII), aimed at accelerating the adoption of AI and digital solutions across production facilities. Six plants were carefully selected to represent diverse geographies and production lines (both flat and long products) for accelerated digital deployment.

Additional projects continue to advance across a range of areas:

In 2025, the Sestao plant implemented an AI model to improve the segmentation of different materials within ferrous scrap. This innovation enhances sorting precision and supports the production of high-quality steel from recycled inputs.

At ArcelorMittal Pecém in Brazil, sensors and cameras integrated with AI-driven data and image analysis are improving sinter plant reliability by anticipating critical failures, reducing downtime while boosting efficiency and process safety.

In 2025, ArcelorMittal introduced new AI-enabled tools to enhance safety performance. The following examples illustrate the range of risks AI now helps address – from site-wide hazards to highly specific, task-related exposures.

At Tubarão, Brazil, the iRedZone approach analyzes live video feeds to identify workers entering hazardous zones, enabling faster alerts and interventions than human monitoring alone. iMoveSafe – a new fatigue monitoring system was implemented at Vega, Brazil, strengthening protection in safety-critical roles. At Dofasco, Canada, AI-trained fire recognition models provide earlier detection of smoke or flames.

Several of the company’s expansion plans are extensively modeled in advance using a combination of AI and mathematical optimization, ensuring accurate representation of new investments across diverse business scenarios.

evidence.text:
ArcelorMittal (ENXTAM:MT) Faces Ukraine Disruption As Its Valuation Case Looks Narrower

ArcelorMittal (ENXTAM:MT) is back in focus after another missile strike hit its Kryvyi Rih facility in Ukraine. The incident halted primary steel production and pushed much of the plant to minimum operating levels.

Despite the disruption in Ukraine, ArcelorMittal's share price has held at €63.24, with a 90‑day share price return of 9.37% and a much stronger year to date move of 58.66%. The 1‑year total shareholder return of 118.06% points to momentum that has been building rather than fading.

After a 118.06% 1 year total return and fresh operational risk in Ukraine, the key question now is straightforward: Does ArcelorMittal still offer valuation headroom, or has most of the upside already been reflected in the share price?

Most Popular Narrative: 5.1% Undervalued

ArcelorMittal's most followed narrative pegs fair value at €66.61, a touch above the €63.24 last close, which leaves only modest implied upside once risks and execution hurdles are considered.

Strategic decarbonization projects and investments in green steel are positioning the company to benefit from premium demand and expanding margins. Major expansion in India and Brazil, where steel demand is structurally growing due to continued infrastructure development and urbanization, will increase shipped volumes and profitable market share, benefitting top-line revenue and normalized profitability.

See why 27 investors see ArcelorMittal as 5% undervalued .

Analysts in this leading narrative framework use a 7.68% discount rate and arrive at a fair value of €66.61, only 5.1% above the current share price and close to the €66.73 consensus price target. The message is that most of the assumed improvement in earnings, margins and capital allocation is already in the model, even if the share price still sits at a discount to that fair value estimate.

The same outlook leans on revenue growth assumptions of about 6.2% a year, profit margins rising from 2.9% to 7.6%, and earnings expanding from about $1.8b to $5.7b by 2029. That path also embeds a future P/E of roughly 12.5x. This is lower than both the current 30.2x and the present sector multiple used in the narrative, implying the story depends on higher earnings doing more of the heavy lifting than a lofty valuation multiple.

For readers weighing today's missile-related disruption in Ukraine against this structured view, the key tension is clear. The widely followed narrative assumes project execution, decarbonization spending and capacity shifts in regions like India and Brazil progress broadly in line with plan, while trade policy, global overcapacity and capital intensity do not materially derail the earnings path that underpins that €66.61 figure.

Result: Fair Value of €66.61 (UNDERVALUED)

Still, the missile damage in Ukraine and the heavy cash demands of decarbonization projects could easily upset the neat earnings path that analysts have mapped out for ArcelorMittal.

Another Angle On ArcelorMittal's Valuation

The first narrative leaves ArcelorMittal looking only modestly undervalued. The market multiple tells a different story. The current P/E of 30.4x is more than double the European metals and mining group on 14.5x, and still below a fair ratio of 35.4x that our model suggests the market could move toward. That combination points to a stock where optimism is already embedded, even if the model still flags theoretical upside. This raises the question of how comfortable you are with paying this kind of premium for future execution.

evidence.title: Moeve and ArcelorMittal Launch Green Steel Platform
evidence.text:
Energy group Moeve and steel company ArcelorMittal have established a joint public-private innovation alliance to accelerate the decarbonization of European heavy industry. Operating under the Green Molecules to Green Steel (G2G) framework, the equal-share partnership will establish a dedicated technological platform aimed at making clean-energy steel production commercially viable.

The platform will combine the research capabilities of both companies to scale the application of green hydrogen, biomethane, biogas, and second-generation biofuels across steelmaking operations.

By combining private capital with public support—including backing from regional innovation agency Sekuens in Asturias, Spain—the initiative will also develop carbon capture technologies, biotechnological solutions, and artificial intelligence models for advanced materials.

Designed as an open innovation hub, the ecosystem will collaborate with universities, technology centers, and start-ups to enhance industrial competitiveness while advancing Europe’s broader energy transition.

“Given the complexity of the challenge, we cannot tackle it alone. Now more than ever, we must focus on collaborative innovation models, and this platform is an excellent example of this. We need to continue exploring technologies that enable production to be sustainable from both an environmental and an economic perspective, and to do so as soon as possible,” said Pinakin Chaubal , Vice President, and Chief Technology Officer, ArcelorMittal.

“This partnership strengthens the collaboration between two global groups committed to innovation, decarbonization, and Europe’s competitiveness. The initiative will enable us to develop new solutions and make progress towards greater European energy independence. This is the direction Moeve is taking, through investments and new projects that will enable us to play a leading role in the energy transition,” said Maarten Wetselaar , CEO, Moeve.

evidence.title: Norsk Hydro Brasil nomeia Eduardo Lutz como novo diretor de comunicação
evidence.text:
A Norsk Hydro Brasil anunciou a chegada de Eduardo Lutz para o cargo de diretor de comunicação. O executivo assume a liderança da área com a atribuição de consolidar a narrativa de sustentabilidade e gerir a reputação institucional da companhia no mercado nacional, reforçando os desdobramentos e debates industriais do pós-COP30, conferência realizada em Belém (PA).

Lutz retorna ao país após uma temporada na sede global do grupo em Oslo, na Noruega, onde exercia a função de head global de marca e posicionamento. Com mais de 15 anos de atuação no mercado B2B, o profissional acumula bagagem nos setores de mineração, metais, energia e óleo e gás, com passagens por multinacionais como GE e Baker Hughes. “O Brasil está no centro do debate global sobre uma transição energética justa, e a Hydro tem legitimidade única nessa conversa. Operamos de norte a sul do país, com uma atuação que combina descarbonização, geração de empregos e desenvolvimento das comunidades onde estamos presentes — da mineração e refino no Pará à extrusão no Sul. Vamos dar profundidade a esse posicionamento e mostrar, com transparência, tanto os avanços quanto os desafios”, destaca Eduardo Lutz.

A nomeação ocorre em um momento de maior exposição pública e institucional da empresa no país. A visibilidade impulsionada pelas pautas da COP30 na região amazônica serviu de pano de fundo para a veiculação de campanhas institucionais em âmbito nacional, a exemplo de ações estreladas pela cantora Fafá de Belém sobre as operações e projetos sociais mantidos pela Hydro no estado do Pará.

A multinacional Smollan, especializada em soluções para o varejo e inteligência de trade marketing , anunciou a contratação de Lilian Carelli para o cargo de consultora estratégica de shopper marketing e desenvolvimento de categorias na operação brasileira. O movimento visa expandir a oferta de inteligência de mercado e eficiência de execução nas gôndolas para marcas e varejistas.

Graduada pela PUC-SP e pós-graduada pela Fundação Getulio Vargas (FGV), a executiva reúne uma trajetória profissional de mais de três décadas na América Latina. Sua experiência inclui liderança nas áreas de trade em companhias do setor alimentar e de bens de consumo, a exemplo de Unilever, Kimberly-Clark, PepsiCo e Grupo Pão de Açúcar, além de reconhecimentos do setor como o Prêmio POPAI.

Na nova função, Carelli atuará no desenvolvimento de projetos de gerenciamento de categoria, diagnósticos de comportamento do comprador, pesquisas de campo e estratégias de ponto de venda (PDV).

“Não basta entender o que o cliente compra, é preciso compreender como ele escolhe e o que influencia essa decisão. A execução é onde a estratégia ganha vida. Quando categoria, shopper e operação são trabalhados de forma integrada, construímos soluções muito mais aderentes à realidade do varejo”, destaca Lilian Carelli.

BFerraz reforça lideranças de planejamento e criação para consolidar metodologia baseada em ecossistemas de marca

A BFerraz, ecossistema de brand experience e promoção integrante da rede Biosphera.ntwk, anunciou novidades em sua estrutura executiva para acelerar o desenvolvimento do conceito de Brand Systems . O movimento abrange a contratação de Lara Basso como diretora de criação e o retorno de José Gil, conhecido no mercado como Zé Gil, no cargo de head de estratégia e diretor de planejamento.

A reestruturação visa integrar a análise estratégica à inteligência criativa, alinhando-se ao posicionamento Beyond Experience adotado pela agência. A premissa metodológica defende que as ativações presenciais deixem de ser tratadas como episódios isolados e passem a funcionar como plataformas de relacionamento contínuo, articulando dados, cultura, comunidade e conversão em jornadas de pré, durante e pós-evento.

Lara Basso, que acumula passagens pela Atenas e pela TM1, passa a dividir o comando da criação ao lado de Diogo Bonaparte. Na frente de inteligência, Zé Gil regressa à casa após período na agência Bullet, assumindo a gestão da equipe de planejamento com o objetivo de mapear comportamentos de consumo e oportunidades em territórios culturais.

Ambos os executivos passam a integrar o núcleo de produto da empresa sob a gestão direta de Enricco Benetti, sócio, chief executive officer (CEO) e chief creative officer (CCO) da BFerraz.

“Estamos evoluindo nosso pensamento de Brand Systems porque acreditamos que o valor de uma experiência não termina quando ela acaba. O momento ao vivo é um ponto de intensidade, mas precisa fazer parte de algo maior: um sistema capaz de gerar desejo antes, criar conexões durante e transformar essa atenção em comunidade, relacionamento e conversão depois. É assim que entendemos o Beyond Experience. A chegada da Lara e o retorno do Zé fortalecem a integração entre estratégia e criação para construir esse pensamento desde a origem de cada projeto”, conceitua Enricco Benetti.

Com as novas nomeações, a agência busca consolidar o modelo que transforma ativações temporárias em ativos estruturais para a reputação e o crescimento comercial das marcas atendidas por seu portfólio.

evidence.title: Norsk Hydro: RBC stuft auf Sector Perform ab und senkt Kursziel auf 100 NOK
evidence.text:
RBC bewertet Norsk Hydro nun nur noch mit Sector Perform. Damit rechnet das Analysehaus offenbar nicht mehr mit einer überdurchschnittlichen Entwicklung der Aktie gegenüber dem Vergleichssektor. Gleichzeitig wurde das Kursziel von 120 NOK auf 100 NOK reduziert. Die Anpassung entspricht einer Senkung um 20 NOK beziehungsweise 16,7 Prozent.

Die Einstufung Sector Perform ist nicht mit einer Verkaufsempfehlung gleichzusetzen. Sie signalisiert vielmehr eine erwartete Entwicklung im Rahmen des Sektors. Eine konkrete Begründung für die Abstufung und die Kurszielsenkung liegt in den vorliegenden Angaben nicht vor.

Am 16. September 2026 um 07:47 Uhr wurde Norsk Hydro an der Lang & Schwarz Exchange mit 7,712 Euro gehandelt. Die Aktie gab im Tagesverlauf 0,8 Prozent nach. Auf Jahressicht bleibt die Bilanz mit einem Kursplus von 16,99 Prozent jedoch deutlich positiv.

Analysten-Einordnung: Dies deutet darauf hin, dass sich das Chancen-Risiko-Verhältnis aus Sicht von RBC verschlechtert hat, ohne dass daraus automatisch ein struktureller Abwärtstrend folgt. Für Anleger bedeutet diese Entwicklung vor allem, dass die bisher erwartete Outperformance der Aktie neu bewertet werden muss. Ein direkter Vergleich des Kursziels in NOK mit dem Börsenkurs in Euro ist wegen des unterschiedlichen Währungsformats nicht aussagekräftig.

Die Abstufung erhöht kurzfristig den Bewertungsdruck auf Norsk Hydro, ändert aber nichts daran, dass die Aktie seit Jahresbeginn deutlich im Plus liegt. Entscheidend für die weitere Kursentwicklung werden die operative Geschäftsentwicklung, die Aluminiumpreise und die nächsten Unternehmenszahlen sein. Bis dahin dürfte der Markt insbesondere prüfen, ob die Kurszielsenkung eine vorsichtigere Sektorprognose oder unternehmensspezifische Risiken widerspiegelt.

evidence.title: Norsk Hydro Aktie fällt: J.P. Morgan stuft wegen Gasrisiken in Brasilien ab
evidence.text:
Norsk Hydro Aktie fällt: J.P. Morgan stuft wegen Gasrisiken in Brasilien ab

Investing.com - Die Aktien von Norsk Hydro ASA (OL:NHY) fielen am Freitag um 3 %, nachdem J.P. Morgan die Aktie von "Overweight" auf "Neutral" herabgestuft und sie im Vorfeld der Ergebnisse für das dritte Quartal auf "Negative Catalyst Watch" gesetzt hatte. Als Grund wurden Unsicherheiten bei der Erdgasversorgung und den damit verbundenen Kosten in der Aluminiumoxid-Raffinerie Alunorte in Brasilien genannt, die ein Abwärtsrisiko für das EBITDA im vierten Quartal darstellten.

Das Brokerhaus senkte sein Kursziel für Dezember 2027 von 116 norwegischen Kronen auf 97 norwegische Kronen je Aktie, was einem potenziellen Aufwärtspotenzial von etwa 7 % entspricht.

Norsk Hydro hatte am 11. August bekannt gegeben, dass eine Unterbrechung der Erdgaslieferungen durch den Lieferanten CELBA, der zur New Fortress Group gehört, zu einer vorübergehenden Drosselung der Kapazität in Alunorte um 50 % führte, bevor die Raffinerie am 13. August wieder ihre volle Kapazität erreichte.

Das Unternehmen prognostizierte, dass die Störung und die Notwendigkeit, Gas zu Spotmarktpreisen zu beschaffen, zu einem Produktionsausfall von 100.000 bis 120.000 Tonnen und einer negativen Auswirkung auf das EBITDA von 75 bis 100 Millionen US-Dollar allein im dritten Quartal führen würden.

Der historische Gasliefervertrag von Norsk Hydro ist an die US-amerikanischen Henry-Hub-Preise gekoppelt, die bei etwa 3,2 US-Dollar pro Million British Thermal Units liegen, während die globalen Spotpreise für LNG mit rund 28 US-Dollar pro Million British Thermal Units etwa neunmal so hoch sind. Die Alunorte-Raffinerie verbraucht pro Jahr etwa 29,5 Billionen British Thermal Units an Gas.

J.P. Morgan senkte seine EBITDA-Prognosen für das dritte und vierte Quartal 2026 um 13 % bzw. 24 % und liegt damit nun 12 % bzw. 14 % unter dem Bloomberg-Konsens.

Das Brokerhaus erklärte, dass eine Anhebung der Kostenprognose bei der Veröffentlichung der Ergebnisse für das dritte Quartal am 23. Oktober zu einer Welle von Herabstufungen der Konsensschätzungen führen könnte. Zudem wurden die EBITDA-Schätzungen für 2026 und 2027 um 10 % bzw. 14 % nach unten korrigiert und liegen nun 7 % bzw. 2 % unter dem Bloomberg-Konsens.

Laut J.P. Morgan haben makroökonomische Aufwärtsrisiken die Analysten davon abgehalten, die Aktie auf "Underweight" statt "Neutral" zu setzen. Die Aluminiumpreise fielen im Juni um etwa 20 %, was auf Hoffnungen einer Deeskalation zwischen dem Iran und den USA, eine schneller als erwartete Wiederinbetriebnahme von Schmelzkapazitäten am Golf, raschere Angebotsausweitungen in Indonesien und eine höhere chinesische Produktion zurückzuführen war.

Die Commodities-Research-Abteilung von J.P. Morgan erwartet, dass dies die Aluminiumpreise und die europäischen Regionalprämien kurzfristig stützen wird, bevor 2027 ein größerer Angebotsüberschuss entsteht. Eine erneute Eskalation am Golf oder weitere Beschränkungen für Metalllieferungen aus der Region stellten Aufwärtsrisiken für die Preise dar.

J.P. Morgan führte an, dass Norsk Hydro auf Basis der Spotpreise mit einem EV/EBITDA-Verhältnis für 2026/2027 von 6,1 bzw. 5,5 gehandelt wird, bei einer Free-Cashflow-Rendite von 5 % und 7 %. Im Vergleich dazu liegt der Wert bei europäischen Basismetall-Wettbewerbern bei 9 bzw. 6. evidence.title: Aurubis-Aktie // Korrektur als Einstiegschance?
evidence.text:
Aurubis-Aktie // Korrektur als Einstiegschance?

Bis auf 225,00 Euro war die Aurubis-Aktie (676650) hochgelaufen, was vor allem einer positiven Geschäftsentwicklung, aber auch dein steigenden Rohstoffpreisen, zu verdanken war. Dies war ein neuer Kurs-Rekord . Davon hat sich das Papier inzwischen allerdings rund 25 Prozent entfernt. Hauptgrund dafür ist ein fallender Kupferpreis . Fundamental sieht es bei dem Konzern aber weiterhin sehr positiv aus, wie die jüngsten Geschäftszahlen aufzeigen.

Der Kupfer-Konzern-Aktie hatte zwischenzeitlich geholfen, dass der Vorstand die Prognose für den operativen Gewinn vor Steuern (EBT) erhöht hatte. Waren bei unserer Besprechung im vergangenen Oktober [ HIER klicken ] noch Werte zwischen 300 und 400 Millionen Euro als Ziel ausgerufen, visiert das Management nun Werte zwischen 425 bis 525 Millionen Euro an.

Möglich war dies, da die Zahlen für das dritte Quartal des Geschäftsjahres 2025/26, welches in wenigen Tagen zum 30. September endet, überzeugt haben. So stieg das EBT nach neun Monaten um 31 Prozent auf 374 Millionen Euro. Im dritten Quartal waren es mit 149 Millionen Euro deutlich mehr als im zweiten Jahresabschnitt , welcher ein EBT von 121 Millionen Euro brachte. Zum Vergleich: Im Q3 des Vorjahres lag das EBT lediglich bei 57 Millionen Euro.

Mit Blick auf diese Zahlen ist zu erwarten, dass sogar das obere Ende der Guidance erreicht werden wird. Sofern der Kupfer-Konzern nicht Vorabdaten bekannt gibt, müssen Anleger allerdings noch bis zum 2. Dezember auf die finalen Zahlen warten.

Dank der recht deutlichen Korrektur ist der Wert inzwischen fundamental wieder günstig. So liegt das Kurs-Gewinn-Verhältnis (auf Basis der Schätzung für das kommende Geschäftsjahr) bei 16. Hinzu kommt eine Dividenden-Rendite von immerhin 1,2 Prozent.

Sorgen bereitet allerdings die Charttechnik . Sofern nämlich die aktuelle Unterstützungszone im Bereich von 145 bis 160 Euro nicht gehalten werden kann, droht ein Rückfall bis an die Marke von 120 Euro. Dies halten wir zwar für unrealistisch, da die Substanz des Konzerns enorm hoch ist. In negativen Übertreibungsphasen kann dies aber trotzdem geschehen. Daher raten wir nur langfristig orientierten Anlegern, die noch nicht investiert sind, zum Direktinvestment .

Kurzfristig sinnvoller erscheint es, den Basiswert möglicherweise über ein Discount-Zertifikat ins Depot zu holen. Unser Favorit ist ein Discounter (UR1FEM) mit Cap bei 170,00 Euro und Bewertungstag am 18. Juni 2027. Geht Aurubis unter dem Cap-Niveau durchs Ziel, tilgt der Emittent durch Lieferung der Aktie. Der Einstandspreis läge dann bei 145,17 Euro, was einem Rabatt von 16,0 Prozent entspräche. Klettert die Aurubis-Aktie über den Cap, erhalten Anleger 170,00 Euro in Cash ausbezahlt. Daraus errechnet sich eine Maximalrendite von 17,2 Prozent oder hochgerechneten 22,8 Prozent p. a., was für den entgangenen Aktienkauf mehr als ausreichend entschädigen würde.

evidence.title: Aurubis unter Stromdruck: Hamburg fordert schnelleren Netzausbau für Klimaziel 2040
evidence.text:
Hamburgs Wirtschaftssenatorin Melanie Leonhard drängt die Übertragungsnetzbetreiber 50Hertz und Tennet, den Ausbau sowie die Erneuerung der Stromnetze im Norden zu beschleunigen. In der Region wird viel Strom aus erneuerbaren Quellen erzeugt, zugleich gelten die Anbindungen an Hamburg und die verfügbaren Übergabepunkte als nicht ausreichend für den wachsenden Bedarf.

Hamburg hatte im vergangenen Jahr per Volksentscheid beschlossen, das Ziel der CO2-Neutralität von 2045 auf 2040 vorzuziehen. Nach Einschätzung der Senatorin hängt die Umsetzung wesentlich davon ab, ob die Netzinfrastruktur rechtzeitig leistungsfähig gemacht wird. Die Forderung betrifft sowohl überregionale Leitungen als auch die Schnittstellen zu den lokalen Verteilnetzen.

Aurubis zählt als Kupferproduzent zu den energieintensiven Grundstoffunternehmen am Standort Hamburg. Die Industrie will ihre Fertigung stärker elektrifizieren, um fossile Brennstoffe zu ersetzen. Neben Klimaschutzgründen gewinnt dabei auch die Versorgungssicherheit an Bedeutung, da geopolitische Konflikte die Preise und Verfügbarkeit von Öl und Gas beeinflussen können.

Für Aurubis ist der Netzausbau damit kein rein politisches Infrastrukturthema. Eine stabile Stromversorgung ist eine Voraussetzung dafür, Produktionsprozesse zu elektrifizieren, den CO2-Ausstoß zu senken und den Standort langfristig wettbewerbsfähig zu halten. Verzögerungen könnten Investitionsentscheidungen erschweren oder den Übergang zu weniger fossilen Verfahren verlangsamen.

Analysten-Einordnung: Dies deutet darauf hin, dass der Zugang zu verlässlichem und ausreichend dimensioniertem Strom für Aurubis zunehmend zu einem strategischen Produktionsfaktor wird. Kurzfristig liefert die politische Forderung jedoch keinen direkten Hinweis auf Umsatz oder Gewinn des Unternehmens. Für Anleger bedeutet diese Entwicklung vor allem, bei der Bewertung künftiger Dekarbonisierungs- und Ausbauprojekte neben den Investitionskosten auch Netzanschluss, Strompreise und Versorgungssicherheit zu berücksichtigen.

Der weitere Zeitplan für Netzausbau und Genehmigungen wird entscheidend dafür sein, ob Hamburgs Industrie ihre Elektrifizierungspläne bis 2040 umsetzen kann. Für Aurubis bleibt zu beobachten, welche konkreten Strom- und Infrastrukturprojekte am Hamburger Standort folgen und wie sich deren Kosten auf die Wettbewerbsfähigkeit auswirken.

evidence.title: Aurubis stock slips toward yearly low as guidance hike keeps fundamentals in focus
evidence.text:
Aurubis stock (ISIN DE0006766504) has moved down toward a new yearly low after several consecutive losing sessions, even as the Hamburg-based copper producer is working off raised full-year 2025/26 guidance announced in early May 2026. As of September 15, 2026, the softer share price contrasts with stronger earnings expectations supported by robust copper demand.

Share price pressure despite guidance hike

According to boerse-social.com on September 15, 2026, Aurubis stock recently closed at EUR 163.90 on its home market, having lost 4.29% in the preceding session and marking a new yearly low at EUR 73.10 on that day. In the three most recent sessions cited, the shares declined by a cumulative 3.82% with daily moves of 1.88%, 1.32% and 0.66% down, underscoring a short-term negative trend.

The same radar overview notes that Aurubis stock has slipped below its 200-day moving average after trading above this technical benchmark for 494 consecutive days, which many chart watchers see as a sign that medium-term momentum has weakened. boerse-social.com Year-to-date performance stands at minus 21.31%, so the recent pressure comes on top of an already negative 2026 return.

Raised full-year 2025/26 guidance supports the story

While the share price has weakened in recent sessions, Aurubis has fundamentally strengthened its outlook. As Euronews reported on May 12, 2026, Aurubis raised its full-year 2025/26 guidance for the second time on May 8, 2026, helped by sustained elevated copper prices and strong demand from artificial intelligence data centers, electrification projects and renewable energy investments. In addition, higher revenues from sulphuric acid, a key by-product of copper smelting, were cited as a supporting factor.

The same article highlights that Aurubis, described as Europe's largest copper producer and one of the world's biggest copper recyclers, had seen its share price up by 50% year-to-date at the time of publication. Euronews The contrast between a 50% gain earlier in the year and the current minus 21.31% performance shows how strongly sentiment around Aurubis stock has reversed as 2026 has progressed.

For investors, the key fundamental takeaway is that the current guidance for fiscal year 2025/26 is higher than previously communicated, even though exact earnings and revenue figures are not detailed in recent week-filtered hits. The guidance hike itself is a current fundamental factor within the allowable freshness window, and it stands in tension with the latest share price weakness.

Ownership disclosure adds a regulatory angle

A regulatory disclosure underlines that institutional investors are actively managing positions in Aurubis. According to finanzen.ch on September 15, 2026, Aurubis AG published an EQS-PVR notification under Article 40, Section 1 of the German Securities Trading Act, noting that a reporting threshold in share ownership was crossed or reached on September 8, 2026.

The EQS release confirms Aurubis AG as the issuer and references its corporate details, including the Hamburg address and the company's website. While the notification focuses on transparency rather than earnings, such threshold crossings often indicate notable changes in major shareholder positions, which can influence liquidity and market perception over time. finanzen.ch

Per the Xetra quotation cited in the recent radar overview, Aurubis stock last closed at EUR 163.90, with the shares currently quoted slightly below that level in late trading on September 15, 2026, and year-to-date performance at minus 21.31%. From an investor perspective, that places the current price well below the earlier 2026 highs described in May and far beneath the level implied by a 50% year-to-date gain at that time, indicating a pronounced correction in the stock over the subsequent months.

evidence.title: Accenture launches Accenture Construct to reinvent fragmented capital project delivery amid global investment supercycle
evidence.text:
Accenture launches Accenture Construct to reinvent fragmented capital project delivery amid global investment supercycle

Accenture has launched Accenture Construct, a new global business to help project owners plan, deliver and optimize large infrastructure and capital projects, from airports and power grids to data centers, rail networks and advanced manufacturing facilities.

Accenture Construct brings together Accenture’s capital projects business — which has grown four times over three years across strategic advisory, engineering, project delivery and technology services — to support delivery at scale and give project owners one accountable partner across the full project lifecycle. The new entity is designed to reinvent how capital projects are delivered to overcome delays, cost overruns and execution risk by evolving fragmented project delivery models with the use of AI and data.

Accenture Construct strengthens Accenture’s position to capture growth from three converging demand cycles: the AI infrastructure build-out of data center construction, the global energy transition, and long-term infrastructure replacement. The total addressable market for integrated owner-side capital project services is $260 billion and is projected to grow 7.5% annually to $348 billion in 2030.

“Global demand for critical infrastructure capital programs is accelerating at the same time as AI is fundamentally changing how projects are planned, delivered and operated,” said Julie Sweet, chair and CEO, Accenture. “Together, these shifts are significantly increasing our market opportunity for the capital project services provided by Accenture Construct, which combines deep capital project expertise with global scale, built to give owners a new level of visibility and certainty.”

Project complexity is growing faster than traditional, siloed delivery models can manage. Dozens of advisors, consultants, contractors and specialist firms are each accountable to deliver a piece of a project, while the owner absorbs the costs between them.

Backed by Accenture’s deep capital project expertise and leadership in data and AI, Accenture Construct addresses these challenges through a common project data foundation that creates a single operational view across the entire delivery ecosystem. Accenture Construct’s AI-enabled workflows shift delivery from reactive management to predictive decision-making. These capabilities, combined with Accenture’s global delivery capability, enable Accenture Construct to act as a single accountable partner from strategy through handover, reducing the transition costs, knowledge loss and accountability gaps that accumulate every time ownership transfers between the firms involved in a project. The result is earlier risk identification, better decisions, and greater certainty over cost, schedule, quality and asset performance.

“Capital projects haven’t lacked expertise; they’ve lacked alignment on shared success outcomes. Owners assemble exceptional teams, but accountability is often dispersed across the delivery ecosystem,” said Adam J. Shaw, CEO of Accenture Construct. “Accenture Construct brings those capabilities together under one accountable partner, combining deep delivery expertise with AI and data to help owners make better decisions, reduce uncertainty and deliver better outcomes.”

Accenture Construct serves global private and public sector clients and is organized around five global lines of business, oriented around asset outcomes:

Many leading infrastructure owners already rely on Accenture as a reinvention partner for complex multiphase capital projects. Representative engagements include:

Accenture Construct unites capabilities Accenture has built through organic growth and a series of acquisitions. This includes more than 5,000 practitioners with industry expertise and hands-on delivery experience across the Americas, EMEA and APAC, many from specialist acquisitions including Alfa Consulting (Spain), Anser Advisory (US), Arca (Spain), BOSLAN (Spain), Comtech Group (Canada), Fibermind (Italy), Greenfish (Belgium), IQT Group (Italy), Orlade Group (France), Soben (UK) and Verum Partners (Brazil).

Accenture Construct will work seamlessly with Accenture’s majority-owned joint venture, DLB Associates. DLB will continue to serve as the provider of full data center lifecycle services, including energy optimization and sustainable design, to US-based clients, from early planning and feasibility through to commissioning and operational readiness, complementing Accenture Construct’s global capabilities.

evidence.title: Accenture Invests in Within to Support Enterprise AI Agent Deployment
evidence.text:
Accenture Invests in Within to Support Enterprise AI Agent Deployment

NEW YORK, Sept. 25, 2026 — Accenture has made an investment, through Accenture Ventures, in Within , an AI platform company that helps organizations map, enhance, and automate their business processes and operations. As part of the investment, Accenture and Within are partnering to help clients gain deeper insight into how work gets done, identify opportunities to enhance performance, deploy AI agents, and unlock ongoing productivity and efficiency gains.

Enterprise AI investment is accelerating, but many organizations are still struggling to generate value at scale. Accenture’s latest Pulse of Change survey of more than 3,000 C-suite leaders found that 82% are increasing investment in AI. Yet only 23% report that achieving widespread, sustained business value from the technology, down from 32% earlier this year. One reason is that the as-is processes, exceptions, and workarounds that shape day-to-day operations are rarely documented. As a result, AI often lacks the context it needs to understand the requirements.

Within’s platform captures how employees work across all applications and tracks undocumented offline interactions, including processes, handoffs, and exceptions. The platform automatically compiles that information into Within’s Work Brain, the continuously updated context layer of work that AI agents need to succeed. As information updates with the business, organizations can use it to build AI agents, identify automation opportunities, and improve workflows across finance, HR, sales, marketing, customer service, IT, supply chain, procurement, and commercial operations. By mapping real-time decisions, handoffs, and workarounds that evade official documentation (if any exists), Within enables AI agents to deliver real, measurable ROI.

“One of the most persistent challenges in AI transformation is that organizations often don’t have a clear picture of the starting point—the actual processes, the exceptions, how work actually flows through their teams,” said Jason Dess, Accenture’s Industry and Process Reinvention Lead. “Without that understanding, it’s difficult to scale AI beyond isolated use cases. What’s compelling about Within is that it helps create that operational picture in a fraction of the time, giving both people and AI a foundation to work from immediately. That can accelerate transformation programs, shorten delivery timelines and give leaders greater confidence that the changes they’re making reflect how the business actually operates.”

The partnership will bring together Accenture’s scale in AI delivery and its established ecosystem relationships and industry expertise with Within’s work-to-agent platform to help clients accelerate their path from process discovery to agent deployment and operating model reinvention, with speed and confidence.

“What Within surfaced was the real process, not the one on the diagram—the hidden workarounds, the manual steps, the informal patches our people had built to get the job done. You can’t reinvent what you can’t see. Accenture and Within gave us that visibility, and the plan to act on it,” said David Benjamin, EVP and Chief Commercial Officer, Blackbaud.

Within is built on a private, sovereign architecture, designed to support data privacy and security requirements, making it suitable for regulated industries. In addition to AI transformation, it accelerates ERP and operating model transformation programs, which have traditionally required significant time and resources.

“AI transformation works best when there’s a system of record of work to provide visibility on what to automate and the ability to verify that agents are doing their work the right way,” says Andrew Antos, Within CEO and Co-Founder. “This partnership gives Accenture clients access to that system, so they can reap real business value, whether they’re building large-scale agentic workflows or highly customized agents. People and agents working in harmony is the future of work.”

Accenture Ventures invests in companies whose capabilities extend what Accenture clients can do with AI. The investment in Within reflects the importance of operational knowledge as prerequisite for effective AI deployment—and Accenture’s intent to help clients address that need at scale.

Terms of the investment were not disclosed.

Accenture helps the world’s leading enterprises reinvent by building their digital core and unleashing the power of AI to create value at speed for organizations across industries. Our strategy is to be the reinvention partner of choice for our clients and lead in the safe, widespread adoption of AI, and to be the most client-focused, AI-enabled, great place to work in the world. We bring together the talent of our approximately 799,000 people with proprietary assets and platforms, deep process and industry expertise, and leading ecosystem relationships to deliver end-to-end solutions and measurable outcomes at scale. Through our Reinvention Services, we offer broad expertise across Cybersecurity, Digital Core, Finance, Industry and Enterprise, Song, Supply Chain and Engineering, and Talent, with advanced capabilities in AI and Data, Industry and Process, and Technology. We serve approximately 9,000 clients and generated approximately $70 billion in FY25 revenue. Visit us at accenture.com .

evidence.title: Accenture launches Accenture Construct for infrastructure projects
evidence.text:
Accenture launches Accenture Construct for infrastructure projects

New unit to use AI and data to tackle delays and cost overruns; $260-billion market seen growing 7.5% a year to $348 billion in 2030

Accenture has launched Accenture Construct, a new global business to help project owners plan, deliver and optimise large infrastructure and capital projects, from airports and power grids to data centres, rail networks and advanced manufacturing facilities.

Accenture Construct brings together Accenture’s capital projects business — which has grown four times over three years across strategic advisory, engineering, project delivery and technology services — to support delivery at scale and give project owners one accountable partner across the full project lifecycle. The new entity is designed to reinvent how capital projects are delivered to overcome delays, cost overruns and execution risk by evolving fragmented project delivery models with the use of AI and data.

Accenture Construct strengthens Accenture’s position to capture growth from three converging demand cycles: the AI infrastructure build-out of data centre construction, the global energy transition, and long-term infrastructure replacement. The total addressable market for integrated owner-side capital project services is $260 billion and is projected to grow 7.5 per cent annually to $348 billion in 2030.

“Global demand for critical infrastructure capital programs is accelerating at the same time as AI is fundamentally changing how projects are planned, delivered and operated,” said Julie Sweet, Chair and Chief Executive Officer, Accenture. “Together, these shifts are significantly increasing our market opportunity for the capital project services provided by Accenture Construct, which combines deep capital project expertise with global scale, built to give owners a new level of visibility and certainty.”

Project complexity is growing faster than traditional, siloed delivery models can manage. Dozens of advisors, consultants, contractors and specialist firms are each accountable for delivering a piece of a project, while the owner absorbs the costs between them.

Backed by Accenture’s capital project expertise and leadership in data and AI, Accenture Construct addresses these challenges through a common project data foundation that creates a single operational view across the entire delivery ecosystem. Accenture Construct’s AI-enabled workflows shift delivery from reactive management to predictive decision-making. These capabilities, combined with Accenture’s global delivery capability, enable Accenture Construct to act as a single accountable partner from strategy through handover, reducing the transition costs, knowledge loss and accountability gaps that accumulate every time ownership transfers between the firms involved in a project. The result is earlier risk identification, better decisions, and greater certainty over cost, schedule, quality and asset performance.

“Capital projects haven’t lacked expertise; they’ve lacked alignment on shared success outcomes. Owners assemble exceptional teams, but accountability is often dispersed across the delivery ecosystem,” said Adam J. Shaw, Chief Executive Officer of Accenture Construct. “Accenture Construct brings those capabilities together under one accountable partner, combining deep delivery expertise with AI and data to help owners make better decisions, reduce uncertainty and deliver better outcomes.”

Accenture Construct serves global private and public sector clients and is organised around five global lines of business, oriented around asset outcomes: Data Centres, Utilities & Telecommunications, Transportation & Civic Infrastructure, Advanced Manufacturing and Process Industries.

Accenture Construct will work with Accenture’s majority-owned joint venture, DLB Associates. DLB will continue to serve as the provider of full data centre lifecycle services, including energy optimisation and sustainable design, to US-based clients, from early planning and feasibility through to commissioning and operational readiness.

evidence.text:
Accenture and Within Help Clients Accelerate AI Across the Enterprise Through Strategic Investment and New Partnership

Accenture has made an investment, through Accenture Ventures, in Within, an AI platform company that helps organizations map, enhance, and automate their business processes and operations. As part of the investment, Accenture and Within are partnering to help clients gain deeper insight into how work gets done, identify opportunities to enhance performance, deploy AI agents, and unlock ongoing productivity and efficiency gains.

Also Read: AiThority Interview with Gou Rao, co-founder and CEO at NeuBird AI

Enterprise AI investment is accelerating, but many organizations are still struggling to generate value at scale. Accenture’s latest Pulse of Change survey of more than 3,000 C-suite leaders found that 82% are increasing investment in AI. Yet only 23% report that achieving widespread, sustained business value from the technology, down from 32% earlier this year. One reason is that the as-is processes, exceptions, and workarounds that shape day-to-day operations are rarely documented. As a result, AI often lacks the context it needs to understand the requirements.

Within’s platform captures how employees work across all applications and tracks undocumented offline interactions, including processes, handoffs, and exceptions. The platform automatically compiles that information into Within’s Work Brain, the continuously updated context layer of work that AI agents need to succeed. As information updates with the business, organizations can use it to build AI agents, identify automation opportunities, and improve workflows across finance, HR, sales, marketing, customer service, IT, supply chain, procurement, and commercial operations. By mapping real-time decisions, handoffs, and workarounds that evade official documentation (if any exists), Within enables AI agents to deliver real, measurable ROI.

“One of the most persistent challenges in AI transformation is that organizations often don’t have a clear picture of the starting point—the actual processes, the exceptions, how work actually flows through their teams,” said Jason Dess, Accenture’s Industry and Process Reinvention Lead. “Without that understanding, it’s difficult to scale AI beyond isolated use cases. What’s compelling about Within is that it helps create that operational picture in a fraction of the time, giving both people and AI a foundation to work from immediately. That can accelerate transformation programs, shorten delivery timelines and give leaders greater confidence that the changes they’re making reflect how the business actually operates.”

“What Within surfaced was the real process, not the one on the diagram—the hidden workarounds, the manual steps, the informal patches our people had built to get the job done. You can’t reinvent what you can’t see. Accenture and Within gave us that visibility, and the plan to act on it,” said David Benjamin, EVP and Chief Commercial Officer, Blackbaud.

Within is built on a private, sovereign architecture, designed to support data privacy and security requirements, making it suitable for regulated industries. In addition to AI transformation, it accelerates ERP and operating model transformation programs, which have traditionally required significant time and resources.

“AI transformation works best when there’s a system of record of work to provide visibility on what to automate and the ability to verify that agents are doing their work the right way,” says Andrew Antos, Within CEO and Co-Founder. “This partnership gives Accenture clients access to that system, so they can reap real business value, whether they’re building large-scale agentic workflows or highly customized agents. People and agents working in harmony is the future of work.”

Accenture Ventures invests in companies whose capabilities extend what Accenture clients can do with AI. The investment in Within reflects the importance of operational knowledge as prerequisite for effective AI deployment—and Accenture’s intent to help clients address that need at scale.

evidence.title: ‘Money Never Sleeps’: Capgemini’s 2027 World Payments Report
evidence.text:
‘Money Never Sleeps’: Capgemini’s 2027 World Payments Report

The global payments industry is reaching a tipping point.

So says Capgemini’s Research Institute, which has discovered nearly three-quarters of corporate leaders are unsatisfied with cross-border payments, despite expectations that they will account for 4% of global payments volume by 2030.

As stablecoins, tokenised deposits and central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) move from experimentation to commercialisation, banks face mounting pressure on traditional payments revenue streams.

Although 60% of leaders identify payment innovation as a strategic area of investment, only a third of corporate clients are satisfied with their primary banking partner, revealing a gap between what banks can deliver and what businesses expect.

These findings come from Capgemini’s World Payments Report 2027, its 22nd edition in which it surveyed more than 1,100 large corporates with revenues greater than US$1bn.

The findings are clear: despite improvements in payment infrastructure, operational fragmentation remains the most defining challenge for corporate clients.

Commenting on the findings, FinTech Magazine speaks with Jeroen Hölscher , Global Head of Payment Services at Capgemini, who delineates what banks must do to close the gap.

Jeroen says: “Stablecoins and tokenised deposits are going to have a material impact on the future of payments, that much is clear now.

“What is less clear is how banks will respond.”

Accelerated intelligent money instruments: a catalyst for transformation

Capgemini defines accelerated intelligent money as stablecoins, tokenised deposits and CBDCs that enable money to do more than simply move between accounts.

Yet the report finds only 21% of banks are actively scaling at least one accelerated intelligent money instrument, despite clear interest in using these instruments.

“As adoption grows, traditional payments revenue across areas, including foreign exchange spreads, correspondent banking, float income and transaction processing, are increasingly exposed to disruption,” Jeroen says.

“Banks therefore need to think about new revenue sources and new ways they can provide value.

“That could mean monetising things like settlement certainty, real-time cash visibility and liquidity optimisation.

“Those that act now will build lasting trust, capture new payment flows and retain the corporate deposits that underpin their wider banking relationships.”

As adoption grows, traditional payments revenues are increasingly exposed to disruption

Tokenised deposits are a leading priority

As intelligent money moves towards commercialisation, Jeroen stresses that banks must decide what roles they want to play with urgency.

“Some will preserve client access by distributing third-party capabilities rather than building them themselves," Jeroen says.

“Others will invest selectively in specific corridors, client segments or use cases where they can differentiate. And some will go further, investing in shared infrastructure and helping to establish the standards that shape how the ecosystem evolves.

“At a minimum, banks will need to rethink their technology architecture. The market is evolving, and having technology that connects traditional payment rails with new forms of money will be a massive benefit.”

“Banks have different priorities, capabilities and resources, so there is no one-size-fits-all approach,” Jeroen adds.

Yet even amongst the leading banks acting now, foundational gaps remain.

More than half (56%) report having the digital asset talent, technical readiness and capabilities required to support tokenisation, smart contracts and interoperability across financial networks.

Closing that gap will determine which banks are best positioned to move from experimentation to scale.

“The important thing is to make that decision deliberately and make it now, because the role a bank chooses will determine where it needs to invest and which capabilities it needs to build,” he continues.

evidence.title: Capgemini stock gains as investors focus on AI shift and government unit sale
evidence.text:
Capgemini SE stock (ISIN FR0000125338) closed at around EUR 107.10 on Euronext Paris on September 18, 2026, after a rebound of about 2.6 percent that left the shares near their recent levels around EUR 107.85. As TradingView reported on September 21, 2026, analysts highlighted a 4.9 percent rise to EUR 107.85 as investors welcomed Capgemini's shift toward software and AI pricing and its agreement to sell Capgemini Government Solutions.

AI-driven strategy and portfolio reshaping

According to TradingView on September 21, 2026, Capgemini is moving away from purely labor-based IT services toward software and artificial intelligence solutions, backed by new pricing models that aim to monetize intellectual property more directly. The same report notes that Capgemini shares climbed 4.9 percent to EUR 107.85 as the market reacted to this strategic pivot combined with the planned sale of Capgemini Government Solutions to ITC Federal, signaling a refocus on core commercial and private-sector clients.

The sale of Capgemini Government Solutions, announced in a definitive agreement dated September 12, 2026, was highlighted on the Euronext product page, which notes the transaction as part of the group's broader portfolio management efforts. According to Euronext , this transaction underscores Capgemini's intention to streamline its operations and redeploy capital toward higher-growth areas, including AI-enabled services and platforms.

Half-year 2026 results support guidance upgrade

On the fundamentals side, Capgemini's recent share performance is supported by its half-year 2026 results. As Ideal-Investisseur reported on September 21, 2026, Capgemini used its S1 2026 publication on July 30, 2026, to raise its constant-currency revenue growth target for the full year to approximately 8.5 percent to 9.0 percent, up from a lower prior range. The same article notes that these half-year 2026 results provided the underlying momentum for a 2.92 percent intraday gain to EUR 107.40, with the stock trading above its 20-day moving average.

This guidance implies that Capgemini expects to grow significantly faster than low-single-digit GDP growth in many of its core markets, underscoring management's confidence in demand for digital transformation and AI-related projects in fiscal 2026. When set against the reported half-year performance, the new 8.5 to 9.0 percent constant-currency target suggests an incremental acceleration of roughly 1 to 1.5 percentage points versus more cautious earlier expectations, a shift that investors appear to be rewarding with higher valuations.

Capgemini is also benefiting from positive sentiment toward the broader IT services sector. As Investing.com reported on September 21, 2026, shares in Capgemini rose about 2.5 percent after Citi argued that Accenture's partnership with AI firm Anthropic improves the outlook for AI-driven services across the industry, including for peers like Capgemini. The report notes that the stock tagged along with sector gains, illustrating how external AI announcements can raise expectations for Capgemini's own AI-related pipeline.

The same Investing.com coverage describes Capgemini's move of 2.5 percent on that AI news as part of a broader rally in European IT services, suggesting that investors are pricing in stronger medium-term demand for AI consulting and implementation. For shareholders, the key question will be how effectively Capgemini converts this sector tailwind into concrete revenue and margin gains, especially in light of its new AI-focused pricing strategies.

Capgemini stock level and trading metrics

Per data for the Paris listing, Capgemini shares recently changed hands at around EUR 104.35, with a prior close of EUR 107.10 and an intraday decline of 2.57 percent as of September 18, 2026, on Euronext Paris, based on price information that shows the stock closing at EUR 104.35 at 5:38 p.m. local time and a previous close of EUR 107.10. The same data set indicates that the session opened at EUR 106.70, highlighting intraday volatility as investors digested both the AI strategy news and the announced divestment of Capgemini Government Solutions.

According to Ideal-Investisseur on September 21, 2026, Capgemini gained 2.92 percent in a session where it traded at EUR 107.40, ranking among the strongest performers in the CAC 40 while the Paris benchmark rose 0.87 percent. The report also notes that the rebound pushed the share price back above its 20-day moving average, a chart level that some investors view as a short-term support zone after prior consolidation.

While the raised full-year constant-currency growth guidance for 2026 and the AI-focused strategic shift underpin the recent gains, investors also face several risks. The divestment of Capgemini Government Solutions narrows the group's exposure to public-sector contracts in certain geographies, which could reduce revenue diversification if the proceeds are not redeployed quickly into equally resilient segments. Moreover, as TradingView highlights, the success of the new software and AI pricing models depends on clients' willingness to pay for outcome-based services rather than traditional time-and-materials contracts, a transition that could weigh on margins in the short term if implementation is uneven.

From a valuation perspective, the combination of a 4.9 percent rise to EUR 107.85 in reaction to the strategic news and a subsequent 2.92 percent rebound to EUR 107.40 around September 18, 2026, suggests that Capgemini stock is pricing in continued execution on its growth plan. For long-term holders, the most important metrics to monitor will likely be whether revenue growth in fiscal 2026 ultimately lands within the raised 8.5 to 9.0 percent constant-currency range and whether operating margins remain consistent with management's medium-term ambitions in the face of higher AI-related investment.

As of the most recent completed trading day around September 18, 2026, Capgemini stock closed near EUR 104.35 to EUR 107.10 on Euronext Paris, with data showing a 2.57 percent daily decline from a previous close of EUR 107.10 when the price finished the session at EUR 104.35. This placed the shares close to the levels they had reached when they rose 4.9 percent to EUR 107.85 earlier in the period, leaving Capgemini trading not far from those recent highs as investors weigh the impact of its AI-focused strategy and portfolio reshaping.

evidence.text:
Exploring Capgemini’s A World in Balance 2026 Report

Water stress, severe climate disruption, resource constraints and geopolitical volatility have made business resilience transformation a necessity.

Corporate sustainability has evolved far beyond a compliance checklist, emerging as a core discipline focused on crafting climate resilience strategies to maintain growth and business performance.

Capgemini’s fifth annual report, A World in Balance 2026, explores this vital transition.

Drawing on a survey of 2,100 senior executives from 701 organisations across 13 countries, in-depth interviews with corporate leaders and insights from 6,500 global consumers, the report provides a comprehensive blueprint for navigating an uncertain economic landscape.

Escalating physical risks and climate threat

Climate-related disruptions are increasingly impacting everyday operations, supply chains and long-term growth prospects.

Nearly nine in ten organisations (87%) report climate-related supply chain disruptions, highlighting widespread vulnerability across global trade networks.

Simultaneously, water stress has risen to the top of the strategic agenda. 61% of executives believe that water scarcity will become a greater constraint on business growth than energy availability within five years, driving the rapid adoption of water risk management plans.

In response to these pressures, 64% of organisations report revising their sustainability priorities , while 78% are actively integrating energy and resource resilience directly into their corporate strategies.

Cyril Garcia, Head of Global Sustainability Services and Corporate Responsibility at Capgemini, says: “Sustainability is entering a new era. Organisations must move beyond compliance and reporting to build resilience, secure critical resources, create long-term business value and ultimately preserve their sovereignty.

“AI can accelerate this transition, but lasting impact will depend on how effectively organisations embed sustainability into their operations, decisions and innovation strategies.”

Far from being an administrative cost centre, sustainability is increasingly recognised as a key driver of business value creation.

Almost seven in ten (69%) organisations report a positive return on investment from their sustainability initiatives, representing a marked increase from 49% in 2025.

The operational and commercial benefits are widespread: 67% of companies report lower operating costs – achieving average savings of 6% over the past year – while 64% state that sustainability investments have contributed to increased sales.

By linking environmental actions to financial outcomes, businesses are unlocking new opportunities for efficiency, customer acquisition and brand equity.

Despite sustained investment momentum, turning sustainability ambitions into operational reality remains challenging.

Capgemini’s sustainability maturity index declined for a second consecutive year, falling from 111 in 2025 to 105 in 2026.

This widening gap between ambition and execution is particularly acute within net zero programmes.

The proportion of organisations falling behind on their net zero targets rose from 1% in 2025 to 11% in 2026, while 29% have postponed their net zero objectives compared to just 8% a year ago.

Many businesses continue to struggle with fragmented data, limited visibility across value chains and difficulties in managing Scope 3 emissions.

Aiman Ezzat, CEO of Capgemini, said on LinkedIn: “Some say sustainability has slipped down the corporate agenda. Our latest research tells a different story.

“Wider global trends explain why leaders are investing. Sustainability is increasingly viewed as a resilience strategy, not just an environmental commitment. After this year’s exceptional summer, it’s perhaps easier to understand why 71% of executives now say securing access to critical resources has a greater influence on their sustainability decisions than emissions targets alone.

“In a world defined by volatility, sustainability and business resilience are converging into a single strategic discipline. Leaders who treat them as separate agendas risk missing where real competitive advantage now lies.”

AI is emerging as a powerful execution engine for sustainability, helping organisations optimise supply chain resilience, improve energy efficiency , refine reporting and forecast climate risks.

More than 70% of executives believe the benefits of generative AI outweigh its environmental impact.

Nevertheless, rapid AI deployment brings new environmental and governance considerations, particularly regarding resource consumption.

Most organisations still lack visibility into AI's footprint: only 38% measure the energy consumption of AI systems, 34% track AI-related carbon emissions and just 25% disclose AI-related water usage.

To navigate these complexities, the report outlines five priority actions for leaders across strategy, operations, supply chain, procurement, risk management, product development, finance and technology:

Ultimately, building a resilient enterprise requires moving beyond passive reporting to embed climate adaptation into every operational decision.

Executive Board Member, Head of Sustainability and Corporate Responsibility

evidence.title: Capgemini: Businesses Increase Climate Adaptation Spending
evidence.text:
Paris | September 16, 2026: Businesses are increasing their focus on climate adaptation and resilience as climate disruption, water stress, resource constraints and geopolitical volatility put pressure on operations and supply chains, according to the fifth edition of the Capgemini Research Institute’s A World in Balance: The resilience reset report.

The report found that 68% of executives say their organizations actively prioritize climate adaptation, up from 56% in 2025. Nearly nine in 10 organizations reported that climate-related events have disrupted their supply chains.

Access to critical resources is also becoming a stronger factor in sustainability decisions. More than seven in 10 organizations said securing resources such as energy, water and materials now has greater influence on sustainability decision-making than emissions-reduction targets. Meanwhile, 61% of executives expect water scarcity to become a greater constraint on business growth than energy availability over the next five years.

Despite rising attention to climate risks, financial assessment remains limited. Only 15% of organizations have fully quantified the financial impact of climate-related disruptions , while just over one in four executives said their organizations have assessed climate risks across their extended value chains or deployed climate-risk analytics tools.

“Climate change disruptions have become our new normal, and yet there is still a wide gap between business leaders’ awareness of the risks and actual implementation. In order to protect their supply chains, operations, infrastructure, and access to essential energy, water, and materials, they can no longer defer climate action,” said Cyril Garcia, Global head of Sustainability services and Corporate Responsibility, and Member of the Group Executive Board at Capgemini. “It is encouraging to see organizations prioritize adaptation and resilience for sustainable growth. But as climate and political risks evolve, organizations must continue to embed sustainability into their core business strategy and day-to-day operations.”

Sustainability investments are also reporting financial benefits. Nearly seven in 10 organizations said their sustainability initiatives generated a net-positive return on investment. Sixty-four percent of executives said sustainability investments boosted sales, compared with 47% in 2025, while 74% said sustainable practices improved brand equity.

However, progress towards net zero targets remains uneven. While 84% of organizations reported having science-based targets, only 42% said they are on track to meet their 2030 or interim targets . The share of organizations falling behind on net zero goals rose to 11% in 2026 from 1% in 2025, while 29% reported postponing their net zero objectives, compared with 8% last year.

AI is increasingly being used in sustainability initiatives, with nearly two-thirds of organizations reporting its use. More than a third use or plan to use agentic AI for sustainability. At the same time, measurement remains limited, with just over a third of executives saying their organizations measure the energy consumption and carbon footprint of AI systems and workloads.

evidence.title: Cognizant Technology Solutions stock reports AI deal and EPS lift
evidence.text:
Cognizant Technology Solutions (ISIN US1924461023) stood at USD 59.14 on Nasdaq on September 23, 2026, up 0.78 percent from the previous close. The company had a fresh AI catalyst on September 23, when Cognizant and Cognition announced expanded collaborative offerings built around Cognition's AI software engineer Devin, according to MarketScreener .

The announcement adds an operating proof point to Cognizant's AI strategy. A September 23 report cited production results from AI-driven engineering work with Odyssey Logistics, while the company also expanded automation offerings with Cognition.

The commercial question is whether these deployments translate into repeatable productivity gains and larger client commitments. Cognizant's Q2 2026 call showed seven large deals with total contract value above USD 100 million each, including three new logos, according to Yahoo Finance .

In Q2 2026, revenue grew 4.1 percent year over year in constant currency to USD 5.5 billion. Adjusted EPS reached USD 1.37, an increase of 5 percent year over year, while adjusted operating margin reached 16 percent, 40 basis points above the prior-year level, according to the same earnings-call transcript.

Management raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to USD 5.70-5.82, implying 8-10 percent growth versus the earlier 7-9 percent range. Full-year revenue guidance calls for 4-5.5 percent constant-currency growth, while adjusted operating margin guidance remains 16-16.2 percent.

Deutsche Bank raised its Cognizant price target from USD 65 to USD 70 on September 18, 2026, and kept a Buy rating, as reported by MarketScreener . The new target is USD 10 above the September 23 Nasdaq price, a gap of 16.91 percent.

The stock's 2026 picture remains uneven in market terms. Its September 23 price was 28.75 percent below its January 1 level, even as the latest quarter delivered higher revenue, EPS and margin. That contrast makes execution on AI-led contracts more important than the headline guidance alone.
