evidence.title: Globant: The Sector's Cheapest IT Stock Is Shrinking, Not on Sale
evidence.text:
Catch pre-market movers with AI signals.

- Globant's stock has fallen nearly 50% from its 52-week high, trading at 0.6x sales—its cheapest valuation among major IT contractors.

- Revenue growth has stalled, with flat Q2 results, shrinking margins, and reduced guidance, while workforce and customer counts declined.

- Unlike peers like EPAM EPAM -- , Globant's low valuation reflects deteriorating fundamentals, not mispricing, with weak returns on equity and shrinking book value.

- A nascent AI-native business ($52.8M ARR) offers potential but remains just 2% of total revenue, insufficient to offset core business contraction.

- Analysts warn the stock's cheapness signals distress, not opportunity, until organic growth and stabilized guidance demonstrate turnaround credibility.

Globant has been one of this sector's hardest falls. The stock sits near $35, down almost half from its 52-week high around $72, in a group of IT-services 861052 -- names that have all been clobbered. For a bargain hunter that reads as an invitation. Peel the screener and it looks even better: the company trades at roughly 0.6x trailing sales, about 4.7x EBITDA, and below 0.7x book value - cheaper on those bases than Accenture ACN -- (about 1.6x sales, near 10x EBITDA) or EPAM EPAM -- (about 1x sales). On price alone, Globant GLOB -- is the cheapest major contractor on the board.

That is exactly the trap this one hides. A low multiple only means value if the number underneath it is holding still or growing. Globant's is shrinking, and the whole height of its fall is the market marking a stalled outsourcing business down to what a stalled business is worth.

Look beneath the multiple at the quarter Globant reported in August. Revenue was $614.4 million , essentially flat with the year-ago quarter. Almost no growth against sales on the books - a far cry from the high-teens growth rate this company once carried. Margins are compressing: adjusted gross margin fell to 36.5% from 38.1% a year earlier, and adjusted operating margin dropped to 13.2% from 15.0% , landing just below the range management had guided.

The company took the rare step of cutting its own full-year guidance in the same report, lowering revenue to $2.428 billion to $2.462 billion from a prior $2.462 billion to $2.508 billion. Adjusted EPS came in at $1.40 versus $1.53 in the year-ago quarter. And management is executing a restructuring to match - headcount was cut to 27,411 from 30,084 a year earlier, and the number of customers generating more than $100,000 a year fell to 904 from 981 . North American revenue declined 2.4% , with a 17.7% drop in the travel and oil segment. This is not a one-off miss. It is the shape of a base that is contracting.

The simplest way to see the difference between a bargain and a trap is to compare Globant with its closest public peer. EPAM Systems EPAM -- has also fallen sharply from its highs, yet it grew revenue about 11% year over year and earns a return on equity around 11%. Globant is roughly flat to slightly down on revenue with a return on equity in the mid-single digits. Both stocks fell to similar low multiples. One has the earnings base to back it up; the other has a book value that, at a below-book price, the weak return on capital more than explains. Cheapness in the second case is the price correctly reporting deterioration, not a mispricing to exploit.

The market's own forward data agrees. Globant's trailing P/E reads around 13x, but the street's forward multiple runs closer to 27x - roughly double. On a forward P/E, a multiple that wide above the trailing one is an admission that the earnings being estimated ahead are a fraction of today's, not the growth premium a healthy story would carry.

Management's counter-argument is the pivot to AI-native services, and it is real. The Glob.AI platform, priced on output or consumption rather than billable hours, reached $52.8 million in annual recurring revenue in the second quarter, up 61% quarter over quarter, with a goal of at least $110 million by year-end. The CEO frames the shift as " changing how our services are delivered and how they are priced ."

But that story does not change the math yet. The new business is still small: AI Pod revenue is roughly 2% of total revenue . Even tripling it over the coming year would barely move a $2.4 billion revenue base that is being guided flat-to-down. The pivot is a real option on the winner Globant still might become; it is not a replacement for the stalled economics that currently produce the earnings. For an investor, that is the whole distinction: the fast-growing number is the hope, and the flat-to-shrinking number is the present.

There is no sleeve that wants this stock right now. It does not farm growth, because growth is negative. It does not belong in a value sleeve, because a value position requires a stable earnings base, and this one is being revised downward every quarter. It hedges nothing. There is no reward in the price action either - the stock sits below both its 50- and 200-day averages with momentum still negative.

That leaves it, in my book, as an avoid rather than a buy-the-dip. The single variable that would change the call is the denominator: a quarter of positive organic revenue growth with a stabilized or raised guide. Watch whether the AI line begins to move the base rather than decorate it. Until the guidance stops falling, Globant's low multiple is a warning label, not a sale tag.

evidence.title: Can Globant (GLOB)’s AI Pivot Lead to Better Economics? Early Results Offer Hope
evidence.text:
Can Globant (GLOB)’s AI Pivot Lead to Better Economics? Early Results Offer Hope

Artificial intelligence is tearing up the business model that built Globant S.A. (NYSE: GLOB ). The company's stock price has dropped sharply to around $40 from $350 in 2021. Now Globant is attempting to reinvent itself. And it's doing that by leaning more on AI. Its new Glob.AI platform is growing rapidly. But the transition is coming with slower revenue growth and restructuring costs.

Globant's pivot to an AI-based model is about building a stronger, higher-margin business. But there's a heavy price to pay for that, at least in the near-term, as the AI model cannibalizes the legacy model and costs rise.

We recently examined why Globant's rapidly expanding AI business may still be too small to offset weakness in the model it is trying to replace. Read Here: Globant's (GLOB) AI Pivot Masks A Slowing Legacy Business

Globant S.A. (NYSE:GLOB) generated $614.4 million in revenue in Q2, largely unchanged from a year ago. Perhaps the most attention-grabbing figure was Glob.AI's annual recurring revenue. It increased 61% sequentially to $52.8 million. Globant expects Glob.AI's ARR to exceed $110 million by the end of 2026.

The Glob.AI platform is designed to shift clients from paying for human hours toward paying for AI-powered delivery based on consumption or output. Globant says the AI model can generate gross margins roughly 10% points above the legacy hours-based delivery.

Globant's AI model transition involves strategic partnerships. The company has sought to expand its AI capabilities by partnering with Anthropic, OpenAI, and other AI leaders. A recently announced agreement with TCI Entertainment is designed to place Globant's capabilities in interactive commerce and gaming.

Globant S.A. (NYSE:GLOB)'s 2026 outlook brings the challenge into focus. The company cut its 2026 full-year revenue guidance to $2.428 billion to $2.462 billion, from a previous range of $2.462 billion to $2.508 billion. That highlights the challenge Globant faces as it scales its AI-native model while overall revenue growth remains under pressure.

For Globant to justify the change in business model, Glob.AI does not need merely to grow. It also needs to bring about better economics. Globant's AI Pods, for instance, is designed to combine autonomous agents with human oversight. That changes the relationship between revenue and labor, and it should lead to better revenue per employee. Globant says its AI-native model is intended to decouple revenue growth from headcount growth. So far, the direction is encouraging, but investors still need evidence that those productivity gains can materially lift consolidated margins.

If AI Pods allow Globant to handle more work without increasing headcount, the company could expand margins even while the legacy business remains sluggish.

But the transition is already expensive. Globant incurred $32.3 million in restructuring costs in Q2. The restructuring was part of Globant's broader effort to optimize its organization and align its cost base with its business-model transformation. Globant is bracing for more restructuring costs, including $20 million to $25 million in Q3.

If AI adoption proves slower than expected, Glob.AI could remain too small to offset the old model's weakness. And a slow-growing AI business could keep profitability under more pressure.

Globant S.A. (NYSE:GLOB) closed Q2 with 23 hedge fund holders. That was down from 25 in Q1 and 33 in Q4. Yet the three largest funds increased their positions. Pzena Investment Management raised its stake 31% to about 3.9 million shares to remain as the top holder. Alyeska Investment Group raised its stake 79% to nearly 3 million shares, while AQR Capital Management bumped it up 51% to 1.2 million shares.

Still, Globant attracted more bearish bets. As of August 31, nearly 8 million Globant shares were sold short, with 5.6 days to cover. That represented 18.62% of the public float, marking a 3.3% jump in short interest from the previous reading.

The contrasting investor signals fit Globant's AI turnaround situation, where some see a glass half full and others a glass half empty.

While we acknowledge the potential of GLOB as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. evidence.title: Globant nombra COO para escalar AI Pods con agentes de IA
evidence.text:
¿Por qué Globant nombra un COO para escalar AI Pods?

El 20 de agosto de 2026 Globant designó a Fernando Matzkin como Chief Operating Officer ( COO ) de la compañía, según reportó The Globe and Mail. Matzkin, con 17 años en la firma — venía de ser Chief Revenue Officer y Chief Business Officer para Estados Unidos y Europa — quedó a cargo de ejecutar lo que la empresa llama su "Visión 2030", con dos piezas centrales: Glob.AI y los AI Pods , un formato de servicios operado por agentes de IA supervisados por humanos que la compañía vende por suscripción mensual , no por horas-hombre. Para una región acostumbrada a cobrar proyectos tech por headcount, el movimiento es la confirmación de que el modelo de servicios por suscripción potenciado por IA dejó de ser piloto y pasó a ser el eje del negocio.

¿Qué son los AI Pods y por qué no son "otra consultora automatizada"?

Los AI Pods son unidades de servicio conformadas por agentes de IA orquestados y supervisados por expertos humanos de Globant . Cada pod opera con capacidad medida en tokens y se contrata como una suscripción mensual que cubre desarrollo, diseño, producto o testing. El cliente paga por capacidad de cómputo y resultado, no por esfuerzo humano.

La capa de orquestación corre sobre Globant Enterprise AI , la plataforma propietaria que la compañía describe como "agnóstica con opinión": no ata al cliente a un único modelo de lenguaje ni a un proveedor cloud, sino que elige el LLM más adecuado para cada proyecto. En una entrevista con DISRUPTORES – El Español, el CEO y cofundador Martín Migoya lo resumió así: "La industria de servicios profesionales necesitaba una reinvención. El 80% de las compañías ha lanzado iniciativas de IA, pero menos del 10% obtiene un retorno concreto" . Y agregó: "Esto no es sólo una evolución: es una ruptura radical con lo que cualquier otro en nuestra industria está ofreciendo: servicios como si fueran software — continuos, inteligentes y alineados a resultados, no a esfuerzo" .

En la comunidad la aplicamos: automatización, agentes IA y herramientas reales para emprender, no solo para informarte.

Según Globant, la promesa operativa es concreta: hasta un 80% más de velocidad en la modernización de sistemas legados y reducciones significativas en plazos de entrega. La propia compañía dio un ejemplo interno en el lanzamiento original de los AI Pods en junio de 2025: actualizar el código de un sistema core bancario llevó una quinta parte del tiempo habitual gracias a la plataforma, reportó DISRUPTORES – El Español. Sectores como Oil & Gas, Finanzas y Retail ya muestran adopción temprana, según la empresa.

¿Cómo encaja la alianza con Anthropic en la nueva estrategia?

El nombramiento de Matzkin se inscribe en una secuencia de movimientos que llevan 15 meses:

Como parte del acuerdo con Anthropic, Globant accedió a los programas de certificación Forward Deploy Engineer (FDE) para Claude — un perfil de ingeniero que se inserta dentro del cliente para desplegar y escalar flujos agénticos — y se planteó como meta llegar a 5.000 arquitectos certificados internamente, según el comunicado. A junio de 2026, el modelo de AI Pods ya era utilizado por el 40% de las 20 cuentas de mayor facturación de la compañía, reportó PR Newswire.

El movimiento de Globant no es un caso aislado: marca el inicio formal de una economía de servicios por suscripción donde el entregable lo produce un agente y lo supervisa un humano. Para un founder hispano, las implicaciones son directas:

Replanteá el pricing de tus servicios tech. Si tu startup vende proyectos de software por hora, el modelo de suscripción por tokens o por resultado ya es lo que grandes clientes van a exigir. Empezá a cotizar por capacidad de cómputo y outcome, no por headcount. Preguntate qué parte de tu entrega puede empaquetarse en un "pod" recurrente y qué parte sigue siendo consultoría artesanal.

Construí con agentes, no contra ellos. Si trabajás con consultoras o freelancers externos, el nuevo estándar ya incluye agentes supervisados. Pedí a cualquier proveedor nuevo que te muestre qué agentes usa, qué plataforma los orquesta (Globant Enterprise AI, AWS Bedrock, Azure AI Foundry, etc.) y cómo mide el ROI de negocio , no el "esfuerzo". El propio Migoya advirtió que el 90% de las iniciativas de IA corporativas no dan retorno: exigí métricas concretas antes de firmar.

Aprovechá la ola de talento certificado FDE. Anthropic y Globant están formando ingenieros de despliegue de IA agéntica a escala. Si tu equipo está en LATAM o España, esto abre una vía de posicionamiento: formarte en orquestación de agentes, governance y compliance te coloca del lado de la oferta, no de la demanda de servicios. Las certificaciones FDE de Claude son un punto de entrada concreto.

Globant lleva más de dos décadas vendiendo tecnología y, según sus propios números, ya tiene al 40% de sus top 20 cuentas usando AI Pods a junio de 2026, con un ARR creciendo 60% en un trimestre y un pipeline de US$436M. Con el COO puesto, un CEO dedicado a Glob.AI y el acceso a Claude para toda su plantilla, la compañía está midiendo algo más que eficiencia: está midiendo si el modelo "horas-hombre" se puede reemplazar por suscripciones de agentes sin perder margen. Para founders hispanohablantes, la pregunta práctica ya no es si sumarse al modelo, sino cuánto de su propio stack de servicios podría entregarse igual.

En la comunidad la aplicamos: automatización, agentes IA y herramientas reales para emprender, no solo para informarte.

evidence.title: Globant presenta MuleSoft AI Pod para bajar las barreras de integración y escalar junto a Salesforce la IA agéntica en las empresas
evidence.text:
Globant presenta MuleSoft AI Pod para bajar las barreras de integración y escalar junto a Salesforce la IA agéntica en las empresas

El nuevo modelo de delivery busca reducir los tiempos de migración de meses a semanas al combinar agentes de IA especializados con expertos humanos en integración para ofrecer conectividad segura basada en APIs. Globant, compañía global enfocada en impulsar la reinvención empresarial a través de la inteligencia artificial, presentó MuleSoft AI Pod de Salesforce, una … Globant presenta MuleSoft AI Pod para bajar las barreras de integración y escalar junto a Salesforce la IA agéntica en las empresas

El nuevo modelo de delivery busca reducir los tiempos de migración de meses a semanas al combinar agentes de IA especializados con expertos humanos en integración para ofrecer conectividad segura basada en APIs. Globant , compañía global enfocada en impulsar la reinvención empresarial a través de la inteligencia artificial, presentó MuleSoft AI Pod de Salesforc e, una solución que combina agentes de IA especializados con expertos humanos para agilizar la integración de sistemas a través de APIs y acelerar el delivery.

A medida que las iniciativas de inteligencia artificial empresarial se vuelven más complejas, las organizaciones necesitan formas más rápidas y seguras de conectar las aplicaciones, los datos y los flujos de trabajo que impulsan la transformación empresarial.

Las empresas enfrentan una creciente presión para llevar la IA agéntica de la experimentación a la producción. Sin embargo, los sistemas desconectados y los datos fragmentados continúan siendo una barrera importante. MuleSoft AI Pod busca resolver este desafío al acelerar la conectividad segura basada en APIs y el desarrollo de integraciones, manteniendo los niveles de control y seguridad necesarios para cada proyecto.

Este AI Pod estará disponible a través de Glob.AI, el nuevo modelo de delivery de IA de Globant. “A medida que las organizaciones buscan escalar el uso de Agentforce y otras iniciativas de IA en toda la empresa, contar con sistemas integrados y datos preparados para su uso se vuelve esencial” , afirmó Roland Berthelot, Global Head del Salesforce Studio de Globant. “MuleSoft ayuda a establecer la base de conectividad que hace posibles estas iniciativas. Con MuleSoft AI Pod, Globant ayuda a sus clientes a ampliar sus capacidades de integración de forma segura y controlada, con la supervisión de expertos necesaria para implementar estas tecnologías en entornos empresariales.” Salesforce explica que MuleSoft permite conectar Agentforce con sistemas de terceros mediante APIs y conectores , con el objetivo de que los agentes puedan acceder a información y ejecutar acciones en diferentes sistemas de una organización.

Equipos de IA que se adaptan a las necesidades de cada empresa

MuleSoft AI Pod está diseñado como equipos de delivery flexibles que pueden configurarse en función del roadmap de integración, el entorno técnico y las necesidades de delivery de cada cliente. Cada pod combina agentes de IA especializados para tareas específicas de MuleSoft con expertos senior de Globant que guían la arquitectura, validan los resultados y gestionan la ejecución en áreas que incluyen diseño de APIs, desarrollo de flujos de MuleSoft , pruebas automatizadas, gestión y control de las integraciones y modernización de sistemas legacy.

Las configuraciones Lean, Scaled y Advanced están diseñadas para adaptarse a distintos niveles de demanda. Lean permite gestionar aproximadamente 6 flujos de integración o APIs por mes; Scaled , hasta 12; y Advanced , hasta 24, de acuerdo con la información oficial publicada por Globant . Las mediciones realizadas en proyectos de migración actuales, pilotos internos y equipos de delivery indican que el modelo puede generar resultados tangibles, entre ellos:

Estas cifras corresponden a benchmarks reportados por Globant a partir de proyectos de migración, pilotos internos y equipos de delivery.

De meses a semanas en proyectos de migración

Las organizaciones que operan con plataformas de integración desactualizadas suelen enfrentar programas de migración que requieren meses de análisis, rediseño y validación. Este enfoque busca reducir los tiempos de migración de meses a semanas, preservando la lógica de negocio y cumpliendo con estándares de seguridad empresarial, según Globant.

MuleSoft AI Pod ofrece así un camino para fortalecer las bases de integración empresarial, ayudando a las organizaciones a modernizar sus entornos de integración, mejorar la consistencia del delivery y preparar sus ecosistemas tecnológicos para la siguiente etapa de transformación impulsada por IA.

La necesidad de establecer controles alrededor de estas nuevas herramientas también empieza a tomar relevancia. A medida que los agentes de IA se incorporan a las operaciones de las empresas , temas como la gobernanza, los permisos y el acceso a los datos forman parte de los nuevos desafíos tecnológicos para las organizaciones. Salesforce , por su parte, plantea a MuleSoft como una capa que permite gestionar y gobernar APIs, integraciones y agentes de IA desde una infraestructura común.

MuleSoft AI Pod estará disponible a través de Glob.AI

MuleSoft AI Pod estará disponible a través de Glob.AI , la plataforma AI-native de Globant diseñada para ayudar a las organizaciones a acceder y gestionar AI Pods desde un entorno unificado.

Actualmente disponible mediante lista de espera, Glob.AI reúne agentes de IA especializados y expertos de Globant para desplegar servicios de IA de nivel empresarial, con un modelo de precios vinculado a resultados o consumo, en lugar de horas trabajadas o cantidad de usuarios.

La solución se apoya en más de 21 años de experiencia de Globant como partner de Salesforce , con más de 1,200 proyectos entregados y un índice de satisfacción de clientes de 4.7 sobre 5, según información de la compañía. Globant reúne además a más de 27,400 profesionales de tecnología, incluidos más de 2,000 expertos multi-cloud distribuidos en 58 Delivery Centers a nivel global, y señala que ha implementado más de 20 proyectos de Einstein AI y Agentforce.

Como socio fundador de Agentforce Partner Network , la compañía cuenta con más de 500 expertos certificados en Agentforce y más de 200 expertos en Salesforce Data 360, además de haber sido reconocida por Salesforce como Implementation Level Expert en Data Cloud , MuleSoft y Agentforce , de acuerdo con Globant .

La apuesta llega en un momento en que las empresas buscan que la inteligencia artificial deje de funcionar como una herramienta aislada y se conecte directamente con sus sistemas, datos y procesos. El reto, cada vez más, no es solamente incorporar agentes de IA en las organizaciones , sino construir la infraestructura que les permita operar de forma controlada y a escala.

evidence.title: TCI Entertainment Aligns with Globant to Advance its Patented Interactive Commerce Technology
evidence.text:
Agreement with NYSE-listed global technology company establishes framework for development initiatives supporting TCI's vision of connecting commerce with gaming and interactive digital environments

PLANTATION, Fla. , Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TCI Entertainment ("TCI"), a technology company developing a proprietary platform designed to connect commerce with gaming and interactive digital environments, today announced the execution of a Master Services Agreement ("MSA") with Globant (NYSE: GLOB ), a global technology company specializing in digital transformation, software engineering, artificial intelligence, and emerging technologies.

The agreement establishes the contractual framework under which TCI and Globant can undertake specific development initiatives as TCI advances its proprietary interactive commerce technology toward broader platform development and commercialization.

Globant has more than 27,400 employees across 30+ countries and reported approximately $2.5 billion in trailing twelve-month revenue as of the second quarter of 2026. Its global technology capabilities span areas including software engineering, artificial intelligence, gaming, immersive experiences, cloud technologies, and digital commerce.

TCI's technology is designed to enable commerce to become more seamlessly integrated into games, virtual environments, and other interactive digital experiences. The company has developed an intellectual property portfolio that includes issued U.S. patents covering key elements of its technology.

"Executing our agreement with Globant represents an important milestone in TCI's development," said Harry McMillan, President of TCI Entertainment. "We have spent considerable time developing and protecting the intellectual property behind our vision. As we move toward broader platform development, we believe Globant's global technology capabilities and experience can provide an important foundation for the next stage of TCI's growth."

Given the importance of TCI's intellectual property portfolio, TCI worked with Greenberg Traurig to strengthen the MSA and establish appropriate protections for the company's existing patents, proprietary technology, and trade secrets throughout potential development activities.

TCI Entertainment is a technology company developing a proprietary interactive commerce platform designed to connect commerce with gaming, virtual environments, and other digital experiences. Through its patented technology, TCI seeks to create new opportunities for consumers, game developers, brands, retailers, and commerce partners to participate in transactions occurring within interactive digital environments.

Globant (NYSE: GLOB ) is a global technology company helping organizations transform through technology, artificial intelligence, engineering, and digital experiences. Globant has more than 27,400 employees across 30+ countries and reported approximately $2.5 billion in trailing twelve-month revenue as of the second quarter of 2026.

evidence.title: Nagarro stock trades 2.72 percent below the cash offer
evidence.text:
Nagarro stock stood at EUR 78.80 on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange on September 24, 2026, down 0.32 percent for the session and 2.72 percent below Persistent Systems' EUR 81.00 cash offer. The takeover has secured a decisive majority, giving investors a clear reference point for the remaining acceptance period.

According to The Economic Times on September 22, 2026, Persistent Systems' subsidiary lifted its total Nagarro holding to 83.25 percent after acquiring an additional 61.15 percent stake. The initial acceptance period ended on September 17, 2026, and the additional acceptance period runs from September 23 to October 6, 2026.

The offer is a cash payment of EUR 81.00 per share. Persistent expects transaction completion by the end of the first quarter of 2027 and intends to pursue a delisting from the regulated market, according to The Economic Times .

Nagarro's operating backdrop remains visible in its first-half figures. Quartr reports H1 2026 revenue of EUR 501 million, up 0.3 percent in euro terms and 4.2 percent in constant currency from the prior-year period. Q2 revenue rose 2.0 percent in constant currency.

Adjusted EBITDA reached EUR 69.1 million in H1 2026, while the adjusted EBITDA margin was 15.0 percent in Q2. The combination of modest euro-denominated revenue growth and a double-digit adjusted EBITDA margin makes the EUR 81.00 offer the central market benchmark for the stock.

Nagarro's closing price of EUR 78.80 on September 24, 2026, was EUR 2.20 below the cash offer, while the company's market capitalization stood at EUR 975,231,243. The 52-week range was EUR 33.12 to EUR 80.50, placing the stock EUR 1.70 below its yearly high.

evidence.title: Persistent Secures 83.25% Of Nagarro In €81-Per-Share Takeover Offer And Plans Delisting
evidence.text:
Persistent Systems has announced that its voluntary public takeover offer for Nagarro SE has exceeded the required acceptance threshold, with approximately 83.25% of Nagarro’s share capital and voting rights secured through tendered shares and an existing purchase agreement. The offer, conducted through Persistent’s wholly owned subsidiary Galaxy Germany Holding SE, provides shareholders with €81 in cash per share. An additional acceptance period runs from September 23 through October 6, 2026, with the transaction expected to close by the end of the first quarter of calendar year 2027, subject to outstanding regulatory approvals.

The initial acceptance period expired at midnight Central European Summer Time on September 17, 2026.

During that period, Nagarro shareholders tendered 7,568,145 shares, representing approximately 61.15% of the company’s total share capital and voting rights, excluding treasury shares.

Persistent had already secured an additional 22.10% stake through a share purchase agreement with Lantano Beteiligungen GmbH.

Together, the tendered shares and the stake secured through the Lantano agreement represent approximately 83.25% of Nagarro’s outstanding share capital and voting rights.

The result exceeds the 50%-plus-one-share minimum acceptance threshold required under the offer terms.

The successful initial acceptance period represents an important milestone in Persistent’s proposed acquisition of Nagarro and its strategy of combining the two businesses.

Persistent is pursuing the transaction to create a larger global digital engineering and technology services organization with expanded capabilities in artificial intelligence.

The acquisition would bring together the companies’ respective customer relationships, technology expertise, and international delivery operations.

The transaction is being conducted under Germany’s Securities Acquisition and Takeover Act, which provides an additional acceptance period for shareholders who did not tender during the initial phase.

Under those provisions, remaining Nagarro shareholders may accept the offer at the existing €81-per-share cash consideration through midnight Central European Summer Time on October 6, 2026.

Persistent will announce the final number of shares tendered after the additional acceptance period expires.

The company also intends to pursue a delisting of Nagarro’s shares from the Frankfurt Stock Exchange after completing the takeover.

Persistent plans to terminate Nagarro’s admission to trading on the regulated Prime Standard market and, where legally feasible, end trading on the open markets of other stock exchanges.

The delisting forms part of the company’s broader strategy of taking Nagarro private following the acquisition.

If completed, the termination of Nagarro’s regulated market listing would result in the company being removed from Germany’s SDAX index.

A delisting would also reduce the liquidity available to any shareholders who continue holding Nagarro shares after the transaction.

Under the existing business combination agreement, Nagarro’s Management Board has indicated its willingness to support the proposed delisting, subject to its fiduciary duties.

Persistent expects to pursue the delisting as soon as practicable and legally permissible after the acquisition closes.

Although the minimum acceptance threshold has been exceeded, completion remains subject to a limited number of outstanding regulatory approvals.

Persistent currently expects the transaction to close by the end of the first quarter of calendar year 2027.

The company has made the official offer document and a nonbinding English translation available through the dedicated takeover website.

The additional acceptance period gives remaining Nagarro shareholders another opportunity to participate in the offer before Persistent proceeds with the remaining steps necessary to complete the transaction.

“We have offered Nagarro shareholders an attractive opportunity to realize full and immediate value. The success of the offer confirms its appeal and the strategic logic behind combining Persistent and Nagarro. We now look forward to completing the remaining steps toward closing, so we may start building the global AI-led digital engineering leader we envisioned together.”

Sandeep Kalra, CEO and Executive Director of Persistent Systems Limited

evidence.title: Persistent Systems secures 83.25% stake in Nagarro, extends offer window
evidence.text:
Persistent Systems secures 83.25% stake in Nagarro, extends offer window

Persistent Systems has acquired 83.25% of German IT firm Nagarro SE's shares, surpassing the takeover threshold. The deal aims to delist Nagarro and complete by early 2027, enhancing AI-led digital engineering capabilities.

Persistent Systems has crossed the halfway mark in its bid to take over German IT firm Nagarro SE. The Pune-headquartered company said on Monday that it now holds 83.25% of Nagarro’s outstanding share capital, well above the minimum threshold needed to complete its voluntary public takeover offer, as per a regulatory filing.

The acceptance period for the offer closed at midnight Central European Summer Time on September 17. During that window, shareholders tendered 7,568,145 Nagarro shares. This works out to about 61.15% of the company’s total share capital and voting rights, excluding treasury shares.

Persistent already held a separate stake before this. It had secured approximately 22.10% of Nagarro through a share purchase agreement with Lantano Beteiligungen GmbH. Adding the two together takes the company’s aggregate holding to 83.25%.

The offer required Persistent to cross 50% plus one share for it to go through. That threshold has now been cleared by a wide margin.

Nagarro shareholders to get additional acceptance period

Nagarro shareholders who did not tender their shares in the first round still have a chance. Under German takeover law, an additional acceptance period of two weeks will run from September 23 to October 6, 2026.

Shareholders who accept during this window will receive the same cash consideration as those who tendered earlier, which is 81 euros per share. Persistent said it will disclose the final tender numbers once this second window closes.

Persistent has indicated it intends to delist Nagarro from the regulated market of the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, known as the Prime Standard, once the deal is legally allowed to proceed. A delisting would take Nagarro out of the SDAX index and is expected to reduce liquidity in its shares.

Nagarro’s management board has agreed, subject to its fiduciary duties, to support the delisting process, according to the terms of the Business Combination Agreement between the two companies.

Persistent expects the transaction to close by the end of the first quarter of calendar year 2027, pending a limited number of remaining regulatory approvals.

“We have offered Nagarro shareholders an attractive opportunity to realise full and immediate value. The success of the offer confirms its appeal and the strategic logic behind combining Persistent and Nagarro. We now look forward to completing the remaining steps toward closing, so we may start building the global AI-led digital engineering leader we envisioned together,” Sandeep Kalra, Chief Executive Officer and Executive Director, Persistent Systems, said.

Persistent Systems is a global services and solutions company focused on AI-led, platform-driven digital engineering and enterprise modernisation. The company employs over 28,500 people across 21 countries and offers services spanning software engineering, product development, data and analytics, CX transformation, cloud computing and agentic business automation.

Persistent Systems’ share price has declined 1.62% as of intraday on September 23. The company’s share price has declined 7.27% in the past month. Persistent Systems’ share price has increased 0.75% in the last year.

India’s Next Enterprise AI Challenge Will Be Operational, Not Technical

Nagarro unveiled a new suite of agentic AI solutions built on Salesforce at Dreamforce 2026. Under the theme “From friction to flow,” the solutions target operational bottlenecks across various business-critical functions.

A trusted Salesforce Summit partner, Nagarro has been heavily investing in building AI-led capabilities within the Salesforce ecosystem. Established 14 years ago, the company’s Salesforce practice has grown into a global team of more than 800 experts across 15+ geographies, serving over 200 clients worldwide. With a dedicated architecture and innovation board, the company constantly explores the latest technologies and builds solutions that can transform businesses.

The new solutions from Nagarro on show at Dreamforce included:

FieldPursuit : a service assistant for field technicians, with AI-driven job preparation, predictive diagnostics, and repair guidance to improve first-time fix rates, plus automated documentation, compliance checks, and work-order closure. SalesPursuit : an AI lead-management agent that qualifies and prioritizes leads, reads customer signals, and automates activity summaries and CRM updates so representatives can focus on selling. ContractIQ : a contract-review agent that summarizes, redlines, validates clauses, compares versions, and checks policy compliance for faster, more accurate legal and sales reviews. Viyom Jain, Managing Director and Global Business Unit Head, Enterprise Products, Nagarro , said, “ As a member of the Salesforce FDE partner network, we look forward to helping customers turn their agentic vision into production-ready reality and deliver measurable outcomes at scale. Our latest suite of agentic AI solutions enables organizations to accelerate Agentforce success and transform business-critical processes from friction to flow .”

Dreamforce 2026 marked a shift from AI as a feature within CRM to AI as the way enterprises coordinate work, with attention increasingly moving from pilots to production. Salesforce presented its platform as four connected layers: Data 360, Customer 360, Agentforce, and AIforce. It announced AIforce, a live interface layer with experiences including Claudeforce and Slackforce, and introduced Koa, its first CRM reasoning model, built on NVIDIA Nemotron, along with the Enterprise AI Harness for governance and security. Nagarro’s place in the FDE Partner Network, reserved for partners with a proven record of taking Agentforce deployments into production, reflects that same shift.

Security was one of the event’s biggest talking points. Most access models were built with a human user in mind, but agents work at a different scale: there are more of them, they move faster, and new ones are added constantly. Nagarro secures agentic deployments on three fronts: data, platform, and the agents themselves. That means tagging sensitive data and applying the same policy to agents and humans alike, running red-team agents to catch weaknesses early, and building in observability so teams can see what an agent is actually doing, not just what it was scoped to do. But tooling alone doesn’t solve this. The harder question is accountability, having clear lines of responsibility between humans and agents as deployments scale, and that’s ultimately what decides whether an agentic transformation sticks.

Nagarro remains committed to creating seamless and impactful customer experiences through industry-specific Salesforce solutions. By combining deep technical expertise with a keen understanding of industry needs, the company delivers intelligent, scalable AI solutions that enhance operational efficiency, drive innovation, and deliver measurable business outcomes.

evidence.title: Persistent's Takeover Offer for Nagarro Successful
evidence.text:
Additional Acceptance Period to run from September 23, 2026 to October 6, 2026

MUNICH and PUNE, India , Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ --

Galaxy Germany Holding SE (the " Bidder" ), a wholly-owned direct subsidiary of Persistent Systems Limited (BSE: 533179) (NSE: PERSISTENT) (together " Persistent "), today announced the initial results for its Voluntary Public Takeover Offer for all outstanding shares of Nagarro SE (" Nagarro ") (the " Offer "). The acceptance period expired at midnight (CEST) on September 17, 2026.

During the acceptance period, 7,568,145 Nagarro shares were tendered into the Offer. This represents approximately 61.15% 1 of the total share capital and voting rights of Nagarro. In addition, Persistent already secured a stake of approximately 22.10% 1 in Nagarro under a share purchase agreement with Lantano Beteiligungen GmbH (" Lantano "). Together, the tendered shares and the shares secured from Lantano represent approximately 83.25% 1 of the total share capital and voting rights of Nagarro. The minimum acceptance threshold of 50% plus one share required for the Offer to be completed has thus been exceeded.

According to the German Securities Acquisition and Takeover Act (WpÜG), Nagarro shareholders who have not yet tendered their shares can still accept the Offer at the same cash consideration of EUR 81.00 per share by tendering their shares within the additional acceptance period, which will begin on September 23, 2026, and end at midnight (CEST) on October 6, 2026. Persistent will disclose the final number of shares tendered following the expiry of the additional acceptance period.

Sandeep Kalra, Chief Executive Officer and Executive Director, Persistent Systems Limited:

"We have offered Nagarro shareholders an attractive opportunity to realize full and immediate value. The success of the offer confirms its appeal and the strategic logic behind combining Persistent and Nagarro. We now look forward to completing the remaining steps toward closing, so we may start building the global AI-led digital engineering leader we envisioned together."

Potential delisting might reduce liquidity

Following the consummation of the Offer and acting on a taking private strategy, Persistent intends to terminate the admission of Nagarro shares to trading on the regulated market (Prime Standard) of the Frankfurt Stock Exchange and trading on the open market of other stock exchanges as soon as practicable and legally feasible. The termination of admission to trading on the regulated market would result in Nagarro being excluded from the SDAX and a reduction in liquidity of Nagarro shares. Pursuant to the Business Combination Agreement, Nagarro's Management Board is, subject to its fiduciary duties, willing to support the delisting of the Nagarro shares.

The offer document and a non-binding English translation are available at www.galaxy-offer.com . Persistent expects the transaction to close by the end of Q1 CY27, subject to only a limited number of outstanding regulatory approvals.

Disclaimer and forward-looking statements

This press release is neither an offer to purchase nor a solicitation of an offer to sell Nagarro shares. The final terms of the Offer as well as other provisions relating to the Offer are set out solely in the offer document authorized for publication by the German Federal Financial Supervisory Authority ( Bundesanstalt für Finanzdienstleistungsaufsicht ). Investors and holders of Nagarro shares are strongly advised to read the offer document and all other documents relating to the Offer, as they contain important information. The offer document for the Offer (in German and a non-binding English translation) with the detailed terms and conditions and other information on the Offer is published amongst other information on the internet at www.galaxy-offer.com .

The Offer will be implemented exclusively on the basis of the applicable provisions of German law, in particular the German Securities Acquisition and Takeover Act ( Wertpapiererwerbs- und Übernahmegesetz - WpÜG ), and certain securities law provisions of the United States of America relating to cross-border takeover offers. The Offer will not be conducted in accordance with the legal requirements of jurisdictions other than the Federal Republic of Germany or the United States of America (as applicable). Accordingly, no notices, filings, approvals or authorizations for the Offer have been filed, caused to be filed or granted outside the Federal Republic of Germany or the United States of America (as applicable). Investors and holders of Nagarro shares cannot rely on being protected by the investor protection laws of any jurisdiction other than the Federal Republic of Germany or the United States of America (as applicable). Subject to the exceptions described in the offer document and, where applicable, any exemptions to be granted by the respective regulatory authorities, no takeover offer will be made, directly or indirectly, in those jurisdictions in which this would constitute a violation of applicable law. This press release may not be released or otherwise distributed in whole or in part, in any jurisdiction in which the Offer would be prohibited by applicable law.

The Bidder reserves the right, to the extent permitted by law, to directly or indirectly acquire additional Nagarro shares outside the Offer on or off the stock exchange, provided that such acquisitions or arrangements to acquire are not made in the United States, will comply with the applicable German statutory provisions, in particular the WpÜG, and the offer price is increased in accordance with the WpÜG, to match any consideration paid outside of the Offer if higher than the offer price. If such acquisitions take place, information on such acquisitions, including the number of Nagarro shares acquired or to be acquired and the consideration paid or agreed, will be published without undue delay if and to the extent required under the laws of the Federal Republic of Germany, the United States or any other relevant jurisdiction. evidence.title: GFT Technologies stock falls 1.54 percent as H1 profit improves
evidence.text:
GFT Technologies stock (ISIN DE0005800601) was trading at EUR 25.55 on Xetra on September 24, 2026, down 1.54 percent from the prior close of EUR 25.95. The company enters the final months of 2026 with higher first-half revenue, stronger profitability and a major Deutsche Bank modernization project.

GFT Technologies reported H1 2026 revenue of EUR 462.6 million, compared with EUR 441.5 million in H1 2025, a 5 percent increase. That comparison gives the stock a more useful operating anchor than the daily move alone.

Adjusted EBIT increased 8 percent year over year to EUR 32.6 million from EUR 30.1 million, lifting the adjusted EBIT margin from 6.8 percent to 7.1 percent. EBITDA rose 13 percent to EUR 34.8 million, while earnings before tax increased 26 percent to EUR 24.0 million.

On August 27, 2026, Deutsche Bank selected GFT as transformation and system integration partner for a new core banking platform in its German Private Bank, according to GFT Technologies . The project uses Vault Core from Thought Machine and builds on more than 25 years of cooperation between Deutsche Bank and GFT.

The contract connects GFT's banking specialization with cloud engineering and AI-enabled delivery capabilities. For investors, the commercial significance lies in the possibility of turning one large modernization program into a reference for additional core banking work, although the release does not disclose a contract value.

On September 1, 2026, Berenberg raised its GFT price target from EUR 24 to EUR 30 and maintained a Buy rating, according to MarketScreener . The target revision followed the Deutsche Bank announcement and places the analyst view above the current Xetra price.

GFT Technologies stock stood at EUR 25.55 on Xetra on September 24, 2026, with a 52-week range of EUR 13.86 to EUR 27.10. The current price is 5.72 percent below the yearly high, while market capitalization stood at EUR 653,180,844.

evidence.title: Berlin’s AI InsurTech startup omni:us acquired by Dortmund’s adesso to embed AI into core insurance systems
evidence.text:
Berlin’s AI InsurTech startup omni:us acquired by Dortmund’s adesso to embed AI into core insurance systems

adesso , a Dortmund-based provider of insurance-specific software and technology solutions, has acquired omni:us , a Berlin-based startup specialising in AI-powered claims processing.

The transaction combines adesso’s insurance and software expertise with omni:us’ AI technology. adesso also plans to progressively integrate omni:us technology into its core insurance platform, the in|sure Ecosphere. omni:us solutions will be further developed and expanded as a central component of the combined portfolio for insurance AI.

“Artificial intelligence does not become part of the insurance core simply by adding another application alongside existing systems. It has to be connected to the systems, data and control mechanisms insurers use to run their business. With omni:us, we are gaining proven, production-grade AI for claims together with the specialised expertise required to embed intelligence directly into the core insurance landscape,” said Andreas Nolte , Managing Director Insurance Business Solutions at adesso.

Founded in Dortmund in 1997, adesso is one of the leading IT service providers in the German-speaking market and a leading provider of core insurance systems. The company’s in|sure Ecosphere is a modular, cloud-enabled application landscape covering core insurance processes across property and casualty, health and life insurance, and retirement and pension solutions.

The group reported generating revenue of €1.3 billion in 2024 and employs more than 11,100 people across over 65 locations.

Founded in 2015, omni:us is a provider of AI-powered end-to-end insurance claim automation. Its portfolio includes end-to-end automation for standardised claims as well as an agentic co-pilot for complex cases.

The company states that its technology analyses claims information, applies insurance-specific logic and generates traceable outputs that can be integrated into insurers’ existing core system environments. In 2018, the company announced the closing of a Series A round led by Target Global.

Through the acquisition, adesso strengthens its insurance business with proprietary AI technology, an established product organisation, specialised domain expertise and international customer relationships. Simultaneously, omni:us gains access to adesso’s market presence and its capabilities in insurance, integration, implementation and scaling.

Under the terms of this acquisition, the omni:us team will play a central role in the continued development and commercialisation of the combined insurance AI portfolio. Its products, expertise, and customer relationships will remain within the adesso Group under the omni:us brand.

Existing omni:us customers will continue to be supported within their current product and technology environments, and the existing solutions will continue to be actively developed. These customers will gain access to adesso’s broader insurance, integration, implementation and scaling capabilities.

On the other hand, adesso’s customers will gain access to AI technology for claims processing. These capabilities will be progressively integrated into adesso’s existing portfolio for core insurance systems and insurance transformation.

The acquisition also increases the share of proprietary software within adesso’s insurance portfolio and expands its ability to offer existing customers additional AI-powered solutions. omni:us, in turn, gains access to adesso’s market reach, insurance expertise, and implementation and scaling capabilities.

“Claims is where artificial intelligence has to prove that it can perform reliably under real financial, regulatory and operational conditions. “We have spent ten years building that capability. Together with adesso, we can make it accessible to a significantly broader insurance market, integrate it more deeply into core systems and extend the same rigorous approach to further insurance processes,” said Thomas Hauschild , CEO of omni:us.

According to both companies, their joint product strategy addresses two key market requirements. First, specialised AI capabilities will increasingly be embedded directly into insurance products and workflow solutions, creating ready-to-deploy offerings for insurers. Second, customers will be able to develop, integrate, and operate their own or third-party AI agents within a controlled agentic layer.

Both companies highlighted that the joint product strategy will remain aligned with the requirements of regulated insurance processes. These include explainability, human oversight, operational reliability, data protection, information security and full traceability.

evidence.title: «Wir haben das Problem, dass die Arbeit von Juniors mit KI gemacht werden kann», sagt Michaela Gasser, die Schweiz-Chefin des IT-Dienstleisters Adesso
evidence.text:
«Wir haben das Problem, dass die Arbeit von Juniors mit KI gemacht werden kann», sagt Michaela Gasser, die Schweiz-Chefin des IT-Dienstleisters Adesso

Bei dem Unternehmen mit 550 Mitarbeitenden explodierten die Kosten für KI-Lizenzen. Dummerweise bezahlen die Kunden bis jetzt nicht dafür.

Michaela Gasser hat ein Problem: Ihre Kosten laufen gerade aus dem Ruder, und sie kann kurzfristig wenig dagegen tun.

NZZ.ch benötigt JavaScript für wichtige Funktionen. Ihr Browser oder Adblocker verhindert dies momentan.

Die Schweiz-Chefin des IT-Beratungsunternehmens Adesso ist für 550 Mitarbeitende verantwortlich. Die Firma hilft Unternehmen wie Helsana, Postfinance oder Roche, Softwareprojekte umzusetzen.

Die Angestellten von Adesso bekommen von ihrem Arbeitgeber die Lizenzen für KI-Modelle mit einer mittleren Tokenanzahl zur Verfügung gestellt.

Ein Token ist die Baustein-Einheit, in der KI-Modelle Code oder Text verarbeiten. Eine mittlere Tokenanzahl heisst, dass das im Preis inbegriffene Volumen für tägliche Recherchen, das Verfassen von E-Mails und Berichten oder Unterstützung beim Programmieren reichen sollte.

Diese Lizenzen kosteten etwa 3000 Franken pro Mitarbeiter pro Jahr, sagt Gasser. Manche der Mitarbeitenden lägen bei der Tokennutzung aber bereits im Bereich von 6000 bis 12 000 Franken.

Kommt es noch zu einer Verzehnfachung der Kosten?

«Wir sprechen also von bis zu 2,5 Millionen Franken Zusatzkosten. Wir geben bereits gleich viel für Token aus wie fürs Reisen», sagt die CEO. Was ihr Sorgen bereitet, ist, dass die Aufwendungen für KI ungebremst weiter steigen könnten. «Manche Branchenexperten erwarten noch einmal eine Verzehnfachung vom heutigen Niveau aus.»

«Unsere Kosten für die Nutzung von KI-Modellen explodieren», konstatiert Gasser. Deshalb haben sie und die anderen Geschäftsleitungsmitglieder nun beschlossen, das Thema bei allen Kunden von Adesso anzusprechen. Stand jetzt ist erst in wenigen Verträgen geregelt, dass der IT-Dienstleister die Tokenkosten an seine Kunden weitergibt. Die Kunden erwarten, dass Adesso-Mitarbeiter auf ihren Projekten KI-Modelle verwenden, aber sie bezahlen nicht dafür.

Die Konkurrenten hätten genau das gleiche Problem: Das heisst, sie bleiben auf Kosten für Token sitzen, die sie ihren Kunden nicht verrechnen können. «Es ist das Gesprächsthema Nummer eins in der Branche», sagt Gasser.

Adesso hat seine Mitarbeitenden anfangs dazu angehalten, die KI-Tools möglichst viel zu nutzen, um diese schnell zu beherrschen. «Doch jetzt müssen wir genau hinschauen, wo der Einsatz von KI auch sinnvoll ist, wo er einen messbaren Nutzen schafft», sagt Gasser. Adesso versucht die Angestellten für einen wirtschaftlichen Umgang mit Token zu sensibilisieren.

Das Hoffen auf leistungsfähige Open-Source-KI

Und wer weiss, vielleicht wird es der Markt richten: «Wir erwarten, dass bald mehr leistungsfähige Open-Source-Lösungen zur Verfügung stehen werden und diese Anbieter wie Anthropic dazu zwingen, sich bei Preiserhöhungen zu mässigen», sagt Gasser. Open-Source-Software kann frei heruntergeladen und verändert werden. Ihre Nutzung ist daher viel günstiger als jene von Anthropic oder Open AI.

Gassers bevorzugtes Verrechnungsmodell wäre, einen Fixpreis für das jeweilige Projekt abzumachen. Adesso würde mit seinen Kunden zusammen also das Resultat definieren und dann selbst entscheiden, mit wie vielen Mitarbeitern und mit wie viel KI-Anteil das Projekt umgesetzt wird.

Einige der Kunden sagten allerdings, es sei für sie schwierig, die Anforderungen an ein Projekt klar zu definieren, sagt Gasser. Sie bezahlten lieber die Stunden der Adesso-Berater. In solchen Fällen müsse das Unternehmen einen Weg finden, die Tokennutzung in seinen Stundensätzen zu hinterlegen.

Gasser präzisiert, was das heissen könnte: «Wenn wir heute sagen, für das Projekt benötigen wir 1000 Stunden, aber mit dem Einsatz von KI sind es nur noch 800 Stunden, dann kostet die Stunde halt neu 180 Franken statt wie zuvor 150 Franken.»

Darüber hinaus muss das Unternehmen aber auch seine Mitarbeitenden zu einem sinnvollen Einsatz von KI anhalten. Insbesondere die Softwareentwickler hätten bereits ein gutes Verständnis dafür, wie man wirtschaftlich mit Token umgehe, sagt Gasser. Sie will jetzt Schulungen für alle durchführen.

Es gehe nicht nur darum, gut zu prompten, sondern auch darum, das richtige Modell für die jeweilige Aufgabe zu wählen. «Je nach Modell von Claude verbrennt man 15- bis 20-mal so viele Token für die gleiche Anfrage», sagt Gasser. Weil viele Mitarbeiter standardmässig das leistungsfähigste Modell nutzen, gibt es hier noch viel Optimierungspotenzial.

Nicht immer den Ferrari aus der Garage holen

«In der Schulung müssen wir dafür sensibilisieren, dass man nicht immer den Ferrari aus der Garage holen muss, wenn man Brötchen kaufen geht. Es ist besser, das Velo zu nehmen.» Adesso hat auch eine interne Tauschbörse für nicht verbrauchte Token eingeführt.

KI stellt das Unternehmen vor weitere Probleme. Es will weiterhin Nachwuchs ausbilden. Denn Adesso wird in den kommenden Jahren viele Mitarbeitende durch Pensionierungen verlieren. «Aber wir haben das Problem, dass die Arbeit von Juniors von KI gemacht werden kann. Die meisten unserer Kunden wollen keine Jobeinsteiger mehr auf Projekten», sagt Gasser.

Auch deshalb wünscht sie sich Festpreise: «So könnten wir selbst entscheiden, wie viele junge Leute wir an Projekten mitarbeiten lassen.» Gasser hat Verständnis für Kunden , die punkto Jobeinsteiger Vorbehalte anbringen.

Gerade Firmen mit grossen IT-Abteilungen wie Banken, Versicherungen oder auch die SBB hätten selbst viele Auszubildende, die sie beschäftigen müssten. «Sie haben nicht noch den Spielraum, Juniors von Lieferanten auf Projekten unterzubringen.»

Bereits gibt es ein weiteres Thema, das Gasser mit ihren Kunden ansprechen muss. Das Unternehmen hat in letzter Zeit einiges in ein neues Produkt investiert.

Es ist eine Plattform für agentische Softwareentwicklung, die eine massive Kostenersparnis bringen soll. «In den entsprechenden Projekten generieren KI‑Agenten Code, testen und dokumentieren weitgehend automatisch; unsere Teams steuern den Prozess, prüfen die Ergebnisse und tragen die Verantwortung für Qualität und Wirkung.»

Es handle sich gewissermassen um eine Maschine, die mit Token betrieben werde. «Beides, Maschine und Treibstoff, hat einen Wert, der eingepreist werden muss», sagt Gasser. Auch unter diesem Gesichtspunkt eigneten sich Festpreis‑Pakete, bei denen Adesso den Output und den wirtschaftlichen Nutzen verbindlich zusichere.

Ein KI-Agent bricht aus und führt selbständig eine Cyberattacke aus. Wie lassen sich IT-Systeme schützen, wenn die KI unkontrollierbar wird?

Neue KI-Modelle gefährden die Cybersicherheit. Die Politik will mehr Kontrolle, zeigt sich aber hilflos. Das erinnert an die «Crypto Wars» in den USA vor 30 Jahren.

KI wird immer mächtiger. Nun streiten Washington und das Silicon Valley darüber, wie man die Schlüsseltechnologie regulieren sollte

Vor einem Jahr versprach Donald Trump der KI-Industrie freie Fahrt ohne «dumme Regeln». Nun zwingen ihn die Konkurrenz aus China und eigenmächtig agierende Modelle zum Umdenken – an zwei Fronten zugleich.

Die KI von Anthropic und Open AI ist nicht einfach «wild geworden» – die beiden Firmen waren lächerlich unvorsichtig

Die KI-Modelle der beiden grossen amerikanischen KI-Anbieter haben während interner Tests andere Firmen angegriffen. Hinter den Hacks steckt die mangelnde Sorgfalt ihrer Macher.

evidence.title: Driving Agentic AI at Scale: Adesso Expands Operations to Pune and Chennai
evidence.text:
Driving Agentic AI at Scale: Adesso Expands Operations to Pune and Chennai

Discover how adesso is expanding operations to Pune and Chennai to accelerate agentic AI, strengthen digital capabilities, and support enterprise innovation.

Driving Agentic AI at Scale: adesso expands operations to Pune and Chennai

The German IT services company’s planned offices will advance adesso’s Agentic AI capabilities while showing how India’s established technology cities can play different but connected roles in global digital transformation.

India’s technology story is told through the rise of a single hub. The next phase may be more distributed. Cities with experience are becoming part of a global delivery network, allowing companies to place work where the right skills exist. Pune and Chennai are examples. One brings an enterprise technology and engineering base; the other has capabilities in data, artificial intelligence and the modernisation of older systems.

German IT services company adesso is preparing to build on those complementary strengths. It plans to inaugurate an independent office in Chennai on August 3 and open another in Pune on August 5. The locations will expand the company’s Indian network and strengthen its ability to deliver Agentic AI solutions, combining autonomous AI agents with human expertise, for clients in India as well as international markets.

The significance of a two-city move is not the number of offices. Transformation programmes rarely depend on one skill. They may require software engineers, cloud specialists, data teams, testing professionals and people who understand a client’s industry. A location network can help bring those abilities together while giving companies access to different talent bases.

Pune’s value lies in its combination of enterprise IT knowledge and engineering experience. Its wider automotive and manufacturing environment also makes it relevant to businesses working on connected systems, modern platforms and operational change. Chennai offers a different mix. The city has established expertise in data, AI and legacy modernisation, areas that become important when companies want to improve existing systems without disrupting the business processes that depend on them.

Adesso intends to position both offices as delivery and innovation locations for Agentic AI, cloud architecture and intelligent automation. Through its Agentic Scale approach, the company aims to use autonomous software agents and AI-driven development frameworks to accelerate software engineering while retaining human oversight for strategy, governance and quality assurance. The planned service range includes custom software development, quality assurance and testing, DevOps, cloud management, data modernisation, AI, Salesforce solutions and SAP transformation. The company expects the teams to work across sectors including automotive, financial services and life sciences.

This is connected to the growth of Global Capability Centres in India. GCCs are in-house units through which international companies manage technology and business functions while retaining expertise. According to adesso’s announcement, more companies from Germany, Austria and Switzerland are establishing such centres in India. That creates demand for technology partners that can work close to their teams and understand the expectations of European headquarters.

The new adesso offices will not themselves be captive GCCs belonging to one multinational. They will serve multiple clients. Their role is better understood as part of the surrounding capability ecosystem: providing specialised teams that can support a company’s India centre, connect with its global technology organisation and contribute to transformation projects that cross countries and functions.

Chennai already offers an early example of this model. adesso India has operated the Exasol Tech Hub in the city since 2025 for German analytics software provider Exasol. The hub supports work linked to Exasol’s analytics engine and its development. The office planned for August will have a wider purpose. It will be adesso India’s first independent, cross-client location in Chennai rather than a centre dedicated to a single company.

The company’s purpose is to improve the core business processes of companies and public organisations through consulting and customised software. Its approach combines industry knowledge, vendor-neutral technology expertise and methods for delivering software projects, with Agentic AI helping teams automate complex workflows and accelerate development. This matters because digital transformation is not only a technology exercise. New systems must clearly fit the work people do, address a business problem and remain reliable, with human expertise continuing to guide critical decisions.

adesso co-founder and Supervisory Board Chair Prof. Dr. Volker Gruhn has said that “IT belongs at the decision-makers’ table.” The idea is relevant to India’s changing role in global technology. If Indian teams are involved only after important choices have been made elsewhere, their contribution remains limited. When they participate earlier, they can help assess technologies, identify practical risks and shape solutions around real operating needs.

For India, the value of such expansion should be judged by the quality of responsibility it creates. Work in cloud architecture, AI, data engineering, enterprise systems and software quality can help professionals build specialised careers. International projects can also give teams experience of different industries, regulatory environments and customer expectations. Over time, that exposure can support stronger technical leadership and a deeper understanding of how global businesses operate.

There is a local benefit as well. Investment across Indian cities can widen access to skilled roles and reduce dependence on one crowded technology corridor. It can also encourage organisations to develop regional leadership instead of treating every decision as a headquarters responsibility. The result is more meaningful when local teams own outcomes, not merely tasks.

That outcome is not automatic. Offices described as innovation hubs must receive work that justifies the label. Companies need to invest in training, responsible AI practices, collaboration and clear career paths. They must also give teams enough authority to solve problems instead of measuring success only through delivery volume. Without those conditions, geographical expansion can add capacity without adding much capability.

The forthcoming Pune and Chennai offices offer adesso access to two mature but distinct technology environments. For European clients building or expanding operations in India, the network is intended to provide closer support for complex transformation work. For Indian professionals, the opportunity lies in moving further into engineering, product thinking and business responsibility.

The inauguration ceremonies will mark the start of the two locations, not the result. Their real importance will become visible in the kind of Agentic AI and transformation work entrusted to them and the decisions their teams are able to influence. If Pune’s engineering depth and Chennai’s data and modernisation strengths are used together, adesso’s expansion could demonstrate a larger point: India’s advantage increasingly comes from the variety of capabilities across its cities, not from scale alone.

evidence.title: Adesso Aktie: Netz Leipzig SAP-Projekt im zweistelligen Millionen-Bereich
evidence.text:
Der IT-Dienstleister Adesso sieht sich derzeit einer zweigeteilten Wahrnehmung an den Märkten gegenüber. Während die operative Seite durch namhafte Großaufträge und strategische Partnerschaften geprägt ist, spiegelt der Aktienkurs die Herausforderungen des laufenden Jahres wider. Medienberichten zufolge gilt das Unternehmen aufgrund seiner tiefen Verwurzelung in krisenresistenten Branchen wie der öffentlichen Verwaltung und dem Gesundheitswesen inzwischen als potenzieller Übernahmekandidat innerhalb des IT-Sektors.

Strategische Großaufträge stärken Marktposition

Ein wesentlicher Pfeiler der aktuellen Geschäftsentwicklung ist die Gewinnung langfristiger Projekte im Bereich der kritischen Infrastruktur und des öffentlichen Sektors. Anfang Juli konnte Adesso einen bedeutenden Erfolg verzeichnen: Die Netz Leipzig GmbH wählte das Unternehmen als Partner für eine umfassende strategische SAP-Transformation aus. Das Projekt umfasst die Migration auf SAP S/4HANA Utilities sowie den anschließenden Betrieb über einen Zeitraum von fünf Jahren. Das Projektvolumen bewegt sich laut Unternehmensangaben im niedrigen zweistelligen Millionen-Euro-Bereich.

Parallel dazu festigte der Konzern seine Rolle als Dienstleister für staatliche Institutionen. Die Deutsche Bundesbank erteilte Adesso im Juni einen Auftrag zur Unterstützung ihrer digitalen Transformationsprozesse. Diese Auftragsgewinne unterstreichen die Wettbewerbsfähigkeit in einem Marktumfeld, das zunehmend von Modernisierungsdruck geprägt ist. Einer aktuellen Studie von Adesso zufolge sehen 83 Prozent der befragten Entscheider ihre wirtschaftliche Entwicklung durch veraltete IT-Systeme gebremst, was das Marktpotenzial für Dienstleister in den kommenden Jahren untermauert.

Fokus auf KI-Integration und Cloud-Automatisierung

Um technologisch an der Spitze zu bleiben, setzt Adesso verstärkt auf Partnerschaften im Bereich der künstlichen Intelligenz. Anfang Juli schloss das Unternehmen eine strategische Allianz mit dem US-Softwareanbieter Workato. Ziel dieser Zusammenarbeit ist die Implementierung von KI-gestützten Integrations- und Automatisierungsplattformen für moderne Cloud-Architekturen. Damit adressiert der IT-Dienstleister den wachsenden Bedarf an effizienten, automatisierten Schnittstellenlösungen in komplexen IT-Landschaften.

Trotz dieser operativen Impulse wird die Aktie in automatisierten Quant-Analysen aufgrund ihrer historischen Volatilität und des aktuellen Risikoprofils vereinzelt als Depotbremser eingestuft. Dennoch zeigen die jüngsten Geschäftszahlen eine Erholung der Profitabilität. Im ersten Quartal 2026 konnte der Umsatz um 13 Prozent auf 398,1 Millionen Euro gesteigert werden. Das EBITDA verbesserte sich deutlich von 17,1 Millionen Euro im Vorjahreszeitraum auf 27,0 Millionen Euro. Auch das Konzernergebnis kehrte mit 2,7 Millionen Euro in die Gewinnzone zurück, nachdem im Vorjahresquartal noch ein Verlust von 7,3 Millionen Euro verzeichnet worden war.

Bewertung und Ausblick auf den Halbjahresbericht

Am Aktienmarkt spiegelt sich die Zuversicht des Vorstands bisher nur bedingt wider. Die Aktie beendete den Handel am Freitag bei 53,20 € und verzeichnet seit Jahresbeginn ein Minus von 40,22 %. Damit notiert das Papier aktuell rund 47,95 % unter seinem 52-Wochen-Hoch, das im September des vergangenen Jahres erreicht wurde. Anleger blicken nun gespannt auf die kommenden Wochen, um zu sehen, ob die operative Dynamik den Kurs stabilisieren kann.

Für das Gesamtjahr 2026 bleibt die Unternehmensführung optimistisch und prognostiziert einen Umsatz zwischen 1,6 Milliarden und 1,7 Milliarden Euro bei einem EBITDA in der Spanne von 130 Millionen bis 150 Millionen Euro. Ein wichtiger Meilenstein für die Bestätigung dieser Ziele wird der 14. August sein, an dem Adesso den vollständigen Halbjahresbericht für das laufende Geschäftsjahr vorlegen wird. Diese Daten dürften entscheidend dafür sein, ob die aktuellen Übernahmespekulationen weitere Nahrung erhalten oder die fundamentale Bewertung wieder stärker in den Vordergrund rückt.

evidence.title: Devoteam bentuk tim khusus percepat adopsi agentic AI perusahaan
evidence.text:
Devoteam bentuk tim khusus percepat adopsi agentic AI perusahaan

Jakarta (ANTARA) - Devoteam Indonesia membentuk tim khusus Agentic Work Transformation (AWT) Tribe untuk membantu perusahaan mempercepat penerapan teknologi agentic artificial intelligence (AI) ke dalam proses kerja. Chief Technology Officer Devoteam Indonesia Fauzal Atmodirono dalam keterangannya, Jumat, mengatakan AWT Tribe dirancang untuk membantu pelanggan melakukan transformasi dengan mengintegrasikan kemampuan agentic AI secara langsung ke dalam alur kerja perusahaan. “AWT Tribe hadir karena bagi kami pelatihan kepada pelanggan tidak mengubah kebiasaan, akan tetapi tahapan dan proseslah yang mengubahnya,” kata Fauzal dalam CIO Summit 2026 di Lombok, Nusa Tenggara Barat. Menurut dia, transformasi AI tidak cukup dilakukan dengan memberikan pelatihan kepada sumber daya manusia, tetapi perlu diikuti perubahan proses kerja agar pemanfaatan teknologi memberikan dampak nyata. “Proses transformasi bukan hanya tentang mengajarkan materi, melainkan seberapa tepat kita memandu orang melewati proses perubahannya,” ujarnya. AWT Tribe akan berfokus membantu perusahaan merancang ulang cara kerja dengan memanfaatkan agentic AI. Teknologi tersebut tidak hanya ditempatkan sebagai alat tambahan, tetapi diintegrasikan ke dalam proses kerja untuk meningkatkan produktivitas dan memungkinkan tenaga kerja lebih fokus pada pekerjaan bernilai tambah. Pembentukan tim tersebut diumumkan dalam CIO Summit 2026 yang digelar Devoteam Indonesia bersama Google Cloud di Lombok pada 10 September 2026. Pertemuan bertema “Fast Track to Value: Scaling Up Business through Secure AI & Analytics” itu mempertemukan sekitar 30 pelanggan Devoteam dari Indonesia dan Malaysia untuk membahas pemanfaatan AI dan analitik dalam menghasilkan nilai bisnis yang terukur. Selain membentuk AWT Tribe, Devoteam mengumumkan keterpilihannya sebagai salah satu mitra dalam program Gemini Enterprise Transformation (GET) Google. Managing Director Devoteam Southeast Asia Hendrawan Deny Ardiyatman mengatakan program tersebut membuka peluang bagi pelanggan di Indonesia dan Malaysia untuk mempercepat penerapan Gemini dalam skala perusahaan. “Terpilihnya kami sebagai mitra GET mencerminkan kedalaman kerja sama yang telah dibangun tim kami bersama Google Cloud selama ini dan membuka jalan yang lebih cepat bagi pelanggan kami di Indonesia dan Malaysia untuk merasakan manfaat nyata dari Gemini,” katanya. Devoteam juga mengumumkan kemitraan dengan penyedia platform data real-time SingleStore untuk memperkuat kapabilitas data dan analitik yang dibutuhkan dalam penerapan AI. Enterprise Sales Director APJ SingleStore Christin Nataly menyebut ketersediaan data secara real-time menjadi salah satu fondasi dalam pengembangan berbagai kasus penggunaan agentic AI. “Melalui kemitraan Devoteam dan SingleStore, kami dapat membantu pelanggan membangun fondasi tersebut dengan lebih cepat sehingga mereka dapat mempercepat adopsi AI dan menghadirkan nilai bisnis secara nyata,” ujar Christin.

evidence.title: Devoteam étend son partenariat avec Dynatrace à toute la région EMEA
evidence.text:
Déjà partenaires dans plusieurs pays européens, Devoteam et Dynatrace donnent une nouvelle dimension à leur collaboration en l’étendant à l’ensemble de la région EMEA. Le groupe de conseil va intégrer plus largement la plateforme d’observabilité de Dynatrace à ses offres cloud, IA et de transformation numérique.

Devoteam et Dynatrace renforcent leur alliance en mettant en place un partenariat stratégique à l’échelle de l’Europe, du Moyen-Orient et de l’Afrique. Cette extension s’appuie sur des collaborations déjà établies notamment en France, en Espagne et au Benelux, où Devoteam a déployé les solutions de l’éditeur auprès de grands comptes des services financiers, des utilities et du luxe.
