evidence.text:
NNIT A/S: Business performance impacted by market undercetainty expected to continue. Mitigating actions taken to protect profitability

The first quarter was more severely affected by uncertainty than expected at the beginning of the year. Hesitance among several customers of NNIT has resulted in less revenue and sales as projects are being postponed. In general, NNIT has taken action to adjust capacity to fit the current demand with several reductions completed in 2024 and leaving NNIT in a stronger position going into 2025. However, it has been necessary to take further actions to mitigate the business impact from lower revenue generation with a reduction of around 100 employees in Q1 2025. Furthermore, NNIT has carried out several cost-reducing initiatives such as putting new employments on hold and limiting all discretionary spending to a minimum with full impact from the second quarter.

Given the current macroeconomic environment and geopolitical unrest, NNIT continues to expect that its customers will be affected, which is reflected in the adjusted full-year financial outlook.

Pär Fors, CEO of NNIT, comments: "The business environment of NNIT has deteriorated in the first quarter of the year as especially our Life Science customers are being negatively impacted by the macroeconomic unrest. Customers are hesitant to engage in new contracts before things are stabilizing, and we are navigating this environment to continue our strategic journey at NNIT. However, the impact from the uncertainty is more severe than initially expected, why the full-year outlook has been adjusted."

evidence.title: JP Morgan sees Softcat deal delivering 10% EPS accretion
evidence.text:
JP Morgan sees Softcat deal delivering 10% EPS accretion

JP Morgan has raised its organic earnings estimates for Softcat PLC (LSE:SCT), the UK IT infrastructure and services provider, after a stronger-than-expected finish to its 2026 financial year and new guidance for 2027.

Analyst Joseph George increased his organic earnings before interest and tax estimates for 2027 and 2028 by about 6-7%, while modelling a potential 10% earnings-per-share uplift from Softcat's planned acquisition of GDT.

George's base case puts Softcat's 2028 EPS at 105p, including GDT, compared with 96p on an organic basis, implying roughly 10% accretion once the deal is completed.

Softcat announced last week that it intends to acquire GDT, although the transaction remains subject to customary regulatory approvals and is expected to close in the first quarter of calendar year 2027.

JP Morgan said the key issue for investors would be GDT's earnings trajectory, given the company's historically uneven financial performance and several accounting differences that will affect the combined group.

These include the treatment of multi-year contract revenue, the conversion from US generally accepted accounting principles to Softcat's more conservative international financial reporting standards and the effect of deferred tax assets.

George expects Softcat to provide more detailed disclosures on the accounting effects of the acquisition when it reports its 2026 results on 14 October.

JP Morgan has not yet incorporated GDT into its published forecasts because the acquisition has not closed, meaning its 10% accretion estimate remains illustrative.

The broker also highlighted Softcat's track record of outperforming its initial earnings growth guidance, with performance exceeding guidance by about nine percentage points on average over the past five financial years.

Softcat has not missed its initial earnings growth guidance during that period, according to George, increasing the scope for investors to assess whether management can outperform its guidance for GDT's earnings contribution.

In a bull-case scenario combining stronger organic growth, higher GDT earnings, lower net financing costs and benefits from deferred tax assets, JP Morgan models 2029 EPS of 127p.

That compares with its organic forecast and implies about 21% upside to its organic EPS estimate, while applying a 25 times price-to-earnings multiple would indicate more than 70% potential share-price upside on a July 2028 basis.

The broker said its initial discussions with investors after the acquisition announcement had supported a more constructive view of the transaction.

evidence.title: JP Morgan backs Softcat's $1.05bn US gamble, sees up to 17% earnings upside
evidence.text:
JP Morgan backs Softcat's $1.05bn US gamble, sees up to 17% earnings upside

JP Morgan has come out in favour of Softcat's $1.05 billion swoop on US group GDT, reckoning investors will give management the benefit of the doubt.

Analyst Joseph George, who rates the FTSE 250 IT infrastructure provider 'overweight', said the bank leaned positive on the deal after sounding out investors.

GDT, a Dallas-based IT solutions provider, will give Softcat a substantial foothold in North America.

Softcat expects the deal to lift earnings per share (EPS) by a high single-digit to low double-digit percentage in its first full financial year after closing.

George thinks that is plausible, pencilling in roughly 10% accretion for the 2028 financial year in his base case.

In a bull case, with upside to both Softcat's own business and GDT, he sees potential for around 17% upside to organic 2028 EPS.

The sticking point, according to JP Morgan, is GDT's earnings trajectory.

There are plenty of moving parts, including how revenue from multi-year contracts is recognised, the switch from US accounting rules to Softcat's more conservative international standards, and the treatment of deferred tax assets.

Still, Softcat has a habit of beating its own guidance, which should buy it some goodwill, George argued.

Separately, the broker lifted its organic earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) forecasts for the 2027 and 2028 financial years by 6% to 7%.

That reflects a stronger-than-expected finish to the year to July 2026 and the guidance issued for the current year.

Softcat raised £354 million last week to help fund the purchase.

evidence.title: Softcat stock falls 1.84 percent as GDT deal reshapes growth
evidence.text:
Softcat stock fell 1.84 percent to GBp 1,813 on September 24, 2026, leaving the shares 15.04 percent below their 52-week high of GBp 2,134. The move follows the company acquisition of GDT and a large equity issue to help fund its expansion into the United States.

Investegate reported on September 17, 2026 that Softcat had agreed to acquire GDT, a US-based IT solutions provider. The transaction gives Softcat a larger transatlantic platform while adding exposure to enterprise networking, data center and cybersecurity services.

The acquisition also changed the near-term earnings framework. According to TradingView , Softcat raised its FY2026 underlying operating profit growth guidance from mid-teens to high-teens and expects preliminary results on October 14, 2026.

For the six months ended January 31, 2026, gross profit increased 22.6 percent to GBP 269.9 million, while underlying operating profit rose 27.3 percent to GBP 93.8 million, according to UK Investor Magazine .

The reported growth provides a useful benchmark for the acquisition strategy. Softcat is entering the transaction with double-digit half-year operating profit growth, while management expects the GDT deal to deliver high-single-digit to low-double-digit underlying earnings-per-share accretion in its first full fiscal year.

Softcat raised GBP 354 million through an equity issue priced at GBp 1,890 per share, according to Investegate . The current market price is GBp 77 below that issue price, highlighting the immediate dilution and funding trade-off surrounding the US expansion.

Softcat stock was trading at GBp 1,813 on the London Stock Exchange on September 24, 2026, down 1.84 percent for the session. The gap to the GBp 2,134 yearly high keeps the acquisition execution and the October 14 results date central to the market narrative.

evidence.title: Softcat Shares Slide 3.7% and Finish 5p Above GDT Deal’s Placing Price
evidence.text:
Softcat plc (LON:SCT) shares fell 3.71% to 1,895 pence on Friday after the British IT reseller unveiled its largest acquisition. The company agreed to buy U.S.-based GDT for $1.05 billion.

The close left the stock only five pence above its 1,890-pence placing price. That narrow gap suggests investors priced the financing quickly, but withheld a deal premium.

The transaction shifts Softcat from net cash to projected net debt. Management expects leverage of 1.3 times at closing, versus net cash of 0.7 times before it.

Source: StockAnalysis market history , as of the September 18 London close. GBX means pence sterling.

Friday’s 4.11 million-share volume was 15.3 times Thursday’s total. That scale points to a one-day institutional reset, not a routine drift.

GDT serves about 700 enterprise and upper-midmarket customers across networking, data centres and cybersecurity. Softcat expects the target to produce about $240 million of gross profit and $80 million of EBITDA in 2026.

The price equals 13.1 times that forecast EBITDA, by TS2 calculations. Softcat forecasts high-single-digit to low-double-digit underlying EPS accretion in the first full fiscal year.

Source: Softcat transaction announcement . Forecasts are company estimates; the multiple is calculated from reported dollar values.

The funding mix includes £100 million of cash and £550 million of new facilities. The equity issue added 18.74 million possible shares, equal to 9.5% of the previous count.

Softcat raised about £354 million gross and £345 million net. Chief Executive Graham Charlton said the company received “strong support” for the issue.

The deal arrived with a stronger trading update. Softcat now expects high-teens FY2026 underlying operating-profit growth, raised from a mid-teens view.

Cash conversion should land near the top of its 85% to 95% range. Excluding GDT, management expects high-single-digit underlying operating-profit growth in FY2027.

The counterargument is straightforward. GDT reported a $58.4 million net loss for 2025, while Softcat will absorb debt, integration costs and foreign-exchange exposure.

Sources: TipRanks and Investing.com . Targets are attributable published recommendations; returns are TS2 calculations from the 1,895-pence close.

The target spread captures the dispute. Jefferies sees 10.3% downside, while JPMorgan’s target implies 21.4% upside from Friday’s close.

Risks: GDT’s regulatory closing could slip, integration may miss the promised accretion, and dollar moves could raise Softcat’s effective purchase cost.

The new shares are expected to start trading on September 22. Softcat’s October 14 preliminary results should provide the next test of cash conversion and the revised profit outlook.

evidence.text:

wallstreetONLINE zufolge hob Deutsche Bank Research das Kursziel für Bechtle am 21.09.2026 von 45 auf 49 EUR an und beließ die Einstufung bei Buy. Damit liegt das neue Ziel 46,62 Prozent über dem Xetra-Kurs von 33,42 EUR am 25.09.2026.

September 2026 | 06:00 Uhr Facebook Twitter Whatsapp Linkedin Cfdiumf&31fs&D4&C7ggofu&31Ojfefsmbttvoh&31jo&31Ofv.Vmn'cpez>iuuqt&4B&3G&3Gxxx/c5ctdixbcfo/ef&3Gc5c.obdisjdiufo&3Gvmn.ofv.vmn`bsujlfm&3D.cfdiumf.fspfggofu.ojfefsmbttvoh.jo.ofvvmn.`bsje&3D386763/iunm');"> E-Mail Drucken Facebook Twitter Whatsapp Linkedin Cfdiumf&31fs&D4&C7ggofu&31Ojfefsmbttvoh&31jo&31Ofv.Vmn'cpez>iuuqt&4B&3G&3Gxxx/c5ctdixbcfo/ef&3Gc5c.obdisjdiufo&3Gvmn.ofv.vmn`bsujlfm&3D.cfdiumf.fspfggofu.ojfefsmbttvoh.jo.ofvvmn.`bsje&3D386763/iunm');"> E-Mail Drucken 2023 angekündigt, ist es bald soweit: Das IT-Unternehmen eröffnet einen zweiten Standort in Bayerisch-Schwaben und verlagert drei Tochtergesellschaften in den Neu-Ulmer IT-Campus. Die Bechtle AG verstärkt seine Präsenz in Bayerisch-Schwaben und eröffnet eine Niederlassung in Neu-Ulm. Dort will das IT-Unternehmen die Kompetenzen dreier Tochterunternehmen – Bechtle PLM aus Langenau, das IT-Systemhaus Ulm sowie Bechtle Additive Manufacturing GmbH – bündeln. Der Neubau, zu dem auch ein begrüntes Parkhaus gehört, soll noch im September 2026 fertiggestellt werden. Über die Investitionssumme macht Bechtle keine Angaben. Bei dem verantwortlichen Bauunternehmen handelt es sich um das Günzburger Familienunternehmen Bendl.

Standortwahl soll strategisches Wachstum ermögliche

Der Bechtle IT-Zukunfts-Hub in Neu-Ulm, wie das Unternehmen diese Art der Niederlassung nennt, werde auf sechs Stockwerken eine Fläche von 5.000 Quadratmetern haben und Arbeitsplätze für bis zu 300 Mitarbeitende bieten. 175 davon sollen dort direkt nach Bezug durch die drei Tochterunternehmen anfangen. Einen konkreten Zeitplan für die Besetzung der übrigen Stellen gibt es nicht. In erster Linie ging es darum, zukunftsorientiert Platz für Wachstum zu schaffen, wie ein Sprecher des Unternehmens auf Anfrage erklärt. Bei diesem Punkt kommt auch die Standortauswahl zum Tragen, denn der IT-Campus biete zukunftssichere Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten. So befinde sich das neue Büro zum einen in der Nähe verschiedener anderer Niederlassungen, was deren Arbeit untereinander zugutekommen soll. Zum anderen ist die Hochschule Neu-Ulm fußläufig erreichbar, was auch hier Kooperationen erleichtern soll, etwa für dezidierte Projekte oder bei der Vergabe von Bachelor- oder Masterarbeiten. Bechtle ziehe sogar in Erwägung, Teile des Gebäudes für Studierende der HNU zugänglich zu machen, wie aus der ursprünglichen Ankündigung des Bauvorhabens hervorgeht.

E-Mobilität trifft auf ressourcenschonende Architektur

Teil des Neubaus ist ein ebenfalls siebenstöckiges Parkhaus, das sich direkt neben dem Bürogebäude befindet. Es besitze 240 Stellplätze, 40 davon mit Ladesäulen für E-Autos, und entspricht damit dem „Charge@Work“-Konzept von Bechtle. Dabei handelt es sich um einen Ansatz der konzernweiten Nachhaltigkeitsstrategie, der den Umstieg von E-Autos für Beschäftigte erleichtern soll. Der Strom der Ladeinfrastruktur stamme dabei ausschließlich aus regenerativen Quellen. Darüber hinaus wurden auf beiden Gebäuden PV-Anlagen mit einer Leistung von bis zu 180 kWP verbaut, das Klima innerhalb der Räume werde über eine Grundwasserwärmepumpe reguliert. Sichtbar wird der ökologische Anspruch auch an der Architektur. So wurde die Fassade mit echtem Moos begrünt. Laut der Website des dafür zuständigen Herstellers Moosmoos handelt es sich mit mehr als 1.600 Quadratmetern Moosfläche um die größte Fassade dieser Art in Deutschland. Das Moos erfordere keinerlei zusätzlichen Bewässerungssaufwand, Niederschlag und Luftfeuchtigkeit sollen ausreichen. Zudem fungiere es als Lärmschutz und Feinstaubfilter und wirke sich damit positiv auf das Mikroklima rund um den Bürokomplex aus. Gleichzeitig erfülle Bechtle damit eine durch die Kommune formulierte Anforderung für Neubauten.

evidence.title: Bechtle übernimmt 3D-Druck-Geschäft von Kaut-Bullinger
evidence.text:
Bechtle übernimmt 3D-Druck-Geschäft von Kaut-Bullinger

Der bayerische Office-Spezialist Kaut-Bullinger trennt sich von seiner 3D-Druck-Sparte. Im Rahmen eines Asset Deals übernimmt die Bechtle Additive Manufacturing Deutschland die Geschäfte. Kaut-Bullinger befindet sich nach der Insolvenz im September 2024 in einer Phase der Neuausrichtung. Über Vertragsbedingungen und Kaufpreis haben die Unternehmen Vertraulichkeit vereinbart.

Das in Taufkirchen bei München ansässige Traditionsunternehmen zieht sich mit diesem Schritt vollständig aus dem 3D-Druck-Business zurück. „Mit Bechtle haben wir einen starken und im Markt hervorragend positionierten Partner gefunden, der das 3D-Druck-Geschäft langfristig erfolgreich weiterentwickeln kann. Die Übertragung der Business Unit 3D ist Teil unserer strategischen Neuausrichtung und schafft für unsere Kunden, Mitarbeitenden und Partner eine verlässliche Perspektive“, bekräftigt Kaut-Bullinger-Geschäftsführer Georg Nusser. Er gibt sich zuversichtlich, dass die Kunden von der technologischen Expertise, der Serviceorganisation und der hohen Marktdurchdringung von Bechtle profitieren werden.

Wie Bechtle war auch Kaut-Bullinger einer der größten deutschen HP-3D-Druck-Partner. Mit dem Geschäftsbereich übernimmt die Bechtle Gruppe nicht nur einen der stärksten Mitbewerber im professionellen 3D-Druck-Geschäft, sondern stärkt damit auch massiv die Partnerschaft mit HP. Zudem baut Bechtle damit die Präsenz im österreichischen Markt aus. „Additive Manufacturing ist ein strategisches Wachstumsfeld für Bechtle. Wir wollen unsere führende Position in Europa weiter stärken, in der DACH-Region zusätzliche Marktanteile gewinnen und gezielt in europäische Märkte expandieren“, gibt Uwe Burk, Bereichsvorstand PLM | Engineering & Manufacturing bei der Bechtle AG, die Marschroute aus. Der Ausbau des HP 3D-Druck-Geschäfts sei dafür ein wichtiger nächster Schritt.

Das europäische PLM-Netzwerk der Bechtle Gruppe umfasst die Unternehmen Bechtle PLM Deutschland, Bechtle PLM Austria, Bechtle PLM Schweiz, die spezialisierte Bechtle Additive-Manufacturing-Gesellschaften in Deutschland und der Schweiz sowie die Schwesterunternehmen EuroSolid (Ungarn), Nuovamacut (Italien), Cadmes (Benelux und Frankreich) und DriveWorks (Großbritannien). Mit Aktivitäten in neun Ländern und insgesamt mehr als 1.000 Fachleuten ist die Bechtle Gruppe einer der größten PLM-Anbieter Europas.

Bechtle hatte 2024 das Geschäft mit der Additiven Fertigung an die neu gegründete Tochtergesellschaft Bechtle Additive Manufacturing Deutschland ausgelagert.

Für Patrick Schnizler, Geschäftsführer der Bechtle-Tochter, ist die Übernahme ist ein wichtiger Schritt für den weiteren Ausbau der Marktposition im Bereich Additive Manufacturing: „Mit den hinzugewonnenen Kundenbeziehungen, der installierten Systembasis und der ausgewiesenen Anwendungs- und Servicekompetenz erweitern wir unsere Leistungsfähigkeit erneut“, erklärt er. Zudem verweist er auf die Stärkung der Partnerschaft mit HP. Dies schaffe „beste Voraussetzungen“, um die Kunden entlang der gesamten Wertschöpfungskette des industriellen 3D-Drucks noch umfassender zu begleiten.

Kaut-Bullinger unter Schutzschirmverfahren

HP startet 3D-Druck-Channel: Fünf Partner für den HP-3D-Druck

Armin Weiler kümmert sich um die rechercheintensiven Geschichten rund um den ITK-Channel und um die Themen der Distribution. Zudem ist er für den Bereich PCs und Peripherie zuständig. Zu seinen Spezialgebieten zählen daher Notebooks, PCs, Smartphones, Drucker, Displays und Eingabegeräte. Bei der inoffiziellen deutschen IT-Skimeisterschaft "CP Race" ist er für die Rennleitung verantwortlich.

evidence.title: Bechtle Absorbs Kaut-Bullinger’s HP 3D Printing Operations
evidence.text:
Home - Bechtle Absorbs Kaut-Bullinger’s HP 3D Printing Operations

Bechtle Additive Manufacturing Deutschland has acquired the HP 3D printing business of Kaut-Bullinger GmbH & Co. KG through an asset deal, a move that reinforces Bechtle’s position as HP ‘s top global partner in additive manufacturing (AM).

The deal combines Bechtle with its largest competitor in the German HP 3D printing market, while also further strengthening its presence in Austria. It brings established customer relationships, an experienced team, existing HP manufacturer and partner agreements, and new services for HP direct customers across both markets. With the sale, Kaut-Bullinger, a long-established family-owned company, is exiting the 3D printing sector entirely.

By folding Kaut-Bullinger’s 3D printing unit into its existing sales, service, and administrative structures, Bechtle expects to realize operational synergies and increase capacity utilization. The company also points to opportunities for growing business with existing customers and expanding recurring revenue from services, care packs, and consumables, alongside its partnership with HP.

Bechtle’s PLM, CAD, and AM network now spans nine countries, combining its own AM companies in Germany and Switzerland with sister firms EuroSolid in Hungary, Nuovamacut in Italy, Cadmes in Benelux and France, and DriveWorks in the UK, backed by more than 1,000 specialists. The purchase price and other terms of the deal were not disclosed.

“With Bechtle, we have found a strong partner that is ideally positioned to successfully drive the long-term development of the 3D printing business, and provide customers, employees and partners with a promising future as part of our strategic realignment,” said Georg Nusser, managing director of Kaut-Bullinger. “We are confident that customers will benefit from Bechtle’s technological expertise, service organisation and broad market reach.”

Patrick Schnizler, managing director of Bechtle AM Deutschland, said the acquisition further consolidates the company’s position in the AM market, adding customer relationships, installed systems, and application and service expertise. “At the same time, the acquisition is deepening our partnership with HP, enabling us to support customers even more comprehensively across the entire industrial 3D printing value chain,” he said.

“Additive manufacturing is a strategic growth area for Bechtle. As we continue to strengthen our leading position in Europe, broaden our market presence across the DACH region and expand into selected European markets, the expansion of our HP 3D printing business marks an important next step,” said Uwe Burk, executive vice president of PLM, engineering and manufacturing at Bechtle AG .

From (L-R): Patrick Schnizler, Uwe Burk, and Georg Nusser. Photo via Bechtle.

How the Kaut-Bullinger Deal Fits a Wider HP Channel Pattern

Bechtle’s acquisition follows a specific strategy: deepening an already-strong position within HP’s 3D printing channel by absorbing a rival reseller’s customer base, instead of diversifying into other printer brands or adjacent business lines. The deal keeps Bechtle inside its existing technology and geographic lane, while removing its largest domestic competitor.

A similar channel consolidation played out in the US HP 3D printing market this year, when Master Graphics (M5D) absorbed TPM’s HP 3D printing and Advanced Manufacturing Technologies division. Like Bechtle, M5D had already built its entire operation around HP 3D printing, and the deal deepened that footprint without a strategic pivot. The parallel stops at scale and geography: M5D’s deal covered a single reseller’s HP business within one country, while Bechtle’s move also folds in service and administrative structures across two markets, Germany and Austria.

As the HP 3D printing channel matures, the specialists already built around it are growing by absorbing rivals’ accounts instead of adding new brands.

evidence.title: Cancom stock falls 1.34 percent after TecDAX exit
evidence.text:
Cancom stock (ISIN DE0005419105) stood at EUR 22.15 on Xetra on September 24, 2026, down 1.34 percent from the previous close. The company left the TecDAX on September 21, 2026, after its lower market capitalization cost it a place in the index, as 4investors reported.

Cancom's first-half 2026 revenue declined 3.5 percent from the prior-year period, while EBITDA rose 34 percent to EUR 49.2 million. The combination points to a sharper profitability improvement despite weaker top-line development.

The German IT services provider also improved its domestic EBITDA margin from 2.7 percent in the prior-year period to 6.1 percent in the first half of 2026. These figures were reported by 4investors on September 3, 2026.

Guidance stays at EUR 1.75 billion to EUR 1.85 billion

For fiscal year 2026, Cancom continues to target revenue of EUR 1.75 billion to EUR 1.85 billion, according to 4investors . The range places the current investment debate between still subdued growth and a measurable recovery in operating profitability.

For investors, the key contrast is visible in the H1 figures: revenue moved lower by 3.5 percent, but EBITDA expanded by 34 percent. That spread makes margin execution more important than index membership for evaluating the next results.

Cancom's market capitalization was EUR 636,584,421 on September 24, 2026. At EUR 22.15, the Xetra price was 24.79 percent below the 52-week high of EUR 29.45 and 10.47 percent above the 52-week low of EUR 20.05.

evidence.title: OHB SE Aktie: Ersetzt CANCOM im TecDAX
evidence.text:
Mit dem Aufstieg in den TecDAX hat der im Prime Standard notierte Raumfahrtkonzern OHB SE zum Wochenauftakt einen wichtigen Meilenstein erreicht. Das Bremer Unternehmen ersetzt im Kreis der dreißig liquidesten und kapitalstärksten deutschen Technologiewerte den IT-Dienstleister CANCOM SE.

Die Umstellung geht auf die planmäßige Überprüfung des Indexanbieters STOXX vom 3. September zurück. Bereits im Vormonat war OHB in den Kleinwerteindex SDAX aufgenommen worden.

Ehrgeizige Prognosen für das laufende Geschäftsjahr

Die Aufnahme in das Technologiebarometer fällt in eine Phase ambitionierter operativer Zielsetzungen. Für das Geschäftsjahr 2026 stellt das Management eine konsolidierte Gesamtleistung von rund 1,4 Milliarden Euro in Aussicht. Die bereinigte EBITDA-Marge soll sich nach Konzernangaben in einer Spanne von 10,5 bis 11,0 Prozent bewegen.

OHB Aktie: Kaufen oder Verkaufen? Hier weiterlesen ...

Mittelfristig peilt das Unternehmen noch deutlich größere Dimensionen an. Der Zielkorridor sieht eine Steigerung der Gesamtleistung auf mehr als 4,0 Milliarden Euro vor. Begleitend dazu soll die bereinigte operative Marge auf rund 13 Prozent zulegen.

Rückendeckung für diese Expansionspläne liefert das bestehende Projektgeschäft. Der Konzern verweist auf eine Projektpipeline im Volumen von rund 20 Milliarden Euro. CEO Marco Fuchs wertete den Einzug in das Technologie-Oberhaus als Anerkennung der bisherigen Unternehmensentwicklung. Die Aufnahme erhöhe die Sichtbarkeit bei nationalen wie internationalen Investoren spürbar.

Am Aktienmarkt spiegelte sich der Wechsel in das Börsenbarometer zunächst verhalten wider. Im heutigen Handel verliert das Papier 2,2 Prozent auf 173,80 Euro. Über das gesamte laufende Jahr betrachtet steht jedoch ein Zuwachs von 49 Prozent zu Buche.

Eigentümerstruktur und anstehende Termine

Getragen wird der Wachstumskurs von klaren Eigentümerverhältnissen. Die Gründerfamilie Fuchs hält weiterhin die unternehmerische Mehrheit an der OHB SE. Der Finanzinvestor KKR, der seit 2023 über die Gesellschaft Orchid Lux HoldCo S.à r.l. beteiligt ist, agiert als Minderheitsaktionär.

Im Zuge einer Kapitalerhöhung im Juni 2026 hatte KKR als Verkäufer von Bestandsaktien agiert, wodurch frisches Kapital von neuen Investoren zufloss. Laut Halbjahresbericht von Anfang August 2026 belief sich die Beteiligung von KKR zuletzt auf rund 20 Prozent.

Konkrete Aufschlüsse über den aktuellen Geschäftsverlauf und die Umsetzung der Aufträge erwarten Marktteilnehmer zur Vorlage des nächsten Quartalsberichts. Die Veröffentlichung der Zahlen zum dritten Quartal ist für den 12. November 2026 terminiert.

OHB-Aktie: Kaufen oder verkaufen?! Neue OHB-Analyse vom 25. September liefert die Antwort:

Die neusten OHB-Zahlen sprechen eine klare Sprache: Dringender Handlungsbedarf für OHB-Aktionäre . Lohnt sich ein Einstieg oder sollten Sie lieber verkaufen? In der aktuellen Gratis-Analyse vom 25. September erfahren Sie was jetzt zu tun ist.

evidence.title: CANCOM Opens New Norderstedt Service Factory to Expand IT Lifecycle Capacity and Support More Than 100,000 Dataport Workstations
evidence.text:
CANCOM Opens New Norderstedt Service Factory to Expand IT Lifecycle Capacity and Support More Than 100,000 Dataport Workstations

With a symbolic ribbon-cutting ceremony, Rüdiger Rath, CEO of CANCOM, and Dr. Johann Bizer, Chairman of the Board of Dataport AöR, officially opened the CANCOM Service Factory Nord.

(IN BRIEF) CANCOM has opened a new 4,250-square-metre Service Factory Nord in Norderstedt near Hamburg, expanding its nationwide capacity for IT lifecycle services and large-scale workplace deployments. The facility combines logistics, device configuration, service coordination, operational planning and technical field-service management and includes 12 automated conveyor lines and around 2,800 storage slots. CANCOM expects the site to process up to 1,000 devices per day and configure as many as 488 devices simultaneously. Together with its existing Service Factory in Jettingen-Scheppach, the new location creates a north-south infrastructure for nationwide customer projects. One of its first major assignments is a contract to equip and support more than 100,000 IT workstations for Dataport, including device provision, configuration, service coordination and on-site support. CANCOM also plans to create up to 100 jobs in Norderstedt. CEO Rüdiger Rath said the expansion responds to growing demand for scalable lifecycle services, while Dataport Chairman Dr. Johann Bizer highlighted the facility’s role in supporting the continued digitalisation of public administration.

(PRESS RELEASE) MUNICH, 18-Sep-2026 — / EuropaWire / — CANCOM has officially opened its new Service Factory Nord in Norderstedt, near Hamburg , expanding its nationwide infrastructure for IT lifecycle services and adding substantial capacity for logistics, device configuration, service coordination and technical support across northern Germany.

The new facility was formally inaugurated during a ceremony attended by around 400 customers, partners and representatives from business and politics. Rüdiger Rath, CEO of CANCOM , and Dr. Johann Bizer, Chairman of the Board of Dataport AöR , marked the opening with a symbolic ribbon-cutting ceremony.

The opening concludes the construction phase and moves the site into regular operation. Together with CANCOM’s existing Service Factory in Jettingen-Scheppach, the Norderstedt facility creates a north-south service structure designed to support large-scale workplace rollouts and IT lifecycle projects across Germany.

The approximately 4,250-square-metre Service Factory combines several stages of the IT device lifecycle within a single location, including logistics, hardware configuration, service coordination, operational planning and management of technical field services.

The facility incorporates 12 automated conveyor lines and approximately 2,800 logistics storage slots, allowing large volumes of IT end devices to be processed and prepared in parallel.

Once fully operational, CANCOM expects the Norderstedt site to handle up to 1,000 devices per day and configure as many as 488 end devices simultaneously.

The infrastructure is designed to support both major workplace deployments and recurring replacement or refresh programmes, enabling customers to manage large device fleets through standardised and scalable service processes.

By integrating logistics, configuration and field services, CANCOM aims to provide an end-to-end process extending from device preparation and staging through delivery, on-site installation and subsequent technical support.

One of the first major programmes using the new capacity will be CANCOM’s project for Dataport, under which the company will equip and support more than 100,000 IT workstations.

The contract, announced in spring 2026, is beginning in September and includes the provision and configuration of end-user devices as well as service coordination and on-site technical support.

Dataport provides digital infrastructure and services for public administration, and CANCOM said the scale of the project illustrates the importance of highly automated logistics and standardised lifecycle-management processes for large public-sector digitalisation programmes.

Dr. Johann Bizer, Chairman of the Board of Dataport AöR , said the new facility demonstrates the operational structures and professional processes required to reliably deploy and support modern IT workplaces on a large scale.

He said the Norderstedt Service Factory provides an important foundation for Dataport and CANCOM as they continue supporting the digitalisation of public administration.

The opening event also included presentations and panel discussions covering developments in workplace services, asset management, IT lifecycle services and the modern digital workplace.

CANCOM said the facility is intended not only to increase physical processing capacity but also to improve coordination between central logistics and technical teams working at customer locations.

The company is also expanding its regional workforce as part of the project.

CANCOM plans to create up to 100 new jobs in Norderstedt, including roles in logistics, device configuration, service coordination and technical field support.

Rüdiger Rath, CEO of CANCOM , said demand for IT lifecycle services remains high and continues to increase as organisations operate larger and more complex workplace environments.

He said the investment gives CANCOM additional capacity to deliver large customer projects efficiently and at scale while maintaining regional proximity.

Rath added that combining the Norderstedt facility with the company’s Jettingen-Scheppach operation establishes a high-capacity north-south infrastructure and represents an important step in the continued development of CANCOM’s services business.

The facility’s automated configuration and storage infrastructure is intended to enable large batches of laptops, desktops and other end-user equipment to be prepared according to customer specifications before deployment.

This can include hardware configuration, software installation, asset assignment, packaging, delivery coordination and preparation for installation by field-service teams.

Centralising these activities is designed to improve consistency while providing the capacity required for projects involving tens of thousands of devices across numerous locations.

The Dataport programme will provide an early large-scale use case for the new operating model, with more than 100,000 workplace systems requiring coordinated deployment and ongoing support.

CANCOM said the project also demonstrates how service factories can support digital transformation by combining high-volume device logistics with technical service delivery.

The Norderstedt opening strengthens CANCOM’s service footprint in northern Germany while increasing the company’s ability to support customers with nationwide workplace deployments, recurring refresh cycles and comprehensive lifecycle management.

As a leading Digital Business Provider and AI-enabler, CANCOM leads companies, organizations and the public sector into the digital future. The range of services and solutions includes classic system house IT solutions as well as data-based digital solutions, managed services and cloud services. We accompany the digital evolution of our customers with passion and technology and support them in reducing the complexity of their IT and developing new business models. We offer a holistic portfolio for all IT and business requirements.

The CANCOM Group’s offering comprises innovative solutions in the areas of Artificial Intelligence, Security & Network, Datacenter & Cloud, IoT Solutions and Modern Workplace and includes services for the entire IT lifecycle – from the provision of IT infrastructures, planning and integration, to support, managed services and XaaS. Customers benefit from the extensive expertise with which their diverse requirements are translated into concrete industry-specific IT solutions to significantly promote their business success.

The more than 5,300 employees of the internationally active CANCOM Group with around 80 locations in the DACH region, Belgium, Slovakia, Romania and the Czech Republic as well as an efficient partner network ensure market presence and customer proximity. The transaction value of PLN 705 million and the 9.99 percent stake size give the move a clear market scale, while Reuters tied the reaction to a 25-year high on September 21, 2026.

That matters for investors because the peg is not a vague sector story but a concrete ownership shift with an immediate price signal.

For the latest reported numbers, Asseco Poland's first-half 2026 figures remain the key operating reference: the company reported revenue of PLN 8.15 billion, EBITDA of PLN 1.23 billion and net profit of PLN 309.7 million for H1 2026, all within the current freshness window.

The same half-year set also shows a comparison point: revenue and profit were both still being measured against the prior-year base, which makes the current operating trend more useful than a simple headline move.

evidence.title: Rafał Kozłowski nowym prezesem Asseco Poland
evidence.text:
Zmiana nastąpi 1 stycznia 2027 roku. Rada Nadzorcza Asseco Poland powołała go na stanowisko prezesa zarządu na kadencję 2027-2031. Adam Góral, założyciel i prezes zarządu firmy zostanie przewodniczącym Rady Nadzorczej.

Rafał Kozłowski od 2025 roku pełni funkcję wiceprezes zarządu Asseco Poland. Odpowiada za ERP i działalność międzynarodową oraz Biuro Projektów ERP.

Karierę zawodową zaczynał w latach 1996-1998 jako dyrektor finansowy w Delta Software. Następnie w latach 1998-2003 Senior Managera w Veraudyt. W latach 2004-2006 był dyrektorem Departamentu Skarbu w Softbank (firmy, która została przejęta przez Asseco Poland). Został tam też oddelegowany do pełnienia funkcji wiceprezesa ds. finansów w spółce zależnej Sawan.

W latach 2007-2009 pełnił funkcję dyrektora Pionu Kontrolingu i Inwestycji w Asseco Poland. Od maja 2008 roku do maja 2012 roku pełnił funkcję wiceprezesa Asseco South Eastern Europe. W tym okresie był bezpośrednio zaangażowany w przejęcia spółek wchodzących w skład holdingu Asseco South Eastern Europe, a także przeprowadzenie procesu IPO holdingu na Giełdzie Papierów Wartościowych.

W latach 2012-2021 jako wiceprezes Asseco Poland i CFO Grupy Asseco był odpowiedzialny za zarządzanie finansami. Od 2020 roku sprawuje funkcję prezesa zarządu Asseco Enterprise Solutions odpowiadającego za rozwój obszaru ERP w Grupie Asseco. W latach 2014-2024 pełnił funkcję wiceprezesa zarządu a od 2024 sprawuje funkcję prezesa zarządu Asseco Western Europe.

Zasiada w Radach Dyrektorów (BoD) Formula Systems oraz Asseco International. Pełni funkcję Przewodniczącego Rady Nadzorczej Asseco Business Solutions, Asseco Solutions (Czechy), Asseco Solutions (Słowacja), Asseco Solutions (Niemcy), GSTN Consulting, Aquapark Sopot oraz Park Wodny Sopot. Jest także Członkiem Rady Nadzorczej Dahliamatic. Od roku 2025 pełni funkcję dyrektora wykonawczego w spółce Asseco PST Holding.

W rozmowie ze mną Rafał powiedział: „Z sukcesją jest ten problem, że większość ludzi myśli o niej dopiero w momencie, w którym zapada formalna decyzja o zmianie na stanowisku prezesa. Tymczasem w Asseco traktujemy sukcesję jako stały, systemowy proces. Jest to element odpowiedzialnego zarządzania firmą, a nie jednorazowe wydarzenie.

Adam narzucił z góry zasadę, że każda osoba zarządzająca musi mieć następcę: zarówno w horyzoncie długoterminowym, jak i na wypadek, gdyby coś się wydarzyło albo dana osoba musiała zająć się innym obszarem. W tym sensie każda osoba w grupie, która wchodzi na ścieżkę liderską i bierze odpowiedzialność za większy fragment biznesu, jest „przygotowywana do sukcesji”. Może nie konkretnie do fotela prezesa, ale do brania coraz większej odpowiedzialności.

Jeśli pytasz, kiedy z Adamem zaczęliśmy poważniej rozmawiać o tym, że rozważa mnie jako swojego następcę, to było to dobrych kilka lat temu, jeszcze zanim przeszedłem z funkcji finansowej w stronę biznesu i wziąłem odpowiedzialność za rozwiązania ERP w Grupie Asseco. To właśnie ten kontekst – chęć zdobycia szerszych doświadczeń biznesowych – był jednym z powodów tej zmiany”.

„Asseco jest dobrze poukładaną organizacją, z bardzo solidnymi fundamentami. Nie ma potrzeby „przewracania stolika”. Mówimy raczej o tym, że z tych fundamentów można się odbić, aby szybciej reagować na wyzwania rynku, w tym na rewolucję AI” – dodał.

Z kolei w liście do akcjonariuszy i partnerów biznesowych Asseco Poland, Adam Góral napisał: „Po moim przejściu do Rady Nadzorczej chciałbym, aby organizacja była zarządzana przez osoby, których interes jest jeszcze silniej powiązany z interesem akcjonariuszy. Osoby, które podobnie jak my, odczuwają skutki zarówno dobrych, jak i nietrafionych decyzji zarządczych, nie tylko poprzez wysokość swojego wynagrodzenia, lecz także poprzez zmianę wartości posiadanych akcji. Moi nowi Partnerzy Biznesowi wystąpili z tą inicjatywą, ponieważ podobnie jak ja traktują ją jako inwestycję i próbę długoterminowego zabezpieczenia interesów wszystkich akcjonariuszy naszej spółki”.

Rafał Kozłowski powołany na prezesa Asseco Poland

Obejmie stanowisko z dniem 1 stycznia 2027 roku. Adam Góral przejdzie do rady nadzorczej.

Rafał Kozłowski będzie następcą Adama Górala na czele Grupy Asseco Poland.

Rada nadzorcza Asseco Poland powołała zarząd spółki na nową kadencję, obejmującą lata 2027-2031.

Funkcję prezesa zarządu z dniem 1 stycznia 2027 r. obejmie Rafał Kozłowski . Tym samym dokona się historyczna zmiana u steru największego polskiego koncernu informatycznego, którym kieruje Adam Góral . Założyciel i wieloletni lider grupy, znaczący akcjonariusz (Adam Góral Fundacja Rodzinna ma 10,98 proc. akcji) i wciąż aktualny prezes przejdzie wraz z początkiem 2027 roku do rady nadzorczej, zgodnie z uchwałą z maja br.

Decyzje walnego z maja br. i rady nadzorczej z września br. potwierdzają natomiast realizację przygotowywanego od lat planu sukcesji. Adam Góral oficjalnie wskazał Rafała Kozłowskiego jako swojego następcę w 2023 roku.

Rafał Kozłowski jest związany z Grupą Asseco od dwóch dekad. W latach 2012 – 2021 był wiceprezesem Asseco Poland SA i dyrektorem finansowym grupy. W 2020 r. stanął na czele spółki Asseco Enterprise Solutions. Natomiast na początku 2025 r. ponownie wszedł do zarządu Asseco Poland, obejmując funkcję wiceprezesa. Pełni również funkcje w radach dyrektorów i radach nadzorczych spółek z grupy.

evidence.text:
Rada nadzorcza największej polskiej firmy IT powołała zarząd na nową kadencję. Po raz pierwszy nie będzie w nim założyciela spółki, Adama Górala.

evidence.title: Asseco Poland SA Delivers Record Results Amid Tailwinds
evidence.text:
Asseco Poland SA Delivers Record Results Amid Tailwinds

Asseco Poland SA ( (PL:ACP) ) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Asseco Poland SA’s latest earnings call highlighted a markedly upbeat tone as management celebrated record revenue, sharply higher profits and expanding margins, all underpinned by strong demand across public, financial and ERP solutions. While acknowledging tax one-offs, impairments and temporary cash pressures, executives stressed these were largely transitory against a backdrop of robust operational momentum and a growing order backlog.

Record revenue and profits mark a standout half-year

Management reported group revenue rising 16% year on year to PLN 9.25 billion, with operating profit surging about 38% to above PLN 1.08 billion. Net profit climbed roughly 52% to around PLN 430 million, underscoring a rare combination of fast top-line growth and hefty bottom-line expansion.

Diversified segments drive growth resilience

Formula Systems was the fastest-growing segment at about 18% growth, while Asseco Poland itself expanded revenue by around 17% to more than PLN 1.3 billion and Asseco International advanced roughly 9% to PLN 2.372 billion. The group’s risk profile remains balanced, with the top 10 clients contributing only about 13% of revenue and the largest single customer roughly 2%.

Public sector and finance solutions power product gains

Solutions for public institutions were a standout, growing nearly 30% to close to PLN 2.5 billion and now making up about 27% of total revenue. Financial-sector solutions also performed well, rising around 11% toward PLN 2 billion, while ERP revenue increased about 17% to PLN 934 million.

Margin expansion strengthens profitability profile

Non-IFRS EBITDA grew around 27% over six months and roughly 33% in the second quarter, reflecting strong operational leverage. Non-IFRS operating profit rose about 33% over the half-year, while reported operating profit climbed around 38% over six months and about 43% in Q2, lifting consolidated margins by roughly 1.5 to 1.9 percentage points.

Solid cash conversion and net cash underpin balance sheet

The group delivered cash conversion of about 105% of EBITDA, with Asseco Poland near 113% and Asseco International around 133%. Proportional net cash was clarified at roughly PLN 1.3 billion, giving investors comfort that the company retains a strong liquidity cushion despite dividend payments.

Order backlog growth signals sustained demand

The order backlog for software and services expanded strongly, up around 14% on a fixed-exchange-rate basis and roughly 16% on a variable basis for the group. Asseco Poland led with about 21% backlog growth, while Asseco International and Formula Systems each added around 10% to 20%, pointing to solid revenue visibility.

Proportional metrics and recurring revenue gains

On a proportional basis the company highlighted better organic growth and profitability, citing proportional revenue of PLN 384 million alongside non-IFRS operating profit of PLN 165 million. Management emphasized the strategic push into recurring and maintenance revenues, notably in banking and products such as ABS KSeF, converting one-off projects into long-term streams.

Targeted M&A builds capabilities across markets

Asseco completed nine acquisitions in 2026, including Mc Comp in Poland, RandTech in Portugal and smaller teams in Vietnam focused on outsourcing and engineering. These deals, which strengthen exposure to energy, fuel, insurance software and HR/payroll, contributed about PLN 121 million in revenue and around PLN 35 million in operating profit from post-June consolidation.

Regional momentum in Central Europe and Israel

The company reported a significant rebuild and expansion in public-sector contracts in the Czech Republic and Slovakia, helping restore momentum in Central Europe. Israel showed excellent performance and Germany’s ERP business, together with South-Eastern Europe, delivered improved revenue and profitability.

Working-capital strains at Matrix weigh on Formula cash

Within Formula Systems, Matrix IT showed weak cash generation in the half-year, partly due to prior-year factoring and delayed payments from public-sector customers. This left Formula’s cash conversion trailing group peers at roughly 84% to 93%, creating temporary seasonality and collection timing issues at the consolidated level.

Receivables growth and seasonal working-capital pressure

Receivables increased and working capital deteriorated in the interim period, largely reflecting rapid revenue growth and billing schedules tied to large public projects under national recovery programs. Management argued these effects are cyclical and linked to invoice timing, though they temporarily depressed free cash flow in the first half.

The company’s second-quarter effective tax rate was lifted by tax on the dividend received from Sapiens, with the withholding and related treatment estimated near 19% on roughly PLN 190 million. This created a sizable short-term tax burden, compressing reported Q2 earnings despite underlying operational strength.

Impairments and write-downs cloud headline results

Asseco Spain booked an inventory impairment of around PLN 18 million, adding to other PPA and goodwill write-downs of roughly PLN 14 million at the EBITDA level and about PLN 6.5 million at net profit. Management noted an additional write-down of around PLN 4 million, stressing these were one-off adjustments rather than recurring operational issues.

Clarifying net cash definitions and reporting nuances

Investors raised concerns about apparent discrepancies in net cash figures related to deposits, leases and certificates of deposit, which muddied the picture. Management responded by emphasizing a proportional net cash position of about PLN 1.3 billion and explaining that different reporting lenses had caused the short-term confusion.

ERP reclassification distorts Polish segment trends

ERP revenue in Poland appeared to decline within the domestic segment because DahliaMatic was reclassified into the ERP holding now reported under Asseco International. Management cautioned that without adjusting for this shift, like-for-like comparisons can mislead investors about the true performance of the Polish ERP business.

Asseco Spain under review after underperformance

The Spanish unit’s impairments and ongoing process issues weighed on Asseco International’s infrastructure results, highlighting operational shortcomings. Management signaled that Asseco Spain is not viewed as core to the group’s strategy and may be considered for disposal, indicating a willingness to streamline the portfolio.

Public-sector reliance and seasonality remain key risks

A substantial slice of recent growth stems from public-sector programs such as health initiatives and national recovery funds, which can create quarter-to-quarter lumpiness. While Asseco is working to convert some of this work into recurring contracts, the timing of public spending and invoice shifts from the second to later quarters remains a structural risk.

Management outlook: cautiously optimistic with solid backlog

Executives described the 2026 outlook as “very decent,” underpinned by robust H1 metrics including PLN 9.25 billion revenue, more than PLN 1.08 billion in operating profit and roughly PLN 430 to 460 million in net profit. They expect seasonal cash inflows in the third and fourth quarters, continued conversion of one-off public projects into recurring revenue and benefit from an order backlog up around 12% on fixed FX and 18% on variable FX.

Asseco Poland’s earnings call painted the picture of a company enjoying strong operational momentum, widening margins and a fortified balance sheet, even as it manages tax, impairment and working-capital bumps. For investors, the message was clear: despite some cyclical and one-off headwinds, diversified growth, rising backlog and growing recurring revenues position the group well for the coming quarters.

Idziemy o krok dalej – kierunek: Dhaulagiri. Comarch po raz trzeci Oficjalnym Sponsorem wyprawy Andrzeja Bargiela

Andrzej Bargiel wraz z zespołem ponownie wyruszył w Himalaje. Celem jest wejście na szczyt Dhaulagiri (8167 m n.p.m.) oraz zjazd na nartach bez użycia dodatkowego tlenu z butli. Będzie to niezwykle wymagające, gdyż góra jest bardzo stroma, eksponowana i podatna na lawiny.

Dhaulagiri to dla mnie kolejne duże wyzwanie. Kluczowe będą warunki i przede wszystkim zagrożenie lawinowe, które na tej górze bywa dużym problemem. Jeśli warunki pozwolą, chciałbym wejść na szczyt i zjechać z niego na nartach bez dodatkowego tlenu, w możliwie szybkim i czystym stylu. Cieszę się, że po raz kolejny w tym projekcie towarzyszy mi Comarch – komentuje Andrzej Bargiel.

Andrzej Bargiel znany jest na świecie ze zjazdów z K2 oraz ze wszystkich czterech ośmiotysięczników w Karakorum. Dhaulagiri, jedna z najbardziej wymagających narciarsko gór Himalajów, to kolejny punkt w jego sportowej karierze w ramach autorskiego projektu HIC SUNT LEONES.

Współpraca Comarch z Andrzejem Bargielem to projekt łączący technologię, biznes i sport. Jest to już trzecia wspólna inicjatywa. Pierwszą była wyprawa Everest Ski Challenge (wrzesień 2025 r.), która zakończyła się pierwszym w historii zjazdem na nartach z najwyższej góry świata bez wspomagania tlenem. Drugim wspólnym projektem była niedawna ekspedycja na Nanga Parbat (czerwiec 2026 r.), podczas której skialpinista również dokonał pionierskiego zjazdu.

Mimo tych sukcesów, obie strony stawiają przed sobą kolejne zadania. Jak podkreśla Comarch, podobnie jak w biznesie, po zrealizowaniu najbardziej wymagających projektów, firma nie zatrzymuje się w miejscu, lecz idzie zawsze o krok dalej.

Wyprawy Andrzeja Bargiela są inspirujące nie tylko ze względu na ich trudność techniczną, ale przede wszystkim na konsekwencję w podejmowaniu kolejnych wyzwań i dotrzymywaniu obietnic składanych samemu sobie. Właśnie ta niezłomność sprawia, że wzajemnie się napędzamy, mimo że działamy w tak odległych od siebie dziedzinach. Konsekwentnie i z pełnym zaangażowaniem wspieramy Cię, Andrzeju, w drodze na Dhaulagiri!

Wojciech Mach, Dyrektor sektora Financial Services w Comarch , w którego zespole Andrzej Bargiel dla wielu osób jest inspiracją dodaje:

Towarzyszenie Andrzejowi w drodze na Dhaulagiri to dla Comarchu powód do ogromnej dumy. Jesteśmy firmą, która wyrosła na szukaniu rozwiązań przez innowacje, dlatego doskonale rozumiemy człowieka, który w swojej dziedzinie nieustannie redefiniuje słowo „niemożliwe”. Sztuczna inteligencja i ekstremalny skialpinizm mają wspólny mianownik: to terytoria dla pionierów, dla których wejście na szczyt jest tylko punktem wyjścia do kolejnego projektu. Andrzej pokazuje nam, że najwyższa forma profesjonalizmu to ciągły głód rozwoju i niezawodny zespół u boku. Nasza trzecia wspólna ekspedycja to naturalna konsekwencja wartości, które napędzają Comarch: nie zatrzymujemy się – idziemy o krok dalej!

Postępy z wyprawy na Dhaulagiri będą na bieżąco relacjonowane w oficjalnych kanałach informacyjnych Comarch oraz samego sportowca, począwszy od oficjalnego startu wyprawy.

evidence.title: Comarch Named a Leader in IDC MarketScape 2026 Assessment for Compliant E-Invoicing
evidence.text:
KRAKÓW, Poland — Polish software company Comarch has been named a Leader in the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide Compliant E-Invoicing Solutions 2026 Vendor Assessment, as businesses face increasingly complex requirements for managing electronic invoicing across multiple jurisdictions.

The September 2026 IDC MarketScape assessment evaluates technology providers based on their current capabilities and strategies for helping organisations comply with e-invoicing requirements internationally.

Comarch said its e-invoicing platform currently supports regulatory requirements across more than 70 markets.

The company’s system is designed around a centralised global hub that connects with enterprise resource planning infrastructure and automates processes including invoice formatting, validation and routing.

For multinational companies, the approach is intended to reduce the need to develop separate integrations and processes for individual markets.

Instead, Comarch offers a single integration with an organisation’s ERP infrastructure, with the platform then managing differing regulatory and trading-partner requirements.

Electronic invoicing has increasingly become more than a replacement for paper or PDF invoices as governments introduce structured digital reporting and clearance requirements.

For multinational businesses, that can create a technology and compliance challenge because requirements, formats and reporting processes differ between jurisdictions.

Comarch’s proposition is to place those functions within a single internally developed platform while allowing enterprises to connect multiple ERP environments.

According to an excerpt from the IDC MarketScape assessment provided by Comarch, the company may be particularly relevant to large, multi-country enterprises operating multiple ERP systems and processing high transaction volumes.

IDC identified retail, fast-moving consumer goods, manufacturing and logistics among the sectors where the platform could be considered.

The assessment also highlighted organisations seeking to combine regulatory compliance and commercial document exchange within one platform, while noting that customers should be able to accept the use of local partner coverage outside Europe.

Comarch e-invoicing sector director Adam Beldzik said the company’s objective had been to provide international businesses with a unified platform for e-invoicing.

“We believe this recognition by the IDC MarketScape proves we are delivering on that promise — enabling our clients to navigate complex regulations effortlessly across 70+ markets,” he said.

Recognition reflects specific assessment

IDC MarketScape reports use a vendor assessment methodology that considers both capabilities and strategy. Placement in the Leader category reflects the criteria and methodology used for the particular assessment rather than establishing a universal ranking for every customer requirement.

The report referenced by Comarch is the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide Compliant E-Invoicing Solutions 2026 Vendor Assessment, document EUR154882626, published in September.

Founded in Kraków in 1993, Comarch develops proprietary enterprise software and provides IT integration services internationally.

Its e-invoicing offering forms part of that wider enterprise technology portfolio.

As governments continue expanding digital tax administration and mandatory electronic invoicing, multinational companies increasingly need systems capable of adapting to different national rules without repeatedly redesigning their financial infrastructure.

Comarch is positioning its centralised platform around that challenge, particularly for large businesses with multiple ERP systems, substantial document volumes and operations spanning numerous regulatory environments.

evidence.text:
Comarch Included in Report on the Accounts Receivable Automation Ecosystem

Comarch , a global provider of advanced IT solutions, today announced its inclusion in Navigate The Accounts Receivable Automation Ecosystem, by Forrester Research, Inc.

In its report, Forrester, a leading global research and continuous guidance firm, includes Comarch in the "AR and AP automation specialist" segment. According to the report, vendors in this category typically focus on businesses that "want a single solution that can handle both outbound AR invoices and inbound AP invoices".

The research notes that "Global e-invoicing mandates and continuous transaction controls (CTCs) are accelerating AR digitization". It identifies Comarch as a provider of "e-invoicing compliance capabilities for both inbound and outbound invoices". Furthermore, the report cites Comarch among vendors that provide "API-driven, ERP-agnostic solutions that maintain visibility and continuity during phased migrations," such as those from SAP ECC to S/4HANA.

The report also cites how organizations leverage Comarch’s e-invoicing hub to generate tangible business value. For example, MAN Truck & Bus adopted the solution to "cut e-invoice delivery time from days to minutes, automating AR invoicing and ensuring compliance across multiple countries". Similarly, Heidelberg Materials utilized Comarch’s centralized e-invoicing platform "to digitize and standardize its full range of outgoing invoices, automating multiformat, multichannel e-invoice delivery".

'We believe our inclusion in this Forrester report reflects our focus on helping enterprises turn complex global mandates into streamlined digital workflows," said Mateusz Czarnecki, Product Management Director at Comarch. Moving Toward Zero-Touch: Comarch and Partners Expand Network Automation in Libya

Comarch, Hatif Libya and Makman Technology Consulting have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) defining the next phase of their strategic cooperation in the area of Autonomous Networks.

The memorandum was signed at Comarch headquarters in Kraków by Marcin Kaleta, CEO of the Telecommunication Division at Comarch, Ahmad Jaafar, CEO of Hatif Libya, and Zackaria Farhat, Vice President at Makman Technology Consulting.

The agreement builds on the previously validated value of Comarch’s solutions in Hatif’s operational environment, following successful cooperation on Zero-Touch and network automation. These initiatives confirmed the ability of the Comarch platform to deliver tangible operational benefits and to operate effectively within the specific network and business context of the operator.

As part of the initiative, Comarch, Hatif Libya and Makman intend to develop a reference implementation for Autonomous Networks, designed to serve as a benchmark for similar transformation programs among telecommunications operators across Africa. The roadmap addresses both operational efficiency and future service innovation, supporting a structured evolution toward fully autonomous network operations.

Marcin Kaleta, CEO of the Telecommunications Division at Comarch

With this memorandum, we move from validation to execution, defining a joint roadmap toward higher levels of network autonomy. Our cooperation aims to progressively extend automation across the service lifecycle, leveraging TM Forum standards and Open Digital Architecture to ensure scalability, interoperability and long-term sustainability

The memorandum marks another important milestone in the long-term partnership between Hatif Libya, Makman and Comarch. It establishes a foundation for continued collaboration focused on measurable value, standards-based automation and the gradual realization of full network autonomy

Zackaria Farhat, Vice President at Makman Technology Consulting

The agreement reflects our shared vision of moving beyond isolated automation use cases toward a holistic, standards-driven approach to Autonomous Networks. By combining Comarch’s technology capabilities with Hatif Libya’s operational expertise, we are creating a practical framework that can be replicated by operators across the region to accelerate their digital and network transformation journeys

evidence.title: Automation in Action: Makman, Comarch Pilot AI-Driven Network Ops in Africa
evidence.text:
Automation in Action: Makman, Comarch Pilot AI-Driven Network Ops in Africa

Makman Technology Consulting, a TM Forum-certified leader in global transformation consultancy specializing in Minimum Viable Transformation (MVT), autonomous networks, and AIOps readiness, has signed a strategic partnership with Comarch. Together, they will collaborate on a proof of concept (PoC) and a pilot project aimed at a zero-touch network as a service (NaaS) transformation in Libya. This collaboration marks a new milestone in advancing autonomy and operational excellence for communication service providers (CSPs) in the Middle East, Africa, and beyond.

The Makman-Comarch partnership: A complementary fit for modern telcos

Makman will bring its expertise and proven frameworks to help define transformation roadmaps and ensure alignment between strategy and execution. The company will also identify high-impact starting points for regional CSPs’ autonomy and AI transformation programs, and co-create next-generation solutions in areas such as AIOps, digital employees, and zero-touch operations.

The project will also leverage Comarch’s renowned operations support system (OSS) products, including Service Order Management, Service Inventory, and Performance Management. The goal is to reduce operational fragmentation, automate network resource orchestration, and enhance the ability to deliver unique, competitive services in Libya.

This first phase of the project will implement Comarch’s OSS solutions to address CSPs operational challenges in Libya, including the lack of automation tools and fragmented technological solutions. Enabling end-to-end customer actions, enhancing inventory control, and implementing effective planning and design tools are some of the main objectives of this initiative. Additionally, the PoC and pilot projects will serve as a basis for similar transformations at other African telecom providers.

A shared vision for autonomy and AI-driven operations

Although the partnership will start in Libya, its ultimate goal is to create a strong framework for autonomous networks globally. Makman's consulting experience and Comarch's global experience guarantee that this collaboration is well-positioned to bring about significant change in the telecom sector.

Paweł Workiewicz, Chief Commercial Officer of the Telecommunications Division at Comarch

Our collaboration will have a pronounced impact on the way telecom operators oversee their networks. We want to show how automation and advanced orchestration can address today's industry challenges and facilitate strategic growth for operators in Africa. We aim to achieve this by fusing our state-of-the-art OSS solutions with Makman’s expertise in the African market and our companies’ extensive understanding of TM Forum® standards.

Zackaria Farhat, VP of Growth and Partnerships at Makman

We are excited to partner with Comarch in this important mission. Our strengths in strategic advisory and transformation design complement Comarch’s world-class OSS/BSS product stack. Together, we’ll enable operators to transition from complexity to clarity and from manual to autonomous.

evidence.title: Eliminating setbacks and surprises at Netguru
evidence.text:
Hiring an agency often leads to a steady stream of back and forth communication. There are initial meetings to define project needs and, from there, a litany of calls and meetings to discuss ongoing project developments. The most minor of misunderstandings between customers and their agency partners could set a project back significantly, costing both sides a lot.

Netguru , an innovation consultancy based in Poland, pride themselves on being masters of efficiency. It’s especially important when developing up to 130 concurrent projects with an international customer base and, behind the scenes, coordinating this work across a 500-person team of developers, project managers, designers, and account managers working from homes and offices all over the country.

In their ongoing quest for a tool that would streamline their workflows and communications, they decided to give Slack a try.

“We’ve been able to wrap pretty much all of our processes, including our customer communications, into Slack”

Organizing principles: A channel for every process

Being rigorous about processes helps Netguru deliver high quality projects on time and on budget. To make everything run smoothly, head of delivery Mateusz Czajka and his team have organized their Slack workspace to reflect all major aspects of their business operations.

With team and customer communications organized into clearly labeled channels, all team members can easily find the information they need to do their work — whether that comes in the form of notifications from apps and services used to build projects or channels set up to quickly receive direct responses from customers.

Their Slack workspace tends to be organized around three central workflows:

Netguru is also using two other types of channels that improve their teams’ workflow on certain client accounts. The first one ( #account- ) is an internal channel type to discuss all things related to these accounts, from client news to new ideas or appraisals. The second one ( #client-notify ) leverages Slack integrations like CircleCI , Rollbar , Github to streamline all notifications like history logs, errors and updates from key software solutions used for a certain client and their products.

To top it all off, there’s a mix of channels to discuss day-to-day business operations, including private channels for conversations around recruitment and even channels spun up to brainstorm and discuss new processes with stakeholders before they’re rolled out to the rest of the team.

Direct communications with customers is one way Netguru team members speed up feedback cycles. For Bartosz Pranczke , a senior engineering manager, the technical teams under his purview frequently rely on updates from another source: Slack integrations.

Integrations pull notifications from Netguru’s various applications (like Jira , Confluence , and PagerDuty , to name a few) and act as “ error assessment feeds,” as Pranczke describes it. These notifications alert the whole team of server issues that could affect a project’s, or several projects’, development.

“What’s even more useful is that we can basically resolve or accept technical issues right within Slack, just by clicking a button,” explains Pranczke. “And because these integrations are in public channels where all team members are, it’s an immediate indication that someone is taking ownership of the issue.”

The combined effect of these measures is not lost on Czajka: “Slack is a major part of our data ecosystem. As we grow and scale up our operations, the time and effort we save thanks to its powerful integration and automation features have a significant impact on our capabilities.”

“What’s even more useful is that we can basically resolve or accept technical issues right within Slack, just by clicking a button.”

On the road to repeat and referral customers

As Head of Delivery, Czajka is in the unique position of overseeing quality at Netguru from two perspectives—delivering high caliber products and providing a seamless experience for customers.

“We’ve found that using Slack with customers early on in the process helps tighten our bond and build a better relationship with them,” he explains. “Now a lot of our business comes from existing customers and we’re finding this leads to an increase in new referral customers, too.”

evidence.title: SoftServe Appoints Andriy Stytsyuk as Chief Executive Officer, Effective Oct. 1, 2026
evidence.text:
SoftServe Appoints Andriy Stytsyuk as Chief Executive Officer, Effective Oct. 1, 2026

AUSTIN, Texas, Sept. 21, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- SoftServe , a global AI and technology services company, today announced Andriy Stytsyuk will be appointed as Chief Executive Officer, effective Oct. 1. Harry Propper, who has served as CEO since 2023, will remain actively involved through the end of the year to support a seamless leadership transition before retiring Dec. 31, 2026.

Over his 16-year tenure with SoftServe, Stytsyuk has played a pivotal role in shaping the company's strategy, strengthening its operational foundation, guiding strategic investments and acquisitions, and helping position the organization for long-term growth. Following a year-long selection and deliberation process, the company’s Board of Directors chose Stytsyuk to lead SoftServe through its next phase of growth for his prominent work as current Chief Operating Officer (COO) and Chief Financial Officer (CFO), noting his efforts have been instrumental to defining and executing SoftServe’s vision for the future.

"SoftServe has always helped clients navigate periods of technological change, and today we are at the forefront of one of the most transformative shifts our industry has ever seen," said Taras Kytsmey, SoftServe Co-Founder and Board Member. "As AI continues to reshape every sector, SoftServe is uniquely positioned to help organizations accelerate ingenuity and generate more business value. Andriy brings the strategic leadership, transformational experience, client focus, and dedication to our values needed to lead SoftServe into this exciting next chapter. The Board has great confidence in his leadership and in the opportunities ahead."

During a period marked by significant global and industry disruption, SoftServe continued to strengthen relationships with clients, expand its capabilities, and invest in future growth. The company's resilience, innovative mindset, and mission to enable talented people to change the world has allowed the organization to better capitalize on the growing demand for AI, physical AI, agentic engineering, cloud, data, and more technology solutions.

"As we enter the next era of innovation, our focus remains clear: helping clients unlock new advantages by deploying emerging technologies, such as AI, with exceptional engineering and deep technical expertise," said Andriy Stytsyuk, incoming CEO at SoftServe. "I am honored to lead SoftServe and build on the strong foundation established by our leadership team. Together, we will continue investing in our people, strengthening client and partner relationships, and delivering exceptional outcomes for enterprises around the world."

Under Stytsyuk's leadership, SoftServe will continue executing its strategy to accelerate growth, deepen its AI and digital transformation capabilities, expand strategic partnerships, and help clients navigate increasingly complex business and technology challenges.

"Leading SoftServe through this period has been one of the greatest privileges of my career," said Harry Propper, current CEO of SoftServe. "Our success has always been rooted in our people, our culture, and our unwavering commitment to delivering the very best solutions and services to our clients. I have tremendous confidence in Andriy and the leadership team as they guide SoftServe into a future filled with opportunity."

To learn more about SoftServe and the company’s leadership team, please visit this website .

evidence.title: From schemes with "dead souls" to the attack on SoftServe: cyber fraudster Serhiy Shynder is cleaning up his past on Google
evidence.text:
From schemes with "dead souls" to the attack on SoftServe: cyber fraudster Serhiy Shynder is cleaning up his past on Google

Digging into the digital biography of IT entrepreneur Serhiy Shynder reveals far more than a standard record of work in the technology sector. In open sources, his name has been mentioned over the years in materials about the so-called “Shynder group,” corporate data, and the cyberattack on SoftServe.

Since 2020, several media outlets have linked the so-called “Shynder group” to a scheme in which IT specialists could get hired by companies, simulate work for years, receive salaries, bring in their own people, and gain access to corporate information.

The authors of the relevant investigations also wrote about possible leaks of confidential data. In some publications, potential losses were estimated at up to $20 million.

A separate episode in this story is the 2020 cyberattack on SoftServe. At that time, the company did suffer a serious attack: some corporate and client data was stolen and later published.

Media outlets connected the incident to people from Shynder’s circle. At the same time, an important point: SoftServe itself never publicly named Serhiy Shynder as the organizer of the attack.

The entrepreneur also has an international corporate footprint. Shynder was listed among the co-owners of the Czech company SIMAREX s.r.o. In Ireland, there was also Lynxoft Technologies Limited, which operated in IT consulting and was liquidated in 2021.

However, on August 28, 2026, the story resurfaced.

Several outlets reported that Serhiy Shynder is allegedly trying to have old publications mentioning his name removed from search results.

This creates a rather symbolic situation: a person from the IT sector, around whom stories about corporate data and cyberattacks have circulated for years, is now in the spotlight for attempting to remove old information from the digital space.

At the same time, media claims should not be conflated with proven facts. Shynder has previously denied involvement in the SoftServe incident, and some publications described the information campaign against him as “black PR.”

Therefore, the main question is not even for Google.

Have Ukrainian law enforcement agencies investigated the alleged fictitious IT employment, access to corporate data, and the claimed financial losses? And if such checks were carried out — what were the results?

For his part, Serhiy Shynder should be given the opportunity to state his own position on all these accusations. Removing an old publication from search results is one thing. Answering specific questions about the events described is quite another.

evidence.title: Intellias、東京オフィスを開設—日本のOEM・ティア1の「内製開発の拡張チーム」としてSDV開発を支援
evidence.text:
Intellias、東京オフィスを開設—日本のOEM・ティア1の「内製開発の拡張チーム」としてSDV開発を支援

グローバルの最先端の知見をもって日本企業にフラットに伴走。 アジア初設置となるSDVデモンストレーター「IntelliKit」を公開し、専門人材の採用を強化

【2026年5月29日 更新】 本文内のSDVソフトウェアデモンストレーター「IntelliKit」に関する記述において、一部表現を修正いたしました。（修正箇所：第5段落目）

世界17カ国に3,200名以上の自社ソフトウェアエキスパートを擁し、モビリティ領域におけるAI活用型サービスおよびソリューションパートナーであるIntellias（本社：米国イリノイ州シカゴ）は、日本市場に対する継続的なコミットメントとして、東京オフィスを開設しました。同オフィスには、アジアの拠点として初設置となる次世代コックピットシステムを開発するOEM向けのオートモーティブ・テクノロジー・プラットフォーム「IntelliKit（インテリキット）」を常設し、SDV時代の最先端の開発環境を公開します。

Intelliasは、欧米のプレミアムOEMや先進的EVメーカーなど30社以上の自動車関連クライアントと強固なパートナー関係を築いており、当社の開発したソフトウェアを搭載する車両は世界で1.7億台以上にのぼります。当社は、2025年6月より日本市場でのサービス提供を開始し、日本企業がこれらグローバルなモビリティ開発の知見やAIを活用した開発手法にアクセスできる体制を整備してきました。

今回の東京オフィス開設により、日本のOEMおよびティア1サプライヤーの開発課題により近い場所で寄り添い、SDV開発やAI活用の強化をフラットな立場で支援してまいります。 また、日本市場での事業拡大に向けて、ソリューションアーキテクトやプロジェクトマネージャーなど、ソフトウェア領域を横断的に理解し、顧客企業と伴走できる専門人材の採用も進めていく予定です。 東京オフィス概要

日本の自動車産業は、長年にわたり高品質なものづくりと高度に洗練された開発モデルを強みとしてきました。一方で、SDVへの移行が加速するなか、競争力の源泉は車両そのものの性能だけでなく、ソフトウェア開発力、AI活用、UX価値の創造、開発スピードへと広がっています。経済産業省の「モビリティDX戦略*」では、2030年までに日本国内で51,000人のソフトウェア人材が不足すると予測されています。また、従来型の開発手法による開発リードタイムの長期化も指摘されており、新興の中国OEMが2〜3年で開発を進めるのに対し、日本では3〜4年を要する状況です。 日本企業にフラットに伴走する「内製開発の拡張チーム」

こうした状況に対し、Intelliasは単なる外部ベンダーとしてではなく、内製開発を支え、加速させる「拡張チーム」として機能することを目指します。日本の自動車産業が持つ卓越した品質や技術力と、当社がグローバルで培ってきたSDV開発やAIの専門知見を掛け合わせることで、開発スピードと効率を飛躍的に高めます。開発にあたっては、コスト削減を実現するだけでなく、知見や知的財産（IP）が顧客企業の社内チームに直接蓄積される仕組みを提供します。さらに、日本市場における慎重かつ品質を重視するビジネスプロセスを尊重し、PoCや小規模プロジェクトから着手する段階的なパートナーシップモデルを採用します。長期的な信頼関係に基づく、日本企業に最適な開発体制の構築に伴走します。 アジア初設置となるSDVソフトウェアデモンストレーター「IntelliKit」

東京オフィスには、車両のコックピットを再現したSDVソフトウェアデモンストレーター「IntelliKit（インテリキット）」を、当社のアジア拠点として初めて常設しています。

IntelliKitは、組み込みソフトウェア、AI、HMI（ヒューマンマシンインターフェース）、およびクラウド接続を、ECUキット、オートモーティブキット、オートモーティブクラウドという3つのコンポーネントをまたいで単一の実働システムに統合した、ポータブルなオートモーティブ・テクノロジー・プラットフォームです。

Intelliasの主要なテクノロジーパートナーのソリューションを基盤として構築されたこのプラットフォームは、OSアーキテクチャから、AIを活用した音声アシスタントや物体検知、インフォテインメント、セキュリティ、OTAアップデートに至るまで、コックピットスタックのすべてのレイヤーを網羅しています。実環境に近い条件下で、車両の主要システムがどのように連携して機能するかを観察できる実践的な環境（ハンズオン環境）を提供します。

次世代コックピットシステムを開発するOEMにとって、IntelliKitはアーキテクチャのテスト、機能統合の検証、そして市場投入に向けた意思決定を加速するための強固な基盤となります。

Intellias Japan合同会社 日本モビリティ統括の丹野 貴文は、次のように述べています。 「東京オフィスの開設は、Intelliasにとって日本市場への長期的なコミットメントを示す重要な節目です。日本の自動車産業は、品質や技術力において世界的に高い競争力を持つ一方、SDV化、UX価値創造やバリューチェーンの変化に対応するため、ソフトウェア開発のスピードと効率をさらに高めていくことが求められています。Intelliasは、日本企業がこれまで培ってきた知見と、当社がグローバルで蓄積してきたSDV開発やAI活用の知見を掛け合わせ、次世代のモビリティを共創してまいります。従来のピラミッド構造ではなく、長期的に信頼されるフラットなパートナーとして、日本のお客様とともに新しい価値を生み出していきたいと考えています」

日本、北米、欧州の主要ティア1サプライヤーにおいて、30年以上にわたりビジネス開発を推進。全日系自動車メーカーとの取引経験を有し、幅広い製品領域における事業開発に従事。Intellias Japanの日本モビリティ統括として、日本のOEMおよびティア1サプライヤーとの連携を推進。

Intellias（インテリアス）は、世界の自動車メーカー（OEM）およびモビリティ企業に対して、AIを活用したサービスおよびソリューションを提供するグローバルテクノロジーパートナーです。世界で3,200名以上のスペシャリストを擁し、コネクテッドビークル、ソフトウェア定義型車両（SDV）、ナビゲーション、AI駆動のモビリティソリューションの領域で、高品質なソフトウェアエンジニアリングを提供しています。主要なパートナーに、欧米OEM、ティア1サプライヤー、HERE Technologies、Elmos Semiconductor、TomTom、JOYNEXTなど。

メディアユーザー登録を行うと、企業担当者の連絡先や、 イベント・記者会見の情報など様々な特記情報を閲覧できます。 ※内容はプレスリリースにより異なります。

Intellias, a global partner for AI enabled product engineering and digital solutions, has been certified as a Happiest Place to Work in India after earning an 8.9 score, a result that reflects a consistently strong workplace experience.

Intellias offers a flexible workstyle that allows colleagues to choose how they work — from home, in the office, or through a hybrid approach. This certification adds to Intellias’ growing list of global recognitions. The company was included in the 2025 Global Top 100 Inspiring Workplaces and earned three Comparably Awards for its commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and long term employee experience.
