evidence.title: Edenred consolidates its employee engagement services on a single platform
evidence.text:
According to Constance Le Goff, the group offers through Edenred Engagement a range combining multiple services intended for employees: concierge services, psychological support, communications, employee benefits and engagement solutions. The stated objective is to bring these initiatives together at a single point of access, whereas they are often dispersed across different channels. The executive relies on a study conducted by Edenred in 2025 in France, Belgium and Italy among 567 client companies, according to which employee well-being constitutes a priority for nearly half of the human resources directors surveyed.

Modular architecture and additional modules

The platform is presented as modular and adapted to the needs of human resources departments. It provides access to company tools (leave requests, expense reports, safety procedures) and integrates a survey module to collect feedback from employees. Several modules can be added to it: one dedicated to peer recognition with the awarding of points convertible into gift cards, one devoted to content on topics such as parenthood or mental health, and another offering discount vouchers and special offers. Edenred recalls supporting tens of millions of employees for 60 years and being present throughout the world.

evidence.title: Edenred completes acquisition of The Mobility House Solutions
evidence.text:
Edenred completes acquisition of The Mobility House Solutions

Edenred has completed its acquisition of The Mobility House Solutions, strengthening its position in the European fleet electrification market. The business, which specialises in turnkey charging infrastructure and intelligent energy management for fleets, will now operate under the name Edenred E-Mobility GmbH.

Following the transaction announced in June , the former The Mobility House subsidiary is combining its technological expertise with the global sales network of B2B mobility service provider UTA Edenred. The company offers fuel and charging cards, among other fleet services, and serves more than 300,000 corporate customers worldwide. The portfolio continues to centre on the manufacturer-independent ChargePilot charging and energy management system, which is designed to prevent grid overloads and reduce operating costs for fleet operators. Drawing on experience from more than 2,700 managed projects and over 2,500 actively supported fleet depots, Edenred E-Mobility GmbH positions itself as an end-to-end partner for businesses, logistics fleets, car dealerships and property operators. Its portfolio covers the entire value chain, from manufacturer-independent consulting and charging infrastructure installation to technical support and billing services. The company also integrates home charging for company car drivers into its offering.

For The Mobility House, the sale marks a strategic shift towards new business areas. As previously announced, the company plans to focus more strongly on vehicle-to-grid technology, flexibility marketing and energy trading. At the same time, it will remain commercially connected to Edenred through its Energy Unit, with the two companies continuing to work together to integrate electric fleets into the energy system as flexible energy assets.

Heiko Bayer, Managing Director of Edenred E-Mobility GmbH, said the completed transaction marks the start of the company’s next phase of growth. He expects demand for integrated B2B fleet charging solutions to continue rising and believes Edenred’s global sales network will enable the company to scale its end-to-end offering more quickly. The aim is to provide customers with a unified charging platform covering depot, public and home charging.

Pierre Jalady, CEO of UTA Edenred and Edenred Mobility EMEA, said the acquisition strengthens the company’s strategy for fleet electrification. He highlighted Edenred E-Mobility GmbH’s technical expertise and the ChargePilot energy management system as key additions to the group’s portfolio, enabling it to offer fleet operators across Europe an integrated ecosystem designed to simplify and optimise the transition to electric mobility while reducing costs.

For customers and partners, the transaction will not affect existing contracts, contact persons or the company’s Munich headquarters. The established The Mobility House Solutions and ChargePilot brands will also remain in place, while only the company’s legal name changes to Edenred E-Mobility GmbH.

evidence.title: Edenred consolida su ecosistema de inteligencia artificial para acelerar la transformación empresarial
evidence.text:
Edenred consolida su ecosistema de inteligencia artificial para acelerar la transformación empresarial

Ciudad de México, 10 de junio 2026 – Edenred México participó en el State of AI-Ops 2026, un encuentro especializado en inteligencia artificial aplicada a operaciones empresariales, donde compartió su visión sobre cómo las organizaciones pueden pasar de la adopción tecnológica al uso estratégico de la IA como motor de eficiencia, innovación y generación de valor.

En un contexto en el que la inteligencia artificial ya forma parte de la operación de la mayoría de las compañías, Edenred destacó que el principal desafío para las empresas no está únicamente en incorporar nuevas herramientas, sino en integrarlas de forma estructural a sus procesos, cultura y toma de decisiones.

"La pregunta ya no es si las empresas utilizarán inteligencia artificial. La verdadera conversación es cómo integrarla en su operación, toma de decisiones y generación de valor para sus clientes. La IA tiene el potencial de transformar industrias completas cuando se integra a los procesos de negocio con objetivos claros y centrados en las personas", señaló Ulises Aquino, vocero de Edenred.

De acuerdo con datos compartidos durante el encuentro, aunque el 88% de las empresas ya utiliza herramientas de inteligencia artificial, solo el 6% logra capturar valor significativo a escala. En el sector financiero mexicano, la adopción de estas tecnologías pasó de 60% en 2025 a 77% en 2026, lo que refleja una aceleración en la transformación digital y una mayor presión para convertir la innovación en resultados medibles.

Durante su participación, Edenred México presentó el ejercicio estratégico "¿Cómo sería Edenred si naciera hoy?", una reflexión sobre la construcción de un AI Operating System capaz de conectar distintas áreas del negocio mediante inteligencia artificial, con el objetivo de agilizar operaciones, fortalecer la toma de decisiones y mejorar la experiencia de clientes, usuarios y colaboradores.

La compañía compartió casos de aplicación de IA en procesos financieros, cumplimiento normativo, atención al cliente, análisis de negocio, desarrollo de productos y gestión de flotas. Estas implementaciones buscan optimizar tareas operativas, anticipar necesidades del mercado, mejorar tiempos de respuesta y generar mayor eficiencia en áreas clave para las organizaciones.

"La inteligencia artificial deja de ser una iniciativa aislada cuando se conecta con los objetivos del negocio. Su verdadero valor aparece cuando permite resolver problemas concretos, reducir fricciones operativas y abrir nuevas capacidades para los equipos", agregó Aquino.

Edenred también subrayó que la tecnología debe entenderse como un habilitador del talento humano. Para la compañía, la transformación con IA requiere no solo infraestructura tecnológica, sino también capacitación, gestión del cambio, confianza interna y una visión responsable sobre el uso de los datos.

"La tecnología crea apalancamiento pero las personas dan significado. La adopción tecnológica es importante, pero la capacitación de las personas es lo que realmente determina el éxito de una transformación. Por ello, la confianza en el empleado y la gestión del cambio son elementos fundamentales en cualquier estrategia de IA", afirmó Aquino.

Con esta participación, Edenred reafirmó su compromiso de impulsar soluciones tecnológicas que fortalezcan la competitividad empresarial mediante un uso responsable de la inteligencia artificial en sus operaciones.

evidence.title: Edenred Joins Quintessence AI Consortium to Train Its 12,000 Employees
evidence.text:
A Consortium of Ten Industrial Leaders to Train One Million Employees

Edenred is committing alongside nine other major players (Safran, STMicroelectronics, Stellantis, L'Oréal, Sanofi, Thales, Engie, Urssaf, and France Travail) within a consortium led by Quintessence AI. The goal is to develop and deploy a certified training program designed to train one million employees across Europe by the end of 2028. The program is called RITUAL: it is a certified online training course designed by scientists and accessible to any employee, regardless of their industry, role, or level of technical proficiency. RITUAL includes ten training modules at launch, with new content gradually added to keep skills aligned with scientific advancements, evolving practices, and regulatory changes.

AI at the Heart of the Strategic Plan Amplify 25-28

By joining this consortium, Edenred commits to deploying the certification among its 12,000 employees. Artificial intelligence is indeed central to the group's strategy for the 2025-2028 period. The group allocated approximately 520 million euros in 2025 for investments in its products and technology, and plans to invest nearly 1.8 billion euros from 2026 to 2028. Edenred already integrates AI across all its business lines to serve its end-users and partners: virtual HR agents in Latin America, automation of appointment scheduling in Brazil, targeted Retail Media campaigns for its merchant partners, and content production tools. Internally, AI is also deployed among teams and business processes to enhance employee productivity.

Responsibility and Regulatory Compliance

By joining the RITUAL consortium, Edenred asserts that technological innovation must be accompanied by a culture of responsibility. The group thus aims to ensure that the adoption of AI within the organization respects the highest ethical and regulatory standards, in response to the ethical, legal, social, environmental, and economic challenges posed by the deployment of this technology on a large scale.

evidence.title: Edenred Pay Says AI Is Powering the Invisible Guardrails for B2B’s Future
evidence.text:
Edenred Pay Says AI Is Powering the Invisible Guardrails for B2B’s Future

Payments are not just about moving money but about ensuring legitimacy, authenticity and security. With fraud attempts rising, maintaining trust without adding friction has become a top priority.

Yesterday’s innovations like two-factor authentication are now table stakes; AI-driven, behavior-based fraud detection is the new differentiator.

While business-to-business transactions face unique challenges, from legacy check fraud to deepfake-driven scams, the future of payments lies in “intelligent invisible guardrails” that balance security and convenience.

Watch more: What’s Next in Payments: Edenred Pay, Jonathan Beckham

Complete the form to unlock this article and enjoy unlimited free access to all PYMNTS content — no additional logins required.

By completing this form, you agree to receive marketing communications from PYMNTS and to the sharing of your information with our sponsor, if applicable, in accordance with our Privacy Policy and Terms and Conditions .

Payments have never been solely about moving money. Across the context of their utility, payments are fundamentally about trust.

Trust that a transaction is legitimate, that a supplier is real, that the identity behind the purchase is authentic.

The only problem? Increasingly, that trust is under assault.

“As innovation diffuses, the table stakes get higher. And it calls into question how to create a competitive advantage,” PYMNTS CEO Karen Webster observed while hosting a discussion with Jonathan Beckham, chief product and technology officer at Edenred Pay , for the September 2025 What’s Next in Payments series, “From Trend to Table Stakes: Mapping the Next Payment Priorities.”

Against this backdrop, for Beckham the key performance indicators (KPIs) are deceptively simple: no fraud, no friction.

“What I would love to see is zero fraud and a completely frictionless process for our customers. Those are the two KPIs we’re going after,” he said. He noted that in 2024, 80% of companies faced payments fraud attempts, and only 20% of victims recovered their losses.

“We want to make sure all transactions are secure and getting to the right people in the right place, but without gigantic brick walls. Intelligent invisible guardrails. That’s where the industry is headed,” Beckham said.

In payments, it turns out, trusted invisibility might be the new differentiator.

The Future of Payments Is Innovative yet Invisible

The payments industry has always been about balancing security and convenience. But as 2025 leads into 2026, that balance is poised to become harder to achieve than ever before. Fraudsters wield the same artificial intelligence (AI) tools as defenders. Consumers expect frictionless experiences. Businesses can’t afford downtime or false positives.

“It is about trade-offs,” Webster said. “Zero fraud is possible if you’re trading off a really restrictive environment. But you have to be willing to take a little risk to learn.”

“We’ve got this kind of virtual arms race,” Beckham said. “When we talk about security we’re really talking about three different things: people, processes and technology. We often forget about some of those other pieces for it too. But it’s super important that we educate and ensure that the folks that are using different systems and different technologies know how to use them and know how to interact with them.”

What is increasingly emerging is a new model: an invisible infrastructure of adaptive, intelligent and interoperable systems that protect both sides of a transaction without anyone noticing.

After all, the bar has moved. Yesterday’s innovations such as two-factor authentication, rule-based fraud detection are now table stakes.

“If you’re not applying AI and machine learning to your transactions, then you’re behind,” Beckham said. “The fraud of today is not going to be the fraud of tomorrow. We’ve got to continuously adapt and apply the technology and tools to get us there.”

For years, fraud prevention meant rules. Thresholds for payments. Static policies. If you spent a dollar more than your average, alarms went off. Those alarms were, for their part, also often wrong.

“We want to simplify it down and use these systems that are creating intelligent invisible guardrails to only notify us when there’s truly an anomaly,” Beckham said. “We don’t want to get annoyed by a whole bunch of alerts or false positives.”

And while consumer payments often dominate the headlines, Edenred Pay’s own focus is squarely on the more complex world of business-to-business (B2B) transactions. That’s where the invisible infrastructure is being built.

We’d love to be your preferred source for news .

Please add us to your preferred sources list so our news, data and interviews show up in your feed. Thanks!

“We essentially provide integrated payables across all of these different payment modalities,” said Beckham, stressing that each modality, whether it’s checks, ACH transfers, or virtual cards, comes with its own security mechanisms.

In the B2B world, every step, from invoice to settlement, has to be protected. Still, sometimes companies using legacy methods like checks can leave the front door to the operations wide open to fraud.

“We all know that checks are still a problem,” Beckham said. “I think in the U.S. there were some three billion checks for commercial transactions last year … and it’s still the largest vector of fraud.”

At the same time, even the most sophisticated systems are no match if people are tricked. Social engineering, business email compromise and now AI-generated deepfakes are raising the bar for attackers.

“Deepfake technology, even last year, was up five times from the year before,” Beckham said. “Business email compromise used to target CEOs. Now they’re faking vendors and taking over entire company accounts … they’re doing it in very nuanced ways.”

That’s where layered defenses come in: behavioral analytics, employee education and evolving identity management standards.

“For a long time, most organizations have been around local trust and local controls,” Beckham said. “What’s really interesting here is the interoperability of identity management … sharing and validating identity credentials even for businesses and their employees.”

It’s not hard to imagine a near future where vendor identity is validated as seamlessly as tapping an Apple Wallet.

“If I can validate credentials with an independently trusted source,” Beckham said, noting that he sees this happening in the next couple years, “and use that for my business, or even for my employees … I think that’s a really interesting space that’s happening and starting to mature.”

The analogy he draws is with secure websites.

“We have certificate issuers for secure websites, right? Those trusted providers are audited and have credentials themselves. I see that in a similar type of way within these KYB and business identity credentials,” Beckham said.

PYMNTS CEO Karen Webster is one of the world’s leading experts in payments innovation and the digital economy, advising multinational companies and sitting on boards of emerging AI, healthtech and real-time payments firms. She founded PYMNTS.com in 2009, a top media platform covering innovation in payments, commerce and the digital economy. Webster is also the author of the NEXT newsletter and a co-founder of Market Platform Dynamics, specializing in driving and monetizing innovation across industries.

As Chief Product & Technology Officer at Edenred Pay USA, Jonathan Beckham leads at the intersection of business strategy and technological innovation. He spearheads the product and technology vision for Edenred, focusing on next-generation AI and fintech solutions.

evidence.title: Thailand Orders Indra Long-Range Radar for Phuket Air Base
evidence.text:
Thailand has ordered a long-range Lanza 3D radar from Spanish defense company Indra for deployment at Phuket Air Base, located near maritime routes connecting the Indian Ocean and the Strait of Malacca.

This is the third long-range Lanza 3D radar the Royal Thai Air Force has contracted.

The new radar is intended to support surveillance and control of the surrounding airspace.

According to Indra, the Lanza 3D LRR is designed to detect targets ranging from small, slow-moving drones to aircraft, projectiles and missiles.

The contract also includes command-and-control capabilities based on Indra’s AIRDEF system, allowing operators to use the radar’s data in air surveillance and control operations.

Indra’s Lanza 3D LRR has a maximum range of 470 kilometers (255 nautical miles).

Its antenna scans a full 360 degrees every 10 to 12 seconds and is designed to track targets at altitudes from approximately 900 meters (3,000 feet) to 30 kilometers (100,000 feet).

Its stated elevation coverage reaches 20 degrees, rising to 30 degrees in its tactical ballistic missile tracking mode.

The radar uses software-controlled beams and signal processing to distinguish targets from returns caused by terrain and weather.

According to Indra, these features also support the tracking of low-flying targets and help the system operate amid interference.

An integrated identification friend or foe system helps operators identify cooperating aircraft.

AIRDEF combines radar data in an interface operators can use to monitor airspace, assess threats and coordinate a response.

According to Indra, the system can support mission planning, assign aircraft or weapons to a threat, and record data for later review.

It can also exchange information with civilian air traffic control when needed.

AIRDEF includes cybersecurity measures and can be configured for fixed or deployable command centers.

evidence.title: Indra unveils DRIZZLE, its new interceptor to counter mass drone attacks
evidence.text:
Indra unveiled its new autonomous interceptor DRIZZLE at UNVEX 2026 , designed to counter mass drone attacks through a concept based on low-cost effectors employed in volume . The system can operate independently or be carried by a mother drone , which extends its range and allows several interceptors to be released during the mission. According to the company, the interceptor can exceed 400 km/h and reach approximately 80 kilometers , while the use of a mother platform allows the total range to be extended to about 130 kilometers . The system is conceived as a hard-kill effector that can be integrated into counter-drone architectures, although it can also be used as a self-protection element for ground vehicles or aircraft.

One of the central elements of DRIZZLE is its target search and selection system. Indra says the interceptor incorporates a high real-time processing capacity and electro-optical and infrared sensors for the terminal phase of the interception. The company is also working to add a radar in future development stages.

DRIZZLE is an autonomous interceptor unveiled by Indra at UNVEX 2026, designed to counter mass drone attacks using low-cost effectors employed in volume.

It can exceed 400 km/h and reach approximately 80 kilometers; with a mother platform, the total range can reach about 130 kilometers.

The architecture allows a mother drone to carry up to four smaller interceptors and release them in flight, and it also uses high-density vertical ground launchers to deploy numerous effectors without launching each one individually.

The audiovisual material shows a mother platform employed against a tank, which points to a possible use as a one-way attack drone after its transport role, although Indra has not detailed that configuration.

SQUALL, geared toward deep precision strike, and VALERO, conceived as a multi-purpose platform, which together with DRIZZLE form part of Indra's portfolio of low-cost effectors.

The audiovisual material released by Indra alongside the presentation reveals a broader architecture than the one described in the press release. The images show a mother drone capable of carrying up to four smaller interceptors , which are released during flight to carry out the final phase of the mission.

The company also shows vertical ground launchers for the small interceptors. Judging by their configuration, these containers appear intended to carry a large number of effectors, visually on the order of several dozen. Another launcher shown in the video contains two mother drones , each equipped with four interceptors. The architecture allows, at least conceptually, to distribute the interceptors in depth and generate a high density of effectors without having to deploy each vehicle individually from the launch position. Indra even raises the coordinated use of several mother drones to generate a “rain” of interceptors, a concept to which the DRIZZLE name itself refers.

The video also shows a configuration in which one of the mother platforms is employed against a tank , which points to a possible use of this vector as a one-way attack drone once its transport role is completed. Indra has not publicly detailed, for now, the characteristics of that configuration or whether it constitutes an independent operational mission within the family.

DRIZZLE thus joins Indra's growing portfolio of low-cost effectors , alongside developments such as SQUALL and VALERO , albeit with different functions. While SQUALL is geared toward deep precision strike and VALERO was conceived as a multi-purpose platform, DRIZZLE is designed primarily around defence against unmanned aerial threats. Indra unveils SQUALL, its new low-cost cruise missile with more than 300 km of range The common denominator is the search for expendable, scalable systems that can be manufactured in volume , a response to the proliferation of drones and to the need for interceptors whose cost and availability make it possible to sustain prolonged operations.

In DRIZZLE, that philosophy is carried over to the employment concept itself: combining numerous small effectors with mother platforms and high-density launchers to increase the response capacity against saturation attacks, while at the same time preserving the possibility of using the vectors as weapons against ground targets.

evidence.title: Indra Group entra a far parte della Microsoft Intelligent Security Association
evidence.text:
Indra Group entra a far parte della Microsoft Intelligent Security Association

L’intelligence di Microsoft si integra come una capacità importante per l’erogazione del servizio SmartMDR, la proposta di rilevamento e risposta avanzata (MXDR) di Indra Group

Indra Group è entrata a far parte della Microsoft Intelligent Security Association (MISA) , un ecosistema di aziende di sviluppo software e di partner di servizi di sicurezza che hanno integrato le proprie soluzioni con la tecnologia di sicurezza di Microsoft per difendere al meglio i clienti comuni in un mondo in cui le minacce informatiche sono sempre più diffuse.

Questo riconoscimento rafforza il posizionamento di Indra Group e, in particolare, di IndraMind Cybersecurity, fornitore di servizi avanzati di cybersecurity, così come la sua capacità di aiutare le organizzazioni a massimizzare il valore dei propri investimenti in Microsoft Security.

In questo contesto, l’intelligence di Microsoft si integra come una capacità importante per l’erogazione del servizio SmartMDR, la proposta di rilevamento e risposta avanzata (MXDR) di Indra Group. Il servizio consente di portare capacità avanzate di operatività, protezione ed evoluzione continua a organizzazioni di diverse dimensioni, aiutandole a rafforzare il proprio livello di sicurezza a fronte di uno scenario di minacce sempre più complesso e sofisticato, mantenendo al contempo le proprie capacità allineate alle migliori pratiche del produttore.

«Incrementare in modo deciso le capacità difensive non è un’opzione di compliance, ma una leva strategica indispensabile per rendere le aziende più resilienti, competitive e preparate. Oggi nessuna organizzazione può combattere le minacce informatiche in modo isolato: il vero valore risiede nell’allineamento degli sforzi» , spiega Roberto Espina, direttore globale di IndraMind Cybersecurity.

«La Microsoft Intelligent Security Association è diventato un ecosistema dinamico, composto dai fornitori di sicurezza più affidabili e autorevoli a livello mondiale», dichiara Maria Thomson, direttrice della Microsoft Intelligent Security Association . «I nostri membri, come Indra Group, condividono l’impegno di Microsoft verso la collaborazione all’interno della comunità della cybersecurity, per migliorare la capacità dei nostri clienti di prevedere, rilevare e rispondere più rapidamente alle minacce alla sicurezza».

Fondata nel 2018 per riunire i leader di Microsoft e i fornitori di sicurezza, la MISA si concentra sulla collaborazione per combattere le minacce alla sicurezza e creare un ambiente più sicuro per tutti. La sua missione è offrire soluzioni di sicurezza intelligenti e leader di settore che operino in modo integrato per contribuire a proteggere le organizzazioni.

evidence.title: Indra unveils new cruise missile designed for mass attacks
evidence.text:
Indra has unveiled SQUALL, its new cruise missile designed for mass attacks against targets located hundreds of kilometres away.

As disclosed, this system provides a precision-strike solution against strategic targets located in the rear, such as command-and-control centres, air defence systems and high-value military infrastructure.

Its low-altitude flight capability enables it to evade enemy radars and operate with a high degree of stealth. This is complemented by its precision and effectiveness in target acquisition. To achieve this, it is equipped with guidance and navigation systems designed to withstand jamming or spoofing and reach the intended target, according to Indra.

SQUALL also offers enormous flexibility for integration into land or naval platforms. It is a solution designed for launch from ramps, containers, or tactical vehicles.

Compared with a conventional missile, it can be used in both surgical strikes involving a small number of units and mass attacks in which large numbers of this type of missile are launched in a coordinated manner to saturate enemy defenses.

The SQUALL cruise missile joins Indra’s portfolio of defense solutions. The portfolio includes counter-drone systems in fixed configurations for protecting bases and critical infrastructure, as well as mobile systems designed to escort convoys and units in the field.

It also includes the DRIZZLE effector drone, which is designed to intercept drones and engage light assets at ranges of up to 130 kilometers. The Tarsis family of drones provides intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities, target designation, and the ability to engage tactical targets.

These systems are designed to operate as part of a multilayered integrated air defense system and within a combat cloud. According to Indra, this architecture is intended to accelerate decision-making while improving reaction times, intelligence and operational effectiveness.

Indra is also progressively incorporating artificial intelligence capabilities into these systems to further enhance their performance.

evidence.title: Spain Moves Closer to Fielding First Domestic Tactical Drones With Indra’s ‘Tarsis’

evidence.title: NTT DATA y Palo Alto Networks sellan una alianza global para reforzar la ciberseguridad en la era de la IA
evidence.text:
NTT DATA y Palo Alto Networks sellan una alianza global para reforzar la ciberseguridad en la era de la IA

La expansión de la inteligencia artificial dentro de las empresas está abriendo nuevas oportunidades de automatización y productividad, pero también obliga a revisar cómo se protegen infraestructuras, datos, identidades y aplicaciones. En ese escenario, NTT DATA y Palo Alto Networks anunciaron una alianza estratégica global y plurianual orientada a desarrollar servicios de ciberseguridad para organizaciones que buscan acelerar la adopción de IA.

El acuerdo combina las plataformas de seguridad de Palo Alto Networks con las capacidades de consultoría, ingeniería y servicios gestionados de NTT DATA. Las compañías se fijaron como objetivo alcanzar un volumen de negocio conjunto de USD 1.000 millones durante los próximos tres años.

La alianza contempla ingeniería conjunta, desarrollo de nuevas soluciones y una prestación coordinada de servicios a escala internacional. Uno de los objetivos será acompañar a las organizaciones desde la evaluación inicial de riesgos hasta la implementación y operación continua de sus entornos de seguridad.

La seguridad entra en una nueva etapa con la IA

La incorporación de inteligencia artificial está modificando simultáneamente dos frentes de la ciberseguridad. Por un lado, las empresas necesitan proteger nuevas aplicaciones, modelos, agentes y flujos de información. Por otro, los atacantes también están utilizando estas tecnologías para automatizar y acelerar sus operaciones.

Ezequiel Russo, Manager de Cybersecurity de NTT DATA Argentina, señaló que los ciberdelincuentes ya utilizan inteligencia artificial para automatizar y sofisticar ataques que pueden ejecutarse a mayor velocidad.

Según el ejecutivo, el desafío pasa por cerrar la brecha entre esa capacidad ofensiva y las herramientas disponibles para detectar, responder y anticipar amenazas.

En ese contexto, la alianza tendrá el respaldo de más de 2.000 profesionales certificados en tecnologías de Palo Alto Networks , además de especialistas dedicados a acelerar implementaciones y acompañar proyectos complejos.

La colaboración también prevé que NTT DATA tenga acceso anticipado a determinadas funcionalidades de las plataformas de seguridad, con el objetivo de incorporarlas rápidamente dentro de los servicios ofrecidos a sus clientes.

Seis áreas donde concentrarán los primeros proyectos

Las primeras soluciones estarán orientadas principalmente a organizaciones que operan en sectores críticos o altamente regulados, como servicios financieros, salud, manufactura y administración pública.

Uno de los principales frentes será la evolución de los Centros de Operaciones de Seguridad (SOC) . La propuesta contempla incorporar capacidades de IA agéntica para automatizar tareas relacionadas con detección, investigación y respuesta ante incidentes.

Otro eje será la gobernanza de inteligencia artificial. El crecimiento de modelos, aplicaciones y agentes dentro de las compañías está generando nuevos desafíos relacionados con control, trazabilidad, cumplimiento y administración de riesgos.

La seguridad de las identidades también ocupará un lugar central. A las cuentas tradicionales de empleados y usuarios comienzan a sumarse identidades asociadas con máquinas, cargas de trabajo, dispositivos y agentes autónomos de IA.

La expansión de aplicaciones distribuidas y entornos híbridos también impulsa la adopción de arquitecturas Zero Trust y SASE, destinadas a controlar el acceso a aplicaciones y datos independientemente de dónde se encuentren los usuarios.

La estrategia conjunta también incluirá la protección de infraestructuras multicloud, con herramientas orientadas a mejorar la visibilidad sobre configuraciones, cumplimiento y exposición a riesgos.

Otro de los frentes será la modernización de firewalls, con el objetivo de reducir la fragmentación de herramientas y mejorar la visibilidad sobre el tráfico y los activos de las organizaciones.

Nikesh Arora, presidente y CEO de Palo Alto Networks, sostuvo que la expansión de la IA está transformando tanto los negocios como la propia ciberseguridad. En ese escenario, consideró necesario reducir la complejidad generada por infraestructuras heredadas y plataformas de seguridad desconectadas.

Uno de los problemas que busca abordar la alianza es la acumulación de diferentes soluciones de seguridad dentro de una misma organización. Con el tiempo, muchas empresas incorporaron herramientas para proteger endpoints, redes, nubes, identidades y aplicaciones que no necesariamente trabajan de manera integrada.

La expansión de la IA agrega una nueva capa de complejidad , porque introduce modelos, agentes autónomos y nuevas cargas de trabajo que también deben ser monitoreadas y protegidas.

Abhijit Dubey, CEO y Chief AI Officer de NTT DATA, afirmó que las organizaciones necesitan combinar seguridad basada en IA con conocimiento sectorial y capacidad para operar servicios a escala global.

NTT DATA cuenta con más de 7.500 profesionales especializados en ciberseguridad, más de 70 centros de prestación de servicios y más de 20 Cyber Defense Centers. Palo Alto Networks, por su parte, aportará sus plataformas de seguridad y la inteligencia de amenazas de Unit 42.

La alianza refleja una tendencia más amplia dentro del mercado tecnológico: la adopción de inteligencia artificial está dejando de ser únicamente un proyecto de innovación para convertirse también en un desafío de arquitectura, gobierno y ciberseguridad.

¿Qué anunciaron NTT DATA y Palo Alto Networks?

Las compañías firmaron una alianza estratégica global para desarrollar e implementar servicios de ciberseguridad destinados a empresas que están adoptando inteligencia artificial.

Los primeros proyectos estarán enfocados en SOC, gobernanza de IA, seguridad de identidades, Zero Trust y SASE, seguridad multicloud y modernización de firewalls.

¿Cuál es el objetivo comercial del acuerdo?

Las empresas esperan generar un volumen de negocio conjunto de USD 1.000 millones durante los próximos tres años.

evidence.text:
NTT DATA AI factory lab to launch in Riyadh and accelerate enterprise AI adoption across Middle East and Africa

The NTT DATA AI Factory Lab will help organizations move from AI exploration to practical, production-ready implementation

RIYADH, Saudi Arabia - NTT DATA, a global leader in AI, digital business and technology services, today announced its intention to launch the NTT DATA AI Factory Lab in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Designed to help organizations accelerate AI adoption, the lab will bring together NTT DATA's full stack AI solutions and services expertise and technologies from leading ecosystem partners, including Cisco and NVIDIA, to help scale AI with confidence.

Scheduled to open in September 2026, the AI Factory Lab will support executive briefings, AI strategy workshops and hands-on experiences that will help organizations identify high-impact AI use cases, validate business outcomes and accelerate adoption on a secure, integrated foundation spanning infrastructure, platforms and services.

"While interest in AI continues to grow, many organizations are looking for a practical path from experimentation to business outcomes," said Hani Nofal, Executive Head of Infrastructure Solutions in Middle East and Africa, NTT DATA. "The AI Factory Lab brings together the expertise, technologies and ecosystem partnerships needed to help clients identify the right use cases, deploy AI securely and scale with confidence."

Located in Saudi Arabia's leading business and innovation hub, the AI Factory Lab supports the Kingdom's Vision 2030 ambitions by helping public and private sector organizations adopt advanced technologies that drive productivity, innovation and economic growth.

The AI Factory Lab will feature interactive demonstrations of real-world AI use cases across employee productivity, customer experience, intelligent operations, cybersecurity, networking, software development and industry-specific business processes. Organizations will be able to explore how agentic AI can automate workflows, improve decision-making, enhance experiences and unlock greater value from enterprise data.

Featured experiences will include the Cisco Secure AI Factory with NVIDIA, showcasing how organizations can build, deploy, secure, govern and scale AI workloads on an enterprise-grade AI infrastructure foundation. The experience will highlight the data, infrastructure, security and governance capabilities required to move AI from experimentation into production while maintaining visibility, compliance and operational resilience.

Cisco intends to provide the critical AI infrastructure foundation for the lab, including Cisco's leading networking, security, observability and collaboration capabilities that enable enterprise AI adoption. NVIDIA will provide the accelerated computing platform and AI software technologies powering generative AI, agentic AI, computer vision and digital twin workloads.

"In the race to adopt AI, organizations need more than just technology - they need a foundation of absolute trust and control," said Cassie Roach, VP of Partner Sales, AI Infrastructure & Connectivity at Cisco . "By integrating the Cisco Secure AI Factory with NVIDIA into their AI Factory Lab, NTT DATA provides a secure, validated sandbox where customers can test, refine and prove their AI strategies with confidence before making a full-scale commitment, turning 'what if?' into reality."

“Organizations across the Middle East and Africa are moving from AI exploration to production, and NVIDIA accelerated computing and AI software provide the foundation to build, deploy and scale secure AI workloads,” said Dirk Barfuss, Director of EMEA channel at NVIDIA . “Through the NTT DATA AI Factory Lab in Riyadh, customers can experience the Cisco Secure AI Factory with NVIDIA firsthand, helping them validate high-impact use cases and move from experimentation to practical business outcomes with confidence.”

The lab forms part of NTT DATA's global AI strategy to help organizations adopt and scale AI responsibly, securely and effectively through consulting, infrastructure, technology services and industry-focused solutions.

The NTT DATA AI Factory Lab reflects NTT DATA's commitment to helping organizations across the Middle East and Africa transform AI potential into practical, secure and scalable business outcomes.

evidence.title: NTT DATA to acquire Netgain, creating Sweden's largest pure-play ServiceNow company together with The Cloud People
evidence.text:
NTT DATA to acquire Netgain, creating Sweden's largest pure-play ServiceNow company together with The Cloud People

BIELEFELD, Germany, Aug. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- NTT DATA, a global leader in AI, digital business and technology services, today announces the acquisition of Netgain AB . Together with The Cloud People, acquired by NTT DATA in December 2025, Netgain will form Sweden's largest pure-play ServiceNow company, strengthening NTT DATA's ServiceNow business in the Nordics, establishing a leading position in the Swedish market, and expanding its ability to support customers with ServiceNow-driven transformation initiatives across the region. The acquisition is subject to customary regulatory approval and is expected to close within weeks.

Founded in 2008 and headquartered in Stockholm, Netgain has built a strong reputation as a trusted ServiceNow partner, providing end-to-end services across advisory, implementation, managed services and AI-powered workflow transformation. With deep ServiceNow expertise and over 160 ServiceNow certifications, Netgain combines deep expertise with strong business insight to help organizations accelerate digital transformation and improve operational efficiency. Netgain became part of CombinedX , a group of knowledge enterprises, in 2013 and serves medium-sized and large enterprises as well as public-sector organizations across Sweden.

Since joining NTT DATA Business Solutions , a business unit of NTT DATA, in late 2025, The Cloud People has become the company's leading ServiceNow business in the Nordics. Building on NTT DATA's expanded strategic partnership with ServiceNow announced in 2025 , the acquisition of Netgain brings together complementary capabilities, customer relationships and market expertise that will support the company's continued growth in the ServiceNow ecosystem.

"SAP is the foundation of our business at NTT DATA Business Solutions. At the same time, we continue to invest in growth areas that create additional value for our customers," says Norbert Rotter, CEO of NTT DATA Business Solutions. "ServiceNow has become a key pillar of that strategy, and The Cloud People has already proven to be an excellent addition to our organization in the Nordics. With Netgain, we are further expanding our ServiceNow business in Sweden. Netgain's highly skilled consultants, strong customer relationships and deep platform expertise make the company an excellent fit for our business."

"Demand for AI-enabled workflow automation and connected service experiences continues to grow, making the ServiceNow platform an increasingly important part of our customers' transformation strategies," says Jatin Rajpal, Senior Executive, Global Head of ServiceNow at NTT DATA. "As we continue to develop our ServiceNow business, we are focused on expanding our capabilities and strengthening our presence in key markets around the world. The acquisition of Netgain supports that ambition by adding expertise and capacity in Europe that complement the strength of The Cloud People."

"This acquisition is an important step in our ambition to build a leading ServiceNow organization in Europe," says Bjørn Jarl, CEO of The Cloud People. "Beyond the strategic fit, what stands out is the strong alignment between our organizations. We share a customer-centric mindset, a commitment to quality and a passion for helping customers realize the full value of the ServiceNow platform. By bringing our teams closer together, we create new opportunities to exchange knowledge, develop talent and continue building on the strengths that have made both companies successful."

"Joining NTT DATA Business Solutions and The Cloud People represents an exciting next chapter for Netgain," says Eva Sandberg, CEO of Netgain. "Our customers will continue to work with the team they know and trust while gaining access to a broader international network, additional resources and expanded capabilities that will support their long-term success."

Following completion of the acquisition, Netgain will operate using the brand name "Netgain – an NTT DATA company".

NTT DATA Business Solutions is focused on SAP and works within a strong ecosystem of partners including Microsoft and ServiceNow. We enable midmarket and lower large enterprise companies worldwide to become Intelligent Enterprises – from consulting and implementation to managed services. We are part of NTT DATA a $30+ billion business and technology services leader, serving 75% of the Fortune Global 100. We are one of the world's leading AI and digital infrastructure providers, with unmatched capabilities in enterprise-scale AI, cloud, security, connectivity, data centers and application services. Our consulting and industry solutions help organizations and society move confidently and sustainably into the digital future. As a Global Top Employer, we have experts in more than 70 countries. We also offer clients access to a robust ecosystem of innovation centers as well as established and start-up partners. NTT DATA is part of NTT Group, which invests over $3 billion each year in R&D.

The Cloud People Group is one of Europe's leading pure-play ServiceNow partners, helping medium and large enterprises maximize the value of the ServiceNow platform through advisory, implementation, managed services and AI-powered workflow transformation. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Oslo, Norway, the company has offices in 9 countries across Northern Europe, the United States and Brazil, serving customers across both the private and public sectors. With 400+ specialists and deep expertise across the ServiceNow platform, The Cloud People combines specialized ServiceNow capabilities with industry knowledge to help organizations accelerate digital transformation and realize measurable business outcomes. With ~60 specialists and deep expertise across the ServiceNow platform, including ITSM, HR and CSM, Netgain combines technical excellence with business insight to help organizations accelerate digital transformation, improve operational efficiency and achieve measurable business outcomes. CombinedX brings together leading specialist companies across the Nordic region, providing expertise in digital transformation, cloud, ERP, data, AI, and business applications. evidence.title: Fujitsu launches cyber defense service with KELA threat intelligence
evidence.text:
Fujitsu said on September 25 it began offering a security service designed to help companies and organizations practice active cyber defense, combining dark web monitoring, attack surface management and threat hunting to identify signs of attacks and investigate risks inside customer environments.

The service is aimed at private-sector companies and organizations including critical infrastructure operators, as Japan promotes active cyber defense measures intended to detect warning signs of cyberattacks earlier and help prevent damage before it occurs.

Fujitsu said the offering draws on its cybersecurity expertise to help customers detect potential cyber risks at an early stage and formulate countermeasures. For dark web threat information and attack surface management functions, Fujitsu is using solutions based on a collaboration with KELA KK, a threat intelligence provider. Fujitsu and KELA signed an MSSP, or managed security service provider, and reseller agreement in September 2026.

The service consists of three functions. In dark web monitoring, Fujitsu uses threat information collected by KELA from underground forums and attacker communities to investigate, monitor and analyze leaked customer credentials and signs of targeting, then assess potential impact and support response planning.

In attack surface management, Fujitsu continuously tracks customer assets exposed on the internet and uses KELA's threat intelligence alongside its own expertise to visualize vulnerabilities and exploitation risks. It then analyzes the results to help customers identify which risks should be addressed first and formulate countermeasures.

For threat hunting, Fujitsu's white-hat hacker team under consulting brand Uvance Wayfinders analyzes monitoring data and cloud audit logs left in customer systems, drawing on techniques developed through Red Team testing, a form of simulated attack to test an organization's defenses. The service is intended to investigate threats that may not trigger alerts in existing monitoring environments, support initial response where threats are found, and assess customers' log collection and retention arrangements.

Fujitsu said it plans to use knowledge accumulated through customer engagements to further improve and automate threat analysis and response recommendations. It also plans to strengthen cybersecurity services covering periods from normal operations to incidents through coordination with its Cyber Security Nerve Center, due to start in October 2026.

Japan has stepped up focus on cyber resilience as attacks on companies and public institutions have become more sophisticated, with critical infrastructure operators facing particular pressure to improve visibility over external threats such as leaked credentials and exposed internet-facing systems.

evidence.title: Fujitsu launches comprehensive security service for active cyber defense across enterprises and organizations
evidence.text:
KAWASAKI, Japan, September 16, 2026 - (JCN Newswire) - Fujitsu Limited today announced the launch of a new security service, effective September 25, 2026, that comprehensively supports customers from identifying signs of cyberattacks to investigation and response. Leveraging Fujitsu's expertise in cybersecurity, this service combines dark web monitoring, attack surface management[1], and threat hunting[2] to proactively identify potential cyber risks in customer environments and support customers in developing and implementing effective countermeasures. To provide dark web threat intelligence and attack surface management capabilities, Fujitsu will utilize solutions based on an MSSP (Managed Security Service Provider) & Reseller Agreement with KELA Co., Ltd.[3], a provider of advanced threat intelligence, enabling more sophisticated risk visualization and rapid decision-making for countermeasures. In support of Japan's government-led active cyber defense initiatives, this service enables enterprises organizations to strengthen their cyber defense capabilities by moving beyond traditional reactive approaches that focus on responding after an attack has occurred. By identifying early indicators of cyberattacks and implementing preventive measures before damage occurs, organizations can enhance their overall cybersecurity posture and resilience.

In recent years, cyberattacks have become increasingly sophisticated and complex. Companies are now required not only to respond after an attack, as in traditional defense, but also to build a proactive defense system that detects signs of attacks in advance and implements countermeasures before damage occurs. The Japanese government is promoting "active cyber defense" initiatives, and it is becoming increasingly important for critical infrastructure operators and other organizations to establish systems for early detection of cyberattack precursors and indicators to prevent damage. However, many companies face challenges in addressing cyber risks that cannot be identified solely through internal environment monitoring. To detect attack precursors, it is crucial to continuously collect and analyze threat information from the dark web, which is not publicly accessible, evaluate its impact on the company, and continuously monitor internet-exposed assets and systems. Nonetheless, acquiring the advanced expertise and personnel required to implement these measures is not easy. Furthermore, translating threat information into actual countermeasures requires investigating and analyzing customer environments to confirm the presence or absence of compromise and implementing appropriate responses, which poses a significant challenge for companies in establishing such a system.

This service consists of three functional groups: dark web monitoring, attack surface management, and threat hunting. Fujitsu's security experts will analyze risks and threats identified by each function, propose measures to prevent damage expansion, and support continuous monitoring and operation. By providing comprehensive services from threat discovery to analysis and initial countermeasure planning, Fujitsu contributes to strengthening early response capabilities to cyberattacks and enhancing cyber resilience.

Fujitsu will investigate, monitor, and analyze leaked credentials and attack indicators related to customers, leveraging threat intelligence collected by KELA from underground forums[4] and attacker communities on the dark web. Furthermore, Fujitsu will assess the impact of these findings using its cybersecurity expertise and support necessary countermeasures.

Fujitsu will continuously identify customer assets exposed on the internet and visualize vulnerabilities and exploitability using KELA's threat intelligence and Fujitsu's expertise. Furthermore, Fujitsu will analyze the results to identify priority risks for customers and support the development of countermeasures.

Fujitsu's Uvance Wayfinders white hat hacker team will investigate threats that are difficult to detect through existing monitoring environments, such as those that do not trigger alerts, by analyzing monitoring data and cloud audit logs remaining in customer systems. This is based on the knowledge of actual attack methods and extensive response experience gained through Red Team[5] tests. In addition to supporting the initial response to discovered threats and assessing whether customers have been compromised, Fujitsu will also evaluate and verify log collection and storage systems.

Through this service, Fujitsu will support companies in improving their cyber defense capabilities. Moving forward, Fujitsu will leverage the knowledge gained through providing this service to further advance and automate threat analysis and countermeasure proposals. Additionally, Fujitsu will strengthen its cybersecurity services, providing comprehensive support from peacetime to emergencies, through collaboration with the "Cyber Security Nerve Center," which will commence operations in October 2026.

[1] Attack surface management: A method for continuously investigating and monitoring internet-exposed external assets and managing security risks. [2] Threat hunting: A method for investigating signs of cyberattacks, intrusion routes, and potential internal compromises within an organization by analyzing communication, authentication, and file access records remaining in systems. [3] KELA Co., Ltd. : Head office: Minato-ku, Tokyo; Executive Officer & COO: Yuji Hirokawa. [4] Underground forums: Also referred to as "underground communities," these are member-only communities and bulletin boards for cybercriminals and hackers, primarily found on the dark web and deep web, which are not accessible through general search engines. [5] Red Team: A simulated attack team that tests an organization's security by acting as actual attackers.

Fujitsu’s purpose is to make the world more sustainable by building trust in society through innovation. As the digital transformation partner of choice for customers around the globe, our 100,000 employees work to resolve some of the greatest challenges facing humanity. Our range of services and solutions draw on five key technologies: AI, Computing, Networks, Data & Security, and Converging Technologies, which we bring together to deliver sustainability transformation. evidence.title: Fujitsu Launches 3 Services with Israeli Firm to Support Early Detection of Attack Indicators in Japan
evidence.text:
Fujitsu Launches 3 Services with Israeli Firm to Support Early Detection of Attack Indicators in Japan

Fujitsu announced on September 25 the launch of security services to support enterprises and organizations in Japan in implementing active cyber defense. The offering comprises three domains: threat intelligence collection from the dark web, visualization of externally exposed IT assets, and proactive investigation of threats lurking within organizational networks. Beyond post-attack response, the services aim to help clients identify risks before damage occurs.

The new services primarily target critical infrastructure operators—including electric power, railway, and financial companies—that fall under Japan's Active Cyber Defense Act, enacted in 2025. With the Japanese government set to begin full-scale operations under the law in October, Fujitsu aims to help strengthen the security foundations of private-sector enterprises.

For two of the three domains—threat intelligence and ASM (Attack Surface Management)—Fujitsu will leverage solutions from KELA (Tokyo, Minato-ku), an Israel-based cyber threat intelligence company with which it has signed a partnership agreement. KELA collects leaked personal information and authentication credentials from the dark web, which is inaccessible through ordinary web searches. Fujitsu analyzes this information to help clients visualize exploitation risks and develop prioritized response plans and countermeasures.

In the ASM domain, Fujitsu continuously tracks customers' IT assets exposed on the internet, identifying vulnerabilities and exploitation risks. By maintaining constant surveillance of external entry points that attackers target first, the service helps organizations identify weaknesses before they become attack vectors.

The third domain is threat hunting, which proactively investigates signs of compromise within organizational networks. Consultants from Fujitsu's business brand "Fujitsu Uvance" and the white-hat hacker team "Uvance Wayfinders" conduct detailed analysis of customer system monitoring data and cloud audit logs. They actively search for latent threats that existing monitoring system alerts have failed to detect, as well as evidence of potential internal intrusion. The service also evaluates and verifies the adequacy of the customer's log management practices and audit infrastructure, including whether logs necessary for rapid investigation are being properly collected and retained.

Fujitsu plans to integrate these services with its dedicated cybersecurity organization, the "Cyber Security Nerve Center," launching in October 2026. The company aims to build a framework that provides consistent support from peacetime risk assessment to incident response during emergencies—going beyond post-attack response to help enterprises and organizations establish systems that detect attack indicators and potential risks in advance, preventing damage before it occurs.

The services are driven by the accelerating speed and sophistication of cyberattacks amid the expanding use of artificial intelligence (AI). As attack methods grow more sophisticated, the limitations of traditional passive defense—detecting attacks and then responding—have been increasingly highlighted. With the Japanese government set to begin full-scale active cyber defense operations in October, there is an urgent need for critical infrastructure operators in particular to establish systems that detect attacks and their indicators early and prevent damage proactively.

The following table summarizes the three service domains offered by Fujitsu.

With the enforcement of Japan's Active Cyber Defense Act and the government's operational launch approaching, demand is expected to grow in the Japanese security market for services that support peacetime risk assessment, particularly among critical infrastructure operators. Fujitsu's move to partner with an Israel-based specialist firm to deliver advanced dark web monitoring capabilities to Japanese customers could further intensify competition in this segment.

Dark web information gathering, in particular, requires a high degree of specialization and has been considered difficult for Japanese companies to handle independently. Partnerships with overseas threat intelligence specialists like KELA represent a practical option for major Japanese IT firms seeking to enhance the effectiveness of their security services, and this approach could spread to other providers going forward.

Fujitsu has indicated it will strengthen its service delivery framework through integration with the dedicated cybersecurity organization launching in October. The company's positioning of active cyber defense as a pillar of business growth is clear, and its efforts to expand its customer base—centered on critical infrastructure operators—are expected to accelerate.

evidence.title: KELA and Fujitsu Enter into Cybersecurity Collaboration Agreement
evidence.text:
KELA and Fujitsu Enter into Cybersecurity Collaboration Agreement

From "defending after an attack" to "acting before an attack" - combining KELA's global cyber threat intelligence with Fujitsu's advanced service capabilities to accelerate Active Cyber Defense (ACD) in Japan

Tel Aviv, Israel, Sept. 25, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- KELA K.K., the Japanese entity of cyber threat intelligence company KELA Inc. (Head Office: Minato-ku, Tokyo; Executive Officer COO: Yuji Hirokawa; hereinafter, "KELA"), today announced that it has entered into a collaboration agreement with Fujitsu Limited (hereinafter, "Fujitsu") regarding the deployment of KELA Group (Israel) cybersecurity solutions in the Japanese market.

The agreement covers both a Managed Security Service Provider (MSSP) model, under which Fujitsu uses KELA Group solutions to provide managed security services, and a reseller model, under which Fujitsu resells and expands KELA solutions in the market.

Through this collaboration, KELA Group's technologies - including Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) collected and analyzed from the global dark web, underground forums, and cybercrime communities; Attack Surface Management (ASM); Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM); and Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM), including third-party risk visibility and supply-chain risk management - will be combined with Fujitsu's cybersecurity expertise and advanced service delivery capabilities, including consulting and managed services.

By bringing these capabilities together, KELA aims to accelerate the shift for enterprises, government organizations, and social infrastructure operators from conventional defense that reacts after an attack to Active Cyber Defense (ACD): identifying attacker activity and early indicators before an attack, understanding risk before damage occurs, and turning that visibility into decisions and action.

Toward Cyber Defense That Acts Before an Attack

Cyberattacks are becoming faster and more sophisticated than ever. At the same time, the rapid adoption of generative AI and other AI technologies, cloud services, and digital supply chains is expanding the scope of cyber risk beyond what can be understood from inside an organization's own network alone.

Attackers begin collecting information on organizations and their business partners before attempting an intrusion. They steal and trade credentials, identify internet-exposed assets, and assess vulnerabilities and possible attack paths. Cyber defense therefore needs to go beyond monitoring whether an organization has already been compromised. Organizations need to understand what attackers may be preparing against them and act before those activities result in real-world damage.

Starting with CTI that captures attacker-side activity, KELA continuously provides visibility into external risks such as:

Attacker activity on the dark web and across cybercrime communities

Leaked or exposed credentials and corporate information

Internet-exposed digital assets of the organization and its group companies

Vulnerabilities, exposure, and exploitability

Risks arising from business partners, contractors, service providers, and other third parties

With cyber threat intelligence at the core, KELA further integrates visibility across an organization's external attack surface, continuous threat exposure, third-party risk, and management-level cyber risk, enabling organizations to address cyber risk from three perspectives: the attacker, the organization itself, and connected third parties.

The principal KELA Group solutions covered by this collaboration include:

KELA CTI Platform - Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI)

Provides threat intelligence collected and analyzed from the cybercrime ecosystem in which attackers operate, including the dark web, underground forums, and cybercrime communities. It captures attacker activity, leaked information, credentials, and information relating to potential targets to provide early visibility into indicators and risks that may lead to attacks.

ULTRARED CTEM Platform - Attack Surface Management (ASM) and Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM)

Continuously identifies an organization's and its group companies' internet-exposed digital assets and provides visibility into vulnerabilities, exposure, and exploitability. It helps organizations continuously understand how they appear from the internet and prioritize risks that require remediation.

SLING TPRM Platform - Third-Party Risk Visibility and Supply-Chain Risk Management (TPRM)

Continuously assesses and manages cyber risks arising from business partners, contractors, service providers, affiliates, and other third parties and supply-chain relationships. It supports cyber risk management not only for the organization itself, but also across the wider ecosystem of connected organizations.

One of KELA's major strengths is its global cyber threat intelligence derived from the attacker's perspective. KELA uses intelligence from the "attacker's world" - where attackers operate, what they target, what information they trade, and which organizations they are focusing on - to strengthen the defenses of enterprises and organizations.

Fujitsu, meanwhile, has a broad business foundation supporting enterprises, government organizations, and social infrastructure in Japan, together with cybersecurity specialists and advanced service capabilities spanning consulting and managed services.

The ability to understand the organization's own vulnerabilities and exposure

The ability to understand risks affecting business partners, affiliates, and other connected organizations

The ability to validate risk and connect findings to mitigation and improvement through Red Team expertise and comprehensive capabilities

By combining the strengths of both companies, KELA and Fujitsu will expand a more robust approach to cyber defense in the Japanese market.

KELA views this collaboration with Fujitsu as an important initiative that goes beyond the sales and delivery of technology, and accelerates the adoption of Active Cyber Defense in Japan. By combining KELA Group's global threat intelligence with Fujitsu's advanced service delivery capabilities in the Japanese market, the companies will support enterprises, government organizations, and social infrastructure operators in identifying risk, making informed decisions, and taking action before attacks occur.

KELA will continue to accelerate the adoption and development of Active Cyber Defense (ACD) in Japan through its collaboration with Fujitsu, contributing to stronger business resilience and, ultimately, safer and more sustainable business growth for enterprises, government organizations, and critical social infrastructure operators.

Fujitsu Limited, Uvance Wayfinders, Partner, Takeshi Sato says:

"Fujitsu will combine the practical attacker-perspective expertise cultivated through our Red Team activities with KELA's threat intelligence to provide services for enterprises and organizations that support Active Cyber Defense by staying ahead of threats. Threat intelligence only creates value when it is effectively used, and Attack Surface Management becomes truly meaningful once assets and risks have been made visible. Through threat hunting, we connect these capabilities and provide comprehensive support from identifying the risks that require action through to planning initial response measures, helping customers strengthen their defensive capabilities."

KELA Group is a cyber threat intelligence company headquartered in Israel. Since its founding in 2009, KELA has collected and analyzed proprietary cyber threat intelligence from the cybercrime ecosystem in which attackers operate, including the dark web, underground forums, and cybercrime communities, providing visibility into organizations' external risks from the attacker's perspective.

Today, with Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) at its core, KELA provides technologies including External Attack Surface Management (EASM), Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM), and Third Party Risk Management (TPRM), supporting a proactive approach to cyber defense that goes beyond "defending after an attack" to "acting before an attack."

KELA Group serves enterprises and government organizations across global markets, including North America, Europe, and Asia. KELA K.K., its Japanese subsidiary, was established in 2019 and promotes KELA Group's cyber threat intelligence and Active Cyber Defense solutions in the Japanese market.

evidence.title: Darktrace and Fujitsu to lift cyber defence capabilities
evidence.text:
Technology company Fujitsu and cyber security firm Darktrace have launched a new Australian partnership to lift cyber defence capabilities against new and emerging threats.

This partnership, launched in Canberra last week, combines Fujitsu’s Australian Government and Defence delivery experience, operational context and deep capability with Darktrace’s self-learning AI for visibility, detection, investigation and autonomous response to spot unusual behaviour.

Fujitsu’s Head of Defence for Oceania, Kendy Hau, said the threat landscape was becoming faster, more complex and harder to detect.

“In Australia, we’re seeing constant, targeted pressure from state-sponsored actors particularly against government, Defence, critical infrastructure and supply chains,” she said.

“But we’re also dealing with financially motivated cybercriminals and other malicious actors. What’s really changing the game is AI. It’s lowering barriers to entry by letting adversaries move faster, automate activity, and make attacks more convincing.”

Hau said what really kept security teams up at night was the mix of supply chain compromise, credential misuse and the ‘living-off-the-land’ techniques.

“These attacks can use legitimate tools and trusted access paths, making them difficult for traditional signature-based controls to identify,” she said.

Both Fujitsu and Darktrace are well established in the Australian IT market.

Fujitsu is a Japanese technology company which claims to be one of the largest ICT service providers in the world, with more than 40 years of continuous operation in Australia.

In Australia, Fujitsu Cyber helps organisations understand, strengthen and operate their cyber security, combining strategic advisory, practical implementation and 24/7 protection to reduce risk and build resilience.

“Once we assess the risk, we help them uplift their security, whether that's strengthening cloud controls, securing identities, or running penetration testing. From there, we manage their day-to-day operations with threat hunting, monitoring, and incident response,” Hau said.

Darktrace was founded in 2013 in Cambridge by mathematicians and former members of the UK intelligence community.

Its self-learning AI protects some 10,000 organisations globally including governments, defence organisations and critical infrastructure operators across the Five Eyes nations.

Darktrace Senior Vice President of sales for Asia-Pacific and Japan and Middle East and Africa, Trevor Coetzee, said cyber attacks increasingly operated at machine speed.

“Darktrace's technology detects and responds to threats autonomously, in real time, including novel attacks that signature-based defences cannot see,” he said.

“Across Australia and New Zealand, Darktrace supports hundreds of customers spanning sectors including energy, water, healthcare, critical infrastructure, government, manufacturing and transport.”

Coetzee said most security tools assumed there was reliable cloud connectivity.

“But Darktrace can operate locally inside the isolated network it’s protecting, without relying on continuous cloud connectivity, external signatures or external threat-intelligence feeds,” he said.

“This allows detection, investigation, and autonomous response to continue in disconnected or completely cut-off environments. The capability provides improved network visibility and enables organisations to better mitigate against insider threats.

“There’s also a strong sovereignty element here. We're ensuring this capability operates under the customer's governance, so they retain absolute control of sensitive data. Ultimately, we're bringing infrastructure data and security intelligence together, from headquarters right through to deployed environments.”

evidence.title: Trenitalia’s six Hitachi battery trains can run up to 100 km off the wires
evidence.text:
Railway Supply » UK & European Rail News » Trenitalia’s six Hitachi battery trains can run up to 100 km off the wires

Trenitalia’s six Hitachi battery trains can run up to 100 km off the wires

The Hitachi Rail BEMU Intercity, six of which Trenitalia has on order, is on show at InnoTrans 2026 as a diesel-free train rated for up to 100 km on batteries.

Hitachi Rail presents the BEMU at its stand in Hall 4.2 at Messe Berlin , where the fair runs from 22 to 25 September. The train itself is not part of the company’s outdoor display, which consists of four cars of the latest-generation ETR1000 high-speed train it builds for Trenitalia.

The order predates the fair. FS Italiane Group, Trenitalia’s parent, presented the BEMU Intercity at Expo Ferroviaria 2025 and said on 2 October 2025 that the six-train fleet would enter service from June 2026. The trains are part of a €525 million Trenitalia investment in 38 new Intercity trains, funded through Italy’s National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR).

Hitachi Rail says the six units are ordered under the framework agreement for Blues regional trains and come with 15 years of full-service maintenance. Trenitalia has put its investment in the six-train fleet at €80 million , also funded through the PNRR. Hitachi Rail has not said whether the six units count towards the framework ceiling of 135 trains.

The manufacturer pitches the train at partially electrified routes. It can take power from overhead wires where they exist and run on its batteries where they do not. On such lines, it could take over from diesel trains.

Hitachi Rail puts the battery capacity above 600 kWh, which gives the train up to 100 km on lines without electrification . Two pantographs let the batteries be fully recharged in about 30 minutes during a stop. The trains have a top speed of 160 km/h and accelerate at 1.10 m/s². Hitachi Rail gives the seating capacity as 200, while FS Italiane Group puts it at up to 192 seats, 30 of them in the Plus area.

The company estimates that the train can cut CO2 emissions by up to 70% compared with current diesel trains. It also lists uses beyond timetabled services. The batteries allow shunting in depots with no overhead power and boarding ferries with passengers on board, and they keep trains moving during long outages of the overhead supply.

The units are built at Hitachi Rail’s plants in Pistoia and Naples. Hitachi Rail calls the BEMU Intercity the first fully battery-electric train planned for passenger service in Italy.

How the BEMU differs from the Blues trains

The framework goes back to September 2022, when Hitachi Rail and Trenitalia unveiled the Blues at InnoTrans . Hitachi Rail then valued the agreement at €1.2 billion for up to 135 trains. The Blues is a tri-mode design: it uses overhead power on electrified lines, a mix of diesel and battery power on other lines, and batteries alone near stations.

The manufacturer’s figures for the two trains differ. It gave the four-car Blues a top speed of 160 km/h, up to 300 seats and a cut of up to 50% in fuel use and CO2 emissions against current diesel trains. The BEMU Intercity has the same top speed, fewer seats and no diesel engine, and the company puts its emissions cut at up to 70%. Both percentages are Hitachi Rail’s own estimates.

The first 20 Blues trains had left the Pistoia factory by June 2023. At that point, Hitachi Rail said the next model of the platform was expected in about two years and would run on batteries only, with a range of more than 100 km. The company has not said whether the BEMU Intercity is that model. The range it now gives for the BEMU Intercity is up to 100 km.

Within four years, the framework has gained diesel-free battery-electric units alongside the tri-mode trains. Trenitalia separately puts its investment in the six-train fleet at €80 million. Hitachi Rail has not said whether the six BEMU Intercity units count towards the 135-train ceiling. Sources: FS Italiane Group article of 2 October 2025 , a Trenitalia post on the six-train investment , Hitachi Rail press releases of 21 September 2022 , 20 December 2022 and 27 June 2023 , the Hitachi Rail InnoTrans 2026 vehicles page and the company’s InnoTrans 2026 statement placing the order under the framework. The framework value is given as €1.2 billion in 2022 and €1.23 billion in 2023.

FS Italiane Group’s October 2025 target was service from June 2026. Hitachi Rail’s InnoTrans material describes the BEMU Intercity as intended for passenger service but gives no service date, and neither company’s material names the routes the six trains will serve. The company notes that more than 85,000 km of railway in Europe has no electrification, which it presents as the market for trains of this type.

Battery trains from Siemens Mobility and Stadler are also in Berlin, as part of an outdoor display that lists 113 vehicles .

Hitachi Construction Machinery has joined Toyota Motor Corp. and Woven by Toyota's Toyota Woven City as an "Inventor" from Sept. 24, the company said on Sept. 25, positioning the mobility testing ground as a site for demonstrations aimed at future construction work.

Hitachi Construction Machinery is a global construction equipment manufacturer with operations spanning the development, production, sales and servicing of hydraulic excavators, wheel loaders, road machinery and mining equipment. Overseas markets account for 84% of revenue, and the company has about 25,000 employees worldwide.

For fiscal 2025, which ended in March 2026, Hitachi Construction Machinery posted consolidated revenue of 1.4055 trillion yen. The company is scheduled to change its corporate name to Landcros Corp. on April 1, 2027, and adopt LANDCROS as its corporate brand.
