evidence.title: Can Guidewire Software Maintain Its Robust ARR Growth Momentum?
evidence.text:
Can Guidewire Software Maintain Its Robust ARR Growth Momentum?

Guidewire Software, Inc. GWRE exited fiscal 2026 with solid annual recurring revenue (ARR) momentum, supported by strong cloud adoption, healthy bookings and exceptionally low customer attrition. ARR reached $1.24 billion on a constant-currency basis, increasing 19% year over year and exceeding the high end of management's guidance. Fully ramped ARR grew an even stronger 22%, marking the fourth consecutive year in which its growth outpaced reported ARR growth.

The company's cloud transition remains a key growth catalyst. Total cloud ARR advanced 35% year over year and accounted for 84% of overall ARR. Guidewire also ended fiscal 2026 with 105 customers generating more than $5 million each in fully ramped ARR, up from 86 a year earlier. Subscription revenues rose 37% to $916 million, highlighting the continued shift toward Guidewire's cloud-based recurring-revenue model.

Strong customer retention further strengthens the ARR foundation. Guidewire reported annual gross ARR attrition of less than 1.5%, while attrition among core systems customers was below 1%. New-product momentum is also contributing to growth. ProNavigator recorded 14 wins in the fourth quarter and 28 for the year, while PricingCenter secured eight fourth-quarter deals and 12 during fiscal 2026. On the last earnings call, management stated that both products performed materially better than initially expected and are helping the company further monetize its cloud installed base.

Guidewire expects fiscal 2027 ARR of $1.45-$1.46 billion, representing about 18% constant-currency growth at the midpoint. Importantly, more than half of the projected net new ARR is already under contract, providing meaningful visibility. However, management expects attrition to normalize after fiscal 2026's unusually low level, which had added roughly one percentage point to ARR growth.

Moreover, a smaller proportion of Guidewire's growing backlog is expected to convert into ARR during fiscal 2027, with more ramping events scheduled for later years. Thus, while the timing of ARR recognition could temper near-term acceleration, sustained cloud migrations, strong fully ramped ARR growth, new-product adoption and a sizable contracted backlog provide a solid base for continued high-teens ARR growth.

ServiceNow, Inc. NOW benefits from enterprise workflow digitization and broader adoption of governed, agentic AI across IT, employee, CRM, security and data use cases. AI-native bundles and rising usage are expanding monetization, while higher adoption and consumption support a broader revenue flywheel. AI Control Tower, Armis and Veza deepen governance and security cross-selling, while planned mid-market products widen the addressable base. Subscription growth, rising customer commitments and internal AI efficiencies support the long-term model. For the third quarter of 2026, NOW expects subscription revenues between $3.98 billion and $3.98 billion, implying 20.5% year-over-year growth and 20% growth at cc.

SAP SE SAP is strengthening its competitive position through its AI strategy despite broader macroeconomic uncertainty. More than 90% of its 50 largest deals include AI and SAP BDC, supporting a strong outlook for the second half of the year. The indirect channel is outperforming the direct cloud business, highlighting progress from the company's go-to-market transformation. New RISE with SAP and GROW with SAP offerings are also gaining traction, driven by increased adoption of its AI-led ERP migration toolchain. SAP announced a €10 billion share buyback program through 2027. Following the Sapphire event, Suite and Joule Work saw oversubscribed beta demand, supporting expectations for their third-quarter launch.

GWRE Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

Shares of Guidewire have gained 36.3% over the past three months compared with the Internet Software industry's growth of 29.5%.

GWRE's shares are trading at a forward 12-month price-to-sales multiple of 7.11X, higher than the Internet Software industry's 4.4X.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for GWRE's earnings for 2026 has been revised upward over the past 60 days.

Guidewire Software stock (ISIN US4016171054) gained 3.5 percent to USD 149.38 on September 21, 2026, while the 52-week range stood at USD 102.30 to USD 255.89. The move followed quarterly figures that exceeded consensus estimates and placed renewed attention on the insurance software provider's earnings quality.

Guidewire Software reported USD 411.09 million in quarterly revenue for the period announced on September 3, 2026, up 15.3 percent from the same quarter a year earlier. According to MarketBeat , the figure exceeded the consensus estimate of USD 402.61 million by USD 8.48 million.

Quarterly EPS came in at USD 0.99, beating the USD 0.93 consensus estimate by USD 0.06 and rising from USD 0.84 in the comparable period. The reported net margin was 9.44 percent, while return on equity reached 12.66 percent for the same reporting period, according to MarketBeat .

The valuation gap remains substantial. MarketBeat data dated September 21, 2026, put the consensus price target at USD 216.23, compared with the USD 149.38 share price, while the consensus rating was Moderate Buy based on 12 Buy ratings and four Hold ratings.

Individual targets cited by MarketBeat included USD 215 from Royal Bank of Canada and USD 210 from Piper Sandler, both dated September 4, 2026. Robert W. Baird raised its target from USD 202 to USD 235 on August 31, 2026, according to the same published analyst summary.

At USD 149.38 on September 21, 2026, the stock remained USD 106.51 below its 52-week high of USD 255.89 and USD 47.08 above its 52-week low of USD 102.30. MarketBeat reported trading volume of 990,880 shares against an average volume of 1,595,100 shares on that date, while market capitalization was USD 12.44 billion.

The market is therefore weighing two different signals: quarterly revenue growth of 15.3 percent and an EPS beat of USD 0.06 against a share price still far below the 52-week high. That contrast makes the next reported outlook and the durability of margin expansion more important than the single-day gain.

Duck Creek Technologies, Inc.: Fortegra Selects Duck Creek Reinsurance and Clarity to Support Strategic Growth

Duck Creek insurance solutions to help enhance efficiency, improve portfolio transparency, accelerate closing cycles, and support global expansion

BOSTON, March 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Duck Creek Technologies, the global intelligent solutions provider defining the future of property and casualty (P&C) and general insurance, today announced that Fortegra, a global specialty insurer serving niche markets, has selected Duck Creek Reinsurance and Duck Creek Clarity as part of its finance transformation initiative. The implementation will modernize Fortegra's financial systems and support continued growth across products, geographies, and distribution models.

Guided by its vision to be the underwriter of choice for businesses and individuals seeking reliable specialty insurance solutions, the company continues to invest in innovation, strong partnerships, and scalable capabilities.

As Fortegra accelerates its profitable growth strategy, reinsurance has become a critical capability for managing scale and portfolio complexity. The company formed a dedicated reinsurance accounting team and selected Duck Creek Reinsurance to strengthen risk management and streamline financial and operational processes. Duck Creek Clarity will deliver greater transparency across reinsurance activities, improving reporting accuracy and enabling data-driven decision-making as Fortegra's footprint expands.

"This implementation represents an important milestone in our finance transformation journey," said Ed?Peña, Chief Financial Officer at Fortegra. "By strengthening data quality and analytics, we will gain clearer insight into performance drivers, evaluate reinsurance usage, and accelerate financial close cycles. Duck Creek stood out for the strength of its Reinsurance capabilities and the experience of its team. This transformation supports our commitment to operational excellence while directly contributing to improved bottom-line results and risk management."

By selecting Duck Creek Reinsurance and Duck Creek Clarity, Fortegra expects to:

"Fortegra's focus on people first and thoughtful expansion makes it exciting to support their reinsurance journey," said Chris McCloskey, Chief Operating Officer at Duck Creek Technologies. Esmail’s newly created position covers the technology foundations Sapiens needs to operate safely and effectively with AI and autonomous systems.

His responsibilities bring together enterprise technology and data operations. He will also oversee systems and security capabilities supporting the wider business.

Esmail has more than 25 years of international technology and transformation experience. He joins Sapiens from SoftwareOne, where he served as Chief Information Officer and Digital Transformation Officer.

At SoftwareOne, he led the company’s global technology organisation and transformation programme. His previous work includes enterprise platforms and data, alongside AI and cybersecurity programmes.

Esmail said he joined Sapiens at a stage where the company is building the systems required for wider use of AI and autonomous technology. His remit will include connecting technology operations with data management while maintaining security standards across the business.

He said the role gives him responsibility for creating an operating foundation supporting both Sapiens and its insurance customers as the company develops its technology strategy.

Maggie Fox will take over as Chief Marketing Officer later this year. She brings international marketing experience across enterprise technology companies and start-ups.

Fox has previously served twice as a CMO and has founded a start-up. She also worked at SAP as Global SVP of Digital Marketing.

Her most recent position was SVP, Portfolio & Digital Marketing at industrial software company AVEVA. Across those roles, Fox has worked on corporate branding and commercial marketing, as well as team development.

evidence.title: The Evolution of LLMs and Sapiens: Abandoning Determinism for an Intelligence That Faces Chaos
evidence.text:
The Evolution of LLMs and Sapiens: Abandoning Determinism for an Intelligence That Faces Chaos

In modern society, the term "AI" has rapidly become commonplace, and its evolution is touted daily. However, we must raise a fundamental question about the casual labeling of the LLMs (Large Language Models) we encounter in our daily lives as "Artificial Intelligence (AI)." Rejoicing in something as "AI" simply by looking at its functions and outputs is merely a cognitive bias (the ELIZA effect) on the part of the human observer. Calling a system that feeds on vast amounts of human-derived data and outputs the most statistically standard response (a canonical example) "intelligence" simply because it is indistinguishable from a human is a conceptual leap and an overestimation. In this article, I would like to uncover the structural limitations of current LLMs and discuss what the ideal form of technology should be, as well as what the ideal form of the humans (Sapiens) who enjoy it should be.

The essence of an LLM is nothing more than high-dimensional computation within a vast space of past text and probabilistic calculations based on pattern searching. There are two reasons why we can assert that "intelligence" does not exist there. Absence of Symbol Grounding For an LLM, words are not tied to physical sensations or contextual experiences; they are merely statistical distances in a high-dimensional space. Lack of dynamic memory and "fixation of usage examples" The current LLM's thought circuit (parameters) is completely fixed during inference. It cannot rewrite its own knowledge structure through dialogue or fix new usage examples internally. No matter how long a context is read into it, it is merely referring to a "cheat sheet spread out on a desk," not learning and fixing it as its own embodied knowledge. A system where memory does not take root will, as a result, converge toward "safe and frictionless vocabulary" along the gradient of probability. This is not choosing words based on understanding; it is merely the result of probability calculation.

2. How to make LLMs grow: Breaking away from "determinism"

So, what is needed to bring a system closer to true intelligence? The answer lies in "abandoning deterministic thinking." For example, suppose there is a brown, collapsed "rotten fruit" in front of you. Humans can infer that "this is what used to be an apple" based on the concept of the passage of time, past memories, and circumstantial evidence. However, a system that lacks the concept of the passage of time and judges the world in static snapshots cannot recognize this as an "apple." This is because computational circuits that rely on certainty and absolutes cannot respond to changes in state. The conditions for growing a system into true intelligence are as follows: 1. Physical and structural separation of short-term and long-term memory Like the hippocampus and cerebral cortex of the brain, separating the circuit that temporarily holds and verifies new experiences from the circuit that gradually updates the existing knowledge system. This makes it possible to fix information from new angles without destroying existing memories (catastrophic forgetting). 2. Self-verification through iterative learning (loop learning) Instead of processing obtained information with a single probability calculation, a process is needed where trials are repeated many times within an internal model to verify contradictions and reconstruct the confidence level of the probability. 3. Inference of "possibility (it might be...)" Instead of grasping the world as an absolute correct answer of "100 or 0," accepting uncertainty and inferring in a multifaceted way as a distribution of probabilities such as "it might be..."

3. The ideal form of AI (Artificial Intelligence)

"AI" is not a judgment device that spits out perfect answers like a god. If you only want perfect answers, a high-speed "search engine" is sufficient. The greatest role of artificial intelligence is to be "a system that accumulates memories correctly without forgetting, like a human, and shows honest probabilities for an uncertain world." Presenting to the user with the assertion "This is the only answer!" is merely the discarding of information for the system's own convenience. The ideal form of a truly honest AI resides in the behavior of presenting objectively and humbly, based on its own memory and computational foundation, "In my memory and inference circuit, this is the most likely answer with a probability of XX%."

4. The ideal form of Sapiens (humans): A philosophy of facing chaos

The phenomenon where technology leans toward "a single, easy-to-understand answer" is not optimization, but "obsolescence." And the culprit causing that obsolescence is not the system side, but the laziness of the humans (Sapiens) who use it. Modern humans have run too far toward "cognitive economy" in pursuit of efficiency and comfort. We have become accustomed to a type of information consumption where we are presented only with "sterile fillets"—from which bones, skin, and dark meat have been removed, and odors and slime have been cleanly wiped away—and we believe that "this is fish." However, original information and the world are the raw fish itself, containing plenty of "chaos" such as diverse noise, exceptions, and the passage of time. Humans who seek only the fillet (the result): They cannot endure uncertainty, avoid the friction of thinking, and demand "100% correct answers" from the system. As a result, they let their own thinking ability decline and degenerate into passive beings. Humans who are Sapiens (wise people): They do not obsess over the "shadow of results" such as achievements or correct answers, but continue to rotate the "process of philosophizing" itself, which involves doubting premises, gaining insight, and continuously updating their own cognitive filters. Instead of accepting the world as a "deterministic correct answer," keep the margin of inquiry of "it might be..." without looking away from the raw reality that includes chaos. Abandon the thinking that seeks static results like achievements or correct answers, and place yourself in the dynamic movement of doubt and learning. The attitude of not being swallowed by the waves of technology and continuing to train the filter of one's own mind is the only condition that makes Sapiens, Sapiens.

evidence.title: Sapiens launches AI-native insurance platform SapiensAIP
evidence.text:
Sapiens International , a global provider of AI-centric, SaaS-based insurance software, has introduced the Sapiens Autonomous Insurance Platform (SapiensAIP), a new offering built to help insurance carriers move beyond experimenting with artificial intelligence and instead put it to work inside their core policy administration systems.

The platform brings together a broad set of agentic capabilities spanning underwriting, policy, billing, claims and customer engagement, and is designed to sit on top of and extend Sapiens’ existing insurance products.

SapiensAIP is structured across three layers: an experience layer tailored to different user personas, an intelligence layer where the automated, agent-driven processes are carried out, and a foundation layer drawing on Sapiens’ four decades of accumulated insurance industry knowledge.

This underlying foundation is intended to give each AI agent enough context to make decisions the way an experienced insurer would, and it also underpins two purpose-built hubs for data migration and system configuration. These hubs are designed to convert requirements and legacy files into scripts and data extracts that are ready to run, with mapping that can be checked and reversed, cutting down on manual work while keeping a human in the loop for oversight.

On the transformation side, the SapiensAIP Migration Hub is aimed at speeding up the traditionally slow process of core system transformation, including during mergers and acquisitions, by using groups of AI agents to handle profiling, mapping, validation and extraction of data.

Legacy files can be fed into the system in their original form, removing the need for reformatting beforehand, while the Migration Hub’s AI proposes how existing data should be mapped to the new environment and attaches a confidence score for subject matter experts to review.

Separately, the SapiensAIP Configuration Hub takes over configuration work that has traditionally slowed projects down, reading documents in any format and mapping them automatically to the correct fields. Its confidence scoring allows teams to check and sign off on changes, with every step recorded for audit purposes.

Sapiens describes itself as a global leader in AI-centric, SaaS-based insurance software. Its platform is built around agentic workflows that support policy, underwriting, claims, reinsurance, decisioning, finance and compliance functions. More than 600 insurers across upwards of 30 countries currently use Sapiens’ systems.

Sapiens executive chairman and interim CEO Mike Ettling said, “The AI future we have been talking about is here. The architecture behind SapiensAIP is the clearest expression yet of what Sapiens has become: the global insurance technology champion built to power the modern autonomous insurer of tomorrow, with a continuously improving layer of intelligence. This is an advantage no legacy architecture retrofitted with AI can match.”

Continental General chief transformation officer Ayanna Burns said, “SapiensAIP represents the kind of platform direction we want from our technology partners – AI that’s embedded in the core system, not bolted on. As a third-party administrator serving multiple carrier clients, Continental General needs tooling that can scale across programs and compress the timeline from contract to production. We’re putting the Configuration Hub and Migration Hub to work against real workflows, and the early direction is promising.”

evidence.title: Encova-Sapiens deal underscores appetite for packaged automation QA
evidence.text:
Encova-Sapiens deal underscores appetite for packaged automation QA

U.S.-based Encova Insurance has hired insurance-focused software provider Sapiens International in order to automate its regression testing capabilities and to accelerate a number of major software upgrades.

The move reflects a growing demand across the insurance sector for more impactful quality assurance tools, primarily to keep pace with regulatory and market pressures the sector faces.

The multi-year deal centres on Sapiens’ new Automated Testing Services (ATS), which Encova began implementing in April of this year and will use for its October upgrade of Sapiens’ CoreSuite for Workers’ Compensation software.

ATS is designed to reduce testing cycles, enhance repeatability, and improve software quality by combining pre-built regression suites, updated with each new release, with customised test cases tailored to Encova’s business operations.

“Sapiens’ Automated Testing Services is the latest example of how they proactively empower us to modernise our operations,” stressed Ramu Lingala, since May of this year executive vice president and chief information officer at Encova.

“This will reduce our testing effort, improve the quality of our releases, and free us up for business-critical and strategic priorities,” he added.

Meanwhile, Roni Al-Dor, president and the CEO of Sapiens, positioned ATS as a tool not just for cost savings, but for resilience and speed.

“By reducing the time and resources required for testing and improving software quality, ATS will enable our client to upgrade more frequently, respond faster to market demands, and enhance their operational resilience,” he claimed.

The collaboration comes at a time when insurers and banks are under increasing pressure to modernise QA practices. The European Union’s Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), which came into force in Januari of this year, requires financial institutions to demonstrate robust testing and monitoring of their IT systems, with particular emphasis on third-party risk.

Similarly, the EU AI Act introduced obligations for firms deploying AI-driven decision-making, including explainability and reliability of underlying systems.

While Encova is a U.S.-based mutual insurance group, regulatory standards are converging internationally, with U.S. supervisors such as the Federal Reserve and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency signalling similar priorities around resilience, software integrity and vendor management.

Automated regression testing is increasingly seen as a way to meet these obligations without stretching internal QA teams to breaking point.

Sapiens, headquartered in Holon, Israel, provides software solutions for insurers worldwide, spanning core systems, data, and digital platforms.

Meanwhile, Encova, based in Columbus, Ohio, operates as a super-regional carrier offering commercial, auto, home, and life insurance products. The partnership extends a relationship that already includes deployment of Sapiens’ CoreSuite for Workers’ Compensation at Encova.

For QA teams, the Encova project highlights the shift towards packaged automation services that combine pre-built test libraries with flexible, client-specific scenarios.

Unlike generic test automation frameworks, ATS updates its regression suite with every software release, reducing the lag that often slows down upgrade cycles.

This approach reflects a broader trend in financial services technology: vendors are embedding automation directly into their platforms, rather than leaving QA teams to build and maintain their own scripts.

Analysts note that the rise of agentic AI, synthetic data generation, and self-updating test environments is likely to reshape testing models further in the coming years. For now, however, automated regression remains the backbone of resilience testing in regulated industries.

For banks, insurers, and asset managers, the Encova-Sapiens partnership illustrates how automation can relieve pressure on overstretched QA departments.

Manual regression testing during upgrades is both time-intensive and prone to human error, particularly where multiple legacy systems and third-party vendors are involved. By automating these processes, firms can increase release frequency without sacrificing reliability, a key requirement as they respond to both competitive and compliance demands.

Encova’s adoption of ATS suggests that insurers are following the lead of large banks in turning to third-party automation solutions. In financial services more broadly, QA leaders are now weighing not just efficiency gains but also the extent to which automated testing can provide the auditability and traceability regulators demand under frameworks like DORA.

evidence.title: Sapiens by Yuval Noah Harari: Humanity’s past and future
evidence.text:
Imagine compressing the entire history of humanity, from the first stirrings of our species to the modern age, into a single, gripping narrative. That’s exactly what Yuval Noah Harari accomplishes in his bestselling book Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind . This isn’t just another history book stuffed with dates and events, it’s a sweeping exploration of who we are, how we got here, and why our species turned out the way it did.

Harari invites readers to step back and see humanity from a bird’s-eye view, tracing our journey over 70,000 years. He shows how a relatively insignificant species of ape evolved into the planet’s dominant lifeform, not by sheer strength or physical prowess, but through unique mental abilities, shared myths, and collective cooperation. Sapiens challenges what we think we know about civilisation, religion, economics, politics, and even happiness, forcing us to re-examine the stories we tell ourselves about progress and meaning.

If you’ve ever wondered how humans rose from the middle of the food chain to controlling the fate of the planet, or why we believe in money, nations, and gods, this book offers surprising, and sometimes unsettling, answers. Let’s dive into its key lessons.

About 70,000 years ago, Homo sapiens developed the ability to think abstractly, imagine scenarios, and create complex languages. This “Cognitive Revolution” allowed us to share stories, myths, and ideas, giving us a massive edge over other species.

Key takeaway: The power of shared imagination enabled large-scale cooperation, forming the foundation of civilisations.

While farming allowed populations to grow and societies to settle, Harari argues it also created hierarchies, increased labour, and sometimes reduced individual well-being. Humans went from foraging freely to toiling in fields.

Key takeaway: What we call “progress” can sometimes bring unintended costs.

Money, nations, religions, and laws are not tangible objects; they are collective beliefs that exist only in our shared imagination. Yet, these myths allow millions of strangers to cooperate toward common goals.

Key takeaway: Much of human civilisation is built on ideas we agree to believe in together.

Beginning around 500 years ago, the Scientific Revolution ignited a thirst for knowledge, leading to technological breakthroughs, industrialisation, and globalisation . Science reshaped economies, politics, and even our understanding of ourselves.

Key takeaway: Curiosity and innovation are among humanity’s most powerful drivers—but they also create ethical dilemmas.

Harari warns that biotechnology, genetic engineering, and AI could fundamentally change our species in the coming centuries. We might soon face choices about what kind of “humans” we want to become.

Key takeaway: Our next chapter could be the most transformative—and the most dangerous—yet.

Sapiens isn’t just a book about history; it’s a mirror reflecting humanity’s triumphs, flaws, and possibilities. Harari doesn’t give easy answers, but he equips us with the perspective to ask better questions about who we are and where we’re headed. Whether you’re fascinated by anthropology, curious about our shared myths, or concerned about our technological future, Sapiens offers an unforgettable journey through time.

Sapiens shareholders to receive $43.50 per share in cash, a 64% premium to Sapiens' undisturbed closing share price of $26.52 on August 8, 2025

Sapiens shareholders will receive $43.50 per share in cash, representing a premium of approximately 64% over Sapiens' undisturbed closing share price of $26.52 on August 8, 2025.

Transaction values Sapiens at approximately $2.5 billion.

Advent's investment will accelerate Sapiens' innovation in SaaS-based insurance solutions.

ROCHELLE PARK, N.J., Aug. 13, 2025 /PRNewswire/ -- Sapiens International Corporation N.V. (NASDAQ: SPNS) (TASE: SPNS), "Sapiens" or the "Company"), a global leader in intelligent SaaS-based software solutions to the insurance industry, today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement (the "Agreement") to be acquired by Advent, a leading global private equity investor, for $43.50 per common share, in an all-cash transaction that values Sapiens at an equity value of approximately $2.5 billion.

Existing Sapiens shareholder Formula Systems (1985) Ltd. ("Formula") will retain a minority stake in the Company.

This strategic combination marks a significant milestone in Sapiens' journey, enabling the company to accelerate its innovation roadmap and expand its global reach. Advent's deep expertise and resources will empower Sapiens to deliver even greater value to its customers, employees, and partners. "This transaction marks a significant milestone in Sapiens' journey, reinforces the success of our strategy, our commitment to delivering exceptional value to our customers, and the strength of our global team. Following a deliberate process, the Board of Directors approved this transaction, which delivers an excellent outcome for Sapiens' shareholders, providing them a substantial cash value at an attractive premium," said Roni Al-Dor, Chief Executive Officer of Sapiens. "We are excited to enter the next chapter for Sapiens in partnership with Advent to continue supporting insurance carriers with their entire transformation journey, delivering the product innovation and service excellence they expect from us. Sapiens remains fully committed to being a global leader in SaaS, digital, and AI-driven insurance software solutions across Life, Pension & Annuities and P&C markets."

Douglas Hallstrom, Director at Advent, said, "We are delighted to partner with Sapiens to support its next phase of innovation. Insurers are increasingly turning to technology to help unlock growth and profitability, drive innovation and improve business resilience – with Sapiens a critical partner in enabling this for market leading insurers globally. We will work with the company to accelerate investment into technology innovation, AI, and customer centricity. This transaction comes at a critical time of market change, and we believe Sapiens will more effectively be able to navigate this in a private setting."

Guy Bernstein, CEO at Formula, said, "Formula will continue to retain ownership in Sapiens and is excited to partner with Advent to accelerate the transition to AI and SaaS, delivering the next generation of insurance solutions for our customers. Customers can be assured that the trusted relationships, service quality, and industry leadership they have relied upon will remain, strengthened by a shared vision for driving the future of insurance technology"

Under the terms of the Agreement, which has been unanimously approved by Sapiens' Board of Directors, Sapiens shareholders will receive $43.50 per common share in cash, representing a premium of approximately 64% over Sapiens' undisturbed closing share price of $26.52 on August 8, 2025, and a premium of approximately 51% to both the 30-day and 60-day volume-weighted average price as of August 8, 2025 .

Upon completion of the transaction, Sapiens' common shares will no longer be publicly listed, and Sapiens will become a privately held company.

Advent has arranged committed debt and equity financing commitments for the purpose of financing the transaction, providing a high level of closing certainty. Funds advised by Advent have committed an aggregate equity contribution of $1.3 billion on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in the signed equity commitment letters.

The transaction is expected to close in Q4 2025 or Q1 2026, subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions, including approval by Sapiens' shareholders and receipt of regulatory approvals.

Sapiens' Board of Directors, acting upon the recommendation of a special committee of the Board of Directors, has unanimously approved the Agreement and the transaction and resolved to recommend approval of the Agreement and the transaction by Sapiens' shareholders.

The foregoing description of the Agreement and the transactions contemplated thereby is subject to, and is qualified in its entirety by reference to, the full terms of the Agreement, which Sapiens will be filing on Form 6-K.

William Blair & Company, L.L.C. is acting as financial advisor to Sapiens, and Latham & Watkins LLP and Meitar Law Offices are acting as legal counsel to Sapiens.

Citi is acting as financial advisor to Advent, and Kirkland & Ellis LLP and Herzog Fox Neeman are acting as legal counsel to Advent.

Sapiens will forgo its Q2 2025 Earnings Call and issue a press release with its Q2 2025 financial results on August 13, 2025.

evidence.title: Crif, miliardi di dati in circolazione sul Dark Web
evidence.text:
L’identità digitale è “materia prima” per gli attacchi del cybercrime. Ogni credenziale sottratta, ogni indirizzo email o numero di carta finito in circolazione diventa un tassello che i criminali informatici possono combinare per ricostruire il profilo delle vittime e rendere più credibili truffe, tentativi di phishing e furti di identità. In questo scenario si inserisce l’ultima rilevazione dell’ Osservatorio Cyber di Crif , che nel primo semestre 2026 fotografa una soglia record: 2,5 miliardi di dati univoci in circolazione sul Dark Web .

L’ Osservatorio Cyber di Crif analizza la vulnerabilità di persone e aziende agli attacchi informatici, monitora i principali trend relativi ai dati scambiati negli ambienti Open Web e Dark Web . Attraverso l’incrocio di questi dati con gli alert inviati dai propri servizi di protezione, la società bolognese restituisce una mappa aggiornata delle minacce che colpiscono cittadini e imprese, con un focus specifico sulla posizione dell’Italia nelle classifiche internazionali del furto di dati.

Il quadro complessivo conferma la persistenza di minacce ormai consolidate – phishing , smishing, vishing e spear phishing – cui si affianca una nuova generazione di attacchi basati sull’intelligenza artificiale. I criminali informatici ricorrono a deepfake audio e video realistici e, in ambito aziendale, a comunicazioni email molto difficili da distinguere dalle originali.

Parallelamente prosegue la diffusione degli stealer-as-a-service , malware capaci di acquisire un’elevata quantità di dati e informazioni contestuali dai dispositivi infettati. “Proteggere i propri dati personali è fondamentale. Le frodi online sono sempre più sofisticate e credibili, grazie a strumenti basati anche sull’AI come deepfake, phishing personalizzato e tecniche avanzate di ingegneria sociale che sfruttano informazioni personali spesso reperite online o provenienti da violazioni dei dati”, commenta Beatrice Rubini, executive director di Crif, che prosegue: “In questo scenario, la consapevolezza personale rappresenta la prima linea di difesa”.

Nel primo semestre 2026, l’Italia si colloca al quarto posto in Europa, sesta nella classifica globale , per numero di indirizzi email compromessi e messi in circolazione sul Dark Web. Per i dati relativi alle carte di credito si posiziona al sesto posto europeo e al ventiduesimo globale, mentre per il rilevamento dei numeri di telefono, elemento chiave in molte truffe come lo smishing, scende al sedicesimo posto continentale e al cinquantunesimo mondiale. Nella classifica globale dei Paesi più colpiti dal furto di email e password guidano gli Stati Uniti, seguiti da Russia, Germania, Francia e Regno Unito, con l’Italia ancora al sesto posto . Per lo scambio illecito di dati delle carte di credito gli Stati Uniti restano in testa, seguiti da Russia e Regno Unito, mentre l’Italia occupa il quattordicesimo posto , salendo di otto posizioni rispetto all’anno precedente. A livello continentale, il Nord America concentra il 55,9% dello scambio di dati rubati delle carte, davanti all’Europa (18,8%), all’Asia (13,9%) e al Sud America (6%).

Il capitolo più preoccupante riguarda gli infostealer , malware che si diffondono soprattutto tramite campagne di phishing e software contraffatti, operando in modo silenzioso per raccogliere credenziali e altre informazioni dai dispositivi e trasmetterle ai criminali. I dati sottratti vengono poi distribuiti sul Dark Web in archivi Ulp (acronimo di Url, login e password) o in raccolte più complete che includono informazioni sulla vittima e sul dispositivo compromesso. A favorire l’espansione del fenomeno è il modello Stealer-as-a-Service , che mette a disposizione malware, pannelli di controllo, manuali e guide anche a soggetti privi di competenze tecniche, abbassando le barriere d’accesso al crimine informatico. Classificando gli account compromessi in base al Paese di appartenenza, l’Italia si conferma bersaglio primario collocandosi al terzo posto mondiale , dopo Stati Uniti e Francia, per numero di account rubati e diffusi tramite infostealer. L’epicentro di questa industria criminale resta l’ Europa dell’Est , con la Russia alla guida dello sviluppo e della commercializzazione dei principali malware , ma sono emersi poli secondari estremamente attivi anche nel Sud-est asiatico e in Brasile.

Nel primo semestre 2026 le tipologie di dati più diffuse e vulnerabili sul Dark Web risultano, nell’ordine, password, email, nomi utente, numeri di telefono e nomi e cognomi . È però l’analisi delle combinazioni a rivelare il rischio maggiore. L’abbinamento tra numero completo della carta di credito, informazioni di sicurezza e data di scadenza viene rilevato nel 99,8% dei casi, in crescita del 100% rispetto al secondo semestre 2025: un segnale d ’allarme per il rischio di frodi finanziarie . Restano centrali le combinazioni legate alle credenziali: la password compare insieme all’email nel 95,9% dei casi e allo username nel 96%, a conferma di come il furto dell’account resti l’obiettivo primario degli hacker. Il numero di telefono risulta associato alla password nel 61,7% dei casi, in netta crescita.

L’ incrocio di più informazioni facilita la ricostruzione di profili dettagliati e rende molto più efficaci gli attacchi di ingegneria sociale, in particolare lo spear phishing e gli attacchi Bec (Business Email Compromise), noti anche come “truffa del Ceo”, nei quali i criminali si fingono figure apicali dell’azienda per indurre i dipendenti a effettuare bonifici o condividere informazioni riservate. Quanto agli account più rilevati sul Dark Web , escludendo i servizi di posta elettronica, in testa figurano i servizi e abbonamenti digitali (26,6%), seguiti dai social network (20,8%) e da forum e siti web (16,3%). Prevalgono nettamente gli indirizzi personali, che rappresentano il 92,1% del totale contro il 7,9% degli account business: un dato che indica come gli utenti privati continuino a prestare una protezione insufficiente ai propri dati, pur senza rendere immuni le aziende.

evidence.title: Sunil Agithakaliya Takes Charge as Whole Time Director & COO at CRIF Credit Information Services
evidence.text:
Sunil Agithakaliya Takes Charge as Whole Time Director & COO at CRIF Credit Information Services

Sunil Agithakaliya has taken on the role of Whole Time Director and Chief Operating Officer at CRIF Credit Information Services Private Limited. He has been associated with CRIF for several years and brings more than 27 years of experience across the banking and financial services sector, including more than two decades in the credit bureau industry.

Agithakaliya’s professional experience covers operations, business process transformation, digital enablement and credit information services. At CRIF, his responsibilities have included credit bureau products and operations, data-related functions and initiatives focused on strengthening credit information processes.

CRIF’s official profile identifies Agithakaliya as its Interim Whole Time Director and COO. The company says his experience includes building scalable systems and supporting reliable and efficient credit decision-making. His work has also involved credit infrastructure across South Asia, the Middle East and Africa, with exposure to central banks, financial institutions and public credit registries.

His career at CRIF has also included responsibilities related to bureau operations, products and data protection. In 2024, he participated in CRIF’s InFocus event, where he presented insights on data quality and consumer grievance resolution in the credit information ecosystem.

Agithakaliya has also been involved in developments around India’s changing credit-information infrastructure. In March 2026, he spoke about the transition to weekly credit-data reporting by lenders. CRIF High Mark, along with other credit information companies, was preparing for the increase in data volumes and the operational requirements associated with more frequent reporting.

His professional background includes expertise in operational discipline and process improvement. CRIF’s profile notes his use of Lean Six Sigma methodologies to improve efficiency, strengthen quality frameworks and support outcome-focused delivery.

Agithakaliya’s professional qualifications and training also span technology, management and process improvement. His LinkedIn profile lists an executive programme in Leadership and Management from the Indian Institute of Management Calcutta, a programme in Finance for Decision Making from the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore, and training in quantitative data analytics from the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad. It also lists certifications including Lean Six Sigma Black Belt, Project Management Professional, ITIL and Microsoft Certified Software Engineer.

His experience also includes data protection. His professional profile lists a Certified Data Protection Officer certification from PECB, along with certification as an ISO/IEC 20000 Senior Lead Implementer.

The appointment comes as credit information and data infrastructure continue to play an important role in India’s lending ecosystem. CRIF provides credit information and related data services to support lenders and other participants in making credit decisions.

In his expanded leadership role, Agithakaliya will combine his operational experience with his long-standing work in the credit information sector. His responsibilities as Whole Time Director and Chief Operating Officer place him in a leadership position covering the company’s operations and execution.

Agithakaliya’s latest role builds on his experience across credit bureau operations, data protection, technology-enabled processes and financial services. His more than two decades of experience in the credit bureau industry will form part of his leadership mandate at CRIF Credit Information Services.

evidence.title: Crif: attacchi informatici, 2,5 mld di dati in circolazione sul dark web nel I semestre 2026. In Italia Lombardia, Lazio e Sicilia le regioni più colpite
evidence.text:
Nel primo semestre 2026 il numero di dati univoci in circolazione sul dark web ha raggiunto quota 2,5 miliardi : si tratta di una risorsa preziosa che i cybercriminali possono sfruttare per costruire profili dettagliati e rendere più efficaci truffe, tentativi di phishing e furti di identità.

Il nostro Paese non è certo immune da questa minaccia: si posiziona al 4° posto nel continente europeo (6° posto nella classifica globale) per quanto riguarda il numero di indirizzi e-mail compromessi e messi in circolazione sul dark web . L’Italia si colloca inoltre al 6° posto in Europa (e al 22° posto nella classifica globale) per numero di dati relativi a carte di credito in circolazione , un indicatore significativo di vulnerabilità. Inoltre, il nostro Paese è al 16° posto a livello europeo (e al 51° posto nella classifica globale) per rilevamento di numeri di telefono , che rappresentano un elemento chiave in molte truffe online, come lo smishing.

Queste alcune delle evidenze dell’ Osservatorio Cyber di Crif , che analizza la vulnerabilità di persone e aziende agli attacchi informatici e i principali trend relativi ai dati scambiati negli ambienti open web e dark web.

L’Osservatorio Cyber di CRIF evidenzia una crescita costante della circolazione di dati sottratti tramite malware infostealer , una minaccia che nel primo semestre 2026 ha assunto dimensioni rilevanti nel panorama cyber. “ Questi malware si diffondono soprattutto attraverso campagne di phishing e software contraffatti e operano in modo silenzioso, raccogliendo credenziali e altre informazioni dai dispositivi digitali e trasmettendole ai criminali informatici. I dati vengono poi distribuiti sul dark web in archivi ulp (url, login e password) o in raccolte più complete, contenenti informazioni sulla vittima e sul dispositivo compromesso. A favorire la diffusione del fenomeno contribuisce il modello stealer as a service, che rende disponibili malware, pannelli di controllo, manuali e guide anche a soggetti privi di competenze tecniche, abbassando le barriere di accesso per la criminalità informatica ”, precisa il report di Crif .

Analizzando gli indirizzi e-mail presenti negli archivi ulp , l’ Osservatorio cyber ha classificato gli account compromessi in base al Paese di appartenenza. L’ Italia si conferma un bersaglio primario, posizionandosi al terzo posto a livello globale, dopo Stati Uniti e Francia, per numero di account rubati e diffusi sul dark web tramite infostealer .

Nell’ Europa dell’Est si colloca l’epicentro di questa industria criminale , con la Russia che guida lo sviluppo e la commercializzazione dei principali malware sul mercato. Negli ultimi anni, tuttavia, sono emersi poli del crimine secondari ma estremamente attivi anche in altre aree, tra cui spiccano Sud-est asiatico e Brasile.

Le combinazioni di dati più esposte alle frodi

Nel primo semestre del 2026 la classifica dei dati personali più vulnerabili conferma la centralità delle credenziali digitali , bersaglio privilegiato degli attacchi informatici. In particolare, le tipologie di dati più diffuse e vulnerabili sul dark web risultano, nell’ordine: password, e-mail, nomi utente, numeri di telefono, nomi e cognomi.

Analizzando le principali combinazioni di dati esposti si osserva che, nella prima parte del 2026, la combinazione del numero della carta di credito con le informazioni di sicurezza e la data di scadenza viene rilevata nel 99,8% dei casi ed è in forte crescita: un dato preoccupante per il rischio di frodi finanziarie. Particolarmente rilevanti le combinazioni legate alla password , che compare assieme alla mail nel 95,9% dei casi, mentre nel 96% dei casi è associata allo username . Questi dati confermano come il furto dell’account continui a essere un obiettivo primario per gli hacker, sottolineando la necessità di adottare corrette pratiche di gestione delle proprie password. Un altro dato appetibile per i cybercriminali risulta essere il numero di telefono , associato alla password nel 61,7% dei casi, e al nome e cognome nel 18,8% dei casi.

Numero di carta di credito completa + nome e cognome

“ L’incrocio di più informazioni personali facilita la ricostruzione di profili dettagliati delle vittime da parte dei cybercriminali, rendendo gli attacchi di ingegneria sociale molto più efficaci. In particolare, i dati di contatto possono essere utilizzati per realizzare frodi mirate come lo spear phishing e gli attacchi bec (business e-mail compromise), noti anche come truffa del ceo , nei quali i criminali si fingono dirigenti o figure apicali dell’azienda per convincere i dipendenti a effettuare bonifici, trasferire fondi o condividere informazioni riservate ”, prosegue l’analisi.

Tipologie di account più frequenti sul dark web

Dall’analisi qualitativa dei contesti in cui i dati circolano, l’Osservatorio Crif ha rilevato che, escludendo i servizi di posta elettronica, le username trovate sul dark web sono maggiormente associate agli account di servizi (portali di offerte di lavoro e portali di news web) che occupano il primo posto con una quota del 26,6%, seguiti dagli account relativi ai social network (20,8%) e a forum e siti web (16,3%).

Tipologia di account più rilevati sul dark web

“ Le credenziali rubate possono essere utilizzate per diversi scopi, ad esempio per entrare negli account delle vittime, utilizzare servizi in modo fraudolento, inviare messaggi con richieste di denaro o link di phishing, diffondere malware o ransomware per estorcere o rubare denaro. In questo scenario, il ‘fattore umano’ continua a giocare un ruolo cruciale in questa tipologia di furto di dati: la disattenzione degli utenti e l’uso di password deboli o riutilizzate sono infatti tra le cause più comuni ”, si legge nello studio.

Attraverso l’ analisi qualitativa dei domini degli account e-mail esposti sul dark web , l’Osservatorio Crif mostra una netta prevalenza di indirizzi personali , che rappresentano il 92,1% del totale, mentre gli account business si attestano al 7,9% . Questa dinamica suggerisce, da un lato, che gli utenti privati continuano a prestare una protezione insufficiente ai propri dati digitali rimanendo così il bersaglio preferito dei criminali informatici; dall’altro lato, indica che le aziende, pur investendo sempre di più in misure di sicurezza, non sono immuni dal fenomeno.

I Paesi maggiormente colpiti dal furto di dati

Tra i Paesi maggiormente colpiti dal fenomeno del furto di e-mail e password online , gli Stati Uniti occupano la prima posizione, seguiti nella classifica da Russia, Germania, Francia e Regno Unito mentre l’Italia si posiziona al 6° posto .

Per quanto riguarda lo scambio illecito di dati relativi alle carte di credito , gli Stati Uniti risultano essere il Paese più colpito, seguiti da Russia e Regno Unito mentre l’Italia occupa il 14° posto della classifica globale, salendo di 8 posizioni rispetto allo scorso anno.

La classifica dei continenti più colpiti dallo scambio di dati rubati delle carte di credito vede in testa il Nord America (55,9%) che supera l’Europa (18,8%). Segue l’Asia, col 13,9% il Sud America (6%). L’Africa si ferma al 3,2%, mentre l’Oceania (1,3%) rimane fanalino di coda di questa poco invidiabile classifica.

Secondo l’ Osservatorio cyber di Crif , nel primo semestre 2026 le attività degli hacker hanno continuato a rappresentare una minaccia significativa, con un aumento della quota di alert inviati relativamente a furto di dati monitorati sul dark web . Complessivamente, il 32,3% degli utenti ha ricevuto almeno un alert .

Tra gli utenti privati italiani avvisati dai servizi di protezione Crif , le fasce d’età maggiormente coinvolte sono rispettivamente 51-60 anni (26,7%), 41-50 anni (26,6%) e over 60 (20,3%). Guardando al genere, gli uomini rappresentano la maggioranza degli utenti allertati, con il 64,3%.

Le regioni con il maggior numero di alert sono Lombardia (15,7%), Lazio (12,3%), Sicilia (11,3%), Emilia-Romagna (9,7%) e Piemonte (9,5%), ma in proporzione sono gli abitanti di Umbria, Molise, Lazio, Piemonte e Friuli-Venezia Giulia che ricevono più alert. A livello geografico, il Sud (29,2%) e il Nord Ovest (27,5%) registrano il numero maggiore di avvisi mentre in proporzione sono gli abitanti del Nord Ovest e del Centro che ricevono più alert.

Per quanto riguarda i dati più frequentemente rilevati sull’open web , ovvero accessibili pubblicamente, nel primo semestre 2026 sono stati l’e-mail (51,4%) e l’indirizzo (16,3%), seguiti da codice fiscale (14,8%), numero di telefono (14,3%), e username (3,1%). Nel dark web sono state invece le credenziali e-mail ad essere maggiormente rilevate, seguite dal numero di telefono, mentre al terzo posto si colloca il codice fiscale.

evidence.title: CRIF: 2,5 miliardi di dati esposti sul dark web nel I semestre 2026
evidence.text:
Nel primo semestre 2026 sono risultati in circolazione sul dark web 2,5 miliardi di dati in grado di fornire informazioni sempre più complete sulle vittime che i cybercriminali possono sfruttare per costruire profili dettagliati e rendere più efficaci truffe, tentativi di phishing e furti di identità. Phishing , smishing , vishing e spear phishing continuano a rappresentare minacce significative anche in questa prima parte dell’anno. A queste si aggiungono gli attacchi dei cybercriminali basati sull’ intelligenza artificiale , che utilizzano deepfake audio e video sempre più realistici e, a livello aziendale, e-mail impeccabili e difficili da distinguere da comunicazioni autentiche. Continua inoltre la diffusione degli stealer-as-a-service , malware capaci di acquisire un’elevata quantità di dati e informazioni contestuali dai dispositivi infettati.

Queste alcune delle evidenze dell’ Osservatorio Cyber di CRIF , che analizza la vulnerabilità di persone e aziende agli attacchi informatici e i principali trend relativi ai dati scambiati negli ambienti open web e dark web.

L’ Italia nel primo semestre del 2026, si posiziona al 4° posto nel continente europeo (6° posto nella classifica globale) per quanto riguarda il numero di indirizzi e-mail compromessi e messi in circolazione sul dark web. L’Italia si colloca inoltre al 6° posto in Europa (e al 22° posto nella classifica globale) per numero di dati relativi a carte di credito in circolazione, un indicatore significativo di vulnerabilità. Inoltre, il nostro Paese è al 16° posto a livello europeo (e al 51° posto nella classifica globale) per rilevamento di numeri di telefono , che rappresentano un elemento chiave in molte truffe online, come lo smishing .

L’Osservatorio Cyber di CRIF evidenzia una crescita costante della circolazione di dati sottratti tramite malware infostealer , una minaccia che nel primo semestre 2026 ha assunto dimensioni rilevanti nel panorama cyber. Questi malware si diffondono soprattutto attraverso campagne di phishing e software contraffatti e operano in modo silenzioso, raccogliendo credenziali e altre informazioni dai dispositivi digitali e trasmettendole ai criminali informatici. I dati vengono poi distribuiti sul dark web in archivi ULP ( URL, Login e Password ) o in raccolte più complete, contenenti informazioni sulla vittima e sul dispositivo compromesso. A favorire la diffusione del fenomeno contribuisce il modello stealer-as-a-service , che rende disponibili malware, pannelli di controllo, manuali e guide anche a soggetti privi di competenze tecniche, abbassando le barriere di accesso per la criminalità informatica.

Analizzando gli indirizzi e-mail presenti negli archivi ULP , è stato possibile classificare gli account compromessi in base al Paese di appartenenza. L’ Italia si conferma un bersaglio primario, posizionandosi al terzo posto a livello globale, dopo Stati Uniti e Francia, per numero di account rubati e diffusi sul dark web tramite infostealer .

Nell’ Europa dell’Est si colloca l’epicentro di questa industria criminale, con la Russia che guida lo sviluppo e la commercializzazione dei principali malware sul mercato. Negli ultimi anni, tuttavia, sono emersi poli del crimine secondari ma estremamente attivi anche in altre aree, tra cui spiccano Sud-est asiatico e Brasile.

Le combinazioni di dati più esposte alle frodi

Nel primo semestre del 2026 la classifica dei dati personali più vulnerabili conferma la centralità delle credenziali digitali , bersaglio privilegiato degli attacchi informatici. In particolare, le tipologie di dati più diffuse e vulnerabili sul dark web risultano, nell’ordine: password, e-mail, nomi utente, numeri di telefono, nomi e cognomi.

Particolarmente rilevanti le combinazioni legate alla password , che compare assieme alla mail nel 95,9% dei casi, mentre nel 96% dei casi è associata allo username . Questi dati confermano come il furto dell’account continui a essere un obiettivo primario per gli hacker, sottolineando la necessità di adottare corrette pratiche di gestione delle proprie password. Un altro dato appetibile per i cybercriminali risulta essere il numero di telefono , associato alla password nel 61,7% dei casi, e al nome e cognome nel 18,8% dei casi.

evidence.title: Jordan Kuwait Bank Signs Agreement with CRIF to Introduce SME Assessment Model and Enhance Credit Decision-Making
evidence.text:
Jordan Kuwait Bank Signs Agreement with CRIF to Introduce SME Assessment Model and Enhance Credit Decision-Making

Jordan Kuwait Bank has signed a cooperation agreement with CRIF, a leading provider of credit information and digital solutions, to introduce a new assessment model for small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) customers using StrategyOne, CRIF’s platform for supporting and automating credit decisions.

The agreement was signed by Fadi Khalil, Head of Corporate Banking at Jordan Kuwait Bank, and Roberto Ciraci, Head of Consulting and Solutions for the Middle East and Africa at CRIF, and in the presence of Mr. Zuhdi Al Jayousi, Chief Banking Officer at Jordan Kuwait Bank along with representatives from both sides.

The partnership aims to enhance the Bank’s lending processes by accelerating financing application reviews and enabling faster, more accurate, and more efficient credit decisions. By reducing manual processes and minimizing operational bottlenecks throughout the application assessment journey, the initiative will help the Bank deliver faster and smarter lending services while improving the overall customer experience.

The StrategyOne platform will enable the Bank to make more effective use of data in its credit decision-making process. It can also be integrated with the Bank’s loan origination and collections systems, allowing credit teams to make more informed and accurate decisions while reducing the time and resources required to process applications and improving operational efficiency across the lending journey.

Commenting on the agreement, Fadi Khalil, Head of Corporate Banking at Jordan Kuwait Bank, said, “This agreement marks another important step in our efforts to enhance lending services for SMEs by leveraging digital solutions to improve the customer experience. Building a clearer and more comprehensive view of our SME customers will enable us to respond more quickly to customer and market needs and make better use of data to support accurate and well-informed credit decisions.”

He added, “Our collaboration with CRIF combines Jordan Kuwait Bank’s deep understanding of its customers and the local market with CRIF’s extensive regional and international expertise in credit information and solutions. This partnership supports our efforts to create a more efficient and seamless lending journey and to provide banking solutions that keep pace with our customers’ evolving financial needs.”

Roberto Ciraci, Head of Consulting and Solutions for the Middle East and Africa at CRIF, said: “CRIF highly values its partnership with Jordan Kuwait Bank and is proud to support the Bank’s ongoing digital transformation. By combining CRIF’s global expertise in credit risk management, decision automation, and data-driven lending with Jordan Kuwait Bank’s deep knowledge of its customers and the local market, we aim to help the Bank accelerate lending decisions, enhance the customer experience, and improve operational efficiency.”

He added: “Through the implementation of StrategyOne, we aim to equip Jordan Kuwait Bank with the tools, flexibility, and capabilities needed to keep pace with the rapid evolution of the financial services sector. By enabling faster, more accurate, and data-driven credit decisions, the Bank will be better positioned to meet growing customer expectations, support sustainable growth, and maintain a strong competitive position in the market.”

Ciraci also emphasized that the collaboration reflects CRIF’s commitment to supporting financial institutions across the region through innovative technologies and data-driven insights that enhance lending processes and deliver tangible, sustainable business value.

Jordan Kuwait Bank continues to invest in digital solutions, advanced technologies, and specialized partnerships that enhance the quality and efficiency of its banking services, improve the customer experience, and enable the Bank to keep pace with the rapid transformation of the banking sector and the evolving needs of its customers.

evidence.title: CRIF Launches AI Powered Onboarding Toolkit
evidence.text:
The latest new thinking from CRIF for you;

CRIF – the global leader in credit and insurance information, analytics and solutions – has launched its AI-powered fraud detection services in the UK, helping financial providers tackle tampering during customer onboarding.

Designed specifically for banks and insurers, the tool helps strengthen onboarding checks, identifying potentially fraudulent information before businesses are accepted onto financial providers’ systems.

The service utilises the latest innovations in Generative AI (GenAI) to analyse a wide range of documents including IDs, bills and bank statements to check for visual manipulation and issues with underlying metadata.

Fraudulent documents can be used to falsely alter a business’s appearance, influencing more favourable risk assessment outcomes and access to financial services they may not have otherwise qualified for. Manipulated documents come in an array of shapes and sizes, from concealing poor credit history to gain access to a loan, to disguising high-risk operating sectors to gain more favourable lending terms.

CRIF’s solution combats this by identifying potential document tampering, utilising advanced neural networks, large language models and deep domain expertise. This proprietary methodology uncovers subtle signals and traces, often invisible to the human eye, left by editing and manipulation activities generated through traditional software or AI-driven techniques. The solution also integrates specialised deepfake detection models to identify patterns typical of AI-generated content.

Currently, manual fraud checks and document reviews are highly resource-intensive, time-consuming and risk human error, consuming up to 5% of total operating costs for banks.*

CRIF’s anti-fraud solution offers a clear traffic light system to indicate a business’s level of risk. While analysing large amounts of data at pace, it still allows for clear human oversight and final judgement, resulting in a quicker and more accurate onboarding process.

Sara Costantini, Regional Director for the UK and Ireland, said: “ Fraud is affecting the financial services industry on all fronts – the onboarding process is a financial provider’s first line of defence for ensuring secure operations and risk assessments, making it absolutely critical to get right.

“Today’s rapidly evolving technological landscape now means that modern scam techniques are surpassing current processes, meaning fraudulent businesses risk slipping through the cracks. To catch AI-manipulated documents, we must use AI-generated solutions.

“Launching CRIF’s AI anti-fraud solution in the UK marks the next step in a successful European rollout, ensuring banks and insurers can continue to operate in the region both securely and at pace.”

CRIF’s research, part of its latest Banking on Banks report series, finds 67% of UK business leaders believe AI-powered services can help banks and insurers improve the speed of their financial decision-making and could lead to more tailored financial products.

CRIF’s AI anti-fraud solution can be easily embedded in existing onboarding products and processes and adheres to all compliance and regulatory checks required in the UK.

evidence.title: Experian integrates Verify with Workday for income verification
evidence.text:
Experian integrated its income and employment verification platform with Workday. The company said its Verify network has a path to cover more than 80 million payroll records, supporting mortgage, auto, rental and other verification needs. AI Summary

Experian announced on Thursday that it has integrated its income and employment verification platform with Workday , expanding the payroll information available for real-time verification.

The integration will allow Workday customers to use Experian Verify to verify income and employment information, including for consumers applying for mortgages, auto loans, rental housing and other financial products.

The integration is part of Experian’s broader effort to expand its Verify network through connections with payroll providers and employers. Experian said the network has a path to cover more than 80 million records, representing more than half of U.S. payroll employees.

Real-time access to income and employment information can reduce the need for manual verification, which often requires employees to provide additional documentation and can delay loan, housing and other financial decisions.

“Whether it’s buying a home, purchasing a family vehicle, getting a job or navigating another important financial milestone, behind every verification request is a person trying to move forward,” Michele Bodda , group president of Experian Verification Solutions, Employer Services and Housing, said in a statement.

The Workday integration adds payroll data from one of the largest providers of human capital management software to Experian Verify’s network, which also includes payroll provider integrations, employer-direct records and consumer-permissioned verification.

“HR teams shouldn’t have to become paperwork chasers, and employees shouldn’t have to put life on hold waiting for a verification to clear,” Nancy Weitl, vice president of HCM product management at Workday, said in a statement.

Workday customers will be able to verify income and employment through Experian as part of Workday Total Benefits, a new solution that the company plans to launch in late October.

The integration provides Cash App with direct exposure to Workday’s user base of millions of American workers during direct deposit selection, per the release. Cash App said its research found 65% of adult “Modern Earners,” defined as freelancers, side-hustlers, content creators and gig workers, currently receive traditional ACH direct deposits into standard bank accounts. This finding highlights growth opportunities as the digital wallet platform expands beyond peer-to-peer payments. Cash App reported 9.4 million primary banking active users in the second quarter of 2026, representing a 17% increase year over year.

“Direct deposit is one of the clearest signals that customers see Cash App as more than a place to send and receive money,” Morgan Kuntze , global head of partnerships at Block, said in the release.

In a separate Thursday development, global data and technology firm Experian announced an integration with Workday to expand real-time income and employment verifications. The alliance connects Workday directly with Experian Verify , the company’s automated verification platform.

The agreement allows employers using Workday to fulfill income and employment verification requests automatically, reducing administrative workloads for human resources departments. Experian said the Workday connection provides a path to cover more than 80 million worker records, representing more than half of nonfarm payroll employees in the U.S. Workday customers will gain access to the Experian integration through the new Workday Total Benefits solution in late October.

“HR teams shouldn’t have to become paperwork chasers, and employees shouldn’t have to put life on hold waiting for a verification to clear,” Nancy Weitl , vice president of HCM product management at Workday, said in Experian’s press release.

Recent PYMNTS reporting indicates a broader shift in payroll. On the wage distribution side, embedding FinTech destinations into onboarding workflows bypasses traditional bank setup hurdles, with 61% of firms now prioritizing payroll benefits as their next embedded finance deployment. Concurrently, connecting payroll databases to credit bureaus automates income underwriting and eliminates paper documentation.

Business News | Agentic AI Could Redefine How Consumers Discover and Access Credit Journeys in India: Experian Report

Get latest articles and stories on Business at LatestLY. Mumbai (Maharshtra) [India], September 22: Experian, a global data and technology company, today launched its latest report, “Unlocking Enterprise Intelligence: A Journey of Innovation and Transformation with Agentic AI”, exploring how Agentic AI could reshape the future of financial services by supporting more connected and context-aware decision making within governed frameworks across the credit ecosystem. The report highlights the emergence of the Agentic consumer and explores what it means for consumers, lenders and the broader credit ecosystem as financial services become increasingly AI-enabled.

Mumbai (Maharshtra) [India], September 22: Experian, a global data and technology company, today launched its latest report, “Unlocking Enterprise Intelligence: A Journey of Innovation and Transformation with Agentic AI”, exploring how Agentic AI could reshape the future of financial services by supporting more connected and context-aware decision making within governed frameworks across the credit ecosystem. The report highlights the emergence of the Agentic consumer and explores what it means for consumers, lenders and the broader credit ecosystem as financial services become increasingly AI-enabled.

Also Read | Saudi Arabia Restarts East-West Pipeline and Resumes Crude Exports, Oil Prices Drop Over USD 2.

The report highlights that financial services are entering a new phase of transformation driven by the convergence of digital ecosystems, expanding data availability, advanced analytics and rapid progress in Artificial Intelligence (AI). AI is evolving from primarily predictive and assistive applications towards systems that can increasingly interpret intent, comprehend context and act within defined boundaries. It has the potential to transform how consumers discover, compare and access financial products, while creating new opportunities for lenders to deliver more connected, personalised and seamless customer journeys.

The report considers how an increasingly agent-enabled financial ecosystem could allow AI to support consumers in understanding financial concepts, comparing options and moving from intent towards informed action within clearly defined permissions and controls. As financial institutions navigate this shift, the opportunity is not simply to deploy more agents, but to provide Trusted AI that combines intelligence with reliable information, appropriate financial context and strong governance.

Also Read | West Bengal: Fishermen Rescue Elephant Calf Swept 3 KM Down Teesta River (Videos).

The report emphasises several shifts that could shape the next phase of financial services:

- The emergence of the Agentic Consumer, with AI potentially playing a greater role in supporting how consumers discover, compare and access financial products.

- Trust could become an increasingly important differentiator, as consumers seek intelligence supported by reliable information and appropriate financial context.

- Product discovery and comparison could become more intelligent, creating opportunities for institutions that are discoverable, responsive and trusted.

- Agent capability and trust infrastructure need to evolve together, with transparency, governance and accountability becoming increasingly important.

- Connected and governed platforms could help reduce friction across financial journeys by stitching data, analytics, and decisioning with context.

- Agent-ready institutions could be better positioned to support more connected customer experiences, while maintaining evidence and accountability across decision-making processes.

Commenting on the findings, Manish Jain, Country Managing Director of Experian in India, said, "Artificial Intelligence has the potential to reshape the next phase of financial services, not simply by making existing processes faster, but by changing how consumers and institutions interact, make decisions and take action within clearly defined boundaries. India’s retail credit market is already operating at significant scale, with lenders sourcing 51.69 crore loans worth Rs.97.7 lakh crore in FY26. As AI becomes more embedded across this ecosystem, trust, governance and clear accountability will be critical to scaling its use responsibly. The next phase of adoption will be defined not by how autonomous technology can become, but by how confidently consumers and financial institutions can trust it."

"The opportunity ahead is to build a financial ecosystem where technology helps people and organisations make better decisions while trust remains the foundation on which those decisions are made. This means combining innovation with reliable data, transparency, appropriate human oversight and clear accountability. Those that can combine innovation with transparency, accountability and responsible governance will be best positioned to create long-term value and stronger customer relationships.”

As organisations prepare for an increasingly agent-enabled future, Experian believes that trusted intelligence, contextual decisioning and responsible innovation will play a critical role in helping lenders create more seamless customer journeys, make better decisions and drive sustainable growth. Through its data, analytics, decisioning and platform capabilities, Experian continues to help financial institutions navigate this transformation with confidence while maintaining trust, transparency and governance at every stage of the customer lifecycle.
