B2B Director, Sales & Partnerships @Flip.ro

About FLIP

Flip is the leading refurbished electronics eCommerce platform in Southeastern Europe, operating in Romania, Bulgaria, Hungary, and Greece, and part of the eMAG Group. We're building a new B2B sales channel from scratch and looking for the right person to lead it.

The Role

We're hiring a B2B Director to build Flip's B2B channel across all European markets, from zero, with ambitious revenue targets. The channel has two distinct motions: a high-volume network of small and medium retailers (online retailers, small independent shops, GSM stores), and a small number of strategic upstream accounts (telecom operators, large retailers) looking to extend their offering with refurbished electronics.

This is a build role, not a management role over an existing book. You'll design the strategy, close the first major accounts yourself, and hire the team needed to run the long-tail motion at volume.

Role responsibilities:

Design and own the go-to-market strategy for Flip's B2B channel, split across two motions: a high-volume SME/independent retailer network and a small set of strategic enterprise partnerships (telecom operators, retailers).

Build, structure and run the outbound engine for the SME segment: identify targets, contact, pitch, onboard, manage test orders through to repeat ordering, and hire and lead a 2-4 person BDM/account-manager team needed to execute it at volume, rather than running it personally.

Personally originate and sign new enterprise partnerships: lead outreach, RFP response, and negotiation of framework/master agreements with telecom operators and large retailers, including commercial terms, SLAs, grading/return policy, and payment terms.

Set and own the B2B revenue plan and pipeline targets, phased by quarter given the longer sales cycle on enterprise accounts, and report progress against it on a regular cadence.

Build the CRM/pipeline process from scratch — account identification, sequencing, hand-off from prospecting to onboarding to repeat orders — so the funnel is instrumented and auditable across all markets, not run on individual relationships.

Work directly with Flip's demand, supply, and operations teams to make sure B2B commercial terms are consistent with margin, inventory, and grading constraints — not sold in isolation from the rest of the business.

Document and standardize the operational processes behind B2B sales, invoicing, returns, and warranty claims, and work with ops&tech to automate them as account volume grows.

Represent Flip at the industry events and trading networks where this deal flow originates (refurbished and mobile wholesale trade events, telecom industry conferences).

Role requirements:

8-12 years of B2B/commercial sales experience, with direct evidence of building a sales channel, dealer network, or new market from zero, not only managing or growing an inherited book of accounts.

Background in mobile devices, IT hardware, or electronics B2B distribution, or in a telecom operator's commercial/wholesale/device function

Recommerce-specific experience is a plus, not a requirement.

Demonstrated experience negotiating framework/master agreements with enterprise procurement: SLAs, payment terms, RFP processes and not only transactional SME sales.

Comfortable owning both a high-volume, lower-touch sales motion (SME/independent retailers) and a low-volume, high-touch one (enterprise accounts) — or clear strength in one with a credible plan to build the other via the team.

Commercially and financially literate: understands gross margin by grade/SKU, credit terms and DSO, inventory turns, and can negotiate on profitability, not just volume.

Track record hiring and managing a small sales/BDM team, ideally as a player-coach rather than purely as a strategist.

Based in Bucharest, or willing to relocate.

Fluent in English;

CRM and process discipline: has built or run a structured sales funnel before, not just relationship-driven selling.

What Flip offers:

Ownership of a new revenue line from day one, backed by an established eCommerce platform and operational infrastructure across four markets.

Direct access to and sponsorship from the CEO for this build.

As part of Endava's strategic partnership with WTW, who provide data-driven, insight-led solutions in the areas of people, risk and capital, we're building dedicated software engineering teams to support WTW's Insurance Consulting and Technology Division.

WTW's Insurance Consulting and Technology business is a global leader in P&C, Life and Health insurance software and advisory services, with over 1,700 colleagues across 35 markets. More than 1,000 insurers worldwide trust our combination of advisory insight and advanced software to help them navigate complexity and drive sustainable growth.

Joining Endava, you'll work exclusively with WTW to help embed AI-enabled engineering practices, modern ways of working and deep insurance technology expertise, contributing to the next generation of products and services for insurers worldwide. Working as part of a dedicated team established through a Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) model, you'll collaborate closely with WTW while building your career as an Endava employee, supporting the long-term success of this strategic partnership.

About the Role

As a Full Stack Software Engineer, you will join an experienced cross-functional engineering team responsible for designing, developing and evolving the Authentication and Authorization capability used across multiple products and engineering teams.

This is not a traditional application development role. Instead, you will help build a reusable identity platform that enables other engineering teams to adopt standardised authentication and authorisation services while improving security, developer experience and operational efficiency.

The capability provides shared identity and access management services that help applications authenticate users securely, authorise access to business resources and integrate with enterprise identity providers.

Built on Auth0, Fine-Grained Authorization (FGA) and modern Azure services, it includes reusable SDKs, reverse proxy services and developer tooling that make secure integration simpler across ICT’s technology landscape.

You will work closely with architects, product teams, platform engineers and business stakeholders helping deliver secure, scalable and high-quality technology solutions that create value for WTW and its customers.

What Success Looks Like

In this role you will:

Help deliver secure, reusable authentication and authorization services used by multiple product teams.

Build high-quality .NET APIs, Angular administration tools and integration services that are maintainable and easy to operate.

Improve the reliability, scalability and security of shared identity services through well-tested engineering changes.

Support platform adoption by improving SDKs, documentation, developer tooling and integration patterns.

Contribute to automation, CI/CD and cloud platform improvements that make delivery faster and more predictable.

Collaborate with architects, product owners, QA, DevOps and consuming product teams to solve identity and access management challenges.

Actively learn, share knowledge and contribute to a positive engineering culture within the Quartz team.

Key Responsibilities

Identity Platform Development

Design, develop and maintain authentication and authorization services using modern .NET technologies.

Develop reusable platform services supporting secure authentication and authorization across multiple business applications.

Build scalable REST APIs and integration services used throughout the organisation.

Develop and maintain Angular-based administration portals supporting user, group and permission management.

Contribute to the evolution of Fine-Grained Authorization (FGA) capabilities and centralized access management services.

Platform Services & Developer Experience

Develop reusable SDKs, libraries and APIs that simplify integration with the enterprise identity platform.

Build developer tooling that improves onboarding and adoption of shared authentication services.

Improve developer experience by simplifying authentication, authorization and platform integration.

Produce and maintain technical documentation supporting engineering teams consuming the platform.

Help minimise breaking changes by designing stable, reusable platform interfaces.

Cloud & Platform Engineering

Develop cloud-native services running on Microsoft Azure.

Build and maintain reverse proxy capabilities using Azure API Management.

Support Infrastructure as Code implementation using OpenTofu/Terraform.

Contribute to CI/CD pipelines and deployment automation using Azure DevOps.

Support continuous improvements in platform scalability, security and operational resilience.

Engineering Excellence

Write unit, integration and automated tests ensuring platform quality and reliability.

Participate in peer reviews, architecture discussions and technical design sessions.

Promote engineering best practices including Clean Code, automated testing and secure software development.

Collaborate with Product Owners, Architects, QA Engineers and Platform Engineers to deliver high-quality platform capabilities.

Operations & Collaboration

Participate in third-line production support and on-call rotation.

Investigate production issues and contribute to platform reliability improvements.

Work closely with multiple product teams integrating with the platform.

Share knowledge and contribute to establishing long-term Endava ownership of the Authentication & Authorization capability.

Software Engineering

4+ years of commercial software development experience using C# and modern .NET.

Strong experience designing and developing REST APIs.

Experience building scalable enterprise applications or shared platform services.

Strong knowledge of object-oriented programming and modern software design principles.

Identity & Security

Strong understanding of OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect (OIDC) and JWT.

Good understanding of modern authentication and authorization concepts.

Experience integrating applications with enterprise identity providers.

Understanding of secure API design and identity-based access control.

Cloud & Platform Engineering

Experience developing cloud-native applications on Microsoft Azure.

Experience with Azure DevOps, Git and CI/CD pipelines.

Understanding of Infrastructure as Code principles, with the ability and willingness to work with tools such as OpenTofu or Terraform.

Understanding of Azure API Management or similar API Gateway technologies.

Front-End Development

Experience developing Angular applications using TypeScript.

Experience building administrative or developer-facing web applications.

Engineering Practices

Experience writing automated tests (unit, integration and API testing).

Experience working in Agile Scrum teams.

Strong communication and collaboration skills.

Ability to work effectively across multiple product teams.

Preferred Skills and Experience

Auth0

Fine-Grained Authorization (FGA)

Google Zanzibar authorization model

Azure API Management (APIM)

SCIM integrations

Identity Federation

Datadog

Playwright

Trivy

GitLeaks

Invicti

Experience building reusable developer platforms

Experience working with enterprise shared services

For this position, the gross base salary starts from PLN 15 267 PLN Gross per month (full-time employment contract), determined using objective and gender-neutral criteria including skillset, experience and role responsibilities.

Our benefits offering typically include private medical insurance, dental plan, and glasses reimbursement. The figure represents the initial remuneration we expect to offer for this role and does not limit the right to equal pay for women and men performing the same work or work of equal value. evidence.text:
Technology is our how. And people are our why. For over two decades, we have been harnessing technology to drive meaningful change.

By combining world-class engineering, industry expertise and a people-centric mindset, we consult and partner with leading brands from various industries to create dynamic platforms and intelligent digital experiences that drive innovation and transform businesses.

From prototype to real-world impact - be part of a global shift by doing work that matters.

Development is the largest discipline at Endava. Our developers design, build, and release software products in multiple programming languages, frameworks, and libraries. Always collaborating with cross-functional project teams, our developers are adaptable problem-solvers with a client-oriented mindset.

As a Senior Python Developer at Endava, you will play a crucial role in designing, building, and maintaining robust, scalable Python-based applications and data-driven solutions for Banking and Capital Markets clients. You will work on enterprise-grade platforms exposed to complex financial workflows, including trade capture, trade processing, risk analytics, reporting, data processing, and cross-asset solutions used by Trading, Market Risk, Quants, Finance, and Operations stakeholders.

Responsibilities:

Design, implement, and maintain complex Python applications and services, ensuring high performance, security, reliability, and scalability.

Participate actively in all phases of the application development lifecycle.

Collaborate with business analysts, architects, developers, testers, data engineers, and client stakeholders to clarify requirements, processes, architecture, and priorities.

Contribute to solutions supporting Banking and Capital Markets domains, including trade lifecycle, risk analytics, reporting, data processing, analytics platforms, and financial services workflows.

Work with technical and non-technical stakeholders across Trading, Market Risk, Finance, Operations, Quantitative Analysis, and Technology areas.

Develop backend services, APIs, automation components, data processing pipelines, and reporting solutions using Python and related technologies.

Recommend and promote IT industry standards, tools, and practices, including clean code, design patterns, DevOps, CI/CD, testing automation, and cloud-ready engineering.

Propose improvements and escalate risks or issues related to development activities.

Participate in the review of work done by development team members.

Learn and apply new technologies, practices, and tools as appropriate to the project.

Participate in internal and external tech communities, events, and knowledge-sharing activities.

Share experience and knowledge gained from projects, especially around Banking and Capital Markets delivery.

6+ years of experience in Python development.

Experience working in Banking, Financial Services, or Capital Markets environments is highly desirable.

Good understanding of Capital Markets concepts such as trade capture, trade processing, risk analytics, reporting, asset classes, pricing, or trading workflows.

Strong understanding of common programming paradigms, including object-oriented programming, functional programming concepts, and asynchronous programming.

Strong familiarity with design and architectural patterns, clean code principles, and enterprise application design.

Proficient in Python and related frameworks or libraries such as FastAPI, Flask, Django, Pandas, NumPy, SQLAlchemy, PySpark, or similar.

Practical experience with relational and/or NoSQL database systems such as PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, MongoDB, Cassandra, or similar.

Ability to design, build, and analyze complex SQL queries.

Experience building REST APIs, backend services, data processing components, automation tools, or reporting solutions.

Good understanding of version control systems such as Git or similar.

Experience with messaging and event-driven systems such as Kafka, RabbitMQ, Azure Service Bus, AWS SQS/SNS, or similar.

Experience with microservices, distributed systems, integration patterns, and data-intensive applications.

Experience with CI/CD, deployment tools, and container platforms such as Jenkins, GitLab CI/CD, Azure DevOps, Docker, Kubernetes, OpenShift, or similar.

Experience with Agile methodologies such as Scrum or Kanban.

Good problem-solving skills and analytical thinking.

Excellent communication and teamwork abilities.

Ability to collaborate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Advanced English level is mandatory.

Nice to have:

Experience in Capital Markets technology consulting or financial services delivery.

Exposure to Fixed Income, FX, Equities, Derivatives, Fund Transfer Pricing, Asset Liability Management, or Market Risk platforms.

Experience working with Quants, Traders, Risk Managers, or Finance stakeholders, or data analytics teams.

Experience with data engineering, analytics, dashboarding, or reporting tools.

Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP.

Exposure to libraries or tools used in quantitative, risk, or financial analytics.

Exposure to Gen-AI tools applied to software engineering, documentation, productivity, data analysis, or reporting automation.

Discover some of the global benefits that empower our people to become the best version of themselves:

Finance: Competitive salary package, share plan, referral bonus;

Career Development: Career coaching, global career opportunities, non-linear career paths, internal development programmes for management and technical leadership;

Learning Opportunities: Complex projects, rotations, internal tech communities, training, certifications, coaching, online learning platforms subscriptions, pass-it-on sessions, workshops, conferences;

Work-Life Balance: Hybrid work and flexible working hours, employee assistance programme;

Health: Global internal wellbeing programme, access to wellbeing apps;

Community: Global internal tech communities, hobby clubs and interest groups, inclusion and diversity programmes, events and celebrations.

At Endava, we’re committed to creating an open, inclusive, and respectful environment where everyone feels safe, valued, and empowered to be their best. On July 22, 2026, Equifax Inc. (the “Company”) executed an Underwriting Agreement with J.P. Morgan Securities LLC, BofA Securities, Inc., Truist Securities, Inc. and Wells Fargo Securities, LLC, as the representatives of the underwriters named therein (the “Underwriting Agreement”), with regard to the issuance and sale by the Company of $500,000,000 aggregate principal amount of the Company’s 5.000% Senior Notes due 2029 (the “2029 Notes”) and $500,000,000 aggregate principal amount of the Company’s 5.650% Senior Notes due 2033 (the “2033 Notes” and, together with the 2029 Notes, the “Notes”). The Notes were issued pursuant to the Indenture, dated as of July 29, 2026 (the “Base Indenture”), between the Company and U.S. Bank Trust Company, National Association, as trustee, as supplemented by the First Supplemental Indenture relating to the Notes, dated as of July 29, 2026 (the “Supplemental Indenture” and, together with the Base Indenture, the “Indenture”).

Interest on the 2029 Notes will accrue from July 29, 2026 at a rate of 5.000% per year and will be payable in cash semi-annually in arrears on February 15 and August 15 of each year, beginning on February 15, 2027. Interest on the 2033 Notes will accrue from July 29, 2026 at a rate of 5.650% per year and will be payable in cash semi-annually in arrears on February 15 and August 15 of each year, beginning on February 15, 2027.

The 2029 Notes will mature on August 15, 2029. Prior to their maturity date, the Company may redeem the 2029 Notes at its option, in whole or in part, at any time and from time to time, at a redemption price (expressed as a percentage of the principal amount and rounded to three decimal places) equal to the greater of (1)(a) the sum of the present values of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest thereon discounted to the redemption date (assuming the 2029 Notes matured on August 15, 2029) on a semi-annual basis (assuming a 360-day year consisting of twelve 30-day months) at the Treasury Rate (as defined in the Indenture) plus 15 basis points, less (b) interest accrued to the redemption date, and (2) 100% of the principal amount of the 2029 Notes to be redeemed, plus, in either case, accrued and unpaid interest thereon to, but excluding, the redemption date.

The 2033 Notes will mature on August 15, 2033. Prior to June 15, 2033 (two months prior to their maturity date), the Company may redeem the 2033 Notes at its option, in whole or in part, at any time and from time to time, at a redemption price (expressed as a percentage of the principal amount and rounded to three decimal places) equal to the greater of (1)(a) the sum of the present values of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest thereon discounted to the redemption date (assuming the 2033 Notes matured on June 15, 2033) on a semi-annual basis (assuming a 360-day year consisting of twelve 30-day months) at the Treasury Rate (as defined in the Indenture) plus 20 basis points, less (b) interest accrued to the redemption date, and (2) 100% of the principal amount of the 2033 Notes to be redeemed, plus, in either case, accrued and unpaid interest thereon to, but excluding, the redemption date.

On or after June 15, 2033, the Company may redeem the 2033 Notes, in whole or in part, at any time and from time to time, at a redemption price equal to 100% of the principal amount of the 2033 Notes being redeemed, plus accrued and unpaid interest thereon to, but excluding, the redemption date.

The net proceeds from the offering were approximately $990.5 million, after deducting the underwriting discounts and estimated offering expenses payable by the Company. The Company intends to use the net proceeds from the offering for the repayment of borrowings under its commercial paper program.

The following documents are being filed with this Current Report on Form 8-K and are incorporated by reference into the Company’s effective Registration Statement on Form S-3 (File No. 333-295211) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on April 21, 2026: (i) the Underwriting Agreement, filed as Exhibit 1.1 hereto; (ii) the Base Indenture, filed as Exhibit 4.1 hereto; (iii) the First Supplemental Indenture, including the form of 2029 Note as Exhibit A and the form of 2033 Note as Exhibit B, filed as Exhibit 4.2 hereto; (iv) the opinion of counsel addressing the validity of the Notes, filed as Exhibit 5.1 hereto; and (v) the opinion of Julia A. Houston, Chief Legal Officer of the Company, addressing certain other legal matters, filed as Exhibit 5.2 hereto.

Pursuant to the requirements of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, the registrant has duly caused this report to be signed on its behalf by the undersigned hereunto duly authorized.

Our simple goal is to make hiring easy. To help businesses get the talent they need to succeed. And to help people find a job they love.
Everyone is incredibly frustrated by how hard it is to find amazing talent. We share that frustration.
Recruiting is a fragmented, opaque process undermined by outdated technology that turns off candidates and hiring managers.
Now, imagine a world where it’s easy to find great candidates, it’s easy for people to show interest in jobs, it’s easy for hiring teams to collaborate, and your recruiting vendors are just a click away.
We imagined it. And then we delivered it.

Assess patient health problems and needs, develop and implement nursing care plans, and maintain medical records. Administer nursing care to ill, injured, convalescent, or disabled patients. May advise patients on health maintenance and disease prevention or provide case management. Licensing or registration required.
Maintain accurate, detailed reports and records.

Administer medications to patients and monitor patients for reactions or side effects.

Record patients' medical information and vital signs.

Monitor, record, and report symptoms or changes in patients' conditions.

Consult and coordinate with healthcare team members to assess, plan, implement, or evaluate patient care plans.

Customer and Personal Service — Knowledge of principles and processes for providing customer and personal services. This includes customer needs assessment, meeting quality standards for services, and evaluation of customer satisfaction.

Psychology — Knowledge of human behavior and performance; individual differences in ability, personality, and interests; learning and motivation; psychological research methods; and the assessment and treatment of behavioral and affective disorders.

English Language — Knowledge of the structure and content of the English language including the meaning and spelling of words, rules of composition, and grammar.

Education and Training — Knowledge of principles and methods for curriculum and training design, teaching and instruction for individuals and groups, and the measurement of training effects.

These forward-looking statements include statements regarding any direct or indirect impact on us, our customers, or our service providers from conflict in the Middle East or elsewhere; signs of a possible recovery in the ocean market; our ability to use and benefit from our investments in technology, including AI; our expectation that air rates will normalize to some degree over time and that air demand as we enter Q3 remains healthy; our expectation that demand remains strong for airfreight services in support of AI infrastructure deployments; our belief that we may benefit more during times of disruption; our belief that our culture remains strong and is fundamental to our success; our belief that there may be no logical peak to customs growth and that complexity drives sustained demand for customs expertise and creates opportunity for continued growth globally; and our belief that there are additional opportunities to improve productivity through continued investments in technology, artificial intelligence, process improvements, and operational execution. There are more than 67,000 unique flight routes globally, and the impact of the Middle East conflict has not been uniform across the aviation industry. The disruption has been concentrated primarily among Middle Eastern carriers and routes that transit the affected airspace. Many of these carriers are among the world's largest air cargo operators and rely heavily on both wide-body passenger aircraft and dedicated freighter fleets. While some passenger operations have been affected by airspace restrictions and routing adjustments, freighter services have generally remained operational. As a result, the most significant impact has been on capacity availability and payload efficiency, rather than overall network connectivity. Our growth was driven primarily from Asia, where operations experienced limited disruption. Year-over-year volume growth was supported by increased shipments from existing customers, market share gains, strong demand from the technology sector, and our ability to secure additional capacity from carrier partners in key high-demand markets. Our success in securing incremental capacity during a constrained market environment was a significant contributor to our strong Q2 performance, enabling us to support customer growth, gain market share, and capitalize on favorable market conditions.

We do not know how long rates will hold at current levels and we expect them to normalize to some degree over time. Having said that, AI demand seems insatiable and is putting strain on existing air capacity, which may cause a more structural increase to rates. The high growth rates experienced in Q2 are continuing into Q3 through July.

The conflict impacted available capacity, payload utilization, and routing options across affected airspace. As a result, carriers were required to carry additional fuel, reducing cargo payloads and tightening available capacity. This constrained environment supported elevated buy and sell rates during the quarter. Most of our tonnage growth came from the Asia region, which was largely unaffected by the disruption. Growth was driven by a combination of increased volumes from existing customers, market share gains, strong technology-related demand, and our ability to secure additional carrier capacity. These factors contributed to the acceleration of tonnage growth from 13% in April to 15% in June. While we do not provide formal guidance, demand entering Q3 remains healthy. Future pricing trends will depend on several factors, including the pace of capacity restoration, carrier network deployment decisions, geopolitical developments, and the sustainability of technology-related demand, which continues to be strong. Although some conflict-driven pricing benefits may moderate as capacity normalizes, our non-asset-based model provides the flexibility to adapt quickly to changing market conditions.

We do not disclose the specific contribution of any individual customer segment to our airfreight volumes. That said, demand from AI hyperscalers and other high-value technology customers was a significant growth driver during the quarter. Demand remains strong for airfreight services in support of AI infrastructure deployments. Additionally, we noted in our earnings release that because of the current geopolitical state of the world, rising fuel costs, tight capacity, and routing challenges, air carriers are under enormous strain and may continue to be for some time.

While we often point to market disruptions as a factor in our results, and those disruptions may even represent a new normal, they were not unique to Q2 2026. Our results were driven by more than just temporary events. We achieved double-digit growth across most of our products from a diverse range of geographies and business sectors, as we grew market share and executed well across our entire organization. While we may benefit more during times of disruption, we regularly prepare for the disruption that seems inevitable somewhere within our global network.

We are not seeing signs of slowing demand from AI hyperscalers and other high-value technology customers. That business was a key part of our growth, particularly in air and our customs brokerage and other services businesses. We believe that we are likely gaining market share within that space, as current and new customers recognize our expertise in handling such high-value freight.

The restructuring was concentrated within our Global Technology organization and was intended to modernize and reshape that function for the future. The goal was to better align the organization with our long-term technology priorities, improve productivity, and position the company for future growth. We are not providing additional detail on specific teams or functions affected beyond what has been publicly disclosed.

While we have historically implemented a practice of not using layoffs as a lever to reduce costs when business weakens, such as during the 2008-2009 financial crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic, we have never had a formal or blanket “no layoff” policy as may be commonly believed. In our history, we have occasionally reduced our workforce through layoffs for very specific strategic reasons.

Our culture remains strong and is fundamental to our success. We strongly believe that our culture is a significant reason that many people, including most of those in our senior ranks, have chosen to spend the majority of their careers at Expeditors. We work extremely hard to live up to that trust and would not have carried out this restructuring if we did not fully believe that it was in the best interest of our success going forward.

The restructuring does not change our technology or AI ambitions. It was not about cost, nor was it driven by a redirected strategy to outsource our core technology. The restructuring was designed to better position our Global Technology organization for future growth and needs by completing an ongoing modernization of certain legacy systems and practices. While the restructuring was unusual for us, it was not unprecedented as we have had layoffs in the past. We determined that a restructuring was the most direct path to position us for continued necessary investments in technology talent, capabilities, and solutions. We remain committed to developing strong internal technology expertise and systems, while maintaining industry best practices and selectively overlaying third-party solutions where they add value or bring specialized capabilities.

We believe there was some volume in Q2 that was pull-forward business, based on what customers told us, but we would be unable to quantify which loads were pull-forward and which were not. Regarding the outlook for Q3 and Q4, we cannot forecast future volumes or rates, as much depends on the geopolitics impacting some of the world’s most critical waterways, as well as the collective actions by the major carriers with regard to capacity management. Nevertheless, as we noted in our earnings release, the ocean market showed encouraging signs of stabilization in the second quarter. Ocean volumes increased 7% sequentially from the first quarter, marking the first sequential volume increase since the third quarter of 2025. We also saw a flattening of the prolonged downturn in the ocean market as strengthening demand and careful capacity management by ocean carriers contributed to improving rates, particularly late in the quarter. Those trends are encouraging.

We also saw the ocean market materially correct in 2025, beginning in Q3 of that year. As such, our comparables to prior periods will get much easier in Q3 and especially Q4, as opposed to the first half of 2026.

The slight margin decline within Customs brokerage and other services is largely a matter of mix. While all of the businesses generated double-digit growth, our road freight, warehousing and distribution, and other adjacent services businesses were particularly strong during the quarter. Because our road freight business has a lower gross margin than customs brokerage and was the fastest-growing part of the mix during the quarter, our gross margin percentage declined even though profitability and gross profit dollars from the customs business itself improved.

The District Sales Executive (DSE) is responsible for driving new business growth by identifying, developing, and securing new customer opportunities. The focus of this role is on achieving results that align with Expeditors' overall organizational objectives and strategic goals. Initiative, competitive drive, persistence, and the ability to stay focused on results despite changing conditions are essential to success in this position.

The DSE orchestrates the involvement of multiple stakeholders throughout the sales process to consistently secure new customer revenue for both the district office and the Expeditors network. This role operates in a dynamic, fast-paced environment that offers significant opportunities for professional growth, recognition, and reward based on business results achieved.

Key Responsibilities

Business Development & Territory Management

Manage an assigned territory and develop extensive knowledge of target customers, market opportunities, and competitors within the territory.

Identify, prospect, and secure new business opportunities through strategic business development activities.

Build and maintain a robust pipeline of qualified prospects aligned with district sales objectives.

Conduct regular customer and prospect meetings to uncover opportunities and develop long-term relationships.

Develop and execute strategic account plans that drive sustainable revenue growth.

Sales Process & Pipeline Management

Maintain a healthy sales pipeline with opportunities at various stages of the Team Selling Process.

Advance prospects through the sales cycle using consultative selling techniques and value-based conversations.

Ensure timely and accurate data entry within the Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system.

Consistently achieve established call activity, prospecting, and revenue generation expectations.

Effectively manage opportunities to achieve district growth targets and secure new customer revenue.

Customer Solutions & Relationship Management

Orchestrate customer and branch relationships while collaborating with Product, Service, Geo, and Knowledge Management resources.

Participate in the development of customized, value-added logistics solutions, including supporting diagrams, process flows, and cost-benefit analyses.

Build strong relationships with customer stakeholders and position Expeditors as a trusted supply chain partner.

Support the transition of new accounts through customer introductions, information transfer, and completion of required customer documentation.

Assist with accounts receivable collection activities when necessary.

Collaboration & Professional Development

Partner with operations and product teams to ensure successful implementation and growth of new business.

Attend sales training, professional development sessions, and industry education programs to continually enhance selling skills and product knowledge.

Participate in local trade organizations and industry groups as directed by the District Sales Manager.

Take on additional assignments and projects as required to support district and company objectives.

Contribute to a culture of collaboration, continuous improvement, and customer-focused execution.

Key Deliverables

Successful District Sales Executives consistently deliver the following results:

Manage an assigned territory and demonstrate extensive knowledge of customers, prospects, and competitors.

Maintain timely and accurate CRM data.

Coordinate customer, branch, and network resources to support the sales process.

Create value-added logistics solutions that address customer supply chain challenges.

Successfully transition new accounts to operations while ensuring a positive customer experience.

Continuously develop sales capabilities and product knowledge.

Participate in industry and trade organizations to enhance market presence.

Support district objectives through additional projects and assignments as needed.

Preferred Experience

Business development, sales, or account management experience.

Experience within logistics, freight forwarding, transportation, supply chain, or a related industry preferred.

Proven ability to develop new business and manage customer relationships.

Experience navigating complex sales cycles and presenting business solutions.

evidence.title: Warehouse Agent
evidence.text:
“We’re not in the shipping business; we’re in the information business” -Peter Rose, Expeditors Founder

As a Fortune 500 company, Expeditors employs more than 15,000 trained professionals in a worldwide network of over 300 locations across six continents. Expeditors satisfies the increasingly sophisticated needs of international trade through customized solutions and seamless, integrated information systems. Our services include the consolidation and forwarding of air or ocean freight, customs brokerage, vendor consolidation, cargo insurance, time-definite transportation, order management, warehousing, distribution and customized logistics solutions. Expeditors is headquartered in Seattle, Washington.

Ensure timely and accurate receiving, locating and sending of freight and information, conforming to safety standards and requirements as set by Expeditors.

Responsibilities and Tasks

Coordinate all work activities relating to processing freight flow (in- & outbound);

Receive goods and check freight for correct quantity, quality and possible damages;

Picking, checking and loading pallets for outgoing freight

Good knowledge of handling various internal means of transport ;

Loading and unloading of trucks by use of a forklift and/or electric pump trucks;

Create OSD reports and ensure correct completion;

Checking cargo manifests and assign to the Warehouse Agent Senior or Lead;

Perform double checks on the freight, ULDs , references & AWB numbers;

Perform Dangerous Goods and/or Lithium checks (if in possession of IATA DG Certificate);

Different contouring, such as building and breaking down of ULDs;

Adhere to security and compliance rules as set up by Expeditors;

Ensure a safe work environment

Meet KPI standards in accordance with the Company’s procedure

Maintain a clean work environment, all transport systems, storage areas, work places.

Meet compliance at all times to regulations internal and external in accordance with government regulations

Escalation of problems to Management when necessary

Daily process and input of all customer orders and distribution accounts.

Provide daily operational reports that are accurate and timely.

Generate all related paperwork and necessary information required for customer work orders, check all orders for special requests and posts inventory records.

Perform accurate and timely data entry for receiving order allocation, shipping and inventory management.

Rate domestic transportation bills.

Trace orders as required and notify customers of any activity concerning their order.

evidence.title: Senior Risk Analyst – Data Science & Analytics
evidence.text:
Experian is a global data and technology company, powering opportunities for people and businesses around the world. We operate across a range of markets, from financial services to healthcare, automotive, agribusiness, insurance, and many more. Experian invests in people and new advanced technologies to unlock the power of data. We have an amazing team of 25,200 people in 32 countries.

We are looking for a Senior Risk Analyst – Data Science & Analytics to join our Commercial Bureau Analytics & Pre-Sales Consulting team, with a dedicated focus on MSME bureau analytics. This is a senior hands-on role for an experienced credit-risk data scientist who can independently structure complex MSME lending problems, design bureau-led analytical solutions and translate modelling results into client-ready recommendations. You will lead scorecard and model development, portfolio and early-warning analytics, bureau-based proofs of concept and pre-sales solutioning for banks, NBFCs, fintechs and other MSME lenders. The role requires deep Python / SQL capability, strong credit-risk modelling judgement, substantial experience with MSME / SME or commercial bureau analytics, and the ability to guide other analysts while remaining deeply hands-on with data and code.

What you'll do

Lead end-to-end MSME bureau analytics engagements across acquisition, underwriting, risk segmentation, portfolio monitoring, early warning and collections, from problem definition through validation and delivery.

Own the analytical design for complex use cases, including outcome / bad definition, observation and performance windows, sample construction, segmentation, treatment of class imbalance, benchmark / challenger design and validation strategy.

Design advanced bureau variables from longitudinal business-entity and facility / tradeline histories, including repayment behaviour, delinquency patterns, exposure and utilisation, enquiries, account vintage, product / lender mix and changes in credit behaviour over time.

Develop, benchmark and validate MSME credit-risk scorecards and predictive models using interpretable statistical approaches and machine-learning challengers, making explicit trade-offs between predictive gain, stability, explainability and ease of implementation.

Lead portfolio diagnostics including vintage, cohort, roll-rate, risk migration, concentration, delinquency-flow and early-warning analysis, and translate findings into actionable credit-risk recommendations.

Quantify the incremental predictive and business value of bureau variables, scores and analytical constructs through robust benchmark and proof-of-concept designs.

Lead client and pre-sales discussions to diagnose the problem, assess data feasibility, frame the analytical solution, scope proofs of concept, present methodology and respond to technical questions.

Convert recurring MSME lender needs into reusable bureau features, analytical frameworks or product enhancements, and work with Product / Technology teams on UAT, implementation and monitoring requirements.

Review code, model methodology and analytical outputs from other analysts; mentor junior team members for statistical rigour, coding quality, reproducibility and documentation.

Ensure all analytical work meets applicable data-security, model-governance, documentation and compliance requirements.

What success looks like

MSME bureau solutions are methodologically defensible, stable, interpretable and clearly linked to a lender decision or portfolio outcome.

Proofs of concept and client solutioning demonstrate measurable analytical value and materially strengthen opportunity conversion or product adoption.

Reusable bureau variables and frameworks improve speed-to-solution while complex work is delivered with clear documentation, governance and implementation considerations.

Team capability improves through strong technical review, mentoring and standardisation of modelling and coding practices.

What you'll need to bring

Approximately 5-8 years of relevant experience in credit-risk analytics, data science, decision science or statistical modelling, including at least 3 years of substantial experience in MSME / SME / commercial credit-risk or commercial bureau analytics.

Advanced hands-on proficiency in Python and strong SQL, with demonstrated ability to build efficient, modular and reusable analytical code for large and granular credit datasets.

Demonstrated end-to-end ownership of credit-risk scorecard or model development, from target and sample design through feature engineering, modelling, validation and implementation / monitoring considerations.

Deep practical knowledge of scorecard and risk-model development, including binning, WoE / IV, logistic regression, variable selection, multicollinearity, reject-inference considerations where relevant, calibration, segmentation and score scaling, together with experience evaluating tree-based / gradient-boosting challengers.

Strong command of validation and monitoring concepts including KS, Gini / AUC, lift / gains, calibration, out-of-time validation, back-testing, PSI / CSI, stability and challenger comparisons.

Strong MSME credit-risk and bureau-data expertise: delinquency / default definitions, underwriting and segmentation, vintage / cohort and roll-rate analysis, early-warning indicators, and conversion of facility / tradeline histories into robust entity-level risk features.

Experience delivering analytics for banks, NBFCs, fintechs or other business lenders, with the judgement to distinguish statistical results from commercially usable risk solutions.

Strong client-facing and pre-sales capability, including discovery, solution framing, proof-of-concept design, methodology presentation and handling technical questions from senior risk / analytics stakeholders.

Experience reviewing analytical work, coaching less-experienced analysts and improving team standards for code quality, validation, documentation and reproducibility.

Good to have

Direct experience developing or validating commercial credit bureau scores, bureau-based MSME risk models or other bureau-led decisioning solutions.

Experience across multiple MSME lending products or lifecycle stages, such as business loans, working-capital facilities, secured / unsecured MSME credit, acquisition, underwriting, monitoring and collections.

SAS or another statistical programming environment in addition to Python.

Git, peer-review practices, Spark / Databricks or other tools used for large-scale analytical development.

Experience taking risk models or analytics from proof of concept into production, including monitoring and challenger frameworks.

Working knowledge of model-governance, credit-information and regulatory expectations relevant to lending in India.

Experience shaping analytical propositions, reusable solutions or product enhancements from repeated client use cases.

evidence.title: Full-Stack Engineer
evidence.text:
Experian is a global data and technology company, powering opportunities for people and businesses around the world. We operate across a range of markets, from financial services to healthcare, automotive, agribusiness, insurance, and many more. Experian invests in people and new advanced technologies to unlock the power of data. We have an amazing team of 25,200 people in 32 countries.

We are looking for a Full-Stack Engineer to join our development team and contribute to the development of scalable backend and frontend services. You will support core platform functionality across team-owned services, working with technologies including Python, Java, and React.

You will help build reliable APIs, reusable components, service integrations, and user-facing features while contributing to CI/CD practices, code quality, system stability, and continuous improvement. You will report to Senior Software Team Manager.

What you'll do:

Develop backend and frontend services using Python, Java, and React.

Support core platform functionality by delivering scalable, reliable, and maintainable solutions across team-owned services.

Implement reusable components, APIs, and service integrations that support data processing, business logic, and user-facing functionality.

Develop and improve CI/CD pipelines to contribute to ensuring services are efficiently built, tested, and deployed.

Apply sound software engineering practices to deliver performant, maintainable, and scalable solutions aligned with system architecture and engineering standards.

Collaborate with engineers, product managers, and stakeholders to design, implement, and improve features and services.

Enhance existing functionality and support new feature development while maintaining code quality, system stability, and operational reliability.

Participate in code reviews, testing, troubleshooting, and technical discussions to improve solution quality and team delivery.

Support ongoing improvements to engineering processes, development standards, and platform reliability.

What you'll bring:

4+ years of experience developing software using Python and Java.

Experience building frontend applications or components using React.

Experience with backend services, APIs, service integrations, and business logic implementation.

Knowledge of CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and modern software delivery practices.

Writing clean, maintainable, scalable, and performant code aligned with engineering standards.

Qualifications

4+ years of experience developing software using Python and Java.

Experience building frontend applications or components using React.

Experience with backend services, APIs, service integrations, and business logic implementation.

Knowledge of CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and modern software delivery practices.

Writing clean, maintainable, scalable, and performant code aligned with engineering standards.

Experience with React

What you will get:

Personal Development - career pathway for professional growth supported by learning and development programs and unlimited access to online educational training courses, learning materials and books.

Work environment - excellent work conditions with friendly environment, recognized team spirit, and fun and quality recreation time.

Social benefit package including life insurance, food vouchers, additional health insurance, monthly flex allowance and internet coverage, corporate discounts, marriage and childbirth / adoption allowance, Multisport card, Sharesave plan, Employee assistance program, а birthday gift and many other benefits!

Work-life balance - 25 days paid vacation, 1 additional day off for your birthday and extra 3 paid days for participation in Social responsibility event.

Opportunity for Flexible working hours and Home Office.

Experian is an Equal opportunity employer. Everyone can succeed at Experian and bring their whole self to work, irrespective of their gender, ethnicity, religion, colour, sexuality, physical ability or age. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know at the earliest opportunity.

This is a hybrid remote/in-office role.

Experian will never ask candidates to make any payment as part of an application, interview, assessment, onboarding, or recruitment process. To apply for roles or verify opportunities, please visit experian.com/careers.

Senior PMO (Project Management Office) Manager
evidence.text:
Experian is a global data and technology company, powering opportunities for people and businesses around the world. We help to redefine lending practices, uncover and prevent fraud, simplify healthcare, create marketing solutions, and gain deeper insights into the automotive market, all using our unique combination of data, analytics and software. We also assist millions of people to realize their financial goals and help them save time and money.

We operate across a range of markets, from financial services to healthcare, automotive, agribusiness, insurance, and many more industry segments.

We invest in people and new advanced technologies to unlock the power of data. As a FTSE 100 Index company listed on the London Stock Exchange (EXPN), we have a team of 22,500 people across 32 countries. Our corporate headquarters are in Dublin, Ireland. Learn more at experianplc.com.

We are looking for a highly experienced Senior PMO Manager to lead and govern complex strategic initiatives across multiple business functions. This role will be responsible for establishing project governance standards, driving portfolio oversight, managing executive reporting, and ensuring successful delivery of transformation programs aligned with Experian's strategic priorities.

The ideal candidate is a proactive leader with strong stakeholder management skills, extensive experience managing enterprise-scale programs, and a proven ability to drive execution in a fast-paced, matrixed environment.

Portfolio & Program Governance

Lead PMO governance across a portfolio of strategic projects and transformation initiatives.

Ensure projects are aligned with business objectives, priorities, and budget commitments.

Establish and maintain project management standards, methodologies, tools, and reporting frameworks.

Monitor portfolio performance, identifying risks, dependencies, and opportunities for improvement.

Drive consistency in project planning, execution, and benefits realization.

Strategic Program Delivery

Oversee the successful delivery of large-scale, cross-functional programs.

Partner with senior business leaders to define objectives, scope, milestones, and success measures.

Facilitate decision-making through clear governance forums and executive-level reporting.

Ensure effective management of project timelines, budgets, resources, and deliverables.

Support change management and organizational readiness activities.

Stakeholder Management

Build strong relationships with executive leadership and key business stakeholders.

Act as a trusted advisor on project delivery, governance, and transformation best practices.

Prepare and present concise updates to senior leadership, highlighting progress, risks, and mitigation plans.

Facilitate steering committee meetings and executive reviews.

Financial & Resource Management

Track program budgets, forecasts, and resource allocation.

Monitor financial performance and project benefits realization.

Ensure project investments deliver measurable business value.

Support annual planning cycles and portfolio prioritization processes.

Risk & Compliance Management

Implement robust risk management and issue resolution processes.

Ensure compliance with internal governance, regulatory, and audit requirements.

Maintain comprehensive project documentation and decision logs.

Drive continuous improvement initiatives across the PMO function.

Required Experience

Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Project Management, Engineering, Information Technology, or related field.

8+ years of project, program, or PMO leadership experience.

Proven experience managing large-scale transformation, technology, or business change initiatives.

Experience operating in a complex global or multinational organization.

Strong knowledge of project management methodologies (Waterfall, Agile, Hybrid).

Demonstrated experience presenting to senior executives and steering committees.

Preferred Qualifications

PMP, PRINCE2, MSP, Agile, or equivalent certification.

Experience supporting digital transformation, cloud migration, ERP, HR, Finance, or technology programs.

Experience with project portfolio management tools such as Jira, Azure DevOps, Clarity, Smartsheet, or Planview.

Knowledge of financial services, data, analytics, software, or technology sectors.

evidence.title: SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT SPECIALIST
evidence.text:
Experian es una empresa global de datos y tecnología que impulsa oportunidades para personas y negocios en todo el mundo. Ayudamos a redefinir prácticas de préstamos, descubrir y prevenir el fraude, simplificar la atención médica, crear soluciones de marketing y obtener perspectivas más profundas del mercado automotriz, todo utilizando nuestra combinación única de datos, análisis y software. También asistimos a millones de personas a alcanzar sus metas financieras y ayudarles a ahorrar tiempo y dinero.

Operamos en una variedad de mercados, desde servicios financieros hasta atención médica, automotriz, agroindustria, seguros y muchos otros segmentos industriales.

Invertimos en personas y nuevas tecnologías avanzadas para desbloquear el poder de los datos. Como empresa del índice FTSE 100, cotizada en la Bolsa de Valores de Londres (EXPN), contamos con un equipo de 22,500 personas en 32 países. Nuestra sede corporativa está en Dublín, Irlanda. Obtenga más información en experianplc.com.

Descripción del trabajo

Descripción general del área: La subgerencia de Ingeniería de Sistemas tiene como propósito el desarrollar las aplicaciones y

servicios que los clientes nos solicitan y del mismo modo, desarrollar nuevas soluciones que nosotros como organización

requiramos disponer a nuestros clientes.

Propósito del cargo:

Responsable por gestionar e implementar proyectos informáticos para la organización y entregar soporte en ambientes

productivos, para satisfacer los distintos requerimientos del cliente.

Entregables:

• Contribuir a la adecuada evaluación y planificación de los proyectos, así como la correcta asignación de recursos.

• Desarrollar aplicaciones fiables y seguras.

• Generar la menor cantidad de iteraciones en QA y entregar un producto de calidad

• Contar con aplicaciones actualizadas, cambio de forma organizada y gestionada a través del administrador de cambios

• Asegurar la continuidad operacional y SLA de los servicios de la organización

• Contribuir a la generación de soluciones a temas informáticos requeridos por la organización.

• Asegurar la continuidad y soporte a las aplicaciones productivas.

• Aportar a la gestión y resultados del área

Responsabilidades del cargo:

• Participar en la evaluación de tiempos en proyectos que serán asignados dentro del área, facilitando la asignación de roles y tareas

a los participantes por partes de los jefes de Proyectos.

• Levantar y analizar requerimientos asociados al proyecto, llevándolos al lenguaje natural, eliminando cualquier ambigüedad y

documentándolo de acuerdo con los estándares definidos en la organización.

• Llevar a cabo el desarrollo de aplicaciones basados en los estándares definidos por las áreas de Sinacofi a nivel de objetos,

arquitectura y seguridad,

• Mantener y optimizar permanentemente las aplicaciones internas y externas basado en las buenas prácticas, actualizando

documentación de cada nuevo requerimiento y pruebas básicas de las mejoras incluidas

• Dar soporte a las áreas productivas: apoyando las puestas en producción de las aplicaciones, solucionando problemas puntuales

y/o incidencias declaradas, debiendo para ello realizar un análisis del problema para proponer o ejecutar la mejor solución

• Investigar y entregar soluciones para distintas problemáticas que surgen en los desarrollos

• Dar apoyo en diferentes soluciones informáticas de tipo técnico formando grupos de trabajo y encontrar alternativas factibles para

dar solución.

• Entregar la información necesaria para poder realizar un traspaso completo de las soluciones informáticas desarrolladas al área de

mantenimiento correctivo.

• Asumir rol del líder técnico para soluciones informáticas desarrolladas en el área o con empresas externas.

• Participar y realizar las actividades encomendadas por su jefatura, en el ámbito de su cargo

¿Qué estamos buscando?

Educación: Ingeniero Ejecución Informática o carrera afin.

Experiencia: Experiencia en el área de 2 años y al menos 1 años en cargo similiar.

Conocimientos técnicos requeridos:

• Análisis y diseño de soluciones informáticas

• Lenguajes de Programación: shell script, .NET (C#, Visual Basic, ASP), Java (Netbeans, Eclipse).

• Desarrollo de WS JSON, API REST y SOAP.

• Desarrollo de flujos en Control-M

• Sistemas operativos UNIX, LINUX, WINDOWS

• Base de datos relacionales: Sybase, Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL

• Desarrollo de WebServices en plataformas de BUS de Servicio como IBM Broker o alguna similar

• Desarrollo en IBM Datapower (opcional)

• Herramientas ETL Power Center, DataStage o alguno similar

• Metodología Ágil con Scrum

• Herramienta Veracode

• Suite Atlassian; Bitbucket, Jira, Confluence (opcional)

Idiomas: Inglés Nivel Intermedio (deseable)

Competencias:

• Organización del Trabajo

About Us:

Future is building a personalized guidance system for lifelong health. We help people understand what to do next for their body, goals, and stage of life — then support them in turning those decisions into sustained behavior change. By combining AI, human expertise, personal health data, and accountability, Future helps members improve performance today while building the resilience, capacity, and healthspan they need for decades to come.

About the Role

Backend engineers at Future operate at all levels -- building out core services, data pipelines, essential business systems, developer operations, and customer-facing features.

We’re responsible for the entirety of product surfaces across user and trainer experiences, and the initiatives we drive span across foundational core infrastructure to rapid feature iteration. Backend engineers work closely with several engineering teams & product managers to deliver the APIs, infrastructure, and scalability needed for every initiative.

You will:

Design, implement, and test APIs for new products, features, and services

Maintain and optimize existing systems, with emphasis on database-related performance

Collaborate with other engineers across the stack as well as cross-functional stakeholders

Keep up to date with the latest technologies and industry best practices, and encouraging fellow engineers to do so

Serve as on-call engineer approximately one week per month, responsible for triaging incoming issues during non-working hour

You have:

Great Product thinking. You think about the end user experience when you are building to consider whether the features you are building are not only meeting requirements but delighting users.

8+ years of production development experience, specifically working on backend / API

Scrappiness and pragmatism. We are a small and fast-moving startup and value someone who can continually weigh tradeoffs to balance engineering excellence with velocity.

Strong knowledge of Go, AWS, Docker (ECS), Postgres (RDS)

Proven ability to employ software quality measures during development, such as unit/integration testing, monitoring, alerting

Experience managing Docker-based microservice architecture

Experience working in a fast-moving startup environment. You are adaptable to shifting priorities, and have a proven track record of cutting through asks to build what matters.

Nice to have: experience working with ETL, with keen intuition for optimized database performance

Compensation, Benefits & Life at Future:

This role requires someone who thinks in systems. A marketplace is not a single product—it’s an ecosystem. You will report directly to the CPTO and work alongside a small, senior engineering team. There are no layers between you and the work, and no layers between you and the decisions that shape the company.

WHAT YOU’LL OWN:

Product Strategy & Vision

Define the product vision and strategy for the marketplace, grounded in deep user understanding, competitive analysis, and a clear-eyed view of the business model.

Own the roadmap end-to-end. Decide what to build, what to kill, and what to sequence—with conviction, not consensus.

Develop and maintain a strong point of view on where the wellness and longevity market is heading and how our product should evolve to lead, not follow.

TRUE 0→1 product thinking: identify the fastest and cheapest ways to validate core assumptions before committing significant engineering investment.

Marketplace Systems Thinking

Design and optimize both sides of the marketplace: the consumer journey (discovery → trust → booking → retention) and the practitioner journey (onboarding → activation → growth → advocacy).

Develop frameworks for marketplace health: supply/demand balance, liquidity metrics, matching quality, and network effects.

Own the cold-start playbook. Figure out how to bootstrap supply and demand in new verticals and geographies.

Think critically about marketplace trust and safety—credential verification, reviews, dispute resolution—as a product surface, not an afterthought.

Execution & Shipping

Partner with engineering and design to ship continuously. Write clear, opinionated specs. Run structured discovery. Make scope decisions that keep velocity high.

Instrument everything. Define success metrics for every feature. Run experiments. Kill things that aren’t working.

Balance competing priorities across consumer, practitioner, and platform workstreams while maintaining a clear view of the overall system.

Business & Growth

Own the business logic of the marketplace: pricing models, take rates, subscription tiers, transaction economics.

Partner with growth and marketing on acquisition loops, activation funnels, and retention strategies for both sides of the marketplace.

Use data to identify the highest-leverage opportunities. Build the instrumentation and dashboards needed to operate with clarity.

AI as a Force Multiplier

AI should be part of your daily operating system as a product manager.

Research synthesis: distilling user interviews, market data, and competitive intel at speed.

Spec and strategy drafting: using AI to accelerate writing, then applying your judgment to sharpen it.

Data analysis: querying, visualizing, and interpreting data with AI assistance.

Prototyping: rapidly generating UI concepts, user flows, and copy variations.

Workflow automation: building personal and team workflows that eliminate toil.

Bring a perspective on how AI should be woven into the product itself—personalized recommendations, intelligent matching, automated practitioner tools.

Raise the AI fluency bar for the entire team. Share what’s working. Push others to adopt.

Clear, precise communicator—in writing, in specs, in conversation, and in a room with engineers.

About Us:

Future is building a personalized guidance system for lifelong health. We help people understand what to do next for their body, goals, and stage of life — then support them in turning those decisions into sustained behavior change. By combining AI, human expertise, personal health data, and accountability, Future helps members improve performance today while building the resilience, capacity, and healthspan they need for decades to come.

Who We Are

Future pairs each member with an expert coach who gets to know them, their goals, and their data, then builds a healthier life around all of it. We started in fitness, and we're now going further: a coaching-led health experience that brings together movement, nutrition, sleep and recovery, and leverages real clinical data to build precise, custom member protocols. Our offering is continuing to evolve and we're looking for coaches who want to help shape it.

About the Role

Role Type: 1099 (independent contractor)

As a Health Coach, you'll own a caseload of members and guide each of them from their first day through their progress milestones. This is a partner role, not a prescriber role: you draw out what a member actually wants, meet them where they are, and help them build habits that last across nutrition, movement, sleep, and stress. You'll coach through a mix of virtual face-to-face sessions and day-to-day messaging, and you'll use each member's data to make your guidance specific and personal. The members we serve expect high-touch, polished care, with the coach at the center of their experience.

What you'll do

Own your members' experience end to end. Guide a caseload of members from onboarding through their 90-day milestone and beyond, and keep every one of them feeling individually known.

Coach live and asynchronously. Run virtual kickoff and check-in sessions, and support members between sessions over messaging that stays warm, timely, and clear.

Build personalized, data-informed plans. With the support of AI tooling, translate each member's goals and data into a plan across fitness, nutrition, sleep, and recovery, and adjust it as their life and results change.

Coach the person, not just the plan. Use motivational interviewing and reflective listening to help members find their own reasons for change and choose their own next step, rather than handing them a prescription.

Make the data useful. Under the guidance of Future’s Clinical Team, contextualize body composition scans, bloodwork and GLP-1 considerations within your scope, and turn them into everyday actions a member can take.

Make progress visible. Track progress against goals your members helped set, and celebrate the behavior and consistency wins, not just the number on a scan.

Help build. Bring what you learn from members back to the team, and help us shape a program that's ever growing and evolving.

Who you are

Empathetic. You lead with care and meet people where they are, whether it's a member having a hard week or a teammate under pressure.

Independent, and collaborative. You can run your caseload at a high level without hand-holding, and you still genuinely enjoy working alongside your teammates.

An active part of the community. Even though we're a virtual company, you show up: you join calls, contribute to projects, and share honest feedback that makes the team better.

Proactive. You chase down answers, follow up, and take initiative instead of waiting to be told.

Tech-savvy. You pick up new tools quickly and are comfortable working across apps, data, and platforms all day.

What you'll need

Required (non-negotiable)

NBC-HWC (National Board Certified Health & Wellness Coach) — full board certification through the National Board for Health & Wellness Coaching is required. This is our core standard for behavior-change theory, motivational interviewing, reflective listening, and coaching scope of practice.

An associate's degree or higher (or an equivalent, experience-based path to your coaching certification).

2+ years of client-facing coaching or training experience. Enough that you can run a member session on day one, without a ramp.

Proven high-volume caseload management. You've personally carried a large book of clients at once and kept each of them feeling individually known.

Comfort working with a diverse member population. You adapt your style to meet members of different ages, backgrounds, cultures, abilities, and health starting points, and every one of them feels respected and understood.

Strong written communication. Much of your coaching happens over messaging, so you're warm, clear, and personable on the page while staying professional.

Strong verbal communication and presence. You also coach face-to-face over video, and you bring confidence, thoughtfulness and professionalism into every session.

Comfortable synthesizing health data. You keep up with current health trends and have a track record of coaching clients across nutrition apps and wearable devices, bringing their data together into a single comprehensive plan.

Strong plus (not required)

Additional coaching credentials layered on top of NBC-HWC, such as ACE Health Coach, Precision Nutrition L1, or NASM Behavior Change Specialist.

A personal-training or strength credential (CSCS; NASM, ACE, or ACSM CPT; or similar).

A nutrition-coaching certification such as Precision Nutrition.

An advanced degree in exercise science, physiology, kinesiology, or a related field.

Clinical collaboration in functional or integrative medicine. You've worked alongside or under registered dietitians, nurse practitioners, or physicians.

Experience with luxury clientele. You've served high-end members in concierge medicine, a premium gym, or a private club, and you carry that polish into every interaction.

A distinct coaching specialty such as performance, postpartum, pelvic-floor, or eating-disorder-informed coaching, that adds range to our team.

Startup experience, or time spent in a fast-changing, still-being-built environment.

evidence.text:
About Us:

Future is building a personalized guidance system for lifelong health. We help people understand what to do next for their body, goals, and stage of life — then support them in turning those decisions into sustained behavior change. By combining AI, human expertise, personal health data, and accountability, Future helps members improve performance today while building the resilience, capacity, and healthspan they need for decades to come.

About the Role:

We’re hiring a Full-Stack Growth Engineer to build and maintain the product and systems that help more of the right people discover Future, convert into members, and reach their first moments of value.

You’ll work across web and backend surfaces that power acquisition, signup and access, onboarding and activation, and early engagement. You’ll ship experiments end to end, instrument funnels carefully, and partner closely with product, design, data, and marketing on a small, senior team.

This is a hands-on role. You’ll move between product judgment and system design, write production code, run trustworthy experiments, and turn learnings into durable product improvements — not one-off hacks.

What You’ll Own:

Acquisition and Conversion: Build and improve the web and product surfaces that introduce Future to prospective members and turn interest into signup. These include landing experiences, checkout and plan selection flows, and the instrumentation that shows where people drop off.

Access and Onboarding: Simplify signup, login, account creation, and first-session activation. Remove friction, clarify value on Day 1, and help new members connect with coaching and get started quickly.

Experimentation Systems: Design, ship, and analyze A/B and multivariate tests across the funnel. Partner with data to define metrics, guardrails, and experiment hygiene so we learn fast without polluting the product.

Full-Stack Delivery: Implement features across frontend and backend — APIs, services, web UI, and the glue between growth surfaces and the core member product. Prefer clear ownership and fast iteration over brittle one-off paths.

Measurement and Insight: Instrument funnels, cohorts, and activation milestones. Use qualitative and quantitative signal to find leverage, prioritize work, and explain why experiments won or lost.

Reliability for Growth Paths: Keep high-traffic growth journeys fast, stable, and observable. Treat conversion-critical paths with the same engineering care as core product.

Cross-Functional Partnership: Work tightly with product, design, data, and marketing. Translate growth hypotheses into shippable product work and bring engineering judgment into roadmap tradeoffs.

AI-Assisted Development: Use coding agents and AI tools to speed up exploration, implementation, testing, and review. Apply engineering judgment to validate their output before it reaches members or prospects.

Who You Are:

Experience and Background

You have 6+ years of professional software engineering experience, including meaningful ownership of consumer growth, acquisition, activation, or conversion surfaces.

You are strong full-stack: comfortable across modern web frontend and backend services, and able to ship an experiment from UI through API and data without waiting on another team for every layer.

You have run growth experiments in production — A/B tests, funnel instrumentation, and iteration based on measured outcomes, not vibes alone.

You understand customer journeys: segments, touchpoints, dropoff analysis, and how product changes move activation and retention metrics.

You can debug across web UI, networking, backend services, analytics pipelines, and CI.

You have partnered with product, design, and data (or marketing) to take ambiguous growth problems from hypothesis to shipped learning.

You write clear, maintainable code and care about experiment integrity, observability, and long-term operability — not just shipping the next test.

You use AI coding tools in your development workflow and know how to verify their output.

Domain Passion

You care about health, fitness, and helping people start — and stick with — better habits. You’re motivated by the craft of turning curiosity into membership and first value.

Working Style

You bias to action, then measure. You ship small, learn, and compound.

You raise concerns early and bring possible solutions when experiments or funnels look wrong.

You share context, invite feedback, and keep partners aligned on metrics and tradeoffs.

You take ownership from discovery through production support on the paths you ship.

You balance growth urgency with product quality and member trust.

Nice to Have

Experience at a consumer subscription, marketplace, or membership product where acquisition and activation were core to the business.

Familiarity with HIPAA and other laws and regulations that apply to health products and services.

Experience with paid acquisition landing systems, attribution, SEO/organic surfaces, lifecycle messaging, or referral loops.

Experience building or evolving experimentation platforms, feature flags, or analytics instrumentation at scale.

Experience with fitness, health, coaching, or other personalized consumer products.

Prior work on expert tooling, internal operator workflows, or coach-facing surfaces that support member outcomes.
